title: hicasso: the generation fence does not reach the render->commit gap -- a STAGED read tears and never heals
description:
FINDING from rf2-2rtt6.33, which settled HD-002 6.1's [OPEN] question. WITNESS: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/generation_fence_coverage_cljs_test.cljs (three rows, green, mutation-proved).

THE ANSWER TO 6.1 IS NO, and not by an arithmetic margin. The predecessor's commit-side re-read and the generation fence do not guard the SAME WINDOW, so 'which of the three fields does the one fence cover' has one answer for all three.

  predecessor   render probes a site .. COMMIT re-reads that site   (the render->commit gap)
  fence         capture gen .. BODY RUNS .. compare gen .. RETURN   (one body run)

arm1/runtime.cljs render-body captures the generation, runs the body, compares, and returns. The commit that follows -- React calling the read-set entry's subscribe, where acquire-cell! installs the edge and the watch -- compares NOTHING, by design ('no commit-phase deref'). The fence therefore covers a hazard the three fields never addressed (a commit landing BETWEEN TWO READS OF ONE BODY) and does not reach the window they were about. One-for-one on a different axis, not one-for-three.

WHAT DOES REACH THE GAP: the epoch-sum getSnapshot handed to useSyncExternalStore, plus React's own commit-time snapshot re-check. Real, and row 1 proves it works -- but driven by the SAME counter: an epoch moves only when flush! bumps it, flush! runs only from mark-dirty!, and mark-dirty! has exactly one caller, the value-change watch acquire-cell! installs AT COMMIT.

  version axis        covered for a RETAINED key (the watch pre-dates the move).
                      NOT covered for a STAGED key.
  frame/registry      no counterpart at all -- an epoch move is not a value change
  epoch axis          on an acquired reaction, so it cannot reach mark-dirty!.
  node-key axis       no counterpart at all, same argument: nothing in the runtime
                      observes node identity.

THE TEAR (row 2, reproduced): a boundary reads key K, which nothing holds yet. K has no cell, no watch, no epoch; getSnapshot answers 0. A write moves K before React commits. Nothing is marked, the generation does not move (so the change IS within one generation -- exactly the adversarial witness 6.1 asked for), no epoch bumps. The commit then acquires: the baseline deref takes the NEW value and the watch is armed one move too late to have reported it. getSnapshot answers the SAME number, so React's re-check finds no tear and schedules no re-render. The boundary paints the OLD value and NOTHING EVER CORRECTS IT -- the watch's baseline is already the new value, so no later notification is coming for a change that already happened.

This is verbatim Spec 006 invariant 5's stronger half: 'a STAGED site publishes stale and nothing ever corrects it, because a dependency's first render has no earlier channel to heal through' -- 'a panel mounting exactly as a permission drops, a user switches, or a record is redacted'. It is a P0 bug class by validation.md's own words.

REACHABILITY IS NOT EXOTIC. Every boundary's FIRST read of a key nothing else holds is staged, so every mount of a new row/panel/route is a candidate; and Arm 1's own runtime already contemplates a flush raised while a body is running (flush! defers notifications when rendering? is true), which is a sibling boundary writing during the same React render pass -- with the reading boundary's fence already closed. The window is at least as wide as React's passive-effect flush, since subscribe runs in an effect.

WHAT THIS BEAR ON: hd-002-adjudication.md's tripwire checklist item 4 is 'Am I re-reading subscription values at commit? Fired'. This finding does not fire it by itself -- the tear is fixable by channels that are not a per-read commit deref -- but it removes the record's stated reason for believing item 4 can stay unfired on correctness grounds. Under the operator's Surface B ruling a collector loss is NULL, not a fallback, so this is the programme's decision, not the arm's.

NOT IMPLEMENTED HERE, DELIBERATELY. rf2-2rtt6.33 was an analysis-and-witness bead and Arm 1 owns the collector surface. Candidate repairs, none costed, all needing the tripwire read against them:
  (a) make a staged key's FIRST commit compare the acquire-time baseline against the value the render read, and correct when they differ. One comparison per NEWLY ACQUIRED key per commit -- not per read per commit -- so it is O(new edges), zero on a steady-state re-render. This is the smallest repair and the closest to the predecessor's semantics.
  (b) fold identity/epoch into the epoch-sum so the node-key and frame/registry-epoch axes have a counterpart at all.
  (c) argue the staged case away with a reachability bound. The record would have to make that argument; it currently does not make any.

DO NOT close this by widening the fence's retry loop -- the fence's window closes when the body returns, and the tear happens after that.
notes:
CLOSED BY PR #7324 (branch worker/tear-2rtt6-42, head f4e6440e27). The tear is closed with a witness, mutation-proved both ways in node AND in real Chromium.

THE FIX — candidate (b)'s shape, not (a)'s, and smaller than either. A key with NO CELL now contributes its frame's `commit-basis` to the epoch-sum getSnapshot instead of nothing, and a cell records the basis it was CREATED at:

    commit-basis(frame) = @!generation + re-frame.frame/frame-commit-epoch(frame)

The second term is the SUBSTRATE'S OWN observation-port evidence counter — one bump per physical frame-state install at both write chokepoints — and Spec 006 already uses it, verbatim, to detect 'the frame's durable state moved in the render->commit gap ... without watching anything'. The arm was missing the one field the substrate had already built. Being a counter read rather than a watch, it has none of the generation's dependency on a cell existing, which was the whole of the defect.

A staged key therefore reads basis@render while the boundary renders and basis@commit once the commit acquires it: equal when nothing installed in the gap, different when something did. React stores each fiber's render-time snapshot and re-reads getSnapshot immediately after subscribe returns (mountSyncExternalStore pushes subscribeToStore as a passive effect and updateStoreInstance as the NEXT one; updateStoreInstance is checkIfSnapshotChanged + forceStoreRerender — React 19.2, read in react-dom-client). So the comparison is per boundary, is one number, and holds NO RECORD OF WHAT ANY READ RETURNED.

WHY NOT candidate (a). 'Compare the acquire-time baseline against the value the render read' needs somewhere to keep what the render read, and the only ledger-free place to keep it is a second render-populated buffer the commit reconciles — which is the tripwire. Comparing BASES needs no such record because React is already holding the per-boundary render-time value. The tripwire did NOT fire: no second scratch, nothing keyed by render/attempt/lane/generation, no per-read object, no commit-phase deref. hd-002-adjudication.md item 4 stays unfired, now for a mechanical reason rather than an argued one.

THE BASELINE DEREF IS NOT THE FIX, confirmed. It is already in acquire-cell! and is the right repair for the spurious-first-re-render problem; it gives a correct baseline and NO COMPARISON, so it silently adopts the moved value. Asserted as a row (the-baseline-deref-alone-cannot-see-the-move) rather than argued.

SIBLING HOLE ALSO CLOSED: the fence compared the generation, which cannot see a MID-BODY move of a staged key either (no cell -> no watch -> no mark-dirty! -> no bump), so a body that read a staged key, dispatched, and read again could straddle two commits with the generation still. It compares the basis now.

COST: hooks unchanged at 2; subscribe still closes over the read set and nothing else; zero allocation; ZERO in steady state (a mounted boundary holds a reference to every key it reads, so its snapshot has no staged term at all). Conservative only in the safe direction — a boundary mounting exactly as an unrelated write lands re-renders once. Executable change: SIX LINES.

WITNESS: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/staged_read_tear_cljs_test.cljs (new, 6 rows, against the arm's OWN runtime rather than a transcription) + Case 3 in arm1/generation_fence_dom_cljs_test.cljs (real Chromium; staged as a SIBLING boundary writing during the same React render pass, so it needs no guess about passive-effect scheduling). Also noted in that file: its Case 2 is LABELLED as 6.1's case and is not it — it dispatches after the mount settles, so the key is RETAINED.

MUTATION PROOF (fix reverted, witness left in place):
  npm run test:cljs     exit 1 — 12,196 tests / 60,717 assertions, 3 failures, ALL in the new ns and nowhere else. 'expected: (not= at-render (rt/snapshot-of entry)) / actual: (not (not= 0 0))' — the bead's sentence, executed.
  npm run test:browser  exit 1 — 938 / 5,800, 1 failure: actual (not (= "true" "false")) — the real DOM, painting stale forever.
GATES (foreground, exit codes echoed):
  npm run test:cljs     exit 0 — 12,196 / 60,717 / 0 failures
  npm run test:browser  exit 0 — 938 / 5,800 / 0 failures
  scripts/test-fast-pr.sh  PASS, exit 0
  clj-kondo CI-pinned 2026.04.15, full CI --lint set, --fail-level error: exit 0, errors: 0; arm1/ re-lint errors 0 warnings 0.
No page under docs/design/hicasso/** touched, so the mkdocs-does-not-cover caveat applies to nothing here.

SCOPED OUT, FILED AS rf2-2rtt6.44: the registry-epoch axis (a :sub re-registration is not a frame-state install; and observation/registry-epoch* is ^:private with no public reader, so the arm cannot read it without a substrate change — closing it for a RETAINED key means re-rendering every boundary on every re-registration, a design decision rather than a defect fix) and the node-key axis (frame/dissoc-frame! clears the commit-epoch entry, so a same-id reincarnation RESTARTS at 0 — commit-basis is monotone only within one incarnation, which is exactly why the observation port carries :node-key as a third field). Both named in the runtime's docstrings with the bead id.

rf2-2rtt6.43 ANNOTATED: generation_fence_coverage_cljs_test.cljs (PR #7323) TRANSCRIBES the three functions this PR changed, so once #7323 lands its row 2 asserts a defect the arm no longer has.
close_reason: Closed

title: ABLATION: what does dropping the concurrent-store contract return, on clock AND heap — and is the cheap path separable?
description:
OPERATOR-AUTHORISED (Mike, 2026-07-27). This is the one remaining measurement that can CHANGE the answer on rf2-lbs3y rather than refine it.

THE OBSERVATION THAT PROMPTED IT (Mike, verbatim): 'the problem is that Reagent has never really ever shown that problem' and 'Ray frame doesn't even take advantage of Reacts suspense features'.
VERIFIED: there is NO actual React Suspense use anywhere in implementation/*/src. Every hit is a COMMENT or docstring reasoning about Suspense-aborted renders (frame_boundary.cljs, provider.cljs, spine.cljs). The only real integration is in re-frame.ui — the donor tier already ruled out — and ssr/suspense.cljc opens by stating it is NOT React Suspense.
BUT we mount through createRoot, so a CONSUMER can introduce transitions or a Suspense boundary at any time. The substrate defends against a hazard it never creates for itself.

THE REFRAME: the question is not 'is a tear-free guarantee worth ~10x'. It is 'was adopting concurrent React worth what it forces?' — and then 'must EVERY consumer pay for it, permanently, so the one who eventually reaches for Suspense does not get a silent wrong render?'

THE HYPOTHESIS: the two worst rows may be ONE row. useSyncExternalStore is 516 B of the ~1,039 B React's hooks add per boundary (rf2-oob3g's ablation ladder), and the commit-side re-read is the clock cost (~9.9x broad update). BOTH service the same concurrent-rendering contract. Drop it and you may recover a large slice of RETAINED HEAP as well as CLOCK. Every lever tried so far moved its own term and left the row unchanged; this is the only candidate that could move both.

TWO QUESTIONS, BOTH REQUIRED:
  (1) WHAT COMES BACK. Build an ablation arm: the same witness, a boundary wired WITHOUT the concurrent-store contract (no useSyncExternalStore, no commit-side re-read). Measure CLOCK and HEAP against the existing published arms.
  (2) IS THE CHEAP PATH SEPARABLE. Could this be OPT-IN — cheap by default, guarantee switched on when a consumer uses concurrent features? Or does it mean two code paths through the commit machinery, which is a permanent clarity cost? An honest 'not separable without duplicating commit' is a complete and valuable answer.

THIS IS AN ABLATION, NOT A SHIP. Do NOT land a change that drops invariant 5. That is the operator's decision and this bead exists to price it.

CAVEAT TO CARRY INTO THE REPORT: a tear is a SILENT wrong render, and the ugly instance is not a wrong item count — it is a stale panel still showing data after the state that authorised it has gone (a permission dropped, a user switched, a record redacted). Given this project's classification machinery that must be priced explicitly, not assumed away. Reagent's decade is strong evidence it does not bite in practice; it is not proof it cannot.
close_reason: Measured. PR #7159. Verdict in the comment: the ablation returns ~14% of a broad write and 363-376 B/boundary, the two returns come from different halves of the contract, and the decision half is not separable at all. No shipped change; invariant 5 untouched.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MEASURED. PR #7159 (branch worker/uses-ablation-so3io). Report: docs/design/freehand/studio/concurrent-store-ablation.md. Raw data + working: ai/findings/2026-07-27.concurrent-store-ablation-so3io.md and ai/findings/rf2-so3io-raw/.

NO SHIPPED CHANGE. git diff origin/main -- implementation/core/src implementation/freehand/src spec is EMPTY. Invariant 5 is not dropped anywhere.

(1) WHAT COMES BACK. Ablation ladder on B6's window and B7's door, both arm orders, 6 rounds each, every pair carrying a REFERENCE rung (same hand-built body, real shell, real cell/commit!) so the difference is the contract and nothing else.

  broad update   3.4-4.1 fwd / 3.1-3.9 rev  ->  3.0-3.6 / 2.7-3.2   -13.6% / -14.8%, cheaper in 12 of 12 paired rounds
  narrow update  9.9-12.3 / 9.6-12.6        -> 10.1-12.3 / 9.4-11.8  NULL, direction flips between orders
  mount (300)    0.9-1.1 / 0.8-1.1          ->  0.9-1.0 / 0.8-1.0    <=0.1 ms, the clock quantum
  heap sub-free  2,416 / 2,431 B/bnd        ->  2,041 / 2,062        -375 / -369 B, ranges DISJOINT
  heap reactive  4,294 / 4,281 B/bnd        ->  3,918 / 3,918        -376 / -363 B, ranges DISJOINT

THE HYPOTHESIS IS FALSIFIED, AND USEFULLY. The two worst rows are NOT one row. An isolating rung (React's six hooks over a two-field JS object, no ViewCell) returns 355-357 B = 95-97% of the WHOLE heap return; the commit-side re-read retains 8-20 B, i.e. nothing. And the sub-free mount pair has zero dependencies, so its commit loops over zero sites — it bounds the hook half at <=0.1 ms, which puts >=80% of the broad-write saving on the commit re-read. Heap return = the hook. Clock return = the commit. Two levers on two axes, neither large.

WHERE IT LEAVES THE ROW: a contract-free Freehand boundary is still 4.97-5.04x Reagent on sub-free standing heap, 3.79-3.81x on the reactive witness, ~5.5x on a broad write and ~1.6x on mount. rf2-oob3g's ceiling tightens rather than lifts: ViewCell driven to zero AND the contract gone still leaves 2.05-2.07x Reagent.

Also: subtracting rf2-oob3g's 516 B uSES + 145 B useCallback would predict a 661 B return. Measured 355-357 — the replacement (useReducer + the folded subscription) costs ~305 B. The subtraction overstates by 1.85x.

(2) SEPARABLE? Commit half YES, cheaply — a branch in commit-readings plus a flag on the cell, ~12 lines; the ~115 duplicated lines in the bench are an artefact of those fns being PRIVATE, not the cost of the feature. Hook half YES, expensively — hooks cannot be conditional, so it is two shell/renders and two component types keyed into shell-signature (machinery exists, the lowering axis uses it), PLUS a fork in checkpoint.cljs (see below).

THE DECISION IS NOT SEPARABLE, and that is what settles it. Nothing in re-frame2 can observe that a consumer used startTransition / useDeferredValue / <Suspense> — we mount through createRoot and see no signal, and the only detector for an interrupted render is useSyncExternalStore, the thing being switched off. The detection is circular. So the switch must be DECLARED, and a wrong declaration produces exactly the bug class the guarantee deletes, in a build that was told it did not need checking. It also cannot be per-boundary: a tear is not local (a stale panel BESIDE a fresh one), so any honest switch is at least per-root. Permanent cost: two shells, two hook skeletons, a flag through commit, a fork in the window closer, and every ViewCell law verified in BOTH modes.

TWO THINGS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED:

  a) {:ref true, :nc false}, both runs. Without useSyncExternalStore a boundary CANNOT repaint inside react-dom/flushSync. uSES's listener schedules at the SYNC lane; a useReducer dispatch from a microtask takes the default lane and an empty flushSync flushes only the sync lane. rf2-w2m25's synchronous commit door is built on the store — a cheap path must rebuild it by keeping its own queue of pending force-updates and draining it inside a synchronous commit boundary (which is what reagent.core/flush is, and what the nc arm does).

  b) THE STAGED TEAR, on a WATCHABLE browser host, real port, real sub-cache. A dependency moving in the render->commit gap:
       retained + shipped -> revision +1, published FRESH
       retained + ablated -> revision  0, dirty? TRUE,  published stale  (self-heals one window late)
       staged   + shipped -> revision +1, published FRESH
       staged   + ablated -> revision  0, dirty? FALSE, published stale  (NOTHING corrects it, ever)
     obs/acquire! installs the watch DURING the commit that needed it, after the move. So a FIRST render of a dependency paints stale and stays stale: a panel mounting while a permission drops, a user switches, a record is redacted. Spec 006 justifies invariant 5 on the headless case; the browser case is STRONGER than the spec claims. Filed as rf2-anmdr (P1) — PR #7143's two rows are both the RETAINED case and the staged one has no shipped row.

  c) NOT Freehand-only if generalised: in the ADAPTERS, spine.cljs puts the durable sub-cache acquire/release INSIDE uSES's subscribe callback precisely because React never runs it for an uncommitted render (rf2-es09qq, after rf2-879fe). Freehand does not depend on that (its ownership is a layout effect), but a re-frame-wide 'drop the store' policy reintroduces a ref-count LEAK class there.

GATES, all foreground, all exit 0:
  clojure -M:test (implementation/freehand)                    1220 tests / 8225 assertions / 0 failures
  PR #7143's two invariant-5 rows, BY NAME                        2 tests /   11 assertions / 0 failures
  npm run test:cljs                                           11799 tests / 58740 assertions / 0 failures
  npm run test:browser (BROWSER_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS=600000)          833 tests /  5313 assertions / 0 failures
Controls: 0 unverified writes in every clock row; 0 unverified of 195 heap mounts; canonical-DOM parity across 7 mount arms and 6 update arms in both orders; positive control (587,500 unboxed doubles = 4,700,000 B predicted) within 0.061% on reader A and 0.0005% on the independent snapshot reader; published heap rows reproduce to better than 1.2%.

NOT DETERMINED: SSR/hydration under a store-free shell (uSES's getServerSnapshot has no counterpart); heap under update; a v/defview-shaped ablated arm (needs a shell seam in react.cljs, no mandate here) — so the pair's ratios are for a hand-built boundary, with the emitter walk visible beside them as published-minus-ref (~0.7-1.3 ms broad, ~20 B heap) and absent from BOTH rungs.

title: RULED dev-only (a): document reg-app-schema dev-only semantics at point of use + qualify EP-0025 as dev-posture
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-lwtlk while splitting implementation/ssr's flows-integration-test for the production-gate lane rf2-hnrwo. Same CLASS as rf2-rqje9 — a documented, deliberate design choice whose production consequence had never been EXECUTED until a suite ran under the real gate — but a DIFFERENT consequence on a different surface, so the rf2-rqje9 ruling as framed does not cover it.

WHAT THE GATE SHOWS. re-frame.flows-integration-test/flow-output-schema-failure-rejects-candidate-before-install pins the EP-0025 candidate-validation contract: a flow whose OUTPUT violates the registered app-db schema causes the WHOLE candidate to be rejected before install, so neither the flow's write nor the handler's own :db reaches the container.

Under clojure -M:test that holds. Under clojure -M:test:prod-gate (-Dre-frame.debug=false) it does not:

  expected: (= baseline-db (rf/app-db-value :rf/default))
    actual: (not (= {:n 1, :derived {:doubled 2}} {:n -3, :derived {:doubled -6}}))

The schema declares [:derived :doubled] to be [:int {:min 0}]. Under the gate the -6 INSTALLS, and the handler's :n -3 installs with it.

THE MECHANISM IS DOCUMENTED, which is what makes this a ruling rather than a bug report.

  - implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc, validate-event! (~line 763): 'Body gated on interop/debug-enabled?. Spec 010 validate-*! is a dev-only validator surface — per re-frame.schemas.validate SS-Production builds, every dev-time validate-*! body sits inside its own (if interop/debug-enabled? ...) gate and DCE-elides under :advanced+goog.DEBUG=false. The validator therefore unconditionally returns true in production whether or not the schemas artefact is loaded (the boundary-validation seam :schemas/validate-with-registered-fn is the production-side surface, not this one).'

  - implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc (~line 619): 'Per Spec 009 SS-Production builds the entire body lives inside a (if interop/debug-enabled? ... true) gate as the OUTERMOST form ... Production builds return true unconditionally — the rollback path is dev-only (post-commit validation is gated by debug-enabled?, so no failure is observable to roll back against).'

So the elision is intended and the rationale (DCE the reason strings, keywords, validator deref and trace calls out of production bundles) is sound on its own terms. What nobody had seen is the consequence: reg-app-schema is a NO-OP in production, so an app-db value that a developer's tests prove can never exist, can exist on a production server. The atomic-candidate-rejection contract EP-0025 describes is a dev-posture contract.

WHY THIS IS NOT rf2-rqje9. rf2-rqje9 asks whether an unroutable SSR request may answer HTTP 200, and its three candidate shapes are all about SSR status derivation. This is a core app-db integrity question on a surface SSR merely happens to exercise (flows-integration-test lives in ssr/test only because the ssr :test alias is the one whose dep fan-out pulls core + schemas + flows + routing + machines together). :rf.error/schema-validation-failure appears in rf2-rqje9's list of DCE-under-gate categories, but only as one of the four the SSR projector cannot see; the ruling does not address whether the VALIDATION should run.

THE QUESTION FOR THE OPERATOR. Is reg-app-schema documented, and understood by users, as a DEVELOPMENT-ONLY assertion — or as a runtime integrity guarantee? The shapes, none of which a worker should choose:

  (a) Dev-only as designed. Then Spec 010 should say so where an application author will read it, in the words a user needs ('your app-db schemas do not run in production builds'), not only in a source comment about DCE. The migration guide and the reg-app-schema docstring want the same sentence. rf2-lwtlk then splits the deftest with that citation.

  (b) App-db candidate validation should survive the gate, the way the boundary-validation seam :schemas/validate-with-registered-fn does. That is a framework change with a real production cost (the validator deref and the Malli walk on every commit) and needs a perf position.

  (c) A middle position — validation on by default in production but disableable per-frame, or gated on a separate knob from the trace/debug flag, so the DCE win stays available to those who want it.

DO NOT let a worker pick one to shrink the rf2-lwtlk roster. re-frame.flows-integration-test stays rostered as known-red in scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh with this bead named; every OTHER assertion in that namespace has already been posture-split by rf2-lwtlk, so the namespace comes off the roster with a one-line change the moment this lands.
notes:
RAISED P1 -> P0 BY THE MAYOR (2026-07-27). This is the SECOND operator-grade finding from the production-gate programme, and I judge it the more consequential of the two.

THE SYMPTOM: under the documented production gate -Dre-frame.debug=false, a flow output that VIOLATES the registered app-db schema is NOT rejected. The invalid candidate INSTALLS, and the handler's own :db installs with it.

WHAT THAT MEANS IN ONE SENTENCE: reg-app-schema is a NO-OP IN PRODUCTION, and EP-0025's atomic-candidate-rejection contract is a DEV-POSTURE contract.

THE MECHANISM IS DOCUMENTED AND DELIBERATE, which is why this is a ruling and not a bug report. router.cljc's validate-event! and schemas/validate.cljc record it verbatim: 'Production builds return true unconditionally — the rollback path is dev-only.'

WHY I RATE IT ABOVE rf2-rqje9. rqje9 (SSR returning 200 for an unroutable URL) is a wrong RESPONSE on one surface. This one silently admits INVALID STATE INTO app-db in production, and app-db is the thing every subscription, view and effect reads downstream. A consumer who registers a schema reasonably believes it is a guarantee; in production it is documentation. The failure is also silent — no throw, no rollback, no diagnostic, because the diagnostic is the part that got elided.

NEITHER OF rf2-rqje9's THREE SHAPES ADDRESSES THIS. Same class, different surface, and it needs its own ruling. The worker picked no remedy, which was correct.

WHAT AN OPERATOR RULING NEEDS TO DECIDE, and none of these is a worker's call:
  (a) Accept as designed — schema validation is a DEVELOPMENT tool, production trusts the programmer. Then say so LOUDLY in the consumer-facing docs, not only in a source comment, because the current reg-app-schema surface does not read that way.
  (b) Validation stays always-on in production, with the rejection/rollback path unconditional. Changes production cost and behaviour; needs its own perf and egress review.
  (c) A middle shape — e.g. validate always, but on violation log-and-install rather than reject-and-roll-back, so production gets a signal without the rollback machinery.

CONTEXT: the whole reason this surfaced is rf2-f8x2i, which wired the first CI lane ever to run a suite under the real gate. Before today NOTHING in CI set the property, and every suite calling itself a 'production gate' test rebound interop/debug-enabled? with with-redefs — which cannot reach a load-time gate. This class of defect was structurally invisible.

SEQUENCING: 12 of flows-integration-test's 14 reds are ordinary test spelling and are already split; its roster line in scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh comes out with a one-line change once this ruling lands. DO NOT let a worker pick a remedy to shrink that roster.
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-27, dossier review): OPTION (a) — reg-app-schema app-db candidate validation is a DEVELOPMENT-ONLY assertion, as designed. Do NOT make it always-on in production and do NOT add a middle knob (per-frame toggle, separate flag, or validate-and-log-without-rollback). Document the dev-only contract at the point of use, and qualify EP-0025's atomicity language as a dev-posture contract where it is stated. This ruling was reached from the ai/decisions dossier (primary analysis + independent Codex second opinion, which CONVERGED on (a)); the dossier is now deleted and this note is the durable record.

DECISIVE REASONING
1. Posture. Pre-alpha, trust-the-programmer, minimal ergonomic API, no insurance machinery for a consumer nobody has. Schema validation as a dev tool matches clojure.spec instrumentation (official guide advises against production instrumentation for overhead), Malli's own Var instrumentation (documented as development-intended, production an explicit choice), and React PropTypes. Production correctness rules belong in handler/domain logic; untrusted ingress belongs at the explicit :rf.schema/at-boundary event interceptor, which SURVIVES the gate and stays.
2. Always-on (b) is not a one-line fix, it is a new production feature. Codex-verified cost: re-frame.schemas.validate/validate-app-schema! (implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc, lines 619-869) in its live arm walks EVERY registered app-db schema for the frame, does a get-in per registered path, invokes the validator on each slice, and overlapping registrations deliberately re-validate overlapping data — cost proportional to the whole registered schema set plus each schema's data traversal, on every event returning :db, in every production app, forever. Not a cheap changed-leaf check.
3. Production error-channel gap. re-frame.router/run-candidate-validation! (implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc, lines 1079-1190) runs before the single container write; commit-and-flow! maps a false verdict to the always-on :rolled-back outcome, but the failure explanation, failing path, redaction, and malformed-schema diagnostics are all emitted through the DEBUG-GATED trace surface. Merely removing the validator gate would yield production rejections whose only durable signal is the coarse :rolled-back outcome. A sound always-on design would additionally need a production error channel, privacy/egress rules, and a malformed-validator policy. That is (b)'s real price and the reason it needs a consumer before it is built.
4. Knob (c) is exactly the knob-growth the posture rejects: a new configuration surface, a documented mode matrix, and (for log-don't-reject) a THIRD behaviour distinct from both dev and current prod.
5. The mechanism is deliberate and documented in source. router.cljc validate-event! (~line 763) and schemas/validate.cljc (~line 619) both record that the entire validator body sits inside (if interop/debug-enabled? ... true) so reason strings, keywords, validator deref, Malli walk and trace calls DCE out under :advanced+goog.DEBUG=false / -Dre-frame.debug=false: "Production builds return true unconditionally — the rollback path is dev-only." The only genuine defect found is that parts of the consumer-facing surface do not repeat this.
6. If real-world demand for production app-db enforcement ever appears, design it THEN as an explicit production boundary with measured cost and an always-on diagnostic contract — a feature with a consumer, not insurance.

THE CONCRETE WITNESS (preserve for the doc pass and the test split)
re-frame.flows-integration-test/flow-output-schema-failure-rejects-candidate-before-install (implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/flows_integration_test.clj): registered schema declares [:derived :doubled] to be [:int {:min 0}]; an event produces a candidate where :doubled is -6 and the handler's own :n is -3. Dev (clojure -M:test): whole candidate rejected before install, app-db keeps baseline {:n 1, :derived {:doubled 2}}. Prod gate (clojure -M:test:prod-gate, -Dre-frame.debug=false): {:n -3, :derived {:doubled -6}} installs, silently — candidate validation passes vacuously; nothing in flow or commit machinery is bypassed. Surfaced only because rf2-f8x2i wired the first CI lane running under the REAL gate (prior "production gate" tests rebound debug-enabled? via with-redefs, which cannot reach a load-time gate).

IMPLEMENTATION OBLIGATIONS (the doc pass this bead now carries — NARROW scope, per the Codex audit; do not launch a broad documentation project)
Already-right consumer material (verify, don't rewrite): spec/010-Schemas.md already says global validation is compile-time-elided by default and offers :rf.schema/at-boundary for untrusted ingress; docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md already calls a schema "a tripwire, not a guard", keeps the real pos? invariant in the handler, and states the invalid write installs in production; docs/api/re-frame.schemas.md opens with production elision; root README describes the feature as production-elidable with zero overhead.
The actual gaps to close:
  1. Spec 010: one NORMATIVE consumer-facing sentence stating that reg-app-schema candidate validation and its atomic rejection are development-build semantics — production still registers schemas for introspection but does not check them ("your app-db schemas do not run in production builds", in user words, where an application author will read it).
  2. reg-app-schema facade docstrings (BOTH the singular and plural macro/function forms) get that same sentence at the point of use.

Explicitly KEPT as-is: always-on registration-shape checks; the :rf.schema/at-boundary event interceptor as the production-side ingress surface; the boundary-validation seam :schemas/validate-with-registered-fn (the production-side surface, distinct from validate-event!).
Explicitly NOT done now: validate-and-log, per-frame modes, a second flag, any production validation knob.

UNBLOCK — rf2-lwtlk
With this ruling as citation, rf2-lwtlk splits the remaining deftest BY POSTURE: assert rejection only when debug validation is enabled, and assert the production INSTALL explicitly when it is disabled (making the split executable rather than known-red). 12 of flows-integration-test's 14 reds are already posture-split, so the namespace comes off the known-red roster in scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh with a one-line change once the split lands.

DOC PASS SHIPPED — PR #7166 (worker/schema-devonly-bkvu5), 2026-07-27. Documentation only; no behaviour change (implementation diff is docstrings/comments, no code form touched).

ALL FIVE IMPLEMENTATION OBLIGATIONS CLOSED:

Facade docstrings — BOTH singular and plural, in BOTH forms: core.cljc macros + CLJS fn-aliases, core_schemas.cljc defwrappers, and storage.cljc (the canonical docstring the 'full semantics' pointer lands on; it said 'validation runs in dev' but never said what production does). validate.cljc's validate-app-schema! now states the consumer-visible consequence, not just the DCE rationale.

Each distinguishes the DEV-ONLY schema gate from the ALWAYS-ON atomicity and malformed-payload abort — over-qualifying would have been as wrong as not qualifying.

title: RULING NEEDED: under -Dre-frame.debug=false an unroutable SSR request returns 200, not 404
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-hnrwo, the first time implementation/ssr had ever executed under the real `-Dre-frame.debug=false` gate. It is NOT a new defect and NOT a lane bug — the behaviour is documented in the source. It is here because a human should sign off on it, and until rf2-hnrwo nobody could see it.

WHAT THE GATE SHOWS. `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc` registers TWO error listeners under one logical id `::error-projection`:

  - `rf-emit/register-error-listener! ::error-projection` — ALWAYS-ON, survives the gate. Covers the categories that flow through `re-frame.error-emit/dispatch-on-error!`: `:rf.error/handler-exception`, the `:rf.error/fx-handler-exception` family, `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception`, `:rf.error/sub-exception`.
  - `trace-tooling/register-listener! ::error-projection` — the DEVELOPMENT trace listener. The file's own comment: the categories that emit only via `trace/emit-error!` — `:rf.error/no-such-handler`, `:rf.error/no-such-route`, `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure`, `:rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded` — "DCE under `interop/debug-enabled? = false`; the substrate-shipping projector relies on the dev gate for them."

CONSEQUENCE ON A PRODUCTION SERVER. Nothing buffers those four categories, so `flush-response!` / `get-response` has nothing to project and never stamps `:status`. A request for a URL that matches no route renders whatever the app produces for an unresolved route and returns HTTP 200. Same for a schema-validation reject (no 400) and for a drain-depth blow-up. Under `clojure -M:test` all of it projects correctly, which is why every existing suite is green.

EVIDENCE. Under `scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh`'s posture, `ssr-end-to-end-test` (119 red assertions), `ssr-flush-response-result-test` (12), `ssr-error-two-frame-attribution-test` (5), `ssr-error-view-failed-no-project-test` (2) and `ssr-head-resolution-no-project-test` (2) all fail on assertions of exactly this shape — "flush projects the buffered `:no-such-handler` → 404 onto `:status`". Reproduce: `bash scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh` with the roster line for those namespaces removed, or run `clojure -M:test:prod-gate` bare in implementation/ssr.

THE RULING WANTED, one of:

  (a) INTENDED, and the status codes are the substrate's job in production — in which case Spec 011 should say so where a server integrator will read it, and the five test namespaces above get their posture split under rf2-lwtlk with that citation.
  (b) NOT INTENDED — those four categories need an always-on emission path the way `:rf.error/handler-exception` has one, and the projection contract holds in both postures. That is a framework change, not a test change, and it blocks the rf2-lwtlk cluster.

Do not triage the rf2-lwtlk group-(c) namespaces before this lands; the split you write depends on which answer it is.
notes:
RAISED P1 -> P0 BY THE MAYOR (2026-07-27) and surfaced to the operator immediately.

WHY: this is the first finding from the production-gate programme with a DIRECT, USER-FACING production consequence. Everything else the programme has turned up — across implementation/core (91 of 174 namespaces), routing (293 failures) and ssr (217 failures) — has been test spelling or prod-elided annotation. This one is not.

THE SYMPTOM: under the documented production gate -Dre-frame.debug=false, an SSR request for an UNROUTABLE URL returns HTTP 200 instead of 404.

THE MECHANISM IS DOCUMENTED AND DELIBERATE, which is what makes it a ruling rather than a bug report. implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc records that the always-on re-frame.error-emit listener covers handler-exception, fx-handler-exception, flow-eval-exception and sub-exception — while no-such-handler, NO-SUCH-ROUTE, schema-validation-failure and drain-depth-exceeded 'DCE under interop/debug-enabled? = false'. So the design chose to elide those four in production. Nobody had ever EXECUTED the consequence of that choice, because until today nothing in CI ran any suite under the real gate (rf2-f8x2i).

SCALE: it accounts for the five largest ssr known-red namespaces; ssr-end-to-end-test alone is 119 failures. It blocks the ssr triage stream rf2-lwtlk.

THE QUESTION FOR THE OPERATOR: is a 200-for-404 acceptable in production SSR? The three shapes available, none of which a worker should choose:
  (a) It is correct as designed — SSR consumers are expected to determine routability before rendering, and the status code is theirs to set. Then the ssr red cluster is spelling after all, and the docs should say so at the consumer-facing level, not only in a source comment.
  (b) no-such-route specifically should join the always-on set. Narrow, but it changes what production emits and therefore what off-box shippers receive — an egress-surface change with its own review obligations.
  (c) SSR should derive the status from routability independently of the error stream, so the gate cannot affect it at all.

DO NOT let a worker pick one to make the ssr lane greener. That is exactly the pressure that produces a wrong answer, and the lane is already honest with the cluster rostered as known-red.
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-27, dossier review):

DECISION — NOT option (a). A production route miss MUST return HTTP 404. Implement a NARROW form of (b): promote the single URL-driven route-miss emission (`:rf.error/no-such-handler {:kind :route}` from `url-change-fx`) onto the EXISTING always-on error axis, retaining its dev trace; do NOT bulk-promote "the four categories"; do NOT build a second route-slice-to-status pipeline (option (c) rejected). One adjacent correction lands with it: `default-error-projector-fn`'s 404 arm gets gated on `[:tags :kind] = :route` so a `:kind :event` miss (a server defect) maps to the generic 500, not 404. Implementation bead: rf2-ov56u (carries the full brief + acceptance criteria). This adopts the dossier's appended Codex recommendation over the dossier's primary (c) recommendation — every factual claim in the Codex analysis was independently verified against source before ruling (verification detail below).

WHY NOT (a): the deployed server is wrong on the wire regardless of programmer skill — RFC 9110 §15.3.1/§15.5.5 define 200 as success and 404 as no-current-representation, and Google classifies a 200'd not-found page as a "soft 404" and drops it from Search. The framework computes the route miss (it commits the durable `:rf.route/not-found` slice) and then withholds the answer from the wire in exactly the build you ship; every consumer would hand-build the workaround. This is one of the few places "trust the programmer" does not apply. Also: Spec 009's error catalogue ALREADY classifies `:rf.error/no-such-handler` as ALWAYS-ON with mandatory `:kind` including `:kind :route` for `:rf.route/handle-url-change` — so (a) would leave the implementation in breach of the spec's own classification, and the fix is conforming implementation to spec, not new architecture.

WHY NOT (c) (the dossier's primary recommendation): deriving `:status` from `[:rf.runtime/routing :current]` at the SSR host boundary would duplicate routing policy in every host adapter, bypass or synthetically recreate the configured `reg-error-projector` seam (custom projectors, redirect precedence, per-frame attribution, streaming classification), and conflate a durable navigation slice (used on client and server, through programmatic and URL doors) with the per-request HTTP decision. The "status is response semantics, not diagnostics" root-cause framing conflates the two channels: the always-on error-emit axis is NOT the debug-gated diagnostics bus — it is the production-survivable substrate the SSR projector already treats as its status source of truth (sub-exception, handler-exception, ssr-render-failed all project production statuses through it today). The recurrence risk (c) was meant to close is handled by Spec 009's promotion criterion plus the prod-gate lane (rf2-hnrwo/rf2-f8x2i) that caught this one. Under the posture, (b-narrow) is the smaller change on the existing seam; (c) is the over-engineered shape here.

VERIFICATION THAT SETTLED THE DISAGREEMENT (checked 2026-07-27 against source; the bead/dossier "four dev-only categories" premise, taken from ssr.cljc's comment, is STALE):
- `:rf.error/no-such-handler` `:kind :event` is ALREADY always-on: `re-frame.router.diagnostics/handle-no-handler!` fans BOTH channels via the `:error-emit/emit-error-both` hook (always-on `dispatch-on-error!` + dev trace).
- `:rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded` is ALREADY always-on (rf2-fcbrjo): `router/handle-depth-exceeded!` calls `error-emit/dispatch-error-record!` (router.cljc ~3059); it projects 500 via the projector's default arm in production.
- `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` is DELIBERATELY dev-only: boundary validation itself is production-elided (Spec 010 §Production builds — `validate-*!` returns true unconditionally under the gate), so no production reject exists to stamp 400 for. Its prod-gate reds are dev-posture assertions -> posture-split under rf2-lwtlk. The flow-output variant has its own ruling bead (rf2-bkvu5).
- `:rf.error/no-such-route` is the `route-url` CALLER-MISUSE category (throws synchronously; Spec 009 catalogues it diagnostic) — it is NOT the URL-driven miss and stays diagnostic.
- The SOLE production hole is one emit site: `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/url_change.cljc` `url-change-fx` (~lines 331-347) computes the miss, commits `:rf.route/not-found`, builds redacted tags `{:url ... :kind :route :recovery :replaced-with-default (+ :frame :reason)}` via `egress/redact-url-tag` — then routes ONLY through `plan/emit-intents!` -> `plan.cljc` ~246 -> `trace/emit-error!`, which is gated on `interop/debug-enabled?` (trace.cljc ~920). The failing end-to-end tests fire exactly this path (`[:rf.route/handle-url-change "/no-such-page"]`).
- Projector gap confirmed: `default-error-projector-fn` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_projector.cljc` ~163-169) maps EVERY `:rf.error/no-such-handler` to 404 with no `:kind` gate — once always-on producers reach it in production, an unregistered EVENT handler would answer 404; hence the adjacent `:kind :route` gate (amends Spec 011 §Default projector + the kind-less-404 test projections, ssr_end_to_end_test.clj ~846/~912/~941/~964).

MECHANISM RECORD (dossier content preserved; the dossier file is deleted): `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc` registers TWO error listeners under one logical id `::error-projection` — the ALWAYS-ON `rf-emit/register-error-listener!` (-> `error-listener/error-emit-projection-listener`, which consumes `:rf.error/*` union records generically and synthesises the projector envelope) and the DEV `trace-tooling/register-listener!` (-> `error-projection-listener`, buffering `trace/emit-error!` categories; elides under the gate). Projection waits until the settle point (`flush-response!`/`get-response`); last-write-wins + `consume-pending-traces!` makes dev's duplicate buffering benign. The comment blocks in ssr.cljc (~372-396) and error_listener.cljc (~297-316) still claim no-such-handler/drain-depth have "no always-on emission path" — stale; rf2-ov56u corrects them.

EVIDENCE RECORD: under the prod gate (`bash scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh` posture; whole suite measured 2026-07-27: 534 tests / 2503 assertions / 217 failures across 21 of 48 namespaces), the rqje9 cluster is ssr-end-to-end-test 119 red assertions, ssr-flush-response-result-test 12, ssr-error-two-frame-attribution-test 5, ssr-error-view-failed-no-project-test 2, ssr-head-resolution-no-project-test 2 — all of the shape "flush projects the buffered :no-such-handler -> 404 onto :status" observing 200. Direct repro: `cd implementation/ssr && clojure '-J-Dre-frame.debug=false' -M:test -n re-frame.ssr-end-to-end-test` -> 71 tests / 348 assertions / 119 failures.

EGRESS IMPLICATIONS: promotion changes what production emits off-box (shippers now receive `:kind :route` records). The review burden is small and verificatory, not architectural: Spec 009 already promises the category production-survivable; EP-0015 requires it fail closed; the emit site already redacts query/fragment carrier values (`egress/redact-url-tag`) before the record crosses any trace/log/SSR-projection boundary. The record ships category, `:kind :route`, `:frame`, `:time`, `:recovery`, redacted `:url`, structured `:reason` — never raw carrier values or app-db. Review verifies that invariant (routing_egress_test.clj surface).

UNBLOCK / SEQUENCING for rf2-lwtlk (7 roster lines remain in scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh):
- The FIVE rqje9 error-projection namespaces (counts above): wait for rf2-ov56u's PR to MERGE, then re-run; wire-status assertions should go green, and any residue asserting dev-trace SHAPE gets the standard posture split. Do not split them before the merge.
- `ssr-conformance-test` (1): its one blocking fixture `:ssr/error-known-mapping` (a no-such-route URL) clears with rf2-ov56u. Its sibling `:ssr/error-sanitisation` fails INDEPENDENTLY — the runner's `pe-check` sources the error event from `@traces` (the dev bus) before `ssr/project-error`, though its category `:rf.error/handler-exception` IS always-on (the projector itself is green under the gate: `ssr-error-projector-substrate-test` is in-lane). Fix: re-source `pe-check` from the always-on axis (the rf2-7vk3z shape) — clears regardless of this ruling and may proceed NOW. Eight further conformance fixtures are `:trace-emissions` dev-bus claims -> ordinary posture split.
- `flows-integration-test` (2) is NOT this ruling: it stays held on rf2-bkvu5 (production-elided app-db schema validation), a different surface.
- lwtlk groups (a) dev-instrumentation and (b) source-coord are unaffected and already largely cleared.

CLOSING this bead: the ruling is recorded here; implementation is owned by rf2-ov56u (discovered-from edge links them).
close_reason: Ruling delivered (delegated by Mike 2026-07-27, recorded in notes): production route miss must 404 — narrow (b): promote the url-change-fx :kind :route emit to the always-on error axis + :kind-gate the default projector's 404 arm. Implementation owned by rf2-ov56u; rf2-lwtlk group (c) waits on its merge; :ssr/error-sanitisation pe-check re-sourcing may proceed now.

title: STANDARD (Mike, 2026-07-27): Freehand cannot ship slower than Reagent — close the measured gaps
description:
OPERATOR RULING, verbatim: 'Freehand can't be used if it is slower than Reagent.'

This is a PRODUCT STANDARD, not a bug. A view substrate that is slower than the incumbent it intends to replace has no case, whatever else it offers. Treat it as a release gate.

=== MAKING IT PRECISE, BECAUSE 'SLOWER' HAS THREE DIFFERENT ANSWERS ===
From rf2-dq20a (PR #7131), ratio to the shared in-run React floor, :advanced, goog.DEBUG false, 6 rounds:

  MOUNT W1 large template   FH interpreted 2.987 | FH compiled 1.304 | Reagent 1.554 | UIx 1.163
  MOUNT W3 ordinary form    FH interpreted 1.664 | FH compiled 1.325 | Reagent 1.394 | UIx 1.153
  UPDATE broad (300 cells)  FH interpreted 27.78 | FH compiled 24.83 | Reagent 2.639
  UPDATE narrow (1 cell)    FH interpreted 8.802 | FH compiled  8.194 | Reagent 0.587

SO THE STANDARD RESOLVES INTO THREE SEPARATE OBLIGATIONS, ONLY TWO OF WHICH ARE REAL TARGETS:

  (1) INTERPRETED MOUNT — REAL TARGET. The paved path is interpreted, and at 2.987 it is 1.9x slower than Reagent's 1.554 on W1. On W3, the shape most applications are made of, it is 1.664 vs 1.394 — much closer. Target: interpreted mount <= Reagent on both witnesses.
      NOTE: COMPILED mount ALREADY PASSES (1.304 < 1.554). See the consequence section below.

  (2) BULK RE-RENDER — REAL TARGET, AND THE MOST SERIOUS. ~7-8x Reagent on 300 repainting boundaries, and COMPILING BARELY HELPS (27.78 -> 24.83 against Reagent's 2.639). This cannot be explained away by framework overhead and nobody has profiled WHY. It is the deficit that is unambiguously Freehand's own.

  (3) NARROW UPDATE — NOT A VALID TARGET AS MEASURED. ~15x looks worst but roughly 90% of it decomposes to frame/replace-app-db! plus the re-frame signal graph, NOT rendering. The Reagent arm read a bare r/atom (its own idiom, but far less framework). A Reagent app reading re-frame subscriptions would pay the same leg. CHASING THIS NUMBER AS-IS WOULD BE OPTIMISING RE-FRAME UNDER FREEHAND'S NAME. It needs a like-for-like re-measure (Reagent + re-frame subs on one page) before any target is set - now possible since rf2-8cnxg/jt8vz were fixed in PR #7118.

=== A MEASUREMENT DISCREPANCY THAT MUST BE RECONCILED FIRST ===
Two measurements of the SAME quantity disagree materially. rf2-xu6rx / PR #7077 reports W1 interpreted at 1.904x floor after the js/Map memo change. rf2-dq20a reports W1 interpreted at 2.987x floor, measured LATER. Both post-#7077, same witness size (~1,203 elements). That is a 57% gap and it decides how far obligation (1) actually has to travel. Reconcile before setting any target: different build config, different floor arm, different round conditions, or a real regression between the two runs.

=== CONSEQUENCE FOR rf2-zw1oo (KEEP THE COMPILER?) — THIS RULING CUTS THE OTHER WAY ===
I previously recorded that the compiler's case was thinning. UNDER THIS STANDARD THAT READING PARTLY REVERSES: compiled Freehand is currently the ONLY tier that meets the bar on mount (1.304 < 1.554), while the interpreted paved path fails it (2.987). If the interpreter cannot be brought under Reagent, the compiler stops being a 'specialised performance tier' and becomes the thing that makes Freehand shippable at all.
Counter-pressure, unchanged: UIx reaches 1.163 with a macro and no compiler, beating compiled Freehand on every mount witness including the elision-maximising one - so 'compile it' is not the only way to meet the bar.
Do NOT resolve rf2-zw1oo until obligations (1) and (2) have been attempted; the answer depends on whether the interpreter can meet the bar.

=== WHAT IS NOT MEASURED AT ALL ===
Memory, across substrates. The earlier ablation found 6.256x retained heap per elidable boundary WITHIN Freehand. If Freehand wins decisively on memory, that is a real product argument this standard does not capture, and it should be measured before any decision to retire anything.

DO NOT close this bead by weakening the standard or by re-scoping the witnesses to flattering shapes. It closes when the measured numbers meet it, or when the operator revises it.
notes:
=== ABLATION RESULT (rf2-so3io, PR #7159): THE HYPOTHESIS IS FALSIFIED. DROPPING THE CONTRACT IS A BAD TRADE. ===
Headless Chromium 147, :advanced, goog.DEBUG false, both arm orders, 6 rounds each, every pair carrying a REFERENCE RUNG so the difference is the contract and nothing else.

WHAT DROPPING useSyncExternalStore + the commit-side re-read ACTUALLY RETURNS:
  broad update clock   -13.6% / -14.8%   (cheaper in 12 of 12 paired rounds; ranges overlap, paired is the strong reading)
  narrow update        NULL              (direction flips between orders)
  mount                <=0.1 ms          (the clock quantum)
  heap, sub-free       -375 / -369 B     (DISJOINT)
  heap, reactive       -376 / -363 B     (DISJOINT)

AND A CONTRACT-FREE BOUNDARY IS STILL 4.97-5.04x Reagent on sub-free heap, 3.79-3.81x reactive heap, ~5.5x broad clock, ~1.6x mount.

SO THE TWO GAPS DO NOT COLLAPSE TOGETHER. My hypothesis — that useSyncExternalStore and the tear check service one contract and would fall together — is WRONG in the way that matters: heap return is 95-97% THE HOOK (an isolating rung of React's six hooks over a two-field JS object returns 355-357 B of the 375), clock return is >=80% THE COMMIT. Two separate small levers, and neither gets near Reagent. THE GUARANTEE IS NOT WHAT IS COSTING US.

WHAT THE GUARANTEE BUYS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. On a watchable browser host with the source moved in the render->commit gap, real port and sub-cache:
  retained site, ablated -> publishes STALE, self-heals one window late
  STAGED site, ablated   -> publishes STALE AND NOTHING EVER CORRECTS IT
Because obs/acquire! installs the watch DURING the commit that needed it, a FIRST RENDER of a dependency paints stale and stays stale — a panel mounting exactly as a permission drops, a user switches, a record is redacted. Spec 006 justifies invariant 5 on the headless case; THE BROWSER CASE IS STRONGER THAN THE SPEC CLAIMS.
Second casualty: without the store a boundary CANNOT REPAINT INSIDE flushSync (the sync lane is lost), so rf2-w2m25's fix goes with it unless the substrate rebuilds its own render queue.

SEPARABILITY: the commit half is separable cheaply (~12 lines). The hook half is separable expensively (hooks cannot be conditional: two shells, two component types keyed into shell-signature, a fork in checkpoint.cljs). BUT THE DECISION IS NOT SEPARABLE AT ALL — nothing in re-frame2 can observe startTransition / useDeferredValue / <Suspense>, because THE ONLY DETECTOR FOR AN INTERRUPTED RENDER IS useSyncExternalStore, the thing being switched off. So an opt-out must be DECLARED, its failure mode is a silent wrong render, and it cannot be per-boundary (a tear is a stale panel BESIDE a fresh one). Permanent cost: two shells, two hook skeletons, a forked window closer, and every ViewCell law verified in both modes.

MAYOR'S READ: this closes the question in the useful direction. The operator's instinct — Reagent never showed tearing, re-frame2 uses no Suspense — was worth testing and the test says the contract is not the problem. Freehand would still be ~5x Reagent on both axes without it, while losing a protection that is now MEASURED to be permanent rather than transient on first render. Recommend the contract STAYS and this line of attack closes.
Filed rf2-anmdr (P1): the STAGED invariant-5 case — the one that never self-heals — has no shipped test row. That is the worse of the two and it is unpinned.

INSTRUMENT: positive control 587,500 unboxed doubles predicted 4,700,000 B, measured -0.061% / -0.059% on reader A and +0.0005% on an independent snapshot reader. 0 unverified writes on every clock row, 0 unverified of 195 heap mounts, canonical-DOM parity across 7 mount and 6 update arms in both orders. Two instrument faults found and fixed en route (rf2-oob3g's hooks rung threw on every unmount because layout cleanup ran before uSES's passive unsubscribe, killing two runs outright; and two arms fought over one frame id, coupling arm order).
NOT DETERMINED: SSR/hydration under a store-free shell; heap under update; a v/defview-shaped ablated arm (needs a react.cljs shell seam, no mandate). invariant 5 is NOT dropped anywhere — git diff against origin/main over implementation/core/src, implementation/freehand/src and spec is EMPTY.
close_reason:
ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER WAS NO (Mike, 2026-07-30). The standard is discharged by the ruling that Freehand is a failed experiment.

THE STANDARD, verbatim (Mike, 2026-07-27): 'Freehand can't be used if it is slower than Reagent.' A product standard and a release gate, not a bug.

THE VERDICT. Interpreted Freehand — the paved path, and after the compiled tier was ruled out the ONLY path — did not clear it. Ratio to the shared in-run React floor: bulk repaint ~5x Reagent, mount ~1.6x. The narrow-update row was never a valid target as measured (roughly 90% decomposed to replace-app-db! and the re-frame signal graph rather than rendering, against a Reagent arm reading a bare r/atom).

THE GAP IS ARCHITECTURAL, and this bead's own investigation is what established that — closing it needs a dependency-ledger redesign, not an optimisation.

THE ABLATION IS THE DURABLE FINDING, and it corrected the obvious hypothesis. rf2-so3io / PR #7159 dropped useSyncExternalStore AND the commit-side re-read and measured what came back: only -13.6%/-14.8% on the broad clock and -375 B heap. A CONTRACT-FREE boundary was still ~5.5x Reagent on clock, ~5x on sub-free heap, ~1.6x on mount. Heap return 95-97% the React hook; clock return >=80% the commit. THE GUARANTEE WAS NOT WHAT COST US — so 'is tear-freedom worth 10x' was never the trade, and anyone revisiting this must not re-litigate it as though it were.

AND THE GUARANTEE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE SPEC CLAIMS. The same ablation found that without the tear check a STAGED site publishes stale and NOTHING EVER CORRECTS IT — obs/acquire! installs the watch during the commit that needed it, so a first render of a dependency paints stale and stays stale. Spec 006 justifies invariant 5 on the headless case; the browser case is stronger. Invariant 5 was never weakened: git diff against origin/main over implementation/core/src, implementation/freehand/src and spec was EMPTY throughout.

WHAT WAS NEVER DETERMINED, recorded so a future substrate does not assume it: memory across substrates was never measured (the within-Freehand ablation found 6.256x retained heap per elidable boundary, so memory is the one axis where the design might have won outright); SSR/hydration under a store-free shell; heap under update.

INSTRUMENT NOTE. Fifteen instrument faults were caught on this surface, each having produced a plausible precise wrong number first. Every figure above comes from runs carrying a positive control and DOM read-back, reported as 'N unverified of M'.

CLOSED WITH IT: the four bench beads that existed to measure against this standard (rf2-3zenp, rf2-ssn1o, rf2-mapni, rf2-m7xs7), and the Freehand tree under rf2-drpa3.

DO NOT re-file. If a future view substrate needs a performance bar, that is a new standard against a new substrate — this one is spent.

title: hic: the hydration adoption window is page-global, so a second root's mismatch is never emitted
description:
MEASURED BY THE rf2-hic-012 WORKER (PR #7751), not inferred. It reported rather than fixed because impl/roots.cljs is runtime source and its dispatch fenced that with an explicit STOP.

THE DEFECT. The hydration adoption window is PAGE-GLOBAL, not root-scoped. impl/roots.cljs holds ONE boolean for the whole page and the mismatch emit is gated on it. With two overlapping hydrating roots, root A's closer shuts the window before root B's mismatch reports.

THE MEASUREMENT: two overlapping hydrating roots produce TWO React "Hydration failed" complaints but only ONE :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch. Root B's mismatch is invisible to everything reading the instrumentation stream.

THIS IS THE SAME CLASS AS TONIGHT'S OTHER TWO SILENCED DIAGNOSTICS and should be read alongside them: rf2-x874 (a lowered callback silently writes a successor frame when the memo is cold) and the freeze gate that reported zero failures while comparing nothing. In each case the system is quiet when it should be loud, and quiet reads as healthy.

WHY IT SURVIVED. The worker demonstrated directly that value-level assertions cannot see it: replacing root B's hydrate-root! with root! reddened ONLY the node-identity expando while every text assertion stayed green. A DOM-level or text-level witness will report success on a discarded adoption. Any fix must be witnessed at the instrumentation layer, the way PR #7751 does it.

THE FIX touches impl/roots.cljs and impl/mount.cljs, and probably impl/presence_react.cljs. It is runtime source, so it needs the operator's word before dispatch — this is the second bead tonight blocked on that same fence (see rf2-x874).

ALREADY DONE FOR YOU, so the next worker does not redo it: PR #7751's two affected assertions carry IN-FILE instructions describing exactly what each becomes once root-scoping lands. Read those before designing anything.

NOTE ON PROVENANCE: rf2-hic-012's deliverable 3 offered two branches — root-scope the window, OR justify each remaining global in writing feeding rf2-hic-017. The worker took the second branch and made the justification a MEASUREMENT rather than an assertion, which is why this bead can state a defect instead of a suspicion. Both branches remain available to the operator; scoping is the stronger answer but the written justification is already banked.

GATES for the fix: the browser lane PR #7751 established (9 tests / 71 assertions), the hicasso node suite, the freeze gate, and sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh in full. Run each gate ALONE and echo $? to its own file — never append a filter to a gate's command line.
notes:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-10, operator-overturnable): OPTION A — AUTHORIZE ROOT-SCOPING NOW. Make the hydration adoption window (and mismatch emission) root-local; the runtime-source fence on impl/roots.cljs, impl/mount.cljs, impl/presence_react.cljs is lifted for this repair. Option B (keep the banked written justification) rejected: the kernel checkpoint rf2-hic-019 would have to accept a justified global whose MEASURED behavior is a silenced diagnostic, contradicting the trust register hydration-isolation row's own required contract (independent roots cannot suppress one another's complaints) — that signs a known-broken multi-root story into the kernel. Option C (hold) rejected: Wave B would build above a known silent-failure path. WHY: dossier and Codex recommendations independently converged on A; the measurement (PR #7751, MERGED 2026-08-09) removed all doubt — two overlapping hydrating roots produce TWO React "Hydration failed" complaints but only ONE :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch (root A's closer shuts the page-global window; root B's mismatch is silently discarded, so Xray/tests/future SSR witnesses see a healthy root that failed hydration); Codex verified the defect is BROADER than one missing trace — impl/presence_react.cljs is a second reader of the global, so while any root hydrates, a presence component in an UNRELATED ordinary root is also told it is adopting; the global can suppress a legitimate enter transition or let one root end another root's adoption behavior. Correctness currently depends on the relative ordering of commits, passive effects, presence renders, and recoverable-error callbacks across otherwise-independent roots; React's per-root API (onRecoverableError is an option of an individual hydrateRoot; independently configured roots on one page are supported) gives no reason to treat page-wide ordering as an application invariant. Correctness fix, no new application-facing concept; common SPA path pays nothing; keeping the global saves a tiny root-local object at the cost of diagnostics whose silence cannot be trusted.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE: FIX SURFACE: implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/roots.cljs (allocates ONE private JS object at module load; its no-argument open/close/read functions all address that singleton), impl/mount.cljs (opens the singleton for every hydrate-root!; every hydrated root mounts a closer that closes the singleton; every root installs the same hydration-reporter consulting the singleton rather than state belonging to its React root), and impl/presence_react.cljs (second reader). IN-FILE INSTRUCTIONS: PR #7751's two affected assertions carry in-file instructions describing exactly what each becomes once root-scoping lands — read those FIRST; the design is half done. PRIOR ART IN-REPO (established local pattern, not a speculative subsystem): the native substrate creates #js {:adopting true} per root and closes over it in the reporter (implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs); Freehand does the same while also closing over root-id (implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/root.cljs). REPAIR SHAPE (Codex, adopted): one small mutable adoption ref per hydrate-root! call, kept internal. (1) Mint the ref before constructing the root element and reporter; store it on the opaque root handle so every later render! preserves the same root wrapper. (2) Make hydration-reporter a builder closing over that ref; it emits only while THAT root's ref is open, then always delegates to the existing default reporter — do not weaken fail-open. (3) Pass the same ref to that root's closer; close idempotently after the hydration commit, on explicit unmount, and on synchronous hydration-construction failure. (4) Put the ref in a narrow React context around the hydrated app subtree; presence reads that context and treats a missing value as closed — cost is one provider per hydrated root and one context read only in the optional presence component; ordinary roots and ordinary Hicasso boundaries acquire NO object, provider, hook, registry lookup, or branch. (5) When the server entry is promoted into the product, give each render/request its own ref and provider; do not retain the module flag as a separate server mechanism. (6) Remove the global adoption close from runtime reset — a reset must not change the lifecycle state of a sibling root; root teardown owns root state. REJECTED SHAPES: page-global reference count (keeps B's window open when A commits, but a later recoverable error from already-committed A would then be falsely labelled a hydration mismatch; still leaks adoption semantics into presence components outside both hydrating subtrees — converts one interference bug into another); registry keyed by frame (multiple roots may intentionally share a frame); module registry keyed by container (recreates React context badly, adds cleanup risk). SUPPRESSION vs ATTRIBUTION: suppression is fixable NOW without the final public root API; attribution should close over the stable root identity selected by the root-lifecycle work and include it in the trace (as Freehand does). Do NOT use frame-kw as a substitute for root identity, and do NOT delay the local-state repair to settle the public spelling. WITNESS-LAYER REQUIREMENT: value/DOM-level witnesses provably CANNOT see this — the hic-012 worker showed replacing root B's hydrate-root! with a plain root! reddened ONLY the node-identity expando while every text assertion stayed green; a DOM-level witness reports success on a discarded adoption. The witness must live at the instrumentation layer, as PR #7751's does (9 tests / 71 assertions).

FENCES: touch only implementation/hicasso impl/roots.cljs, impl/mount.cljs, impl/presence_react.cljs plus the PR #7751 browser-lane tests (including the two in-file-instructed assertion updates); no spec/* hot-zone files, no facade export changes, no new public API in this PR. Parallel-safe with rf2-x874 (different files: roots/mount vs frames — no fence collision).

WITNESSES (repair complete when these focused browser witnesses pass AND their sabotage controls red): (1) two overlapping divergent hydrations yield two React complaints AND two framework mismatch events; reusing one ref for both roots must make it red. (2) Root A completes while root B remains adopting; an artificial later recoverable error on A does NOT emit a hydration mismatch while B's genuine mismatch still does — this is the witness that rules out a global counter. (3) Presence isolation: a hydrated root is born present, an ordinary sibling root still gets its enter phase, and closing either root cannot change the other; same row covers teardown-before-passive-effect so no open ref survives its root. (4) Once public root identity lands, each emitted event names the correct root (follow-up wiring, not a blocker for this repair); if a server entry ships, add two independently scoped server renders as the request-isolation witness. GATES: the browser lane PR #7751 established, the hicasso node suite, the freeze gate, and sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh in full — each gate run ALONE and FOREGROUND to completion, echo $? to its own file, never append a filter to a gate's command line. Payoff: trust register hydration-isolation row closes properly; rf2-hic-046 per-surface SSR witnesses get a truthful stream; React-compat contract (per-root error attribution, identifierPrefix isolation) becomes implementable.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7756 (2026-08-10 AUSEST) — client/runtime root-scoping PASS; exact repair owner complete.

Completeness: the three blocking witnesses land at the instrumentation layer: two genuinely overlapping divergent hydrations yield two React complaints and two framework events; the direct real-door row distinguishes a completed root's later recovery from a sibling's live mismatch and rules out both global boolean and global count; the presence row covers hydrated-born-present, an ordinary sibling's enter phase, independent close, and teardown-before-effect. The explicitly deferred root-id attribution and real server/request matrix already belong to rf2-hic-046 and were never blockers for this repair.

Correctness: independently traced one minted window object from hydrate-root! into the handle, hydration reporter, closer, and subtree context. Nil is closed; ordinary roots allocate/install nothing; one closer and unmount can close only their own window; render! preserves the hydrated root shape; collector reset has no cross-root close. This matches the established substrate pattern and preserves unconditional recoverable-error delegation. No stale zero-arity Hicasso callers remain.

Implementation quality: the six-file diff is coherent and minimal; collector.cljs is necessary because it owned the forbidden global reset call, and the remaining changes are the three runtime surfaces plus focused tests/support. Merged-tree reruns pass: Hicasso Node 46 tests / 188 assertions, browser 1148 / 7099, freeze 7/7, and git diff --check, all exit 0. The two recorded sabotages discriminate the global reporter and page-wide presence reader.

Non-blocking residual transferred to exact owner rf2-hic-046, not duplicated: roots.cljs:54 and presence_react.cljs:130 speak in present tense as if a server request already installs this provider, but the only product-source with-adoption caller is the client hydrate tree. The presence witness obtains its supposed server bytes by settling an ordinary client root rather than react-dom/server, so it does not prove the future per-surface SSR/request contract. That does not invalidate the measured client isolation repair.
close_reason: PR #7756 completes the root-local client adoption repair. Audit traced the per-root reporter/closer/context ownership, verified the required instrumentation and presence witnesses, and reran Node, browser, freeze, and diff gates green. The already-deferred real-server/request matrix remains on exact owner rf2-hic-046.

title: hic — catalogue Hicasso's 40 diagnostic ids in Spec 009 (blocks rf2-hic-001 merge)
description:
# Catalogue Hicasso's 40 diagnostic ids in Spec 009

**Found by**: rf2-hic-001 (the package extraction), which is BLOCKED ON THIS to merge spine-green.
**Surface**: `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (HOT ZONE — sequence it, do not parallel it).

## What happened

The Hicasso runtime was measured under `implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/`.
Two repo-wide gates scan `implementation/**` but EXCLUDE `test/` trees, so the prototype
never met them. rf2-hic-001 copies that runtime to `implementation/hicasso/src/`, and
`scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py` now — correctly — reports 40 `:rf.error/*` ids
emitted by framework source with no row in `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`.

`rf2-cs0kd1` deleted the `KNOWN_UNCATALOGUED` construct from that gate: it defends TOTALITY
and there is deliberately no debt ledger. So an exemption is the wrong instrument — the rows
have to be written.

## Why rf2-hic-001 did not write them

The bead's one rule is "mechanical namespace rename and build wiring only; make no semantic
edits". A Spec 009 row is not a table entry — the existing `:rf.error/ui-*` rows are dense
normative paragraphs (trigger conditions, emitter roster, recovery ladder, ex-data slots).
Forty of them is a comparable body of work to the extraction itself, in a hot-zone file the
extraction bead was not flagged for.

This is ALSO not rf2-hic-021: that bead's stated surface is
`docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md` (a new product-facing catalogue) plus its own
round-trip tests. Spec 009 is the repo-wide instrumentation catalogue and a different
artefact. The two should agree, and hic-021 can cite these rows, but neither substitutes for
the other.

## The 40 ids

:rf.error/hicasso-bad-head :rf.error/hicasso-deferred-read-at-boundary
:rf.error/hicasso-dispatch-in-render-position :rf.error/hicasso-empty-vector
:rf.error/hicasso-frame-outside-boundary :rf.error/hicasso-generation-fence-exhausted
:rf.error/hicasso-host-bad-ssr-policy :rf.error/hicasso-host-callback-slot-collision
:rf.error/hicasso-host-fallback-boundary-head :rf.error/hicasso-host-no-component
:rf.error/hicasso-host-structural-callback :rf.error/hicasso-host-unclaimed-callback
:rf.error/hicasso-host-undeclared-callback :rf.error/hicasso-host-unknown-option
:rf.error/hicasso-intent-at-a-non-event-contract :rf.error/hicasso-intent-needs-the-event
:rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary :rf.error/hicasso-malformed-navigate
:rf.error/hicasso-malformed-prevent :rf.error/hicasso-merge-not-a-map
:rf.error/hicasso-presence-child-not-hiccup :rf.error/hicasso-presence-child-unkeyed
:rf.error/hicasso-presence-override-on-a-view :rf.error/hicasso-presence-timeout-required
:rf.error/hicasso-raw-no-component :rf.error/hicasso-raw-not-a-component
:rf.error/hicasso-ref-vector-reserved :rf.error/hicasso-revision-from-remainder
:rf.error/hicasso-revision-not-controlled :rf.error/hicasso-route-link-bad-on-click
:rf.error/hicasso-route-link-outside-boundary :rf.error/hicasso-route-link-prefetch-declined
:rf.error/hicasso-state-bad-concern :rf.error/hicasso-state-bad-key
:rf.error/hicasso-state-bad-option :rf.error/hicasso-state-redefined
:rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render :rf.error/hicasso-true-child
:rf.error/hicasso-unknown-callback-contract :rf.error/no-frame-prop

`:rf.error/no-frame-prop` is the odd one out — it is NOT `hicasso-`prefixed and is emitted by
`impl/runtime.cljs`. Decide whether it is a Hicasso id that should be renamed (a naming
question, so coordinate with whichever bead owns naming) or a core id that already has a home.

## Where the content comes from

Every emitter is a call to that namespace's shared `fail!` helper, which already takes
`id`, `where`, `reason` and `recovery` as arguments. So the trigger sentence and the recovery
ladder are already authored at each call site — the work is transcription plus the ex-data
slot column, not invention.

## Acceptance

- `python scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py --verbose` exits 0 with the hicasso
  package on `implementation/hicasso/src/`.
- No `KNOWN_UNCATALOGUED`-style exemption is introduced (rf2-cs0kd1 removed that concept).

Reopen this exact catalogue owner and replace only those emitter/:where paths with collector; ids, triggers, recoveries, and payloads are unchanged, so no broad catalogue rewrite is owed.

The seven stale namespace tokens across spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2515 and :2556-2558 now name re-frame.hicasso.impl.collector and match the literal shell, read-key!, render-body, and frame-prop-shell emit sites. The full Spec has zero remaining impl.runtime references; all 42 Hicasso catalogue table lines retain seven pipe delimiters before and after; catalogue-drift and slug gates pass. Completeness, correctness, and implementation-quality review found no further actionable gap. Close this exact owner.

Nothing in that section, or in the 'K1's denominator was amended' note beneath it, records that the gate is now measured as missed. A reader of the kill table alone cannot tell that the row it gates has published a verdict against it.

Neither decides.

WHAT THE RULING OWES. (1) Whether the two-serious-runtime-iterations condition is met as of today. (2) If it is, what K1 tripping means in practice — 'stop or narrow', and which. (3) Whether validation.md's K1 row itself should carry a dated note recording the measured verdict against the gate regardless of the trigger question, so the kill table stops being the one page in the tree that does not know.
