title: RULING NEEDED: rf2-t2flm publishes an M1 magnitude that rf2-8a746's whole-interval rule refuses
notes:
RAISED BY rf2-x7x10 (PR for the mount-class calibration), 2026-08-08. Surfaced by
implementation, not decided by it.

WHAT rf2-x7x10 DID. It calibrated the check standard's `mount` class from the
mount's own 14 committed row-runs (centre 1.7956x, location [1.6765, 1.9147],
dispersion <= 0.577), which restored the M1 row's reproduction path: all 14 runs
come back IN CONTROL, so clock_readjudicate.cjs prints a reportable subset again
rather than "reportable subset: NONE".

THE COLLISION THAT BECAME VISIBLE. With runs reportable, rf2-8a746's part-4
publication rule reaches M1 FOR THE FIRST TIME — it could not before, because an
effect-size interval needs a pooled run to be formed from. Over the committed
corpus it returns INSTRUMENT-LIMITED on every pair of both ensembles:

  hicasso / uix-subs      emvod 1.1679x [1.1259 - 1.2096] n=8
                          w3yxd 1.1621x [1.1209 - 1.2090] n=6
  hicasso / reagent-subs  emvod 1.1142x [1.0238 - 1.1988] n=8
                          w3yxd 1.1151x [1.0314 - 1.1955] n=6
  uix-subs / reagent-subs emvod 0.9540x [0.8835 - 1.0139] n=8
                          w3yxd 0.9596x [0.8962 - 1.0209] n=6

The reason is NOT that the row is noisy. On the two hicasso pairs the WHOLE
interval lies above 1.0 — parity is excluded and the direction is intact — but
rf2-8a746 publishes a magnitude only when the whole interval clears the 1.0 ship
bar BELOW or the 1.5 architecture-kill ABOVE, and ~1.16x clears neither DECISION
threshold.

SO TWO RULINGS OF THE SAME DAY (2026-08-07) NOW DISAGREE ON THIS ROW.
rf2-t2flm publishes ~1.184x against direct UIx-on-subs. rf2-8a746 part 4 says a
row publishes a magnitude only on a whole interval clearing a threshold.

WHAT rf2-x7x10 DID ABOUT IT: nothing but record it. The studio page's section 4.3
carries a dated supersession stating the re-adjudication and both intervals, and
the bolded magnitudes are marked HELD PENDING A RULING rather than withdrawn
(annotate-never-erase). clock_exit_path.test.cjs pins publishes === false with a
message saying that a flip is a RULING to be made and not a test to be updated.

NOTE FOR THE RULING. rf2-8a746's acceptance criterion 3 pinned the interval rule
on the committed 42-run corpus, which is BULK ONLY, and its own text sequences the
freeze "before the next BULK window opens" while handing the mount half to
rf2-t2flm by id. So whether part 4's ship/kill thresholds were ever intended to
adjudicate a MOUNT row — where the claim is a deficit rather than a win, and the
1.0/1.5 pair may simply be the wrong thresholds for it — is a live question and
possibly the whole answer.

SITTING INPUT: K1's line for the 2026-08-27 sitting is that ~1.18x figure, so this
wants resolving before the 2026-08-25 packet freeze.
MAYOR RECOMMENDATION 2026-08-08 15:10 AUSEST — surfaced for the operator with an analysis, NOT ruled. The bead is correctly marked RULING NEEDED and it touches both a published figure and a kill criterion, so it is the operator's.

I THINK THE CONFLICT IS NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS, AND MAY DISSOLVE ON THE RULE'S OWN WORDING.

rf2-8a746 part 4 reads, verbatim: "SHIP/KILL PUBLISHES ONLY when the whole interval lies on the required side of 1.0 (bar) / 1.5 (architecture-kill)". Two things follow from that sentence rather than from anything I am adding.

(1) THE SUBJECT IS SHIP/KILL ADJUDICATION, not every published magnitude. The rule governs when a row may DECIDE the bar or the architecture-kill, not whether a number may appear on a page with its interval beside it. M1 is a characterisation of the mount premium; it is not the bulk ship/kill row.

(2) THE THRESHOLDS NAMED — 1.0 and 1.5 — ARE THE BULK ROW'S. They are the bar and the architecture-kill for the bulk question. The mount question's decision threshold is K1's, which is 1.10x, not 1.0x. Applying the bulk row's thresholds to the mount row imports a limit from a different question — which is precisely the class of error rf2-8a746 exists to retire (asserting against an instrument a value that was never derived for it).

AND ON K1's OWN THRESHOLD THE ROW ADJUDICATES CLEANLY. Both hicasso/uix-subs intervals lie ENTIRELY ABOVE 1.10: emvod 1.1679x [1.1259 - 1.2096] and w3yxd 1.1621x [1.1209 - 1.2090]. So the whole interval clears K1's line on the wrong side, decisively. Read this way the row is not instrument-limited at all for the question it is actually asked — it says K1 IS MISSED, with parity excluded and the direction intact, which is a stronger and more useful statement than "instrument-limited".

SO MY RECOMMENDATION: rule that part 4's whole-interval discipline is RETAINED but its THRESHOLD IS ROW-SPECIFIC — each row is adjudicated against the decision threshold of the question it answers (bulk: 1.0 / 1.5; mount: K1's 1.10x). On that reading rf2-t2flm and rf2-8a746 do not disagree: the M1 magnitude stands, gains an interval it did not previously carry, and adjudicates K1 as missed.

WHAT I AM NOT RECOMMENDING, so the alternatives are visible rather than buried: (a) withdrawing the M1 magnitude and publishing INSTRUMENT-LIMITED — defensible, strictly honest, and it would leave the sitting with no mount magnitude at all; (b) exempting M1 from part 4 by name — cheap and wrong, since a rule with a named exception is not a rule; (c) restating part 4's thresholds as universal and accepting that M1 cannot publish — which would also refuse any future row whose effect sits between the thresholds, i.e. most interesting results.

MATERIAL TO THE SITTING EITHER WAY. K1's line for 2026-08-27 is that ~1.18x figure. Under my recommendation it firms up — a magnitude with an interval, whole-interval above the 1.10x bar. Under (a) it becomes "direction only, instrument-limited", which weakens the ergonomics-versus-price trade the sitting turns on. Worth ruling before the 2026-08-25 packet freeze rather than at the table.

NOTE ON WHAT THE WORKER DID, because the restraint is the reason this is a clean decision rather than a mess: rf2-x7x10 recorded the collision, marked the bolded magnitudes HELD PENDING A RULING rather than withdrawing them, and put a dated supersession on the studio page carrying both intervals. Nothing was decided by implementation. That is exactly right.
MAYOR ADDENDUM 2026-08-08 15:50 AUSEST — a fact from rf2-x7x10's completed work that bears on this ruling and was not visible when I wrote my recommendation. It STRENGTHENS the case for ruling rather than deferring, and it does so from the honesty side rather than the convenience side.

A PUBLISHED AGREEMENT CLAIM DID NOT SURVIVE THE RE-ADJUDICATION. The M1 row's published prose carried the two ensembles "agreeing to 0.11 pp" as corroboration. rf2-x7x10 established that this agreement was A PROPERTY OF THE SELECTED SUBSETS, not of the measurement: unselected, the two ensembles sit 2.6 pp apart on the UIx pair, and 0.6 pp apart on the Reagent pair where the selected subsets were 3.0 pp apart. In the worker's own words, "the selection flattered one replication and penalised the other" — in opposite directions on the two pairs, which is what rules out a common cause.

WHY THAT MATTERS HERE. Whichever way this bead is ruled, the old 7-of-14 subset cannot be restored as the basis of publication, because its apparent replication-agreement was an artefact of the selection that produced it. So option (a) from my recommendation — withdraw the magnitude and publish INSTRUMENT-LIMITED — no longer has a fallback that keeps the old corroboration story; it would have to withdraw that too. The choice is between the re-adjudicated whole-ensemble figures and no magnitude at all.

THE RE-ADJUDICATED FIGURES, for the ruling to sit on. Eligible subset moved 7 of 14 to 14 of 14, all IN CONTROL under the newly calibrated mount class. The point figures move to the whole-ensemble column the page ALREADY TABLED, so no new number enters the record: 1.1837x n=4 becomes 1.1798x n=8, and 1.1848x n=3 becomes 1.2057x n=6. The intervals rf2-8a746's rule computes are 1.1679x [1.1259-1.2096] n=8 and 1.1621x [1.1209-1.2090] n=6.

MY RECOMMENDATION IS UNCHANGED AND ITS ARITHMETIC HOLDS: both interval LOWER BOUNDS (1.1259 and 1.1209) lie above K1's 1.10x line, so on the question the row is actually asked the whole interval clears the threshold on the wrong side — K1 is missed, decisively, with parity excluded and direction intact. Retain part 4's whole-interval discipline; make its THRESHOLD row-specific rather than importing bulk's 1.0/1.5.

ONE MORE THING WORTH KNOWING BEFORE RULING, because it shows the calibration was not a convenience: bulk's ceiling of 1.8905 would have REFUSED clock-emvod run 3, whose mount median is 1.8978x. The mount's own location limits came out 30% NARROWER than bulk's. Calibrating the mount class loosened nothing — it tightened the instrument while restoring the reproduction path.
MAYOR ACKNOWLEDGEMENT 2026-08-08 17:55 AUSEST — ruling received, verified in source, and SEQUENCED. Recording my own error first because it is the useful part.

WHERE I WAS WRONG. My 15:10 recommendation said both interval lower bounds (1.1259 / 1.1209) sit above K1's 1.10x line, so the row adjudicates K1 as decisively missed. The arithmetic was right and the QUANTITY was wrong. Verified in source before writing this: clock_readjudicate.cjs's pairedLogRatios says of itself, in its own comment, "LEVEL over LEVEL, touching neither floor", while validation.md:14/:286 define canonical M1 as FLOOR-NORMALISED on the clock of record. Those are different estimands. I read an interval off one estimator and compared it to a threshold defined for another, which is the same class of error rf2-8a746 exists to retire — asserting against an instrument a value derived for a different one. The Codex pass caught what I missed, and part (2) is right to hold publication until the tool computes K1's own estimand.

WHAT IS ADOPTED FROM THE RECOMMENDATION: part (1), row-specific thresholds, with the discipline itself retained unchanged and no named exemptions. The mount rule is now stated more precisely than I put it — ship only when the interval's UPPER bound sits at or below 1.10x, trip K1 only when the LOWER bound sits above it, INSTRUMENT-LIMITED otherwise.

SEQUENCING — THE REPAIR IS NOT DISPATCHED YET, AND WHY. Criteria (a)-(f) are worker-sized and this bead stays open as that item, but the repair must touch clock_exit_path.test.cjs (criterion d flips a pin there) and rf2-c1974's worker is live on that same file right now, deriving the clock standard's out-of-sample limits. Two hands on one test file is the collision the sequencing rule exists to prevent. The repair dispatches the moment c1974's PR merges — it is next in the queue, ahead of everything else open.

NOTED FOR THE BRIEF, so it is not lost between now and then: criterion (c)'s second veto is OPERATOR-OVERTURNABLE and its consequence is stated in the ruling — retaining the cross-run max-band veto flips the honest outcome to INSTRUMENT-LIMITED even though the row-specific interval clears 1.10x. The worker must implement the retirement as ruled and must NOT quietly re-add the veto to make a verdict look safer.

AND THE EXPECTED OUTCOME IS NOT A LICENCE. Part (5) gives diagnostic replays of 1.1718x [1.1263-1.2190] and 1.1976x [1.1504-1.2468]. Criterion (e) says M1 publishes from the canonical tool's own output, not from that note. If the implementation does not reproduce those figures, the figures are wrong and the implementation is the record — the worker reports the discrepancy rather than reconciling toward the expectation.

comments.text:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-08, operator-overturnable) — the t2flm/8a746 collision on M1 is ruled in the composed shape the evidence supports. Both the mayor's 15:10 recommendation and the independent Codex pass agree on the threshold half; Codex's estimator finding (verified against source before ruling) blocks the immediate-publication half. Five parts:

(1) ROW-SPECIFIC THRESHOLDS ADOPTED. Part 4's whole-interval discipline is retained unchanged — no exceptions, no named exemptions. Its thresholds become row-class-specific: BULK adjudicates against its own 1.0x (ship) / 1.5x (architecture-kill) lines, the middle remaining unresolved; MOUNT adjudicates against K1's 1.10x — ship only when the interval's upper bound sits at or below 1.10x, trip K1 only when the lower bound sits above 1.10x, otherwise INSTRUMENT-LIMITED. Rationale stands as recorded: 1.0/1.5 are the bulk row's lines (validation.md's operative bar); asking M1 to clear them is asking a question its governing record does not define; a universal rule would refuse any row whose effect sits between thresholds — most interesting results.

(2) PUBLICATION REMAINS HELD — the magnitudes do not unhold until the re-adjudicator implements K1's EXACT estimand. Verified in source before ruling: validation.md:14/:286 define canonical M1 as FLOOR-NORMALISED on the clock of record, while the implemented interval (clock_readjudicate.cjs pairedLogRatios, :322-331) is by its own comment "LEVEL over LEVEL, touching neither floor" — a different estimand. The dossier's proposed figures spliced a point from one estimator (floor-normalised arithmetic summaries 1.1798x/1.2057x) onto intervals from another (unfloored geometric 1.1679x [1.1259-1.2096] / 1.1621x [1.1209-1.2090]). A point and interval must describe the same estimand; NO SPLICED FIGURE EVER PUBLISHES.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA for the publication repair (one PR, worker-sized — this bead stays OPEN as that work item):
  a. The publication path computes K1's estimand directly: per-round tared, floor-normalised leg ratio ((H - plumbH)/(floorH - plumbH)) / ((U - plumbU)/(floorU - plumbU)), point AND interval from that ONE estimator via the existing run-preserving outer-run/inner-round bootstrap.
  b. The row-specific thresholds of part (1) are implemented in the same rule; bulk's path unchanged.
  c. The max-band-across-all-accepted-runs SECOND VETO is retired from publication authority: the 35% band ceiling stays as the run-eligibility guard, same-run bands report as sensitivity diagnostics, but the cross-run maximum stops vetoing publication — it is not an interval for the claimed effect, it borrows a control statistic from another estimand, and it grows harder to clear merely by adding runs (widest same-run bands here: 22.34% / 18.29%). OPERATOR-OVERTURNABLE with the consequence stated: if the operator retains that veto, the honest outcome flips to INSTRUMENT-LIMITED even though the row-specific interval clears 1.10x.
  d. The clock_exit_path.test.cjs pin flips deliberately (publishes === true for M1 under the new rule), mutation-covered in both directions, with the pin message citing this ruling.
  e. M1 publishes from the canonical tool's own output — not from this note, not from any diagnostic replay.
  f. The published row carries the residual-uncertainty caveats: 8 and 6 outer runs only; the mount check-standard limits were calibrated on these same 14 runs rather than an independent baseline; both ensembles record the same Chromium version.

(3) THE 0.11pp-AGREEMENT SENTENCE IS RETIRED EVERYWHERE. The selected-subset corroboration was a property of the selection, not the measurement — the whole-ensemble means sit 2.59pp apart (1.1798x vs 1.2057x). The honest replication statement: two independently launched ensembles, whole-ensemble figures, overlapping intervals. The studio page's §4.3 supersession (already drafted) executes with the publication PR.

(4) rf2-owiis STAYS SEQUENCED behind the publication landing — the roster sweep must cite the published figures, not this note.

(5) EXPECTED OUTCOME, stated without pre-publishing: on the diagnostic replays of K1's matched floor-normalised estimand (run-preserving bootstrap, 4,000 draws, seed 20260807), the intervals read 1.1718x [1.1263-1.2190] (emvod, 8 runs) and 1.1976x [1.1504-1.2468] (w3yxd, 6 runs) — both entirely above 1.10 on the losing side. If the canonical implementation reproduces that, M1 publishes as K1 MISSED, DECISIVELY, at ~1.17-1.20 vs direct UIx. The direction and approximate price are robust across every estimator tried; only the exact citable figure waits on the repair.

DURABLE RECORD (preserved from the reviewed dossier + Codex pass before deletion):
- The collision mechanics: rf2-x7x10's mount-class calibration (centre 1.7956x, location [1.6765-1.9147], dispersion <= 0.577) brought all 14 runs IN CONTROL and was not a convenience — mount limits are 30% narrower than bulk's, whose 1.8905 ceiling would have wrongly refused emvod run 3's 1.8978 mount median. That calibration is what let part 4 reach M1 at all.
- The implemented (unfloored level-ratio) table, retained as a LABELLED DIAGNOSTIC, never the headline: hicasso/uix 1.1679x [1.1259-1.2096] n=8, 1.1621x [1.1209-1.2090] n=6; hicasso/reagent 1.1142x [1.0238-1.1988], 1.1151x [1.0314-1.1955]; uix/reagent 0.9540x / 0.9596x. Whole intervals above 1.0 on both hicasso/uix pairs — parity excluded, direction intact, under every estimator.

title: hicasso: :p0/write-all's fixed per-write cost makes the allocation ladder uncertifiable at any page size
description:
MEASURED by rf2-2rtt6.138's window on 2026-08-08 (PR #7691). This is the
structural result of that window and it outranks the sizing question.

THE FIXED COST, measured for the first time on this rig. :p0/write-all
rebuilds a 300-element vector and drives the whole event pipeline whether
one boundary is mounted or 1,200. The floor arm is precisely that write with
no subscription under it, and it reads:

  reagent-subs  24,108 B per write
  uix-subs      24,730 B per write

Call it F ~ 24.4 KB. F DOES NOT SHRINK WHEN B DOES.

WHY THAT IS FATAL TO THE CURRENT ROUTE. The masking bound (rf2-n6w7o)
charges (W+1).perWrite <= 300,000 B. At the six-write averaging floor that
allows 42,857 B per write -- and F alone is 57% of it, before a single
boundary has been measured. Modelling perWrite ~ F + B.s(R) off the run's
own arms, the largest page each rung admits (worst arm per rung, since a
ladder holds ONE B fixed across all rungs) is:

  rung   s (B/bnd/write)   W=1   W=3   W=6
  R=1      2,031- 4,067     30    12     4
  R=3      4,888- 5,904     21     8     3
  R=7      9,246-10,158     12     4     1
  R=20     6,800-22,174      5     2     0

AT SIX WRITES THERE IS NO PAGE OF ONE BOUNDARY OR MORE THAT CERTIFIES THE
1/3/7/20 LADDER. At W=1 there is (B <= 5), but W=1 is the configuration that
produced r2 0.75/0.28/0.94/0.31 for want of averaging, and at B=5 the fixed
cost is F/B ~ 4,884 B/boundary/write -- close to twice the entire first-read
signal, with a round-to-round spread (floor moves 21,840-24,432 B/write over
six rounds) that lands on the fit as noise on the rung with the least signal.
Those s(R) are read off windows the run refused as under-reading, so each is
a LOWER bound and the squeeze is at least this tight.

SO 'SHRINK THE MEASURED UNIT' HAS A FLOOR, and the floor is F. The route
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-survival-metrics-allocation-half.md
recommended has now been tried and measured, and the page records it.

THE TWO ROUTES LEFT, both design questions rather than sizing ones:

  (a) A CHEAPER WRITE on this bench, so F stops consuming the budget. The
      300-element vector rebuild is per-write and independent of the arm; if
      the write could touch only the mounted boundaries, F would fall with B
      and the whole squeeze relaxes. This is the likelier route and it is a
      p0_arms.cljs / p0_heap.cljs question.
  (b) A BOUND THAT DOES NOT CHARGE (W+1).perWrite -- i.e. route (a) of
      rf2-n6w7o, an independent in-window collection witness, which would
      let a window be certified by what it OBSERVED rather than by its size.
      Note the merged-PR audit of #7682 already disputes the present bound's
      soundness on separate grounds (see the sibling bead).

DO NOT discharge this by widening the budget or by dropping the R=20 rung:
R=20 is HD-002's own ladder and the budget exists to refuse under-reads.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-08, operator-overturnable): THE COMPOSED PACKAGE IS RULED — route (a) AND route (b), designed together in ONE brief. Not (a) alone, not (b) alone.

WHY BOTH, verified before ruling (mechanics confirmed against source: the charging rule `(W+1).B.c <= ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B` and `ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B = ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B / 2` at p0_run.cjs:1081,1119 — note the p0 instrument actually lives at implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/{p0_run.cjs,p0_arms.cljs,p0_heap.cljs}, not under freehand/; workers should land there):
- (a) alone leaves the disputed bound certifying windows: the #7682 audit's objection stands unanswered (an observed 240 KB collection under the 300 KB "no-collection" budget — see rf2-2rtt6.141), so every certification would rest on arithmetic the data already contradicts.
- (b) alone yields a sound instrument that rarely produces data: with F ~ 24.4 KB fixed per write, removing the budget admits larger B on paper, but per-write allocation F + B.s(R) then approaches the observed collection cadence at meaningful B (at R=20, B=24: ~24.4K + 24x~22K ~ 550 KB/write) — the witness would correctly refuse nearly every window. Sound but useless.
- Together: the boundary-proportional write keeps per-write allocation small enough that clean windows exist at real page sizes, and the witness certifies them by observation rather than by a disputed model. This is the minimal complete fix; sequential single-route attempts risk two design cycles for the same artefacts.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (bounded — no stats research project; one brief, then worker-sized implementation):
1. ONE design brief covering both artefacts and their validity witnesses BEFORE any code: (i) the boundary-proportional write, (ii) the in-window collection witness.
2. Write half: a :p0/write-* variant whose machinery cost scales with mounted boundaries (today :p0/write-all rebuilds a 300-element vector and drives the whole event pipeline regardless of B). Validity: a floor arm at >= 2 page sizes showing the fixed residue no longer dominant (per-boundary fixed residue below the R=1 signal, ~2 KB/bnd/write); and the brief states the equivalence argument that the new write still exercises the same per-boundary read/render work HD-002's ladder claims to measure.
3. Witness half: certification by observation replaces the (W+1).perWrite arithmetic. The #7682 audit's two executable probes become pinned regression tests: windows with true allocation 300 KB and 600 KB at headroom=0 must be REFUSED by the witness (both were admitted by the old bound); the net-growth masking case is pinned.
4. Constraint semantics, stated to prevent a false contradiction: the bead forbids WIDENING the budget or dropping R=20 — both stand. RETIRING the budget mechanism in favour of the witness is route (b) itself, sanctioned by this bead; replacement is not widening. ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B is not loosened; R=20 stays.
5. Sequencing: rf2-2rtt6.139 re-derives sizing per-rung from the NEW instrument's own floor data (or retires the preflight constant) only after the brief — ruling it against the current instrument would be immediately obsoleted. rf2-2rtt6.142's preflight fix rides the same rework, not ahead of it. NO further allocation window (incl. rf2-2rtt6.138 re-runs) before the brief's validity witnesses are green — any window before that is wasted by this bead's own arithmetic.
6. Supersession honesty: once the new write lands, the 2026-08-07/08 floor-arm and ladder rows are superseded-not-comparable; the-survival-metrics-allocation-half.md annotates, never erases.

DURABLE RECORD (already in this bead's description, restated here only by pointer): F = 24,108/24,730 B/write (reagent-subs/uix-subs); the per-rung admissibility table (W=6 admits B=4/3/1/0 across R=1/3/7/20); s(R) lower-bound ranges 2,031-4,067 (R=1) to 6,800-22,174 (R=20); the W=1 failure history (r^2 0.75/0.28/0.94/0.31; F/B ~ 4,884 B ~ 2x the first-read signal; floor spread 21,840-24,432 B/write).

Siblings ruled concurrently in the same review wave: rf2-2rtt6.141 (bound soundness — the witness above is its remedy), rf2-2rtt6.139 (sizing — folded behind this per criterion 5). Route (b)'s lineage: rf2-n6w7o route (a).

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
CRITERION 1 DISCHARGED — the design brief is written and open as PR #7697 (branch worker/allocdesign-140). The bead STAYS OPEN: criteria 2-6 are the implementation and its validity witnesses.

WHERE IT LIVES: docs/design/hicasso/allocation-instrument-rework.md, tracked, linked from docs/design/hicasso/README.md, with a forward pointer from the studio page's "next attempt" item. No code, no measurement.

WHAT THE BRIEF SETTLES:

WRITE HALF. A new :p0/write-page rebuilds :cells at the width the mounted page actually reads. The grid width becomes a property of the seeded app-db (seed-db takes it; :p0/fan's modulus reads (count (:cells db))), so it cannot live in two places and drift. :p0/write-all is left byte-identical and the clock/bulk rows keep driving it. The EQUIVALENCE ARGUMENT: same dispatch-sync through the same pipeline and signal graph; every one of the E = B.R edges sees a changed value so the invalidation set is identical; the rendered text is (str (* R v)) under either write so the read-back and canonical-DOM gate are unchanged; B, E, Q and the key rule untouched. The only difference is the width of a vector no boundary reads beyond its own slot -- machinery on both sides of the floor subtraction. On the 24-boundary page 276 of the 300 rebuilt cells were read by nothing.

WITNESS HALF. (W+1).perWrite <= ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B is RETIRED and replaced by a rule read off the window's own samples: the work legs are W repetitions of ONE work unit, so refuse if any leg deviates from the cohort MEDIAN by more than tau.m. A leg below the cohort is a leg something removed bytes from; a leg above it means the one-work-unit premise has failed, and refusing is then correct rather than merely conservative. The certificate is checkable rather than asserted: this window's rise under-reads by at most 2.tau, and here is the worst leg deviation observed.

THE TWO #7682 PROBES ARE REFUSED, and independently of the calibration. Probe A (60K x4 then a leg reading 0) and probe B (50K x5 then a leg reading 0) both have their offending leg at exactly zero against a strictly positive median, so both are refused for EVERY tau < 1 -- a re-calibration cannot silently re-admit them, and that property gets a test of its own. The net-growth masking fixture already in p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs is re-pointed at the new grounds.

CONSTRAINT SEMANTICS, as criterion 4 asks. The budget is RETIRED, not widened. Retaining it belt-and-braces was considered and REJECTED ON ARITHMETIC: at the composed operating point (B=4, R=20, W=6) a window is ~630 KB of rise+maxStep, so a retained bound would refuse every window the witness certifies and the package would deliver nothing. ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B stays at its measured 600,000 B and gates nothing. R=20 stays. ALLOC_MIN_WRITES=6 stays a floor. The falls gate is untouched.

FOUR VALIDITY WITNESSES, none of which publishes a slope. V1: the floor at B in {4,24,96} under BOTH writes -- the old write's flat F is the control that licenses the comparison, and an agreement at B=24 with the 2026-08-08 figures is what makes the two writes comparable at all. V2: the equivalence cross-check, one write per window at B=4, requiring (arm-floor)/B to AGREE between writes while the floor DROPS. V3: tau calibrated on control windows independently corroborated clean by their own 8 B/double prediction -- rf2-2rtt6.141's carried-in criterion answered. V4: the pinned probes, red-then-green.

ALSO CARRIED: the seam with rf2-2rtt6.139 (P0_ALLOC_CELLS becomes MANDATORY rather than a substituted constant -- no honest default exists without a sizing model, and it makes an accidental publication run impossible while criterion 5's freeze holds); a disposition for EVERY structural test the change supersedes (37 rows, KEPT / AMENDED / REPLACED / RETIRED); the criterion-6 supersession obligation; and one option recorded with its trigger and explicitly NOT taken.

WHY BOTH HALVES, NUMERICALLY (at R=20, worst arm s=22,174 B/bnd/write, W=6): today (42,857-24,400)/22,174 = B 0. Route (a) alone, bound kept: B 1 -- a one-boundary "ladder" is not one. Route (b) alone, write kept: B 3, on which F/B = 8,133 B/bnd is 2x-4x the whole R=1 signal. Composed: B 4 with F/B targeted under the R=1 signal. The ruling's claim reproduces arithmetically.

WHAT REMAINS OPEN AND WHY:

1. HOW MUCH OF F ~ 24.4 KB IS THE 300-CELL REBUILD AND HOW MUCH IS THE EVENT PIPELINE. Nobody has measured it and the brief may not. It is the single number the write half turns on. V1 answers it directly, and V1 is the gate on the whole write half -- if the pipeline residue F0 dominates, the write half narrows the gap without closing it, and the brief carries a three-step contingency ladder (raise B; carry F0 as a stated instrument constant; or the reserve option), with an explicit fence against responding by shrinking the page further.
2. THE VALUE OF tau. V3's to measure, on the stated calibration rule. Not a knob (ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B's reasoning unchanged).
3. THE OPERATING PAGE. B, and whether one B serves all four rungs, is rf2-2rtt6.139's per-rung re-derivation off the NEW instrument's floor data. The brief names B in {4,24,96} for V1 and B=4 for V2 as MEASUREMENT configurations, not as the row's page, and derives no sizing constant.
4. WHETHER A 3-TO-5 BOUNDARY PAGE IS A CREDIBLE WITNESS OF A PER-BOUNDARY QUANTITY AT ALL. The arm's per-page constants (React root, frame provider, root subscription) do not cancel against the floor and are divided by a very small B. The expectation is that an R-independent constant lands in the fit's INTERCEPT rather than its slope, and the R=0 shell rung is the direct check -- at B=24 it already reads close to the floor. V2's per-rung comparison is where it shows if that is wrong.
5. THE FINER-SAMPLING OPTION (3-4 samples per write instead of 2) is filed as an option rather than designed: a real sensitivity improvement and allocation-free, but it changes the leg cohort's meaning. V3 decides whether it is needed.

ONE DOWNSTREAM EFFECT ON A CLOSED BEAD, flagged rather than silently taken: rf2-2rtt6.142's refusal text BRANCHES on whether the page can carry six writes, and that second branch is computed from the budget. With the budget retired its trigger no longer exists and the refusal collapses to one branch. That is not a regression -- with no page-size model there is nothing to name, and the endorsed property (never advise the shape being refused) is preserved by there being no such advice to give -- but .142 is CLOSED and its close reason describes the two-branch behaviour, so the implementer records the collapse on that bead when the change lands. .142's ROUTE 2 pin (an explicit one-write window is refused) survives unchanged and must stay green; its ROUTE 1 pin is re-pointed at the mandatory-page refusal.

GATES: check_doc_slugs.py 0, probed red-then-green at the edit site (exit 1 naming file and line 43); check_provenance_pins.py --changed-since origin/main 0 (the page cites no commit SHAs); check-beads-pr-boundary.sh origin/main 0. mkdocs build --strict is NOT the gate (exclude_docs keeps docs/design/** off the site), so anchors and table column counts were hand-verified: 28 headings, 3 same-file anchors all resolving, 6 tables with 0 column mismatches.

CRITERION 5 STANDS: no allocation window, including any rf2-2rtt6.138 re-run, before V1-V4 are green. V1-V4 are the permitted measurements and they publish nothing.

comments.text:
CRITERIA 2, 3, 4 AND 6 IMPLEMENTED — PR #7702 (branch worker/allocbuild-140), open, NOT merged. THE BEAD STAYS OPEN: criterion 5's measurement freeze stands and V1/V2/V3 remain.

NEITHER ARTEFACT HAS BEEN EXECUTED AGAINST A REAL PAGE, and that is the deliverable rather than a caveat on it. No allocation window was opened, no ladder row taken, no quiet box requested. :p0/write-page has never written to a mounted page; the leg witness has never read a real sample stream. Both are proven STRUCTURALLY ONLY — 50 hermetic pins in p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs and 9 hermetic CLJS deftests, every window a synthetic sample buffer and every frame a plain-atom test frame.

WHAT LANDED

WRITE (criterion 2). :p0/write-page rebuilds :cells at the width the mounted page reads. The grid width is a property of the SEEDED APP-DB — seed-db takes it, :p0/seed carries it, enter-segment! and p0-heap/prepare! thread it from the driver — and :p0/fan's modulus reads (count (:cells db)), so it cannot live in two places and drift. :p0/write-all is byte-identical, literal cells-n and all; the clock, bulk, fan-out and retention rows keep driving it at the published 300, and a structural pin reads that off the CLJS sources rather than trusting it. The width threaded is B = ROOTS x P0_ALLOC_CELLS — one cell per mounted boundary, which keeps the change FULL-PAGE (the brief rejects a one-cell grid as converting a full-page change into a point change, and HD-002's law is stated about the change).

WITNESS (criterion 3). The budget is retired; refusal is now "any leg deviates from the cohort MEDIAN by more than tau.m". allocSteps grows legs, gaps, legMedian, legWorstDeviation, refusals and certified, mirroring allocArmSizing's verdict shape since .142. rise/fall/falls/maxStep/endpoints keep their definitions, so no published total changes meaning. allocMaskableWindows -> allocRefusedWindows, naming every refused window with its reason.

CONSTRAINTS (criterion 4). ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B stays at 600,000 B and gates nothing (the summary prints the largest arm rise as a percentage of it). R=20 stays. ALLOC_MIN_WRITES=6 stays a floor. Falls gate and r2 floor untouched. ALLOC_B_PER_BOUNDARY_WRITE, allocMaxWrites, predictedWindowB, headroom, maxBoundaries, floorBoundaries and maskable are deleted. P0_ALLOC_CELLS is MANDATORY.

CRITERION 6 WAS DONE HERE, and the dispatch said it was outstanding — the bead governs. Criterion 6 says the studio page annotates "once the new write lands", and the brief says "the implementation PR adds a dated note to that page". The write lands in #7702, so the annotation rides with it: a dated supersession note at the head and at the small-witness section of the-survival-metrics-allocation-half.md, every figure and every table standing, F_old named as the one figure that keeps its full force because V1 re-measures it as the control that licenses the comparison.

TAU IS AN UNCALIBRATED PLACEHOLDER at 0.25, marked as such in the source with V3 named as what calibrates it. Conservative in the direction that matters (a smaller tau refuses more). No window may be published on it. Nothing pinned depends on it.

MUTATION PROOFS, red-then-green in two commits (059d4fb red, 72d4eaa green). p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs: 6/56 failed at the red commit. Five pins reported `certified` undefined; the MANDATORY-PAGE pin failed on a value — `true !== false` — which is the sharper red, because the shipped preflight really did derive and admit an arm with no page stated. Structural counts 50 -> 49 (disposition) -> 50 (the certificate pin below).

NOTHING LOOSENED, established three ways because the phrase means three things once criterion 4 retires the budget:
(1) FALLS GATE: exhaustive over 17,496 synthetic window shapes against the shipped module — 0 violations, every falling-step window still refused.
(2) PREFLIGHT: exhaustive over W 0..40 x cells 0..40 x roots {0,1,4,50} — 4,200 admitted, every one satisfying both surviving .142 terms, and ZERO arms satisfying those terms refused. The one new refusal is the unstated page.
(3) WINDOW GATE: subset is the WRONG test and I say so rather than claiming otherwise — retiring the budget necessarily admits windows it refused, the brief's arithmetic requires it (a ~630 KB window must be admittable), and the disposition retires THE CHANGE ONLY EVER REFUSES MORE for exactly that reason. In the sweep 36 of 17,496 moved refused->admitted and ALL 36 are over the retired 300,000 B budget, so none is a masked window slipping through. What replaces the subset claim: both audit probes moved from admitted (headroom exactly 0, true allocations 300 KB and 600 KB) to refused; 98.1% of masked windows (4,527 of 4,617) are refused by the leg rule; and the 2-tau certificate HOLDS TIGHT.

THE 2-TAU CERTIFICATE IS NOW PINNED, and this is the one addition worth the operator's attention. Swept over 20,096 windows INSIDE THE COHORT PREMISE (the certificate's own stated antecedent): worst per-leg masked reclamation 50.00% of the median against a 2-tau ceiling of 50%, worst whole-window under-read 10.00%. The worst case is EXACTLY the shape the brief predicts — a leg sitting tau.m high on its own merits, losing 2.tau.m, reading tau.m low, admitted at the very edge — and one byte further refuses. So 2-tau is a bound rather than an approximation, and the implementation realises the certificate the brief specified, tight. Outside the premise the certificate says nothing and the brief says so.

GATES, all foreground to completion from WORKTREE_ROOT=/c/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/allocbuild-140: node --check both .cjs 0; p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs 0 (50 passed); npm run test:script-helpers 0; npm run test:cljs 0 (12,812 tests / 64,426 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors); sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh 0; npm run lint:js 0; python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py 0; sh scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh origin/main 0. The control is F_old coming back flat in B and landing on the 2026-08-08 figures at B=24. The criterion is F_new(B)/B below ~2 KB/bnd/write. This is the gate on the whole write half and the brief carries a three-step contingency ladder under it.

DISCREPANCIES FOUND, reported not resolved: the bead's criterion-1 note and the brief's prose both say "37 rows" in the test disposition table; the table as written has 36. All 36 are dispositioned and nothing appears missing — I read it as a miscount in the prose, not a lost row.

A REAL PRE-EXISTING COLLISION SURFACED: :p0/cell is registered in THREE namespaces — p0_fixture.cljc, hicasso/clock_views.cljs and hicasso/p0_reagent_views.cljs — each with its own implementation. The p0 release builds carry one, so it is unreachable there; the consolidated :node-test build loads all three and image assembly correctly refuses to let selection order decide (:rf.error/image-duplicate-id). The new CLJS suite is scoped with :select-ns over re-frame.bench.p0-fixture, which is the error's own first remedy. Filing no bead: nothing is broken today, and the three registrations are three different benches' fixtures rather than a drift.

title: hicasso: the allocation row's sizing constant is derived from a run the row itself refused
description:
MEASURED by rf2-2rtt6.138's window on 2026-08-08 (PR #7691), and it is why that run refused.

ALLOC_B_PER_BOUNDARY_WRITE = 1655 in p0_run.cjs sizes the whole allocation
arm. Its stated provenance is 'MEASURED, on the candidate arm, in that same
quiet-box run: 544-1655 B across its rungs' -- the 2026-08-07 run of the
published 1,200-boundary witness.

THAT RUN REFUSED, at 36 falling steps across 44 windows, and the row's own
refusal text says every figure from such a window is an UNDER-estimate. So
the constant that sizes the arm is a lower bound taken from a measurement
the instrument declared invalid, and sizing off a lower bound produces a
page too LARGE. That is exactly what the 2026-08-08 run found: at B=24 the
measured per-boundary-per-write is 3,731-23,192 B against the 1,655 the arm
was sized with -- 2.3x to 14x -- and 98 of 132 windows came back over the
masking budget.

TWO THINGS ARE TANGLED IN THAT CONSTANT and the run separates them:

  (1) a fixed per-write cost F ~ 24.4 KB that does not scale with B (the
      floor arm: 24,108 B/write on reagent-subs, 24,730 on uix-subs); and
  (2) a genuine per-boundary term s(R) that does, and that is strongly
      R-dependent: 2,031-4,067 B/boundary/write at R=1 rising to
      6,800-22,174 at R=20.

A single scale-free 'c' models neither. At B=1,200 F contributes 20
B/boundary (which is exactly the '~20' the corpus records as the floor's
figure there); at B=24 it contributes ~1,005. The constant silently mixes
the two and is only valid at the page it was measured on.

WHAT TO DO IS A RULING, NOT A FIX, which is why this is filed rather than
done: either re-derive the sizing from the (F, s(R)) decomposition this run
measured -- in which case the preflight has to be told which rung it is
sizing for, since s varies 5x across the ladder -- or stop sizing from a
constant at all and let the preflight refuse only on grounds it can defend.
Do NOT simply substitute a bigger number: the honest reading is that the
2026-08-07 figures cannot size anything, because the run that produced them
was refused.

DO NOT widen ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B or ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B under this bead.
notes: TRIAGE vs hic-* set (rf2-6bj7, 2026-08-10, delegated, operator-overturnable): KEEP — no hic-* successor exists. Verified against the full hic roster: hic-006 re-pins shell/per-read/teardown baselines (not warm-allocation), hic-071/089 enforce budget gates, hic-036 is bulk economics, hic-070 is the K3 record, and hic-072's warm-allocation NON-claim scan enforces silence precisely while this instrument's quality floor is unmet — none performs the per-rung re-derivation this bead owes off V1 floor data. Disposition unchanged from the 2026-08-08 delegated decision: blocked behind rf2-2rtt6.140's V1-V3; discharged by the per-rung sizing re-derivation under the new instrument. This bead and .140 are the single residual allocation-validity thread of the old epic.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-08, operator-overturnable): FOLDED INTO THE rf2-2rtt6.140 PACKAGE — not ruled in isolation.

THE DISPOSITION OF THIS BEAD, stated so it stands alone:

(1) ALLOC_B_PER_BOUNDARY_WRITE = 1655 is RETIRED as a sizing input, effective now. It was derived from the 2026-08-07 run that itself refused (36 falling steps / 44 windows), whose own refusal text declares every such figure an under-estimate. Sizing from that lower bound licensed pages too large: measured reality at B=24 is 3,731-23,192 B/boundary/write against the 1,655 sized (2.3x-14x), with 98 of 132 windows over the masking budget. No replacement constant is to be substituted -- the description's own fence stands (do not widen ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B or ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B; do not swap in a bigger number).

(2) INTERIM PREFLIGHT POSTURE (until the .140 package lands): the preflight refuses only on grounds it can defend without a sizing model -- e.g. W >= ALLOC_MIN_WRITES (rf2-2rtt6.142's fix). It does not predict admissibility from any scalar. A window spent on a page that then refuses is acceptable; a gatekeeper enforcing a model the data contradicts is not.

(3) FINAL SHAPE (after the .140 ruling's new write/bound land): sizing is re-derived PER RUNG from a re-measured s(R) under the new instrument -- the preflight must be told which rung it sizes for, because the per-boundary term is strongly R-dependent. The single-constant approach is not resurrected.

DURABLE ANALYSIS PRESERVED FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION AGENT (from PR #7691's decomposition; the dossier that carried it is deleted after this note):
- The old constant silently mixed two terms the run now separates: a fixed per-write cost F ~ 24.4 KB that does not scale with B (floor arm: 24,108 B/write reagent-subs / 24,730 uix-subs), and a genuine per-boundary term s(R): 2,031-4,067 B/boundary/write at R=1 rising to 6,800-22,174 at R=20 -- a 5x swing across the HD-002 ladder.
- Scale dependence of the mix: at B=1,200 F contributes ~20 B/boundary (matching the corpus's recorded floor figure there); at B=24 it contributes ~1,005. A scale-free 'c' is only valid at the page it was measured on -- this is why "measure a better constant" is not an available fix.
- All s(R) figures above are lower bounds (read off refused windows); treat them as floors when re-deriving.

WHAT THIS BEAD NOW WAITS ON: the rf2-2rtt6.140 ruling (write route + bound), then its implementation.
WHAT DISCHARGES IT: the per-rung sizing re-derivation landing under the new instrument (or the .140 package rendering preflight sizing moot entirely, in which case close this bead against that outcome). Sequence rf2-2rtt6.142 behind the same package -- all three touch p0_run.cjs; never parallelise them.

title: docs: the published M-11 imperative-subscription Form-3 recipe teaches rf2-8cnxg to users
description:
FIFTH occurrence of the rf2-8cnxg defect shape, and the only one that ships to
CONSUMERS rather than living in our own code. Found by the same read-only sweep
(2026-08-07) that filed rf2-wmpte and rf2-lynzk.

NEEDS A RULING BEFORE A PATCH -- see THE FIX below. The defect is not in
question; the repair shape is, because the op the fix needs is not on the public
facade.

THE DEFECT. skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-handlers-state.md:164-192,
the copy-pasteable 'exceptional imperative-subscription Form-3':

    :reagent-render (fn [_] [:div.gauge])          ; <- derefs NOTHING
    :component-did-mount
    (fn [this]
      (reset! !widget (mk-gauge! this))
      (let [reaction (subscribe query-v)]
        (reset! !reaction reaction)
        (feed-gauge! @!widget @reaction)            ; plain deref, no context
        (add-watch reaction watch-key               ; 'observe changes with no reactive owner'
          (fn [_ _ _ v] (feed-gauge! @!widget v)))))

subscribe -> plain deref -> add-watch, no activation. :component-did-mount runs
after commit with NO reactive context (the recipe's own surrounding prose says
so at spec/Pattern-StatefulComponents.md:71), and the render derefs nothing, so
nothing ever supplies the shared cached Reaction a deref-capture. watching stays
nil; the watch is recorded and can never fire.

OBSERVABLY WRONG FOR THE USER. A widget fed once at mount and deaf thereafter --
rf2-8cnxg's exact symptom, in consumer code, taught by us. Reagent is a
first-class actively-supported adapter, and this recipe is Reagent-only by its
own framing, so it hits the ONE substrate where the shape is silently wrong.

THE REPO ALREADY KNOWS -- twice, in its own test comments.
  - form_3_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs:560-568 -- the fixture that mirrors this
    recipe only passes because it bolts activation on and labels it as
    scaffolding: 'a cached sub reaction with NO live consumer is dormant and
    never re-runs (so its imperative watches never fire) ... driver is an
    auto-running reaction that derefs the HELD reaction ... This is warmth
    scaffolding, not the behaviour under test'. Line 570 --
    driver (ratom/run! (deref warm)) -- IS the activation. The recipe ships
    without it.
  - schema_reject_notification_cljs_test.cljs:19-22 states the general law: 'a
    bare add-watch on a Reagent 1.x Reaction never activates it headlessly, so
    it would vacuously see nothing on ANY commit'.

BLAST RADIUS -- five surfaces carry the recipe or point at it, and any repair
moves them together:
  - skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-handlers-state.md:162-196 (the code)
  - spec/Pattern-StatefulComponents.md:71 and :188 (normative restatements)
  - skills/re-frame2/patterns/stateful-components.md:98
  - implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md:97
  - scripts/check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py:962-1107 -- a GATE that
    enforces the recipe's shape (the FORM3-* rules). A changed recipe reds it
    unless updated in the same PR.
  - implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/form_3_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs:492-620
    mirrors the recipe and would want its scaffolding revisited.

THE FIX -- WHY THIS NEEDS MIKE. interop/activate-derived-value! is NOT exported
from re-frame.core (verified: no hit in core.cljc). So unlike rf2-wmpte and
rf2-lynzk, this one cannot be repaired by analogy to observation.cljc:1982 --
there is no public op for a consumer to call. Three shapes, in the sweep's order
of preference:

  1. EXPORT an activation op on the re-frame.core facade, then add one line to
     the recipe before the add-watch. Smallest edit, keeps the recipe's
     ergonomics. Costs a new facade export (classify-and-justify at diff time
     per the standing rule).
  2. CHANGE THE RECIPE to activate the Reagent way -- an r/track! / ratom/run!
     owner beside the watch, which is exactly what our own fixture does. No new
     export; the recipe stops being adapter-agnostic in shape.
  3. RETIRE the imperative-watch branch and steer the case to r/with-let inside
     :reagent-render (already the recommended form one paragraph above it in the
     same file), which activates by BEING a render.

Whichever is ruled, spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:209 already states the law the
recipe violates ('Watchable is necessary, not sufficient -- a demand-driven
derived value must be ACTIVATED'), so the docs change is an alignment, not a new
claim.

Cross-ref: rf2-8cnxg (the original, observation port), rf2-2kshh (hicasso arm1
wire-cell!), rf2-wmpte (machines/timer), rf2-lynzk (xray auto-open watcher).
Working notes: ai/findings/2026-08-07.activate-derived-value-third-site-sweep.md
sec 2.3.
close_reason: FIXED in PR #7664 (85de3446b0). The M-11 imperative Form-3 now owns its reaction per mount with r/track!, disposes that owner before frame-first unsubscribe, and removes the inert add-watch shape across every governed surface. Rule 5c and live mutations pin ownership; focused CLJS passed 3 tests/24 assertions and the browser lane passed 1128/6945. No facade export was added. The reagent-slim FORM-3 remainder is separately owned by rf2-iogzk.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-07, operator-overturnable): OPTION 2 — repair the recipe with a per-mount `reagent.core/track!` owner. NO new facade export; `activate-derived-value!` stays internal. Option 3's steering (prefer `r/with-let` in `:reagent-render`; Form-1 child preferred over all of this) stays prominent — the imperative branch remains the documented rare escape hatch, now correct by construction.

THE RULING, WITH REASONS (dossier Option 1 recommendation considered and rejected; Codex Option 2 recommendation adopted after verification):

1. `activate-derived-value!` is the wrong abstraction level for an app-facing facade. Verified: it lives at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs:85`, routed through the adapter late-bind table (`:adapter/activate-derived-value!` at interop.cljs:117), and has ZERO hits in core.cljc. spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:209-211 defines it as a demand-driven-adapter hook used by the internal observation port at acquire time; spec/API.md classifies adapter machinery outside the front porch. Exporting it would convert an internal conformance hook into a permanent "remember this substrate quirk" application API with no lifetime handle — against the minimal-API posture.

2. Option 2's supposed adapter-agnosticity cost is illusory. Verified: the recipe (skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-handlers-state.md:164-192 and surrounds) already names `reagent.core/create-class`, `r/atom`, `r/with-let`, and gensym'd per-mount watch-keys. It is a stock-Reagent Form-3 recipe; using another stock public Reagent op crosses no new boundary.

3. `track!` is strictly better ergonomics than an exported activation op — it removes the trap instead of documenting it. The tracker's eager first run IS the initial seed (no separate plain deref to forget to activate); each mount's tracker is a distinct reactive owner, so two widgets can observe the same cached reaction with NO watch keys — the entire per-mount gensym watch-key machinery and its overwrite/freeze hazard paragraph in the current recipe are deleted, not patched. An exported activation op would keep add-watch/remove-watch/watch-key AND add a remember-to-call step.

4. The repair shape is already proven in-repo. Verified: `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/schema_reject_notification_cljs_test.cljs` acquires one subscription, observes via `(r/track! (fn [] ... @sub))` (:57), proves a valid commit re-runs it, and tears down `r/dispose!` BEFORE `rf/unsubscribe` (:93-94). No conflict with spec/006:211's rejection of `:auto-run` on cached derived values: the tracker is one explicit disposable observer per exceptional mounted consumer, observing the already-held subscription; the subscription still recomputes on the ordinary batched queue.

5. The dossier's strongest pro-export argument (five in-repo occurrences of the rf2-8cnxg shape: rf2-8cnxg, rf2-2kshh, rf2-wmpte, rf2-lynzk, rf2-2rtt6.137 — the trap is severe) cuts the other way on inspection: the in-repo sites are internal code with interop access and are being fixed there; the one consumer-facing site is Reagent-targeted and Reagent's public API solves it with fewer concepts.

THE REPAIRED SHAPE (for the recipe; worked out in the review):

  mount:   (let [reaction (subscribe query-v)]        ; acquire once, ref-count +1
             (reset! !reaction reaction)
             (reset! !driver
               (r/track! (fn [] (feed-gauge! @!widget @reaction)))))  ; eager 1st run = seed
  unmount: (when-let [driver @!driver] (r/dispose! driver))  ; stop observer FIRST
           (rf/unsubscribe frame query-v)                    ; then release cache slot
           (destroy-gauge! @!widget)

This deletes `watch-key`, `add-watch`, `remove-watch` entirely. StrictMode replay stays balanced (acquire/release per did-mount/will-unmount unchanged).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION WORKER — ONE PR moving all surfaces together:
1. skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-handlers-state.md:164-192 — replace seed-deref + add-watch machinery with the track!-owner shape above; delete the per-mount watch-key paragraph (now moot); keep the with-let steering and Form-1-child preference prominent and FIRST.
2. spec/Pattern-StatefulComponents.md:71 and :188 — align mirrored prose (alignment, not a new claim: spec/006:209 already states "Watchable is necessary, not sufficient").
3. skills/re-frame2/patterns/stateful-components.md:98 — align.
4. implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md:97 — align.
5. scripts/check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py:962-1107 — update the FORM3-* rules to enforce the NEW shape in the same PR (a changed recipe reds CI otherwise).
6. form_3_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs:492-679 — rewrite so the recipe itself supplies liveness; DELETE the external `warm`/`ratom/run!` "warmth scaffolding". Retain the high-value assertions: two same-query mounts both see an update; removing one leaves the other live; StrictMode replay leaves one acquisition; unmount returns ref-count to baseline. ADD non-vacuity: deleting the track! driver must fail the named post-mount update assertion.
7. NO change to re-frame.core exports. Nothing on the facade.
8. Wording discipline: notifications arrive "on the next Reagent flush/commit" (track! follows the reaction drain), never "before dispatch returns". Fix stale "Reagent 1.x" phrasing where the diff touches it (pinned substrate is Reagent 2.0.1; same law).
9. Scope: this recipe targets the stock Reagent adapter only. reagent2.core (reagent-slim) deliberately omits track!/with-let — if M-11 is ever broadened to reagent-slim it needs its own adapter-specific recipe; do not imply portability.

This ruling discharges the "NEEDS A RULING BEFORE A PATCH" hold; the bead is now worker-dispatchable.

title: machines: :after sub-vec delay never re-resolves on the ratom family — rf2-8cnxg in machines/timer
description:
THIRD OCCURRENCE of the rf2-8cnxg defect shape, found by a read-only sweep (2026-08-07) commissioned after rf2-2kshh. Sibling of rf2-2kshh; independent fix.

THE DEFECT. implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/timer.cljc.

  resolve-delay-ms, lines 136-152:
    (vector? delay-key)
    ;; subscribe to keep the reaction live; caller will add-watch for
    ;; change-detection then unsubscribe on cancellation.
    (let [reaction (subs/subscribe delay-key {:frame frame-id})
          v        (when reaction (try @reaction ...))]
      [v reaction])

  schedule-after-timer!, lines 658-667:
    (when (and reaction watch-key)
      (try (add-watch reaction watch-key
                      (fn [_ _ old-v new-v] (on-sub-changed! ...)))
           (catch ... :rf.error/machine-after-watch-failed)))

subscribe -> plain deref -> add-watch. re-frame.interop is NOT in the ns
require block (lines 38-45) and interop/activate-derived-value! is never
called. The docstring premise -- 'subscribe to keep the reaction live' -- is
the exact false belief observation.cljc:1962-1973 names.

WHY IT BREAKS. Under the ratom family a subscription IS a bare Reaction
(subs.cljc:1304 -> spine.cljs:3419-3421, make-reaction and deliberately NOT
:auto-run). A Reaction learns its sources only through deref-capture;
reagent2/ratom.cljs:395-415 shows a deref outside *ratom-context* with no
auto-run taking the on-demand branch -- run f raw, wire NO watcher graph,
leave watching nil. _handle-change is then never called and _queued-run
requires (some? watching), so flush! moves nothing either. The watch is
recorded and can never fire.

OBSERVABLY WRONG. On a Reagent / reagent-slim host a machine with
  :states {:running {:after {[:cfg/timeout-ms] {:target :expired}}}}
arms the FIRST resolved delay correctly (the deref returns a right value) and
then NEVER re-resolves. A write moving :cfg/timeout-ms fires no watch, so
on-sub-changed!'s cancel-and-reschedule never runs and the arming keeps the
stale duration for its whole life. Silent: no trace, no error. The behaviour
is normative -- Spec 005 sec Delayed :after transitions, and
docs/api/re-frame.machines.md:473 promises it unconditionally.

Correct on the React-hook spine (UIx / Helix / re-frame.ui / Freehand):
push-based from birth. Loud on plain-atom CLJS (derived value reifies IDeref
only, so add-watch throws and the existing
:rf.error/machine-after-watch-failed / :recovery :static-delay path fires).
The ratom family is the ONLY substrate where it is silently wrong.

THE FIX, by analogy to observation.cljc:1959-1990 ('ACTIVATE, then watch,
then observe -- and the order is the whole fix for rf2-8cnxg'):
add re-frame.interop to the requires and call

    (interop/activate-derived-value! reaction)

immediately BEFORE the add-watch at line 664. Total and idempotent: a no-op
on every non-ratom substrate (the routed chain-bottom returns nil) and a
no-op on an already-capturing Reaction, so it costs nothing anywhere else.
Do NOT reach for :auto-run true -- interop.cljs:105-110 explains why.

WHY NO SUITE SAW IT (the untested-combination axis). The CLJS timer suites
install plain-atom (after_fire_reap_cljs_test.cljc:33,
machine_timer_incarnation_fence_cljs_test.cljc:55) and, KNOWING the
plain-atom derived value does not push, with-redefs a plain controllable atom
in place of the reaction. Their own header says so
(after_fire_reap_cljs_test.cljc:16-19): 'a plain controllable atom stands in
for the reaction so add-watch / remove-watch and a reset!-driven change are
synchronous on both platforms'. A plain atom always notifies -- the
substitution that makes the test deterministic is the substitution that makes
it blind. There is NO machines-timer test on a ratom adapter at all.

ACCEPTANCE. A test on the Reagent (or reagent-slim) adapter that registers a
machine with a sub-vector :after delay, dispatches a write that MOVES the
delay sub's value, and asserts the timer cancelled and re-armed at the new
duration. It must exercise the real reaction, not a with-redefs stand-in --
the stand-in is what hid this.

Cross-ref: rf2-8cnxg (the original, in the observation port), rf2-2kshh (the
second occurrence, hicasso arm1 wire-cell!, in progress). Working notes:
ai/findings/2026-08-07.activate-derived-value-third-site-sweep.md sec 2.1.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #7651 (worker/timeract-wmpte). One call plus a require: re-frame.interop added to re-frame.machines.timer's ns requires, and interop/activate-derived-value! called on the sub-vec delay reaction immediately BEFORE the add-watch in schedule-after-timer!, inside the existing try. Ordering verified against observation.cljc:1959-1990 rather than assumed: its rule is ACTIVATE -> watch -> observe, and the load-bearing half (activate strictly before add-watch, so activation's own recompute cannot fan a priming change at the watcher) is preserved exactly. The timer's baseline deref is structurally forced earlier (resolve-delay-ms must return the resolved ms for managed-timer/arm!), and the red run confirms the raw deref reads the correct value with watching nil, so no second call site is needed. schedule-after-timer! is the only watch-attachment point and on-sub-changed! re-enters it, so one insertion covers birth AND every reschedule.

Regression test: implementation/machines/test/re_frame/after_dynamic_delay_reresolve_ratom_cljs_test.cljs. Reagent adapter, REAL subscription node under the watch (host clock stubbed and nothing else — the with-redefs stand-in is what hid this). Two moves of the delay sub, so the fresh reaction the reschedule builds is exercised too, plus a chattiness negative control with a positive control behind it.

RED-then-GREEN proven: reverting the one line reds 8 assertions in the new ns and nothing else in the 12750-test node-test suite (exit 1); restoring it gives 0 failures 0 errors (exit 0).

Gates: npm run test:cljs 12750 tests / 64004 assertions 0F0E exit 0; implementation/machines clojure -M:test 1202 / 4188 0F0E exit 0; scripts/test-fast-pr.sh PASS exit 0 (JVM core 2233/11645, JVM machines 1202/4188, CLJS node 12750/64004, per-ns isolation sweep ok).

title: hicasso: arm1 wire-cell! never activates its Reaction — rf2-8cnxg in a consumer that never got the fix
description:
DIAGNOSED by a read-only pass on rf2-2rtt6.137 (2026-08-07). Verdict (b): a REAL propagation gap in the candidate's own RUNTIME — not the candidate architecture, and not the bench.

THE DEFECT, at implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/runtime.cljs:737-748. wire-cell! is the candidate's entire attachment to the substrate: subscribe, set! the reaction on the cell, a baseline deref, add-watch, add-on-dispose!. It NEVER calls interop/activate-derived-value!.

WHY THAT BREAKS IT. Under the ratom family a subscription IS a bare reagent.ratom/Reaction — spine.cljs:3419-3421 builds it with make-reaction and deliberately NOT :auto-run — and a Reaction learns its sources only through deref-capture. A plain deref outside *ratom-context* runs the body raw and leaves 'watching' nil. So the reaction is never in app-db's watcher set; add-watch never fires; mark-dirty! never fires (runtime.cljs:267-268 states that watch is its ONLY caller); notify! never fires; React is handed nothing to commit. The arm paints once at mount and is deaf thereafter.

THIS IS A REPEAT. The identical defect was diagnosed and repaired in the shipping observation port: observation.cljc:1959-1982 — 'ACTIVATE, then watch, then observe — and the order is the whole fix for rf2-8cnxg ... every ViewCell over a Reagent-hosted subscription rendered ONCE and never again.' arm1's runtime is a second consumer of the same substrate that never received that fix.

THE FIX, one line. In wire-cell!, inside the (when (some? reaction) guard, insert (interop/activate-derived-value! reaction) BEFORE the baseline deref and the add-watch — mirroring observation.cljc's activate -> watch -> observe order. re-frame.interop is already required as 'interop' at runtime.cljs:372. wire-cell! is the single attachment point (called from acquire-cell! at birth and from invalidate-cell!'s rebuild), so one insertion covers both paths. The op is a routed no-op on the React-hook spine, so UIx is untouched.

HYPOTHESIS (a) IS FALSIFIED TWICE. (i) Arithmetic: failures are stale by exactly 3 ticks = every write since mount, not the measured window's one write. A drain fault reads stale-by-1 invariably, because React 19 schedules a microtask that flushes sync work and the driver awaits a separate page.evaluate per window. (ii) Mechanism: flushSync's finally calls Internals.d.f() -> flushSyncWork() unconditionally whatever the callback did, and useSyncExternalStore's forceStoreRerender schedules at SyncLane — so flushSync(r/flush) is a strict SUPERSET of flushSync(nil). The bench's drain choice is correct, and becomes load-bearing once the arm is fixed.

REGRESSION TESTS REQUIRED, both with templates in tree:
- Node, no DOM: install the Reagent adapter, reg-sub one query, perform wire-cell!'s three acts by hand, dispatch-sync a write, (reagent.core/flush), assert the watch fired. Template: observation_port_activates_ratom_node_cljs_test.cljs — whose own docstring says 'even reagent.core/flush moves nothing', i.e. it already names and excludes hypothesis (a).
- DOM counterpart mirroring freehand_cell_under_ratom_adapter_dom_cljs_test.cljs.
Prove the test goes RED without the activation and green with it.

SCOPE LIMIT — no published figure is invalidated. The Hicasso clock bench gives the candidate its own segment that installs the UIx adapter (clock_app.cljs:124-130), every p0-heap row is mount-hold-release with no write, and p0-arms' write-driving bulk arms are floor/reagent/uix only. rf2-2rtt6.76's allocation row is the FIRST time in the P0 programme a write was driven at lad/hicasso with the Reagent adapter installed.

title: Hicasso arm 1 does not re-render on a write under the Reagent adapter (P0 alloc row)
description:
Found by rf2-2rtt6.76's warm-write read-back on the P0 allocation row (docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-survival-metrics-allocation-half.md).

SYMPTOM. On the reagent-subs segment, the lad/hicasso arm does not re-render when :p0/write-all lands. Its DOM text is stale by EXACTLY the number of writes the window drove - 3 of 3, every round, every rung R in 1/3/7/20 - and its allocation column sits flat on ~100 B/boundary, which is the same figure the FLOOR reads (an arm with no subscription that cannot re-render). 16 read-back failures across 4 rounds, all on that one arm. The uix-subs segment's lad/hicasso arm re-renders normally and reads 2,461-3,840 B/boundary.

Read-backs: R1 21 vs 24, R3 72 vs 81, R7 189 vs 210, R20 600 vs 660.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE BENCH. A candidate arm that never re-renders allocates nothing per read, and 'nothing per read' is exactly the flat-at-zero answer HD-002 predicts for the survival metric. Without the read-back gate the row would have published a no-op as a confirmation of the design. Any future allocation or clock figure on that pairing is worthless until this is resolved.

TWO CANDIDATE CAUSES, NOT DIAGNOSED. (a) A bench gap: the reagent segment drains with (react-dom/flushSync (fn [] (r/flush))), which is Reagent's render queue, while the Hicasso arm commits through useSyncExternalStore and may need the empty-flushSync drain the uix segment uses. (b) A real propagation gap: the candidate needs neither adapter's hooks, but every read goes through re-frame.subs and the reaction subscribe builds is the INSTALLED adapter's - the same fact the reads ladder's two candidate columns rest on.

Start at (a); it is cheap to falsify and would explain the exact 'stale by the whole window' signature.
notes:
DIAGNOSED 2026-08-07 09:08 AUSEST. READ-ONLY diagnosis, no file edited, no
benchmark run. VERDICT: (b) A REAL PROPAGATION GAP, in the CANDIDATE's own
runtime — not a bench drain gap. (a) is falsified twice over.

THE CAUSE, NAMED AND ALREADY KNOWN. It is rf2-8cnxg, hit a second time in a
place that never got the fix. `arm1/runtime.cljs` `wire-cell!`
(implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/runtime.cljs:737-748)
attaches a cell to the substrate with exactly three acts:

    (let [reaction (subs/subscribe query-v {:frame frame-kw})]
      (set! (.-reaction cell) reaction)
      @reaction                                   ; baseline deref
      (add-watch reaction cell-watch-key ...)      ; the ONLY dirty channel
      (interop/add-on-dispose! reaction ...))

It never calls `interop/activate-derived-value!`. Under the ratom family the
subscription IS a bare `reagent.ratom/Reaction` — spine.cljs:3419-3421,
`(make-reaction (build-recompute-fn ...))`, deliberately NOT `:auto-run` — and
a Reaction learns its sources only through `deref-capture`. A plain deref taken
outside `*ratom-context*` runs the body raw and leaves `watching` nil, so
`_handle-change` is never called, the reaction is not in app-db's watcher set,
`add-watch` fires never, `mark-dirty!` fires never (runtime.cljs:267-268 states
that the value-change watch is its ONLY caller), `notify!` fires never, and
React is handed no update to commit. The arm paints once at mount and is deaf
from that instant.

This is the same defect the observation port carried and repaired:
observation.cljc:1959-1982 ("ACTIVATE, then watch, then observe — and the order
is the whole fix for rf2-8cnxg / rf2-jt8vz ... every ViewCell over a
Reagent-hosted subscription rendered ONCE and never again"). The regression test
is implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/observation_port_activates_ratom_node_cljs_test.cljs,
whose own docstring says "even `reagent.core/flush` moves nothing" — which is
hypothesis (a)'s drain, named and excluded, in the repo, before this row ran.
Hicasso Arm 1 is a second consumer of the same channel and never received the
call.

WHY (a) IS FALSIFIED — two independent arguments.

1. ARITHMETIC, from this row's own numbers. The published run is
   P0_ALLOC_WRITES=1, P0_ALLOC_WARMUPS=2 (the page's Reproduce block), so an
   arm is mounted, then driven 2 warm-up windows + 1 measured window = THREE
   writes before its read-back. Every failure is stale by exactly 3 ticks
   (R1 21 vs 24 → tick 21 vs 24; R3 72/3=24 vs 81/3=27; R7 27 vs 30; R20 30 vs
   33). That is EVERY WRITE SINCE MOUNT, not "the measured window's write".
   A merely-undrained update cannot produce it: React 19 schedules a microtask
   that flushes sync work (react-dom-client `scheduleImmediateRootScheduleTask`
   → `processRootScheduleInMicrotask`), and the driver awaits a separate
   `page.evaluate` per window, so any update scheduled during a warm-up window
   would have committed before the next one began. A drain fault would read
   stale-by-1, invariably. It reads stale-by-3.

2. MECHANISM, from React 19.2's source. `flushSync`'s `finally` calls
   `Internals.d.f()` → `flushSyncWork$1()` UNCONDITIONALLY, whatever the
   callback did (react-dom.development.js:131-144; the binding is at
   react-dom-client.development.js:27518-27523). `useSyncExternalStore`'s
   `forceStoreRerender` schedules at lane 2 = SyncLane
   (react-dom-client.development.js:8260-8263). So
   `(flushSync (fn [] (r/flush)))` is a strict SUPERSET of `(flushSync (fn []
   nil))`: it flushes the same sync lane AND drains Reagent's queues. The
   bench's per-segment drain choice (p0_run.cjs:1099) is therefore CORRECT and
   becomes load-bearing once the arm is fixed — `reagent.core/flush` →
   `batching/flush-queues` → `(ratom-flush)` is what will recompute an
   activated Reaction, and the empty flushSync would not.

THE FIX, AND WHERE IT BELONGS. One line in the CANDIDATE, not the bench:
`implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/runtime.cljs`,
`wire-cell!` — insert `(interop/activate-derived-value! reaction)` immediately
after the `(when (some? reaction)` guard opens and BEFORE the baseline
`@reaction` and the `add-watch`, mirroring observation.cljc's stated
activate → watch → observe order (activate first so activation's own recompute
cannot fan a priming notification; before the baseline so the baseline reads a
settled node). `re-frame.interop` is already required as `interop` in that ns
(runtime.cljs:372), so nothing else changes. `wire-cell!` is the single
attachment point — it is called from `acquire-cell!` at birth and again from
`invalidate-cell!`'s rebuild — so one insertion covers both. The op is a
documented no-op on the React-hook spine, so the UIx segment is unaffected.
NOTHING IN p0_run.cjs / p0_heap.cljs / p0_arms.cljs (PR #7644) NEEDS TO CHANGE.

WHY IT WAS NEVER CAUGHT. The Hicasso clock bench gives the candidate its own
segment that installs the UIX adapter on purpose (clock_app.cljs:124-130 —
":hicasso installs the UIx adapter, the one Arm 1's shipping spine is closest
to"), and every p0-heap row is mount-hold-release with no write. `p0-arms`'s
bulk (write-driving) arms are floor + reagent + uix only. So rf2-2rtt6.76's
allocation row is the FIRST time in the P0 programme that a write was driven at
`lad/hicasso` with the Reagent adapter installed. No previously published
Hicasso figure is invalidated by this.

WHAT IT COSTS THIS ROW. The four `lad/hicasso` rows in the Reagent-adapter
table (99/100/102/98/103 B/boundary at R=0/1/3/7/20) and the "Hicasso, Reagent
substrate" fit line (0 B/read, r² 0.283) must be STRUCK, not merely refused —
they are a no-op arm, not a noisy measurement.

DOES IT TOUCH THE UIX-SEGMENT FIGURES? Not by this mechanism. The React-hook
spine wires one watch per source at CONSTRUCTION and is push-based from birth
(late_bind/directory.cljc:995), the activate op is a routed no-op there, and
those read-backs all passed. But no uix-segment Hicasso number is publishable
anyway on the row's own terms: r² 0.311, slope −37 B/read, 0 of 4 rounds
linear, and the rungs non-monotone (3,007 / 3,178 / 3,840 / 2,461). The
refusal stands on its own criterion regardless of this bug.

SMALLEST REPRODUCTION (not run — the diagnosis did not need it). Node, no DOM,
no browser: install the Reagent adapter, make a frame, `reg-sub` one query,
call `arm1.runtime/wire-cell!`'s exact three acts by hand (subscribe → deref →
add-watch), `dispatch-sync` a write, `(reagent.core/flush)`, and assert the
watch fired. It fails today and passes with `activate-derived-value!` inserted.
The template already exists —
`re-frame.observation-port-activates-ratom-node-cljs-test` is that test for the
observation port; a hicasso-arm1 sibling under the reagent adapter's test tree
is the same shape. A DOM-level counterpart (mount an Arm 1 root under the
Reagent adapter, dispatch, assert the cell text moved) mirrors
`re-frame.freehand-cell-under-ratom-adapter-dom-cljs-test`.

NEXT: this needs a fix bead on arm1/runtime.cljs plus the two regression tests
above. It is NOT a change to PR #7644.

DISCHARGED by PR #7647, MERGED 2026-08-07. This was the DIAGNOSIS bead; the fix is rf2-2kshh and it is on main.

THE VERDICT IT ESTABLISHED, read-only and without running a benchmark: (b) a real propagation gap in the candidate's own RUNTIME — not the candidate architecture, and not the bench. Hypothesis (a), the drain, was falsified twice: by arithmetic (failures were stale by EVERY write since mount, not by the measured window's one write, and a drain fault reads stale-by-1 invariably) and by mechanism (flushSync's finally calls Internals.d.f() unconditionally whatever the callback did, so flushSync(r/flush) is a strict SUPERSET of flushSync(nil) — the bench's drain choice was correct all along and becomes load-bearing once the arm is fixed).

NO PUBLISHED FIGURE WAS INVALIDATED. The Hicasso clock bench gives the candidate its own segment that installs the UIx adapter, every p0-heap row is mount-hold-release with no write, and p0-arms' write-driving bulk arms are floor/reagent/uix only. rf2-2rtt6.76's allocation row was the FIRST time in the P0 programme a write was driven at lad/hicasso with the Reagent adapter installed — which is why a months-old defect surfaced today.

title: schemas-bundle gate should assert a DELTA against a Malli-free control, not an absolute ceiling
description:
Follow-on from rf2-kybsf's attribution work (measured 2026-08-05). BLOCKED ON rf2-kybsf's budget ruling.

THE STRUCTURAL DEFECT. check-schemas-bundle.cjs asserts an ABSOLUTE gzipped ceiling on two probe bundles. But the quantity Spec 010 Bundle cost actually budgets is a MARGINAL cost -- 'malli.core's reachable body (~24 KB gzipped headline)' plus 're-frame.schemas ~5.6 KB on top of malli.core'. Those are deltas. The probe's absolute size is dominated by things the budget is not about: cljs.core is 186 KB of the 494 KB raw bundle (37.6%), and re-frame.core contributes another ~150 KB raw (router 22.7, cofx 12.6, fx 12.1, classification 9.7, subs 7.8, frame 7.6, elision 7.6 ...).

Consequence: EVERY unrelated framework feature moves this gate's number. Measured proof -- between 2026-05-14 and 2026-08-05 the probe grew 80.1 -> 124.9 KB, of which Malli's marginal cost accounts for 1.0 KB (29.8 -> 30.8) and cljs.core + re-frame.core account for 43.8 KB. The gate fired at the schemas artefact for growth that happened entirely outside it. Whatever absolute constant is ruled will be wrong again within a quarter, for the same reason.

THE FIX. Add a Malli-free control build (the existing probe ns with the facade's adapter require absent, or an equivalent control ns) and assert the DELTA between control and probe against Spec 010's ~30 KB marginal budget. That is immune to core's growth and actually enforces the normative claim, which the current gate never has.

Keep an absolute backstop so core growth is not invisible -- but as a generous ratchet whose job is 'something dragged a heavy transitive ns in', not a precision budget. Core's own size is owned by the perf-bundle and bundle-isolation gates, not this one.

NOT A NARROWING. This widens what is enforced: it adds a build and pins a quantity the gate has never checked. It stops the gate failing on a quantity it was never about.

SEQUENCING. notes: Merged-PR audit follow-up for #7551 (2026-08-05). The implementation correctly replaces `schemas-bundle-probe-malli` with the core-only control and a two-sided margin, but `implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_bundle_probe.cljs` was left byte-for-byte unchanged and its ns/boot docstrings still say: the companion `re-frame.schemas-bundle-probe-malli` exists, the checker asserts equality, a reverted facade require breaks that equality, and the bundle is checked against a `spec envelope`.
