comments.text:
BRIEF AMENDED TO THE RULED DESIGN 2026-08-05 20:00 AUSEST (rf2-kybsf ruling recorded — the blocker this bead was waiting on now exists; dep edge removed, bead is dispatchable). The ruling sharpens the description's fix in three ways; where they differ, THIS comment wins.

1. THE CONTROL IS A CORE-ONLY BUILD, NOT AN ADAPTER-STRIPPED FACADE. Description said "probe ns with the facade's adapter require absent"; ruled instead: a minimal control probe requiring re-frame.core ONLY, because the A/B must price what a consumer actually opts into — re-frame.schemas pulls the Malli adapter statically (schemas.cljc line 21), so the full schemas+adapter surface IS the opt-in cost. The counterfactual adapter-stripped build measures a posture no consumer can buy; it stays an attribution technique, not the gate.
2. REPLACE, DO NOT ADD. schemas-bundle-probe-malli is byte-identical to its sibling (5-12 B across runs; both require the same graph, the explicit adapter require is redundant). Replace it with schemas-bundle-control (init-fn touches minimal core surface; identical :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false + browser target). Two builds total, ~47s unchanged. Update the npm script, shadow-cljs.edn build entries (HOT-ZONE file — flag for mayor sequencing), the BUNDLES array, and delete probe_malli's ns.
3. ASSERT THE DELTA TWO-SIDED, NUMBERS FROM THE FIRST MATCHED RUN. (schemas-probe minus control) <= ceiling AND >= floor. Ceiling = Spec 010's marginal budget, set from the first matched A/B run + stated headroom (measured vicinity: 30.8 KB marginal; do NOT inherit 100/125 or any prior constant). Floor (~15-20 KB region, set from the same run) restores rf2-fqbcy's original strictly-larger methodology guard: a reverted facade require collapses the delta to ~5.6 KB and trips it — the in-gate structural echo of schema-implies-validation AND the gate's non-vacuity guard. title: test:schemas-bundle is RED: schemas probe bundle is 124.9 KB gzipped against a normative 100 KB ceiling
description:
Found by rf2-a9oic while giving the three orphaned verdict gates homes (PR for
rf2-a9oic / rf2-k78o2). The bead's filer warned: run each gate green locally
first, or you file an issue on alerting's first night. Two ran green. This one
did not.

MEASURED, cold, on origin/main (c17e9437e3), Windows, node 24, malli 0.20.1:

  [FAIL] schemas-bundle-probe        124.9 KB gzipped (127927 bytes)
  [FAIL] schemas-bundle-probe-malli  124.9 KB gzipped (127939 bytes)
         threshold: 100.0 KB (102400 bytes) -- over by 24.9 KB
  [OK]   schema-implies-validation guard: |delta| 12 bytes (<= 2 KB)

So the STRUCTURAL claim still holds -- both probes carry Malli, the facade
still auto-wires the adapter, schema still implies validation. What has
regressed is the ABSOLUTE budget, by 25%.

WHY NOBODY KNEW. test:schemas-bundle runs nowhere. check-schemas-bundle.cjs is
referenced by that npm script and by nothing else in the repo, so the gate has
never executed in CI since it was authored. That is precisely the class
rf2-6ckzl's audit was built to surface, and this is the audit's first real
catch rather than a bookkeeping one.

THE CLAIM THAT IS NOW FALSE, IN TWO PLACES.

  spec/010-Schemas.md 'Bundle cost' catalogues the row
    '[re-frame.schemas] required => Malli wired | ~91 KB'
  and states 'the current schemas-bundle-probe measures ~91 KB gzipped,
  within the <= 100 KB gate ceiling'.

  implementation/scripts/check-schemas-bundle.cjs repeats it:
    gzippedMaxBytes: 100 * 1024,   // 100 KB (empirical ~91 KB + ~9 KB headroom)

The real figure is 124.9 KB. The spec's normative budget table and the gate's
threshold comment are both stating a measurement that no longer holds.

LIKELY PROVENANCE (dates from git log, not asserted as cause):
  2026-05-12  2252f1f379  metosin/malli 0.13.0 -> 0.20.1 (rf2-zyiy, PR #468)
  2026-05-14  ce6c0f4784  the bundle-cost gate is authored (rf2-fqbcy)

Bundle composition of out/schemas-bundle-probe/probe.js (499280 raw / 127927
gz): malli.core PRESENT, malli.error PRESENT, and malli.transform /
malli.generator / malli.registry / malli.util / clojure.test.check all ABSENT.
malli.error is on Spec 010's own 'restrict to dev/test' list at ~6 KB, so it is
worth asking whether the facade is dragging the humanise path into production
-- but 6 KB does not explain 34 KB, so that is a lead, not the answer.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT. It is not 'bump the threshold'. The checker's own
failure text says it: 'if the new figures reflect a deliberate substrate
change, update the spec section first, then bump the thresholds here in
lockstep.' Spec 010's budget table is normative, so the order is a spec ruling
first and a threshold second. rf2-a9oic deliberately did NOT touch either --
narrowing a gate to make it pass is the one thing that audit exists to
prevent.

REMEDY, in order:
  1. Attribute the 34 KB. Compare against the 0.13.0 pin and against a build
     with the facade's adapter require removed, to split 'malli grew' from
     'the facade pulls more'. Decide whether malli.error belongs on the

  2. Mike rules on the budget: is ~125 KB the accepted cost of

  3. Update spec/010-Schemas.md 'Bundle cost' -- the table row and the

  4. Bump gzippedMaxBytes in implementation/scripts/check-schemas-bundle.cjs

Until step 5, scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py keeps test:schemas-bundle

title: tools/template's SSR scaffold declared its :root-view in the UNRESOLVED form — server and client hashed different trees
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-q1b96 (PR #7520), WHICH IS CORRECT AND STAYS. That change made ssr-ring omit the render hash for the unresolved root form (a callable-headed vector), because its canonical EDN is a constant. Three tools/template SSR tests went red on unrelated branches, asserting data-rf-render-hash is present.

THE TESTS WERE RIGHT. The template is a Reagent host — HICCUP tier — and Spec 011's hash channel is exactly its. What was wrong is the scaffold's own :root-view spelling:

  server (core_with_ssr.cljc)  (defn root-view [] [(rf/view :app/root)])   ;; reference
  client (:render-tree-fn)     (fn [] ((rf/view :app/root)))               ;; resolved tree

Those two ends can never hash the same thing. MEASURED in the emitted project: the client tree hashes a2aa3d1d, the server's unresolved root hashes f1d63f7e — the exact per-arity constant render_hash_tier_test.clj pins for [(rf/view :anything)]. So BEFORE rf2-q1b96 the emitted SSR scaffold shipped a hash that mismatched on EVERY page; after it, the hash is simply absent. Both are wrong for a hiccup-tier host.

This is the SECOND, SEPARABLE HAZARD rf2-q1b96's description flagged 'VERIFY BEFORE FIXING' and its close note recorded as unknown ('whether the :root-view [#'app/root] vector reportedly making the server hash shallow while the client hashes deep reproduced'). IT REPRODUCES — tools/template is the concrete instance. Recording that here so the unknown is closed.

FIX (fenced to tools/template/**): root-view gains the outer call, ((rf/view :app/root)) — the spelling resolve-root-view's own docstring names as the hiccup tier's way to keep the channel. Byte-identical HTML; the hash returns and now equals the client's. Plus one added assertion in the emitted ssr_test.clj pinning the pairing itself: (= render-hash (rf/render-tree-hash (app/root-view))). No assertion deleted, no hash re-added to ssr-ring.

MUTATION-PROVEN: with the old form the new assertion reads (not (= "a2aa3d1d" "f1d63f7e")) and the three original failures reproduce; with the fix, both SSR emitted cells are 0 failures / 0 errors.
close_reason:
CLOSED — the fix is on main as f8e2de3025 "fix(template): the SSR scaffold's :root-view resolves, so it keeps a render hash", merged as PR #7540. Verified by reading origin/main, not inferred from the PR state.

WHAT IT ESTABLISHED, and it is the more useful half: the template's root IS hiccup-tier and SHOULD carry a hash. It was merely spelled the one way that structurally cannot have one - server (defn root-view [] [(rf/view :app/root)]), a REFERENCE; client ((rf/view :app/root)), the TREE. Measured in the emitted project: client a2aa3d1d, server f1d63f7e - the exact per-arity constant render_hash_tier_test.clj pins for [(rf/view :anything)].

SO THE TEMPLATE WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: before rf2-q1b96 it shipped a hash that MISMATCHED ON EVERY PAGE; after, the hash was simply absent. rf2-q1b96 is vindicated - it did not over-remove, and its fix stands untouched.

TWO THINGS WORTH CARRYING FORWARD:

1. THIS CLOSED AN UNKNOWN I HAD RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. rf2-q1b96's close said "whether the SECOND, separable hazard reproduced... WHOEVER TOUCHES pipeline.clj NEXT SHOULD RE-CHECK IT rather than assume it was handled." The very next worker in that area found it reproduces, and tools/template was the live instance. Recording an unknown as unknown is what made that possible.

2. A FAIL-OPEN IN THE VERIFYING LANE: plain `clojure -M:test` in tools/template SKIPS the failing rows - they sit behind RF2_TEMPLATE_RUN_EMITTED_TESTS=1, and the fixing worker's first run came back GREEN with the bug live. Anyone verifying that lane locally must set the env var or they get a false green. Also note the job is SURFACE-GATED and never ran on main at all, which is why main showed green while the artefact was broken.

THE NEW ASSERTION IS BETTER THAN THE ONES IT JOINS: the old rows could only say "a hash is present"; the added row asserts (= render-hash (rf/render-tree-hash (app/root-view))) - the RIGHT hash, which is the property that was silently false.

title: Xray nightly gate: 'static mode chrome and chord' flakes ~29% of nights (5s locator timeout)
description:
Found while costing rf2-rliq7 (2026-08-05 16:40 AUSEST).

The nightly full Xray feature matrix (expensive-tests.yml, 'Gate - Xray
feature matrix') has failed 4 of the last 14 nights, ALWAYS on the same
scenario and ALWAYS with the same signature:

  FAIL static mode chrome and chord: locator.waitFor: Timeout 5000ms exceeded.

Runs: 2026-07-22 (29935235079), 07-24 (30106705162), 07-27 (30282895276),
07-31 (30645068521). Green on 07-23/25/26/28/29/30 and 08-01..08-04, and
green in a local full sweep on 2026-08-05. So it is INTERMITTENT, not a
standing red - roughly a 29% per-night failure rate, unfixed for two
weeks.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE FLAKE. 'static mode chrome and chord' is a
NON-SMOKE scenario, so it never runs at PR time; the nightly is its only
executor. A system of record that reds ~1 night in 3 for a known flake
cannot be used to distinguish a NEW regression from the usual noise -
which is precisely the fail-open shape this project has been clearing
out. rf2-rliq7's option (1) (WONTFIX, 'the nightly sweep is the system of
record') is only honest once this is green, and its option (3) (arm the
full sweep at PR time) is actively DANGEROUS while it stands: it would
red ~1 in 3 PRs touching scenarios.cjs for an unrelated known flake.

So this is on the critical path of the rf2-rliq7 ruling and should be
fixed before that policy call is taken.

SCENARIO: tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs, the scenario
named 'static mode chrome and chord' (runStaticModeChromeAndChord). The
5000ms figure is a locator budget inside the scenario, well under the
gate's own 45s XRAY_FEATURE_GATE_TIMEOUT_MS ceiling - the same class
rf2-taj9b fixed for the one bare navigation in that file. History note:
this same scenario was RED for real once before (rf2-wxu4l3, fixed in
9bc9e6c9a2 2026-06-10) for a genuine ':rf.error/no-frame-context' crash
in the Static Machines browse-list, so a timeout here is not
automatically 'just a flake' - confirm which.
close_reason:
PR #7535. NOT a short timeout and NOT runner slowness — a TOCTOU double-toggle in the scenario harness's openXray helper, reproduced under control.

MECHANISM (from the 2026-07-31 nightly, run 30645068521, plus source): Ctrl+Shift+C is a TOGGLE (mount/toggle!), and Xray's preload runs a second concurrent opener — mount/auto-open-inline! polls every 50ms until rf/init! has installed the substrate adapter, then calls open!. openXray sampled shell PRESENCE once (count()) and pressed the chord on a 0. When auto-open landed in the gap between that sample and the keydown, the chord arrived at an already-open shell, toggle! took its close! branch, and close! hid the container while leaving the React tree mounted. expectVisible then burned its full 5000ms on a shell the helper had hidden itself. CI evidence is decisive: '15 x locator resolved to hidden <div ... data-testid="rf-xray-shell" data-rf-xray-mode="inline">' with diagnostics reading 'mounted=true visible=none', epochCount=1, and ZERO pageerrors. Raising the timeout could never have gone green — nothing was going to un-hide it.

SECOND DEFECT, one line apart: count() asks 'is it in the DOM', but close! keeps the node, so presence never meant open. The failure state is itself one the old code would misread as 'already open', skip the chord for, and then fail the visible-wait on.

REPRODUCED: a scratchpad A/B forced the interleaving deterministically (early presence sample, then a widened gap so auto-open lands inside it). OLD 6/11 failures, byte-identical signature (resolvedToHidden=true, final mounted=true/display=none); NEW 0/11. Perfect correlation — every OLD failure had sample=0, every OLD pass sample=1.

WHY ONLY THIS SCENARIO, of ~14 calling openXray: it is the SOLE navigate/reload site in the 3991-line file. On the harness's cold page.goto the adapter is installed long before 'load' resolves, so auto-open always wins the peek; on a warm reload the two converge and the race opens. The nightly record matches: ~180 cold-path openXray calls over 14 nights with zero failures, 14 warm-path calls with four.

FIX: one ordering guarantee, not a longer wait. Settle on presence first (mount-state is a monotone latch — once mounted, auto-open's tick short-circuits forever), then decide on VISIBILITY, the same condition the assertion uses. Settle budget = auto-open's own retry bound (120x50ms), the point at which it has provably stopped. No duration raised; the 5000 assertion is untouched. No assertion weakened, no retry added, chord still fires at most once. 53 insertions / 2 deletions in one file.

RULED OUT with evidence: runner slowness (element present+hidden for all 15 polls); chord-handler registration race (keybinding/attach! runs synchronously at preload, before auto-open; the keydown was plainly received — that is what hid the shell); transient selector match (one stable element for 5s); product ordering bug (zero pageerrors, clean boot); and the historic rf2-wxu4l3 :rf.error/no-frame-context crash (that one threw; this does not).

GATES: fast-PR spine PASS(0); tools/xray clojure -M:test 1271 tests / 5909 assertions, 0 failures(0); xray-feature-gate:smoke 5 scenarios 0 failures(0); eslint clean(0); FULL xray-feature-gate run 6x (5 pre-rebase + 1 post-rebase), 17 scenarios each, 0 failures every run = 102 scenario executions, 0 failures.

NOTE FOR rf2-rliq7: this unblocks the policy call — the nightly's known flake is now mechanised and fixed, so a red nightly can again be read as a real regression.

NOTE ON THE TWO WEEKS: the gate's diagnostics were ALREADY sufficient to diagnose this from the first failure on 2026-07-22 (mounted=true visible=none + 'resolved to hidden' is the whole answer). No instrumentation was missing and none was added. What was missing was anyone being told — the expensive-tests.yml alerting gap, rf2-6sg25.

title: RED ON MAIN: cljs-browser aborts — PR #7522 merged before its worker's fixture fix; PR #7531 is the repair
description:

is the whole fix.

main, not just on the worker branch.

compile gate and the fast-PR spine were all green at 49acc9a704. #7531 also
carries three small review-pass commits that were in the same push (a
vacuity fix in the carry-refusal id comparison, W4's premise asserted
rather than described, and the design record marking W7 unbuilt).

PROCESS NOTE for the merge loop, not a complaint: a PR whose worker has not
yet reported is not necessarily at its final commit. The green that was
merged was CI's read of an intermediate commit.

Close when #7531 is merged.
close_reason:
CLOSED — MAIN IS REPAIRED (mayor, 2026-08-05). Verified rather than assumed.

THE FIX IS ON MAIN: 863b3d428b "fix(hicasso): the h/frame DOM suite needs the map-shape fixture", merged as PR #7531, reachable from origin/main.

THE CAUSE WAS MINE. I merged PR #7522 on green while its worker was still running gates. Four of its commits had not travelled, and one carried the map-shape fixture. Main was left with an async test under a fn-form fixture, which cljs.test refuses - "Async tests require fixtures to be specified as maps. Testing aborted." - taking the WHOLE browser run at that namespace, so every namespace after it went unrun and the required cljs-browser job failed.

THE BLAST RADIUS, recorded because it is the real cost: two other PRs went red on the identical abort, neither at fault. Worse, I told one of them main was green - citing three runs that PREDATED my own merge - and it spent over an hour hunting a hang in its own test that did not exist. It eventually ran the decisive control I never did: PURE origin/main with none of its commits, exit 1, identical abort. Both PRs cleared the moment their branches were rebased onto the repaired main.

TWO DIAGNOSTIC ERRORS OF MINE WORTH KEEPING, because each cost a cycle:
1. "main is green" IS A CLAIM WITH A TIMESTAMP. I quoted three green runs without checking whether my own merge had invalidated them.
2. gh run rerun RE-RUNS THE SAME RUN ID, so createdAt never moves. I read the unchanged timestamp as evidence the re-run had not happened; it had, and could not help, because the BRANCH lacked the fix. The discriminator is git branch -r --contains <fix> - a stale red re-runs clean, a stale BASE needs a rebase.

THE GENERAL RULE THIS EARNS: green is a property of a TIP, not of a worker's intent. A worker that is still committing has commits that have not travelled, and merging its current tip merges unfinished work. Merging promptly remains right - it has caught far more than it cost today - but not while a worker is demonstrably mid-flight.

title: test:perf-bundle is wired to nothing -- Spec 009 names it as the perf-elision CI gate and no workflow runs it
description:
# `npm run test:perf-bundle` — the gate Spec 009 names as its perf-elision enforcement — is wired to NOTHING

FOUND while delivering rf2-2rtt6.125 (Spec 009 `:render` for Hicasso `defview`), looking for the gate that would catch a perf bracket surviving DCE.

## The claim, and the fact

Spec 009 §Production-elision verification (the one inside §Performance instrumentation) says:

> "The bundle-isolation contract is enforced in CI by `npm run test:perf-bundle` (the dual of `npm run test:elision`)."

It is not. `git grep` over `.github/`, `scripts/` and `TESTING.md` finds **zero** invocations of `test:perf-bundle`, `check-perf-bundle`, or the `:examples/counter-perf` build:

- `implementation/package.json` line 58 defines `"test:perf-bundle": "shadow-cljs release examples/counter examples/counter-perf && node scripts/check-perf-bundle.cjs"`.
- `implementation/scripts/check-perf-bundle.cjs` exists (8,736 bytes, executable).
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` declares `:examples/counter-perf` (line ~1629) with `:closure-defines {re-frame.performance/enabled? true}`.
- **No workflow runs any of it.** `.github/workflows/*` has no match. `TESTING.md` has no row. `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` mentions "perf-bundle" only in a comment listing gates the spine does NOT run — so `check_fast_pr_gap.py` cannot surface it either, because the gap script derives from the workflows, and the workflows do not contain it.

Its stated dual, `npm run test:elision`, **is** wired (`cljs-elision`: "CLJS production elision (Spec 009, bead rf2-11hn)", green on every PR). The asymmetry is the whole finding.

## Why this matters more than an unwired script usually would

The perf channel's entire safety argument is compile-time: `mark-and-measure` expands to `(if enabled? <bracket> (do body))` and Closure is trusted to fold and DCE it. The dual-bundle grep is what makes that trust checkable, and Spec 009 explains at length why it must be a DUAL:

> "Without the on bundle the off-bundle assertion would be vacuous — a refactor that MOVED the strings out of the gated branch would silently turn the negative grep into a false pass."

So the repo reasoned carefully about how the gate could go fail-open, built the non-vacuous version — and then never ran it. **A gate nobody has watched fire is not evidence.** As of rf2-2rtt6.125 there are now five `:render`/`:event`/`:sub`/`:fx` bracket call sites relying on it, one of them newly added.

## Remedy

1. Add a `cljs-perf-bundle` job to `.github/workflows/test.yml` beside `cljs-elision`, running `cd implementation && npm run test:perf-bundle`. **HOT-ZONE** (`.github/workflows/*`) — sequence it, do not parallel it with another workflow edit.
2. Add the matching row to `TESTING.md` so the catalogue and the workflow agree.
3. Run it once by hand first and record the result on this bead. If it is RED today, that is the more urgent half of this bead and the fix belongs before the wiring — a newly-wired red gate blocks every open PR.
4. Consider whether `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py --list` should also flag npm scripts that exist but appear in no workflow; that is what would have caught this class automatically. Separate bead if wanted.

## Not blocked on

rf2-2rtt6.125 (PR #7524). That PR's `:render` bracket uses the identical macro with a compile-time-constant id, and its own witnesses assert the off-path at `:node-test` optimization; but neither it nor any other perf call site has an `:advanced` bundle grep actually running anywhere.
notes:
RUN BY HAND 2026-08-05 (rf2-2rtt6.125's worker, clause 3 of the remedy). THE GATE PASSES TODAY, so wiring it is safe and will not red every open PR:

    cd implementation && npm run test:perf-bundle
    [:examples/counter]      Build completed. (147 files, 92 compiled, 0 warnings, 28.50s)
    [:examples/counter-perf] Build completed. (147 files, 92 compiled, 0 warnings, 11.55s)
    PASS perf-bundle: off-count=0; on-count=8;
      off=out/examples/counter      (627300 chars)
      on =out/examples/counter-perf (628089 chars)
    exit 0

So this bead is purely 'unwired', not 'red'. Clause 3 is discharged; clauses 1, 2 and (optionally) 4 remain.

SEPARATELY, the same dual-bundle methodology was run by hand against a HICASSO arm (:hicasso-bench :advanced release of jsfb-hicasso-app, cache cleared either side per rf2-2rtt6.20), because rf2-2rtt6.125 added a fifth bracket call site in that tree:

  OFF bundle (651632 bytes): performance.measure 0, clearMeasures 0, "rf: 0, performance.mark 0
  ON  bundle (652430 bytes): performance.measure 4, clearMeasures 4, "rf: 1, performance.mark 0

798 bytes is the entire cost of the perf channel with the flag on, and zero with it off. Non-vacuous in both directions. That run is also unwired anywhere -- if clause 1 lands, consider whether the arm deserves a row too, or whether the counter's coverage of the shared macro is enough (probably it is; the macro is the thing being trusted).
DELIVERED 2026-08-05 — PR #7530 (worker/perfgate-eegpw).

OUTCOME: wire it per-PR. Remedy clauses 1 and 2 done; clause 4 filed as rf2-6ckzl.

MEASURED (cold, fresh worktree, empty .shadow-cljs):
  [:examples/counter]      29.99s   [:examples/counter-perf] 13.64s
  PASS perf-bundle: off-count=0; on-count=8 -- 75s wall clock end to end, exit 0.
  46s warm. Per-PR territory, so a PR job, not nightly. Confirms the filer's by-hand run.

NOT REDUNDANT WITH test:elision -- checked, not assumed. Different goog-define
(re-frame.performance/enabled? vs goog.DEBUG), different entry (counter.core/run vs
re-frame.elision-probe/run), disjoint sentinels: grep -c 'performance.measure|clearMeasures'
over check-elision.cjs returns 0. :elision-probe is built goog.DEBUG=false with the perf flag
at default, so the perf brackets elide there too -- but nothing asserts it and there is no
perf-ON control, so test:elision cannot make the claim even accidentally.

WIRED AS: new cljs-perf-bundle job in test.yml immediately after cljs-elision, gated on the
SAME cljs_prod output as its dual, added to all-required-passed needs: (a job absent from that
list is advisory whatever its own gate says). A job, NOT a step inside cljs-elision -- the two
prove different claims from disjoint sentinel sets and one job would make one failure
indistinguishable from the other in the checks UI. test:elision untouched.
Step list mirrors cljs-freehand-evidence-elision: JDK 21 + Node 24 + Maven cache, no Playwright
and NO Clojure CLI (shadow-cljs.edn resolves through :dependencies, not :deps), sharing that
job's runner.os-cljs- cache key rather than minting a fourth ~/.m2 entry.

NOT added to expensive-tests.yml: _rigorous-local-inventory.test.cjs asserts lockstep between
that workflow's browser-bundle-and-story-gates job and scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh, so a step
there obliges an edit outside this bead's fence. Deliberate. Same reasoning left release.yml
alone. Both worth a follow-up if the nightly superset is wanted.

PROOF IT CAN FAIL (both arms broken, watched red, restored; build cache cleared each run):
  A. mark-and-measure CLJS expansion (if enabled? ...) -> (if true ...) -- the exact regression
     the gate exists to catch. All three sentinels FAIL as PRESENT in the off bundle,
     off-count 0 -> 8, exit 1. The off bundle also grew 627300 -> 628089 chars, byte-identical
     to the on bundle: the signature of a flag that no longer discriminates.
  B. build-name prefix "rf:" -> "xx:" -- the 'a refactor MOVED the strings' scenario Spec 009
     names as why the dual must exist. Off arm all OK; perf-ON control FAILs on the missing
     sentinel; exit 1. So the non-vacuity control has teeth too.
  Restored: git status clean, PASS off-count=0 on-count=8, exit 0.

SPEC 009 NEEDS NO CHANGE. Its sentence ('enforced in CI by npm run test:perf-bundle') is now
true as written. No spec/** file touched.

GAP MAP STAYS DERIVED: check_fast_pr_gap.py derives the required set from each aggregator's
needs: and reads each reproduce command from the step's own run: body, so adding the job to
needs: is the whole maintenance. --check now reports 76 required jobs (was 75) and stays clean;
--list names cljs-perf-bundle with 'cd implementation && npm run test:perf-bundle'. No edit to
the script, none to the spine (whose one-invocation-per-line shape is untouched).

GATES: perf-bundle cold 0; test:elision 0 (dual verified not weakened); test-fast-pr.sh 0
('PASS fast PR spine', 1927s); check_fast_pr_gap.py --self-test 0; --check 0;
check_ci_reproduce_commands.py 0; check_jvm_lane_rosters.py 0; mutation A 1; mutation B 1;
perf-bundle after restore 0.
close_reason: Wired: cljs-perf-bundle job in test.yml gated on cljs_prod, required via all-required-passed, plus the TESTING.md row. PR #7530. Both arms proven able to red. Spec 009 wording needs no change. Follow-up rf2-6ckzl.

title: mayor-hygiene.md still reaps on PR state — the exact proxy rf2-k3j2w retired
description:
FOUND by the rf2-k3j2w worker, 2026-08-05, while fixing the script side.

rf2-k3j2w corrected the METHOD docs (docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md and
README.md) so they no longer recommend proxies that have failed. But the file
the mayor loop ACTUALLY EXECUTES was out of that worker's fence and still
carries the original defect, verbatim:

  .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md, line 4:
    "For each worker worktree: verify its PR via `gh pr view <#> --json state`
     — only if state==MERGED, prune it."

That is precisely the first of the six failed proxies. A merged PR is the
worker's last REPORTED act, not its last act; it may still be running gates.
Six times in one session reaping on this and its successors destroyed a live
worker's gate run, twice producing a red that named real, present files as
missing and was mistaken for a genuine regression.

WHAT THE COMMAND BODY SHOULD SAY INSTEAD (the ruling already recorded on
rf2-k3j2w and now in docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md):

  Do not reap a worktree until its owning agent has delivered a completion
  report. Not on merge, not on cleanliness, not on quiet. The two signals that
  have never been wrong are reads rather than inferences — the agent's own
  completion report, and SendMessage's response shape ("queued for delivery"
  means alive; "had no active task, resumed from transcript" means idle).
  The cost of waiting is a stale directory; the cost of being wrong is a
  destroyed gate run and a false red.

  And: ONE WORKER IS NOT ONE WORKTREE. A worker may create a second worktree
  for its gate run. An unfamiliar worktree belongs to someone until its agent
  reports — do not reap it as an unowned stray.

SECOND, SMALLER ITEM IN THE SAME FILE. mayor-hygiene.md documents how to read
remove-worker-worktree's output (DISARMED=, NO_LINKS=, CANARY_BEFORE/AFTER)
but predates the new outcome added by rf2-k3j2w (PR #7511):

  REMOVE_PARTIAL=<path>, exit 3 — the worktree is already GUTTED (git
  deregistered it and deleted its .git, then hit a file lock on the
  directory). Retrying is futile and `git worktree prune` will not clear it;
  only an ordinary directory delete remains. Exit 1 now means the worktree is
  INTACT and the script is still the right tool; exit 3 means it is not.

  A partial removal kills a running gate exactly as a complete one does, so
  REMOVE_PARTIAL must never be read as "nothing happened".

SCOPE: .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md, and mayor-merge.md if it also reaps
on merge. Docs-only; no code. Note that a script CANNOT check agent liveness —
this is caller discipline by construction, which is exactly why it has to be
written where the caller reads it.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7514 (branch worker/hygienecmd-40d9d). .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md's 'verify its PR via gh pr view --json state - only if state==MERGED, prune it' is replaced with the rf2-k3j2w ruling: reap a worktree only once its owning agent has delivered a completion report; the only reliable signals are the report itself and SendMessage's response shape; one worker is not one worktree. Branch rule left verbatim (merge state IS the right test for a branch) with an explicit sentence naming the branch/worktree conflation as the original error. REMOVE_PARTIAL= / exit 3 added as the fourth removal outcome, with 'exit 1 means intact and this script is still the right tool; exit 3 means it is not'. Frontmatter description carried the same defect and was corrected. Siblings checked: mayor-merge.md has only the (correct) branch rule and never mentions worktrees; mayor-dispatch.md mentions worktrees for creation and load-counting only; mayor-posture.md and mayor-cluster.md carry no reaping rule. +11/-4 on one file.

title: nine bench drivers are FAIL-OPEN on pageerror — confirmed live; wire the refusal to the exit code
description:
CONFIRMED LIVE by rf2-jvheq's audit (PR #7494, 2026-08-04). The audit asked
whether the nine drivers' `pageerror` path is reachable without the sentinel.
It is — settled by RUNNING it, not by reading — so the conditional remedy the
audit bead named is now unconditional. This bead carries it.

THE NINE, each a bare handler that prints and records nothing:

  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b6_prod_run.cjs      ~90
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b6_profile_run.cjs   ~96
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b7_run.cjs           ~190
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b8_run.cjs           ~185
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b10_prod_run.cjs     ~123
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/reads_ladder_run.cjs ~200
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/spine_ablation_run.cjs ~222
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs                        ~383
  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso_narrow_run.cjs ~317

THE EVIDENCE, all measured against this repo's own pins rather than argued:

  1. Playwright 1.59.1 raises `pageerror` for a throw inside
     `requestAnimationFrame`, a throw inside `setTimeout`, AND an unhandled
     promise rejection — while a completion sentinel set elsewhere STILL
     becomes true. All three exit 0 today.

  2. THE ONE THAT MATTERS, because it defeats every page-side try/catch:
     React 19.2.0 does NOT rethrow an uncaught render error to the caller of
     `flushSync`/`render`. `defaultOnUncaughtError` hands it to
     `reportGlobalError` -> `reportError` (react-dom-client.production.js
     ~5888-5890, ~2307). Measured live: `pageerror` fires, THE SURROUNDING
     CATCH NEVER RUNS, no `window.*_ERROR` is set, the `page.evaluate` does
     not reject, and the app carries on and sets its sentinel. Every one of
     the nine mounts through `react-dom/flushSync`. Adding `catch :default`
     to the apps would NOT close this — only wiring `pageerror` to the exit
     code closes it.

  3. b10_prod_run.cjs has a SECOND, non-React path and is the worst of the
     nine: b10_two_clock.cljs ~670/694/709 drives the run from two
     `setInterval`s and a live `MutationObserver`. A throw in any of those is
     a detached task that escapes both `-main`'s try and the promise chain's
     `.catch`, and `setInterval` keeps firing after a throwing callback — so
     the run COMPLETES, sets `B10_DONE`, and publishes a mangled M3 record.

WHY THE AUDIT PR DID NOT SHIP THE FIX. Each of the nine needs an `:advanced`
release build and a headless Chromium to make its refusal fire, and a gate
nobody has watched fire is not a gate. Nine unproven exit wirings would be
the same fault in reverse. The finding is recorded in `sentinel.cjs` (the
file that already states the policy) so the next reader does not re-derive
it.

THE REMEDY, which the audit bead was explicit about: collect into an array
and refuse, matching the six neighbours that already do
(`coldmount_run.cjs` ~193, `p0_converge_run.cjs` ~236, `ime_run.cjs`,
`chrome_run.cjs`, `adoption_witness_run.cjs`, and now `hd8_run.cjs`).
DO NOT remove a handler and DO NOT relax a sentinel.

SCOPE NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: none of the nine is invoked by CI or by an
npm script — they are operator-run measurement drivers — so the blast radius
of a new refusal is an operator investigating, not a red lane. That is what
makes this safe to do properly rather than urgently. Budget for the builds:
each driver must be watched refusing on a page that actually threw, and
watched still exiting 0 on a clean run. Consider splitting across two or
three workers by tree (freehand / core / adapters), since the nine share no
file.
notes:
WIRED IN PR #7505 (rf2-sib23 worker, 2026-08-05). ALL NINE ARE WIRED. FIVE WERE
WATCHED REFUSING. FOUR WERE NOT — THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN, and the split is the
deliverable rather than nine green wirings.

WHAT SHIPPED. Each bare handler is REPLACED by sentinel.cjs's watchPage — the
lane's one collector, which the six neighbours this bead names already use.
Nothing was removed: it still prints the same error, additionally records it,
and additionally sees `crash` and a failed document/script request, which a
bare handler never could. Every driver then reads watch.failures at its exit.
NO NEW EXIT CODE ANYWHERE: the refusal takes each driver's existing 1, so a run
that exited 2, 3, 4 or 5 before exits the same code now.

  b6_prod / b6_profile / b10_prod   inline exit block -> one pure exported
                                    `verdict` behind require.main (rf2-y7mw7's
                                    lift-it-to-make-it-observable shape)
  b8 / hicasso_narrow               the existing pure `verdict` gains it
  b7 / p0                           the existing failure slot / list gains it
  reads_ladder / spine_ablation     a refusal ahead of the enumerated gates

THE PROOF, against this repo's pins (Playwright 1.59.1, react-dom 19.2.0):

  PROVEN END TO END, driver's own process, both directions — b6_profile_run.cjs.
  `--no-build` plus a stub in out/b6-profile that sets B6_READY, completes, and
  throws from a detached task AFTER the sentinel is set. Clean stub exit 0; the
  same stub plus one throwing line exit 1, naming the error.

  PROVEN AT THE DECISION, live — b6_prod, b10_prod, b8, hicasso_narrow. A real
  Chromium throwing inside rAF, inside setTimeout and via an unhandled
  rejection; the real watchPage recorded all three WHILE THE SENTINEL STILL
  FLIPPED; each driver's real exported `verdict` fed exactly that array
  returned 1, and 0 on the clean page.

  NOT PROVEN — b7, reads_ladder, spine_ablation, p0. No pure exported decision
  (enumerated inline exit blocks) and no --no-build knob, so the refusal is
  reachable neither from a unit test nor end-to-end without an :advanced build;
  and their page APIs (window.B7H, the ladder/ablation plans, p0's four rows at
  one page per clock round) are too large to stub faithfully. TRACKED AS
  rf2-va5nm (P2) with the two honest ways to close it.

A FALSE GREEN ON THE WAY, worth recording because it is the exact shape this
whole class wears: the FIRST throwing stub also exited 0 — correctly. The stub
finished in milliseconds, so neither the rAF callback nor the timer ever ran
and the page genuinely never threw. The pair above uses a stub whose B6_RUN
returns a promise settling after 150ms. A refusal that did not fire is as worth
chasing as one that fired wrongly.

THE GATE THAT OBJECTED, and it was right. heap_control_exit_path.test.cjs's
"the control gate is APPENDED as 5, shifting no existing code" fingerprinted
EVERY process.exit in reads_ladder's drive() as the literal [1,3,4,2,5,1], so
any new refusal anywhere in that function reddened it — INCLUDING ONE THAT
SHIFTS NOTHING, which is what its own title says it guards. Told the policy
about the shape rather than narrowing it: it now asserts the ENUMERATED codes
and their order ([3,4,2,5], control last), plus a new sibling pinning that the
page-error refusal took no number of its own.

NEW PIN: pageerror_exit_path.test.cjs (48 checks, in test:script-helpers) —
each pure verdict in both directions, the handler-to-exit wiring in all nine,
and the CLASS derived by walking the four bench trees rather than listed, since
both beads' rosters were wrong in opposite directions. It deliberately does NOT
demand watchPage: the seven hicasso drivers that collect into a local array and
refuse are sound.

ALSO FILED: rf2-qv761 (P3) — the nine still burn a full 15/20-minute sentinel
budget when the page dies BEFORE its sentinel. Their waits were deliberately
NOT converted to watch.race: that is rf2-f5roa's separate remedy and a change
to when a FAILING run reports, while the fault here is the page that throws and
STILL reaches its sentinel.

No measurement, arm, threshold or dataset touched. CI green on #7505.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #7505 (2026-08-05) — UPDATED, NOT DUPLICATED. The shipped behavior is sound in the five observable decisions, the targeted 48-check helper suite and full script-helper suite pass locally, required CI is green, and no measurement/threshold/data path changed. Completeness is honestly partial and already owned by rf2-va5nm for the four drivers never watched returning nonzero; rf2-qv761 separately owns prompt failure before a sentinel. No new owner is needed.

ONE ACTIONABLE GAP IN THIS OWNER'S NEW CLASS PIN. `pageerror_exit_path.test.cjs` advertises a derived fleet guard against print-only handlers, but its offender loop searches only `s.indexOf("page.on('pageerror'", i)`. A live `page.on("pageerror", (e) => console.error(e))` is skipped by that loop; the later fallback regex sees that a handler exists, so it also declines to report "no signal". Reproduced synthetically against the exact predicates: handlerDetectedByFallback=true, offenders=[]. ESLint has no quote-style rule, so this is a real false green, not an impossible spelling. Iterate handler sites with the same quote-agnostic regex used elsewhere (or parse them) so both quote styles enter the offender check.

THE SAME PIN IS WEAKER THAN ITS CLAIM FOR LOCAL COLLECTORS: any inline handler with `push(` in the next 220 characters passes even if that array never reaches an exit; only shared `watchPage` callers get the separate reader check. Keep the intentionally permitted seven local-array drivers, but derive/prove their sink is read before allowing the class test to claim every fleet member refuses.

PR-RECORD COMPLETENESS. The merged PR body still leaves `sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` as "_running locally; this row is updated when it lands_" even though the PR is merged and CI is green. Preserve the otherwise excellent five-proven/four-unproven accounting, but leave a durable final result rather than a stale running claim.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7517 (merged 2026-08-05T01:05:38Z, f2052d1a37f4ebe3232b4845dbfc710ba77ae883) — CORRECTNESS / SELF-PROOF GAP IN THIS EXACT OWNER. The quote-agnostic handler discovery repairs the first #7505 audit finding, but the new local-sink reader test overloads sink.from/to with the whole 220-character handler search window and then excludes every occurrence in that window as “the push itself.” Independent synthetic execution of the landed predicates gives both opposing failures: `const errors=[]; page.on(... errors.push(e)); if(errors.length) ...` is classified UNREAD when the genuine read falls within 220 characters, while `const errors=[]; // errors collector only` followed by a push and unconditional exit 0 is classified READ because a comment token outside the excluded window counts. The current fleet suite is green (55 checks), so it does not protect either predicate. Track the exact push/declaration spans rather than the whole search window, distinguish code reads from comments/strings, and add executable positive/negative fixtures for the two known false-green classes. PR #7517's body also says proofs and gate results were added before review, but its durable body contains neither; retain the existing PR-record repair in this owner. No duplicate Bead.
THE LAST REMAINDER IS DISCHARGED (PR #7546, 2026-08-05). It was a HOLE, not a
scope line — both of #7517's audit claims reproduced independently before
anything was touched, by lifting the landed predicates verbatim out of
f2052d1a37 and running them: a genuine read one line under the registration
came back UNREAD, and a trailing comment naming the array came back READ.

WHAT WAS WRONG. `sinkOf` returned `{from: site.at, to: site.at + 220}` — the
window the handler was HUNTED in, handed on as though it were the span of the
push found there — and the reader discarded every occurrence inside it as "the
push itself". So a refusal written where refusals are actually written was
thrown away (FALSE OFFENDER), while a mention of the array in a comment or a
printed message sat outside the window and counted as a read (FALSE GREEN — an
unread collector passing the check written to catch it).

THE REPAIR. `sinkOf` carries `pushAt`, the exact index of the push it followed.
Every exclusion is now a test on ONE occurrence: that push, an occurrence
written by another `.push(`, an occurrence declared or reset with `= []`.
Nothing is discarded for being near the handler. Occurrences are read from a
masked copy in which comments and string literals are blanked to spaces with
every index preserved — and in which a template's `${...}` is deliberately LEFT
STANDING, because `${errors.length}` is code wearing a string's clothes. The
sink is also nominated from the masked text now, so a commented-out push cannot
vouch for a handler.

THE MASK'S SAFETY PROPERTY, stated in the file because it is what makes the
missing regex-literal lexer tolerable: masking only ever DELETES candidate
reads, so its worst case is a loud UNREAD naming the file — never a silent pass.

PROVEN BOTH DIRECTIONS, ON REAL DRIVER CODE. Three mutations of
retention_run.cjs, each applied and reverted:
  A  a plainly unread collector            landed: offender / repaired: offender / suite RED
  B  sound collector, refusal one line down landed: FALSE OFFENDER / repaired: silent / suite green
  C  unread collector named in a comment    landed: SILENT (the false green) / repaired: offender / suite RED
Clean fleet: silent under both. It was green by luck, exactly as the audit said.

title: hicasso SSR: defhost :ssr has NO value that renders CHILDREN — a provider crossing deletes its subtree from the server render
description:
FOUND while writing raw-escape design C (rf2-2rtt6.103, docs/design/hicasso/studio/raw-escape-design-c-ergonomics.md, section 'Needs a ruling' R1). Not the escape's defect — defhost's, which the escape inherits.

THE SHAPE. mint-host-gate! (front/codec.cljs) walks the declaration's :ssr fallback into a SINGLE element once, at the declaration, and the gate returns THAT element when unadopted:

    (let [placeholder (when (some? fallback) (as-element fallback))
          gate (fn [props]
                 (if (useSyncExternalStore ...)
                   (react/createElement component props)
                   placeholder))]

props is ignored on the unadopted branch, so props.children is DROPPED. :client-only (fallback nil) renders nothing; {:fallback hiccup} renders that hiccup INSTEAD of the children.

WHY IT MATTERS. For a LEAF widget (a chart, a date picker) dropping children is right — there are none. For a TRANSPARENT WRAPPER it deletes the application. A context provider contributes no markup of its own and exists solely to carry a subtree, so a provider at a crossing renders NOTHING server-side and takes every descendant with it. The server sends an empty document and the whole page appears after hydration.

THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. The draft guide's own provider example is exactly this shape — 05-interop.md:120, '(h/defhost themed (.-Provider some-context))' — and it has no :ssr option, so it takes the :client-only default. Providers are also one of HD-011's five NAMED use cases for the raw escape (decisions.md ~:412-421), so the escape has no recovery either: [:>] carries no declaration, so its only answer to 'my provider vanished server-side' is 'declare it', and declaring it does not help.

RULING NEEDED. The 2026-08-04 :ssr ruling (rf2-2rtt6.85) says TWO VALUES and 'there is no third value', and mint-host!/declared-ssr enforce that at the declaration. Either:
(a) a THIRD value exists — :ssr :children (or :transparent): render props.children in place of the component until adoption. One extra row in a table the guide already has; the honest reading of what a transparent wrapper IS; and
(b) providers are ruled OUT of SSR and 10-server-side-rendering.md + 05-interop.md's Providers section say so in terms.

DESIGN C RECOMMENDS (a). Without it the provider use case has no recovery at any crossing form.

NOT A BLOCKER FOR rf2-2rtt6.103's implementation: [:>] inherits whatever defhost's answer is, and clause 6 (renders nothing) is unchanged either way.
notes:
DECISION INPUT FROM rf2-nv07k (mayor, 2026-08-05) — THE FALLBACK ASYMMETRY CONSTRAINS THIS RULING BOTH WAYS, so its worker deliberately took no position and stopped. Read this before ruling on :ssr.

THE ASYMMETRY IS NOT A RULE, IT IS THE ABSENCE OF ONE. A fallback is walked into an element ONCE, at the declaration, outside any frame. So what gets refused is exactly what that walk can EVALUATE: an intent vector, a sub call in the form, non-hiccup. A boundary head is neither - it is an element whose body runs later - so THE WALK NEVER LOOKS INSIDE IT. The bead's framing that "the rule is simply narrower than it reads" is generous; it is not narrower, it is about a different thing.

TWO FACTS THAT WERE NOT ON THE RECORD AND THAT DECIDE IT:

1. THE DECLARED PLACEHOLDER IS NOT A VALUE. One declaration, walked once into one element, renders ALPHA in frame A, BRAVO in frame B, and ALPHA-TWO after a write. mint-host-gate!'s OWN justification for walking once is "a placeholder that differs per site is not a placeholder" - and that justification is FALSIFIED BY WHAT IT PERMITS.

2. IT DOES NOT SURVIVE THE ARM'S OWN OTHER BOUNDARY VARIANT. mint-frame-prop-view! (rf2-2rtt6.39) reads intent/*frame* at ELEMENT-CREATION time, which in a fallback is mint time, where the var is nil. It bakes nil in and throws mid-server-render. So whether a boundary head in a fallback works is a property of WHICH MINT THE HEAD CAME FROM - which is not a rule an author can hold in their head. That removes "bless it as it stands" from the table.

HOW IT CONSTRAINS THIS BEAD, BOTH DIRECTIONS: refusing the defview head deletes l0wfx's ONLY recovery and empties candidate D, whose content IS that workaround - favouring A or B. Blessing it sanctions "write your subtree twice" - favouring D. Either direction pre-empts this P1, which is why its worker took no ruling.

THE EVIDENCE HAS A DIRECTION AND IT WAS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: the codec's own law - walk once, reuse everywhere, BECAUSE a placeholder that differs per site is not a placeholder - ENTAILS OPTION (b), INERT MARKUP. And that removes the only thing people can do today. Its worker's recommendation: this should probably be ruled TOGETHER WITH rf2-l0wfx rather than ahead of it.

WHAT LANDED MEANWHILE (PR #7525): docstrings only on the executable side - every changed codec.cljs line is inside a docstring literal, no executable form changed, no hook added. The new arm1/fallback_contents_cljs_test.cljs is written as A RECORD OF TODAY, NOT A CONTRACT, so it does not entrench either answer before you rule.
close_reason: RULED AND SHIPPED — PR #7549, merged as 5ee86836e6 (+ docs 6db595ce21). The third :ssr value exists and it is :render, per the 2026-08-05 ruling. Implemented with rf2-nv07k in one PR. MECHANISM. front/codec.cljs: declared-ssr accepts the bare keyword :render as a third policy; mint-host! then mints NO GATE — the head's 'gate' slot (the React type host-element creates every crossing from) carries the foreign COMPONENT itself, HD-011's original zero-wrapper/zero-fiber/zero-hook shape restored for this policy. displayName is deliberately not stamped onto the foreign object. Server render, hydration's first client pass and a fresh createRoot mount therefore render the same element type with the same props, context and children: one tree everywhere, zero mismatch by identity, no adoption event, no type swap, NO REMOUNT. :children/:transparent/:passthrough/:server stay refused; :client-only stays the default. WITNESSES, all green: - host_ssr_dom_cljs_test §3: the provider crossing's SUBTREE is in the server HTML, and a consumer below reads dark — the DECLARED value — against a measured control with no provider above it that reads 'unset'. The :client-only defect is kept live beside it as the row :render exists to answer. - host_ssr_dom_cljs_test §5: a-render-crossing-hydrates-once-and-never-remounts — zero React error-channel traffic (the (is (empty? seen)) pattern across onRecoverableError + a console.error spy + a window error listener) and a mount counter reading exactly ONE. That is the closing browser-lane measurement the costing doc left open; the remount was reasoned-from-law before, it is measured now. - ssr/entry_cljs_test: a new corpus row defhost-ssr-render at a handed-in position, plus the :render crossing inside nested-host-panel's defview body. MUTATION PROVED, both directions: route :render through mint-host-gate! -> host_ssr 5 failures, entry 5 failures; fallback_contents 0 (not visible to the nv07k half) remove :render from declared-ssr -> the bundle fails to LOAD on the declaration itself GATES (fresh worktree off origin/main containing both commits): test:cljs 12639 tests / 63317 assertions 0F0E exit 0; test:browser 1101 tests / 6818 assertions 0F0E exit 0; test:hicasso-compile exit 0 (126 lane namespaces, zero warnings); clj-kondo at the CI pin 2026.04.15 exit 0, errors 0 / warnings 4536 (baseline); check_doc_slugs exit 0 and MUTATION-PROVEN; mkdocs --strict built clean; test-fast-pr.sh exit 0. CO-EDIT BILL: every Hicasso-scoped site in defhost-ssr-provider-costing.md's roster covered. ssr/driver.cjs and ssr/bake_bytes.test.cjs needed nothing — that file pins the byte ARITHMETIC over its own escaped fixtures, not per-row budgets, and no baked fixture is committed. Spec 011 / Spec 009 / the Spec 009 catalogue take zero edits, re-verified. Freehand's v/defhost takes zero, deliberately. draft-guide/11-performance.md and draft-guide/README.md left UNTOUCHED because PRs #7527/#7528 are open on both — the optional one-line delta there is the operator's to sequence, and 11's existing {:ssr :client-only} sample is not made wrong by this ruling. FILED: rf2-56iys (P3) — React 19's ctx.Provider IS the context object and self-references, so render-tree-hash recurses forever on a provider host head. Reachable only from the kept measurement row; the :render corpus row is a separate screen because of it. RECORDED HONESTLY, unchanged from the ruling: a provider whose VALUE is genuinely client-only still has no server story.

comments.text:
RULING 2026-08-05 20:02 AUSEST (delegated review pass, dossier ai/decisions/rf2-l0wfx.ssr-transparent-children.md — now deleted; operator-overturnable). Ruled TOGETHER with rf2-nv07k as one coupled ruling.

THE RULING: a third :ssr value EXISTS and it is :ssr :render — not :children/:transparent. Paired with nv07k's (b'): fallbacks become genuinely inert, boundary/host heads refused at mint. Option (b) (providers ruled out of SSR) is DEAD — it contradicts the operator's 2026-08-04 required-scope SSR ruling, and providers are an HD-011 NAMED use case (decisions.md ~:415, "providers an ecosystem library hands you").

WHY NOT :children (the dossier's main rec — REFUTED on the repo's own measured record, defhost-ssr-provider-costing.md + the dossier's Codex section, claims verified against codec.cljs and React 19.2.0 installed):
1. WRONG BYTES: :children renders the subtree with NO provider above it, so every consumer reads the context DEFAULT (measured: "unset" vs "dark", costing doc candidate-A control + Codex's independent run — same result). Server HTML under the wrong theme/locale/auth/route. Silent-absent becomes silent-wrong.
2. REMOUNT AT ADOPTION: the gate's client snapshot is constant true (codec.cljs gate-adopted), so adoption fires right after hydration, and the position's type swaps children->Provider(children). React reconciles by type at position: the whole just-hydrated subtree is destroyed and rebuilt (react.dev preserving-and-resetting-state; witnessed in-kind by the green fallback-swap row). Every provider wrapping the app root remounts the app immediately after hydrating it.
3. UNVERIFIABLE ASSERTION: :children on a non-transparent wrapper emits HTML structurally unlike the client render, and both passes agree so nothing reports it.
The "zero-mismatch" argument for :children covers hydration pass 1 only; it is true and beside the point — the defects are the bytes and the post-hydration swap.

:ssr :render CONDUCT (exact): the declaration asserts "this component is safe to render on the server". declared-ssr accepts the bare keyword :render as the third policy. For :render, mint-host! mints NO GATE — the head's "gate" slot carries the foreign component itself (HD-011's original zero-wrapper/zero-fiber/zero-hook shape restored for this policy; do not stamp displayName onto the foreign object, the head map already carries it). Same component, same props (host-entry walk unchanged), same children run on the server, on hydration's first pass, and on a fresh createRoot mount. SYMMETRY: one tree everywhere — server HTML, hydration pass and fresh mount render the SAME element type with the same props/context/children, so zero mismatch by identity, no snapshot pair, no adoption event, no swap, NO REMOUNT. For the case that filed this bead the assertion is trivially true: a Context.Provider is React's own component and the server renderer fully supports context — consumers below read the DECLARED value in the server HTML (the costing doc's "dark" control becomes the contract).

SPELLING justification (one sentence): :render names both the conduct (the component renders) and the assertion (server-safe to render) — where :children/:transparent assert an unverifiable structural property and deliver wrong-context bytes. :children, :transparent, :passthrough, :server STAY REFUSED (:rf.error/hicasso-host-bad-ssr-policy; the no-ssr-value-expresses witness keeps those rows, drops :render). :client-only stays the DEFAULT — the conservative reason in the .85 addendum stands; :render is the author saying, never the door guessing (costing-doc candidate C stays rejected on exactly that law).

CHILDREN / FRAME BINDING (.74 composition, verified): children are lowered in the CALLER's body inside its render window (host-element/make-element run there), so intents in them close over the caller's frame-locked dispatch and a frame-fed head among them gets rfFrame baked in the caller's body (codec.cljs boundary-element :1550; mark-frame-prop!'s own docstring: a foreign component between two Hicasso boundaries passes children through with the prop already in them). :render changes ONLY the element type; the children path is today's adopted-arm path, byte-identical. Composes.

[:>] (clause 6 UNCHANGED): the escape carries no declaration, so no server-safety assertion to carry — it renders nothing server-side, and it must never grow an :ssr spelling of its own (raw-escape-spec standing instruction unchanged). The answer to "my provider vanished server-side" becomes "declare it: (h/defhost themed (.-Provider ctx) {:ssr :render})" — which now actually works.

NV07K HALF (b', ruled here, cross-ref on that bead): with :render the write-your-subtree-twice workaround is unnecessary, so the mint walks the declared fallback hiccup STRUCTURALLY and refuses any boundary head (boundary-head?) or host head (host-head?) at any position — new error id :rf.error/hicasso-host-fallback-boundary-head, naming the host, the offending head's displayName and its position; recovery: a fallback is inert markup — write plain hiccup, or declare :ssr :render and render the real subtree. title: hd8_run.cjs is FAIL-OPEN: a failed DOM read-back and a REFUSED yield correction are printed and never reach the exit code
description:
FOUND by rf2-y7mw7's sibling sweep, 2026-08-04, while repairing the same
defect in clock_run.cjs. Established by CODE READING, not by a run — whoever
takes this should reproduce it first, as rf2-y7mw7 did.

hd8_run.cjs's exit block (implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/
hd8_run.cjs ~608-631) reads exactly three things — `hardFail` (~608),
`contractFailed` (~612) and the arm-order `refused` (~619) — and then prints

    [hd8] ok — measured, and no arm reads differently for its position in the plan

Two refusals it COMPUTES AND PRINTS never reach that block.

(a) A FAILED DOM READ-BACK. hd8_rows.cljs ~913-944 (`mask-failed-read-backs`)
writes `{:unpublished :failed-dom-read-back :unverified n :of m}` into the
row's `:summary`. It does NOT set HD8_ERROR (only hd8_app.cljs ~53-56 does,
from -main's catch), so `out.err` stays null and `hardFail` stays null. The
driver renders `UNPUBLISHED (1/78 unverified)` in the cross-run table
(~321-324, ~396, ~405) and exits 0. Every sibling instrument treats the
identical condition as a hard refusal: hd8_clock_run.cjs ~760-766 (exit 3),
shapes/census_clock_run.cjs ~805-811 (exit 3), clock_run.cjs ~2177-2185
(exit 1), p0_run.cjs ~1333-1338, b7_run.cjs ~673-675, reads_ladder_run.cjs
~814-817, spine_ablation_run.cjs ~923-928.

MITIGATION TO WEIGH, so the bead is not overstated: the figure IS suppressed
— replaced by the UNPUBLISHED marker, and head-to-head pairs touching the arm
are dropped at hd8_rows.cljs ~939-944 — so a reader cannot copy a number out.
What is missing is the process's own statement, and a green exit is what a
future worker banks.

(b) A `:refused` YIELD CORRECTION. hd8_rows.cljs ~1307/1315/1330/1365 emit
`:verdict :refused` with reasons `:unevaluable`,
`:correction-exceeds-window`, `:correction-changes-the-verdict`. The driver
prints `YIELD CORRECTION: REFUSED (correction-changes-the-verdict)` at
~365-371 and then reads the flag ONLY for `c.verdict === 'corrected'`
(~378-379). On `refused`, `cSummary` is `{}`, `correctedBand` (~391) returns
null, and the UNADJUSTED number is printed at ~396 with no [UNADJUSTED] label
and no stamp — directly beneath a line saying the correction was refused
because it CHANGES THE VERDICT. Exit 0.

(c) `watchPage` FAILURES ARE NEVER INSPECTED. ~259/292 call `watchPage` and
never read `watch.failures` after `race` returns. coldmount_run.cjs ~192,
p0_converge_run.cjs ~236, ime_run.cjs, chrome_run.cjs and
adoption_witness_run.cjs all do. A pageerror arriving after the sentinel
fires is recorded, printed, and read by nobody — a third instance of the same
shape in the same file.

hd8_run.cjs is also the only driver of its size in these trees with NO
*_exit_path.test.cjs pin, and it exports nothing (no module.exports), so its
decision is not reachable from a unit test at all.

THE REPAIR IS THE ONE THE TREE HAS ALREADY MADE FIVE TIMES (rf2-tb345,
rf2-rr6do, rf2-y7mw7): lift the decision into ONE pure `verdict(summarise())`
over a flat per-row summary, export it, put the driver behind
`require.main === module`, and pin it with an exit-path test that drives the
pure function directly and asserts the wiring. See
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/clock_exit_path.test.cjs
for the shape, and rf2-y7mw7's PR for a worked example including the mutation
proof in both directions.
notes:
SEQUENCING NOTE (mayor, 2026-08-04) — HELD BEHIND PR #7489, AND THESE TWO BEADS SHOULD PROBABLY BE ONE DISPATCH.

WHY HELD: PR #7489 (rf2-y7mw7, the clock driver's adjudication fail-open) is open and edits implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/clock_run.cjs. BOTH rf2-x6g04 and rf2-jvheq name clock_run.cjs in their own file lists. Dispatching either now puts two workers on one file, which is the collision the hot-zone rule exists to prevent.

WHY THEY ARE PLAUSIBLY ONE PIECE OF WORK: their rosters overlap by eight drivers - adoption_witness_run.cjs, b7_run.cjs, clock_run.cjs, coldmount_run.cjs, p0_converge_run.cjs, p0_run.cjs, reads_ladder_run.cjs, spine_ablation_run.cjs. Two workers sweeping overlapping halves of one fleet will conflict on the intersection and will each have to reason about the same shared shape.

THE CLASS, which is the thing worth seeing: this is now the THIRD fail-open found in the bench-driver fleet today. rf2-y7mw7 (a row whose every bar reads UNADJUDICATED still exits 0, found by the quiet-window worker while measuring), rf2-x6g04 (a failed DOM read-back and a REFUSED yield correction still exit 0), and rf2-jvheq (nine drivers print an uncaught page error and exit 0). Each was found independently, by a different worker, in a different driver. That is the signature of a COPIED SHAPE rather than three coincidences - the same eight-or-so lines of exit handling replicated across the fleet, exactly as rf2-2rtt6.73 found eleven drivers carrying one copied fail-open earlier in this programme.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: these drivers produce the evidence a graduation decision reads. A driver that exits 0 while its own output says REFUSED or UNADJUDICATED does not merely fail to catch a defect - it publishes a green that a future reader will bank. The quiet window was saved from exactly this only because a second row happened to share the invocation.

DISPATCH SHAPE WHEN #7489 LANDS: one worker, both beads, reading #7489's landed fix FIRST so the fleet converges on one exit-handling shape rather than three. Require the sibling sweep to be derived (grep the pattern across every driver) rather than taken from either bead's list, since the two lists already disagree about which drivers are affected - and neither may be complete.
DELIVERED in PR #7494 (worker/benchexit-x6g04), 2026-08-04.

REPRODUCED FIRST, as the description asked. The pre-fix exit ladder, replayed
verbatim over the exact state hd8_rows.cljs produces, returns 0 while the table
says UNPUBLISHED (1/78 unverified) and YIELD CORRECTION: REFUSED.

All three sub-defects fixed, and all three were as described:
  (a) failed DOM read-back  -> exit 3 (the code hd8_clock_run.cjs already uses
      for the same refusal)
  (b) :refused yield correction -> exit 4
  (c) watch.failures never read -> folded into exit 1, the code the file's
      header already documented for a page error

The decision is now one pure verdict(summarise(...)) over a flat record,
exported, driver behind require.main === module, 19 fixtures run by a new
--selftest and by clock_exit_path.test.cjs (+16 cases, 71 passing).

MUTATION-PROVED BOTH DIRECTIONS: refusing state -> exit 3/4 naming the reason;
clean run -> exit 0 with zero lines; fix deliberately broken -> back to exit 0
while STILL PRINTING both refusals, caught by --selftest (exit 1, 5 failures)
and by the pin (exit 1, 3 failures).

NOTHING WEAKENED: exits 1 and 2 are unchanged and pinned by explicit
'unchanged' cases. No measurement, arm, threshold or dataset touched.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE DESCRIPTION. The roster was derived rather than taken:
across all 23 tracked *run.cjs in the lane, hd8_run.cjs is the ONLY one of the
six watchPage callers that never read .failures. Sub-defect (c) is a
single-driver defect, not a fleet-wide one — the other five (coldmount,
p0_converge, ime, chrome, adoption_witness) all read them AND reach an exit.
MAYOR CORRECTION 2026-08-04: MY "COPIED SHAPE ACROSS THE FLEET" FRAMING WAS WRONG, AND SO WAS THIS BEAD'S. Measured by the sweep worker across the whole lane; recording it because the wrong framing invites a fleet-wide refactor nobody needs.

WHAT I SAID: three fail-opens found by three different workers in three different drivers "is the signature of a copied shape, not three coincidences", and I put roughly sixteen drivers in the affected set. This bead's own framing called its defect "a third instance of the same shape".

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, from a derived census of all 23 tracked *run.cjs (48 .cjs total) rather than from either bead's list: THE LANE PARTITIONS CLEANLY - 1 defective, 5 correct watchPage callers, 9 bare handlers, 7 already collect-and-refuse. hd8_run.cjs is THE ONLY ONE of the six watchPage callers that never read .failures; the other five read them AND reach an exit. So there is no widely-copied fail-open in the watchPage family. There is ONE defective driver, now fixed.

The nine-driver pageerror class (rf2-jvheq) is REAL and SEPARATE, and its audit came back POSITIVE rather than speculative: nine demonstrated-live, zero structurally-impossible, zero could-not-determine, SETTLED BY RUNNING IT rather than by reading. Its mechanism is not a copied mistake either - React 19.2's defaultOnUncaughtError routes through reportGlobalError to reportError INSTEAD OF RETHROWING, so a page-side try/catch cannot see it; measured live, pageerror fires, the surrounding catch never runs, and the app carries on to READY. All nine mount through flushSync, so it is NOT closeable inside the apps.

WHY THE DISTINCTION MATTERS: "sixteen drivers share a copied fail-open" argues for a shared exit-handling framework. "One driver was defective and nine are defeated by a React behaviour they cannot catch" argues for exactly what shipped - a narrow fix in the one driver, no framework, and the nine recorded once in sentinel.cjs where the policy already lives rather than in nine drifting copies. The worker declined to ship nine unproven gate wirings on the ground that "nine unproven wirings would be this same fault in reverse", which is the right call and the reason rf2-sib23 exists instead.

GENERAL LESSON FOR ME: I inferred a class from three independent sightings and stated it as a signature. Three sightings are a reason to COUNT, not a count. The instruction that produced the truth here was "derive the roster, do not take it from either bead" - and what it found was that both beads' rosters were wrong in opposite directions, one overstating the family and the other exactly right about its nine.
