THE WORKTREE IS EXEMPT FROM THE HYGIENE REAP until this is resolved. Its shape - zero commits, clean-looking, no PR - is EXACTLY the profile the reap rule matches for an abandoned worktree, and reaping it would destroy the only in-place copy. Do not remove it on that signal.

TO RESUME: after the session limit resets, message that same agent rather than dispatching a fresh one - it holds the reasoning behind the spec and its first act should be to COMMIT AND PUSH what it has before doing anything else. If it cannot be resumed, a fresh worker should read the preserved copy as INPUT rather than starting over, and must re-verify it against the six designs rather than trusting it - it was mid-flight and its final ancillary steps (the bead note and the studio README index row) were never done.

THE SIBLING WORKER, spinecheck-ejm7m (rf2-ejm7m), was killed in the same window with NOTHING uncommitted - its last line was "Baselines measured", so its measurements lived only in its transcript and are lost. That one is a clean re-run, which is cheap; it does not need preservation, only re-dispatch.
SYNTHESIZED SPEC LANDED (2026-08-05) — docs/design/hicasso/studio/raw-escape-spec.md, on branch worker/rawsynth-2rtt6-103. This note is the operative summary; the page carries the argument. IMPLEMENTATION RE-DISPATCHES FROM THE PAGE, NOT FROM THIS NOTE — but a dispatcher who reads only this note gets every ruling.

WHAT IT SYNTHESIZED: TEN inputs, not three and not six. The three tracked studio designs (A minimal / B correctness / C ergonomics), the six local-only ai/findings documents (parity + minimal + migration designs and their three adversarial passes), and THIS BEAD'S OWN 12:06 COMMENT, which is itself a synthesis of the local six and had never read A, B or C. Everything relied on from the gitignored set is quoted into the tracked page, so none of it dies with the local tree.

THE FIVE EDGES, RULED:

E1 SSR/HYDRATION — hard :client-only through ONE module-level shared gate reusing the landed snapshot triple (codec.cljs:1035-1037) with placeholder nil. No fallback spelling of any kind. Server-absent and hydration-first-pass-absent are ONE fact that React chooses, not two facts kept in step. The only unanimous edge across all nine design/attack documents. Carrier: two slots on the gate's own props (#js {c, p} — the boundary-element rfProps idiom); children on the OUTER element via make-element's existing arms. Design A's strip-a-key carrier is rejected on A's own pricing: it costs a shallow copy per crossing per render and leaks an internal key A itself says must be witnessed, where the two-slot shape makes that leak unrepresentable instead.

E2 PROPS — the door's unclaimed-slot conduct of host-entry with an empty declared map, exactly, and with no branch of its own. Vectors and key-maps at event-spelled slots refuse loudly; marked h/fn and plain fns cross BY IDENTITY with returns ignored; :& merged before conversion; :key to the outer element; :ref through check-ref!.

E3 IDENTITY — four statements. Canonical DOM is NOT reduced at all, and this is provable rather than asserted: lane/canonical serialises element and text nodes and ignores comments, so a nil-rendering gate is invisible to it. The data lane is reduced at EXACTLY ONE SLOT (slot 1 compares by JS identity; total everywhere else in the vector) and that is the whole of the ruled phrase. One shared gate type, displayName the constant "[:>]", and NO name extraction — React resolves displayName || name || null, Closure renames .name under :advanced, and foreign production bundles drop displayName, so any derived identity is build-dependent. Plus a recorded forward obligation for the unbuilt headless render.

E4 LEGAL VALUES — a pinned roster REFUSED AT THE CROSSING in the owner's render. Strings and nil refused. React's own refusal is minted at fiber creation, which behind the gate is post-adoption and client-only, and for any ClojureScript value its message reads "got: object" because it names typeof — so delegation loses on timing, on stack, and on message. The pinning witness is NOT optional: it is what turns a React upgrade into a red row instead of a silent false-refusal, which is the worst failure a hatch can have.

E5 CHILDREN — nothing new. Eager lowering in the owner's render window through the same make-element arms. Unanimous across all six designs.

EDGES 2 AND 5 ARE ONE AND A HALF DECISIONS — not one (design C's claim) and not two independent ones. E5's CHILDREN half is invariant under every candidate answer to E2, because E2 governs props on the [:>] node while children carry their own positions inside hiccup the author owns; every one of the six designs states the children rule identically regardless of its E2. So it is stated independently and is SAFE TO BUILD BEFORE E2 IS FINALLY RULED. E5's render-prop-PROP half is wholly determined by E2, and C is right about that half — which is why the message repair in (e) below stops being a nicety and becomes that half's deliverable.

WHERE THIS DEPARTS FROM THE 12:06 COMMENT — one substantive difference, stated so it is not read as an oversight. That comment ships a DEV-ONLY WARNING at [:>] only, while the same programme files rf2-2rtt6.117 asking whether the door should get the same diagnostic. That is a fork at the one edge whose entire argument is zero-fork. The spec instead PINS the escape to the door: the escape's conduct at an unclaimed prop is whatever .116 rules for the door, and its diagnostic whatever .117 rules. Refuse at both, warn at both, or leave both — in all three branches the zero-fork invariant holds and no line of the escape's mechanism changes. The decisive reason, which only the attack on the migration design states in full: IF THE ESCAPE REFUSES WHAT THE DOOR ACCEPTS, [:> X ...] -> (defhost x X {}) IS NO LONGER BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING, AND THAT REWRITE IS THE WHOLE THEOREM OF rf2-2rtt6.106'S CODEMOD. Design A's and the local minimal design's h/fn refusal is therefore rejected on composition grounds, not on its merits in isolation — it is the only stance with no silent cell and both pages price it honestly.

WHAT THE SYNTHESIS ATTACKED THAT NOTHING HAD (the adversarial wave ran on the local three only, so A, B and C had never been attacked at all):

(a) THE HEAD TEST COSTS NOTHING, and design B's "must cost nothing" constraint — for which B offers no mechanism, falling back on "or measure and publish the delta" — is exactly satisfiable. hiccup-tag? has EXACTLY ONE CALLER (vec->element's cond) and sits AFTER the fragment-head? arm, yet its body still re-asks (not (fragment-head? head)). So EVERY NATIVE TAG ON EVERY PAGE PAYS THE FRAGMENT = TWICE TODAY. Drop the provably-dead second test and add raw-head? as a cond arm before hiccup-tag?: a keyword tag pays two = and one type predicate before, and two = and one type predicate after. Identical. Nobody in ten documents noticed, and it matters because this codec has costed a keyword? short-circuit at +/-51-67% of a walk.

(b) DESIGN B'S MECHANISM IS DEAD TWICE OVER. Its WeakMap-keyed gate throws on React's built-in wrapper types, which are registered symbols that ES2024 excludes as WeakMap keys — re-verified on this repo's pinned React 19.2.0 under Node v24.13.0. AND its edge-4 table refuses symbols while its edge-4 prose four paragraphs later accepts Suspense. Keep the prose and the WeakMap throws; keep the table and the escape refuses Suspense while accepting React.lazy, which REQUIRES a Suspense ancestor — the exact pairing HD-011 names as a reason the escape exists.

(c) DESIGN C'S E2 falls to the two attacks that killed migration's identical move, neither of which was ever run against C, plus a charge neither made: C routes an h/fn at a non-event slot to the RENDER contract, which mints a fresh wrapper per lowering and destroys the function identity host-prop-value preserves deliberately so that React.memo and every downstream bail-out comparing handler identity keep working (HD-024's own Rationale says so in terms). C never prices this. And C's showcase spelling, renderRow, is the one that survives; the spelling C concedes it gets wrong, onRenderRow, is the ecosystem one (Fluent UI).

(d) h/as-element DOES NOT EXIST. Four of the six designs name it as the recovery for the two sharpest SILENT traps at this crossing — hiccup written in a prop, and a function child or render-prop body returning hiccup — and design C's entire render-prop worked example is built on it. Verified: ZERO occurrences of as-element anywhere under docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/; the guide's taught h/ roster is h/hicasso, h/root, h/fn, h/render, h/defhost, h/presence, h/child-key, h/boundary; arm1/lang.clj exports exactly three macros (defview, hfn, defhost) and no as-element. The MECHANISM is public as codec/as-element (codec.cljs:1708); the TAUGHT NAME is not. An error message naming a spelling the reader cannot call is worse than no message. FILED AS rf2-2rtt6.120 (P2) — resolve it BEFORE .103's refusal messages and guide rows are written, not during.

(e) THE 12:06 COMMENT DROPS TWO LOAD-BEARING CARRIES, both restored on the page. First, the X2 body-run restatement. Second, design A's intent-outside-boundary message repair: at [:>] the author IS inside a boundary's render as far as they can see, since they wrote the crossing in a body, so the current message and its :lower-intents-inside-a-boundary-render recovery will read as a framework bug. The runtime cannot tell the two causes apart from *dispatch* = nil alone, so the message must offer BOTH readings and name defhost with :callbacks {... :render} as the second. A dispatcher briefing from that comment alone ships without either.

FOUR RULINGS LEFT TO THE OPERATOR AND NOT TAKEN — recommendation and cost are on the page, and in every case the spec is written so that no line of the escape's mechanism changes with the answer:

R1 — h/fn at an unclaimed prop slot (rf2-2rtt6.116, with rf2-2rtt6.117 for the door's diagnostic). Recommendation: rule it for the DOOR and let the escape inherit. Cost of refusing: it chips HD-024's cleanest claim, that the marked form is callable everywhere and degrades to a defensible contract rather than a crash. Cost of leaving: a silent dead return on the guide's own taught path for value-first invokers. Cost of warning: a diagnostic surface the record must justify against the anti-nag posture.

R2 — defhost's :ssr has no value that renders children (rf2-l0wfx, P1). A provider — one of HD-011's five named use cases, and the guide's own example at 05-interop.md:120 — deletes its subtree from the server render. Design C recommends a third :ssr value meaning render the children in place of the component. The attack on the local minimal design offers a second route: a Context-head carve-out, since a React 19 Context is detectable at the crossing by $$typeof and its server render is React's own context machinery, deterministic and with no window risk — so the "nobody can vouch for the server render" defence is false for providers specifically. Cost of neither: providers are ruled out of SSR and the guide must say so. THE ESCAPE MUST NEVER GROW AN :ssr SPELLING OF ITS OWN; it inherits whatever the door becomes.

R3 — refusing a Hicasso view or host head in Component position exceeds clause 5's letter, since both are values React accepts. Recommended anyway: a defview head is fn?-true, so a bare "is it a function" test accepts [:> my-view ...] and mounts the shell raw, the body reads rfProps, gets undefined, and receives nil props. That is silent breakage of the kind a migration produces. Removable without touching the mechanism — it is a predicate and two message flavours.

R4 — rf2-2rtt6.115's dated scope-note on HD-024's row 3 must land before or with the escape. E2 rests on that resolution, and it is decisions.md, outside the synthesis fence, so it is named here rather than discovered by the implementer.

IMPLEMENTER'S CARRY-LIST — six facts verified against main, in full on the page. (1) :> IS NOT CURRENTLY AN ERROR: hiccup-tag? (codec.cljs:1673-1675) accepts any keyword that is not :<>, and vec->element (:1689) routes it to native-element, so [:> Foo {}] today asks React for an element named <>. The branch must PRECEDE hiccup-tag? and compare with = and never identical?, or it is DEAD CODE THAT COMPILES CLEANLY. (2) The head test is free, per (a). (3) X2's body-run equality at arm1/hydrate_dom_cljs_test.cljs:414 GOES RED ON CORRECT CODE at the first client-only crossing — via [:>] or via a defhost :ssr :client-only — and must be restated as boundary count PLUS the number of client-only crossings, never deleted and never loosened to a range. (4) The argv indices shift by one: component at 1, attr map at 2 when it is a map, children from 3 or 2; bare [:>] takes the no-component refusal. (5) check-ref! refuses only a vector, so an object ref passes today (rf2-d03av) — do NOT add a [:>]-only ref refusal, because a rule enforced at one crossing and not the other is worse than one enforced at neither. (6) host-entry has no class branch (rf2-2rtt6.119), and note the trap: edge 3's canonical-parity row CANNOT catch it, because both forms are identically wrong.

NOT CLOSING THIS BEAD — it stays open for implementation, and rf2-2rtt6.109 reads the page.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #7497 (merged 2026-08-04T17:36:54Z, a1f59a0a3bbc8ba0c41bcf9d5f7b63cdb1f45a59) — CORRECTNESS FOLLOW-UP. The synthesized spec's implementer carry-list (§8.3) says the X2 body-run equality goes red at the first client-only crossing and must become boundary-count PLUS the number of client-only crossings. That is not true for the mechanism this same spec selects. `mint-host-gate!` and the proposed shared raw gate are explicitly not Hicasso boundaries and have no Hicasso body (`front/codec.cljs`:1646-1647); `runtime/body-runs` increments only inside `run-once`, where an actual Hicasso boundary body is invoked (`arm1/runtime.cljs`:1532-1550, 1615-1640). Adoption's `useSyncExternalStore` update rerenders the gate. A plain foreign component behind `[:>]` or a `defhost :ssr :client-only` therefore adds zero body runs; a gate can add zero, one, or many only insofar as it defers actual Hicasso boundaries beneath it. Following the stated crossings formula would make a correct implementation's witness fail or encode a topology-dependent miscount. Correct `raw-escape-spec.md` §8.3 and this bead's appended synthesis note before implementation: keep X2 exact, but derive its expected count from the boundary bodies in the fixture, including any bodies first mounted beneath client-only gates—not from the number of crossings. This already-open implementation/spec owner is exact; no duplicate Bead.

PR #7607 correctly landed the shared host-entry refusal and the decisions.md ruling, but docs/design/hicasso/studio/raw-escape-spec.md still instructs the superseded behavior in four load-bearing places: the Edge 2 table says a marked h/fn crosses by identity; the following decisive argument rejects refusal; section 7 R1 still calls refuse/warn/leave unresolved; and R4 still demands a marked-h/fn identity witness. Those statements now contradict both host-entry and HD-011/HD-024. CORRECTNESS / IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the guide's new Component-position contract exposed that the shipped early refusal is broader in prose than in code. `raw-component` says it accepts what React 19 mints a fiber for and refuses everything else at the crossing, in the owner's render and on the server; however `react-exotic?` accepts every JavaScript symbol and `react-wrapper-object?` accepts every object carrying any non-nil `$$typeof`. Make the accepted predicate match React 19's actual symbol/brand roster (or use an equally authoritative exact validator), pin bogus-symbol and bogus-brand refusals alongside every accepted category, and retain an explicit React-upgrade pin. If forward-permissive delegation is intentionally ruled instead, narrow the guide/decision/code claims and admit the delayed client-only error; do not keep claiming every invalid value is refused early. DESIGN SYNTHESIS (2026-08-04; 3 designs — parity/minimal/migration — + 3 adversarial reviews; verdicts 0F/5M, 0F/5M, 1F/3M; all three forced choices converge on a parity–minimal hybrid). MAYOR-DISPATCHABLE from this comment. Full record: ai/findings/2026-08-04.rawescape-* (local-only; this comment is self-sufficient). HD-011's core stands untouched: same foreign path, same default conversions, .cljs-only at the node, explicitly secondary, "declare what you use twice", bare-head auto-hosting stays rejected.

THE RULED SHAPE, per edge:

E1 SSR/HYDRATION (unanimous): hard :client-only via ONE shared module-level raw gate reusing the landed gate-adopted/gate-unadopted snapshots (codec.cljs ~:1035-1066). Server emits nothing; hydration's first pass emits nothing; adoption swaps the component in — R2 zero-mismatch by construction. NO inline fallback spelling (a fallback is policy; policy lives on declarations — want one, write defhost {:fallback}). The guide TEACHES the 3-line userland wrapper-host pattern for per-site fallbacks. Provider-subtree SSR hole: sequenced behind rf2-l0wfx; the Context-head carve-out question is flagged to the .88 SSR sitting, not solved here.

E2 PROPS (adjudicated across a 2-1 attacker split): vectors and key-maps at event-spelled props REFUSE LOUDLY (:rf.error/hicasso-raw-intent-needs-a-declaration; message names defhost :callbacks as the door AND states that h/fn returns do not dispatch here). Marked h/fn and plain fns cross BY IDENTITY (the door's landed undeclared-slot conduct — zero behavioural fork with defhost), with returns ignored. NEW: a DEV-ONLY loud warning (goog.DEBUG; the codec's dev-warning idiom) whenever a MARKED h/fn lands on any [:>] prop — naming the silent-return fact and both real doors — closing the taught-path silent cell the minimal attack proved (guide 05 teaches h/fn for value-first invokers) without forking runtime semantics. Vectors at non-event slots are data via the door's conversion. MIGRATION'S SPELLING-CLASSIFIER E2 IS REJECTED (FATAL: Fluent onRender*/Ant onRow are event-spelled render-props/return-readers — nil-returning event wrappers blank them silently); the position table survives ONLY as the codemod's static-analysis vocabulary.

E3 IDENTITY: the :> head keyword is the data-lane marker; ONE shared gate type in the fiber lane (no per-component gates — that is the rejected auto-hosting cache); NO name extraction into fiber identity (displayName/name are :advanced-hostile); a name RESOLVER for diagnostic messages only. Canonical DOM at the node is provably indistinguishable from the defhost equivalent (lane/canonical reads element/text nodes only) — witnessed. Inner element typed by the component value: state preserved iff same component identity (the runtime-selected use case remounts on type flip, correctly).

E4 LEGAL VALUES (minimal's mechanism, three verdicts concur): a pinned roster — fns, React's built-in Symbol.for exotics, $$typeof ∈ {context, consumer, forward_ref, memo, lazy} — refused AT THE CROSSING in the owner's render (React's own invalid-type error fires at fiber creation = post-adoption, client-only, names nothing the author wrote — verified). REFUSED: strings (the grammar owns tags; Reagent's [:> "input"] took the controlled wrapper, so acceptance would silently drop caret protection — donor-verified), nil/undefined (broken-import diagnosis), defview/defhost marked heads (silent nil-props breakage otherwise), and non-fn IFns (r/partial/multimethods — WORKING Reagent sites that would die as opaque objects; loud refusal steers to fn-wrapping). Error id :rf.error/hicasso-raw-not-a-component with shape-specific fixes.

E5 CHILDREN (unanimous): trailing forms lower eagerly in the owning boundary's render window — intent closures capture the owner's frame-locked dispatch at lowering time (the .74 temporal ruling; the arming gate composes when [:>] sits inside a declared :render callback). Render-prop PROPS on the raw node are out of scope (defhost :render territory); render-prop-SUPPLIED components are in scope. :& merged before conversion per clause (d) — witnessed at the crossing.

INCIDENTAL FIX: the codec currently MIS-PARSES :> as a native tag named ">" — the new branch replaces that; add the regression row.

rf2-2rtt6.115 RESOLVED (three independent adjudications concur): the CODE side is authoritative — HD-024's row 3 at decisions.md:1015 OVER-RECORDS; the door's undeclared-slot identity crossing was deliberate (one-commit evidence 86ed3a330e + the .65 landing's reasoned docstring). EXECUTE IN THIS PR: a dated scope-note on row 3 + a witness pinning the door's undeclared marked-h/fn identity crossing (currently unwitnessed — host_hatch pins only a plain fn). The migration design's "align defhost with row 3" follow-up is STRUCK as adverse.

WITNESSES: conversion parity with defhost on the same fixture component (the load-bearing row); every refusal row (vectors, key-maps at event slots; strings; nil; marked heads; IFn) + the dev-warning row for marked h/fn; SSR-absent + hydration-adoption rows; :& at the crossing; callback-ref legal + string/keyword ref refused (HD-016); children-capture row (an intent inside [:>] children dispatches to the owner's frame); canonical-DOM indistinguishability; the mis-parse regression; the .115 door witness + scope-note.

SIZE: ~100-140 lines in front/codec.cljs + witnesses. FENCES: bench lane + decisions.md (the row-3 scope-note + a dated [:>]-shape note on HD-011, digtt pattern). SEQUENCING: codec.cljs now has THREE beads touching it (.103, .104, .107's pre-merge read) — mayor sequences; .104's warning inherits [:>] children automatically once both land. Gates: hicasso compile + DOM suites + fast-PR spine, foreground. Guide: the code PR carries the tense-flips (02:78, 05:48/:148-163/:174, 08:44); bead .109 teaches fully after MERGE. The codemod contract for .106: hoist-only is mechanical and behaviour-preserving; :callbacks synthesis is never mechanical (human or explicit flag); four Reagent-input rewrites + first-class report. title: clock_run.cjs is FAIL-OPEN on adjudication: a row whose every bar is UNADJUDICATED still exits 0 and is announced 'REPORTABLE ... Publish those'
description:
FOUND by rf2-0qj9w's second quiet window, 2026-08-04 (PR #7486), while
verifying the run's own exit code rather than trusting it.

THE GAP. clock_run.cjs computes two verdicts per row and only one of them
reaches the exit code.

  * ROW-LEVEL: did the positive control see the change its arithmetic
    predicts? This is `ctlFailed` (clock_run.cjs ~2098), and it is the only
    thing the final block gates on: `if (ctlFailed.length > 0) { ... exit(1) }`,
    else `console.error('[clock] ok')` and an implicit exit 0.
  * BAR-LEVEL: does the row have a band-supplying control, so that a magnitude
    can be adjudicated at all? On the keystroke row the answer is NO — the
    fixed-50 ms control makes control/floor read (F+50)/F, so the driver
    prints `band NOT AVAILABLE on this row` and labels all three bars
    UNADJUDICATED (that gap itself is rf2-swwud).

These never meet. A row can pass its control, clear every whole-run gate, and
have no adjudicable bar — and the driver exits 0 announcing success.

THE CONCRETE FAIL-OPEN. `HCLOCK_ONLY=keystroke` alone, on a perfectly clean
box, produces: both controls PASS, guard reportable, canonical DOM identical,
0 unverified of 756, the four-field witness reconciling exactly — and
`ctlFailed` empty, therefore `[clock] ok`, therefore EXIT 0. Every bar in that
run is UNADJUDICATED. A worker reading the exit code as a pass publishes an
unadjudicated magnitude and is not warned.

WORSE, THE SUMMARY LINE ACTIVELY INVITES IT. Even when another row refuses,
the driver prints (clock_run.cjs ~2133):

  [clock] REPORTABLE: keystroke — control passed, guard clean, canonical DOM
  identical, 0 unverified. Publish those and mark the rest.

"Publish those" names a row whose every bar the same driver has just labelled
UNADJUDICATED, four hundred lines above.

WHY IT HAS NOT BITTEN YET, WHICH IS LUCK RATHER THAN DESIGN. Both windows ran
HCLOCK_ONLY=M1,keystroke, and in both M1's ctl-2x refused, so the driver exited
1 for an unrelated reason and the worker read the block carefully. Run the
commissioned keystroke row on its own — which the payload permits and a
rebook might well do — and the protection disappears.

THE FIX IS SMALL AND IS NOT A BAND. This bead does NOT ask for the missing
control (that is rf2-swwud, and it is the real repair). It asks only that the
driver stop claiming success it has not established:

  1. Fold "every published bar carries a band" into the exit condition, so a
     run whose bars are all UNADJUDICATED exits non-zero naming itself, in the
     idiom of the six witness refusals.
  2. Make the REPORTABLE line say what it means — a row that is reportable but
     unadjudicated is not a row to publish, and the sentence should not say
     "Publish those".

Whichever way it is resolved, the property to preserve is the tree's own
standard: an instrument that can exit 0 while emitting a verdict nobody may
act on is a fail-open instrument.

EVIDENCE. PR #7486, docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-candidates-clock.md sec 3.5,
and the retained dataset
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/clock-0qj9w/run2.json.
notes:
BASIS OF THE COUNTERFACTUAL, stated so nobody has to re-derive it: the HCLOCK_ONLY=keystroke-alone claim is established by READING clock_run.cjs's final block, not by running it. The block is unambiguous — 'if (ctlFailed.length > 0) { ...; process.exit(1); } console.error("[clock] ok");' — and on a keystroke-only invocation ctlFailed is empty because that row's two controls pass, so control falls through to the ok line and node exits 0 naturally. The window did not spend box time proving it empirically; whoever takes this bead should run it once as the first act, because a fail-open is exactly the kind of claim that deserves a reproduction rather than a reading.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7489 (merged 2026-08-04T11:46:14Z) — REOPENED. The fix correctly closes the concrete “every bar UNADJUDICATED” path, but the new fold does not implement its own stronger contract. `clock_run.cjs` sets `adjudicable` with `names.length > 0 && unadj.length < names.length`, and `clock_readjudicate.cjs` uses `names.some(!unadjudicated)`: one adjudicated bar therefore makes a row reportable even when another published bar is UNADJUDICATED. The driver then exits 0 and says “every published bar adjudicated,” and the readjudicator admits that run into the reportable subset for every pair, including the unadjudicated one. Current `seam.assess` makes availability row-wide, so today's generated rows are uniform, but the persisted-data reader and advertised fail-closed contract must not rely on that incidental coupling. Require a nonempty bar set and zero unadjudicated bars in both places, and add the missing mixed-bar fixture/mutation proof. No duplicate bead: this is the exact fail-open owner and a one-condition completion of its acceptance.
Merged-PR audit follow-up for #7550 (2026-08-05). The mixed-bar rule is strict, but field presence is still fail-open in both exported seats: `rowAdjudication` filters on truthiness (`src[n].unadjudicated`), and `adjudicated` accepts `!bars[n].unadjudicated`. A persisted bar `{}` therefore yields driver `{adjudicable:true, ..., unadjudicatedWhy:"the run adjudicated no bar on this row at all"}` and reader `true`, verified directly against current main. This contradicts the PR's own absent-is-not-clean contract and matters especially in the reader whose datasets outlive the writer. Require an explicit clean verdict (`unadjudicated === false`) in both functions; treat a missing/null bar or missing flag as unadjudicated/invalid, and add the same absent-field fixture to both exported-function test blocks. Keep the fix to this Boolean contract—no dataset schema framework.
THIRD PASS, PR #7596. Reproduced against 57e0e68 BEFORE touching anything, as the bead requires: rowAdjudication({'h / r': {}}) returned {adjudicable:true, barCount:1, unadjudicatedBars:[], unadjudicatedWhy:'the run adjudicated no bar on this row at all'} — contradicting itself inside one returned object — and adjudicated/reportable both returned true on the same shape. A bar stored as null did not fail open in either seat: it THREW 'Cannot read properties of null'.

FIX. Both seats now require an explicit clean verdict. clock_run.cjs filters on !(src[n] && src[n].unadjudicated === false); clock_readjudicate.cjs asks !!bars[n] && bars[n].unadjudicated === false. unadjudicatedWhy gains a fallback naming a bar that carries no verdict. Two Boolean conditions, no schema framework, no dataset validator, no measurement/arm/threshold/dataset/published row touched.

ONE JUDGEMENT CALL BEYOND THE TWO CONDITIONS, flagged in the PR body for the mayor to reject if it reads as scope: the reader's printed verdict column moved to the same token (barRec.unadjudicated !== false). Left at !!, it would print 'clears its band' for a silent bar the subset beside it had just refused — the column/decision disagreement clock_readjudicate.cjs's own comment on that line says this bead is about. One token to revert.

NO PUBLISHED FIGURE MOVES, checked rather than assumed: every retained dataset carries an explicit boolean on every bar (14 files, 12 bars, 0 missing, 0 null), and the readjudicator's 137 lines of published output over data/clock-0qj9w/run{1,2}.json are byte-identical before and after.

GATES. clock_exit_path.test.cjs 119 passed exit 0 (111 before, 8 fixtures added: 4 per exported-function block, plus 2 in the driver's own reportabilitySelfTest). npm run test:script-helpers full chain exit 0. THREE mutation proofs, each seat certified independently — clock_run truthiness restored: exit 1, 4 red, all in the clock_run block while the readjudicate block stayed green; readjudicate truthiness restored: exit 1, 3 red, all in the readjudicate block while the clock_run block stayed green; printed column restored to !!: exit 1, 1 red on the source pin. Each mutation confirmed applied by git diff --stat AND grepping the token back out, each restore confirmed byte-identical. Each block also carries a non-vacuity case so none of it would pass on a rule that always returned false.
MAYOR RULING on the worker's flagged judgement call (2026-08-06): the printed verdict column moving to 'unadjudicated !== false' is IN SCOPE, not creep. clock_readjudicate.cjs's own comment on that exact line names rf2-y7mw7 as the owner of the column/decision disagreement, so the file itself declares that line part of this bead. Left at '!!', the reader prints 'clears its band' for a silent bar the reportable subset beside it has just refused - a verdict that contradicts the decision printed next to it, which is precisely the fail-open class this bead exists to close. Keep the token. Mutation proof C already pins it.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7596 (merged 2026-08-06T05:54:18Z) — REOPENED exact owner. The explicit-field repair is correct for verdict keys that exist, but the advertised "every published bar" rule is still not total over the published bar set. At merge commit e35b4a85e9dde4809d6492b0f20c5c591fd44e92, `adjudicated(row)` enumerates only `Object.keys(row.seamTask.rows)`. A direct pure-layer probe with two published `barTask` bars (`h / r`, `h / u`) but only one verdict key (`h / r: {unadjudicated:false}`) returns `adjudicated:true` and `reportable:true`; the missing `h / u` verdict is never examined, so that pair's magnitude enters the reportable subset. The driver-side `rowAdjudication` has the same blind spot because it receives only the verdict map. This is the same absent-is-not-clean fail-open, not a new architecture. Make the actual published/expected bar keys authoritative and require one explicit-clean verdict for each; add a missing-key fixture distinct from the landed present-`{}` and null-value fixtures, including the persisted reader seat. Keep it a bounded key-set comparison, not a schema framework.
close_reason: SHIPPED in PR #7596 (merged). Both exported seats now require an explicit unadjudicated === false; a missing/null bar or missing flag is treated as unadjudicated. Reproduction on unmodified main confirmed the bead verbatim, and found beyond it that a null bar THREW rather than failing open, because truthiness dereferences the record before testing it. Three independent mutation proofs, each seat separately: restoring clock_run.cjs truthiness redded 4/119 in its own block while the readjudicate block stayed GREEN, and vice versa 3/119 — that separation is what makes the pair trustworthy rather than one blanket mutation certifying both. The readjudicator's 137 lines of published output over data/clock-0qj9w/run{1,2}.json are byte-identical before and after, so no published figure moved. The printed verdict column moving to the same token is in scope by the file's own comment, which names this bead as the owner of that disagreement.

title: hicasso: implement h/reg-state — the instance-key sugar (explicit-key ruling, 2026-08-04)
description:
IMPLEMENT h/reg-state — the instance-key sugar, per the 2026-08-04 ruled design (3 designs, 3 adversarial reviews, unanimous synthesis on the epic; operator ruled the feature INTO v0, amending HD-009). Bench lane.

THE SURFACE (exact; do not grow it):
1. (h/reg-state ::concern {:default v}) — a plain .cljc FUNCTION (not a macro). One namespace-qualified concern keyword; {:default v} is the ONLY option; unknown options refused loudly at registration. It mints, as ORDINARY core artefacts (no new runtime state, no hooks, no context — nothing for the anti-regression fence to catch):
   • parametric sub: (sub [::concern ikey]) -> (get-in db [:ui ::concern ikey] default)
   • concern-named setter event: [::concern ikey v] -> assoc-in
   • the documented path [:ui ::concern ikey] (the tier: ONE app-space conventional root, concern-first; per-frame free because app-db is per-frame; NEVER an :rf/* app-db root — Conventions two-partition doctrine).
2. Clear is a FRAMEWORK-NAMED EVENT, not a value sentinel: [::h/clear ::concern ikey] restores the default by REMOVING the entry (dissoc-in; empty concern maps pruned). The value-sentinel variant (::h/clear in v position) is REJECTED by the ruling — a keyword-valued concern could silently dissoc.
3. Loud refusals: nil or non-(keyword|string|number|vector-of-these) instance keys refuse at read AND write with :rf.error/hicasso-state-bad-key naming the concern — converting the guide's silent every-instance-shares pitfall into a loud error. Registration refuses a non-namespaced concern kw and unknown options.
4. (h/child-key k part) => (if (vector? k) (conj k part) [k part]) — the one pure composition helper for widget-in-widget nesting.

WITNESSES (unit + DOM, bench lane): two instances of one widget with distinct ikeys are independent; same ikey shares (and that is stated as correct); [::h/clear ...] restores default and removes the entry (db shape asserted, pruning included); bad-key refusal fires on nil and on a map key, naming the concern; frames isolated (two frames, same concern+ikey, independent state); h/child-key induction (nested widget forms [parent-key part] and deep-nests conj); HD-028 memo bail-out unaffected by fresh-but-equal key vectors (value equality row). Register-twice behaviour: re-registration with a different :default refuses (or last-wins with a loud warn — pick the stricter, state it).

TAUGHT RULES the implementation does NOT police (they land in the guide bead, but your docstrings state them in one line each): domain ids first; entity-qualified id VALUES ({:id [:order/id 42]}) when one widget serves multiple entity types (bare-id cross-entity bleed); placement-like concerns key by placement, value-like by entity; "if it would be a good React :key, it is a good instance key" (SSR determinism); graduation to named domain events when an occurrence means more than an assignment.

FENCES: bench lane only (front/ or arm1/ as fits — likely a new front/state.cljc consumed by both); no spec/* edits; no implementation/core edits (reg-sub/reg-event are consumed, not modified); the SSR payload obligation is NOT this bead (sibling witness bead); coordinate with any in-flight bead touching front/ files. Docstrings carry the determinism rule and the tier statement.

title: hicasso SSR: the Node render entry must open the adoption window around renderToString (presence ships ::h/mounting overrides)
description:
PREDICTED by the rf2-2rtt6.84 worker, then MEASURED by rf2-2rtt6.86 and pinned
as a corpus row + a red-when-fixed witness rather than left as an argument.

THE DEFECT. `arm1/presence.cljs` starts a child at `:mounting`
(`(react/useState presence/initial)`) and applies that child's `::h/mounting`
attribute overrides for as long as it is in that phase. The SSR entry renders
with no adoption window open — it cannot open one, see below — so the server
HTML ships the ENTER appearance: the class (and, in the shapes that use one, the
`opacity: 0` style) an animation is about to move off.

rf2-2rtt6.84 makes the hydrating client's FIRST pass render those same children
`:present` instead — born-present under an open adoption window, its clause 3.
Server markup and client first pass then disagree, and React reports a hydration
mismatch on every presence-managed node. That is exactly the class rf2-2rtt6.87's
X-rows exist to catch, and it is better caught here.

MEASURED. `implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/ssr/fixtures.cljs`
carries a `presence-mounting` corpus row whose children declare `::h/mounting
{:class "toast--enter"}`; the baked fixture contains `toast--enter` twice.
`the-server-render-ships-presences-mounting-overrides` in
`ssr/entry_cljs_test.cljs` asserts that, with a non-vacuity control that the
tray rendered its children at all. The row is written to go RED when the repair
lands — its docstring says to delete it and assert the opposite.

THE REPAIR, AND WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN .86. One line: `renderToString` in
`ssr/entry.cljs` must run between `runtime/open-adoption-window!` and
`runtime/close-adoption-window!`. NEITHER FUNCTION EXISTS ON MAIN — both are in
rf2-2rtt6.84's PR #7469, still open at the time .86 was written. A call to a var
that does not exist does not compile, and guessing at one is how two beads come
to race one file. So .86 named the gap in `ssr/entry.cljs`'s docstring (§The one
thing this entry does not do yet) and filed this.

BLOCKED ON: rf2-2rtt6.84 merging.

ALSO CHECK WHEN WIRING IT: #7469 puts the hydrated root's shape in one place
(`mount/tree`, keyed off `:hydrated?`) — a Fragment carrying the
adoption-window closer beside the app, because React reconciles a root by its
top element and a bare provider tore the adopted tree down. The SSR entry builds
its own root shape today (`(mount/provider frame … (codec/root-element …))`);
confirm it agrees with `mount/tree`'s, and prefer calling that once it exists.

FENCES: bench lane. No implementation/ssr or ssr-ring edits.
notes:
MAYOR 2026-08-04: dispatched and STOPPED CLEANLY at the condition the brief named. All three artefacts the repair touches (ssr/entry.cljs, ssr/entry_cljs_test.cljs, ssr/fixtures.cljs) are new files in OPEN PR #7470 and absent from main -- git ls-tree -r origin/main | grep hicasso/ssr/ returns 0. Nothing was edited; no worktree was created. SEQUENCED behind #7470: re-dispatch once that merges, branching off main.

THREE THINGS THE STOPPED WORKER ESTABLISHED, so the next dispatch does not re-derive them.

1. THE REPAIR IS NOT ONE LINE. ssr/entry.cljs does not require arm1.runtime at all. It needs: the require added, (rt/open-adoption-window!) before renderToString, and (rt/close-adoption-window!) in the EXISTING try/finally that already wraps destroy-frame!. The close belongs in the finally specifically because a render that throws must not leave the process permanently adopting -- which is what close-adoption-window!'s own docstring warns about.

2. THE mount/tree ROOT-SHAPE NOTE RESOLVES TO 'DO NOTHING'. arm1/mount.cljs tree is defn- (private). Its non-hydrated branch returns exactly (provider (:frame handle) (codec/root-element (:frame handle) hiccup)), and entry.cljs already builds (mount/provider frame (codec/root-element frame hiccup)). The shapes ALREADY AGREE. Calling tree would require widening a deliberately-private var whose docstring says the one-place arrangement is the point, for zero behavioural gain -- and would risk the byte-for-byte fence on the ordinary render path. CONFIRM AGREEMENT, DO NOT WIDEN.

3. THE WITNESS QUESTION IS SETTLED, and it was my brief that was ambiguous rather than the bead. The witness the-server-render-ships-presences-mounting-overrides currently asserts (str/includes? html 'toast--enter') and (= 2 (count (re-seq ...))), with a non-vacuity control on 'toast 0'/'toast 1'. Its own failure message says 'delete this row and assert the opposite'. That means DELETE THE ASSERTION OF THE BUG AND ASSERT THE OPPOSITE -- i.e. INVERT the row to zero occurrences, keeping the control. It does not mean remove the witness: a deleted witness protects nothing, an inverted one is a regression guard.

CORROBORATION, already on main and independent of both workers who reported it: runtime/adopting?'s docstring (arm1/runtime.cljs, landed in #7469) states the requirement itself -- 'A server render entry opens the same window around its own renderToString, so the two halves of an SSR route answer this identically.' Three workers, three routes, one conclusion. The diagnosis is not in doubt.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7470 (2026-08-04) — landed chronology refresh.

PR #7469 / rf2-2rtt6.84 is already on main before #7470's rebased commits, and open-adoption-window!, close-adoption-window!, and the hydrated root-shape helper now exist. Yet the landed entry still calls renderToString without the server adoption window and its test still asserts toast--enter as a red-when-fixed defect. The prerequisite is satisfied: wire the window around the server render, share/verify the root shape, invert the witness, and remove the stale "functions do not exist on main" prose.

title: hicasso SSR: :rf/render-hash is DEGENERATE for an interpreted root — the hydration-mismatch instrument is fail-open
description:
MEASURED BY rf2-2rtt6.86 while building the SSR Node render entry, and pinned
there by `the-render-hash-is-degenerate-for-an-interpreted-root` in
`implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/ssr/entry_cljs_test.cljs`
so it cannot quietly become load-bearing.

THE FINDING. Spec 011 §Hydration-mismatch detection carries `:rf/render-hash` —
a structural hash of the RENDER TREE, computed server-side and recomputed by the
client at hydrate so a divergence is caught rather than rendered. The framework's
own door is `re-frame.ssr.hash/render-tree-hash` (via
`ssr-ring/lifecycle/render-document-hash`), and it works because a
hiccup->hiccup substrate hands it the WHOLE tree.

Hicasso does not. Its root hiccup is `[<minted head> {props}]` and the tree is
walked INSIDE React, so what reaches the hash is one vector whose head is a
function — and `canonical-edn` renders every function identically. MEASURED: the
dogfood screen (`[dogfood-collector/screen {}]`) and the ~1,200-element Conduit
feed page (`[large-template/page {}]`) BOTH hash `83b865f8`. A root whose hiccup
is ordinary markup hashes differently (`04cc3cdb`), which is the non-vacuity
control — the hash function is fine; the interpreted root defeats it.

CONSEQUENCE. Server and client would compute the same constant and always agree,
so the instrument never fires: a FAIL-OPEN gate of exactly the class this repo
has been closing all week. It is not wrong today (nothing computes a client-side
hash yet — that is rf2-2rtt6.84/.87's half), but it will be silently vacuous the
moment hydration verification is switched on.

WHY rf2-2rtt6.86 DID NOT FIX IT. R0: that bead does not invent a payload byte,
and a real repair is a SERVER AND CLIENT contract — whatever normalisation the
server hashes, the client must reproduce exactly, and inventing one server-side
ahead of the client half would make every page a mismatch instead of a
non-check.

THE WORK. Decide what Hicasso's render-tree hash should be over, and land both
ends together. Candidates named but not chosen: (a) normalise minted heads to
their `displayName` before hashing, so the hash is at least a function of WHICH
screen rendered (cheap, still shallow); (b) have the runtime record the walked
tree's shape during the render and hash that (deep, costs a server-side
accumulator); (c) accept the shallow hash and say so in the spec, relying on
React's own hydration-mismatch reporting for the deep case. (c) is a legitimate
answer and should be argued rather than defaulted into.

FENCES: whatever lands must keep the payload path R0-clean — the bytes stay
the framework's.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7484 (merged 2026-08-04T09:47:51Z) — USER-GUIDE CONSEQUENCE. The rewritten draft-guide/10-server-side-rendering.md says the client verifies its first tree against the structural render hash and that disagreement raises :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch. That reads as a reliable deep parity guard, but this exact open owner proves Hicasso's interpreted root makes :rf/render-hash degenerate: different screens share 83b865f8, and the #7480 witness explicitly refuses to lean on it. Until this owner chooses and lands a real hash contract (or explicitly accepts the shallow hash), true up the guide to state the limit and distinguish the fail-open hash comparison from React's real onRecoverableError mismatch report. No new bead: rf2-2rtt6.91 is the exact owner.
DELIVERED via PR #7510 (green: 50 success / 33 skipped / 0 fail).

OUTCOME 1 OF THE THREE: THE SPEC ALREADY ANSWERED IT. Spec 011
§Hydration-mismatch detection tiers detection BY RENDER-TREE
REPRESENTATION, not by adapter brand. The hash channel is the HICCUP
tier's (Reagent, reagent-slim — pure fns returning a hashable data
tree). Every root that reaches React as an ELEMENT is in the adoption
tier: the compiled donor-substrate root ('no hashable client
render-tree ... the hash channel does not apply'), a native UIx root
(trace carries 'no hash'), and a Freehand root (§Hydration on the
Freehand paved path: 'Verification is React's own adoption, and it is
bounded exactly as the compiled and native tiers' is'). 011 says of
those tiers verbatim: they 'deliberately carry NO such hash'.
re-frame.ssr.boot's own docstring names Freehand explicitly:
'Compiled view — Freehand ... likewise NO :render-tree-fn'.

So Hicasso was emitting where the spec says not to. The fix was to STOP
EMITTING, not to hash better.

ON CANDIDATE (c): it is HALF the spec's answer, and the weaker half.
(c) said 'accept the shallow hash and say so in the spec, relying on
React's reporting for the deep case'. The reliance-on-adoption half IS
the spec's answer. The keep-a-shallow-hash half is NOT — the spec
carries NONE. A degenerate value is worse than an absent one: an absent
key cannot be mistaken for evidence, a constant one is a fail-open gate
wearing the shape of a check.

CANDIDATES (a) AND (b) ARE BOTH UNAVAILABLE, for one shared reason.
(a) normalise minted heads to displayName — reverses rf2-jsa2ml's
ruling (the #fn[] token exists because no fn .toString is stable across
JVM and CLJS, and dropping fn identity is what stops the HICCUP tier
firing a spurious mismatch on every page), and would still only say
WHICH screen rendered: every divergence WITHIN a screen — the entire
class this instrument exists to catch — would still compare equal.
(b) accumulate the walked tree server-side — needs the client to
reproduce the accumulation byte-for-byte, i.e. re-deriving the hiccup
tier under a substrate built not to have one.

MEASUREMENT RE-DERIVED, NOT QUOTED. 83b865f8 is not a Hicasso fact: it
is the FNV-1a of the canonical-EDN string '[#fn[] {}]', and ANY
[<some fn> {}] root takes it. Reproduced on the JVM with two throwaway
fns written for the purpose; a markup root gave 9e28d7ef as the
non-vacuity control.

WHAT LANDED. entry.cljs stops computing the hash, stamping
data-rf-render-hash, and passing one to build-payload.
payload-policy/build-payload now OMITS :rf/render-hash on a nil hash —

:string', NOT '[:maybe :string]', so a present-and-nil key is not a
legal spelling of absence. The 'three always-present keys' docstring was
drift; the spec's payload table has said '(optional)' throughout.
Spec 011 gains the SERVER end of the tier rule — it had stated the split
almost entirely as a client-side 'do not pass :render-tree-fn', which is

The draft guide's false structural-hash-verify claim is trued up — the
merged-PR-audit-of-#7484 obligation recorded on this bead.

said in its own docstring it should go red the day the defect was

title: hicasso SSR: the Node render entry — renderToString of the existing runtime, fixture bake, live dogfood demo
description:
THE NODE RENDER ENTRY + FIXTURE BAKE + LIVE DEMO — one renderer, run in two places. From the 2026-08-04 SSR design programme (consensus on the epic): the server engine is the EXISTING Hicasso runtime under Node react-dom/server renderToString — hydration parity by construction, no second renderer anywhere.

WHY THIS IS SAFE (verified in the programme): every shell already passes getServerSnapshot (arm1/runtime.cljs:1540/:1595), so under renderToString React never subscribes, every sub read is the mutation-free cold probe, commits/effects never run — the render is HD-002's abandoned render by design, leaving zero durable registration (the ledger discipline holds). react-dom 19.2.0 ships server.node.js (pinned); the runtime already loads under Node on every PR.

THE WORK (bench lane):
1. The render entry: a Node namespace that (a) makes a per-request gensym frame, (b) seeds app-db via the framework doors (:initial-events / snapshot-in), (c) renders (provider frame (codec/root-element frame hiccup)) via renderToString, (d) builds the payload with the FRAMEWORK'S OWN bytes — ssr apply-policy + build-payload + escape-edn-script-body producing the #__rf_payload EDN script — nothing Hicasso-specific in the payload path (R0), (e) destroys the frame after render (destroy-frame! — lifecycle verified sound, frame.cljc:2076-2091; no per-request leak).
2. Determinism: same bundle + same snapshot means byte-identical HTML (SHA-256 double-render check in the driver). Verified in the programme: no useId anywhere, no randomness on the render path (the lane's seeded LCG stands), comment separators deterministic; renderToString runs synchronously so module-level render context is sound per-request. NO streaming — renderToPipeableStream is out of scope, per adversarial review.
3. The BAKE: a driver producing static HTML+payload fixtures in the existing SSR-testbed pattern (testbeds/ssr_basic bakes at build time — reuse the shape), for the witness bead's X-rows and as the standing conformance corpus (feature census over the dogfood + tier-1 shapes).
4. The LIVE DEMO driver: a minimal node script that serves the dogfood screen per-request (frame, render, payload, HTML out). PAGE-LEVEL, bench-lane, explicitly NOT a production host: Spec 011's HTTP response contract (accumulator, cookies, redirects, CRLF fail-fast) stays ssr-ring's; this driver exists so live per-request Hicasso SSR is DEMONSTRABLE at the P2 sitting (the adapters demo live SSR; Hicasso must too).
5. Build id: FIRST try to carry this on existing node-build infrastructure (:freehand-bench-node pattern, shadow-cljs.edn:1067); mint :hicasso-ssr-node ONLY if needed — a shadow-cljs.edn edit is HOT-ZONE and must be sequenced by the mayor, stated in the PR.
6. defhost regions honour the :ssr policy (sibling bead) server-side: :client-only renders nothing; {:fallback ...} renders the fallback hiccup.

FENCES: bench lane (+ possibly one sequenced shadow-cljs.edn hot-zone edit). No implementation/ssr edits — its payload fns are consumed, not modified. No ssr-ring edits. The production host story is NOT this bead: it is priced and ruled at the P2/graduation sitting (see the ruling-prep bead).
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7470 (2026-08-04) — correctness / implementation-quality finding, reproduced on the landed tree.

The bake manifest and console/live metrics label JavaScript UTF-16 code-unit counts (string.length) as bytes. npm run --silent ssr:hicasso-bake succeeds, but filesystem evidence contradicts every documentBytes claim: dogfood-snapshot 3101 claimed vs 3119 UTF-8 bytes (body 2359 vs 2375), dogfood-initial-events 1798 vs 1806, conduit-feed 79070 vs 79072, presence-mounting 452 vs 454, and defhost-ssr-policy 485 vs 491 (body 152 vs 156). payloadBytes happens to agree because those payloads are ASCII. sha256 is correct because it explicitly hashes UTF-8.

Repair the driver to use Buffer.byteLength(value, "utf8") (or the written file's stat size) for manifest fields and all B log claims, including the live-server response log. Add a non-ASCII automated witness that the manifest's document/body/payload byte counts equal the actual files. Preserve the existing deterministic double-render and SHA-256 checks.
close_reason: RE-CLOSED by the mayor 2026-08-04 after a silent revert to OPEN — the third such revert this session, all caught by the per-tick closure re-check the method's tracker-revert bullet requires. The work landed: PR #7470 merged. Verified against the tree, not memory: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/ssr/ exists on main with entry.cljs, entry_cljs_test.cljs, node.cljs, driver.cjs and the fixtures; the render entry seeds a per-request gensym frame, renders through mount/provider, takes the payload from the framework's own bytes, and destroys the frame in a finally; determinism is asserted by byte-for-byte double render; npm run ssr:hicasso-bake and ssr:hicasso-serve are wired. No shadow-cljs.edn edit was needed — it rode :freehand-bench-node via --config-merge. Follow-ups from that work are tracked separately as rf2-2rtt6.91 (degenerate :rf/render-hash), rf2-2rtt6.92 (retire the server walk) and rf2-2rtt6.94 (the adoption window, PR #7471 in flight).

title: hicasso SSR: the hydration door — hydrate-root!, reaper 0->4, born-present, HD-019/HD-028 riders
description:
THE HYDRATION DOOR — the client half every SSR route shares. From the 2026-08-04 SSR design programme (3 audits, 3 designs, 3 adversarial reviews; consensus architecture recorded on the epic). Bench lane only.

THE WORK (implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/):
1. hydrate-root! beside root! (arm1/mount.cljs / runtime.cljs — root! is createRoot().render only today). Call hydrateRoot PLAIN — NO flushSync: adversarial review F4 verified no in-tree code forces hydration synchronously; adopt the spine's own closer pattern (spine.cljs:1127-1145, :1245-1251 — a closer COMPONENT's passive effect closes the adoption window). Return the same handle shape as root!.
2. Entry reaper 0→4 ms: arm1's provisional-entry reaper is still setTimeout 0 and would race hydrateRoot's passive subscribe — the exact class rf2-2rtt6.71 fixed in the spine. Move to 4 ms with the margin-not-contract prose; no caller may rely on it (spine precedent text).
3. Presence born-present under adoption: presence-managed nodes hydrate in their PRESENT state (no enter animation replay; also fixes server HTML carrying ::h/mounting opacity-0 overrides). Scoped as adoption behaviour, not a new render mode (charter one-mode law respected).
4. HD-019 rider: hydration NEVER converges controlled text; the defaultValue invariant row extends to the hydrated path (server HTML for a controlled input must satisfy what hydrateRoot demands — witness it).
5. HD-028 rider: the memo wrapper must not fake adoption — body-run accounting must be real (counted), never memo-inferred.
6. Instrument visibility (adversarial F6): the body-run counter used by the later X-witnesses is DCE'd goog.DEBUG-gated today; land an always-on cheap counter (or a declared dev-build witness row) so the witness build can actually see body runs. Decide and document which.

WITNESSES IN THIS BEAD: unit/DOM rows for the door itself (hydrate a small fixture; adoption completes via the closer; reaper does not detach the adopted subscription; presence born-present; controlled defaultValue row hydrated). The full X1-X5 dogfood spike is the SEPARATE witness bead and depends on this one.

FENCES: bench lane only; no spec/*, no implementation/core edits (spine.cljs:3031 already passes getServerSnapshot both-args — verified three times; no core change needed). Parallel-safe vs the defhost-policy bead (different files) — coordinate on runtime.cljs if both touch it.
notes:
Merged-PR audit #7465 follow-up (2026-08-04): the docs-only ruling record is coherent, but the live bench-lane namespace docstring at implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/shapes/ordinary.cljs:66-68 still says "SSR is out of v0". This hydration-door bead is the first in-scope owner for the reversed posture. When landing the door, reconcile that sentence with the 2026-08-04 HD-020 ruling while preserving the true .cljc-compatibility constraint. Repo-wide stale-phrase census otherwise found only the deliberately retained historical ruling text; the EP index omission already has exact owner rf2-2rtt6.90.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7469 (2026-08-04) — REOPENED for two concrete completion gaps.

1. THE HYDRATION-MISMATCH CAPTURE ENDS BEFORE HYDRATION. hydrate_dom_cljs_test.cljs:183 capture-console! installs the window error listener and console.error spy, calls f inside try, and restores both in finally. Every caller passes only the synchronous mount/hydrate-root! call. That door deliberately returns while rt/adopting? is still true, and adopted! waits for later timers and the passive closer. The listeners are therefore gone throughout the concurrent hydration interval in which React reports mismatches; the later assertions that @captured is empty cannot see those failures. Two hydration rows do not call the helper at all. This contradicts the PR claim that every row watches both React 19 default channels and invalidates the premise open rf2-2rtt6.93 records for X2. description:

So the ship-bar consistency edit has no owner, and picking one of the two texts as authoritative is a governance act on an operator-owned standard. The mayor declined to make it.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. The P2 fork ruling is pending and both HD-013 advisory passes are recorded on this bead. A programme whose written bar and operative bar disagree cannot have its fork adjudicated cleanly against either: a stop or a continue ruled against <= 1.0x Reagent means something different from one ruled against <= 1.10x direct UIx. The adversarial pass independently found that K3 is the only criterion the programme can currently adjudicate and that the fork question "is not currently answerable on its own terms"; this is one of the reasons why.

title: MEASURE: the per-keystroke row has NO band-supplying control, so a clean run still yields an UNADJUDICATED magnitude
description:
RAISED by rf2-0qj9w's quiet window, 2026-08-04 (PR #7459), where this was the finding rather than a side note.

THE GAP. clock_run.cjs's keystroke row is gated by ctl-50ms, which burns a fixed 50 ms inside its own handler. That makes it an excellent CONTROL — it proves the instrument moves when the work moves, and it passed convincingly in the window (49.84 ms [49.43 - 50.27] of extra task time over 18 segment-rounds against a predicted >=40, and Event Timing interactions at duration p50 48.0 ms over n=180 against a predicted >=48). But control/floor reads (F + 50)/F, which MOVES WITH F. It is therefore not a pair whose true ratio is a property of the page, and the-candidates-clock.md sec 6.2's band is defined on exactly such a pair. The driver knows this and says so: it prints 'band NOT AVAILABLE on this row' and labels all three bars UNADJUDICATED.

WHY THAT IS DECISIVE RATHER THAN COSMETIC. Under sec 6.2's rule a magnitude whose distance from 1.0 is inside the band is instrument-limited, and a bar with NO band is not adjudicated at all. So the per-keystroke row cannot produce a publishable magnitude no matter how clean the run is — and rf2-0qj9w's window produced a maximally clean one. Every gate the row has cleared: both controls, arm-order guard reportable, canonical DOM identical (9320 B), 0 unverified of 756, the repaired four-field witness reconciling 540 keys sent as 466 observed + 74 censored, and a recompute census reading exactly p0/cell x100 + p0/draft x4 on all three substrate arms and no subscriptions at all on every floor arm. It was still unpublishable. This is a property of the rig, not of the box or the arms, and no scheduling fixes it.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT OBSTRUCTION AT THE SAME PLACE. The row's smallest non-zero per-sample delta was 0.146 ms over 1003 distinct values, while the candidate/Reagent separation is 0.052 ms per sample on raw TaskDuration — about a third of one grid step. Even given a band, this witness may not have the resolution to state a sign. A median over many samples can resolve below the grain, but the driver's own ranges agree that it does not here: every bar straddles 1.0. Any repair should say what separation the row is powered to detect, not merely give it a band.

NOTE THE CONSEQUENCE FOR WHAT IS ALREADY PUBLISHED: the-candidates-clock.md sec 5's figures predate the band rule and would be labelled UNADJUDICATED if re-taken today. rf2-0qj9w's window banded sec 5 accordingly (for the separate reason that its witness was the superseded one-field one) but published no replacement.

CANDIDATE REPAIRS, none tried, and choosing between them is likely a ruling:

1. Give the row a three-point control on an axis it actually varies, in the idiom of docs/design/hicasso/studio/a-control-that-differences-the-constant-away.md — the construction that differences the additive constant away rather than assuming it cancels. The keystroke row's natural axis is the number of subscriptions a keystroke dirties (the witness already localises 100 cells + 4 fields), so arms dirtying 1 / 100 / 200 boundaries per keystroke are available on the page that exists.
2. Add a SECOND control alongside ctl-50ms whose ratio to the floor IS a page property — the simplest being a ctl-2x-style doubled page driven by a keystroke — purely to supply the band, leaving ctl-50ms as the sensitivity control. Note this inherits ctl-2x's additive-constant undershoot, which is rf2-jcm3p's open problem.
3. Rule that a paint-inclusive per-keystroke row is adjudicated by Event Timing rather than by the band — every arm reads 16.0 ms, one frame, and the honest published statement is 'indistinguishable, all three one frame' with the censoring published. That is arguably what sec 5 already says in prose, and it would make the taskNet bars diagnostics rather than magnitudes.

Option 3 costs nothing and may be the right answer: the row's job is to show the candidate is not over the frame budget, and it is not. Options 1 and 2 are instrument work.

SEQUENCING: this blocks any rebook of rf2-0qj9w's per-keystroke row. Rebooking the window without it buys another clean run and another UNADJUDICATED bar. rf2-jcm3p is the sibling gap on M1 (ctl-2x undershoots and no changed-set control reaches a mount) and is likewise held for a ruling; the two are the same shape and may want one ruling between them.

EVIDENCE: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/clock-0qj9w/run1.json on worker/window-0qj9w, re-adjudicable with clock_readjudicate.cjs — the clean keystroke run is on disk, so any repair can be adjudicated against real samples without a new window.

DO NOT DISPATCH AS IMPLEMENTATION until Mike has ruled which repair, for the same reason rf2-jcm3p carries that hold.
notes:
CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY by rf2-0qj9w's SECOND quiet window, 2026-08-04 (PR #7486, run2.json).

Reproduced exactly, on a different tree (070be81738) and a different box state. The keystroke row again cleared EVERY gate it has — ctl-50ms 49.84 ms [49.36 - 50.45] over 18 segment-rounds against predicted >=40; Event Timing p50 56.0 ms over n=180 against predicted >=48; arm-order guard reportable; canonical DOM identical 9320 B; 0 unverified of 756; the repaired four-field witness reconciling 540 keys pressed as 449 observed + 91 censored under the 16 ms floor, 60 sent on each of nine arms; the recompute census reading p0/cell x100 + p0/draft x4 on all three substrate arms and no subscriptions at all on every floor and control arm. And all three bars are UNADJUDICATED again, for exactly the reason this bead names.

TWO CLEAN RUNS, TWO IDLE BOXES, SAME UNPUBLISHABLE ROW. That settles the question this bead was raised on: the blocker is the rig, not the box, and no further scheduling can move it. This bead is the repair.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT LIMITER SHOWED UP ON THE SAME ROW and whoever designs the control should know it: the keystroke grain is 0.181 ms over 1002 distinct values, and the candidate-to-UIx separation is 0.043 ms — under a QUARTER of one grid step. So even given a band-supplying control, that pair is not resolved as to sign at this n. Candidate-to-Reagent is 0.277 ms, about 1.5 steps. A control alone may not be sufficient to make this row adjudicable; the design should say what n it needs.

RELATED DEFECT FILED: rf2-y7mw7 — the driver's exit code does not gate adjudication at all, so HCLOCK_ONLY=keystroke alone exits 0 and prints 'REPORTABLE: keystroke ... Publish those' for a row whose every bar is UNADJUDICATED. That is a separate fail-open from this bead's missing control, and it is what would let this gap actually bite.
RULING 2026-08-06 11:24 AUSEST (delegated dossier review, Mike 2026-08-06; operator-overturnable): REPAIR (3). The paint-inclusive per-keystroke row is adjudicated by EVENT TIMING, not by the sec-6.2 band.

VERIFIED BEFORE RULING: seam.cjs:416 prints 'band NOT AVAILABLE on this row' and both retained runs carry UNADJUDICATED with the (F+50)/F why-string verbatim; PRs #7459/#7486 both MERGED (2026-08-03/04); run1.json/run2.json + clock_readjudicate.cjs on disk under implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/; per-arm ET medians recomputed directly from the raw entries — every observed non-control interaction in BOTH runs sits in the 16 ms bucket (min=max=16 on hicasso, reagent-subs, uix-subs and every floor), ctl-50ms at 48 (run1) / 56 (run2) ms median, so the instrument demonstrably moves when the work moves and the arms are indistinguishable at its resolution; run1 granularity floor exactly 0.146 ms as recorded. Dossier's Codex section independently reached (3) from the landed evidence; no dissent to adjudicate.

WHY NOT (1)/(2): a band does not survive the resolution obstruction — arm separations 0.043-0.277 ms/key against a 0.146-0.181 ms per-sample grid, every TaskDuration bar straddling 1.0 in both runs. (1) is new apparatus for a magnitude no current decision needs (measurement gold-plating at pre-alpha); (2) imports rf2-jcm3p's additive-constant undershoot. Both remain available ONLY if a decision ever turns on a pre-declared sub-frame effect size — at that point power the dedicated experiment for that effect before choosing its control.

RE-ADJUDICATION PUBLISHES (from the two on-disk runs via clock_readjudicate.cjs — NO new window): 'On this four-field/100-cell witness, Hicasso, Reagent-on-subs and UIx-on-subs are indistinguishable at Event Timing's resolution; every observed interaction was one frame (16.0 ms, both runs)', with per-arm censoring published (run1: 466 observed + 74 censored of 540 keys; run2: 449 + 91). POWERED-TO-DETECT RIDER, mandatory beside it: Event Timing resolves 8 ms buckets above a 16 ms floor, so the row detects only differences crossing a frame-bucket boundary; the arms' sub-frame separations sit two orders below that, and the diagnostic TaskDuration bars straddle 1.0 at this n — do NOT state the implementations are equal below that resolution; indistinguishable-at-one-frame is not a measured microsecond tie.

STUDIO PAGE (the-candidates-clock.md sec 5): relabel the TaskDuration/taskNet bars DIAGNOSTIC - UNADJUDICATED (never magnitudes); replace the superseded one-field-witness figures with the repaired-witness re-adjudication above; sec 5's existing 'indistinguishable, and all three are one frame' prose becomes the row's published verdict rather than a caveat. DRIVER: two explicit dispositions — 'magnitude' rows still require every published bar to carry a band; this row becomes a 'responsiveness-regime' row, reportable ONLY when key accounting, recompute census, arm-order/DOM gates and both fixed-work controls pass (meshes with rf2-y7mw7's exit-code fail-open fix, tracked separately).

UNBLOCKS the rf2-0qj9w rebook: the per-keystroke half is now re-adjudication of the on-disk runs; rebook a live window only for what still needs live rows (the current-tree M1 re-take). POSTURE, as this bead's ruling: control-refused or band-less rows publish as regimes/frame-statements, not magnitudes; instrument upgrades happen only where a decision turns on the magnitude. The same posture is proposed on sibling rf2-jcm3p; its reviewer rules it there. Hold released — dispatchable as implementation.

SEC-5 RELABELLED (the-candidates-clock.md, italic dated parentheticals, this page's own idiom): the TaskDuration/taskNet bars are DIAGNOSTIC - UNADJUDICATED, never magnitudes; the superseded one-field-witness reading is replaced by the repaired-witness re-adjudication in a new banner carrying the per-arm table, the key accounting, the verdict and the mandatory powered-to-detect rider; and sec 5's existing 'indistinguishable, and all three are one frame' prose is promoted to the row's PUBLISHED VERDICT rather than a caveat. rows-re-adjudicated sec 4's keystroke row relabelled in that page's strikethrough idiom.

title: clock_run.cjs REFUSES on main on every row tried (M1 and bulk300), and destroys the ex-info that would say why
description:
BLOCKER FOUND WHILE TAKING rf2-2rtt6.72's CLOCK HALF. It blocks the mount
row of rf2-2rtt6.72 and of every other bead that needs `clock_run.cjs`'s M1.

## The symptom

    HCLOCK_ONLY=M1 node implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/clock_run.cjs
    ;; HCLOCK ready
    [clock] row M1
    [clock] FAILED: M1: page.evaluate: vj
    exit 1

It dies in round 0, immediately after `HCLOCK ready`, in the first
`page.evaluate` of `runRow` — the `enterSegment` / `plan` / `canon` /
`prepare` sequence at clock_run.cjs:885-899. No `[clock] PAGE ERROR:` line
is printed, so the throw is a `page.evaluate` REJECTION and not a
`pageerror`.

## What has been ruled out, by running it rather than by reasoning

1. **Not the caller's tree.** Reproduced on pristine `origin/main`
   `1ce64c06a2`, `arm1/runtime.cljs` blob `9f3d42be7b3aa529e8fc6ef8531262ceb4d65f1a`
   — the shipped blob.
2. **Not PR #7416's `root-element` change.** `arm1/mount.cljs` reverted to
   `1c4d395374^` (the `codec/as-element` `render!` that predates the
   frame-prop landing) fails identically, same message, exit 1.
3. The bulk rows are a separate question and are being taken separately;
   this bead is about M1.

## The second, compounding fault: the message is destroyed

`vj` is not a symbol from this lane. In the `:advanced` bundle
(`implementation/out/hicasso-clock/main.js`) `vj` is
**`cljs.core/ExceptionInfo`** — its neighbours are `wj` = `ex-info` and
`xj` = `ex-data`:

    function vj(a,b){var c=Error(a);this.message=a;this.data=b; ... }
    vj.prototype.__proto__=Error.prototype;
    function wj(a,b){return new vj(a,b)}
    function xj(a){return a instanceof vj?a.data:null}

So the page threw a CLJS `ex-info` — almost certainly one of the arm's own
`fail!` calls, which carry an `:rf.error/*` id, a `:where`, a `:recovery`
and an ex-data map — and **the driver reported its minified TYPE NAME and
nothing else**. Every field that would identify the fault was discarded at
the boundary.

This is the same class PRs #7448/#7450 closed across four bench runners:
a condition that reports a token instead of the fault. Here it is worse
than a silent exit-0, because the run DOES fail loudly and still hands the
reader nothing to act on. An `ex-info` crossing `page.evaluate` needs its
`ex-message` and `ex-data` serialized — Playwright cannot do it, because
the value is not a plain `Error` and `ex-info`'s `toString` is `pr-str` of
a `#error {...}` map that minifies away.

## Suggested shape of the fix (not prescriptive)

Have the in-page entry points catch, and re-throw as a plain `js/Error`
carrying `(ex-message e)` and `(pr-str (ex-data e))`, or park the fault on
`window.HCLOCK` for the driver to read back. Then re-run M1 and diagnose
the ACTUAL fault, which is still unknown and is the real subject of this
bead. **Fixing the reporting is not fixing M1** — it is what makes M1
diagnosable.

## Repro

    node implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/clock_run.cjs --selftest   # exit 0, 20+17+12 checks ok
    HCLOCK_ONLY=M1 node implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/clock_run.cjs  # exit 1

Box was quiet throughout (occupancy 2.3-3.0%, zero java, no other worker,
no open PR), so this is not a load artefact. `clock_run.cjs` blob
`0bdb9eaa6a9559775b4a67471a8a1c34c65aca9c`.
notes:
FIXED — PR #7456 (branch worker/clockerr-029ed). Both stages.

STAGE 1 (the deliverable). lane.cljs gains `legible-doors` / `describe-throw`:
a front door's functions are wrapped once, at construction, ON THE PAGE SIDE
where ex-message/ex-data are still in vocabulary, and any throw leaves as a
plain js/Error naming the door, the :rf.error id and the ex-data. Nothing is
special-cased to an id. clock_run.cjs also carries a `trace.step`, so a death
names the round and segment (and inside the sample loop the sample and arm) —
the rotating segment order no longer hides WHICH segment threw.

THE ERROR, as it now prints:
  [clock] FAILED: M1 at round 0, segment reagent-subs: page.evaluate: Error:
  enterSegment threw :rf.error/image-duplicate-id — rf/image assembly: id
  [:sub :p0/cell] is selected from 2 distinct source namespaces with different
  implementations within image nil ... — ex-data {:rf.error/id
  :rf.error/image-duplicate-id, :where rf/make-frame, :recovery
  :narrow-the-selection-or-rename-the-id, :reason "...", :image nil, :kind :sub,
  :id :p0/cell, :colliding-coordinates [{:ns "...p0-reagent-views"}
  {:ns "...clock-views"}]}

MUTATION PROOF, both directions. A known ex-info with a distinctive id thrown
from inside the first page.evaluate printed
  enterSegment threw :rf.error/mutation-probe-029ed — MUTATION PROBE rf2-029ed
  — ex-data {... :canary 4242, :seg "reagent-subs"}
i.e. id + message + every ex-data key crossed. Reverted byte-identically
(git grep for the probe is empty). A first probe attempt was refused by the
lane's own build door for `unreachable code` — that door working as designed.

REAL COUNT of front doors that swallowed ex-infos: FOUR, all the identical
`#js {...}` shape, so one line each against the shared helper — HCLOCK
(clock_app), HD8CLOCK (hd8_clock_app), C56CLOCK (shapes/census_clock_app),
HCHROME (chrome_app). All four fixed here. window.RETENTION
(retention_probe.cljs) is NOT this class and is left alone: it does not require
lane, and its one door is a heap census running no arm code.

STAGE 2 — THE ACTUAL FAULT, and it is not the runtime.
[:sub :p0/cell] is registered AT LOAD from TWO namespaces in this bundle:
p0-reagent-views/register! (the shared floor accessor every other row's arms
read) and clock-views/register-subs! (the same computation via v/cell-value,
behind the keystroke witness's recompute census). A second reg-sub from a
second namespace does NOT overwrite the first — the registrar keeps both,
tagged with provenance, and default image assembly refuses to let selection
order decide. The refusal is CORRECT. Introduced by bacb5dc4db (rf2-0qj9w,
2026-08-03), which added the second registration; the clock driver has been
dead on every row since that commit.

FIX: the override is made deliberate, through the mechanism the refusal itself
names — two composed images unioning to the whole store, the census-bearing
registration in the LATER one. That reproduces exactly the registry
register-subs!'s own docstring already describes (enter-segment! calls it on
every segment entry, for every row, so the census-bearing body was always the
intended survivor).

CONFIRMED BY THE HARNESS'S OWN WITNESS, not by argument: the keystroke row's
recompute census now reads `p0/cell x100, p0/draft x4` on ALL THREE substrate
arms and `no subscriptions at all` on every floor arm — validation.md's stated
104 layer-1 recomputes. That shape is only reachable if the census-instrumented
registration is the one the Reagent and UIx arms run.

The clock lane is unblocked: M1 and keystroke both run the full row end to end,
0 unverified writes, teardown clean.

NO MEASUREMENT TAKEN. No timing row published or amended, no figure quoted. The
two live runs were 1-round designs run to verify the driver RUNS; both exited 2
on the arm-order guard — the instrument correctly refusing a statistically
meaningless design.

GATES (all foreground to completion): test-fast-pr.sh 0 (PASS fast PR spine),
lint:js 0, test:hicasso-compile 0 (101 lane namespaces, zero warnings),
clock_run.cjs --selftest 0.
