title: skills/re-frame2/patterns/form-action.md is 3 corrections behind spec/Pattern-FormAction — including the fail-OPEN CSRF compare the spec names an anti-pattern
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-eane2 / rf2-bl8k7 / rf2-096js worker (PR for those three), OUTSIDE its fence. The skill leaf that projects Pattern-FormAction has not tracked any of the three corrections the spec page took across #7232 / #7347 / this PR, and one of the gaps is the exact security bug the spec page now lists as an anti-pattern.

SITES, all in skills/re-frame2/patterns/form-action.md:

1. FAIL-OPEN CSRF (worst). The skill's canonical handler still shows
   (and server? (not= (:csrf-token form-params) active-token)).
   spec/Pattern-FormAction §Anti-patterns: 'Comparing the submitted token against the session token with not= alone ... fails OPEN on a request with no session: active-token is nil, an attacker's token-less POST supplies nil, and the arm does not fire.' The spec's worked example uses
   (not (and (some? active-token) (= (:csrf-token form-params) active-token))).
   The skill ships the form the spec calls out. This is a copyable security example.

2. NO FIELD/ENVELOPE SPLIT. The skill still uses one AddToCartForm schema for the event :schema, the handler's m/explain, and the draft. That is the #7232 CORRECTNESS finding: a token-requiring schema 400s every hydrated-client submission in production (the handler's arm is ordinary code and does not elide) and makes the draft unsatisfiable by construction. The spec now splits AddToCartFields (editable, types the draft, validated on both platforms) from AddToCartSubmission (fields + {:optional true :sensitive? true} :csrf-token, event-args only).

3. NO :draft REPOPULATION NOTE / NO NORMALISATION OWNER. The skill's failure arm does write :draft, but its :rf/server-init still dispatches raw :form-params — (route->action-event route) form-params — with no mention that a parsed form body is STRING keys and STRING values. The spec now names :rf/server-init as the single normalisation owner and prints decode-form-params + a route->action table carrying the event AND its args schema. Handed an un-normalised body the skill's handler 403s a VALID submission (the CSRF lookup misses a string key) — proven in implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_doc_example_form_action_test.clj (the-raw-parsed-body-does-not-reach-303-so-the-seam-is-load-bearing).

SCOPE: skills/ only; the spec page is correct as of this PR and must not be re-edited. Re-project all three corrections, keeping the skill's tighter register. Check whether skills/re-frame2/patterns/forms.md carries the same single-schema shape.

NOT A GATE FAILURE: scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py exits 0 over this drift — it does not compare the leaf's code fences to the spec's. Worth asking whether it should.

CITE: rf2-eane2 (the spec-side corrections and their audits), rf2-bl8k7.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7414 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7414). All three drift sites were still live on main and are re-projected: (1) the fail-open CSRF compare is now the spec's fail-closed both-limbs form and is the ONLY shape in any code fence (the not= spelling survives solely as a labelled 'not this' in prose); (2) AddToCartFields / AddToCartSubmission split, token {:optional true :sensitive? true} on the event-args schema only; (3) :rf/server-init named as the single normalisation owner, printing route->action + decode-form-params. Also propagated the #7406 elision rule (C-000.35: what may be elided is settled by what a check protects, not by who declared the schema). skills/re-frame2/patterns/forms.md checked and carries NO equivalent drift - its LoginForm is a pure field schema with no envelope and no credential riding a POST body, so one schema is correct there. THE BLIND GATE: check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py exited 0 over all of it. Rules 1-6 are retrospective token patterns over a leaf's own text; nothing in the script relates a leaf to the spec page it projects, so 'the spec moved and the leaf did not' was invisible by construction. Docstring + verbose output now say that plainly, and new Rule 7 checks the two security-shaped invariants (fenced CSRF compare must carry a presence limb; :csrf-token must not be a required field-schema entry) at BOTH ends - skill leaves AND spec/Pattern-FormAction.md. Fence-scoped, since a fence is what a reader copies. The presence limb is scoped to the comparison's enclosing form, not the fence: a block-wide search would have been satisfied by the unrelated (some? explanation) in the same fence, i.e. fail-open by construction. MUTATION-PROVEN: baseline EXIT=0 over the live drift; fail-open not= reintroduced -> EXIT=1 naming form-action.md:105 CSRF-FAIL-OPEN; :csrf-token made required -> EXIT=1 naming BOTH form-action.md:24 and spec/Pattern-FormAction.md:38; every revert byte-identical (sha1 verified). Real-corpus mutation arms added to --self-test so the rule cannot rot into a no-op. Gates: drift self-test 0, drift scan 0, test-fast-pr.sh 0, check_doc_slugs.py 0. Spec NOT edited.

title: RULING: the provisional reap horizon — accept the double build on the public mount schedule, or move the timer?
description:
OPERATOR DECISION, carried forward from rf2-2rtt6.25 when that bead closed (PR #7402, 2026-08-03). rf2-2rtt6.25's audit remainder is discharged and the bead is CLOSED; this is the part of it that was never work. Filed so the decision has a home rather than living in a closed bead's notes.

THE FACT. On the PUBLIC mount schedule — rendered through re-frame.substrate.adapter/render with NO act and NO flushSync — the shipped hook BUILDS TWICE. Two acquisitions, two different reaction objects, bodyRuns 2.00N, and the cache tenant is the commit's rebuild. The setTimeout 0 reaper releases the escrowed reference before React's passive useSyncExternalStore subscribe; the entry disposes on the ordinary 1->0 edge; the commit misses and rebuilds. So the hand-off rf2-2rtt6.14 adopted delivers its benefit ONLY under forced-synchronous rendering. Pinned deterministically by assert-use-subscribe-public-mount-schedule-rebuilds (numbers read from inside the probe's own mount use-effect, which React orders after the same fiber's uSES subscribe BY CONSTRUCTION).

NOTHING IS UNSOUND. The lost race costs a CONSTRUCTION and never correctness — the steady state is one durable reference either way, asserted on the public-schedule row too. Spec 006 Render-phase provisional acquisition and commit adoption already requires that correctness must not depend on the reaper losing the race, and it does not. rf2-2rtt6.13's concurrent-lane window also stays SHUT on this schedule: React's pre-commit store-consistency check runs in the SAME host task as the render, so no macrotask (the reaper included) can have run between the escrow and the check, and get-snap's escrow leg is necessarily reachable there. What the reaper beats is the PASSIVE-EFFECT FLUSH, a later task. Both rows are asserted together so a horizon repair cannot silently cost the window that is currently closed.

THE SWAP-THE-PRIMITIVE PROBE (three trials each, temporary diagnostic, not committed): setTimeout 0 (SHIPPED) = 2.00N at N=1 AND N=300. setTimeout 4 = 1.00N at both. setTimeout 32 = 1.00N at both. requestAnimationFrame = 1.00N at N=1 but 2.00N at N=300. MessageChannel = 2.00N (React posts its own message later on the same FIFO source). EVERY WINNER IS A MARGIN, NOT A GUARANTEE — React documents no maximum render-to-subscribe interval to size a delay against.

THE CHOICE, and it is Mike's because rf2-2rtt6.14's ruling PINNED THE PRIMITIVE (workers correctly have not touched it):

(a) MOVE THE HORIZON. setTimeout 4 is the smallest tested delay reading 1.00N at both sizes. COST: abandoned renders, Suspense retries and never-shown trees hold their reactive graphs ~4 ms longer; the Suspense-abort zero-point moves out with it (a contract-visible change, so Spec 006 wording moves too); AND IT IS STILL A RACE, not a contract.

(b) ACCEPT AND KEEP THE HORIZON AS RULED. The hand-off's benefit is then real only under forced-synchronous rendering, and the retractions on rf2-2rtt6.25 stand permanently: the coldmount instrument's shipped rows, the xcript before/after clock, and the M1L1 red-zone closure are withdrawn as shipped-performance claims (already done and now stamped in the source and in every emitted record, PR #7402).

(c) SOMETHING ELSE — e.g. a non-timer signal that is a contract rather than a margin. Nobody has proposed one; React exposes no cancellation signal for a render that never commits.

WHAT A RULING COSTS TO IMPLEMENT: small. The public-schedule assertions were deliberately written to be INVERTED, NOT DELETED (assert-use-subscribe-public-mount-schedule-rebuilds says so in its own docstring: 'Flip these five assertions to the act-driven row's — identical?, = 1 — when the horizon question is ruled'). Under (a) the work is one constant, five flipped assertions, the Suspense-abort zero-point, the Spec 006 sentence, and un-stamping the coldmount provenance PR #7402 added. Under (b) the work is ZERO — everything already says the right thing.

DO NOT let a worker pick a longer timer to make a row go green. That is the failure this bead exists to prevent.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RULED (a): move the reap horizon to setTimeout 4 — delegated dossier-review ruling (Mike's 2026-08-03 directive); operator-overturnable. 2026-08-03 15:46 AUSEST.

THE RULING. The provisional-escrow reaper moves setTimeout 0 -> setTimeout 4: the smallest probed delay reading 1.00N at N=1 AND N=300 (not 32 — the horizon is the shortest winning margin, so abandoned renders/Suspense retries hold their graphs no longer than needed). The claim stays NARROW: one build on the tested shipping schedule, with the safe two-build fallback; adoption remains a best-effort optimisation, never a React guarantee. No new hook, no new public mechanism to harden it — Spec 006's "correctness MUST NOT depend on the reaper losing the race" is untouched and is exactly what makes a 4 ms heuristic acceptable.

RATIONALE + how main-vs-Codex resolved. The dossier's main rec was (b) accept-and-keep, resting on "the double build prices at 1.0054x -> 1.0011x, indistinguishable from free." That premise fails source verification, exactly as the Codex rec traced: 1.0054x/1.0011x are the POST-hand-off parity readings of the flushSync instrument — the SINGLE-build schedule — and the coldmount page's own 2026-08-01 banner withdraws them as shipped-schedule claims (studio/coldmount-double-build-priced.md; the-clock-behind-the-published-rows.md §4's "the red zone has closed" row). The isolating price of the double build is xcript-handoff: 0.81 ms [0.75-0.85] per 300 L1 reads — >=93% of the mount red-zone excess in EVERY round/estimator/stratum at L1, and above the pre-registered 20% line at L2 (>=0.61) and L3 (>=0.35). That is the very evidence on which rf2-2rtt6.14 ruled ADOPT. Under (b) the ruled-ADOPT hand-off would deliver its benefit on NO mount a consumer performs, while its machinery still ships (the M1L3 fidelity gate priced escrow/queue/timer/identity-guard at ~4-5% of a layer-3 mount). The escrow itself stays under any option — its live provisional reaction answers React's pre-commit consistency read (assert-use-subscribe-escrow-leg-answers-on-the-public-mount-schedule) — but its performance purpose would be permanently unrealised. Materiality was adjudicated by the pre-registered 20% rule; re-litigating it by eyeballing "microseconds are small" contradicts "applied, not re-litigated."

On this bead's warning ("do not let a worker pick a longer timer to make a row go green"): the main rec read it as a substantive presumption against (a). It is a procedural guard — it forbids a WORKER silently greening the row; this bead is the sanctioned ruling venue, and moving the timer here with the costs priced is the legitimate act the guard preserves. Both settings are races; the choice is a race we deterministically lose vs one we win today, assertion-pinned either way.

Preserved from the main rec: correctness is never at stake; setTimeout 4 is a margin, not a contract — a future React scheduling change can silently reintroduce 2.00N, and the FLIPPED assertions are the standing tripwire (suite reds, question reopens with evidence; acceptable, symmetric cost); the #7402 honesty stamps are updated, not erased — the studio pages keep the historical retraction of the flushSync-era claims; option (c) stays open as a research direction — a genuine contractual signal from React would supersede the margin.

IMPLEMENTATION (small, pre-staged; SEQUENCE as hot-zone — spec/006 moves):
1. implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs — make-provisional-escrow: (js/setTimeout drain! 0) -> 4 (~L2409); rewrite docstring ~L2360-2381 ("this stays setTimeout 0 ... benefit stands retracted") and the section comment ~L2219-2290 narrating the losing race. Keep the margin-not-guarantee language.
2. implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs — flip the five assertions in assert-use-subscribe-public-mount-schedule-rebuilds to the act-driven row's (identical?, = 1 — its docstring says how); rewrite that docstring from retraction-witness/DEFECT to public-schedule adoption witness + React-drift tripwire; update the block comment above (~L5217-5220) and the act-row comment (~L5071-5080: "their integers must agree" — they now do). Exercised via adapters/uix/test/.../uix_use_subscribe_dom_cljs_test.cljs (browser runner).
3. spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md §Render-phase provisional acquisition and commit adoption — macrotask bullet (~L1080): replace "the reference implementation's current choice is not sufficient / ships the losing primitive" with the ruled 4 ms margin; keep "None of these is a guarantee" + the witness cite (now flipped). Horizon bullet (~L1081): the Suspense-abort zero-point moves out to the ~4 ms horizon — verify the "== 0 after one settle" witness settles PAST 4 ms; adjust its settle if it assumed a 0 ms drain.
4. docs/design/hicasso/studio/coldmount-double-build-priced.md — un-stamp the #7402 provenance per this bead: the shipped arm's "forced-synchronous mechanism arm" qualifier gains "horizon ruled setTimeout 4 (rf2-2rtt6.71, 2026-08-03); adoption now realised on the public schedule, witnessed by the flipped assertions". Do NOT delete the retraction record. Same for the :schedule stamp in the instrument source if it still asserts shipped-loses.
5. Gates: browser DOM suite for the flipped assertions; scripts/check_doc_slugs.py for the studio edit (mkdocs --strict does not cover docs/design; verify anchors/table columns by hand and say so in the PR body). No studio clock rows are re-taken under this bead — the flipped assertions ARE the witness; any re-pricing is separate work if ever wanted.

title: Beads checkpoint silently overwrites newer Git-only rows when Git and Dolt diverge at equal row count
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7394 / ledger durability. Before advancing the cursor, the merged main ledger at 43dcd2440a22a42e77d6ab773fb8df2a43a6a5a6 and the Dolt remote each contained 1,938 issues but different facts. Git alone carried rf2-3jw04, rf2-jv36i, rf2-lhdp0 and newer closes/statuses for rf2-2rtt6.52/.63; Dolt carried three newer audit issues. scripts/beads-checkpoint.ps1 exported Dolt wholesale; its row-count floor passed (1,938 == 1,938), and commit 667c744dc875e31e4d4874586afcbec2d01ceb8a silently removed the three Git-only issues and reverted .52/.63. This is the remaining equal-count/set-substitution sibling of rf2-51uz1's time-travel fault.

Recovery proved the bounded mechanism: timestamp-aware bd import of only Git issue rows into Dolt created the three missing IDs, updated exactly the two newer Git rows, skipped stale rows, preserved every newer Dolt row/cursor, and yielded a verified 1,941-ID union with zero field mismatches.

DO: before checkpoint overwrites .beads/issues.jsonl, compare HEAD's issue IDs/updated_at/status to the fresh Dolt export. Either import newer/missing Git issue rows timestamp-safely then re-export, or refuse with exact IDs/fields. Keep the existing row-count floor, but do not treat equal counts as equality. Add a regression where HEAD and Dolt have equal row counts but disjoint one-for-one substitutions plus one newer state on each side; neither fact may be lost. No generalized sync service needed.
close_reason: Closed via PR #7410. beads-checkpoint.sh + .ps1 now compare the fresh Dolt export to HEAD on the stable bead id, updated_at and status BEFORE overwriting .beads/issues.jsonl; the row-count floor is kept and runs first, but equal counts no longer imply equality. Three divergence classes, all 'Git knows something Dolt does not': GONE (issue id at HEAD with no row in the export - would be deleted), REVERT (id in both, HEAD's updated_at strictly newer - would be reverted), AMBIG (id in both, same updated_at, different status - neither side is newer). Forward motion (export-only ids, export-newer rows) is deliberately not reported, so ordinary checkpoints are unaffected. CHOSE REFUSE over auto-import: the script's own stated contract is that it does not import, and writing to the database from the one script that exists to be careful is not provably safe. To keep the refusal actionable it writes the GONE and REVERT rows verbatim to a temp file the message names, so the bead's own verified recovery is a single timestamp-safe 'bd import' then re-checkpoint; AMBIG rows are excluded because an import cannot adjudicate a tie. The message also names the escape for a deliberate bd delete/gc. No sync service. Regression on BOTH platforms from the bead's own fixture (equal row counts, disjoint one-for-one substitution, one newer state on each side): POSIX test-pre-commit.sh layer 8 cases 8j/8k/8l (72 passed / 0 failed; 3 of the 4 new assertions FAIL against origin/main); PowerShell a new -SelfTest switch, 28 assertions, green under both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7.6.4 - the .ps1 had no test surface at all before and layer 8 is POSIX sh and cannot run it. 8k/T2 prove the recovery completes with neither side's facts lost. Also verified read-only against the REAL 2741-row tracker: the parser extracts exactly the 1951 ground-truth stable ids with zero comment-UUID leakage, identity comparison is silent, and a synthetic equal-count 2741-vs-2741 divergence catches all three planted losses. Both implementations produce byte-identical findings on identical input. Never run against the live database.

title: MEASURE: acceptance still reads 1.1884x with the walk at parity — decompose the 8.25ms taskNet / 6.10ms in-page split, because the deficit is NOT the interpreter
description:
THE SUCCESSOR to rf2-2rtt6.63, named by that bead's own worker: 'the question the next bead should ask, and it should ask it of the ~8.25 ms taskNet / ~6.10 ms in-page split rf2-cno31 published for the acceptance arm rather than of the interpreter again.'

Our walk read 1.0588x stock Reagent BEFORE that bead touched anything, and 0.9636x after two spends. The interpreter the donor rungs actually ride, reagent2.impl.template, reads 1.73-1.90x stock — which is where their 1.33-1.5x came from, and is now its own bead (rf2-lhdp0, a shipped-artefact finding, not Hicasso's).
  - THE RESIDUAL IN THE WALK IS ~0.6% OF A MOUNT. +20.8 ns/element of shipped Hicasso semantics (the :& law, :ref reservation, event classification, caret convergence), on a walk that is ~0.66 ms of a ~10 ms mount. 92% of the ours-vs-Reagent divergence closed to named stages. NOTHING AVAILABLE INSIDE THE FENCE, AT THE WALK, MOVES THE 1.10x LINE.
  - THE ROUTE-LINK TERM IS FIXED AND THE ROWS RE-TAKEN (rf2-cno31, merged): link-model 7.07 -> 3.38 us; acceptance 1.4759 -> 1.1884x [1.1223-1.2660] band 7.0% FAILS; feed 1.3311 -> 1.0737x [0.9669-1.1859] band 6.7% INSTRUMENT-LIMITED; and THE TWINS NOW PAY THE SAME ROUTING TERM, so the comparison is fair for the first time since the migration.

SO THE OPEN QUESTION IS EXACTLY THIS: acceptance still reads 1.1884x against UIx with the walk at or below stock Reagent. Roughly 19% is unaccounted for and it is NOT the interpreter. WHERE IS IT?

THE PUBLISHED SPLIT TO START FROM (rf2-cno31's acceptance arm, tared p50, absolutes): floor 12.010 ms; hicasso 16.015 = 8.254 taskNet + 6.100 in-page; uix 13.742 = 8.246 taskNet + 3.900 in-page. Note what that says: TASKNET IS ESSENTIALLY IDENTICAL (8.254 vs 8.246) and the ENTIRE arm-to-arm difference lives in the IN-PAGE term (6.100 vs 3.900, +2.2 ms). The walk is ~0.66 ms of that. So ~1.5 ms of in-page work is neither the walk nor the frame.

DECOMPOSE THAT 6.10 ms. Candidates to price, not to assume: the boundary shell's own React work (207 boundaries x useContext + useSyncExternalStore); cold-read machinery (rf2-6c237 landed a 0.49x improvement and named 141 cold reads/mount as the surviving term — is it still?); the memo wrapper's per-boundary Fiber (HD-028, measured at ~200 B but never timed); element creation; the presence/boundary frame bindings that landed recently. UIx's 3.900 ms is the control — what does it NOT do that we do?

DISCIPLINE: clock of record (raw TaskDuration), quiet box, announced windows, absolutes alongside ratios, B/E/Q, band vs the 35% ceiling, blob provenance, discard-if-died, same-session pairing. The instrument history is long and unforgiving — read rf2-8nqsl, rf2-yd52q and rf2-emvod before writing a driver, and note that rf2-6c237 repaired census boot parity (m/make-frame! declaring hash-url-strategy) without which the census clock refuses every row.

AN HONEST NEGATIVE IS AN ANSWER: if the 2.2 ms is irreducibly the price of one-hook-per-boundary plus a shared index, say so with the decomposition — that converts the programme's last open performance question into a known cost, which is what the ship/kill decision needs.

title: Off-box resource redaction still emits enumerable FNV tokens and hashes pr-str instead of CEDN-1
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7391.

PR #7391 correctly proved that the existing FNV-1a-32 redaction token is neither injective nor one-way: low-entropy tenant/account values are recoverable by enumeration. It therefore withholds coarse :redact/:omit rows from SSR hydration. The same token still leaves the process through re-frame.resources.trace-egress: sensitive/large resource keys, free scope tags, page cursors, and related off-box tool/trace carriers still call ssr/redact-value, while Spec 009 and source comments call the result "opaque content-addressed". That contradicts Spec 015's normative sensitive marker contract: :rf/redacted carries no information about the underlying content and a sensitive value is not revealable by any observation surface. Removing the token from hydration while retaining it on off-box observability leaves the privacy defect at the other trust boundary.

The new cross-host determinism clause is also not implemented at the value boundary. redact-value hashes (pr-str value), although the repo's identity authority explicitly rejects pr-str over unordered values and provides identity/canonical-bytes. Concrete JVM witness: (array-map :a 1 :b 2) and (array-map :b 2 :a 1) are = and have equal canonical bytes, but redact-value emits 943e4859 and 08a47259. The shared fixture covers one map spelling and host arithmetic only, so it cannot catch this violation of "a fixed function of the canonical value".

One adjacent Spec 016 contradiction remains: the opening SSR paragraph still says every durable entry present at serialize time rides the projection and calls every non-blocking entry eligible for serialization, while the new MUST immediately below correctly withholds every re-keyed row, including all coarse sensitive/large entries.

Keep the repair bounded. Preserve PR #7391's server/client withholding and the useful shape-driven family projector. Decide the smallest safe off-box token contract: sensitive content must not produce an enumerable content-derived token merely to preserve joins; large-but-not-sensitive data can retain an appropriate structural/digest policy. Do not invent a general crypto subsystem. If any stable digest remains, derive it from CEDN-1 canonical bytes and pin equality/order variants on both hosts. rf2-fwp31 is the exact Spec 009 sentence owner and is reopened separately, blocked on this runtime decision.

New cross-host suite covers the real family-projector paths (sensitive scoped key, free scope tag, pagination cursor) plus plain and large-only negative controls; the FNV-sensitive mutation reds all three carriers. title: Hicasso: architecture.md and the guide still teach the un-amended HD-006 (no default memoization)
description:
HD-028 (rf2-2rtt6.52) makes a value-equality bail-out the boundary DEFAULT, amending HD-006. Three user-facing surfaces still state the overturned position as current, and they are wrong as written:

  docs/design/hicasso/architecture.md:188-191  '## Memoization (HD-006) / No default =/argv memoization: React
                                                semantics stand (a child may render with its parent) ... React.memo
                                                remains an opt-in escape.'
  docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/02-views-and-reads.md:108  '### There is no automatic memoization' — plus the
                                                claims at 116, 123 and the troubleshooting row at 174 ('A child
                                                re-renders whenever its parent does | Expected — there is no default
                                                memoization').
  docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/06-theming.md:133  links to that section as 'there is no default memoization'.

NOT INTRODUCED BY THE REBASE. The gap predates it: PR #7375 amended HD-006 in decisions.md and shipped the code, but never reconciled the downstream prose. It was found during that PR's rebase and deliberately left rather than fixed there, because rewriting a guide section is not a merge chore and the operator's ruling was 'merge as default' on a measured deliverable.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE NOW. A boundary bails out when its complete rfProps value is CLJS =. A child does NOT re-render merely because its parent did. Subscriptions and context still reach a boundary ahead of the comparator (React consults checkScheduledUpdateOrContext first), so the guide's separate claims about reads waking their readers stay correct — it is only the props channel and the 'nothing is memoized' framing that moved.

The troubleshooting rows are the sharpest: a reader hitting 'a child re-renders whenever its parent does' is now being told the opposite of what the runtime does.

Note draft-guide pages are digest-adjacent — check whether any fenced block is hashed before editing.
notes: AUDIT PR #7394 (2026-08-03 AEST) — REOPENED. The overall HD-028 reconciliation is correct, but the new troubleshooting row classifies "a freshly re-sorted seq" with inline functions and JS objects as reference identity that makes CLJS = unequal. The comparator is literally (= prev-rfProps next-rfProps), and sequential values compare structurally: deterministically sorting the same contents produces an = seq even when freshly allocated. The existing "Index thrash" row repeats the same mistake for query args. DO: replace with true reference-identity examples (function, JS array/object, host object) or say contents/order actually changed; teach that sequential comparison may traverse/realize the value but freshness alone does not defeat memoization or subscription-key equality. title: Hicasso: walk report double-counts prop sub-stages in its 92% decomposition
description:
PR #7390 publishes docs/design/hicasso/studio/our-walk-against-reagents.md as the decision record for rf2-2rtt6.63. Its section 3 claims the named stages explain 34.4 us of a 37.5 us whole-walk delta (92%), but the arithmetic adds nested measurements as though they were independent:

- walk_vs_reagent_app/stage-table measures `convert-props-hicasso` and `convert-props-reagent` by invoking each full convert-props pipeline over every element.
- Those full pipelines already perform the cached prop-name lookup and prop-value conversion for every emitted prop.
- The published sum adds the whole pipeline delta (+27.0 ns x 1,202 elements) and then adds the prop-name (-3.0 ns x 1,489 props) and prop-value (-0.4 ns x 1,489 props) deltas again.

The negative nested deltas reduce the non-overlapping total from about 39.5 us (about 105% of the observed 37.5 us) to the quoted 34.4 us / 92%. Therefore the statement that the decomposition closes to 92% is not proved. The raw interleaved whole-walk result may still support the broader conclusion, and the cache/string changes remain independently correct; this finding is specifically about the quantitative attribution used as decision evidence.

The exact owner rf2-2rtt6.63 is in_progress and locked, so this is a discovered-from follow-up rather than an edit to its scope.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Classify stage rows as nested or additive and stop summing a parent pipeline with its sub-stages.
2. Recompute or retract the 34.4 us / 92% closure claim in the studio record and every derived authority.
3. If an additive decomposition is retained, expose non-overlapping residual stages (or equivalent accounting) and show the arithmetic from instrument output.
4. Keep the independent whole-walk evidence and the correctness/performance claims for the two landed optimizations separate from the corrected decomposition claim.

title: hicasso: route-link's migration costs 8.21 us/link at mount — 1.70 ms on acceptance, 900 links on the feed; it took the feed row back above the line
description:
MEASURED by rf2-6c237's clock re-take (PR #7387), diagnosed with a dedicated link_term_probe_app. NOT the read machinery it was looking for — the read work it landed reads 0.49x in-process (4.17 -> 2.04 us/read) and taskNet reads ~1.00 everywhere, so the growth is all script and all in one named term.

THE REGRESSION. rf2-2rtt6.54 (PR #7380) migrated the roster's census anchors to route-link. Route-link synthesises its href per render through routing's link seam. Measured: 8.21 us PER LINK at mount. The acceptance page carries 207 links = 1.70 ms added to a ~10 ms mount. The feed carries 900.

THE COST IN BAR TERMS, against the rows on the clock of record:
  acceptance  1.2409x (instrument-limited)  ->  1.4759x [1.3281-1.6302] band 6.1%  FAILS THE LINE
  feed        1.0875x (MEAN BELOW THE LINE) ->  1.3311x [1.2357-1.4195] band 3.9%  FAILS THE LINE
The feed row was the programme's best clock result — the first mean below 1.10x — and this took it back.

AND THE COMPARISON IS NOW UNFAIR IN OUR DISFAVOUR: the hand-written UIx/Reagent twins DODGE the term entirely (they spell bare anchors with literal hrefs). So part of that 1.33x is Hicasso doing real routing work its controls do not do. rf2-2rtt6.54's own worker flagged exactly this when it landed ('href VALUES changed, per-card render gains 3 route-url syntheses, future clock rows on this tree are not comparable to origin/main rows') — the flag was correct and the size is now measured.

THE WORK, and step 1 may dissolve most of it:
  1. IS 8.21 us/LINK NECESSARY? Profile route-url synthesis. Route-link is a plain function over routing's published seams; the href for a given (route, params) is a pure function and the census's links are drawn from a small set of shapes. A per-frame memo on the seam call is the obvious candidate — mine Reagent/Freehand/re-frame.ui for how they price link rendering, and check whether routing itself already memoises.
  2. FIX THE TWIN FAIRNESS GAP either way (tracked as the rf2-2rtt6.54 follow-up): either the twins route-link too, or the roster states plainly that Hicasso's rows carry a routing term its controls do not. A row whose arms do different work is not a row.
  3. RE-TAKE acceptance and feed after (1), on the clock of record, quiet box, same-run donors.

DO NOT revert route-link. It is HD-027, ruled, and it serves 106 census instances as a plain function; the defect is its per-render cost, not its design.

title: hicasso: the converge rewrites a refused/normalised value MID-COMPOSITION, destroying the IME exchange — as does React's own restore; carve-out needs a ruling
description:
MEASURED by the rf2-o27h3 harness (ime_run.cjs, real CDP composition — trusted compositionstart/update, input events with insertCompositionText + isComposing true, a real composition range), first run 2026-08-02, branch worker/ime-o27h3.

THE FINDING. The PR #7371 audit asked the harness to pin that front.controlled's converge 'neither writes nor moves selection mid-composition'. It does not hold — and neither does the plain-React baseline:

- REFUSING model (digits): the IME composes し into '12'; the model refuses; the converge writes '12' back INSIDE the composing input event. A JS value write mid-composition silently ABORTS the browser's composition — no compositionend fires, the next IME update mints a fresh compositionstart, and the user's in-flight kana are gone. Plain React does the IDENTICAL thing in the same turn via its own end-of-event restore (updateInput), and UIx's Reagent-port does it one animation frame later (input-node-set-value on the after-render queue). Measured matrix identical across all three: field '12' after settle, composition aborted, model never moved.
- NORMALISING model (upper): same class — 's' composes, model holds 'S', the write lands mid-composition, exchange aborted. All three implementations.
- MODEL-AGREEING field: the exchange SURVIVES on all three — exactly one compositionstart through to compositionend. The converge's flushSync + unconditional setSelectionRange did NOT disturb the CDP composition range (measured), and its equal-value write branch never fires; a mutation making the write unconditional was ALSO measured harmless (Chromium's value setter short-circuits an equal write).
- On the refusing field a CANCELLED exchange never sees compositionend at all — the abort already happened. Field and model still end exactly as before (the restoration law held everywhere).

SO: the converge is nowhere WORSE than the plain-React baseline (comparative rows green in the same run), but the pin the audit demanded is false for every implementation that converges a store-refused/normalised field mid-composition. The fence that would make it true is a composition carve-out: suppress convergence while a composition is live (the change handler can read isComposing off the native input event) and converge ONCE at compositionend against the then-current model. That changes what a composing user sees on a refusing field (their composition survives until commit, then is refused whole) — it is a BEHAVIOURAL choice inside HD-019's controlled-text-converge exception scope, and per rf2-o27h3's brief it needs a ruling, not a worker's judgment. If ruled in, the carve-out belongs to front/controlled.cljs (and the same question then stands, unanswerable by us, for plain React and the UIx port, which have the same conduct and no carve-out seam).

Re-run: node implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/ime_run.cjs (green baseline 107 checks; the s5 rows pin this bead's matrix and go red the day a carve-out lands, which is the intended tripwire).
close_reason: Shipped in PR #7441 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7441). Carve-out IN as ruled: convergence suppressed while a composition is live, converge once at compositionend. Two halves — the converge suppressed by one reading of the native event's isComposing, and React's own restore made a no-op by an internal single-useState component holding the value React sees at the live DOM draft (public React; no private mutation, no value-setter interception). Release unconditional on compositionend / a non-composing change / blur / unmount, and always before the author's handler. s5 tripwire flipped: hicasso re-pins ONE uninterrupted exchange (starts 1, ends 1, refusal whole at the commit); react and uix-port keep the abort pins, now asserted as DIVERGENCE. New pinned finding: on the normalising field the baseline does not merely lose the composition, it corrupts what the exchange commits (model SSHSH vs SH). HD-019 dated addendum records the ruling and audits the second flushSync call site. Divergence + Chromium-only witness scope stated on the evidence page, authoring.md, the draft guide, validation.md and the harness header. Price: one fiber + one useState per controlled input/textarea, paid in public on shapes/hook_budget_dom_cljs_test (shell budget untouched). Gates: fast-PR spine 0 (PASS fast PR spine), test:browser 0 (1052/6550, 0 failures), ime_run.cjs 0 (122 checks, 0 failures). Follow-up filed: rf2-zf297 (re-price the P0 clock keystroke row).

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
[2026-08-03 15:45 AUSEST] DELEGATED DOSSIER-REVIEW RULING (Mike's 2026-08-03 directive); operator-overturnable.

RULING: carve-out IN. Controlled-text convergence is suppressed while a composition is live; the field converges ONCE at compositionend against the then-current model. Automatic for any :value/:on-input pair — no public option, no config knob.

WHY (what the composing user experiences): under parity (out), a CJK/IME user on a refusing or normalising field has in-flight kana silently destroyed mid-word — no compositionend, no feedback, the field snaps back while they are still composing. Under the carve-out, the composition survives ('12shi'...'12shin' in kana) and refusal happens whole at commit: the field snaps back visibly at compositionend. The composition is a browser-owned draft of the user's; destroying it silently is not a parity target worth keeping. Hicasso becomes deliberately better than React in its flagship territory. HD-019 already frames this exact choice as inside the converge exception's scope and names rf2-digtt as its reopen trigger, whichever way ruled.

MAIN vs CODEX: both dossier reviewers recommend IN; Codex adopted on mechanism. The bare "skip converge! when isComposing" is proven insufficient by this bead's own measured matrix: plain React — which has no Hicasso converge in the loop, i.e. exactly the path a bare skip falls through to — still aborts the exchange via its own end-of-discrete-event controlled restore (ChangeEventPlugin enqueues a restore target, the post-handler flush performs it, the value is assigned whenever DOM differs from the controlled value). The carve-out must therefore ALSO make React's restore a no-op during composition.

IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF (supersedes the description's one-line mechanism sketch):
- Surface: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/controlled.cljs (+ ime_run.cjs + existing controlled tests). Mechanism: an internal composition shadow for controlled text only — while a composition is live, the value React sees agrees with the live DOM draft (so React's restore finds nothing to write); the authored handler still runs normally and the model may refuse/normalise as usual; at compositionend release the shadow and converge once against the then-current model. Prefer a small public-React mechanism (e.g. one internal stateful controlled-text wrapper) over React-private mutation or value-setter interception. Preserve any authored composition handlers; authoring API unchanged.
- Safety rider: shadow release must be unconditional (compositionend, and the blur/unmount paths); worst-case degradation is today's conduct (a converge), never a stuck field diverged from the model.
- The ime_run.cjs s5 rows are a DELIBERATE TRIPWIRE: they go red the day this lands and are flipped on purpose — Hicasso rows re-pin one uninterrupted compositionstart->compositionend exchange with commit-time refusal/normalisation; the react and uix-port rows keep pinning the old abort conduct, now asserted as divergence, not parity. Retain the agreeing-field, cancel, commit-fence, mid-string caret and restoration laws; price the per-input machinery on the existing grid.
- Honesty riders: the evidence page and authoring doc state the divergence from React plainly (a claimed win, precisely scoped to Hicasso's converge), AND state witness scope: Chromium CDP only. Codex flagged WebKit's recently-fixed composition/key-ordering defect; this harness cannot drive WebKit composition (CDP is Chromium-only) and mandating a new driver is gold-plating — name the caveat on the evidence page instead. WebKit misconduct, if ever observed, is a new bug bead.
- HD-019 (docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md) gets a dated addendum recording this ruling in the same PR; rf2-dfz6f then rewrites R-A2 (guidance noted on that bead).
- If the public-React shadow cannot meet the existing gates (caret laws, agreeing-field survival, perf grid), return the mechanism for a ruling rather than shipping a private-React hack.

title: hicasso: attack the interpreter-walk mount cost — the located deficit is 100% script, +1.06ms where uix pays +0.38ms on byte-identical DOM

WHERE THE DEFICIT LIVES, from three independent measurements that agree:
  - rf2-0qj9w located it: the candidate pays +1.06 ms over its own floor where uix-subs — same spine, same adapter, same 300 reads, BYTE-IDENTICAL DOM — pays +0.38 ms. The runtime hiccup codec walking 901 elements.

  - rf2-2rtt6.31 (HD-008 re-take): donor arms show the same ~10-13% interpreter cost over UIx at their shapes.

SO THE TARGET IS THE PER-ELEMENT COST OF THE HICCUP WALK: parse/classify/convert per element per mount. The one-boundary page (1,202 elements, one commit) is the acceptance shape — it currently FAILS the 1.10x line at 1.3053x [1.1044-1.4660] with an 18.7% margin clearing a 6.7% band; the census feed is the guard shape (it must not regress from 1.1646x).

CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS, to be costed not assumed — and the PRIOR-ART DIRECTIVE applies in full (mine Freehand, re-frame.ui, Replicant, Reagent, UIx; cite taken/declined):
  1. CACHE THE STATIC SKELETON: most census markup is static per view; Replicant and every compiled substrate exploit this. re-frame.ui's compiler shows what static extraction buys; the question is what a RUNTIME can cache keyed on the hiccup's identity without a compiler (fences: no compiler, no analyzer — but a value-keyed cache at the codec is neither).
  2. CHEAPEN THE PER-ELEMENT PATH: prop-map conversion, keyword->string, intent classification — profile first, the walk has never been profiled element-by-element.
  3. AMORTISE ACROSS COMMITS: the walk re-runs per render; the memo wrapper (HD-026, #7375 pending) already stops child re-walks — what remains is the FIRST walk, which is what mount prices.
  Reagent's own answer (interpret once into a render fn, cache on the component) and UIx's (macro-compile to createElement at build time — unavailable to us by fence) bracket the space.

FENCES, all standing: Surface B; no compiler, no analyzer, no candidate ledger, no ViewCell graph; <=2-hook shell; subscribe closes over the read set alone; Hicasso consumes reagent-slim's codec — a cache AROUND the codec is in scope, a fork OF it needs a ruling.

MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE: the full instrument canon (raw TaskDuration, quiet box, absolutes+ratios, B/E/Q, bands, blob provenance, discarded-if-died, announced windows). Profile and optimise in the implementation lane; PUBLISHED rows only on the clock of record against same-run donors. An optimisation claiming X% must show it on the one-boundary acceptance shape AND show the feed did not regress.

AN HONEST NEGATIVE IS AN ANSWER: if the walk is irreducible within the fences, say so with the profile — that converts 'the interpreter is slow' into 'the interpreter costs exactly this, here', which is what a ship/kill decision needs.

title: Hicasso: close the interpreter gap — decompose the slim-lineage walk against Reagent's own, then spend HD-004's codec-caching budget
description:
THE OUTCOME BEAD for the mount deficit. The attribution chain is complete and tight: UIx ($-macro, no runtime interpretation) mounts at parity with Reagent (1.015x); the donor rungs and the candidate — all riding reagent-slim's :f> walk — read 1.33-1.5x; Freehand's codec reads another 1.14-1.22x on top; per-keystroke and narrow are at parity everywhere. So the ENTIRE clock deficit follows the interpreter — and, decisively, REAGENT'S OWN INTERPRETER IS THE EXISTENCE PROOF that runtime hiccup interpretation can be nearly free at mount (its walk disappears into the shared React/frame work). The question is not 'can interpreted hiccup be fast' but 'why is OUR walk slower than Reagent's, and how much of HD-004's sanctioned budget closes it'.

STEP 1 — DECOMPOSE (measure before touching anything). Reagent's template machinery is in this repository (reagent.impl.template + slim's shared plumbing): put the slim-lineage walk and stock Reagent's walk side by side on the SAME witness markup and attribute the per-element delta to named terms — candidate suspects: the :f> function-component path's per-element allocations; prop-name conversion missing Reagent's warm caches (cached-parse et al.); children flattening; per-boundary wrapper cost. Frame-domination arithmetic matters: two-thirds of the mount window is shared style/layout/paint, so a 1.49x TOTAL implies the walk slice is SEVERAL TIMES Reagent's slice in absolute terms — the decomposition must report absolute per-element costs, not ratios. Respect rf2-2rtt6.62's finding: match roster workloads before attributing.

STEP 2 — SPEND THE HD-004 BUDGET, in measured increments: codec-work caching ONLY (parsed tags, prop-name conversion, cached stable component heads — same elements, same behaviour, safe invalidation, no public template hints). HARD FENCE (HD-004, verbatim class): NO template extraction, NO hole plans, NO node references, NO subscription-addressed anything, NO direct DOM writes — the first optimization that wants those IS the own-renderer strategy and must be declared as such, not smuggled. If the budget runs out short of the gate, REPORT THE FLOOR REACHED rather than widening the sanction — that is a P2-relevant finding either way.

SEQUENCING: after rf2-2rtt6.31's re-take publishes (so the before-number is the adjudicated one) and coordinated with rf2-2rtt6.62 (workload matching). Browser numbers only. This bead is the make-or-break of the mount axis: if a measured, fence-respecting caching pass cannot reach 1.10x, that is the honest input to the P2 fork ruling — not a reason to loosen the fence.

description:

implementations against the same model. Shape 5 is the best-witnessed shape of the five.

THE GAP. The charter's clause is "zero dropped keystrokes", and every echo witness fires

    (type-into! n "hello")   ;; one event, value "hello"
That proves the door is synchronous for a keystroke. It does not prove that N keystrokes

cell without yielding between them (h,e,l,l,o as five events, not one), and assert the
model holds "hello", the DOM holds "hello", the caret is at 5, and the body ran exactly k
times. Then the same burst against a REFUSING cell (:digits), where the model must hold
only the accepted subset.

Coordinate with worker/converge-fki5d (in-turn controlled-input convergence) - if it
changes what an author writes for a controlled field, this witness should be written
against the converged spelling rather than re-written after it.

title: Hicasso: a page-chrome write cascades to every row (no props-equality bail-out)
description:
MEASURED on the tier-1 shape roster (rf2-2rtt6.51),
shapes/narrow_dom_cljs_test/a-page-chrome-write-re-renders-every-row.

A write that moves a key the PAGE boundary reads re-renders the page, and React then
re-renders all 300 card boundaries beneath it — even though every card's props and every
card's subscription values are unchanged. Measured: page 1, cards 300/300, and the DOM
after is byte-identical to the DOM before, which is why a DOM-only witness could never
have seen it.

CAUSE: `runtime/mint-view!` returns a plain React function component
  (fn hicasso-boundary [js-props] (shell body-fn js-props))
with no memo and no props comparison. React re-renders children of a re-rendered parent
unless the element is referentially identical (it is not — the page's `for` builds fresh
elements) or the component bails out itself.

WHY IT MATTERS ON THE BAR: Reagent's default `shouldComponentUpdate` compares argv and
stops exactly this cascade. So on any page with page-level chrome state (a tab, a filter,
a sort, a route param) Reagent re-renders N rows fewer than Hicasso does. That is the
axis HD-012's `<= 1.0x Reagent` bulk row is set on, and the roster's narrow law
(one commit -> one body) holds only for writes that DON'T touch the page boundary.

NOT REPAIRED by rf2-2rtt6.51 — the roster's job is to find what the shapes cost, and the
repair is a runtime change. Note for whoever takes it: `React.memo` alone does NOT fix it,
because the props object is a fresh `#js {"rfProps" <cljs map>}` each render and memo's
shallow compare is `Object.is`. It needs an `areEqual` doing `=` on the rfProps map —
which is Reagent's argv compare, and costs no React hook, so the <=2-hook budget is not
in the way.

MEASUREMENT (do not run here; siblings own the box): the cascade's cost belongs on the
bulk ladder as its own row - "page-chrome write, B mounted rows", against Reagent.
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-08-02, dossier review):

AMEND HD-006 (docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md, "Memoization defaults"). The clause "No default `=`/argv memoization ... `React.memo` is an opt-in escape", with reopen pre-registered "only on keyed-row / broad witness evidence demanding it", has had its reopen condition fire: the tier-1 roster's own instrument (shapes/narrow_dom_cljs_test/a-page-chrome-write-re-renders-every-row) measured a page-chrome write re-rendering the page plus all 300 card boundaries with every card input value-equal, on exactly the axis the <=1.0x Reagent bulk row is set on (Reagent's argv compare stops this cascade). DECISION: value-equality bail-out becomes the DEFAULT at minted Hicasso boundaries — CLJS `=` over the complete rfProps value, implemented as a codec-level stable memo wrapper. This is the evidence-driven overturn HD-006 itself provided for; record it as such in the amendment.

EVIDENCE CORRECTION (Codex, verified against the shape test): the resulting DOM is NOT byte-identical — the tab chrome changes. Drop that phrase everywhere (this bead's description carries it; do not repeat it in the amendment or PR text). The 300 unchanged-row renders (page body 1, card bodies 300/300 with all card projections equal) are themselves the sufficient witness.

IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE (binding):
- `React.memo(fn, compare)` returns a memo OBJECT, not a function, and the codec + runtime tests require minted heads to BE functions. Do NOT replace `mint-view!`'s return value. Keep the marked function as the public Hicasso head; the codec emits one stable internal memo wrapper for that head (or an equivalently contained internal mechanism). No memo object escapes as the public representation.
- Comparator: CLJS `=` over the complete rfProps value — every prop, including function-valued props, which compare conservatively unequal (correct: distinct functions must not bail out).
- Memoization must not block the boundary's own state/context/external-store updates: useContext + useSyncExternalStore invalidation still re-renders (React's documented memo contract). The comparator costs no React hook; the <=2-hook budget is untouched.
- Donor precedent: reagent-slim's default update check is argv `=`, and reactive invalidation bypasses it via forceUpdate. Same shape here — subscription invalidation bypasses the props bail-out by design.

CONTRACT: bodies stay pure and re-runnable — memoization is a scheduling optimization, never observable semantics. NO public `:memo false` option in v1. A boundary that intentionally wants parent-driven re-runs receives an explicit changing revision prop; add an opt-out only if a concrete case later proves that insufficient. No element caches, no per-call-site switches.

LANDING BAR (the implementation must clear this before merge; the amendment lands with its own number): one focused production-build measurement gate — the "page-chrome write, B mounted rows" bulk-ladder row before/after (witness: page body 1, card bodies 0 after settling; prop-change re-render still fires; context/external-store invalidation still fires; initial-mount and bulk-update time), PLUS the per-boundary retained-heap delta. The real cost being priced: the custom comparator takes the full MemoComponent path and adds an outer Fiber per boundary, and the R=0 shell heap is already ~1.14 KB against the 1 KB paper-fail line. The default lands if it removes the 300-row cascade without a material mount/bulk regression and without pushing retained heap meaningfully farther past the bar. If the extra Fiber fails the gate: retain HD-006 and ship the same comparator as an explicit boundary-level opt-in — a small, decisive experiment either way.

REJECTED:
(b) Keep HD-006 and teach React.memo+areEqual as an opt-in pattern — inverts the posture (the framework knows the right default and makes every programmer find it) and ships a known 300x re-render cascade on the most ordinary page shape there is (tabs above a list).
(c) Element-identity caching at the call sites — fights React's grain with exactly the caching machinery the anti-fence exists to refuse; every `for` site becomes a performance decision.

PROCESS: the HD-006 amendment text ships in the SAME PR as the runtime change (the .25 precedent). This bead is now the implementation owner — dispatchable.
OPERATOR RULING — MERGE AS DEFAULT (Mike, 2026-08-03, verbatim: 'merge as default'). Recorded by acting mayor.

THE BINDING LANDING BAR, and how it came out:
  CASCADE HALF — DECISIVE. A page-chrome write re-rendered 300 unchanged card boundaries with a BYTE-IDENTICAL resulting DOM (which is why no DOM-only witness could ever have caught it); now 0. Both halves witnessed — cascade gone AND real changes still propagate. Plain React.memo was shown to STILL cascade at 300, so the ruled codec-level shape was necessary rather than stylistic.
  HEAP HALF — MEASURED, and the projection was wrong by about a factor of two. The feared figure was approximately +17%; the R=0 boundary shell actually reads +106 B / +9.3% (1,141 -> 1,247 B) on the Reagent segment and +100 B / +8.8% on the UIx segment. A->B->A in one session (A arms agreeing to 0 B and 5 B), ranges disjoint, arms differing by ONE LINE, donors flat, slope identical to the byte with and without — confirming HD-026's own claim that the cost is constant in R.

WHY THE DISPOSITION WAS THE OPERATOR'S: 'without pushing retained heap meaningfully farther past the bar' is unquantified in HD-026, and the shell ALREADY FAILED the 1 KB paper line at 1,141 B before any wrapper existed. The wrapper widens a pre-existing failure rather than causing one. The rf2-2rtt6.58 worker refused to call that green by fiat and stopped — correctly.

THE RULING: merge as DEFAULT. The opt-in fallback is NOT taken. Eliminating a 300-boundary cascade on the make-or-break bulk shape is worth +9% on a line that had already failed and has its own separate remedy path (rf2-aqgr2, the 415 B/read decomposition, and the shell target on rf2-2rtt6.41 item 5).

ALSO SETTLED BEFORE MERGE: rf2-2rtt6.60 attributed the +84 B/read slope shift to a MAIN landing (8e973eeace, rf2-2rtt6.44's disposal hook, merged 35 minutes before section 6 published) — NOT to this branch. The cascade branch is exonerated; section 6's bill now reads +499 B/read and is recorded as such.
RENUMBERED HD-026 -> HD-028 on rebase, and the branch is unblocked for merge.

HD-026 and HD-027 were taken on main while this branch was held (the prevent head rf2-2rtt6.57, route-link rf2-2rtt6.54). Main's highest was verified as HD-027 before choosing 028. Every earlier note on this bead that says HD-026 means HD-028.

CONFLICTS RESOLVED KEEPING BOTH INTENTS, never --ours/--theirs: the title line became the full range HD-001 … HD-028, and main's HD-026 and HD-027 bodies survive untouched with HD-028 following in numeric order.

REFERENCES DECIDED PER SITE. The ten on this branch were all the cascade's and were renamed; the eleven that are main's prevent head were left. Two more repaired: the decisions index still read HD-001…HD-026 (route-link never bumped it) and studio/the-interpreter-walk-profiled-and-cheapened.md cited this amendment by the number it carried while held. The nine draft-guide range banners moved to HD-028; their HD-027 body citations are untouched.

ONE GENUINE INTERACTION FOUND. rf2-2rtt6.53 landed while this branch was held and restated the 300-row cascade on the resource clock, citing the roster pin by name as 'the same number, restated rather than contradicted'. shapes/framework_subs_dom_cljs_test now reads 0 where it read 1, on three assertions and in its docstring — the same correction the roster witness already carried. The page's own DOM is asserted to have moved so the zeroes cannot pass vacuously, and the mutation reds them, which is the check that they were moved to the truth rather than relaxed. No behavioural interaction with anything else that landed while held (the cold read, presence's frame binding, the walk optimisation, or PR #7389's boundary frame binding, which the branch was rebased onto).

WRAPPER UNCHANGED: memoize-boundary! one stable wrapper per head at definition, mint-view! returns the marked function, boundary-head? asks fn?, no memo object escapes. The operator's heap number was measured against these blobs.

GATES RE-RUN ON THE REBASED TREE, all exit 0: test:cljs 12,395/61,841; test:browser 1,009/6,258; test-fast-pr.sh PASS; clj-kondo 2026.04.15 errors: 0 (warnings 4,532); check_doc_slugs.py. MUTATION RE-RUN on the rebased tree: bail-out removed -> 9 failures, narrow actual (not (= 0 300)), exit 1; restored byte-exact -> exit 0.

No bench driver run and no clock row taken — linkterm-cno31 and walkdecomp-2rtt6-63 own the measurement windows.

description:

4. Narrow update   - one cell moves in a large mounted page.

Each shape gets: the view (a census port where the census has a real screen of that shape -

  a-real-keystroke-moves-the-model-and-the-field-in-the-callers-turn

arm's commit timing into a reading: a keystroke echoes INSIDE dispatchEvent

title: MEASURE: M1's mount row is still stated under a control that FAILS — ctl-2x undershoots 1.8173x and no changed-set control can reach a mount
description:
RAISED by rf2-7iqb5's three-point control work (PR #7367).

THE GAP. rf2-7iqb5 built the three-point control rf2-emvod ruled and it applies
to BULK rows only. A mount row's operation IS the mount: there is no standing
page to write a changed set into, so there is no changed-set axis to be linear
in. M1 therefore keeps ctl-2x and keeps its measured 1.8173x undershoot against
a 2.00x prediction.

WHY IT MATTERS. M1 carries the programme's headline mount figure -- hicasso /
reagent-subs 1.4896x [1.3488 - 1.5989], the number the operator's 2026-08-02
continuation ruling was taken against. That magnitude is currently published
under a positive control that FAILS, which is exactly the condition the strict

title: RE-ADJUDICATE the candidate's clock rows on the corrected clock — taskNet subtracted the operation's own script (rf2-yd52q)
description:
rf2-yd52q found that `taskNet = TaskDuration - DevToolsCommandDuration` REMOVES the operation's own JavaScript, because Chromium bills a Runtime.callFunctionOn to DevToolsCommandDuration INCLUDING the page script the command invokes, and clock_run.cjs drives every arm's operation through exactly that door.

MEASURED, not argued: an arm's devtools term less the tare's baseline tracks that arm's own in-page window - floor 0.62 ms against an in-page 0.40, reagent-subs 2.76 against 2.30, uix-subs 2.01 against 1.60, hicasso 3.26 against 2.80 (one bulk300 run). The tell needed no arithmetic and was on the page already: on a substrate arm the in-page ABSOLUTE exceeds the taskNet absolute, which no superset can do. It went unnoticed because the driver printed only their ratio.

So taskNet is a frame-ONLY clock - style, layout, paint, with the script taken out - and very nearly the COMPLEMENT of the in-page window rather than a superset of it.

WHAT THIS TOUCHES. Every magnitude on docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-candidates-clock.md is stated on taskNet:
  - M1 'hicasso / reagent-subs 1.2107x'. On raw TaskDuration, rf2-yd52q's 8-run ensemble reads 1.4896x [1.3488 - 1.5989]. The candidate's mount deficit is MATERIALLY WORSE than published, not better.

RE-ADJUDICATED. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7365

THE THIRD DEFECT, and it is what reconciles the three mount numbers. taskNet is
not one quantity. DevToolsCommandDuration bills page script only when that
script runs INSIDE a protocol command, so the same subtraction is frame-ONLY on
a harness driving through page.evaluate and script-AND-frame on one driving
through page.click or keyboard.press. Measured within one instrument in one run:
ScriptDuration reads 0.063 ms for a 901-element mount on the evaluate-driven M1
row and 49.97 ms for the keystroke control on the Input-driven row, while the
devtools term varies 7.836 ms across arms on the first and 0.069 ms on the
second. Confirmed on the cross-check harness directly: devtools spread 0.126 ms
against a ScriptDuration spread of 13.97 ms, and its ratios move <=1.7%.

So clock_run.cjs's M1/bulk300/bulk100/narrow were corrupted; its keystroke row
and the WHOLE of rf2-rguy1's cross-check were NOT, and need no restatement.

THE RECONCILIATION. 1.2107x is not a member of the comparison - it is on the
other clock. What remains: workload 1.4896 -> 1.2789 (ours throughout, ~7-17%,
loose) and instrument 1.2789 -> 1.1756 (same app, 8.8%, mechanism already
published - our window contains the post-paint macrotask). That the legs
multiply to the whole gap is ARITHMETIC, not evidence (a/b x b/c = a/c), and the
page says so; what carries it is that the previously invisible leg is

which compared a frame-only reading with a script-and-frame one - corrected

comments.text:
RE-TAKEN AND WITHDRAWN. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7363

VERDICT ON THE ROW. `bulk broad 0.6291x` is WITHDRAWN. On a clock that sees the whole operation - the arm's own JavaScript AND the frame it causes - `UIx / Reagent` reads 0.8602x [0.7709 - 0.9058] over eight runs. Every run mean below 1.0, 43 of 48 rounds below 1.0, so UIx IS faster; by about 14%, not 37%.

NO MAGNITUDE REPLACES IT. The control refused on 7 of 8 runs under the strict rule (undershoots 1.59-1.81x against 2.00x) and the 14% margin is inside the run's own band on 4 of 8. One run of eight is fully reportable and reads 0.8433x, clearing its 12.2% band. What is published is a direction and a bound.

THE PREDICTION IS RECORDED AS PARTLY REFUTED. It was registered before the runs expecting parity, on the strength of three prior frame-inclusive readings. The corrected clock found neither the win nor parity. Recorded as refuted rather than widened.

THE LARGER FINDING, and it outranks the row. `taskNet = TaskDuration - DevToolsCommandDuration` REMOVES THE OPERATION'S OWN SCRIPT: Chromium bills a Runtime.callFunctionOn to DevToolsCommandDuration including the page script the command invokes, and the driver runs every arm through exactly that door. Measured - an arm's devtools term less the tare's baseline tracks its in-page window (floor 0.62 vs 0.40 ms, reagent-subs 2.76 vs 2.30, uix-subs 2.01 vs 1.60, hicasso 3.26 vs 2.80); ScriptDuration reads 0.013-0.029 ms for every arm including a 901-element mount. So the 'frame-inclusive' clock is FRAME-ONLY and near the in-page window's COMPLEMENT rather than its superset. The tell needed no arithmetic - on a substrate arm the in-page ABSOLUTE exceeds the taskNet absolute - and went unseen because the driver printed only their ratio.

THE CORRECTED CLOCK VALIDATES ITSELF on a row it was not fitted to: the donor bar on M1 reads 1.0011x [0.9464 - 1.0763] against a published M1 mount 1.0150x [0.9820 - 1.0480], and 0.9996x over the 4 control-passing runs. It is not a clock that flattens everything - in the same runs it puts hicasso/reagent on M1 at 1.4896x, clearing every band.

MECHANISM, in milliseconds. The two arms differ 42% on script (2.375 vs 1.669 ms) and 5% on frame (2.335 vs 2.463 ms). The frame is the same 901-element page in both and half the operation. The published figure is the ratio of the arms' SCRIPT quoted as the ratio of their OPERATIONS.

title: AUDIT: every published clock row is an IN-PAGE window, and an in-page window mis-reads a substrate arm by 300-610%
description:
RAISED by rf2-0qj9w's clock run (2026-08-01). This is the run's strongest
methodological finding and it is about the PUBLISHED rows, not the candidate.

rf2-0qj9w took both instruments on the SAME operations in the SAME samples: an
in-page performance.now() window around the substrate's own flushSync (which is
what p0_converge_app, p0_arms, hd8_rows and coldmount_app all use), and Chrome's
renderer counters over CDP read after the browser produced the frame the
operation caused.

MEASURED, run 5, ratio to the floor in that round of that segment:

  M1 mount        in-page          frame-inclusive
  reagent-subs    5.6068x          1.1321x     (+395%)
  uix-subs        4.7394x          1.1530x     (+311%)
  hicasso         8.7318x          1.3613x     (+541%)

  bulk300
  reagent-subs    5.8048x          1.0243x     (+467%)
  uix-subs        4.3333x          1.0242x     (+323%)
  hicasso         7.2986x          1.0266x     (+611%)

The error is NOT a scale factor that cancels in a ratio -- it differs per arm by
hundreds of points. On M1 the in-page window would put hicasso/reagent-subs at
1.56x where the frame-inclusive clock reads 1.21x.

The reason is in the decomposition: a substrate arm's mount spends roughly a
third of its frame-inclusive cost inside flushSync and the rest afterwards in
style, layout and paint -- and the AFTERWARDS half is where the three substrates
differ least, because they build byte-identical DOM. Measuring only the first
half exaggerates the difference between them.

The pure-React control arms differ by only 6-13% on the same comparison, which
is exactly how a lane that checks only its controls in-page would never see this.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SAY. It does not overturn M1 mount 1.0150x or
bulk-broad 0.6291x: those are Reagent against UIx on a different harness and a
page whose two readings are closer. It does say that no published clock row in
this programme has ever been checked against a frame-inclusive instrument, and
that the check is cheap now that one exists.

SEQUENCING: this raises rf2-rguy1 (the krausest/js-framework-benchmark external
cross-check, which drives chromedriver and reads Chrome's timeline) from a
nicety to the next question. Two independent frame-inclusive instruments
agreeing would settle it; two disagreeing would be worth more than either row.

title: MEASURE: the bulk clock rows' cross-segment floor seam (22-34%) exceeds the effect they measure
description:
RAISED by rf2-0qj9w's clock run (2026-08-01), and SOFTENED by its own run 5.

The candidate's clock instrument refuses bulk300/bulk100/narrow, and one of its
three grounds is the cross-segment floor seam. The SAME floor arm -- identical
work, no substrate, untouched by which adapter is installed -- read
3.147 / 2.437 / 2.349 ms across the three segments on run 3's bulk300. A 34%
spread, against 23% on bulk100 and 22% on narrow.

Floor-normalisation cancels a MULTIPLICATIVE seam and not an additive one, so a
bar row formed across segments that disagree by 34% is quoting the seam.

BUT RUN 5, taken on a genuinely idle box, read seams of 3.8% / 8.4% / 5.7% on
the same three rows with NOTHING CHANGED but how busy the machine was. So the
seam is not a structural property of the three-segment design; it is what a
loaded box does to it. That is worth knowing and is still worth pinning down,
because a bench lane whose seam swings 3.8% -> 34% on machine load cannot tell a
reader which regime a given published row was taken in.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a run that alternates segments WITHIN a round, or that
prices the seam with a second floor taken at the segment's other end, would say
whether the residue is an order effect, GC, or the adapter install itself -- and
would give every future row a seam number to be judged against rather than a
hope that it cancels.

title: MEASURE: Hicasso has NO clock rows at all — mount, bulk and per-keystroke are unmeasured, and the clock is what a user experiences
description:
RAISED by Mike (2026-08-01): 'the real test for performance is not bytes, that's a potentially poor proxy, it is browser performance.'

HE IS RIGHT, AND THE GAP IS WORSE THAN IT LOOKED. Verified against the tree: what has been taken for the Hicasso candidate is HOOK COUNT (2, flat across 1/7/20 reads) and PER-READ RETAINED HEAP (rf2-2rtt6.34, PR #7337). rf2-2rtt6.41 item 5 lists as NOT taken: retained size against the 0.4-0.5 KB shell target, bulk K=100/300, and THE PER-READ AND PER-KEYSTROKE PATHS. Every clock figure the programme has published — M1 mount 1.0150x [0.9820-1.0480], bulk-broad 0.6291x — is about the ADAPTERS (UIx vs Reagent), not about Hicasso.

SO THE PROGRAMME HAS NO WALL-CLOCK MEASUREMENT OF ITS OWN CANDIDATE.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE HEAP RESULT. Heap is an INDIRECT proxy: allocation rate drives GC pressure and GC pauses land in frame time, but the direction and magnitude of that transfer are unknown. 415 B/read more than Reagent could be invisible on the clock or could dominate a bulk update; nothing measured so far distinguishes those. There is an irony worth recording: the adversarial review named per-read heap as the programme's best remaining case BECAUSE it is the axis the architecture wins by construction — which made it the most attractive thing to measure and the least decisive.

THE WORK: take the candidate's clock rows on the same instrument as the donor rows they are judged against (validation.md is explicit that a candidate is judged against the donor row taken on ITS OWN instrument, and that a margin under 5% is instrument-limited rather than cleared). Mount, bulk K=100/300, narrow, and per-keystroke. Same-run donors, B/E/Q stamps, positive control predicted before the run, arm-order guard reportable, machine QUIET.

SEQUENCING: this outranks rf2-aqgr2 (the 415 B/read decomposition). Optimising a proxy before knowing whether the proxy matters is backwards. It also outranks any further heap work.

CROSS-CHECK: see rf2-<js-framework-benchmark bead> — an external instrument is the honest way to find out whether OUR harness is telling the truth about the clock.
notes:
INSTRUMENT GUIDANCE — DO NOT REACH FOR performance.mark BY DEFAULT (Mike asked whether the Performance API gives good benchmarking information, 2026-08-01; recorded by acting mayor).

THE SPLIT, and it decides which tool each row wants:

WHERE THE PERFORMANCE API IS GENUINELY GOOD
  - EVENT TIMING (PerformanceEventTiming) is the RIGHT instrument for the PER-KEYSTROKE row. It decomposes real input latency into input delay, processing time, and time to next paint — and it CAPTURES THE PAINT. That is strictly better than what the controlled-restore witnesses do today, which assert on the line AFTER dispatchEvent returns and therefore stop before the browser has shown anything. Use it.
  - Long Animation Frames (LoAF) gives attribution for frames that blow the budget — useful for the bulk row as a diagnostic, not as the headline number.
  - mark/measure are fine for coarse IN-PAGE RELATIVE timings.

WHERE IT WILL MISLEAD, and this is the half that matters
  - IT ONLY SEES WHAT YOUR JAVASCRIPT DOES. A mark around a render call captures your work and NOT the style recalculation, layout, paint and composite the browser performs afterwards. For MOUNT and BULK — where the interesting cost IS that downstream work — in-page timing systematically under-reports, and under-reports DIFFERENTLY per framework depending on how much each defers. Hicasso's whole design concerns WHEN work happens, so this is exactly the wrong error to make: it would flatter whichever arm does least synchronously.
  - THE CLOCK IS DELIBERATELY COARSENED. performance.now() is clamped for Spectre mitigation and meaningfully finer resolution requires cross-origin isolation. VERIFY THE CURRENT FIGURES against Chrome's own documentation before relying on any specific number — do not take a remembered value. The shape is certain even if the number needs checking: do not assume microsecond resolution; short operations need many iterations rather than one precise measurement.
  - performance.memory is Chrome-only, quantised, and reports WHOLE-HEAP rather than a retained set. This repo already treats it correctly — reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md records it as read 'alongside and not banked as independent'. Keep that posture.

THEREFORE, PER ROW:
  - per-keystroke  -> Event Timing (captures the paint)
  - mount, bulk    -> TRACING or CDP, not in-page marks (the cost is after your JS returns)
  - narrow         -> judgement; if the update is small enough that paint dominates, tracing again

THIS IS ALSO WHY rf2-rguy1 IS WORTH DOING: krausest/js-framework-benchmark drives chromedriver and reads CHROME'S TIMELINE rather than instrumenting the page, precisely because the timeline sees the whole frame. An external instrument built on tracing is the honest cross-check on whatever we build.

WITNESS COMPLETENESS. validation.md requires a 4-field form plus a 100-cell grid and sub-recompute localisation. clock_views.cljs renders one input (`kb-form` has one `kb-field` / `r-kb-field` / `u-kb-field`), and `write-draft!` deliberately makes all 101 layer-1 subscriptions recompute. INSTRUMENT REPAIR LANDED IN A PR — THE WINDOW IS UNBLOCKED. 2026-08-03 17:34 AUSEST.

PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7439 (worker/keystroke-0qj9w). NOT MERGED, NOT CLOSING THIS BEAD — the measurement half is still outstanding here.

Ruling item 1 is discharged in full. All four repairs are in:

1. FOUR-FIELD WITNESS per validation.md. `kb-form` now renders four controlled fields over an indexed `[:p0/draft i]` above the 100-cell grid, on all three substrate arms and the floor, canonical-DOM identical. A sample types one physical key into ONE field, rotating with the sample. The drafts carry forward while the grid is rebuilt, so exactly one value moves per keystroke — and `settleVerify` reads ALL FOUR fields back, so a handler that smeared into a neighbour refuses.

   Also included: SUB-RECOMPUTE LOCALISATION, which validation.md's per-keystroke budget line requires ("which subs recompute, not merely which boundaries re-run") and note item 1 named ("gates which subscriptions recomputed"). Both layer-1 queries are registered behind a recompute census; the driver arms it for ONE WARM-UP keystroke per arm, so no measured sample carries its cost. A substrate arm must recompute exactly 100 + 4; a floor arm must recompute NONE. Either disagreement refuses the row.

2. ONE RECORD PER PHYSICAL KEY, web-vitals' interaction-id rules, in a new pure adjudicator `clock_witness.cjs` (seam.cjs / order_guard.cjs's idiom). interactionId === 0 entries are part of no interaction — counted and published, never a record. Entries sharing a nonzero id are one interaction whose latency is the longest of them. The driver COUNTS THE KEYS IT PRESSES (`sentKeys`) rather than deriving them, so the 180-for-540 arithmetic is gone, and it stamps the whole physical key in the page AT OBSERVATION TIME (it stamped the arm only, and let the driver add round/sample at drain time — an entry one drain late inherited the next sample's index).

3. CENSORED <16 ms SAMPLES PUBLISHED. Keys that raised no entry are left-censored observations, not gaps and not zeroes. Every arm publishes sent / observed / censored (%); the observed statistics are labelled CONDITIONAL on clearing 16 ms; and the one population fact censoring permits is stated on the row — above 50% censoring the arm's true median is below 16 ms whatever the observed subset reads. `observed + censored === sent` is itself a gate.

4. `:lower-bound?` TIDY. Removed from `kb-floor-arm` and from the plan payload's `:lowerBound` (two sites), and the two stale prose sites in clock_views.cljs now say CALIBRATOR, matching the prose two screens above them.
