description:
FOUND while fixing rf2-210uq (diag-value-summary disclosure). tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/share.cljs carries value-free-summary, an INDEPENDENT hand-rolled EP-0015 shape summariser for share-URL decode errors. It is not a mirror of re-frame.error/diag-value-summary (so rf2-210uq did not touch it), but it reproduces the same two defects rf2-210uq removed, over an input the function's OWN docstring describes as attacker-controlled:

  (map? v)     {:type :map :keys (vec (sort-by str (keys v))) :count (count v)}
  (keyword? v) {:type :keyword :value v}

1. The :keys leg returns every top-level key, uncapped and unsanitised. The docstring says 'a forged share URL can smuggle :snapshot {:data ...} / arbitrary runtime values' -- so the key set is attacker-chosen, both in CONTENT and in SIZE, and it rides into a thrown ex-info that names itself value-free.
2. The keyword leg returns the raw keyword as :value, justified inline by 'a keyword IS a state name/address, not data'. That is the same guess rf2-210uq rejected in core: (keyword attacker-string) is not structural, and the leg applies no length bound.

rf2-210uq's ruling for the core primitive was to make the summary content-free BY CONSTRUCTION -- a closed :type vocabulary plus an integer :count, nothing else -- rather than bound a raw prefix. The same argument applies here, and this input is less trusted than core's.

DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED IN THE rf2-210uq PR: different artefact, different tree (tools/, bundle-isolated from production per CLAUDE.md), its own gates (tools_jvm_machines_viz / cljs-tools-machines-viz), and the keyword :value leg carries an explicit inline design justification that deserves its own ruling rather than a drive-by change.

NOT IN SCOPE (checked, different primitive): tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp's :rf.mcp/summary marker and its mcp-conformance wire-vocab schema deliberately ship :keys and a scalar :value as a documented cross-MCP dev-tool wire protocol. That is a token-budget marker, not an EP-0015 redaction primitive.

ACCEPTANCE: make value-free-summary content-free by construction or state why the share-decode path warrants keys; add a witness with a forged-URL payload carrying sentinel-bearing keys and an attacker-sized key set, asserting no sentinel in the thrown message or ex-data and a fixed serialized bound.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #7345 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7345), merged as 71d18ca62a. NO RULING NEEDED on the keyword leg: its inline justification was read, and it does not survive its own threat model — see below.

FIVE PATHS, not the two the bead named. I walked the summariser leg by leg and then walked the ex-data of every throw site in the namespace:
1. :keys on a map — every top-level key, uncapped/unsanitised, attacker-chosen in CONTENT and SIZE; removing it also removed the (sort-by str (keys v)) that ran str over caller-supplied keys, where a key with a THROWING toString replaced the documented ex-info with its own exception (the rf2-210uq path-5 shape, reproduced here and witnessed).
2. keyword :value — raw, unbounded.
3. {:url url} on :malformed-fragment — the WHOLE caller URL, raw. NOT IN THE BEAD. The encoder forty lines up already refuses to record :host because 'a viewer URL can carry a query string with a token in it' (rf2-8nzxib, hence :fragment-index); the decoder — handed URLs from elsewhere, so the more exposed side — carried the lot.
4. :cause (.-message e) on the base64 + transit stages — NOT IN THE BEAD, and a leak nobody wrote: transit/read calls JSON.parse and V8 embeds a prefix of its input in the SyntaxError (Unexpected token 'h', "hunter2-sw"... is not valid JSON), so the slot named for the cause republished the payload's plaintext.
5. :payload-version — NOT IN THE BEAD. The forged :v, raw and unbounded, reachable with arbitrary content through the string-compare fallback as well as the numeric path.

THE KEYWORD LEG'S JUSTIFICATION, quoted: '; a keyword IS a state name/address, not data'. It is a real argument — allowlist-chart-state says almost exactly that of :snapshot's :state — but it does not hold HERE, for three reasons all visible in the same file: (a) this function is NEVER handed a :state; its three call sites pass the whole chart-state / envelope / chart; (b) the leg therefore fires only when the payload is not the shape it was meant to be, i.e. when someone forged it — its premise is false exactly in the situation that runs it; (c) transit decodes ~:<anything> into a keyword of any length, namespace and content, with no bound applied anywhere. So brief-option (a): fixed, not escalated. The reasoning is recorded in the docstring so the next reader meets the decision rather than its absence.

REMOVED, NOT BOUNDED: :keys, the keyword :value, :cause, the raw :url. The summary is now a :type from a closed vocabulary plus an integer :count and nothing else — content-free BY CONSTRUCTION, fixed serialized size whatever arrives. KEPT: size/cardinality (an integer cannot carry a token fragment, and '2000-key map where an envelope was expected' IS the diagnosis) and the version, as the INTEGER the comparison used (nil when :v did not parse). Vocabulary aligned with re-frame.error/diag-value-summary (:length->:count, :value->:scalar, :symbol/:fn added) — still an independent implementation, not a mirror, but no reason for the two to disagree about what to call a set.

THE CAPSTONE IS A GRAMMAR, NOT A SENTINEL HUNT — which is the point, because the section it joins already claimed to assert this and passed anyway: it planted a secret in a VALUE position and walked STRINGS only, so leaked keyword KEYS were invisible to it. Now: content-free-summary? (key set subset of #{:type :count}, :type in the closed vocabulary, :count a non-negative integer), discloses? (pr-str of the whole ex-data and the thrown message must contain no 8-CHARACTER WINDOW of the sentinel — a fragment proves a leak, since a host parser message discloses exactly a prefix), and a fixed serialized bound (summary <48 chars, ex-data <600) against ~50 KB payloads, plus a growth pin: a 2000-key forged envelope throws ex-data at most 4 characters larger than a 2-key one. A sixth leak fails those with nobody planting a sentinel for it.

ADVERSARIAL CORPUS: sentinel-bearing keys of every key type transit carries (string, keyword, namespaced keyword, symbol, vector, MAP-as-key, number, boolean); keys that are <script> markup, an ANSI escape, CR/LF and a NUL byte; a 2000-key map; a keyword built from a 20x-repeated sentinel; a 4004-char string; a 16-digit card number; nesting; a lazy seq; a live fn; an opaque host object; a host object whose toString THROWS and a map KEYED by one; a URL with the sentinel in a query string; a fragment decoding to sentinel-bearing non-transit; forged :v on both the numeric and the string-compare paths.

MUTATION PROOF, witnesses written and watched failing FIRST: machines-viz-node-test exit 1 with 50 failures / 0 errors on unmodified share.cljs (the log prints the whole leaked key set verbatim, ANSI and markup included, and :rf.error/id nil for the exploding key — the summariser destroying the failure it was called to describe), exit 0 with 832 tests / 3470 assertions / 0 failures after.

GATES, all foreground, all re-run after rebasing onto a main that had moved 16 commits, all repeating their result: cljs-tools-machines-viz rc=0 (832/3470, compile 250 files 0 warnings), tools_jvm_machines_viz rc=0 (632/2537), scripts/test-fast-pr.sh rc=0 (PASS fast PR spine; consolidated node suite 12263/61442), clj-kondo 2026.04.15 at CI's flags rc=0 errors:0 (4527 warnings, all pre-existing), check_doc_slugs.py rc=0. The rf2-hofhx load flake did not appear in either spine run. tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md gained a 'What the thrown ex-data may carry' section; mkdocs does not cover that tree (no machines-viz entry, not under docs/), so check_doc_slugs.py is its gate and the added table's column counts + the new anchor were verified by hand.

FILED, NOT FIXED: rf2-oztox (P2) — grammar/definition-summary is the THIRD independent summariser in the repo and carries the same :keys (vec (sort-by str (keys definition))) leg over definitions arriving from forged share URLs, LLM responses and SCXML/Mermaid input. Not a copy of this fix: it deliberately carries structural diagnostics this one does not (:parallel, :state-count, :region-count, and the rf2-j538f7.18 :defect, which may itself name offending keys), three emitters stash it, and spec/API.md documents its shape under :spec-summary. That needs a ruling on what a definition's structural diagnostic may name, not a drive-by deletion. tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp's :rf.mcp/summary correctly left alone per the bead.

title: diag-value-summary leaks raw scalar prefixes and unbounded map keys into safe diagnostics
description:
FOUND auditing merged PR #7204. That PR deliberately routes malformed reserved-SSR-fx values through `re-frame.error/diag-value-summary` in BOTH the thrown message and ex-data, explicitly noting that a cookie `:value` may be a session token and claiming the summary carries shape, never value. The shared primitive does not meet that claim.

`diag-head` returns any scalar string of 24 characters or fewer verbatim and the first 24 characters of longer strings. Thus a short token/password is reproduced whole, while a longer bearer/session token leaks its raw prefix into exception messages, browser consoles, SSR host logs and ex-data before any record projector can classify it. The current test only proves a long fixture is not reproduced WHOLE and that its tail was truncated; it expressly accepts the raw prefix. The map leg separately returns every top-level key, uncapped and unsanitised. App/user-controlled map keys can therefore carry secret content and arbitrarily enlarge the supposedly bounded summary.

DEDUPLICATION: the durable note on closed rf2-zwgqe previously called out the unbounded map-key leg and explicitly said it needed a separate bead; no such Bead exists in the remote ledger. This issue owns both value-level failures of the one shared primitive rather than reopening that unrelated query-vector owner.

BLAST RADIUS: `diag-value-summary` is shared by core and mirrored into bundle-isolated adapter diagnostics (the source docstring names reagent-slim); audit all callers/mirrors. PR #7204 is a concrete always-on path, not the only possible egress.
acceptance_criteria: Make the summary genuinely content-safe and bounded: arbitrary strings/unknown scalars must not expose a raw prefix, and map summaries must not reproduce attacker/app-controlled key content or grow with an unbounded key set. Preserve only the minimal shape information callers actually need; if a structural identifier is required, pass it through an explicitly trusted field rather than guessing that arbitrary values are structural. Update every in-repo mirror and parity guard. Add dual-runtime witnesses using (1) a short secret, (2) a long secret whose first 24 characters are the sentinel, (3) sentinel-bearing dynamic map keys, and (4) a very large map; assert the serialized summary, thrown message and ex-data contain no sentinel and have a fixed bound. Include the PR #7204 `:rf.error/server-fx-args-invalid` path with a malformed cookie/header value so the production-facing use cannot regress.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7341 (branch worker/diagleak-210uq, 3 commits).

ENUMERATION FOUND FIVE PATHS, not the two named. Beyond the string :head and the map :keys the bead called out: (3) keywords/symbols got a :head with NO length bound at all, on the guess that such values are always structural -- (keyword user-string) is not; (4) numbers/booleans/unknown :scalar got a :head, and the :scalar leg called toString on a value the framework knows nothing about; (5) that same (str v) THREW on a hostile toString, so summarising an exploding value destroyed the failure it was describing, and the leaked :keys propagated the exploding object into whatever printed the ex-data. Paths 1/3/4/5 all traced to one helper (diag-head).

FIX: removed :head and :keys entirely. The summary is now {:type <closed-vocabulary keyword>} plus an integer :count for a counted collection or string, and nothing else -- content-free BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by redaction quality, so there is no prefix to bound, no key set to cap, and a FIXED serialized size whatever arrives. (str v) is gone from the path. Size/cardinality kept deliberately: it is the diagnostic value ('a 4000-char string where a keyword was expected') and an integer cannot carry a fragment of a token. No speculative trusted-id API added -- no production caller read :head/:keys (verified by sweep), and emit sites that need a structural identifier already pass it through their own trusted slot (ssr.response's :fx-id / :key).

MUTATION-PROVEN. Witnesses written first and watched red, then the fix reverted in place and watched red again: core witness exit 1 (65 failures, 2 errors) -> exit 0 (12 tests, 152 assertions); SSR witness exit 1 (18 failures) -> exit 0 (15 tests, 148 assertions). The mutated SSR run printed the production leak verbatim -- :head "SENTINELSENTINEL", the whole 16-char token, in the thrown message AND the ex-data.

ACCEPTANCE COVERED: all four required witnesses (short secret, long secret whose first 24 chars are the sentinel, sentinel-bearing dynamic map keys of every key type, 2000-key map) plus markup/ANSI/CRLF/NUL keys, nesting, and hostile toString. Capstone is a GRAMMAR check (keys subset of {:type :count}, closed :type vocabulary, integer :count, fixed 64-char bound) so a sixth leak fails without anyone writing a sentinel for it. The PR #7204 :rf.error/server-fx-args-invalid path is pinned by 11 token-bearing malformations driven through the real public fx handlers, posture-independent. Mirror (reagent2.impl.diag) updated byte-identically + parity corpus extended; Spec 015 and 009 restated.

GATES: core JVM 2205/11472 0F, reagent-slim 11/12 0F, routing 513/2983 0F, ssr 595/2941 0F, freehand 1288/8857 0F, npm test:cljs 12256/61283 0F exit 0, clj-kondo 2026.04.15 errors:0, mkdocs --strict exit 0. fast-pr spine exit 1 SOLELY from 35 failures in the untouched child-process-spawning test-quiet self-test ns (load contention, rf2-hofhx/rf2-2i1ay); same suite same tree is 0F standalone.

FOLLOW-UP FILED: rf2-m46qv -- tools/machines-viz value-free-summary is an INDEPENDENT (non-mirror) summariser with both same-class defects over forged-share-URL input. Not fixed here: different artefact/tree/gates, and its keyword leg carries an inline design justification needing its own ruling.

title: uix adapter: which controlled-input implementation a consumer gets depends on whether Reagent is in the bundle
description:
RULING NEEDED, and it is cheap to act on once made.

UIx decides, per element and at element-creation time, between plain React and
a port of Reagent's controlled-input workaround.
`uix.compiler.aot/create-uix-input` branches on
`uix.compiler.input/should-use-reagent-input?`, which — with
`*use-reagent-input-enabled?*` unset, the shipped default — answers "is
`reagent.impl.util/*non-reactive*` present, and false?" (uix.core 1.4.4,
`uix/compiler/input.cljs:15-21`).

So a consumer's decision to ALSO use the Reagent adapter silently changes how
the UIx adapter's `<input>` elements behave. Measured in real Chromium
(rf2-n3dxw, docs/design/hicasso/studio/controlled-input-two-implementations.md):

- plain React: the value converges INSIDE the discrete event; the caret is
  thrown to the end of the field on every write React makes.
- the port: the value and the caret both converge correctly, by offset from the
  end of the string — but one `requestAnimationFrame` later, never in-turn.

Those are materially different products. Today which one a consumer gets is a
fact about their classpath.

THE ACTION, once ruled: one `set!` of
`uix.compiler.input/*use-reagent-input-enabled?*` at
`re-frame.adapter.uix` load, pinning the semantics re-frame2 wants. The cost is
the ruling, not the implementation.

NOT DISPATCHABLE WITHOUT THE RULING: pinning to `false` takes the caret
behaviour away from mixed-bundle consumers who have it today; pinning to `true`
makes every UIx consumer's controlled input converge a frame late and couples
the UIx adapter to Reagent's batching queue. Mike decides.
notes:
RULING (Mike, 2026-08-01, verbatim: 'rule rf2-heqwo — make the React path the default'). Recorded by acting mayor.

WHAT IS RULED: the UIx adapter's controlled-input implementation is REACT'S OWN by default. It must NOT be selected by whether Reagent happens to be on the classpath.

THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES. uix.compiler.aot/create-uix-input branches on uix.compiler.input/should-use-reagent-input?, which asks 'is reagent.impl.util/*non-reactive* PRESENT and false?'. Every :browser-test bundle carries Reagent, and so does any app using both adapters — so adding Reagent alongside UIx SILENTLY changed how UIx's controlled inputs behave, with no diagnostic and no opt-in. The Reagent port makes the element UNCONTROLLED (deletes :value, installs defaultValue + a ref) and drives it from reagent.impl.batching/do-after-render, a requestAnimationFrame queue — one frame late. React's own path converges IN-TURN, before dispatchEvent returns, via its restore machinery (verified against react-dom 19.2.0 source in this repo).

THE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE CONSUMERS WILL SEE, stated plainly because it is real and must be documented rather than discovered: on a REFUSED keystroke the two paths differ. React converges in the same turn but THROWS THE CARET TO THE END ('12345' + a refused 'z' with the caret at [2 2] lands at [5 5]). The Reagent port preserves the caret but only one animation frame later. This ruling takes in-turn convergence and React-native, predictable behaviour over late caret preservation — and, more importantly, takes DETERMINISM over a silent classpath dependency. An app that behaves differently because of what else is in its bundle is the worse defect.

WHAT THIS RULING DOES NOT DO: it does not settle rf2-n3dxw, which stays open because NEITHER shipped path gives both same-turn convergence AND the caret where the edit left it. rf2-fki5d is the priced prototype that gets both halves (one flushSync per keystroke, a per-instance last-rendered value, no user-visible ref/effect/hook) and remains blocked on an element path to put it in. This ruling makes the default honest; fki5d would make it complete.

DISPATCHED. Operator-overturnable.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7339 (branch worker/heqwo-default).

RULING IMPLEMENTED (Mike, 2026-08-01: 'make the React path the default'). re-frame.adapter.uix now requires uix.compiler.input and pins the selector at namespace load:

  (set! uix.compiler.input/*use-reagent-input-enabled?* false)

It really was one set!. Production diff = one require + one set! + the comment block explaining both. Namespace load runs ahead of any render and therefore ahead of element creation, which is where uix.compiler.aot/create-uix-input reads the var. No classpath sniffing on the default path.

OVERRIDE PRESERVED: the var stays ^:dynamic and public, so a consumer who genuinely wants Reagent's port asks for it explicitly with (set! ... true) after requiring the adapter; binding works too. PR #7330's per-row pinning witnesses are undisturbed — all 16 pass in the browser (53 assertions), and NO measured row's expectation changed.

TWO WITNESS CHANGES, both explained in the PR: (1) unpin-input-implementation! now restores the adapter's pin (:react) rather than nil — release! calls it after every with-grid, so on main every row left the var cleared, handing the choice back to the bundle for every namespace running later in the same build; (2) the deftest was renamed the-input-implementation-is-the-adapters-choice-not-the-bundles, since its old premise ('the shipped default here is the port') is now false for a re-frame2 UIx app. It still asserts UIx's raw classpath answer, inside a with-uix-raw-default that clears and restores the pin.

MUTATION-PROVEN. Forcing the classpath-sniffing branch back on (set! ... nil) reds the new adapter suite: exit 1, 2 failures. Reverted with git diff empty. The proof is deliberately ORDER-INDEPENDENT: the suite snapshots the var at its own namespace load (value-at-load), because a live read inside a deftest can be masked by whichever sibling suite pins the implementation first.

DOCUMENTED, not hidden. docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md (published; mkdocs --strict covers it) gains a '## Controlled inputs and the caret' section stating the behaviour change consumers will see: React converges in-turn but throws the caret to the end ('12345' + refused 'z' at [2 2] lands at [5 5]); the port preserves the caret one animation frame late. It says why (a silent classpath dependency is the worse defect), how to opt back in, and names rf2-fki5d as the priced route to both halves. The hicasso studio page records Option C as TAKEN and re-hashes the witness blob.

DOES NOT SETTLE rf2-n3dxw — left OPEN deliberately. Neither shipped path gives both same-turn convergence and the caret where the edit left it.

SCOPE confirmed by the sibling: rf2-2rtt6.41 (PR #7338, not yet on main) proved Hicasso's boundaries are immune by construction (front.codec emits :input via react/createElement against the tag string, so create-uix-input is never on that path). This change is correctly confined to the UIx adapter. #7338 rebases onto this and updates its one row, the-selector-is-live-in-this-bundle.

GATES, all foreground with exit codes: test:cljs 0 (12226 tests / 61080 assertions, re-run post-rebase); test:browser 0 (908 tests / 5742 assertions); focused 7330 witnesses in browser 0 (16 tests / 53 assertions); test:adapter-smokes 0 (3 specs — reagent, uix, ui); test:bundle-isolation 0 (uix-reagent-free PASSES, so the new require drags no Reagent into a UIx-only bundle); test:browser-prod-elision 0 (120 tests / 527 assertions); scripts/test-fast-pr.sh 0 (PASS fast PR spine); UIx JVM probe 0; clj-kondo at the CI-pinned 2026.04.15 with lint.yml's exact invocation, errors: 0 and zero findings on any changed file; check_doc_slugs.py 0; mkdocs build --strict 0.

title: hicasso: a refused keystroke stays on the screen on the React adapter (controlled-restore, mined from Arm 2)
notes:
STILL OPEN 2026-08-02, and deliberately not rounded up. rf2-fki5d shipped
(PR #7371) and answers the headline residue FOR HICASSO'S ARM 1 ONLY.

WHAT IS ANSWERED. On Arm 1's element path a refused keystroke now converges
inside the discrete event WITH THE CARET AT THE POSITION BEFORE IT — mid-string
included — and so does every keystroke a normalising model rewrites. Both halves,
same turn, no ceremony in the view and no hook in the boundary shell. Measured on
the 100-cell grid at
`arm1_controlled_grid_dom_cljs_test/the-family-converges-in-one-turn-with-the-caret-where-the-edit-left-it`.

WHAT IS NOT, and why this bead stays open:

1. THE REACT ADAPTER — which is what this bead is titled for — IS UNCHANGED. A
   UIx consumer's `:input` is minted by `uix.compiler.aot/create-uix-input`, not
   by `front.codec`, so it is not on the path the converge was installed in.
   For that consumer a mid-string refusal still converges with the caret thrown
   to the end of the field ([5 5] where [2 2] is wanted), and so does every
   normalisation. Closing this bead would require either porting the converge
   into `re-frame.adapter.uix` — which today mints no `:input` of its own — or a
   ruling that Hicasso is the answer and the UIx adapter keeps React's caret.
   That is a decision, not an implementation, and it is filed separately.

2. THE RANGE ROW. A range still does not survive a converge that WRITES, on any
   path: React collapses to a cursor at the end of the value it wrote, the UIx
   port writes one offset into both ends. Restoring a range is a second
   algorithm — two offsets, not one — and out-of-band corrections (a server
   normalisation, a debounce) fire no change event at all, so they are off the
   converge's path by construction. Asserted as recorded behaviour on both
   shipped paths and on the arm.

3. IME. Still not established either way; rf2-o27h3 holds it with the real
   `CompositionEvent` harness that would settle it. Nothing in rf2-fki5d touches
   composition — the converge wraps the CHANGE slot only, never a key or
   composition event.

Matrix, the third column, and the mutation evidence:
docs/design/hicasso/studio/controlled-input-two-implementations.md.
close_reason: Closed on rf2-47sko's ruling (b) — delegated dossier review 2026-08-03 (operator-overturnable). Headline defect fixed for Hicasso Arm 1 by rf2-fki5d (PR #7371): every refusal and every normalising rewrite converges inside the discrete event with the caret where the edit left it (100-cell grid at arm1_controlled_grid_dom_cljs_test). On the React-pinned adapter path the refused keystroke ALSO converges in-turn (never stays on screen); the residue was the end-of-field caret, now RULED intended divergence — adapters keep substrate-native React semantics, in-turn+caret-correct together is Hicasso's differentiation. Durable record of the divergence: executable witness pair in controlled_restore_dom_cljs_test (react [5 5] where [2 2] is wanted, beside hicasso [2 2] / uix-port [3 3]), the matrix at docs/design/hicasso/studio/controlled-input-two-implementations.md, and docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md 'Controlled inputs and the caret' (which also documents the existing one-line consumer opt-in to UIx's caret-correct port). Range row: stays recorded behaviour on all paths (two-offset restore out of scope, asserted in tests). IME: settled separately — rf2-o27h3 harness measured it, rf2-digtt ruled and shipped the Hicasso carve-out (PR #7441).

title: hicasso: a deferred read forced inside ANOTHER boundary's render is permanent silent staleness, not just 'the wrong reader'
description:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF LANDED CODE, origin/main @ 40e309600e (arm1 last touched by 7e40db6481).

THE DEFECT. `read-key!`'s guard is `(nil? (.-frame rstate))` — "is ANY body running", not "is
THIS boundary's body running" (implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/runtime.cljs:569-580;
`rstate` is one module-level object at :277-283). So a deferred read forced while a DIFFERENT
boundary is rendering does not throw: it is silently pushed onto that boundary's scratch.

The case IS named in docs/design/hicasso/studio/arm1-lean-react-dogfood-judgement.md:237-241, and
dismissed there as "not a missing edge — the reader does re-render — but it is the wrong reader".
THAT DISMISSAL IS WRONG. A LazySeq caches its realised values, so the wrong reader re-renders
exactly ONCE; on that re-render its body walks the already-realised seq, `sub` is not called
again, the row keys leave its read set, `subscribe` identity changes and React unsubscribes those
edges. The correct reader never re-rendered, so the seq is never rebuilt. Net: one correction,
then PERMANENT SILENT STALENESS with no edge left to notify — precisely the "correct on screen,
frozen thereafter, attributable to nothing" class the same page (:229-230) calls the worst
failure the ruled surface can have.

AND THE STRUCTURAL SAFETY ARGUMENT HAS A HOLE. judgement:206-212 and runtime.cljs:119-124 justify
laziness-safety with "a seq at a prop position goes through `clj->js`". True for a NATIVE tag
(front/codec.cljs:232-242, `convert-prop-value` sends any `coll?` through `clj->js`). FALSE for a
BOUNDARY: `boundary-element` (front/codec.cljs:341-349) builds `body-props` as a plain CLJS map
and hands it through untouched as `#js {"rfProps" body-props}`; `shell` reads it back as a CLJS
map (runtime.cljs:883). No conversion, no realisation. And `realize-children`
(front/codec.cljs:288-298) flattens EXACTLY ONE LEVEL, so a nested seq in a boundary's children
survives unrealised too.

REPRODUCTION (carrier (a) — lazy seq at a boundary's prop position; state layer is the arm's own):

  (defview child [{:keys [rows]}]
    [:ul.child (for [r rows] [:li.cell (str r)])])        ; realised HERE, in child's window

  (defview parent [_]
    [child {:rows (for [id (sub [:dogfood/visible-ids])]
                    (:title (sub [:dogfood/todo id])))}])

With visible-ids = [0 1 2]:
1. `parent` renders. `(sub [:dogfood/visible-ids])` IS called (the for's binding expression is
   eager); `(sub [:dogfood/todo id])` is NOT. parent's read set = #{[F [:dogfood/visible-ids]]}.
2. `boundary-element` puts the unrealised seq in `body-props` under :rows.
3. `child` renders; its `for` walks `rows`; `read-key!` sees rstate.frame = F (non-nil) -> NO
   THROW. Three [:dogfood/todo id] keys land on CHILD's scratch. parent holds no row edge.
4. dispatch [:dogfood/edit-draft 1 "x"] then [:dogfood/commit 1] -> [:dogfood/todo 1] moves ->
   index dirties CHILD.

   dropped and the cells released.
6. EXPECTED: .cell for id 1 reads "x". ACTUAL: it still reads "todo 1", and no later write to any
   row will ever move it.

Carrier (b) is the same fault through nested children:
  (defview parent2 [_] [child2 (for [g groups] (for [id (ids g)] [:li (str (sub [:dogfood/todo id]))]))])

NOT COVERED BY ANY EXISTING WITNESS. `a-lazy-for-registers-its-edges-and-its-readers-re-run`
(arm1/runtime_cljs_test.cljs:126-160) and `reads-inside-a-lazy-for-update-the-dom-on-a-later-write`
(arm1/dogfood_dom_cljs_test.cljs:197-217) both keep the `for` inside a NATIVE tag in the same
boundary — the one path the codec does force.

RECOMMENDED FIX — realise at the boundary hand-off. In `boundary-element`, walk `body-props` for
seqs the way `convert-prop-value` already does for native props, and flatten children fully
rather than one level. Cost is paid where the escape is and the read lands on the RIGHT boundary.
This is also the only change that makes judgement:206-212's structural claim true as written.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: giving `read-key!` a per-boundary render token to refuse against. That is
per-boundary render identity — one line from the HD-002 candidate-ledger tripwire — and must not
be taken.

ACCEPTANCE: a witness in the arm's own suites that mounts carrier (a) (and ideally (b)), writes
to a row query the parent produced, and asserts the DOM moved; plus judgement:237-241 corrected
so the residual case is not described as benign.

FIXED — PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7329 (branch worker/escape-2rtt6-45).

REPRODUCED FIRST, independently, at the seam on the unfixed runtime: the parent's read set was #{[F [:dogfood/visible-ids]]} alone, the three [:dogfood/todo id] keys were on the CHILD, the child's second render with the same props read NOTHING, and a write to a row notified the child (hits 1) and not the parent (hits 0). Carrier (b) reproduced the same way once the outer for was written as the boundary's single trailing form (an 'into' at the call site splices it early and hides the fault).

THE FIX is the bead's own recommendation: realise at the hand-off. codec/realize-deep, called once on body-props in boundary-element —

  (defn realize-deep [v]
    (if-not (coll? v) v
      (do (if (map? v) (reduce-kv realize-entry nil v) (reduce realize-item nil v)) v)))

It forces every lazy sequence reachable from the props map and returns the map BY IDENTITY: realising a LazySeq caches into the seq, so nothing is rebuilt or copied. :children is a key in the same map, so ONE call covers both carriers — the nested-children carrier needed no change to realize-children's one-level flatten, and the ABI is therefore unchanged (forcing is sufficient; fully flattening would have altered documented semantics for no correctness gain). The two reducing fns are top-level vars because a fn literal at a reduce site mints a function object per collection visited and run! mints one of its own — hoisting them made the walk allocation-free and 31% faster.

NOT per-boundary render identity: rstate is still one object, nothing can tell one render attempt from another, no candidate ledger, no third hook. The <=2-hook budget is intact and measured at React's dispatcher (hook_ledger_dom_cljs_test's 1/7/20 rung, green); subscribe still closes over the read set and nothing else (make-subscribe untouched).

COST, MEASURED not assumed (:none build, Node 22, best of five): 69 ns for the dogfood row's props = 6% of the 1089 ns the boundary element build already costs; 233 ns with two hiccup children; 13.5 us for a 100-row collection prop against 15.1 us for the whole build. That ceiling compares outwards: the SAME collection at a NATIVE prop position costs 70.7 us through clj->js, so the position the structural claim already rested on is 4.7x dearer than the one this repairs.

WITNESSES, mutation-proved by removing the single call and restoring it. arm1/boundary_crossing_cljs_test.cljs (8 rows, node): exit 1 with 7 failures before, exit 0 / 24 assertions after. arm1/boundary_crossing_dom_cljs_test.cljs (2 rows, real Chromium): exit 1 with 4 failures before — the cell frozen at 'todo 2' through TWO writes and the edge count collapsing 7 -> 1 on the first — exit 0 / 10 assertions after. Every first-paint assertion passed on the BROKEN runtime, which is exactly why the second half is asserted.

title: hicasso: settle HD-002 6.1 -- does ONE generation fence cover the THREE fields the commit-side re-read compared?
description:
FROM the EP-0038 adversarial design review (2026-07-31). Assessed as the single
largest correctness risk in the programme, and it has had no bead.

THE SUBSTITUTION EVERYTHING RESTS ON. HD-002's allowed edge-diff operation is
affordable only because the commit does NOT deref. The predecessor's
`cell/commit!` called `obs/read` on every handle -- "a SECOND deref of every
subscription, after render already read it" -- as the invariant-5 tear check,
comparing THREE things (node-key, version, and frame/registry epoch) between the
render that produced the element and the commit about to publish it. It cost
1.19 ms of a 4.0 ms write for 300 reads
(docs/design/freehand/studio/bulk-rerender-where-the-time-goes.md:228-251, and
:239-243 for the three fields).

Hicasso replaces all of it with a GENERATION FENCE -- one O(1) comparison per
boundary (docs/design/hicasso/architecture.md:57-60;
docs/design/hicasso/hd-002-adjudication.md:146-163).

THE HOLE, marked [OPEN] by the repo's own adjudication
(hd-002-adjudication.md:459-476):

  "the record does not demonstrate that one epoch comparison covers all three
   failure modes. This page cannot verify it on paper, and if it is wrong the
   allowed operation in section 2 is under-specified rather than merely fast."

WHY IT IS THE TOP RISK. The tripwire's checklist item 4 is "Am I re-reading
subscription values at commit? ... Fired" (hd-002-adjudication.md:74). If the
fence proves insufficient, the tear check must come back -- and item 4 then
fires on CORRECTNESS grounds. Under Mike's Surface B ruling a collector loss is
NULL, not a fallback to grouped. So this substitution can end the product, and
it can do so however good the clock numbers are.

And EP-0036's withdrawal note is explicit that the guarantee is worth MORE than
spec/006 claims for it: the ablation found that "without the tear check a staged
site publishes stale and nothing ever corrects it", so the tear check was
retained and vindicated, not implicated
(docs/EP/EP-0036-the-freehand-view-substrate-programme.md:25-34).

WHAT SETTLES IT -- already specified, hd-002-adjudication.md:470-476. Two
witnesses, both stated as obligations BEFORE the fast path is trusted:
  (i) the staged-stale CI witness the record already names;
  (ii) an ADVERSARIAL witness that changes a subscription's VALUE between a
       boundary's render and its commit WITHIN ONE GENERATION, and asserts the
       committed DOM is not stale.

If (ii) cannot be constructed, record why -- the adjudication says that is
itself the answer, and it would be a strong one.

DO THIS BEFORE THE FAST PATH IS TRUSTED, not after. It is a witness, not a
runtime; it does not need the product to exist.
notes:
SETTLED — THE ANSWER IS NO. PR #7323 (branch worker/genfence-2rtt6-33). Witness: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/generation_fence_coverage_cljs_test.cljs. Doc: hd-002-adjudication.md §6.1 is now [SETTLED — NO] with the verdict recorded on the page that marked it [OPEN].

THE GROUND TRUTH (three fields, each independently load-bearing). cell.cljc:811-824 moved? / ui reactive.cljc:3048-3071 evidence-moved?: cold branch = rf= on :value; live branch = four clauses over three axes — :version (ordinary value move), :node-key (a same-id frame REINCARNATION whose version and epochs can tie exactly; cell.cljc:99-110 pins observation-port ABI v2 for it and asserts it AT LOAD), :frame-epoch/:registry-epoch (a frame or registry move that did not change the value). Spec 006 invariant 5 is the normative statement. Axis-isolation is already pinned by shell_cljs_test.cljc:841 invariant-5-every-axis-is-still-compared-on-a-retained-handle, and I mutation-proved it: deleting the :node-key and :registry-epoch clauses reds exactly those two sub-rows ({:delta 0} vs {:delta 1}), leaving :version, :frame-epoch and the unmoved control green.

WHAT THE FENCE COMPARES IN THE BUILT RUNTIME (read off origin/worker/arm1-2rtt6-9 arm1/runtime.cljs, not the design record): render-body captures !generation, runs the body ONCE, compares, and on a match RETURNS. !generation has exactly one writer — flush! — reached only from mark-dirty!, whose only caller is the per-cell value-change watch that acquire-cell! installs AT COMMIT. The commit itself compares nothing ('no commit-phase deref' is the stated fence).

VERDICT: DOES NOT COVER, and the three axes share one answer because the two mechanisms do not guard the same WINDOW. Predecessor = render probe .. COMMIT re-read (the render->commit gap). Fence = capture gen .. one body run .. compare (closes when the body returns). The fence covers a hazard the three fields never addressed — a commit landing BETWEEN TWO READS OF ONE BODY — and does not reach the gap. One-for-one on a different axis, not one-for-three.

Residual coverage of the gap comes from the epoch-sum getSnapshot + React's own commit-time snapshot re-check — real, and row 1 proves it works — but keyed on the same counter: version axis covered for a RETAINED key only; node-key and frame/registry-epoch axes have no counterpart at all.

THE CONCRETE TEARING INTERLEAVING (row 2, reproduced green over the real sub layer / real frames / real watches on the React-spine host): a boundary reads key K that nothing holds; K has no cell, no watch, no epoch, getSnapshot = 0. A write moves K before React commits. Nothing is marked -> the generation does NOT move, so the change is genuinely WITHIN ONE GENERATION (exactly the adversarial witness §6.1 demanded). The commit acquires: baseline deref takes the NEW value, watch armed one move too late. getSnapshot answers the SAME number, so React's re-check finds no tear and schedules nothing. The boundary paints the OLD value and NOTHING EVER CORRECTS IT. Verbatim Spec 006 invariant 5's stronger half.

DIVERGENCE FROM THE DESIGN RECORD worth noting: arm1's own generation_fence_dom_cljs_test 'Case 2' is labelled as §6.1's case but dispatches AFTER the mount has settled — ordinary invalidation on an already-committed key, i.e. row 1's case, not the staged one. Its comment concedes 'the fence cannot see this one'. Also, acquire-cell!'s own comment records that HD-002's 'acquire without deref' is not implementable against this substrate; the baseline deref it added is the thing that swallows the staged move.

FILED, NOT IMPLEMENTED (Arm 1 owns the collector surface): rf2-2rtt6.42 (P0) the defect, with three candidate repairs costed against the tripwire — smallest is one comparison per NEWLY ACQUIRED key per commit, O(new edges), zero on a steady-state re-render, so it does NOT by itself fire tripwire item 4; what the finding removes is the record's stated reason for believing item 4 can stay unfired on correctness grounds. rf2-2rtt6.43 (P2) re-point the witness at the arm's runtime once it is on main (the generation machinery is transcribed today because the runtime is on a spike branch).

title: hicasso: a read outside the render extent must be a LOUD ERROR, not a missing edge -- four witnesses
description:
FROM the EP-0038 adversarial design review (2026-07-31). This is the deepest
consequence of the laziness finding recorded on rf2-2rtt6.

THE FAILURE MODE. A `(sub q)` evaluated outside the boundary's render extent
registers no edge. The boundary then never re-renders when that subscription
moves. The symptom is a permanently stale region of the page with NO error, no
warning and no diagnostic -- the worst bug class this repository has a name for.
Under Arm 1 an eager codec (HD-016's ABI: "nested/lazy sequences are realized
once and flattened one level", docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md:337) fixes the
`for` case. It does NOT fix the residue.

THE RESIDUE, four cases that survive an eager codec:
  1. a lazy seq handed straight to React as `children` -- React iterates it
     during the PARENT's reconciliation, after the component function returned;
  2. `(sub q)` inside a render prop passed to a `defhost` / `[:> ...]` component
     -- invoked in the foreign component's render, a different extent and
     possibly a different boundary's;
  3. `(sub q)` inside an event handler (the charter retires `@`-anywhere,
     docs/design/hicasso/charter.md:255-258, but nothing enforces it);
  4. `(sub q)` inside a `delay` / `lazy-seq` the author returns as a prop value.

THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS IN THIS REPOSITORY AND IS THREE LINES. Freehand's
collector refuses a read with no active candidate:

  implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/cell.cljc -- `observe!` (426)
  raises :rf.error/view-read-outside-render; `with-capture` (380-397) binds the
  candidate for the SYNCHRONOUS body evaluation only, and its docstring already
  names this exact hazard: "A view's children are elements the host renders
  LATER, outside this extent".

Hicasso's design record does not carry that guard anywhere -- not in HD-002, not
in HD-016, not in the HD-002 adjudication.

WHAT TO DO.
  - Pin "a `sub` with no bound collector THROWS" as a v0 runtime obligation, in
    production as well as dev (it is a branch on a nil check, not a subsystem;
    HD-005's zero-cost-when-absent posture is about the evidence sink, not
    about correctness).
  - Add the four cases above to the P1 witness set (validation.md:315-326) as
    named rows, each asserting the throw rather than asserting a re-render.
  - Record the verdict either way. If any of the four CANNOT be made to throw --
    e.g. because the read lands inside another boundary's live extent and is
    silently attributed to it -- say so explicitly; that is a real limit of the
    Surface B ruling and the guide must state it.

WHY P1. The Surface B ruling makes the ambient collector the only acceptable
read surface, so a silent-staleness class in it is a product defect, not a
polish item. It also converts the laziness finding from an open correctness
question into a bounded, testable one.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7329: PARTIAL DISCHARGE, owner stays OPEN. codec/realize-deep now closes the lazy-seq-at-boundary-prop carrier and the nested-boundary-children carrier inside the producing body's collector window; the node and real-Chromium witnesses prove ownership, two later writes, durable edges, teardown, and fail when the one hand-off call is removed. This does not discharge this Bead's explicit-deferral/render-prop remainder: PR #7329 itself correctly records that a delay handed across a boundary and deref'd in the child is the same wrong-owner/permanent-staleness fault, and a foreign render callback can still run under another live boundary extent. Keep the exact owner here; do not create a duplicate or extend realize-deep into forcing delay/function semantics. Finish the remaining loud-error/declared-limit witnesses at their real crossings.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7333 FOLLOW-UP. In merge 9d3b423d17a0d971a06de0538ed9ffa880020a7d, realize-entry is (defn- realize-entry [_ _ x] (realize-deep x) nil): map values are checked, keys are not, despite the stated invariant covering every reachable unforced delay. Bound the repair to walking map keys and values through the existing refusal, without forcing delays or adding render identity/general walker machinery. Add a mutation/direct witness: a key-held unforced Delay must be loud; with the key check removed, first child render records the edge and the cached second render drops it. Preserve ordinary map behavior and key/value identity semantics. Also add the originally requested named P1 validation rows, or explicitly record why their normative location changed.
close_reason:
AUDIT-REOPEN #7333 discharged by PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7370.

MAP KEYS. realize-entry was (defn- realize-entry [_ _ x] (realize-deep x) nil); it now walks the key half through the same realize-deep, so a key-held unforced Delay meets the same refusal, in the same window, with the same recovery. No general walker, no render identity, nothing forced. The comment that justified skipping keys was wrong twice and both are now asserted: a Delay hashes by object identity (cljs.core extends IHash on default to goog/getUid) so hashing never forces one, and a PersistentArrayMap hashes nothing at all, so even an unrealised lazy seq can sit at a key position.

MUTATION PROOF. Restoring the exact pre-fix text: node exit 1, 24 tests / 80 assertions, 9 failures, the decisive row two renders deep printing 'UNREFUSED: the child's first render holds the edge and its cached second render drops it -- actual: (not (= #{[.../arm1-deferred-read [:dogfood/todo 1]]} #{}))', with the parent's own read set #{} in the same output. Restored: exit 0, 24 tests / 79 assertions, git diff empty. Every first-paint assertion passed on the mutated runtime, which is why the decisive witness renders twice.

COST, MEASURED. Walking keys unconditionally costs +51-67% of the walk at the dogfood row's props and 7.6-9.9% of the whole boundary element build. A keyword? short-circuit -- a Keyword is provably neither a collection nor a Delay, and proving it via coll? falls through to native-satisfies? -- takes that to 0.2-2.8%. The first cut of the measurement was confounded (a local arm against the real realize-deep measured the throw form, reporting the shipping arm 9-20% faster than a walk doing strictly less work) and was re-taken with all three arms identical on an idle box.

NAMED P1 ROWS. validation.md's P1 Witness set now carries the four deferred-read crossings as four named rows with their real verdicts, not four assertions of a throw: (1) lazy seq as children is repaired and a throw would be wrong; (2) a render prop invoked inside another boundary's live extent CANNOT be made to throw -- recorded as a declared limit of the Surface B ruling, since read-key! asks whether any body is running and refusing it needs the per-boundary render identity HD-002 rejected; (3) event handler throws; (4) delay refused / seq repaired, now at both halves of a map entry. The mutable-reference case is the second declared limit.

GATES. test:cljs exit 0 (12,287 tests / 61,536 assertions); test:browser exit 0 (931 / 5,840); test-fast-pr.sh exit 0; clj-kondo 2026.04.15 (CI's pin) exit 0, errors: 0; check_doc_slugs.py over 653 files exit 0. Hook budget and identity semantics unchanged and asserted.

title: hicasso: win condition (1) is internally inconsistent -- mount<=1.0x Reagent and codec<=1.10x UIx cannot both hold (OPERATOR)
description:
FROM the EP-0038 adversarial design review (2026-07-31). ONLY THE OPERATOR
AMENDS THE BAR -- this bead surfaces an arithmetic contradiction, it does not
propose to resolve it under delegated authority.

THE CONTRADICTION. docs/design/hicasso/validation.md:240-241 states the
given-continuation win condition as:

  "(1) mount <= 1.0x Reagent-on-subs, same run and same instrument, with the
   codec inside 1.10x of direct UIx `$` on M1"

Post-rf2-2rtt6.25, UIx-on-subs and Reagent-on-subs are at PARITY on that exact
row: 1.0243x [0.9937 - 1.0549] (validation.md:268;
docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-converged-witness-set.md:522). A codec at exactly
1.10x direct UIx therefore lands at 1.0243 x 1.10 = 1.127x Reagent.

The two clauses cannot both be satisfied. Satisfying the codec clause fails the
ship clause by ~13%. Satisfying the ship clause requires a runtime hiccup
interpreter to run for <= 0.98x the cost of UIx's compile-time `$` -- i.e.
interpretation must be free or negative.

THE MEASURED COST OF INTERPRETATION, two independent instruments:
  - donor-r2 / uix (equal hooks, codec the only variable): 1.162-1.286 on
    mount-M, 1.125-1.222 on mount-U
    (docs/design/hicasso/studio/hd8-composed-donor-arm.md:231,253)
  - free-i / free-ik (interpreted leaf vs compiled leaf, ViewCell held): 1.216
    [1.092-1.425]
    (docs/design/freehand/studio/compiled-tier-browser-worth-it.md:275)

AND THE ONE MECHANISM THAT COULD CLOSE IT IS RULED OUT OF THE SURVIVING ARM.
HD-004 (docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md:98-110) permits only codec-work caching
in the lean arm and assigns template extraction with data-encoded hole plans to
the PATCH arm. PATCH has been dropped by operator ruling. So the accelerant
class that could make interpretation approximately free is no longer in the
programme.

WHAT IS BEING ASKED. A ruling on the mount row. Candidates, stated without
preference:
  (a) mount <= ~1.15x Reagent, with bulk-broad and bulk-narrow as the hard rows
      (bulk is where the parent already wins: UIx 0.6291x Reagent,
      p0-converged-witness-set.md:347);
  (b) mount graded DIAGNOSTIC and the "codec <= 1.10x direct UIx `$`" clause
      promoted to the gate in its place;
  (c) leave the bar exactly as written and accept that K1/K7 is the likely
      terminal state -- a legitimate and pre-registered outcome
      (validation.md:356,362), and adapters-only is recorded as SUCCESS.

Whatever is ruled, the two clauses of win condition (1) must stop contradicting
each other before a worker is scored against them.
close_reason: RULED by Mike 2026-08-01: 'relax "as fast as Reagent on mount"'. The self-contradiction is resolved — mount <= 1.0x Reagent is no longer the gate; the codec-within-1.10x-of-direct-UIx condition stands as the operative mount criterion, with ~1.18x Reagent as its consequence when a Reagent-relative figure is wanted (derived by the acting mayor under delegation, operator-overturnable). Full text on rf2-2rtt6.1.

title: hicasso: enter Freehand's codec as a fourth donor arm before writing a third interpreter
description:
FROM the EP-0038 adversarial design review (2026-07-31).

WHY. HD-008's verdict is that "the residual mount deficit is the hiccup
interpreter rather than the spine" (docs/design/hicasso/validation.md:238). But
the arm it measured was reagent-slim's interpreter, and it read
`donor-r1 / reagent-slim` = 1.000-1.120, i.e. INDISTINGUISHABLE from
reagent-slim itself (docs/design/hicasso/studio/hd8-composed-donor-arm.md:239).
So what HD-008 actually established is that *reagent-slim's* interpreter is the
deficit. This repository contains a SECOND runtime hiccup interpreter that was
never entered in that comparison:

  implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/react.cljs   (1,203 lines)
  implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/conversion.cljc (906 lines)

conversion.cljc is the profile-driven, bounded js/Map-backed codec cache
(new-cache 111-114, remembered 116-130) that PR #7077 built after caller
attribution; docs/design/freehand/studio/bulk-rerender-where-the-time-goes.md
:277-281 names exactly that mechanism as the proven shape of the win.

WHAT TO DO. Add a fourth arm to the HD-008 instrument
(implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/hd8_*): Freehand's
`react/element` codec driving the SAME `:f>` function-component boundaries and
the SAME UIx `use-subscribe` spine as `donor-r1`, on the SAME M and U witnesses,
in the same run. Everything except the codec held fixed. Canonical-DOM parity
gates it as usual.

WHAT IT ANSWERS. The single question the mount row turns on: is the deficit
"hiccup interpretation" or "reagent-slim's hiccup interpretation"? The published
figures make it decidable -- `donor-r2 / uix` is 1.162-1.286 on mount-M and
1.125-1.222 on mount-U (hd8-composed-donor-arm.md:231,253), and win condition
(1) asks for a codec inside 1.10x direct UIx `$` (validation.md:240-241). A
Freehand-codec arm either lands inside that band or it does not, and either
answer is worth more than six weeks of writing a third interpreter to find out.

FENCES. Instrument-only, bench lane (HD-017 carve-out). No shadow-cljs build id
(ride :hicasso-bench via the existing route). Do NOT edit
implementation/freehand/src -- the donor freeze stands; a bench arm may
`:require` it. Publish to docs/design/hicasso/studio/ and to this bead with the
producing commit SHA and reproduction command per validation.md:335.
notes:
MEASURED AND PUBLISHED (worker, rf2-2rtt6.29). Freehand's codec is entered as
HD-008's FOURTH DONOR ARM. Two full three-run sweeps, both exit 0, every gate
green. Studio page: docs/design/hicasso/studio/hd8-freehand-codec-donor-arm.md

=== THE ANSWER: FREEHAND'S CODEC IS MATERIALLY WORSE THAN REAGENT-SLIM'S ===

donor-fh / donor-r1 is THE CODEC RATIO — the boundary (slim's own :f>), the
outer skeleton, the single use-subscribe hook at its two-arity form with the
frame PINNED, the dispatch-for lookup, the author's handler closure, the page,
the floor arm, the rounds and the interleaving schedule are all held FIXED.
Only the codec that builds the markup inside the 300 boundaries varies: 900 of
the M page's 903 elements and 300 of the U page's 301.

Over both sweeps:

  write-narrow  1 boundary re-renders    0.898 - 1.143   INDISTINGUISHABLE 2/2
  mount-U       300 bnd x 1 el, + mount  0.973 - 1.363   disjoint above 1.0, 5/6
  mount-M       300 bnd x 3 el, + mount  1.078 - 1.306   disjoint above 1.0, 6/6
  write-bulk    300 bnd re-rendered      1.273 - 1.550   disjoint above 1.0, 2/2

Not one of the sixteen codec ranges sits disjointly BELOW 1.0, so nothing in
the record says Freehand's codec is ever the faster of the two. The gap tracks
how much of the window is markup construction, which is exactly what a codec
difference should do.

AGAINST RAW UIX (the comparison the operator asked for, since the mount bar is
suspended):
  donor-fh   mount-M 1.358 - 1.746   mount-U 1.127 - 1.655   bulk 1.722 - 2.000
  donor-r1   mount-M 1.179 - 1.373   mount-U 1.051 - 1.328   bulk 1.111 - 1.429
Both indistinguishable from uix on the narrow row.

AGAINST THE SHIPPING PATHS, sweep 1: donor-fh / reagent 1.391 - 1.625 (M) and
1.322 - 1.425 (U); donor-fh / reagent-slim 1.018 - 1.237 (M) and 1.036 - 1.135
(U). For scale in the same runs, donor-r1 / reagent 1.172 - 1.278 and
donor-r1 / reagent-slim 0.900 - 0.979.

=== WHAT THIS SETTLES FOR THE PROGRAMME ===

1. HD-008's conclusion SURVIVES and is now quantified rather than inferred.
   "The residual mount deficit is the hiccup interpreter" was drawn from a row
   (donor-r1 / reagent-slim = 1.000-1.120) that is INDISTINGUISHABLE, so it
   established only that reagent-slim's interpreter is the deficit. Swapping
   ONLY the interpreter now moves mount-M by up to 31% and bulk re-render by up
   to 55%. Interpretation is the dominant term a codec controls.

2. "CONSUME FREEHAND'S CODEC RATHER THAN AUTHOR ONE" IS NOT A FREE WIN, and
   this arm makes that decidable without six weeks of work. On these witnesses
   it is the worse of the two codecs already in the tree. That does not make it
   the wrong codec to consume - it is also the more capable one (per element it
   asks the controlled-input door, the v/spread-safe caller split, the DOM
   top-layer pair, the declared custom-element property set, the id-slot
   cardinality check and the exact-first class/style alias composition, none of
   which reagent-slim's walk asks) - but the choice now has a price on it.

RECOMMENDATION (advisory, not a ruling): Hicasso should NOT author a third
interpreter AND should NOT adopt Freehand's. The cheapest runtime codec in the
tree is reagent-slim's, and the arm carrying it (donor-r1) is already at or
below reagent-slim on mount and within 1.05-1.37x of raw UIx. Consume it, and
spend the programme's clock on the three genuinely new REACTIVITY mechanisms
the adversarial review identified.

=== METHOD, AND WHAT IS NOT LEVELLED ===

NEW GATE 0b, codecs-differ?, fatal before anything is measured. A
donor-fh / donor-r1 reading of 1.0 would be unreadable without it: it could
mean "the codecs cost the same" or "the arm ran one codec twice", and no clock
reading tells those apart. The parity gate cannot answer it - making the arms
agree is its whole purpose. So the difference is DEMONSTRATED on a form the two
treat differently and no arm uses: ^{:key ...} vector metadata, which slim
honours and Freehand refuses by name. Pass on every run of both sweeps.

RESIDUALS, each with its direction stated:
 (a) :f>'s wrapper always converts the body's return through as-element.
     donor-r1 returns hiccup (the call does the work); donor-fh returns a
     finished element (the call is a pass-through). donor-fh therefore pays one
     extra call plus ~5 predicates per boundary. Bounded: the measured mount-M
     gap is 0.60-0.80 ms over 300 boundaries = 2-3 us per boundary, against
     tens of nanoseconds for the residual - under 1% - and it runs AGAINST
     Freehand.
 (b) The codec is measured with NO candidate above it, which is IN FREEHAND'S
     FAVOUR: a Freehand application renders inside a declared boundary and
     additionally records an event site per handler. So this prices
     Freehand-the-CODEC exactly and Freehand-the-SUBSTRATE from BELOW.
 (c) Adding the arm changes k in the interleaving schedule, so EVERY column
     here (including donor-r1/r2/uix/reagent/reagent-slim) is a fresh take on a
     5/6-arm plan and is NOT comparable figure-for-figure with the four-arm
     rows on hd8-composed-donor-arm.md. Nothing is quoted from that page and
     nothing here amends it. The one re-taken column that moved visibly is
     named on the page: donor-r1 / reagent-slim on mount-M reads 0.900-0.979
     here where that page published 1.000-1.120.

THE ONE UNSTABLE ROW, named rather than averaged away: mount-U in the uix run
straddles 1.0 in sweep 1 (0.973-1.247, one round at 0.9726 and five at
1.1233-1.2466) and is disjoint above 1.0 in sweep 2 (1.065-1.164). Read it as
"between indistinguishable and ~1.25x slower" and judge nothing on a finer
margin. Every other U row, both sweeps, is disjoint above 1.0.

GATES, both sweeps, every one of the three adapter runs: arm-order guard 12/12
reportable and ZERO refusals; canonical-DOM parity with can-fail? true (this is
what proves Freehand's codec builds the SAME page); codecs-differ? pass;
positive control predicted 1.9934 from the witness arithmetic BEFORE the run,
+/-30%, every round inside - pass 6/6 segments with 16 of 18 rounds BELOW
prediction, the direction a fixed per-mount term predicts; DOM read-back 0
unverified of 7,722 writes per sweep; rung-2 lowering check green; and the
guard's, the yield-correction contract's and the corrected-table's own
self-tests all before anything was measured.

NO BAR VERDICT IS ISSUED. The mount win condition is suspended pending the
operator's amendment (post-.25 UIx/Reagent parity at 1.0243x makes "mount <=
1.0x Reagent" require a free-or-negative interpreter and contradicts the
codec-within-1.10x-of-UIx condition). Everything is reported against raw UIx
and the existing donor arms.

FENCES HELD: instrument-only, bench lane; nothing under implementation/*/src
touched; no shadow-cljs build id added; :hicasso-bench reused.
FOLLOW-UP FILED: rf2-2rtt6.40 - stamp the LANDED whole-tree anchor on the
studio page after the PR merges (a worker cannot know its own rebased sha).
PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7322 (branch worker/codecarm-2rtt6-29,
producing commit 62059f140bbac5d0cdeb11e1a72ee922d5dd3883). NOT merged - the
mayor merges.
close_reason: VERIFIED DONE ON MAIN (PR #7322 merged). Three commits carry it: e385cef113 'Freehand's codec enters HD-008 as a fourth donor arm', f7feccac06 'publish the fourth donor arm's two sweeps', c5c64ad4e7 'count the falsifiable prediction over both sweeps, not one'. VERDICT: Freehand's codec is WORSE than reagent-slim's on every row that resolves — donor-fh/donor-r1 mount-M 1.078-1.306 (disjoint above 1.0 in 6/6 segments), write-bulk 1.273-1.550, mount-U 0.973-1.363; against raw UIx, donor-fh 1.358-1.746 on M where slim's codec reads 1.179-1.373. Not one of sixteen codec ranges sits disjointly below 1.0. That verdict grounded the standing ruling recorded on rf2-2rtt6: Hicasso AUTHORS NO CODEC and consumes reagent-slim's. No audit note on this bead; the close simply had not stuck. Closed on verification of main, not memory.

title: STANDARD: restate the CLOCK gate lines post-.25, and clear five stale-figure sites the advisory found
description:
RAISED by the rf2-2rtt6.7 donor-gate advisory (full text: ai/findings/2026-07-31.rf2-2rtt6.7-donor-gate-advisory.md, local-only; compact advisory note on rf2-2rtt6.1). The advisory calls the first item a PRECONDITION before any candidate mount row is judged — Wave-1 will produce candidate mount rows, so this is on the critical path.

1. THE CLOCK GATE LINES HAVE HAD NO POST-LANDING RESTATEMENT. The standard publishes M1 at 1.2310x, measured PRE-rf2-2rtt6.25. The coldmount page re-derives the SAME witness POST-.25 at 1.0054x (excess mean 0.00 ms — the L1 mount red zone closed). MERGED-PR AUDIT #7309 — completeness / correctness / implementation quality.

The restatement is impressively systematic: it updates every operative page, preserves the historical measured rungs, distinguishes marginal slopes from boundary totals, carries instrument/regime stamps, qualifies ratio portability, builds strictly, and its two authored patches landed exactly around one unrelated audit checkpoint. The gate's warrant and causal provenance nevertheless need repair.

The new normative line relies on PR #7306's component decomposition and says `R2Q2B` was held out of every identification and supplies a check the derivation never used. That observation already feeds `key-2`/`key-gap` and mandatory `key-ok?` model admissibility. The direct `R2Q2B − R1Q1` check also shares `R1Q1` with the R=1 regression used to derive the key term. These are useful consistency calculations, but not independent evidence; "four readings, three instruments" overcounts reuse of the same sweep observations. Upstream evidence owner rf2-5prok and normative component owner rf2-hvl5s are already open for this exact dataflow defect.

The pages also state that both .13 and .25 cut UIx retained heap and that .25 removed the shipping cold read's double build. Audit #7305 drove the canonical bare `createRoot.render` adapter path and measured 2N constructions through N=10,000: the timer wins before passive subscribe on the public schedule. No retained-heap delta from .25 is established, either; the explicit ladder correction `3,552 − 769 = 2,783` is entirely .13's retained-reaction term.
