title: P0 heap red-zones are not comparable: rf2-2rtt6.4's 4 roots share one subscription set (amortised 4x) while the ladder uses distinct queries
description:
P0 AUDIT FINDING (read-only cold read of the P0 baseline wave, 2026-07-31, before candidate results open).

THE TWO RETAINED-HEAP RED-ZONE SETS ON rf2-2rtt6.1 ARE BOTH MARKED OPERATIVE AND THEY MEASURE DIFFERENT QUANTITIES.

WHAT IS WRONG. rf2-2rtt6.4's heap driver holds P0_ROOTS=4 roots per arm and divides the retained delta by ROOTS*perRoot = 1,200 boundaries (implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs lines 264 and 347). All four roots render (ux/u-root arms/frame-id) / (rg/u-root arms/frame-id) -- THE SAME frame-id and THE SAME [:p0/cell 0..299] query vectors (p0_uix.cljs:111, p0_heap.cljs arm-table, p0_arms.cljs frame-id). One frame means one subscription cache, so the page holds 300 reactions at refcount 4 and divides them over 1,200 boundaries. ITS "EXCLUSIVE RETAINED PER BOUNDARY" AMORTISES THE SUBSCRIPTION HALF OF EVERY READ ACROSS FOUR BOUNDARIES.

rf2-2rtt6.5's ladder is the opposite BY EXPLICIT DESIGN and its page says so: "Every read is a distinct query ... so no two boundaries share a reaction and the per-read figure carries the subscription as well as the hook. That is ... the honest worst case: a page where many boundaries read ONE shared sub pays the reaction once, not once each."

MARKUP DENSITY AND BOUNDARY COUNT DO NOT EXPLAIN THE GAP -- THEY ARE HELD CONSTANT. .4's grid witness is 301 elements over 300 boundaries (1 el/boundary) x 4 roots = 1,200 boundaries. The ladder's Curve B is 1,200 span.cell boundaries (1 el/boundary). Same reader (CDP getHeapUsage after a forced collection), same arm-minus-floor rule against a component-free React floor, same one read per boundary. The answers still differ:

  exclusive retained B/boundary @ 1 read | .4 grid (4 shared roots) | .5 ladder (distinct queries) | gap
  Reagent-on-subs                        |   947                    | 1,565                       | 1.65x
  UIx-on-subs                            | 2,134                    | 3,811                       | 1.79x
  UIx / Reagent                          | 2.254x                   | 2.435x                      | 8%

THE SHARING MODEL PREDICTS THE GAP AND A THIRD INSTRUMENT CONFIRMS IT. Solving S + H = ladder and S/4 + H = .4grid for the subscription half S gives Reagent S ~= 824 B and UIx S ~= 2,236 B. rf2-2rtt6.12's same-run ablation (distinct queries) measures the Reagent subscription half directly at 866 B (5% apart) and the UIx side at 1,684 B live + 769 B retained-dead = 2,453 B (9% apart). Three instruments, one arithmetic. The RATIO survives only because the amortisation is common-mode across both arms.

WHY THIS MATTERS NOW, BEFORE THE TOURNAMENT.

(1) THE STATED REASON FOR NOT RE-RUNNING THE HEAP AXIS IS FALSE AS STATED. rf2-a4x1o, the studio README and p0-uix-on-subs-frontier-arm.md's "not superseded" banner all justify converging only the clock with: "three shapes differing 4x in markup density agree within 8% -- retained bytes per subscribing boundary is a property of the BOUNDARY". That is a RATIO agreement produced by a bias that cancels in the ratio. The QUANTITY the red-zone table is stated in disagrees by 65-79% between the two sources, on witnesses whose markup density and boundary count are identical. Portability of the ratio is real; portability of the quantity is not demonstrated and is contradicted by the wave's own numbers.

(2) THE BEAD PUBLISHES BOTH FORMS AS OPERATIVE AND THEY GIVE OPPOSITE VERDICTS. .4's ratios (list 2.262x, grid 2.254x) and .5's absolutes (208 B shell, 3,552 B/read, 3,807 B @1 read, 10,785 @3, 24,758 @7, 71,229 @20) are both on this bead as red-zones and neither is superseded. A candidate at 2,600 B/boundary at one read is 2600/947 = 2.75x -> RED under .4, and 2600 < 3807 -> NOT RED under .5. That is a red/green flip on the same measurement, decided by which published red-zone a reader reaches for.

(3) THE K3 / PAPER-BUDGET QUESTION HAS TWO PUBLISHED ANSWERS. validation.md line 35 sets exclusive retained per boundary at ~0.4-0.5 KB target, >1 KB paper-fail. .4 puts the Reagent denominator at 954 B -- UNDER the line, and its page says the denominator is "close to it". .5 puts it at 1,565 B -- 1.6x OVER it. Whether the shipped Reagent adapter already fails the paper budget at a single read is K3-relevant and is currently answered both ways in the same governance record.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, cheapest first:

  (a) STATE THE SHARING REGIME ON EVERY HEAP RED-ZONE ROW. A retained-per-boundary figure is only defined relative to how many boundaries share a subscription. The ladder's distinct-query regime is the honest worst case and is the one HD-002's grouped-tier prize (~2,600 B/read, ~18 KB on the seven-read archetype) is already priced against.
  (b) PREFER THE RATIO FORM for the red-zone, since it is the form that survived (2.262 / 2.254 / 2.435), and drop or relabel the absolute-byte red-zone rows so a candidate cannot be judged against two incompatible scales.
  (c) IF THE ABSOLUTES ARE TO STAND, re-take .4's heap rows with P0_ROOTS=1, or with per-root disjoint query ranges, so both sources measure the same quantity. This is an instrument change, not a witness change, so it does not disturb the clock convergence.

NOT A CLAIM THAT ANY NUMBER IS WRONG. Every figure cited is reproducible as published; each is a correct measurement of what its own arm measured. The defect is that two different quantities are labelled with one name and both are operative.

Files: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs (ROOTS, boundariesOf, bytesPerBoundaryCdp), implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_heap.cljs (arm-table, mount!), implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_uix.cljs / p0_reagent.cljs (u-root, w1-root), docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-uix-on-subs-frontier-arm.md, docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md, docs/design/hicasso/studio/README.md, docs/design/hicasso/validation.md.

RED-ZONE AMENDMENT IS THE OPERATOR'S. This bead surfaces and prices the incomparability; it does not amend the bar, the budgets, the kill criteria or any red-zone.
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-31, dossier review):

MECHANICS. rf2-2rtt6.1 is append-never (rf2-0znkn column limit) and was NOT touched. This note on rf2-2rtt6.16 is the AUTHORITATIVE INTERIM RECORD of the ruling. OBLIGATION: transcribe this ruling onto the standard's successor record as soon as rf2-0znkn's remedy executes (being ruled in parallel today). This bead stays open until that transcription lands.

THE FINDING RULED ON. The two P0 retained-heap red-zone families published as operative measure different quantities under one name. rf2-2rtt6.4's heap driver holds 4 roots rendering the SAME 300 [:p0/cell 0..299] query vectors against ONE frame -> one subscription cache, 300 reactions at refcount 4, divided over 1,200 boundaries: its "exclusive retained per boundary" amortises the subscription half of every read across four boundaries. rf2-2rtt6.5's ladder gives every boundary a DISTINCT query by design -- the honest worst case, carrying the full subscription per read. Same reader (CDP getHeapUsage after forced collection), same arm-minus-floor rule, same 1 element/boundary, same boundary count -- and the absolutes differ 1.65-1.79x: Reagent 947 (.4 grid) vs ~1,562 (.5 ladder) B @1 read; UIx 2,134 vs ~3,807 B. (This bead's description quotes 1,565/3,811 -- the superseded ladder publication; the current tracked publication after the R=0-fit correction reads 1,562/3,807, a <0.3% move that changes nothing in this decision.) The sharing model predicts the gap and a third instrument confirms the arithmetic: solving S + H = ladder and S/4 + H = .4grid gives Reagent S ~= 820-824 B vs rf2-2rtt6.12's directly measured 866 B (5% apart); UIx S ~= 2,231-2,236 vs 2,453 B (1,684 live + 769 retained-dead; 9% apart). Three instruments, one arithmetic. The "8% agreement across shapes" (2.262 / 2.254 / 2.435x) that justified not re-running the heap axis was RATIO agreement produced by a common-mode bias that cancels in the ratio: portability of the ratio is real; portability of the quantity was not demonstrated. Live consequence pre-ruling: a candidate at 2,600 B/boundary @1 read was RED under .4's family (2600/947 = 2.75x > 2.254x) and NOT RED under .5's (2,600 < 3,807) -- a verdict flip decided by which published row a reader reached for; and K3's paper line was answered both ways (.4's 954 B put shipped Reagent under the 1 KB line, .5's 1,565 put it 1.6x over).

SYNTHESIS. This ruling merges the dossier's three-part recommendation with the Codex Recommendation appended to the same dossier (source-verified down to the cache-key mechanics). Adoptions and rejections are attributed inline.

PART 1 -- CACHE CARDINALITY IS PART OF THE WITNESS; THE DISTINCT-QUERY LADDER IS THE MANDATORY WORST-CASE WITNESS AND THE OPERATIVE ENVELOPE (dossier part 1, sharpened per Codex rec 1). Neither published absolute family is crowned a universal bytes-per-boundary red-zone. The sharing regime (cache cardinality) is part of the witness definition. Every heap red-zone row stamps at least B (boundaries), E (boundary-query edges), Q (unique live query keys) -- hence reads/boundary E/B and mean fan-out E/Q -- alongside the version and instrument-hash provenance the studio pages already carry. The .5 ladder (Q = E) is the MANDATORY distinct-query capacity witness: its rows are the operative red-zone family, and where governance needs one conservative number (paper sizing), the distinct-query row is used and labelled "upper-envelope capacity budget", never "retained bytes per boundary" unqualified. The .4 grid is NOT corrected and is NOT an alternative calibration of the same quantity: it stands as valid evidence for the shared-query fan-out witness class (E/Q = 4); its absolute rows are relabelled "fan-out 4 (amortised x4) -- shared-query witness evidence, not comparable to distinct-query rows"; its ratios (list 2.262x, grid 2.254x) stay published as the cross-regime check that survives regimes. A candidate row is judged ONLY against donor rows measured under the same regime on the same witness (same B/E/Q and query values) -- which blocks the verdict flip in BOTH directions: an amortised candidate flattered against the worst-case family, and a fan-out-heavy candidate punished against worst-case-only baselines. Mechanism, source-verified (Codex): the production cache key is the query vector itself; a hit returns the existing reaction and increments a scalar ref-count; the per-frame cache is {query-vector {:reaction ... :ref-count n}} (subs.cljc 508-543, 1315-1378, 1662-1681; subs/cache.cljc 1-20) -- four consumers of one (frame, query-vector) retain ONE reaction plus four attachments. .4's driver divides the held delta by ROOTS*perRoot while every root renders the same frame-id and query vectors (p0_run.cjs 103, 312, 377-395 at the current tree -- this bead's description cites 264/347 at its revision; p0_heap.cljs 82-142, 176-192; p0_reagent.cljs 81-101; p0_uix.cljs 84-113): 1,200 edges over 300 unique keys, and a shared reachable cache node is counted once by the heap readers, so dividing by four consumers necessarily amortises it. CONFIRMATION AND PRICING SWEEP ADOPTED (Codex rec 4, subsuming the dossier's optional ROOTS=1 re-take): bench bead rf2-5prok -- non-gating for this ruling (which stands regardless), gating for freezing Part 3's component budgets. Prediction on record: the fan-out-1 rung lands on the ladder's distinct-query family (Reagent ~1,562 B, UIx ~3,807 B @1 read) within instrument noise; a material miss reopens this part.

PART 2 -- TWO MEMORY GATES, BOTH REGIME-MATCHED: THE RED-ZONE STAYS UIx-SOURCED AND THE REAGENT LINE GOVERNS THROUGH K3 (Codex rec 2 adopted OVER dossier part 2; the dossier's part 2 as stated -- replace the UIx red-zone source with per-axis-best Reagent -- is REJECTED). The finding that motivated the dossier stands and is recorded: on retained heap the frontier INVERTS. UIx wins the per-boundary shell (208 B vs Reagent 428 B, 0.49x) and loses the read by 3.77x (3,552 vs 943 B/read marginal; first-read increment 3,600 vs 1,137 B). The crossover is below one read -- any boundary that subscribes at all is cheaper on Reagent -- and the census seven-read archetype costs 24,758 B/boundary on the raw UIx spine vs Reagent's 6,587 B. A UIx-derived per-read red-zone is therefore 3.77x looser than the best measured option on the axis memory was declared most winnable. WHY THE REJECTION: HD-012 already assigns the two comparators different jobs -- K3 = per-boundary heap worse than matched Reagent with no paper path down (kill rule); the UIx material-cost rule = materially worse than direct UIx (the 2026-07-30 red-zone). Redefining the red-zone source as Reagent would collapse the two gates and erase the informative between-state: a candidate between Reagent and UIx has CLEARED the UIx material-cost threshold while K3 is STILL UNRESOLVED until it names and demonstrates a path down, and calling that state either "green" or "red" loses information. OPERATIVE STATEMENT: every candidate heap row reports BOTH matched-regime ratios. On the mandatory distinct-query witness the lines are: UIx 3,552 B/read [3,551-3,553] -- worse than this is RED, needing an explicit operator waiver naming the dogfood benefit (the 2026-07-30 threshold ruling's heap arm is not replaced but regime-QUALIFIED: "the measured UIx ratio for that witness family" now reads the witness family as including cache cardinality, so the amortised 2,134 B figure is never the threshold for a distinct-query candidate row); Reagent 943 B/read [935-944] -- worse than this with no named paper path down is K3 territory; between them is "UIx-rule cleared, K3 open until a path down is named", never plain green. The dossier's crisp tournament target survives untouched: BEAT 943 B/read is the K3-clean line -- what moved relative to the dossier is only where Reagent's line lives (in K3, where HD-012 already put it), not whether it governs. Resolution of the flip example: 2,600 B/boundary @1 read on the distinct-query witness = below UIx's 3,807 -> not red; above Reagent's 1,562 -> K3 open pending a named path down. Single-valued, three-state, no reader-dependence. The clock axis is untouched (the converged witness set governs there).

PART 3 -- THE K3 PAPER LINE SPLITS: SHELL vs READ, WITH THE THREE-TERM DECOMPOSITION AS THE TARGET SHAPE (dossier part 3 adopted now; Codex rec 3 adopted as the budget's end state, its numbers gated on the sweep). validation.md's "exclusive retained per boundary: target ~0.4-0.5 KB; >1 KB fails on paper" is amended to say explicitly that this target/fail line is the R=0 BOUNDARY SHELL. Both measured shells comply: Reagent ~418-428 B, UIx ~208 B. The per-read axis is judged separately, under Part 2's regime-matched gates. Consequences: the shipped Reagent adapter is NOT retroactively K3-failed -- its ~1,562 B @1 read = measured shell (~428 B; the dossier quotes ~418) + first-read increment (~1,137 B [1,125-1,141]), each judged on its own axis -- and candidates cannot pass the paper line by amortising subscriptions across boundaries. The K3 both-ways contradiction (954 B "under the line" vs 1,565 B "1.6x over") is dissolved: both were correct measurements of different quantities; neither was a K3 verdict. Codex refinement adopted as the budget's target shape: the read side decomposes into a per-edge (consumer attachment) term and a per-unique-subscription-key term; in the distinct-query witness (Q = E) the ladder's 943 B slope is their SUM -- a valid total marginal cost in that regime only, not a pure view-layer per-read price. Component budget rows (shell / per-edge / per-unique-key) enter validation.md only after the bench sweep verifies the additive model and prices the terms; freezing them today from cross-instrument algebra is REFUSED -- the algebra is sufficient to reject the unqualified scalar (solved subscription term ~820 B Reagent / ~2,231 B UIx vs .12's directly measured 866 / 2,453 B -- 5% / 9%) but the paired rows came from different instruments and runs.

WHY NOT THE OTHER ALTERNATIVES. Keeping both families operative leaves every future heap verdict reader-dependent -- the donor ruling would be contestable the day it issued. Ratio-only (this bead's option b) survives measurement but prices nothing absolute: HD-002's collector survival metric and the grouped-tier prize (~2,600 B/read, ~18 KB on the seven-read archetype -- priced in the distinct-query regime) lose their denominators. Crowning .4's amortised family would systematically flatter candidates that share subscriptions across boundaries -- the shape the census says real pages sometimes have, but the worst case doesn't.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS. The donor-gate advisory ruling (rf2-2rtt6.7, the HD-008 delegated advisory) was waiting on single-valued heap numbers. They are now single-valued per witness and regime: mandatory distinct-query envelope; UIx red-zone line 3,552 B/read; Reagent/K3 line 943 B/read (first-read increment 1,137 B; ~1,562 B @1 read); shell target 0.4-0.5 KB with both measured arms compliant.

DOC FOLLOW-THROUGH (mayor to dispatch as doc beads; deliberately not filed from this ruling seat): (i) p0-uix-on-subs-frontier-arm.md heap table -- relabel the absolute rows "fan-out 4 (amortised x4), shared-query witness -- not comparable to distinct-query rows", stamp B/E/Q, keep the ratios as the cross-regime check, point the operative family at the ladder; (ii) reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md -- stamp "distinct-query (Q = E), mandatory worst-case witness, operative upper-envelope family"; (iii) validation.md -- amend the budget row per Part 3 (shell line now; component rows only after the sweep); (iv) studio README banner accordingly.

title: spec/conformance/freehand/ donor ledger is a work-plan for the withdrawn EP-0036 programme
description:

The rf2-o61sn ruling ('a sentence that describes shipped behaviour is correct; a sentence that promises a future slice / a coming deletion / a transitional window is false — prefer the smallest correction') does NOT decide this site, so it was deliberately left untouched.

WHY IT DOES NOT DECIDE. spec/conformance/freehand/donor-inventory.md is not a document containing a few false sentences — it is WHOLLY a programme work-ledger. ~500 rows, each naming an owning programme slice (F0-F6) and a status of 'pending' or 'done'. Its opening premise: 'the standalone day8/re-frame2-ui artifact is deleted once every row below has been disposed. Absorption completeness is one of the release gates, and this ledger is the artifact that gate reads.' EP-0036 is withdrawn, so that release gate does not exist and the pending DELETE rows have no owner. There is no smallest sentence-level correction: the choice is between (a) a withdrawal banner that reframes the whole ledger as a historical record (mirroring how EP-0036 itself was kept under EP-0009's terminal-status rule), (b) freezing it, or (c) removing it. That is a ruling.

SECOND SITE, same class: spec/conformance/freehand/conformance-index.md:9 — 'The index is empty at establishment and grows one row at a time: each slice that lands a contract appends its own rows.' A one-clause fix on its own, but it was held back so the conformance/freehand/ tree gets ONE coherent disposition rather than two inconsistent ones.

IT IS LOAD-BEARING — this is a PAIRED spec + gate change, not a prose edit. scripts/check_donor_inventory.py enforces that its ESTABLISHED_ROWS roster covers the ledger EXACTLY (every roster identity still in the ledger AND every ledger row in the roster), that no row may be deleted (disposal = flip to 'done', the row stays as audit record), that no pending row goes stale, and that no live re-frame.ui consumer is unclaimed. It runs in .github/workflows/freehand-conformance.yml alongside check_freehand_conformance_index.py. Any banner/freeze/removal must land with the gate in the same PR or CI reds.

FENCE when dispatched: spec/conformance/freehand/** plus scripts/check_donor_inventory.py and scripts/check_freehand_conformance_index.py. spec/ is hot-zone — sequence, never parallel. Do not touch docs/EP/** (the withdrawal record landed and is correct) or docs/design/freehand/** (frozen).
notes:

Two independent analyses (dossier + Codex second opinion) converged on this; counts and checker structure spot-reverified against the working tree 2026-07-31 before recording. This bead is now the dispatchable implementation owner. (This note is the sole record: the prior dossier edition was consumed unrecorded; the dossier file ai/decisions/rf2-lrtwj.donor-ledger-disposition.md is folded in full here and deleted.)

DISPOSITION — one atomic hot-zone PR; every piece in the same commit as the gate change or freehand-conformance CI reds:

(i) donor-inventory.md: a dated withdrawal banner as the FIRST substantive content, ahead of the current opening premise — the ledger is a snapshot at EP-0036 withdrawal. `pending` (149 rows: 96 MOVE, 41 REPLACE, 12 DELETE; 75 done; 224 total, exactly counted against the checker's grammar — not the ~500 this bead's description estimated) means "not disposed when the programme was withdrawn"; it confers no owner, authorises no work, and is not a release count; neither the pending count nor the artifact-deletion sentence authorises anything. ALL rows and their withdrawal-time statuses preserved.

(ii) scripts/check_donor_inventory.py, SAME commit: from live programme gate to snapshot-integrity validator. KEEP parsing, vocabulary, uniqueness, established-row retention; PIN the COMPLETE normalized row tuples, not just identities (disposition/slice/status/description could otherwise drift silently in an archive). REMOVE the worktree-comparison arms — check_partition, check_consumers, check_current (verified present today at lines 377/432/508) — and the pending-to-zero report. Any still-wanted product-neutral rule (e.g. donor-must-remain-unpublished, or a no-new-donor-consumers freeze during EP-0038) gets its own named authority and gate with a P2 sunset — never smuggled through the historical `pending` statuses of a withdrawn programme.

(iii) conformance-index.md: replace ONLY the stale growth sentence (line 9: "…and grows one row at a time: each slice that lands a contract appends its own rows") with timeless roster language. NO banner; its validator (check_freehand_conformance_index.py) and CI stay intact. Rationale (the Codex nuance the first dossier edition missed): EP-0036's withdrawal killed the PROGRAMME (F0-F6 ownership, drive-to-zero) but explicitly left the Freehand implementation, CI lanes, and shipped-behaviour specs in force pending separate disposition (docs/EP/EP-0036-...:352-354), and spec/Ownership.md still assigns those shipped contracts. The index is the live roster of executable laws for shipped code — archiving it would misclassify current behavioural evidence as history.

(iv) SUNSET (new from Codex; record it on the snapshot): EP-0038's HD-018 says a P2 win deletes the public Freehand and re-frame.ui surfaces and leaves "no donor inventory ledger". The archive's end condition: on a P2 win the snapshot and its snapshot-check retire WITH the donor surfaces they map; on a loss/null the snapshot stays as the historical record, and any future donor policy is made under fresh authority, never by reviving F0-F6. Removal before P2 is premature either way.

(v) freehand-conformance.yml: update workflow wording/comments and donor step names in the same commit, WITHOUT renaming the required job/status context.

VERIFIED FACTS to preserve (dossier + Codex, spot-reverified 2026-07-31): 224 parseable rows (149 pending / 75 done); pending split 96 MOVE, 41 REPLACE, 12 DELETE; matching 224-entry ESTABLISHED_ROWS retention roster; 229 tracked donor-tree files covered by 106 donor-tree row patterns; 30 mechanically detected external consumers; checker self-test AND live --ci --report both pass today; 42 commits touched the ledger between establishment 2026-07-22 and last update 2026-07-26. REJECTED:
(b) Freeze verbatim, no banner — leaves an authorised work queue and release gate standing in present tense: the exact class of spec lie the rf2-o61sn cleanup just purged. The inventory's present-tense release gate, slice ownership, and pending-to-zero meanings are false authorities, not harmless old wording.
(c) Remove the tree, retire both gates — cleanest tree, but deletes the only structured absorption/consumer map while its subject code still exists; HD-018 contemplates deleting those surfaces on a P2 win — exactly when a consumer map is wanted; reconstruction from git history later costs far more than the banner costs now; and it would wrongly take conformance-index.md (live laws) down with it.

RISKS + mitigations: (1) a historical file under spec/ misread as normative -> the front-loaded dated banner is the mitigation; (2) losing the current census's protection against a new donor dependency -> if that protection is still wanted, an explicit narrow EP-0038 freeze rule under its own authority with a P2 sunset.

Do NOT touch docs/EP/** (the withdrawal record landed and is correct) or docs/design/freehand/** (frozen). The spec edits and the gate conversion MUST land in the same PR (same commit) or CI reds — this is a PAIRED spec + gate change, not a prose edit.

title: P0 lane driver: the CLOCK row's unverified count and the positive control are printed, never adjudicated (p0_run.cjs)
description:
FOUND BY rf2-2rtt6.3's audit discharge (PR #7272), REPORTED NOT REPAIRED — it is a fourth instrument, outside that bead's three riders, and worker/lane-control-cluster is live on the adjacent lane.cljs (rf2-egdaq control-verdict, rf2-pq7d8, rf2-9zysg).

THE SHAPE IS THE ONE THE PR #7262 AUDIT NAMED on hicasso_narrow_run.cjs item 2, and it is present in implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs:

1. THE CLOCK ROW'S DOM VERIFICATION IS NOT A GATE. `unverified` is accumulated (lines 283, 331), stored (387) and printed (412) — 'N unverified of M mounts'. The exit logic then adjudicates ONLY the heap row: line 491 reads `out.heap.verification.unverified > 0`. A clock run in which writes never reached the page therefore prints its count beside 'VERDICT: reportable' and exits 0. Compare hicasso_narrow_run.cjs, which now exits 1 on any nonzero count from a verifiable arm.

2. THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS PRINTED WITH A RATIO AND NEVER ADJUDICATED IN THE DRIVER. p0_run.cjs line ~409 prints 'predicted N B | measured M B [min-max] (ratio X)' and nothing reads the ratio. lane.cljs has `control-verdict` for exactly this, so the machinery exists and the heap driver does not call it.

WHY IT MATTERS: these rows feed rf2-2rtt6.1's P0 table, and 'the driver exited 0' is being used as evidence that the gates passed. rf2-2rtt6.1 already carries a MERGED-PR AUDIT #7265 note making precisely that point about a sibling driver ('do not treat driver exit 0 / reportable as evidence those omitted gates passed').

SUGGESTED FIX, small and fail-closed, NOT a framework: adjudicate the clock row's unverified count in the same place the heap row's is adjudicated, and route the heap driver's control through lane.cljs's control-verdict rather than printing a bare ratio.

SEQUENCING: the control half touches control-verdict's callers, and rf2-egdaq is tightening control-verdict right now. Sequence this AFTER that PR merges.
close_reason: Wired and proved in PR #7276 (worker/p0-driver-95s5b, commit 2fd3a362176e9a01b42dad5992e16817bdb5d1d5). p0-app/adjudicate replaces aggregate as the ONLY door onto the clock fold and returns the summed N-unverified-of-M plus lane/control-verdict's answer with the record; P0H.controlVerdict routes the heap row's control through the same lane rule. Driver exits 1 on either row's nonzero unverified count and on either control that is not ok, and names EVERY failed gate. control-verdict's DECISION logic untouched (rf2-egdaq remains the operator's). mount-sample! now excludes an unverifiable window (expected nil - the positive control) from the denominator instead of counting it as verified; control-round! always discarded those counts so no figure moves. Proved by mutation: floor bulk force! no-op -> 96 unverified of 264, exit 1; control-2x building the same page as control-1x -> measured 1.210x vs predicted 1.998x DISJOINT, exit 1; P0H.control allocating a tenth -> 470610 B vs 4700000 B, exit 1. Mutations restored byte-identical (p0_arms.cljs blob 89d26f8b9853d4fd06abfbdd99e6c7ac8a4cc060 == origin/main). NO PUBLISHED NUMBER WOULD HAVE FAILED: a clean run at the published sizes reproduces the studio page's denominator exactly - W1-list 200 + W3-form 1600 + bulk-broad 800 + bulk-narrow 4000 = 6600, 0 unverified; heap 0 of 48; both published controls sit INSIDE the +/-25% band, so neither reading of rf2-egdaq changes them. title: Stop retaining the disposed render-phase reaction in the spine's use-subscribe
description:
MEASURED, PRICED, NOT LANDED by rf2-2rtt6.12 (production edit to a first-class shipped adapter, deliberately left for a reviewed change).

re-frame.substrate.spine/use-subscribe takes a balanced render-phase round trip (subs/subscribe then subs/unsubscribe) so a render that never commits retains no ref-count (rf2-es09qq). For a query with NO live cache entry that goes 0 -> 1 -> 0, and 1 -> 0 is the disposal edge: re-frame.subs.cache/unsubscribe! disposes in-tick with no grace period. The commit-phase subscribe-fn then misses the cache again and builds a SECOND reaction. The first is retained for the component's lifetime by use-memo's hook slot and by get-snap's closure - a disposed reaction with no source watches, no cache slot and no verb that can reach it.

MEASURED (docs/design/hicasso/studio/uix-spine-per-read-decomposition.md, commit 0cf86fb580, :advanced, headless Chromium): 769 B [765-793] and 23.0 objects per read, 22% of the shipped 3,501 B / 125.8 obj read. Witness counters (exact integers, twice over disjoint cells): rebuilt = 1.00N, bodyRuns = 2.00N on UIx against 0 and 1.00N on Reagent.

THE CHANGE (~6 lines): have the render-phase use-memo deref the handle and return the VALUE; have get-snap's pre-commit fallback read that value. Every subscribe/unsubscribe call, every hook and every watch stays put.

EFFECT: 3,501 -> 2,720 B/read, 125.8 -> 102.8 obj/read, UIx/Reagent 4.04x -> 3.14x. The noretain ablation arm in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/spine_ablation.cljs IS this change; re-measure after landing since the arm is a transcription.

BLAST RADIUS: make-react-spine is shared by re-frame.adapter.uix (shipped, first-class), re-frame.freehand.substrate and re-frame.ui.substrate. One change, three beneficiaries.

CORRECTNESS: the fallback stops being a live re-read. React calls getSnapshot again after subscribe returns, by which time subscribe-fn has published the committed reaction - so that call reads the LIVE one and a write landing between render and commit is still detected. That is measured, not inferred: bodyRuns = 2N is exactly that second call. A frozen value also satisfies React's cached-getSnapshot rule at least as well as the current live deref. The key-change guard (rf2-naz09e) is unchanged in shape.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: making the fallback live without retention via subs/subscribe-once is UNSAFE - a fresh reaction per call means a fresh memo cell, so a collection-returning sub yields a non-Object.is value every getSnapshot, React's documented infinite-loop condition.

Needs a spine unit test pinning the no-retention property and the post-subscribe live re-read.

driven by the UIx DOM suite) writes app-db from the RENDER BODY of a sibling that
renders after the subscriber in the same pass — so the write lands strictly between

the FIRST committed, layout-visible DOM from a useLayoutEffect (a render React
discards before committing never runs one). Four rows: blocking and concurrent lanes,
each with an UNMOVED CONTROL on its own frame so every row is a genuinely cold read
and a null result cannot be confused with a probe that never fired.

MEASURED, BEFORE THE REPAIR:
  blocking   control    first commit {:dom "g=0" :db 0}   consistent
  blocking   moved      first commit {:dom "g=0" :db 1}   stale (React's own)
  concurrent control    first commit {:dom "g=0" :db 0}   consistent
  concurrent moved      first commit {:dom "g=0" :db 1}   STALE FIRST COMMIT
Both moved rows settled at {:dom "g=1" :db 1} — the passive-effect repair does
arrive, one commit AFTER the stale value was committed and paint-eligible.

a same-commit layout effect or ref read observes it with no paint at all. The two
lanes are two different findings, because React pushes its pre-commit
store-consistency check ONLY on a non-blocking lane (0 !== (renderLanes & 127) ||
pushStoreConsistencyCheck) and consults it only when the render time-sliced:
  * BLOCKING (default lane, every shipped consumer's normal root.render) — React does
    NO pre-commit re-read at all. NOT a #7304 regression: identical before and after,
    React's semantics, unreachable by any getSnapshot implementation. Now PINNED so a
    React release that starts checking blocking lanes surfaces as a failure.
  * CONCURRENT (startTransition / useDeferredValue — opt-in, but per rf2-so3io

Not the rejected alternative: this READS a reference something else already owns, so

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7304 — completeness / correctness / implementation quality.

The retention repair is small and its object-tenancy proof is strong for the defect it targets. But it changes `getSnapshot`'s unmatched/pre-commit branch from a live deref to the frozen render value. The landed docs explicitly concede that on a concurrent lane a write in the render→commit gap is no longer rejected before commit; React's passive/post-subscribe check repairs it one commit later. That is a real stale commit/possible paint, not merely delayed bookkeeping, and it is the exact security-shaped class already priced in rf2-so3io/rf2-anmdr (permission drop, user switch, record redaction).

The new `assert-use-subscribe-render-phase-reaction-not-retained` test does not inject any write in that gap and does not assert the first committed/layout-visible value. It only proves that React later dereferences the committed reaction, so it cannot validate the prose claim that the render→commit window remains covered.

Keep the repair bounded: add a deterministic concurrent render→commit mutation row that observes the first commit (with an unmoved control), and preserve the pre-commit live-consistency contract without retaining the disposed handle. If the project intentionally accepts a one-commit stale window, that is an operator-level contract change and must be ruled explicitly rather than inferred from post-subscribe ordering. No new framework is warranted.

title: Decompose the UIx spine's 3,550 B per subscription read
description:
rf2-2rtt6.5's ladder measured a re-frame2 subscription read at 3,550 B/boundary on the UIx spine against 942 B on Reagent — 3.77x, and reader C says the whole difference is object COUNT (128.5 objects/read against 36.2) at ~27 B per object on both. 128 objects for one read is a lot for uSES + two useRefs + a useMemo, so something in re-frame.substrate.spine's use-subscribe is allocating more than the hook stack accounts for (the spine's own comments mention a durable subs/subscribe in the render-phase useMemo alongside the committed-ref path — worth checking whether a read registers twice).

This is not a Hicasso-only question: UIx is a FIRST-CLASS shipped adapter, so if the per-read cost can be brought toward Reagent's 942 B that is a direct win for shipping consumers, and it also moves the bar Hicasso is measured against.

Method: ride the same instrument. reads_ladder_run.cjs already takes LADDER_SUBSTRATES and the arms come from the page, so an ablation ladder over the spine's hooks can reuse the collector, the in-situ control and the order guard rather than growing a second one — which is how rf2-2rtt6.5 itself was built on B7.

Evidence: docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md sections 1 and 3.
notes:

The central validity checks are fail-open. `spine_ablation_run.cjs` prints the witness counts but never compares `commits/rebuilt/bodyRuns` with the declared N/N/2N and 0/0/N predictions; computes fidelity only for reader-A bytes (not the headline object count) and deliberately does not fail a mismatch; catches a reader-C snapshot failure and continues; and never fails bad positive-control error or poor bytes/objects r².    - the witness counts were printed beside the N/N/2N and 0/0/N predictions and never compared with them; now compared per offset per counter. It came back exact for the second time: commits 1.00N, rebuilt 1.00N, bodyRuns 2.00N on UIx against 0/0/1.00N on Reagent, twice over disjoint cells.

description: Tournament arm 2 for EP-0038 (epic rf2-2rtt6; architecture.md Arm 2). THE HARD GATE IS MET. The decisive row is the rejection: the model refuses the keystroke, NOTHING re-renders (dirty-boundaries = 0), and the field still comes back to the model — from converge-focused! at the end of every commit, one activeElement read rather than a walk of the other 99.

INVARIANT 5 BY CONSTRUCTION: sub cannot read without a bound snapshot; the snapshot is bound in exactly two places; commit! is non-reentrant (a deferred-commits counter observes the door). No fence, no generation counter, no staleness check.

DIFFER TIERS: (1) template extraction with data hole plans, entered by a shape signature computed on the new tree and answered O(1) by a node stamp — CSP-safe, no new Function, no compiler; covers mount (one native cloneNode) and the steady-state re-render of every static element. TWO REAL BUGS THE BROWSER SUITE CAUGHT, BOTH FIXED:
(a) LAZINESS vs the ambient collector. Hiccup is lazy, so a `for`'s reads happen when the differ walks the children, not when the body returns. A collector closed at the body's return recorded the list query and LOST every row query. runtime/with-collected-reads keeps it open across the body AND the patch. THIS IS A SURFACE B FINDING, NOT AN ARM 2 ONE — Arm 1 should check it.
(b) A KEYED CHILD must refuse the hole plan. A literal keyed list is a static shape, so tier 1 claimed it and patched slot 0's text instead of moving the node that owns the key: correct markup, and every piece of DOM state a row holds (focus, scroll, a controlled field's live value) on the wrong row.

title: Wave-1 arm: Hicasso lean-React (tournament)
description: Tournament arm 1 for EP-0038 (epic rf2-2rtt6; architecture.md Arm 1). React FCs minted by defview; <=2 shell hooks (subscription/epoch + frame, HD-020; callback refs, never useRef in the shell); re-render via commit->index->dirty set->epoch bump; generation fence (staged-stale CI witness); codec caching only (no extraction — that is PATCH machinery). Instrument: hooks/boundary, retained size vs the 0.4-0.5KB target, bulk K=100/300, per-read + per-keystroke paths, and the HD-002 tiers — grouped use-subs (the product default; canonical spelling in authoring.md) AND the ambient-collector challenger under the standard bead's adjudication clauses (tripwire overrides the clock). Build the DOGFOOD SCREEN (list + controlled field + sub reads) in THREE renderings — collector, grouped, raw UIx — judged on diff + preference. THE SIX-WEEK CLOCK STARTS at this arm's (or PATCH's) first commit that mounts the dogfood screen. Runtime skeleton stays OFF MAIN (spike branch); witnesses/instruments in the bench lane. Hard fences: no compiler, no dual mode, no ViewCell-class graph (= failed spike), no candidate ledger. Time-boxed per validation.md; results with commit SHA + repro command to the standard bead + studio.
notes:
LANDED AS PR #7321 (branch worker/arm1-2rtt6-9, head 9f614fe7e8). Runtime skeleton is in the bench/test lane at implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/ — off every production source path (HD-017).

WHAT IS DONE.
- The two-hook shell, COUNTED AT REACT'S DISPATCHER rather than self-reported: ["useContext" "useSyncExternalStore"], and 2 hooks at 1, 7 and 20 reads. No useRef, useState, useMemo or useCallback. The mechanism that made two reachable is that the shell holds NO per-instance render-phase state at all: `subscribe` closes over the read SET only, so it is cached by that value, shared across boundaries, and identity-stable exactly while the reads are unchanged — which is React's own re-subscribe condition. React then hands that shared closure each fiber's own onStoreChange, and the registration minted inside is the commit-owned boundary id.
- HD-002 clause (a): no render-phase code mutates the index or a ref-count; one scratch array, reset by overwrite; abandoned renders need no cleanup. Clause (b): edge set replaced wholesale at commit, only when it changed, with the unchanged case detected WITHOUT BUILDING ANYTHING. The tripwire did not fire.
- The generation fence with its staged-stale witness, plus the 6.1 adversarial case (commit landing after the body returns).
- The dogfood screen MOUNTED in three renderings — K7 IS RUNNING. Canonical-DOM parity across all three with a can-answer-false control; narrow write touches one row; keyed reorder keeps the node; controlled field echoes in the caller's turn.
- The laziness finding from Arm 2: CHECKED AND REFUTED for this arm, structurally (the collector window closes around the eager codec), with three witnesses. Plus four deferred-read escapes now witnessed converting into a LOUD error rather than a silent missing edge.

GATES (all foreground, exit codes echoed): npm run test:cljs 12,104 tests / 60,508 assertions / 0 failures; npm run test:browser 878 / 5,617 / 0; scripts/test-fast-pr.sh PASS; clj-kondo on the CI-pinned 2026.04.15 errors: 0, zero warnings from this arm. mkdocs --strict does NOT cover docs/design/hicasso/** (excluded in mkdocs.yml) — the studio page was checked by hand.

TWO FINDINGS WORTH OTHER WORKERS' TIME.
1. HD-002's "acquire without deref" is NOT implementable against this substrate and fails silently: a derived value's `unset` baseline is never rf= a real value, and the render's own read went through subscribe-once (a different reaction, disposed), so a freshly acquired reaction reports movement on the first later commit whatever it did — every newly mounted boundary re-rendering once for nothing. One baseline deref per NEW UNIQUE KEY closes it.
2. The ambient frame outranks React context invisibly: the carried-invariant chain resolves the dynamic-var tier BEFORE context, so an ambient use-subscribe answers for the ambient frame while use-current-frame reports the provider's. It presents as a rendering difference. :ambient-frame nil is set in every DOM fixture here and a probe asserts the two read forms agree.

WHAT REMAINS (not blockers for this PR; each wants its own bead): the 100-cell controlled grid (K4's full row — caret, selection, IME, unchanged-model rejection, async normalisation); StrictMode / HMR body swap / a real h/boundary error boundary; H2 (render-side positional verification) untried; the survival metric's allocation-slope half; and no bar row published, per the restated-bar posture (rf2-b0tz5).

DESIGN INPUT FOR rf2-2rtt6.39 (delete the frame hook by threading the frame as a codec-supplied prop): I analysed exactly this while designing the shell and rejected it for v0 on CORRECTNESS, not cost. Threading works for boundaries the codec creates, but a frame-provider interleaved between two Hicasso boundaries is a React component the codec never sees, so a props-threaded frame would silently keep the outer frame across it. Any measurement of .39 needs an interleaved-provider witness or it will measure a design that is wrong in the one case providers exist for.

Make the stated 2x workload load-bearing; a control that renders only the base prefix must fail before any figure is reportable.
2. Teardown is part of the repeated-mount instrument but failures are silently swallowed: `lane/release!` catches every arm unmount exception, `release-bulk-arms!` does the same, removes the container, and the driver can still exit 0. There is also no post-release root/subscription-residue assertion. A failed Reagent unmount can leave roots or sub ref-counts alive across hundreds of later samples and bias the denominator while the guard sees only the contaminated page. `lane/release!` and `release-bulk-arms!` call an arm's `:unmount` and then unconditionally remove its container. `lane/residue` can thereafter see only body child count plus the re-frame sub-cache entry/ref-count census. title: STANDARD: the Hicasso bar, budgets, and kill criteria (operator-owned)
description:
The operator-owned governance record for EP-0038 (the lbs3y pattern; rf2-lbs3y is the retired predecessor standard). Workers append measurements; only the operator (or an explicitly recorded delegation) amends the numbers.

THE BAR (HD-012): ship = mount AND bulk view-work <= 1.0x Reagent, like-for-like (both sides on re-frame2 subs), CLOCK ONLY as the ship number; memory first-class via kill rules (K3 + UIx material-cost). ALL BAR NUMBERS ARE BROWSER NUMBERS (:advanced, real browser); JVM/Node = diagnostic only. Architecture-kill: bulk > 1.5x after two serious runtime iterations.

RED-ZONES (set when P0 publishes, BEFORE candidate results open): one UIx clock ratio + one UIx retained-heap ratio per witness family; a red row needs an explicit operator waiver naming the dogfood benefit; silence is not a pass; the donor-gate 'acceptably close' is judged against these.

BUDGETS: <=2 runtime/shell hooks per product boundary (scalar comparator exempt, priced by the 1/3/7/20 ladder); ~0.4-0.5KB exclusive retained target (>1KB paper-fail); ViewCell-class object graph = failed spike; per-read tier-3 survival metric = steady-state allocation slope across warm 1/3/7/20 reads + zero retained per-occurrence objects after commit/teardown; per-keystroke path stated (4-field form + 100-cell grid) with sub-recompute localization; template identity named for any cached shape work.

HD-002 ADJUDICATION (pin before P1 code): (a) render/commit ownership state machine for the collector (candidate reads survive winning renders, vanish on abandon/replay/teardown; needing the forbidden candidate ledger = immediate tripwire); (b) the exact allowed edge-diff op vs the forbidden ledger class; (c) two pre-registered collector strategy hypotheses, counted only by benchmarked commits; (d) tripwire OVERRIDES the clock.

KILL CRITERIA K1-K7 + the six-week clock (starts at the first Hicasso-arm commit that mounts the dogfood screen; P0/donor/paper are off-clock) per docs/design/hicasso/validation.md. DECIDERS (HD-013): donor gate = delegated advisory ruling (adversarial+creative pass vs the published P0 table, recorded here, operator-overturnable); P2 fork = THE OPERATOR, advised by recorded reviews. Adapters-only is a successful outcome.

P0 BASELINE TABLE lives here + docs/design/hicasso/studio/: Reagent-on-subs mount/bulk, ratom write+flush, UIx-on-subs, the 1/3/7/20 ladder, and the W1 carry-over (~2.99-3.08x floor / ~1.9-2.0x Reagent, already resolved in docs/design/freehand/studio/bulk-rerender-where-the-time-goes.md appendix — no re-litigation).
notes:
=== DELEGATED RULINGS (mayor, 2026-07-30, on Mike's explicit 'accept your recommendation and proceed'). OPERATOR-OVERTURNABLE. Recorded here because this bead is the governance record and silence is not a pass. ===

RULING 1 — THE RED-ZONE RULE, so P0 publishing does not stall Wave-1.
The standard requires red-zones set when P0 publishes, BEFORE candidate results open, and rf2-2rtt6.4 names UIx as the arm they are set from. Numbers cannot be pre-stated because P0 has not run, so the operator supplies a RULE instead:

  RED-ZONE THRESHOLD = THE MEASURED UIx RATIO FOR THAT WITNESS FAMILY, on both axes (clock, retained heap).
  A candidate row WORSE THAN UIx on either axis is RED.
  A red row needs an explicit operator waiver naming the dogfood benefit. Silence is still not a pass.

  THE SHIP BAR IS UNCHANGED: mount AND bulk <= 1.0x Reagent, like-for-like, clock only as the ship number. Red is not fail — red is 'needs a waiver'. The two are independent: a row can clear the bar and still be red (if UIx beats Reagent), and that is the intended tension.

  RATIONALE. UIx is the frontier comparator: the best existing React-idiomatic option on re-frame2 subs. A native view layer that cannot match it has no case — that is precisely the lbs3y lesson, where the predecessor sat ~5x Reagent and was withdrawn. Deriving the threshold from the measurement rather than from a guessed constant also means nobody has to defend a number invented before the data.

  MECHANICAL, SO NO WORKER NEEDS TO ASK: when rf2-2rtt6.4 publishes its UIx rows, those figures ARE the red-zones. Append them to this bead's table labelled as such. No further operator input required to proceed.

RULING 2 — HD-002 ADJUDICATION IS A DELEGATED ADVISORY, not an operator gate tonight.
The standard requires HD-002 pinned before P1 code: (a) the render/commit ownership state machine for the collector, (b) the exact allowed edge-diff op vs the forbidden ledger class, (c) two pre-registered collector strategy hypotheses counted only by benchmarked commits, (d) the tripwire.

  This is delegated to a dedicated worker producing a written adjudication into docs/design/hicasso/, recorded on this bead, ADVERSARIALLY REVIEWED, and OPERATOR-OVERTURNABLE — the same pattern HD-013 already uses for the donor gate.

  RATIONALE. It is deep design, not a coin-flip, and it should be argued on paper by someone who has read HD-002 properly rather than ruled from the mayor's chair. It gates only the tournament arms (rf2-2rtt6.9, rf2-2rtt6.10), which are post-donor-gate and start the six-week clock, so there is time to do it properly.

  NOT URGENT TONIGHT: P0 (.2/.3/.4/.5), the draft guide (.6) and the donor-gate measurement (.7) all run without it.

(d) THE TRIPWIRE — one question a worker applies at the moment they reach for a data structure: "does anything I am about to write need to survive from one render attempt to a DIFFERENT render attempt of the same boundary, or need to be told apart from another render attempt's version of itself?" Yes = candidate ledger = the collector has LOST, regardless of clock. Six mechanical checks (a second candidate slot; anything keyed by render/attempt/lane/generation id; render-phase mutation of shared state; commit-phase re-read of sub VALUES; a per-read object required for CORRECTNESS; a registry of in-flight renders). Tripwire vs budget failure is NECESSITY vs COST: needed-for-correctness is fatal on sight, merely expensive is measured and survivable. On firing: stop collector work, record the construct + the correctness obligation + the commit SHA on rf2-2rtt6.9 and here, arm continues on grouped. A firing kills the TIER, not the arm and not the programme. Operator may waive; default is loss; silence is not a pass.

(b) THE BOUNDARY — allowed: ONE operation, commit-phase only. Symmetric difference over sub-keys between the committed sequence P and the candidate sequence N; add/remove edges on the shared index; then P := N. Three constraints keep it out of the ledger class: (1) THE COMMIT DOES NOT DEREF — zero subscription values read at commit; the generation fence (O(1) per boundary) replaces the predecessor per-read commit-side re-read, measured at 1.19ms of a 4.0ms write for 300 reads against Reagent 1.4us for its entire layout phase; (2) ALLOCATION IS PROPORTIONAL TO THE CHANGE, NEVER TO THE READ COUNT — this is the standard warm-1/3/7/20 survival metric seen from the other side; they are the same statement, and a collector satisfying one but failing the other has an instrument bug; (3) the unchanged case must be detectable without building anything. NEAREST ALLOWED: a per-boundary reused scratch buffer overwritten unconditionally each render (the closest allowed construct to the fence); the retained committed set P; a generation counter compared once per render; ONE candidate slot. NEAREST FORBIDDEN: a SECOND candidate slot (one line from the allowed buffer, and the definitional case); any map keyed by render/attempt/generation over read sets; per-read records (the predecessor five-key :observations maps); commit-phase value re-read; a root registry of in-flight renders; a content HASH of the read set used to decide "unchanged" (a collision is a silently missing edge and therefore a stale boundary, not a slow one — a device whose failure mode is wrongness).

(a) THE OWNERSHIP STATE MACHINE — four states (UNMOUNTED / RENDERING / PENDING / COMMITTED) reduced to ONE invariant: no render-phase code mutates anything outside the boundary own single candidate slot; the index is mutated ONLY in the commit phase. THE MACHINE DOES NOT DETECT ABANDONED RENDERS, IT MAKES THEM COSTLESS — an abandoned render needs no cleanup because it never did anything that needs cleaning. Abandon and replay are both PENDING to RENDERING, where the unconditional top-of-render reset destroys the prior candidate by overwrite (the reset must be unconditional, or StrictMode double-invoke concatenates two renders worth of reads). PENDING to nothing (tree discarded) leaves the index describing the last COMMITTED render, which is what is on screen; a boundary whose first render is abandoned never had index membership at all. Teardown removes P edges (the standing zero-leaked-refcount assertion). Forced consequence, INFERRED and NOT collector-specific: render-time reads must not acquire — warm reads are pure derefs, cold reads use subscribe-once semantics (acquire and release both complete inside the render, so abandonment leaves nothing behind), and acquisition happens at commit. useSyncExternalStore has the same shape, so grouped and the scalar comparator inherit the identical constraint: SHARED FRONT-HALF CONCERN, CHARGE IT TO NOBODY.

(c) TWO PRE-REGISTERED HYPOTHESES — both inside the allowed operation, differing only on WHERE unchanged-case detection happens (the sole strategic axis the operation leaves open). H1 COMMIT-SIDE ORDERED COMPARE: fill the scratch in read order; at commit compare length then pairwise, falling through to the diff on mismatch. Predicts ZERO BYTES steady-state commit allocation on the 300-boundary bulk witness and a FLAT allocation slope across warm 1/3/7/20; the clock prediction is directional only (not worse than grouped) because no P0 baseline exists to state a number against. H2 RENDER-SIDE POSITIONAL VERIFICATION: each (sub q) verifies itself positionally against P as it reads, setting a divergence flag; the commit is O(1) and independent of k when the flag is clear; yields allocation-free RENDERS, not merely allocation-free commits. Falsified if the render leg rises by more than the commit leg falls at k=7 and k=20 — directional, needs no P0 number. Risk asymmetry recorded: H2 loads the hot render path the predecessor measured at 0.77-0.86ms per 300 reads. COUNTING RULE: a hypothesis is CONSUMED only by a commit implementing it PLUS a bench row citing that SHA and its repro command — both halves, or it is not consumed. Tuning passes consume nothing and un-consume nothing. An abandoned implementation that produced no bench row leaves the hypothesis unconsumed, but the attempt is recorded (an unrecorded abandonment is how two swings quietly become five). Both consumed and neither meeting the survival metric means the collector loses, grouped stays default, and there is no third hypothesis without an explicit operator ruling — the same grammar HD-014 uses for the clock: never silently. A TRIPWIRE FIRING CONSUMES NOTHING AND ENDS THE TIER; it overrides the count as it overrides the clock.

AUDIT PR #7261 — adversarial review of the delegated HD-002 advisory found a material correctness contradiction; update this exact governance owner, no duplicate. The allowed "single candidate slot" cannot establish concurrent React ownership. If the reused scratch/candidate is shared, a later suspended or urgent WIP render can overwrite it before a different render's effect commits, so "the effect runs only for the render that won" does not make the slot belong to that render. If the candidate is captured/render-local, concurrent attempts necessarily retain distinguishable candidates — exactly the second-slot/attempt distinction that the document's tripwire declares fatal. Before collector P1, either record that the tripwire has fired and promote grouped, or prove a representation under a transition+suspense/urgent-commit witness that associates the committed key sequence with the winning render without shared render-phase mutation or multiple live candidates.

The cold-read ruling is also not correctness-pinned. Section 3 says commit acquires without deref because the render value is already known and claims useSyncExternalStore has the same shape, while section 6.1 leaves a same-generation subscription-value change between render and commit OPEN. React's external-store contract performs a second getSnapshot just before applying every Transition and restarts when it changed; the proposed acquire-without-deref path names no equivalent freshness barrier. Resolve that witness before treating the allowed commit operation as adjudicated. This audit is the required adversarial pass; the document's authored and landed patches are range-diff exact, and its structure/provenance are otherwise coherent.

=== PROVENANCE PRACTICE: ANCHOR A PUBLISHED ROW BY BLOB HASH, NOT ONLY BY COMMIT SHA (mayor, 2026-07-31) ===

WHY. A producing commit SHA is rewritten by rebase and again by rebase-merge. Twice today a published row cited a SHA that was no longer an ancestor of main, and once a worker discovered its published SHA COULD NOT RUN ITS OWN REPRODUCTION COMMAND and had to re-take every number. A row nobody can reproduce is not a measurement.

THE PRACTICE, proposed by the rf2-9zysg worker and adopted: alongside the producing SHA and the repro command, record the BLOB HASH of each instrument file the row was produced by (git rev-parse HEAD:<path>, or git hash-object <path>). A blob hash is content identity — it survives rebase, squash and merge, and it answers the only question that matters: is the instrument that produced this number the same bytes as the instrument in the tree today?

HOW IT HAS ALREADY PAID: the PR #7268 rebase was trusted because all four bench files came out blob-identical; the #7267 rebase likewise verified eight instruments byte-identical; and #7270 anchored its re-published narrow-write rows by blob hash precisely because it knew the merge would rewrite its SHA a second time.

SO A PUBLISHED ROW SHOULD CARRY THREE THINGS: (1) the producing commit SHA, as history; (2) a reproduction command VERIFIED TO RUN AT THAT SHA; (3) the blob hash(es) of the instrument file(s), as content identity. Cite the SHA for provenance; check the blob hash for validity.

COROLLARY FOR REBASES: after any rebase of a branch carrying published numbers, verify by blob hash that the instruments are unchanged BEFORE pushing. If a blob moved, the row is either re-run or marked superseded in place — never left reading as current. That rule has held across five rebases today with no published row silently invalidated.

=== CORRECTION TO MY OWN RULING: THE HEAP AXIS IS NOT PORTABLE ACROSS WITNESS SHAPES (mayor, 2026-07-31) ===

I RECORDED, EARLIER TODAY, that rf2-2rtt6.4's retained-heap thresholds STAND while its clock rows are superseded, and I justified it like this: 'retained bytes per boundary is a property of the boundary; the clock is not, because element count decides what fraction of the window is React's own work.' Three shapes differing 4x in markup density agreed within 8%, and I took that as portability.

THAT JUSTIFICATION IS FALSIFIED. The rf2-p0-audit cold read (findings doc, gitignored) established the mechanism:

  rf2-2rtt6.4's heap driver sets P0_ROOTS=4 and divides by ROOTS x perRoot = 1,200 boundaries. But all four roots render the SAME 300 query vectors against the SAME frame. One frame means one subscription cache: 300 reactions at refcount 4, divided over 1,200 boundaries. So its 'exclusive retained per boundary' AMORTISES THE SUBSCRIPTION HALF OF EVERY READ ACROSS FOUR BOUNDARIES. rf2-2rtt6.5's ladder gives every boundary a DISTINCT query by explicit design, and its own page already names the shared case as the cheaper one.

  Hold markup density and boundary count constant — .4's grid (1 el/boundary, 4x300 = 1,200) against the ladder (1 el/boundary, 1,200) — and the answers still differ: Reagent 947 vs 1,565 B (1.65x), UIx 2,134 vs 3,811 B (1.79x).

  The sharing model SOLVES: a Reagent subscription half of ~824 B against rf2-2rtt6.12's independently measured 866 B (5% apart), and a UIx half of ~2,236 B against its 2,453 B (9% apart). THREE INSTRUMENTS, ONE ARITHMETIC.

  THE 8% RATIO AGREEMENT I RELIED ON SURVIVES ONLY BECAUSE THE BIAS IS COMMON-MODE. Both arms amortise identically, so the RATIO is preserved while both ABSOLUTES are wrong. That is exactly the shape a ratio-only check cannot see, and I read agreement-of-ratios as evidence-of-portability.

WHAT IS NOW LIVE AND CONTRADICTORY, and this is the operator's to settle (rf2-2rtt6.16, P1):
  (a) THIS BEAD PUBLISHES BOTH .4's RATIOS AND .5's ABSOLUTE BYTES AS OPERATIVE RED-ZONES, AND THEY GIVE OPPOSITE VERDICTS. A candidate at 2,600 B/boundary at one read is RED under .4 and NOT red under .5.
  (b) The K3 paper-budget question — does the SHIPPED Reagent adapter already fail the >1 KB line at a single read — is answered BOTH WAYS: 954 B under .4, 1,565 B under .5.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DISTURB. The heap RATIO between two arms measured in one run remains sound, because the amortisation is common-mode; UIx is still worse than Reagent on the read by a factor the audit did not challenge. What is unsafe is (1) any ABSOLUTE bytes-per-boundary figure from .4, and (2) any comparison of a .4 absolute against a .5 absolute.

SO THE CORRECTED ASYMMETRY IS NARROWER THAN I WROTE: a heap RATIO is portable across witness shapes; a heap ABSOLUTE is not, because it depends on how many boundaries share a query. I generalised from the ratio to the absolute without checking, and the check that would have caught it is the one this programme keeps rediscovering — ask what would have to be true for the number to be measuring something else.

WHAT IS RULED. Of the two real candidates the guide sets out, SURFACE B — the ambient collector, where 'sub' is an ordinary function call usable inside a when, inside a for, and inside an inlined helper, with one fixed runtime hook collecting reads and the runtime diffing the edge set after the body returns — is the only ergonomically acceptable authoring surface. SURFACE A (grouped use-subs: one hook at the top of the body receiving the complete query collection before the body runs) is ergonomically REJECTED. The guide states the mechanism of A's limitation plainly: 'Grouped takes the complete query collection BEFORE the body, so a helper's queries are out of reach' — helpers cannot read, loops cannot read conditionally, and the author must hoist every query.

WHAT IS **NOT** RULED, and must not be read into this. The collector's CORRECTNESS and COST gates are untouched and still bind:
  - The standing TRIPWIRE that OVERRIDES THE CLOCK: the first time correctness requires a candidate ledger or generic post-render dependency reconciliation, THE COLLECTOR DIES, however good its numbers look. This ruling does not waive it and cannot.
  - The four pre-registered adjudication clauses (render/commit ownership state machine; the exact allowed edge-diff operation distinguished from the ledger class; two pre-registered strategy hypotheses each counted only by a benchmarked commit; the survival metric — steady-state allocation slope across warm 1/3/7/20 reads plus zero retained per-occurrence objects after commit or teardown).
  - hd-002-adjudication.md stands as written.

THE CONSEQUENCE THE PROGRAMME MUST NOW CARRY. The guide names three outcomes: collector wins and ships; collector loses and grouped stays the default; both fail and the outcome is null. THIS RULING REMOVES THE COMFORT FROM OUTCOME 2. 'Grouped stays the default' is no longer a benign fallback — it is now, by the operator's own judgement, shipping an ergonomically unacceptable surface. So if the collector trips its tripwire or fails its survival metric, the honest positions are (a) the outcome is NULL and no Hicasso read surface ships, or (b) a mechanism not yet on the table earns its way in. Falling back to grouped and calling it a result is closed off. Whoever adjudicates HD-002 must state which of those it is rather than defaulting to A.

Ergonomics is half the verdict per the guide; that half is now decided. The other half is still measured, not asserted.
RULING REINFORCED (Mike, 2026-07-31, verbatim): 'use-subs (Surface A) is not sufficiently ergonomic for a programmer to use.'

This is STRONGER than a preference between two workable surfaces and must be read that way. Surface A is not merely less pleasant than Surface B — it is judged BELOW THE USABILITY BAR for the programmer this library exists to serve. It is therefore NOT a viable fallback, NOT a viable default, and NOT a viable ship state.

Restating the consequence so no future adjudicator can soften it: the guide's outcome 2 ('collector loses and grouped stays the default') is CLOSED.
