--- WHAT I FOUND THAT CONTRADICTS THE FIGURES I WAS BRIEFED WITH ---

1. THE ACCEPTANCE ROW IS NOT AT 1.2409x AND ITS VERDICT IS NOT
INSTRUMENT-LIMITED. 1.2409x [1.0371 - 1.5371] is rf2-y1jkm's reading. It then
moved to 1.4759x when rf2-2rtt6.54 migrated the census anchors to route-link,
and rf2-cno31's remedy took it to 1.1884x [1.1223 - 1.2660], band 7.0%, control
PASS — where the page's own verdict is "FAILS THE LINE: whole range above 1.10,
margin 8.0% clears the band". That is a RESOLVED failure, not an instrument-
limited straddle. The row that reads INSTRUMENT-LIMITED is FEED, at 1.0737x
[0.9669 - 1.1859]. The brief understated the acceptance failure and attached the
straddle to the wrong row.

2. THE reagent-slim CENSUS FIGURE IS REAL BUT IS NOT IN THE DOC TREE. 1.1667x ->
0.9762x (and 0.9649x on a second after-run) is verified, but only in rf2-e7zxb's
close reason for PR #7427; the string 0.9762 appears nowhere under docs/. The
single strongest piece of evidence for the null hypothesis currently lives only
in a bead close reason, and a P2 ruling that turns on the null's strength should
have it on a studio page.

3. K3's CURRENT RATIO IS 1.3492x, NOT 1.44x. The 1.44x that appears in this
bead's 2026-08-01 note predates the fusion; the live figure is 1,278 B/read
against 947. The verdict does not change, but the magnitude has moved and the
older number is the one still circulating.

Everything else in the brief verified exactly as stated: the 994/992 and
1,099.5/1,097 B shell pair and HD-028's withdrawn justifying sentence and live
fallback; the walk at 1.0588x before and 0.9636x after against the donor
interpreter's 1.73-1.90x; rf2-409ab's 70% read-shape / 30% interpreter split
with no fence-legal remedy surviving pricing; the frame-as-a-prop variant
returning 45 of 105 B, below the ~75 B shape sensitivity, not clearing the line;
rf2-swwud's structural (F+50)/F obstruction; rf2-0qj9w's M1 control refusal on a
verifiably idle box against a band that is widest at 24.6% when idle versus 8.3%
at four competing cores; and rf2-2rtt6.1 still open.

=== END OF ADVERSARIAL PASS. Advisory only. No bead was closed, reprioritised or
amended; no measurement was taken; no file outside this note was written. ===
=== HD-013 CREATIVE ADVISORY PASS — 2026-08-04 07:44 AUSEST, prepared by a
delegated worker, ADVISORY ONLY. THE DECIDER IS THE OPERATOR. ===

Read-only over the mayor checkout at e160af77a5. No code, no decisions.md, no
validation.md, no bead closed or reprioritised. The adversarial pass ran
independently; nothing here was coordinated with it.

WHAT THIS PASS WAS ASKED FOR: not optimism and not advocacy — reframings the
record has not considered, options that are cheap because of what has landed,
and paths that dissolve a problem rather than solving it. Three findings
survived that test. NONE OF THEM IS A ROUTE TO A "GO" ON NUMBERS, and the pass
says so up front: the mount gate (1.10x direct UIx, the 2026-08-02 amendment on
this bead) is failed on every row that resolves, and I found no framing that
turns that into a pass.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
FINDING 1 — THE P2 NULL MOVED, THE PROGRAMME IS WHAT MOVED IT, AND NO ROW
MEASURES IT.
----------------------------------------------------------------------

The facts, all committed.

rf2-2rtt6.63 put three interpreters over one witness value in one process and
found ours already at stock Reagent's cost (1.0588x before the bead touched
anything, 0.9636x after two cheapenings), while the interpreter the donor rungs
actually ride, reagent2.impl.template, read 1.7273-1.9020x stock. That finding
was handed to reagent-slim as its own defect. Two landings followed, both in the
SHIPPED adapter at implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:

  rf2-lhdp0 (PR #7405)  1.82x -> 1.19-1.24x stock Reagent
  rf2-e7zxb (PR #7427)  1.1667x -> 0.9762x and 0.9649x, guard clean on both

Canonical DOM byte-identical at 1,202 elements / 58,529 bytes across all five
runs, agreement failures empty including 22 hostile heads. Both are on main.

Three consequences, and they do not all point the same way.

(a) THE NULL IS NOT WHERE IT WAS MEASURED. Adapter-Prime — the P2 null, the
composed reagent-slim :f> plus UIx use-subscribe arm — rides that walk. HD-008's
donor rungs read 1.33-1.5x stock Reagent, and rf2-2rtt6.63 attributed that
deficit to exactly this interpreter. The last time the donor rows were taken is
rf2-2rtt6.31, 2026-08-02, which predates BOTH landings. So the fork's null
control has probably become materially faster since anything measured it, and
the ruling is scheduled to compare the candidate against a control whose current
position is unknown. This is the cheapest decision-relevant measurement I found
anywhere in the record and nobody has booked it.

(b) THE CODEC ADVANTAGE OVER THE DONOR HAS EVAPORATED. Hicasso reads 0.9636x
stock Reagent on the walk witness; reagent-slim now reads 0.9762x and 0.9649x on
the same witness. That is parity. rf2-2rtt6.63's hicasso/slim of 0.5567 and
0.5579 is stale — it was a ratio against a codec the programme has since fixed.
Any statement of the form "we extracted the donor's plumbing and cheapened it,
we read 0.56x the donor we were built from" is no longer true of main. I flag
this because it is a figure a decider could reasonably carry forward, and it has
moved against the candidate.

(c) THE PROGRAMME'S OUTPUT IS ALREADY BANKED IN A SHIPPED ARTEFACT. On a P2
stop, "adapters-only is a successful outcome" stops being a consolation clause
and becomes a description of something that has already happened: a
first-class, shipped adapter is 1.87x faster on the census witness than it was
two beads ago, its caches are structurally safer than the guards they replaced
(null-prototype rather than defended-against), and the mechanism came out of
Hicasso's codec. That is a real deliverable that survives either ruling, and the
record does not currently frame it that way anywhere.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE (b) AND (a), AND WHAT IT COSTS. (b) is one run: the
walk_vs_reagent_app instrument already runs all four arms in one process on one
witness value under the arm-order guard, so a single run on current main puts
hicasso and post-fix slim in the same windows and answers it outright. Roughly
ten minutes of box time. Note the two figures I have compared are from different
sessions on a shared box, which the instrument's own discipline says is exactly
what its ratios are NOT for — so (b) is a hypothesis until that run exists. (a)
is larger: a donor-row re-take on the census or M1 instrument, which needs a
window that can adjudicate — see Finding 2.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
FINDING 2 — QUIET IS THE HARD CASE. THE PROGRAMME'S SCARCEST RESOURCE MAY BE
THE WRONG RESOURCE.
----------------------------------------------------------------------

The brief asks whether the measurement crisis is a reason to stop or a sign the
evidence needs a different instrument. I think it is neither, and the record
already contains the reason.

The band ladder (rf2-ymi6j, nineteen runs, same box, both clocks) measured the
band at 24.6% at zero competing cores against 8.3-13.2% everywhere from four
cores to twenty, with corr(band, floor) = -0.49, and the floor's per-sample
coefficient of variation falling MONOTONICALLY with load, 30.0% -> 15.2%. A busy
box is slower and steadier; an idle one is faster and jumpier. rf2-0qj9w's
window then refused M1's positive control on a verifiably idle box — ctl-2x at
1.8443x with at least one segment-round below the 1.5 floor, band 21.4% — and
its own note says the rebook should not assume more quiet is the repair.

WHAT NOBODY HAS PROPOSED. The refusal mode is per-round dispersion, and
dispersion is the one quantity the ladder measured falling with load. So the
affirmative move is to run the adjudicating rows under a DECLARED, CONTROLLED
synthetic load — four to twelve competing cores — rather than under maximum
quiet. I searched the tree and the open beads: rf2-h8o80 proposed a
floor-in-calibrated-range precondition and was refuted; the band page names
pinning the CPU governor as a falsification of its mechanism hypothesis; no page
and no bead proposes load as a measurement CONDITION.

WHAT MAKES IT MORE THAN A GUESS. The ladder also measured what happens to an
arm-to-arm floor-normalised ratio across those same rungs: ctl-2x/floor reads
1.7347 / 1.7272 / 1.6818 / 1.6604 / 1.7111 / 1.7604 at 0/2/4/8/12/20 competing
cores, with corr(ctl-2x/floor, floor) = -0.04. That is direct evidence that the
KIND of quantity the bar adjudicates does not trend with load over exactly the
range that cuts the band by two to three times. The instrument to do it also
already exists: seam_ladder.cjs forks N spinners, runs the clock and kills them.

COST AND THE EXPERIMENT. One row, taken at rung 0 and rung 8 in one session,
asking two questions: does the ratio agree across the rungs, and does the strict
every-round control rule pass at rung 8 where it refused at rung 0? Half a day,
no new driver. If it holds, the programme's scarcest pre-P2 resource — quiet
windows, named as scarce in rf2-0puue's own parking ruling — is partly
self-imposed, and rows that have been unpublishable for weeks become takeable.

HONEST LIMITS, STATED. The ladder is a bulk300 ladder and M1 is a mount row, so
this is an extrapolation across witnesses. The mechanism (an idle machine parks
cores and drops clocks between samples) is the band page's own hypothesis and it
did not measure frequency or C-state residency. Pinning the governor, if this
box permits it, is the cleaner variant of the same idea — steadiness without the
load — and it is the falsification the page already invited and nobody has run.
And none of this touches the three-point control's OTHER refusal, which is a
property of the page rather than the box: paint saturating once the damage
region covers the viewport is not a constant, so no differencing removes it.

ONE ADJACENT OPTION, CHEAPER THAN A NEW INSTRUMENT. Bulk is unadjudicable on our
harness and the record says so in terms. But the krausest cross-check
(rf2-rguy1) is the ONE harness the clock correction never touched — it drives
through page.click, an Input-domain door, so its taskNet was script-and-frame
all along and its ratios move under 1.7% between the clocks — and it already
carries all three arms implemented against one shared model with canonically
identical DOM. It is the instrument in this tree least exposed to the defect
that broke ours. Its own limits are real and must ride with it: its positive
control failed at 13.1-13.7x against a pre-registered 8-13x, and its app has
trivial state, so it prices rendering and says nothing about subscription
fan-out — which is the term rf2-409ab found dominant. It cannot answer the read
question. It may be able to answer bulk, which ours cannot answer at all.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
FINDING 3 — THE 1 KB LINE ADJUDICATES ABOUT 2% OF WHAT A PRODUCT BOUNDARY
RETAINS, AND THE CRITERION THAT ACTUALLY KILLS IS ABOUT REAGENT.
----------------------------------------------------------------------

The rows are exact and I take them as published. R=0 shell, tree that ships:
994 / 992 B without the wrapper, 1,099.5 / 1,097 B with it. Marginal slope on
the same runs: 1,278 B/read (Reagent segment). Donors in the same runs: Reagent
shell about 505 B and 947 B/read, UIx shell about 224 B and 2,979 B/read.

Both candidate fits are lines in R on all six rounds, so the page's own model
gives a three-read boundary. The arithmetic, which is mine over two published
terms rather than a measured rung:

  Hicasso, wrapper       1,099.5 + 3 x 1,278 = 4,933 B
  Hicasso, no wrapper      994   + 3 x 1,278 = 4,828 B
  Reagent                  505   + 3 x   947 = 3,346 B
  UIx                      224   + 3 x 2,979 = 9,161 B

The wrapper is 2.1% of what the candidate's three-read boundary retains. Against
Reagent the candidate is 1.47x with it and 1.44x without. Against UIx it is
0.54x either way. On the card-shaped boundary that was actually measured, the
page-chrome row put the same fiber at +1.8% of 11,018 B.

THE REFRAMING THIS MAKES AVAILABLE, offered as a framing and not a
recommendation. The disposition under ruling is not "does the wrapper fail the
bar" — it is "which of two configurations does v0 ship", and the R=0 line does
not separate them at the level a product pays. Meanwhile K3, which is the
criterion that actually kills, reads "per-boundary heap worse than Reagent with
NO paper path to the floor": the candidate is worse than Reagent on both terms
with or without the wrapper, so the wrapper does not decide K3 either, and the
"paper path" half is exactly what rf2-0puue's ruling has already recorded in
staged form (91-92 B/read of reader array, with a mechanism named and a probe
that reads it as mostly push growth). The 1 KB line is the only place the
wrapper is decisive, and it is a paper budget written before any code, on the
one boundary shape a product never ships.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, WHICH IS STRONG AND BELONGS HERE. The R=0 regime was ruled
deliberately, on 2026-07-31, precisely so a candidate cannot pass the line by
amortising subscriptions across boundaries. So the framing above argues against
a live ruling and needs the operator to WANT it. It is not a worker's to assume,
and I do not assume it.

THE LEVERS WERE PRICED BUT NOT COMBINED. The frame-as-a-prop variant returns
45.0 / 46.5 B of the wrapper's 105.5 / 105.0 B, on the same instrument, the same
rung and the same A-B-A design, with the two sections' A arms reproducing each
other to half a byte. Both terms are measured as exactly R-independent
per-boundary constants. Composing them predicts a no-wrapper frame-prop shell
around 949 / 946 B. That is a PREDICTION, not a row — and it would not resolve
as a clear pass anyway, because 51 B under 1,000 is inside validation.md's own
~75 B component-shape sensitivity. Cost to turn it into a row: one more A/B on
the rung both sections already share, one session.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
THE QUESTION I JUDGE THE PROGRAMME HAS BEEN ASKING WRONGLY
----------------------------------------------------------------------

The programme is spending its scarcest resource — adjudicable box time — on a
performance residual its own decomposition says is a capability price, while the
one input the P2 ruling genuinely lacks costs no box time at all.

rf2-409ab took the acceptance row apart through the published in-page door and
reproduced ship/uix to within 0.6% of the published ratio before decomposing it.
Of a 1.858 ms deficit: 55% the read term by ablation, 30% the interpreter
against a compile-time macro, 8% routing spelling, 2% the shell and the memo
fiber together and both indistinguishable from zero. A coarse arm — the
candidate at the twin's read shape, byte-identical DOM — prices the read-shape
asymmetry directly at 1.300 ms, 70% of the deficit. And the roster's own second
row corroborates it: on feed, where both arms spell 603 per-instance reads, the
published ratio is 1.0737x. Where the read shapes match, the deficit is
essentially gone. The page's honest negative is that nothing available inside the
fence moves this row much, and its own sentence is that the comparison charges
the candidate for a capability the control does not have.

So the residual is priced, named and attributed. Another quiet window does not
change what it IS. What the ruling is actually missing is on this bead already:
the charter-v0 dogfood preference verdict, outstanding since 2026-08-03, held
across three delegated dossier rounds, each landing "preferred, with
reservations", and the hold note says in terms that until a dated operator note
records it, the HD-013 P2 graduation advisory HAS NO ERGONOMICS LEG. With K5
removed by ruling on 2026-08-04, ergonomics no longer has a kill criterion
either — which makes the preference verdict the only place ergonomics enters the
fork at all.

Put plainly: the open P2 question is no longer "can interpreted hiccup be fast".
It is "is a read surface that can sit inside a for, inside a branch, inside a
plain helper worth about 1.2x direct UIx on pages where UIx cannot spell the
same reads, and about 1.07x where it can" — and that is a preference question
with a measured price, not a measurement question. One dated sentence on this
bead is worth more to the ruling than any row still outstanding.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
CORRECTIONS TO FIGURES I WAS BRIEFED WITH, VERIFIED IN TREE
----------------------------------------------------------------------

1. "The interpreter the donor rungs actually ride reads 1.73-1.90x" is TRUE of
   rf2-2rtt6.63 and STALE of main. rf2-lhdp0 and rf2-e7zxb have since taken it
   to 0.9762x / 0.9649x. See Finding 1.

2. "read shape ~70%, interpreter-vs-macro ~30%" reads as a partition and is not
   one. rf2-409ab's ablation partition is reads 55 / markup 30 / routing 8 /
   shell+memo 2 / residual 4. The 70% is a separate counterfactual measurement
   (local minus coarse, 1.300 ms of 1.858 ms), and the coarse arm still walks
   hiccup, so 70% and 30% overlap and must not be added.

3. The reagent-slim 1.1667x -> 0.9762x figures are on rf2-e7zxb's close note,
   not in any studio page, and they are the diagnostic in-page walk clock on
   walk_vs_reagent_app — not the clock of record and not the census clock rows.

4. Worth the decider's attention because it is not a briefing error but a doc
   one: validation.md still states the ship bar as "mount AND bulk view-work
   <= 1.0x Reagent". The operative mount gate since the 2026-08-02 amendment on
   this bead is one line, <= 1.10x direct UIx-on-subs, and that amendment
   explicitly REJECTED keeping <= 1.0x Reagent (as an implicit kill of the mount
   axis) and named "a bounded consistency edit to the stale HD-012 /
   validation.md Reagent-parity wording (docs follow-up, not performed here)".
   That edit does not appear to have been made. A decider reading validation.md
   today reads a bar that is not the operative one. Recorded as a fact; the
   correction is not mine to make.

Everything else I was briefed with reproduced exactly: 1.0588x / 0.9636x on the
walk; 994/992 and 1,099.5/1,097 B on the shell; 45.0/46.5 B for the frame-prop
variant against 105.5/105.0 B for the wrapper, not clearing the line at
1,054/1,051 B; -60 B/read banked by the fusion with 91-92 B/read of surviving
reader array parked at P3; the per-keystroke row's missing band and the
(F+50)/F control; M1's control refusing on a verifiably idle box; the band
widest when idle; K5 removed 2026-08-04 with K1-K4, K6, K7 standing and the
guide at nine pages.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
HOW THIN IS THE CREATIVE GROUND — HONESTLY
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Thinner than the volume above suggests, and I would rather say so than pad.

There is no reframing here that makes the clock evidence a pass. The mount gate
is failed clearly on M1 and on the one census row that resolves; the bulk leg of
the bar cannot be produced on our harness at all; the outside instrument puts
candidate bulk at 1.43-1.62x, its worst row, agreed by both instruments. What I
found instead is one measurement nobody has booked whose answer moves the NULL
rather than the candidate, one instrument option that is cheap and unnamed and
may unblock rows that are currently unpublishable, one framing of a heap line
that argues against a live ruling and therefore needs the operator to want it,
and one observation that the ruling's remaining gap is a preference verdict
rather than a number.

If the operator's reading of the numbers is that the candidate does not clear
its bar, nothing in this pass should be read as arguing otherwise. What the pass
does argue is that two of the four things above are cheap enough that not doing
them before the ruling is a choice worth making deliberately.
ADVISORY INPUT LANDED — the production server arm is priced (mayor, 2026-08-04). Pointer appended here because the dossier worker correctly declined to write into this bead's notes itself: its brief fenced them, the bead it worked told it to land here, and it flagged the disagreement rather than resolving it silently.

THE ARTEFACT: docs/design/hicasso/production-server-arm.md, landed by PR #7488 under rf2-2rtt6.88 (now closed). Twelve sections - the three jobs both arms must do, the shipped floor, how R0 bites each, Arm A (JVM structural walk), Arm B (Node sidecar), the two instrument facts, what the spike corpus licenses, the unmeasured roster, a thirteen-axis asymmetry table, bead and week estimates, per-arm tripwires, and an explicit section on what the page does NOT say. Indexed from the design-record README and pointed at from draft-guide/10's Not settled row.

THE FOUR THINGS THE SITTING SHOULD READ FIRST:

1. THE FLOOR IS HIGHER THAN THE BEAD IMPLIED. emit-ui-tree ships and is final, and a JVM interpreted structural walk to the v1 tree ALREADY SHIPS for Freehand, driving emit-ui-tree behind the Independence wall. So the walk arm's back half is a thing to be CALLED, not a thing to be built. What has no precedent is READS - Freehand's JVM walk fails a v/sub loud rather than resolving one.

2. THE SPIKE BUILT THE NODE ARM'S RENDER, NOT ITS TOPOLOGY. ssr-ring is JVM-only .clj in every file, so entry.cljs hand-writes the payload tag and the page envelope and says in terms that it is not a production host. THERE IS NO JVM-TO-NODE CONTRACT ANYWHERE IN THE TREE. The R0-compliant sidecar has not been built or measured, and the page names that as the largest unmeasured thing on it.

3. THE SHARPEST ASYMMETRY, and it is a composition neither document states alone: spec 004B says two emitters diverging is DETECTED, NOT PREVENTED, while spec 011 says React-native adoption deliberately does not report attribute-only mismatches. Composed, THE WALK ARM'S LIKELIEST DIVERGENCE IS INVISIBLE AT RUNTIME. The Node arm cannot produce that class of defect at all.

4. THIS IS NOT A SCHEDULE CHOICE. Walk 6 beads / 5 to 8.5 weeks; sidecar 6 beads / 4 to 6.5 weeks. THE BANDS OVERLAP. Anyone hoping the estimates would decide it should stop hoping.

WHAT THE CORPUS DOES AND DOES NOT LICENSE: X2 through X5 are client-half rows and transfer to BOTH arms unchanged; only X1 speaks to a server half, and only Node's. So the spike is not evidence for the walk arm in the way a quick reading might suggest.

RENDER-HASH: nothing in the dossier leans on it, and neither arm repairs it - production takes it from the root hiccup at pipeline.clj:543 regardless. One observation recorded for rf2-2rtt6.91's owner rather than as a ruling: spec 011 already tiers detection so that React-element roots carry NO HASH AT ALL, which may mean .91's candidate (c) is the spec's own existing answer for Hicasso's tier.

NO VERDICT WAS DRAWN, and the disagreement about whether one was wanted is recorded in the page's own section 0. Mike's 2026-08-04 directive commissioned a NO-VERDICT dossier; the bead's older description asked for the recommendation stated. The page prices both arms and stops.

ALSO FILED: rf2-2rtt6.114 (P2, bug) - the Node entry's byte accounting reports UTF-16 code units labelled as UTF-8. I had told the worker rf2-2rtt6.86 was reopened for this; IT IS NOT - .86 is closed and its close reason enumerates .91, .92 and .94 as follow-ups while omitting this one. No size figure from that manifest appears anywhere in the dossier.
=== OPERATOR VERDICT — THE CHARTER-v0 DOGFOOD PREFERENCE GATE, RECORDED 2026-08-08 09:36 AUSEST. Mike Thompson, in his own words, verbatim: ===

  "Hicasso is the surface I would choose for ordinary re-frame screens;
   raw UIx remains the escape for React-specific work."

THAT IS THE VERDICT AND IT IS RECORDED AS GIVEN. No mayor gloss is added to the sentence, and none should be added later — the operator's wording is the artefact. Where a summary is needed downstream, quote it rather than paraphrasing it.

WHAT IT DECIDES. The charter-v0 gate — "a dogfood list+form screen preferred over raw UIx by its authors" — is MET, affirmatively, for ordinary re-frame screens. rf2-2rtt6.67 (closed 2026-08-03, PR #7413) delivered the evidence only and said so; this note is the operator call that record was waiting for.

WHAT IT UNBLOCKS. HD-013's P2 graduation advisory now HAS its ergonomics leg, which it explicitly lacked until a dated operator note landed on this bead. The dogfood verdict was the single outstanding critical-path input for the P2 sitting; the remaining operator item is booking it.

THE SCOPE LIMIT IS IN THE OPERATOR'S OWN SENTENCE, not bolted on afterwards. "Ordinary re-frame screens" is the claim; "raw UIx remains the escape for React-specific work" is the boundary. That matches what the evidence page and the seventh dossier round both recommended scoping it to — arm1's macros deliberately do not inspect view bodies, so correctness rides the bespoke collector/codec/intent-lowering/lifecycle/SSR/escape machinery, and the dogfood screen does not exercise most escape paths. The verdict is therefore a preference about the AUTHORING SURFACE for ordinary screens, not a claim that Hicasso subsumes UIx.

WHAT THIS VERDICT IS NOT. It is not a P2 graduation decision — HD-013 reserves that to the operator at the sitting, advised by the recorded reviews, and adapters-as-success remains a SUCCESSFUL outcome. It is not a clock or heap result and moves no K-criterion number: K1 stands at ~1.18x vs direct UIx [1.13-1.24] conditionally labelled (rf2-t2flm), K3 stands tripped as written. It does not retire the honest losses the evidence page states — UIx keeps compile-time shape checking, the live event in hand, fixed subscription identity, and the smaller machinery bet.

PROVENANCE. Verdict given by the operator in chat, 2026-08-08 09:36 AUSEST, against the inspected evidence (route A of the 2026-08-03 15:49 protocol: sign, amend, or contradict the advisory template). The operator amended the template — he gave the substantive sentence without its "Preferred, with reservations" prefix — and the sentence above is what he wrote.
OPERATOR RULING (2026-08-10 03:00 AUSEST, Mike, in session) — OPTION A: SUPERSEDED AND CLOSED. The new product governance records govern from this date. Pointer map (old element -> new home):
- SHIP BAR (mount AND bulk <=1.0x Reagent, clock-only) -> K1: price-acceptance amendment rf2-hic-003 (operative default; 1.25x ceiling vs direct UIx; user-visible budgets, spec §6). K2 bulk: verdict protocol rf2-hic-036 (stop/narrow per red cell), gated on the Reagent pair per the decision brief scoreboard.
- RED-ZONES -> spec §6 comparative bands + budget gates rf2-hic-089 (early) / rf2-hic-071 (late populations).
- BUDGETS: <=2 hooks -> ceiling frozen at rf2-hic-018; ~0.4-0.5KB target and >1KB paper-fail -> byte-exact shell line + breach disposition rf2-hic-006/018; ViewCell-class graph -> decision-brief kill rules + architecture census rf2-hic-087; per-read survival -> evidence-baseline pinned rows re-pinned by rf2-hic-006; per-keystroke path -> rf2-hic-045/078.
- HD-002 ADJUDICATION -> kernel witnesses rf2-hic-010/011, design-laws lane, substrate adjudication rf2-hic-018 (tripwire-overrides-clock preserved as correctness-blocks-performance in the delivery gates).
- K1-K7 + SIX-WEEK CLOCK -> K1 ruled tripped-and-superseded (rf2-sza0w, same date); remaining kill surface = decision-brief kill rules + the eleven-row trust register; the six-week clock is moot after the selection.
- DECIDERS -> unchanged: the operator; K3 disposition record rf2-hic-070.

=== APPENDED MEASUREMENT (worker, rf2-2rtt6.4) — THE P0 RED-ZONE THRESHOLDS ===
Workers append; only the operator amends. Full page:
docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-uix-on-subs-frontier-arm.md

PRODUCING COMMIT ea5d01ab9d (arm at bc5f38f10a).
REPRO clock: P0_ROUNDS=5 P0_SAMPLES=10 P0_WARMUPS=4 node implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs --only clock
REPRO heap:  P0_ROUNDS=5 P0_ROOTS=4 node implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs --only heap
RUNTIME: HeadlessChrome 147.0.7727.15 (Chromium/Playwright), Windows x64; :advanced,
goog.DEBUG false, plain :browser module; React 19.2.0, Reagent 2.0.1, UIx 1.4.4.
BROWSER NUMBERS ONLY. No JVM/Node figure appears.

Per RULING 1 these figures ARE the red-zones. A later candidate row worse than
the stated mean on either axis for that witness family is RED and needs an
explicit operator waiver naming the dogfood benefit.

--- RED-ZONE, CLOCK: UIx-on-subs / Reagent-on-subs, both floor-normalised in the
--- same round and the same adapter segment. 5 rounds, ranges are min-max.

  W1-list mount (1,203 el, 300 boundaries, 1 sub/boundary)
      1.057x  [0.907 - 1.156]   STRADDLES 1.0 -> INDISTINGUISHABLE
  W3-form mount (51 el, 12 fields, 1 sub/field)
      0.893x  [0.843 - 0.956]   UIx faster, disjoint from 1.0
  U-broad bulk  (301 el, 300 boundaries, one commit ALL read)
      0.838x  [0.760 - 0.953]   UIx faster, disjoint from 1.0
  U-narrow bulk (301 el, one commit exactly ONE reads)
      1.536x  [1.226 - 1.876]   UIx SLOWER, disjoint from 1.0

  Against the floor: reagent-subs 2.350 / 1.948 / 8.064 / 4.277;
                     uix-subs     2.472 / 1.738 / 6.729 / 6.502.

--- RED-ZONE, RETAINED HEAP: exclusive (arm - floor) B/boundary, UIx / Reagent,
--- same segment. CDP getHeapUsage after a forced collection, 4 roots held.

  list (300 sub-reading rows)   2.262x  [2.196 - 2.335]   (absolute 1.580x)
  grid (300 sub-reading cells)  2.254x  [2.217 - 2.288]   (absolute 1.989x)

  Exclusive per boundary: Reagent-on-subs ~954 B (list) / ~947 B (grid);
  UIx-on-subs ~2,156 B (list) / ~2,134 B (grid). NOTE FOR K3 AND THE BUDGET:
  the frontier comparator is itself over the 1 KB paper-fail line by >2x, and
  the Reagent denominator is close to it. Red (>2.26x) and over budget (>~0.5 KB)
  are far apart; a candidate can sit between them.

--- INSTRUMENT DISCIPLINE
  Arm-order guard REPORTABLE on every row, both axes; driver exit 0. Self-test
  8/8 before anything was measured. Canonical-DOM parity clean under :advanced in
  both segments and across the seam, all rounds. Every measured write read back
  out of the DOM inside its own window: 0 UNVERIFIED OF 6,600 clock windows and
  0 OF 48 heap mounts. Both orders: segment order and witness order alternate
  with the round; arm order within a segment chosen by measured adjacency.
  POSITIVE CONTROLS, predicted vs measured, every run:
    heap  predicted 4,700,000 B  measured 4,700,317 B [4,699,074-4,700,974] 1.0001x
    clock predicted 1.9975 (2403/1203 elements) measured 1.8381 [1.8182-1.8548].
    The 8% shortfall is the mount window's FIXED per-root term: solving
    (f+2403k)/(f+1203k)=1.8381 gives f ~= 229k, ~19% of the 1,203-element page.
    Consequence: the clock compresses ratios toward 1.0, so a threshold above 1.0
    is conservative and one below 1.0 is generous to UIx.

--- WITNESS-SET CAVEAT THE OPERATOR SHOULD SEE
  These shapes do NOT match rf2-2rtt6.2's (unmerged at time of measurement): that
  arm uses a 901-el M1 list and a 51-el M2 form, both reading [:p0/cell i]; this
  arm uses a 1,203-el W1 reading [:p0/row i], a 51-el W3 reading [:p0/field i],
  and a 301-el 300-boundary grid reading [:p0/cell i]. The thresholds remain
  sound AS THRESHOLDS because each is a ratio between two arms measured in the
  same run, same shapes, same sub graph, same rounds -- but they are thresholds
  ON THIS WITNESS SET. If P0 converges on rf2-2rtt6.2's witnesses the UIx arm
  must be re-pointed and the red-zones re-derived. Closest correspondence today:
  this arm's U-broad (300 boundaries, one commit all read, [:p0/cell i]) matches
  that arm's bulk row in boundary count and sub graph, differing only in markup
  density. Filed as a follow-up bead.

--- WHAT THE NARROW ROW SAYS
  U-narrow is the only row where UIx-on-subs is materially behind, and the window
  decomposition puts the cost in the WRITE leg -- before React is involved --
  i.e. the useSyncExternalStore notification fanning out across 300 subscribed
  boundaries, not UIx's rendering. That is the row a native view layer has the
  clearest structural claim on.

SCHEDULE 5 rounds x 2 adapter segments x (8 warm-up + 12 samples) per arm;
        three arms per segment interleaved at the sample level, order rotating
        AND reflecting; segment order alternating with the round; ONE ROW PER
        PAGE.

--- WHY THIS ARM EXISTS. rf2-2rtt6.4 measured the frontier on a 1,203-el W1
--- reading [:p0/row i], a 51-el W3 reading [:p0/field i] and a 301-el grid;
--- rf2-2rtt6.2 supplies the BAR'S DENOMINATOR on a 901-el M1 and a 51-el M2,
--- both reading [:p0/cell i]. Each of .4's ratios is sound AS A RATIO. The
--- TABLE was not, because a threshold and the bar row it qualifies were on
--- different pages. Converged onto rf2-2rtt6.2's witnesses: that arm is on
--- main, owns the lane per HD-017, is the denominator HD-012 states the bar
--- against, already carries the in-plan control and the labelled lower bound,
--- and .4's own Open items nominated it.

--- RED-ZONE, CLOCK: UIx-on-subs / Reagent-on-subs, both floor-normalised in
--- the same round and the same segment. 5 rounds, ranges are min-max.

  M1 mount (901 el, 300 boundaries, 1 sub/boundary)      [BAR ROW]
      1.2301x  [1.1099 - 1.3538]   UIx SLOWER, disjoint from 1.0
  M2 mount (51 el, 12 fields, 1 sub/field)               [DIAGNOSTIC ONLY]
      1.0539x  [0.8572 - 1.4286]   STRADDLES 1.0 -> INDISTINGUISHABLE
  BULK BROAD (M1 page, one commit ALL 300 read)          [BAR ROW]
      0.6239x  [0.4701 - 0.7857]   UIx FASTER, disjoint from 1.0
  BULK NARROW (M1 page, one commit exactly ONE reads)    [NOT RESOLVED]
      1.1556x  [1.0417 - 1.2500]   direction UIx-slower, but see STABILITY

  Against the floor: reagent-subs 4.352 / 2.102 / 7.443 / 1.820;
                     uix-subs     5.343 / 2.261 / 4.607 / 2.117.

--- HOW MUCH THE MISMATCH MATTERED: THREE OF FOUR VERDICTS FLIP.

  large-list mount  .4 W1  1.057 [0.907-1.156] INDISTINGUISHABLE
                    ->  M1 1.2301 [1.110-1.354] UIx SLOWER, DISJOINT
  form mount        .4 W3  0.893 [0.843-0.956] UIx faster, DISJOINT, published
                            as a THRESHOLD
                    ->  M2 1.0539 [0.857-1.429] INDISTINGUISHABLE, and graded
                            DIAGNOSTIC to match its bar row
  broad commit      .4 U-broad 0.838 [0.760-0.953] -> 0.6239 [0.470-0.786]
                            same direction, MUCH larger margin
  narrow commit     .4 U-narrow 1.536 [1.226-1.876] DISJOINT
                    ->  1.1556 / 1.0405 depending on the run: direction the
                            same, strength COLLAPSES, does not stably resolve

  MECHANISM. The broad margin widens on the 901-el page because more of the
  window is markup construction, where UIx's compile-time $ beats Reagent's
  runtime hiccup walk; the narrow margin narrows because the floor's top-down
  re-render — the thing a narrow write is compared against — is 3x the work.
  A clock ratio on this axis moves by more than the effects being measured
  when the page changes. That is the whole case for converging.

--- A GRADE MISMATCH THAT IS NOT ABOUT WITNESSES AT ALL. rf2-2rtt6.2 grades its
--- 51-element form row DIAGNOSTIC and says it must not be quoted against the
--- bar (3-6 clock quanta at one mount a sample). rf2-2rtt6.4 batched 8 mounts a
--- sample, lifted the same-sized witness clear of the clamp, and published its
--- form row as a THRESHOLD. So a candidate's form row would have been judged
--- red against a threshold whose bar-row counterpart is unquotable. Resolved
--- here by grading the converged form row diagnostic, like its bar row.

--- ONE ARM RE-RUN, NOT TWO. THE HEAP AXIS WAS ALREADY CONVERGED IN SUBSTANCE.
  .4 list (1,203-el page)     2.262x [2.196-2.335]
  .4 grid (301-el page)       2.254x [2.217-2.288]
  .5 ladder (1,200 bnd, 1 rd) 2.435x  (3,811 B / 1,565 B above a React floor)
  Three shapes differing 4x in markup density and 4x in boundary count agree
  within 8%. Retained bytes per subscribing boundary is a property of the
  BOUNDARY; the clock is not, because element count decides what fraction of
  the window is React's own work. THE HEAP RED-ZONES ON THIS BEAD STAND
  UNCHANGED. (Stated as a claim the operator may reject: the three figures come
  from two instruments and are not a strict replication.)

--- THE DENOMINATOR REPRODUCES rf2-2rtt6.2. The Reagent arm here is a second
--- implementation on the same witnesses, different app ns, different schedule.
--- Its reagent-subs/floor ranges OVERLAP that arm's published ranges on all
--- three shared rows: M1 3.899 [3.447-4.300] vs 4.352 [4.063-4.625];

--- [0.448-0.650]; narrow 1.1972 [1.111-1.250].

  per-root term predicts. (The +/-0.001% standard of this wave is the HEAP
  control's; no clock control can honestly be held to it, and this run measures

--- UNTOUCHED.

      2.1739x FIRST-THIRD, ranges DISJOINT; every other arm on the page climbed

  broad  reagent-subs  write 0.0  gap 0.0   drain 2.10

(i) The charter-v0 gate - "a dogfood list+form screen preferred over raw UIx by its authors" - is NOT yet decided, and the call is Mike's alone. rf2-2rtt6.67 (CLOSED 2026-08-03, PR #7413) delivered the EVIDENCE only; its close note: "NO VERDICT PUBLISHED - the preference call remains the operator's". Do not mistake that close, or the 2026-07-31 Surface A/B ruling above (grouped-vs-collector INSIDE Hicasso), for this verdict. Until a dated operator note on THIS bead records it, the HD-013 P2 graduation advisory has no ergonomics leg.

(ii) Evidence page: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-dogfood-preference-case.md. It establishes: both renderings current and idiomatic (the UIx control strengthened, not strawmanned - its dead IME gate fixed to read the native event); same-screen proof on elements AND intents (canonical-DOM parity at mount and again after a 17-step real-DOM script driving all 8 handler sites and both branches of both key-maps; dispatched vectors captured at the :events port, asserted equal AND equal to a stated expectation; mutation-proved, incl. one divergence the DOM half structurally cannot see); authoring measured: 47 vs 72 lines (symmetric count, arithmetic shown twice), 8 data event positions vs 8 hand-written closures, 0 vs 2 threaded values, 5-5 concept-count tie; honest losses stated (UIx wins compile-time shape checking, event-in-hand, fixed subscription identity, smaller machinery bet). Over-claim retracted on the page: UIx CAN express conditional/helper-local reads - at the price of a component boundary or a hook call-site contract; one case (a read inside a variable-length for) has no hook-shaped route. HD-028 makes the value-equality bail-out Hicasso's boundary default; uix.core/memo is a per-component opt-in no repo example uses.

(iii) HOW TO MAKE THE CALL WELL (dossier recommendation): read the page once; then make the SAME small edit in BOTH renderings - e.g. add a "priority" field with a validation rule (touch model, event, row rendering) in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/dogfood_collector.cljs and dogfood_uix.cljs; record the verdict HERE the same day, while the feel is fresh, in whatever form is true - "preferred, with reservations" is a valid sentence. If NOT preferred, name the loss that decided it: that sentence is the top input for interpreter-gap/surface work, and not-preferred removes the ergonomic-win half of the K-rule defence (weighs toward adapters-as-success).

(iv) JUDGING CRITERIA worth keeping (compressed from both dossier sections): do not rule from the summary table - the counts favour Hicasso, but the 5-5 concept tie means the win is texture, visible only in the editor. Markup is a draw; the gap concentrates where events and reads live - the edit stays local data + local reads in Hicasso, while in UIx it also grows the fixed hook set and the event plumbing (dispatch acquisition, event extraction, submit prevention, app-owned IME gate). Intent-as-data is the stronger win (the first UIx cut got the IME law wrong - React's synthetic event drops isComposing; vectors are equality-visible to tests and tools). Weigh honestly against: compile-time checking, the live event in hand, stable subscription identity, far less novel machinery, and Hicasso's still-incomplete tool payoff (headless render API unfrozen; manifest/explain doors post-v0). The memo default is supporting evidence, not the reason.

CODEX ADVISORY (the dossier's independent second review; it re-counted the forms and traced the priority-field edit through both sources): lands "preferred, with reservations" and would record now, without another trial edit. Advisory only - no agent may record the verdict. If the page plus that trace settles your taste, adopting it is one dated sentence here; otherwise run (iii). Its post-verdict advice, useful for HD-013 either way: freeze the small core surface; the next ergonomics investment is one excellent diagnostic/structural-testing path (editor linting, source-rich runtime errors, the minimal headless render door), not more syntax or another authoring mode.

title: EP-0036 records the Freehand programme as withdrawn, and the six EPs that cite it stop implying it is live
description:

The tracker half is done (rf2-drpa3 and its tree). This bead is the normative half: the EP corpus still describes Freehand as an accepted, in-flight programme.

WHAT IS WRONG TODAY
1. docs/EP/EP-0036-the-freehand-view-substrate-programme.md carries 'Status: accepted'. Per EP-0009 that means 'ruled by the operator; graduation into the normative home' - it asserts a live programme.
2. Six further EPs reference Freehand and were written when it was the intended destination: EP-0030 (the compiled-view-substrate program), EP-0031, EP-0032, EP-0033, EP-0034, EP-0035.
3. docs/EP/README.md indexes them.

THE STATUS VALUE, AND WHY
EP-0009:85-87 makes the Status line MACHINE-READABLE with a CLOSED vocabulary: proposal, accepted, final, active, rejected, withdrawn, deferred, superseded-by EP-NNNN. Do not invent a value.

  WITHDRAWN is the honest one. EP-0009:79 glosses it 'author retracted - kept'. The programme was accepted, attempted at length, and retracted on evidence.
  NOT 'rejected' - EP-0009:78 is 'ruled no' - that describes a proposal turned down before implementation. Freehand was built.
  NOT 'superseded-by EP-NNNN' - there is no successor EP. A third view layer (Hicasso) is in design in ai/findings/new-view/ but has no EP number. If one is later written, THAT is the moment to consider re-pointing, and it is a separate decision.

  If the implementer believes a different value is more honest, STOP AND REPORT rather than choosing - the vocabulary is normative and this is the operator's call.

WHAT ELSE THE EP MUST SAY. A bare status flip loses the finding. The EP should carry, briefly, WHY it was withdrawn, because that reasoning is the durable value:
  - the Reagent standard (rf2-lbs3y, Mike 2026-07-27, verbatim 'Freehand can't be used if it is slower than Reagent') was not met;
  - the residual gap is architectural, not an optimisation backlog - see docs/design/freehand/studio/ and the ablation on rf2-lbs3y;

The guarantee is not what cost us. The same ablation found invariant 5 is worth MORE than Spec 006 claims (a staged site publishes stale and never self-heals).

THE OTHER SIX EPs. Do NOT rewrite them. EP-0009:118 says amendment is allowed only before implementation, and rf2-drpa3.57 records the standing intent that EP-0030..EP-0035 REMAIN as the historical record of the donor programme. What is needed is only that a reader does not mistake them for live: a one-line pointer where each names Freehand as its destination. Judge per file; several may need nothing.

THE CODE STAYS. Mike: 'not removed yet'. No implementation/freehand/** deletion, no build-id removal, no CI lane changes. This bead is docs/EP only.

ACCEPTANCE
  1. EP-0036's Status line is a legal EP-0009 value and the withdrawal reason is stated in the EP itself, not only in beads.
  2. No EP reads as though Freehand is a live destination.
  3. docs/EP/README.md agrees with the new status.
  4. python -m mkdocs build --strict exits 0 (note: mkdocs is not on PATH in Git Bash here - use python -m mkdocs), and check_doc_slugs.py exits 0.
  5. No file under implementation/ is touched.

title: A malformed test (ns ...) form is silently dropped from the JVM lane
description:
Observed while landing rf2-d2841 pass 5 (worker/core-roster-p5).

A test file whose `(ns ...)` FORM is malformed — a stray unescaped quote in the
docstring is enough — is INVISIBLE to `cognitect.test-runner`'s namespace
discovery. `clojure.tools.namespace.find` cannot read the form, so the
namespace never enters the discovered set:

  * `clojure -M:test -n <that-ns>` reports `Ran 0 tests`, exit 0 (only the
    RF2_MIN_TESTS floor made it red, and only because the probe run had the
    floor pinned to 1).
  * a FULL `clojure -M:test` ran 2182 tests instead of 2190 — exactly the
    eight deftests of the broken file — and reported `0 failures, 0 errors`.

So a whole test namespace can leave the lane with the suite still green. This
is the same class of false green `scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh` exists to
close, arriving by a different door.

NEITHER EXISTING GUARD CATCHES IT:
  * the prod-gate script's `verify_roster` guard #1 compares the file count
    under `test/` against the scraped `-test` namespace count, but it scrapes
    the `(ns ` line as TEXT with sed — it never reads the form, so a file with
    a broken body still scrapes fine;
  * the RF2_MIN_TESTS floor is a COLLAPSE detector calibrated ~3% under the
    observed count; eight missing tests out of 2190 is far inside that.

Remedy candidates (not ruled):
  a. have the runner compare the namespaces it DISCOVERED against the file
     list under `test/` and fail on any file it could not read;
  b. add a `-n`-selector post-check: every requested namespace must have
     contributed at least one test;
  c. make `verify_roster` require the scraped namespace to be loadable.

Reproduce: break the docstring of any `*_test.clj` (an unescaped `"` inside the
ns docstring), then run the suite.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7249 (2026-08-01) — REOPENED exact JVM discovery-integrity owner; no duplicate.

The malformed-form and wrong-path-name doors are fixed, but the shipped claim that the per-file path comparison also makes discovery injective is false for two legal source layouts:

1. One discovery root contains both `probe/duplicate_test.clj` and `probe/duplicate_test.cljc`, each declaring `probe.duplicate-test`.
2. Two `-d` roots each contain the same relative path and declaration.

In both cases every file passes the current check because `discovery-defects` derives `ext` from that file and compares it only to its own relative path. There is no cross-file uniqueness pass. Direct probe against the exact runner blob shipped by PR #7249 (blob 9d5e997024, unchanged on current origin/main) produced:

`{:discovered [probe.duplicate-test probe.duplicate-test], :defects []}`

This is the shadowing door the PR says the one rule closes. Cognitect `test` mapcats those duplicate namespace symbols, requires them in order (the second require is already loaded), then passes both symbols to `clojure.test/run-tests`; one physical file is loaded and run twice while the other never runs, green. A count/floor cannot detect the substitution.

Repair narrowly in this owner: retain the readable form + own-path comparison, then enforce global uniqueness of each declared JVM namespace across all files from all selected discovery roots, independent of `.clj`/`.cljc` extension. Name every colliding file in the diagnostic. Add regression controls for same-root `.clj` + `.cljc` siblings and same relative `.clj` path across two `-d` roots; keep the unreadable, wrong-declaration, multi-dir parsing, clean-tree, and process-boundary controls green. No new runner, roster, manifest, or source-root policy.
close_reason:
AUDIT REOPEN CLOSED — discovery is now injective, not merely per-file correct. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7353 (MERGED 710f9b0e73).

THE DOOR, CONFIRMED. Probed the exact blob the audit named (9d5e997024, unchanged on the base): both layouts reproduced verbatim — {:discovered [probe.duplicate-test probe.duplicate-test], :defects []} for a same-root .clj+.cljc pair AND for one relative path under two -d roots. discovery-defects derived ext FROM the file and compared it only to that file's own relative path, so there was no cross-file pass at all.

END-TO-END PROOF, not just the predicate: the .cljc sibling carried a deftest that fails if it ever executes. The shipped runner reported 'Ran 2 tests containing 2 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.' exit 0. The .clj's single passing test ran TWICE; the failing file never loaded. The tally goes UP, so neither the summary nor the RF2_MIN_TESTS floor (a collapse detector) can see the substitution — that is what made it fail-open rather than merely wrong.

THE REPAIR, narrow to this owner as ruled. discovery-defects now runs two rules over one scan: own-path-defect (the existing readable-form + own-path comparison, behaviour unchanged) and collision-defects (global uniqueness of every declared namespace across ALL selected roots, independent of .clj/.cljc). Collisions are computed over the files that already spell their own path, since a file that does not is already named by the first rule. Every colliding file is named and each complaint points at the others. The scan dedupes by CANONICAL path so a lane naming one directory twice is not reddened over its alias spelling. verify-discovery!'s diagnostic now explains both doors, ASCII-only. No new runner, roster, manifest, or source-root policy.

NO ALLOWANCE WAS NEEDED and nothing was widened from error to warning — neither layout is ever legal on a JVM classpath.

WHAT IT HAD BEEN HIDING: NOTHING. Swept every quiet-runner lane in the repo — 44 aliases across 34 deps.edn, each with its own -d set resolved from its :main-opts (per-lane is the only correct semantics; separate lanes are separate classpaths), including the five-root tools :test lane. TOTAL DEFECTS 0. The door was open; nothing had walked through it.

MUTATION: collision present + fixed runner => exit 1 naming both files; collision removed, git diff empty => exit 0 reporting 'Ran 1 tests' (not 2 — direct confirmation the earlier 2 was one test run twice).

CONTROLS ADDED (each pins the DEFECT before the guard, via find-namespaces-in-dir first): clj+cljc sibling named both ways; one relative path under two roots named, AND either root alone stays clean so a single-root lane is not falsely reddened; canonical-path dedupe pinned so a refactor cannot reintroduce a false red. Unreadable / wrong-declaration / multi-dir / clean-tree / process-boundary controls unchanged and green.

GATES (all exit 0): test-jvm-implementation.sh (23 suites), test-jvm-tools.sh (five-root lane), test-fast-pr.sh (incl. CLJS node 12263 tests), clj-kondo 2026.04.15 CI pin with CI's exact --lint set, errors: 0. Rebased onto 4a9cfc71e7 (rf2-g7p7l) before the final gate run.

INCIDENTAL, left alone deliberately: top-level implementation/deps.edn :test resolves a test/ root that does not exist; it is not on the JVM roster and is never invoked, and roster policy was explicitly out of scope.

title: migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:2940 teaches v1 migrators that a boundary rejection 'reports nothing on either axis'
description:
FOUND BY rf2-j6e7r/v94d6/zfw16's sweep (2026-07-28 19:36 AUSEST, PR #7234).

VERBATIM on origin/main, migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:2940:

  '**Surviving the build is not the same as being visible in it.** A boundary rejection in production reports nothing on either axis: the emit is dev-gated along with the rest of the trace surface, the error category was never promoted onto the always-on substrate, and — because the skipped handler wrote no :db — the always-on :events record for that dispatch reads :outcome :ok. A quiet dashboard is therefore not evidence that nothing was refused. If the v1 interceptor you are replacing *logged* its rejections, that half does not come across: validate in the handler body and emit the signal from handler code.'

Every clause after the bold lead is false since PR #7203 (rf2-mwv4e), and the last sentence is the damaging one: it tells a migrator that the framework will NOT count their boundary rejections, so they must hand-roll the signal. The always-on record IS the count, so the advice creates the duplicate emission it was written to prevent.

This is the audience that can least afford it. A v1 migrator replacing a check-spec-style interceptor reads this paragraph to decide what they lose, and the honest answer is now 'less than this says': the rejection fans one always-on structural :rf.error/schema-validation-failure record (:source :boundary, identifiers only), settles :outcome :rejected on the dispatch, and — being projection-eligible — draws a 400 from SSR's default projector. What does not come across from a v1 interceptor that LOGGED the offending value is exactly that: the value. The record is deliberately structural, because a boundary payload is attacker-controlled.

THE BOLD LEAD SURVIVES AND SHOULD BE KEPT. 'Surviving the build is not the same as being visible in it' is the right frame; this arm simply moved to the other side of it, so the paragraph becomes a worked instance of C-000.35 rather than its counter-example. spec/010-Schemas.md §Production builds (corrected in PR #7234) is the wording to agree with; spec/Security.md §Input validation is the pattern-level statement.

GREP THE SURROUNDING MIGRATION PROSE for the same premise — the sweep pinned only :2940, and the :spec/at-boundary → :rf.schema/at-boundary vocabulary rows at :2180/:2188 sit in the same chapter.

description:
SEQUENTIAL FOLLOW-UP to rf2-6jqa8's AUDIT-REOPEN tightening (PR #7205). spec/** is HOT-ZONE, so the worker reported rather than edited. Obligation (6)(c) of the rf2-6jqa8 ruling — it was assigned to rf2-rprfg, which CLOSED on PR #7192 before this tightening existed, so it needs its own bead.

THE DRIFT. PR #7205 made the always-on safe-redirect record a strict STRUCTURAL PROJECTION of the diagnostics: it carries #{:frame :recovery :reason :scheme :host} and NOTHING else. It no longer carries :location in any form (scrubbed or otherwise), and no longer carries :allowlist. The dev trace still carries both. spec/009 does not yet distinguish the two axes:

  (a) Tags column, :rf.error/safe-redirect-invalid-url (~line 2140):
      reads ':frame, :location, :reason, plus :scheme on the :scheme-without-host arm'
      — the always-on record carries :frame, :reason, and :scheme; never :location.
  (b) Tags column, :rf.error/safe-redirect-scheme-rejected (~2141):
      reads ':frame, :location, :scheme, plus :reason on the non-http(s) arm'
      — always-on carries :frame, :scheme, and :reason on that arm; never :location.
  (c) Tags column, :rf.error/safe-redirect-host-disallowed (~2142):
      reads ':frame, :location, :host, :reason ..., :allowlist (the allowlist vector, when supplied)'
      — always-on carries :frame, :host, :reason; NEVER :location and NEVER :allowlist.
  (d) The always-on paragraph (~line 1949) says 'the tag map is built ONCE for both axes with the EP-0015 egress scrub applied to :location INSIDE the builder: the query / fragment carrier VALUES are redacted while the structured path, the scheme and the host are kept'. True of the DEV TRACE. False of the always-on record, which carries no URL at all. The 'built ONCE' claim stays true — the builder still runs once and the record is a projection of its output.

WHY THE TIGHTENING (recorded here so the spec edit can state the reason). The carrier scrub is the Spec 015 blanket policy and does string surgery only after the first '?' or '#'. Over the app's OWN URL space (rf2-ov56u's route-miss :url) that is right. Over an ARBITRARY ATTACKER-SUPPLIED FOREIGN URL it is not fail-closed: userinfo (https://alice:pw@host/), the whole path (a reset token), and value-less query keys all sit LEFT of the carriers and rode out verbatim. Demonstrated against HEAD under -Dre-frame.debug=false before the fix. :allowlist is the app's own security configuration — unbounded policy data naming the boundary being probed.

SUGGESTED SHAPE. The row's Tags column describes the trace tags; add a short always-on clause per row (or one sentence in the always-on paragraph) saying the always-on record is the closed structural projection #{:frame :recovery :reason :scheme :host} with :scheme / :host lower-cased for aggregation, and that :location / :allowlist are DEV-TRACE-ONLY. Source of truth is re-frame.ssr.egress/safe-redirect-record-slots, pinned closed by the-production-record-carries-exactly-the-enumerated-slots in re-frame.ssr-safe-redirect-production-test.

NO CONFORMANCE TEST REDS TODAY. The always-on-categories literal is a set of CATEGORIES (unchanged by #7205), and there is no SafeRedirect*Tags Malli schema, so the rf2-6tags Tags-column arm has nothing to compare against these rows. The drift is therefore silent — which is why it needs a bead rather than a CI failure.

CROSS-REF rf2-mt4v3 (spec/011 should state the rejection never projects, plus the understated spec/Security.md entry) — same spec pass, adjacent scope; consider sequencing together since spec/009 and spec/011 are both hot-zone.
notes:
Audit of merged PR #7207: the axis split accurately documents PR #7205's current key set, but it also canonises the unsafe premise found while auditing that implementation: lower-cased `:scheme` and `:host` are still raw, unbounded attacker-selected URL components. Closed keys do not make their values structural or secret-free; custom schemes and DNS labels can carry sentinel material and attacker-driven cardinality. Exact implementation owner rf2-6jqa8 is reopened P1.

This Bead remains the exact Spec 009 Tags/paragraph owner. Reopen it, dependent on rf2-6jqa8, and do not duplicate the runtime design. After the always-on discriminator shape is made content-safe and bounded, update all three safe-redirect catalogue rows, the shared always-on paragraph and the named source-of-truth/key-set prose in one sequenced pass. Preserve the rich dev trace, one-record semantics and non-projecting wire behavior. Coordinate the hot-zone edit with already-open rf2-rprfg, which owns the separate promotion-criterion contradiction.
close_reason:
TAGS COLUMNS AND ALWAYS-ON PARAGRAPH RECONCILED WITH THE SHIPPED SHAPE — PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7342 (with rf2-6jqa8 + rf2-ycbhx's dependency rf2-6jqa8, one PR, which is what the reopen note asked for: 'after the always-on discriminator shape is made content-safe and bounded, update all three rows … in one sequenced pass').

THE DRIFT, AS FILED AND AS EXTENDED. The three Tags columns listed :location (and :allowlist on host-disallowed) as always-on tags; both had become dev-trace-only under #7205. The 2026-07-31 reopen then correctly refused to let the bead merely document #7205's key set, because that set canonised an unsafe premise — lower-cased :scheme and :host are still raw, unbounded caller-selected URL components. rf2-6jqa8 fixed the runtime in the same PR; this bead's edits describe the SETTLED shape rather than the interim one, so the spec never records a claim that was already known to be wrong.

WHAT SPEC/009 NOW SAYS.
(a)(b)(c) Each of the three rows' Tags columns is split explicitly into AXIS 1 and AXIS 2, so the two are never again confusable:
  invalid-url      axis 1 = :frame :recovery :reason, plus :scheme-class (:http/:https) on the :scheme-without-host arm; the parse-failure arm carries no class at all.
  scheme-rejected  axis 1 = :frame :recovery :scheme-class (:javascript/:data/:vbscript, or :other on the non-http(s) arm), plus :reason on that arm. The row states what the class does NOT do — it never spells the caller's scheme, so mailto: and s3cr3t-probe-token: both arrive as :other.
  host-disallowed  axis 1 = :frame :recovery :reason, and nothing else. ':host is DEV-TRACE-ONLY' is called out in bold with the three reasons it was given up.
Every row's axis-2 clause names :location, the raw :scheme spelling and (on host-disallowed) :host + :allowlist as the dev trace's own.
(d) The always-on paragraph's shape claim is rewritten: BUILT FROM #{:frame :recovery :reason :scheme-class}, built from rather than filtered down to, and by NAME as well as by slot. It carries the reasoning the reopen demanded — 'a closed set of keys is not yet a closed set of values', with the RFC 3986 s3.1 scheme-grammar and RFC 1035 s2.3.4 DNS-length facts, both the CONTENT and the CARDINALITY costs, and why :host was dropped rather than hashed or truncated. 'Built ONCE' stays true and stays stated.

SOURCE-OF-TRUTH PROSE now names egress/scheme-classes and its parity test beside safe-redirect-record-slots, both pinned by ssr-safe-redirect-production-test.

ALSO CORRECTED, found by corpus sweep: re-frame.privacy.url's ns docstring described the allow-list as 'over parsed structural components' — the exact premise this audit corrected. Swept spec/011, spec/Security.md, spec/API.md, docs/ssr/response.md, docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md and docs/core/how-to/configure-dev-and-prod.md: they describe categories, validation order and non-projection only, never the tag shape, so they needed no edit. rf2-mt4v3 (spec/011 + Security.md) left alone — separate owner, as cross-referenced.

STILL NO CONFORMANCE TEST COVERS THIS (always-on-categories is a CATEGORY set; no SafeRedirect*Tags schema exists), so the drift stays silent by nature — which is why the PR carries the by-hand table-column check (7 pipes per row, unchanged) and why the key sets are pinned in ssr-safe-redirect-production-test rather than only described here.

title: Spec 010 + 011: state that step-5 fx-args is dev-posture for user fx, and that the reserved :rf.server/* family guards its own args in all builds
description:
rf2-dtpfv IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT ITEM 5, deferred out of PR #7204 (which landed the CODE — items 1/2/4 — plus the one Spec 009 catalogue row its new error id required). Both files below are HOT-ZONE: sequence this against any other spec-touching PR.

THE CODE IS ALREADY ON MAIN (PR #7204), so this is prose catching up to shipped behaviour, not a design question. The ruling is settled; do not re-litigate.

WHAT TO WRITE.

 spec/010-Schemas.md §Per-step recovery row 5 — qualify the GENERAL step-5 fx-args gate (a user reg-fx :schema) as DEV-POSTURE: validate-fx! is (if interop/debug-enabled? (run-validation ...) true), read once at namespace-load time, so under -Dre-frame.debug=false the boundary does not run and the documented :skipped recovery does not happen. State it ONCE, LOUDLY, in the same pattern rf2-bkvu5's (a) ruling uses for reg-app-schema. Then add that the reserved :rf.server/* family INDEPENDENTLY guards its own args in ALL builds (a handler-owned invariant), with the richer Malli diagnostic available only in dev. Trust-the-programmer covers USER declarations; it does not cover the framework's own wire-adjacent contract.

 spec/011-SSR.md — the standard SSR fx handlers preserve :rf/response integrity UNCONDITIONALLY, so every host adapter inherits a well-formed accumulator from get-response. Adapter-side coercion (ssr-ring's fail-closed-status, the header/cookie string coercions) is defence-in-depth, explicitly NOT a normative obligation — this is the clause that REJECTS option (a)'s 'a host adapter MUST fail-closed' formulation.

REFERENCE MATERIAL, all already on main:
 - implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc — the '---- the reserved :rf.server/* ARGS SHAPE gate (rf2-dtpfv) ----' section header comment states the ruling, the mechanism (throw-through-containment), the taxonomy line (malformed CALL throws; untrusted-INPUT policy rejection stays emit-and-no-op), and the posture split, in the form the spec prose should mirror.
 - implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/server_fx_schemas.cljc ns docstring '## What runs when (rf2-dtpfv)'.
 - spec/009-Instrumentation.md's :rf.error/server-fx-args-invalid row (landed in #7204).
 - implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_reserved_fx_guards_test.clj — the executable statement of the contract.

FENCE: spec/010-Schemas.md + spec/011-SSR.md ONLY. No code. Gate: mkdocs build --strict.
notes:

title: Promote ssr-ring fail-closed-status's silent 200->500 flip to the always-on error axis
description:
rf2-dtpfv IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT ITEM 3, deferred out of PR #7204 (which landed items 1/2/4). Explicitly ruled NOT a prerequisite for the guards, and an egress-surface change of a different review class (same class as rf2-6jqa8; wants an rf2-ov56u-style review).

THE RESIDUE. implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj's fail-closed-status coerces a non-integer :status to 500 and its ONLY signal is (trace/emit! :warning :rf.ssr/ssr-non-integer-status ...) — the DEV bus. On a production JVM the app's 200 silently becomes a 500 with nothing on either error axis. rf2-dtpfv named this 'problem 2' and its ruling note says the promotion 'probably wants promoting alongside' the guards.

WHAT CHANGED UNDER IT. PR #7204 made the reserved :rf.server/* fx guard their own args unconditionally, so the ACCUMULATOR is now well-formed in every build and fail-closed-status should no longer fire from the framework's own fx path at all. It stays as the last-line backstop for a host that hand-builds a response map, and the ruling is explicit that it is NOT the primary owner. So the promotion is now about an ADAPTER-level defect signal, not about the fx path — re-measure whether it can still fire before writing the promotion.

WHAT TO DO. Route the flip through the error-emit/emit-error-both! seam (the rf2-2hkfy pattern) with a CONSTANT :reason and never the offending value (the rf2-s3n6h precedent). Keep the Ring materialiser coercions as backstop. If a new :rf.error/* category is needed it MUST land with its Spec 009 §Error event catalogue row in the same PR — implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj source-scans every artefact src/ for throw-error!/emit-error! literals and its allow-list is EMPTY (TOTALITY), so an uncatalogued category reds the core lane. PR #7204 catalogued :rf.error/server-fx-args-invalid the same way and may be a usable model.

FENCE: implementation/ssr-ring/src + test. spec/009-Instrumentation.md is HOT-ZONE if a row is needed. Gates: implementation/ssr-ring clojure -M:test, plus the core error-catalogue conformance namespace.
notes:
PR #7210 (worker/ring-status-gblft). Item 3 of rf2-dtpfv landed.

RE-MEASURED FIRST (the bead's instruction), under the real gate (clojure -J-Dre-frame.debug=false -M:test, never with-redefs):
 - warning count under -Dre-frame.debug=false = 0; dev = 2 (a DOUBLE-EMIT, see below); always-on records = []. Total silence in production, confirmed.
 - AFTER #7204 the framework fx feeder is DEAD: [:rf.server/set-status "not-an-int"] leaves :status 500 (Long — guard threw, containment fanned :rf.error/fx-handler-exception, projector stamped); [:rf.server/redirect {:location "/ok" :status "302"}] leaves :redirect nil. Projector path closed too (public-error-shape? requires integer 400-599, else locked 500).
 - NO ARM IS DEAD. nil->fallback and integer?->passthrough run every request; the flip arm is a LIVE backstop reachable only from a HOST that hand-builds the accumulator (public response/swap-response!) or calls the public materialiser with its own map — exactly the caller the ruling reserved it for. Backstop, not dead code.

PROMOTION. One emit site (report-non-integer-status!) so the two axes cannot disagree. Record BUILT FROM the closed #{:error :frame :time :where :status-type :reason :recovery}. :frame is ALWAYS nil by design (the materialiser is a pure map->map fn; both with-frame blocks close before the happy-path call site, so an ambient read would be nil on the very path this bead is about) — the malformed-hydration-payload frameless spelling. :status-type is a CLASS NAME (program structure, the :ex-class residual class). REJECTED the raw :status value (rf2-s3n6h) — dev-trace-only, absence asserted by name AND by scanning every slot value.

CATEGORY MINTED, not reused: :rf.error/ssr-ring-response-status-invalid. server-fx-args-invalid names an fx arg + carries :fx-id (no fx ran — false attribution); sanitised-on-projection names a projector failure + carries :projector-id (no projector here). Spec 009 row + the coupled core always-on-categories literal in ONE commit. Also joined non-projection-eligible-errors (fires post-resolution; frameless so nothing routes today, but it stops a future frame-carrying change silently status-flipping).

BONUS DEFECT FIXED: a target-less redirect with a non-integer status called fail-closed-status TWICE (no-target warning payload + response map) = 2 signals for 1 rewrite. Would have been a double alert on a shipper. Wire status now resolved once.

title: spec/009 + API.md: add :rejected to the event-outcome contract (follows rf2-mwv4e)
description:
SEQUENTIAL FOLLOW-UP to rf2-mwv4e (PR #7203), which adopted a NEW public event outcome. spec/** is HOT-ZONE, so the worker reported rather than edited. Split from rf2-lvsen because that bead's edit is coupled to the always-on-categories literal and this one is not — but both touch spec/009, so SEQUENCE them, never parallel.

THE ADDITION. `:outcome :rejected` on the always-on event-emit record: the `:rf.schema/at-boundary` interceptor REFUSED the event's payload against the handler's `:schema`. The handler never ran; entered interceptors still unwound in full.

WHY IT IS NOT AN OVERLOAD, which the spec should say once and plainly. Both existing non-ok values are wrong here: `:error` means the interceptor chain threw (it did not) and `:rolled-back` means a candidate state transition was refused before install (no candidate ever existed — the handler never ran). Keeping `:ok` preserved a known lie: the event stream's own stated contract is that an aborted dispatch is never reported as a clean settle.

THE SHARPEST LINE TO ADD is the COMPLEMENT of the `:rolled-back` caveat the spec already carries at length. `:rolled-back` has NO PRODUCER IN A PRODUCTION BUILD (candidate validation is dev-only). `:rejected` DOES — boundary validation is the one schema surface Spec 010 keeps ungated — so it is the outcome to alert on for hostile or malformed input at an untrusted ingress. Stating the pair together is what stops a reader generalising the `:rolled-back` warning to the whole vocabulary.

PRIORITY: `:rejected` is the LOWEST-priority discriminator. A chain throw, flow throw or candidate rollback during the unwind still wins; it fires only when the boundary skip is the whole story.

SITES:
  - spec/009-Instrumentation.md line ~1220 — the event-emit listener surface's `:outcome` enumeration (the long inline list).
  - spec/API.md line ~859 (Event-emit) — the record-shape paragraph.
  - spec/Spec-Schemas.md — no event-emit record schema with a closed `:outcome` enum exists today (verified: line 4314's enum is the EPOCH record's separate `:ok`/`:halted-*` vocabulary). If one is added, it needs the fifth member.
  - docs/core/observability.md line ~435/447 — the `:outcome :ok | :error | :rolled-back | :flow-error` comment + the prose after it.
  - docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md lines ~255-260 — SEE THE SIBLING DOC BEAD; that page's warning box is now actively wrong, not merely incomplete.

CODE IS ALREADY DONE and needs no further change: `re-frame.event-emit`'s ns docstring carries the full member contract, `re-frame.router`'s `commit-and-flow!` docstring and the pipeline-phase map comment enumerate it. Every consumer was audited in PR #7203 and none switches on a closed vocabulary — `observability/route-handled-event!` passes it to `:status`, `projection/project-handled-event` passes `:status` through as a summary key, the epoch and Xray-mutation `:outcome`s are separate vocabularies on separate records.
close_reason: PR #7207. :rejected added to the 009 :outcome enumeration (line ~1220) with the not-an-overload reasoning and the lowest-priority discriminator rule, plus the sharp line: :rejected is the exact COMPLEMENT of :rolled-back on the production question — :rolled-back has no producer in a release build, :rejected does, because boundary validation is the one ungated schema surface. spec/API.md 859 record-shape paragraph now enumerates all five members and carries the same asymmetry. No code change (event-emit ns docstring + commit-and-flow! already carry it); Spec-Schemas.md needs nothing — no event-emit record schema with a closed :outcome enum exists.

title: spec/009: the three :rf.error/safe-redirect-* rows must read Channel=always-on (follows rf2-6jqa8)
description:
SEQUENTIAL FOLLOW-UP to rf2-6jqa8, which promoted SSR's safe-redirect rejections onto the always-on error axis in code. spec/** is HOT-ZONE, so the worker on that bead reported rather than edited.

THE DRIFT. spec/009-Instrumentation.md lines ~2138-2140 classify all three categories as Channel = diagnostic:
  :rf.error/safe-redirect-invalid-url
  :rf.error/safe-redirect-scheme-rejected
  :rf.error/safe-redirect-host-disallowed
As of rf2-6jqa8 they fan BOTH axes from re-frame.ssr.response/emit-safe-redirect-error! -> dispatch-safe-redirect-record! -> the :error-emit/dispatch-error-record late-bind hook. The implementation is always-on; the spec says diagnostic. The spec is the artefact, so the spec is the thing that is now wrong.

THE CO-EDIT, and it is MANDATORY IN THE SAME PR. implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj invariant 4 asserts that the always-on set PARSED OUT OF THE CATALOGUE equals the literal always-on-categories in re-frame.always-on-axis-conformance-cljs-test. Editing spec/009 alone REDS that test; editing the literal alone reds it too. Both move together:
  1. spec/009-Instrumentation.md — the three Channel cells diagnostic -> always-on. Also worth a sentence per row recording WHY (the rejection is otherwise invisible to a production shipper) and noting the EP-0015 :location scrub.
  2. the always-on-categories literal in implementation/core/test/re_frame/always_on_axis_conformance_cljs_test.* — add the three. That test then drives each through the listener automatically, which is what keeps promotion real rather than documentary.

ALSO WORTH STATING IN THE SPEC while the row is open: rf2-6jqa8 added the three categories to re-frame.ssr.error-listener's non-projection-eligible-errors, so they ship a record but NEVER project a status. That is load-bearing, not incidental — without it the default projector's :else arm stamps the locked generic 500 and ?next=javascript:alert(1) becomes a denial of service. Measured, mutation-proved: with the three entries removed, all three arms of ssr-safe-redirect-production-test's wire deftest go 500 under -Dre-frame.debug=false.

AND A SEPARATE FACT THE SPEC SHOULD RECORD (measured 2026-07-28, NOT introduced by rf2-6jqa8): at HEAD, in DEV posture, a rejected safe-redirect ALREADY stamped 500 via the trace-cb buffering path, while production answered 200 — a dev/prod wire asymmetry on a security surface. rf2-6jqa8's eligibility skip is at the shared chokepoint, so both postures now answer 200. Spec 011 should say the rejection never projects.

close_reason:
PROMOTION-CRITERION CONTRADICTION RECONCILED — PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7342 (with rf2-6jqa8 + rf2-ycbhx, one PR).

THE 2026-07-31 AUDIT COMMENT'S FINDING. The three rows were correctly always-on (that half landed in #7192), but leg 2 of the authoritative criterion read 'contract breach or resource leakage … rather than a malformed input the caller can observe and fix at the call site'. A correctly refused attacker-controlled redirect is neither a leaked resource nor a corrupted invariant, so the criterion literally excluded the rows sitting beneath it.

BROADENED, NOT EXCEPTED — and that choice is the substance. The rf2-6jqa8 ruling offered either 'record the narrow exception' or 'broaden leg 2'. Broadening is right because the exception would have to be granted FOUR times over: :rf.error/machine-spawn-unregistered-type, :rf.error/unsupported-scroll-strategy, the :rf.schema/at-boundary arm of :rf.error/schema-validation-failure and the three safe-redirect rejections are ALL refusals rather than leaks, and every one of them was promoted on the same reasoning. Leg 2 was under-described relative to what the axis already carried; naming the shape reconciles the criterion with the catalogue instead of carving a hole in it.

WHAT SPEC/009 NOW SAYS. Leg 2 is 'Locally invisible' with two limbs — (a) contract breach or resource leakage, unchanged; (b) a refusal whose only local effect is the ABSENCE of the action: a fail-closed gate declining as a NO-OP, nothing thrown, nothing returned, so the call site has no value with which to distinguish 'refused' from 'never asked'. A blockquote names the four families already on limb (b) so a reader sees it is descriptive, not an escape hatch.

THE EXCLUDED CASE IS UNCHANGED AND NOW SHARPER: a malformed input the caller can OBSERVE, where observing means something threw or returned. :rf.server/safe-redirect carries the whole contrast inside one effect — its CR/LF/NUL gate THROWS, so the caller is told and it rides :rf.error/fx-handler-exception; its scheme/host gate NO-OPS, so before promotion the identical class of refusal reached nobody. Two halves of one security surface, and only the silent half needed leg 2(b). That is the asymmetry this bead's own description cited, now doing work in the spec.

CHANNEL-PROMOTION CATALOGUE. Second graduated entry added (one per limb): 'Security-boundary refusals', walking the three legs for the safe-redirect family and naming its siblings on the same limb. It carries the record discipline this family taught — the criterion's closing 'structured data only … never raw values' is a PROJECTION obligation here rather than a redaction one, and the test to apply is 'could a caller choose the bytes in this value, or the number of distinct values it can take? If either, it is not structural.' The section header moves from 'one graduated catalogue row' to two.

Also made precise: the two DEMOTED resource categories now read 'fail leg 2 under BOTH limbs', so widening the leg cannot be misread as sweeping them onto the axis.

NO CONFORMANCE IMPACT, VERIFIED NOT ASSUMED. No Channel cell moves, so error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test's catalogue-vs-literal invariant 4 is untouched — run green (22 tests / 55 assertions, exit 0) rather than reasoned about.

GATES: mkdocs --strict exit 0; check_doc_slugs exit 0; core 2198/11341 exit 0; clj-kondo 2026.04.15 errors: 0. Table column counts checked BY HAND (7 pipes per row on all three edited rows, unchanged from HEAD) since nothing validates table shape.
