title: Spec 010 step-5 fx-args validation is dev-only, so malformed :rf.server/* fx args are NOT skipped in production — they land on the response accumulator
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-28 00:30 AUSEST on worker/ssr-triage-76gom, running `re-frame.ssr-end-to-end-test` under the REAL gate:

    cd implementation/ssr && clojure -M:test:prod-gate -n re-frame.ssr-end-to-end-test

`ssr-server-fx-args-schema-boundary` contributes 16 of the namespace's 116 reds, and — unlike every other red in it — SEVEN of those are not trace spelling. They are the SEMANTIC assertions, and they fail because the behaviour differs.

WHAT THE GATE SHOWS. `re-frame.schemas.validate/validate-fx!` (validate.cljc ~989) is `(if interop/debug-enabled? (run-validation …) true)`. `interop/debug-enabled?` is read ONCE at namespace-load time, so under `-Dre-frame.debug=false` the Spec 010 §Validation-order step-5 fx-args boundary does not run AT ALL. Its documented recovery is `:skipped` (Spec 010 §Per-step recovery row 5 — "the caller skips the offending fx only"). In production NOTHING is skipped: the malformed fx runs, and its args reach the per-request response accumulator.

MEASURED, at the documented host-adapter surface `ssr/get-response`:

  [:rf.server/set-status "not-an-int"]
      dev : fx skipped, (:status (get-response f)) = 200
      prod: (:status (get-response f)) = "not-an-int"   ;; a STRING status
  [:rf.server/set-header {:name "X-Foo"}]           ;; :value missing
      dev : skipped, no X-Foo header
      prod: (:headers …) = [["content-type" …] ["X-Foo" nil]]
  [:rf.server/set-cookie {:name "session"}]         ;; :value missing
      dev : skipped, (:cookies …) empty
      prod: (:cookies …) = [{:name "session"}]
  [:rf.server/safe-redirect {:location "/ok" :status "not-int"}]
      dev : skipped, no :redirect
      prod: (:redirect …) = {:location "/ok" :status "not-int"}

rf2-kjf3m.2 built this boundary for exactly the first case — its own comment reads "the bead's concrete failing scenario: a string status that pre-rf2-kjf3m.2 rode straight onto the wire". The gate says that scenario is still live in a release build.

WHAT SAVES THE WIRE TODAY, AND WHY THAT IS NOT ENOUGH. `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj` is defensive on purpose: `fail-closed-status` coerces a non-integer `:status` to 500, `Location` is `str`-coerced, and header values are string-coerced in `headers/merge-pair-into-header-map`. Its own docstring says "schema validation is optional, so this adapter is the last line". So on a Ring host the wire is well-formed. Three residual problems:

  1. The net is HOST-SPECIFIC. Spec 011 §1070 requires non-Ring adapters to emit the same error categories; nothing requires them to re-implement `fail-closed-status`. A host that trusts the accumulator (the surface `get-response` documents) ships a malformed response.
  2. The 200 -> 500 flip is SILENT in production. `fail-closed-status`'s only signal is `trace/emit! :warning :rf.ssr/ssr-non-integer-status` — the dev bus. On a production JVM the app's 200 becomes a 500 with nothing on either error axis.
  3. `get-response` / `flush-response-result!` are PUBLIC host-adapter surfaces whose contract now differs by posture. A host adapter branching on `(:status response)` or `(:cookies response)` sees a different shape in the build it ships.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD AND NOT rf2-bkvu5 / rf2-mwv4e / rf2-byexd. Those cover ADJACENT surfaces:
  - rf2-bkvu5 (RULED (a), dev-only as designed) is the app-db candidate / flow-output validation — `reg-app-schema`.
  - rf2-mwv4e is the `:rf.schema/at-boundary` interceptor, which DOES run in production and has no surviving diagnostic.
  - rf2-byexd is the DOCS correction for the SSR 400 arm being dev-fed.
This one is the step-5 fx-args hot-path boundary, and its consequence is not observability — it is that a malformed fx RUNS and mutates the response accumulator where the spec says it is skipped.

THE RULING WANTED, one of:

  (a) INTENDED — hot-path fx-args validation is a dev-time developer aid, and the HOST adapter is the production boundary. Then Spec 010 §Per-step recovery row 5 should say the `:skipped` recovery is dev-posture, Spec 011 should state that a host adapter MUST coerce/fail-closed on the accumulator (making ssr-ring's `fail-closed-status` a normative adapter obligation rather than one adapter's belt-and-braces), and the seven semantic assertions in `ssr-server-fx-args-schema-boundary` get a dev arm citing this bead.
  (b) NOT INTENDED for the RESERVED `:rf.server/*` family specifically — the framework's own reserved fxs should guard their own args unconditionally (cheap, closed set, no user schema involved), independent of the optional schemas artefact. Narrow, and it does not change the general step-5 gate.
  (c) NOT INTENDED generally — step-5 validation runs in production. Largest blast radius (a hot-path cost on every fx in every app) and almost certainly wrong under the project's posture.

Do NOT let a worker pick one to make the lane greener. Whatever lands, `fail-closed-status`'s dev-only warning (problem 2 above) probably wants promoting alongside it.

BLOCKS: `re-frame.ssr-end-to-end-test` cannot come off the `scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh` roster until this is ruled. Its OTHER ~100 reds are all mechanical trace-sourcing (see the roster comment for the per-cluster method) and can be done in the same PR once the ruling is in.
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28, dossier review): (b) — the reserved :rf.server/* fx family guards its own args UNCONDITIONALLY; the general Spec 010 step-5 fx-args gate for user fx stays dev-only. Recorded 2026-07-28 07:50 AUSEST; the ai/decisions dossier is deleted per protocol, so this note carries everything.

WHY (b). (a) rejected: it assigns the repair to every adapter AFTER the malformed value has crossed the public get-response boundary, cannot repair correctly (a missing cookie :value is not inferable as "", omit, or bug), leaves the 200->500 rewrite silent, and makes get-response's contract permanently posture-dependent. (c) rejected: a hot-path cost on every fx in every app to protect seven closed framework effects — posture-hostile, and contra Spec 010's own production section. (b) is the rqje9 logic exactly: trust-the-programmer covers USER declarations, not the framework's own wire-adjacent contract. Decisive evidence beyond the dossier (verified in source 2026-07-28): the ownership pattern (b) asks for ALREADY EXISTS in the very file the fix lands in — implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc's validate-header-name!/validate-header-value!/validate-cookie-name!/validate-cookie-attr!/validate-redirect-location! all error/throw-error! unconditionally before swap-response! (the CRLF/token/injection surface). And the repo ruled this bug-class once already: routing scroll.cljc's emit-unsupported-strategy! docstring records rf2-px26m -> rf2-2hkfy — a rejection that fired only where the optional schemas artefact had already caught the value at step-5, fixed with an unconditional handler-owned rejection. (b) is not new policy; it completes an existing one. The Codex second opinion independently reproduced the failure and reached (b) on the same ownership grounds; its implementation contract is ADOPTED (below), including where it differs from the primary dossier's skip-silently sketch.

MECHANISM RULED (Codex contract over the dossier's skip-silently variant): the guards THROW through the canonical re-frame.error/throw-error!, before the first swap-response!. Existing registered-fx containment then supplies the wanted semantics with ZERO new machinery: no accumulator mutation, sibling fx continue, an always-on :rf.error/fx-handler-exception record survives production, and SSR's error projection serves the sanitised 500. Chosen over skip-silently because (1) it matches the sibling guards in the same file for the same fx family, (2) it needs no new skip/record plumbing, and (3) fail-closed is right for a wire-adjacent programmer error that survived to production — a silently-dropped Set-Cookie under a 200 is worse than an honest, observable 500. Taxonomy: malformed framework call (programmer error) -> throw/containment; untrusted-input POLICY decision (safe-redirect target rejection) -> stays the existing non-projecting no-op.

MECHANISM OF THE BUG (for posterity): re-frame.schemas.validate/validate-fx! (implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc, gate at ~989-990) is (if interop/debug-enabled? (run-validation ...) true); interop/debug-enabled? is read once at namespace-load time, so under -Dre-frame.debug=false the Spec 010 §Validation-order step-5 boundary does not run AT ALL and the documented :skipped recovery (§Per-step recovery row 5) never happens — the malformed fx runs and mutates the per-request response accumulator.

MEASURED at ssr/get-response (dev vs real prod gate):
  [:rf.server/set-status "not-an-int"]                   dev: skipped, :status 200 | prod: :status "not-an-int" (string status)
  [:rf.server/set-header {:name "X-Foo"}] (no :value)    dev: skipped              | prod: ["X-Foo" nil] in :headers
  [:rf.server/set-cookie {:name "session"}] (no :value)  dev: skipped              | prod: {:name "session"} in :cookies
  [:rf.server/safe-redirect {:location "/ok" :status "not-int"}]  dev: skipped     | prod: the malformed redirect installs
Independently reproduced (Codex): ssr-server-fx-args-schema-boundary = 18/18 green on :test, 16/18 failures under :test:prod-gate, zero :where :fx-args traces. rf2-kjf3m.2 built the boundary for exactly the string-status case ("pre-fix rode straight onto the wire") — live again in every release build.

THE THREE RESIDUAL PROBLEMS, AND HOW THE RULING RESOLVES EACH:
  1. HOST-SPECIFIC NET — ssr-ring's fail-closed-status/coercions save the wire on Ring only; Spec 011 requires non-Ring adapters to emit the same error categories, not to re-implement coercion. RESOLVED: the handlers own the invariant; every adapter inherits a well-formed accumulator.
  2. SILENT 200->500 FLIP — fail-closed-status's only signal is the dev-bus trace. RESOLVED: promoted to the always-on axis (item 3 below).
  3. POSTURE-DEPENDENT PUBLIC CONTRACT — RESOLVED for the part that matters: get-response never yields a malformed :rf/response shape in ANY build. The recovery PATH still differs and is documented, not hidden: dev-with-schemas = Malli step-5 skip + rich :where :fx-args diagnostic, page renders; prod or schemas-less dev = guard-throw -> containment -> always-on record + sanitised 500.

IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT (this bead IS the implementation owner — it is a [bug]; no split):
  1. Cheap predicate guards (int?, string?, required keys — NO Malli, no schemas-artefact dependency) beside the existing always-on guards in implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc, covering the seven standard fx per their published contracts: status int in 100-599; set-header/append-header explicit string :name and :value; set-cookie explicit string :name/:value plus documented optional attr types; delete-cookie per its published contract; trusted redirect optional string :location (KEEP its intentional no-target behaviour); safe-redirect required string :location; redirect statuses/:relative-only?/:allow per documented types. Args maps stay OPEN (no closed-map rejection of extra keys). Every guard runs before the first swap-response! and throws via error/throw-error!. Safe-redirect POLICY rejections unchanged.
  2. Tighten the status schema in implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/server_fx_schemas.cljc to int-in-100-599 in the same change; guards and registered schemas share a small table-driven acceptance corpus so the canonical cases cannot drift. No :validate-in-production? flag, no generic second validator, no runtime Malli interpretation.
  3. Promote fail-closed-status's silent flip (implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj) to the always-on error axis via the error-emit/emit-error-both! seam (rf2-2hkfy pattern; constant :reason, never the offending value, per the rf2-s3n6h precedent). The Ring materialiser coercions STAY as last-line backstop — explicitly NOT the primary owner. Egress-surface change, same review class as rf2-6jqa8 (rf2-ov56u-style review); may ride the same PR or a sibling; NOT a prerequisite for the guards.
  4. Tests: convert ssr-server-fx-args-schema-boundary into a two-posture semantic contract — assert the bad fx never mutates the raw accumulator and sibling fx still run (both postures); assert posture-specific diagnostics separately (dev: Malli :where :fx-args skip; prod-gate arm: always-on :rf.error/fx-handler-exception + sanitised-500 projection at get-response).
  5. Spec edits, BOTH HOT-ZONE (sequence this PR against any other spec-touching PR):
     - spec/010-Schemas.md §Per-step recovery row 5: qualify the general step-5 fx-args gate (user reg-fx :schema) as dev-posture — the :skipped recovery is a dev-time aid, stated once, loudly, in the bkvu5-(a) pattern; add that the reserved :rf.server/* family independently guards its own args in all builds (handler-owned invariant; richer Malli diagnostic in dev).
     - spec/011-SSR.md: the standard SSR fx handlers preserve :rf/response integrity unconditionally, so every host adapter inherits a well-formed accumulator from get-response; adapter-side coercion is defence-in-depth, NOT a normative obligation (explicitly rejecting option (a)'s "adapter MUST fail-closed" clause).
  6. Fence/sequencing: code surfaces (implementation/ssr/src + test, implementation/ssr-ring/src) are per-feature and parallel-safe; spec/010-Schemas.md + spec/011-SSR.md are hot-zone. implementation/schemas/validate.cljc is NOT touched — the general gate stays dev-only by design.
  7. The mechanical 39-deftest split of ssr-end-to-end-test can ride the same PR: the per-cluster method is recorded verbatim in the scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh roster comment (fx-handler-exception cluster needs NO guard; ditto projector-diagnostic; :rf.warning/* + hydration-mismatch genuinely dev-only; safe-redirect dev arms for the diagnostic only).

UNBLOCK PATH (rf2-lwtlk): once the guards + the 39-deftest mechanical split land, delete the ssr-end-to-end-test roster line in scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh, re-raise RF2_MIN_TESTS, and drop the -n machinery; that completes the lwtlk triage (flows-integration-test's line waits only on the bkvu5 doc pass already in flight).
Audit of merged PR #7204: the guard/schema parity claim is false for presence and cookie-name cases that the shared corpus omits. Malli optional keys reject an explicitly present nil, but the always-on guard uses `some?`/`or`: `{:path nil}` / `{:secure nil}` on set-cookie are treated as absent and the nil-bearing cookie is persisted; redirect `{:status nil}` defaults to 302; safe-redirect `{:status nil :relative-only? nil :allow nil}` likewise passes the guard while the dev schema rejects it. Separately, the cookie schemas and Spec 011 publish string `:name`, while `validate-cookie-name!` intentionally accepts keyword/symbol names and the corpus explicitly excludes that widening "by design". Production therefore still admits accumulator shapes that dev skips, contradicting the bead's central invariant that both enforcements implement one published contract and `get-response` is posture-independent.

Bounded acceptance: decide one public shape for explicit nil and cookie names, then make the Malli schemas, unconditional guards, Spec 011 text and raw accumulator agree. Extend the ONE acceptance corpus with every optional key explicitly nil plus keyword/symbol cookie names; drive each row through both enforcements and add raw-accumulator witnesses under the real production gate. Preserve open-map semantics, the redirect no-target path and existing cookie string tolerances. Do not duplicate the already-closed followups rf2-gblft/rf2-759sp.

title: at-boundary rejections are UNOBSERVABLE in production — the one surviving validation surface has no surviving diagnostic
description:
FOUND BY rf2-eane2 while giving spec/Pattern-FormAction a production-real validation story. This is a FRAMEWORK finding, not a doc bug — filed for an operator look, no remedy picked.

rf2-bkvu5 RULED (a) — reg-app-schema validation is dev-only, and explicitly KEPT ':rf.schema/at-boundary as the production-side ingress surface'. It is the one validation surface the ruling points production users at. But its failure is entirely silent in a production build:

implementation/core/src/re_frame/spec.cljc, validate-at-boundary-interceptor :before (~line 246):
  - the VALIDATION runs (correctly ungated — this is the whole point of the interceptor)
  - on failure it calls (trace/emit-error! :rf.error/schema-validation-failure ...)
  - then (assoc ctx :rf/skip-handler? true)

trace/emit-error! (implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:920) opens with (when interop/debug-enabled? ...). So in production the trace does NOT fire. The source comment at spec.cljc:239-245 already says so verbatim: 'Per Spec 009 SSProduction builds emit-error! itself elides under :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false, so this body only fires under JVM / dev-CLJS with debug-enabled? flipped off.'

CONSEQUENCE: in a release build, a boundary rejection skips the handler and emits NOTHING — no trace, no always-on error-emit record, and (the handler having produced no :db) the always-on :events record reports :outcome :ok. An operator sees a dispatch that succeeded. The untrusted payload was correctly refused and nobody can tell it happened, or how often, or which payloads.

This is the SAME 'quiet by construction' class as rf2-cojqr's :rolled-back — but on the surface the ruling designated as the production answer, which makes it sharper. rf2-bkvu5's decisive reasoning SS3 anticipated exactly this requirement ('A sound always-on design would additionally need a production error channel, privacy/egress rules, and a malformed-validator policy') but raised it as the PRICE OF OPTION (b); nobody checked whether the KEPT surface already pays it. It does not.

NOTE the SSR consequence, which is what surfaced this: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_listener.cljc:305-309 states plainly that the trace-cb listener covers ':rf.error/no-such-handler, :rf.error/no-such-route, :rf.error/schema-validation-failure, :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded. They elide under interop/debug-enabled? = false.' So on an SSR request path an at-boundary rejection projects NO status — the request answers 200 with the page unchanged. That is why spec/Pattern-FormAction (rf2-eane2) routes form-POST validation into the handler body instead of reaching for at-boundary.

SHAPES, none of which is a worker's call:
  (a) Accept. at-boundary is a silent gate; document 'a production boundary rejection is unobservable' at the point of use and let apps that need the signal validate in the handler instead.
  (b) Promote :rf.error/schema-validation-failure with :source :boundary onto the always-on error-emit substrate (the axis already exists — error_projector/emit-always-on-error!). Smallest real fix; needs a privacy/egress position on the payload tags, which already route through the redaction seam.
  (c) Give the boundary interceptor a recovery richer than skip-handler so a request-answering ingress can respond.

CITE: rf2-bkvu5 (ruling), rf2-eane2 (surfacing bead), rf2-cojqr (sibling quiet-metric defect).
notes:
IMPLEMENTED by PR #7203 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7203 (branch worker/rejected-outcome-mwv4e). Both halves landed exactly as ruled; no deviation from the adopted record spec or the outcome verdict.

SHAPE AS BUILT. One internal marker `:rf/boundary-rejected?`, stamped by BOTH enforcement routes — the production interceptor (spec.cljc) alongside `:rf/skip-handler?`, and `run-chain` (router.cljc) when step-1 refused an event whose handler-meta references `:rf.schema/at-boundary` (new public predicate `events/boundary-guarded-handler?`; evaluated ONLY on the refusal path, so the hot path keeps its single `if`). The router tail reads the marker ONCE: `emit-boundary-rejection-record!` fans the structural record through `error-emit/dispatch-error-record!`, and `commit-and-flow!`'s `:else` arm selects `:rejected` as the LOWEST-priority discriminator (every higher outcome has already returned). Emit keys off the rejection FACT, not the outcome, so a refusal whose unwind then threw reports both. Record shape adopted VERBATIM from the ruling; 9 keys.

NARROWNESS, decided and pinned: an UNGUARDED handler's dev-only `:schema` refusal does NOT take the marker. That surface has no production counterpart (rf2-bkvu5), so marking it would invent a production signal that cannot exist. Pinned by `unguarded-schema-refusal-is-not-a-boundary-rejection-in-every-posture`.

PROOF under the REAL gate (`clojure -M:test:prod-gate`, not with-redefs). Target ns 6 tests / 21 assertions -> 11 / 42, all green in BOTH postures. Mutation-proved separately: neutering the fan-out gives 11 failures across the two record deftests; reverting the outcome to `:ok` gives exactly 1 failure, precisely isolated on the outcome deftest. Gates all exit 0 — core dev 2168/10766, core prod-gate 1201/5551 (102 ns under -Dre-frame.debug=false), schemas 363/19188, conformance trio 29/168, routing at-boundary consumer 13/166. The core lane was run in both postures because the egress-chokepoint source-scan reddens core on a new fan-out caller; `re-frame.router` was ALREADY an allow-list member (depth-halt record) so the caller set is unchanged, and its written rationale is extended to cover the second record.

EGRESS REVIEW, per the paired obligation with rf2-6jqa8: no scrub applies because no attacker-controlled field is carried. Deliberately omitted, each named in the allow-list rationale and asserted ABSENT by key in the test: the event vector, `:value`, `:received`, `:explain`, the schema form, and `:reason` — the last because the dev trace's `:reason` interpolates the offending value (the ssr/hydrate prose hazard). A sentinel-secret payload is additionally asserted absent from `(pr-str record)` by any route. Key set pinned CLOSED.

CONSUMERS OF `:outcome` — audited, none switches on a closed vocabulary: event-emit listeners see it verbatim; `observability/route-handled-event!` passes it to `:status`; `projection/project-handled-event` passes `:status` through as a summary key under every egress profile; SSR's generic tag-lift means the default projector's existing `:where :event` arm answers 400 with NO ssr code change. The epoch `:outcome` (`:ok`/`:halted-*`) and the Xray optimistic-mutation `:outcome` are separate vocabularies on separate records, untouched.

THE :advanced PIN INVERTED HALF-WAY, and the half that stayed is the right one. schemas_boundary_prod_test's `(empty? @traces)` does NOT invert — that recorder reads the `:trace` stream, which is still gated, and that silence is exactly the rejected value + explain that must not egress. Kept, with corrected prose, and given a counterpart deftest asserting the always-on record survives the same closure-define. Browser `:advanced` run deferred to CI.

OUT OF FENCE, filed rather than edited: rf2-lvsen (spec/009 Channel cell + the always-on-categories literal, MANDATORY same-PR co-edit, plus the four sites resting on the removed premise; fold or sequence rf2-05hy2), rf2-ovjty (`:rejected` on the event-outcome contract in spec/009 + API.md), rf2-qwydk (SSR: the stale error_listener bus comment, which its own docstring calls authoritative, plus the missing 400 witness under the gate and a dev/prod symmetry measurement), rf2-5ny45 (docs re-arm — report-errors-in-production.md's warning box is now actively WRONG and advises against the surface that works; coordinate rf2-mk8up).

Both ruled halves landed: the always-on STRUCTURAL-ONLY :rf.error/schema-validation-failure record (:source :boundary, 9-key closed set, adopted verbatim) and the new public :outcome :rejected. Fail-closed skip and full interceptor unwind preserved; no recovery protocol. One internal :rf/boundary-rejected? marker, stamped by both enforcement routes, read once in the router tail. Proof under the REAL gate: target ns 6 tests/21 assertions -> 11/42, green in both postures; mutation-proved both halves (fan-out neutered = 11 failures across the two record deftests; outcome reverted to :ok = exactly 1 failure, isolated). Gates 0: core dev 2168/10766, core prod-gate 1201/5551 across 102 ns, schemas 363/19188, conformance trio 29/168, routing consumer 13/166. Egress: no scrub applies — every attacker-controlled slot omitted outright, absence asserted by key plus a sentinel-secret pr-str check. Out of fence, filed: rf2-lvsen (spec/009 Channel + always-on-categories co-edit), rf2-ovjty (:rejected on the outcome contract), rf2-qwydk (SSR comment + 400 witness), rf2-5ny45 (docs re-arm).

title: Ship the checked {:reactive false} shell-free opt-out — the spike is answered; close the three event-site forks
description:
Ship the CHECKED {:reactive false} opt-out. Ruled on rf2-h4j7k (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-27); gated on rf2-3slzz, which is now ANSWERED — see the spike verdict below, the findings doc ai/findings/2026-07-27.reactive-false-runtime-check-totality.md, and the three probe suites on PR #7171.

=== THE SPIKE'S VERDICT, WHICH THIS BEAD IMPLEMENTS ===
TOTAL on the reactive-READ half. NOT total on the EVENT half as the code stands — but the gap is three (some? cand) forks, not an analysis problem, and closing it needs no static analysis at all. Nothing escapes OBSERVATION; what escapes today is only the RESPONSE at three positions that observe the situation and answer nil or a raw function instead of raising.

Load-bearing corollary the spike proved, which this bead should not re-litigate: the compiler's static proof is ALREADY defeatable. A {:compiled true} view whose body reads through an ordinary two-hop helper analyzes to :view-cell :elided and mounts shell-free; it does not go silently stale — it fails loud at the read via cell/observe!'s candidate check, in development AND in an :advanced production bundle. The runtime check this bead ships is therefore not a downgrade from proof; it is the net that was already doing the catching.

=== CONTRACT ===
"This boundary is SHELL-FREE: its own render performs no v/sub read and produces no committed event site. It may freely mount reactive child views; those children own their own shells."
Shell-free, not merely sub-free — a ViewCell owns the selected render's committed event sites and frame binding as well as its dependencies, and the elision oracle already keeps the cell for either live site family. This is the EXACT eligibility the compiler used; no new optimization category is invented.

=== IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE (from the spike; do not grow a policy framework around it) ===
One dynamically scoped assertion context, one stable diagnostic.

  ;; re-frame.freehand.cell
  (def ^:dynamic ^:private *shell-free* nil)          ; the declaring view id, or nil
  (defn with-shell-free-assertion [view-id thunk]
    (binding [*render* nil, *shell-free* view-id] (thunk)))
  (defn shell-free-view [] *shell-free*)

- MASKING IS THE (*render* nil) BINDING, and it is why the context must live in cell.cljc: *render* is ^:private there and nothing outside can mask it. Masking is load-bearing, not belt-and-braces — the spike pins, as a passing witness, that on the JVM structural host (and inside t/with-render, and under v/render-static) a nested body runs INLINE in the caller's dynamic extent, so a shell-free boundary rendered there would find the OUTER candidate and silently DONATE its read to the outer boundary. A violation that passes a structural test and only fails in a browser is exactly what this flag must not permit.
- READS NEED NO NEW CALL SITE. observe!'s existing nil-candidate branch forks on *shell-free*: set -> the opt-out diagnostic naming the view id and the :sub capability; unset -> today's :rf.error/view-read-outside-render, unchanged.
- EVENT POSITIONS ARE EXACTLY THREE FORKS, enumerated and verified: react.cljs:263 (native element handler — v/spread-safe's put-caller! fold routes through it too), react.cljs:965 (declared-host callback), reactive.cljc:100 (the compiled event site). Each consults shell-free-view in its existing else branch: set -> raise the same diagnostic naming the offending event capability; unset -> degrade exactly as today, so fr/element's documented "no boundary above this call" behaviour is untouched.
- CLASSIFY WITH events/event-plan BEFORE RAISING. nil is an empty position and legal. :render-fn and :raw-fn are explicitly OUTSIDE the committed-proxy scheme (events/site hands the function back and records nothing), so they need no cell and may pass through. Every other role — :event-vector, :event-options, :event, :handler, :bare-fn — requires a committed site and must raise.
- DO NOT BIND frame/*current-frame*. There is no candidate and therefore no frame to bind, and ambient resolution keeps working anyway (see the contract notes below).
- HOT RELOAD IS ONE LINE. react.cljs/shell-signature is [lowering (:view-cell (descriptor/manifest view))], and a signature change mints a new component type — React's own instruction to remount cleanly. Interpreted views all sign [:interpreted nil] today (pinned by the spike probe); route the flag through the manifest (or an equivalent signature axis) and acceptance 5 falls out.

=== WHAT TODAY'S THREE EVENT FORKS ACTUALLY DO SHELL-FREE (the spike measured each on a real mount, each against a shell-owning control arm) ===
  [:spike/pressed] declarative vector    -> prop NEVER WRITTEN. Element mounts, click does nothing, nothing throws.
  {:event [...] :once true} options map  -> same silent drop (same fork).
  (v/event ...) / (v/handler ...)        -> silent drop. handler-proxy's fallback is (when (fn? raw) raw), and a Callback deftype is DELIBERATELY not fn? in CLJS.
  a bare (fn [e] ...)                    -> PASSES THROUGH AND FIRES, with no frame binding, no :once, no retirement at unmount, no controlled-input door, no stable identity — and no signal at all. The most dangerous of the shapes for an OPT-IN, because it looks like success.
  v/defhost :onSelect (v/event ...)      -> handed over RAW via events/callback-fn; the foreign component calls the carrier's fn, receives an intent vector, and discards it.

=== CONTRACT DETAILS THE WORDING MUST CARRY ===
1. rf/subscribe-once AMBIENT STAYS LEGAL, and the reason had to be checked rather than assumed. The shell's with-capture binds frame/*current-frame* and a shell-free boundary gets none — but frame/resolve-current-frame has a SECOND tier: it reads the React frame context through the :adapter/current-frame hook, available to any component under the provider v/mount installs. The spike mounts an elided boundary performing an ambient subscribe-once and reads the resolved value back off the DOM. The boundary does NOT acquire a useContext subscription (it calls no hook), but it performs no reactive read either, and its reactive children own their own useContext.
2. IN PRODUCTION THE REFUSAL IS NOT CATCHABLE BY THE MOUNT CALLER. React 19 routes an uncaught render error to the root's onUncaughtError and does not rethrow — not even inside flushSync (react/act is a development-only export and answers "act is not a function" under :advanced). The read IS refused, with its stable id, and NOTHING is committed; the failure arrives as an uncaught page error (window error event, console, any installed onerror reporter). One sentence in the contract.
3. SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY. Total over Freehand's SUPPORTED reactive semantics. rf/subscribe held directly, raw atom derefs and other private state channels were never ViewCell-tracked and remain the programmer's responsibility — the same scope the compiled tier's elision always had.

=== SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT ===
implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/cell.cljc is a SERIALIZED lane — rf2-lbs3y (P0) and rf2-9f1s7 (queued cleanup) each hold it, one worker at a time. This bead MUST touch it (the masking binding), so it queues behind them rather than running in parallel.

=== ACCEPTANCE (the ruling's five; the spike's evidence already stands for 2 and 4, and half of 1) ===
1. A shell-free view mounts with no ViewCell and no shell React hooks, and the flagged-vs-ordinary INTERPRETED ablation confirms the retained-heap and mount benefit (6.256x retained heap / 1.712x wall clock per boundary, 2,348 B standing heap each). The no-ViewCell half is already pinned for the compiled elided path; the interpreted ablation pair does not exist yet and is this bead's to build.
2. Inline, helper-mediated and later-branch v/sub violations fail before observation or ownership, in development AND production builds. ALREADY PROVEN for the no-candidate configuration by reactive-false-totality-jvm-test (both -Dre-frame.debug postures) and reactive-false-check-elision-prod-test (:advanced + goog.DEBUG=false). What this bead adds is the same under the FLAG's own diagnostic, plus the MASKED case (a shell-free child inside an open outer capture), which nothing proves today.
3. Native event intent, v/event / v/handler, bare handler functions and declared-host callback positions all FAIL rather than disappear or lose committed-site semantics. This is the bead's real work — see the table above. Each shape already has a shell-owning control arm in reactive-false-shell-free-dom-cljs-test, so each row flips from "silently dropped" to "raises" while the control stays green.
4. A reactive child mounted by a shell-free parent stays fully reactive. ALREADY PROVEN on a real mount.
5. Adding or removing the flag changes the hot-reload shell signature and causes ONE clean remount; React must never reuse hook state across the transition.

EVIDENCE: ai/findings/2026-07-27.reactive-false-runtime-check-totality.md; PR #7171 (three probe suites, kept); rf2-h4j7k RULING notes; rf2-3slzz.
UNBLOCKS: rf2-h4j7k closes when this ships and its elision value is verified, which releases rf2-zw1oo's Option C compiler deletion.

title: Generator template emits :mvn/version coords for Xray and Story, which a framework v* tag does not publish
description:
Found while preparing rf2-snjn5's install-docs flip. NOT fixed there — that PR is fenced out of tools/** and is documentation-only.

tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/deps.edn:32 emits

    day8/re-frame2-xray {:mvn/version "{{rf2-version}}"}

and deps_with_ssr.edn:49 and deps_with_story.edn:38 do the same, with deps_with_story.edn:39 additionally emitting day8/re-frame2-story {:mvn/version "{{rf2-version}}"}.

THE PROBLEM: {{rf2-version}} is the repo-root VERSION, i.e. the FRAMEWORK version. But a v* tag publishes thirteen framework coordinates and NO tools (docs/release-process.md §The tools tier — Xray ships on xray-v*, Story on story-v*, machines-viz on machines-viz-v*). No xray-v* or story-v* tag has ever been cut, and release-xray.yml currently REFUSES its own deploy pending the open Freehand decision (release-xray.yml:40-55, rf2-5dut1).

So the moment v0.0.1.alpha publishes the framework,  emits a deps.edn whose framework coords resolve and whose day-one Xray coord 404s. Before the tag the whole file was equally unresolvable, so the mismatch was invisible; the tag is what makes it a real, reachable failure — a generated project that will not build on its first .

This is exactly the asymmetry rf2-snjn5 documented on the manual path: skills/re-frame2-setup/references/deps-versions.md now teaches a deliberately MIXED greenfield deps.edn — three :mvn/version framework coords beside one :git/sha Xray coord — with the reason stated inline. The template contradicts the skill it is supposed to match (deps-versions.md §Greenfield day-one shape cites the template as the source of truth for that shape).

OPTIONS: (a) template emits the git/local-root coord for -xray and -story until their tags ship, matching the skill; (b) cut xray-v* and story-v* in the same cut session so the template's :mvn/version coords are true — blocked on rf2-5dut1 and the Freehand decision for Xray; (c) template drops Xray from the day-one emission, which contradicts the documented day-one shape.

RECOMMEND (a) — it is the only option available without an operator decision, and it makes the template agree with the skill.

URGENCY: this should be settled in or immediately after the alpha cut session (rf2-vxgfnd.99), because the generator is a public front door and it starts emitting a broken file the moment the framework publishes.

Before the tag the whole file was equally unresolvable, so the mismatch was invisible; the tag is what makes it a real, reachable failure — a generated project that will not build on its first `npx shadow-cljs watch app`.

title: spec/Pattern-FormAction builds a PRODUCTION SSR form-POST validation path on a dev-only check
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-bkvu5's doc pass. spec/ pattern documents were outside that bead's fence (hot-zone, and the ruling authorised only the Spec 010 statement plus the EP-0025 qualification), so they are filed here rather than fixed.

THE SHARPEST SITE. spec/Pattern-FormAction.md describes the SSR progressive-enhancement form-POST path — a PRODUCTION server request path — and rests its validation story on app-db / event schema validation, which is elided from production builds (rf2-bkvu5 ruling, Spec 010 §Production builds).

  - spec/Pattern-FormAction.md:122 — 'If form-params fails the AddToCartForm schema, the framework structured-error trace fires (:rf.error/schema-validation-failure); the error projector maps it to a 400 response with the public-error shape. THE APP DOES NOT WRITE A SEPARATE VALIDATION BRANCH.' That last sentence is the load-bearing wrong advice: in a production server build the trace never fires, so the 400 never happens and the malformed form-params flow onward.
  - spec/Pattern-FormAction.md:21 step 4 — 'The domain event handler validates the form-params against the registered schema for the form. On schema failure, the handler writes structured errors into the form slice :errors map; the standard SSR render reads the slice and emits the form again with errors.' Same production path, same gap.

WHAT THE FIX PROBABLY IS (needs a ruling, do not let a worker pick): either the pattern routes its form-params check through :rf.schema/at-boundary (which SURVIVES the gate and is the designed production ingress surface), or the pattern states plainly that a server deployment must write the validation branch in the handler. The former is more likely right — a form POST is untrusted ingress, which is exactly at-boundary's job — but it changes the pattern's normative shape and Pattern-FormAction is hot-zone.

LOWER-PRIORITY SIBLINGS in the same class (schema-as-guarantee with no dev-only note), same sweep:
  - spec/Pattern-RemoteData.md:277 — 'Slice is reg-app-schema-bound (dynamic hosts) or typed (static hosts).' A conformance criterion equating a dev-only assertion with a static host's TYPE SYSTEM. The equivalence is false in production.
  - spec/Pattern-Forms.md:54-55 — two reg-app-schema calls introduced as 'Both are registered' with no timing note.
  - spec/Construction-Prompts.md:638 — a REQUIRED per-feature artefact row, '(rf/reg-app-schema [:feature] FeatureSchema)', no caveat.
  - spec/Conventions.md:323 — 'reg-app-schema | the registrar name itself (THE VALIDATOR *IS* THE REGISTRATION)'. That parenthetical is precisely the conflation the elision breaks: the registration happens in every build, the validation does not.

CITE: rf2-bkvu5 (RULED option (a) — dev-only as designed). Spec 010 §Production builds now carries the normative statement and both validation tables mark the reg-app-schema rows dev-only.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7172 (2026-07-28). The new explicit m/explain branch is the correct production-real validation seam, but the worked no-JS failure path is incomplete. On a server POST, form-params comes from the request while the rendered fields come from [:cart :add-form :draft]. The failure arm calls write-form-errors, whose shown implementation updates only :status, :errors, and :submit-attempted?; it never copies the submitted :item-id/:quantity into :draft. The following prose nevertheless promises that the user sees their bad input and no information is lost. With JS disabled, the re-render therefore shows the pre-submit/empty draft instead. Bounded repair: have the failure arm retain only the safe editable fields (not :csrf-token or other secret carriers) in the form draft before rendering errors, and make the prose/example agree. No framework form subsystem.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7232 (2026-08-01) — REOPENED exact owner; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS: the docs-only gates prove links and vocabulary, but no executable witness checks that the canonical no-JS POST shape and hydrated-client dispatch shape are both accepted by the shared handler/schema. That missing cross-platform shape proof hides a contradiction in the copyable example.

CORRECTNESS: `AddToCartForm` requires `:item-id`, `:quantity`, and `:csrf-token`. The hydrated `:on-submit` dispatches `(assoc draft :item-id item-id)` and deliberately does not add the token; the handler then unconditionally runs `(m/explain AddToCartForm form-params)`. The client path therefore always takes the validation-failure arm in production and never navigates. In development, the event's `:schema [:cat ... AddToCartForm]` rejects the same client event before the handler. The example also registers `[:cart :add-form :draft]` against `AddToCartForm` while repeatedly ruling that the secret token must never live in that draft, so its own canonical draft is invalid by construction.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / BOUNDED REPAIR: preserve the strong server-only CSRF boundary and do not put the token into app-db or a client event merely to satisfy one schema. Split the editable field schema from the POST envelope (or otherwise select the schema by the already-computed platform boundary): validate the field schema on both hosts, require/check the token only for the server POST, type the draft with the field schema, and make the dev event tripwire accept exactly the two intended shapes. Add one small executable or mechanically checked witness for a valid client draft and a valid server POST. No framework form subsystem.
COMPLETE — PR #7406 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7406), branch worker/validscope-bl8k7, 2026-08-03. NOT MERGED. Rode one worker with rf2-bl8k7 + rf2-096js because two of the three edit spec/Pattern-FormAction.md. Addresses the 2026-08-01 audit comment on merged PR #7347 (the transport seam), which was this bead's live obligation.

THE AUDIT WAS RIGHT. The page required the host adapter to parse the request body and then defined no keywordisation or coercion contract over what it produced. HTML form encoding has no types and no keywords, so a real parsed body is {"quantity" "2"} — string keys, string VALUES. Handed straight to the documented handler a CORRECT submission fails: the CSRF compare looks up :csrf-token in a string-keyed map and finds nothing, so a valid token 403s; and even with keywordised keys "2" is not an :int and takes the 400 arm. The suite hid this by hard-coding already-normalised values as "the canonical body a browser submits".

THE OWNER IS :rf/server-init, and the reason is structural rather than stylistic. It is the one place the wire crosses into the domain, and normalising THERE is what makes the pattern's central claim true — below that dispatch the server's args and the hydrated client's args are the same shape, so "one handler, both platforms" is a fact rather than an aspiration. A handler that normalised its own input would first have to work out which platform called it, which is exactly the knowledge this pattern spends its effort not needing. That reasoning is on the page, not just in this note, and the converse is stated as an anti-pattern ("Normalising inside the action handler").

SHIPPED (spec/Pattern-FormAction.md):

- The section is renamed to "§:rf/server-init routes GET vs POST, and owns normalisation". The old anchor had NO inbound links — verified by grep before renaming.
- Copyable code now on the page. route->action is a single table carrying the action event AND its args schema, so a form cannot acquire an event without also declaring the shape its wire body decodes to. decode-form-params keywordises the keys and lets the SCHEMA drive the value coercion via mt/string-transformer.
- VERIFIED FROM SOURCE before writing it, not assumed: malli's string-transformer does decode [:and :int [:>= 1] [:<= 99]] from "2" to 2, and does leave "abc" untouched. Probed against the real ssr :test classpath.
- The seam NEVER throws and never rejects. A value the transformer cannot decode reaches the handler unchanged and fails the handler's own arm, so malformed input still takes the documented 400-with-repopulated-draft path. That is stated on the page, because the tempting alternative — reject at the seam — would quietly relocate the 400 away from the arm this bead exists to make load-bearing.
- Host variance addressed without hedging: a host that already keywordises (Ring's wrap-keyword-params) makes update-keys a no-op, one that also coerces makes the transformer one, and neither changes which layer is RESPONSIBLE.
- Also: shape steps 2-3; the Server-vs-client table (new Normalisation row, 3 cells like its siblings, checked by hand); the §Composition with :rf.server/request note (the declared-coeffect route hands the handler the RAW body, so a handler taking it owns the decode and owns keeping its client arm out of it); the §CSRF sentence about what the token travels through; two anti-patterns ("Assuming :form-params arrives as domain data", "Normalising inside the action handler"); two conformance criteria.

ACCEPTANCE (implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_doc_example_form_action_test.clj). Starts from a literal csrf-token=tok-abc&item-id=sku-1&quantity=2, parses it the way Ring's wrap-params does, and drives it through the page's OWN EXTRACTED seam — route->action and decode-form-params are read out of the markdown fence at run time like every other schema and helper in that suite, so a page that drops either goes red naming the anchor. Five new deftests:

- the parsed body is asserted to be strings keyed by strings, and to carry exactly the input names the view fence renders (the tie to the HTML is kept);
- the seam produces the handler's shape, and the route table resolves to both the event and the schema;
- a valid no-JS request reaches 303 from the wire bytes;
- THE COUNTER-PROOF: the UNDECODED parsed body is asserted to 403, so the seam is provably load-bearing and cannot be quietly dropped without going red. A page that deletes the normalisation step would otherwise turn the suite green in the worst possible way;
- quantity=0 reaches the 400 path with the coerced value back in :draft and no token beside it, and quantity=abc passes THROUGH the seam rather than exploding at it, landing on the same safe 400.

server-post is now a delay derived from the wire body rather than a hand-written map, so every PRE-EXISTING assertion in the suite is now downstream of the transport seam too. 16 tests / 50 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors.

PRESERVED: the typed hydrated-client path and both limbs of the fail-closed CSRF arm, unchanged.

RESIDUE FILED, NOT FIXED — rf2-1iclq (P1, bug): skills/re-frame2/patterns/form-action.md is three corrections behind this page, INCLUDING the fail-OPEN CSRF compare (not= alone) that this very page lists as an anti-pattern, plus the single-schema shape the #7232 audit rejected. Out of this worker's fence and wider than this cluster. scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py exits 0 over that drift, which is itself worth a look.

Gates foreground, unpiped, worktree-local logs: mkdocs --strict 0 (python -m mkdocs; bare mkdocs still absent from PATH), check_doc_slugs.py 0, test-fast-pr.sh 0 ("PASS fast PR spine"), the ssr acceptance namespace 0, check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py 0. Fresh worktree had no node_modules — the first spine run failed at CLJS node integration on a missing shadow-cljs; ran a real npm ci in implementation/, created NO junction, mayor node_modules never touched, then re-ran the spine from the top.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #7406 — REOPENED (completeness / correctness / implementation quality).

The new POST normalisation seam blanket-keywordises every untrusted form key: `(update-keys form-params keyword)`. That includes unknown attacker-chosen parameter names, not just `AddToCartSubmission`'s declared vocabulary. On long-running JVM SSR, each novel name is interned into the process-global, never-GC'd keyword table. This is the exact keyword-interning DoS the repo's security contract forbids: `spec/Security.md` requires bounded interning for structured input, and `spec/012-Routing.md` closes the analogous query path by promoting only schema-declared keys while leaving undeclared keys as strings. The page also says an unknown form key is “passed through untouched”; turning it into a keyword is observably not untouched.

The acceptance suite exercises only the three known static names, so it cannot detect this. An attacker can send a fresh unknown field name on every POST while all 16 tests remain green.

Bounded repair: keep `:rf/server-init` as the single seam and keep schema-driven value coercion, but promote only names from the route action's declared schema (or an equally explicit finite wire-name map); leave unknown keys as strings. A per-request cap is the fallback only if the implementation genuinely must keywordise arbitrary keys. Add one adversarial witness with a fresh undeclared string key: declared fields become their known keywords and coerce, while the undeclared key remains a string and no unbounded keyword universe is opened. No general form framework or second schema is requested.
close_reason: MAYOR RE-CLOSE 2026-08-03. This bead was closed when its PR merged, then REVERTED TO OPEN by a tracker-state rollback (the same class as rf2-rjqtj / rf2-51uz1 — five early closes reverted while every later one held). Re-verified before re-closing: PR #7406 is MERGED and 3 commit(s) naming this bead are on origin/main. No work is outstanding from the original scope; if an audit later reopens it for a NEW obligation, that reopen is legitimate and separate from this rollback.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: Audit of merged PR #7347: the new test calls its server-post the canonical body a browser submits, but hard-codes {:item-id "sku-1" :quantity 2 :csrf-token "tok-abc"}. HTML form encoding submits names and values as strings; the pattern only requires the host to parse form-urlencoded or multipart and defines no keywordization or type-coercion contract. A normal parsed body therefore has string keys and "2" for quantity. With string keys the handler sees no token or fields and returns 403; even if the host keywordizes keys, AddToCartFields requires an integer so "2" takes the 400 arm. The test derives only the input-name set and silently supplies the normalized values whose missing boundary is the defect, so its claimed browser-to-handler proof is vacuous at the transport seam. Bounded acceptance: state one normalization owner explicitly and include the copyable normalization code in the page; drive the extracted example from a representative application/x-www-form-urlencoded body or its actual string-key/string-value parsed shape, then prove the valid no-JS request reaches 303 while malformed values still reach the safe 400 draft path. Preserve the typed hydrated-client path and the fail-closed CSRF arm.

title: Skills corpus prescribes reg-app-schema as a trust-boundary guard without the dev-only caveat
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-bkvu5's doc pass (the RULED dev-only documentation sweep). rf2-bkvu5 fixed the docstrings, Spec 010, the migration guide, docs/api and the EP-0025 qualification; the skills/ corpus was OUTSIDE that bead's fence and is the largest remaining always-on-sounding surface.

THE PROBLEM. The agent-facing skill corpus prescribes reg-app-schema as THE tool for trust boundaries, with no mention that it is compile-time elided from production builds. An agent following this guidance will write an app whose 'boundary validation' does not exist in the deployed bundle.

SITES (all verified, line numbers as of 2026-07-27):
  - skills/re-frame2/SKILL.md:74 — Cardinal Rule 4: '**Schemas at boundaries.** reg-app-schema for paths that cross trust boundaries (HTTP payloads, persisted state, snapshot restores).' No elision caveat. This is the load-bearing one: it is a CARDINAL RULE.
  - skills/re-frame2/patterns/remote-data.md:17 — 'reg-app-schema — schema-binds the slice path so the slice shape IS ENFORCED AT BOUNDARIES (per cardinal rule 4).' 'Enforced' is exactly the reading the elision destroys.
  - skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:15 — the two-word gloss for rf/reg-app-schema is 'boundary validation'.
  - skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/schemas.md:36,84,92 — the PRIMARY agent-facing schema reference. Its dev/prod paragraph at :49 covers ONLY the handler :schema; the app-db surface is taught with no elision note anywhere on the page.
  - skills/re-frame2/decision-trees/slice-or-machine.md:98 — 'Register a schema for the slice via reg-app-schema only if the slice crosses a trust boundary.'
  - skills/re-frame2/patterns/forms.md:15,94-95 — no dev/prod word anywhere in the file.

THE MODEL TEXT ALREADY EXISTS IN-REPO: skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md:30 gets it right — 'Because :schema and reg-app-schema are dev-elided, a handler carrying only those is validated in dev but unvalidated in the deployed bundle' — and :63 annotates the call site '(rf/reg-app-schema [:article :data] Article) ;; dev-only'. Mirror that voice.

THE RULING TO CITE: rf2-bkvu5, option (a) — app-db candidate validation is a DEVELOPMENT-TIME assertion as designed; production trusts the programmer. The production-side surfaces that DO survive the gate are the :rf.schema/at-boundary event interceptor and the :schemas/validate-with-registered-fn seam. Cardinal Rule 4 should point at :rf.schema/at-boundary for the genuine trust-boundary case and keep reg-app-schema as the dev tripwire.

NOTE: skills/ has a skill-drift CI gate; check whether these files are digest-pinned before editing.
close_reason: Closed

title: SSR prod 404: promote the URL-driven route-miss emit to the always-on error axis + :kind-gate the default projector (ruling rf2-rqje9)
description:
IMPLEMENTATION of the rf2-rqje9 ruling (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-27; ruling recorded on rf2-rqje9). A production SSR route miss must return 404. The fix is NARROW: promote the ONE dev-only emit site onto the existing always-on error axis, and :kind-gate the default projector's 404 arm. Do NOT bulk-promote other categories; do NOT build a route-slice-to-status pipeline.

WHY (one paragraph). Under `-Dre-frame.debug=false` an SSR request for a URL matching no route renders the app's not-found markup and answers HTTP 200. RFC 9110 defines 200 as success and 404 as no-current-representation; Google treats a 200'd not-found page as a "soft 404" and excludes it from Search. Spec 009's error catalogue ALREADY classifies `:rf.error/no-such-handler` as ALWAYS-ON with a mandatory `:kind` tag that includes `:kind :route` for `:rf.route/handle-url-change` — so this is conforming the implementation to the spec's existing classification, not new architecture.

THE PRODUCTION HOLE (verified 2026-07-27 against source):
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/url_change.cljc` (`url-change-fx`, the `[:emit-error :rf.error/no-such-handler ...]` intent at ~lines 331-347): computes the route miss once, commits the durable `:rf.route/not-found` slice, builds tags `{:url (redacted) :kind :route :recovery :replaced-with-default (+ :frame, :reason)}` via `egress/redact-url-tag` — but sends the fact ONLY through `plan/emit-intents!` -> `plan.cljc` line ~246 -> `trace/emit-error!`, which is gated on `interop/debug-enabled?` (trace.cljc ~line 920). Under the prod gate nothing buffers, `flush-response!` has nothing to project, `:status` stays 200.
- Contrast the EVENT-kind miss: `re-frame.router.diagnostics/handle-no-handler!` already fans BOTH channels via the `:error-emit/emit-error-both` late-bind hook (always-on `dispatch-on-error!` + dev trace). That is the shape to match.

THE FIX (two parts):
1. At the route-miss source in `url-change-fx`, emit ONE tight always-on record alongside the existing dev trace (the `emit-error-both!` / `dispatch-error-record!` substrate — routing sits above core's require graph, so reach it via the late-bind hook like router.diagnostics does). Production record carries: category `:rf.error/no-such-handler`, `:kind :route`, exact server `:frame`, `:time`, `:recovery :replaced-with-default`, the already-redacted `:url` and structured `:reason` — NEVER the raw query/fragment carrier values or any app-db slice. The redaction (`egress/redact-url-tag`, EP-0015 fail-closed) is already applied at this site; the egress review verifies that invariant rather than reopening the architecture. The SSR always-on listener (`re-frame.ssr.error-listener/error-emit-projection-listener`) already consumes `:rf.error/*` records generically and synthesises the projector envelope — no listener change expected.
2. ADJACENT CORRECTION (same PR): `default-error-projector-fn` in `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_projector.cljc` (~lines 163-169) maps EVERY `:rf.error/no-such-handler` to 404 with no `:kind` gate. Once always-on producers reach the projector in production, an ordinary unregistered EVENT handler (`:kind :event` — a server defect) would answer 404. Gate the 404 arm on `(= :route (get-in trace-event [:tags :kind]))`; `:kind :event` / `:kind :frame` fall through to the locked generic-500. This amends Spec 011 §Default projector (spec/011-SSR.md — HOT-ZONE file, sequence accordingly) and the tests that project a kind-less `{:operation :rf.error/no-such-handler :tags {}}` expecting 404 (ssr_end_to_end_test.clj ~lines 846, 912-914, 941, 964-971). Leave the `:rf.error/no-such-route` -> 404 arm alone (that category is the dev-only `route-url` caller-misuse throw, Spec 009 catalogues it diagnostic; it cannot reach the projector in production).

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE (ruled, do not do):
- `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` stays dev-only: boundary validation ITSELF is production-elided (Spec 010 §Production builds — `validate-*!` returns true unconditionally under the gate), so there is no production reject to stamp 400 for. Prod-gate assertions on it are dev-posture -> posture-split under rf2-lwtlk. The flow-output variant has its own ruling bead (rf2-bkvu5).
- `:rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded` is ALREADY always-on (rf2-fcbrjo; `router/handle-depth-exceeded!` calls `error-emit/dispatch-error-record!`, router.cljc ~line 3059) and projects 500 via the default arm. Residual reds asserting its dev-trace tags are spelling -> rf2-lwtlk.
- No status derivation from `[:rf.runtime/routing :current]` at the SSR host boundary (rejected option (c)): it would make every host adapter reimplement routing policy, bypass the configured `reg-error-projector` seam (custom projectors, redirect precedence, per-frame attribution, streaming), and conflate the durable navigation slice with the per-request HTTP decision.

DOC CORRECTIONS (same PR): the two-listener comment block in `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc` (~lines 372-396) and the matching docstring in `error_listener.cljc` (~lines 297-316) are STALE — they claim `no-such-handler` / `drain-depth-exceeded` have "no always-on emission path", which predates the event-kind and drain-depth promotions. Rewrite to state the real coverage after this fix. Keep Spec 009's catalogue row for `:rf.error/no-such-handler` in sync (it already says always-on + `:kind :route`; add the projector's `:kind` gate to the Spec 011 cross-ref).
