title: SPIKE: is the {:reactive false} runtime check TOTAL? Gate before the flag ships and rf2-zw1oo deletes the compiler
description:
SPIKE, one dispatch, small. This is the gate rf2-h4j7k's ruling (ADOPT the checked {:reactive false} opt-out, delegated by Mike 2026-07-27) placed before the flag ships and before rf2-zw1oo's Option C compiler deletion executes. DO NOT implement the flag on this bead — answer the question, then file the flag-implementation bead if the answer is TOTAL.

THE QUESTION, PRECISELY: Is there ANY way, inside a view body declared {:reactive false}, to (a) read reactive state (a v/sub-family read) or (b) produce a committed event site, that the runtime CANNOT observe at render time? "Total" means total over Freehand's SUPPORTED reactive semantics, not arbitrary Clojure: rf/subscribe-once is explicitly non-reactive and stays legal under the flag (the programmer asked for a snapshot); raw atom derefs and other private state channels were never ViewCell-tracked and remain the programmer's responsibility — chasing them would turn the opt-out back into a compiler.

WHAT TO VERIFY (chokepoints, per the Codex second opinion recorded in rf2-h4j7k's RULING notes):
1. Reactive reads: every supported read converges on cell/observe! (public v/sub is an alias; the compiled spelling reaches the same recorder via observe-site!). Both consult the render's dynamically scoped candidate before resolving/probing; an absent candidate already raises :rf.error/view-read-outside-render (implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/cell.cljc). Dynamic capture means a v/sub reached through an arbitrary ordinary helper is caught exactly like an inline read — FH-SUB-010 pins that (implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/sub_cljs_test.cljc). Confirm there is NO second sanctioned reactive-read door.
2. Event sites: the ViewCell also owns committed event sites and frame binding, so the flag's real contract is SHELL-FREE (no v/sub read AND no committed event site in the boundary's own render; reactive children fine — they own their own shells). The elision oracle already keeps the cell for either live site family (implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/viewcell_elision_oracle_jvm_test.clj; implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/react.cljs). Known gap: react.cljs has two no-candidate fallbacks — native element handlers and declared-host callbacks — where declarative intent can currently disappear or a function pass through without committed-site guarantees. Confirm both are interceptable chokepoints (i.e. a dynamically scoped shell-free assertion context can make them RAISE rather than silently degrade). The structural interpreter records every filled event position in :events (implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/node.cljc).
3. Confirm the check can fire on the FIRST OFFENDING RENDER in production builds as well as dev (it is the safety mechanism, not authoring lint), and that a later-executing props-controlled branch fails loudly at the read rather than committing stale UI.

EXIT CRITERIA: a verdict, TOTAL or NOT-TOTAL, with evidence. If TOTAL: file the flag-implementation bead (contract wording, implementation shape — one dynamically scoped assertion context masking any outer render candidate, one stable diagnostic carrying view id + offending capability — and the 5-item acceptance proof are all recorded in rf2-h4j7k's RULING notes) and the sequencing proceeds: flag ships -> flagged-vs-ordinary interpreted ablation verifies the elision value (6.256x retained heap / 1.712x wall clock per boundary, 2,348 B standing heap each) is delivered -> rf2-h4j7k closes -> rf2-zw1oo deletion dispatches. If NOT-TOTAL: name the concrete escape path, implement nothing, and surface to Mike — proof would then be genuinely irreplaceable for elision, the honest answer reverts to a narrowed compiler (rf2-zw1oo Option B), and zw1oo's Option C ruling needs revisiting.

Evidence: docs/design/freehand/studio/compiled-tier-browser-worth-it.md section 1a (PR #7112); rf2-h4j7k RULING notes; rf2-zw1oo ruling + notes.
notes:
=== SPIKE ANSWERED (2026-07-27). VERDICT: the runtime check IS total over what it must observe; it is NOT yet total in what it DOES about three of the things it observes. Bounded fix, no static analysis needed. Flag-implementation bead filed: rf2-oxlpy. ===

Findings doc: ai/findings/2026-07-27.reactive-false-runtime-check-totality.md (local-only). Probe suites kept on PR #7171 — reactive-false-totality-jvm-test, reactive-false-shell-free-dom-cljs-test, reactive-false-check-elision-prod-test.

THE QUESTION AS POSED — is there ANY way to read reactive state, or produce a committed event site, inside a declared-inert body that the runtime CANNOT OBSERVE at render time? — ANSWER: NO. Every such capability reaches the runtime through a small, enumerable set of forks that already consult the render candidate: one for reads (cell/observe! / observe-site!, and the JVM probe asserts mechanically that cell.cljc is the ONLY Freehand namespace requiring re-frame.substrate.observation, plus (identical? v/sub cell/observe!)), and exactly three for event sites (react.cljs:263 native element handler — v/spread-safe's put-caller! fold routes through it too; react.cljs:965 declared-host callback; reactive.cljc:100 the compiled site). There is no fifth door. What escapes today is only the RESPONSE: the read fork raises, the three event forks answer nil or a raw function instead.

CHOKEPOINT 1, READS — TOTAL, INCLUDING PRODUCTION. Capture is dynamic and the candidate is consulted BEFORE resolve/probe, so the refusal is indifferent to how the read was reached. Pinned for: inline; through two ordinary defns; inside a lazy child run the WALK realises after the body returned; and on a props-controlled branch the first render does not take (the inert first render succeeds — no false positive — and the reading render fails at the read). Not gated: the candidate check is an unconditional `when` and error/throw-error! consults no flag. The JVM probe reads System/getProperty "re-frame.debug" and asserts the live interop/debug-enabled? matches, so the two runs are demonstrably two postures — never a with-redefs, which cannot reach a load-time def. Production proved separately under the real :browser-test-prod-elision build (:advanced + goog.DEBUG=false), asserting (false? interop/debug-enabled?) first, then the read still raising with its stable id, then a REAL MOUNT of a shell-free helper-reading boundary refusing and committing nothing.

CHOKEPOINT 2, EVENT SITES — NOT TOTAL TODAY. Measured on real mounts, each against a shell-owning control arm: a declarative [:evt] vector and an options map have their prop NEVER WRITTEN (element mounts, click does nothing, nothing throws); a (v/event ...) / (v/handler ...) carrier is dropped the same way, because handler-proxy's fallback is (when (fn? raw) raw) and a Callback deftype is DELIBERATELY not fn? in CLJS; a bare (fn [e] ...) PASSES THROUGH AND FIRES with no frame binding, no :once, no retirement at unmount, no controlled-input door and no stable identity — the most dangerous shape for an OPT-IN because it looks like success; and a v/defhost :event callback is handed over RAW, so the foreign component calls the carrier's fn, receives an intent vector and discards it. All three forks are single (some? cand) tests, so a masking assertion context can make each RAISE while leaving fr/element's documented "no boundary above this call" degrade untouched.

THE FINDING THAT DECIDES rf2-zw1oo: THE COMPILER'S PROOF IS ALREADY DEFEATABLE, AND THE RUNTIME CHECK IS ALREADY WHAT SAVES IT. A {:compiled true} view whose body reads through an ordinary two-hop helper analyzes to :view-cell :elided — asserted off v/manifest in the same test, so the claim is non-vacuous — and mounts with NO shell. It does not go silently stale: it fails loud at the read with :rf.error/view-read-outside-render, in development AND in an :advanced production bundle. So compiled elision was never backed by proof alone; it was backed by proof PLUS the same candidate check the flag would rest on. Replacing the proof with an author declaration does not remove a safety net — it removes one that was already porous and leaves the one that was doing the catching.

MASKING IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT BELT-AND-BRACES. Pinned as a passing witness: on the JVM structural host — and inside t/with-render, and under v/render-static — a nested view's body runs INLINE in the caller's dynamic extent, so ONE bracket covers the whole tree and a shell-free boundary rendered there would find the OUTER candidate and silently DONATE its read to the outer boundary. cell/observe! cannot tell the two apart. In the browser this does not arise (React renders each component in its own work-loop turn, after the parent's render returned), but a violation that passes a structural test and only fails in a browser is exactly what this flag must not permit. The masking binding must live in cell.cljc, because *render* is ^:private there.

THE OTHER ACCEPTANCE SHAPES. (4) A reactive child of a shell-free parent stays fully reactive — proven on a real mount. (5) The hot-reload mechanism already exists: shell-signature is [lowering (:view-cell (manifest view))] and a signature change mints a new component type; the compiled tier already signs [:compiled :present] vs [:compiled :elided], and the probe pins that every interpreted view signs [:interpreted nil] today, so the flag has one axis to move. (1) The no-ViewCell half is already pinned for the compiled elided path; the flagged-vs-ordinary INTERPRETED ablation does not exist yet and belongs to rf2-oxlpy.

TWO CONTRACT DETAILS FOUND BY RUNNING IT, BOTH CARRIED ONTO rf2-oxlpy. (a) rf/subscribe-once AMBIENT stays legal, and not for the reason assumed: the shell's with-capture binds frame/*current-frame* and a shell-free boundary gets none, but frame/resolve-current-frame has a SECOND tier — the React frame context via the :adapter/current-frame hook — so the ambient 1-arity still resolves the mounting frame with no shell above it (mounted and read back off the DOM). The first draft of this spike predicted the opposite; the probe corrected it. (b) IN PRODUCTION THE REFUSAL IS NOT CATCHABLE BY THE MOUNT CALLER: react/act is a development-only export ("act is not a function" under :advanced) and react-dom/flushSync does not rethrow either — React 19 routes an uncaught render error to the root's onUncaughtError. The read IS refused with its stable id and NOTHING is committed, but the failure arrives as an uncaught page error rather than something a caller can try/catch.

ALSO FILED: rf2-nzmuy (P3, latent) — the same no-candidate fallback drops v/raw-fn and v/render-fn, the two roster roles that need no committed site at all. Not reachable from any shipping declaration today; fixed as a side effect if rf2-oxlpy lands as briefed.

SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY: total over Freehand's SUPPORTED reactive semantics. rf/subscribe held directly, raw atom derefs and other private state channels were never ViewCell-tracked and remain the programmer's responsibility — the same scope the compiled tier's elision always had.

GATES (all foreground, all exit 0): freehand JVM focused ns dev; freehand JVM focused ns -Dre-frame.debug=false; freehand JVM full suite (1227 tests / 8247 assertions); npm run test:cljs (11809 / 58761); npm run test:browser (843 / 5400); npm run test:browser-prod-elision, :advanced (120 / 526); check_test_lane_bijection.py + check_jvm_lane_rosters.py + check_freehand_conformance_index.py.
close_reason: Spike answered: the check is total over what it must observe; three event-site forks need to raise rather than degrade, which is a bounded fix. Flag bead rf2-oxlpy filed and now blocks rf2-h4j7k.

title: test(freehand): the STAGED invariant-5 case has no shipped row — and it is the worse one
description:
FROM rf2-so3io (PR #7159), measured on a WATCHABLE browser host over the real observation port and the real sub-cache.

PR #7143 added the repo's only invariant-5 coverage: two rows, and BOTH are the RETAINED case (the site was committed once before, so its change watch was installed by that earlier commit). The rf2-so3io ablation measured the two cases side by side and the uncovered one is strictly worse:

  site      commit    revision advanced?  cell dirty?  value published
  retained  shipped   yes                 no           FRESH
  retained  ablated   no                  YES          stale
  staged    shipped   yes                 no           FRESH
  staged    ablated   no                  NO           stale

A RETAINED site whose source moves in the render->commit gap self-heals one window later even without the commit-side re-read, because its watch fires. A STAGED site — the FIRST commit of that dependency — does not: obs/acquire! installs the watch DURING that commit, after the move already happened, so no channel is left at all. The bundle publishes the render's stale value, the cell is not dirty, and the boundary paints stale and stays stale until something else moves that source.

That is a first render of a dependency: a panel mounting while a permission drops, a user switches, a record is redacted.

WHAT TO DO: add a staged-case row beside the two in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/shell_cljs_test.cljc. The existing 'invariant-5-a-real-node-moving-in-the-gap-corrects-a-retained-site' is the template — drop its first render+commit so the site is staged rather than retained, keep the unmoved control, and assert the revision advance and the FRESH published value. Roughly 25 lines, same fixture, same helpers.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND COVERAGE: Spec 006 justifies invariant 5 on the headless case ('on a non-watchable headless host a retained site has no value-movement watch, so this comparison is its only correction'). The staged case is stronger than that — it holds on a WATCHABLE host too — and nothing in the spec or the suite currently says so. Consider whether spec/006 should say it (HOT ZONE, report don't edit).

Instrument that found it: b9_nc.cljs/tear-probe! on branch worker/uses-ablation-so3io.
close_reason: PR #7160 — staged invariant-5 row added over the real port (shell_cljs_test.cljc, cold + live probe, each with an unmoved control) plus a watchable-host row (shell_tear_dom_cljs_test.cljs). Mutation-proved: ablating cell/commit-readings reds both, and the browser ablation produced exactly 2 failures in 835 tests, both mine. #7143's two rows run by name and stay green. Spec 006 justification gap filed as rf2-locmf.

title: bench: rf2-jr76s's published per-sub figures are the COORD-LESS shape and understate a real app by up to 6x
description:
FOUND by rf2-zxv06 (PR #7158).

write_attribution.cljs registers its 300 ladder subs through re-frame.core's reg-sub FUNCTION -- the ns requires [re-frame.core :as rf] WITHOUT :include-macros true -- so the macro's source-coord capture never runs and every registrar slot comes out {}. The harness now prints this (';; registered sub-meta coord keys = {}') and WA_COORDS=1 registers the realistic shape.

WHY IT MATTERS. handler-scope-from-meta's cost is dominated by whether the slot carries coords: with :ns/:file/:line, trigger-handler-from-meta builds a cumulative coord map AND a 3-key trigger map on top of the HandlerScope record; without them it returns nil and the record is all there is. Measured (node V8, :advanced, goog.DEBUG=false): 120.1 B/sub coord-less vs 744.2 B/sub coord-carrying -- a factor of 6.2.

A real application's subs ARE macro-registered and DO carry coords in production builds (:column is dev-only; :ns/:file/:line are the locked keys per source-coords/prod-coords-form). So the ladder's registration is NOT the production shape.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RECORD: ai/findings/2026-07-27.jr76s-narrow-write-attribution.md quotes P-SCOPE at 120.8 B/sub and a post-fix per-sub slope of 940.8. Both are coord-less readings. Measured on the coord-carrying ladder the same pre-PR-#7158 slope is 1724.6 (forward) / 1567.5 (reversed) -- i.e. the published narrow-write slope understates a real application by ~65-85%. The other terms in that decomposition (P-BODY, P-EQDB, Q-SCHED, P-VALS) are coord-independent and unaffected.

NOT URGENT and NOT a defect in the fix -- PR #7158 measured BOTH ladders and its saving lands on the paired-control prediction in each. This bead is about whether the published jr76s doc should carry a correction note, and whether the DEFAULT for the harness should flip to WA_COORDS=1 (it was left coord-less so the recorded slope stays comparable).

Mike's call: (a) annotate the jr76s findings doc, (b) flip the harness default, (c) both, (d) leave it -- the mechanism is now printed in every run's header, which may be enough.

Evidence: ai/findings/2026-07-27.prod-write-costs.md SS1; raw runs ai/findings/2026-07-27.prod-write-costs-wa-*-coords-*.txt
notes:
MAYOR RULING (2026-07-27): BOTH — correct the findings doc AND flip the harness default. Raised to P1, because a benchmark that under-measures the real case by 6x is worse than no benchmark: it produces confident, precise, wrong numbers, and several beads have already been RANKED off it.

THE FAULT: the allocation ladder registered subs through `reg-sub`-the-FUNCTION, with no `:include-macros true`, so the registered slots came out {} carrying NO source coords. A REAL application's subs carry :ns/:file/:line. Measured difference on the same ladder: 120.1 B/sub coord-less vs 744.2 B/sub coord-carrying — A FACTOR OF SIX.

(1) FLIP THE HARNESS DEFAULT to the coord-carrying registration, because that is what a consumer's application actually does. The coord-less arm may stay as an explicitly-labelled control — it is useful for isolating the coord cost — but it must not be the default any figure is quoted from.
(2) ADD A CORRECTION NOTE to the jr76s findings doc and to any other findings doc quoting a per-sub figure from this harness, stating which arm produced the number and that a coord-carrying app pays up to 6x on that term. DO NOT restate any ratio: the fault inflates or deflates an ABSOLUTE, and a ratio between two arms measured the same way is unaffected. Correcting a ratio on the strength of an absolute-only fault would repeat, in the opposite direction, the error being fixed.
(3) RE-RANK anything ranked off a coord-less absolute. This is the second time this session that beads were ranked off a profile that did not match the target: the first was JVM figures where the largest term (dynamic `binding`, ~760 B) does not exist in ClojureScript at all (rf2-x0fe2).

THE GENERAL LESSON, and it now has three instances: BEFORE RANKING WORK OFF A MEASUREMENT, ASK WHETHER THE HARNESS'S CONFIGURATION MATCHES A REAL CONSUMER'S — runtime (JVM vs CLJS), engine build (Node's pointer compression OFF vs Chrome's ON, ~2x on absolutes), and now REGISTRATION SHAPE (macro vs function, 6x on the coord term). Each was invisible in a passing run and each produced plausible precise numbers.

This is a factual-accuracy correction to published measurement, not a product decision, which is why I am ruling rather than holding it for the operator.
close_reason:
PR #7161 merged (recovered by the mayor after the worker died between its last commit and its PR). The allocation ladder now registers subs through reg-sub-the-MACRO, so slots carry :ns/:file/:line the way a real application's do. The coord-less arm survives as an explicitly-labelled control, useful for isolating the coord term.

WHY IT MATTERED: same ladder, both shapes measured 120.1 B/sub coord-less vs 744.2 B/sub coord-carrying — A FACTOR OF SIX. Several beads had been RANKED off the coord-less absolute.

NO RATIO WAS RESTATED, deliberately: the fault moves an ABSOLUTE, and a ratio between two arms measured the same way is unaffected. Correcting a ratio on an absolute-only fault would have repeated the error in the opposite direction.

RUNTIME CAVEAT CARRIED INTO THE CORRECTION, at the operator's prompting: these are JVM figures and the target is the BROWSER. The largest single term in one JVM profile (~760 B, the dynamic binding) does not exist in ClojureScript at all, and Node differs from Chrome by ~2x on pointer compression. Absolutes from this harness may mis-rank for the browser. rf2-x0fe2 tracks the missing CLJS figures and is the bead that actually closes this gap.

THE GENERAL LESSON, now with three instances (JVM-vs-CLJS, Node-vs-Chrome, macro-vs-function registration): before ranking work off a measurement, ask whether the harness's configuration matches a real consumer's. Each of the three was invisible in a passing run and each produced plausible, precise, wrong numbers.

title: No CLJS allocation figure exists for the re-frame read path - and the largest JVM term is JVM-only
description:
Every allocation figure on this surface -- rf2-21pck, rf2-mvqwe (PR
#7151), rf2-j8ls2 / rf2-ncjyt (PR #7154) -- is JVM, via
`com.sun.management.ThreadMXBean/getThreadAllocatedBytes`. The bytes do
not transfer to ClojureScript. That was always stated. It now MATTERS,
because the decomposition found that the LARGEST single term is one that
does not exist in CLJS at all:

  the dynamic `binding` of registrar/*generation* in
  call-with-frame-resolution        ~760 B/call on the JVM
                                    ~0 in ClojureScript

JVM `binding` = push-thread-bindings: a hash-map for the pair, a fresh
TBox assoc'd into the thread's binding map (a path copy), a new Frame.
CLJS `binding` expands through `with-redefs` to `let` + `set!` +
try/finally restore -- confirmed from cljs/core.cljc in
clojurescript-1.12.145. No allocation.

So the JVM ranking of `subscribe`'s cache-HIT cost is

  binding ~46%  >  ref-count attach ~32%  >  frame value 12%  >
  error payload 8%

and the CLJS ranking is CERTAINLY different -- most likely the
persistent write on top, with the frame value second. We are optimising
against a profile whose top row a browser app does not pay.

WHAT IS NEEDED: a CLJS per-read allocation figure for `@(subscribe [:q])`
of the same evidential quality as the JVM set -- controls whose size is
computable, predicted-vs-measured reported, multiple rounds, ranges not
means, arm order reversed in some rounds.

INSTRUMENT WARNINGS, EARNED ON THIS EXACT SURFACE (nine fault classes
caught so far -- read them before building anything):
  * CDP `getHeapUsage` and `performance.memory` are TWO DOORS ONTO ONE
    V8 COUNTER. Agreeing to the byte is not corroboration.
  * a positive control built from `'x'.repeat(n)` read as six kilobytes
    on all three readers.
  * so: build the control from a type whose retained size is COMPUTABLE
    and use TWO of them a decade apart, so a constant error and a scale
    error look different. The JVM set used two `long-array`s and hit
    +0.000% in 18 rounds; match that standard or say plainly that you
    could not.
  * a NOOP arm must read exactly 0, so no subtraction is load-bearing.

DEPENDS ON NOTHING. It gates the honest ranking of rf2-8gb3t (frame
value), rf2-ezwnl (registrar key vector) and rf2-k9iu4 (the binding
ruling) -- and it may moot rf2-k9iu4 entirely.

P1 because three open beads are currently ranked off a profile that is
known to be wrong for the target runtime.
notes: 2026-07-27 22:32 AUSEST: rf2-k9iu4 (the binding ruling) is now CLOSED and is NO LONGER ranked off this bead's output. Ruled: no change; the wrapper stays; EP-0023 not reinterpreted. Basis: CLJS binding verified zero-allocation from the actual macro expansion (set!/try-finally, no TBox/Frame) plus a null-result Node timing microbenchmark, and the JVM persistently-held-hit shape is not the real JVM workload (subscribe-once disposes in-call, so ordinary SSR/tool reads are misses). This bead's CLJS measurement still gates the honest ranking of rf2-8gb3t (frame value) and rf2-ezwnl (registrar key vector), but a ~zero binding figure here will NOT reopen rf2-k9iu4 - it reopens only on (a) a representative optimized CLJS/browser benchmark attributing material wall-clock to the binding, or (b) a real JVM SSR/tool workload with persistently-held cache hits at consequential scale. See rf2-k9iu4's close reason for the full ruling.
close_reason:
PR #7238. MEASURED (CLJS, node 24.13.0 / V8 13.6.233.17-node.37, :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false, pointer compression OFF, n=300, 6 rounds, both arm orders, guard reportable in both, 0 UNVERIFIED of 1638 windows, controls +0.03%/+0.04% predicted-vs-measured). Instrument: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution_cljs.cljs, the counterpart of read_attribution.clj arm for arm. Write-up: docs/design/freehand/studio/read-path-on-the-shipping-host.md.

THE FIGURE. subscribe on a cache HIT = 1698.1 B/read; @(subscribe [:q]) = 1698.1 (the deref of a cached node is FREE, <= floor). Decomposed, net of NOOP:

  the ref-count attach     1224.9-1225.0 B/read   72.1%
  require-current-frame!          264.1           15.6%
  call-with-frame-resolution      112.3            6.6%
    - the generation read          48.0            2.8%
    - the harness's own thunk      64.0            3.8%  (instrument, not product)
    - THE BINDING                 <=0.1            0.0%
  frame + cache get                96.7            5.7%
  frame-target->id                  0.0            0.0%

THE BINDING IS ZERO, three independent ways, all at/under the 0.053 B/read
instrument floor and therefore UPPER BOUNDS not measurements:
  N-BINDONLY standalone (no thunk to elide)          0.1 B/read
  budget (N-CWFRRAW - N-CALLTHUNK - N-GENREAD)       0.1 B/read
  symmetric pair (N-CWFRBIND - N-CWFRGEN)            0.0 B/read
Same-session JVM run of read_attribution.clj reads 696.0 B/call for the same term.

RANKING. JVM: binding > attach > frame value > error payload. CLJS: attach >
ambient frame reader > frame/cache lookup > generation read, binding LAST.

VANISHES: the binding (~760 -> 0). Also the cached-node deref, though JVM and
CLJS are not the same measurement there (JVM plain-atom recomputes per deref;
CLJS spine caches).
SHRINKS: call-with-frame-resolution as a whole, 41% -> 6.6%.
HOLDS: the ref-count attach (41% -> 72.1%); the generation read; both retired
spellings (rf2-a8bw0 216.5 B/read vs JVM 136; rf2-8gb3t 520.0 vs JVM 200.0,
predicted by the independent N-RESTGT arm to 0.0%). Irreducible persistent
write 954.0 B/read; rf2-j8ls2's rewrite saves 1045 B/read vs 224-248 JVM.
APPEARS: require-current-frame!, 264.1 B/read, CLJS-ONLY -- filed rf2-f70iq.

BEAD RE-RANKING:
  rf2-k9iu4 CONFIRMED, stays closed -- this is the allocation measurement its
    ruling anticipated and it agrees. Now measured rather than derived.
  rf2-8gb3t retirement MORE justified on CLJS (520 vs 200), already closed.
  rf2-ezwnl DO NOT REOPEN. The key vector is 408-444 B/read, 4.5x the JVM's
    ~98 -- but subscribe's cache-HIT branch performs NO registrar/lookup; it
    runs per dispatch/fx/cofx/miss, which this measurement does not price.
    Reopening would be on evidence the condition does not ask for. Figure
    banked for a future dispatch-path measurement.
  The published JVM absolutes stand as JVM figures; their shares and paired
    comparisons remain sound, the ORDERING of terms does not transfer.

THE GUARD REFUSED TWICE AND WAS RIGHT BOTH TIMES: (1) N-CALLTHUNK, an arm I
added, whose thunk V8's escape analysis elided in some windows and not others
-- repaired the ARM, tolerance untouched; (2) an RA_N=1000 run, where
calibration bottoms out at reps 1-2 and the controls stop landing -- n=1000 is
outside the working regime and no figure from it is quoted. Forward-plan
refusals were NOT tuned away. Filed rf2-ktrvw.

THREE SUBTRACTIONS THAT LOOK RIGHT AND ARE NOT are on record in the harness and
the write-up, including the JVM harness's own (it conflates the generation read
with the binding -- invisible at 2-5% on the JVM, the whole answer here).

read-attribution RM_SUITE=subs 0 (controls +0.000%); write-attribution x3 all 0

title: observation port: resolve-target + probe is 81.5% of Freehand's render-leg allocation — 3733 B per dependency read
description:
Measured on rf2-21pck (PR #7147), JVM, 300 dependencies, production-gated
(-Dre-frame.debug=false), exact TLAB accounting via
com.sun.management.ThreadMXBean/getThreadAllocatedBytes. All arms in ONE
process against the REAL port and a REAL 300-entry prior committed set;
calibration REAL vs simulated-shipped agreed to 0.09%.

Attribution of a 300-dependency Freehand render (1 374 416 B total):

  resolve-target + probe          1 119 944 B   81.5%   3733 B/dependency
  stabilization (prior lookup,
    2x rf=, the record map)          28 140 B    2.0%     93.8 B/read
  the dependency ledger write       227 610 B   16.6%    758.7 B/read

rf2-21pck took 36% off the LEDGER row (the only row cell.cljc owns) for
-6.06% of the leg, disjoint and exact. The 81.5% row is untouched and is
where this leg's cost actually lives.

3733 bytes allocated per dependency read, for a subscription whose entire
body is (get-in db [:items i]). That is framework overhead, not application
work. It is in re-frame.substrate.observation and the per-frame sub-cache
(core), not in Freehand, so it was outside rf2-21pck's fence.

Rank against the honest prior: the render leg is ~19% of the 4.05 ms
broad-update window PR #7139 profiled, so even halving this row is ~9% of
the window — still likely under B6's +-15% round noise on the row, but it is
the largest single allocation term anywhere on the measured path and it is
paid by EVERY substrate consumer of the port, not only Freehand.

FIRST STEP is measurement, not a change: decompose the 3733 B/read inside
resolve-target and probe the same way rf2-21pck decomposed the ledger (one
process, ablation arms, ThreadMXBean). The instrument is
scratchpad/ledger_arms.clj in rf2-21pck's raw findings
(ai/findings/2026-07-27.render-leg-21pck-raw.md, local-only) and is ~150
lines; it can be pointed at the port directly.

HOT-ZONE WARNING: any change lands in implementation/core and may touch
spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md. Sequence, do not parallel.
notes:
RAISED P2 -> P1 BY THE MAYOR (2026-07-27), and the reason is WHERE the cost lives, not how big it is.

MEASURED (rf2-21pck, PR #7147): resolve-target + probe is 81.5% of the render leg's allocation — 1,119,944 of 1,374,416 bytes, 3,733 B PER DEPENDENCY READ — for a subscription whose entire body is (get-in db [:items i]). By comparison the dependency ledger that bead was dispatched to fix is 16.6%, and stabilization is 2.0%.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE. It is in CORE's observation port and sub-cache, NOT in Freehand. That relocates a large share of the render leg's cost off the substrate under judgement and onto the shared framework path — which is the SAME argument that already cut the narrow-update CLOCK result from 15x to parity: '~90% of it decomposes to frame/replace-app-db! plus the re-frame signal graph, and a Reagent app reading re-frame subs would pay that same leg.'
SO THE OPEN QUESTION IS: does an application reading re-frame subscriptions pay 3,733 B per read REGARDLESS of view substrate? If yes, this is a re-frame cost that the Freehand-vs-Reagent comparison has been silently attributing to Freehand — and the honest table changes. If no, it is Freehand's observation port specifically, and it is the second-largest lever anyone has found.
ANSWER THAT FIRST. It is a measurement, not a refactor, and it decides whether this is a Freehand bead or a core bead.

CONTEXT: the operator ruled Freehand cannot ship slower than Reagent (rf2-lbs3y, P0). Interpreted Freehand currently trails on mount (~2x), broad update (~9.7x, architectural) and retained heap (2,430 B vs 410 B per boundary). There is no axis on which it leads. A cost that turns out to be shared framework overhead rather than substrate overhead is directly material to that standard.

METHOD NOTE from the discovering worker: it reused an ablation harness that isolates the leg in-process, and the bead names measurement as the first step. Do not start with a refactor.
INSTRUMENT NOTE: its allocation figures came from JVM ThreadMXBean/getThreadAllocatedBytes and were disjoint to the BYTE across rounds; a port-only control read 48 bytes apart in 1.1 MB. That is the standard to match. JVM byte figures do NOT transfer to ClojureScript — the shape does, the numbers do not.

=== ANSWERED 2026-07-27 04:40 AUSEST (PR #7151, worker/port-attribution-mvqwe) ===

THE QUESTION: does an application reading re-frame subscriptions pay the
~3733 B/read REGARDLESS of view substrate?

ANSWER: YES. JVM, 300 dependencies, -Dre-frame.debug=false, 9 rounds
(6 forward + 3 reversed arm order), one process, real sub-cache, 300 real
live nodes, ThreadMXBean/getThreadAllocatedBytes.

  PORT    (probe (resolve-target ...))  freehand's per-read   3656 - 3784 B/read
  RGREAD  @(subscribe q)                reagent's per-read    3484 - 3684 B/read
  DEREF   @held-reaction                reagent form-2        1808 - 1816 B/read

RGREAD is 95.3% - 97.4% of PORT in every one of nine rounds. The PAIRED
per-round difference (both arms in the same process, so pairing is the
right statistic) is 100 - 172 B/read = 2.6% - 4.7% of PORT, never negative.
A Reagent form-2 component that holds its reaction still pays 48.0% - 49.5%.

So: every substrate reading a re-frame subscription pays AT LEAST 48% of the
port's per-read allocation, and the common `@(rf/subscribe [:q])` idiom pays
95%-97%. Freehand's own share is UNDER 5%. THIS IS A CORE BEAD, and the
"second-largest lever anyone has found" is not a lever on the
Freehand-vs-Reagent comparison at all.

CLOCK: PORT 356.5-543.7 us vs RGREAD 319.3-514.0 us per 300 reads. Ranges
overlap almost entirely -- INDISTINGUISHABLE, paired difference changes sign
twice. Null result, not a win for either reader.

CONTROLS: two long-arrays a decade apart, sizes computable from the JVM
object model, +0.000% error in all nine rounds. NOOP = 0 bytes in all nine.
Census 300 LIVE / 0 COLD every round; all four readers agree on the value
the writer just wrote or the run throws. rf2-21pck's 1 119 944 B sits inside
this harness's independently-derived 1 096 800 - 1 135 200 B.

DOES NOT TRANSFER TO CLJS: byte counts, and the JVM plain-atom adapter's
recompute-on-every-deref. The attribution survives both because the term is
SHARED -- remove the recompute from both readers and RGREAD is 94.9% of PORT
instead of 97.4%.

INSTRUMENT (committed, reusable):
implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution.clj
RAW DATA: ai/findings/2026-07-27.port-attribution-mvqwe.md (local-only)

NO SOURCE WAS CHANGED. The bead asked for a measurement and got one.

FOLLOW-ONS FILED: rf2-j8ls2 (subscribe's ref-count attach ~1.8 KB/call --
the largest substrate-side term found, and unexamined because every prior
comparison used a Reagent arm that never calls subscribe), rf2-ncjyt
(probe's pre-node lookups ~1120 B/read; the cache get is 0 B), rf2-9f2w4
(RULING: the published report scopes its shared-re-frame caveat to the
write leg, but the render leg is 95%+ shared too), rf2-m7xs7 (B6 has no
Reagent-reading-re-frame arm).
close_reason: Measurement delivered, PR #7151. Answer: YES -- 95.3%-97.4% of the port's per-read allocation is paid by a substrate-free @(subscribe q). Core bead, not a Freehand bead. Four follow-ons filed.

title: bench: the ViewCell wrapper costs 2,430 B of standing heap — attack it, or accept the memory row
description:
FOLLOW-UP from rf2-9oj7v (PR #7146).

The cross-substrate memory row landed the same verdict the clock did, on the same term. A Freehand boundary that reads NOTHING retains 2,430 bytes above the React floor; Reagent's costs 410 and UIx's 251. That 5.93x is the ViewCell wrapper alone — no app-db, no subscription, no cursor on either side of the comparison, so nothing about it can be attributed to re-frame.

WHY IT IS THE SAME TERM TWICE. freehand-vs-reagent.md's item 4 already names bulk re-render of boundaries as the one clock gap that is squarely Freehand's own (4.0-5.4 ms against Reagent's 0.6-0.7, ~7-8x on 300 repainting boundaries) and observes that compiling barely moves it, 'which suggests the cost is in the ViewCell wrapper rather than in the markup walk'. The heap row is independent evidence for exactly that reading: the wrapper is expensive to keep, and it is expensive to re-render. One object, two rows.

WHAT A ViewCell IS, per the ablation: a cell object, a hook record, a subscription registration and two layout effects, all living as long as the mount. 2,430 bytes is a lot for that inventory and the composition is worth knowing before anything is cut - a heap snapshot taken by b7_run.cjs's snapshot pass can be re-read for retainer paths rather than just a self_size total, which would say WHICH of the four dominates.

SEQUENCE against rf2-wxrrp (retained-set fast path in cell/commit!) rather than racing it - that bead is already in cell.cljc and its measurements are against B6.

NOT A REQUEST TO REDESIGN ON THIS EVIDENCE ALONE. The decision this feeds is whether Freehand can ship at all under rf2-lbs3y's ruling. If the wrapper cannot be made materially cheaper on both axes, the honest conclusion is that the memory row stands beside the clock row and both point the same way. File the composition finding first; the remedy is a separate decision and Mike's.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
VERDICT: ACCEPT THE ROW. No PR; cell.cljc is byte-identical to origin/main. Full byte accounting in ai/findings/2026-07-27.viewcell-byte-accounting-oob3g.md; instrument + raw logs in ai/findings/rf2-oob3g-raw/.

WHERE THE 2,430 B GO. An ablation ladder between B7's storm/floor and its storm/freehand, every rung building the identical 301-element DOM, 3 rounds, arm order rotating, reader C (full heap snapshot, self_size summed). Per boundary above the 461 B floor:

  +132   a React function component per leaf, ZERO hooks
  + 45   useContext (the frame read)
  + 96   useRef (incl. a two-object stand-in store)
  +145   useCallback (the stable subscribe)
  +516   useSyncExternalStore          <-- more than Reagent's WHOLE boundary
  +111   useLayoutEffect - reconcile
  +126   useLayoutEffect - lifecycle
  ----   1,171 B: the shell's six hooks over a TWO-FIELD JS OBJECT
  +1245  the real ViewCell / candidate / event owner (shell/render)
  + 32   the interpreted emitter walk (v/defview)
  ====   2,448 B  [ Reagent 418, UIx 252 ]

So: 5% a component per leaf, 42% React's own hook machinery, 51% the ViewCell, 1.3% the walk.

WHY THAT IS A VERDICT AND NOT A STARTING POINT. A Freehand boundary with NO ViewCell at all - the six hooks over a two-field JS object, no candidate, no event owner, not one CLJS data structure - already retains 1,171 B against Reagent's 418. That is 2.80x WITH THE VIEWCELL SET TO ZERO. The ceiling on any attack confined to cell.cljc is 5.86x -> 2.80x: not parity, not the same order, and the residue is React's charge for six hooks, not Freehand's. Reagent is cheap here precisely because it uses none of them - its boundary is a CLASS component instance (w2_leaf carrying a .refs object) with an update queue, 12 extra heap nodes, no hook chain and no useSyncExternalStore bound functions anywhere in the diff.

INSIDE THE 1,245 B: the Atom + 11-key state map 457 (measured), the transient-built :observations vector 231 (measured), the RETAINED render candidate + its 4 volatiles 160, the :events committed table ~100, :listeners ~100, committed closures+Contexts ~90, the :fired set 80 (measured), the :deps map 51 (measured), ViewCell+EventOwner 36. Sums to ~1,305 against the measured 1,245 - the ~5% is stated, not reconciled away. The structural driver: a CLJS persistent collection costs THREE heap nodes (object + JS Array + V8's separate backing store), and a Freehand boundary holds NINE such arrays of its own (~536 B) against Reagent's two (67 B).

The render candidate is retained for the life of the mount (the reconcile layout effect closes over it and React keeps effect.create). It CANNOT be cleared after commit!: StrictMode's mount->unmount->mount re-invokes the SAME effect object's create, so a candidate emptied by its first commit would publish an empty dependency set on the second. Spec 006's selection law, working as written, with a standing price.

TWO LEVERS EXIST AND ARE PRICED, FILED AS rf2-9f1s7 (a decision, not a fix): the state map's 11 keys -> 8 (193-200 B, two runs, disjoint ranges) and commit-readings' transient vector (231 B empty / 172 B at four observations - it is the retained editable root, not the emptiness). Together 424 B, 17.3%, moving 5.86x -> 4.85x. Neither decides anything under rf2-lbs3y; one ripples the published shape of cell/evidence and cell/dependencies; the other buys retention with render-leg throughput, which is the OTHER axis Freehand is losing. This bead said the remedy is a separate decision and Mike's - agreed.

UPPER BOUND ON A REDESIGN: driving the ViewCell to a plausible ~300 B floor (mutable deftype fields, JS objects, no retained candidate) still leaves ~1,500 B = 3.6x Reagent, and costs the atomic publication ('nothing can observe a partial bundle'), the JVM's thread-safety on :revision/:dirty/:listeners, and the 'everything here is common' property. Spec 006 promises, hot-zone, operator's call.

INVARIANT 5 UNTOUCHED AND GREEN. PR #7143's two rows run BY NAME: 2 tests, 11 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0. Whole shell suite on JVM 25/129/0. freehand JVM 1220 tests / 8225 assertions / 0 failures. npm run test:cljs 11798 tests / 58732 assertions / 0 failures.

INSTRUMENT: B7's snapshot reader with one change - the streaming scan sums self_size PER CLASS and charges each anonymous node to the object that first points at it, under the property name it is held by. Same bundle, same window.B7H door, same arms, same DOM read-back, same collector, same control. The ladder's rungs are extra ARMS on that door, never edits to bench/. Class names come from the same :advanced build run with Closure :pseudo-names; the two builds' totals agree to 1.1%. Positive control (587,500 unboxed doubles, predicted 4,700,000 B) across five runs: 4,700,268 / 4,700,232 / 4,700,064 / 4,700,496 / 4,699,972 - worst error 0.0106%. 0 unverified of 120 mounts.

title: studio: heap UNDER UPDATE — the one memory question Freehand still has an argument in
description:
FOLLOW-UP from rf2-9oj7v (PR #7146), and the only surviving memory line for Freehand.

The cross-substrate STANDING-heap row went decisively against Freehand: 5.93x Reagent per sub-free boundary, 4.19x per reactive one, disjoint ranges, two independent instruments agreeing to 1%. That measurement mounts K roots and holds them still. It says nothing about what a WRITE costs in bytes.

WHY THIS IS NOT A CONSOLATION-PRIZE BEAD. Fine-grained reactivity's whole trade is meant to be that a write touches only what changed. Reagent's broad write re-renders 300 components through its own reaction graph; Freehand's notifies 300 ViewCells. If Freehand allocates materially LESS per write than Reagent, that is a real property of the design and it is the one memory claim still available — standing heap is a per-boundary constant an app pays once, whereas allocation per write is paid at every interaction and drives GC pauses. The compiled-tier report's §1a explicitly names transient garbage as the thing retention cannot see and the likeliest explanation for its 1.216 clock term not showing on retained bytes.

INSTRUMENT WARNING, and it is sharper here than for the standing row. The retention instrument in b7_heap.cljs CANNOT answer this: what a write allocates and drops is by construction invisible to it. And the obvious tool is the exact one that is broken — V8's CDP SAMPLING heap profiler drops the samples of collected objects, which is what makes it useless for a mount/unmount loop and what produced the earlier wrong table. Measuring allocation-per-write therefore needs a DIFFERENT instrument from either, and choosing it is most of the work. Candidates worth pricing before committing: HeapProfiler.startSampling/stopSampling with a small sampling interval read as a RATE over many writes (the sampler's failure mode is dropped collected samples, which is fatal for a one-shot delta but may be tolerable when the quantity of interest is a steady-state allocation rate); Runtime.getHeapUsage sampled at high frequency across a long write loop to observe sawtooth amplitude x frequency; or Chrome's allocation-timeline. WHATEVER IS CHOSEN MUST CARRY AN IN-SITU POSITIVE CONTROL OF PREDICTED SIZE, as b7_run.cjs does — a known allocation rate driven beside the arms.

FIXTURE: b6's update grid already exists in both dialects (300 cells, Freehand v/sub against Reagent r/cursor) and both broad and narrow writes are already driven by b6-rows/timed-write! with DOM read-back. Reuse it; do not build a third grid.

Note the standing asymmetry that §2a of freehand-vs-reagent.md bounds rather than removes: the Freehand arm reads app-db through a subscription graph, the Reagent arm a bare ratom. Split the write leg from the render leg as that report does, or the number will be a re-frame result wearing a Freehand label.
close_reason:
Measured and reported. Freehand LOSES on transient allocation too — the memory hypothesis is falsified on both axes.

Broad write 4,572,680 B vs Reagent 269,229 (17.0x); narrow 478,787 vs 23,648 (20.2x); all ranges disjoint. But the narrow 20.2x is 95.5% re-frame's write leg (457,181 B re-evaluating 300 subs to find 299 unchanged — filed rf2-jr76s), and stripping it leaves Freehand's view substrate at 21,376 B against Reagent's 19,307 — 1.107x, disjoint, both ~7x better than the top-down React floor. Closest to parity anything in this studio has reached, still a loss.

The broad view-leg 13.5x is published as an UPPER BOUND not a substrate result: rf2-40kdm measured the read path as 95.3-97.4% shared re-frame cost and this Reagent arm pays none of it. rf2-mapni files the arm that would close it.

Instrument: collection-free window over V8's used-heap counter. Decisive control is kept-vs-dropped at 1.0001 (125,139 vs 125,121 B/copy allocated, 99,417 vs 11 B retained) — the counter does not care whether an object survives. title: bench: B6's mount arm creates a frame per sample INSIDE the timed window — does the mount row overstate?
description:
Found while reconciling the W1-interpreted mount discrepancy on PR #7139.

B6's Freehand mount arm (b6_rows.cljs, freehand-mount-arm) calls v/mount with a :disambiguator and NO :frame:

    (v/mount [view props] container {:disambiguator (keyword "b6" ...)})

With no :frame in opts, v/mount runs plan-for / preflight! and creates a FRESH FRAME — and it does so inside the flushSync that b6-harness/mount-arm! is timing. So every B6 mount sample bills per-sample frame construction to the substrate, and the floor arm (a bare createRoot) never pays it.

The rf2-lnecd / rf2-xu6rx studio probe did NOT do this: it mounted every arm into ONE pre-existing shared frame (:frame fid). That is one of four named differences between the two harnesses, and it is the one that would bias in the observed direction (B6's ratio higher).

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND BOOKKEEPING: the mount row is on the release gate too. Interpreted W1 mount is 2.987-3.075x floor against Reagent's 1.518-1.554, and if a measurable slice of that is per-sample frame creation rather than substrate cost, the published mount row overstates how far interpreted mount has to travel.

CHEAP TO SETTLE: mount the Freehand arms with an explicit pre-created :frame and re-run measure-mount!. If the delta is material, either hoist frame creation out of the timed window or state the inclusion explicitly in the report's method.

Do NOT change the published numbers without re-running the whole row — the ratio is only meaningful against a floor measured in the same run.
acceptance_criteria: A measured delta between B6's W1 interpreted mount with a per-sample frame and with a shared pre-created frame, and either a harness fix or an explicit statement in freehand-vs-reagent.md's method.
close_reason:
PR #7146. NULL RESULT: the mount row does NOT overstate, and the premise does not hold.

v/mount with NO :frame creates NO frame. root.cljs: plan-for answers nil when opts carries no :frame; preflight! opens (when (some? plan) ...); root-element wraps in the frame provider only (if (some? frame-id) ...). A frameless mount runs no plan, creates no frame and binds none - it does LESS than a mount that names one, not more.

Measured anyway, four arms differing only in the :frame opt, b6-harness unchanged, 6 rounds x (5 warmup + 20 samples), ratio to the in-run floor:
  W1  floor 1.000 | fh-no-frame 3.109 [2.889-3.588] | fh-shared-frame 3.229 [3.000-3.706] | fh-frame-per-sample 3.347 [3.111-4.059] | reagent 1.545 [1.471-1.647]
  W2  floor 1.000 | fh-no-frame 8.667 [7.00-10.00]  | fh-shared-frame 9.611 [7.67-11.00]  | fh-frame-per-sample 9.917 [7.00-11.50]  | reagent 2.528 [1.67-3.00]

Ranges overlap, so on ranges alone the three Freehand arms are indistinguishable. But the arms interleave WITHIN a round, so the paired comparison is available and is decisive:
  shared frame / published arm      W1 x1.038 higher in 6 of 6 rounds | W2 x1.109 in 6 of 6
  frame-per-sample / published arm  W1 x1.074 in 6 of 6              | W2 x1.138 in 5 of 6

The published arm is the CHEAPEST of the three shapes. Correcting to the studio fixture's shared frame moves W1 UP 3.8% and W2 UP 10.9%. Even the feared counterfactual would have been worth 7.4% on W1 against a 2x gap. NO PUBLISHED FIGURE CHANGES; acceptance criterion met by explicit statement in freehand-vs-reagent.md's method plus §3 of the new memory report.

BONUS: the row REPRODUCES on a different day against current main (incl PR #7133's extra React commit). Reagent W1 1.545 [1.471-1.647] vs published 1.554 [1.520-1.583]; FH interpreted W1 3.109 [2.889-3.588] vs published 2.987 [2.840-3.167]. That reproducibility had never been shown.

title: freehand: a retained-set fast path for cell/commit! — the largest single lever on bulk re-render
description:
Profiled on rf2-dq20a's follow-on (PR #7139, docs/design/freehand/studio/bulk-rerender-where-the-time-goes.md).

cell/commit! is 29.43% of a broad-update window — 1.23 ms of 4.05 ms per write, against Reagent's ENTIRE layout-effect commit phase at 1.4 us. It is the single largest term in the ~10x deficit and it is O(DEPENDENCIES), not O(boundaries): an ablation that collapsed 300 boundaries into 1 (same DOM, same 300 reads) only moved it 1.23 -> 0.86 ms.

On a broad write EVERY site is RETAINED — same query, same target, same handle — and commit! still, per dependency: allocates two maps in stage! to say so; calls obs/read to re-deref the node; allocates a 300-element :observations vector of five-key maps; and republishes the whole dep map in one swap!.

THE OBSTACLE IS NOT CACHING. The commit-side re-read is the invariant-5 TEAR CHECK — it compares node-key, version and frame/registry epoch between the render that produced the element and the commit about to publish it. So a fast path is a change to WHEN the invariant is checked, not an optimisation. It needs a spec conversation against spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md §The Freehand atomic shell before any code.

Estimated ceiling if fully realised: ~1.2 ms of a ~3.65 ms deficit (~33%). Would NOT on its own bring interpreted Freehand under Reagent — see the sibling beads.

## Context
cell.cljc is held by PR #7133 as of 2026-07-27 — sequence after it merges.
acceptance_criteria: A design decision recorded on whether the invariant-5 tear check can be satisfied without re-reading every retained dependency at commit; if yes, an implementation with before/after broad-update ranges from b6_profile_run.cjs.
notes:
PR OPEN: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7143 (worker/commit-fastpath-wxrrp, 2 files, +270/-73).

VERDICT. commit! is ~25% cheaper on a fully-retained 300-dependency broad update — 371.5-411.7 us BEFORE vs 287.5-333.7 us AFTER, 16 interleaved rounds each, DISJOINT, production-gated (RE_FRAME_DEBUG=false). B6's broad-update row CANNOT resolve it and is reported as indistinguishable: freehand/reagent per round BEFORE [9.20-11.17] mean 9.91 vs AFTER [8.29-11.17] mean 9.66, 12 rounds each, overlapping. commit! is 29% of the window and B6's round noise is +-10-15%, so a quarter off the term is ~7% of the window — under the instrument. The two instruments agree about why the row did not move.

THE BEAD'S PREMISE IS FALSE, and that is the most useful finding. 'The staged map could be republished by identity instead of rebuilt' cannot be done: a retained record carries the render's :value and :evidence, and on a broad write BOTH have moved — that is what a broad write is. Republishing prior by identity would feed last render's values into the next render's stabilization in record-read!. There is no identity republish available on this row at any price. What is available is the bookkeeping BETWEEN the reads: stage! now reports its own acquisitions (fresh-handles + :retained? deleted) and stages through a transient; commit-readings reads, tear-checks and builds the observations in ONE pass instead of three walks plus a re-lookup each; superseded-handles answers the fully-retained set in two counts; :dep-order publishes the render order instead of copying it.

INVARIANT 5 UNTOUCHED, and now tested for the first time — the repo had NO invariant-5 coverage before this branch. Two rows: one moves each of :node-key/:version/:frame-epoch/:registry-epoch ALONE over a mocked port with the kept-check held open (so the site is RETAINED), each paired with an unmoved control; one moves a real node in the real render->commit gap over the real port and sub-cache. Both falsified against two mutants — (a) the comparison dropped, (b) correction skipped when staging acquired nothing, i.e. the exact fast path this bead hypothesised. Each mutant: exit 1, 5 failures, all 5 the new assertions, nothing else in 8225 assertions moved.

INSTRUMENT FAULT CAUGHT: the first JVM microbench ran with interop/debug-enabled? TRUE (the JVM default), so it was timing the dev evidence plane including commit-facts' 300-element mapv select-keys, which Closure DCEs out of the bundle B6 measures — ~70% of the reading (1000 us with, 300 us without). Those numbers were discarded and everything quoted is production-gated. Positive control: zero-dependency commit 1.3-2.5 us vs 300-dep 300-400 us. Every measured commit verified by reading the written value back out of the published bundle's first and last observation: 0 unverified across every round of every run; 0 unverified writes in all four B6 runs.

GATES all exit 0: freehand JVM (1220/8225), npm test:cljs (11796/58722), BROWSER_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS=600000 test:browser (833/5313), b6_prod_run.cjs x4. Full-spine + mkdocs deferred to CI.

NOT COVERED: the microbench is JVM and JIT-warmed (absolutes do not transfer to the browser; only the ratio, and only about commit!); one boundary holding 300 deps, not 300 boundaries holding one; no memory measurement; the browser row remains a null result.

rf2-21pck IS WARRANTED and its cheapest first move is on the RENDER leg: record-read! rebuilds the candidate's {:order :by-site} wrapper TWICE per reactive read (update :order conj, then assoc-in [:by-site ...]), so 300 reads allocate 600 wrapper maps nobody reads, on a leg #7139 profiled at 0.77 ms. Bounded, no invariant attached.

Raw per-round data: ai/findings/2026-07-27.commit-fastpath-wxrrp-raw.md (local-only, gitignored).
close_reason: PR #7143 open. commit! ~25% cheaper on a fully-retained 300-dependency broad update (371.5-411.7 us -> 287.5-333.7 us, 16 interleaved rounds each, disjoint, production-gated); B6's broad-update row cannot resolve it and is reported as indistinguishable (fh/reagent BEFORE [9.20-11.17] vs AFTER [8.29-11.17], 12 rounds each). Invariant 5 untouched and now covered for the first time, falsified against two mutants including the exact fast path this bead hypothesised. The bead's premise — republish the retained staged map by identity — is FALSE: :value and :evidence move on every broad write, so an identity republish would feed stale values into the next render's stabilization. Design decision recorded: the tear check cannot be satisfied without re-reading every retained dependency at commit; what can go is the bookkeeping between the reads.

title: [test] Flip b6_update_dom_cljs_test's flushSync non-vacuity row — Freehand now commits inside the flush
description:
PR #7133 (rf2-w2m25) fixed the defect that `a-freehand-write-does-not-commit-inside-flushsync` PINS as expected behaviour. That test is in the Freehand-vs-Reagent bench worker's branch (worker/bench-vs-reagent), NOT on main, so #7133 could not flip it — file ownership fence — and it will start failing the moment both land.

The test says so itself: 'If this test ever starts failing, Freehand has gained a synchronous commit and the update row should be re-taken without the microtask yield.' It has.

Three things to do in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b6_update_dom_cljs_test.cljs (+ b6_rows.cljs):

  1. FLIP AND RENAME the non-vacuity row — never delete it, never loosen it to accept both outcomes. It now asserts the opposite: `(react-dom/flushSync (fn [] ((:write! arm) 0 4242)))` leaves the DOM reading 4242 on the very next line. Something like `a-freehand-write-commits-inside-flushsync`.
  2. CORRECT the namespace docstring's four-way table. The 'flushSync(write) -> no' row is now 'yes', and the paragraph that derives the measurement window's shape from it no longer holds.
  3. RE-TAKE the update row without the microtask yield if the numbers move. The window was shaped as 'write, yield one microtask, force the substrate's own synchronous drain, stop the clock' precisely BECAUSE the slowest arm needed the yield. Freehand no longer does — `flushSync(write)` is now a complete window for it — so the row can be timed the same way the mount row is, and the floor/Reagent arms stop paying a microtask they never needed.

PERF NOTE for whoever re-takes it: the fix arms one extra React commit per render batch — a two-fiber detached root rendering nil, whose layout effect closes the window. Outside flushSync the microtask closer still gets there first, so the sentinel's commit lands AFTER the measured window and does no work; but it is real wall-clock and the B6 numbers are the place it would show. If it is measurable, say so on rf2-w2m25 rather than absorbing it silently.

Sequence AFTER whichever of #7133 / the bench PR merges second.
notes:
=== MAYOR MERGE-ORDER RULING (2026-07-27). DO NOT MERGE #7131 AND #7133 INDEPENDENTLY. ===

This is the mutually-invalidating pair the method warns about: a test pinning today's broken behaviour, and the fix for it. Each is GREEN ALONE. Whichever merges second turns MAIN RED.

  PR #7133 (worker/flushsync-w2m25) FIXES that defect (rf2-w2m25), so the pin becomes false the moment it lands.

THE ORDER, and it is not optional:
  1. Merge #7131 FIRST. It is the Freehand-vs-Reagent measurement and its pin is accurate against current main.
  2. Then #7133 REBASES on main and, IN THE SAME PR, FLIPS AND RENAMES that test - never deletes it, never loosens it to accept both outcomes. Per the method: the only coverage of this case must survive the flip. Its four-way docstring table needs correcting too, and the update row can be re-taken without the microtask yield.

Outside flushSync it lands AFTER the measured window and does no work, but it is real wall-clock, and B6's update row is exactly where it would show. title: [bug] The production-surviving redaction path had zero test coverage in any posture
notes:

title: Xray's published pom would drop 8 of its 10 in-repo runtime coords, and one (freehand) is unpublishable
description:
Found while reconciling the release inventories for rf2-gugc3. NOT fixed there — the fix lands in .github/ files fenced to other lanes, and one part is an operator decision.

tools/xray/deps.edn declares TEN in-repo :local/root runtime coordinates in its main :deps (deps.edn line numbers on main):
  19 day8/re-frame2                (implementation/core)
  23 day8/re-frame2-epoch
  27 day8/re-frame2-routing
  31 day8/re-frame2-flows
  34 day8/re-frame2-schemas
  38 day8/re-frame2-resources
  42 day8/re-frame2-machines
  53 day8/re-frame2-freehand       (implementation/freehand)
  57 day8/re-frame2-machines-viz   (tools/machines-viz)
  62 day8/reagent-slim

Two things do not line up with that.

1. .github/workflows/release-xray.yml rewrites only TWO of them to
   :mvn/version before deploy — core (line 205) and reagent-slim
   (line 206). `clein pom` SILENTLY SKIPS :local/root coordinates, so
   the published day8/re-frame2-xray pom would declare core +
   reagent-slim and omit the other eight. That is exactly the failure
   class release-story.yml's header says its rewrite + package
   preflight exist to prevent (rf2-wht9a / rf2-r8trk: consumer gets
   'No such namespace'). Story got a five-coordinate rewrite AND a
   pom preflight that refuses to deploy unless all five are present;
   Xray has neither.

2. .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh TOOLS_LOCAL_ROOTS
   inventories exactly ONE coordinate for xray (core). Story's entry
   lists five precisely because rf2-wht9a found the same hole there
   and closed it. So the gate that is supposed to assert 'every
   in-repo coordinate is rewritable' is blind to nine of Xray's.

The operator question, which is why this is filed rather than fixed:
day8/re-frame2-freehand cannot be rewritten to a :mvn/version at all.
implementation/freehand/deps.edn carries NO :clein/build — deliberately
(its own header: 'NO :clein deploy aliases — deliberate, not an
omission. Publication is F6 territory'). So Xray currently declares a
RUNTIME dependency on an artefact that is not publishable until the
EP-0036 F6 gate. Either Xray is not publishable until Freehand ships,
or the Freehand edge has to move to late-bind the way the independence
rule handles cross-feature references. That is Mike's call, not a
reconciliation.

Note this also makes CHANGELOG.md's current line — 'each ships on its
own tag rather than the framework's: xray-v*, story-v* and
machines-viz-v* each have a release workflow' — optimistic for xray:
the workflow exists, but a jar cut from it today would ship an
incomplete pom.

Fence note: the fix touches .github/workflows/release-xray.yml and
.github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh.
notes:
Merged-PR audit #7140 (2026-07-26): reopen. The PR correctly preserves relay-1 ex-data and adds an elegant fail-closed generated-pom preflight, but it closes this owner without resolving the defect it names. Xray still carries ten in-repo runtime local/root dependencies, release-xray rewrites only core and reagent-slim, and Freehand is now explicitly withdrawn/unpublished; the release path therefore remains deliberately fatal while CHANGELOG still says xray-v* ships. Resolve the Freehand edge (remove or late-bind at the tool seam), rewrite every remaining publishable runtime dependency, make the generated-pom preflight pass, and correct release documentation if Xray intentionally remains unpublished.

PR #7349 (2026-08-01) — packaging half fixed and proved; the Freehand half needs the ruling, so this stays OPEN.

VERIFIED against the build, not the bead. Ten :local/root coordinates in tools/xray/deps.edn, release-xray.yml rewriting two, `clojure -M:clein pom` printing ten `Skipping coordinate` lines and writing a pom of four third-party deps and nothing else. Bead's count exact.

FIXED (7 of the 8 missing). epoch, routing, flows, schemas, resources, machines and machines-viz are all publishable (each target carries :aliases/:clein/build) and are now rewritten, through the shared comment-aware rewrite-local-root-coord.sh rather than the bespoke raw-text counter it replaces (the rf2-ldkuk shape). Generated pom after the rewrite: nine in-repo coordinates, all at lockstep 0.0.1.alpha, one Skipping line (freehand). None of the ten is dev/test-only — Xray's test-only coords live under :aliases and correctly never reach a pom — so the partition is publishable-vs-not, read structurally.

NOT FIXED, and not workable around: day8/re-frame2-freehand. Rewriting it would be WORSE than omitting it — the pom would name a GAV that cannot exist and the presence-based preflight would pass it to a registry with no yank. Left absent; preflight-xray-package.sh refuses the deploy naming it.

REACH IS WIDER THAN THE BEAD SAYS. tools/story/deps.edn declares day8/re-frame2-xray as a runtime coordinate and tools/story-mcp/ pins Story, so the Freehand edge blocks THREE of the five tool jars. Only machines-viz and mcp-base can ship independently of it.

THE RULING, three routes as costed in the PR:
 (1) Xray waits for Freehand's EP-0036 F6 publication. Nothing to do; blocks xray + story + story-mcp.
 (2) Late-bind the Freehand edge. Xray's only production require is day8.re-frame2-xray.mounted-views. The catch is Freehand-side: re-frame.freehand.tool is a leaf NOTHING in implementation/freehand/src requires, so late-bind hooks published from it would never load — something always-loaded in Freehand must pull the tool door in, which puts a dev-only namespace into the D021 production-bundle measurement. That is a change in Freehand's lane, not packaging.
 (3) Drop the Views panel's Mounted Views / Declared View Sites sections. Feature decision.

RECURRENCE GUARD ADDED. The tag-push preflight was the only shape gate, which is why the two-of-ten roster stayed green on every PR. implementation/scripts/_preflight-xray-package.test.cjs (new, in test:script-policy) derives coordinates from deps.edn and the roster from release-xray.yml and asserts every publishable coordinate is rewritten and no unpublishable one is — mutation-checked in both directions. It also gives the preflight its first suite.

DOCS CORRECTED: docs/release-process.md's open-question callout (described the pre-fix state), its release order (had xray as "core only" and in the same step as machines-viz), and CHANGELOG.md's tool-release claim.
RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-03 11:20 AUSEST (worker/toolsbugs-oztox, no code change). The
packaging half is on main and holds; nothing remains but the ruling, so this bead
stays OPEN and no commit was made against it.

Verified against the BUILD, not the bead:
- `clojure -M:clein pom` on the pristine tools/xray/deps.edn prints exactly TEN
  `Skipping coordinate` lines and writes a pom whose <dependencies> are FOUR
  third-party artefacts (clojure, zprint, reagent, editscript) and ZERO in-repo
  ones. The mechanism the bead names is reproducible today.
- The rewrite could NOT be exercised end-to-end locally: after
  rewrite-local-root-coord.sh pins the nine, `clein pom` cannot build a classpath
  ("Could not find artifact day8:re-frame2-routing:jar:0.0.1.alpha in central") —
  nothing is published at the lockstep version yet. That is expected, not a

- The assertion that WOULD have come from that pom is instead proved by the
  recurrence guard PR #7349 added: `node implementation/scripts/
  _preflight-xray-package.test.cjs` — 15/15, exit 0. It derives the coordinate
  set from deps.edn and the roster from release-xray.yml and pins, in both
  directions, "rewrites EVERY publishable in-repo coordinate", "rewrites NO
  unpublishable coordinate", "the two-coordinate rewrite fails — the shipping
  state rf2-5dut1 found", and "the nine-coordinate rewrite fails on Freehand
  ALONE".
- verify-version-lockstep.sh's TOOLS_LOCAL_ROOTS now inventories all TEN xray
  coordinates (bead body item 2 — closed), and cross-checks every roster entry
  against the set derived from the committed deps.edn.
- CHANGELOG.md and docs/release-process.md both now state plainly that xray-v*
  does not ship and what it blocks.

WHAT REMAINS IS EXACTLY ONE OPERATOR RULING — `day8/re-frame2-freehand`. The three
routes, unchanged from PR #7349's costing:

  (1) Xray waits for Freehand's EP-0036 F6 publication. Nothing to implement;
      blocks xray + story + story-mcp (3 of the 5 tool jars) indefinitely.
  (2) Late-bind the Freehand edge. Xray's only production require is
      day8.re-frame2-xray.mounted-views. The catch is Freehand-side:
      re-frame.freehand.tool is a leaf nothing in implementation/freehand/src
      requires, so hooks published from it would never load — something
      always-loaded in Freehand must pull the tool door in, which puts a dev-only
      namespace into the D021 production-bundle measurement. That is a change in

title: Freehand v/sub does not repaint inside react-dom/flushSync — its notification rides a microtask
description:
FOUND BY rf2-dq20a (the Freehand-vs-Reagent measurement), on the UIX adapter, in a real browser.

SYMPTOM. A mounted Freehand view whose body reads `(v/sub [...])` is NOT repainted by a state write made inside `react-dom/flushSync`. The store is written, the subscription recomputes, and React learns about it only after the current task's stack unwinds.

MEASURED, four ways, on one mounted 300-cell grid (implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b6_update_dom_cljs_test.cljs pins the first two as a regression test):

  flushSync(write)                                -> DOM UNCHANGED
  write; await one microtask; flushSync(noop)     -> DOM updated, ~1 ms
  write; setTimeout 0                             -> DOM updated, ~2 ms
  write; requestAnimationFrame                    -> DOM updated, ~32 ms (two frames)

Neither `frame/replace-app-db!`, `rf/dispatch-sync [...] {:frame fid}`, nor `(:dispatch-sync (rf/capture-frame fid))` commits inside the flush. Reagent (r/cursor + reagent.core/flush) and plain React (root.render inside flushSync) both commit in the same window.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE BENCH.
1. It is a real product property: a re-frame2/Freehand consumer cannot force a state change to the DOM synchronously through any public door. Anything that needs to read the DOM immediately after a write — a measurement, a scroll-into-view, a focus move, a test — has to yield a microtask first, and nothing documents that.
2. It cost this bead a whole measurement pass. The first update instrument timed each write inside flushSync and produced numbers for Freehand arms whose DOM never changed at all; only a DOM read-back inside the measured window caught it.
3. It is NOT the ratom-adapter bug. rf2-8cnxg / rf2-jt8vz record inert subscriptions under a ratom adapter. This is the UIX adapter, subscriptions are live, and the repaint does happen — one microtask late.

WANTED: either a documented synchronous-commit door (the equivalent of reagent.core/flush), or a spec sentence stating that Freehand commits are microtask-deferred and what a caller must do to observe one. Note the UIX adapter's own `flush-views!` did NOT commit the write when measured, and `react/act` did but cost ~600 ms a call.

Evidence: PR for rf2-dq20a; the four-way table is in the b6-update namespace docstring and pinned by `a-freehand-write-does-not-commit-inside-flushsync`.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7133. Root cause: cell/mark-dirty! schedules no React work, so react-dom/flushSync had nothing to commit. Fix: the pending window gains a second, React-visible closer (re-frame.freehand.checkpoint) armed by the same first mark and running the same idempotent cell/flush!; the microtask is untouched. All four measured cases pass in a real browser under the UIx adapter, plus the flushSync(dispatch-sync) door. Batching proven unchanged by an adversarial three-writes-in-one-task row. Follow-ons: rf2-mo5mk (Spec 006 sentence, hot-zone), rf2-0fgth (flip the b6 non-vacuity row that pins the broken behaviour).
