title: Bounded production-browser comparison: interpreted vs compiled Hiccup, with a keep/demote/remove recommendation
description:
OPERATOR RULING (Mike, 2026-07-26), quoted verbatim — this bead exists to execute the measurement half of it:

  "Reopen whether compiled Hiccup earns its permanent product cost. Pause discretionary compiler expansion
   and .182.6; common/interpreted correctness continues. D022 may use its already-accepted source-located
   compiled refusal rather than expanding lowering. Run one bounded production-browser comparison of
   interpreted versus compiled, including cell elision and bundle reachability, then return a keep/demote/
   remove recommendation. Profile before optimizing the interpreter. Do not build another syntax
   experiment."

THE DELIVERABLE IS A RECOMMENDATION: keep / demote / remove. Not a fix, not an optimisation, not a verb.

SCOPE — ONE bounded comparison, in a PRODUCTION BROWSER, covering at minimum:
  - interpreted versus compiled Hiccup on the same view
  - CELL ELISION — what the compiled tier actually elides that the interpreted tier does not
  - BUNDLE REACHABILITY — what each tier drags into an :advanced bundle

HARD BOUNDARIES from the ruling: do NOT build another syntax experiment (v/$ is settled as a non-goal — see rf2-drpa3.182.2 and docs/design/freehand/studio/er-01-architecture-comparison.md). Do NOT optimise the interpreter as part of this; PROFILE FIRST, and any optimisation is a separate bead after the recommendation lands.

WHY NOW: the ER-01 spike measured allocation on the JVM structural emitter and put compiled at 1.000 against interpreted 1.244, but stated plainly that the REACT HOST WAS NOT MEASURED and named that as the one avenue that could reopen the performance half. This bead measures that avenue.

MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE, learned expensively in this repo:
  - Wall-clock is unreliable here under concurrent load — the same primitive measured 10.4ns and 21.7ns in two JVMs. The ER-01 spike used getThreadAllocatedBytes and got min = p50 = max in nearly every arm. Prefer allocation; quote wall-clock only as a direction WITH the observed spread stated. That spike refused to give a wall-clock percentage because a 7-point spread on a 5-point effect does not support one — copy that refusal.
  - For BUNDLE questions, two naive oracles are both wrong: counting goog.DEBUG fails (225 occurrences survived a release where the surface was fully eliminated — docstrings carried in by var reification) and grepping function names fails for small functions (Closure inlines them). STRING LITERALS are the reliable sentinel, and a two-bundle control is INSUFFICIENT — you need a THIRD bundle with the tier absent, or a sibling namespace vocabulary reads as a survivor.
  - Interleave arms, clear the cache before each build, and state the method before the numbers.

DO NOT COMMIT THE SCAFFOLDING. The ER-01 worker committed its four measurement arms so an outage could not lose them, then DELETED them before the PR, and proved the deletion took the scaffolding and nothing else by showing the CLJS delta was exactly its one parity deftest. Copy that.
notes:
OPERATOR RULING (Mike, 2026-07-26) — KEEP, on a DIFFERENT rationale from the report. Quoted verbatim:

  "We will keep the compiler because there will be performance critical applications not seen yet,
   where 3x performance is essential."

HOW THIS RELATES TO THE REPORT VERDICT. The report also said KEEP, but explicitly on ELISION grounds and with the headline "stop describing it as a performance tier". The operator keeps it FOR performance, on the unseen-application argument. Both land on KEEP; the rationale differs, and the operator rationale governs.

THE MEASURED BASIS FOR THE 3x, so nobody later treats it as folklore: compiled beats the TUNED interpreter 3.35x on 300 SUB-FREE boundaries, 1.22x on 100 REACTIVE ones, and is INSEPARABLE on an ordinary form (1.054, spread straddling 1.0). Updates were a null result on every arm. So the 3x is real and is specific to the sub-free-boundary shape — which is precisely the shape a performance-critical application would exhibit. The operator argument is that such applications exist but are not yet in the corpus, and no measurement here can refute that: every witness in the repo is one we chose.

WHAT THIS RULING DOES NOT DO. It does not retire the report other findings, which stand as measured: no application in the repo declares a compiled view; Xray reads the DONOR compiler; Story consumer is test-only; MCP manifest read serves interpreted views too; and the best defect the analyzer once caught exclusively is no longer exclusive because the fix taught the interpreter to refuse it too. Those remain true and remain the reason the non-elision parts of the tier are unpriced.

STILL LIVE AND STILL THE OPERATOR CALL: the report named the single change most likely to undermine KEEP — an opt-in {:reactive false} CHECKED rather than proven, which would take most of the measured advantage at a fraction of the cost. Under the new rationale that option is MORE interesting, not less: if a checked flag delivers the 3x for performance-critical applications without the compiler permanent cost, the unseen-application argument would point at it instead. Uninvestigated.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7032 (merge 6c35e4ec9b4d6551e255dc5e3f7c22d50a111f45, merged 2026-07-25T21:45:28Z) — exact owner reopened; no duplicate. Completeness: the requested production-browser report, three realistic witnesses, shipped/equal-semantics analysis, profiling-before-tuning, product-cost ledger, real-consumer census, bundle controls, recommendation, and scaffolding deletion are all present. The caller-key-slot cache is bounded and behavior-preserving over the same total name projection as before; all six authored commits landed exactly and checks were 41 pass/34 intentional skips/0 fail. Correctness residual: the report repeatedly says W2 and W2r differ only in reactivity and that the whole 3.35x-vs-1.22x contrast is ViewCell elision. The recoverable landed fixtures disprove that isolation: probe.cljs sets w2-free=300 and w2-reads=100; w2-free renders a literal leaf while w2-read additionally executes (str (v/sub [:studio/tick])); and W2r has no React-floor arm. Comparing speedup ratios across different boundary counts plus added common subscription/string work cannot assign the entire difference to elision. The 3.35x elidable-witness result and KEEP recommendation remain real, but the exclusive causal claim is not measured. Bounded completion: either run a same-count same-leaf ablation that forces the compiled ViewCell kept versus elided, with the same in-run floor where applicable, or qualify the report and rf2-xu6rx so the contrast is evidence consistent with elision rather than proof that elision is the whole delta.
AUDIT-REOPEN OBLIGATION DISCHARGED — the ablation was run, not a qualification written. PR #7112 (docs-only, one file).

The audit's finding was correct: W2 vs W2r varied THREE things (300 vs 100 boundaries, literal leaf vs (str (v/sub ...)), and no floor arm on W2r), so the 3.35x-vs-1.22x contrast could not assign the difference to elision.

THE ABLATION. react.cljs/compiled-component selects its wrapper from the manifest's :view-cell verdict 'and by nothing else', so the arm is leaf-free's own descriptor with that one entry flipped to :present — same compiled body OBJECT (asserted identical?, not assumed), same props, same 300 boundaries, same canonical DOM (gated, agree? true in all 12 rounds). free-ik - free-ic is 300 ViewCells and nothing else; free-i - free-ik is interpretation and nothing else. Base is post-#7077, so the interpreted arm is faster than any interpreter the report measured.

  RETAINED HEAP (6 rounds, 10 roots x 300 boundaries held live, CDP sampler AND performance.memory occupancy agreeing to 2%, ~4.7 MB positive control each round):
    one kept ViewCell                                   2348 B per boundary (2295 by occupancy)
    free-ik / free-ic  ViewCell kept vs elided          6.256
    free-i  / free-ik  interpreted vs compiled, both keep 1.011
    read-i  / read-ic  reactive leaf, neither may elide  1.003

  WALL CLOCK (12 interleaved rounds, fresh process each, floor-normalised in-run; floor drift 58%):
    free-ik / free-ic  the ViewCell alone     1.712 [1.583-1.879]
    free-i  / free-ik  interpretation alone   1.216 [1.092-1.425]
    free-i  / free-ic  the two together       2.079 [1.896-2.419]
    read-i  / read-ic  neither may elide      1.045 [0.922-1.173]  STRADDLES 1.0
  Decomposition closes: 1.712 x 1.216 = 2.082 vs measured 2.079. Elision is 73% of the log-effect.

VERDICT ON THE AUDIT'S QUESTION. 'The whole difference is the ViewCell' is right about which term dominates and wrong to claim all of it. On RETAINED HEAP it is exactly right (1.011). On the CLOCK elision is the dominant but not the only term — interpretation contributes a real 1.216 whose range excludes 1.0.

TWO HEADLINE FIGURES REVISED, and this is the consequential part: 3.35x -> 2.079x, and 1.22x -> 1.045 (inseparable). Both moved toward 1.0 for two compounding reasons — the counts and leaves now match, and the interpreter is post-#7077. The 3.35x was not wrong when taken; it is no longer the number. Anywhere the '3x' is quoted, the wall-clock figure is 2.08x.

KEEP IS UNTOUCHED and the operator rationale is undisturbed — every witness here is still one we chose. What the ablation ADDS is that the memory case is stronger and far better conditioned than the time case: 6.26x with disjoint ranges and two agreeing instruments, against 2.08x on a clock whose own floor drifts 58%. If the tier is defended on performance, standing heap per elidable boundary is the number to defend it with.

METHOD FINDING worth more than the numbers: the recovered driver's PRIMARY instrument was measuring nothing. Its header claimed 'allocation is a counter, not an occupancy sample: a collection inside the window cannot make it smaller'. FALSE — V8's sampling heap profiler DROPS the samples of collected objects. The same 80,000 objects report 4.77 MB when a global holds them and 0.00 MB when nothing does. Pointed at a mount/unmount loop it was reporting the residue of a discarded page; that is why every arm came back at 10-25 KB for a 301-element React tree. A positive control of KNOWN SIZE, IN SITU, is now the first thing the retained-heap mode does.

DECLINED, on the report's own refusal discipline: no CPU-time split. Three repeats of the same pair returned free-i/free-ik = 1.81, 0.85, 1.85.

Scaffolding committed for durability then DELETED before the PR; branch diff is the one doc. Findings doc (local-only, NEVER commit or link): ai/findings/2026-07-26.hiccup-elision-ablation-same-count-same-leaf.md

FOLLOW-UP BEADS: rf2-h4j7k ({:reactive false} checked opt-out — operator call, stakes now exact)
FOLLOW-UP BEADS (running list): rf2-h4j7k ({:reactive false} checked opt-out — operator call), rf2-9oj7v (B2 prices elision in retained bytes, not just counts).
close_reason:
AUDIT-REOPEN obligation discharged by running the ablation, not by qualifying the report. PR #7112 (docs-only, one file: docs/design/freehand/studio/compiled-tier-browser-worth-it.md 1a).

The audit offered two exits and this took the harder one. Same 300 boundaries on both witnesses, same leaf body, a floor arm each, and the compiled body OBJECT asserted identical? between the ViewCell-kept and ViewCell-elided arms — so free-ik - free-ic is 300 ViewCells and nothing else.

Elision is the dominant term but not the whole of it on the clock (1.712 of a 2.079 total, 73% of the log-effect, with a real 1.216 from interpretation whose range excludes 1.0) and IS the whole of it on retained heap (1.011 once both tiers keep a cell). Two headline figures revised: 3.35x -> 2.079x and 1.22x -> inseparable. KEEP untouched; the memory case (6.26x, 2348 B of standing heap per boundary, two agreeing instruments, disjoint ranges) is stronger and better conditioned than the time case.

Follow-ups filed: rf2-h4j7k ({:reactive false} checked opt-out, operator call, stakes now exact), rf2-9oj7v (B2 prices elision in retained bytes rather than only counting it). rf2-xu6rx qualified in place per the audit's wording. Method lesson recorded via bd remember (the CDP heap sampler reports retained, not allocated).

Findings doc, local-only, never commit or link: ai/findings/2026-07-26.hiccup-elision-ablation-same-count-same-leaf.md

title: Control witness: first-party typeahead with anchored popover
description:
OUTCOME
Deliver the first post-field control witness: a versioned first-party typeahead with an anchored menu/popover, proving reusable control and host-boundary laws without starting a widget catalogue.

USER SURFACE
A short ordinary Freehand/re-frame call site with explicit value/query/selection intents, public props and semantic parts, controlled ownership, and optional vendorable skin. Protocol-critical state transitions and accessibility behavior remain versioned.

LAWS
Correlation and supersession fence stale async replies; debounce/timing uses existing explicit mechanisms unless evidence proves a missing primitive; composing input does not commit; keyboard/pointer/focus/dismiss behavior is real-browser proven; open/query/selection live in app-db while geometry/observers stay host-private; cleanup is total.

HOST/MODE
Pure transition tests, JVM structure, interpreted browser, compiled parity or an explicit source-located limitation, SSR fallback/structure where applicable.

CANONICAL OWNERS
Product-completion DC-04 and ER-05; D003/D004/D009/D013/D015-D018; spec/004-Views.md, 008, 009 and applicable FH-CTRL/FH-INPUT/FH-TOPLAYER/FH-BEHAVIOR rows.

NON-GOALS
No generic async engine, geometry DSL, universal listbox framework, generic put/merge/toggle events, or catalogue commitment.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Real-browser proof covers keyboard navigation, pointer choice, focus return, dismissal, IME, stale reply, retry, and exact listener/observer cleanup.
2. Anchoring uses platform top layer/CSS anchors where fit and an established focused positioning engine for collision rather than Freehand geometry.
3. Interpreted/compiled structure and event semantics agree or the limitation is explicit.
4. The workshop, guide, Xray and API/parts contract project one fixture identity.
5. Measured work at the async/positioning edge is published without inventing new scheduling policy.
notes:
PROJECTION PASS — PR #7244 (worker/witness-project-1828), opened green locally. STAYS IN_PROGRESS: acceptance 4 is not fully dischargeable, and the reason is structural rather than effort. Corrects the delivery note's stale id: this is FH-CTRL-020 (019 is the splitter, rf2-drpa3.182.10).

ACCEPTANCE 1 — DISCHARGED. The audit's missing clause was retry in the browser (grep -c retry on the mounted suite was 0). New mounted row fh-ctrl-020-a-retry-is-a-real-button-and-supersedes-the-failure-it-retries never names :kit.ui.typeahead/retried — it waits for the failure to render a real <button data-part="retry">, CLICKS it, asserts the new correlation, then lets the failed request answer LATE against a live mounted control (opens nothing) while the retry's own answer opens the list. The answer sets differ in length, so the option ids tell them apart. MUTATION: repointing the button's :on-click at :kit.ui.typeahead/toggle-reported reds EXACTLY ONE test, this one; the structural retry row stays green, which is precisely the gap it fills. Restored blob-identical.

ACCEPTANCE 3 — DISCHARGED AS AN EXPLICIT, FALSIFIABLE LIMITATION. There is still no compiled twin, and the docstring claiming one is FIXED. v/check — the grammar's own read-only checker — was run and answers: typeahead ELIGIBLE? false, :rf.ui.compile/loop-capturing-handler on [:kit.ui.typeahead/chosen k g i on-select], recovery [:keep-interpreted] (one rung); reviewer-form ELIGIBLE? true. The option's commit is an event site inside the `for` and closes over the loop's `i`; a compiled site is lexical. That verdict is now a VALUE in the fixture (:compiled) and an ASSERTION in the structural suite under #?(:clj …), so the limitation goes RED the day the grammar grows a per-item lexical site rather than outliving its reason.

ACCEPTANCE 4 — HALF DISCHARGED; THE OTHER HALF IS BLOCKED BY THE EPIC'S OWN SCOPE DECISION, NOT BY EFFORT. Guide: docs/core/freehand/advanced/semantic-controllers.md §Async search / typeahead now names FH-CTRL-020 as the packaged version's executable home, with the anchoring / composing-Enter / no-timer-to-cancel facts and the compiled limit. Workshop already projected. XRAY AND API/PARTS CANNOT, for ONE shared cause: the witness is test-only because promoting a control onto the published door is the API-manifest serial lane and this bead deliberately did not take it. spec/api-manifest.edn is GENERATED and drift-checked from real public vars, so it cannot carry a var that does not exist; Xray's Freehand surface is a shipped testbed deck reading re-frame.freehand.tool and cannot reach test/. Both see shipped code only. Additionally no FH-* id appears under tools/ for ANY row, so there is no convention to follow either. DECISION NEEDED FROM MIKE: either promote the typeahead onto the published door (which discharges both surfaces and is the serial-lane call), or amend acceptance 4 to the surfaces a test-only witness can reach.

FENCED OUT, worth a follow-up: spec/004-Views.md#the-first-party-control-kit — the paragraph this row cites — carries **Conformance:** FH-CTRL-016, FH-CTRL-017 and does not cite FH-CTRL-020 back. One-line hot-zone edit.

GATES (foreground, exit echoed): freehand JVM clojure -M:test exit 0 (1285/8809, was 1284/8803); npm run test:browser exit 0 (842/5469, was 841/5459); check_freehand_conformance_index.py exit 0; python -m mkdocs build --strict exit 0; guide digest roster exit 0.
close_reason:
CLOSED — FREEHAND IS A FAILED EXPERIMENT (Mike, 2026-07-30). Verbatim ruling: close out the Freehand EPIC as a failed experiment, no further work to be done on it, but not removed yet.

WHY IT FAILED. The Reagent standard (rf2-lbs3y, Mike 2026-07-27: 'Freehand can't be used if it is slower than Reagent') was not met, and the residual gap is architectural rather than an optimisation backlog. Interpreted Freehand measured ~5x Reagent on bulk repaint and ~1.6x on mount.

DO NOT REPEAT THE SUPERSEDED REASON. An earlier summary said the cost WAS the invariant-5 tear check. rf2-so3io / PR #7159 falsified that by ablation: dropping useSyncExternalStore AND the commit-side re-read returned only -13.6%/-14.8% on the broad clock and -375 B heap, and a contract-free boundary was still ~5.5x Reagent on clock and ~5x on heap. The guarantee was not what cost us — and the same ablation found invariant 5 is worth MORE than Spec 006 claims, since a staged site without it publishes stale and never self-heals.

THE CODE STAYS. 'Not removed yet.' No implementation/freehand/** deletion, no build-id removal, no CI lane or roster change. The Freehand prod-gate lane (137 of 137, roster empty) keeps running until an explicit removal ruling.

NORMATIVE HALF: rf2-lgleu (P1) records the withdrawal in the EP corpus — EP-0036 moves to Status: withdrawn per EP-0009's closed vocabulary, and the six EPs citing Freehand stop implying it is live.

DO NOT re-file this work as follow-ups. The programme is retracted, not paused.

description:

title: Freehand forms foundation: pure transitions, field, buffered-field, owner clear
description:
OUTCOME
Ship the first Freehand form/control product slice: pure CLJC transitions in re-frame.freehand.form plus field, buffered-field, and one causal owner-clear operation in re-frame.freehand.controls.

PUBLIC CONTRACT
Start with init/edit/visit/seed/reset/rebase/set-errors/attempt-submit/reset-key. Model baseline, draft, visited, edited, per-leaf reset revisions, errors, submit attempt/status, vector leaf paths, stable domain ids, and causal owner. Keep operations side-effect-free; applications own event registration, validation policy, app-db placement, and rendering.

LAWS
Seed is leafwise and preserves edited/unrelated state; reset and rebase differ; invalid submit reveals errors; stale async and buffered operations are inert; composing Enter does not commit; narrow fields need not subscribe to the whole draft; owner clear removes form plus owned controllers atomically and is never inferred from unmount.

HOST/MODE
Pure CLJC/JVM first, interpreted and compiled structural parity, real-browser controlled/buffered input including caret/selection/IME/reset. Public namespaces participate in the API-manifest serial lane.

CANONICAL OWNERS
Product-completion DC-03/DC-04 and ER-04/ER-05; D003, D004, D009, D016, D017; spec/004-Views.md, 008, 009, API/Ownership and FH-CTRL/FH-INPUT plus any narrowly allocated form rows.

NON-GOALS
No form runtime, atom, validator engine, schema renderer, generic local store, unmount cleanup, full re-com port, or widget catalogue.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Pure transition tests cover nested late seed, keyed rows, visited vs edited, reset/rebase, invalid submit, pending save, stale result, and exact owner clear.
2. field and buffered-field present short ordinary re-frame call sites and pass same-tick, same-value reset, caret, selection, IME, HMR, retry, and stale-cancel browser proofs.
3. One serious executable form fixture proves narrow render dependencies and exact cleanup.
4. Public docs/spec/API/conformance and guide source land with the code.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #7091 — exact forms owner reopened; no duplicate. Two public-function witnesses violate the landed pure-model contract. (1) Seed overlap: `(-> (form/init {:contact {:email "base"}}) (form/edit [:contact :email] "typed") (form/seed {:contact {}}))` answers draft `{:contact {}}` while `:edited` still contains `[:contact :email]`. leaf-entries deliberately treats an empty map as a leaf, and seed protects only exact path membership, so an ancestor leaf from the payload wipes an edited descendant (the reverse shape change can likewise overwrite an edited ancestor). This contradicts “edited leaves survive” and leaves the edit marker describing data no longer present. Make seed define and enforce overlap semantics, with ancestor/descendant witnesses, without replacing its simple leafwise model with a runtime. (2) Scoped reset of a draft-only leaf: `(form/reset (form/edit (form/init {}) [:nickname] "typed") [:nickname])` answers draft `{:nickname nil}` rather than `{}` because get-in cannot distinguish an absent baseline key from a baseline nil and assoc-in always materializes it. The contract says reset discards back to baseline; preserve absent-vs-nil exactly, including nested paths, and pin both cases. The missing FH-CTRL-018 merge tail is already resolved by #7095 and is not reopened here.

Therefore a broken implementation that reads only `isComposing` stays green: the test never exercises the stated Chromium fallback where `isComposing` is false/absent and `keyCode` alone is 229. The planted mutation `(composing? e) -> false` disables every signal and cannot establish this branch. Add a separate real-browser keydown with `isComposing` false (and native flag absent/false) plus `keyCode 229`, retaining the plain-Enter positive barrier so the listener remains non-vacuous; pin the complementary native-event-only path if that compatibility branch is part of the public promise. title: [BUG] :rf.resource/route-plan's :blocking / :identities scoped keys escape the resources off-box egress projector
description:
Found by rf2-wsopx while verifying the `:rf.resource/route-plan` tag roster against
its emitting site (PR #7011). Documentation-only bead; this is the runtime half.

THE GAP. `:rf.resource/route-plan`'s activation shape carries TWO slots that are
VECTORS OF SCOPED RESOURCE KEYS — `:blocking` and `:identities`
(implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc:1091-1092). A scoped
resource key is `[scope resource-id canonical-params]`, so both slots carry the
resolved SCOPE and the CANONICAL PARAMS of every requirement in the plan.

The resource family's off-box egress projector
(implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/trace_egress.cljc) exists precisely
to tokenize those through the resource OWNER classification. Its `scoped-keys-slot`
vocabulary (:127-137) is:

  #{:resource/keys :matched :removed :keys :exempt :committed :patched :populated
    :invalidated :restored :conflicted :refetched :restored-keys :conflicted-keys
    :refetched-keys :reconciliation-refetches :affected-keys}

NEITHER `:blocking` NOR `:identities` is in it.

The projector DOES run on this row — `project-resource-trace-egress` is applied to
every resource-family op (`resource-family-op?` is operation-agnostic,
implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1493-1497). And the
fail-closed default added by rf2-7qbxbm covers only MAP-valued unknown slots
(trace_egress.cljc:334); a SEQUENTIAL unknown value falls through to the verbatim
`:else` at :337. So a `:sensitive?` / `:large?` / derived-sensitive / unregistered
owner's scope and params egress RAW on this row, where the very same scoped keys
under `:matched` or `:keys` would tokenize to `{:rf/redacted <digest>}`.

WHY THE SLOT VOCABULARY MISSED THEM. The vocabulary was enumerated from the
events/mutation/reconcile rows (its own docstring lists exactly those families).
`:rf.resource/route-plan`'s `:blocking` / `:identities` slots are EP-0037 R1/R2
additions to a row that predates the projector, and the projector is keyed on slot
NAME rather than on value SHAPE, so a new scoped-key-bearing slot name is silently
uncovered. That is the class to fix, not just the two instances.

ADJACENT HAZARD, CHECKED AND BENIGN. `:removed` IS in `scoped-keys-slot`, and this
row carries `:removed` as an INT count, not a key vector (route.cljc:1090). The
`(sequential? v)` guard at :259 means it falls through harmlessly. No bug — but it
is evidence that the row and the projector were written against different mental
models of what `:removed` means, which is worth a comment wherever this is fixed.

WHAT THE WARM SHAPE DOES. `route-resource-warm-plan` (route.cljc:1236-1241) carries
NEITHER slot, so the warm-mode prefetch row is unaffected.

REPAIR (small, one file):
1. Add `:blocking` and `:identities` to `scoped-keys-slot` in
   `resources/trace_egress.cljc`, with a comment naming this bead and stating that
   they are `:rf.resource/route-plan`'s plan-membership slots.
2. Extend the projector's own tests with a `:rf.resource/route-plan` row over a
   `:sensitive?` owner, asserting BOTH slots tokenize per-key (so a tool's per-key
   joins survive) and the row is stamped `:sensitive? true`.
3. Consider — and this is the real question, so RULE it rather than assume — whether
   the fail-closed default should extend from map-valued unknown slots to
   VECTOR-OF-VECTOR-valued unknown slots. That would close the class rather than the
   instance: any future scoped-key-bearing slot name would fail closed instead of
   riding verbatim. The counterweight is over-redaction of legitimate scalar-vector
   slots (`:branch` is a vector of route ids on this very row and MUST ride
   verbatim; `:invalidated-tags` likewise), so a shape test alone is not sufficient
   discrimination and the guard would need to be "vector whose members are vectors"
   at minimum. My recommendation: do (1) + (2) now, and treat (3) as a separate
   design decision.

DO NOT widen the 009 documentation for this — PR #7011 already documents both slots
as scoped-key vectors, which is what makes the gap legible. This bead is the runtime

title: F6c: migrate Xray's view instrumentation onto re-frame.freehand.tool - the ownership/receipt plane has no Freehand counterpart
description:
Split out of F6c (rf2-drpa3.55) after survey: this is a bead-sized architectural change, not a rename, and doing it half-way would ship a panel that displays facts Freehand does not have.

WHAT XRAY READS TODAY. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/viewcell_evidence.cljs (466 lines) requires [re-frame.ui.tool] AND [re-frame.ui.tool.evidence]. Its whole reason for existing is an OWNERSHIP/RECEIPT ledger layered over the donor evidence tier's install/uninstall registry: evidence/install!, evidence/uninstall!, evidence/installed-owner, evidence/force-release!, plus a per-span opaque receipt fencing every read against a same-key ABA reclaim, plus an ownership-revision reactive bridge into Xray's own :rf/xray app-db (panels/reactive_panel_subs.cljs).

WHY IT IS NOT A RENAME. re-frame.freehand.tool has NO registry and NO ownership plane, deliberately and permanently - its own docstring says 'There is no accumulator... no root registry, no interval log and no history store' and names rf2-drpa3.167 as having ruled the donor accumulator out permanently rather than deferred it. So none of install!/uninstall!/installed-owner/force-release! has a counterpart, and the receipt fence protects against a hazard that cannot occur. The ownership plane and its reactive-revision bridge should be DELETED, not ported.

AND THE PANEL'S VOCABULARY CHANGES. viewcell_evidence/project-occurrence shapes rows around :count (lifetime render total), :batches, :first-epoch, :latest-epoch, :lifecycle (hide-vs-unmount interval log), :targets + :targets-exact?, :dropped-count + :dropped-exact?. Every one of those is a fact rf2-drpa3.167 named as DELIBERATE FIDELITY LOSS. reactive_panel_view.cljs:647-760 renders them, including a literal 'Cumulative per-incarnation render evidence' label. Freehand's read-mounted-views gives current-state rows (:view-id :occurrence :lowering :generation :connection :root :dispatch-id :at :commit, with :occurrence-facts naming the closed set) and explain-render gives a bounded read-time fold with :cap / :uncorrelated loss and :candidates as leads. The panel must be re-authored to those, showing honest absence where a lifetime figure used to sit - per the ruling, degrading a missing fact to an explicit unknown SATISFIES acceptance 2; fabricating one does not.

ALSO. The consumer-owned version pin moves from the integer expected-schema-version 3 (:rf.ui.tool/version) to :re-frame.freehand.evidence/v1 (:schema), exactly as pair-mcp did in the first F6c increment - see that PR for the shape.

SCOPE (ledger rows). tools/xray/deps.edn (drop the day8/re-frame2-ui coordinate), viewcell_evidence.cljs, panels/reactive_panel_{view,subs}.cljs, test/viewcell_evidence_cljs_test.cljs (682 lines), test/realworld_ui_evidence_cljs_test.cljs, tools/xray/spec/* - and per standing rule every dispatch touching tools/xray/ updates tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR. tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs mounts donor views and is a separate row.

SEQUENCING NOTE. realworld_ui_evidence_cljs_test.cljs reads a donor-authored example under examples/, whose migration is a carved-out parallel bead - sequence after it, or repoint the test at a Freehand fixture.
notes:
OPERATOR RULING (Mike, 2026-07-26), quoted verbatim across the two messages that settle it:

  "But xray and story should not be using the donor, they should be across onto freehand"
  "We intend to remove the donor (re-frame.ui)"

THIS SETTLES THE GATE. Both of the F6c gate beads asked the same either/or: build the Freehand counterpart, or retire the seam with the donor. The answer is BUILD THE COUNTERPART AND CROSS OVER. The donor is going (rf2-drpa3.57 / F6e deletes implementation/ui wholesale), so a tool still reading it is not a stable position — it is a dependency on an artefact scheduled for deletion.

WHAT IT UNBLOCKS: rf2-drpa3.55 (F6c) has been in_progress and gated on exactly these two. F6c releases F6d (rf2-drpa3.56, the donor inventory ledger to zero) which releases F6e (rf2-drpa3.57, the deletion). That chain has sat at 97.3% all session with no dispatchable work in it.

WHAT THE RULING DOES NOT SAY, and workers must not infer it: it does not say the Freehand counterpart must reproduce the donor design. Both beads record that Freehand DELIBERATELY AND PERMANENTLY lacks the donor evidence registry and ownership plane. Crossing over means serving the need through what Freehand actually offers, and where a donor-shaped fact has no Freehand counterpart, saying so explicitly rather than inventing a registry. rf2-drpa3.167 already records several such facts as deliberate loss.

ALSO SETTLED TODAY AND RELEVANT: the compiled tier is KEPT, for performance, as a SPECIALISED requirement — the paved path stays interpreted. And the absence of a current consumer is explicitly NOT disqualifying for this class of work; the operator reasoning is that value accrues to applications not yet seen.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7038 (2026-07-26) — REOPENED: schema-4 live upgrade deletes the donor plane from source but does not tear down the plane an already-running schema-3 process owns.

EVIDENCE. Before this PR, preload/core acquired re-frame.ui.tool.evidence under :rf.xray/viewcell-evidence. That install arms the donor reactive sink and preserves owner, retained entries and generation in defonce state; the Xray wrapper separately preserves its receipt, ownership listener and globalThis sentinel in defonce state. Schema 4 explicitly exists for no-reload upgrades from schema 3, but migrate-schema! only calls reactive-panel/install-mounted-views-subs!. It never calls the old release-current!/uninstall!, clears the old ownership listener/sentinel, or unregisters the obsolete :rf.xray/viewcell-evidence, :rf.xray/viewcell-evidence-version, :rf.xray/view-evidence-sites, :rf.xray/viewcell-evidence-ownership and :rf.xray/viewcell-evidence-ownership-changed handlers. Removing the namespace/require does not execute teardown in an already-loaded HMR process; every former teardown call was removed from preload, core and test-support.

IMPACT. Until a full page reload, Xray still owns and runs the donor sink, retains the donor span, leaves its sentinel visible, and rejects another tool attempting to claim the slot. The old handlers/listener also remain process-resident. That contradicts this bead's central completion claim that the ownership plane was deleted and Xray holds no state, and it makes the documented schema-4 no-reload migration incomplete precisely on the stateful boundary it removes.

ACCEPTANCE. Add a schema-3 -> schema-4 upgrade proof starting from a genuinely acquired donor span and installed old bridge. After register-xray-handlers! migrates, assert the Freehand subs work; donor installed-owner and installed-sink are nil; Xray's old listener/sentinel are cleared; all five obsolete registrar ids are absent; a different donor-tool owner can acquire immediately; and a second schema-4 call is idempotent. If cross-generation teardown is intentionally reload-only, remove the no-reload schema-4 claim and force/document a reload instead of stamping the live process current over resident donor state.

The separate lack of a populated Freehand-hosted browser row is already tracked by rf2-6pohj; no duplicate was created.

title: Configure the beads Dolt remote (operator action)
description:
FOLLOW-UP from the .beads guard work. This is layer 4 of that bead and is OPERATOR ACTION — it cannot be done or verified from a worker worktree, which is why it was carved out rather than attempted.

THE WORK: configure the Dolt remote for the beads database so tracker state has a durable home independent of the git-tracked JSONL export, and confirm bd dolt push / bd dolt pull round-trip.

WHY IT MATTERS: the JSONL export is a mirror, not the source of truth. Today a git-side accident is recoverable only because Dolt still holds the real state locally; without a configured remote there is no off-box copy.

ACCEPTANCE: bd dolt push succeeds; bd dolt pull round-trips on a second checkout; the configuration is recorded somewhere durable rather than living only in one machine's local config.

ASSIGNEE: Mike (operator). Do not dispatch a background worker at this.
notes:
OPERATOR-OWNED DECISION BEAD (Mike, 2026-07-26): one of six to be taken one at a time — rf2-ayq3v, rf2-9sluz, rf2-mhrwq, rf2-o0agl, rf2-4l67v, rf2-2ii52. Do NOT dispatch; do NOT re-surface as a ready-queue candidate.
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-27, dossier review): ROUTE = dedicated private GitHub repository as the Dolt origin, over HTTPS — github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads — per the Codex second opinion in the dossier. NOT DoltHub (the dossier's original recommendation), NOT a self/file-based remote, NOT nothing. Pre-authorized fallback: if the initial push trips GitHub's 2 GiB per-push ceiling, switch the same origin to a private DoltHub repo and accept the $50/month — do not build split-push tooling. Timing: before the alpha tag.

WHY (facts re-verified 2026-07-27 against the installed bd 1.0.3 and primary sources):
- DoltHub private storage is free only up to 1 GB/month, then $50/month (dolthub.com/docs/concepts/dolthub/permissions/ — fetched today). The live embedded DB measures ~1.8 GiB, so the DoltHub route costs $50/month from day one. A private GitHub repo is free, the same vendor/trust shape that already holds the code, and this machine's GitHub HTTPS credentials already work (SSH currently fails).
- Git-backed Dolt remotes are first-class in bd 1.0.3, not a trick: the installed `bd bootstrap --help` lists both "If sync.remote is configured: clones from the remote" and "If git origin has Dolt data (refs/dolt/data): clones from git". Dolt stores git-backed data under refs/dolt/data; ordinary source clones never fetch that ref, so a DEDICATED repo keeps ~1.8 GiB out of the code repo entirely.
- Current origin is file://C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/.beads/backup/origin (~3.7 GiB) — same disk, same checkout, gitignored. That is not durability; it is what this ruling replaces.
- The remote must be PRIVATE: the Dolt DB carries ~15K historical event rows including old/new values — more history than the public JSONL mirror exposes.
- Rejected: self/file-based off-box storage (setup + credential overhead matches or exceeds DoltHub with fewer affordances); doing nothing (standing single-disk loss of all tracker + ruling history, and a session-close protocol mandating a push with nowhere to go).

OPERATOR RUNBOOK (~15 min, mayor checkout):
1. Create an empty private repo: `gh repo create day8/re-frame2-beads --private` (no README — Dolt data lives under refs/dolt/data).
2. `bd dolt remote remove origin` then `bd dolt remote add origin https://github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads.git`; confirm with `bd dolt show`.
3. `bd dolt push` — the first push uploads ~1.8 GiB, let it run to completion. Verify off-box: `git ls-remote https://github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads.git` must list refs/dolt/data. [acceptance 1]
4. Durable config: check `bd config get sync.remote` and `git diff .beads/config.yaml` — bd should record sync.remote in the tracked config.yaml; if it did not, run `bd config set sync.remote https://github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads.git` and confirm the tracked-file diff. Commit config.yaml via the normal path (it is committable human-authored .beads config; do NOT hand-commit issues.jsonl outside the checkpoint script). [acceptance 3]
5. Round-trip in a genuinely separate fresh clone — NOT a worktree (a worktree can resolve the mayor's database): `git clone https://github.com/day8/re-frame2.git <tmpdir>`, then inside it `bd bootstrap --yes` followed by `bd dolt pull`; verify `bd show rf2-4l67v` displays this ruling and `bd dolt show` matches the primary checkout. Delete the tmp clone afterwards. [acceptance 2]
6. FALLBACK if step 3 fails on the 2 GiB per-push ceiling: create a private DoltHub repo, repoint the same origin (`bd dolt remote remove origin` / `bd dolt remote add origin <dolthub-url>`), accept the $50/month, re-run steps 3-5 (recording the DoltHub URL as sync.remote in step 4).
7. Optional cleanup once acceptance passes: delete the old same-disk file remote .beads/backup/origin (~3.7 GiB) to reclaim disk. The JSONL checkpoint remains the cheap human-inspectable recovery floor. Do NOT add a second cloud remote, scheduled backup system, or remote-management abstraction.

Bead stays OPEN, assigned to Mike; close when acceptance 1-3 pass.
DOSSIER REVIEW (2026-07-28): ruling unchanged — route stays a dedicated private GitHub repo (day8/re-frame2-beads) over HTTPS as the Dolt origin, DoltHub fallback, executed before the alpha tag. The dossier's Codex second opinion concurs with the ruled route on every point (GitHub first, one push as the go/no-go, no dual remotes, no split-push tooling) and its mechanics claims all re-verified today against the installed bd 1.0.3 (1b2dd2cb): sync.remote still unset, origin still the same-disk file://.../.beads/backup/origin, embedded DB 1,864,657,504 bytes (~1.74 GiB), file remote ~3.97 GB (step 7's reclaim figure stands).
ONE VERIFIED CORRECTION ADOPTED — DoltHub pricing: DoltHub repriced on 2026-04-24 (primary source fetched today: dolthub.com/blog/2026-04-24-announcing-dolthub-pro-for-5-dollars-per-month/) — private storage over 100 MB is now USD 5/month up to 5 GB, then USD 1/GB/month; the USD 50/month figure in the WHY and runbook step 6 above was the PRIOR pricing (the docs page cited on 2026-07-27 was stale). AMEND step 6 accordingly: the fallback costs ~USD 5/month, not USD 50/month. This changes no part of the route — GitHub remains free, already-authenticated, and first — it just makes the fallback cheap if the ~1.74 GiB initial push trips GitHub's 2 GB per-push ceiling.
URGENCY unchanged: execute before the alpha tag. The tracker's ruling history (including this one) still has no off-box copy.
RUNBOOK AMENDMENTS (dossier review, 2026-07-28 PM): the dossier's Codex second opinion carried TWO required corrections plus refined figures. Both corrections VERIFIED today — pinned upstream sources fetched, plus local checks against the installed bd 1.0.3 (1b2dd2cb) and this checkout's armed pre-commit guard. They SUPERSEDE runbook steps 1, 2 and 4 above; steps 3, 6 (price already corrected to ~USD 5/mo in the note above) and 7 stand, with the order sharpened below (step 5's round-trip now comes AFTER landing config.yaml).

CORRECTION A — SUPERSEDES step 1 (was: create an EMPTY repo, "no README"). Do NOT create a branchless repo: the exact Dolt revision bundled by bd 1.0.3 errors on a git remote with no branches — VERIFIED in the pinned source (dolthub/dolt @ 005921bd, go/libraries/doltcore/dbfactory/git_remote_test.go: test TestGitRemoteFactory_GitFile_RemoteWithNoBranchesFails asserts ErrGitRemoteHasNoBranches). Seed it instead:
  gh repo create day8/re-frame2-beads --private --add-readme
  gh repo view day8/re-frame2-beads --json visibility,defaultBranchRef
Require visibility PRIVATE and a non-null defaultBranchRef before configuring Dolt. The README/branch never mixes with the data — Dolt stores git-backed data under refs/dolt/data, which ordinary clones do not fetch.

CORRECTION B — SUPERSEDES step 2's bare remove/add and step 4's commit guidance. VERIFIED in bd 1.0.3 source (gastownhall/beads @ 1b2dd2cb): `bd dolt remote add origin <url>` writes sync.remote into .beads/config.yaml AND auto-invokes commitBeadsConfig("bd: update sync.remote"), which runs a plain `git commit -m <msg>` with NO pathspec (cmd/bd/dolt.go remote-add handler; cmd/bd/sync_remote.go) — it sweeps EVERYTHING already staged. Also VERIFIED locally: this mayor checkout's guard is armed (.git/mayor-marker present) and the mayor allow-list is exactly .beads/issues.jsonl + MEMORY.md (scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-mayor-commit-boundary.sh), so the auto-commit carrying .beads/config.yaml will be REFUSED here and will leave config.yaml staged. Therefore:
- BEFORE `bd dolt remote remove origin` / `bd dolt remote add origin https://github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads.git`: verify `git diff --cached --name-only` prints NOTHING. Never run remote add with .beads/issues.jsonl (or anything else) staged — the no-pathspec auto-commit must never capture it.
- AFTER: confirm `bd dolt show` lists the new origin and `bd config get sync.remote` returns the URL. Expect the auto-commit to warn/fail with config.yaml left staged — that is the guard working, not breakage.
- Land the isolated .beads/config.yaml change through the normal worker/PR path (VERIFIED: workers may carry it — scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-beads-boundary.sh explicitly permits .beads/config.yaml; the mayor checkout cannot commit it), and land+push it BEFORE the fresh-clone round-trip test so bootstrap can find sync.remote.

REFINED FIGURES (re-measured 2026-07-28, drifting upward — the tracker is live): embedded store 1,872,694,753 B (1.744 GiB); old file remote directory 3,977,884,735 B total (~3.98 GB, includes accumulated non-live material — step 7's reclaim figure stands); the remote's LIVE manifest now references 240 table files / 1,842,305,776 B (1.716 GiB) (dossier measured 224 / 1.711 GiB — it grows). Headroom under GitHub's enforced 2 GiB per-push limit is only ~262-291 MiB today and shrinking, so the GitHub-first attempt is a genuine ONE-SHOT go/no-go: on `pack exceeds maximum allowed size` (or equivalent 2 GiB failure) go STRAIGHT to private DoltHub (~USD 5/month after the free 100 MB, through 5 GB; then USD 1/GB/month). No split-push tooling, no second cloud remote. Largest live table file is 1,079,296,714 B (~1.005 GiB) but this is NOT a 100 MB-object-ceiling problem: the bundled Dolt defaults git-backed storage to 50 MiB parts (VERIFIED in pinned source: defaultGitBlobstoreMaxPartSize = 50*1024*1024, dolthub/dolt @ 005921bd go/store/nbs/store.go) — aggregate push size is the only real capacity risk.

PUSH VERIFICATION: `git ls-remote https://github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads.git refs/dolt/data` must return the ref. The GitHub web UI shows NOTHING for custom refs — its silence is not evidence either way.

AMENDED ACCEPTANCE SEQUENCE (order is load-bearing): (1) seed + verify the private repo per Correction A -> (2) clean index, repoint origin, confirm sync.remote per Correction B -> (3) one ordinary `bd dolt push` -> (4) ls-remote proof of refs/dolt/data -> (5) land the .beads/config.yaml change via the normal path and push it -> (6) THEN the fresh-clone round-trip (NOT a worktree): `bd bootstrap --yes` + `bd dolt pull`, verify this bead and representative counts -> (7) only after the round-trip passes, delete the old file:// remote (.beads/backup/origin). ACCEPTANCE:
1. All six gate rows verified green with the artifact named for each - proof: the PR body enumerates all six. A missing row blocks the merge.
2. implementation/ui/ is gone and nothing references it - proof: full CI green.
3. Release topology no longer names the donor artifact - proof: .github/workflows/release.yml inspection.
4. The donor EPs and the docs/design/freehand record still exist - proof: assert their presence (this bead must not over-delete).
5. Deletion is ONE ordering-safe change: a source-removal-first PR reds itself on always-on policy tests that read the deleted files, so use one combined PR or prune configuration first. This is a known failure shape from the Helix removal - do not rediscover it.

notes:

  1. ELEVEN GATES NAME DONOR SOURCE PATHS and were classified by measurement, not inspection. NON-GOALS: preserving a donor API merely because its implementation proved useful (EP-0036 non-goal); a compatibility facade in Freehand (any temporary facade lives ONLY in re-frame.ui, gains no semantics, and is not Freehand API).

DECISIONS: EP-0036 "Conformance and donor deletion gate" row "absorption completeness".

ACCEPTANCE:
1. The ledger script reports ZERO undisposed rows - proof: run it; the count is 0.
2. Every DELETE row is actually gone - proof: the file/symbol is absent from the tracked tree.
3. Every MOVE row is present under Freehand ownership - proof: the target path exists and its tests run.
4. Every REPLACE row names WHAT replaced it - proof: the ledger's replacement column is non-empty for every REPLACE.
5. Freehand declares and resolves no dependency on the donor - proof: git grep plus a classpath assertion.
6. The trend is published: the undisposed count from the F0c baseline down to zero - proof: report it.

GATES: deterministic - zero undisposed rows, absence of DELETE rows, presence of MOVE rows. Evidence-only: the burn-down trend.

DEPENDS: F6a, F6c.
notes:
CAVEAT ON WHAT "ZERO" MEANS, from the F3a compiler transplant (#6698, merged 2026-07-23). The transplant marks its donor rows done while the DONOR SOURCE COPY REMAINS ON DISK. That is forced by the acceptance set, not sloppiness: the moved analyzer recognises Freehand vars and the moved emitters lower to re-frame.freehand.runtime/.tree, so the donor cannot run on its own absorbed code; yet the donor must still BUILD during coexistence, and Freehand may not depend on the donor. Donor TESTS did genuinely leave the tree (15 files git mv-ed). The ledger "How to read a row" now states both rules explicitly. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD: a zero undisposed count does NOT by itself prove the donor source tree is gone — it proves every row has a disposition. The physical deletion is rf2-drpa3.57 F6e. When driving this to zero, verify BOTH: (a) the count is zero, AND (b) for each done MOVE row, the Freehand target exists and its tests run. Do not let (a) stand in for (b). Current baseline after #6698: 203 rows, 177 undisposed, 26 disposed and retained.
STATUS RECONCILIATION 2026-07-25: LIVE — substantial real work remains; premise re-measured on main (9cdc3652e6). Ran 'python scripts/check_donor_inventory.py --report', exit 0: 'donor inventory: 203 rows, 161 not yet disposed, 42 disposed and retained as the audit record.' Undisposed by slice F1:23 F2:25 F3:15 F4:7 F5:16 F6:75; by disposition MOVE:115 REPLACE:31 DELETE:15. MERGED-PR AUDIT #6978 FINDING (2026-07-25): the five-read Pair migration missed the new absence semantics of Freehand xplain-render. e-frame.freehand.tool/explain-render explicitly returns nil for an undeclared supplied view id (and separately nil in production), but xplain-render-tool always builds its nil envelope as :view-tier-inactive with no :view-id, even when the call supplied one. Also make `re-frame.freehand.tool/event-site` name the vocabulary: its still-ambiguous “any other classification ... callback” sentence is the exact source wording that triggered this defect. Keep this existing owner open; no duplicate bead.

title: Freehand view substrate programme (EP-0036)
description:
Umbrella epic for the Freehand programme per docs/EP/EP-0036-the-freehand-view-substrate-programme.md.

MISSION: one re-frame-native view substrate — Freehand (re-frame.freehand, alias v) — with two required execution modes over ONE semantic model. The interpreted mode is the paved path (full Clojure, no grammar, v/sub returns a value, event intent is data, Hiccup is interpreted). The compiled mode is the hot tier, selected by {:compiled true} on the SAME v/defview declaration, lowering to the finite versioned grammar :re-frame.freehand/v1. A declared view var is a non-IFn descriptor in both modes, and promotion changes one declaration and no call site and no structural test.

ABSORPTION, NOT REINVENTION: the useful re-frame.ui machinery (analyzer, both emitters, ViewCell reactor, presence runtime, manifest/elision, diagnostics, structural test surface) MOVES into Freehand as the compiled mode's implementation. re-frame.ui is DONOR-ONLY now: it receives no new standalone surface, Freehand never depends on it, and the standalone artifact is deleted when the conformance contract, the component and React-library pilots, and consumer migration are all green. A gate, not a date.

OWNERSHIP: implementation extends the EXISTING canonical spec owners. There is NO spec/0XX-Freehand family and NO spec-only waterfall. Donor Spec 004 moves by rename to spec/004D-Freehand-Compiled-Grammar.md (filename fixed by the EP); a new common spec/004-Views.md owns declaration/authoring/semantics/host boundaries; 004B keeps the tree and conversion table; 004C keeps roots and mount; 006 the observation port; 008 testing; 009 diagnostics and evidence; 011 SSR; 012 routing. Executable laws live under spec/conformance/freehand/ with stable FH-<AREA>-<NNN> ids.

SLICES (dependency direction, not seven sequential tasks): F0 ownership cut, F1 paved-path spine, F2 reactive intent, F3 compiled absorption, F4 data and host lifecycle, F5 composition and integration, F6 proof and retirement. Independent work inside a slice runs in parallel when it does not edit the same canonical owner; a later slice may start on an independent surface as soon as its stated dependency is green. F0 is NOT followed by a document barrier.

DECISIONS: D001-D021 are ALL RULED (docs/design/freehand/decisions/README.md). Do not reopen them to revisit details. Codex (docs/design/freehand/codex-design.md) is the ratified target design; fable-design.md and studio/fitness-harness.md are supporting evidence and add no API. If a slice finds a genuine contradiction it proposes ONE explicit amendment; it never preserves both answers.

POSTURE: pre-alpha. Elegance, power and excellent programmer/AI ergonomics, without gold-plating, defensive ceremony, or distrust of the programmer.
notes:
BOOTSTRAP (2026-07-22): programme booted via PR #6677 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/6677) — tracked design snapshot at docs/design/freehand/ + EP-0036 (docs/EP/EP-0036-the-freehand-view-substrate-programme.md). Bootstrap children: W1 spec beads rf2-drpa3.1-.7 (hot-zone sequential), W2 ABI/shell rf2-drpa3.8 (blocked by all W1), B1-B5 harness rf2-drpa3.9, component pilots gate rf2-drpa3.10. W3/W4/W5-remainder/W6-remainder filed as future children at wave entry. NOTE: the EP is numbered EP-0036 (EP-0031-0035 were already taken by the re-frame.ui per-domain EPs).

F1 = .15-.19 (artefact skeleton / descriptor+defview / interpreted tree / mount+HMR / test surface). F2 = .20-.24 (atomic shell / v-sub / event materializer / key maps / controlled-input door). F3 = .25-.30 (compiler transplant / compiled selection / crossings / manifests+elision / checker / props schemas). Evidence = .47-.52 (B-spine + B1-B5, each attached to its enabling slice per D021, NOT deferred to the end). F6 = .53-.57 (conformance / browser / migration / absorption / donor deletion). FH-* ids DO NOT EXIST YET anywhere in the repo - .12 establishes the scheme and each slice allocates its own rows.
API-MANIFEST SERIAL LANE (mayor, 2026-07-23): re-frame.freehand is now a FULLY-ROWED manifest surface. Every new PUBLIC VERB must co-edit five files in one PR — implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc (facade), spec/api-manifest.edn (regenerate via gen), spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn (classification row), spec/API.md (roster row + vacancy-prose removal), docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md (member heading + vacancy removal). So public-verb beads (v/mount, presence/top-layer/behavior verbs, slots, ->react, route-link done) are a SERIAL LANE: merge one at a time, rebase the next onto it, tell each worker to add its classification row + API.md row + docs/api member in the SAME PR or the gate reds. title: codemod: the printed defhost sketch emits an untaught :fn contract, and authoring.md still calls the tool a hoist
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-2rtt6.112 WORKER (PR #7750) while documenting the shipped tool, and verified by the mayor. Two small fixes, same programme, one worker.

FIX 1 — THE SUGGESTED SKETCH WOULD BE REFUSED IF A USER PASTED IT. A REAL DEFECT.
migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod/src/re_frame/migration/hicasso/report.clj:84 builds the defhost sketch as:
    (for [s slots] (str s " :fn"))
so the report suggests {:callbacks {:on-pick :fn}}. But `:fn` is NOT one of the three callback contracts the door teaches — those are :event, :handler and :render. A user who copies the sketch the tool printed gets a refusal at mint.

This is the worst shape a diagnostic can take: the tool tells you what to write, and what it tells you is wrong. The doc worker documented the suggestions block WITHOUT quoting the sketch, precisely so the guide would not teach the defect — so the docs are currently protecting readers from the tool.

DECIDE WHAT THE SKETCH SHOULD EMIT. It cannot always know the right contract from a call site, so the honest options are: emit a placeholder that is obviously a placeholder rather than a plausible-but-invalid keyword; emit the contract when it IS inferable and a marked placeholder when it is not; or omit the callbacks map and say why. Do NOT invent a fourth contract to make :fn valid. Whatever you choose, pin it with a corpus case that asserts the emitted sketch is acceptable to the door — a sketch nobody round-trips is how this defect survived.

FIX 2 — docs/design/hicasso/authoring.md:304 STILL DESCRIBES THE CODEMOD AS THE HOIST.
The line reads: "migration codemod (collect `[:> X …]` sites -> emit the defhost block -> rewrite". That is the HOISTER, which was DEMAND-GATED AND DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT. What shipped is the fixer: six rewrites, eighteen refusal classes, three ratified amendments. Reword so it describes the tool that exists and does not imply the hoist is coming. rf2-2rtt6.112 re-scoped guide 05 the same way and its wording is the model.

WHY THESE CLUSTER: both are "the tool's own words are wrong about the tool", both are small, and a worker reading report.clj to fix the sketch is the right person to correct the one-line description of what that tool does.

GATES: clojure -M:test from migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod (the golden corpus is the spec — a new corpus case is the pin for fix 1); python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py for fix 2, with a sabotage control; and sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh in full. Run each gate ALONE and echo $? to its own file — never append a filter to a gate's command line.
NOTE the codemod now has a CI lane (PR #7746), so a corpus change is actually enforced.
notes: Merged-PR audit of #7762 independently confirmed the fix through all three lenses. Completeness: the printed scaffold, native-string suppression, authoring guidance, corpus coverage, and mirrored door roster all landed. Correctness: the codemod suite passed 28 tests / 300 assertions and generated sketches parse, stay def-able, carry no invented callback contract, and fill every reported callback position from the door's actual roster. Implementation quality: the reporting change stays a non-hoisting scaffold, derives only a harmless name, keeps contracts human-chosen, normalises regenerated corpus newlines, passes the documentation-slug and 1,834-file/49-lane bijection gates, and the PR-authored range passes git diff --check. No residual defect remains on this owner.
close_reason: PR #7762 supplies a door-acceptable printed scaffold, round-trip coverage, native-head suppression, and accurate fixer guidance.

  2. its arm in .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh

A roster line without a job fails gate R1; the pair must land together.

THE PLAYWRIGHT DETAIL, and it will waste a worker's afternoon if it is not carried into the brief. Do NOT let the CI step run a bare `npx playwright install`. It resolves a NEWER Playwright than the repo pins, fetches the wrong browser revision, and PRUNES THE PINNED WEBKIT OUT OF THE SHARED CACHE - so the job breaks the very engine the gate exists to exercise. Use the pinned CLI.

WHY IT MATTERS. The bead this came from proved something the value-level assertions could not: the caret is the only observable in a real browser that separates this runtime from plain React, because React's own end-of-event restore repairs value errors inside the same discrete event. That evidence is worth nothing to future changes if the suite never runs unattended.

title: hic — ratify the authoring names: h/fn vs hfn, h/frame vs hframe, and mount's unfrozen root!/release!
description:
# Close the gap between Hicasso's var names and its authoring surface

**Found by**: rf2-hic-001, which was instructed to keep the prototype's names and did.
**Surface**: `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc` (the public door) + guide prose.

The prototype spells two authoring verbs one way and DOCUMENTS them another, because in the
bench tree they were `:refer`red into the consuming namespace and the intended product
spelling is qualified:

| authoring surface (docs, 49 + 65 mentions) | var in the package today | prototype's stated reason |
|---|---|---|
| `h/fn`    | `hfn`    | "spelled `hfn` here because `h/fn` is qualified in the product and a bare `fn` would shadow `cljs.core/fn` on a `:refer`" |
| `h/frame` | `hframe` | "Spelled `hframe` here … a bare `frame` would shadow" |

Now that the package exists and the intended consumer spelling is
`(:require [re-frame.hicasso :as h])`, both reasons are spent: `h/fn` and `h/frame` are always
qualified through the alias, so the vars COULD be named `fn` and `frame`. That is a naming
decision with a real trade-off (a consumer who `:refer`s either one gets a shadow warning, and
`fn` shadowing `cljs.core/fn` is nastier than the warning suggests), so rf2-hic-001 did not
take it — it renamed nothing.

Note the marker keywords need no such decision and already work: `::h/value`, `::h/prevent`,
`::h/navigate`, `::h/mounting`, `::h/unmounting`, `::h/revision`, `::h/checked` and
`::h/clear` were minted as `:re-frame.hicasso/…` in the prototype, so aliasing the package as
`h` resolves them exactly as the guide teaches.

Also unresolved and cheap to fold in: `impl/mount.cljs`'s own docstring says "the names stay
unfrozen (HD-021 pins the semantics, not the spelling) and nothing here is a public API", yet
`root!` and `release!` are on the door because a package that cannot mount is not usable.
Ratify or replace that pair.

## Acceptance

- A ruling recorded, and the door matching it.
- If anything is renamed, `implementation/hicasso/frozen-sources.edn`'s `:renames` table and
  the note in `re-frame.hicasso`'s namespace docstring are updated in the same PR.
notes:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-10, operator-overturnable): ROUTE ALL THREE QUESTIONS TO THE NAMING LEDGER; RENAME NOTHING NOW. Dossier Option A's process — the only one consistent with the ruled machinery (ledger accumulates -> rf2-hic-065 packet applies recommendations as defaults -> rf2-hic-066 sweeps once -> operator's single sitting overrides asynchronously) — with the recommendation columns informed by the Codex analysis where I verified it against the repo. Ledger rows landed via PR #7753 (docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md rows 1, 13, 18). The door keeps the prototype names until the sweep; frozen-sources.edn :renames untouched (nothing renamed). Acceptance met: ruling recorded; door matches it (no rename ordered now).

THE THREE RULINGS (as ledger recommendations, all settled finally at the operator sitting):
(1) hfn (taught h/fn) — row 1 now carries BOTH candidates, h/handler (spec section 4 facade table) and h/event (Codex naming view), with h/event RECOMMENDED. Verified in-repo: the established cross-adaptor vocabulary reserves "event" for convert-the-invoker's-arguments-to-one-event-vector-or-nil (spec/004-Views.md:653 v/event; spec/004D-Freehand-Compiled-Grammar.md:1079 ui/event, nil => no dispatch) and "handler" for imperative return-ignored work (004-Views.md:654 v/handler; 004D:1080 ui/handler). Hicasso's form has exactly the event contract (capture frame; run later; dispatch returned vector; nil = no event), so h/handler would be a cross-adaptor false friend. Never a var named fn: alias-qualified h/fn is technically viable, but fn shadows cljs.core/fn for any :refer user (silent behavior change for every anonymous fn in that namespace) and says only "callable", not "the return is an event". Either surviving candidate kills the shadow hazard outright.
(2) hframe (taught h/frame) — new row 18 carries candidates "frame" (mechanical rename) vs RETIRE in favour of the core doors, with retire RECOMMENDED. Verified: specification.md section 4 (line ~139) already says "Existing rf/current-frame-id and rf/capture-frame remain the frame doors; Hicasso should not duplicate them", and hframe returns a frame-id KEYWORD while ui/frame and n/use-frame name frame OPERATIONS — a second false friend. The retire path is SEMANTIC, not mechanical: Hicasso currently refuses ambient frame resolution during its body, so the refusal seam must be corrected to admit exactly :current-frame-id and zero-arity :capture-frame during a Hicasso render extent, resolving to the body's known extent frame (the refusal record already carries :extent-frame, and require-current-frame! already receives the attempted operation — no adapter hook, no collector edge). Ambient rf/subscribe and rf/dispatch MUST stay refused (they would bypass Hicasso's read and intent accounting); outside a frame-bearing render the core doors keep their loud no-context behavior. Per hic-066's own law (a rename that turns out semantic stops the row and files a bead), the sweep files a dedicated bead for this seam correction rather than improvising. The committed hframe witnesses (multi-root, foreign-callback, reincarnation, SSR) prove the capability is real and must survive the retirement.
(3) root!/release! — RATIFIED PROVISIONAL until the sweep (a package that cannot mount is not usable; impl/mount.cljs's own docstring says the names are unfrozen and nothing there is public API). Row 13 recommends the spec section 4 lifecycle: mount! (from root!, a create-and-render), hydrate! (from the already-implemented hydrate-root!), render!, unmount!. All four underlying operations already exist in impl/mount.cljs (root! :105, hydrate-root! :233, render! :89, unmount! :293), so the rename exposes real states rather than inventing concepts, and matches React's public client model (createRoot/hydrateRoot each yield a root with render and unmount). release! is NOT root-lifecycle vocabulary: verified it calls process-wide collector/reset-runtime! (mount.cljs :313/:323) — a test-fixture door, unsafe as lifecycle in a multi-root product; it moves to the test kit under an explicit test-wide-reset name, off the application facade.

REJECTED: Option B (rename to fn/frame now) — buys the core-shadowing hazard for :refer users and then a likely second rename at the sweep; two churns, one hazardous, against the one-sweep ruling. Option C (ratify prototype names as final) — the guide would have to teach h/hfn (noise) and the facade disposition would be silently overturned without the evidence the freeze process expects. Codex's decide-now framing is adopted only as recommendation-column content: the physical rename still happens exactly once, at the sweep; no compatibility aliases ever (pre-alpha; hic-066 already bans shims).

NO ACTION on: guide prose (keeps teaching the target spellings until the sweep; the door/guide gap is the ledger rule working as designed, and a one-line "prototype names until the sweep" note is at the sweep-owner's discretion); marker keywords (::h/value, ::h/prevent, ::h/navigate, ::h/mounting, ::h/unmounting, ::h/revision, ::h/checked, ::h/clear already resolve exactly as taught — no decision needed).

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE FOR hic-065 (contract behind the recommended names, preserved from the dossier before deletion):
- The event form is a dispatching callback, not a position-sensitive marker: it captures the rendering boundary's exact frame incarnation, runs later with the invoker's arguments, dispatches one returned event vector, and treats nil as no event. A declared :handler or :render position should REJECT the form rather than reinterpret it; ordinary fn remains the imperative/render-callback escape. At an undeclared raw React escape it remains an ordinary callable carrying its own event semantics — the programmer deliberately chose the untyped edge. (Today impl/intent.cljs gives the marker positional treatment at :event/:handler/:render; the product specification already rejects positional meaning and asks for one event-producing form — the packet confirms one invariant meaning under whichever name wins.)
- Root contract: (h/mount! container frame hiccup) creates and initially renders, returning an opaque handle; (h/hydrate! container frame hiccup) adopts server markup and returns the same handle shape; (h/render! handle hiccup) updates either kind of live handle and returns it; (h/unmount! handle) is idempotent, cleans only that root, returns nil, must NOT remove a caller-owned container, and must NOT erase global collector state to manufacture a clean result — root-teardown residue after quiescence is a defect to expose, not to reset away.
- Core-door admission stays narrow: during a Hicasso render extent rf/current-frame-id returns the extent frame and (rf/capture-frame) captures that exact incarnation; no collector edge and no React hook is added; rf/subscribe and rf/dispatch still raise the existing ambient-frame refusal. A small correction to the refusal seam, not a second frame system.

REQUIRED WITNESSES BEFORE THE SWEEP IS ACCEPTED (carry into hic-066 acceptance):
- A clean CLJS consumer using only (:require [re-frame.hicasso :as h]) compiles the winning event form; the final public namespace contains none of hfn, fn, hframe, frame, root!, release!, nor the losing event/handler candidate.
- The event contract proved at a native event prop, a value-first declared host callback, and a retained raw callback: a vector dispatches once to the captured incarnation; nil dispatches nothing; a successor frame with the same public id is never reached by an old callback; declared handler/render slots reject the form rather than changing its meaning; a plain function returning a vector remains just a plain function.
- rf/current-frame-id and (rf/capture-frame) answer the Hicasso body's frame in two simultaneous roots, in a supplier-owned foreign render callback, and during per-request SSR; the captured operation still targets that incarnation after the body unwinds; outside a body they refuse; a sabotage proves ambient rf/subscribe and rf/dispatch still refuse and the hook/read-edge counts do not move.
- mount! and hydrate! return one interoperable handle shape; render! preserves an adopted subtree after hydration settles; unmount! is double-call safe, leaves the supplied container in place, releases only its own root, and cannot make a sibling root's evidence disappear; residue is measured BEFORE any test reset.
- A hydration witness proves that calling render! before adoption settles is either explicitly refused or follows a deliberately documented React contract; it must not silently switch the root to client rendering (React documents that early render as destructive to the server DOM).
close_reason: Routed to the naming ledger per the ruled one-sweep machinery (rows 1/13/18, PR #7753); nothing renamed now; full delegated-decision record with implementation guidance and sweep witnesses in the bead notes.

title: cross-checked-against-an-outside-instrument.md: 3 provenance-pin findings exposed by the row scope, one needs a ruling
description:
PR #7734 (rf2-xlsh) scoped provenance-pin accompaniment to the table ROW rather than the whole table. That newly exposes three findings on docs/design/hicasso/studio/cross-checked-against-an-outside-instrument.md. The page was left UNTOUCHED because one of the three cannot be repaired without a ruling, and a partial edit would have redded #7734's own changed-pages gate.

MECHANICAL, no ruling needed:
  :541 19a3710bc9604684ddbc7b2b72ec901dcc0f0ea7 [STRANDED]
  :541 3680992949a6eec842ba033ae50f3a9a34af7884 [STRANDED]
Row 540, directly above, already asserts -- and says it verified by identical 'git patch-id --stable' -- that f6cb3584fb (confirmed an ancestor of origin/main) is what 19a3710bc9 became when it landed. Naming f6cb3584fb inside row 541 is the census's own repair pattern and invents nothing.

NEEDS A RULING:
  :544 247fafa22c1f2caeb4cad179aa64cf444398cbc7 [UNRESOLVABLE]
This is NOT a citation defect. The row cites a commit in krausest/js-framework-benchmark and says so in its own text: 'That SHA belongs to the benchmark's repository, not to this one, so it resolves there and nowhere else.' No SHA of THIS repository belongs in that row, so there is no accompaniment to add. The gate reads 'at commit `X`' and classifies it as a local pin, which it has no way to know is false.

The options, for whoever rules:
 (i) teach the classifier a foreign-repository context, so a token the writer explicitly attributes to another repo is not read as a local pin. Closest in spirit to how the checker already separates blobs from commits by the writer's own vocabulary, and needs no page edit.
 (ii) annotate the page so the row carries no bare commit citation.
 (iii) accept the finding and leave the page red whenever it is touched. Not recommended -- it lays a trap for the next editor.

Do NOT weaken the gate or add an ignore mechanism. Whoever fixes :541 must resolve :544 in the same PR, or the page's changed-pages gate stays red.
notes:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-10, operator-overturnable): OPTION (i) AS AMENDED BY THE CODEX RECOMMENDATION — teach scripts/check_provenance_pins.py a foreign-commit citation, where "foreign" is an explicit canonical GitHub commit permalink, never a conclusion drawn from nearby prose. Prose words ("foreign", "upstream", "another repository", "belongs to") are NEVER an exemption. Rationale: prose-attribution vocabulary would be the first vocabulary that turns the gate OFF for a token rather than classifying the writer's claim, and is launderable by a magic phrase — the dossier's own stated risk. A typed permalink binds the full SHA to a repository identity mechanically, is clearer to a reader, easier for an AI tool to generate correctly, and keeps the checker's fail-toward-refusal design intact. Option (ii) rejected: the page bends to the tool and hiding the SHA from the scanner is a fail-open shape; the next outside-instrument page hits the same wall. Option (iii) rejected: a standing trap, and a red gate people learn to ignore is the exact habit the corpus forbids. FENCE PRESERVED: this neither weakens the gate nor adds an ignore mechanism — it teaches the gate the writer's explicitly-declared, strictly-typed citation form.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (one worker, ONE PR: checker change + fixtures + all three page findings together, so the changed-pages gate stays green — a partial edit reds the page on every touch):

THE THREE FINDINGS on docs/design/hicasso/studio/cross-checked-against-an-outside-instrument.md:
1. :541 19a3710bc9604684ddbc7b2b72ec901dcc0f0ea7 [STRANDED] — MECHANICAL. Row 540 directly above already asserts-and-verifies (git patch-id --stable) that f6cb3584fb is what 19a3710bc9 became when it landed; f6cb3584fb re-verified an ancestor of origin/main 2026-08-10. Name f6cb3584fb inside row 541 per the census's own repair pattern; invents nothing.
2. :541 3680992949a6eec842ba033ae50f3a9a34af7884 [STRANDED] — MECHANICAL via the same same-row landed anchor, BUT (Codex-verified) f6cb3584fb's stable patch id matches 19a3710bc9 ONLY, NOT 3680992949. The repair text must NOT describe f6cb3584fb as the landed counterpart of the second authored commit; the landed anchor in the row satisfies the row-scoped accompaniment rule for both tokens while the prose stays accurate about which authored commit it corresponds to.
3. :544 247fafa22c1f2caeb4cad179aa64cf444398cbc7 [UNRESOLVABLE] — NOT a citation defect. Foreign commit of krausest/js-framework-benchmark (Stefan Krause, "incremental run", 2026-07-28; identity confirmed by two primary sources: the surviving clone's remote https://github.com/krausest/js-framework-benchmark.git resolves it, and GitHub's canonical commit page resolves the same full SHA).
