title: check_provenance_pins.py fails open: a bad hash in a table is shielded by a landed hash in the same block
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-mcwm WORKER (PR #7727) while running an unrequested extra control on the pins gate. It substituted a known-bad hash (a PR head that is not an ancestor of main) into resource-demand-criteria.md in three places, and the gate reported only ONE of the three.

THE MECHANISM. check_provenance_pins.py enforces accompaniment PER BLOCK, not "every cited SHA must be an ancestor of origin/main". Two of the three substituted occurrences sat in the record table alongside the landed original-freeze hash c8b8de6d28. Because a landed SHA was present in the same block, the block satisfied the accompaniment rule and the bad hashes beside it were not reported. Only the prose citation, alone in its own block, was caught.

WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A CURIOSITY. The gate's whole purpose is to stop a page citing a commit that does not resolve. On the page it was guarding, the ROW THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS -- the operative frozen hash that rf2-hic-044 and rf2-hic-050 will cite -- lives in a table next to a landed hash. So the guard would not have caught a wrong hash in exactly the field whose wrongness costs most. It was caught only because the same value also appeared in prose.

THIS IS THE FAIL-OPEN CLASS THE REPO HUNTS EVERYWHERE ELSE: a gate that verifies the absence of bad news in aggregate rather than the presence of good news per citation. Any page that cites a hash ONLY inside a table alongside a landed one is unguarded today.

WHAT TO DECIDE (this is a ruling, not an obvious fix). Options, roughly in increasing cost:
  (a) Report every cited pin that is not an ancestor of origin/main, regardless of what shares its block. Strictest and simplest to explain; may be noisy on pages that deliberately cite historical or superseded commits.
  (b) Keep per-block accompaniment but additionally flag any cited SHA that resolves to no commit at all, since that can never be legitimate.
  (c) Treat table rows as their own blocks, so a cell cannot be shielded by a sibling cell.
RECOMMEND (b) AT MINIMUM -- an unresolvable token is never correct and the check is cheap. (a) is the honest end state if the noise turns out to be tolerable; check first how many legitimate historical citations exist in docs/design/**.

DO NOT weaken any existing behaviour, and do not silence the gate anywhere. Note also that the gate already refuses correctly on the other axis: it caught a bootstrap RNG seed (20260807) and a placeholder (abc1234) today, both false positives that cost fix-worker round trips. Whatever changes, keep that fail-toward-refusal posture -- the defect here is a fail-OPEN, and fixing it must not trade one for the other.

EVIDENCE: PR #7727's report. Reproduce by substituting 92cd524aeeb0132f51f8e3376e313d7819f8813c (a PR head, not an ancestor of main) for the operative hash in docs/design/hicasso/product/resource-demand-criteria.md and running: git fetch --no-tags origin main; python scripts/check_provenance_pins.py --changed-since origin/main --verbose
notes:
WORKER STOPPED AND DID NOT IMPLEMENT (b). Measured evidence says (b) is the wrong shape; the brief instructed STOP-and-report in that case. No code change, no PR. Bead left open for a re-ruling.

THE FAIL-OPEN IS REAL AND REPRODUCED. Substituting 92cd524aeeb0132f51f8e3376e313d7819f8813c for the operative hash afbb58febc at line 19 (the "Pre-registration commit ... this is the hash to cite" row) of docs/design/hicasso/product/resource-demand-criteria.md, then running --changed-since origin/main --verbose, gives EXIT 0: "1 files, 5 cited pins (4 landed, 1 stranded, 0 unresolvable) ... every cited pin is an ancestor of origin/main or shares its block with one." The landed c8b8de6d28 one row above shields it. Confirmed exactly as described.

WHY (b) IS THE WRONG SHAPE. "Resolves to no commit at all" is not a property of the citation; it is a property of whatever happens to be in the local object store. The script's own FAILURE DIRECTION docstring already says this ("the stranded pins are precisely the objects a fresh clone does NOT have"). Measured, same corpus, same 346 citations:

  local dev checkout (PR heads fetched over time):  238 landed, 100 STRANDED,   8 UNRESOLVABLE
  fresh clone, main only:                           238 landed,   0 stranded, 108 UNRESOLVABLE
  fresh clone + all branches + all tags (= exact
  actions/checkout fetch-depth:0 shape used by
  the provenance-pins job in docs.yml):             238 landed,   0 stranded, 108 UNRESOLVABLE

STRANDED is empty in CI. Every retained authored head is UNRESOLVABLE there, because a commit that is not an ancestor of main is by definition not reachable from main, and merged worker branches are deleted. So in the only environment where this gate blocks, (b) flags all 108.

CONSEQUENCE 1 - in CI, (b) IS (a), bit for bit. Findings measured in the CI-shaped clone:
  TODAY (per-block accompaniment)   18 findings / 10 pages
  (b) + every unresolvable         108 findings / 28 pages   (+90 findings, +18 pages)
  (a) every non-ancestor           108 findings / 28 pages   (+90 findings, +18 pages)   IDENTICAL to (b)
  (c) table rows are blocks         23 findings / 13 pages   (+5 findings, +3 pages)
The ruling picked (b) expressly to avoid (a)'s noise. In CI there is no difference between them. The ruling's stated justification - "adds no false positives on pages that deliberately cite historical or superseded commits" - inverts in CI: those deliberate historical citations ARE the unresolvable tokens, and all 90 new findings are exactly those pages. That is the "punish the careful ones and be routed around within a week" outcome the script's WHAT IS ENFORCED paragraph exists to refuse.

CONSEQUENCE 2 - (b) does not fix the bead's own reproduction in a dev checkout. Prototyped (b) correctly (keep accompaniment for STRANDED, always report UNRESOLVABLE) and re-ran the probe locally: STILL EXIT 0. The probe resolves locally, so it is STRANDED, so it stays shielded. (b) catches it in CI only, and only as a side effect of also catching 90 legitimate ones.

CONSEQUENCE 3 - (b) widens the false-positive class that already cost two fix-worker round trips. Both of yesterday's refusals (the 20260807 bootstrap seed, the abc1234 placeholder) are UNRESOLVABLE tokens. Verified both still fire on current code (exit 1, both reported). Under (b) they would additionally be reported when a landed hash shares their block - strictly more of the same false positive, i.e. the fail-closed trade the brief forbids.

WHAT I RECOMMEND INSTEAD - (c), which the ruling excluded. Measured, not argued:
  * It catches the probe in BOTH environments (local run with a (c) prototype: EXIT 1, reports line 19). "Is an ancestor of origin/main" is checkout-invariant, so unlike (b) its verdict does not depend on the object store.
  * It costs 5 new findings on 3 pages, against 90 on 18 for (a)/(b). The three: studio/cross-checked-against-an-outside-instrument.md, studio/the-candidates-clock.md, studio/the-in-page-mount-term-decomposed.md.
  * It matches this bead's own title - "a bad hash in a table is shielded by a landed hash in the same block". The shielding is between ROWS; (c) removes exactly that and nothing else. Prose paragraphs are untouched, so the retained-authored-head-plus-anchor sentence the census repaired keeps passing.
  Caveat for the ruling: the docstring says the census's repairs put the landed SHA "in the same table cell or the same sentence", which is what makes (c) cheap - but the 3 pages above are the cases that relied on a sibling ROW, and each needs a human.

A fourth option, if (c)'s 5 findings are unwelcome: (d) require that a token the WRITER calls landed/effective/"the hash to cite" actually be an ancestor of origin/main, regardless of block, leaving "authored at X on worker/y" alone. Checkout-invariant, near-zero corpus cost, but it needs new vocabulary in _COMMIT_WORDS and is more machinery than (c).

METHOD, so this is re-checkable: fresh clone via `git clone --no-local --single-branch --branch main file:///C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2`, then `git fetch origin '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*' --tags` for the all-refs variant. Every probe reverted; worktree ends at e914fc8b7c with `git status --porcelain` empty. Gates on the clean checkout: --self-test --verbose exit 0 (all 33 passed), --changed-since origin/main --verbose exit 0, check_doc_slugs.py exit 0. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh does cover this script (lines 1191-1205 run both the self-test and the changed-pages gate), so any change here reds the fast-PR spine.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7734 (correctness/implementation quality): REOPENED exact owner. Citation.scope correctly prevents a LANDED hash in one row from accompanying a STRANDED hash in another, but scan_file still calls classify -> _left_context, which reads two prior nonblank source lines without respecting the new row scope. Reproduction: in a neutral table, put `bbbbbbbbbb` in a preceding `Blob hash` row and stranded `aaaaaaaaaa` in the next `Original freeze` row. scan_file returns ZERO citations: the preceding digest word repaints the next row before evaluate() can enforce row scope. A bad operative commit can therefore still fail open. Bound the repair to extraction context: never cross a prior table-row start, while retaining same-row wrapped continuations and digest-header classification; add this exact sibling-digest regression. Existing 36 self-tests, changed-page gate, diff check, and fast-PR spine all exit 0, proving the coverage gap. The already surfaced corpus findings remain owned by rf2-styo and rf2-iseb; no duplicate Bead.
Merged-PR audit #7742 (2026-08-10): PASS; the reopened owner is complete. Independent parent/tip probes show the sibling-digest fixture (including blockquote form) changes from zero citations to the operative `aaaaaaaaaa`, while a wrapped same-row digest remains excluded. All 39 self-tests and changed-page/diff gates pass. Full-corpus comparison is exact on findings: 20 before and 20 after, with no set difference; extraction rises 347→354 citations as intended. rf2-styo retains the separate page-level backlog; rf2-iseb is already repaired. No duplicate filed.

title: hic-071 — Budget enforcement gates
description:
# hic-071 — Budget enforcement gates

**Phase**: 2→4 · **Wave**: C/E · **Est.**: L · **Depends**: hic-006, hic-025 (extends over hic-078 and hic-047 apps as they land)
**Surface**: CI gate suites + the budgets document's status column (new files; budgets.md rows updated by this owner only)

## Goal
Turn the transcribed budgets into enforced gates. Transcription is not enforcement.

## Deliverables
- **User-visible gates**: representative discrete interactions reach next paint ≤50 ms p95 / ≤100 ms p99; broad operations ≤100 ms p95; keystroke echo within one frame — measured on the slice app (then the editor/grid and vendor apps as they land), deterministic-blocker style where possible, pinned interleaved runs where distributional.
- **The 5% same-instrument regression gate**: pinned ordinary-Hicasso benchmark compared per PR-relevant change; a regression blocks until the instrument owner validates and the change is fixed or reverted.
- **The escape-benefit rule enforced**: every landed escape (direct output, island) carries its measured benefit; an escape below 20% / 2 ms / budget-flip is removed by this gate's acceptance, not documented around.
- **Budget-line reconciliation table**: registered line, current value, status, authority, prospective disposition — one row per budget; checkpoints read it.

## Acceptance
- Gates run in CI on the named suites; each gate has an eligibility/sabotage control; one seeded regression reddens the 5% gate; the reconciliation table has no silent breach rows.

## Worker notes
Read spec §6 (all subsections); the evidence-protocol rules (estimand, population, refusal on unhealthy instrument).

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).

title: hicasso: build the Reagent [:>] codemod FIXER from the ratified design (three amendments)
description:
BUILD THE CODEMOD FIXER. rf2-2rtt6.106's design is ACCEPTED and RATIFIED (PR
#7646, docs/design/hicasso/studio/reagent-codemod-against-the-landed-escape.md).
This bead is the implementation half that closing .106 discharged the spec for
but never filed — the tracker had a design bead and a docs bead (rf2-2rtt6.112)
with nothing between them.

SCOPE IS THE FIXER ONLY. The HOISTER (the declare-what-you-use-twice defhost
hoist with dedupe) is DEMAND-GATED by the same ratification and is NOT in scope:
build it only when a real migrator reports the manual declarations as the pain.
The 2026-08-07 corpus scan (tools/machines-viz/src, the only application-shaped
[:>] corpus in-repo) found 15 executable [:>] forms over 7 component
expressions, and NONE of the 15 triggers a text-changing fixer rewrite — that is
evidence of ergonomic value with no urgency, and it is why the gate stands.

ORDERING GATE IS MET. The ratification's condition was "dispatched after
rf2-2rtt6.103's [:>] implementation merges"; .103 is CLOSED with PR #7635 merged
(raw-head?/raw-element/raw-gate/raw-component in front/codec.cljs). The SHIPPING
precondition rf2-ani6y is CLOSED (PR #7665, shared front/slot.cljc with a
cross-host equivalence test), so the JVM prop-name is pinned equal to the codec.
The donor-side row rf2-d2mwk is CLOSED.

THE THREE RATIFIED ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, which are corrections to the landed
design and must be implemented as amended rather than as written:

(A) W4 MUST CAPTURE AT PROP-EVALUATION TIME. The design's stated rewrite
(reagent-codemod-against-the-landed-escape.md:154) is (fn [& args] (apply f a
... args)), which re-evaluates every nontrivial callee/argument form on EACH
callback invocation; Reagent's make-partial-fn evaluated them ONCE at
construction. Required shape: a hygienic let capturing the callee and every
bound argument once, left-to-right, before minting the wrapper (or refuse
non-atomic arguments). Witness pins: a dereferenced-snapshot case and an
effect-count/ordering case.

(B) W2 MUST REFUSE NORMALIZED-KEY COLLISIONS. Reagent's kv-conv writes each
nested-map key under cached-prop-name, so :foo-bar/:fooBar, :class/:className
and :foo-bar/"fooBar" siblings each collapse to ONE JS property with an
iteration-order winner. Required shape: before rewriting any nested literal map,
require the normalized names to be injective; otherwise refuse the WHOLE map
with a report line naming every colliding source key. Witness pins: an ordinary
camel-case collision, a seeded rename, a keyword/string collision.

(C) KEY-SLOT REPORT ENTRY. The key-slot exclusion from the named-value rewrite
is RATIFIED (:foo and "foo" sibling keys COLLIDED under Reagent and are DISTINCT
under Hicasso; rewriting would restore the defect rf2-vrvv9 removed). But the
counter-cost is understated: a changed key resets the subtree's React state on
live reconciliation. The report must carry a dedicated entry per key-slot site
saying so.

STANDING RIDER, unchanged and quoted: the ~6-8 door-side codemod-contract-* rows
remain the only executed evidence the tool is correct — "Not optional, not
deferrable."

THE GOLDEN-FILE CORPUS IS THE SPEC (design section 5): input namespace ->
expected output + expected report, covering the rewrite, each preserve class,
each report class, and idempotence (running twice = no-op).

RESIDENCE: dev tooling operating on consumer source. Check how existing tools
are packaged and honour the bundle-isolation law (nothing in implementation/ may
:require from tools/). Verify what parsing substrate the repo already depends on
before adding rewrite-clj or an equivalent.

EXTERNAL REFERENCES for the worker: Reagent v2.0.1
src/reagent/impl/template.cljs (convert-prop-value, kv-conv, cached-prop-name)
and src/reagent/impl/util.cljs (make-partial-fn/PartialFn); React v19.2.0
packages/react/src/jsx/ReactJSXElement.js (key coercion). In-repo:
front/codec.cljs (prop-name, host-prop-value, host-entry, raw-element,
vec->element), codec_cljs_test.cljs, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn (the Reagent
2.0.1 pin).

DO NOT let the codemod become a general Reagent migrator — [:>] sites only.
Silent behaviour change is the only fatal class. No AI attribution.
notes:
MAYOR 2026-08-09 14:20 AUSEST — FILED, NOT DISPATCHED. Holding for the operator on two grounds, both worth stating.

(1) THE RATIFICATION'S OWN WORDING. rf2-2rtt6.106's close reason reads 'the fixer is dispatchable WHEN THE OPERATOR WANTS IT'. Every mechanical precondition is now met — .103 merged (PR #7635), rf2-ani6y merged (PR #7665), rf2-d2mwk closed — so nothing technical is holding it. What is left is a want, and that is Mike's.

(2) K1 IS HALF-FIRED, AND THIS IS DISCRETIONARY SPEND INSIDE THE PROGRAMME IT GATES. rf2-diaud (PR #7704) published the M1 mount row on K1's own floor-normalised estimand and adjudicated the gate MISSED, DECISIVELY. K1's consequence is 'stop or narrow'; its second conjunct (two serious runtime iterations) is the open ruling on rf2-sza0w, and K1's line for the 2026-08-27 sitting is that row, with the packet freezing 2026-08-25. Committing a worker to a new migration tool two weeks before a sitting that may narrow or stop the programme is a call I should not make quietly. The fixer protects against silent behaviour change, which is why it was ordered first — but there is no migrator in flight today, and the corpus scan found zero sites that would trigger a rewrite. CORRECTNESS — W4 is not hygienic despite the acceptance criterion and README claim. The generated fixed locals `f__rf2`, `aN__rf2`, and `args__rf2` can shadow locals already in consumer code. title: RULING NEEDED: rf2-diaud (b) and (c) collide on the bulk rows — retiring the cross-run band veto there promotes two donor-vs-donor pairs out of the 42-run corpus
description:
SURFACED BY IMPLEMENTATION, NOT DECIDED BY IT — rf2-diaud's publication repair, 2026-08-08.

THE COLLISION. rf2-diaud's acceptance criteria (b) and (c) cannot both be satisfied globally on the committed corpus.

(b) says: 'The row-specific thresholds of part (1) are implemented in the same rule; BULK'S PATH UNCHANGED.'
(c) says: 'The max-band-across-all-accepted-runs SECOND VETO is retired from publication authority ... the cross-run maximum stops vetoing publication' — with three structural reasons that are general, not mount-specific: it is not an interval for the claimed effect, it borrows a control statistic from another estimand, and it grows harder to clear merely by adding runs.

WHAT RETIRING IT ON BULK ACTUALLY DOES, measured rather than argued. Two pairs of the committed 42-run corpus flip from INSTRUMENT-LIMITED to MAGNITUDE PUBLISHABLE:

  bulk300  uix-subs / reagent-subs   [0.8327 - 0.9031]  n=8  (clock-emvod)
  bulk100  uix-subs / reagent-subs   [0.8870 - 0.9675]  n=8  (clock-emvod)

Both were held only by the band veto; both intervals lie wholly below 1.0. Under rf2-8a746's rule as frozen, EVERY pair of EVERY bulk row published INSTRUMENT-LIMITED, and its own text says the 42 committed row-runs 'remain calibration/diagnostic evidence and are NOT retroactively promoted to published magnitudes'. rf2-diaud amends that ruling for the row it is about; it does not overturn that sentence.

AND BOTH FLIPPED PAIRS ARE DONOR AGAINST DONOR. uix-subs / reagent-subs is UIx-on-subs against Reagent-on-subs — it answers no ship question. Publishing 'MAGNITUDE PUBLISHABLE, the whole interval is below the 1.0 bar' on it would assert that UIx-on-subs meets the CANDIDATE'S bulk ship bar. That is the same pair-scoping looseness rf2-vp0j7 records, and the band veto has been incidentally masking it.

WHAT WAS IMPLEMENTED, PENDING THIS RULING. The veto is retired on the MOUNT class — where rf2-diaud states its consequence, and where M1 now publishes K1 MISSED, DECISIVELY at 1.1718x [1.1263-1.2190] (n=8) and 1.1976x [1.1504-1.2468] (n=6) from K1's own floor-normalised estimand. It is RETAINED on the bulk class, which is what 'bulk's path unchanged' says in the one place the two criteria disagree. The asymmetry is a named field on the bulk entry of clock_readjudicate.cjs's PUBLICATION table, cites this bead, and is pinned by a test in both directions, so flipping it is a one-line change.

title: hicasso: the clock check standard is not independent of its own baseline, which its ruling requires
description:
RAISED BY THE MAYOR 2026-08-08 17:25 AUSEST, from comparing two standards landed the same day. Not a defect found by measuring; a criterion its own ruling states and the landed artefact self-discloses it does not meet.

WHAT THE RULING REQUIRES. rf2-8a746 part 3: "FREEZE RUN-LEVEL LOCATION AND DISPERSION LIMITS FROM AN INDEPENDENT BASELINE; prove them against the sabotage fixture; recalibrate on any browser, harness, page or clock change (NIST e-Handbook 2.3.5 check-standard doctrine)."

WHAT LANDED, IN ITS OWN WORDS. clock_check_standard.json says it plainly and to its credit rather than hiding it. classes.bulk.provenance.independence: "NOT INDEPENDENT OF ITS OWN BASELINE, and said here rather than left to be discovered. v1 is seeded from the same 42 row-runs it is quoted against, so 0-of-42 is a consistency check and not a false-refusal measurement." classes.mount.provenance.independence says the same on a smaller baseline: "v2 is seeded from the same 14 M1 row-runs it is quoted against, so 14 of 14 is a consistency check and not a false-refusal measurement."

SO THE HEADLINE NUMBERS ARE WEAKER THAN THEY READ. "0 of 42 refused" and "14 of 14 in control" are not evidence the limits admit good runs — they are arithmetic consequences of deriving the limits from those very runs. Nothing published depends on this today, because the direction is safe (a standard fitted to its own data is if anything too permissive, and no row has been published through it). But the moment a NEW run is judged in control by this standard, that verdict rests on limits nobody has validated out of sample.

THE METHOD IS ALREADY DEMONSTRATED ON THIS CORPUS, which is why this is a bounded task rather than a research question. rf2-pzqy8's census standard (PR #7701, same day) did exactly what the ruling asks: the corpus splits by COMMIT, so the four 2026-08-02 sessions became the baseline (8 row-runs, 144 blocks) and censusclock-jv36i (2026-08-07, five days and one commit later) was HELD OUT — and both hold-out row-runs came back IN CONTROL against limits derived without them. That is a real out-of-sample validation, and it is the standard this bead asks the clock rig to meet.

THE WORK. Re-derive the clock standard's bulk and mount limits from a genuine baseline SUBSET of the retained corpus, hold the remainder out, and report whether the held-out runs are in control. The clock corpus plausibly splits the same way — clock-emvod run1-8 and clock-w3yxd run1-6 are two ensembles — but ESTABLISH the split from commit provenance rather than assuming ensemble equals commit. Version the result (v2/v3 as appropriate), keep the amendment idiom the file already uses, and REPLACE each independence field with what the hold-out actually showed.

IF THE HOLD-OUTS COME BACK OUT OF CONTROL, that is the finding and it must be reported, not tuned away. A standard whose limits do not survive out-of-sample is telling you something about the instrument, and rf2-8a746's own diagnosis of ctl3 is the precedent for taking that seriously.

FENCES: do not widen any limit to make a hold-out pass; do not touch the census standard (a different rig, already independent); do not re-open the retired ctl3 gate or the all-blocks rule; take NO measurement — the corpus is retained and this is arithmetic over it.

WHY P2 AND NOT P3: the clock standard gates M1 and the bulk rows, which are K1 and K2's evidence at the 2026-08-27 sitting. An out-of-sample validation before the 2026-08-25 packet freeze is worth having; after it, the sitting reads numbers whose gate was never tested against data it had not seen.
notes:
MAYOR CORRECTION 2026-08-08 17:30 AUSEST, made BEFORE dispatching rather than after — the description's assumption about how this corpus splits is wrong, and the difference changes what the work can claim.

WHAT I WROTE: "the clock corpus plausibly splits the same way — clock-emvod run1-8 and clock-w3yxd run1-6 are two ensembles — but ESTABLISH the split from commit provenance rather than assuming ensemble equals commit."

WHAT THE DATA SAYS: it does NOT split by commit. Every run in both ensembles carries a `when` timestamp of 2026-08-07, and the two ensembles are about NINETY MINUTES apart — clock-emvod run1 at 05:37:29Z, clock-w3yxd run1 at 07:04:47Z. Same day, and on the evidence the same tree. rf2-pzqy8's census corpus split across FIVE COMMITS over five days, which is what let it hold out a genuinely later commit. That option is not on the table here.

SO THE ACHIEVABLE INDEPENDENCE IS WEAKER, AND MUST BE CLAIMED AS SUCH. What the clock corpus supports is a SESSION-level hold-out: derive limits from one ensemble, judge the other against them. That tests whether limits fitted to one sitting admit runs from a different sitting ninety minutes later — real, and the dominant practical failure mode for a check standard, but it is NOT commit-level independence and must not be written up as if it were. The census standard's hold-out crossed five days and a code change; this one crosses a coffee break.

REVISED ACCEPTANCE, replacing the description's: derive bulk and mount limits from ONE ensemble, report whether every run of the OTHER is in control against them, and do it BOTH WAYS (emvod-derived judging w3yxd, and w3yxd-derived judging emvod) so the answer does not depend on which ensemble happened to be chosen. State the independence achieved in the file's own `independence` field in exactly those terms — session-level, same-day, same tree — replacing the current honest admission with an honest measurement.

IF THE TWO DIRECTIONS DISAGREE, that is the finding and it is a more interesting one than either verdict alone: limits that admit the other ensemble one way but not the other say the two sittings differ by more than the limits allow, which is a statement about the instrument's between-session stability and belongs on the bead.

UNCHANGED: do not widen a limit to make a hold-out pass; do not touch the census standard; take no measurement. And the ruling's criterion is still only partly discharged by this work — commit-level independence needs a future ensemble taken on a different tree, which is worth recording as the standard's stated recalibration trigger rather than pretending this closes it.

title: census rig's ordinary row: the control's CENTRE is mis-specified, and it refuses every committed run (0 of 10)
description:
MEASURED under rf2-y0pkh, 2026-08-08, over the committed censusclock-* datasets. NO MEASUREMENT TAKEN — arithmetic over retained data.

rf2-y0pkh asked whether the census rig's all-18-blocks strict run-rejection rule refuses at a rate a run cannot survive. On the two rows that carry the gated pair it does not (large-template 98.9% of blocks in band -> 8 of 10 runs; feed 97.2% -> 7 of 10). The rule is RETAINED there on measured grounds.

THE ORDINARY ROW IS A DIFFERENT FAULT AND THE RULE IS NOT IT. Over 10 committed row-runs (180 blocks) the ctl-2x/floor block median is 1.2264x against a predicted 1.7255x — 71.1% of P, and 5.2% BELOW the tolerance band's lower edge of 1.2941. Per-block in band 56/180 = 31.1%; strict runs passed 0 of 10. RELAXING THE RUN RULE DOES NOT REACH IT: allowing up to three out-of-band blocks per run still passes 0 of 10. The centre is outside the band the rule enforces, so this is a mis-specified CENTRE — the same defect class rf2-8a746 diagnosed on ctl3 (whose true centre sat 2.6% above its refusal edge; this one sits 5.2% below).

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ROW. verdict()'s ctlFailed condition is RUN-WIDE: one failing row exits 5, and destination() then routes the WHOLE run's datasets — including the large-template and feed rows that passed every gate — to the sibling .unpublished directory. Driven on the real exported functions: a full-shape run with large-template and feed clean and ordinary's control failed returns exit 5 and dir censusclock-2rtt6-56.unpublished, canonical false. SO NO FULL-SHAPE CENSUS RUN CAN EVER BE CANONICAL while the ordinary row's centre stands. All five committed sessions have ordinary failing on both adapters.

THE INSTRUMENT PREDICTED THIS. census_clock_run.cjs's prediction P4, registered before any clock: 'the ORDINARY row (51 elements) sits near this door's own floor; if its control or band cannot hold, the row publishes a REFUSAL with the reason, not a number.' Note the scope: the ROW publishes a refusal. The implementation refuses the RUN. That scope mismatch is the second half of this bead.

CONTEXT THE NUMBERS GIVE. The ordinary row's tared floor is 1.4585 ms against a plumb of 0.7795 ms, with a between-block SD of 0.4382 ms — 3.33 sigma from zero, against large-template's 4.20 and feed's 4.65. Block IQR is 17.0% of the centre against 7.7% on both other rows. The row is at this door's resolution limit, which is what P4 anticipated.

TWO DIRECTIONS, AND THE CHOICE IS A RULING NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION:
(a) Calibrate an empirical check standard for this rig in the idiom of clock_check_standard.json, per rf2-8a746's ruling part 3 — the ordinary row's observed run-median centre is 1.2102 with a between-run SD of 0.0593 over 10 row-runs. Re-centring on the measured 1.2264 with the same +/-25% slack raises per-block in-band to 90.0% and passes 3 of 10 strictly. NOTE that is still a poor rate, so re-centring ALONE does not make this row publishable; the standard would also need a run-level location/dispersion rule as the clock's does. Also note rf2-8a746's own independence caveat: limits seeded from the runs they are judged on are a consistency check, not a false-refusal measurement, and the census rig has no sabotage fixture to prove them against.
(b) REFUSE THE ROW BY CONSTRUCTION, as the roster's write rows already are (rf2-7iqb5, rf2-d2tzk), on the ground that 51 elements through this door is below the instrument's resolution — and separate the refusal's SCOPE so a row-level refusal stops discarding the two rows that passed.

Direction (b) is the cheaper and arguably the more honest one: it states what the instrument cannot measure rather than calibrating a standard for a row that would still refuse most of the time. But it is Mike's call, not a worker's.

FENCE: do NOT change the run-rejection rule. rf2-y0pkh measured it and retained it, and rf2-8a746 rejects retiring a control merely because it shares a shape with one that failed.

Related: rf2-y0pkh (the measurement), rf2-8a746 (the ruling and the clock-side implementation), rf2-2rtt6.56 (the driver).

DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-08, operator-overturnable): the landed implementation is RATIFIED; the bead's close stands; no reopen.

CONTEXT: the operator's dossier and an independent Codex pass both recommended Option B — refuse the ordinary row BY CONSTRUCTION (below the door's resolution, per pre-registered prediction P4 and the rf2-7iqb5/rf2-d2tzk precedent) plus the row-scoped publication repair — and Codex specifically argued PR #7701's empirical standard should not merge as the ordinary adjudicator. #7701 MERGED (all checks green) before this review ran, carrying the empirical standard AS the adjudicator plus the scope fix. This note records why ratification, not reopening, is the right disposition, and fences what the landed standard may be used for.

WHY RATIFY DESPITE THE DIVERGENCE:
1. The higher-leverage half landed exactly as both recommendations wanted: destination() reads run shape only; per-row canonical/notCanonicalWhy with rowsRefused indexed; run-level exit-5 refusal untouched; strict rule untouched for large-template (8/10) and feed (7/10). Counterfactual over the ten committed run-files: 6 with all three rows citable, 4 with one refused beside two citable — vs 0 files with any citable row before. That is the precondition rf2-jo60g's ruling needed.
2. The adjudicator divergence changes NO published claim today. Codex's own independent recompute: the ordinary row's hicasso/uix block ranges STRADDLE the 1.10 line in all ten row-runs — the row is instrument-limited for magnitude purposes even with its control passing. Empirical-standard-adjudicated vs refused-by-construction differ only in whether ordinary's diagnostics are retained as canonical data; neither publishes a magnitude.
3. The landed file is honest about its own blindness, in numbers: the location limits admit P_eff in [1.1295, 2.3216] against a declared 1.7255; the 140-of-300-class sabotage rf2-8a746 proved its own standard against reads 1.1077x here and is ADMITTED — the file calls this P4 restated as a number. Eight mutation proofs pin the rest.
4. Reopening a merged, gates-green, mutation-proved implementation to flip an adjudicator with zero published-claim consequence is litigating minutiae against the operator's posture.

FENCES RECORDED WITH THE RATIFICATION (these are load-bearing, not commentary):
A. census_check_standard.json v1 is DIAGNOSTIC-GRADE until re-baselined. Its false-refusal properties rest on a hold-out of TWO row-runs from one session: zero refusals in two trials leaves a one-sided 95% upper bound of 77.6% on the false-refusal probability — it cannot validate the nominal ~0.4% (NIST control-chart guidance assumes known parameters and wants on the order of 100 baseline values; the five baseline sessions also span five commits, so exchangeability rests on argument, not replication). The file's own demand — a fresh independent baseline next time — is BINDING before this standard's verdicts are treated as strong evidence. Do not quote v1's in-control verdicts as validated-rate adjudications.
B. MAGNITUDE FENCE: no ordinary-row magnitude publishes under any control outcome — all ten hicasso/uix ranges straddle 1.10 (instrument-limited). P4's substance stands: this 51-element witness is below the door's useful resolution for magnitude claims. Publishing an ordinary magnitude would need a fresh ruling of the rf2-diaud class, not a test edit.
C. The tangible reading of the location limits: the lower limit corresponds to ~58 effective elements where the control intends 88 (one extra comment card of five) — the timing check cannot distinguish ~20% from 100% of the intended extra work. The element-count read-back is the actual guard against a structurally truncated arm; it must stay a hard row gate.
D. THE RESCUE PATH (preserved from the Codex pass): if an ordinary-screen magnitude ever becomes decision-critical, reopen as a separate instrumentation task — a finer door, or a genuinely fresh, stable, adequately replicated baseline plus an ordinary-shaped sensitivity witness proven BEFORE calibrating limits. Nothing in this ratification prevents that rescue; the current ten runs do not justify doing it now.

title: hicasso: the published M1 row is conditioned on a rule rf2-8a746 retires — the mount class needs a decision function
description:
RAISED BY THE MAYOR 2026-08-08 14:10 AUSEST from a cross-bead consequence of PR #7698 (rf2-8a746), caught before merging it. Nobody did anything wrong here; the consequence simply falls between two correctly-executed rulings.

THE COLLISION, stated exactly.

rf2-t2flm published the M1 row at ~1.184x vs direct UIx-on-subs (emvod 1.1837x n=4, w3yxd 1.1848x n=3) and put MANDATORY LABELS on every figure, the first of which is: "reportable-subset conditional — THE SUBSET IS THE RUNS PASSING THE STRICT EVERY-BLOCK ctl-2x RULE", with the yield stated as 7 of 14 eligible. Its close reason also records "VERIFIED, NOT MEASURED: clock_readjudicate.cjs over both ensembles exits 0 and reproduces every published figure exactly".

rf2-8a746's criterion 4 retires the all-18-blocks strict rule EVERYWHERE ON THIS INSTRUMENT. That is the rule the label names.

SO AFTER #7698 MERGES: the published figure carries a label referencing a rule the instrument no longer implements, and the tool that was verified to reproduce it no longer does. The #7698 worker reports M1 moving from 4-of-8 to 0-of-8 reportable, because it deliberately left the MOUNT class UNCALIBRATED AND FAILING CLOSED rather than calibrate it — the 8a746 ruling seeds only the bulk class, and calibrating mount there would have taken rf2-t2flm's seat. That restraint was correct.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT AT RISK. The published row is NOT invalidated: it was adjudicated under the rule in force when it was taken, the underlying figures are unchanged, and the new posture is STRICTER not looser, so nothing was published that would now be refused. What breaks is REPRODUCIBILITY — a reader who runs clock_readjudicate.cjs against the committed ensembles to check the M1 row will now get "no reportable subset" rather than the n=4/n=3 the page cites. For a programme whose whole discipline is "a fresh clone can recompute the published claim", that is a real defect even though no number moved.

THE WORK: give the mount class its own decision function, in the idiom rf2-8a746 established for bulk — a level-denominated, empirically calibrated, versioned check standard, seeded from the mount class's own observed behaviour rather than from a theoretical value. rf2-8a746's own finding is the seed and is already on that bead: ctl-2x's true centre is EMPIRICAL (~1.72-1.80 by row class), not 2.00x, "so any mount decision function should state its expectation empirically too".

THEN RECONCILE THE LABEL. Either the M1 row's conditioning label is restated against the new mount rule (annotate-never-erase; the figure does not move), or — if the new rule yields a different eligible subset — the row is re-adjudicated under it and the change recorded as a dated supersession. Which of those applies is an outcome, not a choice to make up front.

FENCES. Do NOT calibrate mount by copying the bulk standard's limits: the classes differ (bulk centre 1.7207x with between-run SD 0.0566; mount's observed behaviour is its own). Do NOT loosen anything to make the published subset reappear — if the honest new rule reports fewer eligible runs, that is the answer and the row is restated. Do NOT touch the bulk standard landed by #7698.

SEQUENCING: after #7698 merges. This is a sitting input — K1's line for the 2026-08-27 sitting is that ~1.18x figure — so it wants resolving before the 2026-08-25 packet freeze.
close_reason:
Implemented and shipped in PR #7700 (branch worker/mountclass-x7x10).

title: hicasso: the masking bound's disputed soundness is unresolved, and rf2-n6w7o was re-closed as a tracker glitch
description:
RAISED by rf2-2rtt6.138's measurement window on 2026-08-08, from reading the
tracker rather than from the run. It is a governance/correctness question and
needs a ruling, not a worker.

THE SUBSTANTIVE HALF. The merged-PR audit of #7682 recorded on rf2-n6w7o says
the 300,000 B masking budget IS NOT PROVED BY ITS PREMISES, on two grounds:

  (1) the code correctly calls 600 KB (the first VISIBLE fall) an UPPER bound
      on where the first collection runs, while safety needs a LOWER bound;
      halving an upper bound does not create one, and the only corroborated
      clean point cited is 240 KB, below the admitted 300 KB boundary;
  (2) a masked leg's true A_k is not bounded by the observed maxStep, because
      maxStep sees only NET positive deltas.

The audit reports EXECUTABLE probes through the merged allocSteps that are
admitted at headroom=0 while their true allocation is 300 KB and 600 KB. If
that is right, the bound can admit a masked window -- i.e. it can fail in the
under-reading direction it exists to close.

THE PROCESS HALF, and it is why nobody has adjudicated (1) and (2). The same
audit says 'exact owner reopened' -- a DELIBERATE reopen. rf2-n6w7o's close
reason then attributes that reopen to a 'second silent tracker revert this
session' and re-closes it, citing merged commits and PR state as evidence.
Both statements cannot be right: the audit says it reopened the bead on
purpose, the close says nothing reopened it. The merge evidence in the close
reason is real but answers a different question -- it proves the PR landed,
not that the bound is sound. The audit's objection has therefore never been
answered on its merits, and the bead is CLOSED.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. rf2-2rtt6.138's run refused on this very bound (98 of 132
windows over budget) and the refusal is recorded on the studio page as
authoritative. THE REFUSAL DIRECTION IS SAFE EITHER WAY -- a bound that is
too permissive still correctly refuses a window 4 MB over it -- so nothing
published so far depends on resolving this. But the moment any window is
CERTIFIED by this bound, its soundness is load-bearing.

WHAT IS WANTED: adjudicate the audit's (1) and (2) on their merits. Either
answer them, or accept them and re-open route (a) -- the independent
in-window witness -- as the way through. Also worth a look: whether the
'silent tracker revert' diagnosis was correct at all, given the audit says it
reopened the bead itself; if the diagnosis was wrong, two other beads closed
on the same reasoning that session (rf2-ih772, rf2-w3yxd) may deserve a
second look.

DO NOT resolve this by widening or deleting the bound.
notes:
MAYOR ADJUDICATION 2026-08-08 13:05 AUSEST — THE TRACKER-DIAGNOSIS HALF OF THIS BEAD IS DISCHARGED. It asked, correctly, whether the "silent tracker revert" diagnosis was right at all, and whether two beads closed on the same reasoning deserved a second look. I answered that this morning; recording it here so the bead narrows to its substantive half.

THE ANSWER: THE DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG ON TWO OF FIVE, AND THIS BEAD WAS RIGHT TO ASK. Five beads went CLOSED -> OPEN on the night of 2026-08-07 and I read all five as one phenomenon. They were two:

- rf2-n6w7o and rf2-w3yxd were DELIBERATE AUDIT REOPENS, each carrying a note reading "exact owner reopened" (the merged-PR audits of #7682 and #7680 respectively). I closed over both.
- rf2-ih772, rf2-2ze1h and rf2-ne3ey carried no such note; those three were genuine reverts and the re-closes stand.

THE TEST I USED WAS THE WRONG ONE, and the failure is reusable: I keyed the re-close on "did this bead's work land on main?" — and it always had. That question cannot distinguish a tracker revert from an audit reopen, BECAUSE AN AUDIT REOPENS PRECISELY WHEN THE WORK HAS LANDED AND LEFT A RESIDUAL. The discriminator was one grep for "exact owner reopened", on the bead the whole time.

REMEDIED, both of them, on 2026-08-08: rf2-n6w7o's close reason now carries a correction retracting the false "nothing reopened it" and cross-referencing this bead, which owns the substantive finding it closed over. rf2-w3yxd was REOPENED with its live remainder (the retained-reader output is 5 row blocks x 3 PAIR blocks x 3 estimator windows = 45 comparisons, not the 42 the page and my close record said), that fix landed in PR #7692, and the bead re-closed on evidence.

SO NOTHING IS OUTSTANDING ON THIS HALF. Do not re-litigate it; the three other beads (ih772, 2ze1h, ne3ey) were checked for the same marker and have none.

WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD IS THE SUBSTANTIVE HALF ONLY: adjudicate the #7682 audit's two grounds against the 300,000 B masking budget — (1) that 600 KB is an UPPER bound on where the first collection runs while safety needs a LOWER one, and halving an upper bound does not create one; (2) that a masked leg's true A_k is not bounded by the observed maxStep, which sees only NET positive deltas. Either answer them, or accept them and re-open route (a), the independent in-window witness. The refusal direction remains safe either way and nothing published leans on the bound — but the moment any window is CERTIFIED by it, its soundness becomes load-bearing. And, unchanged: do NOT resolve this by widening or deleting the bound.
close_reason: RULED 2026-08-08 (delegated, operator-overturnable; full ruling in the comment). Substantive: the #7682 audit is ACCEPTED — probe B (600 KB true allocation admitted at headroom=0) executably falsifies A_k <= maxStep, and clean evidence stops at the 240 KB control while the 300 KB budget admits the unevidenced 240-300 KB band. The bound is DEMOTED to refusal-only; nothing may be certified by it; its replacement is rf2-2rtt6.140's in-window collection witness, with witness-validation-before-certification carried into that package as an acceptance criterion. Process: n6w7o's mis-diagnosis already conceded on n6w7o (mayor, 10:20); rf2-ih772 reopened by this review — its #7679 audit reopen was steamrolled and its provenance fix (the-candidates-clock.md:19-24, 1.4896x is yd52q's eight-run ensemble, not emvod's seven-run) is still unactioned in the tree.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-08, operator-overturnable). Both halves ruled; dossier ai/decisions/rf2-2rtt6.141.masking-bound-soundness-ruling.md folded in and deleted.

SUBSTANTIVE HALF — THE AUDIT IS ACCEPTED. The 300,000 B masking bound will not be defended further, because its second premise is executably falsified and its first stands on evidence that points the wrong way:

- Probe B is decisive: five 50 KB legs followed by a 350 KB leg that reclaims 350 KB reach TRUE allocation 600 KB yet return falls=0, rise=250 KB, maxStep=50 KB, headroom=0 — and are ADMITTED. That falsifies "a masked leg's true A_k <= observed maxStep" (maxStep sees only NET positive deltas). Probe A (five 60 KB legs, fifth reclaims 60 KB: true 300 KB, admitted at headroom=0) shows the same hole at the budget's own boundary.
- Premise (1), read precisely: the 240 KB D=1,000 control (8.13 B/double against a predicted 8) is genuine POSITIVE evidence of no collection at 240 KB — that is the defence's valid half and it is preserved. But clean evidence STOPS at 240 KB; the 300 KB budget admits windows in the 240-300 KB band where no clean evidence exists, under a 600 KB first-visible-fall figure that is an UPPER bound on where collection starts while safety needs a LOWER bound. Halving an upper bound does not create one. (Correction to the review dossier's own text, for the record: 240 KB is a corroborated CLEAN point, not an observed collection.)

DISPOSITION: the bound is DEMOTED TO A REFUSAL-ONLY GATE, effective now. It may refuse windows (refusal is safe in both readings — nothing published depends on it) but NOTHING MAY BE CERTIFIED BY IT. Its replacement is the independent in-window collection witness of rf2-2rtt6.140's composed package (route (b) there = route (a) here); see the dated 2026-08-08 decision on rf2-2rtt6.140. Per the bead's own fence, the bound is neither widened nor deleted — it is superseded-by-witness.

CARRIED INTO THE .140 PACKAGE AS AN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION (the defence's second valid half, and the audit's own closing line): the witness must be empirically validated before any window it certifies is published — "a witness whose own reliability is unmeasured is a second thing to distrust"; route (b)-style bounds would need a measured lower bound plus an independently justified per-leg maximum. The untouched falls gate stays.

PROCESS HALF — RESOLVED, WITH ONE REOPEN:

- rf2-n6w7o: the mis-diagnosis is already conceded on that bead itself (mayor correction 2026-08-08 10:20: "MY RE-CLOSE REASON ON THIS BEAD CONTAINS A FALSE STATEMENT"). n6w7o stays closed; THIS bead is the audit finding's durable home, and the finding's resolution rides rf2-2rtt6.140.
- rf2-ih772: VERIFIED NOT CORRECTED, and its steamrolled audit item is still live in the tree — the-candidates-clock.md:19-24 attributes 1.4896x to rf2-emvod's SEVEN-run ensemble, while bulk-broad-re-taken.md:195,243,360 records 1.4896x as rf2-yd52q's EIGHT-run quiet-box ensemble (1.3737x is emvod's heavier-regime figure). REOPENED by this review with that worker-sized doc fix as its remaining scope.
- The habit lesson stays where the mayor recorded it (rf2-w3yxd's 2026-08-08 10:20 reopen): "did the work land?" cannot distinguish a revert from an audit reopen — before re-closing an unexpectedly-OPEN bead, grep its notes for a deliberate reopen marker ("REOPEN exact ... owner", "AUDIT-REOPEN") first.

title: hicasso: the allocation row needs an in-window collection witness that net growth cannot mask (blocks rf2-2rtt6.138)
description:
RAISED by the merged-PR audit of #7644, recorded as the newest note on rf2-2rtt6.138, and CONFIRMED unmet by reading the code during rf2-2rtt6.138's quiet-box attempt on 2026-08-07 (abcb34217c).

THE FAULT. p0_run.cjs's allocSteps counts a collection ONLY when an adjacent in-page usedJSHeapSize delta is negative. If V8 collects during write-all!/flushSync and the allocations in that same sampled leg equal or exceed the reclaimed bytes, post >= pre, falls stays 0, and the vanished allocation is silently omitted from rise. The row then reports a clean window that under-reads — and under-reading allocation is precisely the direction that manufactures HD-002's predicted flat-at-zero.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN THE RIG TODAY, verified rather than assumed:
  - allocSteps (p0_run.cjs ~1001) is the ONLY collector detector, and it is the sign test above.
  - cdpBracket (post.cdp - pre.cdp) is recorded on every control and every arm and appears in NO failure path. It brackets the window from OUTSIDE and cannot speak to what happened between the in-page samples.
  - p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs contains no allocation coverage whatsoever — zero matches for alloc, falls, collection or masked across its 288 lines. There is no allocation-row structural test in which to pin the masked-GC case.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. The 2026-08-07 quiet-box run of the published witness (P0_ALLOC_ROUNDS=2 P0_ALLOC_WRITES=6 P0_ALLOC_WARMUPS=2) refused on 36 falling steps across 44 windows, so the fail-open did not decide that run. But the fits it produced show exactly the shape the fault would manufacture: candidate slopes 36-55 B/read against donors 289-610, i.e. candidate MINUS donor of -234 and -574 B/read. An instrument that under-reads is an instrument that hands HD-002 its own prediction, and the row must not be able to publish that on any config.

WHAT IS REQUIRED, per the audit, before rf2-2rtt6.138 may publish a small-witness fit — EITHER:
  (a) an independent in-window collection witness or refusal that net growth cannot mask; OR
  (b) a comparably rigorous BOUND proving the measured window cannot collect.

(b) is the likelier route for a small-witness arm and is worth costing first: at a few dozen boundaries a window's cumulative garbage is orders below the measured ~600 KB fall threshold and far below what a young-gen scavenge reclaims, so the masking condition (in-leg allocation >= reclaimed bytes) may be excludable by arithmetic rather than by a new counter. But the bound has to be MEASURED and stated, not asserted — which needs a per-window cumulative-garbage reading the row does not currently take.

AND, either way: pin the masked-GC case in the allocation-row structural tests. Today a synthetic sample stream in which a collection is fully masked by net growth would pass allocSteps silently, and nothing anywhere would notice.

DO NOT discharge this by widening the falls gate or by trusting cdpBracket as-is. The falls gate is the part that works.
notes:
DISCHARGED via PR #7682 (worker/allocwitness-n6w7o). ROUTE (b) — the bound —
enforced as a refusal. No measurement was taken: the box is shared.

THE BOUND, and why it is not circular. Masking cannot precede the FIRST
collection, so `rise` counts every leg before it EXACTLY. The collector does
not fire until ~ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B of cumulative garbage has built up
since the driver's forced GC. So if a collection fired in leg k:

    rise >= (every leg before k) >= ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B - A_k

and A_k (that leg's own allocation) is bounded by the largest rising step the
window shows, because the legs are n repetitions of one work unit and every
earlier leg is counted exactly. Contrapositive, and it is the gate:

    rise + maxStep <= budget  =>  NO collection ran, masked or otherwise.

NET GROWTH CANNOT DEFEAT IT, which is the property the bead asked for.
Masking only REMOVES bytes from `rise`, moving a window further under budget
— but the allocation that gave the collector its reason to run is already
counted in full, in the legs before it, where no masking is possible.

BUDGET = ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B / 2 = 300,000 B. Measured, not asserted, and
both halves stated: (1) 600 KB is where the first VISIBLE fall appeared in the
standalone probes, so it is an UPPER bound on where collection actually starts
and the gate must take the conservative side; (2) 300 KB sits just above the
240 KB D=1,000 control window at the default 30 writes, which reads 8.13
B/double against a predicted 8 — a window that under-read would not hit its
prediction, so the control is POSITIVE evidence of no collection at that
scale, where a fall count of zero is not. Not an env knob, and a `lacks`
assertion pins that.

WHY NOT ROUTE (a). Every in-page witness available (WeakRef /
FinalizationRegistry liveness, or promoting cdpBracket into a failure path)
would itself need empirical validation before the row could lean on it, and
no measurement taken on a shared box is valid. A witness whose own
reliability is unmeasured is a second thing to distrust, not an improvement
on the sign test. cdpBracket is untouched and still appears in no failure
path, as instructed.

THE FALLS GATE IS UNTOUCHED and still exits. This is a SECOND, independent
refusal beside it: a falling step is a collection the counter SAW, a window
over budget is one it could not have seen.

WHAT THE BOUND DOES NOT CLOSE, stated in the p0_run.cjs header rather than
glossed: a window in which EVERY leg is masked defeats both terms. `falls`
catches it the moment one collection overshoots, `maxStep` the moment one leg
runs unmasked, and nothing catches it if neither happens — that needs a
per-leg allocation counter V8 does not expose in-page. It is unreachable for
the small-witness arm, whose warm write is too small to cross the threshold
inside a single leg at all.

STRUCTURAL PIN, hermetic. p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs went 14 -> 27 tests.
MUTATION PROOF on BEHAVIOUR, not on a missing symbol: commit 1f71231e6c
exports the UNREPAIRED allocSteps and the pin fails 13/27, exit 1, with the
assertions BEFORE the failing one all passing — falls===0, fall===0,
rise===600000 on a stream that hid a 200 KB collection. Repair 1408de6b9d:
27 passed, exit 0.

GATES: node --check both files 0; structural 14 baseline / 13-of-27 red /
27 green; npm run test:script-helpers 0; sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh 0
("PASS fast PR spine"); sh scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh main 0.

p0_heap.cljs was NOT touched — the bound needed no new page-side reading, so
the per-window cumulative-garbage reading the description anticipated turned
out to be unnecessary: maxStep is derivable from the samples the page already
returns. That is the one place this discharge differs from what the bead
predicted it would cost.

NOT WRITTEN TO THE STUDIO PAGE. docs/design/hicasso/studio/*.md is held by
worker/m1row-t2flm and was outside my write fence. The
implementation-governing conclusion is in the p0_run.cjs header
(ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B), which is the tracked record for the instrument's
method. If a note on
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-survival-metrics-allocation-half.md is wanted,
it needs a separate bead once that fence lifts.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7682 (completeness, correctness, implementation quality): exact owner reopened; no duplicate. The proposed 300,000 B bound is not proved by its premises. First, the code correctly calls 600 KB (the first VISIBLE fall) an UPPER bound on the first possible collection, while safety needs a LOWER bound; halving an upper bound does not create one, and the only corroborated clean point cited is 240 KB, below the admitted 300 KB boundary. Second, a masked leg's true A_k is not bounded by maxStep, because maxStep sees only NET positive deltas; repetition of one work unit does not prove allocation equality. Executable probes through the merged allocSteps show both holes: five 60 KB legs with the fifth reclaiming 60 KB have true allocation 300 KB but falls=0, rise=240 KB, maxStep=60 KB, headroom=0 and are admitted; five 50 KB legs followed by a 350 KB leg that reclaims 350 KB reach 600 KB true allocation yet return falls=0, rise=250 KB, maxStep=50 KB, headroom=0 and are admitted. The first is consistent with a first collection anywhere between the evidenced-clean 240 KB point and the acknowledged 600 KB upper bound; the second falsifies A_k <= observed maxStep. Keep the untouched falls gate, but route (b) still needs a measured lower bound plus an independently justified per-leg maximum, or route (a). The 27-case suite and syntax/diff checks pass because its masked fixture is already far over budget and does not witness either admitted boundary.
MAYOR CORRECTION 2026-08-08 10:20 AUSEST — MY RE-CLOSE REASON ON THIS BEAD CONTAINS A FALSE STATEMENT. Recording it plainly rather than quietly amending it.

WHAT I WROTE, at 23:06 on 2026-08-07: "RE-CLOSED after a second silent tracker revert this session ... read OPEN again at 23:04 — NOTHING REOPENED IT."

THAT IS WRONG. Something did reopen it: the MERGED-PR AUDIT OF #7682, recorded on this bead above, which states "exact owner reopened; no duplicate." The bead went OPEN deliberately and for cause. I read the transition as an instance of the silent-revert pattern that genuinely hit three other beads that night (rf2-ih772, rf2-2ze1h, rf2-ne3ey) and re-closed over a live audit finding.

WHY I GOT IT WRONG, because the failure is reusable. I keyed the re-close on the wrong question — "did this bead's work land on main?" — and it had: three commits and a merged PR at 86/86. That test cannot distinguish a tracker revert from an audit reopen, because an audit reopens a bead PRECISELY WHEN the work has landed and left a residual. The distinguishing signal was on the bead the whole time, one grep away: a note reading "exact owner reopened". My own standing memory (gcchurn-reclose-misses-audit-obligations) says to grep for exactly that before closing, and I did not.

THE FINDING I CLOSED OVER IS SUBSTANTIVE, and is now carried by rf2-2rtt6.141: the 300,000 B masking budget is not proved by its premises — 600 KB is an UPPER bound on where the first collection runs while safety needs a LOWER bound, and halving an upper bound does not create one; and a masked leg's true A_k is not bounded by the observed maxStep, which sees only NET positive deltas. The audit reports executable probes admitted at headroom=0 whose true allocation is 300 KB and 600 KB.

WHAT SAVES THE PROGRAMME FROM MY ERROR, and it is luck rather than judgement: rf2-2rtt6.138's window (2026-08-08) refused anyway — 98 of 132 windows maskable, tightest headroom -3,999,106 B — so nothing has been published on the strength of this bound. A too-permissive bound still correctly refuses a window four megabytes over it. But nothing may LEAN ON IT TO CERTIFY until .141 is ruled.

THIS BEAD STAYS CLOSED because .141 now owns the open question and a duplicate would help nobody. The correction is recorded here so the record is not left asserting something untrue.

title: hicasso: read_profile phase B cannot reach a number — the entry reaper (4 ms) outlives lane/settle! (one macrotask)
description:
FOUND by rf2-d360z's granted quiet-box re-take, 2026-08-07, at abcb34217c. Two attempts, runner exit 1 both times, identical failure — the re-take produced NO phase-B number and the published absolutes stand unchanged.

SYMPTOM. read_profile_app.cljs completes phase A cleanly (arm-order guard reportable, positive control PASS on both attempts) and then throws in phase B on the first sampled arm:

  phase-B residue after commit — expected {:cells 141, :cell-refs 141, :boundaries 1, :edges 141, :entries 6}, found {... :entries 5}

Byte-identical on both attempts: same arm (commit), same counts, 6 -> 5.

THE MECHANISM, read out of the code rather than inferred. rf2-2rtt6.84 (337b2c2fb4, 2026-08-04) moved arm1/runtime.cljs's entry-reap-horizon-ms from 0 to 4, so the provisional-entry reaper could not beat React back to its own passive flush on a hydrateRoot. lane/settle! is ONE macrotask — js/Promise over setTimeout 0 — and 4 ms is strictly outside it.

  1. phase-B setup harvests four read-set entries via rt/render-body (one per commit-frame). Each is minted with refs 0 and each arms a reaper at +4 ms.
  2. baseline (rt/residue) is read after ONE lane/settle!, i.e. at ~0 ms — before any reaper can fire. It therefore counts all six live entries.
  3. the reapers fire ~4 ms later, during the first sampled arm. commit is the only phase-B arm that raises refs (via rt/commit-boundary!) and its teardown drops them again, so any entry whose reaper lands while refs is 0 is evicted.
  4. rounds-async!'s gate compares residue by EQUALITY against that baseline, sees 5 against 6, and throws.

WHY IT NEVER FIRED BEFORE. With the horizon at 0 the reaper's setTimeout was armed BEFORE settle!'s and fired first, so every residue read saw the same post-reap state and the equality held deterministically. Both published phase-B runs (cb41ee537b and 0c0ff21f0d, both 2026-08-02) predate 337b2c2fb4 — which is why the-cold-read-mount-term.md could record a residue gate that never fired.

THE GATE IS RIGHT AND MUST NOT BE WIDENED. It is reporting a real disagreement: the baseline phase B computes is no longer reachable under the runtime the arms measure. The repair belongs on the instrument's SETUP or on the settle point (e.g. settle past the reap horizon before baselining, or hold the harvested entries' refs above zero for the row's duration) — never on the gate's equality, and never by reverting the 4 ms, which rf2-2rtt6.84 measured and needs.

NOT URGENT AS A CORRECTNESS MATTER. read_profile_app is a DIAGNOSTIC clock and publishes no gated row. But it is the only instrument that decomposes the commit half, and until this is repaired rf2-d360z cannot run and the commit/c-local absolutes on the-cold-read-mount-term.md sections 1 and 4 cannot be re-taken at all.

SIZE THE FIX AGAINST THE PRIZE FIRST. rf2-d360z's own arithmetic says the drift it wanted to resolve is 141 mints x 53 ns = 0.0075 ms/commit against a 0.025 ms grid — under a third of a quantum, and the two published absolutes sit 5 quanta apart run-to-run. So repairing this instrument does NOT make that re-take resolvable; it makes phase B runnable again for the next question.
close_reason:
REPAIRED, PR #7683 open (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7683), branch worker/phaseb-981nt, rebased on origin/main.

THE REPAIR SITE, and why the other was rejected. The bead offered two: settle past the reap horizon before baselining, or hold the harvested entries' refs above zero for the row. Took the SETTLE POINT. The refs-hold cannot be done without changing what the arm measures: the only honest way to raise an entry's refs is to commit a boundary on it, which pre-acquires all 141 cells per frame, so the sampled 'commit' arm would then be acquiring existing cells instead of minting them and the arm's entire subject (cell construction, reaction wiring, reader membership) evaporates. The alternative -- a runtime mutator poking refs for no reason but this rig -- bends the runtime to accommodate the instrument.

The settle point costs the measurement nothing: a reaped entry is dropped from the runtime's entry CACHE, not destroyed (the object survives in the closure phase B holds), and rt/commit-boundary! reads the entry and never the cache.

WHAT LANDED (three files, all under implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/):
- arm1/runtime.cljs gains a public quiesced!, a promise resolving strictly past entry-reap-horizon-ms. Callers settle against the runtime's own horizon instead of a copy of it -- the copy is what drifted, and this file already carries that lesson once (rf2-6wh9o, cell-watch-key). The horizon stays a margin no caller may rely on; the promise says 'wait for me', never 'here is my number'.
- read_profile_app.cljs names the concept it never had: residue-settle!, the ONE point behind which the baseline, the between-sample gate and the final zero are read. The defect was invisible for exactly as long as the concept was unnamed.
- read_profile_baseline_cljs_test.cljs, the witness -- three rows driving residue-settle! ITSELF rather than rt/quiesced!, because a witness on the primitive would stay green however the instrument settled (that vacuum is what let the horizon move with nothing going red).

THE GATE WAS NOT WIDENED AND THE 4 ms WAS NOT REVERTED.

A SECOND, LATENT FAILURE FOUND AND FIXED en route: the FINAL residue check had the same defect. Releasing the warm hold arms that entry's reaper too, and a bare macrotask lands in front of it -- the 'final residue not clean' gate would have thrown on :entries 1 after phase B had been repaired. It is behind the same settle point now.

RED-THEN-GREEN, proven: with residue-settle! reverted to (lane/settle!) -- the protocol exactly as it stood on main, everything else unchanged -- npm run test:cljs exits 1 with 3 failures, baseline {... :entries 4} against a settled {... :entries 0}, the instrument's six-against-five in miniature. With the repair: 12797 tests / 64387 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors, exit 0.

GATES (all foreground, worktree-local logs, gate root verified as the worker worktree): test:hicasso-compile exit 0 (137 lane namespaces, 0 warnings); test:cljs exit 0; scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 (61 stages); clj-kondo exit 0 over the three changed files (local v2025.10.23, CI pins 2026.04.15 -- CI decides); check-beads-pr-boundary.sh exit 0.

NO MEASUREMENT TAKEN. No quiet window opened, no number published, no absolute re-taken -- five other workers were on the box.

rf2-d360z IS NOW UNBLOCKED once #7683 merges: phase B can reach a number again. Its scope correction stands -- the sub-quantum drift question is dead and the re-take is worth a window only as a refresh against the current runtime.

title: docs(method): measurement-window shape, beads audit hook, reading a live worker
description:
Three field-learned rules exist only in chat and bd remember; a fresh mayor inherits none.

GAP 1 - dispatch-prompt-template.md has five shapes, all assuming iterate-until-green. A measurement-window worker must do the opposite. Written from scratch twice in one day. Add a sixth shape.

GAP 2 - bootstrap.md says nothing about the beads audit hook pushing chore(beads): audit merged PR NNNN to main asynchronously after every merge, so during a merge burst main never holds still and the next merge is refused Base branch was modified. GAP 3 - bootstrap.md forbids reaping on a proxy signal but does not say how to tell a live long-running worker from a stranded one. Got it wrong twice today in opposite directions. Discriminator: has the commit count on its branch moved since last tick.

Fence: docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md, plus counterpart wording in .claude/commands/mayor-*.md.

title: RULING NEEDED: M1's ctl-2x DID pass on a quiet box, 4 runs of 8 — rf2-jcm3p's premise needs re-examining
description:
rf2-jcm3p ruled (2026-08-06) that the M1 mount row publishes a REGIME and not a magnitude, and the stated ground was that its positive control cannot adjudicate it ANYWHERE: 'the row's ctl-2x fails at 1.8173x against 2.00x'.

rf2-emvod's quiet-window ensemble measures otherwise. Over 8 full-roster runs at c172f22bb0 on a box with Processor Queue Length 0 before and after, M1's ctl-2x read a mean of 1.8000x and PASSED the strict rule on 5 of 8 runs on the published clock and on 4 of 8 runs on BOTH clocks. clock_readjudicate.cjs consequently draws a reportable subset on M1 - the only row in the ensemble that has one - at:

  hicasso / reagent-subs   1.1402x  (n=4, whole ensemble 1.1429x [1.0723 - 1.2640])
  hicasso / uix-subs       1.1837x  (n=4, whole ensemble 1.1798x [1.1346 - 1.2347])
  uix-subs / reagent-subs  0.9651x  (n=4, whole ensemble 0.9757x [0.9094 - 1.1235])

NOTHING IS PUBLISHED FROM THIS AND NO PAGE IS RESTATED. The worker recorded it on rows-re-adjudicated-on-the-corrected-clock.md section 7.2 and stopped there, because whether the ruling changes is a RULING and not a measurement, and because a control passing on 4 of 8 runs is not obviously the same claim as a control that can adjudicate the row.

Note also that these magnitudes sit well below both figures the programme has carried on this row (1.4896x and 1.3737x), so accepting them would be a material restatement and not a confirmation. The reportable subset is n=4 and the whole-ensemble spread is wide.

Datasets retained, so the mayor can re-adjudicate without the box:
  node freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/clock_readjudicate.cjs     freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/clock-emvod/run*.json

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-07 ~21:45 AUSEST, operator-overturnable): M1 REGAINS A MAGNITUDE — modified Option A, on both retained ensembles, both estimators published.

THE RULING. The regime-only statement is superseded. M1 publishes:
- vs direct UIx-on-subs: ~1.184x on the programme's floor-normalised TaskDuration estimator (emvod reportable subset 1.1837x n=4; w3yxd reportable subset 1.1848x n=3 — two independently launched ensembles agreeing to 0.11 percentage points), with the raw quotient (~1.155x — the direct arm-to-arm comparison touching neither floor) stated BESIDE it, never hidden. Whole-ensemble bands quoted: 1.1798 [1.1346-1.2347] n=8; 1.2057 [1.1731-1.2390] n=6. All fourteen whole-ensemble run means sit above 1.10x.
- vs Reagent-on-subs: TWO ensemble-specific estimates, not a pooled point — 1.1402x n=4 (emvod) and 1.1100x n=3 (w3yxd) floor-normalised; raw quotients 1.1545 / 1.0969. The replication is looser here; a falsely precise single figure is refused.
- MANDATORY LABELS on every quoted figure: reportable-subset conditional (the subset is the runs passing the strict every-block ctl-2x rule), and the control yield stated plainly: 7 of 14 runs eligible, Wilson 95% ~0.27-0.73 — this control CAN adjudicate M1, not "usually will".

WHY THIS SHAPE AND NOT THE DOSSIER'S OPTION C (write a k-of-n decision function, then re-adjudicate): retro-writing a rule with outcomes visible is not pre-registration and cannot remove researcher degrees of freedom. It is also unnecessary: the operative per-run eligibility rule (controlVerdict: EVERY one of 18 blocks inside the 2.00x +/-25% band, clock_run.cjs:344-362) was committed 2026-08-01, BEFORE either ensemble was captured — genuine pre-registration already exists — and the second ensemble (clock-w3yxd, same clock_run.cjs blob c6a4f249153f, independently launched) supplies the replication that the n=4 objection wanted. A pre-committed decision function is the right tool only PROSPECTIVELY: if stronger precision ever becomes decision-critical, pre-commit the estimator, the pair-level clear rule, the required eligible count and the precision target BEFORE collecting a genuinely new ensemble. That standing condition is part of this ruling.

THE PREMISE CORRECTION (why jcm3p's ground fell): the 2026-08-06 ruling treated ctl-2x mean 1.8173x-vs-2.00x as categorical failure. The implemented rule never required the mean to equal 2.00x — controlVerdict tests per-block band membership; the 1.80x centre is the KNOWN additive undershoot the code itself documents as a signal check, not an exact model. Seven of fourteen runs pass the implemented rule on both clocks. rf2-8a746's diagnosis explains the mechanism (level denominator, centre 20% above the refusal edge; per-block in-band rates ~95% predict exactly the observed pass rates) — the passes are mechanistic, not luck.

VERIFIED BEFORE RULING (this pass, from committed data only, no window): clock_readjudicate.cjs over data/clock-emvod/run1-8.json and data/clock-w3yxd/run1-6.json both exit 0 and reproduce every figure above exactly; the strict rule's source location and its pre-ensemble commit date confirmed; both ensembles' datasets present in tree.

DISCLOSURE OBLIGATION FOR THE PUBLISHING WORKER (disclose, don't build): the readjudicator's row-level pool accepts a bar carrying an adjudication record even when marked clear:false. title: hicasso: read_profile_app's cost model transcribes a wire-cell! shape the runtime no longer has (rf2-2kshh follow-up)
description:
rf2-2kshh added (interop/activate-derived-value! reaction) to arm1/runtime.cljs wire-cell!. read_profile_app.cljs:405-424 hand-transcribes wire-cell!'s shape as a retained-heap cost model — subs/subscribe, @r, add-watch, add-on-dispose!, with the C-NOSUB / C-NOWATCH / C-NOREADERS ablations hanging off it — and does NOT include the activation. The rig therefore models a shape the runtime no longer has.

NO PUBLISHED FIGURE MOVES. The app installs the UIx adapter (rf/init! uix-adapter/adapter, line 576), and activate-derived-value! is a routed no-op on the React-hook spine, so the omitted call prices exactly zero there.

BUT THE CAPTURE RUN BELONGS IN THE PRICED SHAPE, for two reasons. Structurally: the rig's whole claim is that it transcribes wire-cell!, and a transcription that has silently diverged is what the rf2-2rtt6.32 call-convention discipline exists to prevent — these arms are deliberately LOCAL COPIES of shipping code, so they drift by construction. Numerically: it would matter the moment the rig is pointed at a ratom host, because deref-capture retains a watching array per reaction and adds an entry to each source's watcher set — per-key retained heap the model would understate — and it is not purely additive either, since the capture run REPLACES the raw (f) the baseline deref would otherwise perform.

Suggested: add the activation to the transcribed shape, and consider whether it wants its own ablation mode (C-NOACTIVATE) so the capture's retained cost is attributable rather than folded into the subscribe term.
notes:
WORKER RECORD (worker/profshape-lzpfj, commit e58400ef62, PR #7657, merged as 04bb0fa73a).

THE C-NOACTIVATE ABLATION FIT THE RIG UNCHANGED, exactly as this bead proposed — no substitute shape was needed. The phase-B arms are a (mk-local <mode>) family over one commit-local!, every delta is quoted as c-local - variant, and lane/slot-order is generic in (count arms) with only n=2 special-cased. So the whole wiring is: one more ^:const (C-NOACTIVATE 5), one more {:id :c-noactivate} arm entry, one more id in the report roster, one more delta-line. It sits between :c-local and :c-nowatch, mirroring wire-cell!'s activate -> baseline -> watch order, which commit-local! now performs.

NO MEASUREMENT WAS TAKEN, and none was required to land it honestly. The delta line carries its own annotation in the log output — 'routed no-op on this UIx host — expect the noise floor; real only under the ratom family' — so a reader cannot mistake ~0 for 'the capture is free'. The two ratom-host facts this bead stated (the retained watching array + per-source watcher entry, and the capture run REPLACING the raw (f) so the delta is bookkeeping rather than a second evaluation) are both written into the namespace docstring, not just the PR.

No 'bundle changed on disk during the sweep', no spawn-contention child failures.

title: hicasso: strike the survival-metric page's four Reagent-segment rows — they are a no-op arm, not a noisy measurement
description:
FILED BY THE MAYOR 2026-08-07, on merging PR #7644 (the-survival-metrics-allocation-half.md is now on main at 5af99f27ff).

THE PROBLEM. That page publishes four Reagent-segment lad/hicasso rows (99/100/102/98/103 B/boundary) and a 'Hicasso, Reagent substrate' fit line (0 B/read, r2 0.283), presented as REFUSED-for-noise. The rf2-2rtt6.137 diagnosis established they are something worse: the arm NEVER RE-RENDERED. Its DOM was stale by exactly the number of writes each window drove, every round, every rung, and its allocation column sat flat on ~100 B/boundary — which is the FLOOR's figure, an arm with no subscription that cannot re-render.

WHY 'REFUSED' IS THE WRONG WORD AND MATTERS. A refusal says 'we measured and the fit did not hold'. The truth is 'we measured nothing — the arm was deaf'. Left as-is, a future reader could reasonably re-run those rungs hoping for a quieter box, when no box will ever help. Worse, ~0 B/read on a no-op arm is EXACTLY the flat-at-zero answer HD-002 predicts for the survival metric, so the rows read as weak confirmation of the architecture's central claim while being an artefact of a bug.

SCOPE: strike the four rows and the fit line — do not merely re-caption them — and state the cause (the arm did not re-render; see rf2-2kshh) with the read-back evidence. Keep the UIX-SEGMENT figures: they are untouched by this mechanism (React-hook spine is push-based from birth, and those read-backs all passed). They remain unpublishable on the row's own fit criterion (r2 0.311, slope -37 B/read, 0 of 4 rounds linear) — that refusal is genuine and stands.

SEQUENCING: rf2-2kshh (the one-line activation fix) is in flight. This bead may land before or after it — the strike is correct either way, because the rows were invalid when taken. If 2kshh has landed, say so and note that a re-take is now POSSIBLE; if not, say the re-take is blocked on it.
