title: xray: auto-open-on-error never fires on the ratom family — rf2-8cnxg in the settings watcher
description:
FOURTH OCCURRENCE of the rf2-8cnxg defect shape, found by the same read-only
sweep (2026-08-07) that filed rf2-wmpte. Sibling of rf2-2kshh; independent fix.

THE DEFECT. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/settings/effects.cljs:600-634,
install-auto-open-watcher!:

    (when-let [reaction ((:subscribe (rf/capture-frame :rf/xray))
                         [:rf.xray/issues-ribbon])]
      (let [watch-fn (fn [_k _r _old new-val] ...)]
        ;; Seed the baseline from the reaction's CURRENT value before
        ;; add-watch -- a reagent/re-frame reaction is already live the
        ;; instant subscribe returns ...
        (reset! last-issue-count (count (:issues @reaction)))
        (add-watch reaction ::auto-open-on-error watch-fn)
        (reset! auto-open-watcher reaction)))

subscribe -> plain deref -> add-watch, with no interop/activate-derived-value!.
The comment at line 621 states the false premise verbatim; it is the exact
belief observation.cljc:1962-1973 was written to refute.

WHY IT BREAKS. Under the ratom family the subscription IS a bare Reaction
(subs.cljc:1304 -> spine.cljs:3419-3421, make-reaction, deliberately NOT
:auto-run). A Reaction captures its sources only through deref-capture; a deref
outside *ratom-context* with no auto-run takes the on-demand branch
(reagent2/ratom.cljs:395-415), runs the body raw and leaves watching nil.
_handle-change is never called, _queued-run requires (some? watching), so a
source write reaches nothing. Watchable, watched, silent.

UN-ACTIVATED BY CONSTRUCTION, not by luck -- checked three ways:
  1. :rf.xray/issues-ribbon has EXACTLY ONE reference in the whole src tree --
     this line. Every other hit is a test.
  2. panels.cljs:307-311 says so outright: 'There is no dedicated Issues tab or
     aggregate panel ... the :rf.xray/issues-ribbon composite ... is the
     auto-open-on-error signal source.' It is a signal, never a rendered value,
     so no component render ever supplies it a capture context.
  3. mount/close! (mount.cljs:898-907) is a CSS-only hide -- the shell's
     mounted-ness is not the variable. Even a fully open shell renders no
     consumer of this sub.

OBSERVABLY WRONG. With :auto-open-on-error? true, on a Reagent or reagent-slim
host, Xray NEVER auto-opens on the first error. The empty -> non-empty edge
raises no notification. It works on UIx / Helix / re-frame.ui / Freehand
(push-based from birth), so the feature is adapter-dependent while the spec
promises it unconditionally -- xray/016-Auxiliary-Panels.md:657,
xray/018-Event-Spine.md:1028.

THE FIX, by analogy to observation.cljc:1959-1990 ('ACTIVATE, then watch, then
observe -- and the order is the whole fix for rf2-8cnxg'):

    (interop/activate-derived-value! reaction)   ; <- add, before the seed
    (reset! last-issue-count (count (:issues @reaction)))
    (add-watch reaction ::auto-open-on-error watch-fn)

Keep the seeding deref -- activation runs the body once and the seed wants a
settled node, which is exactly the ACTIVATE -> watch -> observe order
build-node-handle! uses. Total and idempotent: a no-op on every non-ratom
substrate. Tools may require re-frame.interop (the bundle-isolation rule runs
the other way: implementation must not require from tools).

WHY NO SUITE SAW IT -- both axes are pinned in the repo's own words.
  - The unit suite runs headless plain-atom and skips the path DELIBERATELY:
    settings/effects_cljs_test.cljs:218-223 -- 'the full
    install-auto-open-watcher! add-watch path can't be driven under this
    suite's headless plain-atom adapter (its derived subscriptions reify
    IDeref/IDisposable only, not IWatchable); that reactive glue is exercised
    in the browser suites.'
  - It is NOT exercised in the browser suites. tools/xray/testbeds/ mentions
    auto-open-on-error only in comments; the setting defaults to false
    (xray/spec/015-Configuration.md:541) and panel_gallery/gallery_settings.cljs:81
    pins it OFF. The deferral points at coverage that does not exist -- and the
    browser testbed that would have caught it runs the Reagent adapter
    (testbeds/standard_epochs/core.cljs:844, (rf/init! reagent-adapter/adapter)),
    the exact exposing combination.

ACCEPTANCE. Drive the watcher on a ratom adapter: flip :auto-open-on-error? on
with the shell hidden, produce a first issue, assert the shell reopens. It must
go through install-auto-open-watcher!'s real add-watch on the real reaction --
calling watch-fn directly (what the current unit suite does) is what hid this.

Cross-ref: rf2-8cnxg (the original, observation port), rf2-2kshh (second
occurrence, hicasso arm1 wire-cell!), rf2-wmpte (third, machines/timer).
Working notes: ai/findings/2026-08-07.activate-derived-value-third-site-sweep.md
sec 2.2.

Fixed in PR #7650 (branch worker/xrayact-lynzk, not yet merged).

before the baseline seed in settings/effects.cljs install-auto-open-watcher!.

from tools/xray (six src namespaces require it; the edge runs tools ->

'a reaction is already live the instant subscribe returns' as law. A new

installs the reagent-slim adapter (the ratom-family adapter xray/deps.edn

The sibling suite's deferral comment ('that reactive glue is exercised in the

It now points at the new file.

title: hicasso: nothing pins the codemod's JVM prop-name against the codec's .cljs slot rule — extract it to .cljc
description:
FOUND by the rf2-2rtt6.106 codemod design pass (PR #7646), recorded there as the one open question it could not close.

THE GAP. The migration codemod must decide prop-name slots on the JVM, but the codec that decides them at runtime is .cljs. So the tool REIMPLEMENTS prop-name. The corpus pins the tool; the door's suite pins the runtime; NOTHING PINS THEM EQUAL.

WHY IT IS THE defect class the codemod exists to delete. A drift between the two is SILENT: the tool rewrites a prop one way, the runtime reads it another, and the author's source now says something the framework does not do. That is precisely the silent-divergence failure the whole design is built to prevent, reproduced in the tool itself.

WHY NO MITIGATION INSIDE THE TOOL WORKS. Every remedy available within the codemod's own tree is a CONVENTION — a comment, a test that restates the rule, a checklist. Conventions do not pin. The design pass says so explicitly rather than papering it.

THE STRUCTURAL ANSWER: extract the slot rule from the codec to .cljc so both the JVM tool and the CLJS runtime consume ONE implementation. That is door-side work, outside the design pass's fence, which is why it is filed rather than done.

SEQUENCING: this is a precondition for TRUSTING the codemod, not for designing it. It does not block rf2-2rtt6.106's acceptance. It DOES block shipping a codemod anyone should run on a real codebase. Do not build the codemod without settling this first.

Pre-alpha posture note: extracting a shared rule to .cljc is the opposite of over-engineering — it deletes a duplicate rather than adding a mechanism. But confirm the slot rule is genuinely self-contained before extracting; if it drags half the codec across, stop and report rather than forcing it.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7665 (2026-08-07). COMPLETENESS / IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the extraction is otherwise coherent. One self-contained `front/slot.cljc` now owns the rule; the codec, both benchmark arms, and cache seeds consume it; no `codec/prop-name` caller remains. `check_test_lane_bijection.py` passes (1815 test-defining files / 46 lanes), the normal JVM suite passes 3 tests / 92 assertions, the CLJS node build compiles 2173 files with zero warnings, and the focused codec + shared-slot + walk-profile suites pass 73 tests / 661 assertions.

CORRECTNESS — DO NOT CLOSE THIS OWNER YET. The shared source still does not give the JVM codemod and browser runtime one semantic answer on arbitrary developer machines. `capitalize` calls `clojure.string/upper-case`; on the JVM that consults the process default locale, while CLJS uses JavaScript casing. Reproduced at the landed merge with `clojure -J-Duser.language=tr -J-Duser.country=TR -M:test -n re-frame.bench.hicasso.front.slot-cljs-test`: exit 1, 4/92 assertions fail; `:on-input` and `:tab-index` become `onİnput` / `tabİndex` instead of the browser's `onInput` / `tabIndex`. The ordinary-locale JVM run and CLJS run remain green, proving the current cross-host lane only observes the CI host's locale and does not pin this deployment dimension. This is exactly the silent divergence rf2-ani6y exists to remove: a Turkish-locale JVM codemod rewrites a prop to a slot the browser runtime will never read.

Required before closure: make the capitalization rule locale-independent with the browser/React result authoritative (for example JVM `Locale/ROOT` or a small explicit ASCII hump rule, while preserving CLJS semantics), and add a JVM witness that forces a Turkish default locale and restores it in `finally`, pinning `:on-input` and `:tab-index`. Keep the existing two-host corpus and codec-cache equivalence pin. No duplicate Bead created; rf2-ani6y is the exact owner and remains in_progress.
close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-08-07 after an eighth silent tracker revert wave (this bead reverted from CLOSED to IN_PROGRESS). Notes grepped for AUDIT-REOPEN / obligation / unmet first — none found, clean re-close. PR #7665 verified MERGED; front/slot.cljc confirmed present on main.

The codemod's prop-name contract is pinned — the precondition the operator sequenced BEFORE the rf2-2rtt6.106 fixer. prop-name moved whole to front/slot.cljc with only its two vocabularies and its own capitalize; the new namespace requires clojure.string and nothing else. Caches, PropSlot, the prototype guard and every walk stayed in the codec. No STOP was needed. re-frame.freehand.rules/react-prop-name was checked and established NOT to be the same rule (a react-dom possibleStandardNames table for the Freehand compiler vs the donor kebab->camel rule for the Hicasso codec) and left alone.

Equivalence pinned on BOTH hosts, red then green: slot_cljs_test.cljc is .cljc so the lane bijection runs its 41-key corpus on JVM and CLJS against ONE implementation. Cross-host sabotage -> JVM red, 6 failures. Codec-level sabotage -> the shared-rule test red at 9 failures while slot-cljs-test stayed green, which is the correct split.

Two findings recorded as memories because they generalise: CLJS answers a REMOVED VAR with a warning and undefined so the compile stays exit 0 and the breakage surfaces downstream (the signal is the WARNING COUNT, not the exit code); and the three cache seeds were hand-typed twice, with an :each fixture making the second copy live, so drift in the first was measurably invisible.

title: hicasso: implement the revision prop on controlled elements per revision-prop-spec.md
description:
FILED BY THE MAYOR 2026-08-07 on closing rf2-2rtt6.107. That bead's DESIGN landed on 2026-08-04 and its ruled synthesis is tracked at docs/design/hicasso/studio/revision-prop-spec.md — but the implementation had NO OWNER. front/controlled.cljs is untouched. A ruled design with no implementation bead is unowned work that only gets rediscovered.

SCOPE: implement the ruled shape exactly as the spec states it. Do not re-open the design — the design pass, its adversarial pass and the operator's synthesis all ran, and the spec adjudicates itself against the current tree.

THE RULED SHAPE, from the spec (read it, do not work from this summary): ::h/revision, [unfrozen], exact-keyword and NEVER slot-claimed; re-baseline WITHOUT remount on React's own per-commit controlled re-assert, so ZERO new machinery and NO third flushSync site; the mid-composition reset DEFERS to the exchange's close, because the only immediate write available is the measured composition abort. Plus the three mandatory repairs the spec enumerates — of which the :& door is the one that would otherwise ship a hostile remainder the power to force field re-baselines.

WATCH FOR: the spec records that its own law cite has already drifted seventy-four lines since it was written, that the native walk's stringification was NOT narrowed by rf2-vrvv9 (so one honest loss is worse than the spec states), and that the canonical-slot doctrine its spelling excepts has since been reinforced twice by name. Re-verify each cite at the line it names before relying on it.

NOT A DEPENDENCY: rf2-2rtt6.116, ruled explicitly.

GATES: the reset law is behavioural, so witnesses must exercise the actual reset path rather than a proxy — prove each goes red without the change. rf2-2rtt6.113 (guide 04 teaches the revision prop) gates on THIS bead landing, not on the design.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7655 (merged 2026-08-07T01:38:38Z; landed 125863a1bca0fdd8d23d085333ecd8d49f0317ae) — REOPENED this exact implementation owner; no duplicate.

CORRECTNESS: controlled/revision-slot is the ordinary string "hicassoRevision". The native prop walk canonicalizes :hicasso-revision to that same emitted slot; install! then mistakes the authored ordinary prop for the private marker, deletes it, and on a non-controlled tag raises :rf.error/hicasso-revision-not-controlled. This contradicts the exact-key contract that every spelling except :re-frame.hicasso/revision remains an ordinary attribute. Use an unforgeable carrier (for example a JS Symbol) or pass presence/value separately, and pin both :hicasso-revision and "hicassoRevision" on controlled and non-controlled elements.

COMPLETENESS: native-element stashes the marker with when-some over get. THE BIND. The P0 allocation row now exists and its arithmetic is validated (positive control 8.13 B/double direct, 7.99 differential, against a predicted 8; idle window 32 B). But it has a MEASURED ceiling: the reading is accurate only while no collection falls inside the window, which is ~600 KB of cumulative garbage. Above it the reading degrades monotonically (the same object reads 23.92 B then 6.94 B as falls go 3 to 10) and ALWAYS DOWNWARD - the direction that manufactures HD-002's predicted flat-at-zero.

Enlarging the young generation does not move the threshold. Tried at --max-semi-space-size=128 and =512; identical tables, falls unchanged to the unit. Do not spend the afternoon on it again.

So: at B=1,200 (the published witness) a single warm write allocates 1.2-1.7 MB, two to three times over the threshold, and 32 collections fell inside 44 measured windows - the row refuses. At B=300 with ONE write per window the falls go to 0 across 88 windows and the controls pass, but a one-write window has no averaging in it, and all four fits come back under the 0.98 r2 floor (0.75 / 0.28 / 0.94 / 0.31, none linear in more than 1 round of 4). The rungs are not scattered around a line; they are NON-MONOTONE.

THE FIX IS TO SHRINK THE MEASURED UNIT, NOT THE WINDOW. The metric's quantity is per BOUNDARY, so an arm of a few dozen boundaries would put a MANY-write window under the fall threshold and restore the averaging a fit needs. That is a new arm on the existing --only alloc row (p0_heap.cljs lad-arm / p0_run.cjs ladderPlan), not a new instrument.

Take it on a quiet box, as .76 was, and do not interleave it with other bench work on the same instrument.

title: the-mayor-method: the merge rule an empty rollup satisfies, and the bead-governs-the-brief rule that is only in my habit
description:
FILED BY THE MAYOR 2026-08-07. Two defects in the method's own text, both earned in the field today, both on files no open PR touches.

DEFECT 1 — THE MERGE RULE IS UNSAFE AS WRITTEN, and it has already caused an incident.
bootstrap.md says to merge on 'CI 0-fail AND 0-pending'. An EMPTY rollup satisfies that: zero failures and zero pending is exactly what a PR reports when its workflow runs were never created. PR #7628 reached main that way today — merged at 17:38:11Z, its runs created at 17:38:22Z, rollup showing 0/0/0 at the moment I evaluated it. Content was fine (prose-only, and I re-ran its gates against main afterwards at exit 0), but it went in unverified and I reported it as green.

This is not a one-off. During the GitHub Actions outage SIX PRs simultaneously reported MERGEABLE with zero checks, zero failures, zero pending. The rule as written would merge every one.

THE FIX: the criterion needs a COMPLETENESS clause — a non-empty, fully-concluded rollup whose total sits in the repo's expected band (~86 checks here; a partial rollup of 11 is not a green one). Update bootstrap.md AND .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md, which carries the same wording. State the reasoning, not just the rule: a gate that verifies the absence of bad news rather than the presence of good news is the same fail-open class this project spent the day hunting in its own instruments.

DEFECT 2 — 'THE BEAD GOVERNS OVER THE BRIEF' IS NOT IN THE TEMPLATE.
dispatch-prompt-template.md does not tell a worker to read the bead bottom-up and treat the bead as authoritative over the dispatching brief. I add it by habit to every dispatch. It caught FIVE stale briefs of mine today: rf2-409ab's LF fix (already landed two days earlier by a sibling bead), rf2-409ab's scope (I named the wrong audit item), rf2-2rtt6.103's .115 resolution (already merged in PR #7607), rf2-y1jkm's framing (a scope correction had redefined it from an allocation leak to a baseline-contamination leak), and rf2-2rtt6.56 (three wrong path/flag/script details).

bootstrap.md already carries the ROOT CAUSE under its hard-won list — 'an audit that reopens an issue may already be stale ... read the current source at the named site before dispatching' — but the REMEDY lives only in my habit, so a fresh mayor inherits the warning without the countermeasure. bd show prints DESCRIPTION first and a description is the OLDEST text on a bead; notes accrete below it. That single fact is why top-down reading fails, and it belongs in the template's common preamble as a mandatory block, alongside the worktree-boundary block.

FENCE: docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md, docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md. Verified touched by no open PR at filing time — re-verify before starting.

SEQUENCING: hold dispatch while the GitHub Actions queue is starved. A PR here adds CI runs that compete with PRs already 2-4 checks from complete. Dispatch when the queue drains, or immediately if the operator wants it sooner.

title: scripts/test-fast-pr.sh: a signalled run leaves a live process tree that corrupts the next run's log AND reds its gates
description:
FILED BY THE MAYOR 2026-08-07 on a worker's explicit recommendation (rf2-y1jkm, PR #7636). This has now bitten two workers on the same day and produced a SPURIOUS GATE FAILURE that reads as a real regression.

WHAT HAPPENS. A worker invokes 'sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh' in the foreground. The harness's 10-minute cap fires and signals the call. The tool returns — but on Windows the script's PROCESS TREE SURVIVES. It keeps compiling, and it keeps writing to the same log path the worker will use when it relaunches.

TWO DISTINCT DAMAGE MODES, both observed:
(1) TWO WRITERS, ONE FILE. The orphan and the relaunch interleave into one log, producing NUL-riddled output. A worker reading that log cannot trust any line in it.
(2) A SPURIOUS RED IN THE GATE'S OWN ENVIRONMENT CLASS. The orphan's 'npm run test:cljs' unlinks out/node-test.js underneath the relaunch's live per-ns isolation sweep, which then fails with 'the bundle changed on disk during the sweep' and MODULE_NOT_FOUND. That is the sweep CORRECTLY detecting that something mutated the bundle — the something is a dead run. It looks exactly like an isolation regression introduced by the worker's own diff. An earlier worker on rf2-2rtt6.103 hit the same red from the same cause.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN DOCUMENTING. The failure is indistinguishable from a real finding at the moment a worker meets it, it is self-inflicted by the tooling rather than the diff, and the cost is a worker bisecting its own change for a defect that belongs to a dead process. Both workers who hit it recovered only because they thought to look for orphans.

SKETCH, not a ruled design. Two candidate remedies, either or both:
  (a) TRAP AND REAP — have test-fast-pr.sh trap INT/TERM and kill its own child process group before exiting, so a signalled run does not outlive its invocation. Must work under Git Bash on Windows, where process-group semantics differ; verify rather than assume.
  (b) UNIQUE LOG PER INVOCATION — the script derives its own log path including a per-run token, so two concurrent invocations physically cannot share a file. This does not stop the bundle race but removes the corrupted-log half, and it is the cheaper of the two.
The bundle race arguably also wants the sweep to hold a lock, but do NOT build that without ruling it first — it is the kind of thing that becomes over-engineering.

ACCEPTANCE: demonstrate the trap BEFORE the fix (signal a run, show the tree survives) and its absence after. A fix that cannot be shown to close the observed behaviour proves nothing.

FENCE: scripts/test-fast-pr.sh and whatever it sources. Cross-platform per this repo's rule — Mike is on Windows, maintainers are on Mac/Linux, so a POSIX-sh fix must work on all three.
notes: Merged-PR audit #7642 (2026-08-07): REOPEN. Correctness/safety: the durable claim stores only a PID and spine_pid_is_this_gate accepts any command containing test-fast-pr (lines 715-720); after a crash and PID reuse, a live gate in another worktree passes both guards and is killed. Completeness: spine_claim_run is a non-atomic check then overwrite (lines 752-777), so simultaneous starts can both observe no predecessor and recreate the two-writer/bundle race. The POSIX arm also enumerates and kills descendants before stopping the runnable root (lines 689-703, 765-769), leaving a successor-spawn window. Bind identity to this invocation/root with a reuse-resistant fingerprint, make claim/reap atomic, freeze or re-sweep before declaring reaped, and add deterministic Windows/POSIX regression coverage. The cited 37-case self-test covers tier selection only; this PR changed one file and added no executable coverage for the new process protocol.
close_reason: RE-CLOSED 2026-08-07 after a second silent tracker revert. PR #7642 verified MERGED just now. A signalled or capped fast-PR run can no longer outlive its invocation: a trap covers genuinely-signalled cases and the same reap runs at the START of the next run, which is the only moment anything can act when no signal arrives. The worker MEASURED that the harness BACKGROUNDS rather than signals (log grew 41822 -> 49220 bytes after the tool returned), that 'kill the child process group' would have killed the CALLER since every child shares its PGID under Git Bash, that bash defers a trapped signal until the foreground child returns (22s measured), and that taskkill /F /T is silently mangled into 'taskkill F:/' behind the customary || true. My bead's own model was wrong on all three.

title: FIX: the-candidates-clock.md asserts floor-cancellation on evidence its own section 6.1 marks WITHDRAWN (three surviving sites)
description:
Raised by the 2026-08-07 read-only floor-cancellation audit (companion to rf2-8nqsl / rf2-es04f). Working notes: ai/findings/2026-08-07.floor-cancellation-identity-audit.md.

SEQUENCE BEHIND PR #7632 (worker/clockprose-jcm3p) - same page, and #7632
already fixes a fourth site of this exact class at line 1198.

THE FACT. Two claims are in play and they fail differently:

  A (algebra, FALSE):  (U/F) / (R/F) = U/R
     Each arm is normalised against the floor measured in ITS OWN segment, so
     the true identity is (U/F_U) / (R/F_R) = (U/R) x (F_R/F_U). The floor
     contributes a second term.

  B (empirical, WITHDRAWN):  floor-normalisation removes a segment-common
     MULTIPLICATIVE perturbation, and therefore 'cancels exactly'.
     rf2-ymi6j refuted this: pure multiplicativity predicts ctl-2x / floor =
     2.00 with no variance; nineteen fresh runs read 1.7138 [1.6228 - 1.8417].
     the-band-re-calibrated.md section 6 is titled 'Multiplicativity is
     withdrawn'. clock_run.cjs carries the withdrawal at :110 and :1183.

The DRIVER is correct and current. Only the studio page is stale, and it
contradicts its own section 6.1 banner at line 1000, which already reads
'~~The perturbation is multiplicative, so floor-normalisation cancels it, and
the arithmetic is exact~~ WITHDRAWN by the re-take'.

THREE SURVIVING SITES (line numbers on main at 01c1a5938e; verified absent from
the #7632 branch's diff).

1. Lines 186-192, the page's own method description - claim A AND claim B in
   one paragraph, read before anything else on the page:

     'Every figure is a ratio to the floor measured in **that round of that
     segment**, so a cross-segment figure is a ratio of two floor-normalised
     ratios with the seam cancelled. ... **That the seam cancels is now
     measured rather than asserted** ([section 6.1](...)): the perturbation a
     busy box applies is multiplicative, and a multiplicative perturbation
     cancels exactly.'

   Correction: the seam is not cancelled - a cross-segment figure is
   (H/F_H) / (R/F_R) = (H/R) x (F_R/F_H). What section 6.1 established and
   what survives is that the seam does not track load and is not attributable
   to the segment; the multiplicativity clause is withdrawn. The page's own
   seams run 4.9% / 22% / 23% / 34% within a run, and rf2-8nqsl read 31.9% in
   one round, so the second term is not nominal.

2. Lines 892-895, section 6 ground 3's explanation of its own withdrawal:

     'Floor-normalisation cancels a multiplicative seam and not an additive
     one, and [section 6.1](...) measures which this is: it is multiplicative,
     it cancels exactly, and the seam is not attributable to the segment at
     all.'

   Correction: strike the multiplicativity/'cancels exactly' clause, per
   section 6.1's banner. NOTE - ground 3's WITHDRAWAL still stands, on its
   other leg: the relabelling null showed the seam is not segment-attributable
   and the variation lives on the round. Only the reason changes, not the
   verdict, and the rows stay refused on grounds 1 and 2 and on the band.

3. Lines 1328-1331, section 8 handoff:

     'The seam does not track load, is not attributable to the segment, and is
     multiplicative - so it cancels, exactly.'

   Correction: keep the first two clauses, strike the third. Under the 2026-08-06
   annotate-never-erase ruling, strike through rather than delete, as #7632 did
   at line 1198.

NO PUBLISHED FIGURE MOVES. This page publishes no cross-segment magnitude - every
row is a regime and ctl-2x fails - so there is no number for the second term to
corrupt. This is a documentation repair.

DO NOT ALSO EDIT section 6.1 lines 1052-1057 - that is rf2-es04f's, and see the
note on that bead: its stated remedy preserves a conclusion that is itself
withdrawn.

VERIFICATION: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py, plus hand-checked heading
anchors and table column counts (mkdocs --strict excludes docs/design/).

title: adapter reg-view stamps displayName with a colon the rf:render: measure strips
description:
Found while fixing rf2-2rtt6.136 (freehand's identical defect, PR #7623). The bead for the freehand fix asserted the divergence was 'confined to the product path'. It is not — the ADAPTER path has it too, and that is the first-class, actively-supported substrate.

implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs, the reg-view wrapper every adapter (Reagent / reagent-slim / UIx / Helix) composes:

  L552  (performance/mark-and-measure :render id (apply render-fn args))
  L586  (when interop/debug-enabled? (set! (.-displayName ^js wrapped) (str id)))

A reg-view id is a keyword, so (str id) keeps its leading colon. React DevTools shows ':cart/total-line' while the bracket writes 'rf:render:cart/total-line'. Spec 009 §Naming convention (L1494) requires the measure's <id> and the id the substrate publishes to the developer — it names React displayName explicitly — to be ONE identifier, 'so a name read off the User-Timing stream is directly jumpable in the tooling'. Pasting the DevTools name into the documented rf:render: filter yields rf:render::cart/total-line and matches nothing; docs/core/how-to/fix-a-slow-view.md sends the reader down exactly that path.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED WITH THE FREEHAND HALF. Two reasons, both operator calls rather than fence questions:

1. The current spelling is DELIBERATE and LANDED. rf2-fa4ly's comment at views.cljs:575 says DevTools should show '<:cart/total-line>', and implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/reg_view_devtools_cljs_test.cljs PINS it — display-name-on-wrapped-fn-matches-view-id asserts ':re-frame.reg-view-devtools-cljs-test/dn-auto' and display-name-honours-rf-id-override asserts ':rf.devtools-test/dn-explicit'. Fixing this deletes two landed assertions and changes what every existing consumer sees in DevTools.
2. It is a visible change to the shipping surface, not the EXPERIMENTAL one.

THE FIX IS ONE TOKEN if ruled. PR #7623 extracted the shared builder as re-frame.performance/entry-id (build-name's own <id> half, unchanged behaviour, all four buckets), precisely so a substrate can publish the measure's own spelling rather than re-deriving it. So this is:

  (set! (.-displayName ^js wrapped) (performance/entry-id id))

plus updating the two adapter assertions to the colon-free spelling, plus a row that asserts the two strings are EQUAL rather than each well-formed (the shape that let both halves of this ship). views.cljs already requires re-frame.performance.

DECIDE WITH THE FREEHAND HALF IN VIEW: if the adapter path keeps the colon and freehand drops it, one framework publishes two spellings depending on substrate — which is worse than either spelling chosen consistently.

title: Studio provenance pins name AUTHORED SHAs that rebase-merge strands — a reader cannot resolve them
description:
FOUND while fixing rf2-zn7pj (PR #7610, 2026-08-06). The SSR spike witness pinned its provenance to 952a3f2024, and that commit IS NOT AN ANCESTOR OF MAIN — verified with git merge-base --is-ancestor, which returns non-zero. Nor is its sibling 6f40304011. The branch was REBASE-MERGED, which rewrites SHAs, so the authored head the page named was stranded the moment it merged.

THAT IS WORSE THAN THE DRIFT THE BEAD DESCRIBED. Stale figures under a resolvable pin are checkable and wrong. Figures under an UNRESOLVABLE pin are not checkable at all: a reader cannot get the tree the measurement was taken on, so the page's central verifiability claim fails silently. It looks pinned.

THE CHECK, one command per pin: git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main. Non-zero means stranded.

THE FIX SHAPE that rf2-zn7pj adopted and that should generalise: PIN TO A COMMIT ALREADY ON MAIN. The measurement happens upstream of the documenting edit, so no merge of the documenting PR can move it — main advanced eight commits during that pass and the pin never had to change. That dissolves the problem rather than managing it, and it is strictly stronger than a blob table, which pins the instrument but not the corpus, entry, substrate, adapter or pinned react-dom.

SCOPE TO ESTABLISH FIRST — this is a CHECK, not an established finding beyond the one page. Census the provenance pins across docs/design/hicasso/studio/** and the witness pages, run the ancestor check on each, and report how many are stranded. If the answer is one, close it. If it is many, that is a systemic verifiability defect in the evidence corpus and wants a convention (pin to a merged commit, never an authored head) plus possibly a checker.

DO NOT re-take any measurement to fix a pin. A stranded pin is a provenance defect; re-measuring is a different and far more expensive job, and re-taking a row after reading its published result creates a selection opportunity that invalidates both draws.
notes:
MAYOR RULING (2026-08-06), and my proposed fix was UNSOUND — the worker was right to refuse it mechanically.

MY ERROR. I wrote 'pin to a commit already on main; the measurement happened upstream of the documenting edit, so no merge can move it.' That holds for the SSR spike, where the run was taken on an UNMODIFIED MAIN TREE. It does NOT generalise, because most of this corpus measures the worker's OWN instrument changes — so the measured tree was never on main and NO COMMIT CARRIES IT. Re-pinning restores the PATCH, not the TREE.

Applied mechanically my fix would have made two pages WORSE IN THE EXACT WAY THIS BEAD EXISTS TO PREVENT: swapping an UNRESOLVABLE pin for a RESOLVABLE BUT WRONG one, which fails silently instead of visibly. The two are 'the-page-chrome-row…' (rebase resolved conflicts in arm1/runtime.cljs, front/codec.cljs and shapes/feed.cljs, all on the measured path) and 'our-walk-against-reagents' (rebase moved front/codec.cljs, the file its decomposition turns on). Annotating them rather than re-pinning them was correct.

THE RULING ON THE CONVENTION: ADOPT IT, in the worker's formulation rather than mine. The enforceable rule is 'EVERY CITED AUTHORED HEAD MUST BE ACCOMPANIED BY A RESOLVABLE LANDED SHA' — NOT 'no authored heads'. Several pages legitimately retain the authored head deliberately, alongside a blob-table fallback, and a checker enforcing must-be-on-main would red them for being careful. That distinction is the whole difference between a useful gate and one everyone routes around.

RE-PINNING IS PERMITTED ONLY WHERE THE REBASE PRESERVED EVERY BLOB THE COMMIT CONTRIBUTED. Where it did not, the page says so instead. That is the discriminator, and it must be in the convention text, not left to judgement.

BUILD THE CHECKER: yes, but as a follow-up bead, not folded in here. It is one command per pin (git merge-base --is-ancestor) plus the accompaniment rule, and the failure is systemic — 44 stranded pins, 79 occurrences, 24 pages, all reachable from no remote ref.

METHOD I AM ENDORSING FOR REUSE: the recovery was VALIDATED BEFORE BEING TRUSTED, against three pages that already document authored->landed mappings as ground truth — stable patch-id is invariant across this repo's rebase-merge, and 43/44 mapped exactly. And the worker caught its own first blob check comparing WHOLE TREES, which differ for every rebased pair; the correct check is the commit's OWN CONTRIBUTED BLOBS. Both of those are the difference between a census and a guess.
close_reason: Merged PR #7616 audit: completed the systemic census and landed the bounded 12-file provenance repair. All replacement landed SHAs resolve on main; stable patch-id and contributed-blob checks substantiate the mappings and the two measured-tree exceptions; doc slugs, diff hygiene, headings, and changed table rows pass. Remaining corpus repair plus the ratchet is owned by rf2-kqac1.

title: spec/009: the ambient-frame-refused row needs :extent-frame / :carried-frame, and its 'every ambient resolution goes through require-current-frame!' claim is false
description:
FOLLOW-UP from rf2-nqj22 (PR #7604). That PR fenced spec/** out because
spec/009-Instrumentation.md was claimed by another worker this session, so
the catalogue row is now BEHIND the code in two ways.

1. TWO NEW PAYLOAD KEYS. :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused now carries
   :extent-frame (the frame the refusing extent is rendering — substrate-
   supplied via the refusal detail's :extent-frame key, normalized to an id
   by ambient-frame-refused-payload) and, on the mismatch arm only,
   :carried-frame (the stamp that was carried). The row's key list mentions
   neither. Both are load-bearing: a mismatch diagnostic that names only one
   of the two frames sends the author looking for the wrong one.

2. A FALSE CLAIM IN THE ROW'S PROSE, and it is the interesting half. The
   row says "The category is defined by the DOOR, not by a list of ops:
   every ambient resolution, whatever the op, goes through
   re-frame.frame/require-current-frame!". That is NOT true.
   subs/subscribe's 1-arity inlines
   `(or (frame/resolve-current-frame) (frame/require-current-frame! ...))`
   so its error payload is built only on the path that reads it (rf2-a8bw0,
   whose comment says "Do NOT collapse this back") — so an ambient subscribe
   with a carried stamp in scope never reaches the requiring primitive at
   all. rf2-nqj22 found this by measurement: the first implementation put
   the mismatch check in require-current-frame! only, and the subscribe arm
   of the witness went red with the read silently succeeding. The fix moved
   the check into resolve-current-frame, so the ROW's claim should be
   restated about the RESOLVER (the reader every ambient path funnels
   through) rather than about the requiring primitive.

3. The row's :operation enumeration is also still narrow — see rf2-e28wl,
   which filed the same shape of gap. Sequence with it and with rf2-k0rbk.

Also worth a line in spec/002's §Frame target resolution: 'a carried stamp
wins' now has exactly one documented exception, opt-in and substrate-
declared, and the reason is the standing frames-are-isolated-contexts
principle rather than a resolution rule.
close_reason: SHIPPED in PR #7614 (merged), commit 06c0330cc1 'docs(spec/009): the ambient-refusal row names the two frames, and its door is the READER'. Verified on main. Zero audit-reopen notes on the bead, so this was a lost close rather than a legitimate reopen — the discriminator held. Both halves delivered: the :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused row now names :extent-frame / :carried-frame, and the false 'every ambient resolution goes through require-current-frame!' sentence is restated about the RESOLVER — which is the truth, because subs/subscribe's 1-arity deliberately inlines (or (frame/resolve-current-frame) (frame/require-current-frame! ...)) to keep its error payload off the per-read fast path (rf2-a8bw0: 'Do NOT collapse this back'), so an ambient subscribe with a stamp in scope never reaches the requiring primitive. That optimisation is exactly what turns a documented funnel into a bypassed one, and it is why PR #7604 placed its check in resolve-current-frame.

comments.text:

title: spec/004 Theming says a theme switch 're-renders nothing'; the ruled default re-renders one boundary
description:
Guide 06 now teaches option A as the theming default (rf2-2rtt6.108, HD-010 addendum 2026-08-06): one scope view reads the theme sub and renders data-theme on the frame's root, so a theme switch re-renders exactly ONE boundary and the memo default keeps the tree below it quiet.

spec/004-Views.md SS 'Theming and semantic parts' still reads: 'Inheritance reaches every descendant, so switching themes changes that one attribute and **re-renders nothing**: no token subscription per leaf, no remount, and no reactive fan-out proportional to the tree.'

The colon-clause is all still true. The bare phrase 're-renders nothing' is not, once the SAME sentence's 'ancestor scope the application renders once' is a rendered scope reading a sub -- which is exactly what the ruling teaches and what the repo's own witnesses do. implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/pilot_field.cljc reads (v/sub [:acme.invoice/theme]) inside the invoice-line boundary and puts :data-theme on the form, so that boundary re-renders on a switch; guide 06's own Tradeoff paragraph now says so out loud ('The boundary that reads the theme re-renders on every switch -- one boundary, known cost').

Remedy is one clause, not a design change: qualify to 're-renders one boundary' / 'costs zero React work AFTER the flip', which is the split guide 06 layer 1 already makes ('That claim is about *after* the flip').

Found while implementing rf2-2rtt6.108; spec/** was outside that PR's fence (PR #7587).
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7594 (2026-08-06): reopened exact owner. The new spec phrase "re-renders one boundary, nothing after the flip" is still unconditional, and the PR body explicitly claims it stays true whatever sits below the scope. The cited authority says the opposite at docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/06-theming.md:158-165: what happens below depends on what sits there; only an immediate memoized defview head bails, while a native-tag subtree, fragment, defhost crossing, or plain-function app re-runs with the scope. Keep the correction that the scope boundary re-renders, but make subtree quietness conditional on the taught/default immediate defview boundary (or simply avoid claiming nothing below). Do not restore the original zero-render claim.
close_reason: SHIPPED in PR #7597 (merged), correcting PR #7594's own regression. The audit reopened this because #7594 replaced 're-renders nothing' with 'one boundary, nothing after the flip', and the second half is NOT unconditionally true. The worker re-read guide 06 rather than trusting the audit summary and found something neither the audit nor my brief had: guide 06 uses 'after the flip' at LAYER 1, about the CASCADE RECOMPUTE, not the subtree — so parked after 'one boundary' it reads as a subtree claim, which is exactly how #7594 went wrong. It dropped the phrase rather than qualifying it, since the colon-clause already carries its true content. spec/004-Views.md:1752 now reads '...re-renders one boundary, and nothing behind a memoized view immediately below it', in vocabulary the ownership table already uses. Invariants PROVED by joining the paragraph from HEAD and the working file: colon-clause byte-identical, scope ruling untouched, and paragraph-minus-phrase compares EQUAL — so the bolded phrase is provably the only text that differs. Both doc gates mutation-proven rather than trusted.

title: code units published as bytes: the pair RUNTIME's live 5 MB queue gate, plus the framework's own elision walker
description:
RESIDUE from rf2-2rtt6.132, which repaired the four sites inside tools/**
and swept that fence to exhaustion. These three carry the same shape and
sit OUTSIDE it -- implementation/** and skills/** were both hard fences
for .132. Cited by SYMBOL, not by line. Ordered WORST FIRST.

THE SHAPE. A value that is (count s) -- UTF-16 code units on BOTH
platforms, since JVM String.length is also code units -- published or
ENFORCED under a bytes name. It fails OPEN: on ASCII the two agree
exactly, so the wrong expression prints the right number and a green
suite never notices.

1. skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/pure.cljc -- THE WORST
   ONE IN THE REPO and the only remaining LIVE REFUSAL GATE. `enqueue!`
   accumulates :queue-bytes as (count (pr-str ev)) and `evict-oldest`
   compares that running sum against `max-buffered-bytes` (default
   5,000,000) to DROP EVENTS. So the figure is not merely published --
   an under-count by up to 3x (4x on astral) means the queue holds up to
   3x the intended payload before it starts evicting, and the operator's
   published :queue-bytes / :dropped-bytes under-report by the same
   margin. Also runtime.cljs:1477's head comment ("running sum of
   (count (pr-str ev)) for queued events") and :1887's list-streams
   read.
   TWO SURFACES MOVE IN LOCKSTEP with whatever is decided here, and
   BOTH are self-contradictory TODAY, which is the tell:
     - tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/.../tools/descriptors_data.cljs:1693
       publishes the arg description "Runtime-side queue cap in BYTES
       (pr-str char count)" -- both units in one sentence, to an agent.
     - tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md:3531 says
       ":queue-bytes <integer> ; pr-str chars buffered server-side",
       honest about chars while the slot says bytes.
     - tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/.../subscribe_test.cljs's
       `event-byte-size` is a DELIBERATE parallel fixture of the runtime
       (its own comment says so), so it must mirror whichever way this
       goes -- it is not an independent site.
   .132 left all four alone rather than half-fixing a contract across a
   fence: relabelling the descriptor while the runtime kept a bytes
   name, or vice versa, just moves the contradiction.

2. implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc -- pr-str-bytes, the
   FRAMEWORK's own producer:
     #?(:clj (count (.getBytes ^String (pr-str v) "UTF-8"))
        :cljs (count (pr-str v)))
   The exact CLJ/CLJS asymmetry rf2-2rtt6.131 repaired in xray's
   format/pr-str-bytes and story-mcp's read-edn-body, still standing in
   the framework the tools imitate. It is PUBLISHED (every
   {:rf.size/large-elided ... :bytes N} marker body, via ->marker) AND
   ENFORCED (the :rf.size/threshold-bytes comparison around line 986).
   One budget, two rulers: the same app-db leaf can warn on the JVM and
   pass in the browser. Note xray's format/pr-str-bytes docstring
   already claims parity with "the framework's re-frame.elision walker"
   -- since .131 that claim is true only on the JVM arm.
   .131 named implementation/ a hard fence; .132 inherited it. Nobody
   has actually looked at this one yet -- it was found by .132's sweep,
   not carried forward from a list.

3. implementation/core/test/re_frame/observation_render_law_drift_test.clj
   -- :bytes accumulated via (count content) and printed as bytes. Named
   in rf2-2rtt6.121's merged-PR audit note, carried unactioned through
   .131 and .132, out of fence for both. A test-local figure; the
   smallest of the three.

THE REPAIR, where converting is the answer:
  (alength (.getBytes s "UTF-8"))                on the JVM
  (.-length (.encode (js/TextEncoder.) s))       on CLJS
TextEncoder is UTF-8 BY DEFINITION -- no encoding argument a later edit
can drop -- and is present in every browser and in Node. FOUR worked
examples are now in main: re-frame.bench.hicasso.lane/utf8-bytes
(rf2-2rtt6.121), day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.epoch.format/pr-str-bytes
(rf2-2rtt6.131), and from rf2-2rtt6.132
day8.re-frame2-machines-viz.chart.context-redaction/utf8-bytes (the
.cljc pair) and re-frame2-pair-mcp.tools.summary/utf8-bytes.

A RULING IS OWED ON (1), AND ONLY ON (1). Everywhere else the correction
has been monotone-TIGHTENING and needed none -- UTF-8 bytes are never
fewer than UTF-16 code units, so nothing previously refused becomes
admitted. Site 1 inverts that: the cap is on a BUFFER the runtime is
already holding, so counting honestly makes the queue evict SOONER, and
a 5 MB default calibrated (if it ever was) against code units is
effectively 5 MB of characters today. Either the cap converts and the
default is re-derived, or the whole chain relabels to chars -- runtime
symbol, descriptor text, spec table and mirror fixture together.

AN ASCII-ONLY TEST CANNOT SEE THIS BUG -- that is why it survives. Use a
discriminating fixture set where code units, code POINTS and bytes are
three different numbers: U+2014 (1 unit / 1 point / 3 bytes) and the
ASTRAL U+1D11E (2 units / 1 point / 4 bytes), written as \uXXXX escapes
so the source stays pure ASCII. Mutation-prove BOTH directions and,
where the file is .cljc, BOTH hosts.

VERIFIED NOT SIBLINGS, so no work is owed (checked, not assumed):
tools/xray edn_inspector's (* mono-char-width-px (count (pr-str value)))
is an honest characters-to-pixels width; pair-mcp's dedup_test /
diff_encode_epochs_test and story-mcp's dedup_test use raw-size /
full-size / enc-size with no byte claim anywhere; mcp-base
overflow/token-estimate and cap/sum-payload-by are honestly-named
character-to-token estimates; story-mcp protocol.cljc's max-frame-bytes
is a genuine per-code-point UTF-8 accumulator (rf2-sibl4f) and must not
be disturbed.
notes:
SITES 2 AND 3 DELIVERED (PR #7582). Recording on the worker's behalf - it deliberately did not mutate the tracker to avoid racing the mayor's .beads checkpoint loop, which is the right instinct.

THE INVERSION QUESTION IS SETTLED, AND MORE SOFTLY THAN MY BRIEF ALLOWED FOR. I hedged "if it gates elision rather than retention". IT GATES NEITHER - it gates A DEV WARNING ONLY. Established from three independent sources rather than assumed:
  - spec/Privacy.md configure table: the threshold is "advisory, NOT a cap. An over-threshold value at an undeclared path fires :rf.warning/large-value-unschema'd but SHIPS UNCHANGED; only declared / schema-marked entries elide."
  - spec/009 error-catalogue row: recovery is :warned-and-replaced, "the unschema'd value is not auto-elided."
  - The code: walk-decider's :leaf arm uses the comparison solely for warn-large-unschema'd! and returns v regardless. The elide/retain decision lives in :decide, driven by the declaration tables, and NEVER CONSULTS THIS NUMBER.

So tightening yields strictly more diagnostics and zero data loss. No ruling owed. AND IT ADDED A TEST ASSERTING THE SHIP-UNCHANGED HALF OUTSIDE THE DEBUG GATE, so this cannot silently become a cap later - the fail-open lesson applied forward rather than backward.

SITE 2 CONVERTED: pr-str-bytes is now .getBytes/alength on the JVM and TextEncoder with ^js hints on CLJS. Both arms verified LIVE (core targets JVM and browser), so unlike story-mcp's dead arm neither is deleted. TextEncoder rather than Buffer.byteLength because this is re-frame.core and it compiles into the browser bundle.

SITE 3 RELABELLED: the census (count content) runs over a slurped, ALREADY-DECODED String, and the figure is a same-vs-same anti-vacuity floor check. :bytes -> :chars beats re-encoding 500+ files to satisfy a name - the same call the sibling made on max-cursor-bytes.

THE FIXTURE DESIGN IS THE BEST PART: three fixtures share ONE pr-str code-unit length (42) with THREE different byte lengths (42/122/82), so the defective expression answers 42 for all three. astral-20 also separates code POINTS (20) from code UNITS (40). Built from explicit code points so the source stays pure ASCII and no re-encoding can mangle the surrogate pair. Under-count leaves the ASCII assertions GREEN - the failure is specific to non-ASCII rather than "everything reds", which is what makes it a discriminating test rather than a smoke alarm.

XRAY'S PARITY CLAIM IS TRUE AGAIN ON BOTH ARMS. Its format/pr-str-bytes is now byte-for-byte identical to elision's; since rf2-2rtt6.131 that claim had held only on the JVM.

NO SPEC ROW OWED: Spec-Schemas' ElisionMarkerBody already types the slot "pr-str byte count" and 009 already MUSTs it. THE SPEC WAS RIGHT; THE CLJS ARM WAS WRONG.

SITE 1 UNTOUCHED, verified: git diff origin/main...HEAD -- skills/ is 0 lines, and its three lockstep surfaces all sit under tools/ and are likewise untouched. The bead stays OPEN for site 1's ruling - the pair queue, where counting honestly makes eviction happen SOONER, and that is the operator's call.
RULING 2026-08-06 11:24 AUSEST (dossier review, delegated by Mike; operator-overturnable): SITE 1 = OPTION 1 — measure TRUE UTF-8 BYTES, cap STAYS 5,000,000, vocabulary UNCHANGED (max-buffered-bytes / :queue-bytes / :dropped-bytes; no rename, no compensating raise). The cap exists to bound memory; 5M was the chosen byte budget (introducing commit b3d3ccf2b6 describes it as wire-size-aligned; nothing calibrates 5M code units); the bug under-delivered eviction, not intent. Pre-alpha, no back-compat duty. Option 2 makes the cap stop meaning memory; option 3 enshrines an accident — and (Codex, verified) NO multiplier reproduces old behaviour: worst valid ratio is 3x (BMP U+0800+, e.g. U+2014 1 unit/3 bytes), astral is 2x in code units (U+1D11E 2 units/4 bytes) — the bead's '4x astral' is 4x vs code POINTS, not units. Dossier + Codex both recommended option 1; reviewer verified all cited sites and concurs. VERIFIED: pure.cljc:233 (count (pr-str event)) feeds enqueue/evict vs 5M; descriptor 1693 'BYTES (pr-str char count)' + catalogue 3531 'pr-str chars' under a bytes slot both self-contradictory verbatim; subscribe_test.cljs:372 fixture is a declared mirror; TextEncoder idiom has 5+ worked examples on main incl elision.cljc itself. BRIEF (one worker, one PR — sites 2-3 ALREADY LANDED on main under this bead, implementation/core is OUT of scope): (1) skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/pure.cljc event-byte-size -> UTF-8 bytes of pr-str, BOTH arms (.cljc): :clj (alength (.getBytes ^String s "UTF-8")), :cljs TextEncoder per elision.cljc pr-str-bytes; keep the try/fallback-0; fix the docstring — note its 'same units as the wire-cap helper' claim becomes TRUE again (summary.cljs utf8-byte-count is UTF-8 since .132). (2) runtime.cljs :1477 head-comment ('running sum of (count (pr-str ev))') + :1887 list-streams prose -> UTF-8 bytes. (3) tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/.../descriptors_data.cljs ~1693 -> 'Runtime-side queue cap in UTF-8 BYTES of pr-str' (kill the char-count parenthetical). (4) tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md ~3531 -> ':queue-bytes ; UTF-8 bytes of pr-str buffered server-side'. (5) subscribe_test.cljs:372 parallel fixture mirrors the runtime. WITNESS: multi-byte fixture proving CLJ/CLJS arms agree AND eviction fires at the true byte boundary; build from source-ASCII escapes (U+2014, U+1D11E) on the .134 design (shared code-unit length, differing byte lengths — under-count stays green on ASCII, reds only on non-ASCII). Prose says 'UTF-8 bytes of pr-str' — an honest deterministic wire proxy, not a literal heap ceiling. Behaviour change accepted: heavy non-ASCII evicts up to 3x sooner (intended conduct arriving late); ASCII unchanged. Elision/xray parity already restored on both arms — no action. Fences: skills/re-frame2-pair/** + tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/** only; no hot-zone files. Dossier file deleted per protocol.

title: guide 06's option A sample throws on a fresh app-db: (name nil) when :theme/current is unset
description:
Guide 06-theming.md's Option A block reads (name (sub [:theme/current])) and its reg-sub is (fn [db _query] (:theme/current db)). On a fresh app-db -- before any :theme/choose has run, which is every first paint and every server render that was not seeded -- the sub returns nil and (name nil) throws in ClojureScript ("Doesn't support name"). Nothing in the chapter seeds the key and :initial-events is not mentioned there.

This matters more once rf2-2rtt6.108's ruling lands, because Option A becomes THE TAUGHT DEFAULT: the copy-paste sample a new author starts from would crash on the state the app starts in, and on the server it fails the render rather than painting the default theme.

Repair is a spelling, not a design change: a total form such as (name (or (sub [:theme/current]) :light)), or an explicit :initial-events seed shown in the chapter. Either way the chapter should say which, because the CSS half already has an answer for the no-stored-choice case (:root defaults, optionally @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)) and the Clojure half should agree with it.

Found while adjudicating rf2-2rtt6.108 (docs/design/hicasso/studio/108-the-theming-taught-default-priced.md SS8). Not fixed there: 06-theming.md was outside that page's fence and has open PRs against it. Fold into the 108 guide rewrite.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7580. The default now lives in the guide's own reg-sub for :theme/current -- (:theme/current db :light) -- which matches the repo's worked pilot (:acme.invoice/theme in pilot_field.cljc defaults in its reg-sub). Both limbs measured under cljs 1.12.145: a fresh app-db reads nil, and (name nil) throws 'Doesn't support name: '. Guide-only fix: :theme/current appears nowhere in implementation/, tools/ or spec/. The boot option was relocated rather than rejected -- :initial-events now appears in layer 3 as how a REMEMBERED choice lands before first paint, since seeding cannot be the answer to nil (a fixture or second frame that skips it puts the crash back). Plus one troubleshooting row naming the blank page and the console string. Net +15/-1.

title: SSR: the inline HydrationPayload conformance schema is still loose in three more slots
description:
SPUN OUT of rf2-2rtt6.91's MERGED-PR AUDIT #7510 remainder, which fenced its own scope: 'Align that ONE schema slot ... do not broaden into a payload-schema rewrite.' PR #7545 aligned :rf/render-hash and stopped there. This bead carries what it deliberately left.

implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/payload_policy_cljs_test.cljc pins an inline HydrationPayload it calls 'the canonical v1 HydrationPayload schema (Spec-Schemas :rf/hydration-payload)'. Against spec/Spec-Schemas.md's block (~L3793-3801) three divergences remain:

  1. :rf/schema-digest  — test says {:optional true} [:maybe :string]; spec says {:optional true} :string.
  2. :rf/runtime-db     — test says {:optional true} [:maybe :map];    spec says {:optional true} :rf/runtime-db.
  3. :rf/head-hash      — ABSENT from the test schema; the spec carries it {:optional true} :string, and build-payload emits it. The map is open, so a payload carrying :rf/head-hash validates while nothing checks its type.

NOT A LIVE DEFECT TODAY. payload-policy/build-payload assembles via cond-> with (some? runtime-db), schema-digest and head-hash arms, so it provably never emits a present-and-nil value in any of the three. The gap is that the schema calling itself canonical would ACCEPT shapes the spec forbids — the same fail-open class rf2-2rtt6.91 closed for :rf/render-hash, one slot over.

THE WORK. Tighten 1 and 2 by dropping the [:maybe ...] (NOT by importing the spec's :rf/runtime-db registry ref — that needs a malli registry in the test ns and IS the rewrite the audit fenced). Add slot 3. Each wants a focused case in the manner of build-payload-render-hash-is-optional: real value preserved, nil omits the key, hand-stamped nil rejected. Mutation-prove each new assertion.

JUDGEMENT CALL AVAILABLE. If the mayor would rather the inline schema stop claiming canonicity than chase Spec-Schemas slot by slot, retitling the comment is a legitimate cheaper answer and should be argued rather than defaulted into.
close_reason:
TIGHTENED (not retracted). Landed on main as 169d4b633c via PR #7555.

THE JUDGEMENT CALL. The bead offered retracting the canonicity claim as the cheaper answer. Argued and declined, on one fact: retraction has to say what guarantees the payload shape instead, and the answer is nothing. `git grep HydrationPayload` over *.clj{,c,s} returns payload_policy_cljs_test.cljc and no other file - it is the only place in the corpus that types the payload's slots at all. The spec section's own '> Conformance:' pointer names implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_hydration_test.clj, but that namespace exercises the CONSUMER (:rf/hydrate installing, failing closed on a malformed payload, round-tripping through the router); it holds no schema and calls no m/validate on a payload shape. Retracting would have left build-payload's emitted shape unvalidated corpus-wide, and would have put a disclaimer directly above the six-line comment rf2-2rtt6.91 wrote to explain why :string rather than [:maybe :string] is what canonicity MEANS here.

:rf/head-hash settled it. build-payload emits it and the map is OPEN, so the key was not loose - it was SILENT. Mutation A3 below shows the open map admitting both nil and 42 for it.

SLOT DISPOSITIONS.
  1. :rf/schema-digest  [:maybe :string] -> :string.  Matches Spec-Schemas exactly.
  2. :rf/runtime-db     [:maybe :map]    -> :map.     ONE DOCUMENTED DEVIATION, now stated in the header comment rather than implied: Spec-Schemas types this as the registry ref :rf/runtime-db (resolving to RuntimeDb, a map of four optional :rf.runtime/* sub-containers), and resolving a ref needs a malli registry in the test ns - the rewrite the audit fenced and this bead forbade. The base type is weaker than the ref but holds the cardinality the fail-open [:maybe :map] gave away.
  3. :rf/head-hash      ABSENT           -> :string.  Newly typed; first assertions in the corpus that look at it.

SPEC CO-EDIT: NOT NEEDED. The spec block is correct as written in all three slots; the test was the side that had drifted.

build-payload UNCHANGED. All three cond-> arms already omit on nil - (some? runtime-db), and truthy guards on schema-digest / head-hash (neither slot has a legal false value, so truthy and some? coincide). The defect was the schema admitting shapes the builder cannot produce and the spec forbids.

MUTATION PROOF, both directions per slot, against `clojure -M:test -n re-frame.ssr.payload-policy-cljs-test` (baseline 34 tests / 96 assertions, 0 failures):
  Schema side (revert the slot):
    A1 :rf/schema-digest -> [:maybe :string]  = 1 failure (hand-stamped nil accepted)
    A2 :rf/runtime-db    -> [:maybe :map]     = 1 failure (hand-stamped nil accepted)
    A3 :rf/head-hash     slot deleted         = 2 failures (open map admits nil AND 42)
  Builder side (force the cond-> arm to true):
    B1 schema-digest arm     = 9 failures,  every explain {:path [:rf/schema-digest], :schema :string, :value nil}
    B2 (some? runtime-db) arm = 8 failures,  every explain {:path [:rf/runtime-db], :schema :map, :value nil, :type :malli.core/invalid-type}
    B3 head-hash arm         = 10 failures, every explain {:path [:rf/head-hash], :schema :string, :value nil}
  All six reverted; the branch carried the tightened schema plus its assertions and nothing else.

SCOPE HELD. One file, test-only, 143 insertions / 2 deletions. No malli registry, no ref resolved, no production code, no spec/** edit.

GATES. clj-kondo at the CI pin 2026.04.15: exit 0, errors 0, warnings 4536 (baseline). implementation/ssr JVM: 623 tests / 3127 assertions, 0 failures. implementation/ssr-ring: 215 / 1034, 0 failures. scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh: PASS, 625 / 2954, 0 failures - and note the lane now runs the WHOLE suite with no exclusions (rf2-lwtlk's roster reached zero), so this namespace is in the production-gate lane and green there. npm run test:cljs (inside the fast-PR spine): 12642 tests / 63334 assertions, 0 failures. CI on #7555: 50 pass, 0 fail.

The fast-PR spine's final phase (per-ns test isolation) reported FAIL locally with 4 unrelated RED namespaces (views-current-component, story x2, subs-override-seam), each dying on ENOENT for .shadow-cljs/builds/node-test/dev/out/cljs-runtime/goog.debug.error.js. That was the worktree being reaped mid-gate - the PR merged at 12:15:04Z, the branch was deleted and the worktree removed while the phase was still reading build output. Not a regression; CI's CLJS (shadow-cljs :node-test) job passed in 11m58s on the same commit.

title: Nothing gates a docstring's prose against what its module exports — one docstring seeded four design records and a guide page
description:
FOUND while landing rf2-2rtt6.120 (2026-08-05, PR #7543).

THE SHAPE. front/intent.cljs's render-callback docstring illustrated the row a
`renderRow` prop exists to build with `(h/as-element [:li {:on-click [:row/pick
(:id row)]} (:title row)])`. No such var exists: arm1/lang.clj exports exactly
defview, hfn and defhost, the mechanism is codec/as-element and it is internal,
and no h/ spelling reaches it. FOUR independent design documents
(studio/raw-escape-design-{a,b,c}.md, raw-escape-spec.md) plus decisions.md and
one guide page copied the spelling out of that docstring. Design C built its
entire render-prop worked example on it.

WHY IT PROPAGATED. Every executable surface is gated — clj-kondo resolves every
symbol in a form, the compile gate compiles 126 namespaces with zero warnings —
but a docstring is a string literal. Nothing reads the prose inside it, so a
docstring can name a function that does not exist and stay green forever. The
teaching surface with the widest blast radius is the one with no gate behind it.

THE CANDIDATE GATE. scripts/check_retired_spellings.py is the right home in
kind: it already scopes to exact retired SHAPES rather than bare keywords, for
exactly this reason. `h/as-element` is a precise, unambiguous shape — it is not
sanctioned anywhere, so a bare git-grep for it has no false positives, except
that rf2-2rtt6.120's PR deliberately leaves several NEGATIONS in the records
('there is no h/as-element'). So the gate cannot be a bare grep either; it wants
the shape 'h/as-element inside a code fence or a paren-call position' versus
'h/as-element in prose immediately preceded by a negation'. Alternatively, and
more cheaply: a doc-fence-only rule, since every surviving occurrence is prose.

THE GENERAL CASE IS BIGGER AND MAY NOT BE WORTH IT. Verifying every qualified
symbol in every docstring against the ns it appears in is a real analyzer.
Recommend the narrow ratchet (one known-dead spelling, plus a place to add the
next one) over the general check, unless a second instance shows up.

NOT DONE IN rf2-2rtt6.120's PR: scripts/ was outside that dispatch's fence.
Bench lane. No AI attribution.
notes: ADDENDUM: the 2,983-hit sweep was docstring-scoped. Extending it to ';;' comments found NO new phantom spelling, but five further sites of the same three -- four rf/after-render in substrate/spine.cljs (which requires re-frame.interop :as interop and has no rf alias) and one frame/call-with-drain-lock-on-record! in flows/registry.cljc. So: 3 phantom spellings across 8 prose sites, all 8 fixed in PR #7547. The recommendation is unchanged -- extending the sweep to comments found more SITES, not more KINDS, which is further evidence the class is small and closed rather than open-ended.
close_reason:
MEASURED, THREE FIXED, NO CHECKER WARRANTED. PR #7547.

INCIDENCE. Swept all 3,110 tracked .clj/.cljc/.cljs (3,061 namespaces):
extract docstrings, find every prefix/name token, resolve prefix through
the file's own ns :require map, ask whether the target ns defines name.

  2,983  docstring names a qualified symbol its resolved ns does not define
    259  ...restricted to a LOCAL alias (prefix in this file's ns form)
     35  ...further restricted to an indented CODE BLOCK
     19  ...further minus a retirement/negation marker in the sentence
      0  ...of those 19, genuine defects

GENUINE DEFECTS IN THE WHOLE TREE: 3. All fixed in #7547.
  1. front/intent.cljs `h/as-element` -- the bead's origin instance, STILL
     LIVE ON MAIN (rf2-2rtt6.120 filed the bead, did not fix the docstring).
     Now `(hfn [row] (codec/as-element ...))`, matching the DOM test.
  2. react_shared_suite.cljs `rf/after-render` -- the same docstring spells
     the call `interop/after-render` one paragraph earlier. re-frame.core has
     no after-render on either platform (JVM ns-publics: 116, absent).
  3. flows/registry.cljc + flows_reg_flow_destroy_linearization_test.clj
     `frame/call-with-drain-lock-on-record!` -- :drain-lock is a KEY on the
     frame record, not a fn. Real one: frame/call-serialized-with-drain!,
     already spelled correctly at frame.cljc:1148 for the same fact.

WHY NO CHECKER (measured, not opinion).

(a) THE DISCRIMINATOR CANNOT SEPARATE A MISTAKE FROM A DELIBERATE NOTE. The
    dominant legitimate use of "a docstring naming a nonexistent symbol"
    here is a RETIREMENT NOTE -- EP-0007 "One Name Per Fact" REQUIRES naming
    retired spellings. All ~14 rf/* candidates hand-verified were notes:
    rf/dispose-adapter! ("-> rf/destroy-adapter!"), rf/sub-topology
    ("rf2-80mmlf DEMOTED the facade alias"), rf/replace-app-db! /
    rf/handler-ids / rf/runtime-db-value / rf/snapshot-of ("API-shrink #3
    RETIRED..."), rf/epoch-listener-generation ("## The defect this closes").
    A gate here fights the repo's own documentation discipline.

(b) THE BEST DISCRIMINATOR SCORES 0% PRECISION AND 0% RECALL. The bead's own
    proposal (code-block position + local alias + no negation) leaves 19
    survivors, ZERO of them defects -- English pairs (headers/cookies,
    frame/query), concept names (frame/profile), React exports
    (machine-canvas/Chart), reg-view ids (shell/event-list), line-wrap
    artefacts (trace-state/current-state-). And it catches NEITHER real
    instance: h/as-element's prefix is not a local alias (intent.cljs
    requires no h), rf/after-render is inline prose not a code block.
    Widening to non-local prefixes to reach them re-admits 1,543 findings
    (docs/core = a path, tools/call = an MCP JSON-RPC method,
    request/reply = English).

(c) GROUND TRUTH IS NOT SOUNDLY COMPUTABLE STATICALLY. "Does ns X export Y?"
    is defeated three independent ways: macro indirection
    (rm/defreg-macro, defwrapper, defui, multi-line ^{:doc} metadata);
    reader-conditional platform splits (frame-provider is a real CLJS facade
    export, absent from JVM ns-publics); and optional-artefact conditional
    re-exports (clear-flow / machine-meta are on the facade only when the
    artefact is on the classpath -- the same docstring is right or wrong
    depending on deps). A checker wrong on any of these reds a legitimate
    docstring, strictly worse than no checker.

(d) THE NARROW RATCHET WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT THE PROPAGATION. A single
    h/as-element token rule over .clj* is green the moment fix 1 lands, but
    the spelling propagated docstring -> .md design records, which no
    source-suffix gate scans. Extending to .md ships a gate red on arrival
    against 11 occurrences in docs/design/hicasso/**. That tree needs no
    repair: raw-escape-spec.md sec (e) already rules it out in terms
    ("h/as-element ... does not exist in the taught surface") -- the
    synthesis caught it, which is the studio process working. The rest are
    historical proposals and a quotation of the defect, correct as records.

The bead's clause "recommend the narrow ratchet ... unless a second instance
shows up" fired -- but the second and third instances were DIFFERENT dead
spellings (rf/after-render, frame/call-with-drain-lock-on-record!), which is
itself the argument that a one-token ratchet does not generalise: the next
one will be a fourth token nobody has thought of.

NOTHING WEAKENED. No existing checker modified, relaxed or folded into. No
gate added, so check_gate_scheduling.py's reachability derivation and
check_fast_pr_gap.py's literal one-invocation-per-line spine parse are
untouched; both re-verified green.

title: perf+scope: check_ambient_durable_reads walk is 7.0s on a built checkout, but pruning NARROWS the gate — needs a ruling
