title: Three verdict gates run nowhere: test:schemas-bundle, test:ui-warm-watch, test:cljs-perf-emit-nightly
description:
Found while taking rf2-6ckzl's fourth remedy clause (PR #7536). The new
audit .github/scripts/check-gate-scheduling.py enumerates every
`test:*` / `bench:*` command in implementation/package.json and asks
whether any workflow reaches it. rf2-6ckzl named ONE such gate
(test:perf-bundle). The measured answer is FOUR:

  40 gate commands, 30 scheduled, 10 declared,
  4 of the 10 being genuine holes.

  * test:perf-bundle          -- rf2-eegpw / PR #7530 gives it a home.
  * test:schemas-bundle       -- releases `schemas-bundle-probe` +
    `schemas-bundle-probe-malli` and runs check-schemas-bundle.cjs.
    That checker is referenced by this npm script and by NOTHING ELSE
    in the repo, so the malli-boundary bundle claim has never run in CI.
  * test:ui-warm-watch        -- runs check-ui-warm-watch.cjs, likewise
    referenced by this npm script and nothing else.
  * test:cljs-perf-emit-nightly -- the sharpest one: a build named for
    the nightly that is in no nightly. `:node-test-perf-nightly` selects
    `-emit-nightly-test$`, which the consolidated `:node-test` build's
    `cljs-test$` does NOT match, so every `*_emit_nightly_test.cljs`
    namespace runs in that lane alone -- and that lane runs nowhere.
    check_test_lane_bijection.py cannot see this: the lane HAS a
    selector and the selector DOES reach files, so the bijection holds.
    What no gate asserted until now is that the lane is ever RUN.

The other six unscheduled commands are legitimately covered and are
declared as such in the audit's DISPOSITIONS table, with the premise
of each declaration machine-checked (test:security / test:ui /
test:testbed-support are strict `cljs-test$` subsets run by the
scheduled consolidated lane; test:cljs-isolation and
test:mcp-conformance have their teeth run directly by test.yml;
bench:hicasso yields records, not a verdict).

REMEDY. Give each of the three a scheduled home. The cheap one is a
step in expensive-tests.yml's browser/bundle sweep -- which per
rf2-6sg25 now alerts when it reds, so a nightly home is a real home
rather than a second silent one. NOTE THE LOCKSTEP: adding an
`npm run` step to `browser-bundle-and-story-gates` obliges the same
command in scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh
(implementation/scripts/_rigorous-local-inventory.test.cjs pins it).
Run each gate green locally FIRST -- wiring an unvalidated gate into
the nightly the week alerting lands would file an issue on night one.

Delete each command's DISPOSITIONS entry in
.github/scripts/check-gate-scheduling.py as it gains a home. The audit
deliberately does NOT go red when an `unscheduled` entry becomes
scheduled -- that transition is the hole closing, and reddening main
for it would punish the fix.
close_reason:
Delivered in PR #7542 (merged, 25e404f434). Each of the three was RUN before it was scheduled, per the bead's own warning.

test:cljs-perf-emit-nightly -- 32s cold, GREEN (12 tests / 37 assertions).
WIRED into expensive-tests.yml's browser-bundle-and-story-gates as its own
named step. Nightly on the build's OWN documented grounds rather than on cost:
shadow-cljs.edn says its User-Timing assertions are noisy under per-PR runner
load. The defect was the missing schedule, not the tier.

test:ui-warm-watch -- 48s cold, GREEN (all 8 passes + WARM-CACHE REUSE PROVEN).
WIRED into the same job. NOT the watch-mode command the name suggests: it
drives a real Shadow warm watch and one live emitted runtime through eight
scripted edit passes plus a disk-cache restart, then terminates with a verdict.
Nightly because it spawns two watch daemons and a live node child and polls at
50ms under a 120s timeout -- the process-orchestration class, most prone to
false negatives under per-PR load. Cost would have allowed either tier.

Both added to scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh in the same PR: both satisfy that
script's documented two-part derivation (verdict + nightly-only home), and
_rigorous-local-inventory.test.cjs pins the lockstep.

test:schemas-bundle -- 47s cold, RED. NOT WIRED, and that is the real finding.
Both probes measure 124.9 KB gzipped against a 100 KB ceiling, 24.9 KB over,
while Spec 010 Bundle cost still catalogues ~91 KB and the checker's own
threshold comment repeats it -- both statements now false. A gate that had run
nowhere since it was authored had accumulated a real 25% regression. The
schema-implies-validation equality guard is still green (12-byte delta), so the
structural claim holds and only the absolute budget moved.

It stays declared 'unscheduled' repointed at rf2-kybsf (filed, P1), with the
measured red in its why. Not threshold-bumped: Spec 010's budget table is
normative and the checker's own failure text says rule the spec section first,
move the threshold in lockstep. Narrowing a gate to make it pass is the one
move this audit exists to prevent.

DISPOSITIONS entries deleted for the three gates that gained homes
(test:perf-bundle, test:ui-warm-watch, test:cljs-perf-emit-nightly).
Census: 40 gate commands, 31 -> 33 scheduled, 9 -> 7 declared, 3 -> 1 hole.

Mutation-proved: unscheduling either newly-wired gate reds the audit by name
(exit 1); perf flag off reds emit-nightly across four deftests; a shrunk card
fixture reds warm-watch at cold accept. All reverted.

title: expensive-tests.yml nightly has no failure alerting - a red system-of-record is silent
description:
Found while costing rf2-rliq7 (2026-08-05 16:40 AUSEST).

.github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml declares only:

  on:
    schedule:
      - cron: '17 15 * * *'
    workflow_dispatch:

There is no notification step, no issue-filing step, no Slack hook -
nothing fires when the nightly reds. The only way anyone learns is by
opening the Actions tab.

EVIDENCE THAT THIS BITES. Of the last 30 nightly runs, 18 failed. The
run of 2026-07-09 through 2026-07-21 was RED FOR 13 CONSECUTIVE NIGHTS
on 'Run rigorous implementation browser and bundle gates' (that step has
since been restructured into the per-gate steps). Separately the Xray
feature matrix has flaked 4 of the last 14 nights and is still unfixed
(rf2-7jevo).

WHY IT IS A FAIL-OPEN, not just an ergonomics gap. Multiple gates are
DELIBERATELY nightly-only precisely because the nightly is treated as
the system of record - TESTING.md says so, and rf2-rliq7's option (1)
rests on it entirely. A system of record that can be red for thirteen
nights with nobody paged is an instrument that reports nothing and is
believed anyway. That is the same shape as the 26 fail-open instruments
cleared this week, one level up: the gate runs, it catches, and the
catch goes nowhere.

SURFACE: .github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml (HOT-ZONE - sequence
against any live workflow worker). Cheapest credible fix is a final
'if: failure()' step that opens or updates a single tracking issue, or
posts to wherever the team already looks. Deliberately NOT proposing a
specific channel here - that is Mike's call.
notes:
Audit follow-up from merged PR #7536 (2026-08-05). The alert is present, but `derive_signature()` only counts job/step conclusions in `("failure", "timed_out")`. A completed job with conclusion `cancelled` therefore yields an empty signature; `decide([])` treats that as green, so cancellation can produce no incident or advance the green streak and auto-close an existing incident. This contradicts the workflow's stated requirement that a run cancelled or skipped part-way still has a verdict worth recording. Keep the repair small: classify terminal non-success conclusions deliberately (without turning benign skipped dependents into failures), and add exact self-tests proving cancellation cannot count toward recovery or close an open nightly-red issue. Also cover another terminal infrastructure conclusion such as `startup_failure` so the rule is explicit rather than cancellation-specific.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7600 (merged 2026-08-06T05:51:16Z) — REOPENED exact owner. The cancellation/startup_failure repair is correct and the 37 checks pass, but the promised terminal-classification rule remains fail-open. At merge commit 2ae34316e3119604459e23a3941869209a1d7c9d, derive_signature() handles only failure/timed_out/cancelled/startup_failure; a completed job concluded action_required, neutral, or stale (all GitHub conclusion states), as well as a missing/unknown future conclusion, falls through `if conclusion not in FAILED: continue`, yields an empty signature, and decide([]) treats it as green. Direct pure-layer probes reproduce action=none for all of those, so they can advance the green streak and close an open incident exactly like cancelled did before this PR. The code comments explicitly say every conclusion absent from the two tuples becomes green, so this contradicts the PR's “statement of the rule” claim. Keep the repair small and fail-closed: make success and the deliberately benign skipped job the only recognized green job conclusions, synthesize a no-verdict entry for any other completed conclusion (including unknown/missing), and pin at least action_required, stale, and unknown/null plus the skipped exception. Do not duplicate the alert architecture.
close_reason: SHIPPED in PR #7600 (merged). FAILED = (failure, timed_out) — the gate ran and did not pass; ABORTED = (cancelled, startup_failure) — it never reached a verdict. An aborted job contributes a distinct no-verdict signature, so a killed run cannot masquerade as last night's failure; decide() needed no change because a non-empty signature makes the green branch unreachable, so greens cannot advance and close cannot be returned. skipped is in neither tuple and an aborted job's steps are never read at all, making the benign-skipped exclusion structural rather than a filter a later edit could widen. NOT HYPOTHETICAL: two genuinely cancelled nightlies on consecutive nights (28458640816 2026-06-30, 28531231200 2026-07-01) on which the pre-fix script reports action=none notifies=no. Four mutation proofs, each reddening only its own rule. Ten real non-aborted runs give byte-identical verdicts pre- and post-fix, so zero added noise on ordinary nights.

title: cljs_prod / bundle_isolation are not armed by examples/* — both example-bundle gates can be skipped by a change to the example they compile
description:
rf2-eegpw follow-up (found while wiring the cljs-perf-bundle job).

## The gap

.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh's generic `examples/*)` case arms ONLY `cljs_browser` + `cljs_node_test` (plus `examples_compile` from the earlier combined case). It does NOT arm `cljs_prod` or `bundle_isolation`.

But both of those outputs gate jobs whose bundles are compiled FROM examples source:

- `cljs-perf-bundle` (new, rf2-eegpw, gated on cljs_prod) builds `:examples/counter` + `:examples/counter-perf`, both `counter.core/run`.
- `cljs-bundle-isolation` (gated on bundle_isolation) builds `:examples/counter`, `:examples/counter-uix`, `:examples/login`, `:examples/login-uix`, `:examples/realworld-resources`.

So a PR that changes only `examples/counter/**` recompiles the exact entry both gates grep, and neither gate runs. The perf gate would not notice a counter change that stopped reaching a mark-and-measure call site (which would make the perf-ON control vacuous); the isolation gate would not notice a counter change that pulled in a tools/* symbol.

## Why it was not fixed in rf2-eegpw

The fix is one classifier change in `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` that widens BOTH gates at once, and rf2-eegpw's fence was `.github/workflows/**` + TESTING.md + implementation/package.json. It is also a shared decision (how much extra `:advanced` build cost to spend on examples-only PRs), not something the perf-gate bead should decide unilaterally.

## Remedy

Arm `cljs_prod` + `bundle_isolation` from the generic `examples/*)` case — or, if that is judged too broad for the whole examples tree, from the specific example entries the two gates compile. Note the classifier is deliberately conservative elsewhere (see the rf2-8ckcf2 comment in that same case, which widened it to cljs_node_test on exactly this reasoning), so the broad widening is the more consistent choice.

Also consider the second half of rf2-eegpw's remedy clause 4: nothing detects an npm script that exists but appears in no workflow. That is the class that hid test:perf-bundle for as long as it did.
notes:
Audit follow-up from merged PR #7542 (2026-08-05). `scheduled_scripts()` applies `NPM_RUN_RE.findall()` to the raw concatenated YAML text, and `ci-runs-it-directly` likewise accepts `probe in workflow_text`. A comment such as `# documentation only: npm run test:orphan` therefore marks an otherwise orphaned gate scheduled; verified directly against the merged/current checker, which returns `test:orphan` for that comment-only corpus. This defeats the ratchet precisely when an actual `run:` line is removed but explanatory workflow prose remains. Make workflow reachability derive from executable `run` values (including multiline run bodies), not comments or other YAML fields, and add mutation-style self-tests for comment-only `npm run` and comment-only direct probes. Preserve transitive package-script closure and the small pure-static implementation.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7599 (merged 2026-08-06T05:54:28Z) — UPDATED exact open owner. Moving reachability from raw YAML to `run:` values is the right boundary and the 24 self-checks plus live 40/34/6 audit pass, but the promised executable-text classification remains incomplete in both directions. At merge commit dee4a5486eda0f9c0c443dbd98f2e2e438e5638a, direct pure-layer probes show `run: echo ok # retired npm run test:orphan` and the same trailing comment inside a `run: |` body still schedule `test:orphan` (false green), while a real folded scalar `run: >-` whose lines are `npm` / `run test:orphan` schedules nothing even though YAML executes it as `npm run test:orphan` (false alarm). The code claims all comments are excluded and folded scalars count, so these are contract holes rather than broader shell parsing wishes. Keep the repair bounded: interpret the supported YAML scalar value accurately, exclude shell comment text without breaking quoted `#`, and fold `>` bodies as YAML runs them—or fail loudly on forms the static extractor cannot classify. Add these three exact self-test rows; do not grow a general shell parser.
close_reason: SHIPPED in PR #7599 (merged). The classifier arm this bead's TITLE describes had already landed in c1e833bb4c on 2026-08-05; the live charge was its newest note — check_gate_scheduling.py derived reachability from RAW workflow YAML, so a comment naming a command marked that gate as scheduled. Only 8% of the workflow corpus is executable (39,567 of 511,152 chars), so the gate was reading its answer out of the other 92%. Sharpest instance: test:mcp-conformance pinned its ci-runs-it-directly probe on a JOB ID appearing 8x in raw YAML and ZERO times in any run: value — its premise had never once been confirmed by anything CI executes. Reachability now derives from run: values only. Live counts IDENTICAL before and after (40 gates / 34 scheduled / 6 declared), which is what proves nothing real was leaning on prose; deleting one run: while keeping its comment goes baseline-green -> fixed exit 1 naming the gate.

title: hicasso: Spec 009's view-trace pair needs an instance-token, which needs a third hook (HD-020 conflict) -- RULING
description:
# The Spec 009 view-trace pair cannot be emitted by a boundary shell under the ≤2-hook budget

FOUND while delivering rf2-2rtt6.125 (Performance `:render` for `defview`). The Performance half landed; **goal 2 of that bead — the `:view/render` / `:rf.view/rendered` trace pair — is blocked by an architectural conflict, not by effort.**

## The conflict, stated from both documents

Both view ops require `:rf.view/render-key` = `[view-id instance-token]`:

- Spec 009 §Trace ops: `:rf.view/render` carries `:tags {:frame <id> :rf.view/render-key [<view-id> <instance-token>]}`. `:rf.view/rendered` carries the same tuple plus `:rf.view/mount?`, which is **keyed off it** ("stable across an instance's re-renders and fresh per new instance").
- Spec-Schemas §`:renders`: "the second slot is an integer instance-token minted at mount time from a runtime counter atom".
- Spec 009 §`:rf.view/unmounted` already states how the **React-hook family** obtains one: *"The instance-token is minted into a `useRef` so the `:rf.view/render-key` tuple is stable across re-renders."*

A `useRef` is a **third hook**. HD-020(b) spends the whole ≤2 budget on `useContext` (frame) + `useSyncExternalStore` (subscription/epoch), and `arm1.runtime`'s ns docstring is explicit that this is load-bearing rather than incidental: *"no per-instance render-phase state at all … React offers a function component no per-instance storage except a hook cell, so a shell that wants one has spent a third hook (`useRef`/`useState`) before it starts."* `arm1_hook_ledger_dom_cljs_test` counts hooks at React's own dispatcher, so a third hook fails a test rather than a review.

## Why there is no side door

- **The `useSyncExternalStore` registration** is minted inside `subscribe`, which React calls at **commit** — after the body has run, and never at all on a render that does not commit. `:rf.view/render` fires at render START. It cannot supply a render-phase identity, and on a first render it does not exist.
- **The module-level `rstate`** carries the running frame and the scratch read-set. It has no per-instance axis and cannot grow one without becoming per-instance storage.
- **The memo wrapper** is per-element, not per-instance.
- **React's current fiber** (via internals, as `arm1/hook_probe.cljs` reaches for the dispatcher) is double-buffered — React alternates between two fiber objects for one instance — so it is neither stable nor shippable.

## Why a degenerate token is NOT the answer

Emitting `[view-id nil]` for every boundary would collapse every instance of a view into one row in Xray's Views panel, and `:rf.view/mount?` — which is derived from the render-key's stability — would be meaningless. That is precisely the shape rf2-2rtt6.91 ruled against on the render hash: *"A degenerate value is worse than an absent one: an absent key cannot be mistaken for evidence, a constant one is a fail-open gate wearing the shape of a check."* Nothing was emitted for that reason.

## What a decision looks like

This is a genuine ruling, not an implementation task. The options, none of them free:

1. **Spend the third hook** in the boundary shell (`useRef` for the instance token), gated on `interop/debug-enabled?` so production still costs two. React does **not** permit a conditionally-called hook — the gate would have to be compile-time (`goog.DEBUG`), which makes the dev shell and the prod shell two different shells. HD-020's budget would need an explicit dev-build carve-out.
2. **Weaken the trace contract**: make `:rf.view/render-key` `[view-id nil]`-legal and document `:rf.view/mount?` as absent on substrates without instance identity, i.e. accept a documented *subset* (the bead's own escape hatch — "an explicit, witnessed subset documented if any field is substrate-impossible"). Costs Xray's per-instance Views rows on Hicasso pages.
3. **Ship Hicasso without the view-trace pair** and say so — Performance `:render` (delivered) plus React DevTools plus the arm's own `body-runs` instrument, which is always-on and counts real body runs.
4. **Find a render-phase instance identity React actually offers a function component.** As of React 19 there is none that is stable and public. `useId` is a hook.

## Not blocked on

`rf2-2rtt6.125`'s Performance half is delivered and merged independently (PR #7524). This blocks only the trace half and any claim that Hicasso is a full peer for the Xray Views timeline.
notes:
RULING 2026-08-05 20:01 AUSEST (delegated dossier-review pass; operator-overturnable) — OPTION (3): the bench arm ships WITHOUT the :rf.view/render / :rf.view/rendered trace pair, and says so. No degenerate emission of any kind: no [view-id nil] render-key, no absent-or-false mount? through the current pipeline, no fabricated token on :rf.view/unmounted. Absence, never a constant.

WHY (2) FELL — the dossier's main rec was mispriced; verified against the consumer. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc: [view-id nil] does NOT crash (rows are index-keyed) but FABRICATES twice: (a) view-rows' {render-key => render-args} accumulator (~L2632-2693) aliases simultaneously-mounted instances of one view — the panel diffs instance A's props against instance B's = false instance evidence; (b) render-cause (~L2552) reads (true? mount?) — absent mount? classifies every MOUNT as :props '<- parent re-render', wrong cause + wrong mount/re-render stripe (view.cljs ~L1430). Exactly the .91 class ('a constant one is a fail-open gate wearing the shape of a check' — quote verified verbatim). Making (2) honest = marked aggregation shape + spec edits (009 L283: mount? 'Always present'; Spec-Schemas L4347: tuple REQUIRED on :renders rows) + Xray branches suppressing prev-args diff/cause on tokenless rows — a mini-project buying a permanently second-class panel. The Codex section's critique of naked (2) is VERIFIED CORRECT.

WHY NOT (1) NOW — Codex's dev-only useRef is technically sound (uSES registration is commit-time; Rules of Hooks force two compile-time-selected shells; prod DCE preserves the heap claim) but it forks the arm's most defended invariant with ZERO precedent: HD-020(b) carries no build qualifier ('never useRef — a third hook in the shell is a budget breach'), arm1/runtime.cljs claims 'no per-instance render-phase state at all' as a design property, arm1_hook_ledger_dom_cljs_test counts at React's dispatcher (exactly 2, neither useRef nor useState, count independent of read count), and a forbidden-token roster (runtime.cljs ~L1953) pins 'no useRef anywhere in the shell'. Every prior hook spend was priced OUTSIDE the shell (presence's 3, controlled shadow's per-field useState, host gate's 1, class boundary's contextType costing none). A dev/prod shell fork to buy a dev-tool nicety while K1/K2 are open inverts priorities on a bench arm.

WHY (3) IS FREE AND HONEST — verified: views-step is conditional (nil when no view-render AND no unmount events — step OMITTED; projection.cljc ~L2729) and the Reactive panel's reader-join (reactive_panel_subs.cljs ~L325) unions view-ids off :rf.view/rendered ops, degrading to empty reader lists. Absence cannot be mistaken for evidence. Zero consumer change, zero spec edit, HD-020(b) + both witnesses byte-identical. Coverage stated: Performance :render measures MERGED (PR #7524) + the arm's always-on body-runs instrument + React DevTools. The stated gap: Xray's VIEWS step and per-sub reader lists do not populate for Hicasso pages.

GRADUATION CLAUSE (named so it cannot be lost) — when the product shell for implementation/hicasso/ is minted, re-price deliberately: (1) dev-only useRef (Codex sketch is the reference: two compile-time-selected component fns with fixed hook order, two-ledger witness by build, advanced-bundle elision gate proving ref/token/trace machinery absent in prod — if the gate cannot prove absence, fall back) VS an honestly-MARKED tokenless subset (:rf.view/rendered carrying view-id + deref-subs serves per-view aggregation AND the reader-join without instance claims — needs Spec-Schemas change + Xray branches suppressing prev-args diff/cause; priced above, not cheap) VS staying dark. Any non-full-pair outcome amends Spec 009 (mount? 'Always present' + the uniform-wrapper sentence) and Spec-Schemas §:renders — spec/* is HOT-ZONE: sequence that edit, never batch. No spec sentence is needed NOW: the spec's view-trace claims scope over the shipped adapters; the bench arm is not claimed by them.

No implementation follows from this ruling.

title: hicasso: wire defview into Spec 009 Performance :render (and view-render traces)
description:
# Product gap: Hicasso defview does not own Spec 009 Performance :render (or the matching view-render traces)

## Problem

re-frame2's Performance instrumentation (Spec 009 §Performance instrumentation, channel #5) brackets four hot paths when `re-frame.performance/enabled?` is true:

| Bucket | Entry name | Owner today |
|---|---|---|
| `:event` | `rf:event:<id>` | core router — **substrate-independent** |
| `:sub` | `rf:sub:<id>` | core subs — **substrate-independent** |
| `:fx` | `rf:fx:<id>` | core fx — **substrate-independent** |
| `:render` | `rf:render:<id>` | **view substrate** — must call `performance/mark-and-measure` around the user body |

A Hicasso app therefore already gets **event / sub / fx** User-Timing measures under the opt-in flag. It does **not** get a first-class **per-view `rf:render:*`** trail.

Reference shapes that *do* own `:render`:

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs` — `build-frame-aware-view` wraps the user render-fn in `(performance/mark-and-measure :render id …)` and emits the view-render / view-rendered traces Xray's Views panel consumes.
- Freehand — `implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/shell.cljs` (and `react.cljs`) brackets the same `:render` bucket.

The experimental Hicasso arm under `implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/` (`arm1/runtime.cljs` mint path, `front/*`) has **no** `mark-and-measure` / `rf:render` call sites. `defview` is therefore **not a peer** of `reg-view` / Freehand for production-friendly render timing or for the full Xray Views timing story.

This is a **product-parity gap**, not a programme bar row. The Performance guide page (draft-guide/11-performance.md) correctly tells authors to use React DevTools + Xray for islands; it must not claim Hicasso ships `rf:render:*` until this lands.

## Goal

Make Hicasso-minted views **first-class consumers** of Spec 009's Performance `:render` channel (and, in the same seam, the view-render **trace** pair that Xray expects), with the same contract shape as `reg-view*` / Freehand:

1. **Performance** — when `re-frame.performance/enabled?` is true, each boundary body run emits one `rf:render:<view-id>` measure (options-bag measure, clear-after-emit unless `retain-entries?`), including on throw (try/finally). When the flag is false under `:advanced`, the bracket **DCEs** to a bare body call — zero prod cost.
2. **Trace (dev)** — emit the same ordered pair the adapter path uses: render-start then post-render (with elapsed / deref-set / mount flag as the existing Spec 009 view ops require), gated on `interop/debug-enabled?` like core. Do not invent a second op vocabulary.
3. **Id identity** — `<view-id>` must be stable and filterable (`rf:render:…`); align with how `defview` / mint-view already names heads (keyword or registrar id — pin one rule and witness it).
4. **Boundaries only** — plain inlined helpers are **not** separately bracketed (they are not React components and not reg-view peers). Document that.
5. **SSR / abandoned render** — brackets must not leave durable registration or wrong-frame ambient pollution; match Freehand/core discipline for server and StrictMode double-invoke (two measures in dev is correct React behaviour, not a bug).

## Non-goals

- Changing the Performance API surface, goog-define names, or naming convention (`rf:<bucket>:<id>`).
- Instrumenting the Hiccup **walk** as its own User-Timing bucket (interpretation cost is not this bead; read shape remains the primary author-facing lever).
- Replacing React DevTools Profiler or inventing Hicasso-private APM.
- Claiming the programme mount/bulk **bar** is closed by this work — this is observability parity, not a clock row.

## Acceptance

- With `:closure-defines {re-frame.performance/enabled? true re-frame.performance/retain-entries? true}`, a Hicasso page of N distinct `defview` heads produces `rf:render:<view-id>` measures that a `PerformanceObserver` / `getEntriesByType('measure')` can filter by the `rf:render:` prefix; ids match the pinned naming rule.
- With both performance flags **false** and a production-shaped build, no User-Timing calls remain on the defview path (DCE / no-op parity with core tests).
- Dev build: Xray-consumable view-render traces fire for Hicasso boundaries with the same op types and required fields as the reg-view path (or an explicit, witnessed subset documented if any field is substrate-impossible — prefer full parity).
- Witnesses: unit/DOM tests in the Hicasso bench arm (or product tree when graduated) that assert measure names and trace ops; no dependence on internal clock harnesses for acceptance.
- Guide: one honest sentence on draft-guide Performance (and/or Getting started feature map) that Hicasso **owns** `rf:render:*` once this lands — update tense in the same PR or a paired docs child, no overclaim before merge.

## Design notes (implementation sketch — not a free design pass)

- Prefer the **same macro** `performance/mark-and-measure` used by core/Freehand; do not reimplement User Timing.
- Place the bracket at the **single chokepoint** that runs every boundary body (mint-view / render-body), not at every codec site.
- Trace emit helpers: reuse or thin-wrap core's view emit functions if packaging allows (`implementation/` may not `:require` tools; core view emit is fine). If the arm cannot depend on `re-frame.views` helpers, copy the **contract** (op types + field set) not a divergent dialect.
- Confirm interaction with HD-028 memo bail-out: skipped bodies must **not** emit a render measure (bail-out means no body run — same as React not calling the FC).

## Sequencing

- Parent: **rf2-2rtt6** (Hicasso programme).
- Natural follow-on after experimental arm mint path is stable; can land in the bench arm first and carry into `implementation/hicasso/` at graduation.
- Does **not** block controlled-input / interop correctness beads; **does** block any marketing claim that Hicasso is a full peer for prod render RUM.

## Context

Surfaced 2026-08-05 in guide/product Q&A: authors asked whether Hicasso integrates with the Performance API. Answer: event/sub/fx yes; per-view `:render` no — this bead closes that gap.
notes:
DELIVERED IN PART -- PR #7524 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7524). NOT CLOSED, deliberately: goal 1 (Performance :render) plus goals 3, 4 and 5 landed; goal 2 (the view-TRACE pair) is BLOCKED on a real architectural conflict, now on rf2-2rtt6.126. Left open so the mayor rules on whether the remaining goals stay here or move.

WHAT LANDED. mint-view! and mint-frame-prop-view! wrap the component fn React calls in (performance/mark-and-measure :render view-name ...). The bracket is on the COMPONENT FN, not on render-body as the design sketch suggested, and the reason is a cost that would have survived elision: render-body does not know the view's name, so threading one in adds a parameter passed on every render of every boundary, present in the OFF bundle too (and would have forced an edit to arm1.hydrate-cljs-test, which calls render-body directly). view-name is already closed over at the component fn, so with the flag off the macro constant-folds to the bare (shell body-fn js-props) call that preceded it.

Four of the bead's clauses then fall out rather than being arranged: a React.memo bail-out emits nothing (the comparator sits ABOVE the bracketed fn -- HD-028's rider, clause 'Confirm interaction with HD-028'); StrictMode's double-invoke emits twice (correct); the generation fence emits ONCE per React render spanning its retries, so the duration is the wall-clock React paid; a throwing body still emits via try/finally. Clause 4 (boundaries only) holds by construction and is documented in the docstring and in Spec 009.

ID RULE PINNED (clause 3): rf:render:<view-name>, where view-name is the string mint-view! was given and the string stamped as displayName -- so the measure name and React DevTools show ONE identifier. defview makes it "<ns>/<sym>". build-name's :else arm stringifies verbatim, so no spec change was needed to accommodate strings; the RULE is now written into Spec 009 Naming convention.

SPEC EDIT (5 insertions / 1 deletion, hot-zone surgical). The What-gets-bracketed table's Where column said 'Per-reg-view render (the wrapper emitted by reg-view*)', which reads as an adapter-path rule. Per rf2-2rtt6.91's finding (the spec tiers by REPRESENTATION, not adapter brand) it now states the substrate-general rule plus the three consequences above.

WITNESSES (clause: unit/DOM tests asserting measure names; no internal clock harness).
  arm1/render_measure_cljs_test.cljs -- the OFF half, per-PR :node-test. 5 tests / 14 assertions. Asserts the id rule, and that a renderToString of a defview page renders (markup + body-runs delta) while the User-Timing stream stays EMPTY. Every off-path row is paired with a body-runs delta so 'no rf: measures landed' cannot pass over a page that never rendered.
  arm1/render_measure_emit_nightly_test.cljs -- the ON half, the EXISTING :node-test-perf-nightly build (ns-regexp -emit-nightly-test$ already matches, so no shadow-cljs.edn edit). 7 tests / 23 assertions, all green: one prefix-filterable entry per rendered head named by displayName, entryType/duration, no rf: marks, 3 passes x 3 heads = 9 entries matching body-runs, a never-rendered head absent, a throwing body still emitting, and the frame-prop twin on the same channel. Row 0 FAILS rather than skips if the flags are off, so it cannot read as a pass in the wrong runner.

MUTATION PROOF. Removing the mint-view! bracket and recompiling the nightly build turns that suite red: 8 failures, 3 errors. The frame-prop row stayed green, which is the independence proof for the second mint.

ELISION PROVED DIRECTLY, not inferred. :advanced release of a Hicasso arm both ways, cache cleared either side per rf2-2rtt6.20:
  OFF (651632 bytes): performance.measure 0, clearMeasures 0, "rf: 0, performance.mark 0
  ON  (652430 bytes): performance.measure 4, clearMeasures 4, "rf: 1, performance.mark 0
798 bytes on, zero off. npm run test:perf-bundle (the counter dual) also PASSES: off-count=0 on-count=8 -- see rf2-eegpw, which is that gate being wired to no workflow at all.

GUIDE clause is NOT in this PR: docs/design/hicasso/** was fenced (two workers renaming 11-performance.md -> 11-below-hiccup.md in flight). Filed as rf2-2rtt6.127, sequenced after those merge.

GATES. CI on #7524: 48 SUCCESS / 35 SKIPPED / 0 red, including Lint required (pinned clj-kondo), Docs required, :browser-test (carries the hook-ledger fence), CLJS production elision, both :advanced+goog.DEBUG=false browser lanes, all 20 JVM artefacts. Local: fast-PR spine exit 0 (test:cljs 12605 tests / 63166 assertions, 0 failures; mkdocs --strict with spec/ staged into docs/spec by mkdocs_hooks.on_pre_build; hicasso compile gate 122 namespaces; per-ns isolation 17/17).
BLOCK RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-05, NOT CLOSED (worker on rf2-j4bg3, which shared the Spec 009 dispatch). Nothing was delivered here and nothing should be.

rf2-2rtt6.126's ruling is option (3): the bench arm ships WITHOUT the :rf.view/render / :rf.view/rendered pair. Its GRADUATION CLAUSE does NOT release goal 2 -- it defers a re-pricing to 'when the product shell for implementation/hicasso/ is minted', which has not happened, and it names the two candidates to weigh THEN (dev-only useRef behind two compile-time-selected shells, vs an honestly-MARKED tokenless subset). Until that mint, goal 2 is ruled, not pending.

AND THE RULING FORECLOSES A SPEC EDIT EXPLICITLY: 'No spec sentence is needed NOW: the spec's view-trace claims scope over the shipped adapters; the bench arm is not claimed by them.' So there was no Spec 009 work for this bead inside that dispatch's fence -- the row would have had nothing true to say.

WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD IS THEREFORE A BOOKKEEPING CALL FOR THE MAYOR, not work: goals 1/3/4/5 landed in PR #7524; goal 2 is ruled out until graduation (rf2-2rtt6.126, closed); the guide tense-flip is sequenced on rf2-2rtt6.127. If the mayor wants the graduation re-pricing tracked where it will be found, the natural move is to close this as delivered-in-part and let .126's graduation clause carry goal 2 -- but that is the mayor's call, which is why the bead was left open in the first place.
close_reason:
DELIVERED IN PART AND CLOSED (mayor ruling, 2026-08-06). Goals 1, 3, 4 and 5 landed in PR #7524 (merge d35ce411e1, 2026-08-05), verified on origin/main rather than from the note: mint-view! at arm1/runtime.cljs:1891 and mint-frame-prop-view! at :1917 wrap the component fn in (performance/mark-and-measure :render view-name ...), with render_measure_cljs_test.cljs as the OFF half per-PR and render_measure_emit_nightly_test.cljs as the ON half.

GOAL 2 (the :rf.view/render trace pair) IS RULED OUT, NOT PENDING. rf2-2rtt6.126 is CLOSED with option (3): the bench arm ships without the pair, its graduation clause defers a re-pricing to when implementation/hicasso/ is minted, and the ruling explicitly forecloses a Spec 009 edit for it. title: hicasso: a fallback is NOT inert markup — a defview head in :ssr {:fallback ...} renders a live boundary
description:
FOUND while pricing rf2-l0wfx (docs/design/hicasso/defhost-ssr-provider-costing.md). mint-host-gate!'s docstring states the rule the guide teaches: 'a fallback is inert markup — it is not a body, so a subscription or an intent written there is the same loud error it would be anywhere outside a boundary.' MEASURED, both arms, via react-dom/server renderToString on the arm1 bench: [:button {:on-click [:x/y]} "go"] in a fallback -> :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary (enforced, as documented) [some-defview {}] in a fallback -> mints fine; renders a LIVE boundary server-side that READS SUBSCRIPTIONS

SUBTREE

quarterly

WHY. The fallback is walked once at MINT time, outside any frame binding, so an intent vector lowered eagerly there fails. A boundary head does NOT lower eagerly: it creates a React element whose body runs later, inside the boundary's own with-frame, taking its frame from React context. So it is frame-CORRECT — the rule is simply narrower than it reads. WHY IT MATTERS. This is currently the only recovery for rf2-l0wfx: an author who wants a provider's subtree in the server response writes it a second time as the declaration's fallback. That works today by accident of the walk's laziness, not by ruling. RULING NEEDED. Either (a) it is a feature and the docstring + guide say a fallback may carry a boundary (and what a boundary in a fallback may and may not do), or (b) it is a hole and a boundary head in a fallback is refused at the declaration alongside the intent. Doing neither leaves a documented rule that is half-true and a workaround nobody sanctioned. NOT a blocker for rf2-l0wfx: every candidate there is unaffected by which way this goes.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7525 (2026-08-05): UPDATE EXACT RULING OWNER, NOT A DUPLICATE. PR #7525 disproves the older simply-narrower/frame-correct framing: one declaration renders different content per frame and after a write, while a frame-fed view bakes nil at mint and throws :rf.error/no-frame-prop. The mint-time rule is about what the walk evaluates, not inertness. Evidence is pinned in fallback_contents_cljs_test and the provider costing addendum; the ruling stays open and should be taken with rf2-l0wfx.
Merged-PR audit follow-up for #7549 (2026-08-05). `refuse-deferring-heads-in-fallback!` only descends vectors and seqs; every other value returns without inspection. The same PR explicitly blesses an already-built React element, and `as-element` returns any `react/isValidElement` unchanged. Therefore `(react/createElement some-defview #js {})` (or a built DOM element whose React-element child has a defview/defhost type) passes the mint-time fence, then React runs that marked head later under the render frame—the exact per-site/per-write live-placeholder behavior this owner was closed as preventing. The closure claim “a defview or defhost head at ANY position is refused” is consequently false for the supported React-element input branch. Keep the repair narrow: either inspect a valid element’s `.type` and renderable children for the two existing markers, or explicitly rule/document raw React elements as a trusted escape and weaken the inert-markup claim. Add a focused mint-time regression using a prebuilt element with a marked type (plus a plain DOM-element control); do not build a general React-tree analyzer.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7635 (2026-08-07): REOPEN exact invariant owner, not a duplicate. PR #7635 adds a third deferring head, [:>], but front/codec.cljs deferring-head-kind still recognizes only defview and defhost. mint-host-gate! scans a declared fallback through that closed classifier and as-element now accepts [:>], so {:ssr {:fallback [:> Component]}} mints successfully despite the fallback being promised as inert markup. The nested raw gate returns nil on the server and remains a live useSyncExternalStore component during hydration/adoption; fallback_contents_cljs_test has no raw-escape refusal row. Extend the existing classifier/fence and add a focused mint-time regression. The earlier audit note on this owner also records the still-unresolved prebuilt React-element bypass; keep both repairs together or explicitly narrow the invariant.
close_reason:
ALREADY LANDED — verified in tree 2026-08-07 before dispatch, per the standing grep-first rule. Closing as verified-duplicate of work already on main rather than dispatching it.

THE RULING'S half (b') — INERT MARKUP ENFORCED — is implemented AND witnessed. The ruled error id :rf.error/hicasso-host-fallback-boundary-head appears in FOUR files on main: front/codec.cljs (the refusal), arm1/lang.clj, arm1/host_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs and arm1/fallback_contents_cljs_test.cljs. The last of those asserts the id at EIGHT distinct sites (lines 210, 215, 220, 224, 230, 244, 313 and the docstring at :51), which is the flip the ruling required — fallback_contents_cljs_test moving from record-of-today to CONTRACT, with defview-head, defhost-head and frame-fed rows all asserting the mint-time refusal.

WHY IT WAS STILL OPEN. The ruling recorded on rf2-l0wfx said 'One worker implements both halves in one PR (same gate region)'. rf2-l0wfx is CLOSED; this bead was its sibling half and was never closed alongside it when that PR landed. A paired-halves ruling needs BOTH bead ids closed on the merging PR, or the survivor looks like outstanding work forever — which is exactly what happened here.

NOTHING TO DO. If a future reader believes the refusal is incomplete, the discriminator is the walk: it is walk-scoped at mint, so it catches the frame-fed nil-bake variant for free because that is a boundary head.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MEASURED AND PINNED — PR #7525. No ruling taken; the ruling is still yours. THE ANSWER IS NONE OF (a)/(b) AS FRAMED: the rule is ABSENT, not narrow. What is enforced is not a rule about CONTENT but about the WALK. The fallback is walked into an element once, at the declaration, outside any frame — so what is refused is exactly what that walk can EVALUATE: intent vector -> :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary a `sub` call in form -> :rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render non-hiccup -> :rf.error/hicasso-empty-vector a defview head -> MINTS; renders a live boundary, subscription read a defhost head -> MINTS; renders that host's own gate + fallback a FRAME-FED defview -> MINTS; throws :rf.error/no-frame-prop mid-render A boundary head is neither an intent nor a subscription — it is an element whose body runs later — so the walk never looks inside it, and every refusal it carries is deferred past the declaration. That is the one thing the mint-time walk exists to prevent. It is not `defview`-specific: a `defhost` head crosses identically, so the hole is DEFERRAL. TWO NEW FACTS THAT DECIDE IT — neither was on the record. 1. THE DECLARED PLACEHOLDER IS NOT A VALUE. One declaration, walked once into one element, renders three different documents: frame A ...

ALPHA

... frame B ...

BRAVO

... frame A, one write ...

ALPHA-TWO

... mint-host-gate! walks once and reuses the element everywhere, and its stated reason is "a placeholder that differs per site is not a placeholder." A boundary head makes it differ per site AND per write. The design's own justification is falsified by what the design permits. 2. IT DOES NOT SURVIVE THIS ARM'S OTHER BOUNDARY VARIANT. Arm 1 ships two mints: mint-view! (context-fed, what `defview` mints) and mint-frame-prop-view! (rf2-2rtt6.39, which frees a hook slot in a fully spent <=2 budget). A frame-fed head reads intent/*frame* when its ELEMENT is created — in a fallback that is MINT TIME, where the var is nil. So it bakes nil in, mints happily, and throws :rf.error/no-frame-prop one render into the server response. The two heads are indistinguishable in hiccup. => whether a boundary head in a fallback works AT ALL is a property of WHICH MINT the head came from. That removes "bless it as it stands" from the table: what you would be blessing is variant-dependent. If rf2-2rtt6.39 ever wins its measurement, the workaround dies silently. WHERE THE EVIDENCE POINTS (recommendation, not a ruling): the codec's own stated law — walk once, reuse everywhere, BECAUSE a placeholder that differs per site is not a placeholder — entails option (b), inert markup. The refusal would be walk-scoped and would catch the frame-fed case for free. WHY THAT WAS NOT LANDED: it deletes rf2-l0wfx's only recovery, and l0wfx is an open P1 awaiting your :ssr ruling. Both directions constrain it — refusing empties candidate D (whose content IS this workaround) and so favours A/B; blessing sanctions "write your subtree twice" and so favours D. Not this bead's to pre-empt. ALSO: the workaround is WORSE than defhost-ssr-provider-costing.md priced it. Not merely duplication + wrong context value server-side + remount at adoption, but additionally variant-fragile and in violation of the placeholder invariant. LANDED (PR #7525) — docstrings only on the executable side, no hook added, ordinary render path byte-identical: - arm1/fallback_contents_cljs_test.cljs (new): 4 tests, 12 assertions, every row above. Written as a record of TODAY, explicitly not a contract, so the ruling is an edit there and never a silence. - front/codec.cljs: mint-host-gate!'s docstring no longer asserts "a fallback is inert markup" as enforced; states what is, marks the gap UNRULED, names the l0wfx dependency and the frame-fed fragility. - arm1/host_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs: five lines of ns docstring pointing at the new suite ("neither stated nor discoverable" was half this bead). Three mutation proofs, each run, codec restored from a byte copy after each: bind *dispatch* around the mint walk (option (a)'s shape) -> 1 failure force `placeholder` to nil -> 9 failures boundary-element refuses a nil-frame frame-fed head ((b)) -> 2 errors NOT touched: draft-guide/**, spec/**, decisions.md, validation.md, implementation/core/. The guide never made the false promise — it says "placeholder markup" / "a skeleton", not "refused" — so it needs an edit only if the ruling goes toward (b). STILL OPEN. Needs your ruling on (a) vs (b), and it should probably be taken together with rf2-l0wfx rather than ahead of it.

comments.text: RULED 2026-08-05 20:02 AUSEST, together with rf2-l0wfx (full ruling + implementation brief recorded there; operator-overturnable). This bead's half: (b') — INERT MARKUP ENFORCED. A declared :ssr fallback is walked structurally at mint and a boundary head OR host head anywhere in it is REFUSED at the declaration — new id :rf.error/hicasso-host-fallback-boundary-head, naming the host, the offending head's displayName and its position. The workaround this refusal deletes is superseded: l0wfx is ruled as a THIRD :ssr value, :ssr :render (NOT :children — refuted on the costing doc's measured wrong-context-default + reasoned adoption-remount evidence), so a provider's subtree reaches the server response the honest way — the component itself renders server-side with the correct context value, no duplication, no remount. fallback_contents_cljs_test flips from record-of-today to CONTRACT: defview-head, defhost-head and frame-fed rows assert the mint-time refusal; intent/sub/non-hiccup rows unchanged. title: rf2-2rtt6.122 follow-up: confirm or rename the provisional error id, and confirm the always-on elision call
description:
TWO OPERATOR DECISIONS THE rf2-2rtt6.122 RULING EXPLICITLY RESERVED. The refusal itself is
DELIVERED (PR #7513) and neither decision blocks it — but both are CONTRACT SURFACE, so they are
tracked here rather than left as a worker's silent pick. Both are cheap to change now and
expensive later.

DECISION 1 — THE ERROR ID. Implemented PROVISIONALLY as `:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused`.

  Rationale for the pick: it follows the frame-resolution family's past-participle shape
  (`no-frame-context`, `bad-frame-provider-arg`, `frame-context-corrupted`,
  `write-after-destroy`) and names the event from the caller's side — the ambient reach was
  refused.

  Rejected candidates, recorded so they are not re-proposed: `:rf.error/no-ambient-frame-here`
  (reads as an ABSENCE, which is precisely the confusion this id exists to prevent — a frame IS
  in scope); `:rf.error/render-phase-frame-refused` (over-specifies — the tier is scoped to a
  dynamic EXTENT, which a substrate need not use only for rendering);
  `:rf.error/ambient-frame-illegal` (adjective; breaks the family's shape).

  COST TO RENAME: 5 files — `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc` (the payload builder,
  the emit fn, the block comment), `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (the catalogue row),
  `implementation/core/test/re_frame/always_on_axis_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` (the always-on
  literal), plus the two test suites that assert on the id. All mechanical.

  THE MESSAGE, for the same review: it is COMPOSED, not owned by one side. Core states what
  happened, that it is NOT an absence (so adding another frame boundary will not help), and that
  an explicitly carried frame still carries. The refusing substrate appends the sentence naming
  what to write instead, carried verbatim into `:reason`. Hicasso's names the boundary collector.

DECISION 2 — ALWAYS-ON vs DEV-GATED. Implemented ALWAYS-ON, proven green under
`-Dre-frame.debug=false`.

  The project's rule is that elision follows WHAT THE CHECK PROTECTS. This is a programmer's own
  mistake caught at render time, which by the letter of that rule argues elidable. Three reasons
  outweigh it:

  (a) THE REFUSAL IS NOT A DIAGNOSTIC WRAPPED AROUND CORRECT BEHAVIOUR — IT IS THE BEHAVIOUR.
      Dev-gating yields code that throws in development and, in production, silently mutates the
      subscription cache during render, contributes no collector edge, and freezes the boundary.
      That dev/prod divergence is the worst available outcome, and it is the same trade EP-0002
      already refused when it deleted the `:rf/default` floor.
  (b) CONSISTENCY AT THE CALL SITE. `:rf.error/no-frame-context` is always-on and is raised by
      the same primitive (`require-current-frame!`). If one absence survived production elision
      and its sibling did not, that primitive would behave differently in production depending on
      which absence it found.
  (c) DEV-GATING BUYS NOTHING MEASURABLE. The substrate's `binding` is the substrate's own cost,
      and the resolver's one `nil?` test cannot be eliminated while the var is bindable at all —
      a gate would remove the guarantee without removing the work. The dev-only trace emit
      already DCEs; only the production-survivable record ships.

  IF THE ANSWER IS "PERMISSIVE IN PRODUCTION" ANYWAY, the right lever is NOT gating core's tier.
  It is having the SUBSTRATE not establish the extent — one `interop/debug-enabled?` in
  `re-frame.bench.hicasso.front.intent/with-frame` — which keeps core's contract single-valued
  and puts the policy where a substrate can own it per-substrate. That is a 1-line change.

NO CODE CHANGE IS NEEDED IF BOTH PICKS STAND. Close this as confirmed-as-implemented in that
case.
close_reason: Confirmed-as-implemented (delegated ruling, operator-overturnable — see 2026-08-06 comment): :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused stands; always-on stands. No code change needed per the bead's own terms. Remaining touch: the provisional stamps' removal is a one-line comment/docs touch the mayor folds into any nearby PR.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: DELEGATED RULING 2026-08-06 11:21 AUSEST (dossier review, Mike-delegated, operator-overturnable): CONFIRM BOTH. (1) :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused STANDS. Verified: frame.cljc payload builder ambient-frame-refused-payload + emit-ambient-frame-refused! + require-current-frame! two-absences discrimination (refusal tier read only after resolution failed — one nil-test, error path only); Spec 009 catalogue row present, channel always-on. Rejected list stays rejected (no-ambient-frame-here=reads-as-absence / render-phase-frame-refused=over-specifies / ambient-frame-illegal=adjective). Codex concurred; its nuance — catalogue mixes no-*/bad-*/past-participle, name stands on own merits (short, searchable, consistent w/ behavior-command-refused, distinct from no-frame-context) — accepted as sharpening, not counter. (2) ALWAYS-ON STANDS on ground (a): the refusal IS the behaviour — dev-gating = throws in dev, silently mutates sub cache mid-render + zero collector edges + frozen boundary in prod, the EP-0002-refused trade; (b) call-site consistency w/ no-frame-context (verified always-on, same primitive); (c) one flag read on error path. Codex added independent mechanism proof: bare rf/subscribe bypasses Hicasso's read-set collector -> no boundary rerender edge -> stale prod. Witnesses: id in always_on_axis_conformance_cljs_test.cljc always-on set; frame-resolver-test 15/40 + real -Dre-frame.debug=false lane 17/42 green (Codex-run); PR #7513 MERGED. Composed message verified verbatim: what-happened + NOT-an-absence + carried-still-carries + substrate :reason appended.

title: re-frame.ui: rule on whether compiled view bodies adopt core's ambient-frame refusal tier (same silent-freeze class as rf2-2rtt6.122, one substrate over)
description:
FOUND while building the ambient-frame refusal tier for rf2-2rtt6.122 (PR #7513, merged code
below is on that branch). NEEDS AN OPERATOR RULING — it is a behaviour change to a shipped
substrate, not a mechanical follow-on.

THE TIER NOW EXISTS AND IS GENERAL. `re-frame.frame/call-with-ambient-frame-refused` +
`frame/*ambient-frame-refusal*` let ANY substrate declare "no ambient frame is legal in this
dynamic extent"; `resolve-current-frame` withdraws the React-context tier while it is set (a
carried stamp still carries) and `require-current-frame!` raises
`:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused`. Hicasso is wired. Wiring a second substrate is ~3 lines.

RE-FRAME.UI HAS THE IDENTICAL LAW AND THE IDENTICAL SILENT HAZARD, verified file:line:

  - `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/viewcell.cljs:20-27` — render RESOLVES + PROBES *without
    ownership* via `reactive/with-capture`; the LAYOUT commit acquires the captured targets, and
    abandoned renders "acquire no ownership and publish no speculative capture state".
  - `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/substrate.cljs:18-20` — compiled views' "sole read owner
    is `re-frame.ui.reactive` (probe/acquire/read/release)"; `:75-79` the legacy `use-subscribe`
    surface is "deliberately not exported".
  - `implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/reactive.cljc:1059-1098` — `with-capture` binds ONLY its
    own `*ambient*`. `rf/subscribe` knows nothing about it, so an ambient read in a compiled view
    body contributes ZERO to the capture: no dependency edge, no ViewCell revision advance, no
    repaint.
  - AND IT RESOLVES ANYWAY: `substrate.cljs:26-45,:66-72` publishes the React-context reader
    through the `:adapter/current-frame` late-bind hook, so under any `frame-provider` /
    `frame-root` an ambient `rf/subscribe` in a compiled view body succeeds silently and bumps a
    ref-count with no matching release (`subs.cljc:514-543`) during the render phase — a
    StrictMode double-render double-bumps and an abandoned render leaks.

So it is the same silent-freeze class rf2-2rtt6.122 just closed for Hicasso, one substrate over.

WHY IT WAS NOT WIRED IN #7513, deliberately: re-frame.ui is SHIPPED (experimental, but shipped),
and turning an ambient read in a compiled view body from silently-working into throwing is a
behaviour change for any consumer who wrote one. rf2-2rtt6.122's ruling authorised the tier and
Hicasso's use of it; generalising to a second substrate is its own call. Census of in-tree
occurrences was not taken — take it before ruling.

THE DECISION: does re-frame.ui establish the refusing extent around a compiled view body's
render (the same one-line `binding` fusion Hicasso used in `front.intent/with-frame` — here it
would fuse into `reactive/with-capture`, which already binds), or does re-frame.ui accept that
ambient reads in compiled bodies silently produce no edge and document it?

NOT IN SCOPE HERE, and settled the other way: the three shipped ADAPTERS (Reagent, reagent-slim,
UIx) must NOT get this tier. For Reagent / reagent-slim the render body IS the reactive context
(`reagent2/ratom.cljs:87-93` — a deref inside it is how a Reaction discovers dependencies) and
UIx documents ambient reads as the norm (`adapter/uix.cljs:139-160`). Ambient subscribe is
correct there.
close_reason:
RULED — DO NOT WIRE THE TIER INTO re-frame.ui. Rejected at triage under the pre-alpha no-gold-plating stance, and the premise the bead was held on does not hold.

THE BEAD HELD THIS FOR AN OPERATOR RULING because it is 'a behaviour change to a SHIPPED substrate, not a mechanical follow-on'. re-frame.ui is not shipped and never will be. docs/release-process.md:17 records the ruling verbatim: the compiled-view substrate re-frame.ui is 'not in that set and never will be — Mike ruled on 2026-07-22 that day8/re-frame2-ui is not to be published, since it is donor-only code being absorbed into Freehand and the standalone artefact is DELETED at the EP-0036 F6e gate (rf2-a32r7)'. rf2-a32r7 already disarmed its publication, so no consumer can ever depend on it. With no consumer and a scheduled deletion, the work's entire value expires at F6e.

THIS IS THE SAME RULING I ALREADY MADE ON THE SAME SUBSTRATE. rf2-oazgv asked whether the :class/:style refusal should be added to the donor implementation/ui/ custom-element for parity; the answer was no, on exactly these grounds. The generalisation recorded then and reaffirmed now: when a fix lands on Freehand and the question is whether the donor needs parity, the default is NO unless the donor behaviour is reachable by a consumer or by a gate that will outlive F6e. Neither applies here.

THE HAZARD IS REAL AND THAT DOES NOT CHANGE THE ANSWER. viewcell.cljs:20-27 does resolve and probe without ownership, and the silent-freeze class is genuine — the bead verified it file:line. But a guard is warranted when a SILENT failure can reach someone. Here the only reachable path is in-tree transitional code on an artefact being absorbed and then removed. Adding ~3 lines plus their witnesses to code scheduled for deletion is work whose value is bounded by the deletion date.

IF F6e SLIPS INDEFINITELY, or if re-frame.ui acquires a consumer, this becomes live again — that is a new bead with a live subject, and this reasoning is the first thing to re-read.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RULING 2026-08-05 20:00 AUSEST (delegated dossier review, operator-overturnable): DEFER — do NOT wire the refusal tier into the present re-frame.ui donor; the proposed ~3-line fix is INERT, not merely cheap. Re-scope this bead: the SUCCESSOR compiled substrate implements the refusal at absorption (EP-0036 F3+), after sanctioned compiled reads carry their frame EXPLICITLY.

VERIFICATION (all Codex claims checked against tree, file:line):
(a) VERIFIED — viewcell.cljs:324-345 with-current-frame binds frame/*current-frame* to the ViewCell frame around EVERY compiled body (all 5 wrappers: :399,:412,:433,:450,:467); deliberate, commit 4580267a15 (rf2-4rwtd 2026-07-20) fixing :rf.error/no-frame-context under ratom-family hosts.

The .122 witness suite itself proves the inertness: ambient_refusal_cljs_test.cljs:192-207 asserts a *current-frame* binding (rf/with-frame) resolves raw rf/subscribe INSIDE a refused extent by design. viewcell is exactly that binding → wrapping with-capture in call-with-ambient-frame-refused would let raw rf/subscribe keep resolving = false confidence, worse than no fence.
(c) VERIFIED — observation.cljc:1606-1611: resolve-target calls frame/require-current-frame! when site-ctx has no :frame pin, and reactive.cljc:1045-1047 builds site-ctx WITHOUT one — sanctioned compiled sub depends on ambient resolution. Removing/sentineling the viewcell binding breaks sanctioned subs; real enforcement = thread the resolved frame into the observation target (site-ctx :frame) / substrate-owned capture, i.e. the frame/capture architecture the successor owns. No salvage of the 3-line fix exists.
(d) VERIFIED — EP-0036:67-68 "re-frame.ui is donor-only now: no new standalone surface"; :126 never published, deleted at the gate; :315-316 no day8/re-frame2-ui coordinate ever; hicasso/charter.md:147-149 end state. No consumer to rescue.

ACCEPTANCE RULE for the successor (carry forward verbatim-in-spirit, per Codex): inside a framework-owned interpreted or compiled collector body, an unqualified core ambient read/dispatch MUST fail loudly; adapter-native component bodies remain unaffected; explicitly carried frame operations retain core's trusted-programmer semantics. Implementation shape: at absorption, thread the resolved frame through the substrate-owned capture or explicit observation target, THEN establish call-with-ambient-frame-refused around the author body; witnesses for raw ambient subscribe/dispatch (refuse), sanctioned sub (works), carried frames (work), adapter islands (untouched), dev/prod/JVM. If re-frame.ui is ever reversed into a supported product before deletion, implement the real thing there — never land a refusal binding that frame carriage renders inert.

Hazard remains REAL (raw ambient subscribe in a compiled body contributes no capture edge → silent freeze + unbalanced ref-count) — this deferral is not an endorsement; ui/sub stays the taught spelling and the census shows no in-tree offender. Bead stays OPEN, re-scoped as above. Dossier ai/decisions/rf2-iwh5c.ui-ambient-refusal-tier.md reviewed and deleted per process.
