title: ssr-ring emits a render-hash for ANY root shape — including adoption-tier ones Spec 011 now says must carry none
description:
FOUND WHILE LANDING rf2-2rtt6.91 (PR #7510). Not fixed there, because
the fix needs a host-level fact the undecided server arm owns.

rf2-2rtt6.91 established the rule and PR #7510 put it in Spec 011
§Hydration-mismatch detection: an ADOPTION-TIER root (compiled donor
substrate, native UIx, Freehand) MUST NOT carry :rf/render-hash in its
payload nor data-rf-render-hash on its root element, because the only
tree such a root can offer a server-side hash is the UNRESOLVED root
form, whose canonical EDN is [#fn[] {props}] — a constant.

ssr-ring does not know about tiers. pipeline.clj:543 computes
  hash-str (lifecycle/render-document-hash hiccup)
over (lifecycle/resolve-root-view root-view) unconditionally, and passes
:emit-hash? through, for whatever :root-view the host declared. Correct
for a hiccup-tier host; silently degenerate for an adoption-tier one.
The server-arm dossier already recorded that 'the degeneracy reaches
production identically whichever arm renders'. Nothing serves a Freehand
root through ssr-ring TODAY, so this is a trap laid rather than a live
defect — but the first server arm that does will re-create exactly the
fail-open gate rf2-2rtt6.91 just closed, in production rather than in a
bench.

SECOND, SEPARABLE HAZARD ON THE SAME LINE — the HICCUP tier's own root
form. resolve-root-view accepts a hiccup VECTOR verbatim, so a host
declaring :root-view [#'app/root] makes the SERVER hash the shallow
[#'app/root] while the documented client boot (:render-tree-fn
#((rf/view :app/root)) — note the outer call) hashes the DEEP tree the
view returns. Those can never be equal, so that host fires
:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch on EVERY page — and under :ssr
{:on-mismatch :hard-error} that is a crash on every page. Fail-CLOSED
and noisy rather than fail-open, so much less severe than .91, but it is
a live foot-gun: resolve-root-view's docstring says 'Prefer the 0-arity
fn form' for an unrelated reason (opts built before registration) and
never mentions the hash consequence, which is the sharper one.
VERIFY BEFORE FIXING — I read this from the source and did not run it.

Likely shape: a :root-view whose resolved form is a single callable-headed
vector cannot produce a meaningful body hash, so either refuse
:emit-hash? for it with a typed error naming the 0-arity fn form, or
require the host to declare its tier. Ruling needed on which — do not
default into one.

Hot-zone: implementation/ssr-ring/** is not in the hot-zone list, but
spec/011-SSR.md is, and a fix probably touches it.
notes:
THE UNKNOWN THIS BEAD'S CLOSE RECORDED IS NOW CLOSED — IT REPRODUCES, AND tools/template WAS THE LIVE INSTANCE (mayor, 2026-08-05).

WHAT I WROTE WHEN CLOSING: "WHAT I DO NOT KNOW, and am recording as unknown rather than assuming: whether the SECOND, separable hazard on pipeline.clj:543 reproduced - the :root-view [#'app/root] vector reportedly making the server hash shallow while the client hashes deep... WHOEVER TOUCHES pipeline.clj NEXT SHOULD RE-CHECK IT rather than assume it was handled."

IT REPRODUCES. Found by the rf2-qfct9 worker, measured in the emitted project rather than argued: the template's two ends declared the root differently - server (defn root-view [] [(rf/view :app/root)]), a REFERENCE; client (fn [] (rf/with-frame app-frame ((rf/view :app/root)))), the TREE. Client tree hashes a2aa3d1d; the server's unresolved root hashes f1d63f7e - the exact per-arity constant that render_hash_tier_test.clj pins for [(rf/view :anything)].

SO THE TEMPLATE WAS BROKEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, BEFORE AND AFTER THIS BEAD: before, it shipped a hash that MISMATCHED ON EVERY PAGE; after, the hash is simply absent. Both wrong for a hiccup-tier host, which is what it actually is.

THIS BEAD'S FIX IS CORRECT AND UNTOUCHED. The template's root belongs to the hiccup tier and SHOULD carry a hash - it was merely spelled the one way that structurally cannot have one. The repair is the outer call, (fn [] ((rf/view :app/root))), which lifecycle.clj's resolve-root-view docstring already names as the symmetric spelling. HTML is byte-identical either way.

WHY THIS IS WORTH RECORDING BEYOND THE FIX: a worker fenced to implementation/ssr-ring/** could not see that a tools/ artefact asserts on the emitted markup, and nothing connects "this code emits X" to "that test asserts X" across an artefact boundary. The fence was right; the coupling is invisible from both ends. That is the same class as test:perf-bundle wired to nothing and :rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id documented but never set.

AND A FAIL-OPEN IN THE VERIFYING LANE ITSELF, which the fixing worker hit first: plain `clojure -M:test` in tools/template SKIPS the failing rows - they sit behind RF2_TEMPLATE_RUN_EMITTED_TESTS=1. Its first run came back GREEN with the bug still present. Anyone verifying that lane locally must set the env var or they get a false green.
close_reason:
CLOSED BY THE MAYOR FROM THE LANDED EVIDENCE, because the implementing agent was killed by a watchdog stall before it could close this itself (2026-08-05). Its last line was "Green. Committing and opening the PR now" - it did both, and the work merged as PR #7520.

WHAT LANDED, verified on main rather than taken from a report that never arrived:
  fix(ssr-ring): the unresolved root form carries no render-hash on the server either
  test(ssr-ring): pin the server-side tier rule and its measurement
plus implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/render_hash_tier_test.clj, which is the pin.

THE ANSWER IT REACHED, readable from the PR title and worth recording because the brief asked the question directly: THE SERVER CAN DISTINGUISH, AND IT DISTINGUISHES BY ROOT FORM RATHER THAN BY TIER. The brief had flagged that if pipeline.clj could not tell the tiers apart at that point, that would be a design finding worth reporting rather than a hack worth writing. It could tell - by whether the root form resolves - so no hack was needed and no tier-detection framework was built.

THIS COMPLETES THE PAIR. rf2-2rtt6.91 removed the degenerate hash on the client, on the ground that Spec 011's adoption tier deliberately carries none; this removes it on the server, so the first Freehand server arm no longer re-creates the fail-open in production. The two ends now agree.

WHAT I DO NOT KNOW, and am recording as unknown rather than assuming: whether the SECOND, separable hazard on pipeline.clj:543 reproduced - the :root-view [#'app/root] vector reportedly making the server hash shallow while the client hashes deep. The filer flagged it "verify before fixing" and the brief passed that on. If it reproduced and was fixed, it is in the diff; if it did not, that finding is lost with the agent. WHOEVER TOUCHES pipeline.clj NEXT SHOULD RE-CHECK IT rather than assume it was handled.

title: b7, reads_ladder and spine_ablation share one shadow build id with three :init-fns and never reset its cache — it bit a run
description:
FOUND LIVE by rf2-va5nm's worker (PR #7509), 2026-08-05, while proving the
page-error refusals end to end.

THE FAULT, reproduced on demand. b7_run.cjs, reads_ladder_run.cjs and
spine_ablation_run.cjs all build by merging their OWN :init-fn onto the ONE
shadow-cljs build id 'freehand-release':

  spawnSync(node, [runner, 'release', 'freehand-release',
                   '--config-merge', '{:output-dir ... :init-fn <theirs>}'])

so .shadow-cljs/builds/freehand-release carries a cache entry written by a
DIFFERENT program each time. None of the three clears it.

Run b7_run.cjs and then reads_ladder_run.cjs without clearing that directory
and the ladder's page dies at load with

  [ladder] PAGE PAGEERROR: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'd')

exiting 1. rm -rf .shadow-cljs/builds/freehand-release and the identical
command gives '[ladder] done', exit 0. The ladder build reported '11
compiled' on the contaminated run against '105 compiled' on the clean one,
which is the tell.

THE REMEDY ALREADY EXISTS IN THE LANE. p0_run.cjs opens its build() with

  if (resetLaneBuildCache(IMPL, BUILD)) { ... }

and lane_cache.cjs carries the measured fault and the rejected alternatives
(rf2-2rtt6.20) — 'this driver merges its own :init-fn onto BUILD, so BUILD's
cache entry was written by a different program'. The three drivers above
predate it or were never brought onto it. Give each the same call.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A NUISANCE. Since rf2-sib23 the symptom is
an exit 1 with a named pageerror, which is the right answer — an operator
investigating a real fault. Before rf2-sib23 the same contamination would
have printed the error and published the table. And a contaminated cache
that DOES reach the sentinel publishes figures measured on a bundle nobody
built on purpose.

Sites:
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b7_run.cjs
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/reads_ladder_run.cjs
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/spine_ablation_run.cjs
Reference: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs build(), and
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/lane_cache.cjs.
acceptance_criteria:
- A rider with no executable reset whose only `resetLaneBuildCache(IMPL, BUILD)` text is inside a normal string or template text fails the clear-call check; non-code text cannot satisfy clear/build-id extraction.
- A committed rider-shaped fixture proves that failure is exactly `clearsFirst`, while the agreeing-id control and all seven real riders remain green.
- Keep the repair bounded to lexical discrimination needed by this gate; no AST/dataflow framework, driver changes, measurement changes, or lint suppression.
- The focused gate, script-helper suite, and root JS lint pass.
notes:
FOLLOW-UP on PR #7609: the first push was RED on ESLint (job 92560082596).
`npm run lint:js` is `eslint .` from the REPO ROOT and reaches
lane_cache_fixtures/ even though gate discovery cannot. My first pass ran
test:script-helpers and node --check but NOT lint, which is how it reached CI --
the root manifest is a separate npm project (re-frame2-lint) needing its own
`npm ci`, and installing only implementation/node_modules leaves `eslint` absent
and the gate unrunnable locally. Worth knowing for any JS-touching bead.

THE FINDING: `no-unused-vars` fired on commented_clear_run.cjs, which bound
resetLaneBuildCache and never called it -- the exact property the fixture exists
to have. Calling the function was therefore not an option.

BOTH ESCAPE HATCHES ARE CLOSED BY THIS REPO'S OWN CONVENTIONS, and the coach's
premise was one better than stated: the tree is at ZERO suppressions, not one.
rf2-kvsm1 ALREADY retired the last live directive -- eslint.config.mjs records
it ("the suppression went with the code it guarded (rf2-kvsm1)") and the
canonical check `git grep -nE "(/\*|//) *eslint-(disable|enable)" -- '*.cjs'
'*.js' '*.mjs'` returns nothing. A disable here would have been the ONLY one in
the tree. And an ignores entry is precisely what that list forbids: it is for
trees that are GENERATED and can carry JS, "not when a file in it happens to
have complained".

CHOSEN: drop the binding -- `require('./lane_cache.cjs');` with nothing bound.
The gate's `requires` check matches the require CALL, not an assignment, so it
still passes. No suppression, no ignore, no config change.

THIS MAKES THE FIXTURE STRONGER, NOT QUIETER, and the argument is the reusable
part. A refactor that deletes the clear leaves one of two shapes and they are
NOT equally dangerous. Keep the binding and no-unused-vars reports the orphan,
so lint catches that driver a gate EARLIER (the config names that arm outright:
"a bad `require` whose binding is NEVER read is caught"). Drop the binding too
and nothing in the lint path can see anything wrong. The second variant is the
one no other gate owns, so it is the one worth modelling. DEMONSTRATED, not
asserted: with a comment-only rider in the discovery directory, lint:js exits 0
while this gate exits 1 on the same file.

The fixtures deliberately stay IN the lint path rather than being ignored out of
it, held to the same rules as real driver source -- being faithful driver source
is the whole of their value, and an ignore would let them drift into shapes no
driver could take.

ALL THREE PROPERTIES RE-PROVEN after the change: fixture trips exactly
clearsFirst and names it; differing-constants mutation red by name; comment-only
mutation red by name; legitimate double-quoted 8th rider green.

EXIT CODES: lint before 1 (reproduced CI verbatim), lint after 0, lint with
comment-only rider 0 while gate 1, suppression grep no-output, gate 0 (36/36),
mutations 1/1/0, node --check x4 0, npm ci root 0 + implementation 0,
test:script-helpers 0 (fail 0). All four files verified PURE CRLF (line count ==
CR-terminated count), so every run exercised the byte shape CI checks out.

eslint.config.mjs UNCHANGED. Seven drivers still re-diff empty against the merge
base. Mayor node_modules canary re-verified at 103 top-level entries; no junction
left behind.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7609 (merged 2026-08-06T12:01:44Z, landed 5eb06787f2964cc3941e02453932896f57929531): reopened exact owner; no duplicate filed.

Completeness: the PR delivers the different-identifier comparison, comment-only refusal, three committed fixtures, and all-green required checks, but its non-code exclusion stops at comments. String bodies remain searchable even though `codeOnly` skips over them while scanning.

Correctness: the shipped focused gate is green (36/36, exit 0). A deterministic rider-shaped probe with NO executable reset and only `const reminder = 'resetLaneBuildCache(IMPL, BUILD)'` returns null from requires, clearsFirst, noLiteralId, and sameBuildId. `CLEAR_CALL` and `CLEAR_BUILD_ID` therefore accept string content as the real call, the direct sibling of the comment-text fail-open this PR fixes. Authored and landed blobs are identical for all four changed paths; `git diff --check` is clean.

Implementation quality: one comment-masked representation is doing two incompatible jobs—release/require discovery must retain string tokens, while executable clear-call/build-id extraction must exclude string and template text. Keep the follow-through minimal: use a string-excluding projection only for the clear-call/build-id scans (no general parser or dataflow engine), add a rider-shaped string-only fixture that trips exactly clearsFirst, and preserve the legitimate quote-agnostic control.
AUDIT FOLLOW-UP on #7609 shipped as PR #7620. The audit was right and its bound was right: the fix is one extra projection, nothing more.

REPRODUCED FIRST, exactly the audit's probe. A rider-shaped file in the discovery directory with NO executable reset, carrying `const POLICY = 'resetLaneBuildCache(IMPL, BUILD) ...'` plus a template repeating the call text, returned null from requires, clearsFirst, noLiteralId AND sameBuildId on unmodified main: 40 tests, 40 pass, exit 0.

THE REPAIR. codeOnly -> project, returning TWO blanked views of one source rather than one. `code` blanks comments and keeps string bodies, because `'release'`, `'--config-merge'` and the require path ARE string literals in a correct driver, so discovery, `requires` and the spawn-side reads must see them. `exec` blanks comments AND string bodies (quotes retained), and the clear call plus its build-id argument are read from that alone. Both views keep the ORIGINAL LENGTH, which is what keeps clearsFirst's offset comparison sound ACROSS the two views -- that length property is now load-bearing in a second way and is stated where the function is defined.

WHY BOTH HALVES ARE LIVE, proven by mutating the gate rather than asserting it. clearsFirst reading `code` again -> the new fixture fails by name ("must fail clearsFirst and nothing else; it failed: nothing"). sameBuildId reading `code` again -> a correctly-wired probe carrying a decoy log line ("the old wiring was resetLaneBuildCache(IMPL, DECOY)") is FALSELY reported as clearing DECOY while releasing BUILD. So the exec read on the build-id argument is not symmetry for its own sake: over `code` it manufactures a mismatch on a clean driver.

THE EDGE THAT STAYS, written into the header rather than left for the next audit. The spawn-side reads and the require path must read string text, so a string spelling `'release', BUILD` is still visible to them; a rider that clears one id, releases another and carries such a string ahead of its real spawn would be compared against the string. That is camouflage, not the omission this gate exists to catch, and pricing it out needs the scanner to return string TOKENS instead of blanked spans -- a parser, which the bead's bound excludes.

FIXTURE. lane_cache_fixtures/string_clear_run.cjs, rider-shaped, carrying the text in BOTH a single-quoted string and a template so a projection that blanked only one form would still be caught. Like the comment-only sibling it requires lane_cache.cjs and binds NOTHING -- keeping the binding is already reported by no-unused-vars a gate earlier, so the variant no linter can see is the one this gate owns. No suppression, no ignore, eslint.config.mjs unchanged; the canonical directive grep still returns nothing, so the tree stays at ZERO.

FOUR PROBES, all removed before the commit: differing-constants RED exactly sameBuildId; comment-only RED exactly clearsFirst; string-only RED exactly clearsFirst; and the legitimate eighth rider (double-quoted throughout, an escaped quote inside a string body, const LANE_BUILD not BUILD) GREEN on all four checks -- the control that proves identifier comparison rather than memorised names.

EXIT CODES: focused gate before 0 (36/36), after 0 (38/38), with the string probe 1 by name; test:script-helpers 0; lint:js 0 (npm ci at the REPO ROOT first -- the root manifest is the separate re-frame2-lint project and without it eslint is absent and the gate is unrunnable, which is how #7609's first push reached CI red); node --check x5 0; npm ci root 0. Gate and all four fixtures verified PURE CRLF (line count == CR-terminated count) before every run. Seven drivers re-diff empty against merge base 07f3bb42e7; two paths changed; no .beads path staged. Mayor node_modules canary 101 before, junction removed after.
close_reason: PR #7620: string bodies excluded from the clear-call/build-id scans; committed string-only fixture; focused gate 38/38, script-helpers 0, lint:js 0; all 50 required checks green.

title: four of the nine page-error refusals have never been watched firing — b7, reads_ladder, spine_ablation, p0
description:
FROM rf2-sib23 (PR #7505), 2026-08-05. Filed BY the worker that wired all nine,
naming the half it could not prove rather than reporting nine green wirings.

WHAT IS PROVEN, and how. All nine now route `pageerror` through
`sentinel.cjs`'s `watchPage` and read `watch.failures` at their exit. Five of
the nine were watched refusing on a page that had ACTUALLY thrown, against a
real headless Chromium (Playwright 1.59.1, react-dom 19.2.0):

  * b6_profile_run.cjs — END TO END, in the driver's own process, both
    directions. `--no-build` plus a hand-written stub in `out/b6-profile`
    that sets `B6_READY`, completes its run, and throws from a detached task
    AFTER the sentinel is already set. Clean stub -> exit 0. The same stub
    with one line added (the throw) -> exit 1, naming the error.
  * b6_prod, b10_prod, b8, hicasso_narrow — at the DECISION, live: a real
    Chromium page throwing inside rAF, inside setTimeout and via an unhandled
    rejection, the real `watchPage` recording all three while the completion
    sentinel STILL flipped, and each driver's real exported `verdict` fed
    exactly that array. All five returned 1; all five returned 0 on the
    clean page.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN, which is this bead. b7_run.cjs, reads_ladder_run.cjs,
spine_ablation_run.cjs and p0_run.cjs have no pure exported decision — their
exit is an enumerated inline block — so their refusal cannot be driven from a
unit test, and it cannot be driven end-to-end either:

  * none of the four has a `--no-build` knob, so the driver always spends an
    `:advanced` release build before it will serve anything; and
  * their page APIs are far too large to stub faithfully (b7's `window.B7H`
    reader surface; the ladder's and the ablation's `window.LADDER` /
    `window.ABL` plans and rounds; p0's four rows, one page per clock round).
    A wrong stub is not a cheaper proof, it is a fiction that can pass or
    fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the gate.

WHAT COVERS THEM TODAY, so this is a gap and not a hole: the collector is the
same shared `watchPage` proven live above; the mapping
`PAGE_WATCHES.flatMap((w) => w.failures).map(...)` is character-identical in
all four; and `pageerror_exit_path.test.cjs` pins, per file, that the mapping
is read and that its refusal precedes the line announcing a clean run. What is
missing is a run in which one of those four processes actually returns
non-zero.

TWO WAYS TO CLOSE IT, and the choice is a judgement rf2-sib23 declined to make
on its own:

  (a) Give each of the four a pure exported `verdict`, the shape rf2-y7mw7 and
      rf2-x6g04 established. This is the fleet's answer to exactly this
      problem and it makes the refusal checkable in CI forever. It is also a
      real refactor of four long enumerated exit blocks, and rf2-jvheq's mayor
      correction warns against reading this class as an invitation to
      refactor the fleet.

  (b) Run each of the four for real, once, on a page made to throw — which
      needs an `:advanced` build and a way to inject the throw that none of
      them has today.

DO NOT close this by adding `--no-build` to the four as a shortcut. b6_prod
and b10_prod publish production evidence, and a knob that serves a stale
bundle beside a published figure is a new fail-open in the same family.
notes:
ROSTER CORRECTED IN PR #7509 (2026-08-05): THREE OF THE FOUR ARE NOW WATCHED
REFUSING, END TO END, IN THE DRIVER'S OWN PROCESS. THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN FOR
spine_ablation_run.cjs ALONE.

WHAT WAS WRONG IN THE PREMISE, and it is the half that moved. This bead read
the four as unreachable for two reasons at once — no pure exported verdict AND
no way to make the page throw. The first is true. The second is not true of
all four: b7_run.cjs has published `B7_INIT_FN` (documented as the seam an
ablation ladder rides) and p0_run.cjs has `P0_INIT_FN`, already recorded in its
own provenance as `out.initFn`. Pointing an EXISTING seam at a namespace that
`:require`s the REAL app and adds one detached throw reaches the refusal
end to end without touching the driver, without a stub, and without the
`--no-build` knob this bead forbids.

PROVEN, both directions, against Playwright 1.59.1 / react-dom 19.2.0 /
HeadlessChrome 147.0.7727.15, `:advanced` with goog.DEBUG false:

  b7_run.cjs --only mount-frame
    published entry                    -> `[b7] ok`, EXIT 0
    B7_INIT_FN=<probe>                 -> `[b7] PAGE PAGEERROR: ...` then
                                          `[b7] FAILED: the page threw and kept
                                          going`, EXIT 1. Both W1/W2 records
                                          printed BEFORE the refusal.
  p0_run.cjs --only heap
    published entry                    -> `[p0] done`, EXIT 0
    P0_INIT_FN=<probe>                 -> `[p0] PAGE PAGEERROR: ...` then
                                          `[p0] FAILED: the page threw and kept
                                          going — pageerror: ...`, EXIT 1. The
                                          heap table printed before the refusal.

  reads_ladder_run.cjs                 -> PROVEN WITHOUT A PROBE, and it is the
                                          better evidence. A real run refused a
                                          REAL pageerror — `Cannot read
                                          properties of undefined (reading 'd')`
                                          — and exited 1. Cause: b7, the ladder
                                          and the ablation all merge a different
                                          `:init-fn` onto the ONE
                                          `freehand-release` build id and none
                                          resets its cache the way p0_run.cjs
                                          does, so the ladder was served a
                                          bundle b7's earlier run had cached.
                                          Filed as rf2-t4j7c. A cleared cache
                                          and the identical command gave
                                          `[ladder] done`, EXIT 0. So the
                                          refusal fired on exactly the
                                          environmental fault sentinel.cjs names
                                          as the common one. Reproduces on
                                          demand: run b7_run.cjs, then the
                                          ladder, without clearing
                                          .shadow-cljs/builds/freehand-release.

WHAT REMAINS, and why it was not padded. spine_ablation_run.cjs alone has no
`:init-fn` override — it is a bare `const`. Adding one purely so a test could
reach it would be a knob that lets a published figure be measured on an entry
nobody built on purpose, which is a cousin of the family this bead forbids; and
stubbing `window.ABL` (the plan, the rounds, the read-back) is the fiction this
bead already rejected. It WAS run under the PR's diff (ABL_SUBSTRATES=uix): it
passed the raced ABL_READY wait normally, ran all four rounds and both snapshot
rounds, wrote both artefacts, and refused with its EXISTING enumerated exit 4 on
its fidelity control — evidence that no exit code shifted, but not a page-error
refusal. The two honest routes in the description are unchanged for it.

THE FIXTURES, so the next reader can watch it again rather than re-derive it:
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b7_pageerror_probe.cljs
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_pageerror_probe.cljs
Each is the REAL app plus one `js/setTimeout` throw — rf2-sib23's exact fault
shape, a task the app has already returned from, invisible to its
`(catch :default ...)`, setting no `window.*_ERROR`. Each carries the two-command
reproduction in its docstring. pageerror_exit_path.test.cjs pins that each
requires and CALLS the published entry (not a stub), that the throw is detached,
and that NOTHING SHIPS THEM — no driver default, no build id in shadow-cljs.edn.

rf2-sib23's false green was the thing to avoid and was avoided: the exit code
alone was never the proof. `watchPage`'s own `PAGE PAGEERROR` line is in every
throwing log, so the throw demonstrably happened before the page went away.

No measurement, arm, threshold, knob default, exit code or dataset changed.
MAYOR NOTE (2026-08-05): THE BEAD'S PREMISE WAS HALF WRONG, AND THAT IS THE DELIVERY.

This bead read the four drivers as unreachable for TWO reasons at once - no pure exported verdict AND no way to make the page throw. THE FIRST IS TRUE. THE SECOND IS FALSE FOR TWO OF THEM: b7_run.cjs already publishes B7_INIT_FN, documented as the seam an ablation ladder rides, and p0_run.cjs already publishes P0_INIT_FN, recorded in its own provenance as out.initFn. Pointing an EXISTING seam at a namespace that requires the real app and adds one detached setTimeout throw reaches the refusal end to end - no driver change, no stub, no --no-build.

So the answer was neither of the bead's two options. It was that two of the four ALREADY HAD THE INJECTION.

THREE PROVEN, ONE NOT. b7 and p0 proven end to end in both directions through their own seams. reads_ladder proven NOT BY ARRANGEMENT - a clean run refused a REAL pageerror it had no business seeing, which is how the shared-build-cache defect was found (now rf2-t4j7c).

spine_ablation_run.cjs REMAINS UNPROVEN AND THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN FOR IT ALONE. Its :init-fn is a bare const, and the implementer declined to add an override on the ground that a knob letting a published figure be measured on an entry nobody built on purpose is worse than the gap it closes. I agree. It was nonetheless RUN under the diff and refused correctly with its existing exit 4.

ALSO DECLINED, correctly: lifting the four exit blocks to pure verdicts. heap_control_exit_path.test.cjs fingerprints b7's and reads_ladder's drive() source hard, so lifting would have meant rewriting four of its assertions to prove something a live run proves better. That file is unmodified and passes.
close_reason:
CLOSED ON THE RULING ITS OWN IMPLEMENTER MADE, WHICH I ACCEPTED AT THE TIME (mayor, 2026-08-05). Closing rather than leaving it open, because leaving it open asks a future worker to do the thing we decided not to do.

WHAT REMAINED: spine_ablation_run.cjs alone. Three of the four drivers this bead named were proven - b7 and p0 end to end through seams they ALREADY PUBLISHED (B7_INIT_FN and P0_INIT_FN), and reads_ladder not by arrangement but by refusing a real pageerror it had no business seeing, which is how the shared-build-cache defect rf2-t4j7c was found.

WHY THE FOURTH IS NOT WORTH CLOSING: spine_ablation_run.cjs's :init-fn is a bare const. Reaching its refusal needs an override added for no reason except that a test wants one - and THAT KNOB WOULD LET A PUBLISHED FIGURE BE MEASURED ON AN ENTRY NOBODY BUILT ON PURPOSE. Its implementer declined on that ground and I agree: the knob is a worse hazard than the coverage gap it closes, on a driver whose entire job is to be trustworthy about what it measured.

WHAT WE HAVE INSTEAD, and it is not nothing: the driver WAS run under the diff. It passed the raced ABL_READY wait, ran all rounds, wrote both artefacts, and refused with its existing exit 4. So the wiring is exercised; what is missing is only a watched firing of the pageerror arm specifically.

IF THIS EVER MATTERS AGAIN, the honest reopening condition is that spine_ablation gains an :init-fn seam FOR A REAL REASON of its own - not for a test. At that point the proof is free and someone should take it. Do not add the seam to close this bead.

title: hicasso: ambient rf/subscribe + rf/dispatch silently WORK in Hicasso bodies under the UIx/Freehand adapters — HD-002 clause (a)'s forbidden class, fenced only by adapter choice
description: FOUND by the h/frame adversarial pass (2026-08-05, F2; full trace in ai/findings/2026-08-05.hframe-attack.md — this body is self-sufficient). THE HAZARD, verified file:line: Hicasso mounts the shared adapter-context Provider regardless (arm1/mount.cljs:46,:96-97), and make-react-adapter routes :adapter/current-frame to a raw context _currentValue read (spine.cljs:3233-3235) published by the UIx and Freehand adapters — so ambient rf/subscribe (subs.cljc:1773-1777) and rf/dispatch (router.cljc:342-347) resolve a frame and SILENTLY SUCCEED inside a Hicasso body's render on those configurations: render-phase sub-cache mutation, ZERO collector edges (the read is invisible to the boundary's window), a frozen boundary that never re-renders on the sub's movement — exactly HD-002 clause (a)'s forbidden class (runtime.cljs:69-70). Body purity is currently enforced by WHICH ADAPTER THE HOST INSTALLED, not by the runtime. On other configs the same spelling throws; on SSR it throws (context _currentValue is client-only). title: hicasso: the guide owes a prop-VALUE row after rf2-vrvv9, and two namespace-dropping positions are left standing
description:
FOLLOW-ON to rf2-vrvv9 (PR #7500), which narrowed front/codec.cljs's host-prop-value so a keyword crosses a foreign crossing whole instead of via (name v).

## 1. THE GUIDE OWES TWO ROWS (the actual obligation)

rf2-vrvv9's fence kept guide prose out of scope, and no existing sentence became FALSE - docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/05-interop.md's Defaults table speaks only about KEYS ('Props | shallow camelCase - :on-change -> onChange'). But it is now INCOMPLETE, and incompleteness is what made the original bug a trap:

  (a) Defaults table needs a VALUES row. Something like: 'Prop values | crossed whole - a keyword stays a keyword; only :class/:id/:role/:data-*/:aria-* stringify'.
  (b) Troubleshooting needs a row: 'The library ignored my keyword prop | a non-HTML prop name passes keywords through unchanged | write the string, or (name v), at the call site'.

Without (b) the change MOVES the silent failure rather than deleting it: [host {:variant :compact}] used to reach the library as "compact" and now reaches it as a raw keyword the library cannot use. That is a smaller and more local failure than the collision it replaced (it breaks at the node, visibly, with a call-site fix) - and reagent-slim's answer to the same trade was a dev warn-once. Hicasso's answer is to TEACH it, which only works once the guide says it.

## 2. TWO NAMESPACE-DROPPING POSITIONS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE

Both found while fixing vrvv9, both out of scope for 'one conversion rule at one seam', neither obviously wrong. Recorded so the ruling is made rather than inherited:

  (a) A KEYWORD CHILD. front/codec.cljs as-element: (keyword? x) (name x). [:div :theme/dark] renders the text 'dark'. Same namespace drop, but the destination is a DOM text node, so a string is the only representation and the only question is WHICH string - (name x) vs (str x) = ':theme/dark'. Changing it would move the ORDINARY render path, which vrvv9 was fenced from.

  (b) A COLLECTION VALUE. host-prop-value's (coll? v) (clj->js v) branch. [host {:value {:mode :theme/dark}}] hands the library a JS object whose 'mode' is "dark". HD-011's shallow default already documents that collections go through clj->js, so this is stated rather than silent - but a provider whose :value is a MAP is the same use case vrvv9 was about, and it does not get vrvv9's answer.

## 3. TWO STALE CITATIONS, FOR WHOEVER READS THAT COMMENT NEXT

implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs (~:426-470) cites 'rf2-d4sf' for the coerce-context-value seam and 'rf2-6hyy §7.2 D2' in its warning text. NEITHER is a live bead id (bd show: 'no issue found'). And the same comment credits 'the audit (rf2-cgcv + rf2-kfpf)' for finding legitimate non-HTML keyword props - those two ARE live, but they are React-19-READINESS audits (re-com/10x, Dash8/rf8), both CLOSED as superseded with their findings docs unrecoverable. The real, durable decision record is implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md §5 + IMPL-SPEC.md §7.2, and rf2-vrvv9's own description repeated the bad citations from that comment. Not worth a code change on its own; worth fixing if that comment is ever touched.
notes:
SEQUENCED (mayor, 2026-08-05). This bead is the honest other half of rf2-vrvv9's fix and should be dispatched once the codec seam is quiet.

ITS WORKER'S OWN FRAMING, which is why this is not a tidy-up: "without those rows the trap is MOVED, NOT DELETED". Before the fix, {:variant :compact} reached a library as the string "compact" and :theme/dark and :other/dark collided into one value. After it, the keyword arrives as a raw keyword - a smaller, local, call-site-fixable failure than a silent collision, but still a surprise to anyone who expected a string.

reagent-slim answered that same trade with a dev warn-once. THIS WORKER DELIBERATELY DECLINED THAT, and I agree with the reasoning: reagent-slim's warning is a migration net for an installed Reagent codebase, whereas after this fix a keyword at a host prop is the CORRECT, TAUGHT spelling of HD-011's flagship case, and warning on the happy path is a nag. So Hicasso's answer is to TEACH it instead - WHICH ONLY WORKS ONCE THE GUIDE SAYS SO. That makes this bead the thing that completes the fix rather than decorates it.

title: perf: check_retired_image_keys.py is 37.7s — the one required checker the fast-PR spine cannot afford
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-ejm7m, which measured every required python checker before giving it a local lane in scripts/test-fast-pr.sh.

Thirty-seven of the thirty-eight invocations cost 6.4s BETWEEN THEM. This one costs 37.7s cold / ~42s warm by itself — 95% of docs.yml's whole checker batch, and more than double the fast-PR spine's entire documentation tier (~28s, mkdocs --strict included). It is therefore the ONLY required checker rf2-ejm7m deliberately left without a local lane: folding it in would make every worker touching a single .md file pay a 2.4x docs-tier slowdown. Its --self-test arm (0.08s) DID get a lane.

The cost is real CPU, not I/O and not a Windows pathology — cProfile over a clean checkout, 3,534 files scanned:

    53.1s total (under profiler; 37.7s unprofiled)
    28.0s  re.Pattern.search        9,374,502 calls
    11.9s  _mask_multiline_clj_strings  3,064 calls  (7.1s tottime, per-character)
     8.5s  str.join                 2,589,080 calls
     0.7s  actual file reads

Two obvious wins, neither of which should change a single verdict:

1. TOKEN PRE-FILTER. The gate fires on a fixed, small set of literal tokens
   (:include-ns, :exclude-ns, :replace-standard, :rf.image/requires,
   :rf.gen/requires, :capabilities, :replace). Roughly seven patterns are run
   against every line of 3.5k files. A cheap 'if none of the literal substrings
   is in this line: continue' guard in front of the regex battery should elide
   >95% of those 9.4M searches — most lines contain none of the tokens.

2. _mask_multiline_clj_strings IS PER-CHARACTER. 7.1s of tottime plus 2.6M
   str.join calls for what is a string-literal masking pass. A single regex
   sub, or at minimum joining once per file rather than per segment, removes
   most of it.

ACCEPTANCE: the live scan runs in well under a second on this corpus; the
self-test still passes unchanged; and a mutation planting each retired spelling
(fenced code, live .clj, and each sanctioned counterpart that must stay green)
produces byte-identical findings to the current implementation. Then add

    run "retired image keys" "python scripts/check_retired_image_keys.py --verbose" \
      python "\/scripts/check_retired_image_keys.py" --verbose

to the documentation tier of scripts/test-fast-pr.sh, next to its self-test, and
drop the note_skipped line beside it. check_fast_pr_gap.py will stop naming it
by construction — no list to edit anywhere.

check_retired_composition_vocab.py (1.0s, same _EXCLUDE_REL_PREFIXES/masking
design). That one is cheap enough to have a lane already, but it would come

title: hicasso: the guide's taught 'h/as-element' recovery does not exist — four [:>] designs name a spelling no reader can call
description:
FOUND by the rf2-2rtt6.103 synthesis (2026-08-04, verified on main). Four of the six [:>] designs name h/as-element as the recovery for the two sharpest SILENT traps at a foreign crossing: hiccup written in a PROP (which crosses as clj->js data and renders as text, no error), and a function child / render-prop body returning hiccup (React: 'Objects are not valid as a React child'). Design C's entire render-prop worked example is built on it.

The guide's taught h/ roster is h/hicasso, h/root, h/fn, h/render, h/defhost, h/presence, h/child-key, h/boundary. arm1/lang.clj exports exactly three macros - defview, hfn, defhost - and no as-element. The MECHANISM is public as codec/as-element (front/codec.cljs:1708); the TAUGHT NAME is not.

WHY IT MATTERS: an error message naming a spelling the reader cannot call is worse than no message, and the [:>] escape is where authors meet an UNFAMILIAR component and are most likely to guess a prop's shape. Both traps are silent, so the message is the only teaching surface there is.

RESOLVE EITHER WAY, but resolve it BEFORE .103's refusal messages and guide rows are written: (a) export the taught spelling in the arm (one line) and keep every message and guide row as drafted, or (b) rule that the taught name is something else and rewrite the rows to name what the arm actually exposes. title: spec 008 contradicts spec 004B: 'the v1 node set carries no host variant' is stale
description:
FOUND while writing raw-escape design A (rf2-2rtt6.103), researching what 'reduced structural identity' concretely means. Not fixed there: that bead is fenced to docs/design/hicasso/** and this is a spec/** edit in a hot-zone file.

THE CONTRADICTION. Two spec files make opposite claims about the SAME v1 node set.

spec/008-Testing.md:770-771 (the tier/coverage roster, 'qualified host' row):
  'a foreign boundary is opaque to the structural render (the v1 node set carries
   no host variant), so a qualified-host law is proven by connecting the real
   behaviour or wrapper in a browser under its own host-boundary slice, never by
   the structural surface.'

spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:122,134 — heading 'The node schema — version 1',
whose closed roster carries a host variant explicitly:
  | **host** | map | :rf.ui/host :rf.ui/host-ssr :children | :props :rf.ui/host-children :rf.ui/host-map-props :key |
and :146-148 puts :rf.ui/host in the discriminator's pinned order, and :350-353 states
the fields ARE a node rather than annotations on one.

004B IS THE SHIPPED BEHAVIOUR, so 008 is the stale side. Three confirmations:
  1. implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/test.cljc — node-kind's pinned
     discriminator has a host arm reading :rf.ui/host.
  2. implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/structural_test_surface_cljs_test.cljc
     — deftest attrs-reaches-a-declared-hosts-props finds the crossing with
     #(contains? % :rf.ui/host), asserts (= ::date-picker (:rf.ui/host host)) and
     (= :client-only (:rf.ui/host-ssr host)).
  3. That test's own docstring records the repair (rf2-c20nr): before it, the host node
     fell through the discriminator to the FRAGMENT arm and attrs answered {} —
     silently, because that arm is documented total. 004B:459-462 states the same
     hazard as a rule.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. 008's sentence tells a reader that a declared host
crossing CANNOT be asserted structurally and must be proven in a browser. That is
advice to write a browser test where a headless one already works, and it is the
exact wrong reading for anyone reasoning about what a foreign crossing costs a test
suite — which is a live question on EP-0038 (HD-011's 'reduced structural identity').

THE FIX is one paragraph in spec/008-Testing.md: the v1 node set DOES carry a host
variant with an identity (:rf.ui/host), its SSR policy (:rf.ui/host-ssr) and its
:props; what stays opaque to the structural render is what the foreign component
RENDERS BENEATH the crossing, not the crossing node itself. Check the surrounding
tier table (~:620-630) for the same claim restated, and re-grep 008 for 'opaque'
and 'host variant' before editing.

parallel with another spec/008 bead. mkdocs build --strict DOES cover spec/, plus
check_doc_slugs.py and the fast-PR spine.

title: hicasso: host-prop-value DROPS a namespaced keyword's namespace at every foreign crossing — {:value :theme/dark} arrives as "dark"
description:
FOUND while writing raw-escape design C (rf2-2rtt6.103). A defhost/[:>] conversion default, not an escape defect.

THE SHAPE. front/codec.cljs host-prop-value:

    (cond
      (fn? v)                       v
      (or (keyword? v) (symbol? v)) (name v)
      (coll? v)                     (clj->js v)
      :else                         v)

(name :theme/dark) is "dark". The NAMESPACE is silently discarded, so two distinct keywords from different namespaces cross as the same string.

WHERE IT LANDS HARDEST. React-context providers — one of HD-011's five named use cases — whose :value is very often a namespaced keyword. [:> ThemeContext {:value :theme/dark}] hands the provider "dark", and every consumer below reads a string that has lost half its identity.

THE EVIDENCE THAT THIS IS A KNOWN COST. Broad stringification matches STOCK Reagent (verified 2026-08-04 against reagent-project/reagent master, reagent/impl/template.cljs: convert-prop-value's (named? x) (name x) branch). But THIS REPO's own reagent-slim adapter deliberately NARROWED it after an audit — implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs ~:426-470, 'Narrowed convert-prop-value (per DECISION-2 + IMPL-SPEC 7.2)':

  'Keyword values stringify only for HTML attribute names. For non-HTML prop names (e.g. :value on a React-context Provider, custom component props), the keyword passes through unchanged. This deletes the bridge's coerce-context-value seam (rf2-d4sf) — there is no over-stringification to undo because we never broadly stringified.'

Its html-attr-names roster is #{:class :id :role} plus data-*/aria-*, with a dev warn-once for the rest (rf2-cgcv, rf2-kfpf found a small number of legitimate non-HTML keyword props in production code).

So Hicasso's shallow default re-opens the exact seam a prior audit in this repo closed, in the same component position, for the same reason.

QUESTION FOR RULING. Is broad (name v) the default we want at a Hicasso foreign crossing, or does Hicasso adopt reagent-slim's narrowing (stringify for HTML-attribute names only; keywords otherwise cross unchanged)? HD-011 names 'shallow camelCase props' as the default and says nothing about keyword VALUES, so this is open rather than ruled.

NOTE the cost of changing it: keyword values on native tags must keep stringifying (the pure SSR serializer stringifies unconditionally and a divergence is a hydration mismatch — reagent-slim records this at rf2-fdm4rm). Any narrowing is at the FOREIGN crossing only.

title: hicasso: an h/fn at an UNCLAIMED defhost prop slot is a marked callback nothing reads — silent-dead-handler fail-open
description:
FOUND while designing the [:> ] raw escape (rf2-2rtt6.103, design B — docs/design/hicasso/studio/raw-escape-design-b-correctness.md, PR #7490). This is a finding about SHIPPED defhost behaviour, not about the escape, which is why it is filed separately: it is true on main today with no [:> ] anywhere.

THE SHAPE. front/codec.cljs host-entry routes a prop three ways: the canonical ref slot to check-ref!, a slot the declaration NAMES to intent/lower-declared-prop, and everything else to host-prop-value. host-prop-value passes fn? through by identity. intent/callback (h/fn, HD-024) marks the function and RETURNS THE FUNCTION — so an h/fn at a slot no declaration claims crosses to the foreign library as an ordinary function. It is callable, so nothing crashes.

THE DEFECT. The author wrote h/fn to ASK FOR A CONTRACT, and no position selected one. The concrete trap is the :event contract's convenience:

  [my-host {:on-pick (h/fn [x] [:row/pick x])}]   ;; :on-pick NOT in :callbacks

The library calls it, it returns an intent vector, the library discards the return, and nothing dispatches. Silently. The sibling case is already loud — refuse-undeclared-host-event! fires for a bare intent VECTOR at an event-spelled undeclared slot, on the stated ground that the alternative is the author's intent crossing as inert data. An h/fn returning that same vector is the same defect one level of indirection down, and it is accepted.

WHY THIS IS DERIVABLE AND NOT A NEW POLICY. mint-host! refuses an option it does not know (:rf.error/hicasso-host-unknown-option, rf2-2rtt6.85) on exactly this reasoning, recorded in decisions.md HD-011's addendum: a policy could be written and never applied, and 'the silent-ignore was its own defect'. An h/fn whose contract is never selected IS a policy written and never applied.

PROPOSED REMEDY (one branch, fail-closed): in host-entry's else arm, refuse a callback? value with a new named error — the host, the position, the declared slot roster, and the recovery 'declare this slot in :callbacks, or hand a plain function'. Cost is one own-property read behind a fn? guard (intent/callback? already is exactly that), on the host path only. The ordinary render path is untouched.

WHY IT NEEDS THE OPERATOR. It CHANGES A SHIPPED ACCEPT into a refusal at a declared door, so it is a behaviour ruling rather than a bug fix, and it is escalated as R1 in design B's 'What needs a ruling' section. The counter-case is an author who writes h/fn from habit at a prop that needs no contract; the answer to that is that h/fn is documented as the ONE callback form, i.e. the form you write when the position should impose a contract.

THE ESCAPE'S STAKE. If [:> ] lands with an empty :callbacks map, EVERY slot at a [:> ] crossing is unclaimed, so this fail-open goes from an edge case at defhost to the default at the escape. Design B recommends the shared branch precisely so the escape does not have to fork host-entry to be safe.

WITNESS IF ACCEPTED: a red row asserting the new :rf.error/id and :where for an h/fn at an undeclared slot; a green control for the same h/fn at a DECLARED :event slot (still wrapped, still dispatching), so the refusal is not a blanket ban on h/fn at a host. A row that asserts only 'throws' is vacuous — assert the id.

FENCES if dispatched: front/codec.cljs + its witnesses; decisions.md dated addendum under HD-011 or HD-024 only if the operator rules it in. Coordinate with rf2-2rtt6.103's implementation, which touches the same function.

DECISION: an intent/callback? value at an UNCLAIMED defhost slot is refused at lowering, fail-closed, ONE shared branch in host-entry's :else arm (beside the existing event-shaped-data refusal, ahead of host-prop-value). GROUNDS: (a) the sibling refusal's own stated ground covers this one indirection down (codec.cljs:2051 — 'the silently dead handler class every loud error in this codec exists to delete'); (b) HD-011 addendum precedent (decisions.md:463 — 'the silent-ignore was its own defect'); (c) repo-wide law spec/Conventions.md:1178 (a recognised input that cannot be honoured is signalled, never swallowed); (d) the WARN arm (owned here since .117 closed) fails the same tests — dev-only warn leaves prod silently dead, and no [:>] dev-warning symmetry exists to appeal to: raw-escape-spec S3 RETRACTED that grant and [:>] is unbuilt; (e) counter-case cost is a 5-second loud fix at the author's own stack vs a user's click doing nothing. title: DESIGN-DECISION: the theming taught default (A vs B, per-root vs per-document) — delegated ruling via design+adversarial pass; mayor implements the guide change
description:
DESIGN-FIRST DECISION (operator, 2026-08-04: careful design work, step by step; THE MAYOR IMPLEMENTS — here "implement" = the guide rewrite teaching the ruled default, plus any tiny mechanism the ruling names). The theming taught default — guide 06-theming.md:121: "Neither is the taught default yet — whether A's cost holds at one boundary under multi-frame load, and whether the theme attribute is per-root or per-document, are still open."

THE TWO OPTIONS (both already work; 06 documents both):
A. RENDER A FACT: one boundary reads the theme sub and renders the attribute; everything below bails via HD-028's memo default. Cost: one boundary re-render per switch. Keeps derivation (theme can be computed from app-db).
B. IMPERATIVE FLIP: an fx sets the attribute on the root node; zero subscriptions, zero boundary, zero render. Gives up derivation.

DESIGN QUESTIONS:
1. THE MULTI-FRAME COST QUESTION (06's first open): does A's one-boundary cost hold under multi-frame load? Argue it honestly BEFORE reaching for measurement: a theme switch is a rare, user-initiated action (not a hot path); N frames = N one-boundary re-renders per switch with memo bail below each. If argument suffices, SAY SO and close the question without a quiet-box row (over-measurement is a named posture violation); if the designer believes measurement is genuinely warranted, the case must survive the adversarial pass.
2. PER-ROOT vs PER-DOCUMENT (06's second open): frames-are-isolated-contexts is doctrine — a document-level attribute leaks theme across frames (multi-frame testbeds mount one app in N isolated frames; two frames with different themes must be expressible). That argues PER-ROOT decisively. The honest counter to weigh: real apps often want document-level chrome (scrollbars, ::backdrop) themed — does per-root strand any real CSS surface, and is the answer "the app ALSO sets a document attribute itself if it wants, outside Hicasso's contract"?
3. THE TAUGHT DEFAULT: the data-first posture (render a fact; derivation preserved; testable as a :db write; Xray-visible) argues A-as-taught with B documented as the zero-React-work alternative for apps that want it — the same honest-tradeoff shape 06 already has, but with a default stated so a new author does not have to adjudicate. SSR note: A's server render emits the attribute deterministically from the snapshot (rides the existing story); B is a client-side fx (its SSR story is "the server renders A-style or the attribute is absent until hydration" — state it).
4. GUIDE DELTA: 06 rewritten to teach the default + the tradeoff table updated; the troubleshooting row at :156 checked against the ruling.

ADVERSARIAL FOCUS: the per-root argument's CSS reality (option 2's counter), whether declaring a taught default actually helps or just adds prose, and the no-measurement claim.

PROCESS: one designer (both options argued), one adversarial reviewer with a forced verdict, synthesis appended here as a delegated ruling marked operator-overturnable. The mayor implements the guide change from it. No AI attribution.

description:
DESIGN-FIRST (operator, 2026-08-04: careful design work, step by step; THE MAYOR IMPLEMENTS from the spec appended here). The revision prop on controlled elements — guide 04-controlled-inputs.md:159's not-settled row: "Reset law fixed; the attribute name is still open."

STEP ZERO OF THE DESIGN PASS: find the fixed reset law. Grep decisions.md / authoring.md / the studio record for the revision/reset ruling and quote it verbatim in the design doc — the pass designs AROUND a ruled law, it does not re-derive one. If the law turns out to be less fixed than 04 claims, STOP and report the gap (that is a finding, not a licence to invent).

DESIGN QUESTIONS:
1. SEMANTICS TO CONFIRM AGAINST THE LAW: a revision value change resets the field to the model (uncommitted draft discarded) WITHOUT remount. What exactly survives — focus? caret (and to where — start/end/model-length)? selection? The law's own text governs; where it is silent, the design proposes and marks the proposal.
2. SPELLING: the natural candidate under Conventions' reserved namespace is ::h/revision, [unfrozen] like every spelling (the API freeze rides later — the name question in 04's row dissolves into the general freeze rather than needing its own sitting). Confirm no collision in the reserved-key roster.
3. INTERACTIONS, each designed explicitly:
   a. THE IME CARVE-OUT (rf2-digtt, landed): a revision change arriving MID-COMPOSITION — reset immediately (destroying the exchange the carve-out exists to protect) or defer to compositionend like the converge does? The composition-shadow machinery in front/controlled.cljs is the site; the coherent answer likely mirrors the carve-out, but it must be argued, not assumed.
   b. THE CONVERGE PATH: revision-reset vs the in-turn converge ordering; no second flushSync site without naming it (HD-019's addendum audited the existing two).
   c. SSR/HYDRATION: revision is a codec-level prop consumed before emission (never a DOM attribute — verify); server HTML carries the model value; hydration adopts with the defaultValue invariant row extended (the .84 pattern). A revision change during hydration adoption = same deferral question as (a).
   d. HD-028 MEMO: a revision change is a props change — body re-runs; confirm no special-casing needed.
4. REFUSAL EDGES: revision on a non-controlled element (no :value) — silent no-op or loud refusal? (The lane's posture says loud.) Revision value equality semantics (= on any value, the instance-key grammar's lesson about authored data applies).
5. WITNESSES: revision change discards draft + resets to model with focus/caret per the law; unchanged revision never resets; the IME row (mid-composition revision per the designed answer, on the ime_run harness); the hydration row; the refusal row.
6. GUIDE DELTA: 04's not-settled row resolves; the buffered/revision LADDER stays post-v0 (charter) — this bead is the single revision prop only, not the ladder; state the boundary.

ADVERSARIAL FOCUS: the IME interaction (the one place a wrong answer destroys user text), the reset-without-remount claim under React 19.2's actual controlled-input behaviour, and scope creep toward the post-v0 ladder.

Implementation is the mayor's, from the appended spec. Fences: front/controlled.cljs + codec prop handling + witnesses + guide 04. No AI attribution.

DESIGN SYNTHESIS (2026-08-04; design + adversarial review complete; 0 FATAL / 3 MAJOR / 7 MINOR; verdict BUILD WITH THE NAMED REPAIRS). MAYOR-DISPATCHABLE from this comment. Full record: ai/findings/2026-08-04.revision-design.md + revision-attack.md (local-only; this comment is self-sufficient).

THE LAW (found, verified, binding): HD-019 via decisions.md:668-670 carrying D016 — resets fire on EXPLICIT CALLER REVISION, never value equality; a revision may change while the value stays equal; a value change under an unchanged revision continues the draft; the caret may move only when a new revision establishes a new baseline. The attack's law challenge FAILED: an agreeing-field no-op is React's effect-idempotence guard, not a value-equality trigger — D016:40-41 protects equal BASELINE values across revisions, which the design honours.

THE RULED SHAPE:
1. Spelling ::h/revision (:re-frame.hicasso/revision), [unfrozen], exact-keyword match like :& — NEVER slot-claimed. FREEZE FLAG: three reset-ish names now exist (element revision, h/boundary :reset-key remount, D016's ladder :reset-key) — the API freeze must face them together.
2. Semantics: a revision change (CLJS =) re-baselines the field to the model WITHOUT remount — focus and node kept, caret to end-of-model on the carrying commit (platform conduct, D016:225-226 licensed). Equal-but-fresh revision values are inert (= semantics; authored-data rule: a good instance key is a good revision value).
3. Mechanism (verified at react-dom 19.2.0:12537-12541, :20865-20874, :1666-1667): React's own per-commit controlled re-assert off fresh codec props — ZERO new machinery, no keyed re-render, NO third flushSync site (in-turn resets ride the keystroke converge; deferred resets ride the compositionend site; out-of-band resets ride ordinary commits). One invariant row pins the input chain; ADD a textarea row (parallel chain at :20978, unpinned in the design).
4. IME: a mid-composition revision DEFERS to the exchange's close — every shadow-release path (compositionend / non-composing change / BLUR — verified a release path at controlled.cljs:529-533 / unmount) converges to the then-current model; immediate writes re-import the measured abort + SSHSH corruption. ADD a blur-mid-composition witness variant.
5. Refusal: :rf.error/hicasso-revision-not-controlled, per-render, on non-controlled elements (check-ref!'s cost shape). Value-carrying checkbox is accepted-inert — say so plainly, do not overstate refusal coverage.
6. SSR/hydration: the codec strip is server-safe (shared renderer); server HTML carries the model value; the defaultValue invariant row extends.
7. SCOPE: the single prop ONLY. No generation fencing, commit/cancel, controller, acknowledgement, opt-outs — the post-v0 ladder consumes this trigger, never extends the prop.

THE THREE MANDATORY REPAIRS (from the attack; each with its witness):
R1 THE :& DOOR (the big one): the brief as designed matched ::h/revision in convert-entry, which walks the MERGED map — {:& {::h/revision r}} would arm a live reset from the hostile-remainder door (merge-caller denies only #{key ref}+owned, codec.cljs:431/465). FIX: read ::h/revision off the AUTHOR'S OWN pre-merge map in native-element (the :key pattern, codec.cljs:1468/1474), skip-or-refuse it in the walk, and add the witness row asserting {:& {::h/revision r}} NEVER resets (refusal or inert — pick refusal, the lane's posture).
R2 THE OVERCLAIM: strike "the reset cannot be lost" — on an accepting field the post-bump composition echo (including the commit's own final input) overwrites the reset's model write and can resurrect discarded text through the draft echo. The witness row for reset-during-composition pins the ACTUAL conduct at the close (field = the model as of the echo, stated honestly), not the overclaim.
R3 MID-ADOPTION: the "lands on the first post-adoption commit on the server's node" claim has no source cite — DEMOTE to witness-gated intent. Its row RUNS FIRST in the hydration suite; pre-committed fallback if React deopts (server-node loss observed): the reset defers past adoption through the same deferral shape as IME, and the row pins that instead. Never ship the claim unpinned.

WITNESSES: the design's ten rows + R1's :& row + R2's honest composition-close row + R3's gated adoption row (first) + the textarea chain row + the blur-mid-composition variant. Bench lane; ime_run.cjs for the composition rows; the hydration rows on the .84 harness.

title: DESIGN: the Reagent [:>] migration codemod — spec via design+adversarial pass after the [:>] contract lands; mayor implements
description:
DESIGN-FIRST (operator, 2026-08-04: careful design work, step by step; THE MAYOR IMPLEMENTS from the spec appended here). The Reagent migration codemod — guide 05-interop.md:164 + :286: "A codemod is planned and not built."

DEPENDENCY: the [:>] programme (rf2-2rtt6.103) — its migration-fidelity designer is drafting the CODEMOD CONTRACT (what [:>] must guarantee so a mechanical [:> X ...] -> defhost rewrite is always behaviour-preserving). This design pass runs AFTER that synthesis lands and consumes the contract as its ground truth.

DESIGN QUESTIONS:
1. INPUT DIALECT: Reagent [:> Component ...] sites. Survey what else migrating code actually carries — r/adapt-react-class values in head position, reactify/adapt round-trips — and rule each in (rewritable), out (left with a named report line), or [:>]-preserved (now legal in Hicasso, so "leave as [:>]" is a valid output for sites the rewrite cannot make behaviour-preserving; the codemod's job narrows to executing "declare what you use twice").
2. OUTPUT SHAPE: ONE defhost declaration per distinct component (dedupe across N sites), hoisted to namespace level; the minted declaration's naming convention; what happens to per-site prop differences (the declaration carries policy — if two sites need different policies, that is a report line, not a guess).
3. NON-MECHANICAL SITES: dynamic component expressions, computed props spreads, children with Reagent-specific forms — each class enumerated with its disposition (rewrite / preserve-as-[:>] / report). The codemod NEVER silently changes behaviour; the contract from .103 defines "behaviour-preserving" and every site outside it is reported, not rewritten.
4. RESIDENCE + TOOLING: where it lives (tools/ vs scripts/ — it is dev tooling operating on consumer source; check how existing tools are packaged and the bundle-isolation law: nothing in implementation/ requires tools/); rewrite-clj (or equivalent) as the parsing substrate — verify what the repo already depends on before adding a dependency; CLI shape (paths in, diff/report out); idempotence (running twice = no-op).
5. WITNESSES: a golden-file corpus — input namespace -> expected output + expected report — covering the rewrite, the dedupe, each preserve class, each report class, and idempotence. The corpus IS the spec.
6. MIGRATION DOCS DELTA: guide 05:164/:286 + the migration guide tree (migration/from-re-frame-v1/ is hot-zone README territory — check whether the codemod belongs in its docs and flag sequencing if so).

ADVERSARIAL FOCUS: silent behaviour change (the only fatal class), the dedupe-vs-policy-divergence edge, and scope creep (the codemod must not become a general Reagent migrator — [:>] sites only).

Implementation is the mayor's, from the appended spec. No AI attribution.
notes:
MAYOR 2026-08-07: design landed as PR #7646 (docs/design/hicasso/studio/reagent-codemod-against-the-landed-escape.md, 700 lines). NOT closing this bead — the design is for acceptance, and two items came back to me.

THE KEY-SLOT RECOMMENDATION, and I am ACCEPTING the design's reading. The sibling page includes the 'key' slot in the named-value rewrite; the design re-derived it against landed code and found the sense INVERTS — :foo and "foo" as sibling keys COLLIDED under Reagent and are DISTINCT under Hicasso, so preserving Reagent's behaviour would restore the very collision rf2-vrvv9 was filed to remove. Not rewriting costs one remount. A remount is visible, cheap and self-correcting; a restored key collision is silent and was already ruled a defect. EXCLUDE the key slot from the named-value rewrite, as the design recommends. If Mike overturns this, the design states both readings and reverts cleanly.

TWO FOLLOW-ONS FILED, both outside the design's fence: the .cljc extraction of the slot rule (the codemod reimplements prop-name on the JVM and nothing pins it equal to the codec — a silent-divergence class, and a precondition for SHIPPING the codemod though not for accepting this design), and the donor-side M4 contract row (nothing asserts Reagent 2.0.1's answers, which every proof sketch rests on).

OUTSTANDING FOR ME: docs/design/hicasso/studio/README.md has no Pages entry for the new page. It is held by unmerged PR #7644, so the entry is sequenced behind that merge.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7646 (2026-08-07). CORRECTNESS: two rewrite classes currently violate the page's own behaviour-preservation law. (1) W4 rewrites `(r/partial f a …)` directly to `(fn [& args] (apply f a … args))`. In Reagent 2.0.1 the callee and bound-argument forms are evaluated during the render, `make-partial-fn` captures those values, and `convert-prop-value`'s fresh wrapper invokes the captured PartialFn. The proposed output instead evaluates every nontrivial `f`/`a` form on each later callback invocation. A common `(r/partial handler @state)` therefore changes from render-time snapshot semantics to call-time state, and effects/errors can move or repeat. Generate a hygienic `let` that captures the callee and every bound arg once at the prop-expression site before minting the fresh fn (or refuse non-atomic arguments), then pin a deref/effectful bound-argument case; return transparency alone is insufficient. (2) W2 does not detect two literal map keys that `cached-prop-name` maps to the same JS property, e.g. `:foo-bar` plus `:fooBar`, or `:class` plus `:className`. Reagent's `kv-conv` wrote one JS slot with an iteration-order winner, but respelling both source keys produces a duplicate Clojure map key (unreadable) or cannot preserve the donor winner. Add a normalized-key-collision refusal before rewriting a map and pin keyword/keyword plus seeded-rename collisions. COMPLETENESS: section 10.3 also calls rf2-2rtt6.134 an open door-side question even though it was closed at 2026-08-06T06:20:16Z with the explicit LEAVE-IT ruling; record that settled result instead of suggesting it may land. The premise check, refusal taxonomy, report, idempotence goal, key-slot decision, and separately owned slot-rule/donor-contract work are otherwise coherent. `check_doc_slugs.py` and commit diff-check pass. This in-progress design/implementation Bead is the exact owner; no duplicate Bead was created.
DELEGATED RATIFICATION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-07, operator-overturnable). Mike directed a per-dossier review agent to weigh the dossier + an independent Codex inspection and decide; this note records that decision and folds the review's analysis in so nothing is lost (the dossier file is deleted after this note).

BOTH DELEGATED RULINGS STAND. (1) FIXER-FIRST, dispatched after rf2-2rtt6.103's [:>] implementation merges — the silent-vs-loud asymmetry holds ("a silent-failure protection never queues behind an ergonomics win"); the hoister stays DEMAND-GATED: build it only when a real migrator reports the manual declarations as the pain. (2) THE KEY-SLOT EXCLUSION stands — :foo and "foo" sibling keys COLLIDED under Reagent, are DISTINCT under Hicasso; rewriting would restore the defect rf2-vrvv9 removed. Both re-derived independently by Codex from Reagent 2.0.1 source (convert-prop-value applies `name` to named prop values; make-partial-fn stores construction-time values) and React 19.2 (createElement coerces keys by string concatenation, so a CLJS keyword key becomes ":foo" with the colon). The overturn window is closed by this ratification; Mike can still overturn either ruling.

RATIFIED AS ORDERING AND POLICY, NOT AS IMPLEMENTATION-READY. Two independently verified rewrite defects in the landed design become ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA for the fixer implementation (they strengthen fixer-first — both live entirely in the fixer):

(A) W4 MUST CAPTURE AT PROP-EVALUATION TIME. The design's stated rewrite (reagent-codemod-against-the-landed-escape.md:154) is `(fn [& args] (apply f a ... args))`, which re-evaluates every nontrivial callee/argument form on EACH callback invocation; Reagent's make-partial-fn evaluated them ONCE at construction. Verified against the design text this pass. Required shape: a hygienic `let` capturing the callee and every bound argument once, left-to-right, before minting the wrapper. Witness pins: a dereferenced-snapshot case and an effect-count/ordering case.

(B) W2 MUST REFUSE NORMALIZED-KEY COLLISIONS. Reagent's kv-conv writes each nested-map key under cached-prop-name, so :foo-bar/:fooBar, :class/:className, :foo-bar/"fooBar" siblings each collapse to ONE JS property with an iteration-order winner. Respelling both sources either mints a duplicate literal map key or picks a winner the rewrite cannot generally preserve. Verified: the design's W2 (:152, sec 4.2, sec 9.1) has no injectivity guard. Required shape: before rewriting any nested literal map, require the normalized names to be injective; otherwise refuse the WHOLE map with a report line naming every colliding source key (the design's own report-not-rewrite idiom). Witness pins: an ordinary camel-case collision, a seeded rename, a keyword/string collision.

(C) KEY-SLOT REPORT ENTRY. The exclusion is ratified, but the counter-cost is slightly understated: a changed key resets the subtree's React state on live reconciliation, which can be more than a cosmetic remount. The fixer's report must carry a dedicated entry per key-slot site: exact compatibility would require an explicit string key and would restore the collision risk; a state-sensitive migrator makes that exceptional choice manually.

DEMAND EVIDENCE (2026-08-07 corpus scan, tools/machines-viz/src, the only application-shaped [:>] corpus in-repo): 15 executable [:>] forms over 7 component expressions; a namespace-level hoist would yield 8 declarations (Handle appears in two namespaces); NONE of the 15 triggers a text-changing fixer rewrite (their nested {:opacity 0} maps are naming fixpoints; no metadata keys, literal named prop values, r/partial values, inline adapt-react-class heads, or string heads). This is evidence the hoist has some ergonomic value and NO urgency — it lowers confidence in demand and supports the demand gate.

STANDING RIDER UNCHANGED: the ~6-8 door-side codemod-contract-* rows remain the only executed evidence the tool is correct — "Not optional, not deferrable." The two follow-ons stay as filed: rf2-ani6y (.cljc slot-rule extraction — a SHIPPING precondition, not an acceptance one) and rf2-d2mwk (donor-side M4 row pinning Reagent 2.0.1's answers, which every proof sketch rests on).

External references from the review, for the implementation worker: Reagent v2.0.1 src/reagent/impl/template.cljs (convert-prop-value, kv-conv, cached-prop-name) and src/reagent/impl/util.cljs (make-partial-fn/PartialFn); React v19.2.0 packages/react/src/jsx/ReactJSXElement.js (key coercion); react.dev rules-of-keys and preserving-and-resetting-state. In-repo: front/codec.cljs (prop-name, host-prop-value, host-entry, raw-element, vec->element), codec_cljs_test.cljs (conversion-parity-with-the-door-on-one-prop-corpus — proves [:>]/defhost share the Hicasso walk, NOT donor agreement), implementation/shadow-cljs.edn (Reagent 2.0.1 pin).

comments.text:
DESIGN SYNTHESIS (2026-08-04; design + adversarial review complete; 2 FATAL / 5 MAJOR / 7 MINOR; verdict BUILD WITH THE NAMED REPAIRS — both fatals are one root error, repaired inside the fence). MAYOR-DISPATCHABLE from this comment, SEQUENCED AFTER rf2-2rtt6.103's implementation MERGES (migrated output preserves [:>] sites, which must exist at runtime). Full record: ai/findings/2026-08-04.codemod-design.md + codemod-attack.md (local-only; this comment is self-sufficient).

THE TOOL: migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod/ — the exact sibling precedent shape (migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/: standalone deps.edn, rewrite-clj 1.1.49 already a repo dependency, cognitect :test, clojure -M:run CLI, whole-file writes, parse failure = skip file + report). Zero public library concepts. The corpus IS the spec: corpus/<case>/{input.cljs, expected.cljs, report.edn, post-report.edn}, ~40 cases after repairs, one JVM harness deftest asserting every case + IDEMPOTENCE (rewrite∘rewrite = rewrite byte-for-byte + report stability).

THE ONE GOVERNING LAW (the root-error repair, F1): SITE-LOCAL REWRITES APPLY AT EVERY [:>] SITE — collected-and-hoisted OR preserved-as-[:>] alike. The four rewrites are properties of the CROSSING, not the head: (1) ^{:key k} metadata -> :key in props (NO Hicasso path reads metadata — verified; unrewritten = dead keys); (2) nested kebab :style literals -> the shallow-door-safe spelling (unrewritten at a preserved site = silently unstyled); (3) literal :class collections -> the ruled spelling (else "a,b" strings); (4) r/partial and other non-fn IFn LITERALS at props -> plain fn-wrap, or report where non-literal (the door's IFn refusal is [:>]'s to land per .103; the codemod's write-time wrap/report is its OWN net and stands regardless). Plus the guards: vector/key-map literals at event props on STRING-TAG rewrites are the inert->live fatal class — REPORT, never rewrite silently; dangerouslySetInnerHTML at any rewritten site -> report (Reagent deleted it, template.cljs:131-135; both Hicasso paths resurrect it).

INPUT DIALECT (verified against reagent 2.0.1): IN — [:>] sites; adapt-react-class def-site (renamed-preserving defhost) AND inline-head; string tags (MANDATORY rewrite to native tags — the ruled [:>] refuses strings; R1/R3 conduct equivalence verified clean: the converge door, deep-camel boundary, class-names, fn-identity, custom elements all match the donor); ^{:key} metadata. PRESERVED as [:>] + report: dynamic heads, reactify/create-class heads. REPORTED only: :r> (raw JS props unhoistable), :f> (out of scope), r/as-element islands inside rewritten sites, computed props maps (map?-at-index-1 undecidable for non-literals — report-only, coverage capped honestly).

F2 REPAIR (adapt-react-class def-site): a def-site rewrite changes every call site's conversion regime (deep->shallow, live keys->dead) — SAME-FILE call sites of a rewritten def become collected sites (the site-local rewrites apply there); CROSS-NAMESPACE exposure gets a named report line, never silence.

M1+M2 REPAIR (the hoist gate): the sibling's shadowing analysis does NOT transfer (wrong question, rosters missing defn params + with-let — as specified it would hoist the FLAGSHIP ruled use case, (defn row [component] [:> component ...]), into a load-time mint-host! nil refusal). The gate is: ANCESTRY-WALK analysis with POSITIVE VAR EVIDENCE (hoist only heads resolving to a var) + the TEXTUAL-ORDER precondition (the component's def textually precedes the minted defhost's placement — defhost evaluates its component at ns-load, so declare-then-def inputs PRESERVE + report).

DEDUPE + NS SURGERY: one (h/defhost kebab-name X {}) per distinct component EXPRESSION per namespace, placed before first use, reusing pre-existing declarations; collision chain -host suffix -> report+skip (verified non-shadowing). NS injector is the NARROW v1: append to the first :require clause, recognized ns-form shapes only; anything else (reader conditionals, exotic forms) = skip the HOISTS + report, while the require-free site-local rewrites STILL APPLY (a skipped injection never suppresses them).

M4 REPAIR (the equivalence witness): the one fixture-pair witness covers the host walk only — add ~6-8 named codemod-contract rows in the bench lane (door-side, part of THIS bead's PR; witnesses of existing behaviour, not door code) pinning the NATIVE-walk equivalence the string-tag rewrite relies on (same props through Reagent's [:> "input"] conduct vs Hicasso's native [:input]: converge, class, style, fn-identity rows). WEAK-POINT 2 DECLARED, not engineered around: the equivalence theorem is inherited from the one-shared-walk fact — door drift (.119, .104-class changes) invalidates the contract without failing a codemod test; the contract rows are the tripwire, and .119's resolution should land before or with this tool.

REPORT: first-class — suggested :callbacks declarations (the position-table vocabulary as STATIC-ANALYSIS language only, never runtime semantics), computed-props sites, preserved dynamic heads (WITH the warning that Reagent-only literals at those sites were rewritten per the governing law — the report explains what changed and what could not), cross-ns adapt exposure, skipped ns-surgery. Missed sites fail loudly at the doors' own refusals (the runtime net).

DOCS: guide bead rf2-2rtt6.112 (already filed, deps this bead) teaches it after the implementation PR MERGES; the migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md question is flagged there (hot-zone, mayor sequences). No AI attribution.
