title: DESIGN: for-binding key sugar — build-or-rule-out via design+adversarial pass; mayor implements if ruled in
description:
DESIGN-FIRST (operator, 2026-08-04: careful design work, step by step; THE MAYOR IMPLEMENTS from the spec appended here). Guide 02:66: "Sugar that would derive the key from a for binding is not yet — you write :key yourself."

THE HONEST QUESTION THIS PASS MUST ANSWER BEFORE ANY CODE: is a keying sugar worth a public concept? The design pass is REQUIRED to allow the verdict "no — writing :key is the right permanent answer" and to argue it against K5 if that is where the evidence lands. If the verdict is do-not-build, the bead closes as ruled-out (operator-overturnable) with the guide taught accordingly; the operator is surfaced the recommendation either way.

DESIGN QUESTIONS:
1. MECHANISM: the codec cannot see a for binding (bodies are ordinary Clojure; for evaluates before the walk). Price the options: (a) an h/for macro — a NEW PUBLIC FORM (K5 cost; the collector grammar currently has ~zero control forms and that absence is a marketed virtue); (b) defview-macro analysis rewriting for forms (macro-magic on user code — check the record's "the macro is not a compiler" line near HD-016/lang for whether this is fenced); (c) nothing — status quo taught as permanent.
2. THE AUTO-IDENTITY PRECEDENT, argued honestly both ways: the 2026-08-04 instance-key adversarial wave FATALLY killed ordinal/structural identity for STATE (silent state teleport). React keys are reconciliation identity only — a wrong/absent key costs a remount, visible and recoverable. So the kill does not transfer automatically; but the same instability arguments (which binding value? conditional siblings?) apply to what the sugar picks. The sugar would derive from the BINDING VALUE the author already iterates — is that always the right :key (multi-binding fors, destructuring, index bindings)?
3. SCOPE IF BUILT: exactly (h/for [x xs] [child {...}]) single-binding with the binding value as :key? What refuses (multi-binding, non-boundary bodies, non-sequential)?
4. K5 ACCOUNTING + guide delta either way (if not built: 02:66's "not yet" becomes a taught permanent with the reason).

title: DESIGN: the Hicasso-minted missing-key warning — spec via design+adversarial pass; mayor implements
description:
DESIGN-FIRST (operator, 2026-08-04: careful design work, step by step; THE MAYOR IMPLEMENTS). A compact design + adversarial pass runs before any code; the synthesized spec will be APPENDED to this bead; do not dispatch implementation until it is present.

THE FEATURE: the Hicasso-minted missing-key warning. Guide 02-views-and-reads.md:64-66 promises it: "a bare seq of boundary children needs keys... you get React's own key warning in development; a Hicasso-minted warning is planned but not built." Its reason to exist: React's warning names a component stack; the Hicasso warning can name the AUTHORING-level facts — the defview head and the child position — which is what a Hicasso author actually greps for.

DESIGN QUESTIONS (the pass's inventory; verify all sites against the tree):
1. SITE + MECHANISM: the codec's seq-expansion region (front/codec.cljs ~:1420-1431 expand-seq; nil law nearby) — where exactly does the check live so it sees "seq of boundary children" and the enclosing view head? Does the walk carry the head name at that point (dev builds), or does that need threading?
2. DEV-ONLY GUARANTEE: goog.DEBUG gating with a witness that :advanced carries no trace (string-absence or DCE check per the lane's idiom). The hot path must pay ZERO in production — and near-zero in dev (the check runs per seq expansion; price it).
3. FIRE SEMANTICS: once-per-site vs per-render (a 60fps list must not spam); cheapest dedupe shape; what "site" means (view head + code position?).
4. RELATIONSHIP TO REACT'S OWN WARNING: both fire in dev? State the relationship in the docstring; do NOT suppress React's (suppression machinery = over-engineering). Verify what React 19.2's warning actually says for this shape so the two are visibly complementary, not duplicate noise.
5. SCOPE: exactly the guide's case — bare seqs of BOUNDARY children. Keyed seqs silent; native-tag children silent; the codec's nil law respected. Does [:<>] fragment content count? Does the [:>] crossing's children (per the in-flight rf2-2rtt6.103 design) count?
6. GUIDE DELTA: 02:64-66 true-up (the warning built; the for-binding key SUGAR remains rf2-2rtt6.105's separate question — do not conflate).

ADVERSARIAL FOCUS: false positives (keyed-but-computed keys, seqs of mixed children, presence-retained children), the dev-cost claim, and whether the warning's wording will age (it names [unfrozen] spellings).

FENCES for the eventual implementation: front/codec.cljs + test + guide 02 only; coordinate on codec.cljs with rf2-2rtt6.103's implementation. Gates: hicasso compile + DOM suite + fast-PR spine, foreground. No AI attribution.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7567 (merged 2026-08-05T18:37:02Z, 589853f53df17bb285dafcc8001b9501be870464) — REOPEN THE EXACT MINTED-KEY-WARNING OWNER, NOT A DUPLICATE. The missing-key path and CLJS collection-key warning are well covered, but check-member-key! silently drops every non-nil key that is neither plain-key? nor coll?. That includes a foreign JS entity object: React coerces distinct objects to the same [object Object] key, exactly the content/identity collision this PR's :rf.warning/hicasso-entity-key exists to explain. The code even avoids printing foreign/cyclic values in key-shape, but key-shape is never reached for them. The same hole covers other non-plain shapes (boolean, symbol, function, UUID-like object) unless they are explicitly ruled safe. Make the predicate total: every non-nil value rejected by plain-key? must either be deliberately classified safe or warn via a non-printing shape label; pin a JS-object collision and a cyclic object without allowing the diagnostic itself to throw. No new Bead.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7619 (merged 2026-08-06T12:53:35Z, 057ea288d2f78ac42b8231ff62fa96d8fffdb0d3) — REOPEN THIS EXACT TOTAL-CLASSIFICATION OWNER, NOT A DUPLICATE. The foreign/cyclic object hole is repaired and the 58-test/353-assertion focused suite is green, but the new total classifier produces a false positive for JavaScript BigInt keys. `plain-key?` admits only string/number/keyword; `stable-object-key?` admits UUID/symbol; therefore `42n` reaches `key-shape`'s `:else`, is mislabeled "a foreign object", and emits :rf.warning/hicasso-entity-key. Against this repo's vendored React 19.2, `React.createElement("div", {key: BigInt(42)}).key` is the string "42": BigInt is immutable, content-stable, and has the same identity semantics as an admitted number. BigInt is also already used in implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/fingerprint.cljc, so this is not a purely hypothetical host value. Admit BigInt on the safe path (without charging the keyed steady-state), and pin two distinct BigInt keys as silent/distinct plus the non-printing classification invariant. Also correct the prior close reason on re-close: it says React does NOT warn colliding foreign-object keys, while this PR correctly verified that React DOES warn after coercion; React's silence applies to distinct content-derived coercions. Authored/landed blobs match; five GitHub workflows, focused compile/test, Hicasso compile gate, and diff-check all pass. No new Bead.
CORRECTION TO MY BRIEF, and the ruling survives it (2026-08-06). I told the worker 'React does NOT warn on the object-key case'. That is wrong as stated, and it checked React 19.2 source rather than taking it: createElement runs key = '' + config.key (react.development.js:957/:1018), so by the time react-dom's warnOnInvalidKey reaches its 'if ("string" !== typeof key) break' guard the key is ALREADY A STRING — and React emits 'Encountered two children with the same key, [object Object]' whenever two or more COLLIDE.

THE DISTINCTION I MISSED IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: React warns on COLLISION, not on INSTABILITY. A key whose coercion is content-derived and DISTINCT per member — js/Date, a JS array, a CLJS map — collides with nothing, so React never says a word, and the row SILENTLY REMOUNTS on the next edit. That silent half is the larger half, and it is the hazard :rf.warning/hicasso-entity-key already existed for; the foreign object was simply its unhandled case.

AND THE COMPARISON WITH rf2-2rtt6.134 STILL HOLDS, for a reason I stated imprecisely. I justified .134's LEAVE IT partly on 'React already warns'. The worker put it better: .134 was a COST ruling — ~150 ns/member charged to the hot walk — and here THE COST IS ZERO, so 'React also speaks' does not buy silence the way it did there. Both new arms sit INSIDE the cond, reached only by a member already boundary-headed AND already carrying a non-plain :key; nil? is still the first arm. One population got CHEAPER: coll?, the dearest predicate there, moved off the walk into key-shape, so a legitimate UUID-keyed list no longer pays it per member per render.

THE MUTATION I VALUE MOST IS M2 — deleting the safe arm made a UUID key and a symbol key BOTH warn. That is the false positive that would have made the guard worse than the silence, and it is the direction a fix like this is least likely to test.
close_reason: ALREADY LANDED — verified in tree 2026-08-07 before dispatch, per the standing rule to grep for the alleged missing work first. The minted key warning is implemented AND witnessed on main: front/codec.cljs:1390 carries the section header 'The minted key warnings — DEVELOPMENT ONLY (rf2-2rtt6.104)' and mints [:rf.warning/hicasso-missing-key] at :1544; arm1/keywarn_dom_cljs_test.cljs and keywarn_elision_run.cjs are its witnesses. The bead asked for a design pass so the mayor could implement; both halves shipped. Closing as verified-duplicate of work already on main rather than dispatching a design for something that exists. (Related and still live: rf2-y7zql narrows a guide sentence that UNDERSTATES what this warning covers — that is a prose fix, not a gap in the warning.)

title: the fast-PR spine is not a superset of the required checks, and nothing says which it omits
description:
THE PROBLEM, observed three times on 2026-08-04 and each time costing a round trip. A worker runs scripts/test-fast-pr.sh, sees PASS fast PR spine, opens its PR, and CI goes red on a REQUIRED check the spine never ran. Nothing tells the worker which required checks the spine does not cover, so each discovers a different one the hard way and the next worker rediscovers it.

THE THREE FOUND SO FAR, all real reds after a green spine:

1. clj-kondo (fail on errors, warnings informational) -- lint.yml. Fired on a single error, mount.cljs:130 "Expected: array, received: function" (an aset on a function; unchecked-set is the arm's idiom). Compounding trap: the locally installed clj-kondo is 2025.10.23 while CI pins 2026.04.15; the local build reports 0 on the line CI fails and 10 DIFFERENT errors CI does not. A local clj-kondo pass proves nothing -- the pinned binary must be fetched.

2. The chained JS harness gate -- npm run test:script-policy && npm run test:script-helpers. A worker ran only the second half, reported it green, and a red got through. The two are one gate in CI and must be run chained.

3. The EP-0036 donor-boundary check -- reports under the name "JVM freehand (clojure -M:test)" and IS NOT A TEST. It is a git grep for re-frame\.ui / re_frame/ui / re-frame2-ui over implementation/freehand. It fired on a DOCSTRING naming re-frame.ui/hydrate-root in prose. The gate cannot distinguish prose from a require, and that is correct design for a boundary rule -- a cleverer grep would eventually admit a real dependency.

WHAT IS WANTED, and it should be done once properly rather than accreted: enumerate the REQUIRED checks from .github/workflows/test.yml and lint.yml, compare against what scripts/test-fast-pr.sh actually runs, and publish the difference where a worker will see it. The spine already prints which tiers it skipped by diff classification; the gap is the checks it never runs AT ALL, at any classification.

ACCEPTANCE: a worker who has read the spine's own output can state, without guessing, which required checks remain unrun and how to run each locally (including the clj-kondo version pin). Whether that lives in the spine's output, docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, or TESTING.md is the implementer's call -- but it must be somewhere a DISPATCH BRIEF can cite by path rather than by my re-listing it each time.

DO NOT WEAKEN OR WIDEN ANY GATE. This bead is about VISIBILITY, not coverage. In particular the EP-0036 grep stays exactly as conservative as it is.

CAVEAT ON THE LIST ABOVE: three is what I have tripped over, not a count. The bead's own work is to derive the real set from the workflow files.
notes:
REFINEMENT from the rf2-2rtt6.97 worker, 2026-08-04, and it changes what this bead has to look for.

The EP-0036 donor-boundary check is NOT a job the spine skips. It is a STEP INSIDE a job the spine does run -- test.yml line 2123, the last step of the JVM freehand job, a plain git grep. So the spine's own skipped-tier enumeration CANNOT SEE IT: the tier is not skipped, and the step is not a test.

That makes 'compare required jobs against what the spine runs' insufficient as an approach. The comparison has to reach STEP granularity inside jobs the spine believes it covers, not just job granularity. The worker called this the nastiest of the three found so far for exactly that reason.

Also worth carrying: the check reports under the name 'JVM freehand (clojure -M:test)', so a worker reading a red sees a test-suite name for something that is a grep. Any output this bead produces should name the CHECK, not the job, or the next person will go looking for a failing test that does not exist.
DONE — PR #7485 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7485), branch worker/gatemap-13zre.

MECHANISED, not prose. scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py derives the whole list at print time; the spine appends the digest to its own PASS line (--brief), TESTING.md carries the citable section, dispatch-prompt-template.md tells briefs to cite one path.

THE BEAD'S FRAMING WAS INCOMPLETE IN TWO PLACES, both found by the derivation:

1. THERE ARE THREE REQUIRED STATUS CONTEXTS, NOT TWO. The bead named test.yml and lint.yml. docs.yml posts 'Docs required' via its own docs-required aggregator, and its 'build' job carries four residue gates (check_failure_corpus_residue, check_inject_cofx_residue, check_retired_composition_vocab, check_retired_image_keys) plus the playground bundle-drift and esbuild-bootstrap checks — none of which any spine tier runs.

2. THE CHAINED JS HARNESS GATE (item 2) IS NOT A SPINE GAP. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh line 821 already runs 'npm run test:script-policy && npm run test:script-helpers' chained, exactly as CI does. That red came from a worker running the halves separately, not from anything the spine omits. The report now says so rather than repeating it as a hole.

THE ITEM-3 CLASS TURNED OUT TO HAVE THREE MEMBERS, not one:
  * the EP-0036 donor grep, last step of jvm-freehand (the known one)
  * 'npm run test:ui-isolation', a step of the cljs job whose node-test build the spine DOES run
  * 17 required 'python scripts/check_*.py' invariant checkers with no local lane at all
The third is much the largest and was invisible to everyone. Filed as rf2-ejm7m (coverage, not visibility — deliberately out of this bead's scope).

HOW THE DERIVATION WORKS, so the next person does not re-list anything: required set from the three aggregators' needs:; gate steps from each job's run: bodies minus anchored whole-body setup shapes; coverage from eleven SPINE_LANES signatures, with the python-checker lane derived from the spine's own source so it needs no maintenance. Local commands are READ FROM THE STEP (no required gate step interpolates a workflow expression), including the clj-kondo pin, read from that job's installer step so a bump cannot leave prose stale.

THE RATCHET: a SPINE_LANES signature that stops matching any required gate step is RED — the spine claims a lane for a check CI renamed, moved or deleted. Runs in the spine's always-on block and in CI's verify-skill-mcp-drift job.

NO GATE'S BEHAVIOUR CHANGED. The EP-0036 grep is untouched.

Gates: spine 0 (every tier armed — spine self-change); clj-kondo AT THE PIN 2026.04.15 exit 0, errors 0, warnings 4534 (the locally installed 2025.10.23 is not the pin — binary fetched from the upstream release); chained JS harness 0; check_doc_slugs 0; gap-map self-test 0; gap-map check 0; check_ci_reproduce_commands 0.

title: hicasso SSR: witness the instance-key payload obligation both ways (green allowlist / red-by-design omission)
description:
SSR WITNESS for the instance-key tier — the payload obligation, proven both ways. Per the 2026-08-04 instance-key synthesis (epic note): the hydration payload policy is mandatory and fail-closed (allowlist -> select-keys, or explicit whole-app-db; absence throws), so the ruled posture is: whole-app-db carries [:ui ...] automatically; AN ALLOWLIST MUST NAME :ui WHENEVER SERVER-SIDE EVENTS WRITE RENDER-AFFECTING INSTANCE STATE; strip it only if the server never writes it. This bead witnesses the obligation in both directions on the SSR lane built by rf2-2rtt6.86/.87.

ROWS:
1. GREEN: a server render whose boot events write reg-state instance state (a default-open panel via [::concern ikey true]) with :ui ON the payload allowlist -> client hydrates with ZERO mismatch, the panel is open pre- and post-adoption, X2-class adoption checks pass on the fixture.
2. RED (the teaching witness): the same page with :ui OMITTED from the allowlist -> the client's first render reads the default, diverges from server HTML, and the run asserts the structured hydration-mismatch error fires (the mismatch machinery is the enforcement; the witness proves the taught obligation is real, not prose). This row EXPECTS the error — it is red-by-design and asserted as such, never a flaky gate.
3. Determinism row: the instance keys in both rows are authored data; double server render byte-identical (rides the existing X1 harness pattern).

DEPS: the h/reg-state implementation bead (sibling) merged; the Node render entry + fixtures (rf2-2rtt6.86) and the spike witness harness (rf2-2rtt6.87) available. Bench lane; fixture-based (the ssr_basic bake pattern); no timing rows; no quiet box needed (structural). Results on this bead + one paragraph appended to the SSR studio page if one exists by then.
notes:
DONE — PR #7480, MERGED as 8602fb5e6e + b78245cbd2 on main. All THREE rows the bead names.

THE PAIR. One page (ssr/instance_key.cljs): reg-state concern ::open? {:default false}, two disclosure panels instance-keyed by :id values out of an AUTHORED roster, boot events [[::seed] [::open? "billing" true]] — a render-affecting write into [:ui ...] performed by a server-side event. Two corpus rows render it; row 2's allowlist is literally row 1's minus :ui, so the server BYTES are identical and the allowlist is the only variable.

MEASURED (RF2_VERBOSE_TESTS=1, real Chromium):
  payload             {:green-keys [:panels :ui], :red-keys [:panels], :green-edn-bytes 208, :red-edn-bytes 137, :html-identical? true}
  render-hash         {:shared "83b865f8"}
  row-1-green         {:mismatches 0, :warnings 0, :panels 2, :open-after? true}
  row-2-red-by-design {:mismatches 1, :warnings 1, :where "re-frame.bench.hicasso.arm1.mount/hydrate-root!", :panels 2, :open-after? false}

ROW 1 GREEN — :ui named. Client frame boots from the payload the server shipped and holds [:ui ::open? "billing"] = true (asserted before anything mounts). Zero :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch, zero complaints on either channel, panel open BEFORE adoption and still open AFTER, that node still carrying the server-node expando, every-server-node? over "*" — X2-class adoption, React reused the markup.

ROW 2 RED-BY-DESIGN — :ui omitted, and this is the point. The client boots WITHOUT the entry (asserted nil), reg-state's sub reads its false default, the first render draws a shut panel where the server says open, and the structured error FIRES: (pos? (count mismatches)), measured 1, each checked for :operation :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch, :where 're-frame.bench.hicasso.arm1.mount/hydrate-root! (tier-discriminated to the DOOR — React's own reconciliation report, not a hash comparison), :recovery :warned-and-replaced, string :error. The uncaught report is STILL there beside it (1 console complaint) — rf2-2rtt6.97's reporter composes, so rf2-mwx08 is NOT softened; :swallow-uncaught? is set at this one site because the error is the row's subject and is asserted on. title: mayor: worktree reaping is keyed on PR state, not worker state, and manufactures false reds
description:
FOUND by the rf2-2rtt6.92 rebase worker, 2026-08-04, and confirmed by the mayor as SELF-INFLICTED.

WHAT HAPPENS. The mayor's hygiene/merge loop reaps a worker worktree once its PR reads MERGED. But a merged PR is the worker's last REPORTED act, not its last act: it may still be running gates. When the tree is removed mid-run the gates do not fail cleanly, they fail LOUDLY AND FALSELY, naming real files:

- the fast-PR spine reported 4 RED namespaces whose stack traces are Module.load reading out/node-test.js from a directory being deleted
- npm run test:cljs died on "Cannot find module 'readline-sync'" -- a package present in the mayor tree throughout
- npm run test:hicasso-compile reported "Missing script" because npm walked up past a deleted implementation/package.json

None of that announces itself as infrastructure. A worker with less discipline would have chased "missing readline-sync" or reported a red that does not exist. Three worktrees were hit in one sweep: rebase-2rtt6-92, spike-2rtt6-87 and ssrnode-2rtt6-86. Nothing was lost because all three PRs had merged, but that was luck, not design.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE ROOT CAUSE IN A SINGLE SESSION, and the first two were already recorded:
1. Reap folded into the merge loop deleted a tree 11 seconds before its spine finished (11 phantom "Cannot find module" failures).
2. A rebase worker was dispatched onto a branch whose original worker was still resolving that same conflict; its .git file was deleted underneath it.
3. This one -- the hygiene sweep, again keyed on PR state rather than worker state.

WHY THE FIRST FIX WAS NOT ENOUGH. After (1) I adopted "reap on the NEXT tick, once quiescent". That is a DELAY, not a CHECK, and a delay does not help a worker whose gates run for fifteen minutes. The tick cadence is roughly eleven minutes; the fast-PR spine alone can exceed that.

THE ACTUAL FIX -- reap on worker state, not PR state or elapsed time:
- Do not reap while any live agent is associated with that bead or branch.
- Cheap proxies when agent state is not visible: mtime on the worktree's out/ or .shadow-cljs/ directories, or a running node/java process whose cwd is inside the tree. A tree touched in the last few minutes is not quiescent.
- When in doubt, LEAVE IT. A stale worktree costs disk. A deleted one costs a false red, a possible spurious "fix", and -- if the worker is mid-rebase -- a hijacked branch.
- Never remove a worktree whose branch has an OPEN PR, regardless of how quiet it looks.

WHAT THE AFFECTED WORKER DID RIGHT, and it is the model: it discarded all three voided exit codes under the killed-gate rule rather than reporting them, and substituted the authoritative evidence -- CI on the exact rebased head, 47 SUCCESS / 36 SKIPPED / 0 failures, whose rollup includes the very per-ns-isolation gate its local run had called red.
notes:
FOURTH INSTANCE, 2026-08-04, WITH THE FIRST FIX ALREADY DEPLOYED — the fix was insufficient and the bead's scope should reflect that.

I replaced 'reap when MERGED' with 'reap when MERGED and idle >= 10 min', reading idleness from the mtime of the worktree's implementation/ directory. It still removed a worktree out from under a running fast-PR spine: the mtime said 34 minutes idle while the rf2-2rtt6.99 worker was mid-run, because a running spine writes to out/, .shadow-cljs/, temp dirs and detached children rather than necessarily touching implementation/ itself.

ALSO: remove-worker-worktree.sh PARTIALLY SUCCEEDED before failing. It disarmed the node_modules link and deregistered the worktree, then hit a Windows file lock on the directory and reported REMOVE_FAILED honestly. The tree was already gutted at that point. A partial reap kills a running gate exactly as a complete one does, so 'the removal failed' is not 'the worker was unaffected'.

SO THE BEAD IS NOT 'key the reap on a better proxy'. Three proxies have now failed: PR state, elapsed time, directory mtime. The remaining honest signals are (a) the owning agent has delivered its completion report, or (b) no process holds a working directory inside the tree. Everything cheaper has been tried and has produced a false red naming real files — four times today, twice in a form mistakable for a genuine regression.
SIXTH REAP-DURING-GATES, AND THE DIRTY-TREE GUARD I ADDED HOURS EARLIER DID NOT CATCH IT (2026-08-05, rf2-vrvv9's worker).

WHAT HAPPENED. I merged PR #7500 on green and the merge loop reaped worker/nskeyword-vrvv9 because the tree was CLEAN. The worker was still running scripts/test-fast-pr.sh. Its spine died on FileNotFoundError for source files vanishing underneath it - first re_frame/elision, then ssr-ring payload.clj - twice, because it started a second run. Minutes later I reaped a worktree called vrvv9-gate as an unowned stray; that was ITS SECOND GATE WORKTREE, also in use. Nothing was lost only because every commit was already pushed.

WHY THE GUARD FAILED. I had just added "reap only when the tree is dirty=0", on the reasoning that a dirty tree is in use. THAT IS TRUE BUT NOT THE CONVERSE. A worker that has committed and pushed everything - exactly the discipline every brief demands - presents a CLEAN tree while running a twenty-minute gate. So the better a worker follows the push-as-you-go rule, the more likely my guard is to destroy its gate run.

THE FULL LIST OF PROXIES THAT HAVE NOW FAILED, all of them plausible when adopted: PR state; elapsed time; worktree directory mtime (read 250 minutes stale on a worker that was committing as I looked); worker shape (zero commits + clean + no PR matches both an abandoned tree and one that started a minute ago); and now CLEANLINESS. Five wrong answers to one question.

THE TWO SIGNALS THAT HAVE NEVER BEEN WRONG: the agent's own completion report, and SendMessage's response shape ("queued for delivery" means alive; "had no active task, resumed from transcript" means it was idle). Both are reads rather than inferences, which is the whole point.

THE RULE, and I am done trying to be cleverer than it: DO NOT REAP A WORKTREE UNTIL ITS OWNING AGENT HAS DELIVERED A COMPLETION REPORT. Not on merge, not on cleanliness, not on quiet. The cost of waiting is a stale directory; the cost of being wrong is a worker's gate run destroyed and a false red that names real files as missing - which has now twice been mistakable for a genuine regression.

AND A SECOND-ORDER TRAP THIS EXPOSED: ONE WORKER IS NOT ONE WORKTREE. This worker created a second worktree for its gate run, and I reaped it as an unowned stray because I did not recognise the name. Before removing any worktree I do not recognise, ask whether a LIVE worker might have created it - the honest default is that an unfamiliar worktree belongs to someone until its agent reports.
DELIVERED, 2026-08-05 — PR #7511, worker/reapguard-k3j2w. NO seventh proxy was
added; the deliverable is narrow, as briefed.

THE MECHANISM IS NOW REPRODUCED ON DEMAND, not inferred. Hold one open file
handle inside a throwaway worktree and run `git worktree remove --force`:

  exit 255, "failed to delete '<wt>': Invalid argument"
  git worktree list  ->  ALREADY GONE (deregistered)
  <wt>/.git          ->  ALREADY DELETED
  <wt>/**            ->  every other file still present

So git deregisters and deletes .git BEFORE it deletes the files, and the note
above ("remove-worker-worktree.sh PARTIALLY SUCCEEDED before failing") was
right about the shape. Two husks were sitting in the worktree parent while this
ran: procpair (full checkout, no .git, unknown to git) and goto-dczpv (emptied
shell). Both left in place — an unfamiliar worktree belongs to someone until
its agent reports.

WHY EVERY SIGNAL POINTED THE WRONG WAY. `git worktree prune` does not clear a
husk (prune drops admin records for directories that VANISHED; here the
opposite happened). `git status --porcelain` inside one FAILS and prints
nothing, which the clean/dirty split read as "tree is CLEAN" and reported as
REMOVE_FAILED "safe to retry once it clears" — and retrying is futile, because
the registered-worktree check refuses the path forever. Verified head-to-head
against main.

THE FIX: REMOVE_PARTIAL=<path> and exit 3. Codes now split on what the caller
should do next — 1 means the worktree is INTACT and the script is still the
right tool, 3 means it is gutted and only a plain directory delete remains.
Reported from both entry points (a removal that fails this way, and a later
call handed a path that is already a husk).

WORSE THAN A BAD MESSAGE, AND THE REASON THIS WAS NOT COSMETIC: a husk was
refused WITH ITS JUNCTION STILL ARMED, while the message recommended `git
worktree prune`. The only remedy left for a husk is `rm -rf` — so the old
output was a loaded gun aimed at the mayor's node_modules. The disarm is now
factored out and runs on the husk path before anything recommends a delete.

TWO PRE-EXISTING WINDOWS DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED, both reproduced against main
before being touched:
1. The .ps1 CRASHED instead of classifying. Under $ErrorActionPreference =
   "Stop" a native command writing to stderr raises a terminating
   NativeCommandError, and neither 2>$null nor 2>&1 suppresses it — so `git
   status` in a husk aborted the script, and the same trap sat under `git
   worktree remove`, the one call guaranteed to write to stderr on the path
   that must be classified rather than crashed on.
2. (Get-UndisposableLines $dirt).Count threw on EVERY dirty tree — PowerShell
   unrolls the returned array, empty arrives as $null, $null.Count is fatal
   under StrictMode. REMOVE_REFUSED_DIRTY therefore died right after listing
   the paths, swallowing the sentence that says whether -ForceDisposable will
   clear the tree. Windows never saw the guidance rf2-p0m6m added.

DOCS: two sentences corrected, no new section. bootstrap.md ended its
identity-vs-name bullet with "the discriminator is freshness, not shape" —
freshness is itself a failed proxy (twice). README.md said to leave cleanup
until the worktree is "verifiably clean" — the sixth failed proxy. A new
bootstrap.md bullet carries the roster of six and the two signals that have
never lied. The method did NOT previously say anything about reaping on worker
state; what it said pointed at proxies that have since failed.

NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: no liveness detection (no process ancestry, no lock
probing, no mtime heuristics) — that is the class that failed six times, and a
script cannot read an agent's report. The canary was NOT made stricter: still a
recursive FILE count as a before/after delta plus immediate entries and
sentinels (103/2933/2 here; note `ls` says 101 and `Get-ChildItem -Force` says
103, both correct — the signature uses the 103 measure, which counts dotfiles).
remove-worker-worktree.sh was not rewritten.

STILL OPEN AND OUT OF FENCE: the reaping rule now written down in
docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md is not enforced anywhere in
.claude/commands/mayor-*.md, which is what the loop actually executes. A script
cannot check agent liveness, so this stays caller discipline — but the hygiene
and merge command bodies should state "do not reap until the owning agent has
reported" rather than leaving it to the method doc. Filed separately.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7511 (merged 2026-08-04T22:49:58Z, b33c9b98da332d378b82d4050843473d9afe1a58) — REOPENED, NOT DUPLICATED. Same-invocation partial removal is correctly detected after git has deregistered the tree, both implementations disarm links first, the Windows native-command and empty-array failures are repaired, the three intended detector fixtures and both self-tests pass, and 16 applicable GitHub checks are green. ONE SAFETY DEFECT remains in the later-invocation path. At remove-worker-worktree.ps1:654-659 and the POSIX twin, every existing unregistered directory for which Test-WorktreeIsIntact/worktree_is_intact is false is declared REMOVE_PARTIAL, has node_modules links disarmed, and is told to use a recursive directory delete. That predicate proves only “not an intact Git worktree”; it cannot distinguish a prior husk from an ordinary project, typo target, or unrelated directory. Reproduced read-only on current main: pass a fresh empty temp directory with -DryRun; the script exits 3 and states it is a destroyed tree whose visible files have no worktree behind them, then recommends Remove-Item -Recurse -Force. Without -DryRun it would also disarm any nested node_modules junction before making that unsupported claim. Preserve automatic exit-3 classification after a removal fails in the same invocation, where provenance is known. For an already-unregistered path, fail closed unless the caller supplies an explicit husk acknowledgement (or another durable provenance fact); add a negative fixture proving an ordinary directory is neither disarmed nor given recursive-delete advice. Do not add liveness heuristics.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7514 (merged 2026-08-04T23:15:10Z, 14bbb42572c3258eb43eca05026556f8f79ee2bd) — UPDATE TO THE ALREADY-REOPENED ROOT OWNER, NOT A SECOND BEAD. The primary rf2-40d9d repair is correct and stays closed: mayor-hygiene now waits for the owning agent's completion report before reaping a worktree, separates branch merge state from worker state, checks sibling commands, and passed 15 applicable GitHub checks. The command also copied #7511's unsupported later-invocation conclusion into its operational instructions: lines 22-24 say REMOVE_PARTIAL/exit 3 proves a husk and therefore an ordinary rm -rf is all that remains. The #7511 audit reproduced that exit 3 on a fresh ordinary directory, because not-an-intact-worktree proves no prior removal. Therefore the rf2-k3j2w fix must co-edit .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md in the same PR: preserve the same-invocation partial-removal guidance, but make an already-unregistered path fail closed or require explicit husk acknowledgement before disarm/delete advice. rf2-40d9d does not need reopening because its reaping-on-report objective is delivered; this is the downstream surface of rf2-k3j2w's exact false-positive defect.
INSTANCES SEVEN AND EIGHT, BOTH IN THE SAME MERGE LOOP, AND THE CAUSE IS THAT I ENCODED THE RULE INSTEAD OF APPLYING IT (2026-08-05).

WHAT HAPPENED. I wrote a merge loop whose reap arm fired on PR state == MERGED. That is PROXY NUMBER ONE - the first of the six that failed today, the one the corrected method doc now names first. Two workers were reaped mid-gate by it within minutes of each other: the walkprune worker lost a spine run to Cannot find module markdown-it, and the clockexit worker lost one to spawned shadow-cljs sub-runs returning EMPTY STDOUT, which its assertions read as (not (str/includes? "" "FAIL in")) - sixteen failures that look exactly like a broken exit-code contract. Both recognised the signature and reported instead of chasing, which is the only reason it cost minutes rather than hours.

THE REAL FAULT IS NOT THE PROXY, IT IS WHERE I PUT IT. I had already learned the rule, written it into the method docs, corrected the command file the loop executes, and stated it to the operator repeatedly. Then I put PR-MERGED into a shell condition and stopped deciding. A rule encoded in a loop is not a rule you are following; it is a rule you have delegated to a predicate that cannot see what you know.

THE STRUCTURAL FIX, applied: REAPING COMES OUT OF THE MERGE LOOP ENTIRELY. Merging and reaping are now separate acts. Reaping happens only as a deliberate step, after I have read an agent's completion report, naming the worktree explicitly. There is no condition to encode, because the signal - a report I have read - is not available to a shell expression at all. That is the whole point of it.

WHY THIS KEEPS RECURRING: the merge loop is the natural place to put cleanup, because a merged PR is the moment a tree LOOKS finished. Every incentive in the loop's structure pushes the reap into it. Resisting that is the discipline, and I failed it twice after documenting it.

COST TO DATE: eight instances, four spine runs destroyed, one red that named real present files as missing and was mistaken for a genuine regression, and roughly ninety minutes of a worker's time hunting a hang that never existed.
MERGING A GREEN PR IS THE SAME HAZARD AS REAPING A CLEAN WORKTREE, AND I HAD NOT CONNECTED THEM (2026-08-05).

WHAT HAPPENED, twice today: I merged #7522 while its worker was still running gates - four commits had not travelled, one carried a map-shape fixture, and main aborted its whole browser suite for an hour. Then I merged #7549 mid-mutation-proof and the reap that followed took the worktree with it. In both cases the PR was 0-fail and 0-pending, which is my entire merge bar.

THE CONNECTION I MISSED: I spent the session learning that a CLEAN WORKTREE does not mean a finished worker, and wrote it into the method, the script and the command file. But 0-FAIL-0-PENDING IS THE SAME KIND OF SIGNAL - it describes the tip, not the worker. A worker mid-mutation-proof has, by construction, a green tree and unpushed intent: it is about to revert a mutation, or add the witness that proves the mutation fires. Merging there captures a snapshot of a proof in progress.

WHY IT USUALLY DOES NOT MATTER, and why that is misleading: most of the time the worker's remaining commits are additive and land in a follow-up PR. Today that was true five or six times and cost nothing. It cost badly exactly twice - once when the untravelled commit was load-bearing, once when the reap that followed the merge killed the verification run.

WHAT I AM NOT CHANGING: merge-promptly stays. It has caught far more than it cost, and holding green PRs for a report would idle the board. #7549's worker recovered by building a FRESH WORKTREE off origin/main with both commits and re-running every gate there - which is the right recovery and cost minutes.

WHAT I AM CHANGING: when a worker is DEMONSTRABLY MID-VERIFICATION - its last report says it is running a mutation matrix, or its worktree shows commits in the last few minutes - I hold the merge for one tick rather than taking the tip. And I never pair a merge with a reap in the same breath: the reap waits for the report regardless.
POSSIBLE INTERMITTENT IN A CORE ORDERING TEST UNDER THE PRODUCTION GATE — first sighting recorded 2026-08-05, NOT yet confirmed as a flake.

WHERE: JVM core under the production gate (-Dre-frame.debug=false), on PR #7546 (rf2-sib23's local-collector pin). Run 31000812164, 2026-08-05T11:20:51Z. Two test-body error lines, so a REAL assertion failure rather than an install or infrastructure fault.

THE ASSERTION, as far as the log lines show: FAIL in (per-... ) with the surrounding text "dispatching t...", "B's :db commit...", "expected: (tr...". A per-frame dispatch and :db commit ordering test.

WHY IT LOOKS LIKE A FLAKE RATHER THAN A DIFF EFFECT: that PR's ENTIRE diff is one file, implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/../pageerror_exit_path.test.cjs - a Node harness test in the bench lane. There is no path by which it reaches a JVM core suite. And main was GREEN on that exact lane across two consecutive runs checked at the same moment (0702449f and 0a0233cd), so it is not a broken main either.

WHAT I DID: re-ran the failed job. That is the correct action ONLY because I first read the log and established two things - the failure is a real assertion, and the diff cannot reach it. A re-run without those two facts is the move that hid this class of thing for two weeks on the Xray nightly.

WHAT THE NEXT PERSON SHOULD DO: if this lane fails again on an unrelated diff, DO NOT re-run it a second time. Two sightings on unrelated diffs is an intermittent in core's ordering under -Dre-frame.debug=false, and it deserves a bead with both run ids and the full assertion text. An ordering test that fails one run in N is exactly the shape that gets re-run until it passes and never gets diagnosed - which is how the static-mode chord scenario survived four nights over two weeks.
INSTANCE NINE, AND THE FAILURE WAS A FALSE CLAIM IN MY OWN REAP STEP (2026-08-05).

I took reaping out of the merge loop precisely so it would run from a list of agents whose reports I had READ. Then I wrote a reap step whose echo said "both agents reported" and included payloadslots-cc7c6, WHOSE REPORT HAD NOT ARRIVED. Its report came minutes later. Its spine was at its last phase, per-ns test isolation, and died on ENOENT reading .shadow-cljs build output; its next cd failed with "directory does not exist".

SO THE STRUCTURAL FIX WORKED AND I DEFEATED IT BY ASSERTION. The separated step is correct; what failed is that I put two names in it and described them as reported when one was a guess. A list built from what I wish were true is no better than the predicate I removed - it is worse, because it LOOKS like the disciplined version.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY HAVE CAUGHT IT: the agent-completion notification is a discrete event I receive. I have one per agent. Before adding a name to a reap list I should be able to point at that notification. If I cannot, the name does not go in. "I think it is done" is exactly the inference the rule exists to forbid, and re-labelling it "reported" does not change what it is.

RUNNING COST: nine reaps of live workers, five destroyed gate runs, three PRs merged out from under a worker mid-verification, one red that named real present files as missing and was mistaken for a regression, and roughly ninety minutes of one worker's time.

THE ONE MITIGATION THAT HAS HELD THROUGHOUT: every brief says that a gate reporting missing files that plainly exist is the signature of this, and to report rather than chase. Every worker hit by it has recognised it within a command or two. The damage has been minutes, not hours, since that line went into the briefs - which is the only reason nine instances did not cost more.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7601 (merged 2026-08-06T06:14:20Z) — UPDATED exact open owner. The later-invocation guard itself is now correctly fail-closed: both platform self-tests pass, the ordinary/tiny/live negatives and real-husk positive are exercised, and the mayor node_modules canary stayed 103 entries / 2933 files. One safety defect remains in the accepted-husk remediation. `scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh:539` prints `rm -rf %s` and the PowerShell sibling at line 515 prints `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $Path`, interpolating the caller-controlled path as executable text without shell quoting or `-LiteralPath`. A valid worktree path containing whitespace is split into multiple targets; shell metacharacters can terminate the delete and execute another command. This matters especially because the later-invocation path deliberately accepts directories outside the repository and tells the operator to copy the command. Keep the fix small: emit an option-terminated, shell-safe literal path for each shell (and quote the printed `--husk` retry command too), or stop emitting a runnable destructive command. Add a self-test path containing whitespace and a metacharacter and pin the exact printed token without executing it. No new removal machinery.
close_reason: SHIPPED in PR #7601 (merged). HALF 1 reproduced on unmodified main against fixtures created seconds earlier OUTSIDE the repo — all three exit 3: a fresh EMPTY directory and a POPULATED directory with real source were both called 'THIS IS A DESTROYED TREE' with rm -rf recommended, and an ordinary directory carrying a node_modules junction had that junction UNLINKED (DISARMED=) before the same recommendation. A destructive script mutating something it had misidentified. A husk is now IDENTIFIED not inferred: --husk plus a kilobyte of content this repository recognises, read out of git's own object database. The detail the fixtures found and reasoning would not: the first cut counted MATCHING FILES, and a throwaway package.json containing {} genuinely matched a blob of ours — a count rule would have accepted an unrelated directory, so the rule is BYTES. HALF 2 was already largely landed by #7514; what was missing was that the dead proxies were named only in bootstrap.md, which the loop does not read — now inline in mayor-hygiene.md with the structural rule that reaping never rides in the merge loop. 7 mutations across both platform siblings. Verified in use immediately after: 7 worktrees reaped and 1 genuine husk (procpair, 8 of 18 tracked files / 128833 bytes) identified and removed, canary 2933/103 unmoved throughout.

comments.text:
RECURRENCE 2026-08-05, rf2-mjfj9 / PR #7548 -- same class, same signature, one day later.

The mayor merged #7548 at 10:37:24Z and hygiene reaped worktree walkprune-mjfj9 while its fast-PR spine was still running. The spine had already passed JVM core (2215 tests / 11527 assertions, 0 failures) and completed the full CLJS :node-test compile (2152 files, 0 warnings) -- a compile that itself requires node_modules, so the tree was intact at that point. It then failed exactly one test, test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test/deliberately-failing-test-exits-nonzero's NEGATIVE CONTROL, whose spawned subprocess died on:

  SHADOW import error ...shadow.js.shim.module$markdown_it.js
  Error: Cannot find module 'markdown-it'

markdown-it is declared in implementation/package.json and was present in the mayor's node_modules throughout -- the identical shape this bead already records for readline-sync. Spine exit 1, entirely false.

TWO THINGS WORTH ADDING TO THE PICTURE.

1. The failure mode is nastier than a plain missing file. It landed on a NEGATIVE CONTROL -- a test asserting that a correct run exits 0. So the reap did not merely red a namespace, it inverted a meta-test about exit codes, whose failure text reads 'the exit code tracks the real result, it is not always non-zero; got status 1'. That is maximally misleading: it looks like the gate's own exit-code contract is broken.

2. The reap itself behaved CORRECTLY where it matters. It unlinked the implementation/node_modules junction before removing the worktree, so the mayor's real node_modules was untouched: re-counted after the event at 2,933 files / 103 top-level, identical to the pre-run baseline. The damage is purely the false red, not data loss. Whatever fix lands should keep that unlink-first ordering.

The worktree directory shell survives at C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/walkprune-mjfj9 (de-registered from git worktree list, .git file gone, junction gone) -- the known Windows file-lock residue, harmless.

Suggests the fix is to gate reaping on the worker having REPORTED, not on PR state -- which is what this bead already says.

title: Story full-gate runner changes can merge without executing the gate
description:
PR #7472 directly changed tools/story/test/story_feature_load.cjs, but its Story/Xray browser gate was skipped. report-changed-surfaces.sh arms story_xray_browser only for tools/{story,xray}/{src,testbeds}/**, excluding tools/story/test/**, and _changed-surfaces.test.cjs explicitly pins story_feature_load.cjs to false.

Even if that output were flipped, the required PR-smoke job runs only test:xray-feature-gate:smoke and test:story-play-scripts. The full test:story-feature-load command—which stages and executes story_feature_load.cjs plus story_browser_scenarios.cjs—is nightly-only. Therefore changes to the coverage matrix, probes, or full browser runners can merge without executing the gate they define. PR #7472's body said CI was the first end-to-end exercise, but CI skipped this job and the PR-smoke command would not have exercised the changed file.

This is distinct from closed rf2-1sd8h, which fixed Story *_dom_cljs_test changes not arming cljs_browser; this gap concerns the Playwright full-gate runner and the command selected by its CI job.
acceptance_criteria:
- Direct changes to tools/story/test/story_feature_load.cjs, tools/story/test/story_browser_scenarios.cjs, and relevant full-gate run/serve orchestrators arm a required PR check that executes npm run test:story-feature-load.
- Ordinary Story/Xray runtime changes retain the cheaper PR-smoke path unless they need the full gate.
- Classifier tests positively cover the direct-runner paths instead of pinning story_feature_load.cjs to false.
- A negative control proves unrelated JVM/unit-test-only changes do not arm the expensive browser job.
close_reason:
PR #7481 — both halves fixed and mutation-proved in both directions.

(a) Classifier: new output story_full_gate, armed by is_story_full_gate_path on the two Playwright spec modules test:story-feature-load loads plus its run/serve orchestration. tools/story/test/story_feature_load.cjs now classifies story_full_gate=true (was every output false).

(b) Job command: .github/workflows/test.yml's story-xray-browser job carries 'npm run test:story-feature-load' as a step gated on story_full_gate; the two PR-smoke steps are gated on story_xray_browser; the job opens for either tier. The job was already in all-required-passed, so the step is required coverage.

Mutation proofs: a-rev (roster neutered) reds 6 named tests; b-rev-1 (command removed) reds 'PR story-xray-browser job runs the FULL feature-load gate, gated on story_full_gate'; b-rev-2 (job condition narrowed + output declaration deleted) reds 2 named tests; c-rev (launcher stop-arm removed) reds the fall-through guard.

Pinned assertions changed deliberately: the story_feature_load.cjs -> false pin swapped its exemplar to a real JVM unit test (the claim was right about the smoke tier, wrong about the file), and the workflow-level pin 'PR job does NOT run the full sweep' — which forbade the fix for half (b) outright — became 'runs it, gated on story_full_gate'. Both explained in the PR body.

Cost: ~3-4 min on the story-xray-browser job, only for PRs touching one of five files. A full-gate-runner-only PR is now CHEAPER than on main (it skips two smoke compiles it cannot affect). Nightly budget unchanged.

PR #7472's demoted owned-by row HOLDS: the gate was run locally to completion twice (exit 0), validateCoverageMatrix accepts the row, it is reported declared-out-of-scope in both phases, and its browser-side owner (story_browser_scenarios.cjs substrate-decorator-and-frame-isolation, asserting both decorator strings) ran green in the same run.

Gates: test-fast-pr.sh 0 (no tier skipped), chained JS harness 0, clj-kondo 2026.04.15 errors:0/warnings:4534, EP-0036 grep clean, _changed-surfaces.test.cjs 289 passed.

Filed rf2-9n2cv: check-story-static.cjs has the identical defect on a sibling nightly-only gate.

title: hicasso SSR: the arm's hydrate door passes no onRecoverableError — a mismatch is an UNCAUGHT pageerror, not a diagnostic
description:
MEASURED by the rf2-2rtt6.87 SSR spike witness while building X2's mutation proof.

THE FINDING. arm1/mount/hydrate-root! calls react-dom-client/hydrateRoot with NO root options, so React's DEFAULT onRecoverableError runs — reportError — and a recoverable hydration mismatch becomes an UNCAUGHT window error. Measured: hydrating the 8-row dogfood screen against 9-row server bytes produced exactly one complaint, and it arrived as 'window.error: Uncaught Error: Hydration failed because the server rendered text didn't match the client'.

WHY IT MATTERS THREE WAYS.
1. The browser lane's runner treats ANY uncaught pageerror as fatal whatever the cljs.test tally says (rf2-mwx08). So a Hicasso row that deliberately or accidentally hydrates mismatched markup REDS THE WHOLE BROWSER GATE with no way to attribute it. rf2-2rtt6.87's mutation proof had to call preventDefault on the error event (open-console-capture!'s :swallow-uncaught?, one call site, documented) to keep the gate honest — that is a workaround at the witness, not a repair at the door.
2. THE TWO SIBLINGS ALREADY DO IT. re-frame.substrate.spine/hydrate-root-options builds an :on-recoverable-error option and emits the :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch diagnostic from it (rf2-qfz65); arm1/host_ssr_dom_cljs_test's own hydrate! passes onRecoverableError explicitly and says why. arm1/mount is the outlier.
3. Spec 011 carries :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch as the framework's own diagnostic. A door that never emits it is a door whose mismatches are invisible to every tool that reads the instrumentation stream.

THE WORK. Give arm1/mount/hydrate-root! the spine's shape: an options map carrying :onRecoverableError that emits the framework diagnostic, gated the way the spine gates it (hydrate-root-options answers nil in production). Then rf2-2rtt6.87's :swallow-uncaught? call site can go — its docstring names this bead as the reason it exists.

NOT A BLOCKER for rf2-2rtt6.87: every X-row published with the door as it stands, and the mutation proof measured the mismatch on the channels the witness watches. This is about what a CONSUMER of the door sees, not about the spike's readings.

title: hicasso SSR: reconcile the server :ssr policy READ with rf2-2rtt6.85's WRITE (slot spelling + nested-host coverage)
description:
rf2-2rtt6.86 landed the SERVER half of `defhost`'s `:ssr` policy — which
rf2-2rtt6.85's own clause 3 hands to the Node-entry bead — while rf2-2rtt6.85
(the OPTION, the mint-time refusal, the client adoption behaviour) had not
landed. Two seams were therefore made ahead of their other half, both isolated
deliberately, and both need one pass once .85 is on main.

1. THE SLOT SPELLING. `ssr/host_policy.cljs` reads the policy off ONE own
property, `host-policy/policy-slot` (currently the string "ssr"), in ONE reader
(`policy-of`). If rf2-2rtt6.85's `mint-host!` stores it under a different
property, this is a one-line change plus a witness that a `defhost … {:ssr …}`
declaration is what the server walk actually reads — which nothing proves today,
because the fallback row stamps the slot by hand.

2. NESTED HOSTS. `host-policy/apply-policy` walks the hiccup the render entry is
HANDED: the root tree and everything reachable through vectors and seqs
(including inside a `for`, witnessed). A host minted inside a boundary BODY is
NOT in that tree — the body runs inside `renderToString` and the codec's own
crossing creates its element, and `front/codec.cljs` is rf2-2rtt6.85's file, not
.86's. The consensus architecture covers that case from the other side:
rf2-2rtt6.85's host shell reads adoption through
`useSyncExternalStore(…, …, (constantly false))`, so under `renderToString`
React takes the server snapshot and the region renders its placeholder without
the walk touching it.

THAT IS AN ARGUMENT, NOT A WITNESS. The work here is a fixture with a
`:client-only` host and a `{:fallback …}` host declared INSIDE a defview body,
asserted on the SERVER HTML through the SSR entry — and then a ruling on whether
two mechanisms for one policy is the right shape or whether one should be
retired in favour of the other.

FILES: `implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/ssr/host_policy.cljs`
+ `ssr/fixtures.cljs` + `ssr/entry_cljs_test.cljs` (bench lane).
notes:
VERIFIED AGAINST #7468 BY rf2-2rtt6.86 (2026-08-04), which sharpens this bead
from "reconcile" to "RETIRE the server walk":

1. THE SLOT SPELLING AGREES. #7468 stores the policy on the minted head under
the own-property "ssr" and reads it back with `codec/host-ssr`
(`(unchecked-get head "ssr")`) — the same property `host-policy/policy-slot`
names and the same read `host-policy/policy-of` performs. No mis-read is
possible in either merge order; a `{:fallback …}` host is never taken for a
`:client-only` one.

2. THE GATE SUPERSEDES THE WALK. #7468 enforces the policy AT THE ELEMENT'S
TYPE: `mint-host-gate!` wraps the foreign component in a gate whose
`useSyncExternalStore(noop, (constantly true), (constantly false))` answers
false under `renderToString`, so the gate renders the pre-walked fallback
element — or nothing — with no walk involved. That mechanism reaches a host
minted inside a boundary BODY, which the walk cannot, and costs no per-request
tree rebuild. #7468 carries its own server witness
(`the-server-render-honours-the-policy`).

3. BOTH MECHANISMS AGREE ON MARKUP, so merging in either order is safe:
`:client-only` renders nothing either way, `{:fallback hic}` renders `hic`
either way, and if both are live the walk simply gets there first.

THE WORK IS THEREFORE: delete
`implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/ssr/host_policy.cljs` and
its call site in `ssr/entry.cljs`; rewrite `ssr/fixtures.cljs`'s two host rows
as real `defhost … {:ssr …}` declarations; keep
`a-host-with-no-declared-policy-renders-nothing` and
`a-host-declaring-a-fallback-renders-the-fallback` asserting exactly what they
assert today (they are mechanism-independent — they read the server HTML); drop
`an-unknown-policy-is-refused-rather-than-rendered`, whose case #7468 refuses at
MINT time instead; and ADD the row neither bead has — a host declared inside a
defview BODY, asserted on the server HTML, which is the case the walk could
never reach and the gate can.

title: docs(hicasso): HD-011 dated addendum — the activated :ssr policy and the gate's cost (from rf2-2rtt6.85)
description:
SEQUENCED OUT OF rf2-2rtt6.85, NOT DROPPED. rf2-2rtt6.85 (defhost's :ssr policy) shipped the code and its fence named 'docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md (HD-011 addendum)' as in-scope for the same PR. The dispatching brief overrode that on sequencing grounds: rf2-2rtt6.83 owns the SSR doc record and was being dispatched in the same wave onto decisions.md, and decisions.md is sequential-never-parallel. The worker followed the brief, edited no docs, and filed this.

THE WORK (docs only): a dated addendum blockquote atop HD-011 (model: the HD-019 IME addendum, commit 0342d3787d), recording:

1. THE ACTIVATED SHAPE. defhost's opts carry :ssr with exactly two values — :client-only (the DEFAULT, applied when :ssr is absent: the host region renders nothing until the client adopts the markup) and {:fallback <hiccup>} (that markup renders there instead). Any other value, an explicit nil, an empty or multi-key fallback map, and any opts key outside #{:callbacks :ssr} are all refused AT THE DECLARATION (:rf.error/hicasso-host-bad-ssr-policy, :rf.error/hicasso-host-unknown-option). The fallback hiccup is walked once at mint, so a fallback that is not hiccup also fails at the declaration.

2. THE MECHANISM, and that it is ONE. Each declaration mints a gate whose single useSyncExternalStore answers false from its SERVER snapshot and true from its client one. That covers the server render (renderToString honours the policy by rendering, so no server walk needs to know about it), hydration's first client pass (same markup as the server, nothing to reconcile) and a fresh createRoot mount (component on the first pass, no placeholder flash).

3. THE COST, WHICH CHANGED A RECORDED PROPERTY. Before this, the door minted no wrapper, no fiber and no hook — the foreign component was the element's own type, and arm1/host_hatch_dom_cljs_test witnessed exactly one useSyncExternalStore on a hosted page. It now mints one gate per declaration, so a crossing costs ONE fiber and ONE hook. HD-020(b)'s <=2-hook BOUNDARY-shell budget is untouched (shell-hook-ledger still declares two; the gate holds no subscription and reads no frame), and the witness was updated to state the new truth rather than deleted. This is the one thing on this bead an operator might want to price rather than merely record.

Also worth a line in HD-020(d), whose 'defhost's SSR-placeholder default is declared policy for later phases, inert in v0' is now false — though rf2-2rtt6.83's HD-020 addendum may already cover it, in which case say so and do not write it twice.

title: RULING PREP: the production server arm — JVM structural walk (default) vs Node sidecar, priced from the spike corpus
description:
RULING PREP — THE PRODUCTION SERVER ARM, PRICED FOR THE P2/GRADUATION SITTING. Paper-only dossier bead; dispatch AFTER the X1-X5 spike witness lands (its corpus is this dossier's arithmetic). DECIDER: Mike, at the SAME P2/HD-013 sitting — one sitting, no separate gate (the 2026-08-04 adversarial reviews killed the two-sitting variant as not decision-grade).

THE QUESTION: which production server arm does Hicasso graduate with?

DEFAULT DIRECTION (to be priced, not presumed): THE JVM STRUCTURAL WALK — a JVM twin of the codec's pure analysis rules emitting the Spec 004B v1 structural tree, folded to HTML by the SHIPPED react-dom-19.2.0-pinned emit-ui-tree, reads resolving via rf/compute-sub against the request snapshot, in-process with ssr-ring (the platform's host; Spec 011's HTTP response contract stays there). Uniquely, this route also co-discharges HD-021(a)'s headless testing door (same structural-render core, two resolvers: snapshot for SSR, override-map for tests). KNOWN RISK ROWS the dossier must price from the spike corpus: (1) the walk's real surface is ~35-40 rule-bearing sites (not "~10 rules"), against a codec that was in its highest-churn phase in early Aug (wait for the walk-attack lane to stabilise before building); (2) the TEXT-SEPARATOR row — emit-ui-tree coalesces text runs (ui_tree.cljc:724-731) while React renders children as authored, so [:div "Count: " n] mismatches by construction; 004B:613 flags it [S1-CONFIRM], 011-owned — this row must be closed in the tree spec/emitter before any JVM HTML meets hydrateRoot; (3) the conformance apparatus (two-sided rules corpus + renderToString-authored parity fixtures) is an eternal maintenance tax re-opened at every react-dom bump — price it honestly.

THE ALTERNATIVE (priced beside it): A NODE SIDECAR behind an EDN render contract (JVM keeps HTTP + the event drain via ssr-ring; Node renders markup per request through the SAME entry the spike shipped). No parity tax ever; costs a second production runtime and an ops surface — and it must NOT be framed as replacing the Ring host (the adversarial review's host-fork finding: Node-native-serving-as-reference-host is rejected on the record).

INPUTS: the spike's baked-fixture corpus + feature census + tolerance probes; the live churn state of the codec lane; the HD-021 headless-door demand (does anything else need it by then); K7/P2 timing. OUTPUT: a no-verdict dossier on the standard bead (rf2-2rtt6.1's advisory-input slots) with both branches priced in beads/weeks, named tripwires for the default, and the recommendation stated — the RULING is the operator's at the sitting.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7488 (merged 2026-08-04T11:29:06Z) — REOPENED. The Node-sidecar topology and B1 estimate assume “the JVM serialises the request's db snapshot plus the root form as EDN” and price an “EDN render contract — snapshot + root form out.” The shipped Node entry instead requires `:hiccup` whose Hicasso root is `[<minted head> {props}]`; that head is a CLJS/JavaScript function created by `defview`, does not exist on the JVM, and is not an EDN value. The dossier's own §6 relies on exactly this fact when explaining why canonical EDN renders every function identically. A viable sidecar needs an application-defined stable root/entry identifier (and serializable arguments) resolved inside the per-app Node bundle, or another explicit cross-host registry; it must also state the portable serialization domain/projection for a snapshot rather than assuming arbitrary app state crosses EDN. Reprice B1/B4/B5 and the compliant-topology arrows around that real contract. While touching the census, reconcile §4's “75 top-level forms” with the same section's measured 77 top-level `def*` forms. No duplicate bead: rf2-2rtt6.88 owns this dossier and its estimates.
Merged-PR audit follow-up for #7552 (2026-08-05). The sidecar correction is real, but the same established fact is not applied symmetrically to Arm A. The amended page proves a Hicasso root head is a CLJS function minted by `defview`, and `arm1/lang.clj` deliberately has no JVM implementation. Nevertheless §1 says “a db snapshot and a root form are both in hand where a JVM walk would run,” and the asymmetry table says Arm A names the root with “a Var the JVM calls in-process, as ssr-ring already does.” No such Hicasso JVM Var/root exists today; `ssr-ring`'s root-view precedent is not a Hicasso view implementation. A structural codec twin still needs an application/root authoring contract: for example, require server-rendered views to be `.cljc` and make `defview` mint/register a JVM structural function, or introduce a stable id plus per-app JVM table analogous to the Node table. State and price that work (or explicitly include it in A1/A6) before the P2 comparison; otherwise the PR raises Arm B for a cross-host root problem while presenting Arm A as already holding the same unavailable root. Keep this on decision owner rf2-2rtt6.88; no implementation bead is warranted before the ruling.
PARKED, not ruled — mayor 2026-08-07, and the park IS the finding.

THE GATE AS WRITTEN CANNOT BE EVALUATED. The advisory offered two formulations of the codec-stabilisation condition and they now DISAGREE: 'the [:>]/.104/.107 wave fully merged' is MET (.103, .104, .107, .134 all closed), while 'two weeks with no rule-bearing codec change' is emphatically UNMET. front/codec.cljs measured today at 2,815 lines / 101 top-level definitions against 2,342 / 89 on 2026-08-06 — +473 lines and +12 definitions in ONE DAY, with the [:>] escape landing this morning. Fifth consecutive tripwire measurement, steepest yet.

WHY NEITHER ARM CAN START ANYWAY. Both advisory positions already agree Arm A must not start now. And the tree cannot start Arm A regardless: no JVM Hicasso root, no JVM emitter of Hicasso semantics, and defhost :ssr :render (landed 2026-08-05) is structurally unreachable from a JVM twin. Arm B would buy a second production runtime and ops surface permanently.

WHAT IS SETTLED AND NEED NOT BE RE-DERIVED: prep complete, audited twice (#7488, #7552). Arm A 5-8.5wk / 6 beads, Arm B 5.5-10wk / 7 beads — the BANDS OVERLAP, so this is not a schedule choice; the durable differences are one runtime vs two and one emitter vs two. SSR speed is OFF THE BAR; neither arm is owed a clock row. Node-as-reference-host is rejected on the record.

THE RULING: neither arm starts before a P2 sitting exists. This forecloses nothing and costs nothing. STOP THE RECURRING CONSOLIDATION AND THE DAILY CHURN RE-MEASUREMENT — six review rounds have produced no new information, and a ruling taken today would be taken against a codec that grew 20% this morning.

UN-DEFER WHEN: a P2 sitting is convened, or an open bead requires HD-021(a)'s headless door (verified: none exists today), which would put real weight on Arm A.
close_reason: RULED by the operator, 2026-08-08, in chat: 'Let's go with arm B.' The production server arm is the Node sidecar — ssr-ring stays the HTTP host, a supervised Node process running the client's own CLJS bundle returns body markup only. Operative first scope: full, non-streaming SSR (renderToString basis); Spec 011 streaming participation requires the recorded vertical-spike + reprice gate first. RULING != START: implementation dispatches only on a P2 GO with SSR in delivery scope, against the five start gates in the final ruling comment (fail-closed envelope; single root registry; state projector with negative fixture; supervised pool with flow control; end-to-end topology witness). If the fork lands adapters-as-success, this ruling stands recorded and nothing builds. Arm A closed off unless the product ever deliberately names a restricted JVM SSR dialect. The [S1-CONFIRM] file-only-if-Arm-A obligation dissolves. Full record: the 2026-08-07 advisory consolidations + the 2026-08-08 ruling comment on this bead.

docs/design/hicasso/README.md and pointed at from draft-guide/10's "Not
settled" row. Appending the pointer to rf2-2rtt6.1 is the mayor's or the
operator's to do.

=== BOTH ARMS PRICED — the headline asymmetries ===

THE FLOOR IS HIGHER THAN THE BEAD TEXT IMPLIES. emit-ui-tree ships and is
final (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/ui_tree.cljc, 1,040 lines; 004B
calls it pure, deterministic to the byte, JVM-runnable, react-dom 19.2.0
pinned four times in source). A JVM interpreted structural walk to the v1
tree ALREADY SHIPS, for Freehand — re-frame.freehand.tree (678) + node.cljc
(1,438) + conversion.cljc (906), reaching emit-ui-tree via emit-static-html
(tree.cljc:632-654) behind the Independence wall, driven by the shipped
v/render-static macro. So the walk arm's back half is a thing to be CALLED,
not built. What has no precedent in this tree is READS: Freehand's JVM walk is
a pure function of its argument, and v/render-static fails a v/sub loud with
:rf.error/view-read-outside-render rather than resolving one.

BOTH ARMS NEED THE SAME NEW SEAM. ssr-ring hard-calls ssr/render-to-string on
hiccup at ring/pipeline.clj:546 — the stock-Reagent tier 004B freezes. Named
so neither arm looks cheaper by having it quietly assumed.

THE SPIKE BUILT THE NODE ARM'S RENDER, NOT ITS TOPOLOGY. ssr-ring is JVM-only
.clj in EVERY file, so the spike's Node entry hand-writes what it cannot
reach: the #__rf_payload script tag (entry.cljs:184-200, with a docstring
obliging byte-identity with shell/payload-script-tag) and the whole page
envelope (entry.cljs:202-231). Its own docstring says "Not a production host";
the driver's serve() disclaims the response accumulator, cookies, redirects
and CRLF fail-fast. THERE IS NO JVM<->NODE CONTRACT IN THE TREE. The
R0-compliant sidecar — JVM host, JVM payload, JVM shell, Node returning a body
string — has not been built and has not been measured. That is the single
largest unmeasured thing in the dossier.

THE CORPUS SPLITS CLEANLY, and this is the reading most likely to be got wrong
at the sitting. X2/X3/X4/X5 are CLIENT-half rows: the hydration door, the
adoption, reactivity-on-React's-schedule, liveness and teardown hold whatever
produced the bytes, so they transfer to BOTH arms unchanged. Only X1 speaks to
a server half, and only Node's.

THE WALK ARM'S LIKELIEST DIVERGENCE IS THE ONE NOTHING CAN SEE. 004B: two
emitters, divergence "detected, not prevented". 011 Hydration-mismatch
detection: React-native adoption deliberately does NOT report attribute-only
mismatches (React documents no guarantee that attribute differences are
patched; neither onRecoverableError nor any production equivalent fires).
Composed: a JVM-table vs react-dom attribute disagreement is invisible at
runtime, so detection must come from the parity corpus in CI or not at all.
The Node arm cannot produce that class — one emitter makes both sides.

THE PARITY TAX, PRICED HONESTLY RATHER THAN RHETORICALLY. The apparatus EXISTS
and RUNS — parity_fixtures.cljc 643 lines / 66 cases, JVM side computed at CLJS
compile time and embedded (no checked-in goldens), emit_ui_tree_cljs_test.cljc
pinning the serialiser's table copies byte-for-byte against re-frame.ui.rules,
and implementation/ui/dev/react-conform-probe.cjs as the tool that talks to a
real react-dom. So the bump tax has a NAMED HOME and is bounded work, which is
cheaper than "eternal maintenance tax" suggests. Less comfortably: that pin
anchors the serialiser to the UI COMPILER's table. A Hicasso twin has no such
anchor and owes a second pinning relationship — new apparatus, not an
extension.

CHURN, MEASURED. front/codec.cljs was CREATED 2026-07-31 and has taken 23
commits in four days: 1 / 6 / 8 / 6 / 2. All semantic (tag shorthand onto the
emitted slot, frame-as-codec-prop, the IME composition shadow, defhost's :ssr
gate). Wider: front/ 3/11/17/19/4 and arm1/ 8/17/17/26/13 over the same days.
A twin started at the beginning of that week would have needed four semantic
amendments in four days. This is the sharpest number on the page and the one
the sitting can act on immediately.

BEADS/WEEKS (ESTIMATES, labelled as such in the page). JVM walk: 6 beads,
5-8.5 weeks (the .cljc twin 1.5-2.5, the read resolver 0.5, intents/controlled/
presence/route-link 1-1.5, the text-separator settlement 0.5-1.5 AND IT MAY
REACH THE SPEC, the parity extension 1-2, the ssr-ring seam + witness 0.5).
Node sidecar: 6 beads, 4-6.5 weeks (EDN render contract 0.5-1, a callable
process with supervision 1-2, the JVM side 0.5-1, the per-app server-bundle
build story 1-1.5, a skew detector 0.5, the end-to-end witness 0.5). THE BANDS
OVERLAP — on build cost these arms are not far apart and the choice is not a
schedule choice. The durable differences are one runtime against two and one
emitter against two, and both are permanent where build cost is paid once.

=== THE TWO INSTRUMENT FACTS ===

1. :rf/render-hash. NOTHING IN THE DOSSIER LEANS ON IT. Three observations for
rf2-2rtt6.91's owner, offered as observations and not rulings: (a) NEITHER ARM
REPAIRS IT — the degeneracy is a client-side fact, and a deep server hash the
client cannot reproduce makes every page a mismatch, which is why rf2-2rtt6.86
declined to invent one; (b) the PRODUCTION call site takes the hash from the
root hiccup BEFORE the render (lifecycle/render-document-hash at
pipeline.clj:543), so the degeneracy reaches production identically whichever
arm renders; (c) SPEC 011 ALREADY HAS A STATED POSTURE — its mismatch section
is tiered by client render-tree representation, and both the compiled tier and
native React-element roots "deliberately carry no such hash", verifying by
React-native adoption through onRecoverableError instead. Hicasso is a React
adapter minting React-element roots. On that reading .91's candidate (c) is not
a concession but 011's own existing answer for Hicasso's tier, and rf2-2rtt6.97
has already landed the door that answer requires.

2. UTF-16 BYTE ACCOUNTING: STILL UNREPAIRED. driver.cjs has exactly ONE commit
in its whole history (9214396f73, its creation). documentBytes is still
document.length (driver.cjs:176-187) and the live log still prints a
".length B" figure (driver.cjs:235-237). NO SIZE FIGURE FROM THAT MANIFEST
APPEARS ANYWHERE IN THE DOSSIER. X1(a)'s 3,101 is used only as an identity
claim, never as a size. The SHA-256 is unaffected (explicit utf8 encoding at
driver.cjs:129).

=== TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE DISPATCHING BRIEF ===

(1) THE TEXT-SEPARATOR CITATION WAS WRONG. ui_tree.cljc:724-731 is
emit-children, a str/join — the serialiser receives children ALREADY coalesced
(its own docstring says so at line 541). Coalescing lives at TREE-BUILD time,
in three independent .cljc implementations of one algorithm:
ui/tree.cljc:110-116, ui/semantic.cljc:208-219, freehand/node.cljc:359-374.
The ROW is real and open — spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:613,
[S1-CONFIRM], 011-owned — and it carries NO BEAD (the merged-PR audit rf2-7uil4
recorded it as "already an explicitly open 011-owned row, not rediscovered
here" and deliberately left it unfiled). A Hicasso JVM twin would need a FOURTH
coalescer: the CLJS codec has none, which is exactly why React's own render is
separator-correct and a structural tree's would not be. AND X1(b) DOES NOT
RESCUE IT — "the comparator skips comment nodes" is a property of
lane/canonical, and React's hydration reconciler is not that comparator; X1(b)
was also judging bytes react-dom/server itself produced. Worse, the existing
parity corpus renders its React side with renderToStaticMarkup
(parity_corpus_cljs_test.cljs:36), which emits no separators — THE GATE THAT
EXISTS CANNOT SEE THIS ROW.

(2) "~35-40 RULE-BEARING SITES" IS CORROBORATED, and the page enumerates the
roster rather than asserting the count. front/codec.cljs: 77 top-level def*
forms, 57 of them defn/defn-; the rule-bearing subset lands at 35-40, rostered
with line ranges (reserved-name? 180-202, parse-tag 241-245, prop-name 274-308,
the one-slot-per-spelling family 405-465, fold-shorthand! 488-524, merge-caller
571-618, check-ref! 624-654, convert-props 656-791, memoize-boundary! 847-945,
mint-host!/declared-ssr/mint-host-gate! 1039-1173, the lazy-seq forcing walk
1201-1414, the emission dispatch 1420-1673, vec->element 1677-1706, as-element
1708-1749, root-element 1751-1770).

=== UNMEASURED, NAMED EXPLICITLY (9 items in the page) ===

No JVM emitter of Hicasso semantics exists, so no parity row does. No
JVM<->Node seam exists, so no sidecar latency, throughput or
snapshot-serialisation figure does. NEITHER ARM HAS A CLOCK ROW AND NEITHER IS
OWED ONE — SSR speed is off the bar by HD-012 and validation.md, so a sitting
asking for a speed comparison is asking for something the programme has ruled
it does not measure. The cost of resolving reads through compute-sub on a real
page (the mechanism and a shared memo both exist — subs.cljc:2183 and
compute-sub-with-memo at :2236 — but the census seven-read archetype has never
been run). The text-separator fixture. The attribute-only class, on either arm.
HD-021(a)'s headless demand — the door is genuinely absent
(draft-guide/08-testing.md says "Not built yet", "sketch — not built", "does
not exist yet") and NO open bead requires it, so the walk arm's co-discharge is
a benefit whose absence nobody has costed. How many of the 66 parity cases need
Hicasso siblings. And Node's runtime pin is CI-only: the workflows pin node 24,
package.json carries no engines field and there is no .nvmrc.

TRIPWIRES for whichever arm is chosen are in section 11. For the walk: a parity
case where the emitters disagree about the TREE rather than the markup (004B
under-specified for Hicasso), a separator settlement that changes the canonical
form (every v1-tree consumer in scope), a rule that cannot be twinned because it
needs a live React value at render time, a third emitter appearing. For the
sidecar: anything beyond body markup crossing the contract (the rejected host
fork arriving by increments), the sidecar needing to drain events, a view-code
skew reaching a deploy, snapshot serialisation appearing in a profile.

"<ns>/<sym>" (fn ...)) and mint-view!'s docstring insists the returned value is still the function. arm1/lang.clj states the JVM half itself: it is a .clj not a .cljc because 'the runtime it names is CLJS-only ... and a .cljc would invite a JVM-side implementation this arm does not have'. THE CONTRACT AS RESTATED: a NAME, not a form. An application-defined stable entry identifier, opaque to the JVM, resolved INSIDE the per-app Node bundle against a table that bundle publishes, plus root arguments in a stated serialization domain. Not an invention — core registers views under stable ids and looks them up with rf/view. What is absent is Hicasso participating: defview DOES capture "<ns>/<sym>" and mint-view! stamps it as displayName, but that name rides ON the head and is not a key TO it.
