THE SNAPSHOT DOMAIN, and this is the sharper half. payload-policy / project-app-db-egress / project-runtime-db CANNOT be reused: the payload is what the CLIENT may see, the snapshot is what the VIEWS must read, and the second is a superset by construction. So the sidecar needs a SECOND, LARGER EGRESS with no policy written for it. The failure modes are asymmetric — a narrow payload allowlist costs the client a recompute; A NARROW RENDER PROJECTION IS A SILENTLY WRONG PAGE. Spec-Schemas' machine-snapshot round-trip rule ((read-string (pr-str x)) =-equal, 'no functions, atoms, JS objects') is the right rule in the right shape but has never been stated for app-db, and nothing validates it there.

ONE ARROW THE OLD TEXT HID: R0 puts the drain on the JVM, so Node must NOT run :initial-events and everything must arrive as :snapshot. The entry's door is :rf/set-db, which seeds APP-DB ONLY — the frame's runtime-db (route slice, machine snapshots) has NO INBOUND DOOR ON THIS PATH AT ALL.

A JVM walk cannot implement the full declared language; it must narrow the authoring surface or define a server dialect. If Mike adopts the Arm-A-gated advisory anyway, the stabilisation gate MUST be restated in the strict formulation (a named quiet window on rule-bearing codec defs) — the permissive formulation ([:>] wave merged) is already met while the codec grows by hundreds of lines a day, so the gate as previously written cannot be evaluated. React 19.2's hydrateRoot caveats give no guarantee mismatched attributes are patched. The [S1-CONFIRM] separator row is now CONCRETE on the pinned local React 19.2.0: renderToString(
{"a"}{"b"}
) yields
ab
while renderToStaticMarkup yields
ab
, and the shipped structural-tree builders coalesce adjacent strings BEFORE emit-ui-tree sees them — so a JVM emitter cannot reproduce the separator by walking the tree it is given. A corpus detects only the examples it contains; it cannot make two independently evolving interpreters identical by construction. Arm B (same codec + same React renderer as the browser, plus build-identity enforcement) removes this class rather than sampling it. (2) ARM B IS NOT PRODUCTION-READY TODAY — the crossing must be designed, not relabelled: ssr/entry.cljs still accepts an in-process :hiccup carrying a function head and renders a full document/payload; driver.cjs loads the bundle via globalThis.HICASSO_SSR; ssr-ring still hard-calls ssr/render-to-string. (4) NEW UNCERTAINTY FOR THE SITTING: React classifies renderToString as a legacy non-streaming API and recommends renderToPipeableStream on Node. If Suspense/streaming is graduation scope, NEITHER priced arm nor the body-string boundary covers it and Arm B must be repriced before the ruling leans on its band. (5) THE ARM-A CONDITIONAL, stated fairly: if operators categorically cannot deploy a second runtime, Arm A remains choosable — but only with an explicit restricted SSR authoring contract (no :render third value server-side) and permanent React-version parity ownership; the presently-unrequested headless-test benefit is not by itself enough to accept those constraints. [S1-CONFIRM] SEPARATOR-ROW DISPOSITION (decided this pass, operator-overturnable): NO bead filed now. The row is 011-owned, has no bead, and the existing gate cannot see it — but it is a divergence class that EXISTS ONLY UNDER ARM A, and both standing advisories now recommend Arm B. Filing tracker work for a contingency the sitting may never choose is gold-plating. INSTEAD: if the sitting rules Arm A, the separator row MUST be filed as part of Arm A's bead breakdown (it is the concrete counter-example to "the corpus will catch it"), using the reproduction in (1) above as its opening evidence. This note is the pointer of record for that obligation. WHAT REMAINS FOR MIKE: rule the arm at the P2 sitting.

The sitting's streaming question is therefore concrete: does "Hicasso participates in Spec 011" at graduation include that surface? If yes — pause the arm ruling and reprice Arm B around a real streamed Node->Ring bridge first; the body-only boundary does not cover it, and neither arm as currently priced satisfies both full React semantics and shipped streaming semantics. (5) CODEX'S COMPACT DECISION RULE (recorded for the sitting's convenience; consistent with everything above): - Full current Hicasso semantics, non-streaming production SSR -> Arm B. - Deployment that categorically cannot operate Node -> Arm A ONLY as an explicitly restricted server dialect (no server-side :render) with permanent React-version parity ownership. - Streaming required at graduation -> NO ruling on the current prices; run the streamed cross-process spike and reprice. - No production caller, or adapters-as-success wins the fork -> keep deferred or close unruled; buy neither permanent cost speculatively. (6) ARM-B HYDRATION-FIXTURE ROSTER (supplements the four preconditions; adopt or trim at the sitting): adjacent text, controlled inputs, a declared :ssr :render context provider, client-only/fallback hosts, multiple frames, and an :advanced client build. One renderer removes emitter drift; it does not remove state, environment, or deploy-skew mismatches. (7) NAMED RESIDUAL ARM-B UNCERTAINTIES (honest, unmeasured): cross-process render latency, and whether a representative application's full render-visible state is serialisable. Both are measurable only on the real Ring->Node seam and belong in Arm B's first spike if the sitting rules for it. WHAT REMAINS FOR MIKE: rule the arm at the P2 sitting.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
OPERATOR RULING (Mike, 2026-08-08, given in chat — his wording is the artefact): "Let's go with arm B." THE RULING: the production server arm is the NODE SIDECAR (Arm B). ssr-ring remains the HTTP host and owns the request, frame, event drain, status, headers, cookies, redirects, head, hydration payload, shell, and error projection; a supervised Node process running the same compiled CLJS bundle as the client returns BODY MARKUP ONLY through a versioned fail-closed envelope. One emitter — the JVM-twin divergence class cannot exist. Arm A (the JVM structural walk) is not chosen; it remains available in principle only if the product ever deliberately names a RESTRICTED JVM SSR DIALECT with explicit exclusions and accepts permanent React-version parity ownership. OPERATIVE READING (advisory-derived, operator-overturnable): the ruled first scope is FULL, NON-STREAMING Hicasso SSR on the renderToString basis — the shape both advisories priced. Spec 011 streaming participation is NOT covered by this ruling: if graduation scope ever includes it, the recorded extra gate applies (run the streamed Node→Ring vertical spike — two overlapping real requests, one genuinely suspended boundary, pre-commit status/error handling, back-pressure/cancellation, request-scoped adoption/frame cleanup, final payload authority, deploy identity, hydration after the last chunk — and REPRICE before building that tier). The fresh probe evidence behind this gate: renderToPipeableStream returns before onShellReady/onAllReady, while the current entry relies on synchronous renderToString with a process-global adoption window closed in its immediate finally — a naive streaming substitution would tear down before completion, and overlapping streams could close each other's adoption windows. RULING != START. Per the park's own principle and the 2026-08-08 Codex pass ("do not start either production arm merely to preserve the option"): implementation dispatches only when a real production-SSR caller exists — i.e., on a P2 GO with SSR in delivery scope. If the fork lands adapters-as-success, this ruling stands recorded and nothing builds. Selecting Arm B selects a destination; it does not approve the spike as production topology (today there is no JVM<->Node request protocol, no entry registry, no supervised pool, no real body-only round trip; the Ring pipeline still calls JVM ssr/render-to-string; the driver's HTTP server is explicitly a demo). START GATES (acceptance criteria for the eventual bead breakdown, before any build — consolidated from the bead's four gates + the 2026-08-08 Codex refinement): 1. Versioned, fail-closed body-render protocol: correlation id, protocol version, application build/schema identity, stable root id, serializable arguments, validated render-state projection in; body markup or a typed error out. No function crosses the boundary. Unknown root, skewed identity, malformed/oversized input, and missing required render state all REFUSE rather than render partial nil state. 2. One per-application Node registry resolving the stable root id from the exact server bundle shipped with the client bundle. It must not grow into a per-component or per-route RPC catalogue. 3. A per-application state projector with round-trip fixtures over a representative real page and at least one NEGATIVE fixture proving an omitted server read fails. Do not reuse the client payload allowlist — the render-visible domain and the browser-egress domain answer different security questions. 4. Long-lived bounded worker pool: deadlines, cancellation, restart/health behaviour, max message/body sizes, build-skew telemetry, overload behaviour; the chosen transport honors flow control (Node's documented IPC/stream back-pressure semantics — unbounded sends are not safe). 5. The topology fence, witnessed: prove the actual JVM->Node->JVM path end to end, including timeout, worker death, malformed reply, unknown entry, build skew, and hydration of adjacent text, controlled inputs, all three defhost :ssr policies, multiple frames, and an :advanced client build. NEW DURABLE FACTS from the 2026-08-08 Codex pass (preserved here; the dossier is deleted after this note): - The existing parity corpus (parity_corpus_cljs_test.cljs) calls renderToStaticMarkup, so it CANNOT see the hydration separator row (renderToString emits
ab
; renderToStaticMarkup and the JVM emitter both emit
ab
). Load-bearing for anyone revisiting Arm A or extending the corpus. - suspense.cljc returns :rf/suspense-boundary only on CLJ; on CLJS — the branch the Node renderer runs — it returns the body ("Not React Suspense"). Spec 011's shipped stream is a JVM hiccup walker with its own marker/continuation/delta/chunk-order/failure/teardown protocol; native renderToPipeableStream emits React's protocol, not Spec 011's. Streaming is a protocol decision, not a function rename. - NAMED FALSIFIERS (unmeasured, honest): cross-process latency, and whether a representative application's full render-visible state is serializable at acceptable cost. A real application may show the projection is effectively the whole frame, or that operating Node is unacceptable — either finding can disqualify Arm B in practice. Neither overturns the semantic decision rule; both belong in the first implementation bead's measurement plan. CONSEQUENCES: the [S1-CONFIRM] text-separator row obligation DISSOLVES (it was file-only-if-Arm-A). The sitting's agenda narrows — the server-arm item is resolved ahead of it; remaining room items are the K-waiver questions and the fork. The streaming-scope question survives only as the extra gate above.

title: hicasso SSR: activate HD-011's placeholder — defhost :ssr policy (:client-only default, :fallback)
description:
ACTIVATE HD-011'S SSR PLACEHOLDER — defhost :ssr policy. From the 2026-08-04 SSR design programme (consensus on the epic). HD-011 declared "fns pass through, SSR placeholder" as defhost policy; the 2026-08-04 runtime audit found the placeholder is ABSENT, not inert: mint-host! reads only :callbacks and SILENTLY IGNORES every other option (front/codec.cljs:1036).

THE WORK (bench lane):
1. defhost gains an :ssr option: :client-only (DEFAULT — the host region renders nothing server-side) or {:fallback <hiccup>} (server + pre-adoption placeholder markup). Any other value = mint-time refusal. While here: mint-host! refuses UNKNOWN options loudly instead of ignoring them (the silent-ignore is its own defect).
2. Client behaviour: a host boundary renders its placeholder/nothing during hydration adoption and the real component after adoption (and immediately on fresh non-hydrated mounts). Implementation sketch from the design record: the host shell's single useSyncExternalStore((noop), ()=>true, ()=>false) yields false during server/hydration first pass, true after — no new hooks beyond the shell budget (<=2, HD-020), no fake hook dispatcher ever (HD-021(a)).
3. Server behaviour lands with the Node-entry bead (sibling): the server walk consults the same :ssr policy. This bead makes the policy REAL on the client and mint-time.
4. Witnesses: mint-time refusal row; :client-only host absent from a hydration fixture's server HTML then mounted after adoption; {:fallback} host's placeholder present in server HTML then swapped after adoption with no mismatch warning.

HD addendum: record the activated shape as a dated HD-011 addendum in the same PR (rf2-digtt pattern).

FENCES: bench lane + docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md (HD-011 addendum) only. Coordinate with the hydration-door bead if both touch runtime.cljs; front/codec.cljs is this bead's primary file.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7468 (2026-08-04) — REOPENED: the promised mint-time fallback refusal is incomplete.

Landed evidence: front/codec.cljs:1068 declared-ssr accepts any one-key fallback map whose value is merely non-nil. mint-host-gate! then calls the deliberately permissive as-element; at front/codec.cljs:1749 its final branch returns an unrecognised value unchanged. Consequently a declaration such as {:ssr {:fallback {}}} mints successfully, then hands a ClojureScript map to React during server render or hydration, where it fails late as a non-renderable object. Raw JS objects and other unsupported values have the same hole. The only negative witness uses [], which vec->element already rejects, so it does not cover the permissive fallthrough.

This contradicts the owner and PR contract that any non-hiccup fallback is refused at declaration, where the author stack is available. Close the type hole at mint, define the accepted inert-fallback grammar narrowly enough to exclude non-renderable objects, and add regression rows including a plain map (plus one other fallthrough value) while retaining valid fallback coverage.

Duplicate audit: all 2,005 Beads were scanned. Open rf2-2rtt6.92 owns retirement of the redundant server pre-walk and nested-host server coverage; it does not own declaration-time fallback validation. This remains exact scope for rf2-2rtt6.85.

The work landed: PR #7468 merged (defhost :ssr policy — two values, :client-only as the default when absent and {:fallback <hiccup>}), with arm1/host_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs on main and the policy readable via descriptor/host-ssr-spelling (freehand/descriptor.cljc:244). The worker closed this bead when its PR opened; the tracker later read OPEN again with no close reason. Verified against the tree, not against memory.

title: hicasso: the intent surface now costs 125 ns/element where the walk page measured 41 -- same-run, resolved, uncaused
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-04 on origin/main at 77a92185ea, published as the dated
re-take section of docs/design/hicasso/studio/our-walk-against-reagents.md.
One run of walk_vs_reagent_app via run.cjs, four arms, one process, one
witness value, arm-order guard REPORTABLE on every arm by predecessor and
by phase, exit 0, agreement failures [] on both tables.

THE ROW. The `hicasso-native` arm walks the page's OWN intent markup; the
`hicasso` arm walks the same page with every event position replaced by one
shared plain fn. The difference is the price of the authoring surface.

  published (studio page, section 2)   562 -> 603  and  551 -> 593   = ~41 ns/el

-- the authoring affordance the P2 fork is deciding about -- and the studio
page states it as "41 ns/element ... about 7% of the walk. That is the

rf2-digtt. Any of those could own it; this run does not decompose.

instrument already prices stages beside each other in one process on the

notes:
ATTRIBUTED — PR #7625, branch worker/intentprice-vw412. Three runs on
2026-08-06, guard reportable on every arm of all three, exit 0,
agreement [] on every table, twin parity OK.

BOTH PINS RESOLVE. 77a92185ea and 02a440a4d1 are both ancestors of
origin/main. One tree, not two.

THE ROW WAS NEVER PRICING THE AUTHORING SURFACE. The hicasso-native /

15:52. NOT an ancestor of 02a440a4d1 (rc 1); IS an ancestor of

title: Hicasso: the R=0 shell lost ~140 B between rf2-aqgr2 and the fusion, and nothing attributes it
description:
The R=0 boundary shell on the P0 reads ladder (p0_run.cjs --only ladder, Hicasso arm, wrapper present) fell by ~140 B between two published sessions and no section on reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md attributes the move.

Readings, wrapper present in all of them:
  rf2-2rtt6.58 (2026-08-02)      1,247 / 1,236 B  (Reagent seg / UIx seg)
  rf2-aqgr2 A-double-prime/B-dp  1,244-1,246 / 1,236-1,237 B
  rf2-zei9w (2026-08-04)         1,103 / 1,097 B
  rf2-2rtt6.58 re-take (this)    1,101 / 1,097 B on 81321da3fe

So the drop is LATER than rf2-aqgr2 and is fully present by rf2-zei9w. Net
-145 / -139 B on a quantity the validation.md paper line is stated against,
and on which 75 B is the named shape sensitivity — i.e. roughly twice the
resolution of the line itself.

The obvious suspect is rf2-dabt3's sub-index fusion, but the fusion section
(rf2-zei9w) reports the shell UNMOVED by its own ablation (1,103 -> 1,098 and
1,097 -> 1,097). That ablation removes the reader ARRAY, which is per-key and
so cannot be a shell term either way, so it neither convicts nor exonerates
the rest of the fusion. Nothing else in the window has been priced on the
shell axis at all.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the axis HD-028's disposition now turns on. With the
memo wrapper the shell reads ~1,100 B (over the 1 KB paper line); without it
994 / 992 B (at the line). A 140 B unattributed movement is the difference
between those two states, so the programme cannot say whether the shell's
current position is a durable property of the design or an unexplained drift.

DO: bisect the shell rung (R=0 only is enough - a fast plan) across the
landings between rf2-aqgr2's tree and 23d60a1fe9, on a quiet box, and
attribute the -145 / -139 B. If it IS the fusion, the fusion section owes a
shell row it does not currently carry.

Filed by the rf2-2rtt6.58 re-take, which observed it as a same-instrument
same-box difference against two published sessions and declined to guess.
close_reason: Bisected and attributed in PR #7626. Two commits on the sub-index line, neither ever priced on the shell axis: 27f846cf5a (rf2-ixb92) = -75/-68 B and is the ONLY arm commit in its span; 383ba2d645 (rf2-dabt3, the fusion) = -77/-77 B. The six arm landings between them = -2/-1 B (round-to-round floor). Both convicted steps have disjoint per-round bands. Total -154/-146.5 B, and both ends of the bisect reproduce the published sessions they explain (T1 1,237/1,232 vs rf2-aqgr2's 1,244-1,246/1,236-1,237; T4 1,083/1,085.5 vs rf2-zei9w's 1,103/1,097 on that same tree). MECHANISM: both removed per-BOUNDARY index structure, which is exactly what R=0 prices -- :live (a set membership per mounted boundary) and :b->subs (a map entry mount installed whether or not the boundary read). Counted, not inferred: the structural witness passes with boundaries=1200 at R=0 pre-fusion and boundaries=0 post. WHY THE HOLE: rf2-ixb92's own commit message says no byte figure was claimed and none measured; rf2-zei9w's ablation removed the reader ARRAY, which is per key and cannot appear at R=0, so it exonerated the array and never examined the registration. The fusion section now carries the shell row it owed. VERDICT: a SAVING, not a boundary that stopped doing work -- information survives both eliminations, the only thing no longer retained (the record that an edgeless boundary is mounted) is consumed by nothing, teardown residue zero on every arm of every round of five runs. One diagnostic narrowing: stats' :boundaries now means 'retained by at least one cell', already absorbed by rf2-xzg3b's strictly stronger expectation. Deltas only -- box not certified quiet, no absolute republished.

title: bench: the ladder's structural witness still expects the PRE-FUSION meaning of :boundaries, so --only ladder cannot gate the fused arm
description:
FOUND by rf2-zei9w on 2026-08-04 on a verified-quiet box. `p0_run.cjs
--only ladder` EXITS 1 on the current `main` (2926049d5e) with 12
structural read-back failures, all of one kind and all on the R=0 rung:

  round N reagent-subs|lad/hicasso#R0: hicasso boundaries 0, expected 1200
  round N uix-subs|lad/hicasso#R0:     hicasso boundaries 0, expected 1200

EVERY OTHER GATE PASSED. ladder-fit self-test 3/3 ok, arm-order guard
self-test 12/12 ok, positive control OK (4,698,566 B measured against
4,700,000 predicted, ratio 0.9997), `0 unverified of 154 mounts`,
arm-order verdict `reportable`, and zero residue failures. The run is
otherwise clean; only this one expectation refuses.

THE EXPECTATION IS STALE, NOT THE ARM. rf2-dabt3 changed what
`:boundaries` MEANS and `p0_run.cjs` was not moved with it:

  before (383ba2d645^, arm1/runtime.cljs `stats`):
    :boundaries (count (:b->subs idx))
  after  (383ba2d645, the fusion):
    boundaries (reduce-kv (fn [acc _ ^js c] (into acc (.-readers c))) #{} cells)

`:b->subs` was populated by `index/mount!` — one entry per MOUNTED
boundary, whether or not it read anything — so `:boundaries` was
R-independent and 1200 at R=0. Post-fusion there is no per-boundary
registry at all: the forward edge lives on the registration itself
(`.-reads`) and the runtime knows a boundary only through cells' reader
lists. At R=0 nothing is read, so no cell exists, so `:boundaries` is 0.

THE RUNTIME SAYS SO ITSELF. `stats`'s docstring: \":boundaries counts the
distinct registrations holding at least one such slot; a boundary whose
body read nothing retains nothing in this table, so it is correctly
absent (its read-set entry is still counted by :entries)\". And rf2-dabt3
landed a test for exactly this — 7838e3f7ad, \"an edgeless boundary
retains no membership\". `:entries` at R=0 expects 1 and PASSES, which is
the same fact from the other side.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT. `--only ladder` is opt-in and is in no gate;
`p0_run.cjs` was last touched by rf2-2rtt6.34 (f72f2586f5), before the
fusion. rf2-dabt3 deferred its measurement for a quiet box, so between
the landing and 2026-08-04 nobody ran the driver.

THE FIX, three sites in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs`:

  1. line 875, `ladderStructuralFailures`'s `want`:
       boundaries: B                 ->  boundaries: R === 0 ? 0 : B
  2. line 855, the legend comment: \"boundaries === B  one registration
     per boundary, R-independent\" is now false — it is one registration
     per boundary THAT READS, and it is R-dependent only at R=0.
  3. the printed legend (~line 1029): \"boundaries = B\" wants the same
     qualification it already gives `entries` (\"B (1 at R=0)\").

At R>=1 every boundary reads R distinct keys, so every registration holds
at least one slot and `boundaries === B` — which is why only the R=0
rungs failed. Do NOT weaken the check to admit the run: it should assert
0 at R=0, which is a STRONGER statement than the one it makes now (it
pins the edgeless-boundary property the fusion was taken for).

BLOCKS rf2-zei9w, which cannot publish a magnitude until this run exits
0. rf2-zei9w's own runs are recorded on that bead but published nowhere.

title: bench: three more runners compute a refusal, print it, and exit 0 anyway — 7 unread conditions
description:

repairing B8's identical defect. The bead's brief asked for the real count of
computed-but-unread refusal sites rather than the one named site; it is four
files, not one.

THE SHAPE. A runner computes a refusal / contamination / unverified /
unsettled condition, PRINTS it loudly, stores it in the artefact — and the
process exit never reads it. The run says "REFUSED ... no magnitude
reportable" and exits 0.

rf2-tb345 repaired b8_run.cjs. These three remain, verified by reading each
exit path (not inferred):

1. implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/hd8_clock_run.cjs
   THREE unread conditions. Band-ceiling breach: computed :615, prints
   "BREACHED, no magnitude reportable" :619 and verdict='REFUSED' :646-648,
   stored :796. Positive-control failure: computed :587, prints "FAIL
   measured ...x" :592, stored :662/:793. Unverified writes: :490, printed
   :527, stored :788. Exit path :816-826 reads only `failed` and
   `adj.guardRefuse`. Falsely green: quiet box, no thrown page, arm-order
   guard clean, but the band blows past seamlib.BAND_CEILING (or ctl-2x

   Same three conditions (near-copy of hd8_clock_run's report/main). Band

   here: the file's own prediction P4 (:780-782) PROMISES "if its control or

3. implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso_narrow_run.cjs
   The closest twin to the b8 defect: an UNSETTLED WARM-UP. settled[arm]
   computed :422/:434 inside the WARMUP_MAX loop, printed :440-443 ("still

title: The public-mount adoption witness cannot see the ruled 4 ms horizon — the browser runner's render-to-flush gap is >128 ms
description:
FILED BY the rf2-2rtt6.71 implementation worker, 2026-08-03 17:xx AUSEST.
Ruling (a) is IMPLEMENTED (spine horizon setTimeout 0 -> 4). Item 2 of the
ruling — flipping assert-use-subscribe-public-mount-schedule-rebuilds to the
act-driven row's integers — was ATTEMPTED, MEASURED, and HELD. This bead
carries the measurement and the decision it needs.

THE FACT. With the ruled setTimeout 4 in place, the flipped assertions FAIL:
the row still observes two acquisitions, two body runs, and the commit's
reaction (not the render's) as the cache tenant. Deterministic, reproduced in
a narrow single-ns browser-test build in ~1 s, not a load artefact.

THE SWEEP (narrow :browser-test build, uix-use-subscribe-dom-cljs-test only,
one run per cell; the integer is the row's :builds):

  horizon 0 / 8 / 16 / 32 / 64 ms, as shipped (one timer per burst)   2
  horizon 4 / 32 / 128 ms, rewired to one timer per TOKEN             2
  reaper disabled entirely                                            1
  horizon 256 / 1024 / 5000 ms                                        1

So the reaper IS the releaser — disabling it adopts — and the gap this page
puts between the render and React's passive flush is > 128 ms and <= 256 ms.
Two to three orders of magnitude above any horizon worth shipping. Per-token
arming was tested and rejected as the explanation, so burst coalescing is not
the cause either.

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. It is NOT evidence against ruling (a): the ruling's
swap-the-primitive probe measured a dedicated single-mount instrument page,
where the gap is under 4 ms, and nothing here contradicts that. It IS evidence
that this assertion cannot serve as the adoption witness the ruling assumed —
the browser test page (30 async rows, cljs-test done plumbing, a display
renderer competing for the main thread) is not a faithful clock for a
millisecond-scale race. Greening the row would take a horizon in the hundreds
of milliseconds, i.e. holding every abandoned render's reactive graph for a
quarter of a second — exactly the trade rf2-2rtt6.71 declined, and exactly the
"worker picks a longer timer to green a row" failure rf2-2rtt6.25 warned about.
So the worker did not do it.

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD (PR for rf2-2rtt6.71):
  * spine horizon = 4, as ruled, with the margin-not-contract prose.
  * the row keeps its two-build assertions, with the sweep recorded in its
    block comment and the claim narrowed: it witnesses the RUNNER's schedule,
    which is enough to pin the setTimeout-0-era defect (real in every
    environment) and not enough to pin the win.

witness on a representative page — a dedicated single-mount browser target
whose render-to-flush gap is measured and asserted to be small before the

RULED: (ii), SHARPENED — no standing/gating witness. Instead: commit the 71 ruling's probe as a self-reporting ON-DEMAND diagnostic in the Hicasso bench lane; record the revalidation trigger once in Spec 006; do the rename rider; fix a stale spine docstring. The assertion-level-tripwire expectation from rf2-2rtt6.71 is retired on evidence.

The dossier's main rec put the witness "in the bench lane" — but that lane is runtime-on-demand (CI runs only test:hicasso-compile, test.yml ~L2564), so a witness there IS (ii)'s "whenever someone runs the instrument", plus machinery. REFUSED-fails-CI = load-sensitive red (the fleet already fights CI flakes under load); REFUSED-passes = the detector silently declines to adjudicate exactly when the signal appears. Self-gating makes the verdict honest; it cannot make it a stable gate.

The threat is discrete, not ambient. react/react-dom 19.2.0 and playwright 1.59.1 are EXACT pins (verified implementation/package.json; Playwright pins its Chromium) — the only events that can move this race are reviewed lock/posture changes. React drifting reds the suite", false since PR #7440 held the flip (the section comment ~L2278-2285 is honest; the docstring contradicts it). The main rec's fallback clause addressed the wrong failure mode: the 71 probe already proved a quiet page CAN see the race (gap < 4 ms, 1.00N at N=1 and N=300); the real failure modes are adjudication ambiguity at drift and zero information between pinned upgrades. title: worker gates: a backgrounded relative-path gate invocation runs in ANOTHER worktree — reproduced, with the one-token fix
description:
REPRODUCED 2026-08-03 during rf2-6wh9o/rf2-2rtt6.75, not inferred. This is the
harness path-resolution leak CLAUDE.md already names ("mitigates observed
harness path-resolution leaks"), caught with a full log, plus a fix that costs
one token per dispatch.

WHAT HAPPENED. A worker in
C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/insttruth-6wh9o backgrounded its spine
as, verbatim:

  cd C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/insttruth-6wh9o && \
    sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh > <log> 2>&1

The `cd` DID NOT TAKE in the backgrounded shell. The identical command run in
the FOREGROUND minutes earlier resolved correctly, so this is specific to
backgrounding.

WHY THAT SILENTLY RETARGETS THE GATE. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:97-99 derives
everything from its own path:

  script_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
  spine_root="$(cd "$script_dir/.." && pwd)"
  diff_root="$spine_root"

With a RELATIVE invocation, `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` is `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh`,
so `dirname` resolves against whatever cwd the shell actually has. The run
therefore adopted a DIFFERENT worktree wholesale — as its spine root, as its
diff root, and as its classifier input.

THE EVIDENCE, from the log:
  * mkdocs:  "Building documentation to directory:
             ...\re-frame2-worktrees\slimresid-e7zxb\site"
  * story:   approved roots named ...\slimresid-e7zxb\implementation\out
  * shadow:  "config: ...\slimresid-e7zxb\implementation\shadow-cljs.edn"
  * classification: "docs=true jvm=false node=false" — slimresid's diff shape,
    not the running worker's (which is docs=false jvm=true node=true).

CONSEQUENCE, and it is BOTH directions:
  1. The verdict is meaningless — a PASS or FAIL about someone else's diff,
     reported in this worker's PR body as its own gate. A green here is a
     FALSE GREEN of the rf2-n3dxw family: the colour is real, the subject is
     not.
  2. It becomes a SECOND concurrent spine inside a live worker's checkout,
     sharing that checkout's .shadow-cljs — the configuration CLAUDE.md and
     every dispatch brief forbid. It duly produced the documented signature:
     13 phantom `re_frame/test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test` failures
     (unknown-arg-is-fatal-not-false-green, red-run-replays-buffered-console-
     warn, spawn-timeout-kills-a-hanging-child, ...). The victim worker sees
     phantom reds in ITS run and has no way to know why.

BLAST RADIUS IS LIMITED, AND WORTH STATING SO NOBODY PANICS: `git status` in
the invaded worktree was CLEAN afterwards. A spine only writes gitignored
build output (out/, site/, .shadow-cljs/). No source was touched. The damage is
wasted wall-clock, phantom reds, and a verdict attributed to the wrong diff.

THE FIX (one token, no new machinery): invoke a backgrounded gate by ABSOLUTE
PATH. `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` is then absolute and `spine_root`/`diff_root` are
pinned no matter what cwd the shell has.

  sh C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/<wt>/scripts/test-fast-pr.sh

Verified: the same worker's third run, changed ONLY in this way, classified
correctly (docs=false jvm=true node=true), had ZERO occurrences of the foreign
worktree in its log, and reached `PASS fast PR spine` exit 0.

PROPOSED, for the mayor to rule on:
  A. Dispatch briefs' GATE MECHANICS section gains a numbered rule:
     "backgrounded gates are invoked by ABSOLUTE path — `cd` does not survive
     backgrounding, and a relative `BASH_SOURCE[0]` silently adopts another
     worktree." Same register as the existing four (no `tail` pipes, no two
     spines, artefacts to gitignored paths, foreground to completion).
  B. Cheap belt-and-braces in the script itself: have test-fast-pr.sh print
     its resolved `spine_root` as its FIRST line. Today the only way to notice
     is to catch a foreign path in an mkdocs INFO line 90 lines down. One
     echo turns a silent misfire into an obvious one, and makes it greppable
     from a PR body.
  C. Consider whether scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh should be re-run (or
     its WORKTREE_ROOT re-asserted) at GATE time, not only before the first
     edit. The existing guard fires at session start and cannot see a leak
     that happens forty minutes later.

A alone is worth doing immediately; B is a two-line change to one script and
would have made this diagnosable in seconds rather than in a log post-mortem.
close_reason: PR #7436. All eight gate scripts under scripts/ now print 'gate root: <path>' as line 1 (not just test-fast-pr.sh — the pattern was 8-wide). Proposal B implemented; proposal A landed as the fourth GATE MECHANICS rule in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md plus the matching AGENTS.md section, and both files' worked examples now spell the absolute form. Proposal C (re-assert assert-worker-worktree.sh at gate time) deliberately NOT done: the brief ruled against any guard that could refuse a legitimate run. Audit: the spine's other 15 Python checkers derive their root from Path(__file__) and are cwd-immune, so the BASH_SOURCE shell scripts were the only exposed link. Mutation-proved both directions in a throwaway tree; spine exit 0, PASS fast PR spine, 0 FAILs.

title: The band ceiling's bootstrap is pooled-block, not run-preserving — 35% is not a q99 and its false-fire rate is 2.7% (rf2-ymi6j)
description:
AUDIT OF PR #7368, confirmed by independent recomputation from the COMMITTED dataset (implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/ladder-ymi6j.json). Docs restated under rf2-ymi6j; this bead is the CODE half, which a docs-fenced worker must not take.

WHAT IS WRONG. ladder_band.cjs's bootstrapBand() pools all 342 block ratios from all 19 runs and then builds each synthetic 18-block run by drawing individual blocks across unrelated runs and load rungs. That destroys the run-level clustering the 18 blocks of a real run share, so it estimates a synthetic mixed-regime block sample rather than a future run. Recomputed at 200,000 draws on raw TaskDuration:

  quantile   pooled-block   run-preserving
  q50        13.0%          11.5%
  q90        19.9%          23.4%
  q95        22.7%          31.0%
  q99        29.4%          41.4%

  ceiling    P(fire) pooled   P(fire) run-preserving   observed of 19
  20%        9.8%             15.0%                    4
  25%        2.7%             9.1%                     2
  30%        0.9%             5.9%                     1
  35%        0.2%             2.7%                     0
  40%        0.06%            1.2%                     0

So 35% is the q99 of NEITHER distribution, and the advertised 0.2% tripwire rate is understated ~13x. The script already prints the correct number in its 'within-run' column (2.7%) and then argues in a source comment that the pooled column is the wider one a ceiling should be set against. It is not: pooled is narrower in the whole upper tail.

SCOPE (all code, none of it docs):
1. ladder_band.cjs — preserve run clustering in the bootstrap (draw a run, then resample its blocks), or justify a different statistically valid run-level model in the source. Correct the comment at the withinRun computation that argues the pooled estimate is the conservative one.
2. ladder_band.cjs — remove the stale sign interpretation still printed beside corr(ctl-2x/floor, floor): 'an additive c reads (2W+c)/(W+c), which FALLS as c grows, so a NEGATIVE sign is the additive signature'. Section 6 of the-band-re-calibrated.md and seam.cjs withdrew that argument; the printer did not. Across this ladder the varying quantity is W with c roughly fixed, so (2W+c)/(W+c) RISES with W and the sign carries no information.
3. Add a deterministic synthetic regression that distinguishes pooled-block from run-preserving resampling — a fixture of two clearly-different synthetic runs where the two models give different q99 by a wide margin.
4. DECIDE whether seam.cjs's BAND_CEILING moves off 0.35. A ceiling at the run-preserving q99 is ~41%. It is a judgement, not arithmetic: 35% already refuses nothing this ladder produced, and no published magnitude changes at either value (see section 8 of the page). Whatever is decided, seam.cjs's header comment currently states P(band > 35%) = 0.2% per run and must not keep saying so.

NO NEW MEASUREMENT IS NEEDED. Everything above is a recomputation over the committed compact dataset; ladder_band.cjs --from data/ladder-ymi6j.json reproduces the page digit for digit today.

title: Hicasso arm 1: the survival metric's allocation-slope half (warm 1/3/7/20 reads)
description:
Re-homed from rf2-2rtt6.41 item 4, which is otherwise discharged. Not new scope - this is the last unowned half of that bead's witness set.

WHAT IS OUTSTANDING. validation.md's survival metric has two halves. The ZERO-RETAINED-PER-OCCURRENCE half is witnessed (after commit and after teardown, rf2-2rtt6.9 + PR #7338). The STEADY-STATE ALLOCATION SLOPE across warm 1/3/7/20 reads is not: it needs the bench, on the P0 instrument, against same-run donors - the same rig rf2-2rtt6.34 used for the per-read rung (p0_run.cjs / p0_heap.cljs, PR #7337).

WHY IT WAS NOT TAKEN ON 2026-08-03. Deliberate, and the reason is about trust in the number rather than effort. The box was carrying six concurrent workers, and absolute figures on that rig move by roughly 2x run-to-run on UNCHANGED arms under that load. A slope is a difference of such figures, so it is strictly less robust to the contention than the absolute readings are - measuring it then would have produced a number that read as evidence and was not. rf2-2rtt6.41's own worker had already held it off once for the same class of reason (contention with the heap worker's instrument).

PRECONDITION FOR DISPATCH: a quiet box. Take it when the worker count is low, take the warm 1/3/7/20 series in one session on one rig, and cite the SHA. Do not interleave it with other bench work on the same instrument.

Related and already answered, so do not re-measure: the shell-target half of item 5 is closed NEGATIVELY at 1,143 B against the >1 KB paper-fail line - structural, because the subscription hook is per BOUNDARY (rf2-2rtt6.41 notes, from rf2-2rtt6.34).
notes:
TAKEN 2026-08-07 on a verified-quiet box (zero java.exe, three idle MCP/agent node procs, CPU 16-25%). PR #7644. Measured at d31fdb5a06, branched from 6dbf37998d.

OUTCOME: A REFUSAL WITH EVIDENCE, NOT A SLOPE. Published as docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-survival-metrics-allocation-half.md.

THE PREMISE NEEDED CORRECTING FIRST. The P0 rig could not answer this bead as written: p0_heap.cljs's header says 'Nothing here counts allocations', and the reads ladder (incl. its 2rtt6.34 section 6) prices RETENTION per read. HD-002's survival metric is a different quantity - allocation on a warm re-render, predicted FLAT AT ZERO and falsified by a non-flat slope. So the rig got an allocation row: p0_run.cjs --only alloc, opt-in, reusing the ladder's arms, donors, plan and fit rule.

THE CONTROLS PASS. 8.13 B/double direct and 7.99 differential against a predicted 8; idle window 32 B. A retention instrument reads both as zero, so transient garbage IS visible to this counter.

THE SERIES IS REFUSED, ON TWO COUNTS.
(1) The fit rule - the ladder's own, 0.98 r2 floor, self-test proves it can fail - returned 0.75 / 0.28 / 0.94 / 0.31 on the four arms, none linear in more than 1 round of 4. The rungs are NON-MONOTONE, not merely noisy.
(2) The warm-write read-back caught the candidate NOT RE-RENDERING AT ALL under the Reagent adapter - DOM stale by exactly the writes the window drove, allocation flat on the no-op floor. Filed rf2-2rtt6.137 (P1). Without that gate the row would have published a no-op as confirmation of the design, since 'nothing per read' is exactly HD-002's predicted answer.

THE INSTRUMENT'S CEILING, MEASURED: ~600 KB of garbage per window. Above it the reading degrades monotonically and ALWAYS DOWNWARD - the direction that manufactures flat-at-zero. --max-semi-space-size does NOT move it (128 MB and 512 MB tried, falls unchanged). At the published B=1,200 witness, 32 collections fell inside 44 windows and the row refused on that alone.

NOTHING IN validation.md MOVES. No gate line, budget or verdict is restated.

title: Hicasso: a :render prop that returns lowered hiccup poisons the row's own handlers
description:
FOUND while landing rf2-2rtt6.35 (HD-024's two laws). Not fixed there, because it
is a capability question about the :render contract rather than a defect in the
carrier-governance repair, and answering it needs a ruling on which frame a
render-produced row dispatches to.

THE SHAPE. A `defhost` `:render` slot is the ecosystem's `renderRow`/`renderItem`
prop. For React to render what the body returns, the body has to hand back an
ELEMENT, so the author calls the codec's hiccup->element conversion inside the
callback:

    [grid {:on-render-row (h/fn [row]
                            (h/as-element [:li {:on-click [:row/pick (:id row)]}
                                           (:title row)]))}]

THE PROBLEM. `front/intent/render-callback` enforces purity by BINDING the
ambient `*dispatch*` to a poison fn for the call's dynamic extent, and
`front/intent/intent-handler` captures `*dispatch*` AT LOWERING TIME (via
`require-dispatch`). So the `:on-click` above closes over the POISONED dispatch,
and clicking the rendered row raises
`:rf.error/hicasso-dispatch-in-render-position` — for a click, which is a
perfectly legitimate event position that happens to have been LOWERED during a
render.

The rule HD-024 states is "dispatching from inside the call is a loud error". A
closure that will dispatch LATER is not dispatching from inside the call. The
poisoning conflates the two because lowering captures the same var the poison
replaced.

WHY IT MATTERS. A render prop that produces a NON-interactive row works; one that
produces an interactive row does not. That is most of what render props are for,
and the failure lands on the user's click rather than at the author's site.

OPTIONS, none of them ruled:
  (a) Poison only DISPATCH, not lowering: have `render-callback` bind a poisoned
      dispatch that `intent-handler` refuses to CAPTURE, i.e. keep a separate
      "capturable" binding — the callback's enclosing boundary's real dispatch —
      so rows lower against the boundary that owns them and only an immediate
      dispatch during the call is refused.
  (b) Rule the case out: state that a :render body must not build lowered
      elements, and refuse `as-element` inside a render callback with a
      diagnostic naming the position. Cheap, but it removes the interactive
      render-prop entirely.
  (c) Leave it and revisit at the component-library tier (charter.md:144-149
      defers that tier past v0; the census counts 0 foreign components).

NOT WITNESSED DELIBERATELY. rf2-2rtt6.35 did not add a test pinning the current
behaviour, because pinning it would record a defect as the contract.

Sites: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/intent.cljs
  - `render-callback` (the binding)
  - `require-dispatch` / `intent-handler` (the capture)
close_reason: PR #7449: render-position enforcement is invocation-scoped (gate armed in a finally); owner = the supplying boundary's frame, rebound for the invocation. Three witnesses incl. the two-frame ownership row at the declared-:render crossing; both purity edges unmodified and still raising; HD-024 dated addendum.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
[2026-08-03 20:18 AUSEST] DELEGATED DOSSIER-REVIEW RULING (Mike's 2026-08-03 directive); operator-overturnable.

RULING: (a), sharpened — repair now, inside HD-024's existing laws, via an INVOCATION-SCOPED ARMING GATE in render-callback, NOT the naive "second capturable binding" this bead's option (a) text sketches.

MECHANISM (the capture/poison discrimination, exact): render-callback captures the ambient *dispatch* AND *frame* at wrapper-creation (lowering) time — the supplying boundary's, because the wrapper is minted during that boundary's eager with-frame + as-element walk (arm1/runtime.cljs ~1329). Each invocation mints a fresh gate closing over an armed? flag + the captured owner dispatch; binds *frame* = captured frame and *dispatch* = gate around (apply f args); arms the gate in a finally. Gate while active: raise the existing :rf.error/hicasso-dispatch-in-render-position naming the position (message unchanged). Gate after: forward to the captured owner dispatch; if NO owner was in scope at wrapper creation, raise the existing :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary — loud, never silent. require-dispatch / intent-handler / event-callback stay UNCHANGED: they keep capturing *dispatch*, which inside a callback is now the gate — that is what makes lower-now/fire-later work while lower-now/fire-NOW still fails.

FRAME ANSWER (dossier main rec CONFIRMED): a render-produced row dispatches to the frame of the boundary whose codec walk lowered the :render prop — the supplying boundary. Only candidate: the wrapper is created inside that boundary's with-frame extent, the foreign component has no frame of its own, and frames-as-isolated-contexts forbids any other. Rebinding the captured *frame* per invocation is part of the SAME repair, not growth: route-link's require-frame! (front/route_link.cljs ~174) reads intent/*frame* and today fails loudly inside any render-prop body.

WHY NOT NAIVE (a) — the main-vs-Codex resolution: both recs chose repair-now-(a); they split on mechanism, and Codex's objection VERIFIED. deftest at-a-render-position-...-dispatching-is-a-loud-error (front/intent_cljs_test.cljs, second testing block) pins the SYNCHRONOUS lower-and-fire error: it lowers :on-click [:oops] inside the callback and fires it immediately. Under a second capturable binding, that inner handler captures the REAL dispatch and the immediate fire dispatches silently — the pinned witness breaks and law 1 is weakened (a dispatch that actually happens during the call succeeds). The gate discriminates temporally — call-active vs call-complete — which is exactly the law's own line ("dispatching from inside the call"). Codex's gate adopted; Codex's frame-rebinding and two-frame-witness additions verified load-bearing and adopted.

WHY NOT (b)/(c): (b) deletes the interactive renderRow pattern — most of what render props exist for — to preserve a mechanism conflation. (c) ships a booby trap on a surface HD-024 just landed: the error fires at the USER's click, far from the author's site (worst failure geometry), and census-zero measures the old corpus, not this product. Both punish the obvious usage — anti trust-the-programmer.

SCOPE FENCE: front/intent.cljs render-callback (+ its docstring and the ns-docstring's mechanism sentence) only. Change what lowering-inside-a-render-callback captures/forwards; NOTHING about scheduling; no new API, no config knobs, no new error ids; no auto-conversion of arbitrary render returns; no component-library machinery. If implementation hits a genuinely hard case — anything at the no-owner-at-creation edge (a callback lowered outside any boundary) that would be silent or ambiguous rather than the loud outside-boundary error above — STOP and return for a follow-up ruling instead of inventing policy.

WITNESSES to add (the ones rf2-2rtt6.35 deliberately withheld):
1. Two-frame ownership: a render-prop row's :on-click intent AND an event-position h/fn lowered inside the callback both fire LATER into the SUPPLYING boundary's recorder — two frames/recorders so the ownership assertion is non-vacuous.
2. Purity edges stay green UNMODIFIED: immediate direct *dispatch* call (host_hatch_dom_cljs_test deftest a-dispatch-from-a-declared-render-position-names-the-position) and synchronous lower-and-fire (intent_cljs_test deftest above) both still raise :rf.error/hicasso-dispatch-in-render-position.
3. Frame visibility: inside the invocation *frame* is the owner's (route-link in the row body, or a direct read).
At least one NEW witness must go through the declared-:render crossing (lower-declared-prop / host-hatch path) — the real renderRow seam.

HD-024 ADDENDUM (same PR): add a dated blockquote addendum to HD-024 in docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md, rf2-digtt pattern (cf. HD-019's 2026-08-03 addendum): both laws stand; enforcement is invocation-scoped (poison-while-active, owner-forward after; owner = the supplying boundary's frame); supersedes the Rationale sentence "enforced by poisoning the ambient dispatch for the call's dynamic extent" insofar as it implied handlers LOWERED inside stay poisoned forever. decisions.md is NOT covered by mkdocs --strict: verify anchors/table columns by hand and say so in the PR body.

title: The hicasso bench lane is compile-ungated: run.cjs passes with :undeclared-var warnings, and no PR gate compiles the arms
description:
FOUND by the rf2-2rtt6.70 worker while mutation-proving that bead's
repair. It is the same fail-open class rf2-2rtt6.70 names, one level up:
the bead worried about an ARM that measures deleted code, and the answer
to "why did nothing go red" turns out to be "nothing could have".

TWO FACTS, both measured on branch worker/frameprop-2rtt6-39.

1. NO PR GATE COMPILES `walk_profile_app.cljs` — or any other arm in
   the hicasso bench lane. `:node-test` selects `:ns-regexp "cljs-test$"`
   plus transitive requires, and nothing test-shaped requires the arms;
   `:browser-test` selects `-dom-cljs-test$` likewise. Verified by
   grepping the built bundles: `out/node-test.js` contains zero
   occurrences of `walk_profile_app`, and `out/browser-test/js/
   cljs-runtime/` has no such module. The ONLY compiler that ever sees
   these files is `:hicasso-bench`, driven by hand through `run.cjs`.

2. `run.cjs` DOES NOT FAIL ON COMPILE WARNINGS. It checks the
   shadow-cljs child process's exit status and nothing else
   (`if (r.status !== 0)`), and shadow-cljs exits 0 with warnings. The
   mutation that proved it: rename `M-NO-PROPLESS`'s def and leave its
   two use sites alone. Result —

     [:hicasso-bench] Build completed. (186 files, 131 compiled,
                      2 warnings, 35.49s)
     ------ WARNING #1 - :undeclared-var ------
      Use of undeclared Var re-frame.bench.hicasso.walk-profile-app/M-NO-PROPLESS
     ... [hicasso] ok
     MUT_WALK_EXIT=0

   Two undeclared vars, a full run, a printed table of numbers, and
   exit 0. Under `:advanced` an undeclared var is `undefined` at the
   call site, so an arm can silently become a different arm and still
   publish a plausible ns/element.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY. This lane's whole product is numbers,
and its arms are deliberately LOCAL copies of shipping code (that is the
call-convention discipline rf2-2rtt6.32 established and it is correct).
Local copies drift by construction; the only thing standing between a
drifted copy and a published figure is a gate. There is none.

THE WORK, and the cheap half is most of the value:

  a. Make `run.cjs` refuse a build that emitted warnings — parse the
     shadow-cljs output for `WARNING #` / `warnings,` in the build line,
     or pass a compiler option that promotes them. Exit 1 with the
     warning text. This is the one that would have caught the mutation.
  b. Decide whether the lane wants a compile-only PR gate over
     `re-frame.bench.hicasso.**` (a `shadow-cljs compile hicasso-bench`
     with no browser run is ~35-40s and needs no quiet box, so it does
     NOT contend with the measurement lane). If yes, wire it into
     `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh`'s node tier or a workflow; if no, say so
     on this bead so the next worker does not re-derive the question.

NOT a measurement task and NOT clock-contending: (a) is a driver change,
(b) is a compile.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #7423 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7423).

BOTH HALVES DONE, and the finding was WIDER than the bead.

(a) THE DRIVER FIX — and it was ELEVEN drivers, not one. The bead named run.cjs; in fact run.cjs, chrome_run, clock_run, coldmount_run, hd8_run, hd8_clock_run, ime_run, jsfb_build, p0_converge_run, retention_run and z3vlz_run each carried their own hand-rolled copy of the same eight lines with the same hole. A reader of this bead would have fixed one file and believed the lane was safe. lane_build.cjs is now the lane's ONE build door; all eleven route through it. It captures shadow's output rather than inheriting the stream and refuses on: non-zero exit; warnings>0 in any parsed summary; NO parsable summary at all; and a WARNING block the summary did not account for. The last two exist so this fix does not itself fail open.

CONSEQUENCE WORTH RECORDING: mutation proofs previously taken through any of those eleven drivers were worth less than they appeared — other workers used this lane today.

(b) THE COMPILE GATE — ANSWERED YES. npm run test:hicasso-compile compiles every lane namespace (101 today), warnings fatal, ~30s. Wired into the cljs CI job AND the fast-PR spine's node tier. Hosted in cljs rather than cljs-examples-compile because cljs_node_test includes implementation/core/*, which examples_compile deliberately excludes — and a core change is exactly what breaks a local copy of core's calling convention.

NO shadow-cljs.edn EDIT. The gate rides :hicasso-bench via --config-merge exactly as every arm rides it, so HD-017's hot-zone sequencing was not paid. The entry list is DERIVED by walking the tree — proven auto-covering: it compiled 100 namespaces pre-rebase and 101 post-rebase, picking up a newly landed arm with no edit.

PREMISE CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY: grep -c walk_profile_app out/node-test.js = 0; no module under out/browser-test/; control grep p0_converge_order = 1 (so the absence is real, not a broken search).

MUTATION-PROVED BOTH WAYS on the final rebased tree. Mutated: driver exits 1, names WARNING #1/#2 - :undeclared-var, and NEVER REACHES THE MEASUREMENT (HICASSO RUNTIME count 0) — where before the fix the same mutation exited 0 after printing a full table. Reverted byte-identically: driver exits 0 with a full measurement, gate exits 0 at 101 namespaces/0 warnings.

NO PRE-EXISTING WARNINGS were revealed, so nothing was silenced.

GATES: test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 (PASS fast PR spine); test:browser exit 0 (1036 tests/6409 assertions, 0 failures); lane_build.test.cjs 11 passed.

REMAINING GAP FILED as rf2-2rtt6.77 (P3): the compile gate is dev-mode, so :advanced-only breakage in an arm nobody runs is still ungated; that bead also records that the ~15 driver .cjs files are compiled/linted by nothing.

title: MEASURE the frame-as-a-prop variant: heap ladder, mount/bulk clock, studio row
description:
SPLIT OUT of rf2-2rtt6.39 by its worker. rf2-2rtt6.39 is a MEASURE bead
with five scope items; the correctness half (1, 2, 4) is built and
witnessed on branch worker/frameprop-2rtt6-39. Items 3 and 5 are clock
and heap work and were explicitly out of that worker's brief — the box
was oversubscribed by five concurrent workers and the instrument lane
belongs to the siblings who own it.

WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE (do not re-derive it):

  * The prop-threaded variant exists beside the incumbent, both minted
    from one body: front/codec.cljs `mark-frame-prop!` / `root-element`,
    arm1/runtime.cljs `frame-prop-shell` / `mint-frame-prop-view!`.
  * HOOK COUNT, at React's own dispatcher, same probe and same page for
    both variants: context shell 2 (useContext + useSyncExternalStore),
    frame-prop shell 1 (useSyncExternalStore). It does not move with the
    read count on the 1/7/20 rungs.
  * MULTI-FRAME ISOLATION HOLDS. One app in two isolated frames, driven
    through BOTH variants identically; no read crosses. A foreign
    component in the middle preserves the frame through props.children.
    Item 4 of the bead's scope is therefore GREEN, and the hypothesis is
    not dead.
  * ONE DEFECT THE VARIANT CREATES was found and repaired in the same
    commit: React propagates a context change ahead of the memo
    comparator, so the incumbent cannot be bailed out of a frame change;
    a frame-fed boundary can, because the frame is a prop and props are
    the one channel React.memo blocks. `boundary-props=` now compares
    `rfFrame`. The incumbent pays one `identical?` on two undefineds —
    if the ladder wants that gone, a second comparator is the lever, and
    the reason it was declined is written on the fn.

WHAT REMAINS (rf2-2rtt6.39 scope items 3 and 5, verbatim in spirit):

  3. Price RETAINED HEAP per boundary on the 1/3/7/20 ladder, and the
     clock on mount + bulk, for BOTH variants in ONE run against the
     SAME witnesses. Browser numbers only, :advanced, per HD-012
     (decisions.md:256-258); JVM/Node figures are diagnostic and are
     never quotable against the bar. The ledger to beat: the P0 record
     prices an isolated useSyncExternalStore rung at ~516 B
     (charter.md:66-69), of the same order as the whole 0.4-0.5 KB
     boundary-shell target (validation.md:37) — so this is shell-budget
     relevant, not a rounding error. Against it, the cost side is one
     extra entry in every boundary element's props map on every render.
  5. Publish to docs/design/hicasso/studio/ and append to the standard
     bead rf2-2rtt6.1 with the producing commit SHA and the repro
     command.

Also update `retained-inventory`: the frame-fed variant does NOT hold
`:react/use-context`, and the ladder reads that table.

MEASUREMENT POSTURE (unchanged from the parent): quiet box, do not
contend with the instrument workers.
notes:
PROGRESS 2026-08-04 (worker, quiet box). HEAP HALF DONE AND PUBLISHED; CLOCK HALF BLOCKED. Bead stays OPEN — see below.

PR #7454. Producing tree `2303ef6781`, published by `17c7156041`, branch worker/frameprop-2rtt6-72.

SCOPE ITEM 3, heap — DONE. R=0 shell, directly measured, B=1,200, six rounds, Q=E, A1->B->A2 in one session on `p0_run.cjs --only ladder`:
  Reagent segment: context 1,098 / 1,100  ->  frame-prop 1,054   = -45.0 B, -4.1%
  UIx segment:     context 1,096 / 1,099  ->  frame-prop 1,051   = -46.5 B, -4.2%
Bands disjoint both segments (21-25 B and 36-39 B clear air). Slope 1,278 / 2,115 B/read in ALL THREE runs — exactly R-independent. THE VARIANT WINS ON HEAP.

Against the 1 KB line: context+no-wrapper 994/992 = 0.99x (rf2-2rtt6.58); context+wrapper 1,099.5/1,097 = 1.10x; frame-prop+wrapper 1,054/1,051 = 1.05x. IT DOES NOT CLEAR THE LINE — it returns 45 of the wrapper's 105 B (43%), and the saving is BELOW validation.md's ~75 B shape sensitivity, so the A/B comparison stands while the absolute position against 1 KB does not. NOT an alternative to HD-028's pre-registered fallback. No disposition proposed — operator's call.

Prediction registered before the first build and quoted beside the result: |delta| < 100 B, direction NOT predicted, slope unchanged. All MET.

Validity: 3 runs all exit 0; 0 unverified of 154 mounts each; positive control ok under lane/control-verdict +/-25% (0.9997/0.9995/0.9995), the only band registered; arm-order guard reportable; structural read-back every field answered and zero after teardown. Donors reproduce their published anchor (947 and 2,979-2,980 B/read). The A arm reproduces rf2-2rtt6.58's published main rows TO HALF A BYTE (1,099.0/1,097.5 vs 1,099.5/1,097; slope exact). Box quiet: 2.27% / 3.04% / 1.80% real occupancy (summed per-process CPU-time deltas over core count; LoadPercentage NOT used), zero java, no other worker, no open PR.

The toggle is ONE SYMBOL in arm1/lang.clj's defview (mint-view! -> mint-frame-prop-view!). NEITHER SHELL EDITED — both variants already ship from one body. Reverted byte-identically for A2 (blob back to 74cfbfab7e, status clean). The ablation cannot fail silently: resolve-frame-prop! raises :rf.error/no-frame-prop on a nil frame rather than falling back to context.

  [clock] FAILED: M1: page.evaluate: vj        exit 1
  [clock] FAILED: bulk300: page.evaluate: vj   exit 1
That is the INCUMBENT arm on a pristine tree — reproduced at the shipped runtime blob 9f3d42be7b, and again with mount.cljs reverted to the pre-#7416 render! — so it is neither this variant's nor PR #7416's. `vj` is cljs.core/ExceptionInfo: the driver printed a minified type name and discarded the :rf.error id and ex-data. Driver's own offline adjudicators all healthy (--selftest exit 0, 49 checks). FILED rf2-029ed (P1).

WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD: the mount + bulk clock rows, once rf2-029ed unblocks clock_run.cjs. Nothing else.
HOLD ruled 2026-08-07 (delegated, overturnable): context shell stays; clock rows demand-gated on a sitting/v0 naming a use for the freed hook slot or the ~45 B. See decision comment.
close_reason: TRIAGE vs hic-* set (rf2-6bj7, 2026-08-10, delegated, operator-overturnable): CLOSED as a DECLINED optimization — not superseded; no hic-* bead covers or needs it. Verified today: rf2-hic-018's deliverables (substrate adjudication for the under-collector, two-hook ceiling frozen, R=0 shell disposition) name NO present need for the freed hook slot or the ~45 B — the one condition under which this stayed open. The 2026-08-07 delegated HOLD already established the substance: the -45.0/-46.5 B heap win is real (bands disjoint) but buys no gate (frame-prop+wrapper 1.05x vs context 1.10x against the 1 KB line; below validation.md's ~75 B shape sensitivity; NOT an alternative to HD-028's pre-registered fallback), it adds a second frame-delivery invariant with ongoing maintenance cost, and the published heap pair is stale against the since-churned codec. The variant code remains live in the extracted package (implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs and inventory.cljs) and the toggle remains one symbol. REOPEN TRIGGER (unchanged from the HOLD ruling): a sitting, a v0 heap-hardening pass, or hic-018's adjudication naming a concrete use for the freed hook slot (2 to 1 in a fully spent two-hook budget) or the ~45 B — then the adoption bar stands exactly as written in the 2026-08-07 comment: (a) current-tree paired A1-B-A2 heap re-take, (b) reportable M1 + bulk clock rows with no regression, (c) the named concrete near-term use; all existing witnesses preserved as gates.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-07 10:29 AUSEST, operator-overturnable): HOLD. defview keeps the context-fed mint-view! shell. The frame-as-a-prop variant is not adopted now, and its clock rows are DEMAND-GATED rather than queued — do not spend a quiet-box slot on them unless the trigger below fires. Bead moves to deferred with that trigger; the heap half's publication obligations are complete.

WHY (weighing the dossier recommendation and Codex's independent code inspection, which converged on hold but differed on adoption conditions — the stricter bar is adopted because it follows from verified code, not caution):

1. The saving does not buy a gate. -45.0 B / -4.1% (Reagent) and -46.5 B / -4.2% (UIx) are real (bands disjoint), but frame-prop+wrapper still fails the 1 KB paper line (1.05x vs context's 1.10x), returns only 45 of the wrapper's 105 B (43%), and sits below validation.md's ~75 B component-shape sensitivity. Explicitly NOT an alternative to HD-028's pre-registered fallback. A variant that changes no verdict is optionality, not need.

2. It is a performance trade, not an architectural simplification. Verified today: the provider is still installed regardless (mount.cljs render! docstring — the other React-shaped adapters, the error boundary, and the presence tray resolve their frame from context), so the variant does not remove the context channel; it ADDS a second frame-delivery channel with its own invariant: heads marked, rfFrame stamped at element creation, root-element required at ancestor-less creators, and rfFrame compared in the memo comparator (codec.cljs ~814-848, 889-906, 2044-2053, 2777-2796). React context pierces memo; props do not — so the comparator MUST account for the frame, and frame_prop_dom_cljs_test.cljs:268-287 (a-frame-change-with-unchanged-props-still-re-renders) is the witness that this failure mode is real, not theoretical. The fallback-minted-nil edge it already exposed (fenced by refusal, fallback_contents_cljs_test.cljs:34-47, 305-319) is evidence of repair AND of the ongoing maintenance cost of the second channel. Here the codec, not the author, threads the prop, so the usual explicit-data-flow benefit of props does not accrue.

3. The published heap result is mechanism evidence, not a current-tree receipt. The experiment pinned arm1/lang.clj 74cfbfab7e77, arm1/runtime.cljs 8b37dd2cbf67, front/codec.cljs cf9ef32dc8f75; verified today at HEAD 8fd35f25fd the same paths are 8c18fb0c4d43 / 3ac9dcd7579e / 378de06fdc6d. The codec has churned heavily since the runs. Any adoption decision needs the pair re-taken on the tree it would land on.

ADOPTION BAR (all three required; recorded so a future sitting doesn't relitigate from scratch):
  (a) a current-tree paired A1->B->A2 heap re-take reproducing the win on the exact tree proposed for adoption;
  (b) reportable M1 and bulk clock rows for the variant with no reportable regression;
  (c) a CONCRETE NEAR-TERM USE for the freed hook slot (context shell 2 hooks -> frame-prop 1, in a fully spent <=2 budget) — named by a sitting or a v0 heap-hardening pass. Mere future optionality is insufficient: 45-46.5 B alone does not repay a second frame-delivery invariant.
Adoption must also preserve the existing witnesses as gates: multi-frame isolation, foreign-child frame preservation, same-props frame-change, root/outward-bridge, SSR/hydration, and fallback-refusal.

TRIGGER to un-defer: a P2 sitting (or v0 heap-hardening pass) names the freed hook slot or the ~45 B as needed — then run (a)+(b) in one quiet-box window and dispose. rf2-029ed (the clock_run.cjs refusal that blocked scope item 3) is CLOSED, so the rows are runnable the day the trigger fires; the toggle remains one symbol in arm1/lang.clj's defview (mint-view! -> mint-frame-prop-view!), reverted byte-identically in the experiment, with resolve-frame-prop! raising :rf.error/no-frame-prop rather than falling back silently.

(Concurs with the census quiet-box session review: these rows do NOT join that window.)

title: hicasso: the sub-index's reverse edge duplicates the cell table's key space — the largest per-read elimination still on the table
description:
FOUND during rf2-aqgr2, which attacked the per-read gap and landed one
elimination (-107 B/read). This is the biggest one it costed and did NOT
take, because it is a redesign rather than a byte shave.

THE OBSERVATION. On the distinct-query rung the ladder is taken on, the
Arm 1 read path keeps TWO process-global persistent maps keyed by the
SAME B·R sub-keys:

  arm1/runtime.cljs   !cells     sub-key -> the key cell (reaction, epoch, refs)
  front/sub_index.cljs :sub->bs  sub-key -> #{boundary-id}   the reverse edges

Every read therefore pays two persistent-hash-map entries where the
design needs one table keyed by sub-key, plus — at fan-out 1, which is
what Q = E means — a SINGLETON PersistentHashSet per key whose whole job
is to hold one pointer.

THE PRICE, partly measured. rf2-aqgr2 measured one retained hash-set
membership at +46 B/read (Reagent segment) / +47 (UIx) by forcing
`record-reads` to copy the forward edge and re-taking the ladder
(p0_run.cjs --only ladder, 6 rounds, donors unmoved). That prices the
MEMBERSHIP, not the whole singleton-set-plus-map-entry shape, so the
reverse edge's total is not yet split out. It is plausibly the single
largest remaining term in the +391 B/read bill (down from +499).

THE CANDIDATE ELIMINATION. Put the reader set on the cell — one table
keyed by sub-key holding both the reaction and its readers — and the
second map, its per-key entry and its per-key set object all go away.
`dirty-boundaries` becomes a walk of the dirty cells' reader sets;
`commit!` already receives cells (`flush!` maps `.-subKey` over them and
the index maps them straight back).

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE UNDER rf2-aqgr2:

- it dissolves `front/sub-index`'s role in Arm 1, and that namespace is
  the SHARED FRONT HALF with its own six-law discharge
  (`front/sub_index_laws_cljs_test`);
- `architecture.md:33-35` states the design claim in terms of those
  maps ("index edges live in global maps — shared structure, not
  per-boundary object fan-out"), so the doc moves with the code;
- it is a design decision about where the dependency index LIVES, which
  is above a perf bead's pay grade.

WHAT A DISPATCH NEEDS TO DECIDE FIRST: does the reverse edge stay a
general, separately-testable algebra (its current value), or does Arm 1
own one fused key table now that the tournament is over and the shared
front half may be evolved as the adapter needs (epic note, 2026-07-31)?

Measure on the same instrument and the same terms rf2-aqgr2 used:
`p0_run.cjs --only ladder`, 6 rounds, both donors riding as the same-run

title: machines validate-machine! throws a host ClassCastException on a non-Named node key
description:
FOUND while fixing rf2-oztox (machines-viz definition-summary disclosure) and
deliberately NOT fixed there: it is in implementation/machines, a different lane
from tools/machines-viz, and the viz walker is only a MIRROR of it.

implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:1432
carries the same defect the viz copy did:

  (->> (keys m) (remove #(namespace %)) (remove known) vec)

`namespace` THROWS on a key that is not `Named`. So a machine definition
carrying a String / number / vector / host-object key —

  {:initial :a :states {:a {}} "x" 1}

— raises a host ClassCastException out of `validate-machine!` instead of the
documented `:rf.error/machine-unknown-node-key`. `reg-machine`'s registration
gate is the boundary that promises the structured error, and a definition
assembled at runtime (merged from config, decoded from JSON, produced by a
generator) can carry a string key without anyone hand-writing one.

The viz mirror was made total in rf2-oztox by testing Named-ness before calling
`namespace`:

  (remove #(and (or (keyword? %) (symbol? %)) (namespace %)))

which preserves the namespaced-extension carve-out exactly and flags a
non-keyword key as `:rf.error/machine-unknown-node-key` — the right answer, since
a key that is not a keyword is not a legal node key under any reading of the
grammar. Line 192 of the same file has the same `(remove #(namespace %))` shape
and should be checked with it.

NOTE THE PARITY RATCHET. tools/machines-viz/test/.../engine_grammar_parity_test.cljc
asserts viz and engine give the same accept/reject answer. Its corpus carries no
non-keyword keys, so the divergence rf2-oztox just introduced is invisible to it
today — the engine THROWS where viz now REJECTS. Closing this bead re-converges
them; the parity corpus should gain a non-Named-key case at the same time so the
two cannot drift apart again silently.

ACCEPTANCE: `validate-machine!` returns the documented
`:rf.error/machine-unknown-node-key` for a definition with a String / number /
vector / throwing-toString key at the root and at a node; the namespaced carve-out
is unchanged; the parity corpus gains a non-Named-key case.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7419. TWO defect sites, not one: unknown-bare-keys at validation.cljc:1432 AND an inline copy in the :spawn-all block check at :192 — a reader of the bead alone would have fixed one and shipped. Plus a SECOND partial operation one level down: (pr-str offending) in the diagnostic message reaches an arbitrary object's toString, so a throwing-toString key destroyed the failure being described. Both made total once via namespaced-key? + key-label (reusing error/diag-value-summary's closed vocabulary). Engine keeps NAMING offending scalar keys — deliberate divergence from the viz (rf2-oztox/#7408), whose caller is handed a share-URL definition while reg-machine holds its own. Parity ratchet: it was blind for a second reason the bead did not name — the probes were TWO-VALUED, so on CLJS engine-accepts?'s (catch :default … false) recorded a HOST CRASH as a CLEAN REJECTION. Two validators that both explode AGREE, and the equality assertion passes them; that is exactly how this hid. Fixed with three-valued engine-answer/viz-answer plus a definition-validation-is-total deftest, and 5 non-Named corpus entries. Proof it now sees the divergence: (engine :reject, viz :host-throw). Green after #7408 merged: 11 tests / 203 assertions.

title: reagent-slim's residual 1.19-1.24x over stock Reagent is no longer in the prop pipeline — two named candidates, unpursued
description:

TWO CANDIDATES THE CODE SUGGESTS, NEITHER COSTED:

  1. hiccup-shape allocates a 3-element PersistentVector per element — [head has-props first-child] — and every one of its five call sites destructures it immediately and discards it. has-props is (or (nil? head) (map? head)) and first-child is (+ first-pos (if has-props 1 0)); both are one expression. Any change is an adapter-wide one, not a local one.

  2. vec-to-elem asks four (= tag :>) / :<> / :r> / :f> compares before reaching the hiccup-tag? branch that every DOM element takes. cljs.core/= is a fn call that falls through identical? to a protocol -equiv dispatch on a miss, so the common head pays four of them. keyword-identical? is the idiomatic answer and reads as 'these are keyword sentinels'; a case may be better still. Prior art in the same instrument: the CANDIDATES table's dispatch-all-ship 23.6 -> dispatch-all-stringfirst 12.3 rows are the same question asked of Hicasso's dispatch.

METHOD, and it is not optional here. Absolute ns/op in this instrument moves with the box — rf2-lhdp0's three runs differ ~2x on arms that did not change — so cost each candidate BESIDE the shipping shape in ONE process on the page's own roster, the way the SLIM DECOMPOSED table already does, and read the arm RATIO for the verdict. title: reagent-slim's hiccup walk is 1.7-1.9x stock Reagent's, and its prop-name cache is the named term — measured, in a SHIPPED adapter
description:
MEASURED BY rf2-2rtt6.63 (PR #7390), as a by-product of putting three interpreters side by side on one witness value in one process. This is not a Hicasso finding — `day8/reagent-slim` is a PUBLISHED artefact and this is a defect in it.

THE ROWS (`walk_vs_reagent_app`, the census acceptance page's 1,202-element hiccup realized once outside every timed window, 4 arms × 6 rounds × (4 warmup + 10 samples), arm-order guard REPORTABLE on both runs, diagnostic in-page clock):

    slim / stock reagent   1.9020 (run 1)   1.7273 (run 2)
    slim ms/walk           1.2125 [1.1125-1.4500]  vs stock 0.6375 [0.6000-0.9000]
    ns/element             1,009  vs  530

THE NAMED TERM, from the same instrument's stage table over the page's own 1,489 prop occurrences:

    cached-prop-name   slim 49.4 / 53.4 ns/op   stock reagent 24.5 / 26.2   hicasso 21.5 / 16.8

So slim's prop-name lookup is ~2x stock Reagent's for the same answer, and it is asked once per prop on every element of every mount. Stock's is a `.hasOwnProperty` plus a `gobj/get`; slim's adds `reserved-prop-key?` as a SET lookup (a string hash for a roster of three) and `own-key?` as `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call`, both on the HIT path.

Hicasso's answer to exactly this shape is on main as of PR #7390 and is worth reading before re-deriving one: an `Object.create(null)` cache makes the false-hit class structurally impossible and moves the poisoning refusal to the MISS branch, which runs once per distinct literal for the life of the build rather than once per element per mount (18.1 -> 11.1 ns/op on the prop cache, 16.6 -> 11.2 on the tag cache; the fast-mode + `instance?` alternative was costed at 13.8 / 12.1 and declined).

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE NUMBER. Every HD-008 donor rung and the pre-Hicasso candidate ride `reagent2.impl.template`'s `:f>` walk and read 1.33-1.5x, and this is where that comes from — the donor rungs were measuring reagent-slim's walk, not "runtime interpretation" as such. Any consumer of `day8/reagent-slim` pays it today.

WHAT TO DO.

1. Profile slim's `convert-props` / `cached-prop-name` path element-by-element the way rf2-y1jkm profiled Hicasso's. DO NOT assume the prop-name cache is the whole 1.9x — the stage table names one term and the whole-walk gap is far larger than that term explains. title: hicasso: sequence the census mount re-take for rf2-2rtt6.63's increment behind rf2-cno31's route-link fix
description:
FROM rf2-2rtt6.63 (PR #7390). That bead's acceptance asks for the census mount row on the clock of record, candidate/uix-subs, before and after each increment. THE ROW WAS DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN, and this bead carries the obligation so it is not lost.

WHY IT WAS NOT TAKEN. rf2-cno31 owns the census-clock windows and its fix changes the acceptance and feed pages underneath any row taken now: the route-link render term is 8.21 us/link, 207 links on acceptance (1.70 ms of a ~10 ms mount) and 900 on the feed, and it is what took the feed row from 1.0875x back to 1.3311x. A row taken before that fix lands would be a third contested magnitude for the same pages.

AND THE INCREMENT'S SIZE ARGUES THE SAME WAY. rf2-2rtt6.63's decomposition prices the two cheapenings it landed at about 9% of the WALK, and the walk is ~0.66 ms of a ~10 ms mount — so about 0.6% of a mount, which is well inside every band the census clock has ever reported (3.9% at its tightest, 13.7% at its widest). A dedicated quiet window spent resolving 0.6% against a 4-14% band cannot answer anything.

WHAT TO DO. When rf2-cno31's fix has landed and it re-takes acceptance and feed, the row is already the after-row for this increment too — the codec change is on main by then. Read it as such and record the composition on docs/design/hicasso/studio/our-walk-against-reagents.md rather than opening a separate window. If cno31's re-take somehow does not carry the codec change, sequence one re-take after it, same instrument, same-run donors.
