One uninterrupted session should take all three — matched seeds, metric capture, and this increment's after-row — rather than three separate windows.

Sizing note carried forward so nobody re-derives it: the increment is ~9% of the walk, the walk is ~0.66 ms of a ~10 ms mount, so ~0.6% of a mount against a census band of 3.9-13.7%. If the quiet-box session is ever contended, this is the first row to drop — it cannot answer anything under load.
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-07, operator-overturnable) — SESSION SHAPE, superseding the three-item bundled session in the 2026-08-07 scheduling note above. The bundle is not instrument-ready; verified against the working tree today:

THE DECISION:
1. INSTRUMENT PREP LANDS BEFORE ANY WINDOW IS REQUESTED — all worker-sized, no quiet box needed: per-block metric persistence (.56 item 4 / rf2-jo60g), matched-cell roster (rf2-2rtt6.62 prep), skip-quiet routed non-canonical + mutation test (.56), then one reduced-depth dry run outside the publication window.

If it is NOT named relevant, rf2-jo60g's cheaper resolution is striking/annotating the unrecomputable 'layout 2.06x / style 1.85x / script 2.3x' prose — no window at all.

title: RULING NEEDED: the route planner's dedupe grain and the two :rf.runtime/routing identity slots collapse a byte-distinct scoped-key pair
description:
Found closing rf2-dlkou (audit of PR #7228). rf2-dlkou's repair made route-resource-plan's OWN identity arithmetic byte-exact (membership + the removal partition are keyed on state/key-id now, not Clojure =). Two carriers UPSTREAM and DOWNSTREAM of it still collapse the same pair, and closing them needs a ruling because it moves documented cross-feature shapes.

THE PAIR. Resource identity is state/key-id (CEDN-1 canonical bytes), which is collection-KIND sensitive (rf2-wgutc2). [:rf.scope/global :demo/x {:p [1 2]}] and [:rf.scope/global :demo/x {:p (1 2)}] are (= a b) TRUE and (count (set [a b])) 1, while state/key-id yields v[...v[i:1 i:2]] vs v[...l(i:1 i:2)] and state/entry-path yields two distinct cache slots. Verified on the JVM.

WHERE IT STILL COLLAPSES.
1. resources/route.cljc collapse-and-order — (group-by :scoped-key occs). Two route entries in one branch requiring the same resource+scope with vector-vs-list params group into ONE dedup-req, so ONE ensure is dispatched and the second byte identity is never fetched. That is a DISPATCH defect, not a diagnostic one, which is why it was fenced out of rf2-dlkou.
2. The handoff slot [:rf.runtime/routing :resource-plan <nav-token>] is documented as #{<scoped-key> ...}, and its sibling [:rf.runtime/routing :resource-blocking <nav-token>] likewise. A Clojure set cannot hold both members of the pair, so even a byte-exact planner cannot hand both to the next activation, and reconcile-readiness prunes a blocking set whose membership is =-based while looking entries up by byte path.

WHY IT NEEDS A RULING. The fix is a shape change to two cross-feature runtime-db slots, documented in spec/Spec-Schemas.md (:rf.runtime/routing), spec/016-Resources.md, and implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc, plus routing/events.cljc which reads and writes them. The natural shape is the one :entries already uses — {<key-id> <scoped-key>} — which also carries no order promise and so preserves rf2-dlkou's ruling that removal has no meaningful order. But Mike's ruling ON rf2-dlkou declined a cross-feature slot change once already (for the ordering question), so this one should be decided rather than assumed.

ALTERNATIVE WORTH CONSIDERING: rule that a scoped key's params are CANONICALIZED to vectors at construction (state/scoped-resource-key), making the =-collapse correct everywhere instead of making every carrier byte-exact. That is the smaller change but it retires a distinction the repo currently calls supported (rf2-wgutc2), so it is equally a ruling.

REACHED TODAY? A single plan needs two route entries whose :params fns return a vector and a list for the same resource+scope — constructible, not accidental. The cross-navigation case (prior plan list, next plan vector) is REPAIRED by rf2-dlkou and pinned by r2-identity-membership-is-byte-exact-not-clojure-equal in resources_route_cljs_test.
close_reason: PR #7443 — option (a) implemented: the planner's dedupe grain and both :rf.runtime/routing identity slots (:resource-plan, :resource-blocking) are byte-exact {(state/key-id k) k} maps with no order promise. collapse-and-order groups by key-id (stamped once in materialize-occurrences); reconcile-readiness + the SSR blocking drain + the plan diff read the carriers' own keys; xray's panel read adapts. Spec surgical: Spec-Schemas :rf.runtime/routing (2 lines), 016 Plan diff + readiness (2 hunks), 012 readiness cell (1 line), 009 no-order evidence reworded to the map with the no-order promise KEPT. Twin regression added and MUTATION-PROVEN both directions: reintroducing the =-grain dedupe exits 1 with 16 failures, all in the two new deftests naming the collapsed pair; reverted byte-identically -> 0 failures. resources_cache_key_identity (0 lines), r2-identity-membership-is-byte-exact (0 lines) and r2-removed-identities-is-membership (0 assertion changes; 3 prose spots corrected) all stayed green. Gates: test-fast-pr.sh 0, test-jvm-implementation.sh 0, test-jvm-tools.sh 0, npm test:cljs 0 (12500 tests). No guardrail built — the Xray =-equal-sibling lint stays a separate ruling.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RULING 2026-08-03 15:46 AUSEST — delegated dossier-review ruling (Mike's 2026-08-03 directive); operator-overturnable.

DECISION: (a) — CEDN-1 byte identity stays authoritative; make the last two =-based carriers byte-exact using the established shape {(state/key-id scoped-key) scoped-key}. Option (b) (canonicalise params to vectors at construction) is REJECTED on verified facts, not taste. Option (c) rejected: the collapse is a real dispatch defect in a documented slot.

WHY (b) FAILS — every one of the counter-recommendation's factual attacks HELD under verification:
1. VERIFIED: the live route path never calls the defensive state/scoped-resource-key. route.cljc:720-723 builds keys with scoped-resource-key* from params canonicalized upstream (registry/validate+canonicalize-params) + scope via resolve-scope-for-event; scoped-resource-key* does not re-canonicalize (rf2-rplgkw). Changing scoped-resource-key alone fixes NOTHING on this bug — (b)'s "one choke point" premise is false as written.
2. VERIFIED: Spec 016 §Canonicalization rule says "this artefact does not define a second canonicalizer... sets and vectors keep their value semantics." A resource-local seq->vector coercion violates it; moving coercion into CEDN-1 itself (Conventions) rewrites identity for the whole framework — vastly broader than this bug.
3. VERIFIED: b53c1195d7 (Mike-authored, rf2-wgutc2) DELIBERATELY removed the old resource-local list->vector canonicalizer: "it collapsed lists->vectors; now the list-vs-vector EDN distinction is preserved." (b) re-introduces the exact divergence Mike ruled out.
4. VERIFIED: 8589517857 (rf2-9e0tyq) byte-keyed all 4 cache carriers and explicitly rejected normalization: "No list-to-vector normalize (would re-erase the kind)" — and byte-keying surfaced 3 latent production =-collapse bugs, evidence the byte grain does real work.
5. VERIFIED: resources_cache_key_identity_cljs_test.cljc adversarially pins kind-preservation across 4 carriers, incl. "the list entry's :resource/key PRESERVES the list kind (not coerced to a vector)". (b) flips deliberate pins.
6. HELD (structural): scope is arbitrary canonical CEDN too; a vector-vs-list nested in SCOPE collapses identically, so honest (b) means deep-normalizing scope+params — a broad semantic change, not the dossier's one-liner.
So (b) is neither the smaller change nor a fix at the point it names; it fights the repo's ruled, spec'd, adversarially-tested identity architecture. (a) is the same pattern already applied by rf2-9e0tyq (cache carriers) and rf2-dlkou/PR #7391 (planner arithmetic), extended to the last known =-based carriers — one identity story: identity-bearing collections key on state/key-id, values stay kind-preserving scoped keys.

FOOTGUN ASSESSMENT (map->mapv renames a resource): real but self-healing — worst case is a cache-miss refetch under the new identity, and the REQUIRED :params-schema is where an author pins param shape (vec at the boundary). No machinery here. If Mike wants a guardrail (e.g. Xray lint for =-equal-but-byte-distinct sibling keys), that is a separate explicitly-scoped ruling, not this bug.

rf2-wgutc2 DISPOSITION: its kind-distinctness claim STANDS unchanged under (a). NB the id no longer resolves in bd (compacted); nothing to amend. rf2-dlkou stays closed; its close reason already names this bead as exact owner of the handoff shape.

IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF (single worker; spec files are HOT-ZONE — mayor sequences):
- resources/route.cljc: collapse-and-order (~:791) groups + builds the topo graph by (state/key-id scoped-key) (group-of, group-by, gkeys/gedges/group-rank); dedup-req keeps the kind-preserving scoped-key value. Plan return :identities and :blocking become {key-id scoped-key} maps (no order promise — preserves rf2-dlkou's withdrawn-ordering ruling). reconcile-readiness + clear-blocking-slot prune/dissoc by key-id. Plan-diff (:ensured/:kept/:removed + identity vectors ~:1060-1180) reads prev/next off the maps' own keys (the "one derivation of the identity" comment already points there). Rewrite the "WHAT REMAINS" comment ~:1176.
- resources/ssr.cljc: the reconcile-readiness/blocking drain consumes the map shape.
- routing/events.cljc ~:253/:296/:302: prev-identities read + the two assoc-in writes carry maps; verify (seq (:blocking plan)) sites.
- routing/readiness.cljc project-at-commit: consumes :blocking as a map.
- core/late_bind/directory.cljc :routing/on-route-entry description (~:645): :blocking/:identities shapes -> byte-keyed maps.
- SPEC (hot-zone): Spec-Schemas.md :rf.runtime/routing bullet (~:2952) — both slots {<nav-token> {<key-id> <scoped-key>}}; 016-Resources.md (2 refs); 012-Routing.md (6 refs, readiness prose); 009-Instrumentation.md (2 refs — reword the no-order evidence clause "the handoff records a set and hands it back" to the map, keep the no-order promise). ep-0037-r2-* fixture mentions are prose-only; verify no shape pin.
- Ordered trace vectors STAY vectors; only unordered identity carriers become maps. No new panel/public plan value (rf2-9sluz descope stands).
- TESTS: end-to-end twin regression (the acceptance the rf2-dlkou audit demanded): one plan containing BOTH members of a byte-distinct =-equal pair as two route entries -> two dedup-reqs, two ensures, both identities in the :resource-plan map, both independently blocking/reconciled/SSR-drained; and a transition keeping one + removing the other -> exact :kept-identities/:removed-identities/counts + next handoff. Existing pins (resources_cache_key_identity, r2-identity-membership-is-byte-exact, r2-removed-identities-is-membership) stay green unchanged.
- NOT touched: state.cljc constructors, identity.cljc, any canonicalizer.

title: hicasso: h/boundary lowers its fallback and its children with no ambient frame - the retry button HD-020(c) sells cannot be written
description: Sibling of rf2-2rtt6.66, found while repairing it; NOT fixed there because that bead names presence. arm1/boundary.cljs's render does (codec/as-element (if (fn? fallback) (fallback error) fallback)) / (codec/as-element (into [:<>] children)) with NO intent/with-frame binding. Both the FALLBACK and the CHILDREN are hiccup DATA written in the parent boundary's body but LOWERED inside the class component's own React render, where intent/*dispatch* is unbound - the identical mechanism rf2-2rtt6.66 repaired in presence. Consequence: an intent vector at an event position on a fallback node, or on a native child of h/boundary, raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary at render; an h/fn declared :event there raises the same id at invocation. The fallback half is the sharper one and is the surface HD-020(c) is sold on - a fallback whose whole point is a RETRY control ([:button {:on-click [:app/retry]}] beside :reset-key) cannot be written today, and a fallback that fails to render lands the app in the boundary's own error path. REPAIR: identical shape to rf2-2rtt6.66 and CHEAPER - the class already resolves its frame through contextType (frame-of, used by report! for the :on-error intent), so no new hook and no new accessor: wrap both as-element calls in intent/with-frame with rt/frame-dispatch, nil-tolerant the same way presence is. WITNESS: a fallback carrying a retry intent, clicked, plus a native child of h/boundary carrying one; both intent shapes; and the frameless case still naming the intent. arm1/presence_intent_dom_cljs_test is the template - its own h/boundary uses are deliberately fallback-intent-free and cite this bead.
close_reason: Fixed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7389 (branch worker/bdyframe-uo9di). arm1/boundary's render now binds intent/with-frame around its ONE crossing — the fallback and the children both — resolving the frame through the contextType accessor report! already used (frame-of), with runtime/frame-dispatch's memoised frame-locked dispatch. No new hook and no new accessor: the class had its frame already, which is why this was cheaper than rf2-2rtt6.66's presence repair. The binding is unconditional and carries nil with no provider, so a frameless boundary stays legal and an intent under one is still the loud error naming the intent. Reproduced first, on HD-020(c)'s own advertised case: a fallback retry button raised :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary with :intent [:bdy/retry], escaping to the boundary above. New witness arm1/boundary_intent_dom_cljs_test carries 7 rows — retry button + reset-key round trip, h/fn on a function fallback, both shapes on a native child (separate subjects, since the shapes fail at different moments), frame isolation against a second live frame, the frameless case, and a hook-ledger row proving the class spends none even in its error state. Mutation red/green: binding absent EXIT=1 (7 failures + 3 errors, all in the new ns, naming the error id); binding present EXIT=0 (1002 tests, 6229 assertions). Gates: test:browser 0, test:cljs 0 (12387 tests), clj-kondo 2026.04.15 errors 0; CI 48/48 pass. NOT merged — the mayor merges.

title: hicasso: presence lowers its children with no ambient frame - intent props on any presence child are loud-dead
description: Found while proving the host hatch (rf2-2rtt6.65). arm1/presence.cljs presence-body renders retained children via (codec/as-element (into [:<>] (presence/render next))) with NO intent/with-frame binding: children handed to h/presence are hiccup DATA created in the parent boundary's body but LOWERED inside the presence component's own React render, where rstate.frame is nil and intent/*dispatch* is unbound. Consequence, for NATIVE and HOST children alike: an intent VECTOR at an event position on a presence child raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary at render; an h/fn declared/lowered :event that returns an intent raises the same id at invocation. Loud, never silent - but a toast with an inline dismiss button ([:div.toast {:key id :on-click [:toasts/dismiss id]}]) cannot be written under presence today, which contradicts the ruling's whole pitch (the inline tray with no child view). Repair sketch: presence-body resolves the frame once (useContext adapter-context/frame-context - presence is not a boundary shell, HD-020's budget does not apply to it, but its docstring's 'two hooks in THIS component' claim must be updated) and wraps its as-element call in intent/with-frame with the frame-locked dispatch (runtime's memoised frame-dispatch needs a public accessor, or presence goes through rt/dispatch!). Witness: a keyed native child with an :on-click intent + a host child with a declared :event h/fn, both dispatching from the retained AND live phases. The host-hatch suite (arm1/host_hatch_dom_cljs_test) deliberately keeps its presence-tray children callback-free and cites this bead.
close_reason: PR #7388 completed the exact owner: presence resolves the shared provider context and re-binds the stable frame dispatch around its one child-lowering call; browser witnesses cover native vectors, h/fn invocation, retained children, two-frame isolation, child boundaries, frameless diagnostics and the hook ledger. The unavailable defhost-specific witness remains in the active host-hatch owner rf2-2rtt6.65.

title: hicasso: the host hatch, proven end-to-end (charter v0, HD-011)
description: Charter v0 requires 'one host hatch proven'; use case D9 names the claim: hosting React libraries via the one door (defhost) - value/callback, hook/context/ref/compound owners, React-owned animation. SWEPT STATE (2026-08-02): what exists is the CONTRACT HALF ONLY. front/intent.cljs carries lower-declared-prop + declared-callback (the position-table second row: a defhost :callbacks entry's :event/:handler/:render contract, never inferred from an on* spelling), witnessed at closure level in front/intent_cljs_test (a-declaration-can-name-the-contract-instead-of-the-position: :event dispatch, variadic multi-arg forwarding, :handler identity passthrough, unknown-contract refusal). THE DOOR ITSELF DOES NOT EXIST: front/codec.cljs vec->element knows fragment/native/boundary heads only and its docstring names defhost/[:>] interop as deliberately absent (HD-011 - its own surface); no defhost declaration form, no host head, no witness anywhere of a real foreign React component (own useState/useEffect/useContext/ref) hosted through a declared door, driven from Hicasso subs, dispatching intents, surviving presence/re-renders, tearing down clean. Freehand's host_door/host_mounted witnesses are the predecessor's, not Hicasso's. WORK: build the minimal HD-011 door in the bench (mint-host! + host head + host-element in front/codec.cljs, defhost macro in arm1/lang.clj: declared :callbacks normalized to canonical slots, shallow prop conversion, hiccup children to elements, functions pass by identity, :ref callback pass-through with the HD-022 vector refusal, loud refusal of an event-spelled vector/key-map at an UNDECLARED position rather than silent inert data) and prove it end-to-end in arm1/host_hatch_dom_cljs_test against a worst-reasonable-case in-test foreign component: value in from subs, declared :event (incl multi-arg + ::h/prevent + ::h/value marker) and :handler out, React-owned state surviving boundary re-renders and a presence transition around the host, ref attach/detach per the React 19 cleanup-return contract, teardown to the residue witnesses' standard, hook-probe proof that the door adds no Hicasso hooks (the hosted component's hooks are its own affair), React.memo interaction stated honestly. Mutation-prove the dispatch witness and the teardown witness. [:>] raw escape stays unbuilt (secondary; finding if needed).
notes: Door built (mint-host!/host-head?/host-element in front/codec.cljs, defhost in arm1/lang.clj) + 13-deftest proof suite arm1/host_hatch_dom_cljs_test.cljs. Gates so far: test:cljs exit 0 (12369 tests / 61825 assertions, 0 fail); test:browser exit 0 (992 tests / 6188 assertions, 0 fail). Mutation-proved: (1) declared-callback :event gutted -> browser exit 1, exactly the host dispatch witness red; (2) mount/unmount! gutted -> browser exit 1, 14 reds incl all three teardown-witness assertions (hosted cleanups, React 19 ref cleanup, residue census); both restored -> exit 0. Finding filed: rf2-2rtt6.66 (presence lowers children with no ambient frame; intent props on any presence child loud-dead). fast-pr spine + pinned kondo 2026.04.15 in flight.
close_reason:
The host hatch is proven end-to-end. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7396 (NOT merged - the mayor merges).

WHAT EXISTED: the contract half alone. front/intent.cljs could lower a declared :callbacks entry and front/intent_cljs_test witnessed what it lowered TO, at closure level - no door, no foreign component, no DOM. front/codec.cljs named defhost/[:>] interop as deliberately absent and vec->element knew three head classes. Nothing to prove the charter claim against.

BUILT: front/codec.cljs mint-host! (declaration: :callbacks normalized to canonical slots at mint, contracts validated, structural slots + two-spellings-one-slot collisions refused, nil component refused at the declaration site), host-head?, host-entry/host-element (the crossing). arm1/lang.clj defhost - a def of the minted head, no body read, not a compiler. [:>] stays unbuilt (HD-011 explicitly secondary, census-zero). The head contributes no wrapper, no fiber, no hook.

PROVED in arm1/host_hatch_dom_cljs_test.cljs against a worst-reasonable-case component (2x useState, useEffect+cleanup, useContext below the crossing, forwarded ref, three invoker styles): value in and moving with the sub; hosted PROVIDER with consumer below; hiccup children as React children; declared :event dispatching with EVERY invoker argument forwarded; ::h/prevent preventing on the real event then dispatching; ::h/value materializing across the door (the guide open question, answered - it works exactly when the foreign contract hands the event first); :handler crossing by identity with its return going back to the foreign caller; ref attach + the React 19 returned-cleanup on detach; React-owned state surviving boundary re-renders, a hosted-provider context change AND a full presence exit+re-entry with :mounts still 1; teardown running the foreign cleanups + ref cleanup to the residue standard; the hook budget counted at React own dispatcher (shell two hooks first, exactly one useSyncExternalStore on the page, nothing after the shell outside the widget own roster); and the refusal roster each named at its position.

COMPOSITION HAZARDS: host under a memoised boundary - HD-028 landed mid-flight so the hazard is real, and a page-chrome write now re-renders the chrome while the hosted foreign component is not re-rendered AT ALL; host under ::h/unmounting presence; host with ::h/prevent intents; React.memo both directions (holds on shallow-equal props, defeated by an intent vector at a declared :event position - the same price every native event position pays, stated as the honest cost).

FOUND AND FILED, NOT SMOOTHED: rf2-2rtt6.66 - presence lowered its children with no ambient frame, so intent props on ANY presence child were loud-dead. Repaired on main while this was out (and h/boundary took the same repair, rf2-uo9di). That repair could not witness its own host half and its bead named THIS suite fenced children as what it un-fences; the fence is lifted here and both shapes are driven from the retained ::h/unmounting window (a vector, lowered during presence render; a declared :event h/fn, which fails a phase later at invocation).

REBASE INTERACTION, REPORTED: rf2-2rtt6.63 replaced the caches prototype guard - reserved-cache-keys deleted, a prop literal now answered by a cached PropSlot carrying js-name + reserved?/event?/ref?. The host walk was written against the deleted var: undeclared-var at compile, TypeError at EVERY crossing at runtime, refusal rows catching the wrong error. Rewritten as host-entry in convert-entry exact idiom (one slot lookup per prop, :key skipped in-loop, reserved emitted slot never written, event? gated on keyword?); the one difference from its native sibling stays the whole of HD-011 - the declaration decides what a position means.

title: Hicasso clocks: match roster workloads before attributing boundary-decomposition cost
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7372 follow-up, split because rf2-2rtt6.56 became in-progress.

The clock owner currently describes shape 2 and shape 3 as the same page at two boundary decompositions and says the pair isolates shell from interpreter cost. The landed witnesses do not hold workload constant: large-template mounts 69 cards (1,202 elements, 141 reads), while feed mounts 300 cards (5,129 elements, 603 reads). Shared card source and one-card canonical equality establish markup parity, not matched-page workload. Acceptance: run the one-boundary and per-card-boundary decompositions against the identical seed/card count at each rung (at least the meaningful 69 and 300 rungs); assert matched row/element/read/model inputs before timing; attribute only the matched delta to boundary decomposition. Keep this as a diagnostic ladder, not a new bar.

title: uix adapter: a controlled input's caret is still thrown to the end, and the fix exists one arm over
description:
THE DECISION rf2-n3dxw IS NOW WAITING ON, split out so the bug bead is not
holding a ruling.

rf2-fki5d shipped the in-turn caret-correct converge in HICASSO ARM 1's element
path (`front.controlled/install!`, called from `front.codec/native-element`): a
refused keystroke and every normalising rewrite converge inside the discrete
event with the caret at the position the edit left it, at no cost to the
authoring surface and no hook in the boundary shell.

A UIx CONSUMER DOES NOT GET IT. Their `:input` is minted by
`uix.compiler.aot/create-uix-input`, which since rf2-heqwo is pinned to React's
own implementation — so the value converges in-turn and the caret lands at the
END of the field on every mid-string refusal and every normalisation. That is
the exact gap the matrix records:
docs/design/hicasso/studio/controlled-input-two-implementations.md.

THE OPTIONS, and this is a ruling rather than an implementation:

  (a) Port the converge into `re-frame.adapter.uix`. Costly in a way Hicasso's
      is not: the adapter mints no `:input` of its own, so it would have to
      acquire an element path (or wrap `create-uix-input`) purely to hold this.
  (b) Rule that the UIx adapter keeps React's behaviour and the caret is one of
      the things Hicasso is FOR — i.e. the gap is intended product
      differentiation, and rf2-n3dxw closes on that basis.
  (c) Something narrower — e.g. offer it as an opt-in wrapper a UIx consumer can
      reach for.

Mechanism note for whoever takes it: the per-instance record the converge needs
costs nothing — it is `node.defaultValue`, which React maintains itself on every
commit of a genuinely controlled input or textarea. The whole of Hicasso's
mechanism is ~40 lines in
`implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/controlled.cljs`;
what does not transfer is the element path to hang it on.

Blocks the close of rf2-n3dxw.
close_reason: RULED (b) — delegated dossier review 2026-08-03 (Mike's directive; operator-overturnable). The UIx adapter keeps React's controlled-input semantics undisturbed; caret fidelity on refusing/normalising fields is Hicasso's differentiation, consistent with rf2-digtt's same-week ruling on the same axis. No port, no new opt-in surface: docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md 'Controlled inputs and the caret' already documents the divergence AND the one-line opt-in to UIx's caret-correct Reagent-port; the witness pair in controlled_restore_dom_cljs_test stays as the executable record. Codex's onChange-decorator sketch is preserved in the ruling comment as the starting design if a real UIx consumer report ever arrives — nothing pre-filed. Full rationale in the 2026-08-03 20:15 AUSEST comment. Unblocks rf2-n3dxw.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
NOT IMPLEMENTED, DELIBERATELY — this bead is a ruling and the ruling has not been made. Raised by the worker that shipped rf2-fki5d's audit fix (PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7401); dispatched to do both arms, it did the Hicasso one and stopped here.

WHY IT STOPPED. The bead says so in terms: 'THE OPTIONS, and this is a ruling rather than an implementation', listing (a) port the converge into re-frame.adapter.uix, (b) rule that the UIx adapter keeps React's behaviour and the caret is one of the things Hicasso is FOR, (c) something narrower such as an opt-in wrapper. rf2-n3dxw agrees: 'That is a decision, not an implementation, and it is filed separately.' Checked for a ruling before deciding — this bead has zero comments; nothing in docs/design/hicasso/studio/controlled-input-two-implementations.md (its TAKEN markers are rf2-fki5d's Option B and rf2-heqwo's Option C, a different axis); nothing in bd memories. Option (a) would have the adapter acquire an element path, or wrap create-uix-input, purely to hold this — a real architectural commitment to a shipped, first-class, publicly-documented adapter. Not a worker's call.

NOTHING IS MISSING ON THE EVIDENCE SIDE, which is why the ruling is cheap to take now. The gap is already witnessed EXECUTABLY by controlled_restore_dom_cljs_test/a-normalising-model-moves-the-caret-to-the-end-on-react ([5 5] where [2 2] is wanted) beside the-uix-port-keeps-the-caret-mid-string-through-a-normalisation, and documented for consumers in docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md's 'Controlled inputs and the caret'. A second witness would have been duplication, so none was added and the UIx adapter is untouched by that PR.

ONE FACT THE PR ADDS FOR WHOEVER TAKES THE RULING, and it raises option (a)'s price slightly: any port of the mechanism must now carry a POST-FLUSH re-reading of selectionStart as well. install!'s guards are read off the props that mint the wrapper, and the converge's own flushSync is a render — so a handler that re-renders the same <input> from text to number leaves the running wrapper against a caretless element and setSelectionRange throws InvalidStateError. That is not Hicasso-specific; it follows from flushSync being a render, so it is true wherever the converge is hung. The mechanism is now ~45 lines rather than ~40.

UNCHANGED: what does not transfer is still the element path to hang it on.

Still blocks the close of rf2-n3dxw.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
[2026-08-03 20:15 AUSEST] DELEGATED DOSSIER-REVIEW RULING (Mike's 2026-08-03 directive); operator-overturnable.

RULING: (b). The gap is intended product differentiation. The UIx adapter keeps React's controlled-input semantics undisturbed — value converges in-turn, caret lands at the end on a refusing/normalising write. No port (a), no new opt-in surface (c). rf2-n3dxw closes on this basis.

WHY (what a UIx consumer experiences and expects): byte-for-byte stock React — the long-standing, React-documented controlled-input caret jump, which the witness itself pins as "not a re-frame2 defect". Choosing the UIx adapter means choosing React's semantics; re-frame2 subtracts nothing a raw-React user has. The adapter contract since rf2-heqwo is React's own implementation, pinned; growing adapter machinery to out-React React is the over-engineering the posture rejects. Product-line coherence: rf2-digtt (ruled 2026-08-03) kept react/uix-port IME conduct as asserted divergence with Hicasso alone enhanced — caret fidelity is the same class of fact on the same axis. Two rulings in one week say the same thing: Hicasso owns the enhanced controlled-input contract; adapters faithfully host their substrate.

DECISIVE VERIFIED FACT AGAINST (c): the consumer opt-in substantially EXISTS, shipped and documented. docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md "Controlled inputs and the caret" documents the one-line opt-in (set! uix.compiler.input/*use-reagent-input-enabled?* true) to UIx's Reagent-port — caret-correct mid-string (witnessed [3 3] by the-uix-port-keeps-the-caret-mid-string-through-a-normalisation), frame-late — using UIx's own machinery, zero new re-frame2 surface (needs Reagent on the classpath; the doc says so). The only increment a new wrapper could add is in-turn AND caret-correct together, and the same doc already states that combination is Hicasso's differentiation ("Neither implementation gives you both halves").

MAIN vs CODEX: main recommended (b); Codex recommended (c) as one opt-in onChange decorator. Adopted (b). Codex's analysis is credited and kept: the decorator shape DISSOLVES option (a)'s element-path problem (the event target IS the element; no create-uix-input wrap needed), and its kill rule is sound. But the kill rule fires at design time: per rf2-digtt's measured matrix, a converge that writes+setSelectionRange inside a change event mid-composition aborts the IME exchange, so the honest helper needs the isComposing fence plus once-at-compositionend logic — the digtt state machine re-paid on a new public surface — plus the post-flush selectionStart re-read (this bead's 2026-08-03 comment: flushSync is a render; a text->number type-flip leaves a caretless element and setSelectionRange throws) and flushSync's documented last-resort costs. Not "one helper plus focused browser tests", and consumer demand is zero reports.

IF DEMAND MATERIALISES (a real UIx consumer report is the trigger — nothing pre-filed, per posture): start from Codex's sketch — wrap the author's onChange; capture target value+caret; run handler (dispatch-sync required); flush; read the node.defaultValue mirror; write only on disagreement; re-read selectionStart post-flush; restore by offset from end; decline during composition. Weigh it then against steering that consumer to the existing documented opt-in or to Hicasso.

DOWNSTREAM: this bead closes RULED. rf2-n3dxw closes citing this ruling; the durable record of the divergence is the executable witness pair in controlled_restore_dom_cljs_test (react rows [5 5] beside hicasso [2 2] / uix-port [3 3]), the matrix in docs/design/hicasso/studio/controlled-input-two-implementations.md, and the consumer-facing API-doc section.

title: Hicasso authoring: the ^{::h/prevent? true} opt-in is the one spelling that reads badly at the spine shapes
description:
AUTHORING FINDING from the tier-1 shape roster (rf2-2rtt6.51), which was asked to report
plainly if any collapsed spelling was awkward at these shapes.

Three of the four collapsed spellings did not come up at all across shapes 1-4 - `h/fn`
was never needed (every event position took a literal intent vector, matching the census's
~97%), `:&` was never needed (the spine shapes have no remainder-forwarding wrapper; the
article-editor witness is where it earns its place), and presence never came up. That is a
good result and it is stated as an absence, not a pass.

The one that DID come up, and reads badly:

    [:a.nav-link {:href        "#"
                  :data-testid "your-feed-tab"
                  :class       (when your-feed? "active")
                  :on-click    ^{:re-frame.hicasso/prevent? true}
                               [:conduit/show-your-feed]}
     "Your Feed"]

Three things are wrong with it at a call site:

1. IT BREAKS THE ATTRIBUTE MAP'S ALIGNMENT. The value no longer fits on the key's line at
   any sane indent, so the one attribute that carries behaviour is the one that looks
   like a mistake. It is the ugliest thing in the roster and it is in both feed pages.
2. METADATA DOES NOT PARTICIPATE IN `=`. HD-021's headless door returns the tree as data
   with "intent vectors assertable by equality" - and `(= [:conduit/show-your-feed] ...)`
   is TRUE whether or not the prevent metadata is there. So the one axis of an intent that
   metadata carries is exactly the axis a structural test cannot see. (The roster fires a
   real cancelable click to check it instead:
   large_template_dom_cljs_test/the-prevent-metadata-is-what-prevents.)
3. IT IS INVISIBLE TO A READER SCANNING FOR BEHAVIOUR. `^{...}` before a vector reads as
   a type hint, not as "this stops the browser navigating".

WHERE IT BITES: the anchor-acting-as-a-button, which the census home page has three of
(feed tabs, tag pills) and every Bootstrap-shaped nav has more. The dominant case -
`:on-submit` - needs nothing, because the position auto-prevents. So the metadata form is
paying its ugliness exactly where it is used most visibly and never where it is used most.

NOT PROPOSING A SPELLING. authoring.md's rationale for metadata is real ("costs no new
prop, no new spelling, and no second calling convention") and the alternative the census
uses - `{:event [...] :prevent-default true}` - is the options map HD-024's collapse
deliberately deleted. Filed as evidence for whoever re-opens that trade, with the note
that (2) is the strongest of the three arguments because it is a correctness-visibility
problem rather than a taste one.
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-08-02, dossier review): Option (a). Retire the ^{::h/prevent? true} metadata spelling. Adopt ONE in-band decorator head at event positions: [::h/prevent [:app/event ...]]. Both the primary dossier and the Codex review converged here independently. This bead now becomes the IMPLEMENTATION owner of that change — dispatchable.

WHY (defect 2 is disqualifying): metadata does not participate in =. Measured probe on this checkout — a metadata-carrying intent compares = AND hash-equal to the plain intent; the wrapper form does not:

  (= [:app/go] (with-meta [:app/go] {::h/prevent? true})) ;=> true
  (= [:app/go] [::h/prevent [:app/go]])                   ;=> false

So the prevent flag is invisible to HD-021's equality door, and equally to ordinary snapshots and logs (metadata is omitted from printing unless *print-meta*). preventDefault changes observable program behaviour (the event's canceled flag, per the DOM standard) — behaviour, not annotation — and a spelling that hides it from the product's own structural-testing story contradicts that story. Defects 1 (the value breaks the attribute map's alignment at any sane indent) and 3 (^{...} reads as a type hint, invisible to a reader scanning for behaviour) stand alongside; they alone would not have forced the change, defect 2 does.

FACTUAL CORRECTION — the implementation agent MUST NOT assume head-dispatch exists. The primary dossier's premise that "the intent materializer already dispatches on the head" is WRONG about the live code. front/intent.cljs substitutes ::h/value / ::h/checked markers; intent-handler dispatches the vector it is given, unexamined. The wrapper therefore needs a small, explicit CLASSIFY-AND-UNWRAP step at lowering time. That is still the right trade: classification happens once per render, the dispatched inner vector stays ordinary data, and the event-time path acquires no new allocation and no open-ended evaluator.

CLOSED GRAMMAR (keep it closed): exactly one inner intent vector; unwrap BEFORE marker analysis (so ::h/value / ::h/checked markers compose inside a prevented intent); accepted in key-map branches through the same path; fail LOUDLY on malformed decorators (wrong arity, non-vector payload). One reserved head in the same closed, tiny roster as the ::h/value placeholder — not an open DSL.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE (part of the ruling, not optional): keep :on-submit auto-prevent exactly as is. The rare submit OPT-OUT uses the existing h/fn escape — callbacks deliberately do not auto-prevent. Only add a symmetric ::h/allow-default if dogfooding produces a real site needing BOTH native submission AND equality-based structural testing — do not add it speculatively. NO event-options map. NO modifier DSL. (Auto-prevent cannot absorb the click case: a click intent on a real link must NOT prevent by default — modifier-clicks, open-in-new-tab — so the anchor-as-button genuinely needs an explicit opt-in; this ruling only picks its spelling.)

PREVALENCE (why now): 35 direct preventDefault calls in examples/; 10 anchor-as-button sites across the two RealWorld implementations (pagination, feed tabs, active tags, tag pills). The Hicasso metadata key itself currently occurs ONLY in the experimental Freehand front and its tests — pre-alpha is the cheapest, cleanest moment to correct the spelling.

PIN SET (ships with the implementation):
  1. A structural equality assertion distinguishing plain from prevented intents — proving the headless door can now SEE the axis.
  2. The roster's real-cancelable-click behavioural witness (large_template_dom_cljs_test/the-prevent-metadata-is-what-prevents, carried forward to the new spelling) — proving prevention actually happens AND that the inner vector is what gets dispatched.
  3. Marker and key-map composition tests (markers inside a prevented intent; the decorator accepted through key-map branches).
Preserve the existing submit and callback tests unchanged.

REJECTED OPTIONS:
  (b) keyed attribute {:intent [...] :prevent? true} — makes maps legal at event positions: a second broad calling convention at every event key, against the census's ~97%-literal-vector grain, and an invitation to an options language (the shape HD-024's collapse deliberately deleted).
  (c) keep metadata + a headless-door lint — patches defect 2 with tooling (duplicating semantic knowledge there) while defects 1 and 3 stand, and equality/printing stay blind; the ugliest spelling in the roster would remain at the most frequent interactive shape.
  Also rejected (Codex sweep): a sibling element attribute (separates the policy from the intent it decorates); requiring h/fn for the recurring click case (discards the data/headless benefit exactly where a one-head wrapper preserves it).

SPEC HOME: an HD amendment in the HD-016/HD-023 family — one new reserved intent head, the metadata spelling retired, HD-021's equality promise made true at shape 5. The amendment text ships WITH the implementation PR, not as a separate doc change.

RELATION TO rf2-2rtt6.54: the eventual route-link will absorb the NAVIGATION subset of these anchor sites; the anchor-as-button remains this spelling's home. No dependency either way.

Total cost: one reserved head and one extra pair of brackets, for one legible data form that programmers, AI authors, and the equality door all see the same way.
close_reason: Implemented and merged as PR #7374 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7374). The ^{::h/prevent? true} metadata is retired for one reserved in-band head, [::h/prevent [:app/go]], classified and unwrapped at lowering in front/intent.cljs — the head dispatch the ruling's factual correction said did not exist. Closed grammar (exactly one non-empty inner intent vector, no nesting), refused loudly at lowering with :rf.error/hicasso-malformed-prevent naming the position, in Freehand's event-plan diagnostic style. Unwrap precedes marker analysis so ::h/value composes inside a prevented intent; key-map branches come through the same call. HD-026 ships with it, citing what the Replicant reading took (namespaced-keyword head + positional payload) and declined (sibling attribute option keys, which cannot travel with an intent handed to a child; and its no-diagnostics posture). PIN SET delivered: (1) a-prevented-intent-is-assertable-by-equality asserts the retired spelling's =, hash and pr-str blindness against the head's visibility to all three; (2) the roster's real-cancelable-click witness carried forward as the-prevent-head-is-what-prevents; (3) marker and key-map composition tests. Census feed tabs migrated in both spine shapes. Mutation-proved: removing the classification -> test:browser exit 1, the real click stops preventing and the browser follows the href; removing the refusal -> test:cljs exit 1, 7 malformed forms go silent. Gates green: test:cljs 0, test:browser 0, test-fast-pr.sh 0, clj-kondo 2026.04.15 errors:0, check_doc_slugs 0. Hook budget unchanged (2 at 1/7/20 reads).

COMPLETENESS / CORRECTNESS. The valid within-row Hicasso/UIx measurements can remain descriptive, but the cross-row causal isolation, P3 ordering, and workload explanation are not established by this design.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / EVIDENCE. `census_clock_run.cjs` only turns the final exit nonzero for the arm-order guard. A nonzero verification tally, a band-ceiling breach, or `ctl.ok=false` does not refuse the run; four of the six committed rows have failed strict controls, yet the canonical datasets are written and the published run exits 0. The record still uses failed-control reagent rows to confirm P2 and to claim UIx “beats” Reagent. Dataset writes also occur before the final refusal and use the canonical filenames under partial overrides or `--no-build`, allowing a partial/refused/stale bundle run to replace the published evidence. Finally, the compact JSON omits the decomposition and raw metric deltas needed to reproduce the page’s layout/style/script figures despite claiming every statistic below is a function of those datasets. This repeats the fail-open class already recorded for the HD-008 driver on rf2-2rtt6.31; it stays here because this separate driver and record are owned exactly by rf2-2rtt6.56.

ACCEPTANCE. Add matched 69- and 300-card rows for both decompositions, or retract the isolation and every causal conclusion that depends on it. Make validity failures fail closed or suppress affected rows from conclusions; only publish canonical full-shape datasets after all required gates pass, routing partial/refused/no-build work elsewhere. Persist the reduced evidence needed to recompute every published statistic (including the cited metric decomposition), add deterministic gate/write-path regressions, and then restate the studio page and close reason.

title: Hicasso: no route-link, so census ports spell 106 tier-1 links as bare anchors
description:
Found porting RealWorld screens for the tier-1 shape roster (rf2-2rtt6.51).

The census names route-link as one of the FIVE tier-1 shapes and counts 106 of them
across 85 idiomatic files. `front/intent`'s own docstring records that it deliberately
does not implement route-link ("routing-coupled, and outside this bead's three
deliverables"), and no arm has added one since.

Consequence for the roster: every author byline and every article link in
shapes/ordinary.cljs and shapes/card.cljs is spelled `[:a {:href (str "#/profile/" u)}]`,
hand-building the URL the router owns. That is a faithful port of the MARKUP and an
unfaithful port of the AUTHORING - the census author writes
`[ui/route-link {:to :realworld.profile/show :params {:username u}}]` and never sees a URL.

v0's definition of done says "the five tier-1 shapes beautiful". Four of them now have a
roster; the fifth tier-1 SYNTAX (route-link) has no Hicasso spelling at all, so it cannot
be judged beautiful or otherwise. Not blocking rf2-2rtt6.51 - filed so the gap is on the
record rather than implied by the ports.
acceptance_criteria:
- A Hicasso route-link with any present `:prefetch` fails loudly at render under the current HD-027 v0 ruling, including `:prefetch :intent`, and no declined control key reaches the anchor attrs.
- `unwrap-navigate` accepts exactly `#{:frame :payload :native? :veto}` with the existing value contracts; missing `:veto` or any extra key raises `:rf.error/hicasso-malformed-navigate`.
- Focused structural tests pin both refusals and the valid emitted form; the existing node/browser navigation witnesses remain green.
notes:
AUDIT FINDING (PR #7380, merged 2026-08-02). The implementation is complete on the intended framework-sub and route-click happy paths, but HD-027's fail-loud boundary is not closed in two places:

1. `front/route_link.cljs` explicitly declines `:prefetch :intent` for v0, yet `control-keys` omits `:prefetch`. The props map goes through routing's `link-model`, which validates and accepts `:intent`; Hicasso installs none of routing's prefetch handlers and then retains `:prefetch` in passthrough attrs. The result silently does no prefetching and leaks a stray DOM attribute.

2. HD-027 says `[::h/navigate MAP]` carries exactly `:frame`, `:payload`, `:native?`, and `:veto`. `unwrap-navigate` validates only the value types of the first three; a map missing `:veto`, or carrying extra keys, passes despite the promised closed grammar and malformed-navigate diagnostic.

Keep the repair small: under the current zero-census-site v0 ruling, reject any present `:prefetch` at render rather than implementing the trio; require the navigate map's exact four-key set. If HD-027 is deliberately changed to support prefetch, implement routing's full three-handler behavior rather than silent passthrough.
close_reason: PR #7429: closed the two fail-open seams the #7380 audit found in HD-027's boundary. (1) unwrap-navigate now asserts the EXACT key set #{:frame :payload :native? :veto} rather than the value types of three known keys, so a map missing :veto or carrying a fifth key raises :rf.error/hicasso-malformed-navigate; existing value contracts preserved. (2) route-link refuses any PRESENT :prefetch at render (:rf.error/hicasso-route-link-prefetch-declined, contains? not truthiness), before the link model is consulted -- prefetch NOT implemented, HD-027's v0 decline unchanged. Mutation-proved in all three directions on the 12474-test node lane: dropping :veto from the key set, swapping the exact-set check for presence tests, and swapping contains? for truthiness each turn a named refusal green; baseline 0 failures; every revert byte-identical. Gates: test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 (jvm+node classified), npm run test:browser exit 0 (1040 tests). decisions.md HD-027 gained two enforcement clauses; no ruling changed, no spec/ touched.

title: Hicasso: the tier-1 roster does not exercise framework subs (27% of census read traffic)
description:
Found while porting the census screens for the tier-1 shape roster (rf2-2rtt6.51).

The charter counts framework subs at 27% of read traffic and says "the index serves them
first-class". The census screens the roster ports read exactly those:
  [:rf/resource {:resource :realworld/articles :params {...}}]
  [:rf/mutation {:instance [:favorite slug]}]

The roster reads plain reg-subs with the SAME READ SHAPE (a per-instance
:conduit/favorite-pending? alongside the per-row :conduit/article) but not the same
machinery, because standing up a resource cache behind a view-layer witness would put an
HTTP-shaped dependency in the roster's way.

So nothing in the Hicasso corpus currently witnesses that a framework sub reads
identically to an app sub through the collector. Two specific things go unchecked:
  - the query vector's arg is a MAP, not a scalar - so the index's sub-key identity
    (value equality on [frame-kw query-v]) is exercised on scalars only;
  - a framework sub's value moves on a different clock than a db write.

WANTED: one witness that mounts a roster page whose row reads a real [:rf/mutation ...] /
[:rf/resource ...] alongside its app sub, and asserts the same narrow law
(one commit -> one body). Sequence AFTER rf2-2rtt6.51 merges.
close_reason: PR #7380. shapes/framework_subs_dom_cljs_test mounts the census pair ([:rf/mutation {:instance ...}] beside the app sub, [:rf/resource ...] above) on the roster's state layer against the genuine resources machinery, transport stubbed as the resources suites stub it. Witnessed: map-arg sub-key identity is value equality (fresh value-equal key finds cell + readers; shared instance = one cell, two readers, both dirty; no thrash across commits; 5 boundaries / 8 cells / 9 edges as predicted); the different clock both ways (mutation commits move the sub with app-db identical?; an app-db write leaves the runtime sub's reader still and the frame-state resource sub's reader quiet behind its = cutoff); one commit -> one body per reader, with the page-read commits carrying the roster's documented no-bail-out cascade (stated, not contradicted); 2 hooks per boundary at React's dispatcher; zero residue. Mutation-proved: stripping map args from the sub-key reds exactly the three framework-subs witnesses (20 assertions) and nothing else.

title: MEASURE: rf2-emvod's corroboration control failed and the box no longer explains it
description:
RAISED by rf2-ymi6j, which removed the standing explanation without replacing it.

THE OBSERVATION, unchanged. rf2-emvod's seven-run M1 ensemble had every gate
pass — arm-order guard clean on both clocks, canonical DOM identical, 0
unverified, ctl-2x PASS on 7 of 7, every bar row clearing its own band by 3-6x
— and its PRE-REGISTERED corroboration control FAILED. The donor bar
uix-subs / reagent-subs read 0.9394x [0.8958 - 0.9837] against a published M1
mount of 1.0150x [0.9820 - 1.0480], which rf2-yd52q reproduced at 1.0011x on a
quiet box. Outside the published interval on the ensemble mean and on five of
seven runs.

WHAT HAS CHANGED. rf2-h8o80 attributed it to the box: those runs' M1 floor of
5.98-6.95 ms was said to sit above rf2-cvvb7's whole 3.06-5.50 ms ladder, so
the runs were "outside the regime the band was calibrated in". rf2-ymi6j's
ladder re-take dismantles that on two counts.

  1. The two figures are on TWO CLOCKS — 5.98-6.95 is raw TaskDuration,
     3.06-5.50 is taskNet. The same-sample gap measures +1.337 ms over nineteen
     runs, and emvod's own table gives the M1 gap as +1.401 ms. Converted, that
     ensemble's floors are ~4.58-5.55 ms on the ladder's clock — INSIDE the
     calibrated range.
  2. The band does not widen with load anyway. It is WIDEST ON AN IDLE BOX:
     24.6% at zero competing cores against 8.3% at four, corr(band, floor)
     = -0.49, with the floor's per-sample dispersion falling 30.0% -> 15.2% as
     load rises.

So "a busy box" is no longer a mechanism for a donor bar 6% away from a row
three independent ensembles agree on. The failure is now UNEXPLAINED, and it is
the only pre-registered control failure in this lane that is.

WHY IT MATTERS. The corroboration control is the gate that decides whether an
instrument may restate anything. A control that fails for no identified reason
is either finding something real about that ensemble, or is itself noisy enough
that its verdicts do not mean what the pages take them to mean. Both are worth
knowing, and they have opposite consequences for every ensemble that has PASSED
it.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. Take the donor bar uix-subs / reagent-subs on M1 across a
load ladder — the same six rungs, raw TaskDuration — and record, at each rung,
the donor bar beside the band. rf2-ymi6j's ladder ran bulk300 only, so this
specific measurement does not exist on the corrected clock. The question is
whether the donor bar's error tracks anything the run can see (band, floor,
per-sample dispersion, seam) or is independent of all of them. Roughly 19 runs
at ~70 s each on a silent box, plus a second row in the plan.

Instrument: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/seam_ladder.cjs
(--only M1), clock_run.cjs, and ladder_band.cjs for the arithmetic — the last
already emits a committed compact dataset, so this one will be restatable.
Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/rows-re-adjudicated-on-the-corrected-clock.md
section 5, and the-band-re-calibrated.md section 4.
close_reason: CLOSED as disproportionate — triage 2026-08-07. Explaining rf2-emvod's failed corroboration control costs 19 runs x 70 s against an ensemble that now publishes a REGIME rather than a point, so the control's failure no longer impeaches a figure anyone quotes. rf2-jcm3p's policy line applies verbatim. Pre-alpha posture: we do not litigate every last fine detail. Refile if a published row is ever restated as a point estimate that this control would have gated.

title: hygiene: nine worker worktrees will not reap — cause unknown, my first explanation was falsified
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-01/02. NINE worktrees refuse removal across many attempts, several quiet periods and a full session of the box cycling through other workers: axes-2rtt6-44, bulkretake-yd52q, diagleak-210uq, durab-b0tz5, flakes-2i1ay, heapaxis-2rtt6-34, readj-emvod, skills-89cn5, witness-2rtt6-41.

MY FIRST EXPLANATION WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED HERE SO NOBODY REUSES IT. I claimed the discriminator was workload — that a worktree running only doc checkers reaps cleanly while one running shadow-cljs or Chromium never does. I stated it twice with confidence and predicted it in advance. THEN ctl3-7iqb5, which ran a full bench ensemble WITH Chromium, REAPED CLEANLY ON FIRST ATTEMPT. The rule is false. Whatever holds those nine, it is not simply 'ran a heavy suite'.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY KNOWN: removal fails with the branch still in use by the worktree, i.e. something holds an open handle under the tree. scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh behaves CORRECTLY throughout — it disarms the node_modules junction first, refuses rather than forcing when removal cannot complete, and the mayor's real node_modules has held at 101 entries across every attempt without exception. The guard is not the problem and must not be bypassed: following a junction into the mayor's real node_modules has happened twice in this repository and is exactly what it prevents.

WEIGH IT HONESTLY: every one of the nine is INERT — work merged, no branch on origin, nothing at risk. This is disk and clutter, not danger. The cost is that a cluttered worktree list makes the hygiene survey harder to read, which is where a genuinely stale tree would hide.

THE WORK, and step 1 is the real one: FIND OUT WHAT ACTUALLY HOLDS THEM. Identify the process owning a handle under one of the nine (Windows has tooling for this; keep any script POSIX-safe per the cross-platform rule) and compare against ctl3-7iqb5, which reaped. Only then propose a fix. Candidate remedies once the cause is known: have the worker terminate its own children as its last act, the same discipline that already makes it unlink the junction; or have the removal script identify and terminate handle-holders before removing; or accept them and add a periodic sweep that reaps any that have since released.

DO NOT dispatch this while the Hicasso implementation wave is running — it is P3 clutter, and the box is wanted for measurement.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7407 — REOPENED (completeness / correctness / implementation quality).

The new `--force-disposable` / `-ForceDisposable` promise is not fail-closed yet.

1. Both `Get-WorktreeDirt` implementations collapse a failed `git status` into “clean”: POSIX ends the command with `|| true`; PowerShell suppresses stderr and never checks `$LASTEXITCODE`. The caller sees zero dirt/KEEP lines and, under the disposable flag, invokes `git worktree remove --force`. A status failure (permissions, unsafe ownership, damaged worktree metadata, filesystem error) can therefore authorize the exact unreviewed deletion the flag exists to prevent. Direct probe: a failing PowerShell status returned exit 128 and zero lines. Nonzero status must be a refusal, never the clean state.

2. The disposable directory glob `*logs/` is not an anchored log-directory shape. It also matches ordinary untracked names such as `catalogs/` (confirmed in PowerShell; POSIX `case '*logs/'` has the same suffix semantics), so the “anything unmatched is KEEP” claim can silently delete unrelated work. A destructive allowlist must prefer a false refusal to a suffix collision.

Bounded repair: capture status output and exit together; on any nonzero exit, print a distinct refusal and do not force-remove (and ideally classify before unlinking so a refused tree is unchanged). Narrow the directory rules to explicit component shapes/names that mean generated output. Add cheap classifier witnesses in both siblings: failed status refuses; `catalogs/` is KEEP; the intended `logs/`, `bench-logs/`, `.gate-logs/`, `.wtlogs/`, `out/`, `.shadow-cljs/`, and `*.log` shapes remain disposable; tracked modifications remain KEEP. No cleanup framework or content inspection is needed.
close_reason: MAYOR RE-CLOSE 2026-08-03. This bead was closed when its PR merged, then REVERTED TO OPEN by a tracker-state rollback (the same class as rf2-rjqtj / rf2-51uz1 — five early closes reverted while every later one held). Re-verified before re-closing: PR #7407 is MERGED and 1 commit(s) naming this bead are on origin/main. No work is outstanding from the original scope; if an audit later reopens it for a NEW obligation, that reopen is legitimate and separate from this rollback.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: CAUSE FOUND (PR #7407) — nothing was holding them. Every one of the nine was DIRTY, and 'git worktree remove' refuses a dirty tree with 'fatal: <wt> contains modified or untracked files, use --force to delete it' (exit 128, non-destructive; --force then removes cleanly). Reproduced in a throwaway worktree. Field evidence: all nine carried exactly one untracked path (logs/, bench-logs/, .gate-logs/, .wtlogs/, PRBODY.md, g-fastpr2-exit.txt), and the two that reaped cleanly carried none. That is why the 'heavy workload' rule was falsified and why waiting through quiet periods never helped: untracked files do not evaporate, and ctl3-7iqb5 reaped because it left none. NO handle-holder was ever involved, so the candidate remedies aimed at terminating processes are moot. The script's own message was the trap: it reported every failure as REMOVE_FAILED=(safe to retry once the lock clears). Failures are now classified — REMOVE_REFUSED_DIRTY (paths listed, tagged [build output]/[KEEP], waiting will not help), REMOVE_REFUSED_KEEP, and REMOVE_FAILED reserved for a genuinely clean+locked tree. Added --force-disposable/-ForceDisposable, which sweeps ONLY when every untracked path is build/gate output and refuses anything else; a modified tracked file is never disposable. That guard is load-bearing: band-ymi6j held four ladder-*.md analysis files for an OPEN bead, and pairing-2026-07-17 / pr-audit-20260730 / toolsbugs-oztox carried uncommitted source and doc edits — a blanket --force would have destroyed all of it silently. --dry-run now reports the same partition up front so a hygiene survey can act before touching anything. Prevention at source: the dispatch template now tells workers to write gate logs where git ignores them (*.log already is).

title: MEASURE: the corroboration control fails outside rf2-cvvb7's calibrated load regime — the band may not extrapolate
description:
RAISED by rf2-emvod (PR #7365), which hit it and refused to publish past it.

THE OBSERVATION. rf2-emvod's seven-run M1 ensemble had every gate pass — arm-order
guard clean on both clocks, canonical DOM identical, 0 unverified, ctl-2x PASS on
7 of 7, every bar row clearing its own band by 3-6x. And its pre-registered
CORROBORATION control failed: the donor bar uix-subs / reagent-subs read 0.9394x
[0.8958 - 0.9837] against the published M1 mount 1.0150x [0.9820 - 1.0480], which
rf2-yd52q reproduced at 1.0011x on a quiet box.

THE LIKELY CAUSE, and it is why this is worth a bead. That ensemble's M1 floor ran
5.98-6.95 ms. rf2-cvvb7's nineteen-run load ladder swept the floor from 3.06 to
5.50 ms across 0 to 20 competing cores on a 24-core box — so these runs sat ABOVE
the whole calibration range, above even the rung with twenty of twenty-four cores
saturated.

WHY IT MATTERS. The band (ctl-2x / floor, p10-p90 half-width) is the gate every row
is adjudicated against, and rf2-cvvb7 calibrated it over 4.4-18.5% inside that
floor range. Nothing establishes that it still bounds a bar row's reproducibility
outside it. rf2-emvod's bands read 4.9-10.8% on M1 — TIGHTER than much of the
ladder — while the donor bar was simultaneously 6% away from a row three other
ensembles agree on. A gate that looks healthy exactly where the instrument has
stopped reproducing a known row is the shape of gate that should be checked.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. Extend rf2-cvvb7's ladder upward — rungs beyond 20 competing
cores, or the same rungs on a busier baseline — and at each rung record BOTH the
band and the donor bar uix-subs / reagent-subs on M1, whose true value is pinned
by three independent ensembles. The question is whether the band stays predictive
of the donor bar's error as the floor rises past 5.50 ms, or whether it decouples.

If it decouples, the band needs a floor-level precondition attached to it — a row
may only be adjudicated when the floor is inside the calibrated range — and every
page that quotes a band should say which regime it was taken in. rf2-emvod already
states its regime for exactly this reason.

RELATED: rf2-ymi6j (band calibration) is the natural home if it is still open;
this is filed separately because it is a question about the band's DOMAIN rather
than its value.

Instrument: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/seam_ladder.cjs
and clock_run.cjs. Ensemble arithmetic: clock_readjudicate.cjs (new in #7365).
Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/rows-re-adjudicated-on-the-corrected-clock.md section 5.
close_reason: Hypothesis refuted by rf2-ymi6j's ladder re-take: the band is WIDEST on an idle box (24.6% at 0 cores vs 8.3% at 4, corr(band,floor) = -0.49), both ceiling breaches are at zero load, and this bead's central evidence held a raw-TaskDuration M1 floor against a taskNet bulk300 range — a 1.34 ms clock mismatch that puts emvod's floors INSIDE the calibrated range. The proposed floor-level precondition would refuse the most reproducible runs. The unexplained corroboration-control failure is carried forward as rf2-20pab.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
ANSWERED BY THE LADDER RE-TAKE (rf2-ymi6j, PR #7368) — the hypothesis is
REFUTED in the direction it was posed, and its central evidence does not
survive either. Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-band-re-calibrated.md

THE PREMISE IS A CLOCK MISMATCH. This bead holds emvod's M1 floor of
5.98-6.95 ms against rf2-cvvb7's ladder sweep of 3.06-5.50 ms and concludes
"above the entire ladder". Those are two clocks: the first is raw TaskDuration,
the second taskNet. The same-sample gap is measured on nineteen fresh runs at
+1.337 ms (positive on every one), and emvod's own absolutes table gives the M1
gap as +1.401 ms (task 6.242 against taskNet 4.841). Subtracting emvod's own
figure puts that ensemble's floors at ~4.58-5.55 ms ON THE LADDER'S CLOCK —
inside the calibrated range, its top level with the ladder's top rung. Two
further mismatches sit under the same comparison: it holds an M1 floor (901-
element cold mount) against a bulk300 range (300-cell update), and it uses the
floor as a load gauge.

AND THE MECHANISM RUNS THE OTHER WAY. Nineteen runs at 0/2/4/8/12/20 competing
cores, raw TaskDuration, band by rung:

  0 cores   floor 3.780 ms   per-sample CV 30.0%   band 24.6%
  2 cores   floor 4.386 ms   per-sample CV 22.4%   band 11.8%
  4 cores   floor 5.185 ms   per-sample CV 24.0%   band  8.3%
  8 cores   floor 5.901 ms   per-sample CV 23.9%   band 12.8%
 12 cores   floor 6.933 ms   per-sample CV 21.3%   band 13.2%
 20 cores   floor 6.927 ms   per-sample CV 15.2%   band  9.6%

corr(band, floor) = -0.49. THE BAND IS WIDEST ON AN IDLE BOX, by a factor of
three, and both of the ladder's ceiling breaches are at ZERO load. The floor's
per-sample dispersion falls monotonically with load while the floor absolute
rises — a busy box is slower and STEADIER; an idle one parks its cores between
samples and every sample pays a different wake-up.

SO THE PROPOSED REMEDY WOULD DO HARM. "A row may only be adjudicated when the
floor is inside the calibrated range" would, on this evidence, refuse the most
reproducible runs the instrument can take and pass the least. Not adopted.

WHAT THE CEILING FIRINGS ACTUALLY WERE: 25% sat inside the statistic's own
distribution. P(band > 25%) = 2.6% pooled / 9.0% within-run against a run-level
q99 of 29.1%. The ceiling is now 35%, set from that bootstrap. Full reasoning
on rf2-ymi6j.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ANSWER, and it is the part worth keeping. The corroboration
control on emvod's ensemble genuinely failed — donor bar uix-subs/reagent-subs
0.9394x [0.8958 - 0.9837] against a published 1.0150x that three ensembles
agree on and rf2-yd52q reproduced at 1.0011x. This bead's box explanation for
that is now WEAKER, not stronger, so the failure is more open than it was.
Filed as a successor rather than left inside a closed bead.

Closing: the question this bead asked — does the band decouple ABOVE the
calibrated load range — is answered no, and the framing that produced it was a
clock error.

title: The band calibration was taken on the frame-only clock (rf2-yd52q)
description:
rf2-cvvb7's nineteen-run load ladder, its seam null, its orthogonal decomposition and the BAND it calibrated were all computed on taskNet, which rf2-yd52q has since shown is a frame-ONLY reading with the operation's script subtracted out (see rf2-emvod).

WHAT PROBABLY SURVIVES. The band is ctl-2x/floor, and both of those arms are pure React whose script is small and nearly proportional to their frame - rf2-yd52q measured ctl-2x at 1.69-1.80x floor on BOTH clocks, agreeing to within 2%. So the band statistic is likely close to unchanged, and rf2-yd52q's own runs bear that out: band 10.3-23.6% on taskNet against 8.8-19.7% on raw TaskDuration over the same 16 rows.

WHAT NEEDS CHECKING. Whether the 25% BAND_CEILING and the 8.9% ladder average hold on the corrected clock, and whether the multiplicative-perturbation finding - which rests on ctl-2x/floor correlating +0.41 with the floor - is the same on a clock that includes script. title: MEASURE: re-take bulk broad with a control that doubles the CHANGED SET, not the page
description:
RAISED by rf2-rguy1's cross-check run (PR #7359), and it is the same repair rf2-0qj9w already filed for its own bulk rows — now with a second run that hit it.

THE FAULT. Every positive control this lane has for a bulk or update row scales the PAGE. On a mount row the work scales with it and the control passes; on an update row it does not, so even a perfect instrument reads below the predicted factor. rf2-rguy1's control took the other form — create-10,000 against create-1,000, exactly 10x the rows — and FAILED HIGH: 13.696 / 13.583 / 13.112x on Reagent, Hicasso and UIx against a band of 8-13x registered before the run. All three arms overshoot by 1-5%, so what it caught is the WORKLOAD scaling superlinearly (the script term grows faster than layout and style at 10k on every arm), not an instrument mis-reading one arm.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS. An equal overshoot divides out of an arm-to-arm ratio, so rf2-rguy1's ratios are not invalidated by it. But under this lane's strict rule a failed control is a caveat on the rows it guards, and no control this programme currently has can certify a bulk or update row cleanly.

THE REPAIR, which is a different instrument rather than a wider band: a control that holds PAGE SIZE FIXED and doubles the CHANGED SET. Update every 10th row against every 5th row on the same 1,000-row table is the obvious form — element count, layout and paint are constant, only the dirty set doubles, and the prediction is 2.00x on the commit-side work.

Cheap to add to the rf2-rguy1 harness: it needs one more button on the three benchmark arms and one more row in jsfb_ours_run.cjs. The apps are at implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/jsfb_*.

undershoot, and it would still fail the strict rule.

D, dirty 2D at fixed page size — adjudicated as

    (T(2D) - T(eps)) / (T(D) - T(eps))  ->  2.00

which differences the constant away regardless of its size, and needs no claim
about what c is. Prediction 2.00x with the lane's usual slack, registered before
the run that tests it.

description asks for a control that doubles the CHANGED SET; the 2026-08-01

title: MEASURE: ctl-2x is mis-specified for an UPDATE row -- it doubles the page, not the changed set
description:
RAISED by rf2-0qj9w's clock run (2026-08-01).

The lane's clock control is the floor at exactly twice the boundaries, and the
prediction written against it is 2.00x. On a MOUNT row that is right and it
passes: rf2-0qj9w measured 1.845x [1.5365 - 2.1136], every round inside the
+/-25% band under the strict rule.

On an UPDATE row it is wrong by construction. Doubling the page does not double
the work of a commit: rf2-0qj9w's decomposition measured layout scaling 1.79x
where the element count scaled 2.00x, and the non-layout half of the floor's
update barely moved at all. So even a perfect instrument reads below 2.00 on a
bulk row, and the three bulk controls failing at 1.70-1.82x is partly the
CONTROL being mis-specified rather than the clock being wrong.

THE REPAIR: a control that doubles the CHANGED SET at fixed page size -- e.g.
one commit writing 2K cells of a page that already holds 2K boundaries, against
one writing K of the same page. The prediction is then about the quantity the
row is actually about.

This is not a licence to move a threshold after a run. The 2.00x prediction
stands for every mount row; what this bead asks for is a DIFFERENT control for a
different question, registered before the run that uses it.

title: MEASURE: cross-check our clock harness against krausest/js-framework-benchmark — an instrument nobody here wrote
description:
RAISED by Mike (2026-08-01), who asked whether we should be considering https://github.com/krausest/js-framework-benchmark. Verified from the repository rather than recalled.

WHAT IT IS: 12 measured operations — create 1,000 rows; replace all; partial update (every 10th row); select row; swap rows; remove row; create 10,000 rows; append to a large table; clear; plus ready/run/update memory — with additional replace-memory, repeated-clear-memory and startup metrics, and Lighthouse figures (TimeToConsistentlyInteractive, ScriptBootUpTime, MainThreadWorkCost, TotalByteWeight). Driven by chromedriver against Chrome's timeline, with 5 warmup iterations. 186 implementations. Framework entries live under frameworks/[keyed|non-keyed]/<Name>, need npm install + npm run build-prod, FIXED version numbers (no ranges), the reference implementation's exact button ids, and must pass npm run rebuild-ci.

WHY IT IS WORTH USING HERE, and it is not mainly about the leaderboard: THIS SESSION FOUND FIVE DEFECTS IN OUR OWN MEASUREMENT APPARATUS — a contaminated run under load, a stale bundle silently measured after a par-compile abort, a segment-order effect, a null a confounded design could not have produced, and a 'held-out' rung that was an exact algebraic identity of the checks it was meant to validate. Every one was caught by auditing ourselves, which worked but cost a great deal. AN INSTRUMENT NOBODY HERE WROTE SIDESTEPS THAT WHOLE CLASS.

ITS OPERATIONS MAP ONTO EXACTLY WHAT IS UNMEASURED: create-1000 is mount; partial-update-every-10th is narrow; replace-all and swap are bulk. Those are the clock rows Hicasso has never taken. And it reports memory ALONGSIDE duration, which is the direct way to see whether the 415 B/read proxy shows up on the clock at all.

THE LIMITS, stated so nobody over-reads it: its app is a table of rows with essentially trivial state. re-frame2's value is subscription fan-out, frame isolation and boundary-scoped reactivity, NONE of which that workload exercises. It can say whether Hicasso's RENDERING is competitive with React/Vue/Svelte/Solid; it cannot say whether the reactivity design earns its keep — the census-derived witnesses still own that half. There is also a real Goodhart risk in optimising for a public leaderboard rather than for the shapes the census found. AND THERE IS NO CLOJURESCRIPT ENTRY among the 186, so there is no Reagent baseline in that harness; one would have to be written for the comparison to mean anything. That is the real cost.

THE RECOMMENDED SHAPE — a CROSS-CHECK, not a new bar:
  1. Implement the benchmark app in Reagent and in Hicasso, locally.
  2. Run both under its driver.
  3. Compare the RATIO against what our own harness reports for the equivalent operations.
  4. If the two instruments agree on the ratio, our clock rows become trustworthy. IF THEY DISAGREE, THAT IS THE MOST VALUABLE FINDING AVAILABLE — it means our harness has a defect we have not found.

DO NOT upstream an entry yet. That is a maintenance commitment and pre-alpha is the wrong time; it is a separate decision once the numbers are known.
