title: hicasso: attack the 415 B/read gap — can the index edge, key cell or read-set entry be made cheaper or eliminated?
description:
RAISED by Mike (2026-08-01): 'I don't understand how hicasso can be worse than Reagent? At worst, I would expect it to be roughly the same. What is it that hicasso is doing that makes it worse?'

THE ANSWER, from the landed measurement (rf2-2rtt6.34, PR #7337, reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md section 6): Hicasso is NOT doing Reagent's job worse. On the SAME substrate Reagent costs 948 B/read [947-948] and the Hicasso candidate costs 1,363 B/read [1,360-1,364] — 1.4379x, and EXACTLY 415 B/read worse. The page names what buys it: THE INDEX EDGE, THE KEY CELL, AND THE READ-SET ENTRY.

WHY REAGENT DOES NOT PAY IT: Reagent's dependency tracking is free because the ratom's own watcher list IS the edge. A deref inside a reaction is captured by the dynamic binding, and the dependency lives in a structure that had to exist anyway. Nothing extra is allocated.

WHY HICASSO MUST: the operator's Surface B ruling makes sub an ordinary call, legal inside a when, a for, an inlined helper. That means THE RENDER MECHANISM CANNOT BE THE THING THAT RECORDS DEPENDENCIES, so Hicasso keeps its own — a shared boundary-to-query index edge, a per-key cell, and a read-set entry (which is what buys the <=2-hook shell, since subscribe is keyed on read-set CONTENT). The 415 B is the price of decoupling reads from the render mechanism, which is a capability Reagent does not offer at all.

IT IS A TRADE, NOT A REGRESSION: against UIx the same design WINS by 708 B/read on the identical substrate (2,981 -> 2,272, 0.7624x, a 23.8% margin, crossover at R=1.29 reads). Hicasso is cheaper than N useSyncExternalStore hook stacks and dearer than a deref-capture; it sits between them.

THE WORK — nobody has attacked this yet, and it is far more tractable than 'why is it slower':
  1. PRICE THE THREE TERMS SEPARATELY. 415 B is their sum; the split is not published. Which dominates?
  2. For each, ask whether it can be made cheaper or ELIMINATED. Specifically: can the read-set entry be derived rather than stored (it exists to key subscribe identity — is there a cheaper key)? Must the key cell be per-key, or can it be shared? Is the index edge's representation minimal, or is it carrying structure it does not need?
  3. Respect the fences: <=2-hook shell (useContext + useSyncExternalStore, measured at React's dispatcher, 2 at 1/7/20 reads), subscribe closing over the read set ALONE, no candidate ledger, no compiler, no analyzer, no ViewCell-class object graph. A saving that costs a hook or widens subscribe's closure is a finding to REPORT, not a cost to spend.
  4. Any measured claim needs a QUIET BOX, B/E/Q stamps, a positive control predicted before the run, and the arm-order guard reportable. Same instrument (p0_run.cjs / p0_heap.cljs) and same-run donors as section 6, or the numbers are not comparable.

A HONEST NEGATIVE IS A COMPLETE ANSWER: if all three terms are irreducible given Surface B, that is the price of the ruled surface and should be stated as such on the ladder page — it converts an open question into a known cost.

SEPARATELY AND SMALLER: the shell is 1,143 B against Reagent's 508 because the subscription hook is per BOUNDARY, so a boundary that reads nothing still pays it. That is the same design choice seen from the other end and is tracked as rf2-2rtt6.41 item 5's shell-target half, already answered negatively.
notes:
WORKED 2026-08-03 (worker/readgap-aqgr2). PR to follow; measurements and
per-suspect verdicts recorded here so the bead stands on its own.

THE ANSWER TO ITEM 2, PER SUSPECT.

1. THE KEY CELL — REAL, and it is the whole of the saving. Every cell minted
its own watch key, `(keyword "rf-hicasso-arm1" (str "w" (vswap! counter inc)))`,
to buy a uniqueness that was already structural: at most one cell per
(frame, query), `subs/subscribe` hands back that pair's own cached reaction,
and no two cells ever hold the same reaction. The mint retained a Keyword, its
name string and its fully-qualified string PER UNIQUE KEY — per read on the
Q = E rung — plus a field on the cell. Replaced by one namespaced constant;
the global counter goes with it. MEASURED -108 B/read on BOTH segments.

2. THE INDEX EDGE — the duplicate does not exist. HONEST NEGATIVE. It looked
certain: `front.sub-index/record-reads` calls `(set read-sub-keys)` on a value
the caller already holds as a set and retains the result as the forward edge
for the mount's life. An explicit share-if-already-a-set changed the slope by
ZERO — `cljs.core/set` returns a meta-less set unchanged, so the sharing was
already there. The code change was reverted. A probe that FORCES the copy
prices what the existing sharing is worth: +46 B/read (Reagent seg.) / +47
(UIx). That is a TERM PRICE the ladder did not have — one retained hash-set
membership is ~46 B/read on this rung — and the property is now asserted with
`identical?` in the index's law suite.

3. THE READ-SET ENTRY — not reducible as it stands. Its key array and key set
are not redundant with each other: the array is what `entry-matches?` compares
and what `getSnapshot` sums over; the set is what the index and
`acquire-cell!` consume. Eliminating either only moves its work.

THE MEASUREMENT. `p0_run.cjs --only ladder`, 6 rounds, 0/1/3/7/20, Q = E,
B = 1,200 — nine runs. The deciding pair is back-to-back on `main`
`1ef3fdb73e` with only `arm1/runtime.cljs` differing:

  arm                       before     after
  Hicasso, Reagent seg.      1,446     1,338   (-108)
  Hicasso, UIx seg.          2,283     2,175   (-108)
  Reagent donor                948       947   (control)
  UIx donor                  2,979     2,980   (control)

Shell (R=0) unmoved on both segments while the FIRST read falls with the
slope — the signature of a per-KEY saving rather than a per-boundary one.
Positive control ok, 0 unverified of 154 mounts, structural witness fully
answered, arm-order guard reportable, exit 0 — all nine runs.

RESTATED LIVE NUMBERS: the design's bill falls from +499 to +390 B/read
(1.5264x -> 1.4114x); the win against UIx widens from -697 to -805
(0.7661x -> 0.7299x, a 27.0% margin); the bracket becomes 1,338 - 2,175.
943/948 is STILL NOT BEATEN and the verdict's shape is unchanged. The
crossover is deliberately not restated — rf2-2rtt6.34 is reopened on which
model the page states it in.

BOX HONESTY (item 4). The box was NOT quiet — five concurrent workers — so
these are stated as DELTAS against same-run donors, not as replacement gate
rows, and the ladder subsection says so in those words. What makes them
quotable: both donors ride every run and answer 947-948 / 2,978-2,980 in all
nine; the positive control is ok in all nine; and the UNCHANGED arm reproduces
the published `main` figure of 1,447. `main` moved twice mid-session
(rf2-2rtt6.32's codec rewrite, rf2-2rtt6.50's registry term) and the pair was
RE-TAKEN on each new base rather than carried forward — both landings measure
at zero on this axis, which is itself now recorded.

FILED, NOT TAKEN: rf2-dabt3 (P2) — `:sub->bs` is a second global map over the
same B*R key space as `!cells`, plus a singleton reader set per key at
fan-out 1; on the measured 46 B/membership this is plausibly the largest term
left in the +390. It is an ELIMINATION, but it dissolves the shared front
half's six-law algebra and moves architecture.md's central sentence, so it
wants a ruling rather than a perf worker. Also rf2-ixb92 (P3, `:live` is a
redundant index — shell axis), rf2-6wh9o (P3, read_profile_app's local cell
copy still mints a watch keyword, so its "faithful copy" claim is stale) and
rf2-e3i6y (P3, the evidence seam builds its event map before the nil check).

DECLINED WITHOUT FILING: dropping the cell's denormalised `frameKw`/`queryV`
(both are `(nth subKey 0/1)`) — two object slots per read, below what this
instrument resolves, against a second lookup in `flush!`'s hot loop. Minutiae.

FENCES HELD: the shell is not in the diff — hook count still 2 at React's
dispatcher, `subscribe` still closes over the read set alone, no candidate
ledger, bodies unchanged.
close_reason: Closed by PR #7418 (worker/readgap-aqgr2). One of the three suspects was real: the key cell's minted watch identity, -108 B/read on both segments, taking the design's bill from +499 to +390. The index edge's duplicate read set does not exist (cljs.core/set already shares; ablation reads identical to the byte) and the forced-copy probe prices the existing sharing at +46/+47 B/read. The read-set entry's array and set are not redundant with each other. The largest remaining elimination is filed as rf2-dabt3.

title: ci: a diff to the fast-PR spine ITSELF does not arm the docs tier — the spine cannot gate changes to its own doc gate
description:
FOUND by the rf2-g7p7l worker (PR #7352) and reported rather than fixed, correctly — it is a separate defect from the mkdocs probe.

THE OBSERVATION. A diff touching scripts/test-fast-pr.sh classifies as 'unknown surface'. run_docs stays keyed on the doc-surface predicate, and scripts/test-fast-pr.sh does not match it. So A CHANGE TO THE SPINE'S OWN DOCUMENTATION GATE DOES NOT ARM THE DOCUMENTATION TIER. Every verification run during rf2-g7p7l had to pass --with-docs explicitly for this reason.

WHY IT MATTERS. This is the ninth instance of the fail-open family this repository has found in two days, and it is the self-referential one: the gate that decides which gates run cannot gate changes to itself. Someone editing the docs tier — including someone BREAKING it — gets a green spine that never exercised the thing they changed.

SECOND, SMALLER FINDING FROM THE SAME WORKER, worth folding in: scripts/_test_fixtures/test_fast_pr_docs_gate/* is absent from is_doc_surface_path, though its check_readme_links/ and check_doc_slugs/ siblings ARE present. So edits to that fixture tree likewise do not arm the tier they belong to.

THE FIX: make the spine's own path (and its doc-gate fixture tree) arm the documentation tier. Verify the premise first — confirm the classifier's actual behaviour by running it against a spine-only diff rather than reading it — then mutation-prove: break the docs tier via a spine-only edit and show the spine reds WITHOUT --with-docs.

DO NOT widen the classifier so far that every scripts/ change runs the full docs tier; that trades a fail-open for a slow common case. Name precisely which paths should arm it.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7364 (branch worker/spinegate-fhdd3).

PREMISE VERIFIED BY RUNNING, NOT READING. `--plan` against a disposable repo whose only diff is `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` printed `PLAN docs=false jvm=true node=true`, reason `conservative fallback (unknown surface)`; it now prints `PLAN docs=true jvm=true node=true`, reason `spine self-change (every tier)`. The runtime classifier reports every surface false for that path, confirmed directly.

WHAT ARMS THE DOCS TIER NOW — exactly two paths, named path-by-path, never `scripts/*`:
  * `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` — the runner is where the docs tier and the mkdocs resolution are DEFINED. CI already agreed: this path is on docs.yml's documentation surface in both its `push.paths` and its PR-side `detect` classifier, so the fix also closes a local/CI divergence rather than inventing a local rule.
  * `scripts/_test_fixtures/test_fast_pr_docs_gate/*` — the second finding; its check_readme_links/ and check_doc_slugs/ siblings were already on the surface.
Nothing else moved. `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh` and `scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py` stay OFF the documentation surface, and self-test case AB pins that so a later widening cannot happen quietly. The two arms live in ONE roster (`is_spine_self_path`); `is_doc_surface_path` delegates to it rather than re-listing them, so the surface membership and the self-test arming cannot drift apart.

JVM + NODE STAY ON for a spine self-change, deliberately. They already ran via the unknown-surface fallback, which no longer fires now the runner is on the documentation surface; without an explicit branch the fix would have SILENTLY NARROWED the runtime coverage of every spine edit — the same defect wearing a repair.

THE SPINE NOW RUNS ITS OWN SELF-TEST when its own tree changes. Every other gate in the always-on block pairs a self-test with a live scan; the runner had neither. No recursion — the harness invokes `--plan`, which exits before the gate steps. Self-test grew 25 -> 34 cases (Z/Z1/AA/AA1 arm the tier and the self-test; AB/AB1 pin the not-widening).

MUTATION-PROVED, both directions. Mutation = point the docs tier's first gate at a non-existent script, editing ONLY scripts/test-fast-pr.sh; both runs use --repo-root against a spine-only disposable repo, neither passes --with-docs.
  RED  (this branch): `=== fast PR spine: docs=true ... (spine self-change (every tier)) ===` -> `FAIL README link/anchor validator`, EXIT 1.
  CONTROL (origin/main's spine, same mutation): `docs=false ... (conservative fallback (unknown surface))` -> `--- documentation surface unchanged -> skipping doc gates ---` -> `PASS fast PR spine`, EXIT 0, and `grep -c BROKEN_BY_MUTATION` over the log is 0. The broken gate was never invoked.

title: ci: hermetically pin the fast-PR mkdocs module-only fallback
description:
FOUND by merged-PR audit #7352.

PR #7352 fixes the current behavior: the docs tier now prefers a bare mkdocs console script, falls back through python/python3/py -m mkdocs, hard-fails the build wherever a command resolves, and reports an unresolved skip honestly. The motivating module-only path is not durably protected, however.

Case X in scripts/_test_fixtures/test_fast_pr_docs_gate/run-self-test.sh consults the host. If command -v mkdocs succeeds, it accepts PLAN-MKDOCS mkdocs and never executes any module fallback; GitHub CI installs requirements.txt and therefore exercises that bare-console branch. On hosts with only python3 or py, the case's own precondition checks only python and can skip. More importantly, no workflow or npm test command references this run-self-test.sh at all. The worker's Windows run exercised python -m mkdocs once, but a later deletion or breakage of every module fallback can remain green remotely and recreate the exact fail-open on module-only contributor installs.

The source Bead rf2-g7p7l was still in_progress and therefore locked when this audit ran, so this is a follow-up rather than a destructive scope update.
acceptance_criteria:
- Add a hermetic, CI-wired witness that makes bare mkdocs undiscoverable while a controlled module launcher resolves, and assert the exact selected command.
- Exercise the real spine path; do not copy resolve_mkdocs into the test.
- Mutation-prove that removing or breaking the module-only fallback makes a required remote gate red.
- Ensure changes to the witness itself arm that gate.
- Keep this bounded to the existing shell fixture/CI wiring; do not build a general command-resolution framework.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7364 (completeness, correctness, implementation quality; 2026-08-02)

The landed implementation correctly arms the spine + fixture paths, runs the real resolve_mkdocs path, and has green required CI. Two bounded durability gaps remain, both owned here:

1. The required CI wiring has no independent pin. The harness path appears in test.yml, the spine, and its README, but in no script-policy assertion. Deleting the new verify-readme-links step leaves valid YAML and makes the witness local-only again. This repository already pins the analogous adapter-disposition invocations in implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs under the unconditional js-harness-self-tests job. Add the same small invariant for the exact fast-PR harness invocation (and retain verify-readme-links in all-required-passed).

2. Hermetic case AC constructs only a python launcher. On required CI, requirements.txt puts bare mkdocs on PATH, so host smoke X takes the console branch. A regression from `for launcher in python python3 py` to python-only therefore leaves every required check green while breaking python3-only and py-only hosts—the two hosts this Bead explicitly called out. Parameterize the existing controlled-launcher witness (or equivalently pin all three supported launchers); do not build a general resolver framework.

Evidence: PR #7364 landing 0d582fe9122f757919b3c5270063bd94a8ba316b; all-required-passed green; AC-AD-AE pass; git grep finds no harness reference in implementation/scripts policy tests, while _changed-surfaces.test.cjs:1598-1623 demonstrates the established wiring-pin pattern.

title: ci: the fast-PR spine SILENTLY SKIPS mkdocs --strict when mkdocs is not on bare PATH — and it is the only gate covering docs/EP/**
description:
FOUND by the rf2-m6if4 worker (PR #7351) and worth fixing because it is a fail-open gate on a normative surface.

THE OBSERVATION. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh prints 'NOT RUN: mkdocs --strict build (mkdocs not on PATH)' and CONTINUES GREEN. On this machine mkdocs is installed but reachable only as 'python -m mkdocs', not as a bare 'mkdocs' executable — so the spine's probe misses it and the step is skipped, silently, on every run.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC. docs/EP/** is NOT in mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs, and scripts/check_doc_slugs.py's DEFAULT_ROOTS do not cover it either. So for an EP edit, mkdocs --strict IS THE ONLY GATE — and it is the one that silently does not run locally. A worker editing docs/EP/ who trusts a green spine has had NO gate cover their change. The rf2-m6if4 worker caught this and ran 'python -m mkdocs build --strict' explicitly (exit 0) rather than leave it unrun; the next worker may not.

THIS IS THE FAIL-OPEN CLASS THIS REPO HAS NOW FOUND SIX TIMES IN TWO DAYS: a residue gate that reset before asserting; a drift guard that compared the runner against its own regex; a waiver whose 'bare.length > max' with max 1 permitted the FIRST regression; a capstone that walked strings and missed keyword keys; an API manifest that did not scan an unrostered namespace; and a drift check that reported BLINDNESS as though it were drift. Same shape every time: the gate reports success without having examined the thing.

THE FIX, in preference order:
  1. Make the spine's probe find mkdocs the way it is actually installed — try 'mkdocs' then 'python -m mkdocs' then 'py -m mkdocs' — so the step RUNS rather than skips.
  2. If it genuinely cannot be found, the step must be LOUD: name what was not checked and which surfaces are consequently ungated (docs/EP/** at minimum). A skip that reads like a pass is the defect.
  3. Consider whether a skipped-but-required gate should fail the spine outright on a diff that touches a surface only that gate covers. That is the strongest form and worth costing rather than assuming.

VERIFY THE PREMISE FIRST: confirm mkdocs really is absent from bare PATH on this machine and present via python -m, confirm docs/EP/** is outside every other checker's roots, and say so with evidence rather than taking this description's word for it.
notes:
PREMISE CORRECTION — MY BEAD WAS WRONG ON ONE OF ITS THREE CLAIMS, and the worker refused to propagate it (recorded by acting mayor 2026-08-01).

I wrote that 'docs/EP/** is not in mkdocs.yml exclude_docs, and check_doc_slugs.py's roots do not cover it either, so mkdocs --strict IS THE ONLY GATE'. THE SECOND HALF IS FALSE. check_doc_slugs.py's DEFAULT_ROOTS is ('docs','spec','skills','migration') and docs/EP is UNDER docs — driving its own iterator scans 647 markdown files including ALL 40 EP pages.

AND THE COMPARISON RUNS THE OTHER WAY ON ANCHORS. Planting defects in EP-0001 one at a time: a link to a missing .md reds both; a broken SAME-PAGE anchor reds check_doc_slugs and NOT mkdocs; a broken CROSS-PAGE anchor reds check_doc_slugs and NOT mkdocs. mkdocs 1.6 grades a missing anchor INFO and --strict only escalates WARNINGs, so ON ANCHORS MKDOCS IS THE WEAKER GATE.

THE DEFECT WAS REAL AND UNDIMINISHED — the spine did silently skip a hard gate on every run — but its blast radius is the SITE BUILD across the whole docs corpus (nav, exclude_docs, theme, extensions, mkdocs_hooks.py, requirements.txt, staged spec/migration link resolution), NOT docs/EP specifically.

THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR HOW I BRIEF: the worker was asked to write the ungated surfaces into the skip message, and if it had taken my claim on trust the skip message would have stated something false about its own coverage — A SECOND FAIL-OPEN, inside the repair for the first. It verified instead, and the message now names the surfaces that genuinely have no local gate. This is the third time today a worker has caught an error of mine by checking rather than complying, and the reason each caught it is the standing sentence 'the bead governs; this brief is orientation'.

(c) TRUE — pre-fix 'sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh --with-docs' on a clean tree: exit 0, 'PASS fast PR spine', mkdocs listed under NOT RUN.

title: Reconcile Hicasso state-sugar authoring with HD-009's unfrozen contract
description: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7257. The normative HD-009 ruling explicitly leaves the concrete defstate shape, any declared app-db tier, and that tier's frame/persistence scope unfrozen; v0 ships and pre-commits to nothing beyond the response class. The authoring guide instead calls an exact h/defstate form the pre-designed answer and promises a declared :ui tier, Xray/time-travel visibility, and exclusion from persistence. Although decisions.md wins by the record's authority order, this gives programmers a concrete API and storage contract that the ruling expressly declined to make. Reconcile the two documents without implementing or expanding state sugar: either make the authoring passage describe only the reserved response class and mark/remove every unfrozen spelling and storage promise, or explicitly amend HD-009 through an evidence-backed ruling.
acceptance_criteria: decisions.md and authoring.md make one unambiguous statement about what HD-009 has and has not frozen; no exact defstate syntax, :ui tier, frame scope, persistence behavior, or observability promise is taught as settled unless HD-009 explicitly rules it; v0 remains free of new runtime/API work.

Removed: 'the pre-designed answer', the declared :ui tier, Xray visibility, time travel, and exclusion from persistence by convention — all storage/observability promises the ruling expressly declined. title: SSR: per-slot-projected serialize entries hydrate under an unaddressable key but are classified no-refetch
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7255 (2026-08-01).

A fresh `:serialize` resource whose projection-relative `:params` or `:scope` declaration changes its SSR wire key is internally consistent on the wire but not addressable by the live client identity. `project-resources-runtime-db` keys the wire entry by `state/key-id` of the projected key, and PR #7255's own `projecting-the-scope-changes-the-key-id-exactly-as-params-does` test proves the raw key-id is absent. After hydration, however, `route-resource-plan` and `ensure-handler` derive the ordinary scoped key from live scope/params and read `(state/entry-path scoped-key)`, i.e. the raw key-id. They therefore miss the hydrated entry and issue a new load.

At the same time, `project-entry` sets `:refetch-on-client?` from coarse disposition/staleness only, so a fresh declaration-only `:serialize` entry is reported false. `hydrate-refetch-plan` independently sees fresh usable `:data` and omits the entry. Thus the server ships usable data and records no-refetch, while the client cannot consume that entry under the identity it can derive and refetches anyway. The projected ownerless entry can also remain beside the new raw-key entry. This predates #7255 for the params arm and #7255 extends the same behavior to scope; rf2-5e2ye explicitly noted it but fenced it out and no exact follow-up owner exists.

Keep the fix narrow: reconcile addressability, projection metadata, and the actual hydrate/route refetch behavior. Do not weaken key privacy or reintroduce raw declared scope/params on the wire.
acceptance_criteria:
- Choose and implement one coherent contract for a fresh `:serialize` entry whose key is changed by a per-slot declaration: either it remains reusable through a safe client mapping, or it is explicitly metadata-only/not shipped as reusable data and deliberately refetched.
- `:refetch-on-client?`, `hydrate-refetch-plan`, and route/ensure behavior agree; no fresh entry is labelled no-refetch while the live derived identity must miss it.
- Add end-to-end controls for both params- and scope-rooted declarations covering server projection -> hydrate reconcile -> live route/ensure/read. Assert either reuse with no request, or exactly one intentional request with truthful metadata/plan and no persistent unreachable duplicate.
- Preserve declaration privacy, wire map-key/in-entry-key agreement, coarse redact/omit behavior, and byte-identical undeclared-key controls.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7354 (2026-08-01): REOPENED. The landed end-to-end test explicitly gathers projected-key ghost rows after the raw-key ensure, then asserts only that any ghosts carry no :data. Production follows that shape: hydrate-runtime-db drops SSR owners but retains the projected entry and recomputes indexes around it; ensure-handler later assocs the live entry under the raw key without deleting the projected row. The ownerless, unaddressable row therefore persists beside the live entry, contrary to this Bead's exact acceptance criterion of no persistent unreachable duplicate. The returned hydrate-refetch-plan also names that projected identity even though the client cannot derive/use it. Keep the security fix (no data under the many-to-one projected key), but remove or explicitly lifecycle-bound the ghost and replace the weakened every-ghost-is-data-less assertion with a zero-persistent-ghost end-to-end control.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7369 (main: 6c7c19061a + e30e5e8830).

The AUDIT-REOPEN charge is met. The unaddressable row is REMOVED, not emptied. project-resources-runtime-db withholds a :key-projected row rather than shipping it metadata-only (reading project-entry's exact key-id comparison, not a shape sniff), and hydrate-runtime-db drops any such row that arrives anyway — the never-trust-the-wire half, which earns its keep because a hydration payload is HTML and cached HTML from an earlier deploy reaches a newer bundle. ensure-handler was considered and rejected: the ghost is not linked to the raw key, so removal there would be a resource-id-matched scan on every ensure, heuristic rather than exact, and would still leave the rows of every resource the client never ensures.

Established from the code that removal was the ONLY option available, not merely the tidiest: the row is unreachable AND uncollectable. Inactive GC is timer-driven (gc-fired-handler fires against a handle armed by a commit fx) and hydration arms no timers, so an ownerless hydrated row has no collector at all — 'explicitly lifecycle-bound' was not reachable without inventing a sweep.

hydrate-refetch-plan no longer names the projected identity (the second half of the same defect: a plan entry is consumed by its :resource/key, so a key no live derivation reproduces names a fetch nobody can issue). The filter lives in the plan itself, not only on the path that drops the row first, because hosts and tests call it directly on an unreconciled slice.

The security fix of #7354 is intact and the projected key was NOT made addressable. Both barred repairs stay barred, and the many-to-one collapse is now vacuous rather than merely harmless — nothing is shipped, so there is no surviving row to collapse onto. The coarse :redact / :omit arms are untouched in shape and in count (their token is content-addressed, one-to-one, derivable in principle); coarse-redaction-token? exists to stop the client-side scan reading their :rf/redacted map KEY as a per-slot substitution.

Test strengthened from 'ghosts carry no :data' (satisfied by a ghost that persists) to absence of the ROW, with two exact-key-id-set controls so over-withholding fails as loudly as under-withholding. 12 tests/42 assertions -> 17/65. Vacuous-on-nil assertions were re-pointed or restated; the scope arm now carries the same no-duplicate claim the params arm did.

projection-metadata gains :projected-key. Withholding removed the only carrier the projected key had, and the SSR projection must stay byte-equal to trace-egress/redact-key-declarations (rf2-5e2ye, rf2-dl7bz — two derivations, one answer). One observation point now, whether or not the row ships; egresses nothing new.

Mutation-proved at all three removal points: M1 (post-#7354 shape restored) 12 failures/8 deftests; M2 (server regresses, client drop intact) 4 failures, cache controls green — the two points are independently witnessed; M3 (plan filter only) 1 failure. M3 initially came back GREEN — a real gap in my own witness: the forged row carried :data, so freshness excluded it and the filter under test never ran. Fixed in a second commit (the plan control now uses the metadata-only row and asserts entry-needs-refetch? as a premise) before the PR opened.

Gates all exit 0: resources 790/7054, ssr 614/3088, ssr-ring 206/1002, test-ssr-prod-gate 616/2915, npm test:cljs 12286/61535, clj-kondo v2026.04.15 errors 0, mkdocs --strict, PASS fast PR spine. Spec 016 §SSR and hydration rewritten from 'metadata-only' to 'does not ride', including the emptied-row-is-not-sufficient rule and the client's must-not-trust-the-server obligation.

Follow-up filed: rf2-4bjep — the coarse :redact / :omit hydrated rows are unaddressed and uncollected in the same way; deliberately fenced out here because their substitution is content-addressed and one-to-one, so they have a repair (adopt) the per-slot arm does not. This PR's exact-set control pins today's behaviour rather than changing it silently.

title: spec/Pattern-WebSocket states no validation obligation for inbound frame payloads
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-eane2's sibling sweep (the brief asked for other places a production path's validation story rests on a dev-only check, or on nothing).

NOT the same defect as rf2-eane2. Pattern-WebSocket makes no FALSE guarantee — it makes NO statement at all. That is the finding.

WHAT THE SWEEP FOUND. Across spec/Pattern-*.md, the schema-as-production-guarantee class is now clean: Pattern-Forms, Pattern-RemoteData and Construction-Prompts all carry explicit dev-tripwire qualifications, Conventions.md dropped the 'the validator IS the registration' parenthetical, and Pattern-FormAction is fixed by rf2-eane2. Pattern-AsyncEffect:163 mentions :schema only to warn against threading parameters through it. Seven Pattern docs mention schemas not at all.

Pattern-WebSocket is the one with an untrusted-ingress surface and no validation story. Line 429: 'Server pushes (:ws/received events with no :request-id) are translated into named dispatched events the running-app handlers consume. The connection machine's role is mechanical — receive, validate the socket-id, translate, dispatch. The semantic interpretation lives in the per-feature event handlers.' The socket-id IS validated (framework routing concern). The PAYLOAD is handed to app handlers with no obligation stated.

WHY IT MATTERS. A websocket frame is attacker-controllable — 010 §Production builds names 'an untrusted HTTP response or websocket frame' as precisely the :rf.schema/at-boundary case, since at-boundary's check is ungated and survives the production gate. Pattern-WebSocket never mentions at-boundary, never says the receiving handler must validate, and never says a :schema on the translated event would elide. A reader who declares :schema on their :ws/message-received handler and stops has an unvalidated production ingress path, which is the exact mistake Pattern-FormAction now has a whole section warning against (§Validation is the handler's job).

THE RULE THAT SHOULD APPLY, already established twice: rf2-dtpfv/rf2-759sp — a dev-posture convenience check may be elided; a path that RECEIVES untrusted input guards itself unconditionally. The reserved :rf.server/* fx family guards its own args in all builds on exactly that reasoning, and re-frame.cofx's :rf.error/cofx-value-invalid is documented in-source as 'a PRODUCTION hard error'. Both are the framework guarding its own boundary. A websocket payload reaching an app handler is the app's boundary, so it is the Pattern's job to say so.

LIKELY SHAPE (needs a ruling — do not let a worker pick): either Pattern-WebSocket gains a short section pointing inbound-frame validation at :rf.schema/at-boundary (the designed production-ingress surface, and a status/drop is the whole answer owed for a frame — unlike a form POST, there is no page to re-render, so at-boundary fits BETTER here than it did there), or it states that the receiving handler writes the branch itself. The former looks right for exactly the reason the latter was right for FormAction.

FENCE: spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md is hot-zone; sequence it, do not parallel it with another spec/ claimant.

CITE: rf2-eane2 (the FormAction fix and its §Validation is the handler's job), rf2-dtpfv / rf2-759sp (the untrusted-input-guards-itself rule), rf2-bkvu5 (reg-app-schema is dev-only as designed).
close_reason:
COMPLETE — PR #7406 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7406), branch worker/validscope-bl8k7, 2026-08-03. NOT MERGED. Rode one worker with rf2-bl8k7 + rf2-eane2 (hot-zone spec/, and two of the three edit spec/Pattern-FormAction.md).

RULING NOT NEEDED — the bead's two options were already settled by precedent it names itself. rf2-eane2's §Validation is the handler's job is now on main, and it rules the interceptor INSUFFICIENT for a form POST for a reason that is specific to forms rather than general: a form owes the user a re-rendered page, and a skipped handler composes nothing. A websocket frame owes nobody a page, so the same reasoning selects the interceptor here. That is precisely the bead's own "the former looks right for exactly the reason the latter was right for FormAction", so option (a) was taken without inventing anything, and the section makes the asymmetry explicit rather than leaving a reader to infer it.

SHIPPED (spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md):

- §Server-pushed events now says what it was silent about — the socket-id check is the machine's own ROUTING concern and the payload it hands on is unexamined, so the payload check lives in the receiving handler.
- The canonical :ws/handle-message fence carries the schema and :interceptors [:rf.schema/at-boundary], so the copyable code is correct BY DEFAULT rather than by footnote. The example schema is a closed :multi with no default arm, which is what makes an unrecognised :type a rejection instead of a case fall-through inside the handler body — the fence's old trailing "..." arm was quietly the opposite.
- New §"Inbound frames are untrusted, and :schema alone will not check them". A bare :schema is an ordinary registration diagnostic and elides, so on the one build facing the real network there is no check at all; at-boundary reads that SAME declaration at a checkpoint the framework keeps in every build, per the corrected C-000.35 (what a check is FOR, not who declared the schema it reads). One interceptor reference, no second schema.
- The section states why the interceptor fits BETTER here than on a form POST and cross-references Pattern-FormAction, which now cross-references back — so the asymmetry reads correctly from either end. Dropping the frame IS the complete answer: handler skipped so nothing reaches app-db, one always-on structural :rf.error/schema-validation-failure (:source :boundary, identifiers only), and :outcome :rejected on the event-emit stream, which is the counter to alert on.
- SCOPED, not blanket: put it at the ingress, not on the per-feature events it fans out to — those carry a value the app has already accepted, so their :schema stays an ordinary dev tripwire. The correlated request-reply path is named as the SECOND ingress: a reply body under a known :request-id is still the server's bytes.
- New anti-pattern ("Declaring a :schema on the receiving handler and calling the ingress guarded") and two cross-references (010 §Production builds, Pattern-FormAction §Validation is the handler's job).

NOT CHANGED: the request-reply correlation machinery, the connection machine, the epoch guard. No framework websocket surface implied or added — re-frame2 still ships no managed WebSocket, and nothing here changes that.

Verified no test pins the edited fences: implementation/core/test/re_frame/pattern_smoke_test.clj transcribes shapes rather than parsing the markdown, and implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs (a concurrent worker's tree — deliberately untouched) pins the correlation boundary, not this section.

Gates foreground, unpiped, worktree-local logs: mkdocs --strict 0, check_doc_slugs.py 0 (which is what validates the new heading anchor and both cross-reference targets), test-fast-pr.sh 0 ("PASS fast PR spine").

title: machines-viz grammar/definition-summary leaks the top-level key set of a forged definition
description:
FOUND while fixing rf2-m46qv (share/value-free-summary disclosure), and deliberately NOT fixed there: different function, different consumers, its own ruling.

tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/grammar.cljc's `definition-summary` is the THIRD independent EP-0015 shape summariser in this repo (after re-frame.error/diag-value-summary, fixed in rf2-210uq, and share/value-free-summary, fixed in rf2-m46qv). It reproduces the `:keys` defect both of those removed:

  base (if (map? definition)
         (cond-> {:type :map
                  :keys (vec (sort-by str (keys definition)))
                  :parallel (parallel-definition? definition)} ...

1. `:keys` returns EVERY top-level key of the rejected definition, uncapped and unsanitised. A definition reaches this function from a forged share URL (share/decode-share-url validates `…/chart`'s `:definition` through grammar/valid-definition?), from an LLM response (ai_generate.cljc), and from SCXML/Mermaid input (scxml.cljc, mermaid.cljc) — all three are untrusted, and the ai_generate call sites already say so in their own comments.
2. `(sort-by str (keys definition))` runs `str` over caller-supplied keys, so a key whose `toString` throws replaces the documented ex-info with its own exception — the rf2-210uq path-5 shape.
3. The `:else {:type :value}` leg uses a `:type` tag outside the closed vocabulary the other two summarisers now share (`:scalar`).

NOT a straight copy of the rf2-m46qv fix, which is why it is its own bead: this summary deliberately carries STRUCTURAL diagnostics the other two do not — `:parallel`, `:state-count`, `:region-count` and the rf2-j538f7.18 `:defect` (category + path + offending keys). Those are load-bearing for three emitters and are pinned by tests, and `:defect` itself may carry offending KEYS, so the ruling has to decide what a definition's structural diagnostic may name — not merely delete a leg. spec/API.md §SCXML + §ai-generate document `:spec-summary` as this shape.

ACCEPTANCE: rule on what `definition-summary` may carry over untrusted input; remove or justify `:keys`; align the `:else` tag with the closed vocabulary; and add the same GRAMMAR-shaped witness rf2-m46qv added — a corpus of hostile definitions (sentinel-bearing keys of every key type, an attacker-sized key set, a key whose toString throws) asserting the whole thrown ex-data discloses no sentinel fragment and serializes inside a fixed bound.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7408: REOPENED. The disclosure repair itself is sound, but the acceptance's grammar-shaped witness and the new normative API omit a reachable output. `transition-target-defect` passes `:spawn/on-error` into `target-defect`; direct evaluation of `definition-summary` over `{:initial :a :states {:a {:spawn {:machine-id :child :on-error :missing}}}}` returns `{:defect {:category :rf.error/machine-unresolved-target, :slot :spawn/on-error, :depth 1} ...}`. Yet `grammar_validation_cljs_test.cljc` defines `defect-slots` as only `#{:on :after :always :on-done}`, and API.md plus `defect-summary`'s contract list the same four. The hostile corpus has no spawn/on-error target, so both JVM and CLJS suites remain green while the advertised grammar rejects an actual summary shape.

Bounded correction: include `:spawn/on-error` in the closed slot vocabulary (or normalize it consistently if that is the intended public spelling), update the normative table/docstring, and add a spawn-on-error bad/unresolved-target corpus case that fails when the fifth slot is omitted. The value remains fixed and content-free; no new summarizer or abstraction is needed.

title: test-quiet spawn harness flakes under concurrent load: spawnSync ETIMEDOUT at the 60s ceiling, red on main locally
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-01 while gating rf2-6jqa8 in a worker worktree, with sibling workers in flight.

`npm run test:cljs` reds in the `implementation/test-quiet` spawn harness. Every failure cascades from one assertion — `(is (nil? err))` where err is `spawnSync <node.exe> ETIMEDOUT`. That harness re-spawns `out/node-test.js` as a child to exercise the real CLI path end-to-end; `spawn-timeout-ms` (test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test.cljs ~line 348) is a fixed 60000, and the child loads the WHOLE consolidated bundle before it can answer.

MEASURED, three runs, same machine, same session:
  with the rf2-6jqa8 diff, cold : 12249 tests / 61148 assertions, 35 failures, 6 namespaces
  with the rf2-6jqa8 diff, warm : 12249 tests / 61148 assertions, 16 failures, 3 namespaces
  at origin/main (diff reverted in-tree): 12249 tests / 61148 assertions, 14 failures, 3 namespaces

ATTRIBUTION IS SETTLED, and by measurement rather than assertion. The test and assertion COUNTS are identical across all three, so no diff adds or removes a cljs test; the only variable is which spawn happens to hit the ceiling. The failing namespaces differ between runs and only PARTLY overlap (real-shadow-node-green-run-is-quiet / unknown-arg-is-fatal-not-false-green / unmatched-selector-is-fatal-at-real-runner versus deliberately-failing-test-exits-nonzero / large-red-replay-is-not-truncated / red-run-replays-buffered-console-warn). That is what a load-dependent timeout looks like; a semantic regression does not move around. It is red at origin/main with no diff at all.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING MERE NOISE. This is a false RED, and the class it belongs to is the one this repo keeps finding on the other side. A gate whose verdict depends on machine load teaches everyone to discount it, and a discounted gate is one that gets waved through on the day it is telling the truth. The harness is also load-bearing in its own right: it is the guard against a false GREEN in the runner itself (unknown-arg-is-fatal-not-false-green, unmatched-selector-is-fatal-at-real-runner).

SHAPE OF A FIX, not prescribed. The ceiling is a wall-clock constant standing in front of a whole-bundle load, so it measures the machine as much as it measures the child. Options include scaling it, distinguishing 'timed out' from 'answered wrongly' at the ASSERTION level (the harness already captures :timed-out? but the assertions read :error / :status, so a timeout presents as a content failure with an empty 'got:'), or having the spawn tier skip rather than fail when it cannot get a scheduling slot. Whoever takes it should decide which option keeps the false-green guard intact, since that is the property worth protecting.

CROSS-REF: matches the durable 'CI flaky gates under load' pattern. Filed from the rf2-6jqa8 / rf2-rprfg / rf2-ycbhx gating pass (PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7342), whose own JVM surfaces are green and whose cljs delta is nil.
close_reason: RESOLVED BY rf2-hofhx (PR #7343, merged). Same defect, observed independently: test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test's spawn-timeout-ms was a fixed 60000 ms, and the child it spawns re-requires 4,201 modules / 484 MB — 10-13 s idle but 30.5 / 87.3 / 112.4 / 448.9 s under concurrent-worker load, EVERY ONE EXITING 0. The 60 s ceiling was killing healthy children roughly 5x below the worst honest case. Verified on main: default-spawn-timeout-ms is now 600000 (line ~391), env-tunable, with the diagnostic still failing RED rather than passing. A/B under identical load: 60 s -> 35 failures/20 ETIMEDOUT; 300 s -> 4/2; 600 s -> 0/0 across a 2396 s suite in a 2400 s load window. Closed as duplicate rather than dispatched — verified by reading main, not by memory.

title: JS harness self-tests fail under concurrent worktree runs (shared in-tree fixture paths)
description:
Observed twice on 2026-08-01 from worker/heapaxis-2rtt6-34 (rf2-2rtt6.34) while sibling workers were running suites in their own worktrees.

SYMPTOM. `bash scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` fails in the node tier with failures that CANNOT be reproduced standalone:

  run A: implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs -- 127 failed
         every failure an execFileSync('bash', ['-lc', ...]) returning non-zero,
         including a bare 'git ls-files -s -- scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh'
  run B: implementation/scripts/_transform-reagent-slim-ns.test.cjs -- 4 failed
         'abort: destination already exists -> non-zero exit (in-tree ns clash)'
         'abort: ns form not found -> non-zero exit (in-tree source restructured)'
         'fixture path handed to bash is relative + drive-letter-free, and
          resolves under cwd (rf2-6m7pn4)'

EVIDENCE IT IS NOT THE DIFF. The worker's diff touched only
implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_*.{cljs,cjs} and two
docs/design/hicasso/studio/*.md -- it cannot reach either test's surface. Both
suites pass standalone at the same commit in the same worktree:

  node scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs            -> 275 passed, exit 0
  node scripts/_transform-reagent-slim-ns.test.cjs   -> 6 passed,   exit 0
  npm run test:script-policy && npm run test:script-helpers -> exit 0, 0 FAIL

and the full spine went green on a re-run once no sibling was active.

HYPOTHESIS. These tests materialise fixtures at paths that are shared across
worktrees rather than scoped to the checkout -- the 'destination already
exists' and 'in-tree ns clash' wording points straight at it, and this repo
already writes to machine-global locations elsewhere (the spine log shows
STORY_BUILD_INDEX_HTML at 'C:\tmp\downstream\index.html', outside every
approved root). Two worktrees running the node tier concurrently then race
one directory. Mike runs 5-6 workers in parallel by design, so this is the
normal operating condition, not an edge case.

WHY IT MATTERS. It costs a worker a full spine cycle (~16 min) plus the
diagnosis to prove the failure is not theirs, and it trains agents to treat a
red gate as noise -- which is exactly how a real failure gets waved through.

SUGGESTED FIX. Scope every fixture root in implementation/scripts/_*.test.cjs
to a per-checkout temp dir (mkdtemp under the worktree, or keyed on the
worktree path), and assert no test writes to a machine-global path. Same
treatment for whatever hands out 'C:\tmp\downstream'.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7343

ROOT CAUSE, reproduced deterministically rather than inferred. Four
`_*.test.cjs` suites (transform-reagent-slim-ns, preflight-story-package,
preflight-reagent-slim-package, rewrite-local-root-coord) each took a unique
`mkdtemp` dir under the shared in-repo `.scratch/` — correct — and then tore
down with `fs.rmSync(SCRATCH_ROOT, {recursive:true, force:true})`, deleting
the SHARED ROOT rather than their own dir. Any second process using
`.scratch/` in the same checkout had its live fixture removed mid-run.

MEASURED, four suites run concurrently in one checkout:
  before  20/20 suite runs FAILED
  after    0/20
Each passes standalone, which is exactly why it cost a diagnosis: the script
under test then reports `expected source file ... not found` or
`cd: .scratch/...: No such file or directory`, indistinguishable at a glance
from a defect in the diff. That is the signature this bead recorded.

FIX is isolation, not tolerance — no retry, no sleep, no lock. New
implementation/scripts/lib/scratch-fixtures.cjs hands each PROCESS its own
lane and tears down only the lanes that process created; the shared root is
created on demand and never removed, so it stops being a resource one process
can take from another. `.scratch/` (not os.tmpdir()) is retained because the
bash-facing path must be repo-relative (rf2-6m7pn4).

GUARD: new _scratch-fixture-isolation.test.cjs, wired into test:script-policy,
with a behavioural arm (a child process runs the real teardown; the parent
asserts its own fixture survived) and a static arm forbidding a re-rolled
whole-root removal. BOTH arms were confirmed to FAIL against the pre-fix
teardown before being committed, so the gate is not vacuous.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD'S HYPOTHESES:
 - the `C:\tmp\downstream` / STORY_BUILD_INDEX_HTML suspicion was a misreading
   of the spine log. Those are assertion LITERALS in _path-policy.test.cjs
   (enforcePolicy is pure); nothing writes there. Not a collision source.
 - the collision is not cross-WORKTREE — REPO_ROOT differs per checkout, so
   `.scratch/` is already per-checkout. It is cross-PROCESS within one
   checkout, which is what the concurrent node tier produces.
Separately, the one genuine machine-global fixed name (the out-of-tree probe
path in _serve-and-run-cli.test.cjs) is now process-scoped.

title: test-quiet shadow-node self-tests flake under concurrent-worker load (spawnSync ETIMEDOUT)
description:
OBSERVED on worker/durab-b0tz5 (rf2-b0tz5), 2026-08-01, four full `npm run test:cljs` runs on one unchanged tree.

SYMPTOM. Tests in implementation/test-quiet/test/ fail with the child runner never starting:
  spawnSync C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe ETIMEDOUT
  --- stdout ---   (empty)
  --- stderr ---   (empty)
Failing tests seen: real-shadow-node-green-run-is-quiet, red-run-replays-buffered-console-warn,
unknown-arg-is-fatal-not-false-green, unmatched-selector-is-fatal-at-real-runner,
large-red-replay-is-not-truncated, large-replay-warns-then-fails-when-armed.

CAUSE. These tests spawnSync a nested out/node-test.js under a 60,000 ms ceiling
(spawn-timeout-ms, test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test.cljs:348). The comment calls 60s
'generous' on the assumption that 'a correctly-exiting child returns in well under a
second'. That holds on an idle box. It does not hold when sibling worker worktrees are
running browser suites and shadow-cljs compiles on the same machine: the child is starved
and killed before it produces a byte.

EVIDENCE IT IS LOAD, NOT LOGIC.
  * failure count tracks box load on an IDENTICAL tree: 0 failures (quiet box) ->
    9 -> 18 (two siblings running browser tests) -> 9.
  * the root cause is always a wall-clock timeout, never a value assertion, and both
    child streams are empty, i.e. the child never ran.
  * the branch that observed it does not touch implementation/test-quiet/ at all.

WHY IT MATTERS. It is indistinguishable, at a glance, from a real regression: a worker
sees a RED test:cljs and cannot tell whether its own change broke something. It burns a
15-minute suite per retry and can push a worker toward a false 'my change is fine' or a
false 'main is broken'.

CANDIDATE REMEDIES (not a ruling, for triage):
  1. raise spawn-timeout-ms, or scale it from an env var CI/local can set;
  2. on ETIMEDOUT specifically, retry the spawn once before failing;
  3. treat an ETIMEDOUT with both streams empty as SKIP-with-diagnostic rather than FAIL,
     since it is a statement about the box and not about the runner contract.
Option 3 keeps the gate honest (it still says something went wrong) without minting a
false regression signal. Whichever is chosen, the 60s constant should stop being
described as generous without saying 'on an unloaded box'.

SECOND, SMALLER FINDING. A --config-merge '{:ns-regexp ...}' focused compile shares the
node-test build id, so it leaves the cache in a mixed state and the NEXT full compile dies
with 'aborted par-compile ... still waiting for' and no root error. Same class as the
lane_cache.cjs rule the bench drivers already implement (one build id, N configs -> clear
the cache). Worth either documenting on the node-test build or clearing automatically.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7343

CAUSE — the ceiling rested on a premise that was never true of this build.
`spawn-timeout-ms` was 60000, and its docstring justified that with "a
correctly-exiting child returns in well under a second". `out/node-test.js`
is a dev-mode LOADER: every spawn re-`require`s the whole consolidated
node-test output, measured on this tree at 4201 modules / 484 MB. Timing the
exact child `spawn-runner` makes:

  idle box            10.0 s, 11.1 s, 13.3 s      (all exit 0)
  under sibling load  30.5 s, 87.3 s, 112.4 s,
                      448.9 s                     (all exit 0)

So the 60 s ceiling was not catching wedged children — it was killing HEALTHY
ones, ~5x below the worst honest case. The resulting `spawnSync ... ETIMEDOUT`
with both child streams empty is indistinguishable at a glance from a runner
the diff broke, which is exactly why it cost diagnoses, and why the bead's
failure count tracked box load on an unchanged tree (0 -> 9 -> 18 -> 9).

A/B UNDER IDENTICAL LOAD. Same binary, same load generator, same suite; only
the ceiling differs (the old value reinstated through the new env var, so the
BEFORE arm is the pre-fix build in every respect that matters):

  ceiling  60 s (pre-fix)   35 failures, 20 ETIMEDOUT
  ceiling 300 s             4 failures,  2 ETIMEDOUT
  ceiling 600 s (SHIPPED)   0 failures,  0 ETIMEDOUT   (wall 2396 s)

The 600 s arm ran essentially wholly under load — 2396 s of suite against a
2400 s load window — and carried a provenance guard proving the bundle under
test really contained the 600000 ms constant (v1 of that arm was discarded
BECAUSE its compile had failed under load and it silently measured a stale
bundle; see rf2-6t03c).

Load used was HARSHER than the field: 32-48 CPU burners plus 6 I/O and
process-churn loops on 24 cores. The pre-fix arm produced 20 ETIMEDOUT
against the field's worst observation of 18.

WHY THIS IS NOT TOLERANCE. The fail-fast contract is pinned separately and
strictly by `spawn-timeout-kills-a-hanging-child`, which proves a
never-exiting child is SIGTERM-killed using its OWN 1.5 s ceiling. This
constant only bounds how long a wedged child may stall the suite before that
same mechanism ends it, so raising it costs nothing in strictness. An
ETIMEDOUT remains a FAILURE — a run whose child never started has verified
nothing, and downgrading it to a skip (candidate remedy 3 in this bead) would
be a fail-open gate. Candidate remedy 2 (retry on ETIMEDOUT) was rejected for
the same reason: it would hide a genuine hang.

WHAT CHANGED, then: the ceiling is 600 s (set above the slowest HEALTHY child
actually measured, 449 s — not a round number), overridable via
RF2_SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS, with a malformed override THROWING rather than falling
back; the docstring carries the measurements instead of the false claim; and
the ETIMEDOUT diagnostic now names the ceiling, the knob, and what the child
was doing, so a reader can tell an oversubscribed box from a defect in their
change. The ten copies of that assertion message route through one helper.

SECOND FINDING SPLIT OUT to rf2-6t03c, and BROADENED there: the
`aborted par-compile ... still waiting for` failure reproduced on this tree
with NO --config-merge at all — heavy load alone is sufficient — and it
silently left a stale bundle in play for a caller that did not check the
compile's exit code. Its fix belongs in the hot-zone shadow-cljs.edn, so it
is sequenced separately.

test:browser exit 0 (931 tests), test:script-policy exit 0,
test:script-helpers exit 0, clj-kondo 2026.04.15 errors 0 (zero findings on
the changed file). Full CI on #7343: 56 pass / 26 skipping / 0 fail.

title: API manifest silently ignores a newly added public Freehand namespace
description: PR #7212 documents but does not close the recurrence class it repaired: api-manifest gen inspects only the explicit jvm-namespaces list, and doc_api_check derives coverage from the resulting manifest. A newly shipped public re-frame.freehand.* namespace omitted from both therefore leaves gen --check and doc-api-check green while every public var disappears from the manifest/API docs. This happened for re-frame.resources and again for splitter plus collection (21 names); the current sweep is only point-in-time. Add one narrow completeness gate around the explicit roster. Keep intentional classification and do not auto-publish implementation namespaces: every Freehand source namespace must be accounted for as supported/public or deliberately internal/excluded, and an unaccounted new namespace must fail with its name and required classification step. No open matching Bead exists; rf2-h0b0l and rf2-cfhuv are closed point repairs, while rf2-m41gl owns only CLJS cross-host reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: A test/mutation adding a synthetic public Freehand namespace without classifying it makes the manifest gate fail before generation/doc checks can silently omit it. Every current Freehand source namespace is accounted for as supported/public or intentionally internal; internal and ^:no-doc plumbing are not auto-enrolled. Failure output names the namespace and one remediation path. Existing explicit roster and generated docs remain authoritative; no broad reflection framework or automatic public-API inference.
close_reason:
The api-manifest generator now reconciles every namespace under implementation/freehand/src against two rosters — the public one it introspects (jvm-namespaces) and an explicit internal one — and refuses to build the manifest when a source namespace is named by neither, failing with the namespace's name and both remediation paths. The assertion runs FIRST in build-manifest, before the three sidecar reconciliations, because all of those read jvm-namespaces and so can only report on namespaces the roster already names. Reconciliation is symmetric: unaccounted, stale internal entry, and both-rosters-at-once each fail. It infers nothing — no namespace is auto-enrolled and no var auto-published; only the OBLIGATION to classify is automated (^:no-doc could not have been the classifier: only 6 of 61 internal namespaces carry it).

MUTATION-PROVEN: a throwaway public re-frame.freehand.mutation-probe made 'clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check' exit 2 naming the namespace; reverting returned exit 0 with a clean git diff (baseline exit 0 first). The new test namespace was proven non-vacuous by inverting an assertion (clojure -M:test exit 1 naming the test) and reverting (exit 0); nine tests cover all three drift arms, the missing-root case, the file->namespace munge and a synthetic tree driven end-to-end through build-manifest.

NOTHING SLIPPED THROUGH while it was blind: the enrolled set is exactly the door plus the six siblings spec/Conventions.md §Freehand holds as the roster of record, and a test now pins that equality. Recorded rather than hidden: re-frame.freehand.evidence and .presence-runtime are required by TOOL production source (xray mounted_views, story presence_host) and evidence/schema is named in a normative Conventions row — classified internal here because §Freehand does not list them; whether a tool-consumed seam earns a :tooling row like re-frame.mcp-base.elision is left to that roster's owner.

Gates: manifest --check 0, clojure -M:test 0 (161 tests/389 assertions), test-fast-pr.sh 0, npm run test:cljs 0 (12263 tests), mkdocs --strict 0, check_doc_slugs.py 0, clj-kondo 2026.04.15 errors:0.
