title: [bug] core test: the weak-expunge proof pins a process-wide async count with `=`, so a loaded runner reds it
description:
SYMPTOM. `JVM core (clojure -M:test)` went red on PR #7331 (run 30655577476, job
91239771476) with ONE failure out of 2198 tests:

  FAIL in (jvm-provenance-entry-is-weak-and-expunged-when-its-throwable-dies)
       (observation_port_cljs_test.cljc:3515)
  "the cleared entry was expunged - private storage returned to baseline"
  actual: false

NOT THE PR. #7331 changed six `.cljs` files under
`implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/**` plus one design `.md`.
`implementation/core`'s `:test` alias does not put `implementation/freehand` on
the classpath, and a JVM Clojure runner cannot load `.cljs` at all. There is no
mechanism by which that diff reaches this suite.

ROOT CAUSE. The failing assertion is

  (loop [i 0]
    (#'obs/source-covered-always-on? (ex-info \"post-gc access\" {}))
    (cond (= baseline (.size m)) true
          (>= i 40)              false
          :else (do (System/gc) (System/runFinalization) (recur (inc i)))))

`m` is the PROCESS-WIDE `java.util.HashMap` at
`(:by-throwable @#'obs/provenance-storage)`, keyed by weak identity keys and
reclaimed lazily by polling a `ReferenceQueue` in `expunge-stale-provenance!`.
`baseline` is `.size` sampled after ONE `System.gc()` and one drain - i.e. a
count of how many OTHER tests' entries happened to still sit in the map at that
instant. Two facts make the strict `=` unsound:

1. A Reference is CLEARED during GC but ENQUEUED asynchronously afterwards by
   the ReferenceHandler thread. A drain taken immediately after `System.gc()`
   returns cannot see references already cleared but not yet enqueued, so
   `baseline` over-counts by the size of that pending backlog - and the backlog
   grows with machine load.

2. Nothing inside the loop ever ADDS an entry (`source-covered-always-on?` only
   reads and drains), so `.size` is monotonically non-increasing. The instant
   any pending sibling lands, `.size` falls BELOW `baseline` and
   `(= baseline (.size m))` can never become true again; the loop exhausts its
   40 rounds and yields false.

So the test reddens BECAUSE unrelated collection succeeded. The busier the
runner, the likelier it fails - which is the load-sensitivity observed.

THE NAMED PROPERTY HELD ON THE RED RUN. The preceding `(is (gc-until-cleared?
t-ref))` PASSED, so the referent was collected and storage retained it via
neither key nor value. Only the global-count equality failed. The test's
docstring claims \"the cleared entry was expunged\"; what it checks is \"the
map's total size equals a number it had before a 40-round GC storm\". Those are
not the same statement.

NON-DETERMINISM, MEASURED. On #7331's head: `clojure -M:test` in
`implementation/core` green 3x (2198 tests / 11341 assertions, exit 0); the
namespace alone green 8x run CONCURRENTLY under CPU contention. Instrumented,
`baseline` is consistently 0 and the pre-loop size 1 - an idle box has no
pending backlog, which is precisely why it cannot reproduce locally.

RECOMMENDED FIX - stronger, not weaker. Assert the specific claim rather than a
global count. `.size` is `baseline+1` at attestation and can only decrease, so
`(<= (.size m) baseline)` states exactly \"the new entry was expunged\" with no
coupling to unrelated entries. Better still, track that entry's own absence
instead of any count.

PROVENANCE. Introduced 2026-07-14 in 620f5568e7 (rf2-qqvgk1); last touched
2026-07-29 in f685fccf42 (rf2-d2841). Pre-existing and independent of #7331,
and deliberately NOT patched from #7331's branch - different artefact, and
`implementation/core/test/**` is a surface the audit loop works actively.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7336 (branch worker/expunge-8vvdo, commit ab5e32c66d).

The diagnosis was verified against implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/observation.cljc and holds: m is the process-wide HashMap, keys are weak identity keys reclaimed only by expunge-stale-provenance! polling the ReferenceQueue, source-covered-always-on? only reads and drains (never adds) so .size is monotonically non-increasing inside the loop, and a Reference is cleared during GC but enqueued asynchronously afterwards - so baseline over-counts by the pending backlog and the size falls BELOW it under load.

THREE CORRECTIONS to the bead.

1. The RECOMMENDED FIX was NOT applied, because it is unsound. (<= (.size m) baseline) cures the false red by buying a FALSE GREEN under the same load: a sibling expunging in our entry's place satisfies it while our entry is still leaked. Measured, not argued - in a seeded-backlog run the probe (and (<= (.size m) baseline) (.containsKey m our-key)) PASSED, i.e. <= held with our entry demonstrably still in the map, before the throwable had even been released. The bead's own better-still alternative is what landed: the stored key is located by referent identity over the live key set and the assertion is (not (.containsKey m our-key)). Holding that key strongly retains the KEY, never its referent (it is a WeakReference subclass, and the HashMap holds its keys strongly in production anyway), so the lifecycle under test is unchanged.

2. The bead diagnosed only the poll loop at 3515. The SIBLING assertion carried the identical defect: (= (inc baseline) (.size m)) - 'the attestation bound exactly one entry' - reds whenever the attest's own drain reclaims a pending sibling before the .put. Left alone the test would have stayed load-sensitive after the loop was repaired. It is now (= 1 (count our-keys)) - exactly one key in the map has this throwable as referent - which is load-independent and a literal statement of what it claims.

3. Path: the bead names implementation/core/test/re_frame/substrate/observation_port_cljs_test.cljc; the file is implementation/core/test/re_frame/observation_port_cljs_test.cljc (no substrate/ segment). Line 3515 was correct.

MUTATION PROOF. Planted the defect in production code - expunge-stale-provenance! polls but never removes, so a cleared key leaks forever while the referent still clears. RED, exit 1, 1 failure of 4, with gc-until-cleared? and the exactly-one-entry precondition both still passing (the leak isolated from every other assertion). Reverted, git diff empty: GREEN, exit 0. Run twice - once before the mid-task API outage and once after on a since-idle box - identical.

OLD FAILURE MODE REPRODUCED DETERMINISTICALLY. A scratch test (temporary, reverted, not committed) seeded the backlog the async enqueue produces on a loaded runner - a sibling entry cleared and still counted when baseline is sampled. Both OLD forms red and both NEW forms green in the SAME run, 3/3 runs: baseline=1, size-after-attest=1, final size=0 - the size fell below the sampled baseline exactly as diagnosed.

GATES (all foreground, exit codes echoed). clojure -M:test in implementation/core: 0 (2198 tests, 11341 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors) - the gate that reddened. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh: 0 (PASS fast PR spine); its JVM implementation/core leg ran while sibling workers were active, i.e. under load. clj-kondo 2026.04.15 (CI's pinned version, CI's exact --lint invocation; local npm binary was v2025.10.23 so the pinned release was fetched): 0, errors: 0. TESTING.md matrix: the diff is one file under implementation/core/test/** with no production code, so the fast-PR JVM tier is implementation/core alone - confirmed by --plan printing PLAN-JVM implementation/core. test-jvm-implementation.sh is not mapped for this surface (TESTING.md scopes it to a broad refactor reaching artefacts the tier does not select); the wider CI fan-out runs in CI.

PR left OPEN for the mayor to merge.

title: hicasso: converge a controlled element in-turn, with the caret where the edit left it
description:
MEASURED AND GREEN AS A PROTOTYPE; needs a home.

Neither shipped path gives a controlled input both halves of what a
store-backed field owes its user — same-turn convergence AND a caret at the
position the edit left it. React converges in-turn and throws the caret to the
end; UIx's port gets the caret right one animation frame late. The matrix is on
docs/design/hicasso/studio/controlled-input-two-implementations.md (rf2-n3dxw).

THE SHAPE, measured green on all five rows of the family in one turn
(`a-same-turn-converge-can-have-both-halves-at-a-stated-price` in
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/controlled_restore_dom_cljs_test.cljs).
At the end of the change handler, still inside the discrete event and still
ahead of React's own end-of-event restore:

  1. `flushSync` so the synchronous door's commit lands now rather than in the
     `finally` of React's `batchedUpdates$1`;
  2. if the field still disagrees with what the element renders, write the
     rendered value — which also makes React's later `updateInput` a no-op,
     because it only assigns when the two differ;
  3. put the caret back by offset from the END of the string.

PRICE, stated: one `flushSync` per keystroke on a controlled element; a
per-instance record of the value that element last rendered (the handler's own
closure carries the value from the render that MINTED it, which is stale after a
re-render, and `(= (.-value node) dom-value)` alone cannot tell a refusal from a
keystroke the model took verbatim — that trap is measured, not assumed); and the
synchronous door only, because `dispatch` drains on a macrotask so at the end of
the handler the model has not moved.

WHAT IT DOES NOT COST: no user-visible ceremony — the view writes an ordinary
`:value`/`:on-change` pair, no ref, no effect, no escape hatch; and no hook in
the boundary shell, so the HD-020 ≤2-hook budget is untouched. UIx's own answer
costs a wrapper COMPONENT per input with three hooks in it
(`uix/compiler/input.cljs:132-143`); this costs none, because it belongs in the
element path rather than in a component.

BLOCKED ON: an element path to put it in. Neither Hicasso nor the shipped UIx
adapter mints its own `:input` today — UIx does — which is why the prototype
sits in the witness's view labelled as a measurement. Dispatch when Hicasso's
interpreter owns element creation, or alongside a ruling on rf2-heqwo.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-02 (worker/converge-fki5d, PR #7371
https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7371).

WHERE IT LIVES. `front.controlled/install!`, called from
`front.codec/native-element` — the element path, which is what makes it free at
the authoring surface. `grid.cljs` (the 100-cell witness's view) did not change
by a character: an ordinary `:value` / `:on-input` pair, no ref, no effect, no
escape hatch. NO HOOK WAS SPENT — nothing was added to the boundary shell and
`arm1_hook_ledger_dom_cljs_test` still reads exactly
["useContext" "useSyncExternalStore"].

THE FIVE ROWS, in one turn, on the arm's mounted grid
(`arm1_controlled_grid_dom_cljs_test/the-family-converges-in-one-turn-with-the-caret-where-the-edit-left-it`),
every reading on the line after `dispatchEvent`, no `act` anywhere:

  refusal at the end   "12"    + a at [2 2] -> "12"     [2 2]
  refusal mid-string   "12345" + z at [2 2] -> "12345"  [2 2]   (React alone: [5 5])
  uppercasing          "ABCD"  + x at [2 2] -> "ABXCD"  [3 3]   (React alone: [5 5])
  regrouping           "1,234" + 5 at [5 5] -> "12,345" [6 6]
  accepted keystroke   "abcd"  + X at [2 2] -> "abXcd"  [3 3]

Two rows that recorded React's caret jump as RECORDED-NOT-DESIRED are corrected
to what the arm now does.

THE PRICE IS LOWER THAN QUOTED. One `flushSync` per keystroke and the
synchronous door only, as priced. But the third item — a per-instance record of
the value the element last rendered — IS NOT CHARGED. It is `node.defaultValue`,
which React already maintains on every commit of a genuinely controlled input or
textarea (`updateInput:1671-1672` -> `setDefaultValue:1737-1741`,
`initInput:1721`, `updateTextarea:1842-1851`, react-dom 19.2.0). No ref (which
would change the identity React uses to decide whether to re-attach — the
objection `front.intent/ref-position?` already documents), no WeakMap, no extra
prop. What remains is a DEPENDENCY, named in one place
(`front.controlled/last-rendered`) and pinned against a live React tree by
`the-record-is-reacts-own-mirror-and-is-not-the-handlers-closure`, which also
asserts the record MOVES when the rendered value moves — the half a closure
cannot do.

THE TRAP IS REPRODUCED, not assumed.
`front/controlled_dom_cljs_test/the-closure-value-wipes-a-keystroke-the-model-took-verbatim`
calls `converge-to!` twice with ONE ARGUMENT DIFFERENT: handed the handler's own
closure value it writes "abcd" over the user's just-accepted "abXcd" and the
character is gone; handed the record, nothing moves. A companion row measures
why nothing cheaper works — `(= (.-value node) dom-value)` reads TRUE on a
refusal and TRUE on a verbatim keystroke.

MUTATION-PROVED TWICE. Removing the one `install!` call reds 14 assertions, every
caret falling back to [5 5] with the refused character still on screen. Removing
only the `flushSync` reds 4, including the ORDINARY ACCEPTED KEYSTROKE — without
it the record is one render stale. Both restored, green.

GATES: test:cljs 0 (12290 tests / 61538 assertions); full browser 0 (940 / 5895);
fast-PR spine 0 (PASS, 17/17 per-ns isolation); check_doc_slugs 0; clj-kondo
2026.04.15 with CI's exact invocation, errors: 0, zero findings in any changed
file.

RAISED, NOT RESOLVED: HD-019 calls `flushSync` "the evidence-gated last resort,
never the default", and this makes it the default for every controlled element.
The evidence gate is met; the ruling's text is Mike's to amend. Filed separately.
close_reason:
AUDIT GAP FIXED in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7401 (branch worker/caret-fki5d-47sko).

THE GAP, as the #7371 audit stated it: install! decides an element is caret-bearing from the props that MINT the wrapper, but step 1 of the converge is a flushSync — and a flushSync is a render. A synchronous handler re-rendering the same <input> from type=text to type=number keeps the node (React updates the attribute), so the wrapper minted by the text render goes on running against an element with no caret, and setSelectionRange throws InvalidStateError.

THE FIX IS ONE LINE. converge! reads the caret a SECOND time, after the flush, and is inert when the answer changed:

  (when (and (string? rendered)
             (number? (.-selectionStart node)))
    (converge-to! node dom-value caret-was rendered))

converge-to! is untouched, so the trap row that calls it twice with one argument different still says exactly what it said. No hook added — this adds a READING, never a write; arm1_hook_ledger_dom_cljs_test is unchanged and green.

THE ROW: arm1_controlled_grid_dom_cljs_test/a-type-change-inside-the-flush-leaves-the-converge-inert. A live React tree, no act, no flushSync in the path it reads; a type-flipping-cell derives :type from the model so ONE accepted keystroke re-renders text->number inside the converge's own flush. It asserts the premise rather than assuming it — (identical? before after) pins that React really kept the node.

A LISTENER WAS NECESSARY, and this is worth recording. React does not let a throw from inside a discrete event escape dispatchEvent; it hands it to reportError. The first draft of the row was GREEN OVER A LIVE EXCEPTION while the runner's uncaught-pageerror gate (rf2-mwx08) failed the build from outside — cljs.test read 0 failures, 0 errors. The row now installs a window error listener so the throw is its own to assert and it reds BY NAME.

MUTATION-PROVED: deleting only the post-flush reading gives exit 1 and EXACTLY ONE failure, by name —
  expected: (= [] errs)
    actual: (not (= [] ["Failed to execute 'setSelectionRange' on 'HTMLInputElement': The input element's type ('number') does not support selection."]))
Every OTHER assertion in the row passed under the mutation, including the stale-record one. That is what establishes the throw as the defect and record-staleness as the second, quieter reason to be inert.

THE RECORD IS STALE THERE, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED. setDefaultValue skips a FOCUSED number field (react-dom@19.2.0:1738), so defaultValue still holds what the TEXT render wrote — the row asserts (= "" (last-rendered after)) directly. The converge would write that over the field mid-event; React's own end-of-event restore happens to put the committed value back, so the field survives — by accident. The prose says exactly that and does NOT overclaim a data loss that does not occur.

THE FIVE LANDED ROWS ARE UNTOUCHED and green throughout.

rf2-digtt UNTOUCHED: this adds a DOM read and removes a write. It never consults, sets or clears composing state and does not change the composing path in either direction. The carve-out remains unruled and unimplemented.

GATES, foreground with exit codes: scripts/test-fast-pr.sh 0 (PASS fast PR spine, per-ns isolation 17/17); test:browser 0 (1025 tests / 6345 assertions); test:browser under mutation 1 (1 failure, by name); shadow-cljs compile browser-test 0; adapter smokes --filter uix 0 (1 spec). NOT run: docs gates (no doc surface changed), the CI-only tier, and the non-UIx adapter smokes.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7371 — correctness gap in the shipped converge. `install!` decides that an input is caret-bearing from the props that minted the currently running wrapper, but `converge!` reads `selectionStart` before `flushSync` and `converge-to!` calls `setSelectionRange` unconditionally after that flush. A synchronous handler can re-render the same `<input>` from `type="text"` to `type="number"` (or another non-caret type) during the flush; React retains the node, after the commit `selectionStart` is nil, and the old wrapper throws `InvalidStateError` from `setSelectionRange`. Independent Chromium primitive: text/value/defaultValue `12345`, caret 2; switch the focused node to number; value/defaultValue remain `12345`, selectionStart becomes null, and `setSelectionRange(2,2)` throws exactly that error. Add a live React regression where the handler synchronously changes the type and require the converge to re-check post-flush applicability and remain inert, without weakening the five landed rows.

title: MEASURE: the :& attribute-merge spelling's clock cost is unmeasured (HD-023 caveat)
description:
RAISED by the rf2-2rtt6.36 worker (PR #7328), which recorded the gap in HD-023 rather than letting it pass silently.

THE OBLIGATION IT TRIPS. The 'Hicasso authors no codec' ruling (rf2-2rtt6.29, PR #7322) carries an explicit caveat: reagent-slim's codec is cheapest AS MEASURED, and Freehand's extra per-element capabilities (controlled-input door, caller split, top-layer, declared properties, id-conflict, class/style alias composition) are a CAPABILITY difference rather than pure overhead — so 'if Hicasso later needs one of those capabilities, THE COST OF ADDING IT TO SLIM'S CODEC MUST BE MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED'. The :& merge is exactly such an addition: a reserved key the codec must recognise and resolve at every element that carries one.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT KNOWN. The ergonomics case is DEMONSTRATED, not asserted — the RealWorld article editor was ported both ways with elements AND dispatched intents asserted identical, four repeated attribute maps collapsing to one helper plus four call sites, and the helper does not have to defend itself. What is NOT known is what :& costs on the clock, per element and per mount, against the same page without it.

THE WORK: price :& on the existing lane — same witness, same rounds, same arm-order discipline, the only variation being whether the page uses :& or the expanded attribute maps it replaces. Report per-element and per-mount cost with ranges, and state plainly whether it is inside instrument resolution. If it is free, say so and the caveat is discharged; if it is not, the figure belongs beside HD-023 so the ergonomic win is quoted with its price rather than without it.

SEQUENCING: needs a QUIET BOX (browser measurement) and should run after PR #7328 lands so it measures the shipped spelling. Do not re-litigate the ergonomics ruling — that is settled and demonstrated; this bead prices it.
notes:
SHAPE NOTE from the rf2-2rtt6.36 worker (2026-08-03, the merged-PR audit #7332 repair): the codec this bead prices CHANGED SHAPE under it, so measure the shipped one. The tag shorthand is no longer folded into the props map — merge-shorthand and its dissoc/assoc pair are gone, and the shorthand is folded onto the object the walk emits instead (fold-shorthand!). convert-props' three lanes are two: the propless short-circuit, and convert-then-fold. The :& merge itself is unchanged (still one contains?, still the map by identity when absent), but the per-element denominator around it is not what it was, and the class slot now costs a class-names coercion at the slot rather than one in the map surgery. Nothing here is a timing claim — the repair PR ran no bench driver and published no row, deliberately, because siblings held the box. Related: rf2-2rtt6.70 (walk_profile_app's :shorthand-merge / :no-short arms now price a shape that ships nowhere).
DEFERRED BY THE MAYOR 2026-08-08 10:30 AUSEST — the measurement lane is stood down for the P2 sitting, on the operator's instruction. Not abandoned; held. This bead prices the :& spelling to discharge HD-023's caveat, and that caveat is about quoting an ergonomic win without its price — a real obligation, but not an input the sitting needs, and it rides the same clock-of-record family whose bulk gate refused 0 of 42. The ergonomics ruling it prices is settled and demonstrated; only the number is outstanding. Revive it if the P2 fork goes to graduation, where per-element codec cost becomes a shipping concern rather than a caveat.

title: hicasso: record-reads' set difference is dead on the wired path -- every commit diffs against the empty set, so a one-key change costs a full teardown+rebuild
description:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF LANDED CODE, origin/main @ 40e309600e (arm1 last touched by 7e40db6481).

HD-002(b) is discharged against `front.sub-index/record-reads`'s set difference
(runtime.cljs:87-94; studio/arm1-lean-react-dogfood-judgement.md:128-135), and law 4 ("a re-run
with fewer reads drops edges") is proved for that algebra in front/sub_index_laws_cljs_test.

THE WIRED RUNTIME NEVER TAKES THAT PATH. Arm 1's boundary id is the REGISTRATION OBJECT minted
inside `subscribe` (runtime.cljs:738-745). A changed read set means a new entry, a new `subscribe`
closure, and therefore a NEW registration object. `index/mount!` (front/sub_index.cljs:100-108)
installs `#{}` for that fresh id, so in `record-reads` (front/sub_index.cljs:133-156) `held` is
ALWAYS the empty set: `added` is always the whole read set and `dropped` is always empty. The
narrowing half is done by `index/unmount!`'s drop-everything (front/sub_index.cljs:123-131), not
by the diff. arm1/runtime_cljs_test.cljs:309-322 shows the shape without naming it — the test has
to `(release)` before committing the narrower read set.

CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS THE POINT AND NOT THE PEDANTRY: there is no cheap route for "19 of 20 keys
unchanged". Trace what React does when `subscribe` identity moves — previous cleanup, then new
subscribe:
  - cleanup (runtime.cljs:746-752): `index/unmount!` drops EVERY edge, then
    `(doseq [cell cells] (release-cell! cell))` decrements EVERY cell, each one reaching 0 arming
    its own js/setTimeout reaper (runtime.cljs:411-419, 489-492);
  - `entry-for` miss (runtime.cljs:673-686): `.slice`, `(into #{} ks)`, two closures, a
    `swap! !entries`, and one more js/setTimeout;
  - new subscribe (runtime.cljs:738-745): `mapv acquire-cell!` over EVERY key, `index/mount!`,
    `index/record-reads!`.
For a 20-read boundary with one key changed that is 20 releases + 20 re-acquires + ~22 scheduled
macrotasks + two whole-map rebuilds of :sub->bs. The judgement prices it as "an identity change
and one replacement" (:374-378). That understates it, and it is exactly the cost the same page
names as "the thing to watch on the bulk rows".

The steady-state claim is NOT under attack: an unchanged read set really is free and really is
witnessed (runtime_cljs_test.cljs:283-297, :392-400). What is wrong is the changed case.

WHAT TO DECIDE (this bead is a finding + a design question, not a prescription):
  (a) accept the cliff, and correct runtime.cljs:87-94 and judgement:128-135 to describe the path
      that runs (unmount-all + mount-all) rather than the algebra that is tested; or
  (b) give the boundary a durable id across re-subscribes so `record-reads`'s diff becomes live —
      note this needs care: a durable id is per-boundary identity, and the HD-002 tripwire bans
      per-RENDER/per-ATTEMPT identity, not per-MOUNT identity, so a mount-scoped token minted in
      `subscribe` and threaded through the cleanup is likely legal. Argue it against the tripwire
      explicitly before implementing.
Either way, `sub_index`'s law-4 coverage should gain a witness that drives it through the
runtime's own wiring, so the tested algebra and the running path stop diverging.
close_reason: Closed

title: hicasso: the read-set entry cache degrades to an O(N) scan selected by read ORDER, and :read-set-entry is misfiled as :shared
description:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF LANDED CODE, origin/main @ 40e309600e (arm1 last touched by 7e40db6481).
File: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/runtime.cljs

(1) THE O(N) BUCKET SCAN. `entry-for` buckets on `(aget scratch 0)` — the FIRST read — and then
linearly scans the bucket with an ordered pairwise compare (:673-676, :648-662). Read ORDER is
documented nowhere as significant, and it selects between O(1) and O(N) per render:

  ;; O(1): every row's first key is distinct, so every bucket holds one entry
  (defview row [{:keys [id]}]
    (let [todo   (sub [:dogfood/todo id])
          dense? (sub [:ui/dense?])] ...))

  ;; O(N): every row's first key is the SAME, so all N entries share one bucket
  (defview row [{:keys [id]}]
    (let [dense? (sub [:ui/dense?])          ; <- moved up two lines
          todo   (sub [:dogfood/todo id])] ...))

In the second form every probe passes the length test (2 == 2) and the index-0 test (identical
shared key) and fails only at index 1, so nothing short-circuits. Mounting 300 rows costs
sum(i) ~= 44,850 probes ~= 90k `=` calls on nested vectors; a write to [:ui/dense?] dirties all
300 and costs another 44,850. The first form costs 300. Same page, same edges, same DOM, ~150x
the entry-lookup work, chosen by which `let` binding an author wrote first.

Entries with refs >= 1 are never reaped (:638-646, :751), so the bucket does not drain while the
rows are mounted. `drop-entry!` (:630-636) then rebuilds the whole bucket vector per eviction, so
unmounting the list is O(N^2) again.

This lands on the bulk K=100/300 rung the programme benchmarks and is invisible to every current
witness, because the dogfood row happens to read its per-row key first
(arm1/dogfood_collector.cljs:59-61).

Candidate fixes (design, not ruled): bucket on a cheap content hash of the whole key sequence
rather than the first key; or keep a per-bucket map from a joined key-string to the entry. Either
keeps the false-negative-only property (a miss costs a second entry and a replace-set-with-itself,
never a missing edge — runtime.cljs:96-101) and must be argued to keep it.

(2) `:read-set-entry` IS FILED UNDER `:shared` AND IS NOT, IN THE SHAPE THAT MATTERS.
`retained-inventory` puts it under `:shared` at :926-927. For the bulk-row shape — a row body
reading [:dogfood/todo id], i.e. arm1/dogfood_collector.cljs:59-71 — every row has a DISTINCT
read set, so there is exactly one entry per live boundary: a JS object, a key array, a
PersistentHashSet of the same keys, and two closures. Any heap ladder reading the inventory
literally (rf2-2rtt6.34) will under-count per-boundary retention by one entry per boundary, on
the exact rung it is being taken for.

ACCEPTANCE: the scan is no longer O(live boundaries sharing a first key) — with a witness that
mounts N rows in the shared-first-key shape and asserts the probe count (or entry-lookup work) is
sub-linear in N; and `retained-inventory` states honestly that an entry is shared only across
boundaries with an IDENTICAL read sequence, so the bulk case is per-boundary.
close_reason: Closed

title: hicasso: the registry-epoch and node-key axes still have no counterpart in the epoch sum
description:
SCOPED OUT of rf2-2rtt6.42 DELIBERATELY, and filed rather than left implied.

rf2-2rtt6.42 closed the STAGED-read tear on the VERSION axis by giving the
epoch-sum getSnapshot a term that does not depend on a watch existing: a key
with no cell contributes its frame's `commit-basis` = the runtime's flush
generation + `re-frame.frame/frame-commit-epoch`. Two of the predecessor's
three compared fields are still uncovered, and for the same structural reason
rf2-2rtt6.33 gave.

1. REGISTRY-EPOCH. `observation/registry-epoch*` is bumped on every `:sub`
   registration (first-time AND replacement), which is how the observation
   port sees an HMR re-registration land in the render->commit gap. A
   re-registration is not a frame-state install, so it does not move
   `frame-commit-epoch` and does not move `commit-basis`. Row 3 of
   `generation_fence_coverage_cljs_test` is this case and is unmoved by
   rf2-2rtt6.42 -- correctly, since that row uses a RETAINED key, and closing
   the axis for a retained key means adding a registry term to EVERY key's
   contribution, i.e. re-rendering every boundary on every re-registration.
   That is a real design decision (bead rf2-2rtt6.42's candidate (b)), not a
   defect fix, and it wants costing before it is taken.
   BLOCKER IF TAKEN: `registry-epoch*` is `^:private` with no public reader,
   so this needs a substrate change (expose a reader) before the arm can read
   it at all. That is why rf2-2rtt6.42 did not fold it in as a one-liner.

2. NODE-KEY (a same-id frame REINCARNATION). `frame/dissoc-frame!` clears the
   destroyed frame's commit-epoch entry, so a same-id successor RESTARTS at 0
   -- `observation_port_cljs_test` asserts exactly that ("frame-commit-epoch
   ties across the reincarnation (epoch restarted)"). `commit-basis` is
   therefore monotone only WITHIN one incarnation, which is precisely why the
   observation port carries `:node-key` as a third field rather than trusting
   the two epochs. Arm 1 observes node identity nowhere.

REACHABILITY, honestly: (1) is an HMR / dev-time hazard, not a production
one -- an app that never re-registers a sub never moves the registry epoch.
(2) needs a frame destroyed and re-created under the same id while a boundary
is between its render and its commit; `runtime/forget-frame-ops!` exists for
the reincarnation case but is not wired to anything that would correct a
staged read. Neither is the P0 that rf2-2rtt6.42 was; both are the honest
remainder of "one comparison covers three fields", and the record should not
be allowed to imply otherwise.

WHERE THE CLAIM IS WRITTEN DOWN: `arm1/runtime.cljs`'s `commit-basis`
docstring and the ns docstring's "commit basis" section both name this bead.
notes:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW CORROBORATION + one refinement (origin/main @ 40e309600e, read-only).

CORROBORATED, and stronger than the bead claims for itself. I tried to construct a FOURTH axis
and could not, and the reason is structural:
  - The epoch SUM is provably sound. Every term in `make-snapshot` (arm1/runtime.cljs:711-723) is
    non-decreasing — a cell epoch is re-stamped only inside `flush!`, AFTER `(vswap! !generation inc)`
    (:519-523), so the new stamp strictly exceeds the old; a staged key's commit-time term is the
    cell's birth basis, which is >= the basis the render read. So Sum_commit >= Sum_render with
    equality IFF no term moved. Sum collision is impossible, and `Object.is` on it is exact.
  - Every physical frame-state install goes through exactly three sites — `adapter/replace-container!`
    against a frame-state container appears at frame.cljc:1406, :1540, :1563 — and all three bump
    (frame.cljc:1321-1326). The `identical?`-noop short-circuit at :1401-1402 skips the bump only
    when nothing is installed, so no value can have moved.
  - Every subscription in this substrate is a pure function of frame state: there is no
    `reg-sub-raw` and no external-signal registration kind (subs.cljc exposes `:input-signals`
    for the `:static` kind only). So there is no "sub over an external source" axis.
Conclusion: the two axes this bead names really are the two.

REFINEMENT WORTH FOLDING IN — a THIRD FACE of the reincarnation axis, which a reader will trip
over in the source and not recognise. The epoch bump is deliberately FENCED on owner loss
(frame.cljc:1401-1407 and :1568-1570): the install lands in the captured container but the bump is
suppressed so it cannot attribute to a same-id successor. That is an install that genuinely
happened and genuinely did not move the basis. It is reachable only when the boundary's own
incarnation is already gone, so it collapses into `:node-key` — but this bead should name it,
because "installs always bump" has a visible counter-example in the source.

RE-CHECK ITEM: 2d1f36866d ("a movement witness retires the wasted layer-1 compare", subs/spine)
landed after the tree this arm was written against. `acquire-cell!`'s watch gates on `(= old nu)`
(arm1/runtime.cljs:483) and this arm uses the notification ITSELF as the dirty signal, so the
sub layer's notification discipline is load-bearing here in a way it is not for the shipping
spine. Worth one read against the post-2d1f36866d tree.

Full review: ai/findings/2026-08-01.hicasso-landed-adapter-adversarial-review.md (gitignored).
COSTING DONE, BROAD OPTION DECLINED, BOTH AXES CLOSED BY A NARROWER ROUTE.
Branch worker/axes-2rtt6-44. No substrate change: registry-epoch* stays ^:private,
no public reader added, NO SPEC SURFACE TOUCHED.

THE PREMISE WAS WRONG. Neither axis was a blind spot in the epoch sum. Both events
DISPOSE the reaction an Arm 1 cell holds -- a :sub re-registration via
subs.cache/invalidate-sub-on-replace!, a frame destruction via frame teardown -- and
the spine's derived container does (reset! watchers {}) in -dispose (spine.cljs:949),
taking the arm's add-watch with it. MEASURED on the pre-fix runtime:
  registry:  read returns 2 where the live registration answers 20; next write
             notified 0 times; read after it returns 3 where the new handler gives 30.
  node-key:  read returns 1 where the successor holds 99; 0 notifications; still 1
             after a write on B.
  frame-commit-epoch A=1, 0 after dissoc-frame!, B=1 -- the basis TIES EXACTLY across
  the reincarnation, so no arithmetic over those two terms could separate them.
So the boundary is permanently deaf and derives through the RETIRED COMPUTATION (not a
stale value that tracks the db -- a stale computation, which looks alive).

WHY THE REGISTRY TERM WAS DECLINED. (a) It corrects nothing: the extra render a moved
number buys calls read-key!, finds the cell, derefs the disposed reaction. Pinned as an
assertion -- the held container answers 7 where the live registration answers 70.
(b) Frequency: registry-epoch* bumps per :sub registration, first-time AND replacement;

title: MEASURE: thread the frame as a codec-supplied prop and delete the per-boundary frame-context hook
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained; do not rely on any untracked findings file).

A HYPOTHESIS TO MEASURE, not a proposal to adopt. It frees one of the two hook slots
the whole Arm 1 shell is budgeted at.

WHERE THE BUDGET GOES TODAY. HD-020(b) (docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md:404-407) and
the budget table (docs/design/hicasso/validation.md:36) spend the <=2 hooks per
product boundary on "the subscription/epoch hook and the frame-context hook", and
"a third hook in the shell is a budget breach". The Arm 1 lean-React runtime pays the
second as useContext(frame-context) and then memoises the frame-locked op bundle per
frame so the per-render cost is one map lookup
(re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/runtime.cljs, on the arm branch — see the frame-ops
docstring, "HD-020(a) has each boundary read the frame ONCE from the substrate's
single internal context; it does not ask each boundary to rebuild the bundle").

THE HYPOTHESIS. The frame does not need a hook at all, because it is ordinary data
that flows down the tree. When the codec turns [child-view props] into a React
element it can bake the frame into the element's props. The root's element carries it;
every descendant element is CREATED by an ancestor body that already knows it. A
foreign component in between is harmless: children elements were built with the prop
already in them, so passing props.children through preserves it. The only creator that
would lack it is an outward React bridge, which takes an explicit frame anyway.

IF IT HOLDS: one hook per boundary disappears. The P0 record prices an isolated
useSyncExternalStore rung at ~516 B (docs/design/hicasso/charter.md:66-69), which is
of the same order as the whole 0.4-0.5 KB boundary-shell target
(validation.md:37) — so this is a shell-budget-relevant quantity, not a rounding
error. It also frees the second slot for anything v0 later needs, which today it
cannot have.

WHAT IT COSTS. One extra entry in every boundary element's props map, on every render.
That is an allocation and a retention cost on the OTHER side of the ledger, and it is
exactly why this is a measurement rather than a ruling.

MULTI-FRAME CORRECTNESS IS THE HARD PART, NOT THE HEAP. Use case 16 is multi-frame
isolation (charter.md:190-191). Context gets frame isolation for free by construction;
prop-threading must PROVE it. A witness that mounts one app in two isolated frames and
asserts no read crosses is mandatory before any number is quotable.

SCOPE
  1. Build the prop-threaded variant against the SAME witnesses the context variant
     uses. Both variants on one branch, one instrument, one run.
  2. Count hooks at React's own dispatcher, the way the arm's existing hook-ledger DOM
     test does — never self-reported.
  3. Price retained heap per boundary on the 1/3/7/20 ladder, and the clock on mount +
     bulk. Browser numbers only, :advanced, per HD-012 (decisions.md:256-258); JVM/Node
     figures are diagnostic and are never quotable against the bar.
  4. Multi-frame isolation witness (above). A red here kills the hypothesis outright
     regardless of the heap result.
  5. Publish to docs/design/hicasso/studio/ and append to the standard bead rf2-2rtt6.1
     with the producing commit SHA and the repro command.

MEASUREMENT POSTURE: do NOT contend for the box with the instrument workers — build
and self-witness first, take the comparative rows when the lane is free.
close_reason: Correctness half done; measurement half split to rf2-2rtt6.72. Scope items 1, 2 and 4 are green: the prop-threaded variant is built BESIDE the incumbent (bead: 'both variants on one branch'), hooks counted at React's own dispatcher — context shell 2 (useContext + useSyncExternalStore), frame-prop shell 1 (useSyncExternalStore), and the count does not move with the read count on 1/7/20 — and MULTI-FRAME ISOLATION HOLDS, driven through both variants identically, plus a foreign component in the middle preserving the frame through props.children. Items 3 and 5 (retained-heap ladder, mount/bulk clock, studio row, rf2-2rtt6.1 append) need a quiet box and are rf2-2rtt6.72's. ONE DEFECT THE VARIANT CREATES was found and repaired in the same commit: React propagates a context change ahead of the memo comparator, so the incumbent cannot be bailed out of a frame change but a frame-fed boundary can; boundary-props= now compares rfFrame. Mutation-proved (remove the comparison -> exactly one named failure, exit 1). HONEST NOTE: simpler at the shell, slightly MORE machinery in total (codec/root-element for the one creator with no ancestor body, plus the comparator learning a channel it did not have to know existed). PR #7416.

title: Hicasso presence: phase as a prop, and ::h/mounting / ::h/unmounting attribute overrides as data
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained; do not rely on any untracked findings file).

This bead fixes a DOCUMENTED TRAP in the shipped predecessor and answers the
operator's 2026-07-31 steer about expressing mount/unmount as data.

THE TRAP. Freehand's presence boundary exposes phase as an AMBIENT READ,
v/presence-phase (implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc:1756). Its own
guide records what that costs — docs/core/freehand/host/presence.md:62-66, verbatim:

  "Read the phase inside a DECLARED, KEYED CHILD VIEW, as above. Reading it in markup
   written inline in the parent is a trap: those props are evaluated during the
   PARENT'S render, so the phase you get is the parent's, not the per-child one you
   meant."

So a fading toast cannot be written inline. It must be extracted into a defview purely
so a dynamic var resolves against the right child, and getting it wrong yields the
wrong phase SILENTLY. The a11y obligation then costs three separate (when exiting? ...)
attributes on that child (presence.md:157-165).

Freehand explicitly rejected the alternative — presence.md:52-61, verbatim:
  "presence writes nothing onto your markup. There are no ::v/mounting /
   ::v/unmounting attribute overrides ... A boundary that stamped attributes would
   have to guess at a node it never sees."

That reason is sound for a boundary stamping BY ITSELF. It does not survive the AUTHOR
writing the override on the node.

PRIMARY SOURCE, verified 2026-07-31 (replicant.fun): Replicant has two mechanisms and
only one is data. ":replicant/mounting" / ":replicant/unmounting" are ATTRIBUTE
OVERRIDES — "Replicant allows you to specify overrides for any attributes during
mounting and unmounting. This allows you to declaratively transition elements on mount
and unmount". Separately ":replicant/on-mount" / ":replicant/on-unmount" are
CALLBACKS taking (fn [{:keys [replicant/node]}] ...) (replicant.fun/life-cycle-hooks/).
Only the attribute-override half is worth taking; the callback half is LESS
data-oriented than Freehand's registered behaviors and is rejected.

THE PROPOSAL — two changes.

(1) ::h/mounting and ::h/unmounting are ATTRIBUTE OVERRIDE MAPS on a native node. The
    presence boundary merges them into that node's attrs while the child is in that
    phase. The boundary already owns the retained-children list (that is what
    retention IS), so this is a pure hiccup->hiccup transform applied BEFORE the codec
    runs. React sees an ordinary element whose props changed: no wrapper node, no
    stamped data-* attribute, NO REF, NO EFFECT, NO HOOK, and no ambient read.

      (h/presence {:timeout-ms 300}
        (for [t (sub [:toasts/visible])]
          [:div.toast {:key (:id t)
                       ::h/unmounting {:class "toast toast--exit"
                                       :inert true :aria-hidden true}}
           (:message t)]))

    The child view has disappeared, and the three (when exiting? ...) attributes are
    one map.

(2) When the presence child IS a boundary, the phase arrives as an ORDINARY PROP
    ([toast-card {:key id :toast t :rf/phase :unmounting}]), never an ambient read.
    That deletes the trap by construction: a prop cannot be read from the wrong render
    scope, it appears in a structural test's props map, and a headless test can supply
    it with no clock.

Consequence: v/presence-phase has no Hicasso equivalent — one fewer public concept
against K5 (docs/design/hicasso/validation.md:360).

HONEST LIMITS TO RECORD IN THE DESIGN
  - The override applies to a node the boundary can SEE. An override written inside an
    opaque child view is invisible to it; that is exactly what (2) is for.
  - ENTER is the weak half and Freehand already says why (presence.md:130-135): "driving
    enter purely as a :mounting -> :present class flip can race paint ... An ANIMATION
    ON INSERTION (or modern @starting-style) is more reliable." Ship ::h/mounting, but
    teach the CSS answer for enter.

INHERIT UNCHANGED from Freehand: :timeout-ms MANDATORY, as retention length AND
terminal bound (presence.md:48, freehand.cljc:1739); "re-entry cancels exit"
(presence.md:87-89); keys required on every dynamic child; presence never dispatches
domain mount/unmount events (presence.md:181).

WITNESSES
  1. A toast written INLINE (no child view) gets the exit attributes while unmounting
     and loses them on re-entry.
  2. A boundary child receives :rf/phase as a prop and it is assertable headlessly.
  3. The node is gone after :timeout-ms; nothing leaks.
notes:
CORRECTION to the close reason: one phrase lost a word to shell backtick expansion. It should read 'step/expire take the current instant as an ARGUMENT, which is what makes that true' — the machine never reads a clock itself, which is exactly why a headless test can assert every phase, deadline and expiry with no timers at all.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7328: REOPENED. Presence reuses the same RAW #{:key :ref} dissoc for phase overrides. An unmounting override carrying "key" or :x/key survives with-phase and canonicalizes to React key after the child's real :key is removed, remounting the node that presence was meant to retain; ref aliases likewise reach the node. Reuse the canonical structural-slot filter owned by rf2-2rtt6.36 and pin retained key identity through the presence path. No ordering redesign or new presence option.
close_reason: AUDIT-REOPEN repaired in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7332. presence/with-phase no longer dissocs a raw #{:key :ref} from a phase override; it filters through codec/without-structural — the same canonical-slot filter :& uses, owned by rf2-2rtt6.36. Retained key identity is pinned by construction: the only :key in the merged attributes is the one the child is retained under, because no spelling can reach that slot. HD-025 records why sharing the filter is the point rather than a convenience. Witnesses: an unmounting override carrying "key", 'key or :x/key leaves the child's props exactly as found and child-key still answers the retention key; the same for "ref", 'ref, :x/ref; and in a real browser (arm1/presence_dom_cljs_test) a hostile override on a retained toast hands NO node to its "ref" while the appearance half still lands, and the retained node is the same DOM element instance across the exit. Mutation-proved both ways: reverting the filter reds the headless transform witnesses (node exit 1) AND the browser witness (test:browser exit 1 — the override's "ref" was handed a live HTMLDivElement). Honest note recorded on the PR: the key face's DOM consequence was already masked by native-element writing js-props.key from the child's own :key after conversion, so the key face's mutation red is at the transform; the face that was live in the DOM is the ref.

title: Hicasso: one attribute-merge spelling — a reserved :& key, with the owned-literal law unconditional
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained; do not rely on any untracked findings file).

Freehand — the shipped interpreted substrate — makes an author choose between THREE
attribute-merge forms depending on where the target is, and the penalty for choosing
wrong is SILENT:

  docs/core/freehand/authoring/composition.md:233
    v/spread-safe — "internal DOM / library element that must keep controlled +
    identity invariants ... PRESERVES THE CONTROLLED-INPUT DOOR"
  docs/core/freehand/authoring/composition.md:234
    v/spread — "an element you own ... DOES NOT claim the door"
  docs/core/freehand/authoring/composition.md:389-393
    ordinary merge — forwarding onto a declared v/defhost head; "NEITHER SPREAD FORM
    IS LEGAL THERE"

The penalty is recorded twice, as a wall with no error attached:
  docs/core/freehand/operate/limits-and-escapes.md:32 — "Dynamic map on controlled
  input without spread-safe | forfeits door proof"
  docs/core/freehand/authoring/composition.md:416 — same row, "forfeits the door into
  batching"

There is no diagnostic. Caret and IME protection simply stop.

re-frame.ui has the same split (implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui.cljc:539 spread,
:554 spread-safe) and admits the cost at ui.cljc:573 — "General (ui/spread base
overrides) remains the visible-cost escape and STILL FORFEITS THE SYNC DOOR."

THE PROPOSAL. Hicasso has ONE merge, spelled as DATA in the attribute map, with one
unconditional law:

    [:input      {:& caller-attrs :value v :on-input ev}]
    [:div        {:& base :class "own"}]
    [date-picker {:& caller-attrs :selected d}]

  (a) :& is a reserved attribute key carrying a runtime map. It is data, not a call —
      so a forwarded remainder survives into a structural test and into tooling.
  (b) THE LAW: the literal keys written in the map ALWAYS win over :&. This is
      HD-010(a)'s owned-literal merge law (docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md:203-206 —
      ":key, :ref, controlled :value/:checked, and owned event handlers are
      unoverridable by theme or parts") applied to EVERY merge rather than only under
      theming. The controlled-input door then cannot be forfeited by a merge at all,
      which deletes the whole class of silent failure above.

PRECEDENT for the spelling: UIx already uses :& for exactly this in this repo —
examples/substrates/uix/login/core.cljs:148 (":& spreads the substrate-free
model/frame-config into these props").

WHAT IT COSTS. The case where a caller override SHOULD win is now spelled by not
writing the literal. That is the honest way round: the dangerous default is the other
one. ":&" cannot collide with a real DOM attribute.

SCOPE
  1. Specify the merge order and the owned-key set (start from decisions.md:203-206).
  2. Specify behaviour at a defhost crossing, where Freehand needs a THIRD rule today
     because spreads canonicalise :className into :class on the way through
     (composition.md:369-374). One rule must cover it or the bead has not landed.
  3. Witness: a controlled input whose :value and :on-input survive a hostile :&
     carrying :value, :on-input, :key and :ref — asserted through the public door.
  4. Witness: the same forwarding onto a defhost head.

ACCEPTANCE: two public concepts (spread, spread-safe) become zero — an attribute key
is not a concept in the K5 sense (docs/design/hicasso/validation.md:360).
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7328: REOPENED. merge-caller enforces owned literals and the :key/:ref exclusion by RAW map-key identity, but convert-props later canonicalizes strings, namespaced keywords, symbols, and kebab/camel spellings onto the same React slot. A remainder can therefore carry "key", "ref", :x/ref, or an alias such as :onInput against an owned :on-input; structural slots bypass the deny and same-slot aliases make the promised unconditional owned-wins law map-order-dependent. This is the already-established canonical-slot failure class, now on Hicasso's new :& door. Bounded repair: classify once at this merge boundary using the codec's emitted slot and prove alternate spellings cannot reach key/ref or an owned controlled/event slot. No general alias framework.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7332 (2026-08-01): REOPENED. PR #7332 correctly makes merge-caller, presence, ref reservation, and event callback arity total, but merge-shorthand still reads/dissocs only raw :id, :class, and :className even though this codec accepts strings, symbols, and namespaced keys and canonical-slot emits them into the same React slots. The defect is live through this bead's own :& door: [:div#tag.foo {:& {"id" "caller" "className" "bar"}}] passes both alternate keys through merge-caller, then merge-shorthand fails to see either, adds :id "tag" and :class "foo", and convert-props writes each pair to one JS slot in map iteration order. The explicit id can lose to #tag and the caller class can replace or be replaced by .foo instead of composing, contradicting merge-shorthand's explicit-wins/composes contract and convert-props's promise that forwarded class composes with tag shorthand. The same holds for symbol/namespaced aliases and direct attribute maps. Bounded repair: reuse canonical-slot while folding tag shorthand so every accepted spelling of the id/class slots has the canonical behavior; prove #tag plus alternate explicit id yields the explicit id, and .foo plus alternate class/className yields "foo bar", independent of cache/render/map order. Preserve near-miss custom props and the already-correct owned-literal deny. No general alias framework or new public concept.
close_reason:

WHAT THE AUDIT REOPENED IT FOR (merged-PR audit #7332) is closed: merge-shorthand read :id/:class/:className off the props map by RAW KEY, which is three of the spellings this codec accepts, so [:div#tag.foo {:& {"id" "caller" "className" "bar"}}] kept both ids and both classes as distinct map keys landing on one React slot each, and map iteration order decided which survived — the explicit id could lose to #tag and the caller's class could replace .foo instead of composing.

THE REPAIR is the audit's bounded one taken to its conclusion: the shorthand is folded onto the EMITTED object (fold-shorthand!), where the slot is not resolved because it already IS the slot. No general alias framework and no new public concept — PropSlot gained one boolean field.

title: Hicasso: collapse the four callback forms to one — the position selects the contract
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained; do not rely on any untracked findings file).

Freehand — the SHIPPED interpreted substrate this programme is measured against —
requires an author who cannot use a bare event vector to pick from a roster of FOUR
callback forms, each with a different contract:

  docs/core/freehand/authoring/events-and-handlers.md:343-352 (the roster table)
  implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc:1302  (v/event)     -> returns ONE event vector or nil
  implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc:1327  (v/handler)   -> "The body's return is ignored"
  implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc:1344  (v/render-fn) -> pure, runs during a FOREIGN render
  implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand.cljc:1287  (v/raw-fn)    -> identity passes through unchanged

There is a fifth rule on top: the roster only works at prop positions Freehand WALKS.
events-and-handlers.md:361-384 ("Where the roster reaches") and freehand.cljc:2355
record the failure mode outside that reach — a roster carrier handed to a raw
createElement #js prop is a non-callable marker object, and the library gets the
engine's own TypeError "props.onPing is not a function", "naming nothing you wrote".
freehand.cljc:1292 also hands identity management back to the author for raw-fn:
"re-render churn is the author's to manage".

THE PROPOSAL. Hicasso ships ONE callback form. The CONTRACT comes from the POSITION,
not from the form the author chose, because Hicasso already knows every position it
walks and the role is already declared exactly once per crossing:

  - a native :on-* prop      -> event position: a returned vector (or nil) is dispatched
  - a defhost :callbacks entry -> the DECLARATION already says :event or :handler
    (docs/core/freehand/host/host-boundaries.md:59 — "a finite map from EXACT prop
    names to :event or :handler; never inferred from an on* name")
  - a slot / render-prop position -> pure render phase; dispatching is the error
    (freehand.cljc:1395 — arity is "a CONTRACT, not a convention")

WHY THIS IS AFFORDABLE. Kill criterion K5 (docs/design/hicasso/validation.md:360) is
"> ~8 public concepts or > ~8 guide pages to ship CRUD". Four concepts collapsing to
one is half the budget back. The census supports it: keyboard-condition handlers
appear 3 times in 85 idiomatic files and stopPropagation 0 times
(docs/design/freehand/studio/fitness-harness.md:331-332), and foreign React
components 0 times (:339) — the roster is priced for a component-library tier that
charter.md:144-149 explicitly defers past v0.

SCOPE
  1. Decide and record the one spelling (working name h/fn; naming stays unfrozen per
     docs/design/hicasso/authoring.md:3-7).
  2. Specify the position->contract table, including what a render-position callback
     that dispatches must do (a loud diagnostic naming the POSITION, not the form).
  3. State whether raw-fn's identity-passthrough ships in v0. Recommendation: NO —
     0 foreign components in the census; let the component-library phase earn it back.
  4. Witness: one test per position proving the contract, and one proving the
     diagnostic text names the position.

FENCES. No compiler, no analyzer. This is a runtime classification at positions the
codec already walks, not a build-time pass over body forms (charter.md:115-120).
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7328: REOPENED. The new event-callback wrapper accepts exactly [e] and invokes (f e), so a defhost :event callback silently drops every foreign callback argument after the first (or raises an h/fn arity error). That contradicts the form's arbitrary parameter vector and the callback contract's live invoker arguments. Bounded repair: make only the event wrapper variadic and apply the marked function; add a declared :event witness with two arguments while retaining the one-argument native and no-frame diagnostics. No new callback form or ABI.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7396 (merged 2026-08-02T20:35:10Z): REOPENED. The new host door makes the declaration path real end-to-end and its h/fn rows are strong, but `lower-declared-prop` still lets the value override the declared position contract. Only the marked `h/fn` branch consults `contract`; every vector takes `intent-handler` and every map takes `key-map-handler` for `:event`, `:handler`, and `:render` alike. Thus a declaration that says `:handler` silently dispatches a bare intent, and a `:render` position can dispatch during the foreign component's render without the required `:rf.error/hicasso-dispatch-in-render-position`. That contradicts HD-024's core law that the position selects the contract.

Bounded repair: make the declared contract govern every lowerable carrier. Preserve vector/key-map convenience for declared `:event`; reject them precisely at `:handler`/`:render` (or otherwise implement those contracts without dispatch), retain h/fn identity/purity semantics, and add real-host rows for all contract/carrier combinations plus one mutation proving a render-position dispatch goes red. No new callback form or public concept is needed.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7398 (merged 2026-08-02T21:22:39Z): the new interop callback section exposes another carrier/contract mismatch under this exact owner. It says ::h/prevent at a declared :event position calls preventDefault on whichever invoker argument is the real DOM event. The landed vector path does not inspect or forward all arguments: intent-handler returns a unary fn [e] and calls .preventDefault on that first value. A value-first foreign call such as onPick(value, event) therefore calls value.preventDefault and throws instead of preventing the actual event. This differs from the variadic h/fn event-callback path the same paragraph correctly teaches.

Bounded resolution: as part of the existing all-contract/carrier matrix, pin the event-vector argument law with a real host witness. Prefer the minimal coherent API: either document that marker/prevent vectors require an event-first contract, or deliberately implement a stronger declared-event rule and witness it; do not add a new callback form.
close_reason: PR #7420. Both open audits closed. #7396: lower-declared-prop now dispatches on the CONTRACT first and the carrier second — :event keeps the vector/key-map conveniences, :handler and :render refuse both with :rf.error/hicasso-intent-at-a-non-event-contract naming the position; declared-callback deleted. #7398: resolved to ONE law — the vector spelling (::h/prevent, ::h/value, ::h/checked, :on-submit auto-prevent, key-map lookup) reads the DOM event from argument ONE; a value-first invoker raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-needs-the-event naming the position and pointing at h/fn, instead of the engine's value.preventDefault TypeError. The 05-interop.md sentence promising 'whichever argument is the real DOM event' is retired; HD-024 in decisions.md and authoring.md now state both laws and the declared row's third contract (:render). Witnesses: host_hatch §5b full contract x carrier matrix at a real minted host + mounted render-prop row + render-position dispatch refusal + the argument law at the widget's own value-first invoker; intent_cljs_test closure-level rows. Gates: test-fast-pr.sh EXIT 0, npm run test:cljs EXIT 0 (12447/62401, 0 failures), npm run test:browser EXIT 0 (1032/6419, 0 failures), check_doc_slugs.py EXIT 0. Mutation-proved twice (EXIT 1 with named failures, reverted byte-identically). Hook budget unchanged, measured at React's dispatcher. FINDING filed as rf2-2rtt6.74: a :render prop returning LOWERED hiccup poisons that row's own handlers, because render-callback binds the poison into the same *dispatch* that intent-handler captures at lowering time.

title: hicasso: instrument the per-read heap axis early -- the one axis where the ruled architecture can beat its own parent by design
description:
FROM the EP-0038 adversarial design review (2026-07-31). This is a "what
survived" bead: the axis the review could not break, and the one it recommends
the clock be spent on.

THE SITUATION. The per-read gates (docs/design/hicasso/validation.md:136-140),
both on the mandatory distinct-query witness (Q = E), as marginal slopes:

  UIx material-cost red-zone   2,935 B/read  [2,852-3,055]
  K3, Reagent-sourced            943 B/read  [935-944]

and the record's own sentence: "943 B/read remains the number a native layer
actually has to beat."

WHY THIS AXIS IS DIFFERENT FROM THE CLOCK ROWS. On mount, the ruled parent is at
parity with Reagent (1.0243x) and Hicasso's product delta is a tax on top -- the
review's central objection. On bulk-broad the parent already wins (0.6291x) and
Hicasso only has to not squander it. Per-read heap is the ONE axis where the
ruled architecture is structurally CHEAPER than the parent it is built on rather
than more expensive:

  - the parent pays N `useSyncExternalStore` hook cells per boundary;
  - Hicasso pays ONE hook per boundary plus edges in a SHARED GLOBAL INDEX --
    "Index edges live in global maps -- shared structure, not per-boundary
    object fan-out" (docs/design/hicasso/architecture.md:33-35).

That is a difference in kind, not in tuning. The parent's 2,935 B/read is
roughly 3.1x Reagent's 943; the grouped tier's own win condition already concedes
~2,000 B/read with a paper path down (validation.md:245-246). If one hook plus a
shared edge lands materially below 2,000, that is the programme's first
unambiguous structural win over BOTH comparators, and it is available before any
clock row is settled.

WHAT TO DO. Extend the existing reads-per-boundary heap ladder
(docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md, rf2-2rtt6.5) with
a HICASSO-SHAPED rung: one subscription/epoch hook per boundary plus N edges in
a shared index, at 1/3/7/20 reads, distinct-query (Q = E), against the SAME
instrument the gates are stated on (p0_run.cjs / p0_heap.cljs -- validation.md
:180-189 is explicit that a candidate is judged against the donor row taken on
its OWN instrument, and that a margin under 5% is instrument-limited rather than
cleared).

Report: the marginal slope, the shell intercept, and zero retained
per-occurrence objects after commit/teardown (the HD-002 survival metric,
decisions.md:55-56).

WHY NOW. It does not need the collector, the codec, the dogfood screen, or the
mount row. It needs a hook, an index and a ladder that already exists. It is the
cheapest evidence in the programme that the ruled architecture has an axis it
wins on its own merits, and it is measurable inside week one of K7.

NOTE the operator deferred new heap measurement on 2026-07-31
(validation.md:80-82). This bead is filed against that deferral, not around it
-- it needs a release before dispatch.
notes:
RESOLVED by PR #7653 (worker/crossover-2rtt6-34), docs-only, one file, no measurement.

MODEL ADOPTED: the fitted lines, labelled MODEL-INFERRED.
  UIx y = 161 + 2,981R ; Hicasso y = 1,175 + 2,272R
  crossover = (1,175 - 161)/(2,981 - 2,272) = 1.43 reads

BEFORE: (1,134 - 220)/(2,981 - 2,272) = 1.29 reads -- measured R=0 shell difference over fitted slope difference, belonging to neither line. Withdrawn and annotated, never erased (it was quoted downstream).

All five audit numbers verified against the tree before use: 1,175 / 161 (fitted intercepts, :814/:813), 2,981 / 2,272 (fitted slopes), 3,855 / 3,287 (measured R=1, :794), 1,134 / 220 (measured R=0 shells, :793). Every one agreed. Incidental find: the prose read 'a fixed 913 B more at the shell' where 1,134-220 = 914; that sentence is gone in the rewrite.

DIRECT EVIDENCE KEPT DISTINCT: behind at measured R=1 (1.173x), ahead at measured R=3 (0.883x), crossing in (1,3). No R=2 rung exists; the old 'ahead from two' is now explicitly model-inferred. The R=1-anchored alternative (~1.8) is NAMED with its cause (both arms' first read exceeds their marginal, so the fit under-predicts R=1 by 145 B / 408 B) but not quoted as a result -- so 1.43 reads as a model output inside a measured bracket and the next reader does not re-derive 1.8 and think the page wrong.

THREE SITES RECONCILED: sec-6 equation; the rf2-2rtt6.60 re-take row (1.29 -> 1.32 was the same hybrid; run 4's counterpart is 'not restated' because the bisection publishes marginal slopes and no fitted intercepts); and the rf2-aqgr2 subsection that had deferred its crossover pending this bead, now recording the settled reason.

OUT OF SCOPE, CHECKED: the sections 1-4 Reagent<->UIx crossover at :170/:598 is a different comparator pair and NOT the same defect -- 'below one read' is a bracket claim directly supported by the R=1 rows (UIx ~3,038 B vs Reagent 1,562 B), not a point value from mixed terms. No other page in docs/ or spec/ mentions this crossover.

GATES: check_doc_slugs 0 (selection proven by injected broken anchor -> exit 1, reverted), check_provenance_pins --changed-since origin/main 0 (59 pins, 48 landed, 11 stranded all accompanied -- no re-pinning, the PR adds no SHA-shaped token), test-fast-pr.sh 0. Hand-verified 52 tables / 312 rows, 0 column-count mismatches; both introduced anchors resolve.

comments.text:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-07, operator-overturnable) — THE WRITE-BEFORE-REFUSE RULING. This discharges the fence ("an OPERATOR RULING, not a worker's patch"): the ruling below is recorded under Mike's 2026-08-07 direction that the dossier-review agent weigh the recorded positions and decide. The bead is now dispatchable; close it when the acceptance criteria land.

THE RULING: TWO-TIER, MATCHING THE FAMILY'S OWN CONVERGED PATTERN. Preserve every completed measurement; promote only a gate-passing, full-published-shape run to the canonical evidence set. "Canonical" means ELIGIBLE PUBLISHED EVIDENCE, not "the last file the driver wrote". Capture is not publication.

This is not a new invention — it is the rule the family already converged on one file over. census_clock_run.cjs (rf2-2rtt6.56, merged-PR audit #7379) already implements and tests it: a pure destination(shape, code) chosen only AFTER verdict routes any refused / partial-row / partial-adapter / --no-build / overridden-depth run to a `.unpublished` sibling announced on stdout with reasons, and datasetFor serialises `canonical:` and `notCanonicalWhy:` IN the file. clock_exit_path.test.cjs pins each refusal routing and the verdict-before-write ordering hermetically ("the WRITE path, not just the exit path" block, :353+). hd8_clock_run.cjs is the sibling that never received the same repair: its dataset writes (~:881-921, guarded only by `!failed`) precede `verdict(summarise(...))` (~:929), so a control-refused re-run silently replaces data/hd8clock-2rtt6-31/{uix,reagent,slim}.json — the very files the studio page recomputes from.

HOW THIS RESOLVES THE TWO CONTRADICTING RECORDS: both survive in part.
- rr6do's landed intent (hd8_clock_run.cjs ~:720-722: "No refusal suppresses output: the tables are printed and the datasets are written before this is consulted. A refusal is about what may be QUOTED, not about throwing the measurement away") — the PRESERVATION half stands: no refusal ever discards a completed measurement. The CANONICAL-FILENAME half falls: refused output is still written, but never under the published evidence set's names.
- The 2026-08-02 audit acceptance ("canonical data only after gates pass") — stands as the meaning of the canonical directory; its implied discard of refused runs falls.

WHY (the evidence that decided it): the failure mode is real and already bit twice in this family. ctl.ok is false on 5 of 6 committed rows of the current canonical set (uix/M 1.6503, uix/U 1.5566, reagent/M 1.6868, slim/M 1.5518, slim/U 1.7100; only reagent/U passes) — and those refused rows were exactly the DIAGNOSTIC evidence that exposed the control failure, so discarding refused runs (Option B pure) loses the interesting data, while always-write-canonical (Option A pure) lets the next refused draw silently clobber cited evidence. External benchmark practice (SPEC SERT run rules §2.7; SPECjbb2015 run rules §3.1 — invalid reports are retained, stamped Invalid, and excluded from comparison) confirms the same split: retain and annotate, never compare.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (worker-sized, one PR):
1. hd8_clock_run.cjs computes its one authoritative verdict BEFORE choosing a write destination. Mirror census_clock_run.cjs's pure destination(shape, code) — extract a shared helper if it stays small, else copy the pattern verbatim; do not invent a third rule.
2. Full published-shape, exit-0 runs write under canonical data/hd8clock-2rtt6-31/. Refused, partial, or overridden runs write the SAME serialised shape to a `.unpublished` sibling, announced on stdout with every reason. Recommended (not gating): give refused runs unique subdirectories (timestamp/sha) so one diagnostically interesting refusal cannot erase another.
3. Datasets are self-describing: serialise `canonical:` and `notCanonicalWhy:` in-file (census datasetFor shows the exact shape). Consumers/recomputation fail closed: a missing canonical field is not a pass.
4. Update the ~:720-722 intent comment to state the two-tier rule: preserve "no refusal suppresses output", remove the canonical-filename implication, cite this bead.
5. Hermetic write-path tests in the clock_exit_path.test.cjs style: pin verdict-before-destination and each refusal routing for hd8, as the census block already does.
6. Do NOT rewrite the standing datasets under data/hd8clock-2rtt6-31/ — they are the cited evidence base for the audit record; their control-failure status is documented on the corrected pages, and under fail-closed reading their missing canonical field already marks them non-canonical.
7. Same PR (bounded provenance item, #7462 audit item 1): stamp landed whole-tree SHA 1ac48c4a0be1fed3338fbb504f5b023af6d1524d beside the producing commit at hd8-composed-donor-arm.md:218, retaining the authored/producing history.

FAMILY-WIDE SCOPE: this note is the family policy statement. hd8_clock_run.cjs adopts it now (this bead). clock_run.cjs and any other bench drivers adopt the same rule as they are next touched — rf2-emvod's reopen (reportable filter enforcing all serialised gates) is the same rule's consumer half on its own driver; no mass-migration bead is warranted (that would be gold-plating: record once, converge on touch).

title: Worktree hygiene must rmdir a node_modules junction before git worktree remove (second occurrence)
description:
SECOND recorded instance of the class. On 2026-07-31 the worker worktree for rf2-2rtt6.8 (PR #7311, merged green) carried a Windows junction implementation/node_modules -> the mayor checkout's real node_modules, which is the established convention in this repo (a live sibling worktree had the identical junction, and a worker worktree cannot compile without one). Post-merge hygiene ran git worktree remove; it followed the junction and emptied the MAYOR checkout's real implementation/node_modules to 0 entries, breaking every local build in the repo until npm ci restored it (exit 0, back to the canary 101 entries). No source was lost - the PR had already merged.

REMEDY, both halves needed:
1. HYGIENE: before git worktree remove, run cmd /c rmdir <wt>/implementation/node_modules (junctions must be removed with rmdir, not rm -rf), then verify the mayor canary after each removal batch: ls <mayor>/implementation/node_modules | wc -l should stay ~101. Encode this in the hygiene skill/script rather than in an agent's memory, since memory already carried the warning and the class still recurred.
2. WORKER BRIEF: a worker that creates the junction should rmdir it as its last act before reporting done, so hygiene never meets one.

Consider also having scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh (or a companion) provision node_modules in a way that cannot alias the mayor's - e.g. npm ci in the worktree, or a marker file recording that a junction exists so hygiene can find it mechanically.
