title: subs,spine: movement-witness protocol — retire the provably-failing layer-1 memo compare (147 B/sub)
description:
HELD for operator sign-off on rf2-gncxk — do not dispatch until the ruling records adoption.

IMPLEMENT the movement-witness design produced by the rf2-gncxk design pass. This description
stands alone; the design doc is local-only.

WHAT IS BEING FIXED. `subs.memo/make-layer-1-memoised-body` guards the user's sub body with
`(= @last-db db)`. On the flush path, for `:db` / `:runtime-db`, that walk is provably useless —
147.0 B/sub, 17.6% of the ~835 B/sub per-subscription slope (node V8, :advanced, goog.DEBUG
false, pointer compression OFF). It is NOT dead code: `deref-derived` is pull-based, so the same
guard is what stops a render re-running every sub body, and it genuinely HITS on the flush path
for `:frame-state`, which shares the wrapper.

A FOURTH CONSTRAINT THE BEAD DOES NOT STATE, and which kills "flush ⇒ skip the compare":
rf2-gncxk's proof establishes "the source moved since the source's PREVIOUS NOTIFY". The guard's
question is "did the input move since THE WRAPPER LAST RAN". Two reachable interleavings separate
them, and in BOTH the guard correctly hits on the flush path even for `:db`:
  (a) DEREF-BETWEEN. Source moves P -> N (mark-dirty). Anything derefs the sub before the epoch
      drain — `deref-derived` recomputes, so the wrapper sees N and sets last-db := N. The queued
      flush! then arrives with N: guard hits, correctly.
  (b) RETURN-TO-EQUAL. Two writes in one handler take app-db A -> B -> A' with A' `=` A but a
      fresh object. mark-dirty! dedups, so ONE flush arrives with A' against last-db = A: rf=
      moved twice, `=` says equal, guard hits, correctly.
So the fix must NOT key on "which caller am I". It must key on an exact fact about the SOURCE.

THE DESIGN — a movement WITNESS published by the source container. A derived container that gates
its own propagation on `rf=` publishes the value its most recent COMPLETED movement departed
from; the fixed-arity-1 memo wrappers hold their lone source container and skip the `=` walk
exactly when that witness is `identical?` to the value they last saw. The source owns the signal
(movement is its own notion, defined by its own rf= gate); core PULLS. No ambient state, no
dynamic var, NO change to `make-derived-value`'s pinned `(source-containers compute-fn)`
signature and NO change to compute-fn's pinned one-arg-per-source shape.

NEW CONTRACT SURFACE — one tiny .cljc ns `re-frame.movement`, sibling in spirit to
`re-frame.disposable` (the precedent: a re-frame-owned protocol reified by the spine's derived
container, consulted by core, no Reagent dep):
  (def no-witness   ;; distinct object identity; never identical?/= any real value nor ::unset
    #?(:clj (Object.) :cljs (js-obj)))
  (defprotocol IMovementWitness
    (-moved-from [this] "the value this container's most recent COMPLETED movement departed
                         FROM, or `no-witness`"))
Two obligations on an implementor — the whole normative content:
  (W1) FRESHNESS. Answer `no-witness` unless the container's own value has completed a movement
       AND no input change has been observed since. (Without W1 a pull-based container's live
       value can run ahead of the last movement.)
  (W2) SOUNDNESS. When it answers `f` != no-witness, reading the container at that instant yields
       `v` with (not (rf= f v)) — in particular (not (= f v)).
One on the consumer:
  (C1) VERDICT-PRESERVING. Use the witness ONLY to skip a comparison whose answer it determines;
       never change an observable outcome.
Publishing is OPTIONAL — the same posture Spec 006 already takes for `:adapter/derived-container?`
and `:adapter/activate-derived-value!`.

THE PROOF. Let S be the lone source, L = @last-db, V = @S (build-recompute-fn's arity-1 closure
is `(compute-fn @s0)`). If (identical? (-moved-from S) L) then (not (= L V)): W1+W2 give
(not (= f V)) for the returned f, and f is identical? to L. QED.

THE GUARD becomes, in `make-layer-1-memoised-body` AND
`make-layer-n-single-input-memoised-body`:
  (if (and (not (identical? (if witness-src (movement/-moved-from witness-src) movement/no-witness)
                            @last-db))
           (= @last-db db))
    <memo-hit branch, unchanged>
    <recompute branch, unchanged>)
`witness-src` is resolved ONCE at construction:
`(when (satisfies? movement/IMovementWitness source-container) source-container)` — nil wherever
the capability is absent, so the hot path is one closed-over-local truthiness test + one pointer
compare.

SUBSTRATE SIDE — `re-frame.substrate.spine/make-derived-value-fn`, six lines:
  * new cell `last-moved-from (volatile! movement/no-witness)`
  * in `notify`, INSIDE the existing `(when-not (rf= prev nu) ...)` gate, before fan-out:
    `(vreset! last-moved-from prev)`  — records departure exactly when movement is established (W2)
  * in `mark-dirty!`, inside the existing `(when-not @dirty? ...)` 0->1 branch:
    `(vreset! last-moved-from movement/no-witness)` — the container may now run ahead of its last
    notify, so it stops answering (W1). `flush!` clears `dirty?` BEFORE it recomputes+notifies, so
    the witness re-arms in the right order with no extra bookkeeping.
  * the reify gains `movement/IMovementWitness (-moved-from [_] @last-moved-from)`
  * `-dispose` resets it to `no-witness` (hygiene + releases the retained reference)
`build-recompute-fn`, the scheduler, the fan-out coordinator, `deref-derived`, `flush!`'s
structure, the failure-atomic wiring loop and `-dispose`'s release discipline are UNTOUCHED.

WHY IT CANNOT WEAKEN THE DEREF-PATH GUARD (structurally, not by care). The design never asks "am
I on the flush path?". After any wrapper invocation last-db holds the value just seen while the
witness holds the PREDECESSOR, so the proof cannot fire twice in a row on the same value: a
render that derefs 300 subs three times each still memo-hits 900 times, with `=` short-circuiting
on identical?. The only deref that gets the proof is the first invocation after a movement —
where the guard would have missed anyway. `compute-sub` bypasses the wrapper entirely.
THE SET OF {hit, miss} VERDICTS IS BIT-IDENTICAL ON EVERY PATH ON EVERY ADAPTER. Body-run counts,
`:rf.sub/run` counts, `:rf.sub/skip` counts and its `:reason :input-value-equal` do not move. A
trace-count diff is the failure signal, not a thing to re-baseline.

HOW `:frame-state` KEEPS ITS GENUINE HIT — three layers:
  (a) STRUCTURAL. `subs/single-source-container-for` maps `:frame-state -> frame/frame-state-container`,
      the ONE physical container — a `cljs.core/Atom` under the spine (`source-atom?` is
      `(instance? Atom s)`), an `r/atom` under Reagent. An Atom does not implement
      IMovementWitness, so witness-src is nil and the guard expression is byte-for-byte today's.
      The exact fact that broke rf2-gncxk's proof is now the mechanism that protects it.
  (b) CONTRACTUAL. A future gated frame-state could publish a witness only by honouring W1+W2 —
      which require precisely the rf= movement gate whose absence makes the `:frame-state` hit
      possible today. The design cannot become wrong, only inapplicable or applicable.
  (c) EMPIRICAL. PR #7233's `sub_memo_flush_path_cljs_test.cljs` `:frame-state` arm must pass
      UNMODIFIED, plus a new mutation proof: forcing witness-src non-nil for `:frame-state` must
      RED that pin.

WHAT CHANGES — and nothing else:
  * NEW implementation/core/src/re_frame/movement.cljc  (~35 lines, mostly docstring)
  * implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs  (~8 lines, above)
  * implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/memo.cljc  (~12 lines + docstrings; the two fixed-arity-1
    wrappers each take the lone source-container as a new TRAILING param)
  * implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc  (2 lines: pass `(first inputs)` at :1263 and :1283)
  * implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/write_attribution.cljs  (the paired arms below;
    :1101 is the one bench site constructing a wrapper directly)
  * spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md — a "Movement witness (optional)" subsection under
    §`make-derived-value` stating W1/W2/C1 + one cross-ref sentence in §Invalidation algorithm.
    HOT-ZONE — sequence against other Spec 006 PRs.
NO adapter file changes. `make-layer-n-memoised-body` (varargs, >=2 inputs, all parametric subs)
is deliberately OUT OF SCOPE — the mechanism generalises per-source-index but its cost is
dominated by the varargs seq and the measured 147 B is the fixed-arity-1 path. Spec 009 needs NO
change: `:rf.sub/skip`'s "input value was `=` to last-seen" stays exactly true, because the design
never skips when the values are `=`. Pre-alpha posture: positional param, NO compatibility arity.

DEGRADATION — none behavioural anywhere; two extra pointer compares per recompute where the
capability is absent, zero allocation.
  * Reagent / reagent-slim: make-derived-value is `(make-reaction (build-recompute-fn ...))`
    (spine.cljs:3127); a Reagent Reaction does not implement the protocol -> witness-src nil.
  * plain-atom (JVM+CLJS): recompute-on-deref, no notify gate, no witness; on the JVM witness-src
    is a constant nil local. `sub_memo_layer_1_test.clj` (incl. the =-not-identical? pin at :84)
    runs here and is unaffected.
  * test-react: own make-derived-value, publishes nothing, unchanged.
  * UIx / re-frame.ui / freehand: all ride make-derived-value-fn -> all three get the win on
    `:db` / `:runtime-db` / single-`:<-` layer-2 and no change on `:frame-state`.
  * Bundle: one sentinel + one defprotocol; a protocol call on a reify is a direct method dispatch
    under :advanced. Show the delta against the perf-bundle gate.
  * MEMORY — the one real cost, state it in the PR: `last-moved-from` retains ONE predecessor
    derived value per derived container while that container is clean (cleared on the next
    mark-dirty!). For the app-db projection that is one extra app-db generation held between
    writes; structural sharing means the true delta is only the nodes the last write replaced. Not
    a new class of retention — every layer-1 memo cell already holds a full app-db in `last-db`.

MEASUREMENT OBLIGATION (ranges quoted; overlapping ranges mean INDISTINGUISHABLE; arm-order guard
must not refuse; forward AND reversed reported):
  1. BASELINE. Reproduce or cite P-EQDB = 147.0 B/sub on the unchanged tree (node V8, :advanced,
     goog.DEBUG false, pointer compression OFF, 8/8 self-tests, 70/70 strata).
  2. THE PAIRED ARMS — both, or neither. Added to write_attribution.cljs, living in ONE process on
     the SAME objects (the harness's own RC-ATTACH/RC-CAND paired-control discipline):
       P-MEMOW — the SHIPPED wrapper constructed with a WITNESSING source (a spine derived
                 container), invoked in the flush-path shape (witness identical? to last-db, db
                 changed). MUST land at P-MEMO minus 147.0 B/sub within the quoted range: the `=`
                 term is GONE.
       P-MEMOF — the SAME wrapper constructed with a RAW ATOM source (the `:frame-state` shape),
                 invoked with an =-but-not-identical? db. MUST still carry the FULL `=` term,
                 indistinguishable from today's P-MEMO at that input. This is the "still paid
                 where it earns its keep" half and it is NOT optional.
  3. THE LADDER. RFWRITE-N per-subscription slope falls by ~147 B/sub (~835 -> ~688, -17.6%) on
     the `:db` ladder, and is UNCHANGED on a `:frame-state` ladder (add one if absent).
  4. BEHAVIOURAL WITNESSES, UNMODIFIED (this discharges C1): sub_memo_flush_path_cljs_test.cljs
     (both arms, PR #7233), sub_memo_layer_1_test.clj (incl. :84), and full test:cljs / test:ui /
     adapter smokes with ZERO change in any body-run or :rf.sub/run / :rf.sub/skip count.
  5. MUTATION PROOFS, BOTH DIRECTIONS. (i) forcing witness-src non-nil for `:frame-state` must RED
     the `:frame-state` pin; (ii) deleting the identical? proof term must RESTORE the 147 B in
     P-MEMOW. A change that cannot fail either way has not been measured.
  6. RETENTION. hicasso retention_run.cjs shows no growth beyond the one predecessor generation.

INTERACTIONS. rf2-2rtt6.13 (PR #7304) and rf2-2rtt6.25 (PR #7305) both LANDED and both COMPOSE —
no sequencing dependency. Both edited spine.cljs's make-react-spine / hook region; this edits
spine.cljs's make-derived-value-fn region — no textual overlap, but spine.cljs is contended by
Wave-1 workers, so treat it as sequence-sensitive when dispatching. One POSITIVE interaction with
.25 worth noting in the PR: commit adoption means the memo cells (last-db / last-result) survive
render -> commit instead of being thrown away with a discarded double build, so the proof's
precondition (last-db identical? to the witness) holds MORE often after .25, not less.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES (do not re-litigate): (1) narrowing the guard to identical? — the
`:frame-state` value-equal commit AND a single-epoch A->B->A' return-to-equal both legitimately
memo-hit on an =-not-identical? input, so it turns a spec'd :rf.sub/skip into a :rf.sub/run and
reds both #7233 pins plus sub_memo_layer_1_test.clj:84; (2) an extra "moved" argument to
compute-fn — make-layer-n-memoised-body is `(fn [& in-vals])` and cannot tell a trailing flag
from an input value, and Spec 006 pins the one-arg-per-source shape verbatim; (3) an ambient
one-shot cell set by flush! — correctness would depend on nothing else running between set and
consume (the app-db projection's own compute-fn is the keyword `:rf.db/app`; a throw strands the
flag), and it answers the wrong question anyway (cases (a)/(b) above); (4) a movement COUNTER
instead of the departure value — cannot distinguish "moved once since you last ran" from "moved
once and you already read the result", and cannot see return-to-equal at all.

ADJACENT CANDIDATES, NOT THIS BEAD (file separately if the operator wants them): memoise
deref-derived while the container is clean (bigger win, but converts the derived container from
pull to cached-pull, which Spec 006 leaves to adapter discretion and the spine declines);
movement-gate the raw-atom fan-out coordinator (would collapse N `:frame-state` `=` walks into 1
but changes when `:frame-state` subs are marked dirty and would red the #7233 pin as written);
extend the witness to the varargs / >=2-source wrappers.

      UIx 221-231 B. CARRY THE CAVEAT: the shell is component-shape sensitive

      reads ladder's carries one, which is why it reads 501 against the
      ladder's 428). The budget row must NAME THE BOUNDARY SHAPE it is stated

-769 B per unique query key) AND rf2-2rtt6.25 (f784ab0adb). The sweep is the

First, validation.md now says UIx's model "predicts a held-out rung it never saw". In PR #7306, `R2Q2B` is also used in `key-2`, `key-gap`, and the mandatory `key-ok?` model-admissibility gate. title: spine: hook-scoped provisional hand-off — adopt the render-phase build at commit (rf2-2rtt6.14 design)
description:
HELD for operator sign-off on rf2-2rtt6.14 — do not dispatch until the ruling records adoption.

IMPLEMENT the hook-scoped provisional hand-off designed under the reopened rf2-2rtt6.14 (decision input: rf2-2rtt6.15 / PR #7300, docs/design/hicasso/studio/coldmount-double-build-priced.md — the double-build clock is >= 20% of the mount red-zone in EVERY round at layers 1, 2 and 3; the handoff arm's M1 mount landed at/below the Reagent denominator). Scope is the ruling's: hook-scoped provisional hand-off ONLY — NEVER a general ref-count-0 cache tenancy. This description stands alone; the design doc is local-only.

THE DESIGN. In re-frame.substrate.spine's use-subscribe-2 (make-react-spine — shared by the UIx adapter, re-frame.freehand.substrate, re-frame.ui.substrate), the render-phase use-memo factory stops balancing in-render (today: subscribe then unsubscribe, 0->1->0 on cold cache, in-tick dispose, commit-phase subscribe-fn rebuilds — the measured double build, bodyRuns 2N). Instead the factory subscribes and mints a ONE-SHOT ESCROW TOKEN {reaction, frame-kw, query-v, spent? atom} holding the +1 provisionally. Token is (i) stored key-tagged in a hook provisional-ref for the adopter, (ii) pushed on a spine-level pending queue whose macrotask drain (setTimeout-0 class; ONE timer per burst, scheduled on empty->nonempty) is scheduled BEFORE the factory returns. If the ref held a previous unspent token (memo discard / StrictMode double render / interrupted attempt), the factory releases it AFTER its own subscribe (subscribe-then-release ordering; at most one outstanding provisional per hook — this preserves the rf2-8u8tx.2 and rf2-879fe "== 1 after mount" assertions verbatim). The commit-owned subscribe-fn subscribes durably as today (cache HIT -> committed is identical? the render-phase reaction = adoption), publishes committed-ref, then releases the token (2->1). RELEASE = one-shot (spent? CAS) + REACTION-GUARDED via ONE new internal ^:no-doc CLJC helper in re-frame.subs.cache: unsubscribe-if-reaction! [cache k reaction frame-id] — decrement iff (identical? reaction (:reaction slot)), dropped-to-zero? -> dispose-entry-now! (same eviction, same :no-more-derefers emit, same CAS-after-snapshot discipline as unsubscribe!). Unadopted tokens (abandoned render / error / unmount-before-commit / key change) are released by the drain <= 1 macrotask later; 1->0 disposes in-tick per Spec 006 unchanged. The cache NEVER holds a ref-count-0 entry; no cache data-shape change, no entry state machine; unsubscribe!/eviction/cascade untouched. Reagent, reagent-slim, plain-atom: byte-identical (hook-only change + inert CLJC helper).

WHY IT CANNOT LEAK: drain scheduled by the host scheduler before the acquiring expression returns (React cannot unschedule it); one-shot spent? CAS (adoption + drain cannot double-decrement); reaction guard (a slot evicted by HMR/cache-clear/frame-destroy took the +1 with it — stale release no-ops, can never steal a successor entry's ref); one unspent token per hook. Early drain vs React's passive-effect flush degrades to today's dispose+rebuild — correctness NEVER depends on React timing; the perf is opportunistic. Reagent parity: Reagent's released subs already dispose on a macrotask (lane/settle! docstring), so the horizon matches the denominator's shipped behaviour.

CORRECTNESS PROTOCOL MAPPING (rf2-2rtt6.14 clauses): (a) growth bounded by attempts-per-horizon, zero at horizon; Suspense retries within a horizon HIT the provisional entry instead of rebuilding the chain. (b) provisional entry is live+source-wired; extra recompute bound = app-db movements within <= 1 macrotask on abandoned paths only (adopted-path recompute is not extra), vs 2.5-17.2 us/read saved per cold read. (c) reap scheduled unconditionally at acquisition, fires independent of React. (d) second subscriber = plain ref-counting (and can adopt an abandoned materialisation); StrictMode setup/cleanup/setup goes 2->1->2 (today 1->0->1 dispose+rebuild — an improvement); key change = predecessor release + existing rf2-naz09e guard; HMR/cache-clear/frame-destroy = guard no-ops (helper also nil-frame-safe); SSR net-zero after horizon (Node timers) with getServerSnapshot unchanged. (e) JVM sub_cache_test cascade/shared-input pins untouched; rf2-8u8tx.2 + rf2-879fe verbatim; ONE test amended: the rf2-es09qq Suspense-abort witness (react_shared_suite.cljs ~4309) asserts <= 1 immediately after fallback commit AND == 0 after one macrotask settle (zero-leak property kept; zero-POINT moves one macrotask later — this is the single contract-visible change the operator's adoption blesses).

SAME-PR SPEC OBLIGATION (per the protocol): Spec 006 hook-substrate subsection "render-phase provisional acquisition and commit adoption" (amend the rf2-es09qq wording: no retained ref-count BEYOND the provisional horizon = one host macrotask) + cross-ref sentence in §Reference counting and disposal stating the cache algorithm is unchanged; update re-frame.subs.cache ns + unsubscribe! docstrings (the remount-churn-acceptable paragraphs) + full contract docstring on the new helper. Spec 006 is HOT-ZONE — sequence against other spec PRs.

TESTS/BENCH (acceptance): (1) THE ACCEPTANCE WITNESS is the coldmount instrument's uix-handoff arm — post-land the SHIPPED hook must reproduce it: witness counters commits N, rebuilt 0, bodyRuns 1N per layer <= L at layers 1-3, shipped M1 clock inside the handoff arm's band; re-run all five rows of implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/coldmount_run.cjs; re-point the instrument's fidelity gate at shipped-vs-handoff (xcript stays the double-build reference); keep the residue gate (it is the leak detector). (2) adoption-identity unit test (spy-proxy, rf2-sqhjtu style): committed-ref reaction identical? the render-phase build. (3) Suspense-abort amendment per (e). (4) StrictMode: final refcount 1, dispose-count spy 0 across the effect cleanup gap. (5) reaper discipline: adopted token drain no-ops; stale-token-vs-successor entry unchanged; one-shot under adoption+drain. (6) layer-2 abandoned cold render: parent AND inputs gone after one settle (cascade at the horizon). (7) node SSR render without commit -> zero after one timer turn.

INTERACTIONS: rf2-2rtt6.13 (retention fix) COMPOSES — land .13 FIRST (same ~10 factory/get-snap lines; rebase on it; adoption needs no handle from the memo — identity flows through the cache hit, the token carries the reaction for the guard; .13's frozen pre-commit fallback unaffected). rf2-gncxk (flush-path memo guard, HELD ruling) is NOT decided here: no touch to make-derived-value/compute-fn/subs.memo; note for that ruling that cold-mount wrapper invocations halve (2N->1N) post-handoff.

SEQUENCING: depends on PR #7300 merging (the arm + page cited) and rf2-2rtt6.13 landed. Sized for a solo worker: ~20-line CLJC helper, ~50-70 line spine edit, spec wording, tests + bench re-run.

THE WITNESS THE AUDIT DEMANDED. assert-use-subscribe-public-mount-schedule-rebuilds mounts through re-frame.substrate.adapter/render (the Spec 006 client mount entry / adapter :render slot / bare createRoot().render()) with NO act and NO flushSync. Deterministic, not timing-hopeful: the numbers are recorded from inside the probe's own mount use-effect, which React orders after the same fiber's useSyncExternalStore subscribe BY CONSTRUCTION (subscribeToStore is pushed while the hook runs, the probe's use-effect after it, and a fiber's passive effects run in push order in one flush). The poll only yields host turns; its budget expiring fails an assertion rather than hanging.

ANSWER: THE SHIPPED HOOK BUILDS TWICE. Two acquisitions, two DIFFERENT reaction objects, bodyRuns 2.00N, and the cache tenant is the commit's rebuild. The setTimeout 0 reaper releases the escrowed reference before React's passive subscribe; the entry disposes on the ordinary 1->0 edge; the commit misses and rebuilds. The act()-driven adoption row and the coldmount instrument's flushSync arm both force the passive subscribe forward and therefore measured a schedule consumers never mount on. SWAP-THE-PRIMITIVE PROBE, three trials each (temporary diagnostic, not committed): setTimeout 0 (shipped) 2.00N at N=1 and N=300; setTimeout 4 1.00N at both; setTimeout 32 1.00N at both; requestAnimationFrame 1.00N at N=1 but 2.00N at N=300; MessageChannel post 2.00N (React posts its own message later on the same FIFO source). THE INTERACTION FLAG IS ANSWERED, AND THE FEARED OUTCOME DOES NOT OCCUR. assert-use-subscribe-escrow-leg-answers-on-the-public-mount-schedule re-runs the rf2-2rtt6.13 first-commit row on that same schedule beside an unmoved control: get-snap's escrow leg IS still reachable, the moved row's first committed layout-visible DOM is fresh. (3) Spec 006's macrotask bullet said a timer runs after the scheduler's pending work so the commit gets first refusal — FALSE, replaced: a macrotask is necessary and NOT sufficient, and the reference implementation's choice is not sufficient. The bullet that carries the weight (correctness must not depend on the reaper losing the race) is STRENGTHENED. title: bench(hicasso): P0 heap fan-out sweep (E/Q 1-2-4-8, min ROOTS=1+4) to verify the additive heap model and price shell/edge/subscription terms

Preferred form: disjoint/shared query rungs giving mean fan-out E/Q = 1, 2, 4, 8 in ONE scheduled run (per-root disjoint query ranges give fan-out 1 without dropping roots). The .4 driver defaults P0_ROOTS=4 and divides the held-heap delta by ROOTS*perRoot = 1,200 boundaries while all four roots render the SAME frame-id and the SAME [:p0/cell 0..299] query vectors -- 1,200 boundary-query edges over 300 unique keys, so its "exclusive retained per boundary" amortises the subscription half x4. Keep the 4.7 MB dense-array positive control and the post-release residue check on every rung; arm-order guard and mount verification as published (.4 shipped 0 unverified of 48 mounts).

FIT AND REFUSAL RULE. Fit per-boundary = shell + (E/B) x edge + (Q/B) x subscription across the rungs. comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7306 — completeness / correctness / implementation quality.

The B/E/Q witness construction, DOM and cache-cardinality read-backs, GC protocol, positive control, order guard, authored-to-landed range-diff (exact 5/5), and 69 successful GitHub checks are strong. The additive adjudicator's advertised held-out validation is not independent, however.

`R2Q2B` is assigned to `hi` and described as "never used above" / "held out of all of that". The same observation is then used immediately in `key-2 = (hi.y - lo.y) / dx`; `key-gap` feeds `key-ok?`; and `key-ok?` is a mandatory input to `model`. The value later scored as the held-out prediction therefore already participates in model admissibility and in the published alternate key price. For M4 the held-out residual and this R=2-pair key-gap are largely the same contrast, so they are not two disjoint validations. This contradicts the page's claim that R2Q2B is "the only rung whose value nothing above depends on" and weakens the precommitted evidence gate that allowed component prices into validation.md.

There is a second documentation correction, already mechanism-owned by open rf2-2rtt6.25: the provenance says .25 moves retained heap and that a cold read builds once. Audit #7305 demonstrated the public bare `createRoot.render` path still builds 2N because the timer wins; this heap harness forces `flushSync`, and no durable retained-heap delta from .25 is established. The .13 retained-reaction correction is separate and remains supported.

Bounded repair: give `R2Q2B` exactly one role. Preserve the stated independent gate by adding/re-running a genuinely untouched validation rung (or precommit an equivalent disjoint validation), then re-adjudicate the normative prices; alternatively retract the independent-held-out and gating claims and justify the reduced warrant. Correct the .25 provenance claim rather than duplicating its open implementation owner. Downstream normative owner rf2-hvl5s is reopened pending that adjudication.

title: bench(hicasso): test the segment-order effect with independent counterbalanced runs
description:
Found by rf2-a4x1o (PR #7283) while building the fail-closed segment-order verdict for p0_converge_app.

THE FINDING. Across THREE independent five-round runs of the converged witness set — the published run, the rf2-rjfz1 reproduction sweep, and rf2-a4x1o's corrected-instrument run — the cross-segment red-zone figure (uix-subs / reagent-subs, both floor-normalised in the same round and segment) reads HIGHER when the REAGENT segment ran first in 11 of 12 row-runs. One-sided binomial p = 0.0032.

Per-row disjointness could not see this and does not establish it: at rounds=5 the alternation splits 3:2, and under the null a disjoint partition arises in 2 of C(5,2)=10 assignments — 20% per row. Consistent with that, no row is disjoint in two runs (M1 and narrow in the published run, broad in the sweep). It is the SIGN across rows and runs that resolves.

CONSEQUENCE ALREADY SHIPPED (PR #7283): segment-order-verdict publishes :order-balanced-mean — the mean of the two stratum means, which is unbiased under an alternating schedule whatever the parity of rounds — beside the raw mean, and marks a row :claim :direction-only when its strata are disjoint. rf2-2rtt6.1's 1.2301 and the narrow row's 1.1540 are withdrawn as magnitudes on that basis.

WHAT REMAINS, and it is two separable things:

1. BALANCE THE DESIGN. rounds=5 cannot balance two orders. An EVEN round count makes the raw and balanced estimators identical by construction and lifts the disjointness test from 3:2 (20% null rate) to 3:3 (10%). NOT taken in #7283 because it moves four published rows without deciding the question — it is a re-publication, and it should be taken as one: re-run all four rows at rounds=6, republish with a landed SHA, blob hashes and a verified repro, and mark the 5-round rows superseded IN PLACE.

2. EXPLAIN THE EFFECT. Something makes the second segment of a round systematically different from the first, and the page already carries an unexplained candidate: 'the per-page accumulation is still unexplained' — ~12 MB per segment entry, surviving a forced major collection, never reaching the document (rf2-2rtt6.4, rf2-flqpd). If the second segment runs on a heavier heap then whichever adapter goes second reads slower, which is exactly the observed sign (Reagent first => UIx second => UIx/Reagent reads high). retention_probe.cljs already has the census that would test it. That is a hypothesis with a cheap experiment, not a conclusion.

Not urgent: the DIRECTION verdicts survive the partition on every published row, so the bar rows and the red-zone rule still function. What is blocked is quoting a red-zone MAGNITUDE to four decimal places.

Files: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/p0_converge_app.cljs (segment-order-verdict, rounds), .../p0_converge_order_cljs_test.cljs, docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-converged-witness-set.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- Counterbalance or randomize which segment starts across independently launched runs; do not reuse four within-run row signs as independent Bernoulli trials.
- Report inference at the independent-run level or provide and validate a model that accounts for row/run dependence and temporal order.
- Re-run/republish the four rows with the balanced design and preserve the conservative magnitude holds unless stronger evidence resolves them.
- Replace the current corrected-run provenance placeholder with landed SHA 9737ed5cf815817d856c49eefb6824856df51668 plus supporting blob hashes; record landed provenance for the later rerun too.
notes:
AUDIT PR #7283 (2026-07-30; correctness/completeness follow-up). UPDATED this existing exact owner rather than filing a duplicate. The qualitative segment-order suspicion is useful, but the published inferential warrant overstates the evidence: 11/12 signs are four correlated rows inside each of only three sequential browser runs, not 12 established independent Bernoulli trials. The one-sided binomial p=0.0032 therefore has no demonstrated independence basis.

Every run also uses the same deterministic schedule: Reagent-first at rounds 0/2/4 and UIx-first at 1/3. Segment order is consequently confounded with round parity/temporal position, and Reagent-first always receives the extra observation. An even 3:3 count fixes unequal weighting, but a fixed start still does not establish exchangeability or isolate order from time. Treat “real/decisive” and p=0.0032 as unwarranted while retaining the conservative direction/magnitude hold.

Repair the experiment by counterbalancing or randomizing the starting segment across independent process-level runs, then analyze independent run-level replicates (or document a justified dependence model). Also replace the studio's still-landed placeholder “the landed SHA follows the merge” with landed SHA `9737ed5cf815817d856c49eefb6824856df51668` and the supporting blob hashes now, before the later six-round republication.
MECHANISM EVIDENCE from rf2-flqpd's instrument (fresh run on PR #7285's head, full default shape, exit 0, all validity gates green). The RETENTION version of the heavier-heap hypothesis is dead -- the COLLECTED column climbs 0.89 MB total across six segments and does not step at a seam -- but the GARBAGE version is alive and now has a measured, adapter-ASYMMETRIC magnitude: at the segment seams of SERIES C (50 cycles x 4 grid roots per segment, alternating substrate), UNCOLLECTED garbage read uix 17.86 / reagent 85.25 / uix 30.82 / reagent 83.13 / uix 30.45 / reagent 82.46 MB. The prior landed run shows the same asymmetry (reagent seams 65/81/56 vs uix 18/31/12). A Reagent segment's mount/unmount work leaves roughly 2.7-6x the uncollected rubbish of the UIx segment's identical-shape work, and rf2-flqpd settled that exactly this load is what moves an unchanging arm (the floor drifted 3.4->7.0 ms under 30-80 MB of rubbish, because a scavenge inside a timed window measures the collector). So within a round, Reagent-first puts the UIx segment under a far heavier collector debt than UIx-first puts Reagent -- the sign this bead observed (Reagent-first => uix/reagent reads HIGH, 11/12). CAVEAT: seam-level garbage from the retention page's workload, not the converge page's exact witnesses; a mechanism with measured asymmetry, not a verdict -- the counterbalanced independent-run design this bead owns remains the decisive test, and nothing here touches the rounds=6 re-publication.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7303 (2026-07-31): reopened this exact owner rather than creating a duplicate. COMPLETENESS: the six-round counterbalanced instrument, M2 mount-budget repair, four-row republication, tests, and provenance landed, but the durable record contains only group means, intervals, ranges, and p-values. It does not contain the ten per-run threshold means and ten per-run d values, nor a deterministic derivation, so the PRs central statistics cannot be independently recomputed from the repository. CORRECTNESS: the ten start labels were deliberately alternated, not randomly assigned. Enumerating all C(10,5) relabellings is therefore not an assumption-free randomization distribution, and the 2^10 sign-flip result is exact only under an unstated sign-symmetry/exchangeability assumption. Keep the balanced six-round means as useful descriptive evidence, but either state the assumptions and downgrade the inferential wording or take a genuinely randomized assignment if exact randomization inference is wanted. Also reconcile the fail-closed per-run magnitude rule with the ensemble: 3 of 40 row-runs were magnitude-unresolved, yet all ten run means feed each precise ensemble threshold; state and pin the aggregate rule rather than letting an individually unpublishable point silently re-enter. IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: bounded repair only—commit a compact 10x4 observation table or fixture plus its derivation, correct the false one-eight-minute-window wording if it means launch spacing, and avoid a general statistics framework.
CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S CLOSE REASON. I closed this saying the 10x4 observation table 'CANNOT be completed' because the producing worktree was reaped. That was WRONG: the ten runs' console logs had been backed up out of tree and survived intact. The table is now committed COMPLETE -- all forty cells -- on PR #7312, and the two p columns I had recorded as 'not checkable by anyone, now or later' are both recomputed and both reproduce (View 1's 252-relabelling permutation p: 0.770/0.611/0.984/0.992; View 2's 1024-assignment sign-flip p: 0.084/0.889/0.856/0.302). So does every point estimate, every prose count (37 of 40 strata overlapping, 23 of 40 Reagent-first-higher, 59 of 60 M1 rounds above 1.0), and the composite's 0.823. Provenance is stated as RECOVERY, not measurement: nothing was re-measured, and run 1's vectors in the backup match the four the page already printed, which is what identifies the backup as this ensemble rather than a pilot. A test asserts that join. NEW FINDING that only the recovered data could surface: every 95% interval on the page was ~2% too wide. A t multiplier for EIGHT degrees of freedom was used where a mean of ten run means needs NINE (2.2622). The cause is nameable -- eight is CORRECT for the two-sample 5v5 'resolution limit' column beside it, that column reproduces exactly, and the same t was reused for the one-sample case. Reported in neither direction: old intervals struck in place with corrected ones beside them at all ten quoting sites, three tests pin the diagnosis, and the error is conservative so no verdict changes. Also corrected: the open item claiming nine tenths of the table was gone is closed as what happened, and rewritten to what genuinely remains -- this ensemble was verifiable by luck rather than by design. GATE CAVEAT worth carrying forward: mkdocs build --strict does NOT validate docs/design/hicasso/** (mkdocs.yml excludes it), so that page was checked directly instead -- all 15 internal anchors resolve, no malformed tables. Gates: test:cljs exit 0 (11,993 tests / 60,034 assertions, 0 failures); clj-kondo 2026.04.15 errors: 0; mkdocs --strict exit 0.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7312 (merged 2026-07-31T08:47:40Z; landed 64be09b79bb2db511957ba715e3a264b4494e7fc) — REOPENED this exact owner; no duplicate. COMPLETENESS: the recovered 10x4 table, provenance join, deterministic derivations, corrected 9-df intervals, aggregate inclusion rule, false-duration correction, and count-free lane-cache invariant answer the prior audit well. One inference remains uncorrected: the page and this Bead's close reason still say “a confound can manufacture an effect; it cannot manufacture a null,” then use that premise to call the rows insensitive to which segment starts. CORRECTNESS: because starts were alternated, Reagent-start is exactly odd launch parity. An unmeasured session effect can oppose a real start/order effect and cancel it (for example +x from start and -x from odd-launch drift yields an observed zero), just as it can reinforce one. The unconditional sentence is false. For the same reason, averaging the two start groups isolates “ORDER” and half their difference isolates “TEMPORAL” only under an additive, exchangeable/antisymmetric temporal model; the design did not establish that model. The conditional statement “no start effect detectable at this resolution, under exchangeability” is supportable, but the unconditional decomposition and practical insensitivity claim are not. IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: keep the table, arithmetic, p-values, interval repair, and count-free cache comment. This needs a bounded record correction, not a statistics framework or automatic re-measurement: remove the false one-way-confound claim; label the order/temporal split and no-detectable-effect conclusion as conditional/descriptive. If an unconditional causal or schedule-insensitivity claim is still wanted, use genuinely randomized start assignment in a new ensemble.
close_reason:
WARRANT CORRECTED (PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7351). Closing against the NEWEST note — MERGED-PR AUDIT #7312 — not the older #7283 one.

MY BRIEF WAS STALE AND I AM RECORDING IT. It asked me to remove the one-sided binomial p = 0.0032 whose independence basis was unmet. THAT CORRECTION HAD ALREADY LANDED (PRs #7303/#7312): the page has carried 'That warrant was wrong, and it was wrong in two separable ways' and an explicit withdrawal since. Re-doing it would have been a no-op. The live scope was #7312's different, still-uncorrected inference.

THE FALSE SENTENCE, NOW WITHDRAWN IN PLACE. The page argued 'a confound can manufacture an effect; it cannot manufacture a null' and used that premise to call the rows insensitive to which segment starts. It is false: because the ten starts were ALTERNATED, Reagent-start is exactly odd launch parity, so a session drift can OPPOSE a real order effect as easily as reinforce it — a true +x against a -x is observed as zero. A null under a confounded design is evidence of no NET effect along the one axis the design could see, not of no effect.

DOWNGRADED TO CONDITIONAL/DESCRIPTIVE, exactly the bounded repair asked for:
(1) The ORDER/TEMPORAL split no longer 'isolates' anything — the cancellation is exact only under an ADDITIVE, ANTISYMMETRIC temporal model, which counterbalancing makes AVAILABLE but does not test and this design did not. The columns are a descriptive split; the labels are the model's naming, not a measured attribution. Same conditioning applied to the derivation test's two docstrings, which asserted the unconditional version.
(2) 'Which segment starts a run does not detectably move the number' -> no difference RESOLVABLE at this power, under the same exchangeability the permutation p assumes.
(3) 'demonstrably insensitive to the schedule' -> no schedule effect resolvable in these ten runs, under exchangeability. The even round count's design-unbiasedness is kept SEPARATE and unqualified: that one holds by construction and carries no assumption.

DID A DEFENSIBLE STATISTIC SURVIVE? Yes, and nothing had to be removed. The permutation and sign-flip p values are exact UNDER A STATED ASSUMPTION (exchangeability / sign symmetry), and the page now states it at every quoting site instead of at none. The audit's own supportable conditional — 'no start effect detectable at this resolution, under exchangeability' — is what the page now claims, as a conditional.

THE P-VALUE'S LAST TWO LIVE CITATIONS, which the page's withdrawal never reached: p0_converge_app.cljs still said 'It found something ... one-sided binomial p = 0.0032', and coldmount_app.cljs cited it as the REASON for an even round count. Both now carry the withdrawal, and both KEEP the design repair, which never needed the effect — a balanced round count makes the raw and order-balanced means coincide BY CONSTRUCTION.

NO RE-MEASUREMENT: measurement is deferred by the operator and this was a warrant problem, not a data problem. Every number, interval, p-value and table cell is untouched, and test:cljs re-derives the committed 10x4 observation table's arithmetic to prove it.

STILL OPEN, NOT DONE HERE (file follow-ups if wanted): a genuinely RANDOMISED start assignment is what it would take to drop the exchangeability qualifier and support an unconditional causal/schedule-insensitivity claim. The acceptance criteria's earlier items (counterbalanced independent runs, run-level inference, six-round republication, landed SHA 9737ed5c + blob hashes) were satisfied by the #7303/#7312 line.

Gates: test-fast-pr.sh exit 0; test:cljs exit 0 (12,263 tests / 61,442 assertions / 0 failures) — run because this touches the derivation test and two bench app namespaces; check_doc_slugs.py exit 0; mkdocs build --strict exit 0. By hand: 71 tables / 0 column mismatches (incl. View 1 6x4, View 2 6x5, components 4x5); 57 anchors / 0 dead.

title: HD-008 bulk write row: the FLOOR sits on the clock clamp, so a resolved yield correction refuses it
description:
FOUND BY rf2-b69lw (PR #7282) while making the harness-microtask correction contract enforceable.

HD-008's BULK write row passes a batch of ONE — the pre-batch window exactly — and its FLOOR arm reads a p50 of about 0.1 ms, i.e. ONE 100us Chrome clock quantum.

That was tolerable while the harness-microtask asymmetry was unpriced. It is not tolerable now that it is adjudicated:

  * The floor is the row's only YIELD-BEARING arm in the slim run (reagent-slim is :microtask-scheduled, so its window holds no harness turns).
  * The one-turn aggregate yield reading is STOCHASTIC on this host. Across five observed runs of the same source: 0.0 ms three times, 0.0999999 ms twice.
  * When it resolves at 0.1 ms, the correction is THE WHOLE OF THE BULK FLOOR. hd8-rows/yield-correction returns :refused/:correction-exceeds-window and no figure in the row may be published.

This was found the hard way. With the survival test at  the row did NOT refuse — the corrected floor came out at ~1e-8 ms, still positive, and the row published a corrected reagent-slim/floor of 15,518,934x. The survival test is now 'what remains must exceed what was removed', which refuses correctly.

WHAT STANDS. The PUBLISHED bulk row (reagent-slim 11.000-13.667x floor) was taken on a run whose aggregate read 0.0, so :below-resolution applied, nothing was owed, and the figure is unaffected. Nothing is withdrawn.

THE FIX IS THE ONE THE NARROW ROW ALREADY GOT (rf2-9zysg): batch the bulk window so its floor clears the clamp. narrow-batch-k writes share one clock on the narrow row and lifted it from 4-12 quanta to 40-120. The bulk row needs the same, at whatever k puts its floor clear.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN #7282: batching the bulk window CHANGES A MEASURED WINDOW, which obliges a re-take of the bulk row on every adapter. That is a re-publication of HD-008 figures and not a worker's to make on its own authority. rf2-2rtt6.7 is the owning gate bead.

CAUTION, same as rf2-zb3qg's: rf2-2rtt6.2 has a RECORDED GUARD REFUSAL from batching on a witness of this family (batched M2 mounts, 3.2x-5.4x last-third over first-third on all four arms, ranges disjoint, exit 2, batch withdrawn rather than tolerance moved). The arm-order guard must be re-run against any batched bulk window and the ARM repaired if it refuses. A batched figure the guard refuses may not be published at all.

Evidence: docs/design/hicasso/studio/hd8-composed-donor-arm.md, 'Known limitations of this instrument' and 'The correction contract is enforced, not stated'.
notes:
CORRECTION to the description: one sentence lost a word to shell backtick expansion. It should read: "With the survival test at pos? the row did NOT refuse -- the corrected floor came out at ~1e-8 ms, still positive, and the row published a corrected reagent-slim/floor of 15,518,934x."
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7282: the description's "WHAT STANDS" conclusion is not supported by the measurement. :below-resolution treats aggregate max=0 as "nothing to subtract" and publishes unadjusted. With performance.now() quantized to 100 us, 0 means unresolved below one quantum, not true zero. This bead's bulk floor is itself about one quantum, and the same one-turn yield control alternates between 0 and 0.1 ms on the same source/host; unresolved yield can therefore be comparable to the entire denominator and change or refuse the result. Until batching and re-take lift the bulk floor, a zero aggregate must not certify that magnitude as unaffected: mark the bulk magnitude nonreportable or adjudicate against the clock-resolution upper bound. The existing batching/re-take owner remains correct; no duplicate Bead.
RESOLVED BY NARROWING THE CLAIM, NOT BY MANUFACTURING RESOLUTION — PR #7585.

THE MEASUREMENT FIRST. The instrument now takes its own resolution instead of
asserting it (clock-resolution!: read, spin until the value changes, record the
difference; the minimum over n observations is the tick, because a spin that
overran a boundary reports a multiple). Measured on this host, every run:
0.1 ms, 200/200 observations resolved, observed differences {0.1, 0.2, 0.3} --
multiples of the tick, which is what makes it a RESOLUTION and not a latency.

THE BULK ROW'S DISCRIMINATING RANGE, six cold runs of the same source:
  * its floor p50 takes only three values -- 0.10, 0.15, 0.20 ms = 1.0, 1.5,
    2.0 ticks. Adjacent attainable denominators are 33%-100% apart.
  * so every ratio normalised by it is determined only to within a factor of
    about two. It can separate effects LARGER than ~2x and nothing finer.
  * the row says so itself: in one run the reagent-slim numerator moved 1.18x
    across six rounds (1.70 -> 2.00 ms) while the published ratio moved 2.06x
    (8.5 -> 17.5). The whole of that swing is the denominator stepping between
    one tick and two.
  * four unmutated/sub-grain draws of one source published 8.500-17.500,
    9.333-10.500, 7.500-15.000 and 8.000-10.667.

MUTATION-PROVED BOTH DIRECTIONS, live, cold, with the injected work priced
in-page against the same clock:
  * +0.0341 ms per write (34% of a grain, a real +20-30% on the floor's true
    cost) -> 8.000-10.667, which OVERLAPS all three unmutated draws. By the
    instrument's own house rule (overlapping ranges are indistinguishable) the
    change is not resolved. A MUTATION THAT SHOULD MOVE THE ROW AND DOES NOT --
    the finding, not a failure.
  * +0.263 ms per write (2.6 grains) -> floor 4.0-5.5 ticks, the mask RELEASES,
    the row publishes 3.250-4.500, disjoint from every band above. The
    instrument is live and the mask tracks the measurement.

WHAT LANDED.
  * mask-below-grain withdraws figures a sub-grain window forms. Rule:
    (v - tick) > tick -- what the clock resolved must exceed what it could not.
    That is word for word correct-round's survival test with the grain in place
    of the correction; two measured quantities, no constant. The weaker form
    (v > tick) was tried first and DECIDED NOTHING: consecutive draws read a
    worst of 1.0 and 1.5 ticks, so it withheld the row and then published
    9.333-10.500. The final sweep's draw read 2.0 ticks in all three runs --
    exactly the draw the weak rule would have published -- and the tight rule
    withholds it.
  * WHICH FIGURES GO: the floor is every floor-normalised figure's denominator,
    so a floor beneath the grain takes that column. HEAD-TO-HEAD PAIRS SURVIVE
    -- arm over arm, the floor cancels exactly. The clamp destroys the cross-run
    column (the weaker warrant) and leaves the within-run pairs (the stronger).
  * A LIMIT IS NOT A FAULT: below-clock-grain exits 0 and prints NO REPORTABLE
    MAGNITUDE; failed-dom-read-back still exits 3. Exiting non-zero on a
    permanent limit would exit non-zero on every run.
  * THE COIN TOSS IS GONE: yield-correction adjudicates over the figures the row
    still PUBLISHES. The bulk row's only bearer is the floor, its column is
    withdrawn, so the verdict is :moot -- the SAME on a 0.0 aggregate and a 0.1
    aggregate. Fixture 10 replays both. The refusal itself is untouched: fixture
    4 (the 15,518,934x row) is unmasked and still refuses.
  * 13 in-bundle fixtures (5 new) + 6 corrected-table + 24 exit-decision + 90
    harness cases.

NOT DONE, still rf2-2rtt6.7's: batching the bulk window and re-taking the row.
That is the permanent repair; this is the honest statement of the limit until
it lands.

FILED rf2-z8oiq: the studio page's bulk cross-run magnitudes are now withheld by
the instrument, and its "far better resolved than the narrow one beside it"
claim is INVERTED -- the bulk floor is 1.0-2.0 quanta and the batched narrow
floor is 8-13. Fenced for this worker; the operator sequences it.

GATES: fast-PR spine 0 (docs=false jvm=true node=true, classified); lint:js 0;
clock_exit_path.test.cjs 0 (90); hd8_run --selftest 0; lane_build.test.cjs 0;
test:hicasso-compile 0 (129 ns, 0 warnings); full three-run sweep 0 at two HEADs;
HD8_ONLY=slim 0. Every bench build cold by construction (resetLaneBuildCache).
close_reason: The bulk row's floor-normalised magnitudes are withheld by the instrument on every draw (mask-below-grain: what the clock resolved must exceed what it could not), its head-to-head pairs are unaffected, and the yield correction over it is :moot on both draws of the clock instead of publishing on one and failing the sweep on the other — PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7585. The claim narrowed; no resolution was manufactured. Batching the bulk window and re-taking the row remains rf2-2rtt6.7's.

title: Hicasso lane: hicasso_narrow_run.cjs rides :hicasso-bench but is outside rf2-2rtt6.20's fence and still takes the shared-cache poison
description:
FOUND BY rf2-2rtt6.20 (PR #7278) while fixing the shared-build-id cache trap.

rf2-2rtt6.20 established that `:hicasso-bench` hosts N different programs under
one cache entry, that the carrier is shadow-cljs's `shadow-js/` npm-conversion
cache, and that the repair is for each driver to clear
`.shadow-cljs/builds/hicasso-bench` before it builds. Five drivers were fixed:

  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/{run,hd8_run,p0_converge_run,retention_run,z3vlz_run}.cjs

A SIXTH driver also rides `:hicasso-bench` through `--config-merge`:

  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso_narrow_run.cjs

It was outside rf2-2rtt6.20's fence (`implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/**`)
and was deliberately not edited.

RESIDUAL HAZARD, and it is one-sided. The five fixed drivers clear the entry
before building, so this driver can no longer poison THEM. But nothing clears
the entry on this driver's behalf, so it can still be handed a cache poisoned by
whichever arm ran before it — the same "compiles clean, dies at runtime under
:advanced with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'd')`" failure.

This driver publishes docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-ratom-spine-narrow-write.md,
so the trap can make that page look broken at HEAD in exactly the way it made
HD-008 look broken.

title: Hicasso P0 lane: one build id shared by three drivers leaves a cache that compiles clean and dies at runtime
description:
FOUND BY rf2-2rtt6.19 (PR #7277) while re-reading HD-008's yield-cost control.

run.cjs, p0_converge_run.cjs and hd8_run.cjs all drive build id `hicasso-bench` with a DIFFERENT :init-fn supplied through --config-merge. That is HD-017's design and the reason it exists is good: a build-id touch is hot-zone, and four arms would otherwise be four of them.

THE HAZARD: running one driver after another leaves a .shadow-cljs/builds/hicasso-bench cache that COMPILES CLEANLY and then produces a bundle that DIES AT RUNTIME under :advanced.

Observed: after run.cjs (twice) and p0_converge_run.cjs, hd8_run.cjs exited 1 with

  pageerror: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'd')

before taking a single sample. It reproduces at UNMODIFIED HEAD — I reverted my own hd8_rows.cljs change to HEAD and it failed identically, which is how it was localised. It clears COMPLETELY with

  rm -rf implementation/.shadow-cljs/builds/hicasso-bench

after which the same driver on the same tree exits 0 and measures normally.

WHY IT MATTERS. 'Run the P0 lane, then run HD-008' is the natural sequence for anyone checking the wave's numbers, and it silently produces a dead page. The driver's own fail-closed logic (rf2-f5roa) behaves correctly — it refuses to publish anything from a page that threw — but its message cannot say why, so a reader's most likely conclusion is that HD-008 is broken on main. It is not.

CANDIDATE FIXES, in rough order of preference:
  (a) Each driver clears its own build cache entry before building, or keys the cache by :init-fn.
  (b) Distinct :output-dir already differ; the cache dir does not. Give each driver its own cache root via the shadow-cljs cache-root option.
  (c) At minimum, add the rm -rf line to each driver's failure message when a pageerror is the cause, so the next reader spends two minutes rather than an hour.

Not urgent for correctness of any PUBLISHED figure — a page that boots, passes canonical-DOM parity, passes read-back verification on every sample and passes its positive control is not a mis-compiled page, and every published run exited 0. This is a reproducibility trap, not a measurement fault.
notes:
PR #7278 open. REPRODUCED at unmodified HEAD 6509d8e5c5 and fixed.

MECHANISM (isolated, not assumed). Carrier is shadow-cljs's `shadow-js/`
npm-conversion cache, NOT the Closure name-stability maps (that was the first
suspect and is refuted: removing closure.property.map + closure.variable.map
from a poisoned cache leaves it dead). `convert-sources-simple` invalidates the
shadow-js index on SHADOW-CACHE-KEY / cache-affecting-options and never on the
set of npm modules the build needs; the Reagent arms cache 14 modules with no
react/jsx-runtime, and the UIx arm is then linked against that state.

The trap is HISTORY-DEPENDENT AND SELF-HEALING — once the index has accumulated
every arm's modules, re-running the poisoning builds cannot take them back out.
Every trial must start from a cold builds/hicasso-bench. A warm "control" came
back ALIVE and had to be discarded; that is the main methodological trap here.

FIX: each of the five hicasso drivers clears .shadow-cljs/builds/hicasso-bench
before building, via one helper `lane_cache.cjs`. Whole entry, not the one
directory now known to carry it — the failed first guess is why a surgical
clear is not worth a standing bet on shadow-cljs internals. shadow-cljs.edn NOT
touched. Measured cost is inside run-to-run noise (warm 34s/26s vs cleared
33s/37s).

z3vlz_run.cjs was poisoning ITSELF: four variants built back to back in one run.

FILED rf2-2rtt6.22 — hicasso_narrow_run.cjs (adapters/reagent tree) also rides
:hicasso-bench, was outside this bead's fence, and still takes the poison.

GATE NOTE FOR THE OPERATOR: two measurement gates failed on a loaded box and
NEITHER is a cache/boot fault (0 unverified throughout, pages booted and
tabulated normally):
  - p0_converge_run.cjs full sweep: arm-order guard REFUSED (exit 2) on M2, the
    DIAGNOSTIC row, on sub-ms readings (FIRST-THIRD 0.40 [0.30-0.50] vs
    LAST-THIRD 0.70 [0.60-0.80]) against a 100us clamp.
  - hd8_run.cjs slim run: positive control missed by a hair on one round of
    three (1.3529 vs a 1.395 floor).
Re-run from a cleared cache, the slim control PASSED (D=0) and main's own
drivers were run on the same box as controls. NOTE the cleared-cache A/B is
logically a no-op comparison: with the cache already cleared by the harness,
main and branch compile the same program from the same state, so any
disagreement is the instrument's own variance. Guard tolerance NOT touched;
arm NOT repaired (out of fence and it would move a measured window).
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7279: REOPENED because main is still broken and fix PR #7278 remains open. At exact landed 2f3ee069c5, the default four-variant z3vlz run reproduced the known shared :hicasso-bench cache poison on all six pages (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'd')`, exit 1). With builds/hicasso-bench isolated cold before each variant, slim-only, slim+reagent, slim+uix, and mixed all exited 0 and all 1+2+1+2 page contracts passed. This cleanly assigns the failure to this existing cache owner, not PR #7279's adjudication patch.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7278: the landed four-commit series fixes the exact #7279 reproduction. Starting with a populated builds/hicasso-bench cache, the default z3vlz driver cleared the entry before each of its four variants, all six advanced pages met their contracts, and the run exited 0; the same slim-only variant rebuilt after another clear to byte-identical SHA-256 7D8F0C9625C713D0D4C61E24933B85D2D9A356F676D269994CB44F5C79C3A553. All five freehand Hicasso drivers call one bounded helper before their build. The remaining adapters/reagent/hicasso_narrow_run.cjs user is already exact owner rf2-2rtt6.22 and remains in progress. title: bench(hicasso): lane/control-verdict passes a control the HD-008 rule would fail
description:
Found while consolidating HD-008 onto the lane (rf2-f5roa, PR #7267).

The two positive-control adjudications in the Hicasso tree do NOT agree, and the shared one is the weaker:

  lane/control-verdict           ok? = (and (<= min hi) (>= max lo))
                                 i.e. the measured RANGE need only OVERLAP the +/- slack band.
  hd8-rows/positive-control!     :within? = (and (>= lo (* p (- 1 tol))) (<= hi (* p (+ 1 tol))))
                                 i.e. EVERY round must be INSIDE the band.

HD-008's own comment argues the stricter rule explicitly: 'a control whose worst round is wrong has caught something, and letting a good round vouch for a bad one is how an instrument stops being one.' rf2-f5roa deliberately did NOT adopt lane/control-verdict for that reason.

The lane is what the P0 arms use, so under lane/control-verdict a run with one bad round and one good one passes its own positive control. That is the shape of thing this programme keeps finding: a gate that cannot go red has not verified anything.

NOT REPAIRED IN #7267, deliberately: tightening lane/control-verdict changes the adjudication every published P0 row was taken under. Whoever takes this must decide whether the published rows are re-adjudicated (and say so on rf2-2rtt6.1) or whether the change applies only from the next run.

Files: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/lane.cljs (control-verdict); implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/hd8_rows.cljs (positive-control!, the stricter rule).
notes:
FINDING (worker/lane-control-cluster, PR pending): tightening lane/control-verdict DOES retroactively fail a published run, so the strict rule was NOT installed. Re-adjudicating the 11 controls control-verdict has published under the overlap rule flips exactly one: docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-converged-witness-set.md, M2 mount, UIx segment - predicted 1.9412, slack 0.25, band [1.4559-2.4265], published range [1.333-2.000]; worst round 8.4% BELOW the band floor, carries a green tick, holds it only because a good round vouched for a bad one. The other ten (3 in p0-reagent-on-subs-baseline.md, 7 in p0-converged-witness-set.md) pass under EITHER reading. lane.cljs commit b8fb831d1c states the defect in control-verdict's docstring so :ok? cannot be mistaken for the strict answer; no number moved. NEEDS AN OPERATOR RULING on rf2-2rtt6.1: re-adjudicate that row (which also needs a re-run of the converged arm, p0_converge_app) or apply the strict rule from the next run only. Left OPEN deliberately.
FRESH CONTROL EVIDENCE from rf2-6i0i2's balanced ensemble. REPORT ONLY -- the
ruling is the operator's and nothing here decides it.

Ten independently launched six-round runs of p0_converge_app (counterbalanced
start, guard clean on all 40 row-runs, parity clean, 0 unverified of 92,160,
exit 0 on all ten) yield 80 positive controls -- 4 rows x 2 segments x 10 runs.
That is the first sample large enough to price the two adjudications.

  OVERLAP RULE (lane/control-verdict, what the P0 rows were taken under): 80 of
  80 pass.
  STRICT every-round-inside reading (hd8-rows/positive-control!): 64 of 80 pass.
  Runs with all eight of their controls strictly inside: 2 of 10.

Per row, strict passes / worst single round against the +/-25% band:
  M1 mount     20/20   worst 1.6875, inside the band [1.4992-2.4986]
  M2 mount     13/20   Reagent 6/10, UIx 7/10. Worst 1.1667 (Reagent), 19.9%
                       BELOW the floor 1.4559; worst UIx 1.3333, 8.4% below
  bulk broad   11/20   Reagent 7/10, UIx 4/10. Worst 1.3333, 11.1% below floor
  bulk narrow  20/20   worst 1.7544, inside

TWO OBSERVATIONS THAT BEAR ON THE HELD RULING.

1. The number this bead holds on reproduces exactly. Its M2 case is a control
range [1.333 - 2.000] whose worst round sits 8.4% below the 1.4559 floor; this
ensemble's worst M2 UIx round is the same 1.3333, the same 8.4%. Not a
coincidence -- 4/3 is a lattice point of a ratio built from readings of two to
five 100 us quanta. But the ensemble also reaches 1.1667 on the M2 Reagent
segment, 19.9% below the floor, which is more than twice the excursion the
ruling was weighing.

2. The strict failures are not spread evenly and their shape is diagnostic.
Every one falls on M2 or broad -- the two rows whose CONTROL leg is a handful of
quanta -- and every one is a LOW outlier. The two rows measured on 20+ quanta
legs, M1 and narrow, pass strict 40 times out of 40. So the cost of the strict
rule, priced: it would refuse the M2 row in 6 runs of 10 and the broad row in 6
of 10, on a page where every other gate is green. Whether that is the gate doing
its job on a clamp-limited witness or the gate mis-firing on quantisation is
exactly the question this bead owns.

Detail and the full per-run tables are on the studio page under "The strict
reading, over eighty controls (rf2-egdaq)":
docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-converged-witness-set.md
RULING — DO NOT TIGHTEN (issued by the acting mayor 2026-07-31 under authority delegated by Mike for Hicasso items; operator-overturnable).

THE QUESTION. lane/control-verdict adjudicates a positive control on OVERLAP (the measured range need only overlap the +/- slack band); hd8-rows/positive-control! requires EVERY round INSIDE the band. HD-008's own comment argues the stricter rule. The bead asked: re-adjudicate the one published row the strict rule would flip, or apply strict from the next run only.

THE RULING: NEITHER. The overlap rule STANDS, the strict rule is NOT adopted, and no published row is re-adjudicated. What changes is only that the limitation is stated where it can be read.

WHY, on evidence rather than taste:
1. The strict rule's misses are a LATTICE ARTEFACT, not arm defects. The four recorded strict-rule misses miss by 0.0014 on a TWO-QUANTUM floor — that is the 100us Chrome clock clamp being reported as a control failure.
2. rf2-6i0i2's balanced ensemble (PR #7303, merged) re-adjudicated 80 controls: 80/80 pass under overlap, 64/80 under strict, and only 2 of 10 runs pass strict on all eight. The failures fall ENTIRELY on M2 and broad — the coarse-leg rows. A rule that fails 16 of 80 controls by landing on the clock quantum is measuring resolution, not correctness.
3. The specific row this bead was filed over is not the outlier it appeared to be. Its worst M2/UIx round reproduces exactly (1.3333, 8.4% below the band floor) — but in the same 80-control set the REAGENT segment reaches 1.1667, 19.9% below floor, more than TWICE the excursion under review. Tightening on the 8.4% case while the 19.9% case sits in the same data would be adjudicating the arm we happened to look at.
4. Tightening retroactively fails a published run, and this programme's standing discipline is that a superseded figure is re-taken, never rescued or re-labelled by a rule change after the fact.

WHAT IS OWED (already partly landed): lane.cljs commit b8fb831d1c states the defect in control-verdict's own docstring so :ok? cannot be mistaken for the strict answer — that stays. The coarse-leg limitation should be readable beside the affected rows: any control whose legs sit within a few clock quanta is resolution-limited, and its pass is a pass under overlap, not a claim that every round sat inside the band. That is a docs note, not a code change, and it rides the next Hicasso studio-docs pass (rf2-b0tz5 is in flight on those pages).

NOT A CLAIM that the strict rule is wrong in principle. If the clock clamp is ever escaped — batched windows lifting the coarse legs clear of the quantum, as rf2-9zysg did for the narrow row — the strict rule becomes adoptable and should be revisited then.
close_reason: RULED: do not tighten. The overlap rule stands; the strict rule is not adopted; no published row re-adjudicated. Evidence: the strict-rule misses are a lattice artefact (0.0014 on a two-quantum floor); rf2-6i0i2's 80-control re-adjudication passes 80/80 under overlap but only 64/80 under strict with all failures on the coarse-leg rows; and the Reagent segment in that same set runs 19.9% below floor against the 8.4% excursion this bead was filed over. The docstring defect-statement (b8fb831d1c) stays; the coarse-leg limitation rides the next studio-docs pass. Revisit if batched windows ever lift the coarse legs clear of the clock quantum. Ruling by acting mayor under delegated authority; operator-overturnable.

title: P0 bulk-narrow clock row is clamp-limited: batch k writes to a window, then re-guard
description:
The converged P0 clock table (rf2-a4x1o, docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-converged-witness-set.md) resolves three of its four rows. The fourth — bulk narrow, one commit that exactly ONE of 300 sub-reading boundaries reads — does not stably resolve.

Four estimates (two independent 5-round runs x two estimators) read 1.0405 / 1.1556 / 1.1738 / 1.1972. The DIRECTION is the same every time (UIx-on-subs slower than Reagent-on-subs) but whether the range clears 1.0 depends on the run, and one estimate has a minimum of exactly 1.0000 — Chrome's 100us clamp, not a tie. Every leg of the row is 3-5 quanta: floor 2-3, reagent-subs 4-4.5, uix-subs 4.5-5.

REMEDY: k writes inside ONE timed window, which is what rf2-2rtt6.4 did for its own clamped rows (4 writes a sample for the broad write, 8 mounts a sample for the 51-element form). That is a change to the INSTRUMENT, not to the witness, so it does not disturb the convergence.

CAUTION, and it is why this is a bead and not a patch: rf2-2rtt6.2 has a RECORDED GUARD REFUSAL from batching on this witness family — batching M2 mounts produced 3.2x-5.4x last-third-over-first-third on all four arms with ranges disjoint, exit 2, and the batch was withdrawn rather than the tolerance moved. The guard must be re-run against any batched narrow window and the arm repaired if it refuses; a batched figure that the guard refuses may not be published at all.

Until then the row is published as clamp-limited and NOT as a resolved threshold: read it as 'UIx between indistinguishable and ~1.2x slower on a narrow write' and do not judge a candidate red on a finer margin.

Owner surface: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/p0_converge_app.cljs (bulk-write!, bulk-round!). Results append to rf2-2rtt6.1 and to the studio page.
