Price of YES is one serialized hot-zone campaign across spec/API.md + spec/Conventions.md + image assembly + registrar + xray + pair + story + ~50 test assertions.
- Codex second opinion: YES, now, cleanly, no compat mirror. Its strongest point is perf-independent: the sealed resolver's shape is pointed the wrong way for its two runtime reads (lookup manufactures a pair key per call; registrations/ids reduce over the whole map); keep the flat map assembly-local and nest once at the sealing boundary; pre-alpha postponement only grows the external-reader count. Codex independently reproduced the measurement (N-LOOKGEN 138.5, N-LOOKATOM 40.0 B/call).

WHY NO WINS: Codex's shape argument was taken seriously - it is the strongest YES case - but it decides the shape by crowning the runtime lookup the resolver's primary customer, and the only evidence for that priority is the ~98 B/call: small even where measured, unmeasured on the target runtime, and known-unreliable as a browser proxy. Without target-runtime evidence the reshape moves complexity rather than removing it: today lookup pays a small vector per call so that xray's cross-frame keyset comparison, generation-diff, the Pair runtime, and Story read the documented flat shape directly as plain data; after, lookup is free and every one of those consumers projects or walks a nested map instead. The spec is the artefact; {[kind id] descriptor} is one of frame-generation's four documented stable public keys, and reshaping a documented public key on zero target-runtime evidence is gold-plating under the posture. The elegance defect actually FILED - docstring contradicting implementation on a hot chokepoint - is cured and banked. Nothing lies; nothing is broken.

REOPEN CONDITION: CLJS/browser evidence showing the generation-routed lookup's key allocation materially on the target-runtime profile. rf2-x0fe2 is the measurement bead; its CLJS counterpart measurement is the trigger. Secondary fold-in moment: if the :rf.gen/* surface is ever reshaped by spec change for other reasons, ride this re-key along rather than reopening it standalone.

PRESERVED ANALYSIS (so a re-opener does not re-derive it):
- Re-key sketch: {[kind id] descriptor} -> nested {kind {id descriptor}}. Keep the flat map LOCAL to the assembly pipeline (collision detection, image-order layering, shadow construction are naturally [kind id]-keyed) and nest ONCE at the sealing boundary - generations are immutable and cached, so the O(n) conversion is paid once per assembled generation, shared by its frames. Do NOT carry both indexes in the sealed value. lookup then uses the same paired gets on both branches and the docstring's paired-get claim becomes true everywhere.
- Kept as projections regardless: shadows' and generation-diff's public [kind id] result shapes; they do not require the runtime index itself to be pair-keyed.
- Blast radius (worker survey + Codex's count: ~26 non-decision files mention :rf.gen/resolver): spec/API.md L808 (four documented stable public keys); spec/Conventions.md L59 ('map from a [kind id] pair to exactly one descriptor'; :rf.gen/* member set additive-by-spec-change, so a fifth nested-index key is EQUALLY out-of-fence); image_assembly.cljc (assemble builds it, resolve-descriptor reads it, :rf.gen/kinds derived via (into #{} (map first) (keys resolver))); live_frame/generation-diff (diffs the two flat maps); registrar (lookup + kind-registrations-from-resolver); tools/xray image_view_reads.cljs keyset comparison (xray spec 026 pins the [kind id] keyset contract); pair skill preload runtime.cljs x2 (describe-image) + frame_registrar_test; tools/story story_runtime_test.clj; docs/api/re-frame.core.md, docs/core/images.md, docs/EP/EP-0026; ~50 core assertions of the form (contains? (:rf.gen/resolver gen) [:event :x]). If ever scheduled: one sequenced hot-zone worker, one lane, spec + core + three tools + test corpus in a single change.
- Adjacent win carried by the same re-key: kind-registrations-from-resolver walks the WHOLE resolver per registrations/ids call - O(n) where the nested index gives O(1). Query/introspection surface, not per-read hot path: a beneficiary of the re-key, not a justification for it.
close_reason: RULED NO (delegated decision, 2026-07-27): close on the honest docstring. The generation-routed branch's ~98 B/call is ~5% of one path's allocation, JVM-only, and rf2-x0fe2 shows the JVM profile misranks these surfaces for the browser target; reshaping documented public key :rf.gen/resolver (spec/API.md L808, spec/Conventions.md L59) on zero target-runtime evidence is gold-plating, priced at a serialized hot-zone campaign across spec + core + xray + pair + story + ~50 assertions. The filed defect (docstring vs implementation) is cured and banked. REOPEN on CLJS/browser evidence from rf2-x0fe2's counterpart measurement showing this lookup site materially on the target-runtime profile, or fold the re-key into any future :rf.gen/* spec reshape. Full ruling, re-key sketch (nest once at the sealing boundary, flat map stays assembly-local), blast-radius roster, and the O(n)->O(1) kind-registrations adjacent note are preserved in this bead's notes.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
BLOCKED ON A SPEC DECISION — verified, NOT fixed (PR #7157, worker/core-alloc-artefacts).

THE FINDING REPRODUCES EXACTLY. JVM, -Dre-frame.debug=false, ThreadMXBean, n=300,
5 rounds (3 forward + 2 RM_ORDER=rev), controls +0.000% in all 10 rounds:
  N-LOOKGEN  138.3 - 138.5 B/call
  N-LOOKATOM  40.0 B/call
The 40 B on BOTH arms is the arm's own (first query-v), so the registrar-atom branch
is ~0 B and the generation-routed branch ~98 B. Exactly as filed.

WHY THE REMEDY DID NOT SHIP. Re-keying :rf.gen/resolver from {[kind id] descriptor}
to {kind {id descriptor}} is a NORMATIVE SPEC CHANGE, not a local one:

  * spec/API.md L808 pins :rf.gen/resolver ({[kind id] descriptor}) as ONE OF
    frame-generation's 'four documented stable public keys'.
  * spec/Conventions.md L59 fixes the :rf.gen/* member set as
    'fixed-and-additive by Spec change' and spells the resolver as 'a map from a
    [kind id] pair to exactly ONE descriptor'.
  * Adding a FIFTH :rf.gen/* nested index is equally a spec change by the same
    two lines. So neither the reshape nor the additive index is in-fence.

CONSUMERS OUTSIDE core THAT READ THE FLAT [kind id] SHAPE AS PLAIN DATA:
  * tools/xray image_view_reads.cljs — (set (keys (:rf.gen/resolver gen))) and
    cross-frame KEYSET comparison; tools/xray/spec/026 documents the [kind id]
    keyset contract explicitly. (tools/** was DO-NOT-EDIT for this worker.)
  * skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/.../runtime.cljs x2 (describe-image) + its
    frame_registrar_test.
  * tools/story/test/re_frame/story_runtime_test.clj.
  * docs/api/re-frame.core.md, docs/core/images.md, docs/EP/EP-0026.
  * ~50 core test assertions of the form
    (contains? (:rf.gen/resolver gen) [:event :x]).
  * image_assembly.cljc itself: assemble builds it, resolve-descriptor reads it,
    :rf.gen/kinds is derived as (into #{} (map first) (keys resolver)),
    live_frame/generation-diff diffs the two flat maps.

WHAT DID LAND: registrar/lookup's docstring no longer claims something its dominant
branch contradicts. It now says which branch the paired-get argument covers, what the
other costs (~98 B/call, measured), and what removing it would take.

ADJACENT FINDING, same root cause, worth pricing if this is ever scheduled:
registrar/kind-registrations-from-resolver walks the ENTIRE resolver with reduce-kv
per registrations / ids call, because the flat keying gives no per-kind index. The
same re-key makes that an O(1) get instead of O(n). Not measured here — registrations
is a query API, not a per-read path — but it is a second, larger beneficiary and it
strengthens the case for treating this as a spec change rather than dropping it.

RECOMMENDATION: this needs a Mike ruling on whether ~98 B/call on the resolution
chokepoint plus an O(n)->O(1) registrations query justifies reshaping a documented
public generation key. If yes, it is a hot-zone, sequenced, single-worker job
spanning spec/API.md + spec/Conventions.md + image_assembly + registrar + xray +
the pair skill + story + the test corpus. If no, close it: the docstring is now
honest and the cost is documented at the site that pays it.

title: subs/live-frame: frame-resolution-target mints a throwaway frame VALUE on every subscribe, probe and dispatch - 200 B/call
description:
MEASURED (rf2-j8ls2, PR #7154, JVM, -Dre-frame.debug=false, n=300,
ThreadMXBean/getThreadAllocatedBytes, 9 rounds, controls +0.000% in all
of them, arm N-RESTGT): 200.0 B/call, EXACTLY, in every round, and flat
across n = 30 / 300 / 3000.

WHAT IT IS. `live-frame/frame-resolution-target` on a KEYWORD target
calls `live-frame`, which mints a frame VALUE via
`frame/make-frame-value {:id id :runnable-id id}` -- an argument map,
then a `cond->`-assembled two-then-three-entry map. Its SOLE consumer,
`call-with-frame-resolution`, immediately calls `frame-generation` on
it, which normalizes it BACK to the keyword it was built from and reads
the record's `:generation` slot.

EVERY call site in the repo is the same shape:

    (call-with-frame-resolution (frame-resolution-target X) thunk)

subs.cljc x2, substrate/observation.cljc x2, router.cljc x1, core.cljc
x2. There is no other consumer, and the value is discarded within one
function call of being built. It is 11% of `subscribe`'s per-call
allocation and 18% of `probe`'s pre-node lookups (rf2-ncjyt).

SKETCH. `frame-resolution-target`'s keyword branch can return the
KEYWORD rather than a minted value:

    (keyword? target) (when (some? (frame/frame-generation target)) target)

`call-with-frame-resolution` reads `frame-resolution-generation` off it,
and `frame-generation` is identity-on-keywords through
`frame-value->id`, so the resolved generation is the SAME value by the
same path. The frame-OBJECT branch and the nil (absence-is-default)
branch are untouched.

WORTH CHECKING FIRST: whether the seam earns its existence at all. Given
every caller pairs the two functions and the consumer only ever reads a
generation, `frame-resolution-target` may be provably a no-op --
`call-with-frame-resolution` could take the raw target. That is the
cleaner end state but it retires a documented EP-0023 seam and touches
seven call sites plus ep0023_conformance_cljs_test / 
frame_resolution_cljs_test, which call `call-with-frame-resolution`
directly with values, keywords and nil.

FENCE: implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc. May touch
spec/006 or the EP-0023 text -- HOT-ZONE, sequence, do not parallel.

MEASURE WITH THE COMMITTED INSTRUMENT:
implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution.clj,
RM_SUITE=subs, arms N-RESTGT / S2-RESTGT / RGSUB.

JVM ONLY. The byte figure does not transfer to CLJS; the shape (a map
built and discarded per call) is a source fact and does.
close_reason:
PR #7157. ARTEFACT, confirmed and removed — the seam retired outright rather than made cheaper.

WHAT READ THE VALUE: nothing. All seven call sites are the identical shape
(call-with-frame-resolution (frame-resolution-target X) thunk), and the minted
value is discarded within one function call. The composition is provably an
identity for every X — frame VALUE (verbatim on both paths), frame id
(frame-value->id is identity on a keyword), nil, and any other value (frame/frame
is a total (get @frames id) that emits nothing for an unknown address). cwfr's own
docstring already documented accepting a value or an id, and
frame_resolution_cljs_test / ep0023_conformance_cljs_test already called it
directly with values, keywords and nil. No spec, no EP, no doc and no test
referenced frame-resolution-target.

MEASURED (JVM, -Dre-frame.debug=false, ThreadMXBean, n=300, 5 rounds = 3 forward +
2 RM_ORDER=rev, controls +0.000% in all 10): PAIRED CONTROL in read_attribution.clj
— N-CWFRWRAP (retired composition) 920.0-976.0 minus N-CWFRRAW (shipped) 720.0-776.0
= 200.0 B/call in EVERY round, both orders. Predicted by the independently measured
N-RESTGT = 200.0. Error 0.0%.

subscribe as a whole: 1612.0 [1460.0-1668.0] -> 1308.0 [1220.0-1364.0] B/call,
ranges DISJOINT (combined with rf2-a8bw0). JVM only; the shape transfers, the bytes
do not. Clarity: a net GAIN — one function deleted, seven call sites shorter.

Gates: core JVM 2152/10616 green; npm run test:cljs 11799/58740 green.

title: freehand: two costed ViewCell memory levers (193 B + 231 B) — ship, or let the row stand
description:
FOLLOW-UP from rf2-oob3g, which ACCEPTED the memory row. The byte accounting is in ai/findings/2026-07-27.viewcell-byte-accounting-oob3g.md. These two levers are measured, inside cell.cljc's fence, and deliberately NOT taken there, because the bead said the remedy is a separate decision and Mike's — and because together they move 5.86x to 4.85x against Reagent, which decides nothing under rf2-lbs3y.

LEVER 1 — the state map's key count. 193 B/boundary [189-204], 7.9%. ViewCell's state map has ELEVEN keys, so CLJS builds it as a PersistentHashMap (map object + 2 BitmapIndexedNodes + 2 arrays + 2 bitmaps boxed as heap numbers + the transient edit token fromArrays leaves behind). Collapsing the five keys a commit publishes together - :frame :deps :dep-order :evidence and the bundle's :generation - into ONE :bundle value takes it to EIGHT, which is a PersistentArrayMap: one object, one array, one backing store. Measured directly as its own arm, ranges disjoint.

  FOR: commit!'s docstring already says 'ONE publication ... dependencies, frame and evidence become live in a single write' and the code spells that as a five-key assoc; the change makes the code say what the docstring says. It also de-duplicates :frame, which the cell holds twice today (top level, and again inside :evidence).
  AGAINST: the published shape of cell/evidence and cell/dependencies changes, and both are tool/test reads.

LEVER 2 — the observations vector's transient. 231 B/boundary [226-235] on a boundary that reads nothing, 172 B [168-178] on one that reads four things, so it is the editable root and not the emptiness. commit-readings answers (persistent! obs) over a (transient []); persistent! RETAINS the editable root the transient cloned (a VectorNode over a 32-slot array) where conj onto a tail-only vector shares PersistentVector.EMPTY's root and allocates none. Five heap nodes per boundary. This is the single largest recoverable item in the ViewCell.

  AGAINST, and it is why this is a ruling and not a fix: it is a TRADE, not a free win. A transient is the right tool for a large accumulator and the wrong one for a small long-lived value - a boundary with one or two observations pays MORE for the transient than plain conj would cost it, one with hundreds pays less. Swapping it buys retention with render-leg throughput, which is the OTHER axis Freehand is losing (bulk re-render ~7-8x Reagent) and the leg PR #7147 tuned.

NOT A LEVER, recorded so it is not re-proposed: flattening the ViewCell into mutable deftype fields. That is worth ~200 B more and costs the atomic publication ('nothing can observe a partial bundle' - obs/read re-enters application code inside the commit and mark-dirty! arrives from the port's fan-out), the JVM's thread-safety story on :revision/:dirty/:listeners, and the 'everything here is common' property. Spec 006 promises, hot-zone, operator's call.

WHAT NEITHER LEVER FIXES: a Freehand boundary carrying the shell's six React hooks over a two-field JS object - no ViewCell at all - already retains 1,171 B above the React floor against Reagent's 418. useSyncExternalStore alone is 516 B. That half lives in shell.cljs, not cell.cljc.
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-27, dossier review): SHIP BOTH LEVERS, together, as one small ViewCell cleanup in cell.cljc — SEQUENCED so exactly one worker is on cell.cljc at a time relative to rf2-lbs3y (P0): fold this into the first cell.cljc change the lbs3y broad-update profiling mandates, or dispatch it immediately after any in-flight lbs3y profiling/tuning work on that file lands. NEVER concurrent with it. rf2-lbs3y remains the load-bearing investigation; this cleanup must not delay or contend with it.

REASONING (the dossier's two recommendations disagreed — primary: let the row stand, lever 1 opportunistically later, drop lever 2; Codex: ship both now — deciding for Codex on the merits):
(1) Lever 1 is elegance-positive by BOTH analyses; only timing differed. It is the better MODEL, not merely a smaller map: Spec 006 ("The selected render bundle") names the selected render as one bundle with all-or-nothing publication, and commit!'s docstring already says "ONE publication ... dependencies, frame and evidence become live in a single write" — the change makes the state say what spec and docstring say, and de-duplicates :frame (held twice today: top level, and again inside :evidence). "Park it as a rider on a future PR" creates an untracked dependency on an unknown vehicle; a delegated ruling should ship or drop.
(2) Lever 2's sole objection — that it spends render-leg throughput on the axis Freehand is failing worst — is REFUTED for the workload the library encourages. The shipping broad-update witness is 300 fine-grained boundaries with ONE v/sub each (b6_witnesses.cljc, b6_rows.cljs); the 300-read single boundary is explicitly an attribution ablation, "not a shape anybody should write" (b6_witnesses_flat.cljc). A directional Node microcheck against the pinned CLJS 1.12.145 runtime, arm order reversed, put the transient/persistent throughput crossover between two and four items: persistent construction was faster at zero, one, and two observations; transients won as vectors widened. So on the real broad row (one observation per cell), dropping the transient is neutral-to-faster, not a cost; only the anti-pattern-wide boundary may get slower, an acceptable and legible trade for the default representation. The microcheck is directional, not a production benchmark — hence the acceptance re-measure below.
(3) Posture: both levers SIMPLIFY the ordinary representation (fewer keys, plain conj is less machinery than transient/persistent!) while returning a measured ~424 B per mounted boundary — 17.3% of the ViewCell, not noise. That is elegance, not gold-plating; the gold-plating variants are exactly the ones banned below. The ratio motion (retained heap vs Reagent 5.86x -> 4.85x) decides nothing under rf2-lbs3y and is NOT the motivation; representation simplification with measured return is.

IMPLEMENTATION SPEC (the dossier ai/decisions/rf2-9f1s7.viewcell-memory-levers.md is deleted; this note is the complete record).

LEVER 1 — collapse the state map from 11 keys to 8. 193 B/boundary [189-204], 7.9% of ViewCell, measured as its own arm with disjoint ranges. At eleven keys CLJS builds the cell's state map as a PersistentHashMap (map object + 2 BitmapIndexedNodes + 2 arrays + 2 bitmaps boxed as heap numbers + the transient edit token fromArrays leaves behind); at eight it is a PersistentArrayMap (one object, one array). EXACT SHAPE: replace top-level :frame, :deps, :dep-order, :evidence with ONE :bundle key retaining the committed bundle as source of truth; committed-frame, dependencies, dependency-queries, and evidence remain the projection doors reading through it. KEEP TOP-LEVEL :generation — verbatim from the Codex analysis: "One detail matters: keep the top-level `:generation`. It is the cell's *current body authority* and can advance on hot reload before another render commits (`advance-generation!`, `cell.cljc:728-742`). The bundle's `:generation` is the generation of the *last selected commit*. They can intentionally differ. The eight-key shape is therefore obtained by replacing top-level `:frame`, `:deps`, `:dep-order`, and `:evidence` with `:bundle`, not by moving the authority generation into it. That leaves one honest state transition and one honest set of projections without weakening the atom, rollback, or acquire-before-release laws." (Arithmetic cross-check: 11 - 4 + 1 = 8; folding the authority :generation in too would give seven keys — the measured eight-key PersistentArrayMap arm corresponds to keeping it top-level, with the commit's own generation carried inside the bundle value.) The cell namespace is explicitly not application API, so the many tool/test reads through cell/evidence and cell/dependencies demonstrate encapsulation rather than create a compatibility burden — any readers whose read shapes change move in the SAME PR (coordinated, not large).

LEVER 2 — drop the observations vector's transient. 231 B/boundary [226-235] on a boundary that reads nothing; 172 B [168-178] on one that reads four things (so it is the editable root, not the emptiness); five heap nodes per boundary; the single largest recoverable item in the ViewCell. MECHANISM: commit-readings currently answers (persistent! obs) over (transient []); persistent! retains the editable root the transient cloned (a VectorNode over a 32-slot array), where plain conj onto a small vector shares PersistentVector.EMPTY's root and allocates none (tail-only growth below 32 items). CHANGE: start obs at [], use conj, return it directly. Pinned source anchors (ClojureScript r1.12.145 cljs/core.cljs): tv-editable-root, tv-editable-tail, TransientVector.-persistent!, PersistentVector.-conj. Measured directional crossover: between 2 and 4 items; persistent wins below.

DO NOT: no adaptive threshold, no hybrid accumulator, no JS-array special case, no mutable deftype fields. The mutable-deftype flattening stays REJECTED (recorded so nobody re-proposes it): worth ~200 B more but costs atomic publication ("nothing can observe a partial bundle" — obs/read re-enters application code inside the commit, and mark-dirty! arrives from the port's fan-out), the JVM thread-safety story on :revision/:dirty/:listeners, and Spec 006 promises.

WHAT NEITHER LEVER TOUCHES: the shell's six React hooks retain 1,171 B/boundary above the React floor (useSyncExternalStore alone 516 B) — that lives in shell.cljs, not cell.cljc, and the rf2-so3io ablation has settled that the uSES contract STAYS (dropping it returns ~375 B but loses invariant 5's stale-render protection, measured to be permanent on first render).

ACCEPTANCE: the implementation PR re-runs the retained-heap probe and the production B6 broad row. Expected: the measured memory reduction (~424 B/boundary) with no common-case clock regression. If the B6 broad row regresses beyond noise, that falsifies the microcheck's directional claim — revert the lever-2 half; lever 1 stands on its own merits.

EVIDENCE: ai/findings/2026-07-27.viewcell-byte-accounting-oob3g.md (rf2-oob3g byte accounting; both levers measured as their own arms, ranges disjoint).
close_reason: Both levers shipped in PR #7220. Measured on headless Chromium 147 / :advanced / goog.DEBUG false, attributed with a three-build ladder: lever 1 = 198 B (reader A) / 195 B (reader C), lever 2 = 233 B / 230 B on the sub-free boundary — both inside the bead's 193 B and 231 B ranges, ranges disjoint, every untouched control arm flat to the byte. Together 431 B; 5.93x -> 4.88x Reagent. On a boundary that reads one sub, 171 B + 171 B = 342 B (lever 2's smaller return there matches the bead's own 172 B [168-178] four-observation probe). B6 broad row shows NO regression: the apparent 20% rise was machine drift, proved by re-running the PRE-LEVER build LAST and reading 33.08 — identical to the levered build measured immediately before it — with the untouched Reagent control drifting the same +36%. Invariant 5 and the commit-side re-read untouched. Prod-gate lane 137 of 137, empty roster.

title: re-frame: a one-cell write allocates 457 KB re-evaluating 300 subscriptions that did not change
description:
FOUND by B8 (rf2-lcsjg, allocation under update). Not a Freehand finding — a re-frame one.

Changing ONE cell of B6's 300-cell grid allocates 478,787 bytes on the Freehand arm. Of that, 457,181 B — 95.5% — is the WRITE LEG: frame/replace-app-db! and the subscription graph re-evaluating all 300 :b6/cell subscriptions to discover that 299 of them are unchanged. The view substrate's whole share is 21,376 B, within 11% of Reagent's 19,307.

For contrast the same narrow write on a bare reagent.core/atom with r/cursor costs 4,018 B in its write leg. That is not a fair comparison (a cursor is not a subscription graph) but it is the order of magnitude a fine-grained store can achieve.

The measurement is collection-free-window allocation counting, ranges disjoint, 0 unverified of 2,400 writes, and the instrument carries a kept-vs-dropped self-test at 1.0001. See docs/design/freehand/studio/freehand-vs-reagent-allocation.md.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND A BENCH ROW: this is paid on every interaction in every re-frame application, and it scales with the number of registered subscriptions rather than with what changed. It is the largest single allocation term in a narrow write by a factor of twenty.

NOT filed as a defect and no remedy is proposed. Whether the signal graph can skip subscriptions whose inputs are structurally unchanged is a re-frame design question with correctness implications (equality semantics, sub-of-sub layers), and it belongs to whoever owns that graph. Filed so the number is on record.
close_reason:
PR #7156 merged. VERDICT: BOTH INTRINSIC AND ARTEFACT, split along a line the bead did not anticipate.

INTRINSIC — the CARDINALITY. Re-evaluating 300 subs to discover 299 unchanged is CORRECT, proven from the REGISTRATION CONTRACT rather than a benchmark: a layer-1 reg-sub body is (fn [db query-v] ...), an opaque function of the whole app-db; none of reg-sub's four shapes declares a path; the metadata map carries :doc/:schema/:sensitive/:large and nothing path-shaped; and the only graph edge (sub -> app-db projection) carries no path either. NO UNUSED INFORMATION EXISTS. commit-frame-transition! does compute a changed-set, but of PARTITIONS, and it is already fully exploited. Giving the graph path knowledge means a new declaration or read-tracking — a redesign, not a fix. This PR does not touch it.

ARTEFACT — 71% of the PER-EVALUATION cost, and it is fixed. Two private representation choices in re-frame.substrate.spine, neither observable, neither touching when a sub is considered current: :queue/:queued were a persistent vector and set used as single-threaded scratch inside one closure (the same file gives exactly that reasoning ONE LINE ABOVE for depth/flushing?), now a JS array and js/Set; and the >=2-subscriber fan-out walked (vals ws) where the 1-subscriber branch beside it already used reduce-kv.

MEASURED: frame/replace-app-db! on 300 subs 854,788 -> 286,714 B, 2.98x, DISJOINT. Per-sub slope 2,830.7 -> 940.8, and the superlinearity vanished (936.6/947.2/940.8 flat), independently corroborating that the removed term was the HAMT.
CREDIBILITY: the saving was a FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION, not a before/after story — both spellings kept live as paired controls in one process, predicted 1,884 B/sub, measured 1,889.9, 0.3% error.

SCOPE CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISE: 'every re-frame application pays it' is true of the SHAPE, not the BYTES. make-scheduler is reached only via make-react-spine, serving UIx, Freehand and re-frame.ui. REAGENT AND REAGENT-SLIM GO THROUGH make-ratom-spine AND PAY NONE OF THE 60% TERM.
SCALE CAVEAT: figures are Node V8 (pointer compression OFF) against the browser's ON — the same write reads 854,788 Node vs 457,181 browser, 1.87x. Shares transfer, absolutes do not.

FOLLOW-ONS FILED, none actioned: rf2-gncxk (the layer-1 memo guard is provably guaranteed to miss on the flush path but cannot be removed without a contract change), rf2-88pie (tenth instrument fault: a large-object arm inflates its successor 2x, caught only by running both arm orders), rf2-ssn1o (a Reagent write-leg arm), rf2-3zenp (the published 457,181 B is now stale), rf2-78ejq (RFWRITE-0 is 4,470 B at ZERO subscriptions, undecomposed), rf2-zxv06 (production handler-scope 121 B/sub cannot be dev-gated — the always-on SSR error path reads the scope).

title: bench: a Reagent-on-re-frame arm, so the broad view-leg gap stops being an upper bound
description:
B8 (rf2-lcsjg, allocation under update) measures Freehand's broad view leg at 13.5x Reagent's, ranges disjoint. That figure CANNOT be quoted as a substrate result and the report says so.

The two arms do not carry the same framework: Freehand's grid reads 300 v/sub subscriptions through re-frame's subscription graph, the Reagent grid 300 r/cursor derefs on a bare reagent.core/atom. rf2-40kdm (PR #7151) measured the read path directly and found an idiomatic Reagent body reading @(subscribe q) pays 95.3-97.4% of what Freehand's port pays per read — nearly all per-read render allocation is SHARED reactive-system cost. Freehand's arm pays it 300 times a broad write; the Reagent arm pays none of it.

So 13.5x is an upper bound containing an unknown but large amount of re-frame, and the substrate difference could be far smaller.

THE FIX is a third update arm: Reagent views mounted on re-frame subscriptions (reg-sub + @(subscribe [:b6/cell i])), same 300-cell grid, same canonical DOM. Then broad view-leg allocation splits three ways — Freehand, Reagent-on-re-frame, Reagent-on-ratom — and the substrate term is the first minus the second rather than the first minus the third.

The narrow row is much less exposed (one read per write, so the shared term is small in absolute bytes) and already reads 1.107x, which is the closest thing to a like-for-like substrate comparison available today.

Same arm would sharpen the CLOCK rows too — freehand-vs-reagent.md 2a bounds this asymmetry by argument rather than by measurement.

Freehand reading a re-frame SUBSCRIPTION against Reagent reading a bare
`reagent.core/atom` through an `r/cursor`. Both are their substrate's own
idiom, and the report says so -- but it means the headline ratio is a
comparison of two REACTIVE SYSTEMS, not two view substrates, and no row
anywhere isolates the view substrate with the reactive system held fixed.

title: RULING: published freehand-vs-reagent scopes its shared-re-frame caveat to the write leg; the render leg is 95%+ shared too
description:
NEEDS A RULING FROM MIKE -- this is a change to a PUBLISHED comparison
that carries a P0 product standard (rf2-lbs3y: "Freehand can't be used if
it is slower than Reagent"). Filed, not dispatched.

WHAT rf2-mvqwe FOUND. The per-dependency read cost that rf2-21pck
attributed to Freehand's observation port (3733 B/read, 81.5% of the
render leg's allocation) is 95.3% - 97.4% paid by a SUBSTRATE-FREE reader:
a plain `@(rf/subscribe [:q])`, no view layer involved, measured in the
same process against the same sub-cache and the same live nodes, nine
rounds, controls exact. Freehand's own increment is 100 - 172 B/read,
2.6% - 4.7%.

WHAT THE PUBLISHED REPORT SAYS TODAY.
`docs/design/freehand/studio/freehand-vs-reagent.md` is honest about the
fairness question and already carries the caveat twice -- section 2a
splits the measured window so a reader can see the `write` leg
(`replace-app-db!` + the subscription recompute) that "a Reagent
application reading re-frame subscriptions would pay too", and the
limitations list notes that the Reagent arm reads a bare
`reagent.core/atom`. That caveat correctly discounts the NARROW-update
15x to roughly parity.

WHY IT IS NOW TOO NARROW. The caveat is scoped to the `write` leg. But
the RENDER leg contains a re-frame cost too -- one per dependency read --
and that cost is 95%+ shared. The broad row's `force` leg (4.7 ms FH vs
0.6 ms Reagent) is presented as "squarely Freehand's own", and on the
ALLOCATION axis a large part of it is not.

The arms differ in REACTIVE SYSTEM, not only in view substrate, on the
row that carries the headline ratio: `b6_reagent.cljs` u-cell derefs a
`reagent.core/cursor` over `(defonce cells (r/atom []))`; `b6_witnesses.
cljc` u-cell reads `(v/sub [:b6/cell i])`. That sentence exists in the
limitations list; it belongs beside the number.

PROPOSED, in priority order:

1. Move "the Reagent arm reads an r/atom cursor, the Freehand arm reads a
   re-frame subscription" out of the limitations list and into the
   broad-update row itself.
2. Retire "the render leg is squarely Freehand's own" as an UNQUALIFIED
   claim. Defensible for the CLOCK; not defensible for allocation / GC
   pressure.
3. DO NOT restate any ratio. rf2-mvqwe measured allocation on the JVM and
   measured NO browser clock. The ~7-8x broad-update force-leg gap is
   untouched by it, and revising a clock number on the strength of an
   allocation result would be exactly the error this note exists to
   prevent.

EVIDENCE: ai/findings/2026-07-27.port-attribution-mvqwe.md (local-only).
Instrument: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution.clj.

HOT-ZONE-ADJACENT: docs/design/freehand/studio/ is a published surface
under D021's evidence policy. One writer at a time.
notes:
MAYOR RULING (2026-07-27): ADOPT ALL THREE RECOMMENDATIONS. This is a factual correction to a report that now contains a claim measurement has disproved — it is not a product decision, so I am ruling rather than holding it for the operator.

  (1) MOVE the caveat 'the Reagent arm reads an r/atom cursor while the Freehand arm reads a re-frame subscription' OUT of the limitations list and INTO the broad-update row itself. A limitation nobody reads while looking at the number is not a caveat, it is a footnote to a misreading.
  (2) RETIRE 'the render leg is squarely Freehand's own' as an UNQUALIFIED claim. It is defensible for the CLOCK and false for ALLOCATION: PR #7151 measured an idiomatic Reagent view body reading @(subscribe q) at 95.3-97.4% of Freehand's per-read allocation in every one of nine rounds, paired difference 100-172 B/read, never negative. Freehand's own share is under 5%.
  (3) DO NOT RESTATE ANY RATIO. #7151 measured ALLOCATION on the JVM. There is no browser clock and no CLJS figure behind it. Restating a published ratio on that basis would repeat, in the opposite direction, exactly the error being corrected.

ALSO RECORD, so the correction is not over-read: retained heap is UNAFFECTED and still loses badly (Freehand 2,430 B/boundary vs Reagent 410, UIx 251, widest on the witness that reads NOTHING — that is the ViewCell wrapper, not the read path). The broad-update clock gap (~9.7x, architectural) and mount (~2x) are unchanged.

AND THE DEEPER PROBLEM THE CORRECTION EXPOSES, which is rf2-m7xs7's subject: our Reagent arm reads a bare r/atom and NEVER CALLS subscribe, so it has not been paying what a real re-frame + Reagent application pays — including the ~1.8 KB per subscribe call on a cache HIT that rf2-j8ls2 records. Until a B6 arm exists that holds the reactive system fixed, EVERY cross-substrate row in that report compares a substrate difference CONFOUNDED with a reactive-system difference. The prose should say so.

  RGREAD  post-fix, ONE round  3408 B/read          = 89.7% of PORT

title: observation: probe's pre-node lookups are ~1120 B/read - call-with-frame-resolution + registrar/lookup, not the cache
description:
MEASURED (rf2-mvqwe, JVM, -Dre-frame.debug=false, 300 live nodes,
ThreadMXBean/getThreadAllocatedBytes, 3 rounds with the split arms,
controls exact to +0.000%). `probe`'s LIVE branch, re-walked through
public functions only, each arm a strict prefix of the next:

  PRELUDE   resolve-target + frame lookup + call-with-frame-resolution
            + registrar/lookup + the cache get       1400 - 1464 B/read
  node deref (PRENODE - PRELUDE)                     1816 B/read
  PORT - PRENODE  validate-target! + advance-node-record! + evidence
                                                      504 B/read
  ------------------------------------------------- ------------------
  PORT (the whole call)                              3720 - 3784 B/read

The re-walk is faithful: `PRENODE - PRELUDE` lands on the independently
measured bare-deref arm TO THE BYTE in all three rounds, and the three
parts sum to PORT exactly.

Inside PRELUDE, `resolve-target` alone is 280 - 344 B/read and the bare
cache `get` is 0 B/read (measured, all nine rounds). So ~1120 B/read --
roughly 30% of the whole port call -- is `live-frame/call-with-frame-
resolution` plus `registrar/lookup`, per dependency read, on the render
path.

THE TAIL IS ALSO SUSPICIOUS at 504 B/read for `validate-target!` + one
WeakHashMap record advance + a 6-key evidence map.

CONTEXT AND HONEST RANKING. rf2-mvqwe established that 95.3% - 97.4% of
this call's allocation is ALSO paid by a substrate-free `@(subscribe q)`,
so this is not a Freehand lever and halving it does not move the
Freehand-vs-Reagent comparison. It IS the biggest single allocation term
on the shared re-frame read path, and `call-with-frame-resolution` is on
the `subscribe` path too (see rf2-j8ls2), so a fix here likely pays twice.

FIRST STEP IS MEASUREMENT. The instrument is committed:
`implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution.clj`, arms
PRELUDE / PRENODE / PORT. Split PRELUDE further -- is it the dynamic
binding `call-with-frame-resolution` establishes, or the registry lookup?

JVM ONLY SO FAR. `getThreadAllocatedBytes` is a JVM instrument and the
numbers do not transfer to CLJS; the SHAPE (an allocation per read) does.
A CLJS counterpart figure does not exist and is worth having before any
change is designed.

HOT-ZONE: lands in implementation/core, may touch
spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md. Sequence, do not parallel. Sequence AFTER
rf2-j8ls2 if both are dispatched -- they overlap on
call-with-frame-resolution.
notes:
=== ANSWERED 2026-07-27 05:02 AUSEST (PR #7154, worker/subscribe-alloc-j8ls2) ===

suite), JVM, -Dre-frame.debug=false, n=300, ThreadMXBean/
getThreadAllocatedBytes, 9 rounds (6 forward + 3 reversed), controls
+0.000% in all of them, NOOP exactly 0 B.

The bead's ~1120 B/read for call-with-frame-resolution + registrar/lookup
decomposes as:

  the JVM dynamic `binding` of registrar/*generation*   ~760 B  68%
  frame-resolution-target's throwaway frame VALUE        200 B  18%
  registrar/lookup, generation-routed                    ~98 B   9%
  (first query-v) seqs the vector                         40 B   4%
  the late-bind flush consult + generation read            0 B   0%

Sums to ~1098 against the ~1120 attributed.

THE BEAD ASKED: "is it the dynamic binding call-with-frame-resolution
establishes, or the registry lookup?" ANSWER: THE BINDING, by 8x.

THE TAIL (validate-target! + advance-node-record! + evidence, 504

title: subs: subscribe costs ~1.8 KB per call on a cache HIT - the ref-count attach, on every Reagent render
description:
MEASURED (rf2-mvqwe, JVM, -Dre-frame.debug=false, 300 live cache entries,
ThreadMXBean/getThreadAllocatedBytes, 9 rounds, controls exact to +0.000%):

  subscribe q, cache HIT, no deref     1676 - 1868 B PER CALL

That is `re-frame.subs/subscribe` on an existing entry: frame resolution,
`call-with-frame-resolution`, `cache-key`, and the ref-count attach --
`(swap-vals! cache (fn [m] (update-in m [k :ref-count] (fnil inc 0))))`.
The bare cache READ the observation port performs over the same 300-entry
map measured 0 bytes, exactly, in all nine rounds. So the map lookup is
free and the ~1.8 KB is the HAMT path copy the ref-count bump forces,
plus the frame-resolution scope.

WHY IT MATTERS. `@(rf/subscribe [:q])` in a render body is THE idiom --
every re-frame Reagent application on earth re-subscribes on every render
of every component. At 300 reads that is ~0.5 MB of garbage per render,
and it is the single largest substrate-side allocation term measured
anywhere on this surface -- larger than Freehand's entire per-read port
call minus the shared signal graph (1968 B). Nobody has been looking at
it because every previous measurement compared Freehand against a Reagent
arm that reads a bare `reagent.core/atom` and therefore never calls
`subscribe` at all.

FIRST STEP IS MEASUREMENT, NOT A CHANGE. The instrument exists and is
committed: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution.clj`,
arm `RGSUB`. Point it at the ref-count bump the way rf2-21pck decomposed
the ledger: is the cost the `swap-vals!` pair, the `update-in` path copy,
the `fnil`, or `call-with-frame-resolution`? Sweep n (the entry count) --
if the per-call cost scales with cache SIZE rather than staying constant,
that is a different and worse bug than a constant overhead.

Only then consider representations. Do NOT start by proposing a mutable
ref-count: rf2-21pck already measured that Clojure transients beat
host-mutable collections on this exact shape and that S2/S3 were rejected
on CLARITY, and a ref-count is a lifecycle invariant, not a scratch
ledger.

HOT-ZONE: any change lands in implementation/core and may touch
spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md. Sequence, do not parallel.
notes:
=== ANSWERED + FIXED 2026-07-27 05:02 AUSEST (PR #7154, worker/subscribe-alloc-j8ls2) ===

THE BEAD'S HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED. The ~1.8 KB is NOT "the HAMT path copy
the ref-count bump forces". The path copy is 356 B -- 19% of it.

METHOD: the committed instrument, read_attribution.clj, extended with a
`subs` suite (RM_SUITE=subs). JVM, -Dre-frame.debug=false, n=300 live
cache entries, ThreadMXBean/getThreadAllocatedBytes, 9 rounds pre-fix +
9 post-fix (6 forward + 3 with arm order REVERSED in each set), controls
= two long-arrays a decade apart, +0.000% predicted-vs-measured in ALL
EIGHTEEN ROUNDS, NOOP exactly 0 B. Plus an n-sweep at 30 / 300 / 3000.

THE DECOMPOSITION (each arm a strict prefix of the next; every step
cross-checks against an independently measured standalone arm):

  require-current-frame! + its eager error payload    136 B   7%
  + frame-target->id + frame-resolution-target        200 B  11%
  + call-with-frame-resolution                    720-800 B  41%
  + (frame/frame id) + (get @cache k)                 0-8 B   0%
  + the REF-COUNT ATTACH                          732-772 B  41%
  = subscribe, cache hit, no deref               1796-1892 B

  the attach, standalone (764 B):
    swap-vals! machinery ([old new] vector + CAS)       64 B
    + the identity guard (closure + one get)            88 B total
    + update-in                                        652 B
      - irreducible persistent write                   428 B
        (outer HAMT path copy 356 + entry-map copy 72)
      - update-in's own wrapper                        224 B

INTRINSIC OR ARTEFACT:
  ~428 B (23%) INTRINSIC. A persistent one-key ref-count change must
  copy the path to the entry and the entry map. With the CAS pair and
  the identity guard (88 B) required by the CAS-after-snapshot
  discipline, ~516 B is the price of a correct lock-free persistent
  ref-count. A mutable ref-count is not an optimisation of this -- it is
  a different lifecycle model. NOT PROPOSED.
  ~760 B (41%) is the JVM's dynamic `binding` of registrar/*generation*
  and DOES NOT EXIST IN CLJS: CLJS `binding` expands via `with-redefs`
  to let + set! + try/finally restore (confirmed in cljs/core.cljc,
  clojurescript 1.12.145). Zero allocation there.
  ~560 B (30%) ARTEFACT: update-in's wrapper 224, the throwaway frame
  value 200, the eager error payload 136. None touches lifetime.

SCALING (the bead asked): per-call cost DOES track cache size, but
LOGARITHMICALLY, exactly as a HAMT must -- the path copy reads 283.7 /
356.0 / 467.9 B at n = 30 / 300 / 3000, one more node clone per trie
level. Every other term is FLAT in n. This is not the "different and
worse bug" the bead flagged as possible.

THE FIX THAT LANDED: `(update-in m [k :ref-count] (fnil inc 0))` written
out, reusing the `get` the identity guard already performed. The three
byte-identical copies of the swap fn (subscribe's hit path,
compute-and-cache!'s lost-race adoption, the observation port's
acquire!) collapse onto ONE named `subs/bump-ref-count-fn` stating the
CAS-after-snapshot discipline once.

  subscribe, cache hit  BEFORE  1796 - 1892 B/call
  subscribe, cache hit  AFTER   1612 - 1668 B/call

Ranges DO NOT OVERLAP. The isolated paired difference (RC-ATTACH minus
RC-CAND, both expressions live in one process on the same map) is 224 B
in all six forward rounds and 248 B in all three reversed rounds --
never negative. Every OTHER arm is byte-identical pre and post, which is
the internal control that only `subscribe` moved.

NO SEMANTIC CHANGE. Same guard, same result, same pure-swap-fn contract.
`(:ref-count slot)` wrapped in `or` so an explicit nil behaves exactly as
`fnil` did. Lifetime, disposal and ref-count correctness untouched.

CLARITY: one line longer at the point of use, but it names the slot it
had already fetched instead of walking to it twice, and replaces three
copies of a subtle concurrency invariant with one documented function.
Not paid for in clarity.

INSTRUMENT FAULT CAUGHT (the tenth on this surface): the RC-ASSOC arm
first read 16 B because PersistentHashMap.assoc returns `this` when the
new value is `identical?` to the old -- assoc-ing an entry back over
itself measures the no-op path. Fixed to assoc a distinct pre-built
entry. Unnoticed, the "intrinsic" figure would have been understated 22x.

GATES: implementation/core JVM `clojure -M:test` exit 0 (2152 tests /
10616 assertions, 0 failures); `clojure -M:test:slow-test` (the ^:stress
concurrency lane -- this touches a CAS discipline) exit 0; 18
measurement rounds exit 0. `npm run test:cljs` DEFERRED TO CI (no
node_modules in the worktree; the change uses only get / assoc /
identical? / inc / or, no reader conditionals).

RAW: ai/findings/2026-07-27.subscribe-alloc-j8ls2.md (local-only).

FOLLOW-ONS FILED: rf2-x0fe2 (P1 -- no CLJS figure exists and the largest
JVM term is JVM-only, so three beads are ranked off a profile that is
wrong for the target runtime), rf2-8gb3t (the throwaway frame value, 200
B/call, every subscribe AND probe AND dispatch), rf2-k9iu4 (RULING: the
cache-HIT path pays a binding it never uses, but the wrapper also
carries the read-time reprojection flush), rf2-ezwnl (registrar's
generation-routed [kind id] key vector), rf2-a8bw0 (the eager error
payload). Number drift noted on rf2-9f2w4.

Scaling is logarithmic in cache size, as a HAMT must be. Fix: update-in written out, 1796-1892 -> 1612-1668 B/call, non-overlapping. Five follow-ons filed.

MEASURED 2026-07-27 on worker/prodgate-lanes-hnrwo, whole suite under the gate: 534 tests / 2503 assertions, 217 failures, 1 error, red in 21 of 48 test namespaces.

The 21, with red-assertion counts:

  ssr-end-to-end-test                        119

WHAT THE FAILURES ACTUALLY ARE. Sampled across all 21, they fall into three groups.

  (a) DEV INSTRUMENTATION asserted inline with semantics — the large majority. "exactly one `:rf.ssr/schema-digest-mismatch` trace", "`:doc` preserved on the reg-head slot", "a `:rf.ssr.head/cleanup-failed` warning surfaced", "`:rf.cofx/skipped-on-platform` fired once", the `:rf.ssr/suspense-boundary-failed` / `-duplicate-id` streaming traces, the hydration-mismatch trace's `:server-hash` / `:client-hash` tags. Under the gate the framework emits none of it, by design. Legitimate dev-posture tests.

  (b) SOURCE-COORD ANNOTATION — `ssr-source-coord-test`, `source-coord-parity-test`, `ssr-keyword-head-contract-test` assert `data-rf2-source-coord` / `data-rf-view` on rendered HTML. Those attributes are prod-elided at the core `reg-view` boundary, so their absence under the gate is the elision working. Same shape as core's `source-coord-prod-elision-test` cluster.

  (c) ERROR PROJECTION — and this one needs a RULING before it is written off. `ssr-end-to-end-test`, `ssr-flush-response-result-test`, `ssr-error-two-frame-attribution-test`, `ssr-error-view-failed-no-project-test`, `ssr-head-resolution-no-project-test` fail on assertions of the form "the buffered `:rf.error/no-such-handler` projects 404 onto `:status`". `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc` (the two `register-*-listener!` calls near the end) documents the asymmetry deliberately: the ALWAYS-ON `re-frame.error-emit` listener covers `:rf.error/handler-exception`, the `fx-handler-exception` family, `flow-eval-exception` and `sub-exception`; the categories that emit ONLY via `trace/emit-error!` — `:rf.error/no-such-handler`, `:rf.error/no-such-route`, `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure`, `:rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded` — "DCE under `interop/debug-enabled? = false`; the substrate-shipping projector relies on the dev gate for them". So this is a documented design choice, not an undiscovered bug. But its consequence on a production server is that an unroutable URL returns HTTP 200 with whatever the render produced, rather than 404. See the separate bead filed alongside this one for the ruling; the triage of this cluster should not proceed until it lands.

THE SHAPE THE FIX TAKES for groups (a) and (b) is the one rf2-d2841 used for core: keep the instrumentation assertions VERBATIM inside a `(when interop/debug-enabled? …)` arm marked with this bead id, leave everything outside such an arm posture-independent, document the split in the namespace docstring under "## Posture split", then delete the roster line in `scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh`.

DO NOT weaken, skip or delete a failing assertion to shorten the list, and do not guard a namespace whose EVERY deftest is about the dev trace — that would report GREEN for a namespace that executed nothing, the exact false-green the lane exists to close.

`ssr-end-to-end-test` at 119 is the big one and is mostly group (c); split it last.

title: Give the rf2-mszrz pipeline-exception attribution a production witness on the always-on :errors axis
notes:
Split out of rf2-d2841 under its rule 2 ("a suite whose invariant is
production-REAL but observed through a dev-only channel is NOT yours — file a
bead rather than forcing it"). Same shape as rf2-7vk3z.

THE CONTRACT. rf2-mszrz fixed a collapse: before it, a throw from ANY pipeline
component (coeffect supplier, user interceptor, handler-wrapping interceptor)
surfaced as one `:rf.error/handler-exception` attributed to the EVENT. Post-fix
each kind gets its own category with `:failing-id` = the true failing
component, plus `:phase` (:before / :after) for the interceptor case.

WHY IT IS PRODUCTION-REAL. `error_emit.cljc` §`emit-error-both!` lifts
`:failing-id` and `:reason` out of `trace-tags` onto the ALWAYS-ON record —
"but ONLY when the `:failing-id` is present AND DISTINCT from `:event-id`.
That is the case exactly for the categories whose failing component is not the
dispatched event: a user interceptor (`:rf.error/interceptor-exception`) or a
coeffect supplier (`:rf.error/coeffect-exception`) ... The off-box shipper now
learns WHICH interceptor / cofx failed in production."

WHY IT HAS NO TEST. `re-frame.interceptor-test`'s
`pipeline-exception-attributed-to-true-component` captures EXCLUSIVELY through
`(rf/register-listener! :trace …)` (its `capture-error-traces` helper). That is
dev-only, so under `-Dre-frame.debug=false` the helper returns `[]` and every
attribution assertion reads nil. rf2-d2841 put those assertions in a
`(when interop/debug-enabled? …)` arm — correct, but it means the production
lifting above is asserted NOWHERE, in either posture.

THE WORK. A posture-independent pin — modelled on
`implementation/core/test/re_frame/privacy_production_egress_test.clj` and the
rf2-7vk3z twins in PR #7138 — that registers `(rf/register-listener! :errors …)`
and asserts the always-on RECORD carries `:failing-id` = the interceptor id
(and the cofx id for the coeffect case) when it differs from `:event-id`, plus
the negative control that handler-exception stamps nothing extra because its
failing id already EQUALS `:event-id`. It must run in BOTH postures, so it
joins `scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh` automatically (exclusion roster).

Do NOT weaken or move the dev-posture assertions in `interceptor-test`; this is
an additional twin, exactly as rf2-7vk3z was.
close_reason: Closed

title: Production-gate lanes for routing and ssr — the two non-core classification egresses run under no gate
description:
FOUND BY rf2-u2x6w while writing the production-posture witnesses for the two sub-classification egress sites outside implementation/core.

WHAT LANDED. re-frame.routing-sub-egress-production-test (7 tests / 16 assertions) and re-frame.ssr-routing-egress-production-test (4 tests / 15 assertions) are green in BOTH postures and mutation-proved under -Dre-frame.debug=false. They are the payload a lane would carry. NOTHING RUNS THEM UNDER THE GATE: jvm-core-prod-gate covers implementation/core only.

THE SCOPING ANSWER, with the numbers behind it. Each artefact needs its OWN lane row; scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh must NOT be extended to reach them.

  - Neither artefact is green under the gate as a whole. Measured 2026-07-27 on this branch:
      routing  522 tests / 2843 assertions - 293 failures, 9 errors, red in 19 of 44 test files
      ssr      532 tests / 2554 assertions - 217 failures, 1 error,  red in 21 test files
    (core, for scale: 91 of 174 namespaces red; its lane runs the surviving 83.)
    So each artefact needs its own known-red roster and its own triage stream, exactly as core did.

  - The core script's roster is core-specific and load-bearing: every entry names the bead that clears it, and verify_roster hard-errors on an entry that no longer names a real namespace. Three artefacts' triage debt in one exclusion list means a rename in one artefact fails a list another artefact owns.

  - The flag must live in the LANE's definition, not on a command line (the :prod-gate alias's :jvm-opts, so :extra-paths / :extra-deps cannot drift between lanes). Aliases are per-artefact deps.edn, so the lane definition is inherently per-artefact.

  - The :test alias's own shape differs per artefact (routing excludes :slow / :stress; ssr does not), and a single lane cannot compose them.

  - The polarity that makes the core lane work - an EXCLUSION list, so a new namespace joins by default - only holds when the roster and the namespace set live in the same artefact. An allowlist reaching across artefacts has the opposite failure mode.

WHAT THIS BEAD WANTS.
  1. A :prod-gate alias in implementation/routing/deps.edn and implementation/ssr/deps.edn, modelled on implementation/core/deps.edn (jvm-opts [-Dre-frame.debug=false], composed onto :test).
  2. scripts/test-routing-prod-gate.sh and scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh on the test-core-prod-gate.sh pattern: exclusion roster, --plan flag, verify_roster, a lane pin test asserting the property reached the JVM.
  3. WORKFLOW CHANGE (operator-sequenced, deliberately not done in the rf2-u2x6w PR): two jobs in .github/workflows/test.yml, both in all-required-passed's needs:.

The triage of ~510 red assertions across the two artefacts is the bulk of the work and should be split per artefact, and probably per cluster within each, the way rf2-r9bra split core's.
close_reason:
PR #7145. Two per-artefact production-gate lanes on the core lane's exclusion-roster pattern; test-core-prod-gate.sh NOT extended, per the bead's scoping answer.

GREEN TODAY: routing 18 of 37 namespaces / 98 tests / 613 assertions; ssr 28 of 49 / 247 tests / 1379 assertions. Both exit 0.

KNOWN-RED ROSTERED, nothing weakened or deleted: routing 19 namespaces (293 failures / 9 errors whole-suite), ssr 21 (217 failures / 1 error). Each entry grouped by cause with its red-assertion count; triage split to rf2-o5dbf (routing) and rf2-lwtlk (ssr).

PROOF EACH LANE RUNS UNDER THE FLAG: re-frame.{routing,ssr}-prod-gate-lane-pin-test, two unconditional deftests each (property reached the JVM / framework honoured it — different defects). Teeth proven by inverting: clojure -J-Dre-frame.debug=true reds 2/2 in both artefacts, exit 1. Corroborated by the dev lanes still reporting their exact pre-change counts (routing 522, ssr 532) against the gate lanes' 524/534 — the three-way :test/:slow-test/:prod-gate partition holding. verify_roster teeth proven too: a bogus known_red entry exits 1.

ALWAYS-ON WITNESSES KEPT IN: routing-sub-egress-production-test and ssr-routing-egress-production-test are both in the runnable sets (verified via --plan). Excluding routing-egress-test is survivable only because rf2-u2x6w already moved its always-on legs out — the conformance-test trap.

WORKFLOW: jvm-routing-prod-gate + jvm-ssr-prod-gate, both in all-required-passed's needs:. check_jvm_lane_rosters.py baseline still EMPTY (the jobs declare no working-directory and invoke a script, exactly as jvm-core-prod-gate does). report-changed-surfaces.sh extended so widening a known_red list cannot fire zero jobs. TESTING.md updated per-artefact.

OPERATOR-GRADE FINDING, filed not fixed: under the gate an unroutable SSR URL returns HTTP 200, not 404 — no-such-handler / no-such-route / schema-validation-failure / drain-depth-exceeded project only through the DEV trace listener. Documented in ssr.cljc as deliberate, so not an undiscovered bug, but its production consequence had never been executed. rf2-rqje9 (P1) holds the ruling and gates that triage cluster.

title: bench: re-take the broad-update row after PR #7133 lands — it adds a React commit per render batch
description:
PR #7139 profiled the broad-update row on main WITHOUT PR #7133.

#7133 adds a SECOND window closer: a detached React root whose layout effect calls cell/flush!, costing one extra React commit per render batch. Outside flushSync it lands after the measured window, but it is real wall clock.

The broad-update row is exactly where it would show. PR #7139 measured React's commit-phase layout-effect loop at 30.48% of the window — 1.23 ms of 4.05 ms per write — so the commit phase is already the single largest React-side term. An extra commit pass over the tree per batch is a change to the term that is already dominant.

Re-take with:

    node implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b6_profile_run.cjs --arm freehand-interpreted --writes 500

three rounds, plus the published b6_prod_run.cjs row, and compare against PR #7139's ranges: total [3.9-4.5] ms, force leg [3.0-3.5] ms, commit-phase share 30.48%.

Also re-check rf2-w2m25's regression test — if #7133 gives Freehand a synchronous commit, the update row should be re-taken WITHOUT the microtask yield, which would tighten every figure.
acceptance_criteria: Broad-update ranges re-measured on main with #7133 merged, compared against PR #7139's ranges, and the delta recorded in docs/design/freehand/studio/bulk-rerender-where-the-time-goes.md.
close_reason:
Re-taken on main at 7c41225b4b, which carries #7133, rf2-wxrrp (e5cf299fc2) and #7147.

THE FINDING IS STRUCTURAL, NOT THE TOTALS. The window restructured: the empty react-dom/flushSync that carried 3.0-3.5 ms now costs ~0.0, and the microtask gap that was ~0.2 ms now carries 3.6-3.9. Freehand's render moved OUT of the measured flushSync and into the microtask before it. A reader taking force-ms as Freehand's React time now reads 0.0 and would conclude the substrate became free; b6-rows' commentary still describes the gap as a near-empty constant priced by the floor and Reagent arms, and for Freehand that is no longer true.

Totals: 4.0 [3.9-4.5] -> 4.8 [4.6-4.9] ms, disjoint, +20%. Commit phase SHARE fell 30.48% -> 26.77% while its MILLISECONDS rose 1.23 -> 1.38 — the share fell only because the window grew. #7133's extra commit pass costs ~0.15 ms, not the +0.8 the total moved.

Published interleaved row essentially unchanged in ratio: 10.5x -> 9.9x Freehand over Reagent (p50 6.9-9.0 vs 0.7-0.9 ms), 0 unverified writes. The page's conclusion stands. :ratio-to-floor deliberately not quoted — the broad floor p50 is 0.2-0.3 ms, two or three of Chrome's 100 us quanta, and it reads 33.44 [25.67-45.00] for a quantity the direct p50s put at ~30.

Second question — re-take WITHOUT the microtask yield — answered NO, not for free: the 3.6-3.9 ms now in the gap IS the work. Removing the yield either moves it into the flushSync or lands the commit after the measured window and fails the DOM read-back. Filed as rf2-vxfjt (P3), gated on rf2-0fgth's non-vacuity check.

Recorded in bulk-rerender-where-the-time-goes.md §6. PR #7152.

title: freehand: the dependency ledger is persistent maps rebuilt per render — measure a mutable store
description:
Profiled on rf2-dq20a's follow-on (PR #7139).

cljs.core/array-index-of is 10.65% SELF of a whole broad-update capture — the largest named frame in the profile — spread across a dozen callers with NONE above 2.76%. That flat spread is the signature of small PersistentArrayMaps and PersistentHashSets being linearly scanned everywhere, not of one bad call site. The same signature appears in both React phases: get, assoc, hash, inode-lookup, inode-assoc, -as-transient, into, reduce-kv dominate the self time and no Freehand function exceeds 1.6%.

The observation ledger (staged records, :dep-order, the bundle's :observations vector, the cell state map) is persistent structure REBUILT PER RENDER PER BOUNDARY. PR #7077 already demonstrated the shape of the win on the neighbouring surface: moving the memo stores from persistent-maps-in-atoms to js/Map took conversion/remembered from 3.04% to 0.75%.

NOT a bounded optimisation — it is a representation change to cell.cljc with a reader conditional (CLJS js/Map, JVM persistent), the same split PR #7077 confined to the "remembered" projection and its constructor.

Rank it BELOW rf2-wxrrp: the fast path avoids the work entirely, this only makes it cheaper.
acceptance_criteria: A measurement of what fraction of array-index-of and the persistent-collection self time is the dependency ledger specifically, and a decision on the representation. Before/after broad-update ranges if implemented.
notes:
EVIDENCE FROM rf2-wxrrp (PR #7143, 2026-07-27). This bead is WARRANTED, and its cheapest first move is on the RENDER leg, not the commit leg.

CONCRETE, BOUNDED, NO INVARIANT ATTACHED. cell/record-read! rebuilds the candidate's {:order ... :by-site ...} wrapper TWICE per reactive read:

  (vswap! reads (fn [r] (-> r (update :order conj site-key)
                              (assoc-in [:by-site site-key] {...}))))

'update :order conj' allocates one new wrapper map, 'assoc-in' allocates another, and neither is read by anything. 300 reads therefore allocate 600 throwaway 2-key maps per render per boundary, on a leg PR #7139 profiled at 0.77 ms of a 4.05 ms broad-update window. Two ways out, both small: split the reads volatile into two fields on RenderCandidate (.-order and .-by-site), so a read is one vector conj plus one map assoc and zero wrapper allocations — observe! then reads (count @(.-order cand)) instead of (count (:order @(.-reads cand))); or collapse the wrapper rebuild to a single map literal. The first is strictly better and is the natural precursor to the js/Map representation change this bead names.

MEASURED CONTEXT. rf2-wxrrp took the analogous bookkeeping out of the COMMIT leg — three walks plus a re-lookup per dependency folded into one pass, plus a transient staging map — and got commit! from 371.5-411.7 us to 287.5-333.7 us for 300 retained dependencies (JVM, production-gated, 16 interleaved rounds each, disjoint). That is ~25% off a term worth 29% of the broad-update window, and B6's browser row COULD NOT RESOLVE IT (freehand/reagent BEFORE [9.20-11.17] vs AFTER [8.29-11.17], 12 rounds each, overlapping). Two implications for this bead:

1. Persistent-collection churn in cell.cljc is real and reducible — the JVM microbench sees it cleanly.
2. B6's broad-update row is NOT a usable acceptance instrument for a change of this size. Its floor p50 is 0.2-0.3 ms, two or three of Chrome's 100 us performance.now quanta, so :ratio-to-floor moves in +-33% steps; normalise against Reagent in the same round instead, and expect +-10-15% round noise even then. Budget for a direct instrument (rf2-wxrrp's is at ai/findings/2026-07-27.commit-fastpath-wxrrp-raw.md, local-only) and REMEMBER that interop/debug-enabled? defaults to TRUE on the JVM — an ungated run times the dev evidence plane, which was ~70% of the reading and does not exist in the artefact B6 measures.

title: Sub-classification egresses in production from routing and ssr, with no production-posture test
description:
FOUND BY rf2-7vk3z (PR #7138) while building production-visible witnesses for the two gate-red suites that prove production-real invariants.

THE GAP. Inside implementation/core, the PROJECTION half of sub classification has no production egress at all: project-sub-tags is reached only from trace/build-event inside emit!'s debug gate, so under -Dre-frame.debug=false no :rf.sub/run event is built. That is fine and expected.

BUT sub classification DOES egress in production from two places OUTSIDE core, and NEITHER has a production-posture test:
  - routing's :routing/route-sub-egress-path
  - ssr's payload-policy/project-routing-egress

WHY IT MATTERS. 'No cross-frame classification bleed' is a PRIVACY invariant. rf2-7vk3z established a production-visible witness for it inside core (via @(rf/subscribe ...) plus the resolved metadata read through the same registrar/lookup + call-with-frame-resolution path re-frame.subs uses). These two egress sites are the remaining paths where classification actually leaves the box in a production build, and they are unwitnessed.

This is the same shape as rf2-9c2jf and rf2-bza6e: a surface everyone assumes is covered, sitting beside a hundred that are provably dev-only. The gate lane (jvm-core-prod-gate, scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh) covers implementation/core ONLY, so neither site is even in the lane's reach today.

WHAT THIS BEAD WANTS. A production-posture test for each egress site, asserting classification is honoured under -Dre-frame.debug=false. Consider whether the gate lane should extend beyond implementation/core to reach them, or whether each artefact needs its own lane row — that is a scoping question worth answering explicitly rather than by default.

DO NOT add production instrumentation to manufacture an observable. The rf2-7vk3z worker explicitly declined to do that and it was the right call; if an egress site has no production-visible witness, that is the finding.

Filed by the mayor; the discovering worker was fenced out of routing/ and ssr/.
