title: Continuation canary: the inventory generalises the DRIVE set but not the CANARY set (no identity-bearing scope on any mutation drive)
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-l6wjl, which the rf2-22ij6 canary did NOT catch unaided.

WHAT IS GENERAL AND WHAT IS NOT. `declared-continuation-settle-ids` reads the family's source and computes the settle paths itself, so the DRIVE SET cannot fall behind the family — a new settle branch reds the namespace the moment its source is written. `assert-branch-sweep!` is likewise general on the harvest side: a whole-record canary sweep plus a non-vacuity fixture, so whatever slot a continuation gains on an inventoried branch, the sweep sees it.

The CANARY SET is not. A sweep can only find a canary the drive PLANTED, and each drive's planted values are a hand-list — exactly the shape rf2-uufoe retired on the drive side (`the drive is always the gap, never the harvest`).

THE CONCRETE MISS. `drive-mutation-reply-to!` passes no `:scope` at all in its `[:rf.mutation/execute …]` payload, and every scope in the fixture is `:rf.scope/global` — a SCALAR with nothing in it to leak. So `:correlation :scope` never carried the canary on any mutation branch and the ninth leak was invisible to a namespace built to see it. Adding `:scope [:rf.scope/session {:username secret}]` to that one drive reds four deftests:
  RED   79 tests / 591 assertions / 4 failures / 0 errors
  GREEN 79 tests / 591 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors
(measured locally against PR #7134's file, both states, leak paths
`[:trace-events N :tags :rf.fx/args 1 :correlation :scope 1 :username]` and
`[:trace-events N+1 :tags :rf.event/fx 0 1 1 :correlation :scope 1 :username]`.)

THE ASK, minimally. Every inventoried drive should plant the family's identity-bearing values, not just the ones its author was thinking about — at minimum a `[tier {identity}]` resolved scope on EVERY drive (the mutation drives have none today), since `:rf.scope/global` is the one scope shape that cannot leak and it is the one every fixture uses. Whether that generalises further (a per-drive roster of `the runtime facts a reply carries`, derived rather than listed) is the ruling.

SEQUENCING. The drive lives in `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj`, which PR #7134 owns and which is UNMERGED. This bead dispatches only AFTER #7134 merges, and rebases on it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Mutation continuation reply leaks :correlation :scope off-box while its own top-level :scope tokenizes
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-22ij6 generic continuation canary, while choosing a canary for the mutation SUCCESS settle. Not fixed there: that bead was fenced to test fixtures, and this is a production egress-projector change.

MEASURED on JVM (implementation/epoch, epoch_egress_resource_trace_test drive shape). Drive a real [:rf.mutation/execute … :scope [:rf.scope/session {:username SECRET}] :reply-to …] against a mutation that declares nothing, settle it, and project the record off-box (epoch/projected-record). Two of the three spellings of the SAME scope are cleaned and one is not:

  :rf.reply/work-id  (embeds the scoped key)   REDACTED
  top-level :scope   on the reply map          REDACTED
  :correlation :scope                          RIDES RAW

  leaking at [:trace-events N :tags :rf.fx/args 1 :correlation :scope 1 :username]
  and again at [:trace-events N+1 :tags :rf.event/fx 0 1 1 :correlation :scope 1 :username]

Holds on BOTH mutation settle branches (:rf.mutation.internal/succeeded and /failed).

WHY IT LOOKS LIKE A BUG RATHER THAN A POLICY. A resource continuation reply carries the same :correlation :scope and IS cleaned — the passing real-reply-to-read-leaks-no-decoded-body-into-fx-carriers drive puts a secret-bearing {:from-db} scope through exactly that slot and sweeps to zero. So the two carriers of one scope disagree ACROSS FAMILIES, which is the same principle rf2-425mm invoked to make the free :scope arm unconditional in the first place ('the two carriers of one scope must agree'), and rf2-1zc33 established that a free :scope tag classifies unconditionally — it belongs to no owner whose declaration could exempt it. The mutation family's source-side redact-continuation-reply is not the answer either: it re-roots only the owner's DECLARED :sensitive / :large subpaths, and a caller-supplied scope is not a declaration.

NOT the same as the mutation :value question, which IS by design: an undeclared mutation's decoded result rides verbatim because reg-mutation has no coarse :sensitive? root prop and the app's own continuation handler is entitled to it (spec 016 / the §rf2-xx4ty note in the epoch test). :scope is not owner data — it is an identity the framework resolved.

EVIDENCE / REPRO: add ':scope [:rf.scope/session {:username secret}]' to the [:rf.mutation/execute …] payload in drive-mutation-reply-to! (implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj) and run the namespace — real-failing-mutation-reply-to-leaks-no-error-envelope reds with the two paths above. The shipped drive deliberately omits the scope so the suite is green; this bead owns adding it back once the projector cleans the slot.

LIKELY SITE: re-frame.resources.trace-egress — the predicate/arm that descends a continuation reply's :correlation. rf2-rnsv2 widened a sibling predicate by one keyword for :error; this looks like the same shape of miss on :correlation for the :mutation work-kind.

FAMILY: rf2-wd9im, rf2-5o52l, rf2-1kiuj, rf2-1zc33, rf2-425mm, rf2-xx4ty, rf2-rnsv2, rf2-uufoe. Eight leaks found by workers and none by a gate; PR #7122 plus rf2-22ij6 changed that for every branch, and this is the first one the generalised inventory surfaced.
notes:
MAYOR RATIFICATION of a judgement call made while deriving the canary set (rf2-k8vyi, PR #7141): a mutation's :params riding RAW for an UNDECLARED owner is BY DESIGN, not a tenth leak. The worker declared :sensitive [[:params :slug]] on the fixtures rather than filing a bug, and asked me to sanity-check it. I agree, and the reason is consistency with a call already made:

rf2-pwxsk was closed as an ACCEPTED BOUNDARY on exactly this principle — an UNREGISTERED owner has no :sensitive?/:sensitive declaration to honour in the first place, so the redaction obligation that makes the other nine leaks real does not attach. reg-mutation has no coarse :sensitive? root, and the resource side is symmetric (:plain/article is driven with a plain slug for the same reason). Treating the mutation case differently would make the two carriers disagree, which is the rf2-irwsq mirror this family has repeatedly ruled against.

So: not a leak. If a future reader disagrees, the worker noted it is a one-line fixture change away from being a bug report instead.
close_reason:
FIXED — PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7137 (worker resources-ninth-leak, 2026-07-27).

THE ARM, which was the live question. A SEPARATE arm of `project-embedded-keys`'s `entry` cond, gated on `family-reply?` — the canonical `:rf.reply/work-kind` marker ENUMERATED over `#{:resource :mutation}`, never `(some? work-kind)` (managed HTTP stamps `:http` on the same shared substrate and an HTTP reply's correlation is the HTTP family's to classify). Inside a proven family reply, `:correlation` is the map `reply/base-reply` BUILT — a construction proof of the same kind position 1 of a `[:rf.work/resource …]` work-id carries, and strictly stronger than a registry lookup, since it still holds for a mutation whose registration was hot-reloaded away. Only `:scope` takes the family rule (`project-unknown-slot-value`); every sibling fact takes the ordinary walk NAMED iff the family reserved its key, which keeps a read correlation's `:rf.reply/resource-key` projecting exactly as before.

`reply-payload-slot` was NOT used, and the new `reply-correlation-slot` docstring records why the way `reply-error-slot` records its own: that set is consumed under `(and owner-redacts? …)`, so adding `:correlation` to it is a one-token edit that LOOKS like the proven rf2-xx4ty pattern and in fact implements the owner-conditional remedy rf2-1zc33 / rf2-425mm rejected — the two carriers would disagree again for any `:serialize` owner — and it would tokenize the whole correlation map, destroying the `:generation` / `:mutation/id` / `:instance/id` identities every tool joins on.

ROOT CAUSE, and a docstring corrected. `carrier-family-payload?` claimed all THREE `:scope`-bearing payloads satisfied it. There are FOUR. A read completion's correlation wears `:rf.reply/resource-key` (a `family-named-key?`) and proved itself; a mutation completion's wears `{:mutation/id :instance/id}` and nothing reserved — the work-id sits at the reply ROOT, not in the correlation map — so it proved nothing. Same family, same substrate, same datum, two rules.

PROOF — `implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_reply_correlation_egress_cljs_test.cljc`, a real `[:rf.mutation/execute … :scope [:rf.scope/session {:username SECRET}] :reply-to …]` on BOTH settle branches, projected through the same `project-fx-args-egress` hook the epoch tool-pair calls:
  RED   7 tests / 33 assertions / 8 failures / 0 errors
  GREEN 7 tests / 33 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors
Identical test and assertion counts. RED leak paths are this bead's verbatim.

THREE CONTROLS, all passing on RED as well as GREEN: a `:rf.scope/global` mutation reply projects BYTE-IDENTICAL; `:generation` / `:mutation/id` / `:instance/id` / `:cause` ride verbatim; a FOREIGN `:rf.reply/work-kind :http` reply carrying its own `:correlation {:scope …}` rides byte-identical and does not stamp the row. AGREEMENT asserted directly: top-level `:scope` = `:correlation :scope` on one projected reply, and the mutation half's projection is byte-identical to the read half's.

THE CANARY DID NOT CATCH IT UNAIDED — see rf2-k8vyi. PR #7134's inventory reds 4/79 the moment `drive-mutation-reply-to!` plants an identity-bearing scope (79 tests / 591 assertions, 4F -> 0F across the fix), but it plants none today: every scope in that fixture is `:rf.scope/global`, a scalar with nothing in it to leak. The inventory generalises the DRIVE set, not the CANARY set.

REGRESSION: resources 741 tests / 6853 assertions / 0F 0E; epoch 537 / 7005 / 0F 0E. All EXIT=0.

title: [spec] Spec 006 — the ViewCell pending window now has a React-visible second closer
description:
PR #7133 (rf2-w2m25) gave the Freehand ViewCell pending window a SECOND closer, so a write made inside `react-dom/flushSync` repaints before the flush returns.

Spec 006 §Render-batch finalization — the host-checkpoint boundary currently enumerates the window's closers as exactly two: 'the next CLJS host microtask checkpoint, or an explicit headless/test flush', and states 'On CLJS the flush rides a true host microtask — js/queueMicrotask'. There is now a third: a React-scheduled sentinel render whose LAYOUT effect closes the window (`re-frame.freehand.checkpoint`), armed by the same first mark, running the same idempotent `cell/flush!`.

Nothing normative was BROKEN by the change — the four guarantees still hold, and the reasoning is worth stating because it is not obvious:

  1. A run-to-completion drain still cannot be split across batches: both closers are armed by the mark and NEITHER can run while the marking stack is unwinding. flushSync runs its callback to completion first, and only then flushes.
  2. N epochs in one drain still coalesce into one batch, for the same reason.
  3. 'Several drains ... MAY share one batch' is permissive, so an earlier close is allowed.
  4. Drains separated by a real host yield still render separately.

What needs saying is only WHICH checkpoint may close a window a SYNCHRONOUS commit is waiting on, plus the consumer-facing fact the bead asked for: a write inside `react-dom/flushSync` is committed to the DOM before the flush returns, so a caller who needs to measure layout / move focus / set a caret / assert on the DOM has a door that works.

spec/** is hot-zone, which is why PR #7133 touches none of it. Sequence this against whatever else holds spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md.

Surfaces: spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md §Render-batch finalization; §The six frozen invariants invariant 6 (the sentence 'the boundary is the host checkpoint').
close_reason: PR #7136 — spec/006 §Render-batch finalization now enumerates three closers and gains '#### The second closer — a synchronous host commit must be able to close the window': why the microtask is NOT abolished (the invariant-6 trap), the two closers and their lane arbitration, two normative ordering rules (guaranteed closer armed first; host closer best-effort inside a guard; no render scheduler = no second closer), the four guarantees walked one at a time (3 is permissive, so an earlier close spends latitude it already grants), and the consumer-facing fact. Invariant 6's own render-batch definition updated. Read from the OPEN branch worker/flushsync-w2m25 (#7133), not main — PR body states the merge-after-#7133 sequencing.

title: [bug] Two gate-red suites prove PRODUCTION-real invariants through a dev-only observable
notes:
Split from rf2-r9bra triage (2026-07-27). Constrains the rewrite work in rf2-d2841.

All eleven namespaces rf2-r9bra triaged came back TEST SPELLING — but 'spelling'
must not be read as 'delete the assertion and move on'. Two of them use a
dev-only observable to prove an invariant that is REAL IN PRODUCTION, so the
straightforward rewrite (drop the trace assertion) silently retires live
coverage. Each needs a production-visible witness instead.

1. re-frame.frame-upsert-linearization-jvm-test
   Fails under the gate because retained-cap reads
   re-frame.trace.tooling/trace-rings, and the ring is dev-only. But the SUBJECT
   is frame-upsert LINEARIZATION under concurrent construction — which writer
   wins an exclusive-create race, whether a failed re-registration rolls back to
   the pre-attempt generation. That is a production concurrency invariant; the
   retention policy is merely the flag the test reads to see who won. Needs a
   non-trace witness (frame-state / generation identity), not deletion.

2. re-frame.subs-image-local-classification-cljs-test
   Fails on 'frame A's sub ran' — it asserts through :rf.sub/run trace evidence.
   The invariant it proves is 'no cross-frame classification bleed: two frames
   installing the SAME inline sub id with DIFFERENT sensitive classifications
   each redact per their OWN image-local declaration'. That is a PRIVACY
   invariant and it is therefore currently unproven in production, which is the
   multi-frame twin of the single-frame hole rf2-r6zby just closed. The witness
   should be the always-on egress record (see
   implementation/core/test/re_frame/privacy_production_egress_test.clj for the
   pattern), not the trace stream.

ALSO NOTED, much smaller: conformance fixture :dispatch/envelope is the ONE
non-trace mismatch in the whole 242-fixture corpus. Under the gate app-db
carries extra :rf.cofx {:rf/time-ms ...} + :rf.cofx/mint-policy :live keys the
fixture does not expect. Harness determinism (the deterministic mint policy is a
dev affordance), not a production defect — but its expectation is genuinely
posture-coupled and needs a decision when conformance-test is rewritten.

Everything else in the corpus is trace-derived end to end:
conformance_runner.cljc:614 effects-routed-from-traces derives fx routings FROM
THE TRACE STREAM (so 'actual effects routed: (empty)' means the harness could
not SEE them, not that routing stopped), and :1533 public-error-check filters

title: [bug] The two always-on schema-validation surfaces have no production-gate test
notes:
Split from rf2-r9bra triage (2026-07-27).

CONTEXT. Four of the eleven namespaces rf2-r9bra triaged (partitioned-commit-test,
elision-multi-owner-cljs-test, live-run-frame-resolution-cljs-test,
examples-test) fail under -Dre-frame.debug=false on assertions like 'the
schema-rejected transition never installed' — expected app-db {:n 0}, actual
{:n -5}. Under the gate the invalid candidate DOES commit, because validation
never runs. That is SPECIFIED, not a defect:

  spec/010-Schemas.md:202 — 'Validation is elided by default ... every
    validate-*! body is wrapped in (when re-frame.interop/debug-enabled? ...)'
  spec/010-Schemas.md:190 — flow-output: 'Like every other validation surface
    this is dev-only and elides in production.'
  spec/Security.md:264 — the gate strips 'schema-validation calls'.

So those four are dev-posture tests and belong to rf2-d2841.

THE GAP THIS BEAD IS FOR. Spec 010 carves out TWO validation surfaces that are

title: pair-mcp: run-wire-pipeline's canonical ex-message is dead prose — err->result drops it
description:
Found while landing rf2-eaf20's boundary proof.

`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/wire_pipeline.cljs`
(~line 270) carries this comment above its unknown-`:kind` throw:

  'Load-bearing here (rf2-jquiy) — server.cljs's invoke-and-guard relays
   (.-message err) into the :handler-threw envelope, so this text is what
   the agent on the other end of the MCP wire reads.'

That is false FOR THIS THROW SITE. pair-mcp has TWO consumer-facing error
relays, and they keep opposite halves of the exception:

  * server.cljs `invoke-and-guard` -> {:reason :handler-threw :message
    (.-message err)}. Keeps the MESSAGE, drops the ex-data.
  * tools/probe.cljs `err->result` (line ~751) -> (merge {:ok? false}
    (ex-data err)) when ex-data is present. Keeps the EX-DATA, drops the
    message ENTIRELY. The `:message` fallback arm is reached only when
    ex-data is nil.

All FIVE `run-wire-pipeline` call sites (snapshot.cljs:256,
get_path.cljs:204, read_sub.cljs:170, trace_window.cljs:140,
watch_epochs.cljs:143) sit inside an `eval-after-runtime!` /
`eval-after-runtime-signalled!` `on-value` callback, so every one of
them lands in `err->result`. The carefully composed human sentence plus
the trailing [:rf.error/pair-mcp-unknown-wire-pipeline-kind] token
therefore reaches NO consumer. The agent does get an actionable payload
(:rf.error/id + a :reason sentence + :kind ride through as ex-data), so
this is not a consumer-facing hole — it is dead prose plus a comment that
will mislead the next contributor into believing a message is load-bearing
when it is not.

Verified empirically: rf2-eaf20's error_boundary_test drives the real
tools/call path and the unknown-:kind row produces NO 'handler threw' log
line and a nil :message, while the rt-let row (which fires during
synchronous form construction, BEFORE the round-trip) does reach
invoke-and-guard and does carry its message.

Two candidate fixes, mayor to rule:
  (a) Make `err->result` carry BOTH — merge {:message (.-message err)}
      alongside ex-data. One-line change; makes every Spec 009 message on
      this surface genuinely consumer-facing and makes the comment true.
      Widest blast radius (every eval-path tool failure gains a :message
      slot on the wire).
  (b) Correct the comment at wire_pipeline.cljs to name err->result and
      the ex-data half, and stop implying the message is read.

rf2-eaf20's test carries a commented tripwire asserting the message is
nil at that relay; whichever fix lands, update that assertion and the
comment together. eval_form.cljs's equivalent comment is CORRECT and
needs no change.
close_reason: Fixed via option (A) in PR #7135. err->result now merges (ex-message err) alongside the ex-data, so a canonical Spec 009 message composed on a response-shaping path reaches the consumer's agent. Comments at BOTH relay sites now name the two-relay asymmetry. error_boundary_test's commented tripwire is activated and mutation-proved (2 mutations, each reds exactly the 2 new assertions out of 4299). Evidence for (A) over (B): result_envelope/envelope->result already ships :reason + :message + :ex-data together on the same eval-path surface, so relay 2 was the outlier; no ex-data payload in src carries a :message key; conformance fixtures assert :edn-submap so additive keys are safe; cap.cljs already caps error :message blobs. Relay 1's mirror-image defect (drops ex-data) filed as rf2-qoih4.

title: Generic continuation canary: drive every registered :reply-to-bearing settle path, not a hand-listed five
description:
PROPOSED BY the rf2-uufoe worker (PR #7122) as the honest next tier of assurance. Filed rather than built, because #7122 already closes the class it was scoped to close.

WHAT #7122 ESTABLISHED. The continuation-reply egress gate previously drove only the SUCCESS settle. It now carries a whole-record canary sweep across FIVE settle branches - failed-handler's error and abort arms, the legacy aborted-handler, page-failed-handler, and the mutation failure and cancel settles - each asserting that no secret string survives projection. That is a CLASS-level gate rather than an instance assertion, and the reverted-fix run proves it bites (exit 1, 14 failures across 8 deftests).

THE REMAINING BOUNDARY, in the worker's own words: 'the drive is always the gap, never the harvest.' fx-carrier-rows already harvests by slot, so the harvest side is general. The DRIVE side is a hand-listed five. A leak on a carrier no drive produces - a new fx surface, or a new family that plants payloads in foreign carriers - stays invisible.

WHAT THIS BEAD WANTS. A fixture that enumerates every registered :reply-to-bearing settle path a family DECLARES, and drives each one, instead of a hard-coded list that a future branch can silently fail to join. #7122 mitigates the gap with a standing rule stated in the conformance section header ('a new settle branch fanning out a continuation gets a canary drive in the PR that adds it'), but a rule is a convention and this would be a mechanism.

WHY IT IS P2 AND NOT P1. Eight leaks of this family were found by workers and none by a gate; #7122 changes that for every branch that exists today. This bead closes the door on branches that do not exist yet. Worth doing, not urgent.

DO NOT over-engineer this. If enumerating declared settle paths turns out to need a registry that does not exist, say so and close - the standing rule plus the five drives may be the right resting point. The test is whether a NEW settle branch added by an unrelated PR would be caught without anyone remembering the rule.

Evidence: PR #7122; rf2-uufoe and rf2-rnsv2 closed there. Family history: rf2-wd9im, rf2-5o52l, rf2-1kiuj, rf2-1zc33, rf2-425mm, rf2-xx4ty, rf2-rnsv2, plus the mutation :error leak closed in the same commit, and rf2-pwxsk closed as an accepted boundary.
close_reason:
BUILT, not declined — the registry the bead worried might not exist turned out to be the family's own source, read through its one delivery seam. PR #7134.

declared-continuation-settle-ids seeds on every defn calling re-frame.reply/complete, closes under 'is called by', and maps the call-graph roots onto the event ids re-frame.resources registers them under; that set is asserted EQUAL to the keys of continuation-settle-drives. Each entry makes one of two proved claims: :drives (real drive, asserted against the record's own :event-id, whole-record canary sweep) or :cannot-fan-out (a reachability over-approximation, asserted by driving it and finding no reply on any carrier).

ACCEPTANCE TEST MET, measured: adding a synthetic handler that reaches the seam and registering it reds the gate naming :rf.resource.internal/synthetic (exit 1) with nothing in the namespace told it exists. Flipping refetch-handler's :force-new? reds the :cannot-fan-out claim (exit 1), so that arm is not an escape hatch.

The enumeration found NINE settle paths where the hand list named five — page-succeeded, the mutation SUCCESS settle, the synchronous fresh-skip fan-out on :rf.resource/ensure (a settle path with no settle event), and the over-approximated :rf.resource/refetch.

Two findings recorded rather than fixed: rf2-l6wjl filed (a mutation reply's :correlation :scope rides raw off-box while its top-level :scope and work-id are cleaned, and a resource reply's is cleaned — production projector change, out of fence); and the trap that projection must be taken INSIDE the isolating fixture or it fails closed and greens over everything.

Gates: implementation/epoch 535 tests / 7055 assertions exit 0; implementation/resources 734 tests / 6820 assertions exit 0.

title: [bug] story-mcp tools_test record-as-variant-no-cofx-is-byte-identical flakes: recorder captures 0 events in aggregate runs
description:
Observed 2026-07-27 during rf2-jquiy work (PR for rf2-jquiy/rf2-2ii52).

`clojure -M:test` in tools/story-mcp failed once with:

    FAIL in (record-as-variant-no-cofx-is-byte-identical) (tools_test.clj:2149)
    expected: (pos? n)
      actual: (not (pos? 0))

i.e. `:recorded-event-count` came back 0 — `drive-events-during-recording`
dispatched two [:counter/inc] events and the recorder captured neither.

NOT deterministic and NOT caused by the PR's diff:
  * baseline at HEAD, full aggregate: GREEN (303 tests / 1590 assertions)
  * with the PR's new tests, run 1: this failure (306 / 1605)
  * with the PR's new tests, run 2: GREEN (306 / 1605)
  * tools-test ALONE: GREEN (243 / 1347)
  * tools-test + wire-encodability-test together: GREEN (257 / 1421)

So it is an order/timing-sensitive flake in the recorder capture path that
only shows in a full-namespace aggregate run, not a regression. The sibling
test immediately above it (record-as-variant-cofx-*) has a
`(finally (destroy-frame! :story.button/primary))` teardown; this one does
not, which is the first place to look — a frame left over from a prior test
may mean the recorder attaches to the wrong frame and observes nothing.

Worth fixing because a silent intermittent red on a recorder test trains
people to re-run rather than read.
notes: Merged-PR audit of #7129 (2026-07-28): the CountDownLatch handshake does not establish the claimed "worker is in its poll loop" condition. The worker calls .countDown at tools_test.clj:1831 before computing its deadline or polling recorder/recording?, so it can still be descheduled after releasing the caller and miss the caller's fixed 100 ms recording window. More seriously, the caller ignores the boolean returned by (.await polling 5 TimeUnit/SECONDS): after a timeout it returns the worker and opens the recording window anyway; because the worker's own 5 s deadline is created only when that delayed worker eventually runs, it can remain alive and capture a later test's window. Replace the timing assumption with a handoff that makes the event driver and recording window causally meet (for example run the blocking recorder invocation on the worker while the test thread waits for recording? and drives events), and pin the timeout/late-worker path so it cannot leak across tests.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7198. The audit was right: PR #7129's CountDownLatch established 'thread is live', not 'thread is polling' (.countDown was the worker's first act, before its deadline or first probe); the caller ignored .await's boolean; and the worker's 5s deadline was created only when it eventually ran, so a late worker could fire into a later test's window. Replaced the thread+latch+deadline+poll-loop with an add-watch on recorder/state: start-recording! is one (swap! state start ...), so the watch runs synchronously on the tool's own thread INSIDE that swap, with :recording? true and stop-recording! unreached. No interval, so nothing can be early or late; nothing left running when the fn returns. Watch retracts itself before pushing (record-event! swaps the same atom) and the fixture retracts it by fixed key if the window never opens. VERDICT: the product was never wrong and neither was the byte-equality expectation - the test HARNESS was, about scheduling. Capture is now exact, so the test asserts the 2 events it drove instead of (pos? n) and spells its written-back body literally. Gates: 306 tests/1605 assertions 0 failures, plus 3x concurrent core-saturating runs (the flake's own condition) all green.

title: late-bind directory still documents the reprojection hooks as dev-only after rf2-9c2jf un-gated them
notes:

PR #7114 (branch worker/dispatch-sync-9c2jf) un-gates the live-frame reprojection maintainer:

`ensure-reprojection-installed!` rooted from `make-frame`, and both flush consults plus the

`implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc` was NOT touched by that PR
(its diff is live_frame.cljc, registrar.cljc, router.cljc + two new test files), so two rows
still assert the retired rationale. Verified against the fix branch itself, not against main:

- `:live-frame/mark-projection-dirty!` (directory.cljc:1116 on the branch) —
  "Dev-only: published under `interop/debug-enabled?` alongside the auto-reprojection hook;
   production builds never consult it (the registrar stops mutating after boot)."
  Every clause is now false. "The registrar stops mutating after boot" is the exact reasoning
  rf2-9c2jf disproved.

- `:live-frame/flush-projection!` (directory.cljc:1120 on the branch) —
  "the publisher lives in the debug-gated auto-reprojection defonce, and under :advanced +
   goog.DEBUG=false the whole reprojection + image-assembly graph DCEs".
  First clause false. The SECOND clause is still true but for a different reason, and that
  reason is the point: the graph now DCEs by REACHABILITY (nothing but `make-frame` reaches
  the installer) rather than by a gate. The row should say so — that is the template a future
  author needs.

WHY IT MATTERS: the directory is the normative inventory of late-bind keys and is exactly
where someone goes to learn whether a hook is dev-only. Leaving the retired story there is how
this defect class gets re-seeded. `late_bind_drift_test` enforces key/publisher parity but not

title: spec/006: document that a derived container must be ACTIVATED, not merely watchable (the :adapter/activate-derived-value! hook)
description:
FOLLOW-ON to rf2-8cnxg / rf2-jt8vz. The fix adds an optional routed late-bind hook, :adapter/activate-derived-value!, published by the ratom family alone and called by re-frame.substrate.observation/build-node-handle! before it installs its per-handle watch. It rides the late-bind table exactly as :adapter/derived-container? does, so the ten-fn adapter contract SHAPE is unchanged — but spec/006 documents :adapter/derived-container? explicitly in the make-derived-value section, and the new sibling deserves the same treatment.

What the spec text should say:

- Sec make-derived-value already asserts push semantics ('the derived container updates automatically when any source's value changes'; 'subscribe-container works as on a base container'). Reagent and reagent-slim were NON-CONFORMANT with that clause on a surface only ViewCell substrates exercise: their Reaction captures its sources only through deref-capture, so a plain deref outside a reactive context leaves it watchable, watched, and silent. The spec should say plainly that reifying the host watch interface is NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT, and that a demand-driven substrate must publish the activation hook to be conformant.

- The port's obligation: activation happens at ACQUIRE, before the watch install, so it is per-observer and never makes an unobserved subscription eager. (An adapter that instead made make-derived-value eager — :auto-run true on Reagent — would satisfy the notification clause by recomputing every subscription synchronously inside the app-db reset!, discarding batching. The spec should foreclose that reading.)

NOT done in the fix PR because spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md is a hot-zone file and the worker was fenced out of it. Directory entry, adapter impls, port call site and cross-adapter tests all landed; this is the normative text alone.
close_reason: spec/006 §make-derived-value now states that reifying the host watch interface is necessary and not sufficient, that a demand-driven host must publish the optional :adapter/activate-derived-value! late-bind hook, and that activation happens at observation-port acquire (per-observer, never eager) — with the :auto-run true alternative explicitly rejected. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7121. Text verified against branch worker/freehand-ratom-lane (PR #7118), not main: the hook does not exist on main yet, so #7121 must merge AFTER #7118.

title: [chore] Spec 009 reprojection rows still say the sweep is dev-hot-reload-only (stale after rf2-9c2jf)
notes:
HOT-ZONE FILE — the rf2-9c2jf worker deliberately did NOT edit this and is reporting it instead. spec/009-Instrumentation.md is on the sequential hot-zone list, so the mayor should sequence this rather than let a worker race it.

WHAT IS STALE. Two rows in spec/009-Instrumentation.md's error catalogue (around lines 2114-2115) describe :rf.warning/reprojection-failed and :rf.warning/reprojection-flush-failed. They sit inside trace/emit-error!, which is itself gated on interop/debug-enabled?, so the diagnostics still DCE under :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false and still cost nothing in production. Only the 'the sweep itself never runs in production' claim and its justification are wrong.

SUGGESTED EDIT: keep the 'the emit is dev-only / DCEs in production' half of each row; replace the 'production never re-registers after boot, so there is nothing to reproject' clause with the rf2-9c2jf finding (the sweep is a correctness invariant that runs on both hosts under both gate values; only its diagnostic emit is gated).

title: [chore] Audit: which interop/debug-enabled? gates guard CORRECTNESS rather than diagnostics
notes:
Follow-on from rf2-9c2jf. The defect there was not a wrong gate CONDITION, it was a gate on the wrong KIND of thing: the reprojection wiring that keeps a frame's sealed image generation in step with the registration pool was gated on interop/debug-enabled?, while the producer of that sealed generation (make-frame assembling it) was unconditional. Under the production gate the generation froze and dispatch stopped resolving.

The generalisation: interop/debug-enabled? is for DIAGNOSTICS — trace emits, dev warnings, provenance capture, retained buffers. It must never gate a step some unconditional production code path DEPENDS ON. rf2-9c2jf found three such sites in one subsystem (the reprojection hook install, both read-time flush consults, the registrar's removal dirty-marks). There are ~990 debug-enabled? occurrences across 222 files; nobody has checked whether more of them are load-bearing.

WHAT TO DO: sweep the gate sites and classify each as diagnostic (fine) or load-bearing (a bug of the rf2-9c2jf class). The tell is a gate around something with an OBSERVABLE EFFECT on resolution, commit, scheduling, or lifecycle — as opposed to a gate around an emit / a warning / a metadata capture. Late-bind PUBLICATIONS are especially suspect: a set-fn! inside a debug gate silently removes a capability from production, and the consuming site usually reads as a harmless when-let.

Prioritised P2 rather than P1: rf2-9c2jf's own instance is fixed and its regression test is in; this is the systematic follow-up. Best done AFTER rf2-f8x2i gives us a lane that actually runs under the gate, since that lane would surface load-bearing gates empirically instead of by reading.
AUDIT PROGRESS — bead filed: rf2-h8l4x (late_bind/directory.cljc rows for :live-frame/mark-projection-dirty! and :live-frame/flush-projection! still document the retired dev-only rationale; verified stale ON the #7114 branch itself; sequence after #7114 merges). Findings doc: ai/findings/2026-07-27.debug-gated-correctness-audit.md (local-only, gitignored, never commit / never link from a committed doc).
VERDICT: ZERO new correctness-gating sites beyond the five PR #7114 already fixes.
Severity counts — BLOCKER: 0 new (5 pre-existing, all #7114's, all one subsystem).
HIGH/MED/LOW: 0. Suspicious-but-verified-benign: 5. Doc drift: 1 (rf2-h8l4x). Benign: ~240.

This is a VERIFIED nothing, not an assumed one. Criterion applied: a gate is a finding only
when some UNCONDITIONAL production path DEPENDS ON the gated step — the absence must make the
system produce a WRONG ANSWER, not merely LESS INFORMATION. Severity ranked on whether the
gated step maintains state that OUTLIVES the gate check (rf2-9c2jf was severe because the
sealed generation FROZE).

COVERAGE. 1127 raw textual occurrences repo-wide; 655 in **/src/**; of those, 273 are in a CODE
position (a paren-aware scanner excluded strings and ;; comments, so docstring mentions do not
count), behind 249 distinct gate forms. ALL 249 forms were read. Per artefact: core 117, ui 52,
freehand 20, http 19, xray 13, epoch 12, flows 10, machines 10, schemas 5, resources 4, ssr 4,
machines-viz 2, and one each in routing / ssr-ring / scripts / pair-mcp / story.

Three EXHAUSTIVE shape sweeps are what make the negative load-bearing:

1. LATE-BIND set-fn! INSIDE A GATE (the shape this bead named). 178 publications in src, 3
   lexical hits: live_frame.cljc:1319 and :1324 (both #7114's) plus one scanner false positive
   (story/sub_overrides.cljc:260 — the publication is a top-level #?(:cljs …), attributed by the
   column-0 heuristic to the preceding gated form; read directly, it is ungated). The 16
   publications nested inside a defn were each checked for a gated CALLER — none. CONSEQUENCE:
   every late-bind key except #7114's two is published unconditionally, so the entire family of
   "ungated consult of a gated publication" — a capability silently vanishing from production
   behind a harmless-looking when-let — is closed BY CONSTRUCTION, not by inspection.

2. GATED def/defonce (a gate here is permanent for the process). 8 in src. Two are the flag's
   own definitions; one is an unrelated data table. Of the five real ones, one is #7114's
   _auto-reprojection-hook; the other four (adapter/sub_override_context.cljs:55,
   ui/reactive.cljc:3291, ui/tool/evidence.cljc:693 and :704) each have every consumer gated.

3. GATED REGISTRATION / INSTALL. One hit — #7114's add-registration-hook!. No handler, listener,
   interceptor or watch anywhere in the tree registers behind a debug gate. Top-level gated
   side effects: 4 in the whole tree, all diagnostic (two React displayName stamps, two Xray
   installs).

COMPLETENESS CHECKS BEYOND THE LITERAL SPELLING:
- Gate ALIASES swept. re-frame.spec/dev-mode? is INVERTED (production does MORE — the
  :rf.schema/at-boundary interceptor). Direct js/goog.DEBUG: 7 sites, all reagent-slim console
  warnings plus one test-only flush helper. performance/enabled? is an orthogonal opt-in define.
- MACRO-EXPANSION-TIME reads: none. A defmacro reading interop/debug-enabled? UNQUOTED would
  bake the compiling JVM's flag into emitted CLJS — a silent severe variant. Every macro site
  (core_call_site_macros, core_reg_macros, core_reg_view_macro, source_coords, freehand,
  ui/compiler/emit_jvm) emits a QUOTED runtime (if re-frame.interop/debug-enabled? <dev> <prod>).
- STORE SYMMETRY: for every debug-gated store, writer and cleanup are gated TOGETHER (epoch/state,
  trace-rings, freehand/occurrences, views seen-render-keys, subs/cache). In registrar.cljc the
  ungated store mutations (swap! reg, source-store/record-descriptor!, forget-id!) correctly sit
  OUTSIDE the gate — only the emits and the now-unconditional dirty-marks were inside.

SUSPICIOUS-BUT-CLEARED (recorded in the findings doc so nobody re-derives them):
ui/reactive.cljc:3221/3228 (whole staleness test gated, asymmetric with :3606 — cleared:
:generation is written only by advance-generation!, HMR-only); ui/tool/evidence.cljc:704
(transition-lock nil in prod, (locking nil) would NPE — cleared: all six callers gate; latent
trap only for a FUTURE ungated caller); freehand.cljc:438 (gated registry/register! — cleared:
tool-only index, every lookup consumer gated); router.cljc:1999 and spec.cljc/dev-mode?
(inverted — production does more); ui/tree.cljc:608 (strips when gate TRUE — consistent, the
annotation is only attached under the same gate). Sixth family: dev-only VALIDATORS
(router validate-event!, schemas/validate, machines/data_validation) diverge behaviourally
between dev and prod, but that is the documented Spec 010 design and leaves no stale state —
less information, not a wrong answer. Not findings.

NO MECHANICAL GUARD PROPOSED. rf2-f8x2i (P1) already covers the real one: a CI lane running
under the ACTUAL production gate would have caught rf2-9c2jf empirically and would catch any
future member of this class the same way. A source lint for "gate around a mutation" would fire
on ~40 legitimate diagnostic sites and is not worth its false-positive rate.

NOT EXAMINED: test/fixture/script sources (130 code-position occurrences, 93 of them with-redefs
rebinds that #7114 already showed cannot observe a load-time gate); .md/spec prose accuracy
beyond the one directory drift filed and the already-filed rf2-cx3ze; RUNTIME verification —
this is a static read, nothing was executed under -Dre-frame.debug=false or :advanced +
goog.DEBUG=false, so the negative is a structural argument (three exhaustive sweeps + a full
read of 249 forms), with rf2-f8x2i as the empirical complement; non-gate production divergences
(other :closure-defines, performance/enabled?, elision-negative-control?); and whether #7114

title: Continuation-reply egress gate drives only the SUCCESS settle: four failure/cancel branches are structurally untested
description:
THE GAP. Every producer-driven assertion about a :reply-to continuation reply reaching off-box egress lives in implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj, and that file contains ZERO ':status :error' settles — every drive replays a success reply. The sibling conformance fixture (implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj:621-631) states in its own prose that it drives no :reply-to and replays no reply at all, and points at the egress test as the home of that coverage. So the coverage it points at exists only for the success branch.

CONSEQUENCE. Four settle branches each fan out a :reply-to continuation whose reply map has never been projected through epoch/projected-record: events.cljc:2598 (failed-handler), :2839 (aborted-handler), :3096 (page-failed-handler), and mutation_events.cljc:1962 (mutation failure settle). rf2-rnsv2 — the SIXTH leak in this family — lives on exactly those branches and was structurally unreachable by the suite, not merely unnoticed. Six leaks, six found by workers, none by a gate.

SCOPE. Extend the DRIVE matrix, not the assertion count. The machinery already exists in the egress test: drive-reply-to-read! (:1766), carrier-replies (:1736, finds replies by the :rf.reply/work-kind marker), record-carrying-reply (:1755), and the secret-leak-paths canary. What is missing is a failure/cancel counterpart of drive-reply-to-read! and a mutation-continuation drive, each fed a canary-bearing envelope, each swept for ZERO secret paths with a fixture assertion that the unprojected record does leak. One canary sweep per settle branch catches the CLASS; one assertion per named slot catches only the instance somebody already found.

SEQUENCING. rf2-rnsv2's fix will add the read-failure case as its acceptance test. This bead is the remaining branches (abort, page-failed, mutation-failure) plus the standing rule that a new settle branch fanning out a continuation gets a canary drive. Dispatch AFTER rf2-rnsv2's fix merges — same file, would collide.

title: The re-frame.freehand.test mounted lifecycle facade does not exist — three suites duplicate act, root/container and residue
description:
CORRECTS A FALSE PREMISE IN rf2-drpa3.182.7 AND IN THE MAYOR BRIEF THAT DISPATCHED IT. That bead TEST SURFACE section says to "consume the re-frame.freehand.test mounted lifecycle facade ruled in ER-06/ER-08 and owned by rf2-gzmg0" and not to duplicate it. The facade DOES NOT EXIST. rf2-gzmg0 shipped a Story presence bridge, which is a different thing. So the instruction was unfollowable, and three suites have each grown their own.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DUPLICATED — measured by the rf2-drpa3.182.7 worker, and narrower than "everything", which is why this is a small bead and not a framework:

  ALREADY SHARED, needs nothing: frame/runtime reset. All three use test-support/make-reset-runtime-fixture.
  BYTE-IDENTICAL IN ALL THREE FILES: the React 19 act-as-promise wrapper.
  THE SAME TWO LINES TWICE: .unmount + .remove teardown.
  IN ONE FILE ONLY: the leak assertion — which is exactly why the other two cannot claim :residue :none.

SO THE SPEC IS THREE THINGS: act, root/container lifecycle, and a SHARED RESIDUE ASSERTION. Frame reset is done. Nothing else.

WHY THE RESIDUE ASSERTION IS THE LOAD-BEARING PIECE. PR #7105 found all three fixture records declared :residue :none while NOTHING CHECKED IT, and two were overclaiming: FH-BEHAVIOR-005 genuinely earns :none (both projections read the books empty as exact zeros); FH-CTRL-018 only unmounts and removes; FH-REACT-007 resets in its :init-fn — cleanup BEFORE each test rather than an assertion AFTER one, so a retained boundary is masked by the next reset. Those two now say :unasserted, and a JVM row refuses a :none claim whose suites make no emptiness assertion. That converted an unverifiable claim into a countable one — but the only way to move them back to :none is a shared assertion the three can all use.

A leaked React root contaminates every later suite in a shared-process bundle; this repo has seen that produce 98 failures across unrelated suites.

SEQUENCING. The rf2-drpa3.182.7 worker deliberately did NOT build this, for two stated reasons, both still true at filing: it collides head-on with the workers on rf2-drpa3.182.4 and rf2-drpa3.182.3, and its own bead forbids growing a parallel facade. Sequence this AFTER those land. It is also a candidate to fold into rf2-fby7o or a Freehand test-surface bead rather than standing alone — mayor call at dispatch time.

ACCEPTANCE. One facade carrying act, root/container lifecycle and a residue assertion, consumed by all three suites with no pasted copies remaining. FH-CTRL-018 and FH-REACT-007 move from :unasserted back to :none, and the JVM row that refuses an unearned :none still refuses one — prove that with a mutation, since a shared assertion that cannot fail is the defect this bead exists to remove.

DO NOT let this become a browser-action DSL, a query library or a second evidence store. rf2-drpa3.182.7 NON-GOALS names all three, and they still apply.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7111 (2026-07-27 AEST) — REOPENED. The patch renamed matrix-support to mount-support, added a lifecycle ledger/residue-clean!, and changed only the require path in the ten existing matrix consumers. It did not touch the promised owners: controls-kit-dom-cljs-test and host-mounted-dom-cljs-test still carry their private lifecycle helpers, the behavior proofs remain separate, and repository-wide residue-clean!/reset-ledger! have ZERO executable call sites outside their definitions/docs. The fixtures still say FH-CTRL-018/FH-REACT-007 :residue :unasserted, while roster-jvm-test explicitly expects those two unasserted; focused gate is green at 9 tests/33 assertions, proving the PR did not deliver its claimed transition to :none. Complete the exact original acceptance by migrating the named suites, calling the shared assertion after teardown, changing the two fixture records and current-state roster assertion, and proving the refusal mutation. No second facade or broader browser DSL.
PR #7162 (2026-07-27 21:13 AUSEST) — MIGRATION LANDED, ONE FENCED STEP REMAINS. All four mounted projections of the three spine fixtures (controls-kit-dom, host-mounted-dom, behaviors-dom, behavior-async-dom) now consume re-frame.freehand.mount-support for act + root/container lifecycle; four byte-identical act copies deleted. residue-clean!/reset-ledger! went from ZERO executable call sites to 8: every suite scopes the ledger in its :init-fn and reads the books AFTER teardown. roster-jvm-test recognises residue-clean! and gains the refusal mutation (a suite can consume the shared TEARDOWN and never read the shared BOOKS — the rule is run against both halves and still refuses the first). Gates green: freehand JVM 1221/8229 -> 1222/8231 exit 0; node 1302/7219 unchanged exit 0; browser 835 tests/5323 -> 835 tests/5383 assertions exit 0 — test count identical, +60 assertions are the residue rows. Deliberately NOT absorbed (and the bead's inventory held on all three counts): the frame/runtime reset was already shared; the controls kit's typing helpers differ (isComposing false, insert-at-caret not append) so absorbing them would be a behaviour change; host-mounted's teardown goes through the DOOR (v/unmount!) so destroy-root! would be wrong. REMAINING, blocked by the dispatch fence (spec/** = hot-zone, report-don't-edit): flip :residue :unasserted -> :none in spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures/fh-ctrl-018.edn and fh-react-007.edn, and update roster-jvm-test/the-spine-records-what-it-has-not-yet-earned to expect :none for all three. Both suites now EARN it — the gating rule scans the mounted proof for an emptiness assertion and both carry residue-clean! — so the flip is mechanical and green. Needs one hand allowed to touch spec/.

COMPLETE across two PRs. #7162 (merged) delivered the facade; #7163 delivered the conformance claim that had been fenced out of spec/.

WHAT #7162 LANDED. All four mounted projections of the three spine fixtures — controls-kit-dom, host-mounted-dom, behaviors-dom, behavior-async-dom — took act and root/container lifecycle from re-frame.freehand.mount-support; four byte-identical act copies deleted. residue-clean!/reset-ledger! went from ZERO executable call sites (the state audit #7111 reopened this bead for) to 8. WHAT #7163 LANDED. FH-CTRL-018 and FH-REACT-007 flipped :residue :unasserted -> :none in their fixtures, the prose that justified :unasserted rewritten rather than left defending a claim nobody makes, and roster-jvm-test's current-state row renamed and moved to :none for all three.

VERIFIED BEFORE FLIPPING, at the executable sites rather than off the scanner. FH-CTRL-018: finish! calls ms/destroy-root! then ms/residue-clean!, and all five mounting rows end there. FH-REACT-007: released! calls ms/residue-clean! over the door's live-root registry after teardown! (v/unmount! + ms/remove-node!), and all three mounting rows end there — its other two rows are emitter-only adapter refusals that mount nothing and so have no residue to read. residue-clean! carries its own non-vacuity: (is (pos? (count retired))) reds a suite that tore no root down through the facade.

MUTATION EVIDENCE. Removing ms/residue-clean! from finish! AND the one comment naming it reds a-residue-none-claim-is-backed-by-an-emptiness-assertion at exit 1: "FH-CTRL-018 claims :residue :none, but its mounted proof re-frame.freehand.controls-kit-dom-cljs-test makes no emptiness assertion". Restored: 10 tests / 37 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0, git diff --stat empty. So the row that refuses an unearned :none still refuses one — the bead's stated requirement.

AND THE HONEST HALF, WHICH BELONGS TO THE PARENT, NOT HERE. Removing only the EXECUTABLE ms/residue-clean! call and leaving the comment that names it stays GREEN at exit 0: the rule is a whole-file text scan, so a comment satisfies it. host-mounted-dom-cljs-test has the same property from a different direction — an unrelated (is (= [] (read* ...))) would satisfy the scanner on its own. That is NOT a regression from either PR and not this bead's acceptance; it is exactly the weakness the merged-PR audit of #7105 recorded against rf2-drpa3.182.7, which is open, P1, and carries the acceptance "earn :none with executed browser proof tied to teardown and the relevant residue books (prefer the already-owned shared lifecycle/leak assertion over a source scanner), and include a negative witness where comment-only/unrelated emptiness text is refused". The shared assertion this bead built is precisely the thing that acceptance says to prefer, so that owner is now unblocked to replace the scanner with it. Closing here without it is correct: this bead's job was the facade and the honest claim, and both are done.

GATES. implementation/freehand JVM clojure -M:test: 1222 tests / 8233 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, exit 0 (8231 -> 8233 because the residue rule now scans two more mounted proofs). Focused roster-jvm-test green/red/green across the mutation as above. npm run test:browser deferred to CI — #7163 touches no mounted suite; the executed evidence that these assertions actually RUN is #7162's browser gate at 835 tests, 5323 -> 5383 assertions, exit 0, test count identical, the +60 being the residue rows.

FILED, not fixed: rf2-0ke4x — #7162 replaced teardown! (which did not call done) with finish! (which does) and left the pre-existing trailing (done) at all five sites, so each double-fires. cljs.test's run-block guards it with a realized? delay, so it degrades to a console warning rather than corrupting async state, which is why the browser gate stayed green at an unchanged test count. title: machines-viz share host accepts non-URLs despite its absolute-host contract
description: Found by the chronological merged-PR audit of #7088. The PR correctly removes the nonexistent hosted default and repeatedly contracts :host as the absolute URL of a viewer page the caller hosts. The landed encoder enforces only `(string? host)` plus trim/nonblank, then returns `(str host "#machine=" payload)`. Any nonblank value therefore passes: `banana` or `/viewer.html` produces a non-shareable string, preserving the same dead-link outcome the PR was meant to remove. A valid absolute URL carrying an existing fragment is worse: appending a second `#machine=` makes decode-share-url read from the first # and miss the machine payload. Existing tests cover missing/nil/blank only. Keep the repair at this boundary: parse and validate the host according to the documented contract (at minimum absolute http(s), with an explicit fragment policy), return the normalized viewer-page URL plus the one machine fragment, and add witnesses for relative/garbage input and a pre-fragmented absolute URL. Do not add hosting or deployment machinery.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #7102. The worker MEASURED before validating, as instructed, and the measurement changed the answer: it probed encode-share-url with 17 hosts through the real CLJS lane and found TWO classes, not one.

LOUD (no guard warranted): 'banana', '/viewer.html', 'viewer.html', '//acme/viewer.html', 'javascript:alert(1)', 'data:...' all return a string BEGINNING WITH WHAT THE CALLER TYPED, with the payload intact and decoding fine. 'banana#machine=...' is not a link in any browser, the defect is the caller's own word at the front of the string, and it dies at first paste. Nothing is hidden.

SILENT (guard warranted, and this is the real defect): a :host that already carries a fragment. 'https://acme.example.com/viewer.html#foo' yields '...#foo#machine=...' which fails to decode with :malformed-fragment, because extract-fragment splits on the FIRST '#'. Right origin, right path, '#machine=' present, 400 characters of base64 nobody counts '#'s in. THE SENDER SEES SUCCESS AND THE FAILURE LANDS ON THE RECIPIENT.

OUTCOME split on exactly that line: a refusal for the fragment case only (:reason :host-carries-fragment, message naming the fragment, ex-data carrying :fragment-index rather than the host, which can carry a query token — consistent with this namespace's rf2-8nzxib discipline), and a CONTRACT CORRECTION for everything else. share.cljs, tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md and README.md claimed 'the absolute URL' while nothing enforced absoluteness; they now state what IS checked, what is not, and why. Same note added to export/share-url, which passes :host straight through. It refuses rather than strips, because the caller's fragment meant something and discarding it silently is a quieter wrong answer.

TWO REMEDIES THE BEAD ASKED FOR WERE DECLINED, and the mayor endorses both declines: (1) 'at minimum absolute http(s)' validation — file:///.../viewer.html is literally what the README's own build recipe leaves on disk and /viewer.html is a legitimate same-origin base, so a scheme allowlist REFUSES WORKING INPUT to catch input nobody can miss, and it is the per-value closed-set check this project has rejected; (2) returning a 'normalized' URL — normalising is guessing.

THE RULING IS PINNED IN A TEST, which is the part worth copying: non-url-host-is-accepted-and-fails-visibly asserts that 'banana', 'not a url' and 'javascript:alert(1)' STILL ENCODE, with the reason stated, so a future guard-adder must confront the decision rather than quietly reverse it.

MUTATION PROOF, each confirmed applied before its verdict was read: (A) refusal disabled -> 25 failures all in the positive test; (B) over-refuse on '/' -> suite-wide red including the negative control; (C) SURGICAL — still refuses every '#' but additionally refuses a query string -> EXACTLY ONE test red, fragment-free-hosts-are-untouched. C is the recorded failure shape (a guard proven only on refusals that rejects a legal form) and the negative control is its sole witness. Restored 0/0.

Gates rc=0: machines-viz JVM 632/2537, machines-viz CLJS 825/3311 with 0 warnings, plus hardcoded-paths, beads-boundary, thrown-error, test-lane-bijection (1672 files / 45 lanes), doc-slugs, readme-links and keyword-catalogue drift. Sibling rf2-8m344 deliberately untouched — the viewer still is not deployed by this repository and nothing here implies the share path works end to end.

title: 37 more wrong-arity reg-* examples: reg-resource (21), reg-flow (8), reg-mutation (8) all throw ArityException at registration
description:
Found while fixing rf2-txe8o (reg-route :path in metadata, PR #7094). That bead enumerated its verb correctly and completely — and its verb is one of FOUR with the same defect.

THE CLASS. Reading arglists off the live facade (not from memory), exactly four public reg-* verbs have NO 2-arg arity:

    reg-flow     [flow-id metadata derive-fn]
    reg-mutation [mutation-id metadata request-fn]
    reg-resource [resource-id metadata request-fn]
    reg-route    [id metadata path]

A 2-arg (or 1-arg) call of any of them raises a raw clojure.lang.ArityException at registration, so the registration never happens and everything downstream in the worked example is inert. NOTE the symptom is the ArityException, NOT the structured guard: rf2-txe8o attributed the throw to registry.cljc:455, but that guard only fires for a HALF-migrated 3-arg call that still carries :path in the map. The corpus form dies earlier, with no id, no :rf.error/* id and no grammar hint.

COUNTS (reader-based scan of every fenced clojure/edn block in tracked files; generated docs/spec + site excluded):

    reg-resource  21
    reg-route     18   <- rf2-txe8o, FIXED in PR #7094 (8 of 18; 10 left in docs/EP by ruling)
    reg-flow       8
    reg-mutation   8
    TOTAL         55   — rf2-txe8o covered 33% of the class

THE SHARP END: THREE ARE IN THE NORMATIVE SPEC.

    spec/015-Data-Classification.md  156  reg-resource :user-profile
    spec/016-Resources.md           1361  reg-resource :feed/timeline
    spec/016-Resources.md           1698  reg-resource :article/by-slug

Same argument rf2-txe8o made for its seven: the spec is the artefact, and every downstream reader — the guide, an AI generating code from the spec — inherits the broken shape as sanctioned.

THIS IS NOT A THIRD-SLOT MOVE. Unlike reg-route (where the :path was already present, just misplaced), a 2-arg reg-resource has no request fn to promote — the third slot must be AUTHORED. And correcting the arity alone is not enough; verified executably:

    3-arg, no :scope       -> :rf.error/resource-missing-scope-policy
    3-arg + :scope         -> :rf.error/resource-bad-spec (no :params-schema)

So each site needs a :scope policy, a :params-schema, and a plausible :request fn. That is example authoring, and it should be done uniformly across all 21 reg-resource sites by one worker who has measured the class — not ad hoc per file.

LEFT HALF-FIXED BY PR #7094, ON PURPOSE:
docs/core/how-to/keep-secrets-out-of-traces.md:206 has BOTH a reg-route (fixed) and a reg-resource (not fixed) in the SAME fenced block. The page still does not paste. This bead finishes it and should be sequenced accordingly — it is a live how-to whose subject is keeping a reset token out of traces.

DISPOSITION QUESTION, same as rf2-txe8o faced: 28 of the 37 are in docs/EP/**. PR #7094 ruled the EP tree LEFT — EP-0009 durability rule 3 permits mechanical correction but does not require it; the tree already carries 103 fenced blocks across eight retired-grammar tokens (reg-event-fx 34, :include-ns 21, :initial-db 11, reg-event-db 10, :on-create 9, :rf.world/inputs 9, :data-schema 6, :exclude-ns 3), so period-spelling is the established norm there and a partial modernisation cannot deliver paste-ability anyway. title: v/spread at a v/defhost head is accepted and silently rewrites :className to :class - spec/004 now says it is illegal, nothing enforces it
description:
The implementation arm of rf2-33pts (spec half landed in PR #7090). spec/004 Props forwarding now states that v/spread and v/spread-safe are element forms and neither is legal at a v/defhost head. Nothing enforces that today, and the current behaviour is wrong in both directions - measured on the JVM structural path with a real (v/defhost date-picker ... {:callbacks {:onChange :event} :children :none :ssr :client-only}) head and the map built inside the view body:

  remainder key   | v/spread at host head        | plain merge at host head
  :placeholder    | :placeholder            OK   | :placeholder            OK
  :className      | :class  <-- SILENT RENAME    | :className              OK
  "class"         | :class  <-- LAUNDERED        | REFUSED (exactness law) OK
  :class-name     | REFUSED <-- wrongly          | :class-name             OK

Mechanism: node/spread-attrs projects both maps through canonical-slot-keys -> conv/attr-key -> rules/canonical-attr-key, which rewrites EVERY spelling projecting onto the className or style slot into :class / :style. At an element that is correct (they own a slot). At a host head it defeats descriptor/normalize-host-call's inexact-host-prop-names check, which runs FIRST precisely so every later law can be enforced BY name - the same class of hole rf2-c20nr's disjoint-plane guard was just closed against. And :className -> :class is not merely a laundered spelling: it is a DIFFERENT React prop, the one a third-party component most commonly reads, silently renamed to one it does not.

The other direction: assert-forwardable-attrs! applies conv/attr-key-refusal, the DOM attribute grammar, so :class-name, a mixed-case :data-fooBar and :key are refused - all three are ordinary names on a foreign prop ABI, and :key is how a host crossing is keyed at a plain head.

ENFORCEMENT NEEDS A RULING - do not pick one silently. v/spread returns a plain map, so by the time normalize-host-call sees it the provenance is gone. Two candidate mechanisms:
(a) mark the spread's result the way node/carry-caller marks a v/spread-safe caller map, and have normalize-host-call refuse a marked map (reuses :rf.error/view-bad-props, no new id);
(b) leave it unenforced and treat spec/004 + the guide as the whole answer (pre-alpha, trust the programmer).
(a) costs a value mark on the hottest forwarding seam; (b) leaves a silent-corruption path the spec says does not exist. No new public verb is needed either way.
close_reason:
Shipped in PR #7100, merged; trunk re-verified green afterwards at 1212 tests / 8113 assertions, exit 0, on a main that also carries #7096's docs restructure.

MAYOR RULING, RECORDED LATE AND ACKNOWLEDGED AS SUCH: this bead said 'ENFORCEMENT NEEDS A RULING — do not pick one silently' and listed (a) mark-and-refuse versus (b) leave it to the spec. My dispatch brief supplied (a) WITHOUT acknowledging the bead had reserved the question. The worker followed the brief and FLAGGED THE DIVERGENCE, which is exactly right — I tell every worker the bead is authoritative over the brief, so silently overriding a reserved ruling is my error, not its.

I STAND BY (a), on the house test: a guard is warranted when the failure is SILENT and has already happened. :className arriving as :class is a DIFFERENT REACT PROP — the component receives no class and nothing reports it. And the implementation cost turned out to be near zero, which the ruling could not have known in advance but which confirms it: rules/mark-element-forward leaves the author spelling in the result's METADATA and normalize-host-call refuses a marked map. Metadata rather than a value wrapper so the result stays an ordinary attribute map for the element fold — the LEGAL use, which must cost nothing — and =, hash and pr-str all ignore it. No new error id: a new arm of the existing :rf.error/view-bad-props with recovery :forward-to-a-host-with-an-ordinary-map, so no three-file co-edit.

TWO FINDINGS BEYOND THE BRIEF, the first of which the brief should have carried:

1. THE CHECK MUST RUN BEFORE THE EXACTNESS LAW. A spread canonicalises "class" into the keyword :class, so inexact-host-prop-names sees a CLEAN call — exactness would pass and the corruption would be the answer. Asserted, with its own non-vacuity leg.
2. RUNTIME-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION. The compiled tier refuses a v/defhost crossing outright (:rf.ui.compile/host-crossing-unsupported), so the interpreted walk is the only path that can reach a host head; tree.cljc and react.cljs both normalize through the one seam, so one guard covers both hosts.

THE MUTUALLY-INVALIDATING-TEST RISK DID NOT MATERIALISE, and my warning was over-broad: I named four files containing both 'spread' and 'defhost'. NONE pinned the accepting behaviour. composition_cljs_test.cljc already asserts the CORRECT behaviour (#7093 landed that flip); samples_coverage_jvm_test.clj's spread-forms row points at an element-level fixture and no fenced block changed so no digest moved; and pilot_react_interop.cljc / pilot_react_interop_dom_cljs_test.cljs were FALSE POSITIVES — they matched on 'spreadsheet' and 'spreadjs'. It also checked #7098's new roster spine, which mentions neither term.

PROOF: both forms refused with a diagnostic naming form, head and recovery; a control that an ordinary map of the same keys still normalizes; :className end-to-end through a real render against a merge TWIN showing the caller's name surviving — the counterfactual is what makes it more than 'something throws'. Negative control: both forms at an ELEMENT head still fold as before, :className composing into the element's own class. Mutation: neutering the mark reader red 14 assertions across the three refusal rows, exit 1, and left the element rows GREEN — the signature that the guard is load-bearing for the refusal and the control is independent of it.

title: Machines-viz default viewer URL is 404; no workflow ships the page bundle
description:
Found by the chronological merged-PR audit of #7071. The PR correctly moves viewer.cljs out of the published machines-viz jar, but repeatedly asserts that the page still ships as public/viewer.html plus viewer.js and documents https://day8.github.io/re-frame2-machines-viz/viewer.html as the default share host.

That URL currently returns HTTP 404. There is no day8/re-frame2-machines-viz repository, and the re-frame2 repository has no workflow or script that compiles :machines-viz-viewer, stages viewer.js beside tools/machines-viz/public/viewer.html, or deploys those two files. release-machines-viz.yml only tests the JVM artefact and deploys the jar to Clojars. The Shadow build proves the bundle can be produced, but no delivery path consumes it.

This makes the share-url default and the new "ships as a page" API/README claims false end-to-end. Keep the repair bounded to making the existing page contract real; do not turn this into a general static-site framework.
acceptance_criteria:
The canonical machines-viz viewer URL documented and emitted by encode-share-url returns the checked-in viewer.html and its matching compiled viewer.js after the relevant release/deploy flow.
A repository-owned workflow builds :machines-viz-viewer, stages the exact HTML and bundle together, and deploys them to the documented host with a smoke check that loads the page and exported run entry.
The release documentation names who/what deploys the page and does not imply that publishing the Clojars jar deploys it.
If the day8.github.io/re-frame2-machines-viz host is deliberately not available pre-alpha, remove it as a default and stop calling the page shipped until a real host exists; keep self-hosting explicit.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7116 (merge a06227b68c62fdd3ab8ead3531f52302783ebc47, 2026-07-26T14:25:12Z) — REOPENED exact owner. The new A2 gate claims to prove viewer.js INSTALLS the global that viewer.html calls, but bundleExports is only a substring search. Its own green self-test demonstrates the false positive: it accepts a bundle containing only an unrelated array with segments a, b, viewer, run even though that bundle installs no window global at all; the dotted arm likewise accepts any unrelated occurrence of a.b.viewer.run. Therefore the required CI job can report that the page boot global is installed when the bundle merely contains the same segment sequence. This is the load-bearing coupling rf2-8m344 was closed for, so a false-positive proof leaves the exact owner incomplete. Keep the repair small: make A2 recognise an actual Closure export/install expression or execute the built bundle in a minimal isolated browser-like harness and assert the derived window path is callable. Add negative self-tests for decoy array and dotted occurrences, and mutation-prove that removing the install while preserving a decoy occurrence makes the gate fail. Do not turn this into a general browser smoke framework.
close_reason: PR #7186. The 404 half was already on main (ee9ba1bed0): :host is REQUIRED, blank throws :reason :no-host, and the dead day8.github.io URL survives only in comments explaining its removal. This PR closes the audit reopen — a defect in the PROOF, not the page. The A2 assertion in stage-viewer-page.cjs was bundle.includes() over the export-path literal, and a substring cannot tell an export from a coincidence; its own green self-test accepted 'var x=["a","b","viewer","run"]', which installs no global at all. A2 now EVALUATES the bundle in an isolated vm context and asks whether window.<the path the page calls> came out callable. Not a proxy for the coupling - the coupling. Both sides stay derived, run() is never called, so it is a load-and-install proof rather than a render smoke. Self-test 7 -> 11 cases: decoy array literal, decoy dotted occurrence, non-function at the path, and a bundle that throws. MUTATION PROOF on the real 2302 KB bundle, both confirmed applied: (A) ',dY=aa;' -> ',dY={};' severs the install while the export-path array literal survives verbatim - the RETIRED predicate still returns true on that mutant, the new gate fails rc=1; (B) export renamed viewer->page fails rc=1. Unmutated rc=0. NO WORKFLOW CHANGE: the required machines-viz-viewer-page job already exists and already runs the fixed script, and report-changed-surfaces.sh arms it on any non-spec-md change under tools/machines-viz/**, so this diff schedules its own verifier. What cannot be proved is a hosted instance returning 200, because deliberately there is not one and this PR does not invent one - deploying stays nobody's job.

title: tools/ thrown-error subset IS consumer-reachable: story-mcp relays ex-message onto the MCP tool surface, so registrar's bare-keyword throws reach consumer AI
description:
Found by the rf2-eo2y5 "what would change this ruling" check (the ruling asked for exactly one pass over the 38 tools/ sites before closing).

THE RULING'S CONDITION IS MET. rf2-eo2y5 ruled tools/ out of scope for the Spec 009 thrown-error shape on the ground that "its errors are seen by a developer running an inspection tool, never caught by a consumer app", and named the condition that would change it: "if any of those 38 sites throws an error that reaches a CONSUMER -- via the MCP tool surface, a published skill, or an error a consumer app can catch -- then the shape governs it and that subset is real work."

THE CONFIRMED CHAIN (traced end to end, not inferred):

  tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/write.cljc:262-274
    (defn- register-or-error [vk body-v]
      (try (story/reg-variant* vk (assoc body-v :origin config/origin)) ...
        (catch Throwable e
          (result/error-result (str "Registration failed: " (ex-message e)) ...))))

  -> re-frame.story.registrar/reg-variant* (registrar.cljc:451)
       calls assert-id! (:471) and validate-shape! (:477)

  -> registrar.cljc:365  (throw (ex-info (str error-kw) {:rf.error/id error-kw ...}))
     registrar.cljc:302  (throw (ex-info (str error-kw) {:rf.error/id error-kw ...}))

`error-kw` is built as (keyword \"rf.error\" (str (name kind) \"-shape\")) / \"-id-shape\", so ex-message is EXACTLY the stringified discriminator. An MCP client -- an AI agent, i.e. the \"consumer AI\" whose reading is the stated reason the shape is a contract -- calling story-mcp's register-variant with a malformed body receives, verbatim:

    Registration failed: :rf.error/variant-id-shape

That is the precise regression rf2-vvixub abolished, on a tool surface a consumer AI reads, with the human sentence available in ex-data :reason and discarded.

TWO MORE RELAYS ON THE SAME SURFACE, same shape, unaudited per-site:
  * tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/wire_pipeline.cljc:385
        (result/error-result (str \"Tool handler threw: \" (ex-message e)) ...)
    -- a catch-all: ANY story handler throw relays its message.
  * tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/lifecycle.cljc:40
        {... :reason (ex-message e)}
  * tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/server.cljs:535-539
        invoke-and-guard's .catch -> {:ok? false :reason :handler-threw :message (.-message err)}
    -- reaches tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/.../tools/eval_form.cljs:128 and
       .../tools/wire_pipeline.cljs:268, both bare-keyword.

WHAT IS *NOT* REACHABLE (checked, so the subset stays honest):
  * server.cljs:321 / :331 (pair-mcp discovery). handle-call*'s .catch at :563 builds its payload from ex-DATA (:rf.error/id, :hint, :candidates) and never relays ex-message; the message only reaches stderr via log!. Correct by construction -- this is the shape the other relays should copy.
  * mcp-base cursor.cljc:123/188/218. Their own docstrings say \"Caught by the surrounding try in decode-cursor -> ::malformed\" and cursor.cljc:334 confirms `(catch ... _ ::malformed)` -- the message is swallowed, the sentinel is the contract.

TWO OF THE 38 ARE GATE FALSE POSITIVES, not defects:
  tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc:877 and :914 already build a conformant message -- human sentence + trailing [:rf.error/<id>] token, with a comment citing Spec 009 and the bundle-isolation constraint -- but bind it to a local `msg` before the throw. The gate inspects the TEXT of ex-info's first argument, so `msg` shows neither a human-message call nor a literal token and it reports builder-bypass-message. Any future conformant let-bound message under implementation/ would false-red the same way.

SCOPE OF THE REAL WORK (deliberately small): convert only the sites whose ex-message is relayed to a consumer surface. registrar.cljc:302 and :365 are the confirmed pair; plan.cljc:137 (`fail!`, same (str id) shape, reachable from the same registration path) is the near neighbour. Everything else in the 38 stays out of scope under rf2-eo2y5 unless a relay is found for it. Hand-roll the shape inline as story.cljc:877/914 already do -- tools/ MUST NOT :require re-frame.error.
notes:
FINAL: PR #7036 head 8b52a45497. CI GREEN — 32 pass / 43 skipping / 0 fail / 0 pending. MERGEABLE. Left OPEN for the mayor to close on the merged SHA. Follow-ups filed: rf2-2z9u3 (P1, malli :explain not JSON-encodable -> -32603 masks the register-variant diagnostic entirely) and rf2-u3otj (P3, gate blind spot on let-bound / computed-discriminator messages).
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7036: IMPLEMENTATION CORRECT, COMPLETION STILL OPEN FOR DURABLE BOUNDARY PROOF. The three authored commits land exactly and the relay inventory is careful: the converted messages render a human sentence plus the trailing token, the unreachable subsets stay untouched, assert-id reachability is corrected, and the raw Malli explain masking fault is separated to rf2-2z9u3 rather than hidden here.

What did not land is a permanent regression for the behavior this P2 exists to protect. The PR changes six source/comment files and zero test files. Its manual before/after JSON-RPC probe is good evidence for that run, but current main has no test containing the new consumer-visible phrases or tokens for pair-mcp rt-let, unknown wire kind, Story unknown-tag/plan failure, or diff-encode validation. Existing Story tests assert ex-data IDs only. The default thrown-message gate excludes tools/, and four computed-discriminator conversions are deliberately invisible even to an explicit tools scan, so reverting any of those messages to a bare keyword remains a green CI change.

Close the remaining gap with one small table through the existing real boundary helpers, not seven new unit suites: Story MCP handle-frame rows for one registrar failure and one plan failure; pair MCP invoke-and-guard/handle-call rows covering the rt-let binding, unknown wire kind, and diff-encode validation families. Each row should assert an error result rather than a protocol fault, a human phrase, and the exact trailing [:rf.error/...] token; retain the existing machine-id/ex-data assertions where that surface carries them. A mutation back to the pre-PR bare message must red these rows. The #7042 schema-explain regression may count for validate-shape, but it does not cover the other families. No new checker, builder, or broad tools sweep is needed.

The CODE fix was already correct from #7036 — verified: re-frame.story.registrar validate-shape!/assert-id!/validate-tag-membership! and re-frame.story.plan/fail! all build the Spec 009 shape today, so nothing needed changing. What was missing was the regression the merged-PR audit asked for.
