Each row asserts (a) a tool error not a -32603 protocol fault, (b) the human sentence, (c) the exact trailing [:rf.error/<id>] token. Plus a companion row keeping the machine :rf.error/id assertion through wire-safe-ex-data, and a two-sided happy-path control.

MUTATION-VERIFIED as the audit required: reverting fail! to (str id) reds exactly 6 assertions — the human+token rows for all three families — and NOTHING else. tool-error? and the ex-data id still pass under the mutation, which is precisely why the pre-existing tests could not catch this class.

The registrar half (variant-shape, unknown-tag) was ALREADY pinned at the same boundary by #7042's work, so it needed no new rows; the audit's 'one registrar failure and one plan failure' is therefore satisfied.

PAIR-MCP HALF NOT DONE — split to rf2-eaf20 (P2). tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/ was outside this worker's file-ownership fence and is CLJS with a different test harness, so the story-mcp helpers do not transfer. The rt-let / unknown-wire-kind / diff-encode families remain unpinned exactly as the audit described.

Also filed: rf2-zrdog (P2) — record-as-variant-no-cofx-is-byte-identical flakes in aggregate runs (recorder captures 0 events); characterised as pre-existing, not from this diff.

title: Routing doors disagree on a path param the route pattern does not capture
description:
Found while settling rf2-kqxe6.7 (EP-0037 R3 prefetch identity). NOT prefetch-specific: the two ACTIVATION doors already disagree with each other, and prefetch merely inherits one of the two answers.

Route /probe/:id. Address {:to :route/probe :params {:id "7" :extra "x"}} — :extra is a path param the pattern does not capture, so route-url silently ignores it and builds "/probe/7".

MEASURED on JVM (worker/ep0037-remainder, post-fix):
  - programmatic [:rf.route/navigate {:to … :params {:id "7" :extra "x"}}]
      commits :params {:id "7" :extra "x"}
  - a real rf/route-link CLICK (link/link-model -> [:rf.route/url-requested {:url "/probe/7" :to … :params {…}}])
      commits :params {:id "7"} — it resolves through the URL, which cannot carry :extra
  - [:rf.route/prefetch …] warms {:id "7" :extra "x"} (it agrees with the programmatic door)

So hovering a link warms one resource identity and clicking that SAME link activates another — R3's original failure mode, by a different route than the one #6976 named. But the root cause is the door disagreement, not prefetch: Spec 012 §The one planning pipeline says doors differ in cause and history/scroll policy, NOT in target.

RULING NEEDED (this is a contract decision, not a worker fix — it changes :rf.route/navigate semantics):
  (a) reject an uncaptured path param at the address gate as a caller bug (fail-loud, consistent with route-url raising :rf.error/missing-route-param for the inverse), or
  (b) have the ResolvedTarget seam drop path params the route pattern does not capture, so every door commits the URL-expressible identity.

(a) is the fail-loud house style and surfaces the typo; (b) is silent but total. Either way it is ONE rule at ONE place — the address gate or resolve/resolved-target — not a per-door patch.

Deliberately NOT fixed on the rf2-kqxe6.7 PR: that bead's residual was prefetch-vs-navigation, and the two normalisations it did own (nil query values, empty fragment) are fixed at the seam there. A test arm on that PR records this gap and points here rather than asserting either answer.
notes:
MAYOR RATIFICATION (2026-07-27): the worker's ruling STANDS — an uncaptured path param is REJECTED LOUD at route-url (:rf.error/route-url-validation, :reason :uncaptured-params). Merged as PR #7120.

WHY I RATIFIED RATHER THAN REVERSED:
1. It honours an EXISTING spec rule rather than inventing a new stance. spec/012 Validity rule 2 states verbatim that letting address keys 'ride beside it and be silently ignored is the exact failure class this grammar exists to kill'. Verified in the source at spec/012:460.
2. route-url ALREADY fails closed on emission for every other prism break (the empty-string segment, the sequential-optional-group prefix chain). Truncating here would make this the one prism break that passes silently.
3. The decisive argument is the typo class truncation would swallow: /docs{/:section}? with {:sction "x"} elides the optional group and builds /docs cleanly, so :rf.error/missing-route-param can NEVER fire. Silent truncation converts a typo into a wrong-but-plausible URL, which is the worst available outcome.
4. POSTURE CHECK: 'trust the programmer' does not mean 'stay quiet when the programmer typed something the URL cannot carry'. A loud, actionable, immediate error is GOOD ergonomics and low friction; a silently divergent URL is neither. This is not a nag diagnostic.
5. One rule in one place: route-url is the boundary all three named-address doors already share, so prefetch needed NO code (it maps route-url's error ids verbatim per Spec 009) and the URL-driven doors need no rule at all. The single exemption, :rf.route/not-found, is principled — its slice :params are the framework's miss record, not path captures.

REVERSAL RECIPE, if Mike overturns: ~10 lines (swap the throw for a select-keys) plus flipping two pinned tests. The full argument is in PR #7120's body.

FOLLOW-ON SEQUENCED: rf2-jx5bw (P2) records the rejection in spec/012 Bidirectional URL<->params and widens the :rf.error/route-url-validation row in spec/009 to list :reason/:keys. Prose only, no new reserved error id. spec/009 was held by PR #7124 which has now MERGED, so rf2-jx5bw is dispatchable.
close_reason:
Fixed by PR #7120 (worker/routing-doors-0iuh3).

DECISION TAKEN — neither committed value wins. An uncaptured path param is REJECTED LOUD at route-url (:rf.error/route-url-validation, :reason :uncaptured-params), i.e. the bead's option (a) fail-loud, sited at the registry-aware EMISSION boundary rather than the registry-free structural address gate. One rule at one place: route-url is the boundary all three named-address doors already share (programmatic URL build, route-link href synthesis, prefetch destination gate — prefetch needed NO code, it maps route-url's error ids verbatim). The URL-driven doors need no rule: a URL cannot carry an uncaptured param.

WHY NOT (b) drop-at-the-seam: the round-trip argument kills committing :extra, but truncation is the OTHER wrong answer. Spec 012 §Validity rules rule 2 already calls silently-ignored address keys 'the exact failure class this grammar exists to kill'; route-url already fails closed on emission for every other prism break (empty-string segment, sequential-optional-group prefix chain); and truncation swallows a typo class nothing else catches (/docs{/:section}? with {:sction "x"} elides the group and builds /docs clean, so :rf.error/missing-route-param can never fire). Dropping at resolved-target would additionally have had to special-case the reserved :rf.route/not-found params anyway — silently.

ONE EXEMPTION: :rf.route/not-found (its slice :params are the framework's miss record {:url … :reason …}, not path captures). Pinned by tests on both a helper and a live door.

MAYOR: the bead asked for a RULING and the worker took one — please ratify. Reversing to silent truncation is a ~10-line change (swap the throw for a select-keys) plus flipping the two pinned tests; the PR body carries the full argument.

Reproduced first as a failing test (27/43 assertions red on unmodified source, matching this bead's JVM measurements verbatim), then fixed. routing_registry_test/route-url-ignores-extra-path-params — the test that pinned the losing behaviour — was FLIPPED and renamed, not deleted.

Spec follow-up filed as rf2-jx5bw (spec/012 + spec/009 prose; blocked on this).

title: DC-09 evidence: measure the high-rate two-clock operating envelope
description:
OUTCOME
Measure Freehand's two-clock operating envelope and publish evidence-backed guidance for high-rate pointer/camera/animation/scroll hosts and controlled-input contention.

MATRIX
Offer 30/60/120/240 semantic updates per second; run one controlled field with 0/1/10/50/200 already-dirty siblings; compare stable-reference, fresh-but-rf=-equal, and one-leaf-changed behavior config at Vega/Spread-shaped sizes.

MEASURE
Separate offered host events, browser-observed events, accepted semantic events, reducer applications, commits, presentation opportunities, peak backlog, settlement tail, equality cost, host update cost, and p50/p95/p99. Include deterministic count/correctness/cleanup facts and full provenance per D021.

GUIDANCE
Name the default: a behavior may own high-rate host motion while semantic started, optional preview, and committed events cross. Keep host-local style/geometry/motion outside app-db unless semantically required. Measure dispatch-per-move before adding policy.

HOST/MODE
Pinned real browser for timing; structural/config equality probes where applicable; interpreted/compiled attribution.

NON-GOALS
No generic debounce/throttle/coalesce API, equality hooks, host-local state model, or assumption that 60 Hz is inherently safe or unsafe.

ACCEPTANCE
1. The complete matrix publishes deterministic counts and timing distributions with revision/build/browser/hardware/sample provenance.
2. Controlled input proves no drops and correct caret/composition before latency is discussed.
3. Costs are attributed to event/reducer/Freehand/React/host work rather than rolled into one latency number.
4. New scheduling/preview/equality vocabulary is proposed only for a material attributed bottleneck repeated in two realistic witnesses; otherwise the result explicitly recommends no new API.
notes:
AUDIT REOPEN CLOSED — PR #7240 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7240), branch worker/dc09-evidence-18212. All five gates green (exit 0): bench compile 259 files 0 warnings; bench browser 30 tests/482 assertions 0F/0E (466 + exactly the 16 added); order-guard self-test 8 checks, NO REFUSAL; npm run test:browser 841/5459 0F/0E; three b10_prod_run.cjs production runs, each :d021 :release-evidence.

THE FAULT, CONFIRMED AND FIXED. drive!'s :tail-ms was read off a clock started at SETTLE time. The interval callback that notices the drive duration has elapsed is the one AFTER the last offer -- one whole period later, by construction, since it is the next fire of the same setInterval -- so the clock omitted that interval, and where the last generation had already committed (most of the time at low rates) it published approximately the 4 ms polling delay. The audit's diagnosis was exactly right.

SO THE PREVIOUS NOTE'S 'tail <=5.4 ms even at 240 Hz against a 20 ms crossing' WAS THE POLL, NOT THE TAIL. That claim is retracted. Measured with the corrected instrument (HeadlessChrome 147.0.7727.15, rev 65abc3b99e):
  production, tail ms (3 runs): k=0 30/60/120/240 Hz -> 0.8-1.1 / 0.5-0.8 / 0.3-0.5 / 0.4-0.5; k=200 -> 4.6-5.4 / 2.2-2.5 / 2.4-3.7 / 3.2-3.5.
  development, tail ms (1 run): k=0 -> 5.1 / 3.9 / 3.8 / 3.0; k=200 -> 15.8 / 24.3 / 14.0 / 21.1.
  what the OLD field was actually publishing (the poll delay): 4.1-6.0 ms in all sixteen cells, essentially a constant set by the 4 ms poll period.
The old number was FLATTERING at k=200 dev by 3-4x and PESSIMISTIC at k=0 prod by 6-10x.

THE TAIL IS ONE CROSSING, at every rung of both bundles. Prod k=200 tail 2.2-5.4 against the synchronous window's p50 2.6-3.6 / p95 3.3-5.1; prod k=0 tail 0.3-1.1 against p50 0.3-0.5; dev k=200 14.0-24.3 against 18.3-22.2; dev k=0 3.0-5.1 against 3.5-4.6. Stated honestly in the report as an IDENTITY not an independent measurement -- the tail IS the last generation's own latency, same two timestamps -- and what makes it a RESULT is what sits beside it: outstanding 0 and settled? true in all sixteen runs. A settlement tail of one crossing means there was never a second one waiting. A draining queue would scale with the requested rate; it does not (prod k=200 tail at 240 Hz is 3.2-3.5, SMALLER than at 30 Hz's 4.6-5.4).

RECOMMENDATION 'ADD NO SCHEDULING VOCABULARY' HOLDS, and it survived a correction against its own interest: at k=200 dev the true tail is 3-4x the flattering published figure and the no-throttle case holds anyway, because one crossing is one crossing whatever it costs. A throttle exists to stop a queue forming; there is no queue.

C3, THE NEW CONTROL (the audit's 'assertion that would fail if the clock is restarted at settle time'). The gap between the last offer and the settle decision is one interval by construction, and the run predicts it from an INDEPENDENT counter, duration/offered. Predicted vs measured, ms, 3 prod runs: k=0 33.3-35.0 vs 33.4-37.1 | 16.3 vs 15.4-17.5 | 8.0 vs 7.0-8.1 | 4.0 vs 4.2-5.0; k=200 33.3-35.0 vs 32.7-41.0 | 16.3 vs 15.3-16.2 | 8.0 vs 7.1-7.9 | 4.0-4.1 vs 3.5-4.6. Agree at all eight cells, worst within 18% (the 30 Hz rung, where one interval is 33 ms), every other within 15%. :tail-anchored? is also a GATE -- it fails a run whose gap is under half a requested period, a floor setInterval cannot violate however far behind the browser has fallen; a settle-time clock has no last-offer timestamp and cannot produce the gap at all. Asserted in the browser row AND the production entry's coherence filter. :tail-source was :observer in all sixteen -- the poll never had to answer.

C1/C2 unchanged and still exact. 0 UNVERIFIED OF 5760 (0 of 1440 in each of three production runs and 0 of 1440 in the dev run).

AXES REUSED, NOT RE-RUN: the rate ladder, the sibling ladder, the behaviour-config axis (stable-reference / fresh-but-rf=-equal / one-leaf at Vega 96 and Spread 900 leaves) and controlled-input contention were all published by #7179 and #7198. Report sections 3-5 and 7 stand untouched. Re-running a published ladder is waste; the settlement tail was the ONE MEASURE-list item whose published figure did not survive its own audit.

GUIDANCE DELIVERED -- report section 9, 'Guidance for a high-rate host', which is what DC-09 was for and what the report did not have. Section 8 answers Freehand's API designers; nothing addressed the application author. In one line: DRIVE IT DIRECTLY, SPEND YOUR ATTENTION ON HOW MUCH YOU DIRTY RATHER THAN ON HOW OFTEN YOU DISPATCH, AND DO NOT BUILD A THROTTLE. Names the default (a behavior owns high-rate host motion; only semantic started, optional preview and committed cross); four things not to bother building, each answered by a measurement (throttle/debounce/rAF coalescer; memoised or ref-cached configs; a 'settling' UI state; a distinct preview lane); four things to do in priority order (move the v/sub to the boundary that uses it, worth a constant 3.1-3.3 ms; count cells dirtied, ~0.012 ms each; measure dispatch-per-move BEFORE adding policy; type into it); and the one caveat that would change the advice -- real coalesced pointer streams are still unmeasured and are the single shape that could produce a backlog above 1.

NO SRC CHANGE. implementation/freehand/src/** untouched -- this is measurement, not optimisation. No FH- id, no roster change, no shared build configuration touched. Report sections 9 and 10 renumbered to 10 and 11. Raw records local-only at ai/findings/2026-07-28.b10-tail-anchored-prod-{1,2,3}.log. Freehand-vs-Reagent untouched (held on rf2-lbs3y).
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7240 (2026-08-01) — REOPENED exact owner; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS: The merged code correctly repairs the current `:tail-ms` formula and adds useful host guidance, but the promised regression assertion is not coupled to the value it claims to protect. Current origin/main is unchanged on this point.

CORRECTNESS: `:tail-ms` uses `(- t-settle t0)`, while `:tail-anchored?` validates only the separate `gap = t-poll-start - t0`; the browser and production gates then check only `tail-anchored?` plus that `tail-ms` is numeric and nonnegative. Mutating `:tail-ms` back to a settle-clock expression such as `(- t-settle t-poll-start)` leaves `gap`, `:tail-anchored?`, and the nonnegative check unchanged, so every new C3 assertion can remain green while the published field again measures the wrong interval. Thus the PR statement that the new assertion fails if the tail clock restarts at settle time is false.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / BOUNDED REPAIR: Make the final generation observer latency the single source of truth for `:tail-ms`, or expose the retained last-offer and observer timestamps and assert the exact algebraic identity used to publish it. Keep C3 as a separate check that the retained offer timestamp is the immediately preceding interval. Add one small mutation-style witness that changes only the tail start and must fail; do not rebuild the benchmark.
CRASH-RECONCILIATION VERIFICATION (read-only triage, 2026-08-03, tree at 0bfd309b67). Examined for closure; NOT CLOSED. The measurement work landed (5e6f28d26e, 8df9a6b6ab, c31e0ce29d, 662993367e, 3abe0f1be5 — newest 2026-07-28), but the #7240 audit-reopen obligation is UNMET, verified by reading the files, and the audit's 'current origin/main is unchanged on this point' still holds.

implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b10_two_clock.cljs:737 still publishes :tail-ms (when t0 (- t-settle t0)) with :tail-anchored? derived separately at :743 from the gap. The gates only check the anchor plus numeric/nonnegative: b10_two_clock_dom_cljs_test.cljs:385 asserts tail-anchored?, :391 asserts (and (number? tail-ms) (not (neg? tail-ms))); the production coherence filter b10_prod_app.cljs:349-351 checks the same three. Mutating :tail-ms back to a settle-clock expression such as (- t-settle t-poll-start) leaves gap, :tail-anchored? and the nonnegative check all green — so the C3 assertions still cannot fail on the value they claim to protect.

REMAINDER: make the final generation's observer latency the single source of truth for :tail-ms (or expose the retained last-offer and observer timestamps and assert the exact algebraic identity used to publish it); keep C3 as a separate check that the retained offer timestamp is the immediately preceding interval; add one mutation witness that changes only the tail start and must fail. Do not rebuild the benchmark.

(Re-applied by the mayor 2026-08-03 after an interrupted Dolt generational GC rolled the original append back.)
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7631 (2026-08-07) — REOPENED exact owner; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS: The retained MutationObserver timestamp path and exact C4 identity close the original clock-reanchoring defect when the final generation is observed. However, neither the browser row nor the production coherence filter requires :tail-source :observer, :settled? true, or :outstanding 0, even though the report and measurement method define :tail-ms as the last generation's observer latency.

CORRECTNESS: drive! deliberately falls back to :tail-source :poll and sets :tail-observed-at-ms to the poll/ceiling time. That record satisfies tail-identity-holds? exactly because C4 only checks the published subtraction; after a missing observer callback or the 2 s ceiling, the gates can therefore stay green and publish a poll-derived, potentially unsettled value as the claimed observer tail. The synthetic C4 witness does not vary :tail-source/:settled?/:outstanding, so it cannot expose this fail-open.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / BOUNDED REPAIR: Keep the labelled poll fallback as diagnostic data if useful, but make the browser and production evidence gates accept a tail measurement only when :tail-source is :observer, :settled? is true, and :outstanding is zero. Put that small coherence rule in one shared predicate and add a compact synthetic witness that flips those fields; do not rebuild or rerun the benchmark matrix.
close_reason: RE-CLOSED 2026-08-07 after a second silent tracker revert. PR #7631 verified MERGED just now. :tail-ms is now lifted from the final generation's retained observer latency rather than recomputed, and C4 (b10/tail-identity-holds?) asserts tail-ms == observed - offer from one shared predicate used by the browser row, the production filter and the witness. C3 kept separate per the bead; the two interlock. The worker found the audit's own named expression was NOT the sharpest case — it goes negative and the pre-existing nonneg check already caught it; the real fail-open is the historical regression (- now t-poll-start), positive by construction, publishing 4.1-6.0 ms against true tails of 6.4-68.8 ms, green under every gate that existed before.

title: Control witness: fixed-size virtual collection/table
description:
OUTCOME
Deliver a fixed-size virtual collection/table as the fourth accepted control witness, demonstrating large-list ergonomics, caller rendering, narrow reactivity, keyboard/focus continuity, and measurable work.

USER SURFACE
A concise descriptor over item count, fixed extent, viewport/scroll state, stable item identity, caller-supplied row content, semantic parts, and explicit selection/focus intents. It is sufficient for ordinary large lists/tables, not a data-grid product.

LAWS
Visible-window calculation is pure; keyed row identity survives window movement; one row update does not subscribe/render every row; focus and keyboard navigation remain coherent; scroll host facts do not become a second state system; SSR/structure state the finite rendered window honestly.

HOST/MODE
JVM structural calculations, interpreted and compiled browser paths, large-list performance evidence under D021, and exact scroll/listener cleanup.

CANONICAL OWNERS
Product-completion DC-04 and ER-05; D002/D003/D004/D010/D017/D018/D021; spec/004/004D/008/009 plus applicable FH-STRUCT/FH-CTRL/FH-DIAG rows.

NON-GOALS
No variable-height engine, spreadsheet/data-grid, sorting/filtering/query engine, selection framework, or automatic compile promotion.

ACCEPTANCE
1. 10,000-row and approximately 40-visible-window fixtures prove equal structure/DOM and stable keyed identity across interpreted/compiled modes.
2. Deterministic counters report visible rows, row commits, dependency fan-out, comparator work, allocations and cleanup before timing.
3. Keyboard, focus, selection and scroll behavior pass real-browser tests.
4. The same fixture can be reused by the v/$ comparison without coupling the production control to its experimental implementation.
5. The workshop/guide shows a short re-com-porting-quality call site and states omitted data-grid features plainly.
notes:
PR #7180 open. All local gates green (JVM 1245/8405, node 1330/7351, browser 847/5497 x4 runs, prod-elision 120/526, roster 10/66, conformance index + 3 adjacent python gates).

MAJOR FINDING — rf2-86i64 (P1) FILED: the corpus ALREADY contained re-frame.freehand.pilot-virtual-table (1622 lines under test/, from rf2-eq2vx / rf2-g5xxv / rf2-drpa3.176). I did not find it before building — my test-tree sweep was truncated and my greps looked for control/collection, never table. It proves most of the same windowing laws as CONSUMER code but cites no FH id and is in neither the index nor the roster, so this PR is its promotion into a shipped enrolled control rather than a competing design. Two implementations now exist; rf2-86i64 offers three resolutions, one of which (promote the pilot, discard this implementation) is a REWRITE of #7180 rather than a follow-up. The pilot is STRONGER in one place: restore-scroll, a :layout behavior moving a live viewport back to a persisted offset before paint, which this control has no seam for. Recorded in the control docstring, in a PR comment and in an IMPORTANT banner on the PR body.

CI: the browser-test job failed once on a 120s timeout. Confirmed a load flake and re-run — green on main (last 6 runs), the suite had NOT run when the clock expired (last Testing line was the namespace immediately before it), and an A/B locally measured 68s with the suite vs 71s without. That runner compiled in 77s vs 17s locally with four sibling witness PRs in CI. NOTE: the lane has very little headroom at 120s and four witness PRs each add a mounted suite - a shared-capacity problem that will bite whoever merges last.

ID COLLISION unchanged: #7180/#7181/#7182 all claim FH-CTRL-019; recipe posted on #7180.

ALSO FILED: rf2-cfhuv - the namespace is absent from the API-manifest allow-list.
close_reason:
PR #7180 merged as FH-CTRL-021 (Package A of the rf2-86i64 ruling). The fixed-size virtual collection witness is on main.

WHY IT TOOK A REBASE AND A RENUMBER: it was one of five witnesses built in parallel, three of which claimed FH-CTRL-019 because the conformance index allocates ordinals dense-and-ascending. The splitter merged first and took 019, the typeahead renumbered to 020, this took 021. It also went DIRTY against main by creating a fixture at the path the splitter's now occupies. The branch was REBUILT on current main rather than replayed — a faithful commit-by-commit rebase would have clobbered main's file — with all five namespaces restored byte-identically by blob SHA, and 202 changed lines vs the pre-rebase tip of which ZERO lacked the ordinal.

WHAT THE RULING ADDED BEYOND THE ORIGINAL WITNESS: the semantic-neutral engine (virtual-collection owns viewport, canvas, keyed positioned shells and the window arithmetic, names no role, hands its row slot key/absolute-index/total; virtual-list is a listbox wrapper with no second arithmetic and no second scroll host — machine-checked by the manifest, engine [:on-scroll :spread-safe], listbox []), and the controlled :scroll-offset, which ports the pilot's guarded :layout seam as reconcile-scroll, writing before paint only when the node disagrees. No opt-out; :restore-scroll? not ported. The application's :inbox/scroll-to effect was DELETED, so no host-writing effect remains and every scrollTop the browser suite reads is a fact about the collection.

ONE DESIGN DETAIL FORCED BY THE COMPILER, worth inheriting: the engine takes viewport attributes as an explicit :attrs map, because the compiled grammar refuses a render-slot callback anywhere but a LITERAL call-site prop map — so a wrapper cannot merge its props and also pass :row.

A GAP THE WORKER'S OWN CHANGE OPENED, AND CLOSED: the split renders two nodes per row, and the teardown residue read counted only [data-part='row'], so a leaked shell would have been invisible. It now reads three books. :residue :none still holds across 3 cycles x 8 stops, 318 counted row renders, exact zeroes after teardown.

FOLLOW-ONS: rf2-cfhuv must write its manifest roster against SEVEN public names, not the branch's original five — virtual-collection and reconcile-scroll were added. Package B (rf2-pa57v) can now retire the pilot's component half; still owed there and not claimed here are surviving-row DOM node identity across a real scroll, and reorder carrying the row element.

title: Control witness: first-party splitter with pointer and keyboard laws
description:
OUTCOME
Deliver a small first-party splitter control as the third accepted control witness, proving pointer/keyboard ownership and the high-rate host/semantic boundary with a re-com-style everyday call site.

USER SURFACE
Controlled split value with semantic started/optional-preview/committed intents, orientation and bounds, keyboard increments, semantic parts, and an ordinary application-owned persistence story. Visual skins remain replaceable.

LAWS
Pointer capture, lost capture, cancellation, blur, keyboard, RTL/orientation, bounds, and teardown are explicit. Host-local drag geometry may update at host rate; app-db receives only the semantic stream the application chooses. No hidden local state system or unmount domain event.

HOST/MODE
Pure calculations/JVM structure plus real-browser interpreted and compiled parity or honest limitation. Measure offered pointer events, accepted intents, reducer work, commits, presentation and cleanup.

CANONICAL OWNERS
Product-completion DC-04/DC-09 and ER-05; D003/D004/D009/D013/D017/D018/D021; spec/004-Views.md, 008, 009 and applicable control/input/behavior evidence rows.

NON-GOALS
No general gesture framework, drag-and-drop system, generic throttle verb, layout DSL, or full re-com compatibility layer.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Short call site and migration note cover the common re-com split-pane use without mimicking its API.
2. Browser proof covers pointer capture/loss/cancel, keyboard, focus, bounds, orientation/RTL, HMR and exact teardown.
3. High-rate measurements distinguish host offers, accepted semantic events and commits.
4. The witness adds no scheduling vocabulary unless the separate DC-09 evidence gate is met.

title: Ownership routing with Google Maps, Framer Motion, and Radix witnesses
description:
OUTCOME
Publish the ownership-routing guide and prove the two expensive routes: a behavior-owned Google Maps overlay with an explicit nested Freehand root, and a React-primary compound region registered through v/defhost.

ROUTING
Cover pure/headless cores, value/callback React components, hook/context/ref/compound React owners, imperative SDK behaviors, v/->react, host-created panes/nested roots, and explicit islands. State permanent limits and costs beside recoveries.

WITNESSES
1. Google Maps: behavior owns root identity, explicit frame selection, host-removal callback, update, and one idempotent reclamation path shared by host removal and disconnect.
2. Framer Motion: one exit-retention owner per keyed subtree; React-owned animation protocol remains React-primary.
3. Radix UI (or an equivalently popular hook/context/ref/compound library if dependency evidence requires substitution): wrapper uses v/defhost; asChild/ref cloning remains inside React ownership.

EVIDENCE
Each witness publishes top-level exports, boundary crossings, irreducible glue sites, and approximate glue lines as comparative evidence, plus explicit context/evidence/SSR loss. Counts are not a score or threshold.

HOST/MODE
Mounted browser and cleanup first; structural/SSR evidence where the route can honestly provide it; interpreted/compiled claims explicit.

NON-GOALS
No v/->element, behavior outlet, mount-child, portal manager, neutral hooks/refs, or promise that nested roots inherit outer context/Suspense/bubbling.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Maps ends with zero roots/listeners after host removal, disconnect, either order, and repeated reclamation.
2. Framer Motion and Radix witnesses preserve their native React protocols through the one host kind.
3. The routing page lets a programmer select the route from ownership facts, not library branding.
4. Any proposal for a new primitive cites Maps plus a second independent repetition and explicitly amends D013/D015; otherwise no proposal is filed.
notes:
EVIDENCE CLAUSE — DISCHARGED. PR #7251 (worker/evidence-counts-18209), opened green locally. The projection pass's PR #7244 is MERGED (2026-07-28), so acceptance 3's pending-merge hold is also released. All four numbered ACCEPTANCE criteria plus the EVIDENCE clause are now discharged — THIS BEAD CAN CLOSE.

THE FOUR COUNTS, PER WITNESS (exports / crossings / glue sites / glue lines):
  FH-REACT-009    compound React owner (Radix-shaped)         1 / 2 / 0 / 0
  FH-REACT-010    clock owner (Framer-Motion-shaped)          2 / 3 / 1 / 1
  FH-BEHAVIOR-010 imperative SDK + host-created pane (Maps)   1 / 2 / 4 / 27
  pure / headless core — THE CONTROL                          0 / 0 / 0 / 0

HOW THEY WERE OBTAINED: by READING the declarations, not by running anything. These are static properties of a route — they do not vary between node and a browser, so there is no runtime to label and no range across rounds to report. Each fixture carries `:method :read-from-source` in the value itself rather than leaving a reader to assume it was measured. Nothing asserts them and nothing gates on them; per the clause they are not a score or a threshold, and the largest route is largest because the library owns the most.

ONE DEFINITION, IN ONE PLACE. `docs/core/freehand/host/ownership-routing.md` §"What the counts count" defines export / crossing / glue site / glue line ONCE for all three witnesses — three definitions in three files would have been three incomparable numbers. Each fixture then writes out its own arithmetic name by name INCLUDING THE EXCLUSIONS: the library's own side (a wrapper composing a compound library's parts is React code an author writes in a pure-React app too, which is why Radix's glue is honestly 0 and not a sleight of hand), the application, and the fixture's measurement apparatus (Maps' two `:commands`, Radix's `as-child-probe`).

THE CONTROL is the check on the definition: a library that owns nothing routes to nothing, so the pure/headless core must be four zeros, and a definition producing anything else there would be the thing that was wrong. Maps' 27 glue lines were also reproduced mechanically — 1 + 8 + 14 + 3 + 1 over `reclaim!`, `:connect`, `:update`, `:disconnect`, with the suite's own `entries`/`worked` bookkeeping excluded.

NOTHING WAS LEFT OUT. All four quantities are well defined for all three hosts, so there is no honest-gap entry to report.

`:evidence :limits` GAINS ITS OTHER HALF. It carried what the PROOF cannot reach (no `google.maps`, no Radix packages, no `framer-motion`); each fixture now also carries a third entry stating what the ROUTE permanently loses. FH-BEHAVIOR-010: the island inherits no outer React context, Suspense or bubbling; the SDK's subtree is a leaf with no structural render and nothing in any manifest; no SSR for either tree since a behavior connects only on commit. FH-REACT-009: React context does not survive a Freehand boundary (which is WHY the wrapper is registered and not the parts), the withheld asChild/ref promise in the other direction, one manifest crossing with nothing under it, portalled content outside the container, `:ssr :client-only`. FH-REACT-010: retention lives in a ref no substrate vocabulary reaches, the retained child is on the page and in none of Freehand's books, `:ssr :client-only`.

NOTHING QUALITATIVE WAS REVISED. The routing page's verified claims are untouched; this pass only ADDS one section, one paragraph and a `:comparative` key plus a third `:limits` entry per fixture. `:evidence` sub-keys are free-form to the roster spine (only `:residue` is validated), so no roster.cljc change was needed and none was made — no overlap with the sibling worker on deps.edn / core.

GATES (foreground, worktree-local, exit echoed, never piped): check_freehand_conformance_index.py exit 0; freehand JVM clojure -M:test exit 0 (1288/8856, 0 failures, guide digest roster 114 of 138 unchanged); python -m mkdocs build --strict exit 0 (no new warning); npm run test:browser exit 0 (842/5469); scripts/test-freehand-prod-gate.sh exit 0 (137 of 137, 0 excluded as known-red — roster empty, not regressed).
close_reason:
CLOSED — FREEHAND IS A FAILED EXPERIMENT (Mike, 2026-07-30). Verbatim ruling: close out the Freehand EPIC as a failed experiment, no further work to be done on it, but not removed yet.

WHY IT FAILED. The Reagent standard (rf2-lbs3y, Mike 2026-07-27: 'Freehand can't be used if it is slower than Reagent') was not met, and the residual gap is architectural rather than an optimisation backlog. Interpreted Freehand measured ~5x Reagent on bulk repaint and ~1.6x on mount.

DO NOT REPEAT THE SUPERSEDED REASON. An earlier summary said the cost WAS the invariant-5 tear check. rf2-so3io / PR #7159 falsified that by ablation: dropping useSyncExternalStore AND the commit-side re-read returned only -13.6%/-14.8% on the broad clock and -375 B heap, and a contract-free boundary was still ~5.5x Reagent on clock and ~5x on heap. The guarantee was not what cost us — and the same ablation found invariant 5 is worth MORE than Spec 006 claims, since a staged site without it publishes stale and never self-heals.

THE CODE STAYS. 'Not removed yet.' No implementation/freehand/** deletion, no build-id removal, no CI lane or roster change. The Freehand prod-gate lane (137 of 137, roster empty) keeps running until an explicit removal ruling.

NORMATIVE HALF: rf2-lgleu (P1) records the withdrawal in the EP corpus — EP-0036 moves to Status: withdrawn per EP-0009's closed vocabulary, and the six EPs citing Freehand stop implying it is live.

DO NOT re-file this work as follow-ups. The programme is retracted, not paused.

title: test.yml: tools/testbed-support and tools/machines-viz JVM suites gate no CI job
description:
Found while fixing the orphan the rf2-4hc9p bijection gate reported (PR #6988).

tools/testbed-support ships a fully wired :test alias (32 tests / 153 assertions, green, ~6s) whose suite ran in NO lane at all: open_in_editor_server_test.clj is .clj, so the node-test-testbed-support CLJS build that carries the tree on its source paths cannot load it, and the artefact was on neither JVM roster. PR #6988 added it to scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh's sibling scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh so the LOCAL lane exists.

It still has no CI job. test.yml's jvm-tools-* family is xray / story / story-mcp / mcp-base / template; the all-required-passed aggregator lists those five. So two entries on the local tools roster gate nothing in CI:

  tools/testbed-support        (no job at all)
  tools/machines-viz           (on the local roster, no jvm-tools-machines-viz job)
  tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab  (verify: it may be covered by an mcp-conformance job rather than a jvm-tools-* one)

Conversely tools/template has a CI job (jvm-tools-template) but is NOT on scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh's roster, so a template-only change gets no local JVM lane. The two rosters should agree, in both directions.

test.yml is hot-zone, so this is deliberately a separate PR rather than folded into the gate that found it. The cheap shape is: add the missing jvm-tools-* jobs (each is seconds), add tools/template to the local roster, and add the new jobs to the all-required-passed needs list.

A follow-on detector is possible and is the durable fix: the bijection gate's universe today is files on a lane root, so a test tree on NO roster is invisible to it. Repo-wide there are ~15 more deftest-bearing trees outside every roster it reads (tools/template/test, skills/*/tests, migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod, implementation/ui/scaffold-smoke). Asserting the two rosters against test.yml's job list would close that class, but it needs a workflow-job parser.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #6995 (completeness): despite the PR title and body naming rf2-as6bg, the landed patch is exactly one commit changing only docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md (20 additions, 1 deletion). No scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh or .github/workflows/test.yml change landed, so the local/CI roster mismatch remains fully open under this exact owner; do not infer completion from PR #6995's title.
AUDIT PR #6998 (2026-07-25): PARTIAL COMPLETION VERIFIED; keep this exact owner open. The landed patch truthfully fixes the landable half: `tools/template` is now on the local JVM roster, and `tools/testbed-support/**` now arms the existing node and browser jobs with focused classifier assertions. The corrected machines-viz comment also stops claiming its JVM suite does not exist. The remaining acceptance is unchanged and explicit: `tools/machines-viz` and `tools/testbed-support` still need real PR-time JVM jobs, their classifier routing, and required-aggregator edges; setting the shared `tools_jvm` bit alone would run unrelated jobs while still skipping these artefacts. No duplicate Bead. Both authored commits map one-for-one to the landed commits by stable patch-id; all 73 PR checks were non-failing; local changed-surfaces, test-lane-bijection, doc-slug, and diff checks passed. The companion docs-only note reorder is correct, but does not close rf2-boyep: that exact owner already records the still-unqualified 401 hook that treats a bad login as session expiry.
close_reason:
PR #7116 (commit 238264ec0b). The bead's own 'cheap shape' had already landed in #6998/#7055 and I verified it on main before touching anything: the two rosters are bijective at 8 artefacts each way, and tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab is covered by mcp-conformance-wire-vocab (differently named, not missing). What was still open is what the bead calls THE DURABLE FIX, and that is what landed.

scripts/check_jvm_lane_rosters.py asserts scripts/test-jvm-{implementation,tools}.sh against test.yml's required-job list in BOTH directions: R1 every rostered artefact is run by a job in all-required-passed's needs (a job absent from that list is advisory, whatever its own gate says); R2 every required job running clojure -M:test has its directory on a roster. Rosters and jobs are READ, never listed.

WHY THE BIJECTION GATE COULD NEVER HAVE CAUGHT THIS: check_test_lane_bijection.py READS the rosters to discover the JVM lanes, so an artefact missing from a roster is not a violation to it -- it is simply not a lane. The gate that finds orphan FILES takes the roster as ground truth, so the roster is exactly what it cannot check. Worth remembering as a shape: a gate that derives its universe from a config cannot also validate that config.

Mutation-proved three ways against the LIVE tree, not fixtures: drop jvm-tools-machines-viz from the aggregator -> R1 fires naming it advisory; drop tools/testbed-support from the roster -> R2 fires; add an unbuilt artefact -> R1 fires. Its hand-rolled stdlib parser cross-checks exactly against yaml.safe_load: identical 64-job set, identical 63-entry needs list, identical defaults working-directory for all 30 JVM jobs, zero mismatches.

Wired into the fast PR spine and CI's always-on verify-readme-links job. Two pre-existing implementation-side drifts are BASELINED with the bead that clears them (rf2-ftmh0): implementation/adapters/test-react is rostered with no CI job (fixing it adds a REQUIRED check on implementation/adapters/**), and implementation/freehand/scaffold-smoke is run by the required ui-scaffold-smoke job with no roster slot (one line, but that tree had a live worker).
