title: tools/{story,xray,machines-viz}: 52 .cljc test suites that no CLJS lane selects
description:
Found mechanically by the rf2-4hc9p test-lane bijection gate (scripts/check_test_lane_bijection.py, PR #6988).

The three tools test trees are on the consolidated :node-test build's :source-paths (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn lists ../tools/story/test, ../tools/xray/test, ../tools/machines-viz/test) but are only PARTIALLY converted to the dual-runtime *_cljs_test.cljc convention:

  tools/story/test        27 .cljc CLJS-selected, 43 NOT
  tools/xray/test         38 CLJS-selected,        7 NOT
  tools/machines-viz/test 18 CLJS-selected,        2 NOT

That is the rf2-ezbzvm class (a .cljc whose ns ends -test instead of -cljs-test is invisible to the cljs-test$ selector) with 52 live instances. ~20 of the 52 carry #?(:cljs ...) arms in their BODIES, i.e. they contain CLJS code that never executes; the rest are portable and may be JVM-only by intent. One is explicit about the opposite: tools/story/test/re_frame/story/run_owner_cljc_test.cljc documents 'Runs on BOTH runtimes' while its ns ends -cljc-test, which cljs-test$ does not match. tools/story/test/re_frame/story/viewport_test.cljc documents the opposite intent in prose.

The bijection gate's B2 rule deliberately does not reach these: it applies to test roots the CLJS build OWNS (a :source-paths entry local to the shadow project), not to a ../-escaping entry -- a foreign tree borrowed onto the classpath whose lane is defined by its own deps.edn. They are held by B1 (they DO run, on the JVM), so the gate is green. Widening B2 to reach them requires this work first.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD. This is not a rename sweep: rf2-ezbzvm's own experience was that enabling nine such files in the shared node-test bundle EXPOSED two fixtures that called registrar/clear-all! without restoring, breaking sibling namespaces. Doing 52 at once needs per-file triage (does it want CLJS at all?), fixture-isolation review, and a real test:cljs count comparison. Per-file outcome is one of: rename to -cljs-test (dual-runtime), or declare JVM-only. Once every file has taken one of those two, B2's ownership predicate can be widened to the borrowed roots too and the gate holds the result.
notes:
STAYS OPEN ON THE WORKER RECOMMENDATION, and the reason is a real structural blocker rather than remaining effort.

WHAT LANDED (PR #7063, rf2-odlm3 arm): tools/machines-viz/shadow-cljs.edn with a :machines-viz-node-test build, selector scoped to the artefact prefix — NO RENAME, nothing joins the shared bundle. 821/3214 rc=0, both previously-unselected suites mutation-proved to execute, and THE OWNERSHIP MOVE ITSELF MUTATION-PROVED: narrow the selector back and the bijection B2 predicate names both files by path where before it said nothing. Bijection gate PASS at 45 lanes, up from 44.

CENSUS RE-DERIVED with the gate own parser and it matches the corrected premise exactly: 140 .cljc, 57 unselected, 52 define tests, 25 carry :cljs arms.

WHY XRAY AND STORY CANNOT HAVE THE SAME LANE YET — three reasons, and the second is the blocker:
  1. shadow-cljs resolves :deps {:aliases [...]} via clojure -A:<alias> and INHERITS :main-opts, so an artefact :test alias hands shadow arguments to cognitect test-runner. Every lane needs a duplicate, divergable alias.
  2. XRAY TEST TREE ESCAPES ITS OWN DEPENDENCY GRAPH FOUR TIMES — into Freehand TEST tree, into re-frame.story (WHICH DECLARES XRAY AS A HARD DEP, SO THE EDGE CANNOT BE A DEPENDENCY WITHOUT A CYCLE), into a testbed namespace, and into implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/src. A per-tool lane for Xray would be the consolidated classpath under a new name. Story is the same shape and larger.
  3. Two genuinely UNDER-DECLARED DEPS IN THE PUBLISHED machines-viz JAR (uix.core, re-frame.adapter.reagent) — filed as rf2-3d5u3, declared test-only here, published graph untouched.

THE HONEST NEXT STEP IS ARTEFACT WORK, NOT CI WORK: make the test trees separable first. Four concrete :requires are enumerated on this bead. Do not dispatch a CI lane for Xray or Story until that lands — it would produce a lane that looks per-tool and is not.
close_reason:
PR #7116 (commits 64e023f556 + 33a9eda637). THE XRAY ARM IS DONE; STORY IS DELIBERATELY NOT, and the bead's own analysis is why.

WHAT LANDED: the seven .cljc suites under tools/xray/test whose namespaces ended -test rather than -cljs-test renamed to *_cljs_test.cljc with reader-conditional clojure.test/cljs.test requires. NO build config change -- tools/xray/test is already on the consolidated :node-test source paths -- and the ns still ends -test, so cognitect keeps them in the JVM lane. This is the half that needed NO LANE, ONLY THE SELECTOR, which is why it was landable while a per-tool lane is not. Xray unselected: 7 -> 0.

ARMING THEM FOUND A REAL PRODUCTION BUG ON THE FIRST RUN, which is this bead's thesis demonstrated rather than argued. palette/fuzzy.cljc computed (int ch) on a character taken from a string: a code point on the JVM, but cljs.core/int is (bit-or x 0) and JavaScript coerces a non-numeric string to 0, while (nth some-string idx) yields a ONE-CHARACTER STRING under CLJS. So upper? and lower? answered false for EVERY character in the browser -- the only place Xray's command palette runs -- and both bonuses depending on them went dead: word-start?'s camelCase branch and the explicit camel-boundary bonus in the scoring loop. Separator word-starts kept working (\- and friends compare fine as one-character strings), which is precisely why nothing else in the file noticed. The file's own docstring claimed 'every assertion runs equally under JVM clojure.test and the cljs node-test runtime' and that was false.

GENERALISABLE SHAPE: a .cljc helper that indexes into a string is a cross-runtime trap -- Character vs one-character String -- and it is INVISIBLE while the suite runs on one runtime. Suspect (int ch), (Character/...), and ^Character hints in any .cljc that no CLJS lane selects.

REGRESSION PIN: camelcase-boundary-bonus caught it incidentally (two different strings, so a weight change could make it pass for the wrong reason). Added camel-boundary-credited-on-both-runtimes, which isolates the mechanism: same-length separator-free candidates matched at the same two indices, so only the camelCase boundary can separate the scores, and the separator path cannot satisfy it. Mutation-proved BOTH directions on the real lane: restore (int ch) -> 2 failures rc=1; restore char-code -> 11758 tests / 0 failures rc=0.

EVIDENCE: all seven suites mutation-proved to execute (one sentinel deftest each -> exactly seven FAILs naming the seven paths, 11764 tests, reverted). tools/xray clojure -M:test 1271/5909 rc=0. Bijection gate PASS at 45 lanes. tools/xray/spec/017 updated (the hidden-indicator row named the old filename).

STORY'S 43 STAY OPEN-BY-DESIGN, NOT UNFINISHED: re-verified both blockers still hold. Xray's test tree escapes its dependency graph into re-frame.freehand and re-frame.story, and Story declares Xray as a HARD DEP, so that edge cannot become a dependency without a cycle. A per-tool lane for either would be the consolidated classpath under a new name. File a fresh bead against the artefact-separability work if Story's 43 are wanted; do not re-file this one as a CI task.

title: Freehand census: read a TAGGED LITERAL as the two-datum prefix it is (`#js`, `#inst`, `#?`)
description:
Found while discharging the `MERGED-PR AUDIT #6968` metadata-extent reopen on
rf2-drpa3.53 (PR #6984). REPRODUCED, NOT INFERRED. Deliberately NOT fixed there:
the dispatching mayor scoped that bead to `^` and asked not to be handed a silent
scope expansion.

THE SAME ARITHMETIC, A DIFFERENT PREFIX. `_datum_end` in
`scripts/check_freehand_conformance_index.py` now reads `^` as consuming its
metadata and then the annotated target. A TAGGED LITERAL has exactly that shape -
`#tag datum` - and is still read as consuming the tag alone:

    _datum_end("#js {:a fx}")        -> "#js"        (should be the whole literal)
    _datum_end('#inst "2020"')       -> "#inst"
    _datum_end("#?(:clj x :cljs y)") -> "#?"
    _datum_end("#?@(:clj [x])")      -> "#?@"

REPRODUCED against PR #6984's script, both false-green axes of the family:

  * (is (= '#js [fx] 1)) on a row bound to `fx` -> `fx` is read as a live
    reference, because the quote's extent ends after `#js` and `[fx]` stays in
    code. Same for the syntax-quoted twin. Neither evaluates the Var.
  * #_#?(:clj (def fx (conf/fixture :FH-CALL-001))) discards only `#?`, so the
    `(:clj (def fx ...))` list survives and the discarded proof site binds a
    fixture the reader never sees.

LATENT TODAY, NOT LIVE - measured, so the priority is honest. `#js` appears 143
times in `implementation/freehand/test/`, plus 2 `#inst`, 2 `#uuid` and 1
`#queue`, but ZERO of them sit behind a quote prefix or a `#_`, which are the only
positions where extent causes blanking. So no row is currently false-green from
it and the `--report` table would not move. It is a loaded gun rather than a
discharged one: the next author who writes `(is (= '#js [fx] 1))` gets a silent
green, and `#js` is the most common reader macro in the CLJS corpus by two orders
of magnitude.

rf2-mom1g DOES NOT FIRE ON THIS, on the test the mayor recorded for it: this can
be stated as "this existing pass mis-handles form X", not "this needs the pass to
know something only evaluation knows". No dataflow, no binding resolution, no
macro expansion. It is lexically closable by the same recursion `^` now uses.

THE FIX, AND WHY IT WANTS ITS OWN REVIEW RATHER THAN A FOLD-IN. One branch in
`_datum_end`: a `#` followed by a tag character consumes the tag datum and then
its target. But it needs an EXCLUSION LIST that `^` did not - `#'` is a var quote
(one datum), `#(`, `#{`, `#"` are dispatch forms whose datum is the delimited form
itself, and `#_` is already handled upstream. `'` and `_` are both inside
`_SYMBOL_HEAD`, so the naive "symbol character after `#`" rule mis-reads `#'x`.
That exclusion list is the part worth a reviewer's eye, and it is why this is a
bead rather than three more lines on a PR that had a different subject.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `_datum_end` reads `#tag datum` whole, including `#?(...)` and `#?@(...)`,
   with `#'`, `#(`, `#{`, `#"` and `#_` unchanged - proof: the four extents above
   return the whole literal, and a self-test pins each.
2. Red/control pairs on BOTH axes for BOTH quote spellings, in the established
   idiom: `'#js [fx]` and its syntax-quoted twin red at DEAD PROOF SITE;
   `'#js [panel]` beside `(v/defview panel {:compiled true} ...)` reds at
   UNWITNESSED MODE; `#_#?(:clj (def fx ...))` reds at DEAD PROOF SITE.
3. The over-tightening controls, which are the ones that matter here: an UNQUOTED
   `#js [fx]` still reads the fixture, and `'#'fx` has an extent of exactly
   `'#'fx` so a trailing `fx` beside it stays live. Both must be shown red if the
   exclusion list is wrong.
4. Every new case fails before the fix and passes after, both directions shown.
5. The per-row `--report` table stays byte-identical (md5
   bdb95d24524b6a460a687b408a7b1a48 as of PR #6984), and the live census stays
   exit 0.
notes:
SHIPPED in PR #7110 (worker/census-tagged-jl7gz).

THE FIX. `_prefix_end` now stops at a tag `#` the way it already stops at `^`, and `_datum_end` reads both with one recursive two-datum step. All four named inputs return the whole literal. Reproduced the false green first: `(is (= '#js [fx] 1))` had `fx` live because the quote's extent ended after '#js.

THE EXCLUSION LIST, stated positively - a `#` heads a two-datum dispatch when a symbol could start where it points, or a `:` does - with three shapes named out: `#'` (var quote), `#_` (discard), and a LOOKBEHIND for `##Inf`/`##NaN`. That third one is NOT hypothetical: `##NaN` is written straight into the adapter suites, and my first draft regressed `##Inf` to `##Inf 3`. The new extent table caught it.

BEYOND THE BEAD'S FOUR INPUTS, declared not silent: namespaced maps `#:ns{...}` / `#::{...}` are the same two-datum reach spelled with a `:`, measured zero occurrences in the scanned corpus, and included because excluding them would have been the EXTRA rule. Swept every other `#` dispatch: `#(`/`#{`/`#"` need no naming (none of those chars is a symbol head); `#=` gets the same extent either way; `#!` has zero occurrences in any .clj/.cljc/.cljs (the repo's hits are all .cjs shebangs the census never reads).

THE BEAD'S OWN AXIS-2 CASE CANNOT DISCRIMINATE, and this is the finding worth keeping. `#_#?(:clj (def fx ...))` reds under the OLD reader too. The reason is not the extent - read short it does leave `(:clj (def fx ...))` standing, exactly as described - but `_DEFINER_RE` is anchored to the head of a top-level form and the survivor's head is `:clj`, not `def`, so no binding registers and the row reds either way. The wrapper the miscount leaves is INERT. A TAG target is what discriminates, because there the survivor IS the form: `#_#js (def fx ...)` read short leaves the def at top level to bind the fixture -> silent green. Kept the `#?` case anyway, labelled as a regression guard on the top-level anchoring rather than as evidence.

PROOF. Self-test 96 -> 135: a new direct `_EXTENT_CASES` table (26, both directions - the exclusion list has no census-level symptom, so a mini-repo could not tell a correct reading from a lucky one) plus 13 mini-repo cases, 6 red / 7 green. Two of the greens were RED before the fix (the `~#js [fx]` unquote island and reader-conditional arm pairing), so the miscount was dropping real edges as well as inventing them.

GATES. Both CI commands exit 0 locally and 'Freehand conformance index' passes on CI. The per-row --report table is BYTE-IDENTICAL before/after, measured on one rebased tree with main's reader then mine: md5 e8ebf9d786a96d5b8e58e722d67cdc6a, 107 applicable / 107 reached / 108 total / 4 compiled. No row moves - expected, since the bead measured zero corpus exposure. (The bead's md5 bdb95d24... predates 83 commits of corpus movement; before==after on one tree is the invariant that survives.)

MUTATION-VERIFIED THREE WAYS, each confirmed applied via git diff --stat + grepping the marker back out before reading the verdict: reverting both functional lines fails 21 cases (14 extent, 7 mini-repo: 5 false-green, 2 false-red); dropping (?!['_]) fails 3; dropping (?<!#) fails 2.

ONE HONEST CAVEAT: only the `'` half of that exclusion is load-bearing. The `_` half changes just `'#_x y`, where it PRESERVES the pre-existing reading, and `_strip` eliminates every `#_` before any downstream pass asks about extent. Defensive, not weight-bearing.

NOTE ON THE DEFERRAL: this bead carried a 'STAYS DEFERRED - measured zero corpus exposure' note from the #7051 audit. The mayor dispatched it anyway; flagging rather than silently overriding. rf2-mom1g is NOT engaged either way - its own practical test ('can the fix be stated as this existing pass mis-handles form X') answers YES, and its notes already record that it does not fire on a defect in the shipped reduction.

title: docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md's reg-error-projector example is non-conformant: a reader who pastes it silently gets the locked generic-500 instead of their projector
description:
Found by the pre-alpha docs/comments review lens (rf2-ods8n). The most consequential prose-vs-code defect that lens found: the documented example does the OPPOSITE of what the page says it does, silently, with no error the reader will notice.

THE EXAMPLE. docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:369-373:
    (rf/reg-error-projector :app/public-error
      (fn [trace-event]
        {:status  500
         :message "Something went wrong."}))

THE CONTRACT. implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_projector.cljc:73-77 -- `public-error-keys` is #{:status :code :message :retryable?}, "The four locked keys". And :98-105 -- `public-error-shape?` was TIGHTENED (rf2-oytx7j) to a CLOSED shape: `(= public-error-keys (set (keys x)))`. EXACTLY the four keys, no extra and none missing.

CONSEQUENCE. The two-key return is non-conformant, so `project-error` emits `:rf.error/sanitised-on-projection` and returns `fallback-public-error` -- the locked generic 500. The projector the reader just registered is discarded on EVERY error, forever, and the page''s own :391 text convicts the example: "If the projector throws or returns a non-conforming shape, this emits `:rf.error/sanitised-on-projection` and returns the locked generic-500 fallback." So the page states the rule 22 lines below the example that breaks it. :441 states it a third time ("Conformant projector output carries exactly these").

TWO MORE SITES WITH THE SAME 3-OR-FEWER-KEY SHAPE
  - docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:393 -- the `project-error` example return is commented `;; => {:status 404 :code :not-found :message "Page not found"}`. Actual (error_projector.cljc:166-169) includes `:retryable? false`; `:retryable?` is one of the four locked keys and is ALWAYS present.
  - docs/ssr/glossary.md:43 -- "maps a rich internal trace to a sanitized, client-safe `:rf/public-error` shape (`:status`, `:code`, `:message`)". Three keys. A reader writing that shape from the glossary hits the same silent fallback.

ACCEPTANCE
1. The reg-error-projector example returns all four locked keys, and is a shape that actually passes public-error-shape? (400..599 status, keyword :code, string :message, boolean :retryable?).
2. The project-error example return comment includes :retryable?.
3. docs/ssr/glossary.md:43 names all four keys.
4. Ideally: consider whether the api-manifest/doc gates can pin a public-error example against public-error-shape? so this class cannot recur -- the current gates check var EXISTENCE, not example conformance, and would not have caught this.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7168 (2026-07-28). PR #7168 correctly made the built-in projector fail safe: only :rf.error/no-such-handler with [:tags :kind] = :route is a 404; :event, :frame, and kind-less misses are server defects and stay 500. The public reg-error-projector example on this same surface was left behind. implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_projector.cljc (and its docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md presentation) still cases only on :operation and maps every :rf.error/no-such-handler to 404. A programmer copying the canonical example therefore reintroduces exactly the misclassification the PR fixed. The API summary also states the mapping without the discriminator. Bounded repair: make both public examples/summaries name and test :kind :route, with all other no-such-handler shapes taking the generic 500; update generated API prose if applicable. No new mechanism or generalized doc gate.
close_reason: PR #7231. The reg-error-projector example branched on :rf.error/no-such-route -- the category docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md itself says a release build never reaches (caller misuse of route-url, dev-gated trace stream). Its only 404 arm was dead under production hardening, while :rf.error/no-such-handler + [:tags :kind] :route (the arm rf2-ov56u promoted onto the always-on axis, and the one PR #7168 gated) fell through to the example's generic 500 -- a real 404 answered 500. Example now branches on no-such-handler and gates on :kind :route. The default-error-projector-fn summary, which stated the mapping with no discriminator while its own next bullet spelled out the sibling :where :event gate, now names the gate and the three :kind misses. reg-error-projector's docstring in error_projector.cljc carried the same pre-#7168 ungated shape for BOTH gated categories (docstring only, no behaviour change) -- corrected per the bead's audit note, which names that file. Acceptance 4: new re-frame.ssr-doc-example-projector-test READS both examples out of the markdown fence at run time and executes them, so it cannot drift from the page; mutation-proved (reverting the 404 arm reds 4 of 13). No gate had caught this because doc-api-check verifies var EXISTENCE, not example conformance, and the runtime suites pin the BUILT-IN projector, never the documented one. Gates: mkdocs --strict 0, check_doc_slugs 0, ssr dev suite 0 (592/2892), test-ssr-prod-gate.sh 0 (594/2722). Swept the page's other examples -- every ';; =>' result claim matches source; nothing to file.

title: RULED (route b): vendor day8/de-dupe into mcp-base; ship story-mcp + mcp-base publish path
description:
rf2-4u3t1 ruled that BOTH `tools/story-mcp` and `tools/machines-viz` get a release path.
The machines-viz half shipped (new `.github/workflows/release-machines-viz.yml` on a
`machines-viz-v*` glob, plus the `:main` fix its `:clein/build` map needed). The story-mcp
half CANNOT be delivered inside that bead's fence, for three reasons found by actually
running clein rather than reading deps.edn. All three verified locally at main bb86e780a2.

## Blocker 1 — `day8/de-dupe` is not on Clojars, and clein cannot express a git coord in a pom

`tools/story-mcp/deps.edn` declares `day8/de-dupe {:git/url … :git/tag "v0.3.0" :git/sha …}`
as a main-`:deps` RUNTIME dependency (the wire-boundary structural dedup, applied before the
wire-cap check). `clojure -M:clein pom` in `tools/story-mcp` reports:

    Skipping coordinate: {:git/url https://github.com/day8/de-dupe.git, :git/tag v0.3.0, …}

and the generated pom carries exactly two dependencies — `org.clojure/clojure` and
`cheshire/cheshire`. This is the same silent-skip behaviour `clein pom` has for `:local/root`
(rf2-do3m2 / #6340), which the `:local/root → :mvn/version` rewrite exists to repair. There
is no equivalent repair for a git coordinate: a Clojars search for `de-dupe` returns no
results, so there is no `:mvn/version` to rewrite it to.

Consequence: publishing `day8/re-frame2-story-mcp` today would ship a jar whose pom omits a
runtime dependency, and a consumer would fail to resolve `de-dupe.*`. That is precisely the
failure class `preflight-story-package.sh` was written to prevent, and Clojars has no yank.
`tools/mcp-base` carries the same coord and the same problem.

Resolving this is a product decision, not a mechanical fix: publish `day8/de-dupe` to
Clojars, vendor it, or accept that these two artefacts are not Clojars-publishable.

## Blocker 2 — `day8/re-frame2-mcp-base` has no release path either, and is un-BUILDABLE

`tools/story-mcp/deps.edn` depends on `day8/re-frame2-mcp-base {:local/root "../mcp-base"}`.
`tools/mcp-base/deps.edn` declares its own publishable `:clein/build {:lib
day8/re-frame2-mcp-base …}` — so story-mcp cannot publish until mcp-base does. mcp-base is
NOT in `verify-version-lockstep.sh`'s four-entry `TOOLS` array, so it is a fifth publishable
tool jar the lockstep gate does not guard. rf2-4u3t1's fence explicitly barred changing that
array, which is why the story-mcp half stopped there rather than quietly publishing an
unguarded coordinate.

mcp-base is also un-buildable for the same reason machines-viz was:

    $ cd tools/mcp-base && clojure -M:clein pom
    Error in the :clein/build map: {:lib day8/re-frame2-mcp-base, …} - failed:
      (contains? % :main) spec: :noahtheduke.clein.specs/build-opts

The day8 clein fork's `build-opts` spec requires `:main`. Every clein invocation in that
directory aborts before doing any work.

## Blocker 3 — the lockstep gate cannot see either failure

Both blockers are invisible to `verify-version-lockstep.sh`: it reads `:version` and the
`:local/root` coordinates, never whether clein would accept the `:clein/build` map, and
never whether a non-`:local/root` runtime coordinate survives into the pom. It reported
"all 17 artefacts … pinned" while `day8/re-frame2-machines-viz` could not be built at all.
Two candidate hardenings, both cheap:

  - assert every `:clein/build` map satisfies clein's own spec (in practice: assert `:main`
    is present, which is the only required key the repo's maps have been missing); and
  - assert every main-`:deps` coordinate for a publishable artefact is a kind `clein pom`
    can express — i.e. flag `:git/url` coords in a publishable artefact's `:deps`, since
    those are dropped silently.

## Suggested order

1. Rule on `day8/de-dupe` (publish / vendor / accept unpublishable). Blocker 1 gates
   everything else; without it neither story-mcp nor mcp-base can ship a correct pom.
2. Add mcp-base to the `TOOLS` inventory (five tools) and give it `:main`.
3. Add the deploy jobs. Per rf2-4u3t1's ruling story-mcp joins the EXISTING
   `release-story.yml` on the EXISTING `story-v*` glob so the pair cannot skew; mcp-base
   needs to deploy ahead of it on that same glob.
4. Harden the lockstep gate per Blocker 3 so this class cannot recur silently.

Nothing here is an alpha blocker: a `v*` tag does not touch `tools/` (re-verified after the
machines-viz work landed), so `v0.0.1.alpha` is unaffected.
notes:
WORKER PASS 2026-07-27 (PR #7123, branch worker/story-mcp-cluster). ALL THREE BLOCKERS RE-VERIFIED AGAINST THE CURRENT TREE AND AGAINST CLOJARS BEFORE ACTING — the bead was accurate on every point. Two are now fixed; Blocker 1 is untouched and STILL THE OPERATOR'S. Deliberately left OPEN and NOT closed.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE BEAD TEXT: the lockstep gate is at .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh, not scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh.

FIXED — Blocker 2 (un-buildable): tools/mcp-base/deps.edn :clein/build now carries :main re-frame.mcp-base.vocab (the shared wire vocabulary, the artefact's primary public surface; same convention as story's :main re-frame.story). Verified: clojure -M:clein pom in tools/mcp-base now EXITS 0 where it previously aborted on (contains? % :main).

FIXED — Blocker 2b (un-inventoried): mcp-base added to TOOLS / TOOLS_PATHS. The gate now reports 18 artefacts (13 implementation/ + 5 tools/), up from 17 (13 + 4).

FIXED — Blocker 3 (gate blind to both classes): two assertions added to the TOOLS loop, both mutation-verified.
  * check_clein_main — asserts :main on every publishable :clein/build. Removing it from mcp-base reds the gate (exit 1, 1 drift, names the file).
  * check_no_git_coords_in_runtime_deps — asserts every main-:deps runtime coordinate is one clein pom can express. Correctly SCOPED to the main :deps map, so alias :extra-deps (clein itself, cognitect test-runner) are ignored; emptying the allowlist reds exactly story-mcp and mcp-base and nothing else.

NOT FIXED, NOT FIXABLE BY A WORKER — Blocker 1, independently reproduced twice:
  (a) clojure -M:clein pom in tools/mcp-base prints 'Skipping coordinate: {:git/url https://github.com/day8/de-dupe.git ...}' and the generated pom carries ONLY org.clojure/clojure.
  (b) https://clojars.org/search?q=de-dupe returns ZERO results; https://clojars.org/day8/de-dupe is a 404. Both re-checked 2026-07-27.
So there is no :mvn/version to rewrite to, and publishing today ships a jar whose pom omits a runtime dependency, with no yank to undo it.

HOW THE PR HANDLES IT WITHOUT PRE-EMPTING THE RULING: GIT_COORD_KNOWN_UNRESOLVED=(day8/de-dupe) — a one-line, comment-documented exception sitting at the exact place the gate would otherwise fire, naming the three routes and instructing 'DELETE THIS LINE when the ruling lands'. NO deploy workflow was added for either coordinate, deliberately: automating a publish while the pom is incomplete would automate the precise failure preflight-story-package.sh exists to prevent. So nothing can ship a broken pom meanwhile, and the open decision is now visible in the gate rather than only in this bead.

USEFUL FOR THE RULING — the vendor option (route b) is SMALL. de-dupe is not vendored anywhere today, and the production footprint is ONE namespace with TWO call sites: tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc calling dd/make-cache-element and dd/de-dupe-eq. Everything else is 4 test namespaces (11 call sites) and 4 deps.edn coordinate declarations (mcp-base, story-mcp, re-frame2-pair-mcp main :deps; mcp-conformance/wire-vocab :test alias). Note story-mcp's own src/ NEVER requires de-dupe.core — it reaches dedup through mcp-base, so its main-:deps entry is a transitive version pin, not a direct use. A JS re-implementation of expand already exists in-tree at tools/mcp-conformance/lib/dedup-envelope.cjs.

REMAINING OPERATOR STEPS (in order): 1. rule on day8/de-dupe (publish / vendor / accept-unpublishable); 2. delete the GIT_COORD_KNOWN_UNRESOLVED line; 3. add the deploy jobs — per rf2-4u3t1 story-mcp joins the EXISTING release-story.yml on the EXISTING story-v* glob, mcp-base deploying ahead of it on that same glob; 4. do the manual first publish per the protocol documented in release-machines-viz.yml's header.

Also filed rf2-gugc3 (P3): docs/release-process.md documents only the thirteen implementation/ artefacts — the five tool jars have no runbook, and four in-repo inventories disagree about what is publishable.
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-27, dossier review): **Route (b) — vendor/absorb the de-dupe codec into re-frame2-mcp-base**, then remove every day8/de-dupe coordinate. Recorded from ai/decisions/rf2-2ii52.de-dupe-publish-path.md (primary analysis + independent Codex review, both recommending (b); the dossier file is deleted after this note — THIS NOTE IS THE CANONICAL RECORD). The operator hold on this bead is RELEASED: it is now the implementation owner and worker-dispatchable per the brief below.

WHY (b):
- Route (a) as written CANNOT work. Upstream day8/de-dupe has a tagged v0.3.0 at the pinned SHA, a .cljc implementation, green JVM/CLJS CI, tools.build packaging, and a tag-triggered Clojars publish workflow — and that workflow actually attempted the publish on 2026-05-13 and received a Clojars 403: "Group 'day8' isn't verified, so can't contain new projects". Clojars' verified-group policy: new projects must use a verified reverse-domain group; a non-reverse-domain group cannot be verified; existing projects in old groups may publish new versions, but day8/de-dupe would be a NEW project. Re-running the workflow cannot create the coordinate — publication would require a NEW coordinate such as io.github.day8/de-dupe. The v0.3.0 tag also predates the upstream fix marking Clojure/ClojureScript POM deps as provided. So (a) really means: new coordinate + new version/tag + group verification + a permanent standalone release surface — ceremony for a micro-library.
- The surface is tiny and wholly owned. de-dupe's entire implementation is one 271-line core.cljc. Production reach in this repo is exactly one namespace — re-frame.mcp-base.dedup — calling make-cache-element and de-dupe-eq. expand is used only by test support; the Node conformance host already carries an independent decoder (tools/mcp-conformance/lib/dedup-envelope.cjs). The story-mcp and pair-mcp direct coordinates are transitive version pins, not distinct production ownership. Everything else is 4 test namespaces (11 call sites) and 4 deps.edn declarations.
- Absorbing fixes a REAL defect that route (a) would freeze into a public artifact: compression IDs come from a namespace-global atom that each call resets. Concurrent JVM calls can interleave a reset with another call's allocation and reuse an ID inside one cache. Vendored under mcp-base, this becomes a call-local counter.
- Route (c) contradicts the standing rf2-4u3t1 ruling (story-mcp gets a release path) and needlessly makes the most AI-oriented tooling harder to consume, for no savings.
- Posture fit: zero new public artifacts, pom complete by construction, one less external moving part. The pre-alpha freedom goes into removing the external coordinate and the global mutable state — not into packaging machinery or renaming working markers.

IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE (from the dossier — binding for the worker):
- One owner, one public concept: re-frame.mcp-base.dedup owns BOTH the forward transform AND the expansion needed by an agent-side Clojure consumer.
- Preserve the existing dedup-table wire shape unless changing it buys something concrete.
- Replace the namespace-global ID atom with a call-local counter while absorbing.
- Retain the canonical cross-host round-trip tests; add MIT provenance per the upstream de-dupe licence.
- Remove all four day8/de-dupe coordinates (mcp-base, story-mcp, re-frame2-pair-mcp main :deps; mcp-conformance/wire-vocab :test alias) and delete the GIT_COORD_KNOWN_UNRESOLVED=(day8/de-dupe) exception line in .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh (its comment says "DELETE THIS LINE when the ruling lands" — this is that ruling).

EXECUTION ORDER (follows the ruling):
1. Vendor per the shape above; delete the GIT_COORD_KNOWN_UNRESOLVED exception line.
2. Add the deploy jobs: story-mcp joins the EXISTING release-story.yml on the EXISTING story-v* glob (per rf2-4u3t1), mcp-base deploying AHEAD of it on that same glob.
3. Manual first publish per the protocol documented in release-machines-viz.yml's header.
4. Related rf2-gugc3 (tool-jar release runbook; four in-repo inventories disagree) is worth folding into the same wave.

CAVEAT FOR STEP 3 (recorded from the dossier; surface to Mike, do NOT solve inside the vendoring PR): the new day8/re-frame2-* Clojars projects are also currently absent, and the same verified-group rule applies to NEW projects in the day8 group. Vendoring resolves the dependency graph but does not by itself make day8/re-frame2-story-mcp / day8/re-frame2-mcp-base claimable — the manual first publish may hit the same 403 unless day8's Clojars standing permits new projects. Verify before tagging; if it fails, that is a release-wide coordinate-policy question for Mike, not a reason to reshape this vendoring.

OWNERSHIP: no split — this bead IS the implementation bead. The description's Blockers 2/2b/3 are already fixed (PR #7123, see the worker-pass note above); remaining scope is exactly this ruling + execution order. Dispatchable now.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-27 — PR #7169 (branch worker/story-publish-2ii52). The ruling's steps 1 and 2 are done; step 3 (manual first publish) is the operator's and is now BLOCKED on rf2-uelji.

VENDORED per the ruling's implementation shape. re-frame.mcp-base.dedup owns the codec outright (de-dupe-eq, expand, cache-element wire shape) alongside the encode policy it already had. Upstream MIT notice + the list of changes made while absorbing sit above the vendored section in dedup.cljc, so they travel inside the jar. Contract-visible changes: (a) the namespace-global cache-id atom is now a call-local volatile!, making cache-id allocation a pure function of the input — pinned by cache-ids-are-allocated-per-call-not-globally plus a JVM pmap round-trip over 32 payloads; (b) the identity-based encoder dropped, hash-fn/equivalent? collapsed to hash/=; (c) unreached upstream surface (map-from-seq, contains-compressed-elements?, partition-decompressed-elements, contains-only-keys?, the dead ::cache meta branch) dropped rather than carried.

WIRE SHAPE UNCHANGED, deliberately: cache elements stay de-dupe.cache/cache-N symbols because the Node conformance decoder, the wire-vocab DedupTable schema and Spec 009 / Tool-Pair all pin that root. cache-keys-are-de-dupe-cache-namespaced-symbols reds the build if someone renames it.

ALL FOUR COORDINATES REMOVED (mcp-base, story-mcp, re-frame2-pair-mcp main :deps; mcp-conformance/wire-vocab :test), and GIT_COORD_KNOWN_UNRESOLVED deleted from verify-version-lockstep.sh. NO allowlist replaced it — an unpublishable runtime coordinate is not a policy exception to record. Mutation-verified: injecting a :git/url runtime dep into mcp-base reds the gate (exit 1, names the file).

PUBLISH PATH. release-story.yml now ships three artefacts on the EXISTING story-v* glob per rf2-4u3t1: mcp-base and story in parallel, story-mcp behind both (needs: edge + clojure -P ordering gate). Two NEW scripts, both DERIVING their coordinate set from the artefact's own committed deps.edn with Clojure's reader rather than listing it — .github/scripts/rewrite-in-repo-coords.sh (every :local/root, refuses on zero rather than passing vacuously) and .github/scripts/preflight-tool-package.sh (required in-repo set + expected third-party set + refusal on an inexpressible coordinate, all from git show HEAD:deps.edn since the workspace copy is rewritten by then; then ElementTree over the generated pom asserting complete GAVs, presence at the lockstep VERSION, and NO extras so an alias leak reds). mcp-base gets no rewrite step: it has no in-repo coordinate and the derived script refuses rather than pretend otherwise.

POM PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED. mcp-base: straight clojure -M:clein pom, exit 0, ZERO 'Skipping coordinate' lines, pom carries org.clojure/clojure 1.12.0 — complete by construction. story-mcp unrewritten: the de-dupe git-coord skip is GONE, only the two :local/root skips remain (the class the rewrite repairs). Rewriting ../mcp-base puts day8/re-frame2-mcp-base 0.0.1.alpha into the pom for real, and the derived preflight then names exactly the one remaining coordinate ('1 of 2 absent: day8/re-frame2-story'). The second cannot be proved locally because it needs day8/re-frame2-story on Clojars — which is the ordering gate clojure -P enforces in the workflow.

LOCKSTEP INVENTORY SEES BOTH: 18 artefacts (13 implementation/ + 5 tools/), 31 in-repo coordinates, story-mcp's two among them.

GATES (foreground, exit codes read): mcp-base JVM 0 (276/934); mcp-base CLJS Node 0 (37/228); story-mcp JVM 0 (306/1605); story-mcp descriptor drift 0; pair-mcp CLJS 0 (1217/4304); pair-mcp descriptor drift 0 (regenerated — 3 tool descriptions told the agent host to call de-dupe.core/expand, now re-frame.mcp-base.dedup/expand); wire-vocab 0 (100/1069); lockstep 0 + mutation 1; preflight mcp-base 0, story-mcp unrewritten 1, part-rewritten 1; derived rewrite 0; skill<->MCP drift 0; sh -n / bash -n / YAML parse / node --check all 0.

NOT TOUCHED (hot zone, reported instead): four prose mentions of day8/de-dupe remain in spec/009-Instrumentation.md (x3) and spec/013-Flows.md (x1) — they now name an absorbed library rather than a dependency. spec/Tool-Pair.md's :de-dupe.cache/cache-N row is CORRECT as-is (that is the wire shape and it did not change). Three more in implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc and two implementation test files, outside the fence.

ATTRIBUTION: upstream de-dupe is MIT, Copyright (c) 2015-2026 Michael Thompson — the same author as this repo, so the obligation is nominal. Full notice ships inside dedup.cljc. Asked in the PR whether a separate repo-level NOTICE/THIRD-PARTY file is also wanted.
AUDIT REOPEN 2026-07-28 — merged PR #7123 (correctness / implementation-quality residual). The consumer-readable story-mcp boundary tests are complete and correctly drive the real wire. The release-gate hardening on this bead is not yet structurally correct: check_no_git_coords_in_runtime_deps extracts only a library and {:git/url that occur on the SAME physical line (`grep -oE '[^[:space:]{]+[[:space:]]+\{:git/url'`). Valid deps.edn formatting with the library symbol on one line and `{:git/url ...}` on the next produces no finding; a direct parser-shaped probe returned `MISSED`, and the same implementation remains on main after the later vendoring PR. That makes Blocker 3's promised prevention formatting-dependent: a publishable tool can still acquire a runtime git coordinate that clein silently omits from its POM while the lockstep gate stays green. Bounded repair: read the top-level :deps map structurally (Clojure EDN reader or the existing structural dependency tooling), flag every coordinate containing :git/url, and mutation-pin both same-line and multiline forms. Keep alias :extra-deps excluded. No new release framework.
AUDIT-REOPEN OBLIGATION DISCHARGED 2026-07-28 — PR #7217 (branch worker/coord-check-2ii52). NOT CLOSING: see the two reasons at the end.

THE REOPEN'S DEFECT, REPRODUCED FIRST. check_no_git_coords_in_runtime_deps extracted with grep -oE '[^[:space:]{]+[[:space:]]+\{:git/url', which only matches when the library symbol and {:git/url share a physical line. One probe, run UNCHANGED against main's implementation and against the fix — inject a runtime git coordinate into tools/mcp-base/deps.edn in seven valid formattings, ask the gate about each:

  shape                                  BEFORE            AFTER
  A same-line                            CAUGHT (exit 1)   CAUGHT (exit 1)
  B symbol one line, map the next        MISSED (exit 0)   CAUGHT (exit 1)   <- the audit's shape
  C coordinate keys split across lines   MISSED (exit 0)   CAUGHT (exit 1)
  D :git/tag + :git/sha, no :git/url     MISSED (exit 0)   CAUGHT (exit 1)
  E decoy in a ; comment                 CAUGHT (false)    ignored
  F decoy in a #_ discard                ignored           ignored

description:

A shipped Freehand guide that REPLACES the current re-frame.ui guide at docs/core/re-frame.ui/. USE IT AS THE INITIAL DRAFT. Mike wrote it against the ratified target design as the guide's starting point; it is not a from-scratch task. The shape, running order and voice are there. The work is REFINING it against implementation detail — what actually shipped — not reinventing it.

## The hard part

The draft was written against the TARGET design; the implementation landed fast and in places differs. Every code sample and every claim must be checked against the shipped surface. A guide that does not compile is worse than none: it teaches an API that does not exist and the reader blames themselves. At dispatch, re-read the current public surface (spec/API.md, docs/api/re-frame.freehand.md, the door namespace) rather than trusting this bead.

## Sequencing

Do NOT dispatch until the public surface is stable enough that the guide will not be stale on arrival — the signal is the F5 composition/integration slices being largely landed (slots, theming, v/->react, roots/SSR), since the guide covers all of them. A guide authored ahead of that is rewritten twice.

## Acceptance

1. Every code sample in the shipped guide is EXECUTED, not eyeballed — extracted and compiled, or mirrored by a test. State the mechanism. This is the single most important criterion.
2. The guide replaces docs/core/re-frame.ui/ as the canonical view-layer guide; it is in the mkdocs nav; python -m mkdocs build --strict exits 0; python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py exits 0.
3. Every public verb the guide teaches exists in spec/API.md with a classification entry.
4. Where the guide deliberately omits a capability, it says so rather than staying silent.

## Non-goals

Deleting the draft (it remains the design record); documenting unshipped surface; a Reagent-to-Freehand migration skill (that is the sibling skill bead); reference documentation (the spec owns that; docs/core/reference.md was retired).

title: Correct form-action routing guidance across client and server
description: skills/re-frame2/patterns/form-action.md teaches two incorrect/needlessly indirect routing patterns. Its success fx emits both a server redirect and universal :dispatch of :rf.route/navigate while labelling the latter client-only; on the server that event still changes route state and can run route work even though browser history is absent. The same paragraph tells programmers to register an app-owned effect for a bare URL, although the shipped request grammar directly supports [:rf.route/navigate {:url "/cart"}]. This is canonical copyable guidance and creates both wrong behavior and unnecessary app machinery.
acceptance_criteria: Make the worked success path choose the 303 redirect on the server and route navigation on the client using an existing platform boundary; do not claim the navigation event is a server no-op; teach the built-in {:url ...} request for raw URLs and reserve app-owned effects only for deliberate routing bypasses, if that exceptional advice remains useful; keep the change confined to the skill/doc and its existing drift checks.
notes:
PR #6614 three-lens audit (2026-07-21): reopen narrowly. spec/Pattern-FormAction.md and its docs/spec mirror still teach the exact rejected behavior: emit redirect plus navigate together, call route navigation a server no-op, and invent an app-owned fx for a raw internal URL. Reconcile that canonical source and mirror with the corrected skill. Also make the platform choice use coeffect-key presence rather than request truthiness: on a server frame the declared :rf.server/request key can be present with nil when the slot is unpopulated, while the client key is absent. Use one focused presence check; no platform abstraction or broader form-action redesign.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7172 (2026-07-28). The exact defects this owner was meant to remove are still present on origin/main in spec/Pattern-FormAction.md. The canonical :cart/add-item handler says it runs on both platforms but declares :rf.server/request and :app.csrf/active-token, both server-only; platform-skipped ambient cofx deliver no key, so the client arm compares the submitted token with nil and always takes the 403 branch. Its success fx also emits :rf.server/redirect and the universal :rf.route/navigate together while the prose calls navigation a server no-op; routing still runs and can perform server route work. The same paragraph still invents an app-owned bare-URL fx despite the shipped {:url ...} request. Apply this bead's existing acceptance literally: choose the platform arm from coeffect-key presence, emit one success navigation per platform, and teach the built-in URL request. Keep the fix in the canonical pattern and its actual mirrors.
close_reason: PR #7232 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7232. The #7172 audit was right: 073acbd7e4 corrected the skill leaf only, and the canonical spec/Pattern-FormAction.md still taught all three rejected shapes plus a fourth the skill had introduced. All four fixed in BOTH files. (1) The handler declared :rf.server/request + :app.csrf/active-token (both :platforms #{:server}) while its :doc said it ran on both platforms; a platform-skipped supplier delivers NO KEY, so on the client the CSRF arm compared the token against nil and 403'd every submission — the arm is now guarded on the platform test, and §CSRF says why it is a server arm. (2) The success path emitted :rf.server/redirect AND an unconditional [:dispatch [:rf.route/navigate …]] on the theory that each platform no-ops the other's: half true, and the failing half matters — :platforms is a reg-fx/reg-cofx property so the redirect does lapse on the client, but :rf.route/navigate is an EVENT and :dispatch carries no platform gate, so server-side it writes the route slice and can fire the destination's work in a per-request frame about to be discarded. One arm chosen now; the 'server no-op' claim is gone from prose, the server-vs-client table, the second code block and the anti-pattern that asserted it. (3) Platform test is (contains? cofx :rf.server/request), NOT (if request …) — the form the skill shipped, and the fourth defect: a skipped supplier delivers no key, but a supplier that RAN and found its slot unpopulated delivers the key carrying nil, which truthiness reads as 'client'. One contains? is the whole boundary; no platform abstraction. (4) [:rf.route/navigate {:url "/cart"}] taught for a bare URL (verified: address.cljc raw-url-keys #{:url}, :to xor :url); app-owned fx reserved for a deliberate router BYPASS. NO NORMATIVE MOVE — the conformance checklist gains precision about how the platform is decided, not a new obligation. Corpus sweep: no other site in spec/ docs/ skills/ migration/ teaches either defect. Gates: mkdocs --strict 0 (0 warnings), check_doc_slugs 0, check_keyword_catalogue_drift 0.

title: Fence older-first overlapping UI digest activations
description:
PR #5953 added a global monotone generation/high-water pair to digest_carrier, which correctly handles newest-first overlap completion. It cannot identify which reload an after-load callback belongs to because after-load carries no cycle token.

Deterministic older-first interleaving on current main:
1. accepted generation 1 is published.
2. reload A runs before-load and stages dA as generation 2.
3. reload B runs before-load and stages dB as generation 3, but its application sources have not completed.
4. older A after-load runs first.
5. A reads the global generation 3 > activated 1, publishes dB and clears updating before B finishes.
6. If B then throws and skips after-load, current continues advertising dB forever instead of remaining fail-closed.

The shipped fixture explicitly releases newest-first and therefore cannot catch this. The closed source bead's close reason acknowledges the older-first residual, but no open bead owns it. Establish exact activation-cycle ownership or explicitly serialize/reject overlapping script reloads. Keep it dev-only and local; no general scheduler.
acceptance_criteria: RULED 2026-07-18 (delegated per Mike, see notes): keep shipped high-water semantics; doc/test PR only. (1) Carrier semantics unchanged: the generation/activated high-water rule stays; no FIFO/serialization, no overlap-reject fence, no loader-mode detection, no change to stage!/before-load/after-load behavior. (2) Docstring truth: the false ":script reload sources load asynchronously" premise in digest_carrier.cljs (lines 33-35 area) is replaced with the verified host fact (Shadow 3.4.10 reload chain is one synchronous macrotask absent explicit :dev/*-load-async hooks; :loader-mode affects initial-load flush only), and reload atomicity is named as a load-bearing host assumption to re-verify on any Shadow upgrade. (3) check-ui-digest-carrier.cjs: the c3 preamble's copy of the same false premise is corrected, and an older-first characterization stanza is added (before A / stage dA / before B / stage dB / after -> publishes dB early in the modeled world) whose comment carries the reachability rationale and cites the ruling. (4) Existing newest-first, stale-after-newer-fence, initial-load, and failed-reload recovery fixture cases remain green. (5) Advanced production remains free of the carrier machinery; no general concurrency abstraction.
notes:
BLOCKED on premise contradiction (czh5k analysis 2026-07-17, ~70min read-only, 0 edits). The digest-carrier after-load fix (digest_carrier.cljs:145-164, the ^:dev/after-load high-water rule from #5953) must satisfy two PROVABLY INCOMPATIBLE ACs: (a) 'failed-reload recovery stays green' → after-load MUST publish; (b) 'AC1 older-first fence' → overlapping older after-load must NOT publish. At the deciding after-load BOTH present identical carrier state (2 before-loads, 2 stages, 0 prior after-loads, generation 2-ahead-of-activated); Shadow's zero-arg :dev/after-load carries no cycle token, so a THROWN reload is locally indistinguishable from an IN-FLIGHT overlapping reload — opposite handling required, distinguishing fact is future/unobservable. Also the bead's own two new clauses (older-first-B-succeeds-publishes-dB vs B-throws-forward-recovery-publishes-dC) are mutually exclusive for the same reason. Context: :script loader-mode (only mode with older-first overlap) is NOT used for HMR in-repo (only a fixture) — purely defensive for downstream :script consumers. OPTIONS (Mike decides): (A) mode-gated serialize — under :script FIFO cycle-ownership (promote oldest unpromoted), :eval unchanged; achieves fence + older-first-B-succeeds, all tests green, residual: B-throws-recovery needs 1 extra clean :script reload; depends on :loader-mode runtime-readable (unconfirmed). (B) reject-overlap — overlapping reloads don't publish, next clean reload recovers; older-first-B publishes on NEXT reload not at B's after-load. (C) relax the acceptance — drop EITHER older-first-B-publishes-at-completion OR B-throws-recovery-publishes-once (they're exclusive). czh5k REC: (C) relax to preferred behavior, then implement (A) [closest to exact-cycle-ownership, zero test risk].
DECISION (2026-07-18, delegated ruling per Mike 2026-07-18): ADOPT OPTION C — keep the shipped generation/activated high-water semantics in digest_carrier.cljs unchanged. REJECT the dossier's Option B (reject/fence overlap) and the earlier notes' "relax then implement A" plan. One small doc/test PR closes this bead; no semantic change.

RATIONALE (keystones independently re-verified before ruling): (1) digest_carrier.cljs:160-164 is exactly the modeled state machine — after-load promotes whenever generation > activated, publishing whatever :staged holds. title: hicasso: reportability()'s control annotation still says a control failure is 'the reason no magnitude is published'
description: Residual of the same supersession chain, left by rf2-vr1hl, 2026-08-08.
notes:
FILED BY rf2-vr1hl, 2026-08-08, as a residual it declined to take under its own fence
("this changes a printed string and its pins"; "do NOT over-engineer").

WHAT REMAINS. clock_run.cjs's reportability() annotates a regime row's control
status with a conditional suffix:

  const predictedFailure = !r.ctlOk && !g.statementNeedsControl;
  `[clock]     positive control: ${r.ctlOk ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'}${r.ctlNote || ''}` +
    (predictedFailure ? ' — expected, and the reason no magnitude is published' : '')

TWO CLAIMS IN THAT SUFFIX ARE rf2-jcm3p's AND BOTH ARE RETIRED.
  "expected" — rf2-8a746 established ctl-2x was never failing (controlVerdict
  tests per-block band membership, not the mean), so no live ruling predicts a
  control failure on this row.
  "the reason no magnitude is published" — that is THE FAILING CONTROL IS THE
  PUBLISHED REASON, the one sentence rf2-owiis named dead. Under rf2-diaud the
  reason this driver publishes no magnitude is that the published magnitude is
  an ENSEMBLE estimate through a run-preserving bootstrap whose outer unit is
  the run, and one run cannot form the interval.

So after rf2-vr1hl the mount regime's own three strings cite rf2-diaud and this
suffix, printed two lines below them, still cites rf2-jcm3p's dead premise.

WHY rf2-vr1hl DID NOT TAKE IT, stated so the judgement is reviewable rather than
assumed. It is not a roster string: it lives in reportability(), the decision
function, and it is generic over regime rows rather than owned by mount-regime.
rf2-vr1hl's bead named REGIMES['mount-regime'].bead and .publishes; it moved
.why as well, because .why is the second printed line of the same statement and
leaving it would have put the dead premise directly under a corrected bracket.
This suffix is one surface further out, and touching the decision function was
outside the bead's stated fence.

IT DOES NOT FIRE ON THE COMMITTED CORPUS. It needs ctlOk === false on a regime
row, and under the mount class rf2-x7x10 calibrated at v2 all 14 committed mount
row-runs come back IN CONTROL. It fires in the fixtures, which set ctlOk:false
deliberately (to pin that the mount regime does NOT wait on its control — that
independence survives both rulings and is the case's real subject).

THE PINS, so whoever takes it knows it is a coordinated change of the same shape:
  clock_exit_path.test.cjs  :2349 (in 'the M1 refusal now states a REGIME rather
                                   than a control that went wrong')
  clock_run.cjs             reportabilitySelfTest, 'the mount regime STATES
                            itself although its control failed'
Both match /positive control: FAIL.*expected, and the reason no magnitude is
published/. Print and pins move together or the suite goes red on a true string.

SHAPE OF THE FIX. The suffix should say what is true of a regime row whose
control failed: the regime states itself regardless of that control, so the
control's status is not what withholds a magnitude. It must NOT be deleted — the
annotation exists because the ruling that made these rows regimes is ABOUT their
controls and a reader must not have to infer one from the other (the comment
above it says so). Annotate-never-erase, in #7705's idiom, which rf2-vr1hl
matched.

FENCE, inherited: this is a printed string and its pins. Nothing computed,
adjudicated or published. publishesMagnitude stays false — the ensemble reason,
not rf2-jcm3p's.
MAYOR SEQUENCING 2026-08-08 21:56 AUSEST — HELD behind rf2-vr1hl's PR, then dispatches. Same file, live worker.

THIS IS THE THIRD LINK IN ONE CHAIN, and the chain is worth naming because it is converging rather than regressing. rf2-owiis swept clock_run.cjs's PROSE and filed rf2-vr1hl for the PRINTED line it could not take without the test file another worker held. rf2-vr1hl is taking the printed line and its pins, and filed THIS for an annotation outside its own fence ("this changes a printed string and its pins"). Each worker took exactly what it could take cleanly and filed the rest rather than reaching. That produced three small correct PRs instead of one sprawling conflicted one.

IT CONVERGES BECAUSE THE SURFACE SHRINKS EACH TIME: prose (many sites) -> one printed line and three pins -> one conditional suffix in one function. This is the last of it that I can see; if the worker finds a fourth, it should file it the same way, but it should also say plainly whether the chain is still shrinking. title: census clock rig still carries the retired all-blocks strict rule (rf2-8a746 did not reach it)
description:
SCOPE BOUNDARY RECORDED BY rf2-8a746's IMPLEMENTATION, not a defect found by measuring.

rf2-8a746 retired, everywhere on the HICASSO CLOCK instrument, both the three-point
difference-of-differences control and the all-18-blocks strict run-rejection rule. The
grep for the ^18 semantics that the ruling asked for also lands on
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/shapes/census_clock_run.cjs:277 —
controlVerdict with rule 'strict — EVERY block inside the band'.

IT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE, and the reason is the ruling's own. The census rig is a
DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT: a different driver, different rows and witnesses, its own datasets
under data/censusclock-*, and a control whose prediction comes from the row's own element
arithmetic (ctlPredicted, P times the cards) rather than from a page doubling. rf2-8a746's
frozen check standard is seeded from clock_run.cjs's ctl-2x/floor run medians on a
300-boundary page — centre 1.7207x, limits [1.5509, 1.8905], dispersion 0.568 — and
applying those limits to a rig measuring a different quantity would re-commit the exact
mis-specification the ruling retires: asserting a value that was never measured on the
instrument being judged.

WHAT IS INHERITED IS THE ARITHMETIC, NOT THE NUMBERS. p^n on a per-block pass rate below 1
is a property of the rule and not of the clock. If the census rig's per-block in-band rate
is p over n blocks, its per-run false-refusal is 1 - p^n whatever it is measuring; on the
hicasso clock that was 90.5% empirical at n=18. Whether it bites here is a measurement over
the committed censusclock-* datasets, and it needs no window.

THE WORK. (1) Compute the census rig's per-block in-band fraction and per-run pass rate over
its committed datasets, exactly as rf2-8a746 did for the clock — analysis over retained data,
NO NEW MEASUREMENT. (2) If the rule is refusing at a rate a run cannot survive, calibrate a
check standard for THAT rig, from ITS OWN baseline, versioned as data in the idiom of
clock_check_standard.json. (3) If it is not, record the measured rate on this bead and close
it: a rule with a defensible false-refusal rate is not a defect, and rf2-8a746 rejects
retiring a control merely because it shares a shape with one that failed.

Related: rf2-8a746 (the ruling and the hicasso-clock implementation), rf2-t2flm (the mount
half, concurrent).

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MEASURED 2026-08-08 14:35 AUSEST from committed data only. NO MEASUREMENT TAKEN — no census driver, no clock driver, no quiet box consumed. Arithmetic over the committed data/censusclock-* datasets.

THE ANSWER: the all-blocks strict run-rejection rule is RETAINED on this rig, on measured grounds. Outcome (3) of the bead's three.

THE CORPUS. Thirty row-runs — five sessions at five commits (censusclock-2rtt6-56 @7885a7c148, -y1jkm @8ccd9f4b41, -6c237 @ac09504d74, -cno31 @08344cb500 on 2026-08-02; -jv36i @752b8069be on 2026-08-07) x two adapter runs x three rows — 540 blocks, all at design 6 rounds x 3 blocks x (4 warmup + 10 samples) and controlSlack 0.25. n = 18 BLOCKS PER ROW-RUN.

THE RATE, PER ROW (p = per-block in-band fraction, 180 blocks and 10 row-runs each):

  row              p                   1 - p^18   runs passed   exact binomial two-sided p
  large-template   178/180 = 98.9%       18.2%      8 of 10      1.000
  feed             175/180 = 97.2%       39.8%      7 of 10      0.749
  ordinary          56/180 = 31.1%      100.0%      0 of 10      1.000

THEY AGREE, PER ROW. Pooled they do NOT — pooled p is 409/540 = 75.7%, which predicts 99.3% per-run refusal against 15 of 30 observed — and that disagreement is a fact about pooling a mis-centred row with two well-centred ones, not about the rule. Per-row is the honest statistic; the pooled figure is recorded here so nobody re-derives it and reads it as evidence.

WHY IT IS NOT THE CLOCK'S RULE. 18-40% is a rate a run survives; the clock's was 90.5% empirical at the same n, and its premise-meeting ctl3Layout passed 4 of 42. The census rig does not inherit that ill-conditioning because ITS CONTROL IS ALREADY LEVEL-DENOMINATED — the class rf2-8a746's ruling endorses. Tared floor 10.72 / 41.00 ms with between-block SD 2.55 / 8.82, i.e. 4.20 / 4.65 sigma from zero, against the retired ctl3 denominator's 2.09. Block IQR is 7.7% of the centre on both rows. Centres sit 24.9% and 35.4% above the band's lower edge, against ctl3's 4%.

THE CLOCK'S LIMITS WERE NOT IMPORTED, for the reason the bead gives: this rig's prediction is each row's own element arithmetic (1.9759 / 1.9943 / 1.7255), and asserting the clock's 1.7207x centre here would re-commit the mis-specification being retired.

RECOMPUTATION VALIDATED. The per-block statistic recomputed through the driver's own arithmetic reproduces every stored adjudication.ctl.perBlock and every stored ok across all 30 row-runs exactly. The only divergence is band edges, by exactly one unit in the last stored place (1e-4), because datasetFor writes r4(ctlPredicted) while the run adjudicated on the page's raw value; counting was therefore done on the STORED band, which is the band the runs experienced.

THE ONE FINDING, AND IT IS NOT THE RULE. The ordinary row refuses 10 of 10 on its CENTRE: block median 1.2264x against a predicted 1.7255x — 71.1% of P, and 5.2% BELOW the band's lower edge of 1.2941. Relaxing the run rule does not reach it (allowing 1, 2 or 3 out-of-band blocks still passes 0 of 10). Because verdict()'s ctlFailed condition is RUN-WIDE, that also means no full-shape census run can be canonical: driven on the real exported functions, a run with large-template and feed clean and ordinary's control failed returns exit 5 and destination() routes every dataset to .unpublished. FILED AS rf2-pzqy8 (P2) with both candidate directions; the choice is a ruling, not an implementation, and nothing here acts on it.

DELIVERED IN PR #7699 (branch worker/censusrule-y0pkh), which changes no behaviour, no threshold and no gate: the measured rates and the retention are stated above controlVerdict where the ^18 grep lands, the label now reads 'strict — EVERY block inside the band (rf2-y0pkh: measured and retained)' so the next grep does not re-file this bead, controlBlocks is lifted out of report and exported so the witness drives the real arithmetic, and six new cases in clock_exit_path.test.cjs recompute every figure above from the committed datasets (273 -> 279 passed). Mutation-proved: widening CONTROL_SLACK to 0.40 reds it, dropping the cite reds it, a wrong stated rate reds it, and claiming the ordinary centre is in band reds it.

title: chore: pin .beads/issues.jsonl to eol=lf so the tracker export stops churning every tick
description:
FOUND by the mayor 2026-08-08 while diagnosing a rebase abort. It is the same defect class the rf2-rguy1 worker fixed for the retained jsfb evidence in PR #7694, on the file the whole beads-durability section of CLAUDE.md is about.

THE MECHANISM. This box runs core.autocrlf=true and `.beads/issues.jsonl` is NOT pinned in .gitattributes. Every `bd export` writes LF; git rewrites the working copy to CRLF; git then reports the file MODIFIED against HEAD forever, even when the export is byte-identical in content. Confirmed today: `sh scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh` reported "nothing to checkpoint (3296 rows, unchanged)" while `git status` simultaneously showed ` M .beads/issues.jsonl`, with zero divergence from origin (rev-list 0/0). Every bd invocation also emits "warning: in the working copy of '.beads/issues.jsonl', LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it".

WHY IT IS WORTH A LINE OF CONFIG RATHER THAN LIVING WITH IT. A perpetually-dirty tracker file is precisely the state CLAUDE.md documents as aborting `git pull` ("local changes would be overwritten"), which silently freezes HEAD at a stale base. The mayor loop currently pays for this every single tick with a `git reset -q HEAD -- .beads` plus a `git checkout -- .beads` before it can pull — dozens of times per session — and that dance is itself hazardous, because a checkout of this file within a tick of a `bd close` reverts the close (CLAUDE.md's own warning, and it cost real closes here on 2026-08-07).

THE FIX, one line:

  .beads/issues.jsonl text eol=lf

plus, in the same change, a round-trip proof rather than an assumption: delete the file, `git checkout -- .beads/issues.jsonl`, confirm `git status` is clean and the file carries zero CR bytes. Copying and comparing is not sufficient — that tests the copy, not the checkout.

SEQUENCING — THIS IS THE WHOLE REASON IT IS FILED RATHER THAN DONE. PR #7694 (worker/jsfbevidence-rguy1) is OPEN and edits root `.gitattributes` to add its own eol=lf pin. Two hands on that file collide. **Dispatch only after #7694 MERGES**, then add the one line beside its pin.

SCOPE FENCE: `.gitattributes` only. Do NOT touch `.beads/` contents, do NOT re-export, do NOT run bd. Verify with `git status` and a CR-byte count, not by inspecting tracker rows.
notes:
MAYOR CORRECTION 2026-08-08 12:20 AUSEST — I OVERSTATED THIS BEAD'S JUSTIFICATION WHEN I FILED IT, and the worker's own evidence is what exposed it. Recording the correction rather than letting the description stand as written.

WHAT I CLAIMED: that the missing pin left .beads/issues.jsonl PERPETUALLY DIRTY, that this is the state CLAUDE.md documents as aborting `git pull` and freezing HEAD, and that the mayor loop was paying a reset+checkout every tick because of it.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, verified just now on the mayor checkout: a plain `bd ready --limit 0` read leaves `git status .beads` CLEAN. The dirtiness I kept observing came from bd WRITES — every bead update, close and create rewrites the export with genuinely changed content. That is expected and correct behaviour, not churn, and it is not what the pin addresses. The worker found the same thing from the other direction and said so plainly: git's clean filter HIDES a CRLF working copy from `git status`, so `status` was clean before and after the pin in its worktree.

SO THE PIN DOES NOT FIX A DIRTY-FILE PROBLEM, because there was not one.

WHAT THE PIN IS ACTUALLY WORTH, stated honestly and smaller than my filing implied:
- The checked-out file genuinely IS CRLF where bd writes LF — measured, not assumed: 3,297 CRs before, 0 after, with the byte delta 14,236,505 - 14,233,208 = 3,297 corroborating exactly.
- It removes the "LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it" warning that bd emits on every invocation. Real noise, small cost.
- It protects any future byte-wise use of the file (hashing, digest citation, byte comparison) from the platform-dependent-digest trap that PR #7694 had to fix for the retained jsfb evidence.
- It makes this file consistent with the seven other eol=lf groups already in .gitattributes, every one of them added for the same core.autocrlf=true reason.

VERDICT: the change is correct, harmless and consistent with established practice in the file it edits, so it merges. But it is a TIDINESS-AND-FUTURE-PROOFING pin, not the papercut-with-teeth I described. Anyone reading this bead later should not cite it as evidence that a pull-abort was fixed here, because no pull-abort was.

THE LESSON FOR ME, and it is the same one three other beads have taught this session: I filed from a plausible mechanism rather than a tested one. `git status` before and after a bd read is a five-second check and I did not run it until after the work was done.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7696 (completeness, correctness, implementation quality): REOPENED exact owner for the landed rationale, not the LF pin. The attribute itself is correct: git check-attr reports text:set/eol:lf and the current 1,882-row export has 0 CR bytes. But the committed .gitattributes comment still says the unpinned export was perpetually dirty, aborted pulls, and forced a checkout that could revert closes. This Bead's own 2026-08-08 mayor correction establishes that premise was false: Git's clean filter kept the CRLF working copy clean, and bd writes dirtied it only when content genuinely changed. Keep the one-line pin; replace the stale comment with the accurate benefits already adjudicated here — suppress the LF-to-CRLF warning, make checked-out bytes platform-stable for byte-wise tools, and align with the repository's other LF pins. No mechanism or framework.
close_reason:
VERIFIED-DUPLICATE — the pin is on main. Verified by reading .gitattributes rather than assuming.

.gitattributes:68 carries `.beads/issues.jsonl text eol=lf`, and the comment block at :60 names this bead id (rf2-gsjfr) as its reason. It landed in PR #7696, 'chore: pin the beads export to LF so it stops churning on Windows', state MERGED.

The effect is observable: the CRLF churn this bead was filed against is gone from the mayor checkout, and the stale staged exports still sitting in the three July-25 .grok worktrees (which predate the pin) are the last place it shows.

title: hicasso: foldDecomposition accepts truncated evidence — dimensions and roster unchecked against the row's own shape
description:
STRANDED BY THE rf2-jo60g CLOSE, 2026-08-08. Filed by the worker that took the strike route on rf2-jo60g (PR #7692) so the finding keeps an owner. The 10:32 ruling settled the DOC half and says the code half is done; the MERGED-PR AUDIT OF #7681, recorded on rf2-jo60g and sitting directly above that ruling, says one code gap remains and named rf2-jo60g as its exact owner. Closing rf2-jo60g on the doc half leaves it without one. The mayor should reject this outright if the ruling was meant to retire the finding too — it is filed to be adjudicated, not assumed.

THE FINDING, quoted from the audit. PR #7681 repaired the SCALAR and INNER-SHAPE defect: foldDecomposition no longer defaults a missing, null or NaN metric to zero, requires nonempty rounds and blocks, and requires the first block's arm roster as a set in every block. But it still anchors completeness to THE FIRST SURVIVING BLOCK rather than to the row's authoritative shape. A live probe against censusclock-jv36i/uix.json (declared 6 rounds x 3 blocks; row armIds includes uix) showed foldDecomposition ACCEPT all three of:

  1. the final round removed;
  2. one block removed from round 2;
  3. uix removed from EVERY block.

Each is partial or truncated evidence, and each still returns plausible aggregates. Case 3 is the sharp one: a roster check that compares every block against the first block cannot see an arm that is missing from all of them, so the whole point of the roster check is bypassed by uniform loss.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS AFTER THE STRIKE ROUTE. The strike route settled what the CENSUS STUDIO PAGE may claim; it did not change what the fold will accept the next time a canonical census run is taken. rf2-jo60g's own close records that the split becomes recomputable on that run — this is the check standing between that run and a plausible-looking ratio folded from truncated evidence. The defect class is the one rf2-jo60g existed to close.

REMEDY, and it is bounded. Check the expected round and block DIMENSIONS and the blocksDecomp roster against the ROW'S OWN armIds at the real report/driver boundary, rather than against the first surviving block. No schema layer and no validation framework — the audit is explicit that this needs neither, and rf2-jo60g's history is a record of that restraint being the right call twice.

ACCEPTANCE: non-zero driver outcome, wrote===false and destination().canonical===false witnesses for all three cases above, in the same hermetic style as the merged 246-case suite. The audit confirms that suite, both syntax checks and diff-check all PASS today, so the gap is UNWITNESSED rather than a general breakage — expect to add witnesses, not to repair a red.

Surface: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/shapes/census_clock_run.cjs and clock_exit_path.test.cjs. No measurement and no census run required.
notes:
MAYOR ADJUDICATION 2026-08-08 10:45 AUSEST — the filing worker asked to be overruled if the rf2-jo60g ruling was meant to retire this finding too. IT WAS NOT. This bead stands, and the worker was right to file rather than strand it.

WHY IT IS NOT RETIRED. My jo60g ruling this morning said "the code half is done and stays done", and that referred to what had LANDED: PR #7666's per-block persistence and PR #7681's refusal of partial evidence. The merged-PR audit of #7681 raised a NEW finding after those landings and named rf2-jo60g as its exact owner. Ruling the doc half onto the strike route said nothing about it. Closing jo60g on the doc half alone would have left an audit-named finding with no owner — which is precisely the failure I committed last night on rf2-n6w7o and rf2-w3yxd, closing over live audit reopens because the work had landed. The worker avoided repeating it.

VERIFIED BEFORE RULING, not taken on report. census_clock_run.cjs's foldDecomposition docstring states the anchor in its own words: "every block carries the same arm roster as THE ROW'S FIRST BLOCK". So completeness is measured against block 1 rather than against the row's declared shape, and three shapes pass that should not: a removed final round, a removed block, and an arm removed from EVERY block — the last because the roster derived from block 1 also lacks it. Each yields internally consistent survivors and a plausible aggregate.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING despite being P3 and latent. It is the same fail-open class this session has closed four times (the ladder aggregator, the census write path, the WORKLOAD bypass, the unverified-writes line), and it is the exact mechanism that made the cited layout/style/script split unrecomputable in the first place: evidence that looked complete and was not. A validator that cannot see a missing arm is the defect it was written to close.

SCOPE, and it is narrow. Anchor completeness to the ROW'S DECLARED SHAPE — its expected arm roster and its own round/block counts — rather than to whatever block 1 happens to contain. Refuse and name what is missing, in the idiom the file already uses. Do NOT grow a schema validator, do NOT touch the no-blocks refusal or the per-field finite checks that landed in PR #7681, and do NOT loosen anything: this may only ever turn an accepted row into a refused one.

LATENCY IS NOT A REASON TO SKIP IT, but it IS a reason it is P3: the defect bites only when a canonical census run actually happens, and that run is deferred with the measurement lane. Fixing it now means the next run cannot publish over a hole.

CLOSED ON PR #7695 (worker/foldshape-e1tko), NOT merged; mayor merges. 2026-08-08.
