title: hicasso: the allocation preflight licenses a window below ALLOC_MIN_WRITES (audit residual of PR #7688)
description:
The bounded correctness residual the merged-PR audit of #7688 recorded on
rf2-2rtt6.138. CONFIRMED STILL PRESENT on origin/main at 42cf8db7da by
rf2-2rtt6.138's measurement window (2026-08-08), by reading p0_run.cjs.

ALLOC_MIN_WRITES = 6 is used ONLY to derive the default page (ALLOC_CELLS).
allocArmSizing().admissible is:

    admissible: writes >= 1 && boundaries >= 1 && headroom >= 0

so the preflight licenses precisely the low-averaging shape the bead and the
PR rule out. The audit reproduced two routes without launching Chromium:
P0_ROOTS=50 derives {cells:1, boundaries:50, writes:2, admissible:true}, and
an explicit P0_ALLOC_WRITES=1 on the shipped page derives {boundaries:24,
writes:1, admissible:true}. Either can proceed through every publication gate
even though a one-write window has no averaging in it -- and a one-write
window is exactly the configuration whose four fits came back at r2
0.75/0.28/0.94/0.31.

MINIMAL COMPLETION, as the audit stated it: make the allocation-row preflight
refuse ALLOC_ARM.writes < ALLOC_MIN_WRITES (including a large-root default
that cannot fit six) and name shrinking P0_ALLOC_CELLS / P0_ROOTS as the
repair; do NOT advise shrinking the window below the floor. Pin both
reproduced routes plus the shipped six-write green control in
p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs. No generic env-schema layer, no new estimator,
no threshold change, no benchmark run.

PRIORITY NOTE, added by the measurement window rather than by the audit: this
is now LOWER value than it looked when filed. rf2-2rtt6.140 measured that no
page of one boundary or more certifies the R=20 rung at six writes at all, so
the six-write floor may not survive as the right constraint. Sequence this
AFTER rf2-2rtt6.139 and rf2-2rtt6.140 are ruled on, or it will be re-done.

Touches p0_run.cjs, which rf2-2rtt6.139/.140 also touch -- sequence, do not
parallelise.
notes:
MAYOR ADJUDICATION 2026-08-08 11:10 AUSEST — the worker proceeded against this bead's own priority note and offered the PR as the place to hold it. I ENDORSE PROCEEDING, and the reasoning it gave is better than the note it overrode.

THE NOTE, at this bead's lines 39-43: "this is now LOWER value than it looked when filed ... Sequence this AFTER rf2-2rtt6.139 and rf2-2rtt6.140 are ruled on, or it will be re-done." Both are still OPEN and unruled as I write.

WHY PROCEEDING WAS RIGHT. The note guards against ONE risk: rework when the floor moves. The worker structured the change so that risk does not arise — the enforcement is written against ALLOC_MIN_WRITES and never against the literal 6, so a ruling that moves the floor moves the preflight and its tests with it, with no edit. That is not an override of the note; it is the correct answer to it. And the defect itself is value-independent: a preflight that licenses precisely the shape its own row rules out is wrong at any floor value. A floor that adjudicates nothing is not a floor.

MY BRIEF WAS AT FAULT, not the worker. I did not carry that priority note into the dispatch, because I briefed from an earlier reading of the bead rather than re-reading its newest notes at dispatch time. That is the third time in this session a worker has caught my brief stale or incomplete — a wrong test count, a wrong integer bound, and now this. The bead-governs rule is doing exactly what it exists for, but it should not be load-bearing this often.

TWO WORKER JUDGEMENTS I ALSO ENDORSE, both beyond what I asked:

(1) IT PINNED THREE CASES, NOT TWO. My brief asked for the two admitting routes; the bead asked additionally for the shipped six-write green control. The control is what stops the gate being vacuous — two refusal cases alone would pass a preflight that refuses everything.

(2) IT MADE admissible A REFUSALS LIST RATHER THAN A LONGER CONJUNCTION, because the refusal text has to BRANCH. A page still carrying six writes has nothing wrong with its page — the repair there is to RAISE P0_ALLOC_WRITES. A page that cannot carry six gets the page repair and has no window count named at all, because naming what such a page admits is naming a below-floor window. One undifferentiated boolean would have printed the mask-budget prose at a floor refusal and sent the operator to configure the very shape being refused. That is a real ergonomic call and the right one.

EVIDENCE THAT NOTHING LOOSENED, which is the only property this change had to preserve: an exhaustive in-test sweep of W 0..40 x cells 0..40 x roots {0,1,4,50} asserting admissible implies the OLD predicate verbatim, plus the structural argument that the refusal list is the old terms negated with writes<1 subsumed by writes<ALLOC_MIN_WRITES. No threshold moved. Structural tests 41 -> 50; red-then-green demonstrated with a tests-only commit reading 11/50 failed before the driver change.
FORWARD NOTE 2026-08-08 13:45 AUSEST — THE rf2-2rtt6.140 PACKAGE WILL CHANGE THIS BEAD'S SHIPPED BEHAVIOUR. Recorded on the closed bead now, so the change is not made silently later against a record that says it was finished.

THE RULING'S SEQUENCING ASSUMED THIS BEAD WAS STILL AHEAD OF THE REWORK. rf2-2rtt6.140's criterion 5 (written 2026-08-08 03:04) says "rf2-2rtt6.142's preflight fix rides the same rework, not ahead of it". By the time the design brief was written that was already superseded by fact: this bead landed in PR #7693 and merged, so the refusals list is on origin/main and the .140 design brief builds ON it rather than replacing it. No conflict — but the sequencing sentence in that criterion should be read as history, not instruction.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGES, and it is the part worth writing down. The refusal text landed here BRANCHES on whether the page can carry six writes — a page that can gets "raise P0_ALLOC_WRITES", a page that cannot gets the page repair and is deliberately given no window count, because naming what such a page admits would be naming a below-floor window. That branch is COMPUTED FROM THE BUDGET. The .140 package retires the budget mechanism in favour of an observed-collection witness, so the branch collapses to a single arm.

THAT IS NOT A REGRESSION, and the reason matters: with no page-size model there is no admissible-page figure to name, so there is nothing for the second branch to say. The endorsed property — never advise the operator to configure the very shape being refused — survives the collapse intact, because the collapsed message names no shape at all.

WHAT STAYS: ALLOC_MIN_WRITES enforcement itself. The averaging floor is not a budget question — a one-write window has no averaging in it whatever certifies the window, and the r2 0.75/0.28/0.94/0.31 history is why. The implementer of .140 must keep the floor refusal and may only collapse the BUDGET-DERIVED branch of its message.

ALSO CORRECTED BY THE BRIEF, for whoever touches this next: the p0 write's registration lives in p0_fixture.cljc, not p0_arms.cljs. The bead and the dispatch brief both said "a p0_arms.cljs / p0_heap.cljs question"; in fact the event handler and the sub graph are in p0_fixture.cljc, with p0_arms.cljs supplying only the public door and p0_heap.cljs the window. All four files move under the package.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7693 (completeness, correctness, implementation quality): REOPENED exact owner. The claimed strict-subset proof sweeps only finite integers. In JavaScript, x < limit is not the negation of x >= limit when x is NaN, so replacing the old positive predicate with three negative refusal checks changed malformed shipped env values from refused to admitted. Exact snapshot probes compare tests-only commit 53f43ecbe6 with merge 7cd4a52463: P0_ALLOC_WRITES=not-a-number, P0_ROOTS=not-a-number, and P0_ALLOC_CELLS=not-a-number all move from admissible:false to refusals:[] / admissible:true. The later rf2-2rtt6.140 rework happens to refuse the first two through its missing-page path, but P0_ALLOC_CELLS=not-a-number remains live today with boundaries:null, refusals:[], admissible:true. Keep the ergonomic refusal list; add a bounded finite/integer-positive input refusal at the existing preflight/config seam and pin malformed env plus NaN/nonfinite direct cases. No schema or validation framework.

title: jsfb comparator: the unverified-writes line sums absence to zero and prints a clean gate
description:
FOUND by the rf2-110be worker while closing the WORKLOAD bypass (PR #7687). It deliberately did NOT file this itself, to keep tracker mutations out of a worker worktree, and recorded it in the PR body and close reason instead. Verified live at HEAD by the mayor before filing.

THE FAULT. jsfb_compare.cjs:350 folds the per-benchmark unverified counts with

  const unv = Object.values(ours.summary).reduce((a, s) => a + (s && s.unverified ? s.unverified : 0), 0);

then prints it at :351 as the run's unverified-writes gate. A summary entry that carries NO `unverified` field at all contributes 0 — indistinguishable from one that carries `unverified: 0` and genuinely verified every write. So a JSON produced by a rig that never recorded the field, or by a version that dropped it, prints a clean `unverified 0` and the reader believes a gate ran.

THIS FAILS OPEN, which is what makes it the genuine sibling of the bug rf2-110be just closed, and the reason it is worth fixing rather than noting. The absence of evidence is being rendered as evidence of absence, in the one line a reader consults to decide whether the writes were verified.

CONTRAST — the neighbouring site at :347 has the same shape and is NOT a defect:

  ours.parity && ours.parity.identical ? 'IDENTICAL' : 'DIFFERENT'

A missing `parity` object prints DIFFERENT, i.e. it fails CLOSED. Leave it alone; it is the safe direction and changing it for symmetry would be gold-plating.

THE FIX, and keep it bounded to this one line: require the field rather than defaulting it. A summary entry lacking `unverified` should make the line REFUSE and name which benchmark lacked it, in the same idiom the file already uses for its other refusals — not print a number. Do NOT grow a schema validator, do NOT touch the expected-cell roster (EXPECTED_CELLS stays derived from PAIRS), do NOT touch the exit codes or the parity gate. A refusal must stay a refusal.

PROVE IT in jsfb_compare_exit_path.test.cjs (42 cases as of PR #7687, every fixture built in-test under mkdtemp): add the absent-field case and show it red before the change, green after. NOTE FOR THE BRIEF: that suite does NOT carry line-ending handling despite an earlier bead claiming it does — the rf2-110be worker checked and corrected that. If both endings matter, verify them out of tree as it did.

DO NOT RUN THE BENCHMARK. Every decision here is reachable as a pure function through the module's require.main guard.
notes:
CORRECTION TO THE CLOSE REASON ABOVE (rf2-0fixc, by the closing worker). One
fragment of the close reason was eaten by shell backtick substitution before it
reached the tracker, and `bd close` on an already-closed issue does not replace
the stored reason, so it is restored here. The mangled line reads

  `UNSTATED — no \ count under <names>, so no total is derived`

and should read: the repaired line prints, verbatim,

  ;;   unverified        UNSTATED — no `unverified` count under run1k, so no total is derived

naming EVERY benchmark whose summary entry did not state an `unverified` count,
comma-separated, in PAIRS order. Nothing else in the close reason was affected;
PR #7690 carries the same text unmangled in its body.
MAYOR TRIAGE RULING 2026-08-08 00:30 AUSEST — the reported sibling is NOT being filed. Recording the reasoning so it is not rediscovered and re-proposed.

WHAT WAS REPORTED. The worker found that a NEGATIVE unverified count cancels a positive one in the same fold: -5 against +5 still totals 0. It correctly declined to fix it, on the grounds that this is present-but-wrong evidence (rf2-110be's class) rather than absent evidence (this bead's), and that adding the guard would turn "require the field" into "validate the field", which this bead's fence forbids. That judgement was right and the restraint is exactly what the fence is for.

RULED: NO BEAD. `unverified` is a COUNTER of writes that failed verification, incremented by the rig. It cannot go negative unless the rig itself is broken, and a rig broken in that way trips other gates first — the run's own refusal paths, the parity gate, and now the UNSTATED refusal this bead just landed. So the scenario the guard defends against is not reachable by any evidence a working rig can produce, and the conjunct would be a diagnostic that can only ever fire on data no run can emit.

WHY THIS IS THE STANCE RATHER THAN LAZINESS. Pre-alpha, and we reject nag-diagnostics and over-engineering at triage. The session's fail-open theme is real and has been worth chasing — the ladder aggregator, the census write path, the ctl3 sign gate, the WORKLOAD bypass and this bead were all cases where a gate reported on evidence it never had. This is not one of them: the field is present and the arithmetic is correct for every value the producer can generate. Adding a conjunct here buys nothing and adds a branch nobody can test without fabricating impossible input.

IF IT EVER BECOMES REAL, the trigger is specific and cheap to spot: a producer change that makes `unverified` a DIFFERENCE rather than a count. At that point it stops being a counter and the guard becomes warranted. Until then, this is closed reasoning, not an open question.
close_reason:
CLOSED BY PR #7690 (worker/unverified-0fixc), the sibling rf2-110be/#7687 named and deliberately left standing.

WHAT WAS WRONG, verbatim as filed. report()'s OUR RUN'S GATES folded the
per-benchmark unverified counts with `s.unverified ? s.unverified : 0`, so an
entry carrying NO `unverified` field contributed 0 — indistinguishable from one
carrying `unverified: 0` that had verified every write. Reproduced against the
landed file before the change: an --ours JSON whose run1k entry has no
`unverified` key printed a clean `unverified        0`. Absence rendered as
evidence of absence, in the one line consulted to decide whether the writes were
checked. It failed OPEN.

THE REPAIR. The field is REQUIRED, not defaulted. An entry lacking it — or
carrying something that is not a finite number — prints
`UNSTATED — no \ count under <names>, so no total is derived`,
NAMING every benchmark that did not state one; a run that states them all still
prints the SUM (2 and 3 print 5, not merely 'not a refusal'). Number.isFinite is
the predicate, so `null` (a JSON round-trip of NaN) and 'n/a' refuse too — the
old fold took the first as 0 and CONCATENATED the second onto the total as text.
UNSTATED rather than UNMEASURED because nobody measures this one: the rig counts
it and the fault is that it did not say so. The idiom is otherwise #7687's
sibling — all-caps token, em-dash, named cause, 'so no <conclusion> is derived'.

FENCE HELD. The parity and control lines are UNTOUCHED: a missing object prints
DIFFERENT and FAIL, which fails CLOSED, and changing them for symmetry would be
gold-plating. No schema validator. EXPECTED_CELLS still derived from PAIRS;
verdict, buildRows, notMeasured, positive, main and the parity gate untouched.
The whole edit is inside report(), which prints and returns nothing.

NO EXIT CODE CHANGED, established two ways. Structurally: report() is called
before verdict() and mutates nothing. Empirically: the pre-change comparator was
extracted from HEAD (byte-identical) and both versions spawned over one
identical 42-fixture matrix spanning all three documented exit codes, including
nine on the surface the repair reads (field absent from one/two/every benchmark,
null, 'n/a', stated non-zero, a null summary entry, and absent-plus-short and
absent-plus-negative) — '42 fixtures compared; 0 exit-code divergence(s); codes
observed: 0, 1, 2'. A refusal stayed a refusal; this only turns a printed number
into a refusal, never the reverse.

PROVED RED THEN GREEN. Four cases added in the existing in-test mkdtemp idiom,
plus one fixture helper (oursUnverified — JSON.stringify will not write an absent
field any other way). Witness 42 -> 46. The FINAL test file against HEAD's
comparator: 3/46 failed, exit 1. After: 46 passed, exit 0. The fourth case — 'a
run that states every count still prints the SUM' — is green in both BY DESIGN:
the one-way fence a repair turning the line silent, or dropping the sum, would
break. The first also asserts status 0, pinning that a refusal in a REPORTED line
leaves the comparator's own verdict where it was.

GATES: node --check both files 0; witness 0 (46 passed); jsfb_ours_exit_path 0
(41 passed, unchanged); exit-code matrix 0; npm run test:script-helpers 0;
npm run lint:js 0; sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh 0 ('PASS fast PR spine',
docs=false jvm=true node=true); sh scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh
origin/main 0.

THE BENCHMARK WAS NOT RUN and no measurement window was disturbed; every fixture
is synthetic and built in-test, every decision reached through require.main.

CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF (the bead was right): the brief stated 37 top-level cases
on current main and invited me to establish the real number. It is 42, exactly as
this bead's description says. #7687 did not consolidate anything away.

LINE ENDINGS. This bead's own note holds — the suite carries no line-ending
handling — and this change needs none: every new assertion is a single-line
includes or a newline-agnostic regex over spawned stdout. Verified anyway out of
tree rather than by adding machinery: 415-CRLF and 415-bare-LF copies of both
files, 46 passed / exit 0 each. (Counted with node; MSYS grep -c reports the same
count for both files on this box and cannot be trusted for it.)

NOT FIXED, REPORTED — one sibling in the same fold. A NEGATIVE count cancels a
positive one: unverified -5 against +5 still totals 0. That is present-but-wrong
evidence rather than absent evidence, which puts it in rf2-110be's class (a value
that is not a measurement) rather than this one's, and rf2-110be scoped itself to
durations and ratios. The guard would be one conjunct, 's.unverified >= 0', but
adding it here would have turned 'require the field' into 'validate the field',
which this bead's fence forbids. Worth a follow-up bead for the mayor to scope.

title: clock_run.cjs reports a heavy-tailed ratio by its MEAN, and that is why two agreeing ensembles read as disagreeing
description:
RAISED by rf2-8a746's diagnosis (2026-08-07). NOT the gate, and not a licence to touch it: the per-block verdict and the strict rule stay exactly as they are. This is about the number the driver PRINTS and SERIALISES beside them.

WHAT IS WRONG. controlVerdict returns measured: band(perRound), i.e. the arithmetic MEAN, min and max over the run's 18 block ratios. For ctl-2x that is fine — its denominator is a level and its blocks are tight. For the three-point control it is not: the denominator is T(100) - T(1), measured at 1.249 ms against a block-to-block dispersion of 0.599 ms, which is 2.09 sigma from zero. 2.5% of blocks land with abs(den) < 0.2 ms. A ratio with a denominator that close to zero is heavy-tailed and its sample mean is not a summary of anything.

WHAT IT COST. This is not hypothetical — it is the reason two agreeing ensembles were read as disagreeing, and that reading is written into rf2-8a746's description and into rf2-5xrcd. emvod's bulk300 reported "low and tight, 1.3516-1.7838, mean 1.6045" while bulk100 and narrow each reported a run "ranging to 86.05x" and "113.87x". Those are the same experiment: the three-point control's arms are byte-identical on all three bulk rows (clock-app/ctl3-arms takes no row argument). At BLOCK level the three rows are indistinguishable — statistic p50 1.52-1.62, in-band 42-49%, den p50 1.19-1.29 ms on both ensembles. The entire apparent difference in shape is which run happened to draw one near-zero-denominator block, and band().mean then moved that run's headline from ~1.6 to 86x.

WHAT TO DO. Report the three-point control's run figure with a summary that survives its own denominator — the block MEDIAN beside the mean would have shown 1.569 / 1.575 on both ensembles and no shape disagreement would ever have been recorded — and print the denominator in milliseconds beside the ratio, which the JSON already carries as signal.denMs but the console line does not surface. The absolutes-beside-the-ratio rationale is already written into ctl3Verdict's own docstring ("A difference of differences is exactly the statistic whose denominator can quietly shrink to noise, and the only way to see that happening is to look at it in milliseconds") — the data is computed and serialised; it is just not in the summary a reader acts on.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: the band, the slack, the strict every-block rule, the sign gate, the prediction, and any change to what refuses. A refusal must stay a refusal. This changes only how a refused run DESCRIBES itself, so that two ensembles that agree are not read as disagreeing again.

Evidence and arithmetic: ai/findings/2026-08-07.three-point-control-refusal-diagnosed.md sections 1(c) and 4, recomputable from data/clock-emvod/ and data/clock-w3yxd/ with no box.

Headline and ctlNote also now name the denominator in ms; signal.denMs was already computed and serialised but the line a reader acts on did not carry it, exactly as ctl3Verdict's own docstring said it should. The MEAN IS STILL PRINTED, one line down, labelled as the tail-detector it is — a mean far from the median now reads as a statement about the DENOMINATOR rather than about the page. UNTOUCHED as instructed: the band, the slack, the strict every-block rule, the sign gate, the prediction, and ctl-2x (its denominator is a level and its blocks are tight — that is where the scope line falls). NO VERDICT READS p50: controlVerdict.ok is perRound.every(...) over the RAW per-block ratios, ctl3's is that AND sign.ok, ctlBad reads ctl3.ok alone. A REFUSAL STAYS A REFUSAL, proven not asserted: new ctl3SelfTest fixture 10 plus four witness tests drive a run built so the NEW headline looks perfect — 8 clean blocks + 1 with its denominator collapsed to 0.02 ms — median 2.0101x, the prediction to four places, INSIDE the band [1.5076, 2.5126], and ok===false, refused by the band with sign.ok===true. title: MEASURED: the three-point control refuses every bulk run on a quiet box (24 of 24)
description:
rf2-emvod's quiet-window ensemble (8 full-roster runs at c172f22bb0, datasets under implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/clock-emvod/) found rf2-7iqb5's three-point control refusing on EVERY bulk run: bulk300 0/8, bulk100 0/8, narrow 0/8, against a predicted 2.0101x. The box was genuinely quiet - Processor Queue Length 0 before and after, CPU 9-18%.

TWO DISTINGUISHABLE SHAPES, and they are not the same fault:

1. bulk300 sits LOW AND TIGHT: 1.3516 - 1.7838x, mean 1.6045x. That is the same
   direction and roughly the same size as ctl-2x's undershoot on the identical
   samples (mean 1.7880x against 2.00x). A control built to difference the
   additive constant away should not inherit the constant's signature. This does
   not look like box noise.

2. bulk100 and narrow each carry ONE run whose blocks go degenerate: the
   statistic ranges to 86.05x on bulk100 run 7 and to 113.87x on narrow run 7,
   with negative blocks on both. The control's own sign gate caught these, which
   is the gate working; but a per-run rate of 1-in-8 degenerate is itself a
   finding about the estimator's stability at these block sizes.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: no tolerance widened, no gate touched, no third
estimator added. The window was granted for a measurement and the refusal is the
result. Diagnosing it needs a new arm in the page half, which would have changed
the blobs this ensemble was taken at.

The datasets are retained and canonical, so this is re-adjudicable without
re-running the box:
  node freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/clock_readjudicate.cjs     freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/clock-emvod/run*.json

rf2-5xrcd owns the control's calibration. Related: rf2-7iqb5 (the repair),
rf2-emvod, rf2-yd52q.
notes:
ELEVATED BY THE MAYOR 2026-08-07 — this is now the central open question of the programme, not a follow-up.

THE EVIDENCE IS NO LONGER ONE ENSEMBLE. rf2-emvod's window refused 0 of 24 bulk-class runs; rf2-w3yxd's independent census-rig window refused 18 of 18. That is 42 RUNS, NO PASS, across two independent quiet-box ensembles, both with the arm-order guard clean throughout (30 of 30 row-runs in w3yxd, 0 unverified of 42,336) and box counters showing Processor Queue Length 0 before and after.

WHY IT OUTRANKS THE REMAINING MEASUREMENT QUEUE. Six window beads remain at roughly an hour each. If the three-point control cannot adjudicate on a verified quiet box, every bulk row it gates inherits the refusal however carefully it is taken — four more tranches would produce four more correctly-refused rows. Measuring harder cannot repair an instrument that refuses. So this is sequenced BEFORE any further measurement.

IT NEEDS NO WINDOW. Both ensembles are on main (data/clock-emvod/run1-8.json and data/clock-w3yxd/*). This is analysis over committed data, not a re-take, and it must not consume the operator's quiet box.

THE TWO ENSEMBLES DISAGREE ABOUT THE SHAPE OF THE FAILURE, which is itself a clue rather than noise — rf2-5xrcd recorded that. emvod saw bulk300 low and tight (1.35-1.78, the same signature as ctl-2x's undershoot on identical samples) plus one degenerate run each on bulk100 (statistic to 86x) and narrow (to 114x) with negative blocks caught by the sign gate. Whatever explains the refusal has to explain both shapes.

ONE ROW DOES PASS AND THAT CONSTRAINS THE ANSWER: M1's ctl-2x passed 4 of 8 in emvod and 3 of 6 in w3yxd. So the control is not uniformly broken — it discriminates by row class. An explanation that predicts total failure is wrong.
MAYOR CORRECTION 2026-08-07 — my elevation note above contained TWO factual errors, both corrected by the diagnosis, and both were steers I handed the worker as constraints. Recording them so nobody inherits them.

ERROR 1. I wrote: 'M1's ctl-2x passed 4 of 8 and 3 of 6, so the control discriminates by row class; an explanation that predicts total failure is wrong.' FALSE. clock-app/ctl3-arms says the three-point arms 'exist on BULK ROWS ONLY' and arms-for appends them only for :bulk. M1 NEVER RUNS THIS CONTROL. What passes on M1 is ctl-2x — a different statistic. So the three-point control's failure IS TOTAL, 0 of 42, and an explanation predicting total failure is the CORRECT one. I inverted the key constraint and the worker had to overturn it to reach the answer.

ERROR 2. I wrote 'both ensembles are on main'. At the time only clock-emvod was; clock-w3yxd was in open PR #7671 and the worker read it via git show refs/remotes/pr/7671. (7671 has since merged, so the statement is true now but was not when I made it.)

THE REAL DISCRIMINATOR IS THE DENOMINATOR CLASS, NOT THE ROW CLASS. ctl-2x survives because its denominator is a LEVEL — the floor's whole tared reading, ~4.5 ms — carrying the same ~0.4 ms of estimator error, so 9% relative against ctl3's 48%; and its centre sits 20% above the 1.50 edge against ctl3's 4%. Those two numbers, distance-above-edge and per-block scatter, raised to the 18th, reproduce every pass rate in the programme.

AND THE TWO ENSEMBLES NEVER DISAGREED. At block level they agree within 2% on every structural quantity. The apparent disagreement was band().mean over 18 ratios whose denominator sits 2 sigma from zero: 2.5% of blocks have |den| < 0.2 ms, and one such block moves a headline from ~1.6 to 86x. Same rate in both ensembles, all three rows. rf2-5xrcd's premise dissolves; rf2-8bgqq now owns the summary-statistic half.
CROSS-REFERENCE FROM rf2-rguy1 (PR #7673), quiet-box tranche 3 — evidence that
the 42-of-42 refusal is about the CONSTRUCTION, not about bulk operations.

The jsfb harness is an outside workload adjudicated by a DIRECT RATIO against
rf2-reagent, not a difference-of-differences. Re-ran it 2026-08-07 on a quiet box
against the same bundles as the 2026-08-02 published run. On that instrument the
BULK ROWS ARE THE BEST-BEHAVED ROWS IN THE MATRIX, not the worst.

Run-to-run drift, published vs re-take, same box, same bundles:
  replace1k  (BULK)    hicasso +1.7%   uix -2.4%
  swaprows   (BULK)    hicasso +17.0%  uix +7.8%
  run1k      (mount)   hicasso +11.5%  uix +1.5%
  update10th (NARROW)  hicasso -6.3%   uix +32.9%
  clear1k              hicasso +4.3%   uix -1.3%
  create10k  (control) hicasso -1.0%   uix +4.0%

Cross-instrument agreement inside the re-take (ours vs the benchmark's own
driver): "replace all" agrees on BOTH arms (11.9%, 14.3%) and "swap rows" agrees
on BOTH (0.8%, 4.4%); the mount row disagrees on both (21.3%, 24.6%) and the
narrow row disagrees on the donor (21.3%).

So the two bulk rows are simultaneously the most reproducible across two runs of
our instrument AND the most agreed-upon between two independent instruments,
while the NARROW row is the least reproducible of all — the opposite of the
ordering the three-point construction implies.

BOUNDED HONESTLY: one app with trivial state, swaprows drifted 17% on one arm,
and two runs are not an ensemble. This does NOT establish that our bulk rows are
fine. It establishes that a bulk row on this workload is measurable to a couple
of percent by an instrument taking a direct ratio — so the 42-of-42 refusal is
evidence about the difference-of-differences denominator rather than about bulk
operations being inherently unmeasurable. Whether that carries to the census
witnesses is a separate question and is NOT claimed.

Also relevant: the jsfb positive control itself proved non-reproducible across
the two runs (an arm's pass/fail verdict flipped, 12.883x vs a published 13.583x
against an 8-13x band), so control instability is not unique to the three-point
construction either.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7698 (2026-08-09) — REOPENED, NOT DUPLICATED. The calibrated check standard correctly retires the per-block unanimity rule, but the new consumer also accepts incomplete evidence. `checkStandard` validates only a non-empty finite ratio list; a one-element list at the frozen centre returns `ok: true` with `n: 1` and `robustScale: 0`. `checkStandardFor` checks that `roundsTask` is non-empty but never compares its length with `dataset.design.rounds` or the frozen standard provenance. On the committed six-round clock-emvod corpus, truncating a row to one round leaves three segment blocks and several rows still pass the standard. This confuses retiring all-blocks-in-band with allowing blocks to be absent.

Bounded acceptance: enforce the frozen standard's expected evidence cardinality at the consumer boundary (18 blocks for v1, or an explicit expected-blocks field tied to the declared six-round/three-segment design) and reject any missing or extra round/block before computing location or dispersion. Give the direct helper an expected-N contract or keep it private behind that checked boundary. Add a truncated-round/block witness that reaches the nonzero/no-pool decision. Preserve the new location/dispersion rules and do not add a schema framework.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7700 (2026-08-09) — UPDATED EXISTING OPEN OWNER, NOT DUPLICATED. Calibrating mount makes all 14 M1 runs eligible, but the effect-interval consumer can silently select a smaller subset than the runs that cleared every gate. `ivRuns = passIdx.map(pairedLogRatios).filter(Boolean)` drops a reportable run whose raw pair readings are absent or unusable, and `effectInterval` independently filters unusable members. Live witness on committed clock-emvod M1: blanking only `run1`'s `roundsTask[0].hicasso.hicasso` leaves `reportable(row,data) === true`, makes `pairedLogRatios` return null, and still publishes an interval over 7 runs where 8 cleared the gates. The output calls those 7 “reportable run(s)”, concealing that evidence was lost after eligibility was decided.

Bounded acceptance: a reportable run with unusable raw readings for the named pair must refuse that pair/run (with file and pair named) or suppress the entire interval; it must never be filtered into a new unstated subset. Require `ivRuns.length === passIdx.length` and expected per-run round cardinality before pooling, and make `effectInterval` reject rather than filter an invalid member. Add a mutation witness reaching the program's nonzero/no-pool path. This is the same raw-evidence completeness boundary already reopened on rf2-8a746 by audit #7698, so it stays on that owner; preserve the calibrated limits and estimator/publication rulings.
OPERATOR RULING (2026-08-10 03:10 AUSEST, Mike, in session) — OPTION A AT PRIORITY P3: both merged-PR-audit bounded acceptances (#7698 check-standard cardinality; #7700 interval-consumer silent-subset) are RATIFIED and this bead is RELEASED FOR WORKER DISPATCH at P3 (fills idle slots only; never competes with the hic spine). One worker, one PR, both fixes: enforce expected evidence cardinality at the consumer boundary (18 blocks v1 / explicit expected-blocks tied to the declared 6-round x 3-segment design; reject missing/extra with observed/expected); a reportable run with unusable raw pair readings REFUSES that pair/run by name or suppresses the whole interval — never a silent subset; require ivRuns.length === passIdx.length and per-run round cardinality before pooling; effectInterval rejects rather than filters; add truncation witnesses reaching the nonzero/no-pool path; no schema framework. ALL FOUR PARTS of the 2026-08-07 ruling, the fences, and the frozen protocol remain untouched. Bench-tree caution: a file in the rf2-hic-001 freeze manifest stops the worker (surface, do not edit). Twin ruling: rf2-pzqy8 same date, same defect class, census sibling.
MAYOR SEQUENCING NOTE 2026-08-10 03:20 AUSEST — HELD BEHIND rf2-pzqy8, NOT DEFERRED. The operator ruled this bead released and dispatchable, and stated the file sets are disjoint from rf2-pzqy8's. I measured them and they overlap. I am sequencing rather than dispatching concurrently; the ruling is unchanged and this bead goes out the moment pzqy8's PR merges.

THE MEASUREMENT, in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso (hit counts):
  clock_readjudicate.cjs    ctl3=4    checkStandard=8    interval=58
  clock_exit_path.test.cjs  ctl3=34   checkStandard=40   interval=77
  clock_check_standard.cjs  ctl3=2    checkStandard=21   interval=0
rf2-pzqy8's live worker holds all three. This bead's criterion 3 lands the whole-interval verdict rule in the readjudicator, and its criterion 4 removes the all-blocks rule everywhere on this instrument. Both land in those same files.

THE SHARPER REASON, beyond merge conflicts. The two changes pull in OPPOSITE directions in one code path. rf2-pzqy8 ADDS an 18-reading cardinality requirement to the check-standard consumer. This bead's criterion 4 REMOVES the all-blocks rule and says to grep for the caret-18 semantics. Run concurrently, one worker can delete the guard the other is adding, and the trunk ends up with neither or with a half of each. Sequenced, the second worker sees the first's landed code and can tell the census instrument's cardinality rule from this instrument's retired unanimity rule.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: Option A stands, P3 stands (idle-slot only, never a slot from the hic spine hic-001 -> 009 -> the collector chain), both bounded acceptances stand, the four-part 2026-08-07 ruling and its fences and the frozen protocol stay untouched, the worker cites this bead id in code comments, a file in the rf2-hic-001 freeze manifest stops the worker, close on PR-open, and two separate PRs are required.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DIAGNOSED 2026-08-07 18:08 AUSEST from committed data only. NO RUN TAKEN, no quiet box consumed, no gate/tolerance/band/instrument touched. Read data/clock-emvod/run1-8.json on main (3b2ee34754) and data/clock-w3yxd/run1-6.json out of PR #7671's head via git show (nothing on that branch modified). Working notes: ai/findings/2026-08-07.three-point-control-refusal-diagnosed.md.

THE MECHANISM, TWO INDEPENDENTLY FATAL HALVES.

(1) THE PREDICTION IS MIS-DERIVED FOR THE POINTS CHOSEN. (d2-d0)/(d1-d0)=2.0101 is the expectation only if T is affine in d over [1,200]. On the published TaskDuration clock it is not: marginal cost 12.64 -> 6.84 us/cell over [1,100] / [100,200] (emvod), 13.11 -> 7.51 (w3yxd). True centre 1.546 / 1.578 against a band lower edge of 1.5076 -- THE CONTROL'S OWN EXPECTATION SITS 2.6% ABOVE THE VALUE AT WHICH IT REFUSES. Blocks below band 192 of 432 and 135 of 324; above band 35 and 33. That 5.5:1 asymmetry IS the bias as a count.

THE INTERNAL CONTROL THAT PROVES IT: ctl3Layout, the same statistic on LayoutDuration over the IDENTICAL blocks and samples, reads 1.9681 / 1.9801 with marginals 5.42 -> 5.13 and 5.78 -> 5.49 us/cell (affine to 5%), and its sign gate never fired once in 756 blocks. So the arithmetic, the door, the tare and the aggregation are all sound; the PAGE is not affine on the counter the row is published on. The non-layout half carries it: 7.13 -> 1.83 us/cell, a 3.9x collapse, reproduced at 7.36 -> 1.92 on the second ensemble. Until now the paint-saturation account was inherited from a retired witness arm (clock_run.cjs:464-477 records wArm is null on every shipped run); it is now re-measured on both ensembles.

(2) THE ESTIMATOR IS ILL-CONDITIONED, AND THIS ALONE WOULD REFUSE. den = T(100)-T(1) is 1.249 ms carrying 0.599 ms of dispersion -- 2.09 sigma from zero (1.85 on w3yxd). Differencing away the constant also throws away the pedestal that made the relative noise look small: each arm's p50 over 10 samples carries ~0.4-0.9 ms of its OWN estimator error, which is INDEPENDENT between arms and therefore ADDS under differencing. Measured corr(T(1),T(100)) = 0.432 / 0.396, so differencing removes 40% of the denominator's variance where the invariance argument implicitly assumes it removes nearly all (sd(den) 0.599 measured, 0.772 if independent, 0.216 if perfectly common-mode). The construction's claim that an additive constant "cancels in each difference, whatever its size" is TRUE OF THE LEVEL and is not the problem; what destroys the control is the error in each arm's ESTIMATE of that level.

THE FALSIFIABLE CONSEQUENCE, CHECKED ON COMMITTED DATA. On a bulk row the floor arm rewrites all 300 cells of the same page through the same door, so every block already carries a fourth point at d=300. Marginals across all three intervals: 12.64 / 6.84 / 8.27 (emvod), 13.11 / 7.51 / 8.82 (w3yxd) -- [100,200] and [200,300] agree with each other and only [1,100] differs, so THE KNEE IS BELOW d=100 AND THE eps ARM STRADDLES IT. Re-adjudicating the same blocks at 100/200/300 (prediction 2.0000) gives a median statistic of 1.9975 / 2.0777: the premise HOLDS above the knee. AND IT STILL DOES NOT RESCUE THE CONTROL -- den halves to 0.696 ms while its IQR does not (0.516 -> 0.583), so in-band blocks FALL from 47% to 33%. Span the knee and the centre is wrong; avoid it and the denominator is gone. There is no third siting on a 300-boundary page.

THREE FRAMING CORRECTIONS THE EVIDENCE FORCES.

(a) M1 DOES NOT RUN THIS CONTROL. clock-app/ctl3-arms: "they exist on BULK ROWS ONLY"; arms-for appends them only for (= :bulk (:kind ...)). The three-point control's record is 0 of 42 and its failure IS total -- an explanation predicting total failure is the right one. What passes on M1 is ctl-2x, a ratio of two LEVELS not two DIFFERENCES. Its denominator is the floor's whole tared reading (~4.5 ms) carrying the same ~0.4 ms of error, i.e. 9% relative against ctl3's 48%. Centre 1.808/1.780 sits 20% above the 1.50 edge against ctl3's 4%. Per-block in-band 95.1%/95.4% -> 5 of 8 and 4 of 6 runs. On BULK rows the same ctl-2x reads 1.729/1.697 with sd 0.296/0.356 -> 84.7%/77.5% in band -> 4 of 24 and 0 of 18. Two numbers -- distance of the centre above the edge, and per-block scatter -- raised to the 18th power produce EVERY pass rate in this programme, ctl-2x's own row preference included. It is the DENOMINATOR class, not the row class.

(b) THE THREE BULK ROWS ARE THREE REPLICATES OF ONE EXPERIMENT. ctl3-arms takes no row argument: on bulk300/bulk100/narrow the control's arms are byte-identical (floor's own 300-boundary 901-element page, d=1/100/200, one door); only the substrate arms' k changes. Measured per row, T(1) p50 2.63-2.75, den p50 1.19-1.29, statistic p50 1.52-1.62, in-band 42-49% -- indistinguishable. No per-row explanation is needed and none is available.

(c) THE TWO ENSEMBLES DO NOT DISAGREE. At block level they agree to within 2% on every structural quantity. The apparent disagreement is a REPORTING artefact: the run figure is band().mean over 18 block ratios whose denominator is 2 sigma from zero. 2.5% of blocks have abs(den) < 0.2 ms; ONE of them moves a run's reported mean from ~1.6 to 86x or 114x. emvod drew such a block on bulk100 and narrow and not on bulk300 -- that is the whole of "bulk300 low and tight vs two degenerate runs". The rate is the same in both ensembles and across all three rows. The two named degenerates are den=+0.019 ms (T(1)=2.9205, T(100)=2.9395) and den=+0.026 ms (T(1)=3.5090, T(100)=3.5350); in 9 of the 10 worst blocks T(1) is ELEVATED (p50 3.40 against a population 2.66), and T(1) enters BOTH differences, so an excursion in it drives the smaller denominator to zero first. The eps arm is the estimator's single point of failure and the sign gate can only catch it after it crosses (7 of 432, 6 of 324 caught; a further 5 and 3 were positive but under 0.2 ms and were not).

THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION CARRIES ONE INFERENCE THAT DOES NOT SURVIVE: "the same signature as ctl-2x's undershoot on the identical samples". Four lines say they are two phenomena of coincidentally similar size. Per-block correlation between the two statistics is -0.023 (emvod) and +0.036 (w3yxd) over 432/324 PAIRED blocks. On the layout counter they diverge -- ctl3 becomes exact (1.968/1.980) while ctl-2x stays 4-6% short (1.9225/1.8897), because page-doubling has a non-scaling component even in LayoutDuration and the three-point construction does not. The two recovered constants disagree by ~60%: c(2x) = 1.222/1.409 ms against a three-point pedestal T(d=1) tared of 1.732/1.775 ms and a fitted c(3pt) of 1.97 ms -- a genuinely affine T gives one number both ways, and the disagreement IS the non-affinity restated. Mechanically: ctl-2x undershoots on an ADDITIVE constant in d-independent work, which the three-point statistic cancels exactly; ctl3 undershoots on a SATURATING FUNCTION OF THE VERY AXIS THE CONTROL VARIES, which no differencing removes and which ctl-2x is blind to because it never varies d.

HOW MUCH OF THE REFUSAL IS THE 18-BLOCK STRICT RULE, ISOLATED. The layout control has the right centre, healthy conditioning and a sign gate that never fires, with 84.5%/82.1% of blocks in band -- and it STILL passes only 3 of 24 and 1 of 18 runs, because 0.845^18 = 4.8%. Even a control that fully meets its premise barely survives this rule on this instrument.

NO REMEDY IMPLEMENTED AND NONE RECOMMENDED HERE. For the record only, the evidence supports exactly one direction -- a control whose denominator is a LEVEL rather than a DIFFERENCE, i.e. abandoning the difference-of-differences on this rig rather than re-siting its points, since both available sitings are shown to fail and the conditioning arithmetic says why any siting must. That is a decision about what the lane measures, not a threshold to move, and it is Mike's.

WHAT I COULD NOT SETTLE FROM COMMITTED DATA. (i) The attribution of the concave residual specifically to PAINT is inherited, not established: the datasets carry Task/Script/Layout/DevTools and style is 0 throughout -- there is no paint counter. What IS established is that the concave term is in the non-layout half, is 7.1 -> 1.8 us/cell, and saturates below d=100; paint damage-region clipping at the viewport is consistent with that and with layout staying linear, but it is an inference. (ii) The bootstrap SE of a 10-sample median is upward-biased at this n, so treat that table as order-of-magnitude; the corr = 0.43 line is the bootstrap-free version and carries the conclusion alone. (iii) Whether a DIFFERENT instrument reads these rows is not answerable from this data -- rf2-rguy1 is the bead that could.

INHERITANCE FOR THE SIX REMAINING MEASUREMENT BEADS. ctl3Verdict exists in exactly two files, clock_run.cjs and clock_readjudicate.cjs, so only rows taken through clock_run.cjs are gated by it. INHERITS: rf2-2rtt6.59 (names clock_run.cjs and the three-point control explicitly -- its bulk halves refuse on the 0-of-42 evidence, and its M1 half is ctl-2x at ~40% strict pass hunting a few-per-cent effect against a 21-32% band). DOES NOT INHERIT: rf2-pqyxz (walk_profile_app on lane.cljs control-verdict, a two-point overlap-rule control), rf2-ne3ey (arm1/hydration_support.cljs), rf2-2rtt6.138 (p0_heap/p0_run heap ladder), rf2-d360z (read_profile_app, 0.025 ms grid), rf2-rguy1 (external krausest harness). rf2-rguy1 is the one bead that can break the deadlock: its partial-update-every-10th IS the narrow row and its replace-all/swap ARE the bulk rows, on an instrument nobody here wrote whose adjudication is not a difference-of-differences. LOWER CONFIDENCE, offered as a pattern only: rf2-2rtt6.138 and rf2-d360z do not run this control but are both differential measurements whose signal is approaching their instrument's dispersion (.138's r2 of 0.75/0.28/0.94/0.31 against a 0.98 floor; d360z's own "about ONE QUANTUM" of a 0.025 ms grid) -- same class of ill-conditioning, arrived at independently, and a quiet box will not help them either.

DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-07, operator-overturnable): WHAT ADJUDICATES BULK ROWS.

THE RULING, in four parts:

(1) The three-point difference-of-differences control is RETIRED AS A GATE on this instrument — not re-sited, not re-tried. Both dossier and Codex reviews converge here, and the diagnosis is arithmetic: the prediction is mis-derived (TaskDuration is not affine in d — marginal cost 12.6 -> 6.8-7.2 us/cell across [1,100]/[100,200]; the statistic's true centre 1.546-1.578 sits 2.6% ABOVE the 1.5076 refusal edge) AND the estimator is ill-conditioned (den = T(100)-T(1) is 1.249/1.230 ms carrying 0.599/0.667 ms dispersion, 2.09/1.85 sigma from zero, corr(T(1),T(100)) ~ 0.4 — the classic Fieller ratio problem; Franz, arXiv:0710.2024). Re-siting at 100/200/300 fixes the centre (1.9975/2.0777) but halves the denominator: in-band blocks FALL 47% -> 33%. Both available sitings fail; any siting must. The ctl3 statistic may keep printing as a labelled non-gating diagnostic of the page's dirty-set shape (its internal control, ctl3Layout, is healthy: 1.9681/1.9801 on identical blocks, marginals flat 5.4 -> 5.1 us/cell, all 756 numerators/denominators positive — which localises the failure to the non-affine non-layout clock, not the quotient machinery).

(2) The all-18-blocks strict rule is RETIRED WITH IT, everywhere on this instrument. It is a separate defect with its own arithmetic: the premise-meeting layout statistic has 631/756 blocks (83.5%) in-band yet passes only 4/42 runs (0.835^18 = 3.9%); ctl-2x shows the identical pathology (626/756 in-band, 4/42 strict). Swapping controls while keeping "every block" would NOT unblock bulk. Tolerance band and run-rejection rule get DISTINCT, CALIBRATED error rates.

(3) The replacement is a level-denominated, EMPIRICALLY CALIBRATED, versioned check standard — not ctl-2x's literal 2.00x prediction (asserting a theoretical value against a non-affine clock is the exact mistake being retired). Seed from the existing ctl-2x/floor run medians, whose empirical behaviour is already characterised: centre 1.721x, range 1.596-1.829x, between-run SD 0.057 across the 42 committed row-runs. Freeze run-level location and dispersion limits from an independent baseline; prove them against the sabotage fixture; recalibrate on any browser, harness, page, or clock change (NIST e-Handbook 2.3.5 check-standard doctrine). A future same-page arm with KNOWN added main-thread work near the bulk signal scale is the preferred long-term standard but is NOT required to unblock.

(4) The product claim is adjudicated on the quantity it asserts: the paired, same-round Hicasso/Reagent level ratio at fixed witness and fixed K, reported as an effect-size confidence interval from a run-preserving hierarchical analysis (paired log-ratios; resample outer runs before inner blocks — Kalibera & Jones 2013). Ship/kill publishes ONLY when the whole interval lies on the required side of 1.0 (bar) / 1.5 (architecture-kill) AND the effect clears the same-run noise band; otherwise the row publishes INSTRUMENT-LIMITED, never a magnitude. This protocol is FROZEN IN WRITING before the next bulk window opens — rows must never again be taken with no pre-registered rule to adjudicate them.

UNCHANGED: the hard refusals stay hard (read-back, canonical-DOM, page-error, arm-order, quiet-box, band-ceiling). jsfb remains the OUTSIDE CORROBORATOR, never the census witness (its bulk rows are the best-behaved in the matrix — replace1k drift +1.7%/-2.4%, cross-instrument agreement 0.8-14.3% — which is what localises the refusal to our construction; bounded honestly: one trivial-state app, two runs). The 42 committed row-runs (clock-emvod run1-8, clock-w3yxd run1-6) remain calibration/diagnostic evidence and are NOT retroactively promoted to published magnitudes.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA for the implementation worker (one bounded protocol change in the driver + readjudicator; no stats research project):
  1. Bulk verdict paths stop consulting ctl3; its printout is relabelled diagnostic/non-gating; no re-siting code.
  2. The check standard lands as data (versioned expected centre + frozen location/dispersion limits) with the sabotage-fixture proof pinned by a test.
  3. The whole-interval verdict rule lands in the readjudicator with the run-preserving resampling, pinned by a test on the committed 42-run corpus (expected output: instrument-limited or a clean interval — whatever the data says, the test pins the procedure not the answer).
  4. The all-blocks rule is removed everywhere on this instrument in the same PR (grep for the ^18 semantics), with the calibrated replacement's error rates stated in the code comment.
  5. Everything above cites this ruling by bead id.

SEQUENCING CONSEQUENCE: the window beads queued behind this ruling may be scheduled once the protocol freeze (criteria 2-4) lands — rf2-2rtt6.59's bulk halves adjudicate under the new standard; rf2-pqyxz, rf2-ne3ey, rf2-d360z, rf2-2rtt6.138 do not inherit ctl3 (different instruments) but d360z/.138 carry the recorded same-class ill-conditioning caution. No new bulk window before the freeze. The mount half of the instrument question is rf2-t2flm's ruling (concurrent, separate note); one finding here feeds it by id: ctl-2x's true centre is empirical (~1.72-1.80 by row class), not 2.00x, so any mount decision function should state its expectation empirically too.

RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY (carried, not resolved): the datasets carry no paint counter — "non-layout and saturating below d=100" is established; that PAINT specifically causes the concavity is not. Do not state paint-causation in any published row.

title: hicasso: pin the mid-adoption revision timing row on the .84 hydration harness
description:
SPLIT OUT OF rf2-zq8kh, which implemented the revision prop. R3 of docs/design/hicasso/studio/revision-prop-spec.md demoted the design's mid-adoption claim ('a revision arriving during hydration adoption lands on the first post-adoption commit, on the SERVER's node') to witness-gated intent, with the fallback pre-committed: if React deopts, the documented conduct becomes deferral past adoption.

WHAT rf2-zq8kh SETTLED. The claim is not the prop's to make. ::h/revision is consumed at the codec before emission — native-element reads it off the author's own pre-merge map and install! deletes the marker as it reads it — so React is handed a prop-identical element whether the revision moved or not. front/revision_dom_cljs_test pins that structurally: same emitted slots, same values, same element type, with the revision, with a different revision, and with none. Nothing on React's side can branch on a value it was never given. HD-019's addendum and authoring.md both document the deferral as the shipped conduct.

WHAT IS LEFT. Two hand-rolled hydrateRoot arms in that PR disagreed about node identity across consecutive runs — node lost on one run, kept on the next — which is React's own adoption race, not the prop's doing. A row that pins adoption TIMING needs the .84 hydration harness (arm1/hydration_support.cljs), which exists precisely because hydrateRoot returns before the tree is adopted and naive settling is wrong. A hand-rolled race in the DOM suite would be a flake, so it was deliberately not shipped.

SCOPE: add the timing row on the .84 harness — hydrate, bump mid-adoption, and pin whichever conduct the harness can make deterministic. If it cannot be made deterministic, say so and close: the deferral is already the documented conduct and nothing depends on the row.

MEASURED on arm1/hydrate_dom_cljs_test section 6: the server's node survives (identical?, expando stamp intact); React reports on neither channel; ONE body run across the whole adoption, so the mid-adoption write produced no render of its own; the reset does NOT land, the draft typed into the server-rendered field surviving while the defaultValue mirror holds the model's; and the field is not stranded, because the next revision change after the window shuts resets it on the server's own node, without remount, on one ordinary commit.

THE MECHANISM, which also explains why rf2-zq8kh's hand-rolled arms flaked and this does not: the mid-adoption write reaches NO COMMITTED BOUNDARY — the arm acquires at COMMIT and the adoption commit is the first one — so it notifies nothing, and the already-scheduled adoption render reads the new revision as the field's FIRST, a change with no predecessor to be a change from. The hand-rolled arms called root.render mid-adoption and so DID reach React's scheduler; a store write does not.

Nothing can interleave; there is nothing to settle. Ten consecutive narrowed runs: 10/10 identical.

title: hicasso: the census driver collects Script/Layout/RecalcStyle durations and drops them at write time
description:
FILED BY THE MAYOR 2026-08-07 on the rf2-2rtt6.56 worker's hand-off (PR #7639), which left acceptance part (4) of the #7379 audit deliberately unfinished and said why.

THE FINDING. shapes/census_clock_run.cjs collects ScriptDuration, LayoutDuration and RecalcStyleDuration at lines 383-411, then DROPS them when it writes the dataset. So the studio page's cited decomposition — 'layout 2.06x, style 1.85x, script 2.3x' — is not recomputable from any committed dataset. The numbers were real when taken; nothing on disk can reproduce them.

WHY IT WAS NOT JUST FIXED IN #7639. Adding the capture is a small change, but capture alone changes nothing: the existing datasets still lack the fields, so the figures only become recomputable on a RE-RUN. That makes this measurement-coupled, and the box has been contended all day. The worker correctly declined to take a row it could not trust, and declined to add capture that would look like a fix while proving nothing.

SEQUENCING. This belongs BESIDE the matched-workload re-run, not before it — rf2-2rtt6.62's retraction established that large_template.cljs seeds 69 articles and feed.cljs seeds 300 through the same arithmetic, so the roster needs matching seeds before any cross-row row is worth taking. Do both in one quiet-box session: match the workloads, add the metric capture, re-run, republish. One window, one dataset, both problems closed.

ACCEPTANCE: the three durations present in every committed dataset, and the published decomposition recomputable from them by the same fail-closed aggregator discipline used elsewhere in this corpus (a stored figure that does not reproduce must exit non-zero).

Pre-alpha posture: do not add capture as a standalone change. Un-recomputable prose plus capture-without-data is two half-measures where one quiet run closes it properly.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7666 (2026-08-07). COMPLETENESS: the per-block persistence is the right instrument-prep slice, and the current datasets/quiet-window remainder is already exactly owned by open rf2-jv36i, so no duplicate was created for the re-run. The driver now carries the collected Script/Layout/RecalcStyle sums plus n into the dataset, and the report folds the same blocks. Current syntax passes and clock_exit_path.test.cjs passes all 189 checks.

CORRECTNESS — REOPENED THIS EXACT OWNER. `foldDecomposition` is not actually fail-closed at the evidence boundary promised by this Bead. It rejects only a non-array or an outer `[]`; `foldDecomposition([[]])` and `foldDecomposition([[{}]])` both return `{}`. More seriously, `acc[k] += a[k] || 0` silently turns a missing, null, or NaN metric into zero. A live probe on the landed function showed a partial arm lacking task/taskNet/devtools/script/layoutCount/inPage was accepted with every missing field synthesized as 0, and an explicit null script was accepted as script 0. That permits partial/corrupt persisted evidence to become a plausible ratio instead of the required non-zero refusal — the same defect class this PR is meant to close. The new committed-dataset test branches only on the truthiness of `row.blocksDecomp`, so it cannot catch this third state.

Required before re-closing: validate the actual nested evidence shape rather than defaulting it. Require nonempty rounds and blocks; the expected arm roster in every block; every accumulator field present and finite; positive counts where required; and refuse missing/null/nonfinite values. Add hermetic mutation witnesses for `[[]]`, `[[{}]]`, an absent arm, a missing metric, null/NaN, and prove the invalid row reaches a non-zero driver outcome rather than a canonical write. Keep this bounded inside the existing fold/write path; no validation framework is needed. rf2-jo60g is the exact fail-closed persistence owner.

---- NOTES RESTORED 2026-08-07 23:10 AUSEST ----
The notes above were recovered from .beads/issues.jsonl at commit 31099a515d after the mayor overwrote them with `bd update --notes`, which REPLACES rather than appends (the correct flag is --append-notes). The mayor note that caused the loss follows, preserved verbatim.

MAYOR RULING 2026-08-07 22:45 AUSEST, on the worker's flagged question: does the newly-landed censusclock-jv36i dataset satisfy this bead's acceptance?

THE QUESTION. The worker found that censusclock-jv36i ALREADY carries blocksDecomp — the matched-workload re-take landed in 623c9341af, AFTER this bead's 03:46 comment, so the premise that all four datasets still lack the fields is stale. Its stricter validation accepts that dataset unchanged (6x3 blocks, consistent rosters, all fields finite, n=10), which is good evidence the new checks are tight rather than over-tight. But BOTH its files record canonical=false / "C56CLOCK_DATA_DIR named this destination".

RULED: ACCEPTANCE NOT SATISFIED. The re-run half stays open.

WHY. The two-tier write policy (rf2-2rtt6.31) exists to say exactly one thing: only a gate-passing, full-published-shape run may back a published claim, refused/partial/overridden runs write the same shape to a .unpublished sibling and self-describe, and CONSUMERS FAIL CLOSED. A published figure recomputed from a canonical=false dataset is precisely the case that clause forbids. It does not matter that this file's notCanonicalWhy is a PROVENANCE reason (a named destination directory) rather than a quality one — the moment we start reading notCanonicalWhy to decide which false verdicts we are willing to overlook, the field stops being a gate and becomes advisory, and it stops being a gate EVERYWHERE, not just here. rf2-emvod's whole consumer half was landed to prevent that. I am not going to hollow it out for one row.

SO THE BAR HAS MOVED BUT NOT BEEN MET, and the remaining scope is now NARROWER than the description says. Capture has landed; the re-run no longer needs to add anything. title: hicasso: routing is 25% of in-page mount on EVERY arm and no bead owns it as a whole-anchor cost
description:
FILED BY THE MAYOR 2026-08-07 on rf2-409ab's explicit hand-off ('FOLLOW-UP WORTH A BEAD (not filed here, mayor's call)').

THE FINDING, with rf2-409ab's measured absolutes. Routing costs 25% of the census page's in-page mount ON EVERY ARM: 6.26 us/anchor for route-link, 5.50 us/anchor for the twins' hoisted route-attrs, across 207 anchors.

WHY IT WAS NOT FILED AS A DEFICIT. It is not one. Both arms pay it, so it cancels in every ratio the programme gates on and it moves no ship number. That is exactly why no existing bead owns it — every bead in this lane is scoped to a DIFFERENCE between arms, and this is a term they share.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH OWNING. It is the single largest non-React term on the page. A cost that cancels in the ratio does not cancel for the user: it is a quarter of the mount they actually wait through, on the shape the programme has chosen as its witness. Nothing in the tracker currently makes that visible, so it can only be rediscovered.

SCOPE DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN. This is a placeholder for OWNERSHIP, not a dispatch. Before anyone works it, an operator or mayor call is needed on whether a whole-anchor routing cost is in scope for EP-0038 at all, or belongs to the routing surface independently of Hicasso. Do not dispatch implementation off this bead without that call.

Pre-alpha posture note: filed because it is well-evidenced and unowned, NOT because it is automatically work. A future triage may reasonably close it as out of scope — but it should close it deliberately rather than never see it.
close_reason:
CLOSED AS OUT OF SCOPE — deliberate triage call by the mayor 2026-08-07, which is exactly what this bead asked for ('A future triage may reasonably close it as out of scope — but it should close it deliberately rather than never see it').

THE FIGURES, preserved here so closing does not lose them: routing is ~25% of the census page's in-page mount ON EVERY ARM — 6.26 us/anchor for route-link, 5.50 us/anchor for the twins' hoisted route-attrs, across 207 anchors (measured by rf2-409ab).

WHY OUT OF SCOPE. EP-0038 is scoped to DIFFERENCES BETWEEN ARMS. Both arms pay this term, so it cancels in every ratio the programme gates on and moves no ship number. A shared term that cancels in every gated ratio is by construction not this programme's business. Verified: route-link is a CORE surface (core_routing.cljc, core.cljc, frame.cljc), not a Hicasso construct.

THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES IT, and it is sharp: rf2-cno31 (8.21 us/link at mount) was filed AND closed precisely because it MOVED A RATIO. This bead falls the other side of that line.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN IT: a user-facing absolute mount-latency budget. Verified none exists — HD-012's bar is a ratio and validation.md gates nothing on absolutes. If routing cost ever matters, file it against the ROUTING surface with its own witness and baseline, where it belongs, rather than reviving it here.

title: Provenance-pin checker: every cited authored head must be accompanied by a resolvable landed SHA
description:
Follow-up to rf2-owq6p's census (PR #7616), which found 44 stranded pins across 79 occurrences on 24 pages, ALL reachable from no remote ref.

THE RULE TO ENFORCE, in the census worker's formulation and NOT the mayor's first one: 'every cited AUTHORED head must be accompanied by a RESOLVABLE LANDED SHA'. Do NOT enforce 'no authored heads' or 'every SHA must be on main' — several pages legitimately RETAIN the authored head on purpose, alongside a blob-table fallback, and a must-be-on-main rule would red them precisely for being careful. That distinction is the difference between a gate people keep and one they route around.

MECHANISM: one command per pin, git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main; non-zero means stranded. Then the accompaniment check.

THE HARD PART IS THE POPULATION, NOT THE TEST. The census found 319 unique hex tokens under docs/design/hicasso/**, of which only 77 are commits at all — 188 are content digests and FNV hashes that must NOT be treated as pins. Any checker has to distinguish a commit SHA from a digest without a roster, or it will red on hashes forever. Read how the census did it rather than re-deriving.

DO NOT MAKE IT RE-PIN AUTOMATICALLY. rf2-owq6p established that re-pinning restores the PATCH, not the TREE: where the rebase did not preserve every blob the commit contributed, a re-pin swaps an UNRESOLVABLE pin for a RESOLVABLE BUT WRONG one, which fails SILENTLY — worse than the defect. Two of eleven repaired pins were in exactly that state and were annotated rather than re-pinned. A checker may REPORT; a human decides.

FAILURE DIRECTION: this gate must fail toward refusal, never toward silence. A pin it cannot classify is a finding, not a pass.

REMAINING SCOPE not covered by #7616: 33 of the 44 stranded pins are unrepaired, plus production-server-arm.md:704 (952a3f2024) which sat outside that PR's fence, plus two '*(filled on merge — …)*' anchors that were never filled, plus cross-checked-against-an-outside-instrument.md whose 'repaired' pin 3680992949 is ITSELF authored and equally stranded.

title: spec/002 never mentions the ambient-refusal tier, so the ONE exception to 'a carried stamp wins' has nothing to hang off
description:
FOLLOW-UP from rf2-ur3ey (PR #7614), which fixed the spec/009 catalogue row and deliberately did NOT touch spec/002.

rf2-ur3ey's closing aside asks for a line in spec/002 §Frame target resolution: 'a carried stamp wins' now has exactly one documented exception (opt-in, substrate-declared via :extent-frame on the refusal detail), and the reason is the standing frames-are-isolated-contexts principle rather than a resolution rule.

THE OBSTACLE, measured: spec/002 does not mention the refusal tier ANYWHERE. Grepping 002-Frames.md for 'ambient-frame-refused' / 'call-with-ambient-frame-refused' finds nothing; the only 'refus' hits are the tier-3 machine-redirect and dispatch-opt paragraphs. So the exception line has nothing to attach to — writing it means first introducing the REFUSAL tier to 002 (the tier a substrate establishes through re-frame.frame/call-with-ambient-frame-refused, which withdraws the ambient/React-context tier for a dynamic extent). That is a real piece of normative writing, not a clause, so it was filed rather than smuggled in behind a hot-zone fence.

WHAT 002 CURRENTLY SAYS THAT IS AFFECTED, precisely:
- §How a frame is carried — scope / hold / override, the override row: 'Always wins; the right shape for callbacks, tools, tests, SSR.' STILL TRUE and must stay — a {:frame ...} opt never consults the resolver, so it is untouched inside a refusing extent, including on the mismatch arm.
- The SCOPE row (with-frame / frame-provider / frame-root / the router's per-handler binding) is the one the exception bites: inside an extent whose refusal names :extent-frame :a, a with-frame :b stamp is REFUSED (:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused, with :extent-frame and :carried-frame both on the payload). A MATCHED stamp still carries; a refusal naming no :extent-frame admits every carried stamp.

So the asymmetry worth stating is that the exception is scoped to the AMBIENT-resolution spellings, not to carrying as such — which is also why 002's invariant ('frame identity is carried, not found') survives intact: the refusal deletes the FINDING, and refuses only a carried stamp that would put two frames in one body.

SOURCE OF TRUTH for the mechanism: implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc — the block comment at ~L519-566, *ambient-frame-refusal*, carried-frame-admitted-by, resolve-current-frame, require-current-frame!. The spec/009 :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused row (as landed by PR #7614) is the prose to be consistent with.

spec/** is a hot zone; sequence, do not parallelise.
close_reason:
PR #7621. spec/002 §Frame target resolution now carries §The refusal tier, stating the CONDITION (resolving a frame ambiently inside a refusing extent) rather than an enumeration, consistent with the spec/009 row as corrected by PR #7614 — including that the door is the READER, not the requiring primitive.

The tier lands small because it is not new machinery for 002: 002's invariant is 'carried, not found', and a refusing extent is that invariant enforced strictly — the refusal deletes the FINDING, never the carrying. A section, not an apparatus.

OVERRIDE/SCOPE SPLIT VERIFIED FROM SOURCE, with one correction to the filing's two-row framing. override untouched on both arms (subs.cljc:1709/1856, router.cljc:343 all short-circuit on (:frame opts) before the resolver) — 'Always wins' stays verbatim. scope is the row the exception bites (carried-frame-admitted-by; frame_resolver_test.clj asserts matched/mismatched/no-extent-frame). But a THIRD row is touched: HOLD. Its capture-frame entry covers the no-arg form, which resolves ambiently in order to CAPTURE and so refuses inside an extent (1-arity never consults the resolver and still carries). Nothing held is refused — the refusal reaches the ambient capture that STARTS a hold, not the carrying that follows. This is exactly why the condition beats an enumeration: 002 §Resolver surface already lists 'no-arg rf/capture-frame' among the ambient-resolving ops, so the condition covers it for free where a two-row enumeration would have silently excluded it.

Also recorded in the section: the refusal cuts WITHIN the scope intent — the React-context tier (frame-provider/frame-root) is withdrawn unconditionally, the dynamic tier (with-frame / router per-handler binding) still answers except on the mismatch arm.

Two smaller repairs at points 002 was incomplete rather than merely silent: a pointer under the scope/hold/override table (rows read as unconditional), and a third bullet in §The error and its ladder, which presented a CLOSED two-way discrimination (absent vs bad explicit target) into which a refusal fits neither — an implementer reading 002 alone would have emitted :rf.error/no-frame-context for a refused resolution. Plus the §Resolved decisions EP-0002 row amended with a pointer.

title: hicasso: freehand src :render displayName carries a keyword colon the measure name strips
description:
Found while delivering rf2-2rtt6.127 (PR #7613). Reporting only -- which side moves is an operator call, and the worker's fence forbade touching implementation/**.

Spec 009 Naming convention requires that the <view-id> in the measure name and the id the substrate publishes to the developer (React displayName, the registrar key) be ONE identifier, 'so a name read off the User-Timing stream is directly jumpable in the tooling'.

The two live :render emit sites spell it differently:

* arm1 bench -- defview mints a STRING view-name ("my.ns/todo-row", see arm1/lang.clj). mint-view! stamps that verbatim as displayName and hands the same string to mark-and-measure. displayName and the measure id are byte-identical. Witnessed by arm1/render_measure_cljs_test.cljs.

* freehand src -- the descriptor view-id is a KEYWORD: freehand.cljc:335 (keyword (str ns-sym) (str sym)). freehand/react.cljs sets displayName via (str view-id), and CLJS renders a keyword WITH its leading colon -> ":app.todo/todo-row". performance/build-name's keyword arm strips it -> "rf:render:app.todo/todo-row". React DevTools therefore shows one character more than the rf:render: filter accepts; pasting the DevTools name into a filter yields rf:render::app.todo/todo-row and misses.

Arguably cosmetic -- both spellings are jumpable, which is the spec's purpose clause -- but it should be settled deliberately BEFORE the product defview is minted and the spelling freezes. Three ways out: (a) stamp (subs (str view-id) 1) / the namespaced name on the freehand displayName; (b) mint the product view-id as a string as the bench arm does; (c) rule the colon acceptable and say so in Spec 009 Naming convention so the next reader does not re-file this.

No test currently pins the freehand src product-path displayName -- every displayName assertion in implementation/freehand/test is against the bench arm or the codec -- so whichever way it is ruled, a row is worth adding.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7613 (merged 2026-08-06T12:17:21Z, ecc1b643ca5bcb110a284bf407a2b35bf53540c7) — UPDATE THIS EXACT OPEN OWNER, NO DUPLICATE. The PR correctly adds the missing Hicasso :render guidance, but its landed sentence says the profile-filter name is the name React DevTools shows. On the live freehand src path that is false for the keyword view id: displayName is (str :app.todo/todo-row) => :app.todo/todo-row, while performance/build-name yields rf:render:app.todo/todo-row; pasting the DevTools name produces a double-colon filter and misses. Direct JVM probe reproduced both spellings. Keep rf2-2rtt6.127 closed; this bead already owns the exact mismatch. Its resolution must reconcile the landed guide sentence as well as the code/spec choice, and pin the product-path displayName/filter relationship.
MAYOR RULING (2026-08-06): THE displayName MOVES, not build-name. Use the same name-building the measure uses, so the identifier is genuinely one.

WHY THIS SIDE. build-name's keyword arm already strips the leading colon, and it does so for ALL FOUR Performance buckets — rf:event:, rf:sub:, rf:fx:, rf:render:. Changing it would either break three buckets that are correct today or special-case one, and would emit rf:render::app.todo/todo-row with a double colon. react.cljs's (str view-id) is the odd one out, not the convention.

WHY IT MATTERS UNDER THE STANCE rather than being cosmetic. Spec 009's Naming convention states the requirement and its purpose: the measure name and the id the substrate publishes to the developer must be ONE identifier, 'so a name read off the User-Timing stream is directly jumpable in the tooling'. The whole ergonomic point is that a developer reads a name in React DevTools and pastes it into a User-Timing filter. Today that paste MISSES — displayName shows ':app.todo/todo-row' while the measure is 'rf:render:app.todo/todo-row'. A tool that silently returns nothing when you use it exactly as documented is worse than one that has no filter, because the developer concludes the trace is absent rather than that the name is wrong.

WHY IT IS SMALL: one site. The bench arm's defview mints a STRING, so displayName and the measure id already agree there — which is why no existing witness catches this and why the divergence is confined to the product path at freehand.cljc:335 minting a keyword.

SETTLE IT BEFORE THE PRODUCT defview FREEZES THE SPELLING. That is the bead's own reason for existing and it is the right one — after the freeze this becomes a compatibility question instead of a one-line fix. No test pins the freehand-src displayName today, so the fix needs a witness that would have caught it: assert the two strings are equal for a KEYWORD-minted view, not merely that each is well-formed.

Reproduce the mismatch before changing anything, and reproduce the paste failure rather than only the string difference — the failure the user experiences is the filter returning nothing.
close_reason:
DELIVERED in PR #7623 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7623) — open, NOT merged.

RULING PREMISE CONFIRMED IN SOURCE. There is exactly one `build-name`, its `<id>` half is one `cond` with no per-bucket arm, and `mark-and-measure` passes the bucket straight through, so all four buckets (rf:event:/rf:sub:/rf:fx:/rf:render:) share it. PASTE FAILURE REPRODUCED before any change, against the real `v/defview` mint: view-id `:user/todo-row` (keyword), DevTools `":user/todo-row"`, measure `"rf:render:user/todo-row"`, pasted filter `"rf:render::user/todo-row"`, FILTER HITS `[]`. FENCE WIDENED BY TWO STAMPS, deliberately: `behaviors/behavior-el` (the COMPILED twin of the interpreted v/behavior boundary — fixing only react.cljs would show `re-frame.freehand/behavior` beside `:re-frame.freehand/behavior` in one tree) and the v/error-boundary class in error_react.cljs (the last stamp of the same expression; phase.cljs already uses colon-free literals). `v/->react`'s decorated wrapper name left alone.

THE BEAD'S SCOPE CLAIM WAS WRONG — "confined to the product path" is not correct. The ADAPTER path has the identical defect: implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs brackets `(mark-and-measure :render id …)` at L552 and stamps `(str id)` at L586, on the first-class actively-supported substrate, with TWO LANDED ASSERTIONS pinning the colon spelling (adapters/reagent/test/…/reg_view_devtools_cljs_test.cljs). Not fixed here — deleting deliberate landed assertions on a shipping surface is an operator call. Filed as rf2-976bw (P2) with the one-token fix spelled out; entry-id was made public precisely so that path can reuse it.
