GATES all rc=0: freehand JVM 1291/8874, core JVM 2233/11645, node-test-freehand CLJS 1405/7778, full node-test CLJS 12734/63868. Mutations proved both directions on both hosts; the one green (reverting the emitter, on the JVM) is a real property — react.cljs is CLJS-only, so no JVM run can discriminate it, which is stated in the PR rather than hidden.

title: check-ui-adapter-isolation.cjs may share check-per-ns-isolation's three-causes-one-verdict misclassification
description:
Discovered by the rf2-v8561 worker while fixing the sibling gate (PR #7608, 2026-08-06). It did not touch this file and did not verify the defect is present — this is a CHECK, not an established finding.

THE DEFECT IN THE SIBLING, for the shape to look for: check-per-ns-isolation.cjs treated THREE distinct causes of a non-zero standalone exit as one verdict, and reported all three as the first (a fixture leak). The three are ISOLATION (a real leak — fixture remedy), ROSTER (a stale curated list — two prior commits, 9dd9633d0b and d3969eb67b, are both fixes for exactly that after the gate blamed fixtures), and ENVIRONMENT (the bundle vanished mid-sweep — the run is INDETERMINATE and its greens are worth no more than its reds).

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS STRUCTURAL AND TRANSFERS: --test=<ns> is a RUNTIME selector over a bundle that links EVERY test namespace, so a module-load crash cannot single a namespace out. A red carrying 'Ran N tests containing M assertions.' is a verdict ABOUT that namespace; a red without one never was. The repaired gate exits 2 for the environment case and requires a NON-ZERO test count before accepting a green.

WHAT TO CHECK HERE: whether check-ui-adapter-isolation.cjs has the same --self-test shape and the same conflation. If it does, the same three-way split and the non-zero-count floor apply. If it does not — for instance because it does not spawn per-namespace over a shared bundle — say so and close; a sibling sharing a filename pattern is not evidence of a shared defect.

Fence: implementation/scripts/check-ui-adapter-isolation.cjs and its self-test.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: VERDICT: the defect does NOT transfer. check-per-ns-isolation spawns one node process per curated namespace over a SHARED out/node-test.js, so --test=<ns> is a runtime selector and a module-load crash cannot single a namespace out — that is what made the three causes indistinguishable. check-ui-adapter-isolation spawns nothing per namespace: Arm 1 reads out/node-test-ui.js ONCE as text and runs no test; Arm 2 spawns exactly one clojure -Stree. No roster, no sweep, no runtime selector, so the discriminator has no referent. title: Spec-Schemas: three *Tags schemas still declare :where as :any, the slot rf2-j4bg3 just proved is unenforced

title: docs(hicasso): the-candidates-clock section 3 says residue is 'zero on both censuses'; body-children never is

WHY IT MATTERS rather than being pedantry: lane/residue's own docstring says a container whose arm survived its unmount 'shows up here as a page the NEXT row is measured on top of'. That signal is a READING AGAINST A BASELINE -- 3 where 2 was expected. The arm1 census IS zero on all five integers, so the sentence is only wrong about the lane half, and only about that one integer of the three. SCOPE: one sentence in section 3. Decide whether to state the lane census as 'returns to its baseline -- body-children 2, the harness's own div and script, with sub-entries and sub-ref-count zero' or to have the driver subtract the scaffold; prefer the former, since changing what the driver reports is a measurement change. title: fast-PR spine: three CLJS namespaces fail per-ns isolation (views-current-component, story open-in-editor-ownership, story presence-real-clock)
description:
FOUND by rf2-t84ee's worker, 2026-08-06, running `sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` at 5a08b14a29 in a clean worktree with a fresh `npm ci`. THE SPINE EXITS 1 and the classification line is:

  FAIL per-ns test isolation
  repro: cd implementation && node scripts/check-per-ns-isolation.cjs

Three namespaces are RED when run alone and green in the consolidated bundle:

  re-frame.views-current-component-cljs-test
  re-frame.story.open-in-editor-ownership-cljs-test
  re-frame.story.play.presence-real-clock-cljs-test

each exit=1 at `implementation/out/node-test.js:3531` on module load. The gate
states the diagnosis itself: they pass in the consolidated bundle ONLY because a
sibling left runtime state behind (typically an installed substrate adapter), and
consolidated-bundle ordering is not a contract. Its own remedy is to give each
failing namespace a fixture installing its OWN adapter and resetting runtime
state -- `(use-fixtures :each (test-support/make-reset-runtime-fixture {:adapter plain-atom/adapter}))`.

NOT CAUSED BY THE PR THAT FOUND IT. rf2-t84ee's diff is one comment block in
`implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/lane_cache.cjs` -- no
executable line, and nothing that can reach a CLJS namespace. PR #7579 is 50 pass
/ 35 skipping / 0 fail on GitHub, so the surface-detection gates skip this lane
for a diff like that and CI did not see it. The spine on a developer box does.

The three namespaces should be checked against main to confirm the red is
pre-existing rather than a same-day landing, then given the fixture the gate
names. Everything else in the spine was green: JVM core 1288 tests / 8857
assertions / 0 failures, JVM freehand, the JS harness helpers, and the drift and
self-test phases.
notes:
DOES NOT REPRODUCE IN THE MAYOR CHECKOUT, AND MAIN IS GREEN — this is worktree-local, not a tree defect (mayor, verified 2026-08-06).

I RAN THE BEAD'S OWN REPRO: cd implementation && node scripts/check-per-ns-isolation.cjs. EXIT 0, zero fail lines, and all three named namespaces reported ok by name:
    isolating re-frame.subs-override-seam-cljs-test ... ok
    isolating re-frame.views-current-component-cljs-test ... ok
    isolating re-frame.story.open-in-editor-ownership-cljs-test ... ok
CI on origin/main is green on every job at the same moment.

BOTH SIGHTINGS SHARE A CAUSE THAT IS NOT THE CODE. Per-ns isolation recompiles each namespace on its own and reads shadow build output; it fails when that output is missing or half-written under it. Sighting 1 (walkprune worker): I REAPED ITS WORKTREE MID-RUN, and its next command found .git gone - it said so. Sighting 2 (cacheaudit worker): it had just run npm ci in a fresh worktree and built 22 bundles across three drivers; the isolation pass reads the same .shadow-cljs tree those builds churn.

SO THE DISCRIMINATOR FOR NEXT TIME: a per-ns isolation red in a WORKER WORKTREE, with main green and the mayor checkout clean, is almost certainly the build tree moving underneath the gate - not three namespaces that genuinely leak. The cheap check is the one I just ran: execute the repro in the mayor checkout. It takes under a minute and settles it.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT REAL: the same three namespaces failing in a checkout where nothing else is building, or a CI red on that job. Neither has happened. Leaving the bead OPEN rather than closing, because two sightings in one day is a pattern worth keeping visible even when both have benign explanations - and because the gate arguably should distinguish "namespace leaks" from "build output vanished", which is the fail-open shape this project has spent the session removing. THAT distinction, not the three namespaces, is the thing worth fixing if anyone touches this.
CONFIRMED DOES NOT REPRODUCE, and the mechanism is now demonstrated rather than inferred (worker, PR #7608).

Clean worktree off origin/main, fresh npm ci, fresh node-test compile, the bead's own repro twice: exit 0 both times, all 17 namespaces green, 196 tests / 731 assertions. The three named namespaces standalone: views-current-component 3 tests/4 assertions, story open-in-editor-ownership 5/13, story presence-real-clock 6/31.

THE STRUCTURAL TELL the earlier notes did not have: those three are the LAST THREE ENTRIES OF THE ROSTER, CONSECUTIVELY. Not three independent fixture defects - a contiguous tail, which is what you get when something collapses partway through a sweep that spawns one node process per namespace over ~4.5 minutes (measured: 276s).

MECHANISM PROVEN BY INJECTION, not argument. compile-node-test.cjs unlinks out/node-test.js before every compile so a failed one leaves nothing stale (rf2-6t03c) - so a compile starting mid-sweep pulls the bundle from under every run still to come. Unlinking the bundle 225s into the 276s sweep reds EXACTLY those three namespaces, namespace for namespace, with nothing wrong with any fixture. Both recorded sightings were worktrees with other builds running; this matches them.

WHAT SHIPPED is the thing this bead's own last note nominated - the gate now distinguishes cause, instead of answering all three with the fixture remedy: ISOLATION (tests ran and failed), ROSTER (selector matched nothing - a renamed/deleted ns; 9dd9633d0b and d3969eb67b are both commits fixing exactly that after the gate blamed fixtures), ENVIRONMENT (the bundle moved). The discriminator is structural: --test=<ns> is a RUNTIME selector over a bundle linking EVERY test namespace, so a module-load crash cannot single a namespace out. A red carrying 'Ran N tests containing M assertions.' is a verdict about that namespace; a red without one never was. A sweep whose bundle moved is now INDETERMINATE (exit 2, rerun quietly), not red - its greens are worth no more than its reds. Greens must also carry a non-zero test count, and per-ns counts are now printed.

A/B under one injected fault: OLD gate accuses 16 namespaces of leaking runtime state and prescribes make-reset-runtime-fixture, every one of them MODULE_NOT_FOUND; NEW gate reports INDETERMINATE and points at the concurrent build. No test namespace touched, no fixture added, roster unchanged - none was needed.
close_reason: SHIPPED in PR #7608. The reported three-namespace tail was reproduced as a concurrent node-test bundle unlink, not fixture leakage. The gate now separates summary-bearing ISOLATION failures, unmatched-selector ROSTER failures, and pre-verdict ENVIRONMENT failures; detects bundle movement; refuses zero-test greens; and gives cause-specific remedies. Post-merge proof: all 18 classifier self-tests passed, then the real sweep passed all 17 namespaces with 196 tests / 731 assertions.

title: hicasso: the minted missing-key warning does not reach host or [:>] children — check-member-key! gates on boundary-head?
description:
FOUND by the rf2-2rtt6.106 codemod adjudication (2026-08-06), verified at 5a08b14a29.

THE GAP. front/codec.cljs's check-member-key! reaches warn-member-key! only under (boundary-head? h) — a defview product. A MINTED HOST head is not a boundary head, and neither is the :> keyword, so a seq of foreign crossings that carries no :key gets NOTHING from Hicasso at any build. The warning's own text is the evidence the class is known: it tells a defview child's author that 'a key written as Reagent metadata is not read here' — and says it to nobody else.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND SYMMETRY. For a Reagent codebase this is the ENTIRE keying idiom going dead at once: ^{:key ...} metadata was a live channel at every :> site (reagent 2.0.1 native-element sets .-key from (meta argv) AFTER convert-props, so metadata even beat a props :key), and no Hicasso path reads metadata. rf2-2rtt6.106's R2 rewrite (metadata -> props :key) is the only net that exists, and it can only reach sites a source tool can see.

.104's OWN RATIONALE APPLIES UNCHANGED. The reason the warning exists is that React's message dedupes on the parent TAG name (ownerHasKeyUseWarning), so after the first unkeyed list under any :ul every later site is silent. That is equally true of a list of host crossings.

AGAINST. A fourth predicate on the member path is not free — this codec has costed a keyword? short-circuit at +/-51-67% of a walk, and .104 measured its own check at ~150 ns/member in a dev build (check-member-key!'s docstring carries the table). boundary-head? is deliberately asked LAST so an unkeyed [:li ...] pays one fn? and no more; adding host-head? beside it moves that accounting. Note also that a host-headed member's props are read the same way (nth m 1), so the :key lookup itself is already paid.

THIS IS A QUESTION, NOT A PROPOSAL. It may be right to leave it: the door refuses plenty and a missing key is React's own diagnostic. Recorded so the .106 tool is not the only place the gap is written down. Full account: docs/design/hicasso/studio/reagent-codemod-spec.md section 6.3 and 8.2.
close_reason:
RULED — LEAVE IT. Rejected at triage under the pre-alpha no-gold-plating and trust-the-programmer posture. The bead records itself as a question, not a proposal, and its own AGAINST case is decisive.

THE STANDING TEST for whether a guard is warranted is whether the failure is SILENT and has already happened. It is NOT silent: a missing key on a host or [:>] member is REACT'S OWN DIAGNOSTIC, emitted at the boundary the programmer is already looking at. A Hicasso-minted warning there would be a second voice saying what React already says, which is the nag-diagnostic shape this project rejects — and the bead names exactly that ('a missing key is React's own diagnostic').

THE COST IS MEASURED, NOT SPECULATIVE, which is what settles it against the usual 'it is only one predicate' argument. This codec has costed a keyword? short-circuit at +/-51-67% of a walk, and rf2-2rtt6.104 measured check-member-key! at ~150 ns/member in a dev build (its docstring carries the table). boundary-head? is asked LAST by design so an unkeyed [:li ...] pays one fn? and no more; adding host-head? beside it moves that accounting for every member in every walk, to duplicate a warning the host runtime already emits.

WHAT SURVIVES: the gap is now written down in two places rather than one — this bead and the rf2-2rtt6.106 tool — plus the full account at docs/design/hicasso/studio/reagent-codemod-spec.md sections 6.3 and 8.2. That was the bead's stated purpose. If a real case ever shows React's own warning failing to reach an author through a Hicasso crossing, that is a new bead with a live subject and this costing is the first thing to re-read.

title: code units published as bytes: the four sites OUTSIDE the xray/story fence (mcp-base cursor, pair-mcp summary + benchmark, core render-law drift)
description:
RESIDUE from rf2-2rtt6.131, which repaired the two MCP size BUDGETS inside
its fence (tools/xray/**, tools/story*/**) and swept that fence to
exhaustion. These four sites carry the same shape and sit OUTSIDE it. Cited
by SYMBOL, not by line. Each needs the CONVERT-vs-RELABEL judgement, not a
patch.

THE SHAPE. A value that is (count s) -- UTF-16 code units on BOTH platforms,
since JVM String.length is also code units -- published or ENFORCED under a
bytes name. It fails OPEN: on ASCII the two agree exactly, so the wrong
expression prints the right number and a green suite never notices.

1. tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/cursor.cljc -- max-cursor-bytes,
   guarded by (> (count s) max-cursor-bytes) in decode-cursor. rf2-2rtt6.131
   examined this and judges it a RELABEL, not a convert, and says so with its
   reasons so the next author need not re-derive them:
     (a) its OWN docstring already reads "Hard ceiling on a cursor token's
         CHARACTER length" -- the docstring is right and the symbol is wrong,
         the inverse of the xray case;
     (b) the guard runs BEFORE parsing, to bound PARSE cost, and parse cost
         scales with characters, not with wire bytes -- so code units are the
         CORRECT unit for what this guard is for;
     (c) a well-formed cursor is base64 (b64-encode), hence pure ASCII, where
         the two rulers agree exactly. There is no behavioural defect here.
   So: rename to max-cursor-chars and correct the prose. Blast radius is the
   symbol's consumers across mcp-base + story-mcp + re-frame2-pair-mcp, which
   is why .131 left it alone rather than reaching outside its fence.
   NOTE the neighbour that is already CORRECT and must not be disturbed:
   story-mcp protocol.cljc's max-frame-bytes / read-bounded-line is a genuine
   per-code-point UTF-8 byte accumulator with astral surrogate recombination
   (rf2-sibl4f), pinned by read-frame-cap-counts-utf8-bytes-not-chars.

2. tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/summary.cljs --
   THE WORST OF THE FOUR and the one to do first. coll-entry-floor-bytes /
   map-key-overhead-bytes / sample-entry-bytes / approx-coll-bytes /
   approx-map-bytes are all (count (pr-str ...)), and they feed the :bytes
   slot of a REAL {:rf.size/large-elided ...} marker -- the framework's wire
   vocabulary, four emit sites in this file. So the figure is PUBLISHED on
   the wire to an agent, not merely printed. The ns is self-contradictory
   today: the symbols say bytes while their own docstrings say "~16 chars"
   and "~1-4 chars".

3. tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/dedup_benchmark_test.cljs
   -- raw-bytes / deduped-bytes via (count (pr-str ...)), printed by row-str
   with a literal "B" suffix (raw=NB deduped=NB). The RATIO and
   reduction-pct are honest same-vs-same and must not move; the two ABSOLUTE
   figures and the B suffix are the untrue part. Relabel, do not convert.

4. implementation/core/test/re_frame/observation_render_law_drift_test.clj --
   :bytes accumulated via (count content) and printed as bytes. Named in
   rf2-2rtt6.121's own audit note and never actioned. implementation/ was a
   hard fence for .131.

THE REPAIR, where converting is the answer:
  (alength (.getBytes s "UTF-8"))                on the JVM
  (.-length (.encode (js/TextEncoder.) s))       on CLJS
TextEncoder is UTF-8 BY DEFINITION -- no encoding argument a later edit can
drop -- and is present in every browser and in Node. The worked examples now
in main are re-frame.bench.hicasso.lane/utf8-bytes (rf2-2rtt6.121) and
day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.epoch.format/pr-str-bytes (rf2-2rtt6.131).

AN ASCII-ONLY TEST CANNOT SEE THIS BUG -- that is why it survives. Use a
discriminating fixture set where code units, code POINTS and bytes are three
different numbers: U+2014 (1 unit / 1 point / 3 bytes) and the ASTRAL U+1D11E
(2 units / 1 point / 4 bytes), written as \uXXXX escapes so the source stays
pure ASCII. Mutation-prove BOTH directions and, where the file is .cljc,
BOTH hosts.

VERIFIED NOT SIBLINGS, so no work is owed (re-checked by .131, not taken on
trust): mcp-base overflow/token-estimate and cap/sum-payload-by are honestly
named -- they are a (quot (count s) 4) CHARACTER-to-token estimate and every
printed slot says :chars or :tokens; tools/story budgets.cljc caps are cell /
row / variant COUNTS with no byte claim; story a11y/axe-cdn-integrity's
'published bytes' is the CDN file's real bytes for an SRI hash, not a count;
xray edn_inspector + derivation_graph_helpers only RENDER a :bytes produced
upstream.
close_reason:
PR #7581 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7581).

FOUR SITES FIXED, against the bead's four -- but not the same four. Three of
the bead's are in fence and repaired; its site 4 (implementation/core
observation_render_law_drift_test) was out of fence and carries forward. A
fourth in-fence site the bead does not name turned up in the sweep:
tools/machines-viz/.../chart/context_redaction.cljc.

1. mcp-base cursor max-cursor-bytes -> max-cursor-chars. RELABEL, and I AGREE
   with the bead's call. Its three reasons hold. The sweep adds a fourth that
   settles it: the cap's UNIT IS NOT OBSERVABLE through decode-cursor. The two
   rulers agree exactly on ASCII, so they can only diverge on a non-ASCII
   token -- and every non-ASCII token is ::malformed regardless, refused by
   decode-canonical-b64 for a reason wholly independent of the cap. Both units
   return the same verdict on every input that could tell them apart, so
   converting would move no behaviour at all. That reasoning is now in the
   const docstring, in spec/cursor.md, and pinned by
   decode-cursor-cap-is-characters-and-the-unit-is-unobservable (JVM) plus a
   CLJS mirror in cljs_branches_cljs_test. BLAST RADIUS WAS NARROWER THAN THE
   BEAD EXPECTED: cursor.cljc, cursor_test.clj, the CLJS mirror and
   spec/cursor.md. Neither story-mcp nor pair-mcp references the symbol.

2. pair-mcp tools/summary sample-entry-bytes. CONVERT (TextEncoder, ^js
   hinted). The :bytes slot is shared WIRE VOCABULARY -- the pair spec defines
   it against "a precise byte count" and the same name rides
   {:rf.size/large-elided ...} on the same wire -- so renaming the slot would
   break the cross-server contract (mcp-conformance's Summary schema,
   Tool-Pair.md) and split two slots that mean the same thing. The estimate is
   approximate in MAGNITUDE and should be exact in UNIT. Cost model unchanged:
   still one sampled entry, still O(one-entry-depth). The constants (16 / 8)
   did not move -- keyword keys are ASCII, so only their prose was wrong.
   BEAD CORRECTION, minor: these feed {:rf.mcp/summary ...}, not
   {:rf.size/large-elided ...}. The "four emit sites in this file" count is
   exactly right (map / vector / set / seq).

3. pair-mcp dedup_benchmark_test :raw-bytes/:deduped-bytes -> -chars, and the
   literal "B" suffix -> " chars". RELABEL, AGREED. The spec-quoted figures are
   :ratio and :reduction-pct, same-vs-same quotients where the unit cancels
   exactly, so NO MEASURED NUMBER IN THE NS DOCSTRING'S TABLE MOVES. The corpus
   is machine-generated keywords/ints/ASCII, so a UTF-8 count would print
   identical absolutes today and would start lying the moment someone widened
   the corpus.

4. machines-viz chart/context-redaction. NOT ON THE BEAD'S LIST. printed-size
   was (count (pr-str v)) serving TWO purposes wanting DIFFERENT units, so this
   is a SPLIT, not one call: the {:rf.size/large-elided :bytes} slot CONVERTS
   (new .cljc utf8-bytes -- String.getBytes on the JVM, TextEncoder with ^js
   hints in the browser viewer bundle where Buffer is absent), and the
   default-large-char-cap (512) STAYS CHARACTERS, untouched. The cap is already
   honestly named large-char-cap, it guards how much TEXT a chart band paints,
   and large-char-cap is a caller-visible option key. Converting it would have
   started eliding non-ASCII context that renders inline today.
   large-char-cap-is-characters-and-did-not-move pins exactly that: a
   400-character / 1,200-byte value still renders inline.

NO BUDGET'S DIRECTION CHANGED, and no ruling was owed. The correction is
monotone-tightening by construction, but here it is stronger than that: NOT ONE
of the four sites is an enforcement gate on the corrected expression. Sites 2
and 4's converted figures are published-only (a planning hint; a display/export
diagnostic), site 3 is a test log line, and site 1's guard keeps the ruler it
always had.

NO DEAD PLATFORM ARM. Applying .131's test: cursor.cljc's two arms are both
live (story-mcp JVM, pair-mcp CLJS); context_redaction.cljc's new reader
conditional is live on BOTH (the JVM :test alias and machines-viz-node-test each
run its .cljc tests -- proven by the mutation reddening both); summary.cljs and
the benchmark are CLJS-only by file type. Nothing to delete.

MUTATION-PROVED, BOTH DIRECTIONS, BOTH HOSTS, NON-ASCII. Every fixture is
\uXXXX-escaped so the source stays pure ASCII, uses U+2014 (1 unit / 1 point /
3 bytes) AND the astral U+1D11E (2 / 1 / 4) so code units, code points and bytes
are three different numbers, and asserts its own discriminating property BEFORE
it is used.
  - machines-viz marker utf8-bytes -> printed-size: 2 failures on the JVM (641
    tests) and the SAME 2 on CLJS (841 tests). 66 -> 24.
  - summary utf8-bytes -> count: 5 failures -- all four emit sites (60->32,
    15->8, 15->8, 31->24) plus the direction assertion.
  - cursor fixture ASCII-fied (em-dash -> "-"): 2 failures, the anti-vacuity
    assertions. The pin is live.
  - restored: all green.
Opposite direction, unmutated: an ASCII control of the SAME CODE-UNIT LENGTH
produces the identical number under either ruler at every converted site
(summary vector 32, machines-viz marker 24, the 602-byte cap case) -- the
fail-open condition itself, asserted rather than assumed.

tools/xray/spec/* UNCHANGED BECAUSE NO FILE UNDER tools/xray/ IS IN THIS DIFF
(ten files across mcp-base, pair-mcp, machines-viz, mcp-conformance).
tools/mcp-base/spec/cursor.md IS updated, for the rename and its reasoning. One
stray mcp-conformance schema comment (";; pr-str char count") contradicted the
spec and is corrected.

GATES all foreground to completion: all exit 0. test-fast-pr.sh (PASS fast PR spine; classification
'PLAN docs=true jvm=false node=true'), root lint:js, mcp-base JVM 277/948,
mcp-base CLJS 37/239, pair-mcp CLJS 1219/4322, machines-viz JVM 641/2784,
machines-viz CLJS 841/3717, xray JVM 1272/5919, story JVM 1847/6824, story-mcp
JVM 308/1619, npm run test:mcp-conformance (all 6 gates green; wire-vocab
100/1069; the 6 live-server rows SKIP without $SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT).

FILED rf2-2rtt6.135 (P2) for three sites outside this fence, worst first:
  1. skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/.../pure.cljc -- the ONLY REMAINING LIVE
     REFUSAL GATE. :queue-bytes accumulates (count (pr-str ev)) and
     evict-oldest drops events against max-buffered-bytes (default 5,000,000).
     This is the one place the correction is NOT free: counting honestly makes

     003-Tool-Catalogue.md's :queue-bytes row, and subscribe_test.cljs's

  2. implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc pr-str-bytes -- the EXACT

     marker AND enforced against :rf.size/threshold-bytes. Xray's docstring

     JVM arm. Found by this sweep, not carried from any list.
  3. observation_render_law_drift_test.clj -- the bead's site 4, still out of

(* mono-char-width-px (count (pr-str value))) is an honest characters-to-pixels
width; pair-mcp dedup_test / diff_encode_epochs_test and story-mcp dedup_test
use raw-size / full-size / enc-size with no byte claim; mcp-base

title: docs(hicasso): the-candidates-clock section 3 stamps B/E/Q = 101 from the one-field form (rf2-8smbe follow-on)
description:
FOUND 2026-08-06 while fixing rf2-8smbe's 9,117 -> 9,320. Same root cause, NOT
fixed in that PR because it would have been derived rather than measured.

docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-candidates-clock.md section 3, the bullet list
under 'The design', stamps:

  'The keystroke witness is B = 101, E = 101, Q = 101.'

That was true of the instrument section 7 pins by blob. In
clock_views.cljs blob 7e48dbc0b3a974cd61a5c61e606333848877a31f -- the pinned
instrument for the published run -- the form has ONE field: :draft is a scalar
string, kb-form holds a single [kb-field {}], the sub is (rf/reg-sub :p0/draft
(fn [db _] ...)) with no index, and kb-elements is (+ 3 (* 3 n)).

At HEAD, kb-fields-n = 4 (docstring: 'It was one field until rf2-0qj9w'),
kb-elements is (+ 2 kb-fields-n (* 3 n)), and :p0/draft is INDEXED --
(rf/reg-sub :p0/draft (fn [db [_ i]] ...)), read as [:p0/draft i] by all three
substrate arms over (range kb-fields-n).

So 100 cells + 4 drafts, and section 3.5 of the same page reports the recompute
census as 'p0/cell x100, p0/draft x4 ... validation.md's 104'. B/E/Q is
therefore almost certainly 104/104/104 -- but that is DERIVED from the census,
and B/E/Q is a distinct stamp the driver prints. rf2-8smbe corrected 9,117 ->
9,320 because section 3.5 publishes 9,320 B directly as a whole-run gate on the same
page; it declined to touch B/E/Q on inference alone.

SCOPE: read B/E/Q off a keystroke run (or off the retained dataset
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/clock-0qj9w/run2.json
via clock_readjudicate.cjs) and correct the stamp. Check the neighbouring
'0 unverified of 1,008 (756 on the keystroke row)' at the same time -- 756 is
CONFIRMED unchanged by section 3.5 and needs no edit.
close_reason:
Corrected to 104/104/104 in PR #7583, read off a run rather than derived from section 3.5's census.

MEASURED 2026-08-06 11:3x AUSEST. A cold HCLOCK_ONLY=keystroke run of clock_run.cjs at HEAD (b4142351cb) stamps:

  ;;   the witness states 100 grid cells + 4 fields = 104 layer-1 recomputes per
  ;;   keystroke on a substrate arm, and NONE on a floor arm.

with the census reading p0/cell x100, p0/draft x4 on all three substrate arms and 'no subscriptions at all' on all six floor/control arms. The shipped clock_witness.cjs adjudicate+format, replayed over BOTH retained datasets (data/clock-0qj9w/run1.json and run2.json), prints the identical 104 stamp. Nothing under data/ was written or changed.

The same run reprints the two neighbouring figures this bead flagged, both unchanged, so neither was edited:
  ;; parity   6 non-control arms across 3 segments, canonical DOM IDENTICAL (9320 bytes)
  ;; writes   0 unverified of 756

TWO PREMISES IN THIS BEAD DID NOT HOLD, and the added note records both:

1. B/E/Q is NOT a stamp this driver prints. clock_run.cjs emits no such label, at HEAD or at blob 22b53abe9e2fcf172dbb752ed0c2d56c4ec6869c which section 7 pins; grep over the whole 361-line run log returns nothing. The only B/E/Q stamp in the repo is hd8_clock_run.cjs's hardcoded 'B/E/Q = 300/300/300', a different driver and a different page. B/E/Q is the page's own name for what the shape stamp and the census jointly say.

2. clock_readjudicate.cjs cannot answer it either -- it never reads census or kbShape, only ensemble ratios and the additive constant.

Neither premise changed the answer: 104 is what the run stamps.

title: code units published as bytes OUTSIDE the hicasso bench fence: two MCP size BUDGETS and a CLJ/CLJS asymmetry
description:
SIBLING SWEEP RESIDUE from rf2-2rtt6.121, which repaired eleven sites inside
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/**. These are the same shape
found by the same sweep and left out of that bead's fence. Cited by SYMBOL, not
by line.

THE SHAPE. A value that is (count s) — UTF-16 code units on BOTH platforms, since
JVM String.length is also code units — published or ENFORCED under a bytes name.

BUDGETS (worse than a label, because a refusal turns on them):

1. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/format.cljc — pr-str-bytes.
   #?(:clj (count (.getBytes s "UTF-8")) :cljs (count s)). It gates
   render-args-byte-budget, so the SAME payload can pass on CLJS and be
   size-markered on the JVM. Its docstring says byte-exactness 'isn't available'
   on CLJS — THAT PREMISE IS FALSE and rf2-2rtt6.121 is the proof: TextEncoder is
   present in every browser and Node, and lane/utf8-bytes now uses it. The
   docstring is the thing to fix first; it is why nobody repaired this.

2. tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/write.cljc — parse-edn-body's
   byte-count, same #? asymmetry, gating max-body-bytes. One refusal, two rulers.

3. tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/cursor.cljc — the (> (count s)
   max-cursor-bytes) guard is code units on both platforms. NOTE, do not assume:
   tools/story-mcp/test/.../tools_test.clj carries
   read-frame-cap-counts-utf8-bytes-not-chars, so a neighbouring cap WAS
   deliberately made UTF-8 — check whether this one is a deliberate exception
   before touching it.

PUBLISHED FIGURE, named in rf2-2rtt6.121's own audit note and never actioned:

4. implementation/core/test/re_frame/observation_render_law_drift_test.clj —
   :bytes accumulated via (count content) and printed as bytes.

CANDIDATES, needing the same convert-vs-relabel judgement rather than a patch:

5. tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/.../dedup_benchmark_test.cljs — raw-bytes /
   deduped-bytes via (count (pr-str …)). Probably an honest same-vs-same ratio;
   relabel rather than convert.
6. tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/.../tools/summary.cljs — coll-entry-floor-bytes
   against (count (pr-str sample)).

VERIFIED NOT SIBLINGS, so no work is owed: the six
implementation/scripts/check-*.cjs scanners hold an internal bytes: blob.length,
but EVERY printed site says 'chars' or 'c'. Re-checked at 1e100264fb, not taken
on trust from the parent bead.

THE REPAIR, and the reason it is cheap: (.-length (.encode (js/TextEncoder.) s))
on CLJS, (alength (.getBytes s "UTF-8")) on the JVM — or RENAME to say code
units where only a same-vs-same comparison is wanted. rf2-2rtt6.121's
lane/utf8-bytes and its lane_bytes_cljs_test are the worked example, including
the discriminating fixture set (ASCII control + U+00A7/U+2014/U+2026 + an
ASTRAL U+1D11E whose code units, codepoints and bytes are three different
numbers). AN ASCII-ONLY TEST CANNOT SEE THIS BUG — that is why it survives.
close_reason:
PR #7576. Both named BUDGETS repaired inside the fence (tools/xray/**, tools/story*/**), plus a third site the sweep turned up. Sites 3-6 (mcp-base cursor, pair-mcp summary + benchmark, implementation/core render-law drift) are all OUTSIDE that fence and carry forward on rf2-2rtt6.132, with the convert-vs-relabel judgement already made and reasoned for each.

FIXED
1. xray panels/epoch/format/pr-str-bytes -- BUDGET (render-args-byte-budget) AND published figure (the size chip's :bytes). Now .getBytes on the JVM, TextEncoder on CLJS with ^js hints so :advanced cannot rename the call. The docstring's 'byte-exactness isn't available on CLJS' premise is corrected and the bead that disproved it is named -- that false premise was the reason nobody repaired this.
2. story-mcp tools/write/read-edn-body -- BUDGET (max-body-bytes). The :cljs arm was ALSO unreachable: the ns requires clojure.edn and catches Throwable unconditionally, and story-mcp is JVM-only by declaration. A phantom host publishing a WRONG number is worse than no second host, so the conditional is gone and the one ruler that runs is the correct one.
3. NEW, not named by this bead -- story-mcp tools_test.clj's wire-boundary cap head comment claimed the ':text'-slot BYTE COUNT is compared against :max-tokens. It is a (quot (count s) 4) CHARACTER-to-token estimate at every step. Relabelled.

CALIBRATION: no ruling was needed. Neither limit was calibrated against code units -- both docstrings already declared 'UTF-8 bytes' and both JVM arms always counted bytes. The correction is monotone-TIGHTENING and cannot be otherwise (UTF-8 bytes are never fewer than UTF-16 code units), so nothing previously refused is admitted now.

MAGNITUDE. xray on CLJS: a 200-character em-dash prop measured 202, now measures 602 -- it elides where it rendered inline, and its published chip was under-reporting ~3x. Effective headroom for 3-byte content falls 512 -> ~170 characters. Display-only (Xray is read-only, in-process). story-mcp on the JVM, its only host: NO change at all. Had the dead arm run, the mutation showed a 30,000-em-dash body (30,009 code units, 90,009 bytes) was ACCEPTED and REGISTERED past a 64KB ceiling -- a 2.99x under-count.

BOTH HOSTS PROVEN. projection_cljs_test.cljc runs under the cognitect JVM runner AND shadow's :node-test, so its green run IS the agreement. Mutating the :clj arm reds 4 JVM assertions; mutating the :cljs arm reds 4 CLJS assertions; mutating story-mcp's counter reds 4 and registers the oversize body. Fixtures are U+2014 and the ASTRAL U+1D11E as \uXXXX escapes, so code units, code points and bytes are three different numbers; each suite also pins the opposite direction with an ASCII payload of the same code-unit length.

SPEC: tools/xray/spec/021 updated (one table cell, pipe count 4 before and after -- verified by diff, no column change); tools/story-mcp/spec/API.md names the unit. tool-descriptors.edn does not drift (the VALUE did not move); clojure -M:gen --check green.

GATES all exit 0: test-fast-pr.sh (classified docs=true jvm=false node=true), root lint:js, xray JVM 1272/5919, story-mcp JVM 308/1619, story JVM 1847/6824, implementation test:cljs 12704/63686, mcp-conformance test:story + test:flag-gates, story-mcp gen --check.

title: RULING NEEDED: should the five mayor command files carry a 'normative source:' line? (rf2-1yy75 second half)
description:
SPLIT OUT of rf2-1yy75, whose FIRST half shipped in PR #7568. rf2-1yy75 itself said this half NEEDS A RULING BEFORE IMPLEMENTING, and none has been given (no bead records one; bd memories has nothing).

THE ORIGINAL PROPOSAL: give each of the five .claude/commands/mayor-*.md files an explicit 'normative source: docs/the-mayor-method/' line, so a worker correcting a method doc can grep for its dependants. The motivating failure is real: rf2-k3j2w's worker corrected docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md and could not have found .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md from it by any search, so the retired reaping rule survived in the file that EXECUTES for hours and destroyed live worker gate runs (rf2-40d9d).

WHY THE RULING MAY NOW BE MOOT -- READ THIS BEFORE RULING. PR #7568 gave check_readme_links.py a resolver over the tracked .claude/commands/*.md roster, covering BOTH reference forms those files use (repo-root-relative path, and bare filename). Measured on the live tree: renaming docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md now reds naming mayor-hygiene.md:6 and mayor-posture.md:4; renaming dispatch-prompt-template.md reds naming mayor-cluster.md:4, mayor-dispatch.md:20 and mayor-posture.md:4. So the DEPENDANT-DISCOVERY the proposed line was for is already delivered -- by a gate that runs on every PR, rather than by a convention nobody is obliged to maintain, and without adding five lines of ceremony to files whose whole content is prompt text a model reads.

WHAT THE LINE WOULD STILL ADD, so the ruling is made on the real remainder: it would flag SEMANTIC dependence (this command file restates that method doc's rule) rather than mechanical dependence (this command file names that file). rf2-40d9d was a semantic drift, not a broken path -- mayor-hygiene.md's reaping rule contradicted bootstrap.md while every path in it still resolved. So the gate does NOT cover the rf2-40d9d case; it covers the rename case rf2-1yy75 flagged alongside it. rf2-1yy75 is explicit that a semantic doc-consistency checker is not buildable and would be over-engineering, so the question is narrowly whether a human-readable pointer line is worth its ceremony given no gate can enforce what it asserts.

OPTIONS: (a) add the line to all five files; (b) decline -- the gate covers the mechanical half and an unenforceable line is ceremony; (c) something narrower, e.g. the line only on the files that restate a method-doc rule verbatim (today: mayor-hygiene.md).

Docs-only either way. Mike's call.
close_reason: Ruled 2026-08-06 (delegated, operator-overturnable): option (3) — ONE source-end sentence appended to the bootstrap.md ~L160-161 paragraph, exact wording in ruling comment; carrier rf2-cvqyi (P4, may ride any mayor-method PR). Five 'normative source:' destination lines DECLINED: #7568 resolver + existing path refs cover mechanical discovery (verified, self-test exit 0), mayor-merge.md has no identifiable file dependency, and an unenforceable line is ceremony in prompt files.

VERIFIED on live tree: (a) #7568 resolver present in scripts/check_readme_links.py (COMMAND_FILE_PATHSPEC .claude/commands/*.md, git-tracked roster, both reference forms; --self-test exit 0; runs in verify-readme-links + fast-PR spine) — renames red the dependant command files. WHY (3) over (1) close-as-moot: the rf2-40d9d failure was semantic and source-side (the worker was AT bootstrap.md, not at the command file); a source-end sentence covers all five dependants incl. mayor-merge.md, needs no per-file convention maintenance, and nothing buildable checks semantic drift (rf2-1yy75 ruling stands). Rides any mayor-method-touching PR or the filed P4 carrier bead (see close reason). Five destination lines: DECLINED.

title: freehand bench: do any published rows predate the cache clear, and does it matter?
description:
Raised by rf2-t4j7c's worker, which added resetLaneBuildCache() to the seven
freehand-lane drivers that ride the one 'freehand-release' build id
(b7, reads_ladder, spine_ablation, b6_prod, b6_profile, b8, b10_prod).

THE QUESTION THIS DOES NOT ANSWER. Every row those seven have published so
far was measured by a driver that did NOT clear the shared cache. The loud
case is self-limiting: a contaminated bundle dies at load and the driver
exits 1, so it cannot publish. rf2-t4j7c reproduced exactly that
('Cannot read properties of undefined (reading d)', 11 of 160 files
compiled against 105 from cold).

The QUIET case is the open one, and it is documented rather than
hypothetical: lane_cache.cjs records that a warm-cache build and a
cold-cache build of the SAME arm emit different bundles — hicasso_narrow_run.cjs
measured the gap at 4,075 bytes — because Closure's renaming differs for a
build compiled fresh against one compiled with a sibling warm. A bundle that
differs but still runs publishes a figure measured on an entry nobody built
on purpose, and nothing in the drivers would have said so.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. Either (a) an argument that heap-retention and clock
readings are insensitive to the renaming delta, in which case record it and
close; or (b) a re-take of the affected studio rows on cleared caches,
compared against the published figures.

Affected studio pages pin their instrument by git blob hash, so the pinned
blobs still identify what produced each published table — the provenance is
intact, the question is only whether the instrument was reading a bundle it
meant to build:
  docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md
  docs/design/hicasso/studio/uix-spine-per-read-decomposition.md
  docs/design/freehand/studio/freehand-vs-reagent-memory.md
  docs/design/freehand/studio/concurrent-store-ablation.md

NOT urgent and possibly a no-op — filed because rf2-t4j7c's fix makes every
FUTURE run deterministic but says nothing about the past, and that gap should
be someone's decision rather than an omission.
notes:
ANSWERED by PR #7579 (branch worker/cacheaudit-t84ee). Option (a): recorded, no
re-take owed. No measurement, arm, threshold, exit code, dataset or studio page
was touched.

THE CUT. The seven freehand-release riders got resetLaneBuildCache at 448d368bb9,
2026-08-06 04:04 AUSEST. The hicasso-bench lane got it at 974010f69d, 2026-07-31.
So EVERY row the seven have published predates their clear -- there is no subset
to find. Whether any particular run was warm OVER A SIBLING is operator shell
history and is not recoverable; whether the fault could have reached the row is,
and that is what was measured.

THE BEAD'S FRAMING IS INCOMPLETE IN ONE PLACE, AND IT IS THE PLACE THAT MATTERS.
"Loud" and "quiet" are not properties of an arm. They are properties of the
CHAIN. Measured at 5a08b14a29, each arm built once cold and once with a sibling
warm ahead of it, then loaded in headless Chromium:

  reads_ladder    649,251 B cold | 649,251 B over spine_ablation -> RUNS
                                 | 649,140 B over b6_prod+b7     -> DEAD
  spine_ablation  655,896 B cold | 655,896 B over reads_ladder   -> RUNS
                                 | 655,770 B over a deeper chain -> DEAD
  b7              824,837 B cold | 824,837 B over b6_prod        -> RUNS
  b6_prod         841,215 B cold | 841,215 B over b7             -> RUNS
  b8              813,777 B cold | 813,572 B                     -> RUNS
  b10_prod        786,778 B cold | 786,591 B                     -> RUNS
  b6_profile    3,413,752 B cold |3,411,573 B                    -> RUNS

Every arm's bundle changes. The same ladder arm is loud one way and quiet the
other, so "did this row land in the quiet band" cannot be answered per-arm.

THE LOUD CASE IS SELF-LIMITING BY CONSTRUCTION, not by luck: every driver in the
lane waits on its own *_READY / *_DONE global raced against sentinel.cjs, and a
bundle raising "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'd')" before its
entry runs sets no global at all. That holds at every tree; rf2-sib23 only turned
a timeout into a named error.

THE PAIRING THAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED IS THE QUIET ONE. The ladder's SS1-5 were
authored as 09ec4e6b3c and the spine decomposition's confirmation run as
fa09c5ad7a, both on worker/bench-audit-cluster, SIX MINUTES APART on 2026-07-31 --
one .shadow-cljs/builds/freehand-release, two :init-fns, five days before the
clear existed. In either order each emits a bundle the same LENGTH as its cold
one, differently renamed, that runs. So the highest-exposure driver in the lane
sits squarely in the quiet band and the question was live, not moot.

PRICED, WHICH IS WHAT SETTLES IT. Same tree, same driver, same arms, same rounds,
same controls, build short-circuited so only the artefact differs:

  reads_ladder (LADDER_SUBSTRATES=reagent, 6 rounds, exit 0 both, 0 unverified
  of 93 both):  B/read 947 -> 948 ; R=0 shell 431 -> 430 ; first read 1,140 ->
  1,137 ; intercept 397 -> 395 ; B/boundary@R=3 3,189 -> 3,188.

  b7 --only heap (defaults, exit 0 both, 0 unverified of 56 both, all three
  positive controls ok, arm order reportable both): worst arm moves 1 B/boundary
  across 244 / 494 / 656 / 1,278 / 2,247 / 4,303.

Worst movement across both instruments: 1 byte per boundary, 1 byte per read,
against published ranges of +/-0.7%. The delta is Closure renaming and nothing
else -- b7's two bundles are the SAME LENGTH, 4.03% of bytes differ, first
divergence a variable name in the closure_uid_ preamble.

REPLAYED COLD AGAINST THE PUBLISHED FIGURES. Ladder Reagent: B/read 943 [935-944]
-> 947 [945-948] (+0.42%); R=0 shell 428 [421-434] -> 431 [420-441] (+0.70%);
first read 1,137 -> 1,140; intercept 397 -> 397. B7 above the floor: storm UIx
251 -> 250, storm Reagent 410 -> 412, reactive Reagent 1,037 -> 1,034 -- all
inside 0.5% nine days later. The two Freehand arms moved (2,430 -> 2,003 and
4,346 -> 4,059), and they are exactly the two arms that page's own Provenance
told the next reader to re-take because rf2-wxrrp (e5cf299fc2) merged while the
run was in flight. The ruler moved, not the artefact.

CONTROLS. A cleared-cache build is deterministic (ladder cold three times:
649,251 B, sha256 fae288ec... every time). A build warm over ITSELF is
byte-identical (second build 0 compiled, same sha256). "Warm" is not the fault;
"warm over a SIBLING" is -- so the ladder taking its two substrate pages as two
invocations of one driver was never at risk.

WHICH ROWS GATE A DECISION. validation.md's per-read gate table takes its K3 line
(943 B/read) and its shell budget shapes (Reagent ~418-428 B, UIx ~208 B) from
reads_ladder_run.cjs, and graduation win condition (4) names 943 B; the UIx line's
cross-checks 2,783 (ladder) and 2,774 (spine decomposition) are the same two
drivers. bulk-rerender-where-the-time-goes.md (b6_prod_run, b6_profile_run) is
cited by hd-002-adjudication.md and by validation.md's W1 carry-over. The ladder's
SS6 onward is p0_run.cjs -- a hicasso-bench rider, cleared since 2026-07-31 -- so
the memo-wrapper re-take and the sub-index rows were never exposed.

NOT ESTABLISHED, AND SAID RATHER THAN DROPPED. The same A/B on the CLOCK is not
evidence either way. b6_prod_run over its two bundles exits 0 and passes parity
both times, but two bundles mean two runs and this studio's clock method
interleaves arms WITHIN a round because a loaded box drifts between them. It did:
the second run's interpreted W1 reads [2.68-10.21] against the first's
[2.75-4.32]. A cross-run clock A/B cannot separate an artefact from the box.
Nothing in the verdict rests on one, and the affected pages publish their heap
rows on the axis that was settled.

SUBSIDIARY, so a later reader does not suspect the cache of it: the ladder's SS7
anchor records UIx sub-free at 208 B against freehand-vs-reagent-memory's 251 B
(-17.1%). The b7 side replays cold at 250 B, so the published 251 is not a build
artefact and that page's witness-difference explanation stands.
close_reason: Answered by PR #7579: option (a) — recorded, no re-take owed. All rows the seven riders published predate their clear (448d368bb9, 2026-08-06). Loud/quiet is a property of the CHAIN, not the arm: every arm's bundle changes, the loud form is self-limiting by construction (every driver waits on its own *_READY global raced against sentinel.cjs, and a dead bundle sets none), and the quiet form is Closure renaming that moves a retained-heap reading by at most 1 B/boundary and 1 B/read — measured on reads_ladder and b7, each run unchanged over both of its own bundles, exit 0 and zero unverified mounts on all four. Ladder replayed cold reproduces the K3 gate line at 947 against the published 943 B/read and the R=0 shell at 431 against 428. Clock A/B is noise-limited and is reported as such. Filed rf2-v8561 for an unrelated per-ns isolation red in the spine.

title: re-frame.ui rules/sub/frames/test diagnostics pr-str a runtime value, so a cyclic foreign value blows the stack instead of producing the error
description:
FIFTH NAMESPACE GROUP OF THE rf2-9s68n CLASS, found by a full sweep of
implementation/ui/src while fixing rf2-q9q9y (the fourth). NOT a regression
from that PR -- these sites predate it and were outside its measured tier.

rf2-q9q9y fixed the compiled-view CLIENT RUNTIME tier: re-frame.ui.runtime,
re-frame.ui.tree and re-frame.ui.events (12 crossings, all measured). The
sweep that found them also triaged every other pr-str under
implementation/ui/src. Most of the corpus clears by construction; a residue
does not, and it is DIFFERENT THROWERS ON DIFFERENT PATHS -- which is exactly
why it is a separate bead rather than folded in, on the same reasoning the
q9q9y description itself gives for not folding into rf2-1aj9s.

THE SITES (by symbol, with the guard that routes a value there):

  re-frame.ui.rules/assert-safe-caller!            rules.cljc:2153
    (pr-str k) + :extra {:key k}. Reached on the (nil? slot) branch, which
    per caller-key-name means k is NOT a keyword/string/symbol -- i.e. a
    foreign object used as a map key. (ui/spread-safe owned {js-obj "x"}).
    BOTH hosts, NOT goog.DEBUG-gated, so this is production-reachable.
    HIGHEST CONFIDENCE of this group.

  re-frame.ui/sub                                  ui.cljc:337
    (pr-str query) + :extra {:query query}. No guard -- the whole body is
    the throw, reached whenever ui/sub is CALLED rather than compiler-
    lowered. (defn helper [x] (ui/sub [:q x])) with x a React context.
    Both hosts, not debug-gated.

  re-frame.ui.frames/maybe-warn-cross-frame-carried-subscribe!
                                                   frames.cljc:1301, 1305
    A WARN, not a throw (trace/emit! :warning
    :rf.warning/cross-frame-carried-op, :recovery :warned-and-continued).
    query-v is the author's subscription vector. TWO exposures: the pr-str
    at 1305, and the RAW query-v at 1301 under :rf.sub/query-v in the trace
    payload -- the deferred-explosion-at-a-downstream-sink path. Gated by
    interop/debug-enabled?.

  re-frame.ui.test/not-a-node!                     test.cljc:160
    (pr-str x) + :extra {:got x}. The #?(:cljs (when (dom-element? x) ...))
    pre-check catches only js/Element, so every other foreign JS object
    falls through to the pr-str, which sits OUTSIDE the reader conditional.
    Test surface.

  re-frame.ui.test/text*                           test.cljc:214
    (pr-str c) + malformed! ex-data. c is a :children entry that is neither
    string? nor map? -- caller-supplied tree. Test surface.

  re-frame.ui.test/flush!                          test.cljc:601
    (pr-str thunk) + :extra {:got thunk}. Guard (when-not (fn? thunk)).
    Test surface, low severity.

  re-frame.ui.tool.evidence/warn-rejected-install! evidence.cljc:789, 790
    (pr-str current) / (pr-str rejected). owner-id is documented as "any
    comparable non-nil value". CLJS-only, interop/debug-enabled?-gated,
    TOOL-AUTHOR surface rather than app-author. LOWEST severity.

CLEARED BY THE SAME SWEEP, recorded so nobody re-treads it:

  The whole COMPILE/MACRO tier is unreachable by construction -- a form read
  by the Clojure reader cannot be a cyclic foreign JS object. That clears
  compiler.cljc, compiler/analyze.cljc, compiler/header.cljc,
  compiler/root.cljc, compiler/a11y.cljc, fingerprint.cljc (no runtime
  consumer at all) and test.cljc:765 (defmacro render, &form-supplied).

  client.cljs -- ALL 20 pr-str sites clear. root-id is compile-gated by
  compiler/root.cljc:72 validate-authored-root-id! and identifier-prefix by
  the string? check at 593-598; all four client.cljs entry points are
  emitted only from compiler/root.cljc. No caller path reaches any of those
  messages with an arbitrary object.

  hooks.cljc:372 (pr-str ctx) -- the :clj arm (the whole-file reader
  conditional opens :cljs at 36, closes at 291, :clj runs 293-EOF). Not
  CLJS-reachable; on the JVM there is no cyclic foreign graph.

  rules.cljc:2164 and 2246 -- both gated on a NON-nil slot, which means k
  provably IS nameable. Only 2153 (the nil-slot branch) is exposed.

  presence_runtime.cljc:271 -- k is (.-key x) off a React element, already
  string-coerced by React.

  frames.cljc (all other sites), reactive.cljc, rules.cljc:1163/1239/1464 --
  framework-supplied keywords (compile-gated root-ids, registrar view-ids,
  compiler-emitted site ids, shadow build ids).

  semantic.cljc -- NO residual unfixed site. Its two remaining bare pr-str
  calls are framework-built: :245 path is (conj parent-path :children i),
  keywords and ints only; :269 ds is a subvector of the private constant
  node-discriminators. rf2-1aj9s's fix is complete.

THE WORK IS CHEAP -- the mechanism exists. error/pr-form on the message
half, error/safe-form on the :extra / trace-payload half. Every namespace
above already requires re-frame.error except ui.cljc and tool/evidence.cljc,
which need one require line each (watch for an unused-require warning if a
site turns out to be cleared instead).

TEST SHAPE: re-frame.ui.diagnostic-cycle-cljs-test (landed by rf2-q9q9y) is
the template -- the outcome map so an overflow is DATA in the failure text,
a non-vacuity control asserting cljs.core/pr-str itself blows the stack on
the fixtures INCLUDING a mixed chain, and byte-identity rows embedding
cljs.core/pr-str's own output.

SEVERITY P3, as its four siblings: a bad error instead of a good one, no
wrong bytes to the wire. rf2-y1jbaq applies -- state per site whether its
output can reach a page. Note frames.cljc and evidence.cljc are WARN/trace
paths, so their output reaches a TRACE SINK rather than a thrown error,
which is a different consumer with a different appetite for a raw value.

FENCE: implementation/ui/**.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7588: both production-reachable sites (rules/assert-safe-caller! nil-slot branch, ui/sub) now use error/pr-form + error/safe-form; four reverse mutations, all gates green, CI all-pass. The seven residue sites stay recorded triaged-out per the Option 1 ruling.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RULED 2026-08-06 11:25 AUSEST (delegated dossier review, operator-overturnable): OPTION 1 — fix the TWO production-reachable sites only; the rest is recorded triaged-out on the donor, successor inherits the class rule. Dossier + Codex converge on 1 and both were verified against the tree.

WHY NOT (3): iwh5c's DEFER ruling (verified, incl. its 2026-08-06 confirmation) rejected an INERT ARCHITECTURAL FENCE — days of work protecting a zero-occurrence corpus. This bead is a reachable stack-overflow in author-facing diagnostics on a substrate whose EXPERIMENTAL label invites the experimenting author; iwh5c itself keeps ui/sub as "the taught spelling", which makes ui.cljc:337's misuse diagnostic exactly the surface a real author hits. Crash-fix ≠ retrofit; (3) over-reads the ruling. WHY NOT (2): the seven residue sites are debug-gated, test-surface, or tool-author on a tree recorded for deletion — mechanical polish with no present product value; the invariant (any arbitrary runtime value crossing into diagnostic text or a downstream-printable payload uses the cycle-safe pair) carries to the successor via this record, so the class dies there, not here.

VERIFIED: rules.cljc:2153 nil-slot branch pr-str's a non-nameable (foreign) map key + raw {:extra {:key k}}, both hosts, ungated (2164/2246 provably-nameable branches stay cleared). ui.cljc:334-340 always-throw body pr-str's the arbitrary query + raw {:extra {:query query}}, both hosts, ungated. Idiom exists and is landed: error/safe-form (error.cljc:530, byte-identity when acyclic, JVM identity) + error/pr-form (:544, total pr-str) — 21 uses across events/semantic/runtime/tree from the q9q9y wave. Test template exists: implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/diagnostic_cycle_cljs_test.cljs. CORRECTION to this bead's description: ui.cljc ALREADY requires [re-frame.error :as error] (ui.cljc:61) — NO new require is needed at either in-scope file; only evidence.cljc (triaged out) lacks one.

DISPATCH BRIEF: (a) rules.cljc:2153 → (error/pr-form k) in the message, :extra {:key (error/safe-form k)}. (b) ui.cljc:337 → (error/pr-form query) in the message, :extra {:query (error/safe-form query)}. (c) Witness rows in diagnostic_cycle_cljs_test per the landed template: one row per site driving a cyclic foreign value (React-context-like self-referential JS object; include a mixed CLJS/JS chain) through the ACTUAL public path — (ui/spread-safe owned {cyclic-obj "x"}) and a direct (ui/sub [:q cyclic]) call — asserting the typed :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed error surfaces (not RangeError), message carries the bounded elision token, and :extra values are downstream-pr-str-safe; keep the template's non-vacuity control (cljs.core/pr-str itself overflows on the fixtures) and add acyclic byte-identity rows embedding cljs.core/pr-str's own output. No new printer, no new framework. (d) Fence implementation/ui/** — rules.cljc + ui.cljc + the cycle test; isolated surface, parallel-safe. rf2-y1jbaq note: both sites are thrown errors (page-reachable via error surfaces), now bounded.

RAW-QUERY-V TRACE PAYLOAD (frames.cljc:1301): LEAVE-WITH-NOTE — ruled, not deferred. Reasons: (i) the site's message half (pr-str query-v, :1305) is evaluated while the payload map is BUILT, so truncating 1301 alone leaves the site crashing at 1305 first — a half-fix is incoherent, and fixing both is exactly the debug-gated group option 1 triages out; (ii) a trace payload's consumer is a trace sink with its own appetite for the raw live value (tool inspection) — cycle-safety at that boundary is the sink tier's job, and truncate-at-source would degrade every debug-mode cross-frame warn to guard a debug-only path. NOTE for the successor rule: at emission, downstream-printable payload values go through safe-form (or the sink boundary does it) — this site is the recorded witness of the deferred-explosion path.

TRIAGED-OUT ON DONOR (recorded, do not re-tread): frames.cljc:1301+1305 (debug-gated warn, above); test.cljc:160/214/601 (test surface); evidence.cljc:789-790 (tool-author, debug-gated, CLJS-only). Compile/macro tier + client.cljs + hooks.cljc:372 + the other rules/frames/reactive/semantic sites stay cleared by construction per the description's sweep. Dossier ai/decisions/rf2-30dc7.ui-prstr-residue.md reviewed and deleted per process.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:

GATES (all exit 0): test-fast-pr.sh -> "PASS fast PR spine", classification
"docs=false jvm=true node=true (classified)"; JVM core 2222/0; JVM ui 702
tests 17606 assertions /0; test:cljs 12717 tests 63774 assertions /0;
test:browser 1104/0; test:ui 826/0; per-ns isolation all 17 standalone;
clj-kondo @ the CI pin 2026.04.15 with CI's exact --lint set: errors 0,

THE CLASS DID NOT EXTEND. No follow-up bead filed. The invariant the ruling

title: re-frame.ui runtime/tree diagnostics pr-str a runtime value, so a cyclic foreign value blows the stack instead of producing the error
description:
FOURTH NAMESPACE GROUP OF THE rf2-9s68n CLASS, found while fixing rf2-1aj9s (the third). NOT a regression from that PR -- these sites predate it and were never in any of the three beads' enumerated scope.

rf2-9s68n named three namespaces (re-frame.ssr.emit, re-frame.ssr.ui-tree, re-frame.ui.semantic). All three are now fixed and the shared helper (safe-form / pr-form) lives in re-frame.error in core, reachable from every artefact. But re-frame.ui carries MORE sites of the identical class, on PRODUCTION paths, and they are still bare pr-str.

THE SITES (by symbol, not line):
  re-frame.ui.runtime/invalid-slot!        (pr-str x) + :extra {:value x}
  re-frame.ui.runtime/check-dynamic-child! (pr-str x) + :extra {:value x}
  re-frame.ui.runtime/->react-component    (pr-str view) + :extra {:value view}
  re-frame.ui.tree/invalid-slot!           (pr-str v) + :extra {:value v}
  re-frame.ui.tree/classify-handler        (pr-str v) + :extra {:value v}

REACHABILITY, traced statically per site (NOT executed -- a probe is the first
job of whoever takes this):

  invalid-slot! (BOTH copies). slot-ready? routes anything that is neither nil
  nor a marked render-fn here. A React context provider is exactly such a
  value, and passing one to a ui/slot is an ordinary authoring mistake.
  (pr-str provider) is MEASURED to raise RangeError -- it is a row in
  re-frame.ssr.diagnostic-cycle-cljs-test's non-vacuity control and in
  re-frame.ui.semantic-cycle-cljs-test's.

  check-dynamic-child!. The guard is (or (seq? x) (coll? x) (keyword? x)
  (symbol? x)), so a RAW JS object does NOT reach the throw -- but a CLJS
  vector HOLDING one does, and [:p ctx.Provider] is the mixed chain PR #7563
  exists for. (pr-str [provider {...}]) is MEASURED to raise RangeError.

  ->react-component. The guard is (when-not (or (fn? view) (object? view))),

title: re-frame.ui.semantic's malformed-node! pr-strs a runtime tree node, so a cyclic foreign value blows the stack instead of producing the error
description:
THIRD SITE OF rf2-9s68n, LEFT OUT OF PR #7562 BY A FENCE, NOT BY JUDGEMENT.

rf2-9s68n fixed the two SSR-artefact namespaces (re-frame.ssr.emit, 4 throwers; re-frame.ssr.ui-tree, 10 print sites) with one helper, re-frame.ssr.diagnostic. The third namespace the bead named -- re-frame.ui.semantic -- has the identical defect and is untouched:

  malformed-node! is called from three arms of norm-node, each building its message with (pr-str node) over a runtime tree node, and each carrying {:value node} in ex-data. A foreign JS value anywhere in that node (an :attrs prop, or a raw JS object arriving in child position and taking the :else arm) makes cljs.core's printer descend with no seen-set, so a cyclic graph -- a React 19 ctx.Provider is one -- raises RangeError instead of :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed.

  Cleared in the same file and NOT to be re-audited: (pr-str path) (framework-built :children keywords + ints), (pr-str ds) (the discriminator vector, keywords only), and (pr-str supported-tree-versions) (a compile-time constant). The affected sites are line-for-line the same shape as the ui-tree ones already fixed.

WHY IT NEEDS A DIFFERENT FENCE. re-frame.ui and re-frame.ssr are SIBLING artefacts: both depend on core, and neither may require the other (ssr/deps.edn states 'Production re-frame.ssr never :requires re-frame.ui'). So re-frame.ssr.diagnostic is unreachable from re-frame.ui.semantic, and copying the walker into the ui artefact would be a second implementation of one rule -- the thing the dispatch brief explicitly forbade.

THE SHARED HOME IS re-frame.error IN implementation/core. All three namespaces ALREADY :require it, so the move costs no new dependency edge anywhere, and it is where diag-value-summary -- this repo's existing diagnostic-value primitive, with the EP-0015 rationale attached -- already lives. implementation/core/** was outside the rf2-9s68n dispatch fence, which is the only reason this is a separate bead.

THE WORK.
  1. Move safe-form + pr-form from re-frame.ssr.diagnostic into re-frame.error (they are ~40 lines plus docstrings, CLJS-only logic with an identity JVM arm; clojure.walk becomes a CLJS-only :require clause on error.cljc, as it is on diagnostic.cljc today). Delete re-frame.ssr.diagnostic and swap the two :require lines in re-frame.ssr.emit / re-frame.ssr.ui-tree.
  2. Apply pr-form at the three re-frame.ui.semantic message sites and safe-form to malformed-node!'s extra map -- exactly the shape ui-tree already carries.
  3. Extend re-frame.ssr.diagnostic-cycle-cljs-test (or a ui-artefact sibling) with semantic rows in the SAME shape: the outcome map, the non-vacuity control that cljs.core/pr-str itself blows the stack on the fixtures, and a byte-identity row that embeds cljs.core/pr-str's own output in the expectation.

FENCE: implementation/core/**, implementation/ssr/**, implementation/ui/**. Sequence AFTER PR #7562 merges -- step 1 rewrites files that PR creates.

GATES that moved on PR #7562, for comparison: npm run test:cljs 12660/63428 clean; ssr JVM 623/3127 clean; ssr-ring JVM 215/1034 clean; clj-kondo @ 2026.04.15 exit 0, errors 0, warnings 4536 (baseline), zero findings on any changed file.
notes:
WORKER. PR #7564. Gates all green; CI on the head 73 pass / 12 skipping / 0 fail.

THE HOME: re-frame.error IN CORE, as the bead's recipe named -- and the reason was VERIFIED rather than assumed. re-frame.ssr.emit and re-frame.ssr.ui-tree ALREADY :require [re-frame.error :as error], so both LOSE a require line and gain none; re-frame.ui.semantic already required it too. clojure.walk is org.clojure/clojure + clojurescript stdlib, both already direct deps of core, and stays a CLJS-only :require clause (the JVM arm of safe-form is identity). No bundle gate is at risk: test:perf-bundle is a token-ELISION check (off-count/on-count), not a byte budget, and test:bundle-isolation polices re-frame-artefact boundaries, not stdlib. reagent-slim does not :require re-frame.error at all (it replicates diag-value-summary inline by design). LIFTING IT INTO CORE COST NOTHING. It also lands beside diag-value-summary -- the other 'render an untrusted value into a diagnostic without harm' primitive, that one for content safety (EP-0015), this one for termination. re-frame.ssr.diagnostic retired.

THE BEAD UNDERCOUNTED BY ONE, the same way rf2-9s68n's description undercounted ui-tree by six. It names 'the three malformed-node! arms' and pre-clears (pr-str path) / (pr-str ds) / (pr-str supported-tree-versions), but does NOT mention validate-tree-version!'s (pr-str v). v is (:rf.ui/tree-version tree) -- read straight off a caller-supplied tree -- and rides out in ex-data as {:got v}. Fixed, with its own rows. FOUR crossings total.

Reverse (the four semantic call sites reverted to pr-str / bare extra, helper left in place): 14 failures, 0 errors, EVERY ONE in re-frame.ui.semantic-cycle-cljs-test, each carrying {:threw "RangeError", :message "Maximum call stack size exceeded", :error-id nil} in its failure text. title: check_doc_slugs.py does not walk repo-root markdown — 38 links in 6 files are ungated
description:
Recorded as the SECOND FINDING on rf2-raqes and confirmed here while landing it (PR #7559).

THE GAP. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py's _iter_markdown roster is DEFAULT_ROOTS = (docs, spec, skills, migration) plus tools/*/spec (scripts/check_doc_slugs.py:69-82, :444-460). Repo-root markdown is in none of them, so it is never walked. mkdocs.yml does not list those files either, and mkdocs build --strict skips docs/design/** besides — so root-level markdown has NO link gate at all.

WHAT IS UNGATED. Six tracked files at repo root: AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md, CLAUDE.md, README.md, SKILL-REDIRECT.md, TESTING.md. Between them they carry 36 relative .md links and 2 in-page anchors. README.md is the project-layout map and TESTING.md is the canonical testing matrix that tools/*/spec defers to BY NAME (tools/xray/spec/017 and tools/story/spec/015 both cite it), so a broken link in either rots a document other gated documents point at.

PROVED TWICE. rf2-raqes's filer appended a line carrying a broken relative link AND a broken in-page anchor to TESTING.md, grep-confirmed it landed, and the checker still exited 0. The mirror mutation on tools/xray/spec/017-Test-Coverage-Matrix.md (this PR, same checker, same run) exits 1 with BOTH a BROKEN TARGET and a BROKEN ANCHOR diagnostic — so the checker's machinery works and it is purely the roster that omits root.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE LINKS. Several dispatch briefs have asserted check_doc_slugs.py covers TESTING.md. It does not. A brief that nominates it as the gate for a root-markdown edit gets a green exit code that verified nothing — the same false-green shape as scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh's --plan lane.

THE WORK. Add repo-root *.md to _iter_markdown (non-recursive at root — a rglob of '.' would pull the whole tree and every excluded dir back in). Then mutation-prove it: the same broken-link + broken-anchor probe appended to TESTING.md must exit 1, and be reverted. Expect existing breakage to surface on the first run; triage it in the same PR or file what does not belong there.

FENCE: scripts/check_doc_slugs.py plus whatever root-markdown links the new coverage finds broken. Not a hot-zone file.
close_reason:
Closed by PR #7561 — but the roster widened is check_readme_links.py's, NOT check_doc_slugs.py's, and the exposure figure in this bead needs correcting.

CORRECTION TO THE FILING. This bead says six root files carrying 36 relative .md links are ungated. FIVE files carrying 11 are. The root README.md — 25 of those 36 — has been gated all along by scripts/check_readme_links.py, which rglobs for README.md from the repo root and excludes only docs/, spec/, migration/, skills/ and tools/*/spec/. Mutation-proved before any edit: a broken target and a broken anchor appended to README.md red that gate BY NAME at exit 1 while check_doc_slugs.py stays at 0. Measured per file (md-links / in-page anchors): README.md 25/0 GATED; CLAUDE.md 5/1; TESTING.md 4/1; CHANGELOG.md 2/0; AGENTS.md 0/0; SKILL-REDIRECT.md 0/0.

Everything else in the filing reproduced exactly. check_doc_slugs.py's roster is DEFAULT_ROOTS + tools/*/spec, the repo root is in none of it, no root document appears in mkdocs.yml, and the broken-link + broken-anchor probe appended at TESTING.md:274 left the docs gate at exit 0.

THE ROSTER DECISION, MEASURED. Both candidates were built and run. Docs gate + non-recursive root glob: 674 -> 680 files, 8.09s -> 8.56s, 0 findings. README gate + non-recursive root glob: 67 -> 72 files, 0.43s -> 0.43s, 0 findings. NEITHER flags anything on today's tree, so the choice turned on renderer authority and scheduling, not findings.

The README gate won on three grounds. (1) RENDERER: root markdown appears nowhere in mkdocs.yml, so GitHub renders it; check_readme_links.py models GitHub's -N duplicate-heading suffix where check_doc_slugs.py models MkDocs' _N, and rf2-zzt2r established the two deliberately disagree. (2) NO DOUBLE-COVERAGE: the root README.md is already in the README gate, so putting root markdown in the docs gate would cover that one file twice under two conflicting duplicate-suffix rules. (3) SCHEDULING: verify-readme-links runs --ci on EVERY pull request (test.yml's pull_request trigger is unfiltered, the job has no surface guard) where the docs gate is documentation-surface-gated — root markdown lands in the stronger lane. Incidentally the README gate also checks non-.md targets exist, which the docs gate skips entirely, so TESTING.md's links at .github/workflows/test.yml and .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh are covered too.

WHAT THE ROSTER IS. _iter_root_markdown uses `git ls-files -- '*.md'` and drops every entry containing a separator. Non-recursive: git pathspecs are fnmatch without FNM_PATHNAME so `*` crosses `/`, and a bare `*.md` would return markdown at every depth — the naive addition this bead warned about. Git-tracked, not a filesystem walk: a .glob would scan an author's untracked scratch notes and red the gate on one machine while CI stayed green on a clean clone (rf2-k30r7). A glob rather than a six-name list, because a hand-list re-opens this exact gap one file later.

PROOF IT FIRES. This bead's own probe appended to the real TESTING.md, grep-confirmed at line 274: BROKEN TARGET TESTING.md:274 -> znup0-does-not-exist.md and BROKEN ANCHOR TESTING.md:274 -> #znup0-no-such-anchor, exit 1. Reverted; git diff clean. Pinned by two fixtures (root_markdown_ok expects 0, root_markdown_broken_link expects 2 — neither contains a README.md at all, so every count comes from the root roster) plus a non-recursion tooth (tracked markdown one level down resolves as a target but never enters the roster) and a tracking tooth (an untracked root scratch proven poisonous to a walk-based roster, then proven absent from the tracked one). Self-test 16 -> 18; all four ran and passed inside the fast-PR spine.

NO REGRESSION. The old 67-file README roster is a strict prefix of the new 72-file roster, IDENTICAL IN SET AND ORDER; the five appended entries are exactly AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md, CLAUDE.md, SKILL-REDIRECT.md, TESTING.md. All 14 pre-existing fixtures keep their exact counts. check_doc_slugs.py's 674-file roster and its 0 findings are untouched — its only change is a docstring note naming its roster boundary and pointing at the sibling gate, since briefs nominating it for root-markdown edits is the recurring error this bead was filed over.

NOTHING FOUND BROKEN. Zero findings on today's tree, so no root-markdown links needed fixing.

SCHEDULING UNCHANGED. No new gate command, so no lane and no disposition needed: the widened roster rides check_readme_links.py --ci and --self-test, both already one-invocation-per-line in scripts/test-fast-pr.sh and both already required steps of test.yml's verify-readme-links. check_gate_scheduling.py --self-test/--verbose and check_fast_pr_gap.py --self-test/--check all exit 0. check_retired_composition_vocab.py's own root roster is untouched and stayed green.

GATES: test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 (classification `docs=true jvm=false node=false`); check_readme_links --self-test 0 (18/18) and --ci 0 (72 files, 0.74s); check_doc_slugs --self-test 0 (58/58) and --verbose 0 (674 files, 9.95s); check_gate_scheduling --self-test 0 / --verbose 0; check_fast_pr_gap --self-test 0 / --check 0.

title: spec 009: 134 catalogue rows list `:recovery` in the `:tags` cell — is that a corpus-wide row defect or the dual-surface convention?
description:
FOUND by rf2-j4bg3 (PR for the two frame-resolution rows), which was asked by a merged-PR audit note to strike `:recovery` from `:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused`'s `:tags` cell. Measurement stopped that: 134 ACTIVE rows list it. Striking one (or this bead's two, or the three frame-resolution siblings) makes them the odd ones out among 134 — the same 'reads as a deliberate distinction' failure rf2-j4bg3 itself argues against for the parent-dispatch-id claim. Nothing was changed; this is the ruling.

THE TENSION IS INSIDE 009's OWN PREAMBLE, and both halves are true.

(a) The trace-event reading ("Reading the two right-hand columns"): ':recovery is envelope-level — never a :tags key at all.' build-event STRIPS it from tags and hoists it to the envelope top level on every branch. Restating it under :tags names a key no consumer can read there.

(b) The thrown-ex-info reading, same preamble: a thrown row's payload is the FLAT ex-data map, on which §The thrown-error shape declares :rf.error/id, :where, :recovery and :reason REQUIRED — so ':recovery on such a row states the contract rather than breaking it.'

Most of the 134 are BOTH. The three frame-resolution rows are the clean example: emit-no-frame-context! / emit-ambient-frame-refused! / emit-bad-frame-provider-arg! each call trace/emit-error! (payload becomes :tags, :recovery stripped) AND their requiring primitive then throws (error/ex-info-from-data payload) with :recovery present and required.

009 ALREADY NAMES THE CONVENTION FOR THIS: 'A category that reaches two surfaces states both in one cell', with :rf.error/derived-container-replaced as the model — its cell reads '`:reason`; thrown ex-data also carries `:rf.error/id`, `:where` (`'rf/replace-container!`)'. Note the model does NOT list :recovery even though it throws: §The thrown-error shape already declares it required on every thrown error, so a per-row restatement adds nothing.

NO GATE PRESSURE EITHER WAY. error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test's tags-column arm puts :recovery in envelope-only-tag-keys and EXCLUDES it from the diff, so a row may list it or not with no mechanical consequence. That is exactly why the drift reached 134 rows unnoticed, and why this needs a ruling rather than a gate.

THE OPTIONS.
1. LEAVE IT. Declare the current shape the dual-surface convention and amend the preamble's (a) bullet to say a trace+throw row may list :recovery for the thrown surface. Zero churn, and the largest edit is one sentence — but it weakens a rule stated in bold.
2. STRIKE ALL 134 across the catalogue, one mechanical sweep, and lean on §The thrown-error shape for the thrown reading (the derived-container-replaced model's own behaviour). Honest and uniform; a very large hot-zone diff on a single file.
3. STRIKE ONLY on rows that are trace-ONLY, keep it on rows that throw, and mark it the model's way. Most correct, most expensive: each of the 134 must be classified against its emit site.

RECOMMEND (1) unless the mayor wants the sweep — the rule as written is the thing that is slightly wrong, not 134 rows. Whichever is chosen, spec/009-Instrumentation.md is HOT-ZONE: sequence, never parallelise, and a 134-row sweep must not share a PR with anything else.
close_reason:
Ruling implemented in PR #7593 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7593). Option (2) corpus-wide strike, Codex-lite variant.

(a) STRIKE: 134 rows — the recount confirms the ruling's estimate exactly. Every sixth-column :tags cell that LISTED :recovery no longer does; 0 rows list it now, 489 active rows still parse.
(b) PER-ROW GUARD: zero folds needed, as predicted. 13 struck parentheticals — 12 dispositions, all already verbatim in their fifth column; the 13th (machine-spawn-all-duplicate-id's '(spawn-time)') is a surfacing qualifier on the struck slot, not a disposition.
(c) PREAMBLE: the thrown-ex-info bullet's final clause reworded — the shape states the four slots once, the Default :recovery column carries disposition, derived-container-replaced named as the worked example. L1981-1983 untouched.
(d) GATE: tags-column-recovery-listings + tags-column-never-lists-the-envelope-level-recovery-slot + a non-vacuity proof. Made to fail by name against the live corpus (redded naming :rf.error/frame-context-corrupted and :rf.error/ui-duplicate-key), then green on revert.

ONE DIVERGENCE from (d)'s literal wording, and the ruling's own number is the evidence for it: the gate reads LISTED (cell-tag-keys), not MENTIONED. Listed = 134 (the ruling's count); mentioned = 135. A mention-wide rule would have deleted the safe-redirect records' closed allow-list #{:frame :recovery :reason :scheme-class} from three rows, status-defect-record-slots' closed set from another, and two axis-asymmetry sentences — cells that STATE a contract rather than restate a universal. 009's own rule (§'The :tags column is pinned, not documentary') already draws that line.

NO row was load-bearing as a listed key. Verified mechanically: no row's Default :recovery column changed at all; 129 pure token strikes + 5 hand-reviewed prose cases.
