title: SSR emitter diagnostics pr-str an arbitrary hiccup element, so a cyclic foreign value blows the stack instead of producing the error
description:
SIBLING OF rf2-56iys, VERIFIED, and on a LIVE path rather than a test-only one. rf2-56iys fixed re-frame.ssr.hash/canonical-edn-into: CLJS pr-str has exactly two branches that descend into a foreign JS value (object? -> #js {..} over js-keys, array? -> #js [..] over elements), neither carries a seen-set, and React 19's ctx.Provider IS the context object with a self-referential Provider key. The hash walk now stops at those predicates. THE SAME MECHANISM IS UNFIXED IN THE EMITTER. re-frame.ssr.emit/reject-invalid-hiccup-head! builds its message from (pr-str (first el)) and (pr-str el). A JS object is not keyword? and not ifn?, so a provider head falls to that branch, and pr-str explodes. MEASURED (node-test, worktree probe, 2026-08-05): head-is-provider THREW RangeError Maximum call stack size exceeded head-is-cyclic-obj THREW RangeError Maximum call stack size exceeded head-is-plain-js-obj THREW Error :rf.error/invalid-hiccup-head (the CORRECT outcome -- acyclic control) child-carries-provider THREW RangeError Maximum call stack size exceeded attr-carries-provider OK
x
(attrs use str, not pr-str -- safe) So the author who writes [ThemeContext.Provider {...}] on the hiccup tier -- the ordinary mistake the :rf.error/invalid-hiccup-head message exists to catch -- gets RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded and no message at all. THE SITES (by symbol, not line): re-frame.ssr.emit/reject-reserved-head! (pr-str el) re-frame.ssr.emit/reject-invalid-hiccup-head! (pr-str (first el)) and (pr-str el) re-frame.ssr.emit :> throw (pr-str el) re-frame.ssr.emit :rf/suspense-boundary throw (pr-str el) re-frame.ssr.ui-tree four (pr-str node) sites in the malformed-node throws AND THE EX-DATA CARRIES IT TOO. Each of these throws :extra {:element el} / {:node node}, so the cyclic value rides out in ex-data; any consumer that pr-strs the ex-data (a logger, an error projector, a trace sink) explodes at ITS boundary rather than at the emitter's. A fix that only bounds the message strings leaves that door open. WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN rf2-56iys's PR (#7558): different fix class -- bounded diagnostic printing plus ex-data payloads across ten call sites in XSS-sensitive error paths (rf2-y1jbaq locked 'never stringify an unescaped hiccup form to the wire' on exactly these functions) -- and widening a two-branch hash-walk change to cover it would have made the diff unreviewable against its own measurement. SEVERITY. The outcome is a bad error instead of a good one: both paths throw, no wrong bytes reach the wire. That is why it is P3 and not higher. But unlike rf2-56iys it is reachable from re-frame.ssr/render-to-string, which is a shipped production entry point, so it is the more reachable of the two. REPRO. In the node-test build: (require '[re-frame.ssr.emit :as emit]) (def ctx (react/createContext "unset")) (emit/emit-element [(.-Provider ctx) {:value "dark"}]) ;; => RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded ;; expected :rf.error/invalid-hiccup-head
notes:
THIRD AND LAST ENUMERATED NAMESPACE DONE. rf2-1aj9s closed via PR #7564: re-frame.ui.semantic crossed at four sites (the bead's three malformed-node! arms plus validate-tree-version!, which its description omitted the same way this one omitted six ui-tree sites).

THE SIBLING PROBLEM IS RESOLVED STRUCTURALLY, NOT DUPLICATED. safe-form / pr-form moved out of re-frame.ssr.diagnostic (now retired) and into re-frame.error in core. All three consumers already :require re-frame.error, so the move cost no new dependency edge; clojure.walk is stdlib already on core's deps and stays a CLJS-only require clause. One walker serves emit, ui-tree and semantic -- the 'ten sites, ten mechanisms' outcome was avoided.

Reverse mutation at the ui sites reddened 14 rows, all in re-frame.ui.semantic-cycle-cljs-test, all RangeError -- and left every re-frame.ssr.diagnostic-cycle-cljs-test row green, which is the evidence that relocating the helper did not disturb the SSR call sites this bead fixed.

ALL THREE NAMESPACES THIS BEAD NAMED ARE NOW FIXED, so this closes -- BUT THE CLASS IS NOT CLOSED. rf2-q9q9y filed: re-frame.ui carries FIVE more sites of the identical shape (runtime/invalid-slot!, runtime/check-dynamic-child!, runtime/->react-component, tree/invalid-slot!, tree/classify-handler), each pr-str on the message half plus {:extra {:value x}} on the ex-data half. They were in NO bead's enumerated scope and are not a regression from any of these PRs. They are MORE reachable than rf2-1aj9s's site -- ui/slot and ui/render are live client-runtime paths, whereas re-frame.ui.semantic has no production consumer at all today (test-only). The remedy is now cheap: the helper already sits in core.

SCOPE DELIVERED: 18 print sites + every ex-data carrier across re-frame.ssr.emit (4 throwers) and re-frame.ssr.ui-tree (10 sites — the bead undercounted this namespace at four; emit-raw-text-children, all four reject-textarea-content! arms and the version gate are the same class and are fixed too). title: render-tree-hash recurses forever on a defhost head whose component is a React 19 context Provider
description:
FOUND while landing rf2-l0wfx (PR #7549). React 19's `ctx.Provider` IS the context object, and that object carries a `Provider` key pointing back at itself:

  Object.keys(ctx.Provider) -> ['$$typeof','_currentValue','_currentValue2','_threadCount','Provider','Consumer','_currentRenderer','_currentRenderer2']

So any walk that descends into a hiccup form's JS values recurses forever on a `defhost` head whose component is a provider. `re-frame.ssr.hash/render-tree-hash` is one such walk: putting a `(defhost themed (.-Provider ctx) {:ssr :render})` head into `ssr/fixtures/host-screen` made `entry_cljs_test` -> `the-hash-this-root-would-have-had-is-a-constant` die with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. Reproduced, then designed around.

WHY IT IS P3 RATHER THAN P1. Nothing on a live path hashes an interpreted root — the adoption tier deliberately ships no `:rf/render-hash` at either end (rf2-2rtt6.91), and `entry_cljs_test` is the only caller, as a kept measurement of what the hash WOULD have been. So today this is reachable only from a test that deliberately hashes a root form.

WHAT LANDED INSTEAD. The `:render` corpus row is a separate screen, `ssr/fixtures/render-host-screen`, whose docstring records the cycle and why the row is separate. `host-screen` (the hashed one) is unchanged.

WHAT A FIX WOULD BE. `render-tree-hash`/`canonical-edn` should either refuse to descend into a foreign JS object (it already renders every fn as `#fn[]`, so a minted host head is arguably in the same class) or carry a seen-set. The first is cheaper and matches the existing treatment of functions.

RISK IF LEFT: a hiccup-tier substrate that DOES hash, handed a form containing a context object, blows the stack rather than reporting anything useful. That is a different door from this one, and worth checking before the tier-1 hash surface grows a new caller.
notes:
WORKER (PR #7558, branch worker/provcycle-56iys).

MECHANISM VERIFIED, AND IT IS BROADER THAN 'Provider'. The recursion is not in canonical-edn-into at all -- its :else branch calls (pr-str x) ONCE. The recursion is inside cljs.core's printer, which has exactly two branches that DESCEND into a foreign value and neither carries a seen-set: object? (prints #js {..} by walking js-keys) and array? (prints #js [..] by walking elements). Measured, all reproducing 'RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded' on main:

  handbuilt (unchecked-set o "self" o)  -- no React anywhere
  the React context object itself
  (.-Provider ctx)                        -- and (identical? ctx (.-Provider ctx)) is TRUE
  [provider {..} ..] in head position
  a provider nested in markup
  a provider as an ATTRIBUTE VALUE
  a cycle reached through a JS ARRAY
  hicasso/defhost-ssr-render (the row this bead was filed from)

THE FIX took the bead's first option: two CLJS-only cond branches ahead of :else appending #js{} / #js[]. Those are precisely the two predicates cljs.core's printer descends on, so the walk stops exactly where pr-str would have started; #inst / regex / symbol / the terminal #object[Ctor] are bounded and keep the print forms they have today. CLJS-only because the JVM reaches :else with a Java object whose pr-str is its bounded .toString and no cyclic value can be built from persistent collections. No seen-set anywhere; no hash introduced anywhere.

A SECOND REASON THE BEAD DID NOT NAME. Descending re-opened rf2-jsa2ml's identity leak: #js {"component" f} printed #js {:component #object[f]} -- a JS function .name that :advanced renames -- so a tree hashed differently in dev and release. hicasso/defhost-ssr-policy's canonical EDN carried #object[re_frame$bench$hicasso$ssr$fixtures$client_widget] on main.

EXISTING HASHES, MEASURED not asserted. 75-entry corpus (23 parity fixtures + nil-prune pairs + all 9 Hicasso SSR rows + 41 hand-built branch-coverage values) dumped to canonical-EDN AND hash before and after and diffed byte-for-byte: 61 of 75 byte-identical. Every changed entry contains a foreign JS value; no entry without one moved. The one existing hash that moves is defhost-ssr-policy (c5a1cf91 -> 93183e3c) and it moves because it was carrying munged fn names; nothing pins it (entry-cljs-test asserts only (not= dogfood markup), still true; instance-key asserts (= dogfood green red) over three [#fn[] {}] roots, all unchanged at 83b865f8). defhost-ssr-render now hashes 76b17086.

SIBLING FILED: rf2-9s68n. re-frame.ssr.emit/reject-invalid-hiccup-head! builds its message from (pr-str el), so emit-element on a provider head raises RangeError INSTEAD of :rf.error/invalid-hiccup-head -- measured, with the acyclic control still producing the correct error. Ten such sites across emit + ui-tree, plus the cyclic value riding out in ex-data :extra. Left to its own bead: different fix class, XSS-sensitive error paths (rf2-y1jbaq).

FENCE CONFLICT REPORTED: the dispatch brief fenced implementation/ssr/**, which is where render-tree-hash lives and the only place the fix could land.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #7558 (worker/provcycle-56iys), commit a02f700cdf.

Two CLJS-only cond branches in re-frame.ssr.hash/canonical-edn-into: a foreign JS object appends #js{}, a JS array appends #js[], and neither is descended into. Those are precisely the two cljs.core printer branches that recurse, so the walk stops exactly where pr-str would have started. No seen-set; no hash introduced anywhere; the adoption tier still ships no :rf/render-hash.

REGRESSION SUITE: re-frame.ssr.foreign-value-hash-cljs-test (5 deftests, 23 assertions), including a non-vacuity control that asserts pr-str itself blows the stack on the same fixtures and that (identical? ctx (.-Provider ctx)) is TRUE.

MUTATION, BOTH DIRECTIONS: forward all green; reverting the branch reds the named test with 12 failures + 2 errors, each carrying {:threw "RangeError", :message "Maximum call stack size exceeded"} in its failure text.

EXISTING HASHES: 75-entry before/after canonical-EDN dump diffed byte-for-byte, 61 identical, every changed entry provably contained a foreign JS value.

GATES: fast-PR spine PASS (exit 0; JVM core 2215/11527 clean, JVM ssr 623/3127 clean, CLJS node 12647/63357 clean, hicasso-compile 126 namespaces zero warnings); clj-kondo at the CI pin 2026.04.15 exit 0, errors: 0, warnings 4536 (baseline), zero findings on either changed file; GitHub CI on the PR head 50 pass / 35 skipping / 0 fail, including :browser-test and :node-test.

SIBLING FILED: rf2-9s68n -- the same mechanism in the SSR emitter's diagnostics (9 message sites across re-frame.ssr.emit, re-frame.ssr.ui-tree, re-frame.ui.semantic, plus the ex-data carriers), verified reachable from render-to-string.

title: Promote the gate-scheduling audit from the nightly to PR time
description:

.github/scripts/check-gate-scheduling.py asserts that every
`test:*` / `bench:*` command in implementation/package.json is either
reachable from a workflow or carries a machine-checked disposition
saying why not. It is a ~0.1s pure-Python static check with a
self-test arm -- exactly the shape of the twenty-nine checkers already
in test.yml's always-on repo-invariant job and in
scripts/test-fast-pr.sh's always-on block.

It landed in expensive-tests.yml instead, for one reason only: PR #7536
was fenced OFF .github/workflows/test.yml because rf2-eegpw / #7530 was
open on it. Nightly is not nothing -- rf2-6sg25 landed alerting in the
same PR -- but a PR that adds an unscheduled gate should learn so in
three minutes, not in twenty-four hours.

REMEDY, once test.yml is free:
  1. Add the self-test + live arms to test.yml's repo-invariant job,
     with the `id:` + `continue-on-error: true` shape
     scripts/check_ci_reproduce_commands.py requires of every checker
     step there, and the matching aggregator entry.
  2. Add both invocations to the always-on block of
     scripts/test-fast-pr.sh, ONE PER LINE in the literal
     `python "$spine_root/scripts/check_<name>.py"` form --
     check_fast_pr_gap.py derives the spine's coverage by reading that
     literal shape, and a loop breaks the derivation.
  3. NOTE: the script lives at .github/scripts/, not scripts/, so the
     spine's literal-shape derivation may need it moved to scripts/
     first -- check check_fast_pr_gap.py's matcher before wiring.
  4. Drop the nightly `gate-scheduling` job, or keep it; it is ~10s of
     runner time and the nightly's `nightly-result` job `needs:` it.
close_reason:
Delivered in PR #7542 (merged, 25e404f434). PREMISE CHECKED FIRST, as the brief asked: the nightly placement had NO merit -- it was accidental. The workflow comment named the cause (test.yml fenced by rf2-eegpw/#7530 the day it was written) and TESTING.md itself recorded the move as a follow-up. Cost measured before moving: 0.75s / 0.86s / 0.93s for the self-test + live pair over three warm runs on Windows, both arms within ~50ms of each other. Both read only implementation/package.json and .github/workflows/, so neither grows with the tree.

Remedy clause 3 was the load-bearing one and the bead was right to flag it. The script is now scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py -- moved AND renamed to underscores. That is not cosmetic: check_ci_reproduce_commands.py matches ^python scripts/check_[A-Za-z0-9_]+\.py and check_fast_pr_gap.py matches ^python scripts/(check_[A-Za-z0-9_]+)\.py, so a hyphenated .github/scripts/ script is invisible to BOTH. Its failure would have been reported with a reproduce command that does not exist (the aggregator's id-based fallback would emit 'python scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py' for a file that was not there), and the fast-PR gap map would never have counted it. main() also moved parents[2] -> parents[1] for the new depth.

Clause 1: two steps added to test.yml's verify-skill-mcp-drift repo-invariant job in the required id: + continue-on-error: true shape (check_gate_scheduling_selftest / check_gate_scheduling). Verified by check_ci_reproduce_commands.py --check and by --emit on both ids, which now round-trip to the exact commands the steps run.

Clause 2: two invocations added to the always-on block of scripts/test-fast-pr.sh in the literal one-per-line python "$spine_root/scripts/check_<name>.py" form. No loop -- the derivation would have gone fictional. Verified: the spine run shows both arms green, and check_fast_pr_gap.py --check stays clean and derived (76 required jobs, 26 covered, 4 partly, 46 not). The 'MEASURED BEFORE ADDING' comment was extended with the new pair's real numbers rather than left stating 29.

Clause 4: the nightly gate-scheduling job is DROPPED, not kept, and nightly-result's needs: updated to the 4 remaining jobs. An always-on per-PR gate means main cannot carry a violation overnight, so a nightly arm would re-prove a property proven on every merge, and a second copy is a second thing to keep in step. Workflow YAML re-parsed to confirm the job graph.

title: hicasso guide 05: does the value-equality bail-out actually reach a defhost head? mint-host! never calls memoize-boundary!
description:
FOUND while narrowing 02's boundary definition for rf2-2rtt6.102 (PR #7532). NOT decided there -- it is a correctness question about a mechanism, not a wording fix, and it sits outside that bead's scope.

THE CLAIM. docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/05-interop.md, section 'Memo and hosted components' (lines ~164-179):

  'Every Hicasso boundary is a React.memo that compares props by value. That
   bail-out reaches a hosted component the same way it reaches a native one'

and, against a sample where chrome-page re-renders because its own sub moved:

  'A write that only moves :hatch/label re-renders .chrome and stops.
   hosted-row never re-enters the foreign component.'

THE TENSION. front/codec.cljs:912 memoize-boundary! is explicit that the wrapper is opt-in AT THE MINT SITE, with the reason spelled out: 'Opt-in at the mint site rather than applied to every marked head, so heads that are not reactive boundaries -- h/boundary's error-boundary class, presence -- keep the semantics they were written with.'

Its only two callers are arm1/runtime.cljs mint-view! (:1880) and mint-frame-prop-view! (:1905). codec/mint-host! (:1090) does NOT call it. So a defhost head carries no Hicasso memo wrapper, and when its parent boundary re-renders, the parent's body mints a fresh element for it.

WHAT NEEDS SETTLING, one of:
 (a) the guide's claim is right for a reason the page does not name -- React's own reconciliation, or the fact that a library's exported component is often already a memo product -- in which case name the mechanism, because as written a reader will believe Hicasso is doing it; or
 (b) the claim needs narrowing to what actually holds (the enclosing BOUNDARY bails out, and a hosted child of a boundary that did not re-render is not re-entered), which is a weaker and different statement than the sample teaches; or
 (c) mint-host! should carry the wrapper, which is a product decision, not a docs one -- note h/boundary and presence were deliberately left out for a stated reason, so hosts may have been too.

Cheap to check: the arm has host DOM suites (arm1/host_hatch_dom_cljs_test) and the inpage ladder already isolates the memo wrapper's cost (inpage_ladder_app.cljs:47 'nomemo'). A witness that re-renders a parent boundary and counts foreign-component invocations settles it in one test.

FENCE NOTE: 05-interop.md has carried concurrent dispatchers; sequence, do not parallelise.
close_reason: Settled as option (b), and fixed in PR #7557. mint-host! never calls codec/memoize-boundary!; host-element builds the crossing from the head's 'gate' slot, bypassing codec/element-type, which is the only reader of the hicassoMemo slot and is called only from boundary-element. mint-host-gate!'s product is a plain (fn [props] ...), which React does not shallow-compare. So a defhost crossing re-renders whenever the boundary that WROTE it re-renders, and guide 05's sample was built on a boundary that re-renders by construction (its own sub moved) - precisely the case where the claim fails. The chapter's own troubleshooting table already carried the correct rule, so the page contradicted itself. Guide now names the mechanism, keeps the caveat that the library may have exported its own memo, and gives the remedy (put the crossing behind its own defview). Also narrowed 02's 'every minted head carries one stable internal memo wrapper', false in the same way since host heads are minted heads. No product change proposed: option (c) not taken - hosts look deliberately excluded for the same reason h/boundary and presence are.

title: spec 009: the :rf.error/no-frame-context row has the SAME incomplete :operation enumeration, and both frame-resolution rows list a :rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id payload key no builder ever sets
description:
FOUND by rf2-e28wl (PR #7533) while fixing the sibling row. Two defects, one file, deliberately NOT folded into e28wl because that bead scoped itself to one row and spec/** is a hot zone.

DEFECT 1 -- the same enumeration bug, one row up. spec/009-Instrumentation.md's :rf.error/no-frame-context row says:

  trigger: 'A frame-scoped op (subscribe / dispatch, the ambient 1-arity rf/ forms)'
  payload: ':operation (:dispatch / :subscribe), :where (:re-frame.router/dispatch! / :re-frame.subs/subscribe)'

Both are incomplete for exactly the reason e28wl's row was: no-frame-context is raised by the SAME primitive (frame/require-current-frame!), so every op that can hit the refusal can hit the absence. Grepping implementation/*/src finds 18+ call sites and these :operation values: :subscribe :subscribe-once :unsubscribe :dispatch :capture-frame :current-frame-id :use-frame :clear-sub-cache! :elision-declarations :elision-sensitive-declarations :reg-flow :clear-flow :flow-meta-at :route-link :reg-http-interceptor :clear-http-interceptor :machine-by-system-id :frame-provider, plus re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc which passes its CALLER's operation keyword (so the set is open by construction). The :where enumeration is wrong the same way.

PR #7533 fixed the ambient-frame-refused row by stating the RULE (the category is defined by the door) and treating the names as illustration. Same remedy applies here. Doing it makes the two rows consistent; leaving it means one row states the rule and its sibling lists two ops.

DEFECT 2 -- a payload key that is never set. BOTH rows end '...plus the capture-site ancestry correlation keys :rf.trace/dispatch-id / :rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id'. Neither payload builder sets the parent. frame.cljc's no-frame-context-payload and ambient-frame-refused-payload each merge only

  (when-let [did (some-> trace/*handler-scope* :dispatch-id)] {:rf.trace/dispatch-id did})

and the call sites' 'extra' carries only :where / :event-id. :rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id IS set elsewhere -- router.cljc:3982 puts it on the dispatch envelope's trace tags -- but it never reaches either frame-resolution payload. Either the rows should say :rf.trace/dispatch-id alone, or the builders should thread the parent when a handler scope has one; that is a real call, not a wording fix, which is why this is filed rather than guessed.

WHY NOT FIXED IN #7533: defect 2 is a claim SHARED by both rows, and correcting one of two would read as a deliberate distinction to a reader. Both wanted fixing together, and no-frame-context is a heavily cross-referenced always-on / security-surface row (cited by 004D, Security.md, 011) -- out of a one-row bead's scope.

SCOPE: two rows in spec/009-Instrumentation.md (plus, for defect 2, a decision about frame.cljc's two payload builders). spec/** is a hot zone; sequence, do not parallelise.

NOTE :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused remains PROVISIONAL (rf2-k0rbk).

Spec 009 immediately above the catalogue says :recovery is envelope-level and never a :tags key; re-frame.trace/build-event implements that contract by removing :recovery from tags and hoisting it.    mis-layered view async fails loudly today and would merely WORK under
   h/frame. The compensation the ruling accepted is that every guide row
   putting h/frame on the page puts :fx first.

   Hicasso bodies. Post-rf2-2rtt6.122 this is stronger than the design

description:
# Draft guide: say that Hicasso owns `rf:render:*` (the last acceptance bullet of rf2-2rtt6.125)

rf2-2rtt6.125 landed the Performance `:render` wiring (PR #7524): `defview` boundaries now emit one `rf:render:<view-id>` User-Timing measure per render under `:closure-defines {re-frame.performance/enabled? true}`, and the id is the head's `displayName` (`"<ns>/<sym>"`).

That bead's last acceptance bullet asks for **one honest sentence** in the draft guide saying so. It is **not** in PR #7524 and must not be added blind, for a mechanical reason:

- `docs/design/hicasso/**` was fenced during that work — two workers were in flight **renaming `draft-guide/11-performance.md` → `draft-guide/11-below-hiccup.md`** (`worker/hframe-841vn`, `worker/fallback-nv07k`, plus the `docs/hicasso-performance-rename` branch). Writing the sentence into `11-performance.md` would have written it into a file that is being deleted.

## Do this after those PRs merge

1. Confirm the rename has landed on `main`; edit whichever file now carries the Performance chapter.
2. Replace the current framing — which correctly told authors to reach for React DevTools + Xray because per-view `rf:render:*` did not exist — with the true one: **event / sub / fx / render are all live for a Hicasso app** under the perf goog-define; ids are `rf:render:<ns>/<view>`, the same string React DevTools shows.
3. Do **not** claim the trace pair. `:rf.view/render` / `:rf.view/rendered` are NOT emitted by Hicasso boundaries and are blocked on rf2-2rtt6.126 (the `:render-key` instance-token needs a third hook). If the chapter mentions Xray's Views timeline, say plainly that it is the adapter path's today.
4. Worth one line: a memo bail-out emits no measure, and a boundary React invoked twice under StrictMode emits twice — both correct, and both the kind of thing an author reading a measure count will otherwise file as a bug.

Reference: Spec 009 §What gets bracketed (the substrate-general `:render` rule and the three consequences) and §Naming convention (the id rule), both updated in PR #7524.

title: spec 009: the :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused row enumerates :operation as (:dispatch / :subscribe) but at least :capture-frame and :current-frame-id also reach it
description:

catalogue row for :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused says, twice:

  trigger:  'A frame-scoped op (subscribe / dispatch) resolved its frame
             AMBIENTLY inside a render extent that REFUSES ...'
  payload:  ':operation (:dispatch / :subscribe)'

Both enumerations are incomplete. Every op that reaches
frame/require-current-frame! reaches the refusal, and the call sites in
implementation/core/src include at least:

  :capture-frame     core.cljc (capture-frame 0-arity)  <- Spec 002's ONE

  plus adapter/use_frame.cljs, elision.cljc's declarations /

current-frame-id/capture-frame — so the catalogue is behind the code it

:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused), so this is worth sequencing WITH that
bead rather than before it.

title: hicasso/core: an enclosing with-frame makes the ambient carry answer the WRONG frame inside a refusing render extent
description:
FOUND by rf2-841vn while grounding the SSR witnesses; behaviour is PINNED
(arm1/hframe_cljs_test/a-carried-outer-scope-makes-the-ambient-carry-answer-the-wrong-frame)
but NOT endorsed. This is a design question, not a clear-cut fix.

rf2-2rtt6.122's refusal withdraws the AMBIENT (React-context) tier only —
'the refusal deletes the FINDING, never the carrying'. So a tier-1 stamp
still answers inside a Hicasso body:

    (rf/with-frame :b
      (render a boundary whose frame is :a
        (rf/capture-frame)))      ;; => captures :b, silently

Core is behaving exactly as EP-0002 specifies: :b WAS carried. But the
boundary is rendering under :a, and everything else in that body targets
:a — the collector's reads, the lowered intents, the presence tray. One
body, two frames, selected by which spelling the author reached for, with
no diagnostic. That is the 'silently wrong frame' class rf2-2rtt6.122 was
meant to close, surviving in one configuration.

Reachable in practice wherever a host renders a Hicasso tree inside a
with-frame: a synchronous flushSync mount under a scope, an SSR host that
wraps renderToString, a test fixture (test-support's :ambient-frame
default root-binds *current-frame* to :rf/default, which is exactly how
this was found — every SSR witness in ssr/entry_cljs_test runs with that
stamp live).

THE QUESTION, and it is genuinely open:
(a) leave it — the carried invariant is the spec, and a carried stamp
    winning is the whole point of EP-0002;
(b) refuse a MISMATCHED carried stamp inside a substrate render extent —
    i.e. the refusal detail carries the extent's own frame, and
    require-current-frame! raises when tier 1 answers something else.
    Costs a comparison on a path that already failed, and makes
    'a body has ONE frame' true by construction;
(c) diagnose only — a dev-time warning naming both frames.

(b) collides with a-carried-with-frame-still-carries-inside-a-body, which
pins that an explicit with-frame answers inside a body — but that witness
carries the SAME frame the boundary renders under, so (b) would leave it
green. Worth checking rather than assuming.

The composed spelling (rf/capture-frame (h/frame)) is immune under every
option, so rf2-841vn does not block on this.

Related: rf2-hnrww (the refusal's advice text), rf2-k0rbk (the
provisional :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused spelling).
notes:
MAYOR RULING (2026-08-06): take (b) — REFUSE A MISMATCHED CARRIED STAMP INSIDE A SUBSTRATE RENDER EXTENT. Operator-overturnable; surfaced rather than merged quietly.

WHY NOT (a). 'A carried stamp wins' is EP-0002's point, and it stays the rule everywhere a carried stamp is the only frame in play. But the standing principle that frames are ISOLATED CONTEXTS — subs must not reach into other frames — is Mike-ruled, and this configuration violates it silently: the body reads and dispatches against a frame the boundary is not rendering under, with no signal. Two frames in one body is not a carried-stamp win, it is an ambiguity, and (a) blesses it.

WHY NOT (c). A dev-only warning elides in release builds, so the silent wrong-frame read survives exactly where it is least recoverable. The standing test for whether a guard is warranted is whether the failure is SILENT and HAS ALREADY HAPPENED. Both hold: there is no signal today, and the bead found this through test-support's :ambient-frame default root-binding *current-frame* to :rf/default, which means every SSR witness in ssr/entry_cljs_test is running with the mismatched stamp live right now.

WHY (b) IS CHEAP ENOUGH TO BE OBVIOUS. The comparison sits inside an extent that is already refusing ambient reads, so it is not a hot-path cost, and it makes 'a body has ONE frame' true BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by convention. That is the structural-fix-over-N-point-fixes shape this project prefers.

ACCEPTANCE — the collision the bead names must be CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED. a-carried-with-frame-still-carries-inside-a-body pins that an explicit with-frame answers inside a body. The bead reasons it stays green because that witness carries the SAME frame the boundary renders under, so nothing mismatches. Verify that by running it; if it reds, the ruling is wrong and I want to hear so before any fix lands.

The composed spelling (rf/capture-frame (h/frame)) is immune under every option, so rf2-841vn does not block on this either way. Related: rf2-hnrww (refusal advice text), rf2-k0rbk (the provisional :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused spelling) — do not re-spell the id here.

Reproduce this ruling and its reasoning in the merging PR body; a tracker link is not a durable record.
CORRECTION TO MY OWN RULING'S WORDING (2026-08-06). My ruling said 'require-current-frame! raises when tier 1 answers something else'. That names a funnel that is not one, and my close reason repeated it. THE CHECK ACTUALLY LIVES IN resolve-current-frame, and the worker found this by MEASUREMENT, not reading: its first implementation put the check exactly where I said, and the-mismatch-refusal-reaches-every-ambient-door went RED on the subscribe arm with the read silently succeeding.

WHY: subs/subscribe's 1-arity deliberately INLINES (or (frame/resolve-current-frame) (frame/require-current-frame! ...)) to keep its error payload off the per-read fast path — rf2-a8bw0 records 'Do NOT collapse this back'. So an ambient subscribe with a stamp in scope NEVER REACHES the requiring primitive. Putting the check there would have left the largest ambient door unguarded while every test that exercised the smaller doors passed.

Placing it in resolve-current-frame instead — the reader answers nil for a stamp the extent will not accept — fixes every reader-first caller BY CONSTRUCTION and leaves the rf2-a8bw0 optimisation intact. That is a better answer than the one I ruled, not a deviation from it: the DECISION (refuse a mismatched carried stamp) was right and the SITE was wrong.

ACCEPTANCE DISCHARGED AS REQUIRED: a-carried-with-frame-still-carries-inside-a-body, run alone under the fix, 1 test / 1 assertion, 0 failures, exit 0 — not weakened, not touched, and mutation M2 reds it, proving it is load-bearing rather than a passenger. The defect was also reproduced LIVE under renderToString before any change: (rf/capture-frame) in an SSR body answered :rf/default while (h/frame) answered the per-request frame.

Both fences were already settled, not in flight: rf2-hnrww (advice text) and rf2-k0rbk (the error id spelling) are both CLOSED.
close_reason: SHIPPED in PR #7604 (merged) under the mayor ruling of 2026-08-06: option (b), refuse a mismatched carried stamp inside a substrate render extent, making 'a body has ONE frame' true by construction rather than by convention. (a) was rejected because although 'a carried stamp wins' is EP-0002's point, the standing Mike-ruled principle that frames are ISOLATED CONTEXTS makes two frames in one body an ambiguity rather than a win; (c) was rejected because a dev-only warning elides in release builds, leaving the silent wrong-frame read exactly where it is least recoverable. The ruling was explicitly conditional on a-carried-with-frame-still-carries-inside-a-body staying green — that witness carries the SAME frame the boundary renders under, so nothing mismatches — and the worker was instructed to run it rather than assume, and to stop rather than bend the witness if it redded.

title: hicasso: rf2-2rtt6.122's refusal fires on rf/capture-frame but its advice text does not address a CARRY — and no witness pins it
description:
Found while re-grounding rf2-2rtt6.118's design on the post-rf2-2rtt6.122
tree (PR #7519). Small, real, and in LANDED code.

rf2-2rtt6.122 fused core's refusal tier into intent/with-frame -- the one
binding every Hicasso render extent performs -- so ambient frame
resolution refuses for the whole extent. That is correct and is the
point. But the refusal catches a THIRD consumer the arm's advice text was
not written for.

THE DOOR HAS THREE CONSUMERS, and frame.cljc says so itself: ambient
subscribe, ambient dispatch, and current-frame-id/capture-frame. The
arm's refusal detail (front/intent.cljs, ambient-frame-refusal) is
written for the first two -- it advises reading through the boundary's
collector (`sub`) and dispatching through an intent at a handler
position. An author who trips the refusal via (rf/capture-frame) --
0-arity, in a body -- is doing NEITHER. capture-frame is Spec 002's "the
ONE public carry primitive", and the reason it resolves ambiently is to
capture, not to read or to dispatch. They get a paragraph that never
names their recovery.

The honest recovery today is the 1-arity (rf/capture-frame <frame-id>),
which never consults the resolver -- and, once rf2-841vn lands,
(rf/capture-frame (h/frame)), which is the sentence the advice should
contain.

AND NO WITNESS PINS IT. arm1/ambient_refusal_cljs_test covers ambient
subscribe, ambient dispatch, a carried with-frame still carrying, an
explicit {:frame ...} opt still resolving, the unwind, the two-absences-
two-errors split, and the untouched collector. capture-frame under
refusal appears in none of them, so the keystone's behaviour inside a
body is currently a consequence rather than a contract.

SCOPE. Arguably two lines of advice text plus one witness row. It is
filed separately rather than folded into rf2-841vn because it is true of
landed code even if h/frame never ships -- though h/frame's landing is
the natural moment to close it, since the ideal advice sentence names
(h/frame).

Note :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused is PROVISIONAL (rf2-k0rbk).
close_reason:
BOTH GAPS CLOSED in PR #7522 (branch worker/hframe-841vn).

GAP 1 -- THE ADVICE TEXT. front/intent.cljs's ambient-frame-refusal :reason
now carries a third sentence for the third door: 'CARRYING a frame out of
the render is a THIRD thing, and its recovery is neither of the above:
(rf/capture-frame) resolves ambiently, so it refuses here, but
(rf/capture-frame <frame-id>) never consults the resolver at all. Write
(rf/capture-frame (h/frame)) ...'. It is a module-level constant built once
at load, so establishing the extent still allocates nothing.

GAP 2 -- THE MISSING WITNESS, which the bead correctly called the larger
half. arm1/ambient_refusal_cljs_test gains a CARRY section:
 - a-carry-inside-a-body-refuses-exactly-as-a-read-does (the design's W10,
   INVERTED -- the designed row pinned that the 0-arity SUCCEEDS, and
   rf2-2rtt6.122 is exactly the change that made it refuse). Pins

title: Nothing detects drift between docs/the-mayor-method/** and .claude/commands/**
description:
FOUND while fixing rf2-40d9d (PR #7514).

rf2-40d9d existed because PR #7511 corrected the METHOD DOCS (docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md + README.md) and .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md -- the file the mayor loop ACTUALLY EXECUTES -- kept the retired rule verbatim for hours. The description of the method and the instruction executing it drifted apart and only the description was maintained.

THE STRUCTURAL POINT: that drift was invisible to every gate.
  - scripts/check_doc_slugs.py's DEFAULT_ROOTS are docs, spec, skills, migration (+ tools/*/spec). .claude/ is not scanned, so its markdown links and anchors are unvalidated.
  - mkdocs build --strict does not see .claude/ either.
  - scripts/test-fast-pr.sh passes on any content whatsoever under .claude/commands/.
So a .claude/commands/*.md file can contradict the method docs, or link to a heading that no longer exists, and nothing reds.

This is not a request for a semantic doc-consistency checker -- that is not buildable and would be over-engineering. The narrow, cheap version:
  1. Add .claude to check_doc_slugs.py's roots so at least link targets and anchors in the command files are validated. The command files DO cross-reference docs/the-mayor-method/ (mayor-posture.md names two files by path; mayor-hygiene.md now names bootstrap.md), and a rename would silently break them today.
  2. Consider whether the five mayor-*.md command files should carry an explicit 'normative source: docs/the-mayor-method/<file>' line, so a worker correcting the method doc can grep for its dependants. rf2-k3j2w's worker could not have found mayor-hygiene.md from bootstrap.md by any search.

NEEDS A RULING on (2) before implementing; (1) is mechanical. Docs/scripts only.
notes:
RESOLVED in PR #7568 -- but NOT by the remedy the bead proposed, and the measurement is the finding.

MEASURED: adding .claude to check_doc_slugs.py's DEFAULT_ROOTS validates NOTHING. Roster goes 674 -> 679 files (+5) and markdown links +0, headings +0, rendered fragment ids +0. All five tracked command files (70 lines) contain zero [text](dest) links and zero headings. Every reference in them is a backticked path (`docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md`) or a bare filename in prose (dispatch-prompt-template.md, in mayor-cluster.md and mayor-dispatch.md), and BOTH link gates deliberately mask inline code and only examine markdown-link syntax (rf2-mqv8s). The roster entry would scan five more files and check nothing in them -- today, and equally on the day a method doc is renamed. Arming-not-catching.

A filesystem-walk roster would also have been wrong: /.claude/worktrees/ is gitignored and holds whole repository checkouts, so rglob('*.md') under .claude can descend into one.

RENDERED BY NEITHER. .claude/** appears nowhere in mkdocs.yml (docs_dir: docs), and unlike repo-root markdown it is not GitHub-rendered documentation anyone browses -- it is prompt text the Claude Code CLI feeds to a model verbatim. With zero headings and zero links there is no anchor to resolve, so the _N-vs--N duplicate-suffix rule the two gates deliberately disagree on (rf2-zzt2r) does not arise. Only target RESOLUTION is meaningful -- which is why this shipped as a reference resolver, not as a corpus root in either gate.

SHIPPED: check_readme_links.py now resolves every .md reference in the git-tracked .claude/commands/*.md roster (a glob, not a hand-list), in both forms the files use. Chosen over check_doc_slugs.py on the rf2-znup0 criteria: verify-readme-links runs --ci on EVERY pull request (test.yml's PR trigger is unfiltered, the job carries no surface guard) where the docs gate is documentation-surface-gated and .claude/** is on no surface docs.yml filters for. Zero .github/workflows/** change; the scheduling audit demanded none.

PROVED IT FIRES, by mutation on the live tree (both restored): git mv of bootstrap.md reds naming mayor-hygiene.md:6 and mayor-posture.md:4; git mv of dispatch-prompt-template.md reds naming mayor-cluster.md:4, mayor-dispatch.md:20 and mayor-posture.md:4. Green on today's tree -- all four references resolve, so nothing needed fixing.

Two fixtures (0 and 2, the latter carrying a still-resolving reference so it fails both ways) plus a tracked-roster tooth mirroring rf2-znup0's. All 18 pre-existing self-test cases keep their exact counts; check_doc_slugs.py untouched and its corpus run identical (674 files, no broken links).

SECOND HALF SPLIT OUT to rf2-zh8wh -- the 'normative source:' line still needs the ruling this bead said it needed, and none has been given. Note for whoever rules: the gate now delivers the dependant-discovery that line was for, but only for MECHANICAL dependence (naming a file), not the SEMANTIC drift that was rf2-40d9d itself.

title: the nine bench drivers still burn a full sentinel budget when the page dies before its sentinel
description:
FROM rf2-sib23 (PR #7505), 2026-08-05. The OTHER half of `sentinel.cjs`, left
deliberately undone and recorded so the absence is not read as an oversight.

rf2-sib23 gave all nine drivers the collector — `watchPage` — but did NOT
convert their sentinel waits from `page.waitForFunction` to `watch.race`. The
fault rf2-sib23 closed is the page that throws and STILL reaches its
sentinel, where the wait returns normally and the exit block is the only place
the signal can be read; converting the waits would have changed nine
behaviours nobody had watched, for a fault the bead was not about.

What remains open is rf2-f5roa's defect, in the nine drivers that never got
its fix: when a page dies BEFORE its sentinel, the failure is instantaneous
and the report of it is fifteen or twenty minutes late, with a log line that
says `Timeout 900000ms exceeded` when what happened was a ReferenceError at
page load. `sentinel.cjs`'s own header states the case; its `race` already
exists and is used by six drivers in the hicasso tree.

THE CONVERSION IS MECHANICAL — same predicate, same timeout, plus the budget
string each driver already writes in its `navigate()` call, e.g.

  await watch.race('window.B6_DONE === true || window.B6_ERROR',
                   { timeoutMs: 15 * 60 * 1000,
                     budget: 'the 15-minute wait for `window.B6_DONE`' });

WHAT MAKES IT MORE THAN A SED, and why it wants its own bead: `race` THROWS
where `waitForFunction` used to resolve. Three of the nine (b6_prod,
b6_profile, b10_prod) now have a rejection handler on `drive()` that turns
that into a named exit 1; b7, p0, the ladder and the ablation route it into
their existing catch; b8 folds it into `failed`. Each of those paths wants
watching once rather than assuming.

Sites: b6_prod_run.cjs, b6_profile_run.cjs, b7_run.cjs (two rows), b8_run.cjs,
b10_prod_run.cjs, reads_ladder_run.cjs, spine_ablation_run.cjs, p0_run.cjs
(three waits), hicasso_narrow_run.cjs.
notes:
MAYOR RULING ON THE TRADE ITS IMPLEMENTER SURFACED (2026-08-05) — ACCEPTED AS SHIPPED. Recording it so the residue is not later rediscovered as a defect and reverted by someone who does not know it was chosen.

WHAT WAS TRADED. All twelve sentinel waits now race against the recorded-failure array. In the narrow case where a page THROWS AND STILL REACHES ITS SENTINEL, the run now fails at the wait rather than after printing its table, so A LATE THROW'S PARTIAL ROWS ARE NO LONGER PRINTED. The verdict is identical either way; what is lost is diagnostic residue in that one window.

MY BRIEF SAID "no refusal may suppress output" AND THIS IS IN PARTIAL TENSION WITH IT. The implementer said so plainly rather than quietly satisfying the letter, judged it the filer's explicit design (the bead enumerates the rejection path per driver) and consistent with rf2-f5roa's established precedent on drivers that also publish tables, and offered the exact revert lever: drop the four DONE-wait conversions (b6_prod, b7 mount-frame, b10_prod, p0 clock) and keep the eight READY ones, where no table can exist.

I ACCEPT IT AS SHIPPED, for three reasons. The motivating case is a LOAD-TIME ReferenceError where there is no table to lose and 15 to 30 minutes to save, which is the common shape. The verdict does not move, so no published figure and no gate outcome changes. And the lost residue is recoverable by re-running the driver, whereas the wasted budget is not recoverable at all.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN IT: if someone hits a LATE throw whose partial rows would have diagnosed something the re-run cannot reproduce. That is a real possibility on a flaky page, and the revert above is the fix — four conversions, named, no redesign. Do not treat the missing rows as a bug in the refusal; they are a chosen cost.

THE INSTRUMENT DID NOT REGRESS: no measurement, arm, threshold, knob default, exit code or dataset changed, and every rejection lands in a path each driver already had.
close_reason: DONE in PR #7509 (2026-08-05). All TWELVE sentinel waits across the nine now go through sentinel.cjs's `race`: b6_prod (15m), b6_profile (5m), b7 x2 (120s READY + 15m DONE), b8 (5m), b10_prod (20m), reads_ladder (120s), spine_ablation (120s), p0 x3 (the 30m clock wait + two 180s READY waits), hicasso_narrow (5m). Same predicate, same timeout, plus the budget string each already wrote in its navigate() call — the shape this bead enumerated. THE SEAM WITH rf2-f5roa WAS CHECKED AND NOT CROSSED: that bead is CLOSED; it BUILT sentinel.cjs and its race and applied it to hd8_run.cjs and p0_converge_run.cjs after two merged-PR audits found a pageerror costing twenty minutes in each. It never reached these nine. This applies its remedy where it never landed. THE REJECTION PATHS WERE WATCHED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, as this bead asked: b6_prod / b6_profile / b10_prod route into drive()'s existing named rejection handler (verified by reading each: `console.error('[bXX] FAILED: ...'); process.exit(1)`); b7, p0, the ladder and the ablation into their existing catch; b8 into `failed`; hicasso_narrow into main()'s catch. Every one is that driver's EXISTING 1 — NO NEW EXIT CODE anywhere, and the ladder's enumerated [3,4,2,5], b7's 2, b8's 2/3 and hicasso_narrow's 2/3/4 are untouched (heap_control_exit_path.test.cjs passes UNMODIFIED). IT CANNOT SHORTEN A RUN THAT WOULD HAVE PASSED, which was the bead's one hard constraint: `race` rejects only on a failure watchPage recorded, and since rf2-sib23 every one of the nine already refuses at its exit on exactly that array — so any run reported early was already going to be non-zero. What changes is WHEN, and that the line names the cause instead of naming the clock. WATCHED FIRING LIVE, unplanned: reads_ladder_run.cjs hit a real pageerror during this work (a contaminated shared shadow cache — filed as rf2-t4j7c) and printed `[ladder] THE PAGE DIED BEFORE IT FINISHED ... This is reported now rather than after the 120s wait for window.LADDER_READY (uix), which had not yet run out and would have said only that time passed (rf2-f5roa)`, exit 1. The same command on a cleared cache gave `[ladder] done`, exit 0. Also exercised end to end: b7 --only mount-frame (0 and 1), p0 --only heap (0 and 1), spine_ablation (passed the raced ABL_READY wait normally and refused with its own existing 4). WHAT IT COSTS, recorded rather than left to be discovered: in rf2-sib23's own case — the page that throws and STILL reaches its sentinel — the run now fails AT THE WAIT rather than after printing its table, so a LATE throw's partial rows are no longer printed. The verdict is identical either way (that driver's 1, naming the page error); what is lost is diagnostic residue in the narrow window between "some rows measured" and "sentinel set". The motivating case in both beads is a ReferenceError at page load, where there is no residue to lose and up to thirty minutes to save. The exit-block refusals rf2-sib23 installed are NOT removed and are NOT dead — a failure recorded after the sentinel has flipped (during the result evaluates, the measurement loop that follows a READY wait, or teardown) still reaches the exit block and nowhere else, which is how both probe runs above refused. sentinel.cjs's header carries all of this. NEW CLASS PIN in pageerror_exit_path.test.cjs, DERIVED rather than listed: no driver holding the shared collector may wait on a bare page.waitForFunction, plus its inverse (each of the nine must race something, with a NAMED budget) so deleting a wait cannot satisfy it vacuously. It deliberately says nothing about the five hicasso drivers that collect into a local array and wait bare — a different and older shape, not this bead. 48 checks -> 54. No measurement, arm, threshold, knob default or dataset touched.

comments.text:
DESIGN SYNTHESIS (2026-08-05; design + adversarial review complete; attack 1 FATAL / 3 MAJOR / 5 MINOR — the FATAL corrected the design's premise and STRENGTHENED its verdict). VERDICT: BUILD (a) — (h/frame) — from the corrected premise. MAYOR-DISPATCHABLE from this comment. Full record: ai/findings/2026-08-05.hframe-design.md + hframe-attack.md (local-only; this comment is self-sufficient).

THE CORRECTED PREMISE (the attack's F1, verified file:line): the platform keystone rf/capture-frame (core.cljc:1452; spec/002:1421 "the ONE public carry primitive") does NOT throw in Hicasso bodies today — it ACCIDENTALLY WORKS on the dominant configurations: Hicasso mounts the shared adapter-context Provider regardless (arm1/mount.cljs:46,:96-97), and make-react-adapter routes :adapter/current-frame to a raw context _currentValue read (spine.cljs:3233-3235; context.cljs:337-339), published by the UIx and Freehand adapters. ONE SPELLING, SIX BEHAVIOURS: works-correct (UIx/Freehand/plain-atom+ui browser), throws (ratom family, test-react, none), THROWS ON SSR (_currentValue is client-renderer-only, context.cljs:330-335), and sentinel-throw or SILENT WRONG-FRAME inside .74 render callbacks (the ambient chain answers the INVOKING render's context; the arming gate rebinds intent/*frame* to the owner — intent.cljs:424-425,:457). The door is not missing; it is accidental, config-dependent, server-broken, and wrong-frame-capable. A documented nondeterministic keystone is a worse artefact than the ten-line fn that removes the nondeterminism.

title: hicasso: HD-016's 'callback refs only' is UNENFORCED against object refs — check-ref! refuses only the reserved vector
description:
FOUND while writing raw-escape design C (rf2-2rtt6.103), designing the [:>] crossing's ref boundary.

THE RULE AS WRITTEN. HD-016 (decisions.md ~:513) rules ':ref is legal on native tags and defhost/[:>] crossings (CALLBACK REFS ONLY)'. rf2-2rtt6.103's clause 3 restates it. The guide's ABI table (02-views-and-reads.md:78) says 'callback ref, legal'.

THE RULE AS ENFORCED. front/codec.cljs check-ref! is a WHEN, not a cond:

    [k v]
    (when (vector? v)
      (fail! :rf.error/hicasso-ref-vector-reserved ...))
    v

It refuses exactly ONE shape — a VECTOR, which is HD-022's reserved data spelling ({:ref [registered-id config]}) — and passes EVERYTHING else through: a function, nil, a string, and an OBJECT ref. React 19 carries ref as an ordinary prop, so (react/createRef) works fine at a native tag and at a defhost crossing today.

SO 'callback refs only' is a documented rule with no mechanism behind it. A Reagent migrant's object ref will simply work, and the guide says it should not.

EITHER the rule is narrower than it reads — the real rule being 'the reserved VECTOR spelling is not a v0 surface', with object refs an untaught-but-tolerated React fact — OR the check is narrower than the rule and object refs should refuse with a named error.

DESIGN C'S POSITION (recorded, not ruling): do NOT add a refusal at [:>] that defhost does not have. Conversion parity across the two crossing forms is HD-011's ruling, and a rule enforced at one crossing and not the other is worse than a rule enforced at neither. Whatever is decided applies to BOTH, and to native tags.

CHEAP EITHER WAY: one cond arm in check-ref!, or one clause edit in HD-016 plus the guide's ABI table.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7503 (merged 2026-08-04T19:03:47Z, bb942a8c0dbc1141bf037235cba75b93eed2567f) — VERIFIED COMPLETE AS A RECORD. The dated HD-016 note and authoring/interop/spec text now make object refs untaught-but-legal, while the witness pins identity at native and defhost crossings and preserves the reserved-vector refusal. `npm run test:freehand --silent` passed 1,399 tests / 7,753 assertions, and every required merged-commit check passed. Close this exact owner as delivered.
SETTLED in PR #7503 (2026-08-05) as A RECORD, not a refusal -- the bead first horn: THE RULE IS NARROWER THAN IT READS, not the check.

THE ARGUMENT. HD-016 clause reads as a prohibition ("callback refs only"). HD-022 -- LATER, and the ruling actually about :ref value space -- says in as many words: "That is the whole ruling: one refusal branch and one error id." check-ref! is therefore exactly what HD-022 ruled, not a check that fell short of it. Later and more specific governs.

WHAT THAT MAKES AN OBJECT REF: untaught, not illegal. React 19 carries ref as an ordinary prop, so (react/createRef) attaches and detaches exactly as React documents, at a native tag and at a defhost crossing alike. Verified end to end: check-ref! passes it, then convert-prop-value :else (a plain JS object is not map?/coll?) and host-prop-value :else both cross it by identity. NOTHING IS SILENTLY DROPPED AND NOTHING NEEDS REPAIRING -- which is the whole argument against a branch. Refusing a spelling that works correctly is friction rather than safety, and the guide teaching the callback form (React 19 makes attach and teardown structural there) is an ergonomic recommendation the codec has no business policing.

DESIGN C PARITY RULE IS SATISFIED FOR FREE. Whatever is decided applies to both crossing forms and to native tags; doing nothing IS parity. No refusal was added at [:>] that defhost lacks, exactly as design C directs. raw-escape-spec.md sec.8 item 5 now records the outcome as the one it asked for.

SHIPPED: a dated 2026-08-05 note on HD-016 (the repo own amendment form, ruling text left intact) stating the enforced-vs-taught distinction and the HD-022 precedence; authoring.md and draft-guide/05-interop.md true-ed up to say what is ENFORCED (the vector, and only the vector); and -- the part that makes this a decision rather than an oversight -- an executable witness, front/codec_cljs_test/an-object-ref-crosses-by-identity-at-both-positions, covering native + defhost and an alternate ref spelling at each.

MUTATION PROOF THAT DOUBLES AS EVIDENCE FOR THE BEAD OWN CLAIM: adding an object-ref refusal to check-ref! produced 4 errors, ALL in the new witness, and NOTHING ELSE IN 12,585 TESTS MOVED. That is the bead "a documented rule with no mechanism behind it", measured -- the behaviour was pinned nowhere in the suite before this. It is pinned now, so a later refusal cannot land silently: it has to delete those rows first.

title: AUDIT: nine bench drivers print an uncaught page error and exit 0 — is any throw path reachable without the sentinel?
description:
FOUND by rf2-y7mw7's sibling sweep, 2026-08-04. FILED AS AN AUDIT, NOT A
CONFIRMED FAULT — the sweep could name the shape but could not prove it live
without reading the bundles' throw paths, and that is stated here so nobody
banks it as reproduced.

THE SHAPE. Nine drivers install a bare pageerror handler that prints and
records nothing:

    page.on('pageerror', (e) => console.error(`[b8] page error: ${e.message}`))

with no array, no sentinel, and no reference from the exit block:

  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b6_prod_run.cjs ~90
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b6_profile_run.cjs ~96
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b7_run.cjs ~190
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b8_run.cjs ~185
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b10_prod_run.cjs ~123
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/reads_ladder_run.cjs ~200
  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/spine_ablation_run.cjs ~222
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs ~383
  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso_narrow_run.cjs ~317

THE ADJACENT TREE DISAGREES, in writing. run.cjs ~34, clock_run.cjs ~124,
coldmount_run.cjs ~41, p0_converge_run.cjs ~59, z3vlz_run.cjs ~26 and
adoption_witness_run.cjs ~56 all treat the same event as fatal, collect it
into an array and refuse — and sentinel.cjs ~49-51 states the rule: "A
benchmark that threw and kept going publishes a precise number for a page
that is not the page under test."

WHY IT MAY NOT BITE. Each of the nine also waits on
`waitForFunction('... || window.X_ERROR')`, which covers every throw the app
itself catches and reports. The gap is only a throw that reaches Chromium's
pageerror WITHOUT setting the corresponding window.*_ERROR — a React render
throw, or a rejection inside an unwrapped rAF.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and it is a morning's reading: the -main / entry catch
in b8_app, b7_app, p0_app, b6_prod_app, b10_prod_app and the HN bundle. If
any throw path can reach pageerror without the sentinel, the nine are
fail-open and should collect-and-refuse like their neighbours. If none can,
the nine should still say so in a header comment, because the next reader
will ask this question again.

DO NOT WEAKEN ANYTHING TO CLOSE THIS. The remedy, if it is one, is
collect-into-an-array-and-refuse, matching the hicasso tree — not removing
the handler and not relaxing a sentinel.
notes:
SEQUENCING NOTE (mayor, 2026-08-04) — HELD BEHIND PR #7489, AND THESE TWO BEADS SHOULD PROBABLY BE ONE DISPATCH.

WHY HELD: PR #7489 (rf2-y7mw7, the clock driver's adjudication fail-open) is open and edits implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/clock_run.cjs. BOTH rf2-x6g04 and rf2-jvheq name clock_run.cjs in their own file lists. Dispatching either now puts two workers on one file, which is the collision the hot-zone rule exists to prevent.

WHY THEY ARE PLAUSIBLY ONE PIECE OF WORK: their rosters overlap by eight drivers - adoption_witness_run.cjs, b7_run.cjs, clock_run.cjs, coldmount_run.cjs, p0_converge_run.cjs, p0_run.cjs, reads_ladder_run.cjs, spine_ablation_run.cjs. Between them they name roughly sixteen distinct bench drivers. Two workers sweeping overlapping halves of one fleet will conflict on the intersection and will each have to reason about the same shared shape.

THE CLASS, which is the thing worth seeing: this is now the THIRD fail-open found in the bench-driver fleet today. rf2-y7mw7 (a row whose every bar reads UNADJUDICATED still exits 0, found by the quiet-window worker while measuring), rf2-x6g04 (a failed DOM read-back and a REFUSED yield correction still exit 0), and rf2-jvheq (nine drivers print an uncaught page error and exit 0). Each was found independently, by a different worker, in a different driver. That is the signature of a COPIED SHAPE rather than three coincidences - the same eight-or-so lines of exit handling replicated across the fleet, exactly as rf2-2rtt6.73 found eleven drivers carrying one copied fail-open earlier in this programme.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: these drivers produce the evidence a graduation decision reads. A driver that exits 0 while its own output says REFUSED or UNADJUDICATED does not merely fail to catch a defect - it publishes a green that a future reader will bank. The quiet window was saved from exactly this only because a second row happened to share the invocation.

DISPATCH SHAPE WHEN #7489 LANDS: one worker, both beads, reading #7489's landed fix FIRST so the fleet converges on one exit-handling shape rather than three. Require the sibling sweep to be derived (grep the pattern across every driver) rather than taken from either bead's list, since the two lists already disagree about which drivers are affected - and neither may be complete.
AUDIT SETTLED in PR #7494, 2026-08-04 — and the answer is POSITIVE. All nine are
fail-open. Settled by RUNNING it, not by reading, which is what the bead said
was missing.

THE THREE-WAY SPLIT:
  demonstrated-live        9 of 9
  structurally-impossible  0
  could-not-determine      0

TWO INDEPENDENT MECHANISMS, both measured against this repo's own pins:

1. Playwright 1.59.1 raises pageerror for a throw inside requestAnimationFrame,
   a throw inside setTimeout, AND an unhandled promise rejection — while a
   completion sentinel set elsewhere STILL becomes true. All three exit 0.

2. THE ONE THAT MATTERS, and it defeats the mitigation this bead hoped for.
   The bead reasoned the gap was only 'a throw that reaches pageerror WITHOUT
   setting window.*_ERROR'. React 19.2.0 makes that the COMMON case, not the
   exotic one: defaultOnUncaughtError hands an uncaught render error to
   reportGlobalError -> reportError (react-dom-client.production.js ~5888-5890,
   ~2307) instead of rethrowing. Measured live: pageerror fires, THE
   SURROUNDING CATCH NEVER RUNS, no window.*_ERROR is set, the driving
   page.evaluate does not reject, and the app carries on and sets its
   sentinel. All nine mount through react-dom/flushSync. Adding catch :default
   to the apps would NOT close this.

3. b10_prod_run.cjs has a second, non-React path and is the worst of the nine:
   b10_two_clock.cljs ~670/694/709 drives the run from two setIntervals and a
   live MutationObserver — detached tasks escaping both -main's try and the
   chain's .catch. setInterval keeps firing, so the run COMPLETES and sets
   B10_DONE.

THE ROSTER WAS CORRECT: the nine bare handlers are exactly the nine named
here, line numbers included.

NO GATE SHIPPED, DELIBERATELY. Each of the nine needs an :advanced release
build and a headless Chromium to make its refusal fire, and a gate nobody has
watched fire is not a gate; nine unproven exit wirings would be this same
fault in reverse. The finding is recorded in sentinel.cjs — the file that
already states the policy — so the next reader does not re-derive it, which is
the header-comment obligation this bead set for the negative case, honoured
for the positive one.

REMEDIATION TRACKED AS rf2-sib23 (P1, bug), with the evidence and a scope note
(none of the nine is in CI, so the blast radius is an operator investigating).
Closing this bead as the AUDIT it was filed as: the question is answered.
MAYOR CORRECTION 2026-08-04: MY "COPIED SHAPE ACROSS THE FLEET" FRAMING WAS WRONG, AND SO WAS THIS BEAD'S. Measured by the sweep worker across the whole lane; recording it because the wrong framing invites a fleet-wide refactor nobody needs.

WHAT I SAID: three fail-opens found by three different workers in three different drivers "is the signature of a copied shape, not three coincidences", and I put roughly sixteen drivers in the affected set. This bead's own framing called its defect "a third instance of the same shape".

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, from a derived census of all 23 tracked *run.cjs (48 .cjs total) rather than from either bead's list: THE LANE PARTITIONS CLEANLY - 1 defective, 5 correct watchPage callers, 9 bare handlers, 7 already collect-and-refuse. hd8_run.cjs is THE ONLY ONE of the six watchPage callers that never read .failures; the other five read them AND reach an exit. So there is no widely-copied fail-open in the watchPage family. There is ONE defective driver, now fixed.

The nine-driver pageerror class (rf2-jvheq) is REAL and SEPARATE, and its audit came back POSITIVE rather than speculative: nine demonstrated-live, zero structurally-impossible, zero could-not-determine, SETTLED BY RUNNING IT rather than by reading. Its mechanism is not a copied mistake either - React 19.2's defaultOnUncaughtError routes through reportGlobalError to reportError INSTEAD OF RETHROWING, so a page-side try/catch cannot see it; measured live, pageerror fires, the surrounding catch never runs, and the app carries on to READY. All nine mount through flushSync, so it is NOT closeable inside the apps.

WHY THE DISTINCTION MATTERS: "sixteen drivers share a copied fail-open" argues for a shared exit-handling framework. "One driver was defective and nine are defeated by a React behaviour they cannot catch" argues for exactly what shipped - a narrow fix in the one driver, no framework, and the nine recorded once in sentinel.cjs where the policy already lives rather than in nine drifting copies. The worker declined to ship nine unproven gate wirings on the ground that "nine unproven wirings would be this same fault in reverse", which is the right call and the reason rf2-sib23 exists instead.

GENERAL LESSON FOR ME: I inferred a class from three independent sightings and stated it as a signature. Three sightings are a reason to COUNT, not a count. The instruction that produced the truth here was "derive the roster, do not take it from either bead" - and what it found was that both beads' rosters were wrong in opposite directions, one overstating the family and the other exactly right about its nine.

title: Xray full feature-matrix: new non-smoke scenarios merge unrun (policy call)
description:
SPUN OFF from rf2-9n2cv, which fixed the named defect (test:story-static) and deliberately did NOT fix this one, because it is a different shape.

NOT the rf2-65ajl / rf2-9n2cv defect. Those were 'the file that DEFINES a command is classified to no job that RUNS that command' — the file was never loaded at PR time at all. That is not true here: 'npm run test:xray-feature-gate:smoke', a command the story-xray-browser PR job already runs, require's the WHOLE of tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs. The file is loaded, parsed and validated on every PR that touches it, and the launcher fails loud if the smoke set is ever empty. A malformed or unparseable scenarios.cjs cannot merge.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNCOVERED: the non-smoke ROWS are not EXECUTED at PR time. A new scenario added without 'smoke: true' merges having never run. Its first execution is the nightly sweep.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN rf2-9n2cv: that is the documented two-tier policy, not a fail-open instrument. TESTING.md states it outright — tag a scenario 'smoke: true' only if it earns a slot on every PR AND loads an already-staged smoke surface; 'everything else is nightly by default'. Closing this gap means running the all-scenarios/all-surfaces sweep on every scenarios.cjs edit, which reverses a deliberate cost decision. That deserves its own ruling rather than being smuggled into a bug fix.

THE QUESTION TO DECIDE: is 'a new non-smoke scenario merges unrun' acceptable? Options, cheapest first:
  (1) WONTFIX — the nightly sweep is the system of record; a scenario that has never run is no worse than one whose surface regressed overnight, and the author can run the gate locally.
  (2) Run ONLY THE ADDED/CHANGED ROWS at PR time — needs a way to select scenarios by diff, plus staging only the surfaces those rows load. Most signal per second, most machinery.
  (3) Arm the FULL gate on scenarios.cjs changes — trivial to implement (one classifier arm + one conditional step, exactly the rf2-9n2cv shape), but pays the whole nightly matrix for any edit to the file, including a one-word rename.

SURFACES if actioned: .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh, .github/workflows/test.yml (HOT-ZONE), implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs, TESTING.md.

NOTE the current pin: _changed-surfaces.test.cjs asserts doesNotMatch(block, /npm run test:xray-feature-gate(?!:smoke)/) in 'PR story-xray-browser job still keeps the rest of the sweep nightly'. rf2-9n2cv kept that pin deliberately and annotated it with this reasoning. Options (2) and (3) both require changing it — change it deliberately and mutation-prove the replacement.
close_reason: WONTFIX by delegated ruling 2026-08-05 (see ruling comment): two-tier policy stands, nightly is the system of record for non-smoke rows. Docs rider filed as follow-up P4; re-open trigger = 3 never-run-scenario nightly reds in a rolling month.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: RULING 2026-08-05 19:59 AUSEST (delegated review, operator-overturnable): Option (1) WONTFIX. The two-tier policy stands; a new non-smoke scenario may merge having never executed, and the nightly sweep remains its system of record. VERIFIED: (a) TESTING.md already documents this deliberately — the para after the two rf2-65ajl/rf2-9n2cv exceptions says the Xray full matrix is 'deliberately not a third such exception ... policy working as designed rather than a hole in it; everything else is nightly by default'. (b) The pin stays: _changed-surfaces.test.cjs 'PR story-xray-browser job still keeps the rest of the sweep nightly (rf2-wa3oo)' asserts doesNotMatch /npm run test:xray-feature-gate(?!:smoke)/, annotated with rf2-9n2cv's reasoning; (2)/(3) would require a deliberate, mutation-proved replacement of it. (c) LAUNCHER HAS NO PER-ROW FILTER: serve-and-run-xray-feature-gate.cjs selects via SMOKE = RF2_GATE_SMOKE=1 or --smoke, else ALL scenarios (ACTIVE_SCENARIOS = SMOKE ? filter smoke:true : SCENARIOS). No --only/name filter exists, so the dossier MAIN rec's 'npm run test:xray-feature-gate -- --only <id>' spelling is WRONG; the correct local-run line is: cd implementation && npm run test:xray-feature-gate (full sweep, ~3min scenario time + compile). WHY (1): non-smoke rows are by construction lower-stakes; the matrix gates features not releases; the failure mode is a cold-context nightly red, not a shipped defect; (2) is hot-zone machinery for a convenience, (3) reverses the recorded cost decision for any one-word edit. Codex census: recent nightly Xray reds were repeat failures of the EXISTING 'static mode chrome and chord' scenario, not never-run new rows — no present evidence for (2)/(3). DOCS RIDER: one taught line in TESTING.md (follow-up bead filed; no open TESTING.md carrier exists): before merging a new or materially changed non-smoke scenario, run the full gate locally — cd implementation && npm run test:xray-feature-gate — and say so in the PR. NAMED RE-OPEN TRIGGER: three nightly reds in any rolling month attributable to never-run (new or materially changed) non-smoke scenarios re-opens this bead as evidence. Graduated response on re-open: FIRST an author-facing local scenario selector on the launcher (e.g. --only <name>), NOT diff-driven CI selection; escalate to (2) only if manual selection itself proves to be the problem.

title: eslint lints the gitignored .shadow-cljs build output, so npm run lint:js exits 1 after any local :advanced build
description:
After any local :advanced build (e.g. a hicasso bench driver, which builds into implementation/.shadow-cljs/builds/<id>/release/), `npm run lint:js` from the repo root reports ~587 errors from implementation/.shadow-cljs/builds/*/release/externs.shadow.js and exits 1.

Reproduced 2026-08-04 on worker/clockerr-029ed: HCLOCK_ONLY=M1 node .../clock_run.cjs, then npm run lint:js -> 590 problems (587 errors), every error in externs.shadow.js (no-unused-vars on AbortController/Map/NaN/..., no-shadow-restricted-names on NaN/globalThis). Deleting implementation/.shadow-cljs/builds/hicasso-bench/release and re-running -> exit 0.

implementation/.gitignore line 2 already ignores .shadow-cljs/, so this is generated output that is not source. eslint's ignore config does not exclude it. CI never sees it because a fresh checkout has no .shadow-cljs, so the gate is green there and red only locally — which is the wrong way round: it trains a developer to disbelieve their own lint run.

Fix: add .shadow-cljs/ (and any other generated build output) to the eslint ignores alongside the existing ones. Small.

Found while fixing rf2-029ed; not caused by it.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #7460 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7460).

ROOT CAUSE, beyond the missing entry: eslint.config.mjs's ignore block asserted that 'node_modules and dotted directories are ESLint defaults'. Flat config ignores exactly two paths of its own accord — **/node_modules/ and .git/ (eslint/lib/config/default-config.js:68, ESLint 10.8.0). Dot-directories in general were the OLD .eslintrc behaviour. That belief is why .shadow-cljs/ was never listed, so the comment was corrected, not merely extended — otherwise the next generated dot-directory gets omitted the same way.

COVERED, derived from the repo's own fourteen .gitignore files and narrowed to trees that can carry JS:
  **/.shadow-cljs/**           8811 JS files in a fully built checkout (vs 215 tracked JS files in the whole repo)
  **/resources/public/js/**    shadow-cljs :output-dir (minimal-counter example + tools/template scaffold)
  **/public/js/compiled/**     shadow-cljs :output-dir (skills/re-frame2-pair)
  .claude/worktrees/**         whole second copies of the source tree
  examples/.edge-cdp/**        Chrome user-data-dir from the CDP runs

NOT added, each checked rather than assumed: .cpcache/ (34 dirs in a built checkout, zero JS), __pycache__/, .dolt/, .scratch/ (EDN/CLJS fixtures), docs/{spec,migration}/ (staged copies of markdown-only trees).

MUTATION PROOF, both directions:
  - With real :advanced output present: before exit 1 / 542 errors, after exit 0. Then the stronger version — scripts/test-fast-pr.sh itself compiles and leaves 2685 generated JS files, and lint:js is exit 0 afterwards; the old config would have put 161 extra generated files in scope. Running the repo's own canonical local gate is by itself enough to arm this defect.
  - Fail-open check: file census before/after is 307 -> 214 inspected, ALL of the loss under .shadow-cljs (93 -> 0); implementation/ 233 -> 140 and tools/51, examples/13, docs/6, testbeds/2, scripts/1 all unchanged. 214 matches the tracked-file census exactly. A live no-undef + no-unused-vars injected into two real tracked files (one under implementation/, one under examples/) still exits 1 naming both, with build output present; reverted byte-identically (sha256sum -c OK, git diff clean).

No rule was touched, relaxed or disabled, and no suppression comment was added — the fix is what gets linted, not which rules apply.

Gates: npm run lint:js (root, CI form) exit 0; sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0, terminal marker 'PASS fast PR spine' present.

Filed rf2-o4ohg (P4) for three pre-existing dead eslint-disable directives in adoption_witness_run.cjs — warnings only, non-blocking, untouched by this PR.

WHY IT IS WORTH A LOOK. rf2-dabt3's fusion banked -60 B/read in both segments — real, and it won — but that is only ~40% of the ~151 B/read the old reverse edge cost, because the replacement array is ~2x what ONE PersistentHashSet membership costs (+46/+47 B/read, PR #7418 run D). The design predicted the surviving array would be cheap residue; it is not. It is now the largest single term this page has attributed to a CONTAINER rather than to a value.

THE OBVIOUS SHAPE, and it is only a sketch. At the fan-out this table actually sees, the overwhelmingly common case is ONE reader per key. A scalar slot that holds the single reader directly and promotes to an array on the SECOND reader would retain a pointer instead of a JSArray-plus-backing-store for that case. arm1/runtime.cljs's own section header already argues a JS array beats a persistent set here; this asks the next question down, which is whether a container is needed at all in the common case.

THIS IS NOT A DISPATCH. It wants a ruling first, for three reasons:
• release-cell!'s .indexOf, arm-cell-reaper!'s alength and stats's alength all read .-readers directly, and cell-readers/stats are witness surfaces the six laws and the ladder's structural gate are written against — a polymorphic slot touches all of them.
• It is a byte shave on a pre-alpha arm, and the stance is explicit that not every measured term needs actioning.
• The bill it would attack is +331 B/read against Reagent; 91 of that is this term. Worth knowing the size before deciding it is worth the branch in a hot path.

Precondition if it is ever taken: a quiet box, p0_run.cjs --only ladder 6 rounds with both donors as same-run controls, and the same ablation discipline rf2-zei9w used — attribute, do not infer.
notes: PARKED, not ready — restoring the 2026-08-04 ruling to the tracker (triage 2026-08-07). Ruled parked with an explicit build trigger and zero customers; it remained in 'bd ready' regardless. Deferred so the ready queue reflects the ruling. Un-defer when its recorded trigger fires.
