title: bench: three instrument gates are documented or implied but never COMPUTED — the inverse of rf2-rr6do
description:
FOUND by the rf2-rr6do sweep (PR #7450) while classifying every bench runner condition-by-condition. These are NOT the rf2-rr6do defect class — no refusal is computed and left unread — they are its INVERSE: a gate the file promises, or that every sibling has, which is never computed at all. A gate that does not exist cannot be seen to fail, which is why the sweep for printed-but-unread refusals walked straight past them.

1. implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/inpage_ladder_aggregate.cjs
   Its own header (:15-16) states it exits 1 on 'a run that recorded a guard refusal or a failed control'. Nothing in the file reads any guard-refusal or control field out of the EDN datasets it aggregates; the only exit is the 'problems' array (:166-169), which reproduces the published aggregates and nothing else. An unimplemented header promise, the same shape as census_clock_run.cjs's P4 that #7450 repaired — except here there is no computed value to gate, so the repair is to compute one.

2. implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b7_run.cjs :496-509
   implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/reads_ladder_run.cjs :609-617
   Both print an in-situ positive control — predicted vs measured, error % — with NO pass/fail computed at all. Their siblings do compute one: p0_run.cjs gates control.verdict.ok on all four rows (:1309/:1326/:1341/:1364) and spine_ablation_run.cjs collects gateFailures (:561-563). A control printed without a verdict is a number beside a number.

3. implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/p0_converge_run.cjs
   Reads four page flags (pageErrors, refused, controlFailed, orderRefused, :229-233) but NOT window.HICASSO_CLAIM_FAILED, which its near-sibling coldmount_run.cjs reads at :169 and exits 4 on. Only a real gap if the converge page ever sets that flag — CHECK THE PAGE FIRST; if it does not, close this arm as moot rather than adding a read of a flag nothing raises.

ACTIONABLE, but each needs a judgement before code: whether the promise in (1) should be implemented or withdrawn from the header, and whether (2) should adopt a control verdict or state in-file why these two rows are printed-only. Neither is a fail-open of an EXISTING gate, so neither is urgent.

TAKE NO MEASUREMENTS. Any repair here is exit-path only; no timing or allocation row may be published or amended. If a change implies a re-measurement, file it separately with the quiet-box precondition (see rf2-0qj9w / rf2-zei9w / rf2-t0j8b for the established wording).

title: hicasso: defhost's macro docstring teaches ::h/value at react-datepicker's value-first onChange
description:
The `defhost` macro docstring in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/lang.clj (lines 71-80) carries this worked example:

    (defhost date-picker DatePicker
      {:callbacks {:on-change :event}})

    [date-picker {:selected  due-date
                  :on-change [:task/set-due ::h/value]}]

It names date-picker/DatePicker — the exact pair the draft guide's interop opening uses for react-datepicker — and puts a ::h/value-carrying intent vector at :on-change. react-datepicker's onChange is VALUE-first (onChange(date)), so under HD-024's landed event-first law (front/intent.cljs event-arg!) that call raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-needs-the-event. The guide (docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/05-interop.md) teaches the h/fn spelling there for exactly this reason, so a reader who checks the macro against the guide finds the two contradicting each other on the same component.

The docstring is not wrong about the GRAMMAR — ::h/value at a declared :event slot is correct whenever the foreign invoker is event-first — so the fix is to stop naming a value-first library. Either rename the example component to an event-first one (the host-hatch witness's onDraft shape), or keep date-picker and switch the call site to the h/fn the guide teaches.

Found while landing rf2-2rtt6.64; not fixed there because that bead's surface is docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/** and implementation/** was fenced.
close_reason: PR #7447 — defhost's docstring example switched from [:task/set-due ::h/value] at react-datepicker's value-first onChange to (hfn [date & _] [:task/set-due date]), the spelling HD-024's landed argument law requires there; one paragraph added saying why, keeping the grammar half (a marker at a declared :event slot is correct at an event-first invoker). Route: kept date-picker/DatePicker so the macro and the guide's interop opening now teach the same real component the same way — the alternative would have needed an invented event-first library the reader cannot verify. Sweep: exactly ONE site in the repo taught marker-at-a-value-first-invoker (this one); every other ::h/value site is a native DOM position, the event-first :on-draft host callback, or a deliberate refusal witness, and Freehand's v/defhost date-picker examples already spell it (v/event [js-date] …). Witnessed by the-declaration-governs-every-carrier-at-its-position (h/fn at declared :event, invoked value-first, dispatches) and callbacks-cross-out-and-react-owned-state-survives-hicasso-rerenders. No lowering behaviour changed. Gates: test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 with PASS fast PR spine; test:hicasso-compile exit 0.

title: ci: a CANCELLED check fails the aggregate gate, and cancellations are hitting PRs that cannot violate the check
description:
OBSERVED by the mayor across three consecutive merges on 2026-08-03.

THE SYMPTOM. 'Beads PR boundary (no tracker database in a PR)' came back with conclusion CANCELLED on PR #7440 and again on PR #7442. A cancelled required check makes the aggregate 'All required checks passed' report FAILURE, so the PR reads red and cannot merge, even though nothing actually failed.

WHY IT IS SPURIOUS IN BOTH CASES, verified per PR rather than assumed:
  • #7440 changed 8 files (spine.cljs, react_shared_suite.cljs, two studio pages, spec/006, uix dom test, coldmount app/run). NO .beads path.
  • #7442 changed exactly ONE file: docs/design/freehand/studio/fitness-harness.md. NO .beads path.
In both, the gate's own subject is absent from the diff, so it had nothing it could legitimately fail on. In both, a fresh run of the workflow cleared it with no code change.

THE COST. Each occurrence blocks a merge until someone notices the conclusion is CANCELLED rather than FAILURE, verifies the diff cannot violate the gate, and re-runs. That is a judgement call every time, and the failure mode it invites is worse than the delay: a mayor who learns to wave away 'that check is always spurious' will one day wave away a real violation. A gate that cries wolf is a gate that stops being read.

WHAT IS NOT YET ESTABLISHED — do not assume causation. A plausible mechanism is a concurrency group: the mayor pushes a .beads checkpoint to main every ~11 minutes, and if PR runs share a concurrency group with push-to-main runs, a checkpoint push would cancel in-flight PR jobs. Evidence is suggestive but thin: 'gh run list --workflow=test.yml --limit 12' showed exactly one cancelled run in that window and it was event=push on branch=main, not a PR run. So the cancellations may have a different cause. ESTABLISH THE MECHANISM BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING.

DO:
  1. Read .github/workflows/*.yml for concurrency: blocks — which workflows share a group, and whether the group key distinguishes PR head from main.
  2. If a push-to-main run can cancel an in-flight PR run, fix the group key so it cannot (a per-ref key is the usual shape). Keep it minimal.
  3. Independently of the cause: consider whether the aggregate 'All required checks passed' job should treat CANCELLED distinctly from FAILURE, so a cancelled job reads as 'incomplete, re-run' rather than 'failed'. That is the part that turns a transient into a false red.
  4. Do NOT weaken the beads-boundary gate itself — it is load-bearing (a tracker database in a PR time-travels the tracker) and it is not the thing at fault here.

FENCE: .github/workflows/** is HOT-ZONE, sequential-only. Keep the edit surgical and say so in the PR body. Mutation-prove whatever you change: demonstrate the cancellation path before and after, or state honestly that it could not be reproduced.
notes:
MAYOR CORRECTION 2026-08-03 — the leading hypothesis in the description (a push-to-main run cancelling PR runs) is probably WRONG, and the likeliest cause is the mayor's own repeated re-runs. Evidence, from .github/workflows/test.yml:16-18:

  concurrency:
    group: tests-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
    cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

For a pull_request event every run joins group tests-<PR number> with cancel-in-progress TRUE. So a SECOND run in that group cancels the first. On both #7440 and #7442 the mayor called 'gh run rerun' on consecutive ~11-minute ticks while the previous attempt was still queued or running — each new attempt would cancel its predecessor, producing exactly the observed queued -> cancelled -> 'cannot be rerun; already running' -> cancelled cycle. The mayor was cancelling the job it was trying to rescue.

WHAT THIS CHANGES:
• Re-running is the correct remedy for a genuinely cancelled check, but it must be done ONCE and then left alone. Do not re-run on a cadence; a loop that re-runs every tick can never let the job finish.
• The push-to-main theory should not be assumed. Note the group key already distinguishes PR from non-PR (it falls back to github.run_id, which is unique per run, so push runs cannot collide with each other or with PR runs). That is evidence AGAINST the original hypothesis.
• The item that still stands on its own merits is #3 in the DO list: the aggregate 'All required checks passed' job treats CANCELLED as FAILURE. Whatever cancels a job — a rescue attempt, a superseding push, an infra blip — the aggregate turning that into a red PR is what makes a transient look like a defect. Distinguishing 'incomplete, re-run' from 'failed' is the durable fix and does not depend on the cause.
• Items 1-2 (audit concurrency groups) are now LOW VALUE unless a cancellation is observed with no concurrent re-run in play. Do not spend a worker on them speculatively.

METHOD NOTE worth keeping: this is the same family as the day's other findings — an instrument (here, the rescue action) interfering with the subject it was measuring. The tell was 'gh run rerun' reporting 'cannot be rerun; This workflow is already running' and the run then reading cancelled a tick later.
close_reason: PR #7448, item 3 of the DO list ONLY — items 1-2 (concurrency-group audit) skipped per the mayor's correction note that ruled them low-value. The aggregate 'All required checks passed' now adjudicates CANCELLED separately from FAILURE, failure arm first, and the cancelled message names the trap: for pull_request events test.yml's group is cancel-in-progress, so re-run ONCE and leave it alone. BOTH STILL BLOCK — the gate's pass/fail behaviour does not move on any input; only the words change. Verified by simulating every result spread against the committed steps parsed out of the YAML (if: expressions and exit codes read from the file, not hardcoded), before and after: identical verdict in all five cases. Shell bodies extracted and executed: sh -n clean on all three steps, both blocking steps exit 1, the pass step exits 0. HONEST GAP: I could not contrive a real GitHub-side cancellation — inducing one via a superseding push cancels the whole run including this always() job, which is not the observed shape. I did not manufacture a reproduction. NEW FAIL-OPEN INTRODUCED AND PINNED: splitting one blocking step into two means deleting the cancelled arm would let a cancelled required job read green silently (demonstrated — every cancelled spread flips to PASSING). _changed-surfaces.test.cjs now pins both arms with their own exit 1 in that order; mutation-proved by deleting the arm (red) and by reversing the two (red), test.yml restored byte-identically. THE BEADS-BOUNDARY GATE IS UNTOUCHED and is no weaker — job, script and needs: position all unchanged. Hot-zone edit is surgical: 32 insertions / 7 deletions confined to the steps: of all-required-passed; no job added to or removed from needs:.

notes:

No instrument on this rig can resolve it, and a quiet box does not change that. Whoever picks this up must not spend a window chasing that number.

WHAT REMAINS, and it is a different question: 337b2c2fb4 (rf2-2rtt6.84, 2026-08-04) moved the runtime under a faithful instrument, and both published phase-B runs (cb41ee537b, 0c0ff21f0d, both 2026-08-02) predate it. So the commit/c-local absolutes on the-cold-read-mount-term.md sections 1 and 4 are absolutes for a runtime that no longer ships. Re-taking them is worth a window ONLY as a refresh against the current runtime — never as a way to settle the sub-quantum drift.

NOW DEP-BLOCKED ON rf2-981nt. Phase B cannot reach a number at all until the residue-baseline/settle repair lands: the equality gate threw on the first sampled arm, byte-identical across both attempts (expected :entries 6, found 5). The gate is right and was not widened; the 4 ms horizon was not reverted.

ALSO ON THE RECORD from the same run, phase A was clean both times: arm-order guard reportable, positive control PASS (predicted 1.225x measured 1.219x, then 1.000x/1.038x).
DEFERRED BY THE MAYOR 2026-08-08 10:30 AUSEST — the measurement lane is stood down for the P2 sitting, on the operator's instruction. Not abandoned; held.

WHY, and it is a judgement about yield rather than about this bead. Two of the programme's primary instruments have now been shown STRUCTURALLY unable to adjudicate their rows, both with PASSING controls, which is what makes them findings rather than noise. The three-point control refused 0 of 42 across two independent quiet-box ensembles, and rf2-8a746's diagnosis showed both available sitings fail with the conditioning arithmetic explaining why any siting must. The allocation ladder refused this morning (rf2-2rtt6.138): the floor arm costs F ~ 24.4 KB per write, F does not shrink when B does, and at the six-write floor that is 57% of the allowance before a single boundary is measured.

THIS BEAD'S OWN PROSPECTS ARE ALREADY POOR ON THE RECORD. Its original question is dead by arithmetic — 0.0075 ms/commit against a 0.025 ms grid, under a third of a quantum — which is why the scope was corrected on 2026-08-07 to a refresh of absolutes against the current runtime. That refresh is worth having eventually; it is not worth a quiet-box window that the sitting does not need.

WHAT WOULD REVIVE IT: an operator decision that the commit-half absolutes are wanted for their own sake, or a post-sitting programme that needs them. The instrument repair it was blocked on (rf2-981nt) HAS landed, so when it runs it will run cleanly — phase B can reach a number again.

title: method: the mayor must verify a close HELD, not just that it was made
description:
docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md says to close items 'only after merge or verifiable completion' and to record close reasons concretely. It does NOT say to verify the close STUCK. That gap cost real work on 2026-08-03.

WHAT HAPPENED. Five beads closed after their PRs merged — rf2-6t03c, rf2-2rtt6.25, rf2-eane2, rf2-p0m6m, rf2-oztox — were SILENTLY BACK TO OPEN when the mayor later reread the raw list. Each had been verified CLOSED at the time. One (rf2-p0m6m) had additionally been bumped P3 -> P2, which is what made the mayor look twice. Traced through the committed .beads snapshots: rf2-oztox read status open in EVERY snapshot from 11:54 onward while bd show had returned CLOSED right after its merge. All five were from the EARLY merge window and every later close held, so it was a rollback to an earlier snapshot — the same family as rf2-rjqtj (equal-count set substitution) and rf2-51uz1 (checkout-then-reimport), and consistent with the interrupted Dolt generational GC observed the same morning.

The mayor re-verified all five PRs as MERGED with commits on main and re-closed them with evidence. Nothing was lost, but the running 'beads closed' count was overstated for part of the session, and NOTHING IN THE LOOP WOULD HAVE SURFACED IT — it was found only because the operator asked for a full reread.

WHAT TO ADD, and keep it to the register of the existing hard-won list: a tracker write can silently revert, so re-verify closes on a LATER cycle, not only at the moment you make them. Concretely, a cheap per-tick audit: re-check every bead closed this session and re-close any that reverted, with evidence.

TWO METHOD NOTES WORTH CARRYING, both learned by getting them wrong:
• AUDIT ON THE STABLE BEAD ID, never on the row UUID. Row UUIDs are regenerated on re-import, so a UUID-keyed diff reports phantom losses — it flagged three for the mayor and all three beads existed and were closed.
• PARSE THE STATUS FIELD, not the line. A first attempt grepped the whole show output and matched the substring OPEN inside a bead TITLE ('the fail-OPEN CSRF compare'), reporting a false reopen. A verification tool that misreports is the same defect class as the instruments this repo spent the day fixing.

SCOPE: docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md (the hard-won list). This is method prose only — no script, no tooling. The tracker-side fix already landed separately as rf2-rjqtj (PR #7410), which makes the checkpoint compare ids/updated_at/status instead of trusting a row count; this bead is about the MAYOR'S habit, which no script covers.
close_reason: Added one Hard-won bullet to docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md — 'A tracker write can silently revert' — placed next to the tracker-checkpoint bullet. Carries the per-cycle re-verify habit plus both audit caveats (stable item id not row UUID; parse the status field not the line). Kept general to any tracker, no script/tooling per scope. PR #7438. Gates: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 (gate root confirmed as the worker worktree, PASS fast PR spine marker).

title: Hicasso: the memo wrapper's 2x is not double buffering — what IS it?
description:
SUCCESSOR to rf2-2rtt6.61, which is closed as a VERIFIED NEGATIVE.

rf2-2rtt6.61 asked for a fiber count to test the published hypothesis that the
memo wrapper's 2x instrument disagreement (+195/+220 B per boundary on
chrome_run.cjs vs +100/+106 B on p0_run.cjs --only ladder) was React's double
buffering. That hypothesis is now EXCLUDED from the instruments' own committed
source, with no fiber count taken:

  * p0_run.cjs:588-593 — gc, pre-read, mountOne, gc, held-read. Mount and hold.
  * chrome_run.cjs:242-243 — 'the heap half, first, on a quiet page';
    heapForArms runs to completion before the clock half's runOp calls begin at
    line 264. heapOnce (164-182) is resetRuntime -> baseline -> mountArm ->
    held, with no op between mount and read.
  * Byte-identical ordering at cb179b6b3c, the commit that published the
    +195/+220 figures.

BOTH instruments mount and hold. Neither has ever read an updated tree, so the
rule 2rtt6.61 proposed — a memo wrapper costs ONE fiber held and TWO updated —
must not be adopted, and is not.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN. The ~2x itself. Both figures reproduce on their own
instrument and both are published against the shape they were taken on, so
nothing rests on this; it is about being able to state WHY.

THE ASK, and it is a DIFFERENT question from 2rtt6.61's. Classify FiberNode
objects in a heap snapshot on each instrument, by tag, and answer: is the
wrapper ONE fiber in both? If yes, the difference is in what a fiber HOLDS on
each shape, not in how many there are, and the programme should stop quoting a
Fiber as a fixed byte count. If no, the count itself is the finding and the
mechanism has to be named.

NOTE ON COST. No such capability exists anywhere under implementation/: a
tree-wide search for FiberNode, _reactInternals, memoizedState, queryObjects,
Runtime.queryObjects, writeHeapSnapshot and v8.getHeapSnapshot returns nothing.
The nearest scaffolding is snapshotTotal() in
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/reads_ladder_run.cjs:228,
which streams HeapProfiler.takeHeapSnapshot and sums self_size plus a raw node
count — it never reads the snapshot's strings table or a node's type/name, so
it cannot isolate FiberNode. Classification is a new instrument, not a flag.

NOT a clock bead: a snapshot classification is structural and does not need a
quiet box.

Shapes, for whoever takes it: chrome is 301 boundaries, each a 17-element card
reading two subscriptions, ~11 KB retained per boundary; the ladder rung is
1,200 R=0 cells reading nothing, ~1,141 B per boundary. An order of magnitude
apart in what the boundary holds, against a 2x in what the wrapper adds.

Evidence: docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md,
subsection 'Why this instrument reads half of what the card-shaped one did'
(corrected 2026-08-03 under rf2-2rtt6.61).
notes: PARKED, not ready — restoring the 2026-08-04 ruling to the tracker (triage 2026-08-07). This bead was RULED PARKED with an explicit build trigger and has zero customers, but it stayed in 'bd ready', which is part of why this backlog read at roughly twice its real size. Deferred so the ready queue reflects the ruling. Un-defer when its recorded trigger fires.
close_reason: TRIAGE vs hic-* set (rf2-6bj7, 2026-08-10, delegated, operator-overturnable): CLOSED as investigation that does not pay rent — not superseded; no hic-* bead owns or needs the byte-level mechanism. The COUNT half was settled from source by the 2026-08-04 ruling: one extra MemoComponent wrapper fiber per boundary on BOTH witnesses (custom comparator boundary-props= keeps MemoComponent under pinned React 19.2). What remained parked is the byte-level decomposition of +195/+220 vs +100/+106, which needs a differential matched-snapshot instrument (tag counts + self_size + retainer/dominator paths) with zero customers. Verified today: both rigs still read whole-isolate Runtime.getHeapUsage (implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/chrome_run.cjs:160 and implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs:545), attributing nothing to a constructor; no snapshot classifier exists in-tree; and no hic-* bead names a per-fiber cost model — hic-006's budgets pin per-shape baselines, which is exactly the adopted doctrine (a Fiber is not a fixed tax; wrapper costs quoted per-shape, against their instrument, never a per-fiber constant). Both published figures reproduce on their own instrument and are published against their shape, so the record is honest without the mechanism. REOPEN TRIGGER (preserved verbatim from the 2026-08-04 ruling): (a) a consumer-facing/public cost model or v0 doc for the memo default needing the mechanism; (b) a P2 advisory or default/opt-in disposition decision turning on it; (c) a React upgrade or re-measurement moving a per-shape delta unexpectedly. Acceptance bar then: tag counts AND self_size AND retainer/dominator paths, matched snapshots, per witness.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DELEGATED DOSSIER-REVIEW RULING (Mike's 2026-08-04 directive); operator-overturnable. 2026-08-04 04:12 AUSEST.

RULING: PARKED at P3; no instrument built. The COUNT half of the ask is now SETTLED FROM SOURCE, no snapshot needed: the wrapper is ONE extra fiber per boundary on BOTH witnesses. mint-view!'s bail-out is (react/memo f boundary-props=) — front/codec.cljs:935, a CUSTOM comparator — so React 19.2 (pinned, implementation/package.json:19) keeps a MemoComponent wrapper fiber above the component's own instead of collapsing to SimpleMemoComponent; both witnesses share that single wrapper impl (the ladder's Hicasso arm mounts via arm1.runtime/arm1.mount, p0_heap.cljs:73-74); both mount-and-hold, so no alternates (rf2-2rtt6.61). The tree already records this mechanism at arm1/runtime.cljs:1720 (:react/memo-fiber token, rf2-2rtt6.52). The bead's fork resolves YES: the ~2x is NOT a fiber-count difference.

WHAT STAYS PARKED: the BYTE-level decomposition of +195/+220 (card, ~11 KB/boundary) vs +100/+106 (R=0, ~1.14 KB). Do NOT upgrade "shapes differ" into "the delta is what the wrapper fiber holds" — both rigs read whole-isolate Runtime.getHeapUsage (chrome_run.cjs:160, p0_run.cjs:470), which attributes nothing to a constructor; retainers/topology/allocator effects are unexcluded. The tag classifier this bead spec'd would only re-confirm the settled count and cannot decompose the delta; the true instrument is a differential probe on matched memo/plain snapshots (tag counts + self_size + retainer/dominator paths) — MORE machinery than the classifier, with zero customers.

MAIN vs CODEX: both recommended park; no disposition disagreement. Codex sharpened it and every load-bearing claim verified in-tree (comparator; getHeapUsage in both rigs; 19.2 pin; the in-tree memo-fiber token matching its React-source reading). Its cheaper route answers the count free while raising the true cost of the WHY — both strengthen the park. Minor: Codex quoted the ladder as +105.5/+105.0; the published +100/+106 band stands. Rationale: the bead's own "nothing rests on this" + pre-alpha no-gold-plating posture; both figures reproduce and are published per-shape, so the record is honest without the mechanism.

DOCTRINE (adopted): a custom-comparator React.memo adds one outer MemoComponent fiber (React 19.2), but the wrapper's incremental heap price is an empirical property of the complete witness+instrument+version — NEVER a fixed "bytes per Fiber" constant. Wrapper costs are quoted per-shape, against their instrument. The studio ladder page already carries this as its practical-reading line ("a Fiber is not a fixed tax"); any future consumer-facing cost prose for the memo default quotes per-shape numbers, never a per-fiber constant.

BUILD TRIGGER (do not dispatch before one exists): a concrete customer needing the byte-level mechanism named — (a) a consumer-facing/public cost model or v0 doc for the memo default; (b) a P2 advisory or default/opt-in disposition decision turning on the mechanism; (c) a React upgrade or re-measurement moving a per-shape delta unexpectedly. Acceptance bar then: tag counts AND self_size AND retainer/dominator paths, matched snapshots, per witness.

title: hicasso: the-cold-read-mount-term's commit row and copy-fidelity ratio predate rf2-aqgr2's runtime change
description:
FOUND during rf2-6wh9o, which repaired the OTHER side of the same drift.

docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-cold-read-mount-term.md §1 publishes the
commit-half table:

  | whole commit (`commit`, shipping seam) | 0.8875 [0.8000-1.0750] |
    - (6.29 us/key; copy fidelity c-local/commit = 0.9718) |

Both figures in that cell were taken against an `arm1/runtime.cljs` that
minted a `Keyword` per key cell. rf2-aqgr2 (f7fd0c6a52, merged 2026-08-03)
removed that mint from the shipping commit half - it was the whole
-107/-108 B/read saving - so the `commit` arm is now cheaper than the
0.8875 the page reports, and the 0.9718 fidelity ratio compares a local
copy against a seam that no longer does what it did when the ratio was
taken.

SCOPE IS EXACTLY ONE TABLE CELL. The four DELTA rows beneath it are
unaffected and must not be re-taken on this bead's account: they are all
`c-local - variant`, the mint was bound unconditionally in `commit-local!`
(before the C-NOWATCH guard, present in every mode), so it appeared on both
sides of every delta and cancelled. Verified by reading the code, not
inferred. That is also why rf2-6wh9o could make the local copy faithful
without moving a published row.

WHAT IS NEEDED: re-take the `commit` and `c-local` arms on a quiet box and
restate the one cell, or - equally acceptable and cheaper - annotate the
cell with its provenance SHA and the note that it predates f7fd0c6a52. The
page already carries a "nothing here re-baselines the canonical witness"
disclaimer; this is a diagnostic clock, not a gate row, so an honest
provenance note may be the whole fix.

DO NOT bundle this with rf2-0qj9w or rf2-2rtt6.76. Both carry an explicit
quiet-box precondition and both are about axes this cell is not on
(rf2-0qj9w: Hicasso has no clock rows of its own; rf2-2rtt6.76: the warm
allocation slope, a heap axis). This is a stale-provenance repair on one
existing diagnostic cell.
close_reason:
Restated in PR #7434 (docs-only, two pages). NO MEASUREMENT TAKEN — every figure restated from the merged commits and the page's own arithmetic.

THE FOUR PHASE-B DELTAS REALLY DO CANCEL — confirmed against 54a2a78924's diff, not inferred: wk was bound in commit-local!'s let, ABOVE the C-NOWATCH guard, and "watchKey" sat on the cell in every mode including C-NOSUB (where r is nil and add-watch is never reached). 0.4125 / 0.0750 / 0.0375 / 0.0250 do not move.

ONE MORE ROW MOVES THAN THIS BEAD (and rf2-6wh9o's close reason) EXPECTED: the SHARE column. delta-line computes (/ d base) where base is c-local, NOT the whole commit — read_profile_app.cljs:663-666 — and c-local carried the same mint until 54a2a78924, so its absolute moved and all four shares are lower bounds. c-local recovers to 0.8625 two independent ways (0.9718 x 0.8875, and 0.4125/0.478), both on the instrument's 0.025 ms grid. The column header now names its denominator, which nothing on the page did.

NOTHING RETRACTED. 0.8875 and 6.29 us/key are real readings of a real commit; what was stale was what they claimed about today. Provenance stamp + stated direction (upper bounds), the route this bead itself offered.

ONE FIGURE GOT STRONGER. The 0.9718 copy-fidelity ratio STANDS: the mint sat on BOTH arms when it was taken and BOTH have since lost it (f7fd0c6a52 from commit, 54a2a78924 from c-local), so the perturbation is common-mode and cancels in the ratio for the same reason it cancels in the deltas — and rf2-6wh9o restored the copy to STRUCTURAL identity with the seam, a better warrant for the c-* ablations than a clock agreement alone. The window in which the ratio was genuinely broken is f7fd0c6a52 -> 54a2a78924, and it is closed.

SECOND SITE, found by grep: the-in-page-mount-term-decomposed.md §6(b) quotes the 0.7625 beside its own 0.827; its run closed 2026-08-03 05:28, seven hours before f7fd0c6a52. Comparison stays like-for-like, both absolutes are upper bounds, one sentence added. Also stamped: this page's own §4 re-read (0c0ff21f0d, 0.7625 + 51.9/5.6/3.7%), same figure class. No third site.

SIZE OF THE DRIFT: 141 keyword mints/commit against a phase-B grid resolving to 0.025 ms/commit (raw 0.1 ms clock / 4 frames per window — every published phase-B p50 lands on that grid or a half-step). The micro table's nearest anchor, a two-element vector mint, is 53 ns. About ONE QUANTUM; may not be resolvable on this clock at all.

FILED rf2-d360z (P3, discovered-from) — quiet-box re-take of the commit and c-local arms, in the rf2-0qj9w / rf2-2rtt6.76 precondition wording, stating that the deltas and the ratio need no re-take and the instrument must not be edited to chase it.

Gates: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py exit 0; sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 (terminal marker PASS fast PR spine), both foreground. mkdocs --strict ran in the spine and verified NOTHING of this edit (exclude_docs drops design/hicasso/). Hand-verified: 2 outbound / 1 inbound links on the cold-read page, 0 outbound / 1 inbound on the sibling, 0 dead, 0 anchor fragments in play, no heading touched; 8 tables and 10 tables respectively, 0 column-count mismatches.

title: The hicasso compile gate is dev-mode only: :advanced-only breakage in an unrun arm is still ungated
description:
Follow-up to rf2-2rtt6.73, which armed the lane's build door and added a PR-time compile gate (npm run test:hicasso-compile, in the cljs CI job).

THE REMAINING GAP, stated so it is not re-derived.

The PR gate runs a DEV-MODE 'shadow-cljs compile' of all 101 lane namespaces. That catches the class rf2-2rtt6.73 was filed for (:undeclared-var from a renamed/deleted def, a dropped require, a bad arity) because those resolve before optimization, and it is cheap (~30s).

What it does NOT catch is breakage that only appears under :advanced — the mode the drivers actually measure and publish from. Closure renaming, externs-inference faults, and the shadow-js module-index class rf2-2rtt6.20 documents are all :advanced-time. lane_build.cjs DOES refuse those, but only on a driver run someone performs by hand. So an arm nobody has run since it broke can still be :advanced-broken with every gate green.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN rf2-2rtt6.73: an :advanced release of all 101 namespaces in one module is not representative of any real arm build (no arm compiles the union), and doing it per-arm is ~15 builds x ~40s = 10min — a nightly cost, not a PR one.

LIKELY SHAPE, if taken: a NIGHTLY job that releases each arm's own :init-fn through the existing drivers' config-merge path (so each build is the real shape), judged by lane_build.cjs, which already refuses warnings. Wire into expensive-tests.yml rather than the PR spine.

ALSO UNCOVERED, recorded here rather than as its own bead: the ~15 driver .cjs files themselves are compiled/linted by nothing. Only lane_build.cjs's parser has a test (lane_build.test.cjs).
notes:
Verdict PR (comment-only correction, NOT a gate): https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7430

GATES: sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 with its own terminal marker 'PASS fast PR spine' confirmed in the log (not inferred from the wrapper's exit code); npm run test:hicasso-compile exit 0 pre-rebase AND re-run exit 0 after rebasing onto main past #7425, which touches this lane. 101 lane namespaces / 0 warnings both times.
close_reason:
NOT WORTH BUILDING — verified negative. The nightly :advanced gate was NOT built, and no per-arm or partial gate was built either. This bead's premise was TESTED rather than assumed and all three legs of it fail.

MEASURED FIRST, so the cost is on the record (one Windows box, .shadow-cljs/builds/hicasso-bench cleared before each build because the lane's cache rule requires it — so no warm reuse is available between arms):

  dev compile, all 101 lane namespaces (the existing PR gate)   77s   0 warnings
  :advanced release, ONE arm (parity-probe-app)                 64s   0 warnings
  :advanced release, all 101 namespaces in one module          132s   0 warnings

The bead priced per-arm at ~15 builds x 40s. The real count is 25 -main entry points, and a cold-cache :advanced release is 64s here, so per-arm is ~27 minutes local, more on CI. But COST IS NOT WHY IT WAS REJECTED — coverage is. Even the 132s one-module release was rejected.

WHY. The bead states 'Closure renaming, externs-inference faults, and the shadow-js module-index class rf2-2rtt6.20 documents are all :advanced-time'. Each one:

1. EXTERNS INFERENCE IS ALREADY GATED AT PR TIME, IN DEV. :infer-externs :auto is shadow-cljs's OWN default-compiler-options (shadow/build/api.clj), and shadow/build/compiler.clj binds :infer-warning into ana/*cljs-warnings* for every non-jar source in BOTH modes — it is not a release-only pass. MUTATION-PROVED, and deliberately NOT with an :undeclared-var: in parity_probe_app.cljs, (some-> e .-message) (a known extern) became (some-> e .-hicassoAdvProbeZz) (an unknown property on an untyped binding), which under :advanced is renamed and reads undefined at the call site.
     :advanced release, mutated -> 'Build completed. (392 files, 332 compiled, 1 warnings)', WARNING #1 - :infer-warning, 'Cannot infer target type in expression (. G__31147 -hicassoAdvProbeZz)', File: ...parity_probe_app.cljs:52:33.
     npm run test:hicasso-compile (THE EXISTING DEV GATE), same mutated tree -> EXIT 1, same WARNING #1 - :infer-warning, '[hicasso-compile] BUILD REFUSED — :hicasso-bench compiled with 1 warning(s)', in 45s.
   Same catch, half the wall clock. The nightly would have added nothing. check-examples-compile.cjs already listed 'an externs-inference miss' among the classes ITS dev compile catches — compile_gate.cjs's LIMITS block was the outlier, and this bead was filed off that outlier.
   Reverted byte-identically: sha256 6c4983ae2a2f8d49decc61c7e2629029e2e08dbf93bc38c26eca6bd94d36bd86 before and after, git status clean, dev gate exit 0 at 101 namespaces / 0 warnings.

2. CLOSURE RENAMING FAULTS EMIT NO COMPILER DIAGNOSTIC AT ALL, in any mode. A release of a program that will die on a renamed property still exits 0 with 0 warnings. No build gate reaches them; EXECUTION does.

3. THE rf2-2rtt6.20 CLASS IS EXPLICITLY NOT BUILD-OBSERVABLE. That bead's own words: the poisoned shadow-js index 'COMPILES CLEANLY and then produce[s] an :advanced bundle that DIED ON ITS FIRST EXECUTION'. Its fix is lane_cache.cjs, already called by every driver and by the compile gate.

WHAT IS LEFT for an :advanced BUILD over lane sources is Closure hard errors, and that class is empty by construction: no lane source uses js* (no unparsed JS for Closure to reject); the only npm modules the lane requires directly are react, react-dom and react-dom/client, which test:bundle-isolation, test:perf-bundle, test:elision and test:ui-g1 already push through shadow-js under :advanced; and Closure type checking is off by shadow's default (:closure-warnings {:check-types :off}).

So NO FAULT COULD BE CONSTRUCTED that the nightly would catch and the existing gate would miss. A gate nobody can make fire is the fail-open class this lane keeps repairing, not a repair of it — which is why a partial/published-arms-only variant was rejected too: a cheaper slice of zero marginal coverage is still zero. Also worth stating: the one-module release's namespace set is a SUPERSET of every arm's, so per-arm 'representativeness' buys nothing for a BUILD check — it matters only for an artefact you intend to RUN.

THE RESIDUAL, STATED HONESTLY AND NOT CLOSED: an arm nobody has run since it broke can still be :advanced-broken AT RUNTIME with every gate green. That is real. The only instrument that reaches it is a BOOT of each arm's release bundle — ~30 min nightly across 25 arms, plus a per-arm sentinel contract because the drivers' completion protocols differ. Judged out of proportion to a P3 residual; recorded as NOT TAKEN rather than overlooked, so the option survives this close.

SHIPPED: a comment-only correction to compile_gate.cjs replacing the false LIMITS claim with the measurements above, so this is not re-derived a third time. Zero executable lines changed, one file, NO .github/workflows/* edit and NO implementation/shadow-cljs.edn edit.

CARRIED FORWARD: the bead's secondary item (the driver .cjs files are linted by nothing) is now rf2-2rtt6.78. Checked and re-scoped — there is no eslint config anywhere in the repo, so the gap is repo-wide (~50 implementation/scripts/*.cjs are in the same position), not lane-specific.

title: Hicasso: the walk stage table cannot be totalled — a decomposition of record needs a quiet-box re-take
description:
Follow-up from rf2-mgegk, which retracted the "decomposition closes to 92%"
claim on docs/design/hicasso/studio/our-walk-against-reagents.md.

With the double-count removed, the BEFORE table's non-overlapping named
stages sum to +39.5 us against an observed +37.5 us whole-walk delta — a 5%
overshoot, which is inside the instrument's declared limits. Running the same
arithmetic over the AFTER table is worse: the named stages come to +5.6 us
against an observed delta of -25.0 us, so they do not agree in SIGN.

That is not a new defect in the walk or in the two landed cheapenings — the
page's conclusions rest on section 2's same-run interleaved arm ratios, and
the cache/predicate-order changes are adjudicated by their own before/after
micro tables. It is a statement about the stage table: it was taken on a box
section 7 declares was NOT quiet, its absolutes are explicitly ceilings, and
stock Reagent's own string-child row reads 8.8 in one run and 20.3 in the
other on identical code. The record now says so and reads the table as an
attribution rather than an accounting.

IF a per-stage decomposition of record is ever wanted (nothing currently
depends on one), it needs a re-take on a quiet box, and probably a residual
stage so the accounting can close by construction rather than by luck.

PRECONDITION — quiet box. Same as rf2-0qj9w and rf2-2rtt6.76: do not run the
bench drivers while the fleet is oversubscribed. This is not blocking
anything, so it should wait for a genuinely idle machine.

title: hicasso/freehand: R-A2's fitness-harness wording states an IME property no implementation satisfies
description:
Raised by rf2-ncn5p while narrowing HD-019's IME claim.

docs/design/freehand/studio/fitness-harness.md line 117 states R-A2 as
'Caret/selection preservation when the rendered value differs from what was
typed (reject, transform, reformat) - mid-string edits included; IME
composition never broken by value reassertion.'

That last clause is the acceptance bar, and rf2-o27h3's real CDP composition
harness measured it false for EVERY implementation the moment the model
disagrees mid-composition: the corrected value is written back inside the
composing input event and the browser aborts the exchange. Arm 1's converge
does it in turn, plain React does it in turn through its own restore, the UIx
port a frame later (rf2-digtt has the matrix).

So R-A2 as written cannot be met by anything, including the incumbent. HD-019,
docs/design/hicasso/authoring.md and the Hicasso draft guide were narrowed to
the proven commit fence by rf2-ncn5p; the fitness harness page - which is the
SOURCE of the R-A2 wording those pages quoted - was left alone because it is
outside that bead's surface and because the honest restatement depends on how
rf2-digtt is ruled.

REMEDY once rf2-digtt is ruled: restate R-A2's IME clause as what is actually
required (the commit fence, plus whatever the carve-out ruling settles for the
value path), rather than as a property no browser-hosted controlled input has.
Docs only; docs/design/freehand/ is outside the mkdocs site build, so
scripts/check_doc_slugs.py is the gate.

R-A2 restated on docs/design/freehand/studio/fitness-harness.md:117 — PR #7442.

The bead's premise went stale: it was filed blocked on rf2-digtt and says R-A2 'cannot be met by anything, including the incumbent'. rf2-digtt has since been ruled, implemented and merged, so on current main the Hicasso lean-React arm DOES preserve a live composition (converge declines on composing-input?; a one-useState shadow holds the value React sees at the live DOM draft so React's own element.value !== value guard skips its restore). Plain React and the UIx port still abort — ime_run.cjs pins those rows (pinned, DIVERGENT). R-A2 is therefore no longer unmeetable; it is differentiating, and the new wording says so.

The restatement follows the ruling comment's three points: (1) the composing-Enter commit fence, held on all three implementations; (2) composition survival, stated as an obligation on the WRITER — nothing writes the field while a composition runs, neither the substrate's converge nor the host's end-of-event restore, and the refused/normalised value lands once at compositionend — met only by the arm's converge, with the baseline's SSHSH normalising-field corruption pinned; (3) witness scope: Chromium, CDP being Chromium's protocol, WebKit unmeasured rather than passing.

Requirement column stays substrate-neutral as the rest of the table is; who meets it lives in the Evidence anchor column. No criteria added, no neighbouring bar hedged.

title: hygiene: the gate exit-code file the dispatch template asks for is NOT gitignored, so following the guidance creates reap-blocking residue
description:
FOUND during the 2026-08-03 hygiene sweep, measured in a live worker worktree.

THE LOOP. docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md (section 'How a gate is run, not just which one', landed as c6566415b8) tells every worker two things:
  (a) echo the runner's own exit code explicitly and quote it in the PR body; and
  (b) put the gate log where git ignores it -- '*.log already is'.
Workers duly write the log to *.log AND the exit code to a sibling file. But the exit-code file is not a .log. Measured just now:

  git check-ignore -v gate-fastpr.exit   -> NOT IGNORED
  git check-ignore -v g-fastpr-exit.txt  -> NOT IGNORED
  git check-ignore -v gate.log           -> .gitignore:14:*.log

So the untracked exit file survives, and 'git worktree remove' then REFUSES the tree -- exit 128, non-destructive but permanent until someone forces it. That is precisely the mechanism rf2-p0m6m diagnosed (nine worktrees would not reap; every one was dirty with exactly one untracked path, and the script's message misattributed it to a lock). The template's own residue examples even NAME 'g-fastpr-exit.txt', so the hazard was written down while the ignore rule that would prevent it was not added.

LIVE INSTANCE at the time of filing: re-frame2-worktrees/hostile-dhl4d carried '?? gate-fastpr.exit' with everything else clean.

DO, and keep it small -- this is a one-line class of fix, not a project:
  1. Extend .gitignore so gate exit-code artefacts are ignored alongside logs. Something in the shape of '*.exit' plus the '*-exit.txt' spelling the template already names. Check first whether any TRACKED file would be caught -- 'git ls-files | grep -E "\.exit$|-exit\.txt$"' must be empty before adding a broad rule.
  2. Make the dispatch template's wording close the loop: it currently says to put THE LOG where git ignores it, which a careful worker satisfies while still leaving the exit file behind. Say plainly that EVERY gate artefact -- log and exit code -- goes to an ignored path, and give one concrete ignored spelling workers can copy.
  3. Consider the same sentence in AGENTS.md, which PR #7412 established is the file Codex workers here are handed.

NOT IN SCOPE: changing how exit codes are captured. Redirect-and-read-the-file is correct and is load-bearing -- four workers in one day reported a pipe's exit status instead of the runner's. Do not weaken that; only make its artefact ignored.
close_reason: Closed

title: hicasso: the evidence seam's 'detached cost is one deref and one nil test' is false at record-reads!
description:
FOUND during rf2-aqgr2 while reading the read path's allocation profile.
Clock/allocation axis, not retained heap, so it was out of that bead's
scope.

`front/sub_index.cljs`'s HD-005 section promises:

  "Detached cost is one deref and one nil test at each of the two tap
   points. No evidence subsystem ships..."

That holds at the `commit!` tap point. It does NOT hold at
`record-reads!`, which builds the event before it asks whether anyone is
listening:

    (when (not= held reads)
      (evidence! {:event    :edges-changed
                  :boundary boundary-id
                  :added    (set/difference reads held)
                  :dropped  (set/difference held reads)}))

`evidence!` is `(when-some [sink @!evidence-sink] (sink event))`, so the
map literal and both `set/difference` calls are evaluated on every call
whether or not a sink is attached. On Arm 1's wiring `held` is ALWAYS
`#{}` (the boundary id is the registration React mints per `subscribe`,
so a changed read set arrives as a fresh id — `arm1/runtime.cljs` clause
(b), and `the-wired-path-never-takes-the-diffs-dropping-half`), so the
`not=` guard is true for every non-empty read set and the map is built
once per boundary per commit.

The two differences are cheap on this path — `clojure.set/difference`
returns its first argument untouched when the second is empty, and `#{}`
minus anything reduces to `#{}` — so the residue is one four-entry map
per boundary per commit. Nothing is RETAINED (the sink is nil, so the map
is immediately garbage), which is why the heap ladder never saw it.

FIX: move the construction inside the nil check — a thunk, or push the
`when-some` out to the call site — and either way make the docstring's
claim true rather than aspirational. Small, and worth doing while the
claim is still only one call site out of date.
notes:
2026-08-03 — VERIFIED, NOT ACTIONED: the file is held. rf2-ixb92 is IN_PROGRESS
on `worker/subindex-dabt3`, which carries unmerged changes to this same
`front/sub_index.cljs` (plus the law suite). Per the worker fence, stopped
rather than racing it. Everything below is read-only verification from
origin/main @ 5362fdf382, done so the fix is a five-minute job for whoever
holds the file next.

THE DIAGNOSIS IS CONFIRMED, AND UNDERSTATED. The bead says the claim "holds
at the commit! tap point". It does not — `commit!` violates it too:

    (evidence! {:event :commit
                :dirty-subs (set dirty-sub-keys)
                :dirty-boundaries dirty})

is a 3-entry map literal built unconditionally, before `evidence!` derefs the
sink. So the HD-005 docstring's "one deref and one nil test at EACH OF THE TWO
tap points" is false at BOTH, not one of two.

THE ARITHMETIC CHECKS OUT (clojurescript-1.12.42, read from the jar):

  * `clojure.set/difference` with `held = #{}`:
    `(difference reads #{})` -> `(< n 0)` false -> `(reduce disj reads #{})`
    -> reduce over an empty coll returns the init, i.e. `reads` ITSELF,
    identical, zero allocation.
    `(difference #{} reads)` -> `(< 0 n)` true -> `(reduce f #{} #{})`
    -> `#{}`, zero allocation.
    So the bead is right that both differences are free on Arm 1's wiring.

  * `cljs.core/set` on an already-meta-less set is `(with-meta coll nil)`,
    and `PersistentHashSet`'s `-with-meta` returns `coll` when the meta is
    `identical?` -- zero allocation. So `commit!`'s `(set dirty-sub-keys)` is
    free too, and its residue is likewise exactly one map literal.

DETACHED RESIDUE, TOTAL: one 4-entry PersistentArrayMap per boundary per
commit (`record-reads!`), plus one 3-entry PersistentArrayMap per commit
(`commit!`). Nothing is retained -- the sink is nil, so both are immediately
garbage, which is why the per-read heap ladder never saw them.

RECOMMENDED FIX (and it makes the file SMALLER, not larger). Do not use a
thunk: `(evidence! #(hash-map ...))` allocates a closure capturing the same
locals, so it trades a map for an object and the claim stays false. Push the
`when-some` out to the two call sites and drop the `evidence!` indirection --
the indirection is precisely what hides the cost:

    (defn- evidence-sink [] @!evidence-sink)

    ;; record-reads!  (sink test FIRST -- it is the cheaper guard, and
    ;;                 putting it outside is what makes the claim literal)
    (when-some [sink (evidence-sink)]
      (when (not= held reads)
        (sink {:event :edges-changed :boundary boundary-id
               :added (set/difference reads held)
               :dropped (set/difference held reads)})))

    ;; commit!
    (when-some [sink (evidence-sink)]
      (sink {:event :commit :dirty-subs (set dirty-sub-keys)
             :dirty-boundaries dirty}))

Both guards are side-effect-free, so hoisting the sink test above the
`not=` is behaviour-preserving. The ns docstring's "Three lines -- a holder,
a setter, and a nil-checked emit" needs restating to match (holder, setter,
accessor; the nil check moves to the tap points), and that sentence is
adjacent to the data-model paragraph rf2-ixb92 is rewriting -- another reason
these two want sequencing rather than parallelism.

VERDICT: worth doing (it is a load-bearing HD-005 design claim, not
decoration, and the repair removes indirection rather than adding it), but it
belongs in the same hand as rf2-ixb92 or immediately after it merges.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7437. Both tap points violated the claim, not one — the predecessor's correction to two is confirmed against the current post-#7425 file. Changed the CODE, not the docstring: HD-005's own ruling in decisions.md already says 'detached cost is zero', so the design record was right and the code had drifted. Deleted the evidence! indirection and moved its when-some out to record-reads! and commit!, so the nil test is now the outermost form at each tap point. Avoided the thunk trap (a closure captures the same locals and leaves the claim false). Net +1 line, one fewer defn, detached path strictly cheaper. Mutation-proved through npm run test:cljs (when true in place of the reordered not= guard -> exactly 1 failure at sub_index_laws_cljs_test.cljs:333, reverted byte-identically). Gates: test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 (PASS fast PR spine, incl. hicasso bench-lane compile 101 ns / 0 warnings), test:browser exit 0 (1040 tests, 0 failures). Design docs untouched — they were never the drifted party.

title: hicasso: sub-index :live is exactly the key set of :b->subs — a redundant index on the shell axis
description:
FOUND during rf2-aqgr2. Not actioned there: it is a per-BOUNDARY term,
so it moves the shell intercept and not the per-read slope that bead was
attacking.

`front/sub_index.cljs` keeps three structures in one atom:

    :sub->bs   sub-key     -> #{boundary-id}
    :b->subs   boundary-id -> #{sub-key}
    :live      #{boundary-id}

`:live` carries no information `:b->subs` does not already carry:

- `mount` adds to `:live` unconditionally and installs `#{}` in
  `:b->subs` when absent, so after a mount both contain the boundary;
- `unmount` removes it from both;
- `record-reads` only ever assoc's `:b->subs` for a live boundary.

So `(:live idx)` is exactly `(set (keys (:b->subs idx)))` at every
reachable index value, and `live?` is `(contains? (:b->subs idx) b)`.
Dropping it removes one set membership per mounted boundary from the
retained inventory (`arm1/runtime.cljs` `retained-inventory` files it as
`:index/live`), and removes a second place the mount/unmount pair has to
stay symmetric in.

WHAT IT IS WORTH: unmeasured, and honestly small — the per-read heap
ladder shows the Hicasso shell at ~1,240 B against Reagent's ~507, and
one persistent-set membership is a low-tens-of-bytes term in that. It is
filed as an ELIMINATION (a redundant index disappears, and the docstring
gets shorter) rather than as a saving.

WHAT IT COSTS TO DO: the ns docstring's three-line data model, the
matching sentence in `docs/design/hicasso/architecture.md`, `empty-index`,
`mount`, `unmount`, `record-reads`, `live?`, `stats`' `:boundaries`
count, and the law suite's uses of `(:live (idx/snapshot))`. Mechanical,
but it touches the shared front half's published shape, so it wants a
deliberate yes rather than a drive-by.
close_reason: Landed in PR #7425. :live deleted; live? is (contains? (:b->subs idx) b) and stats' :boundaries counts the forward-edge map. No complexity change either way (contains?/count are the same ops on a PersistentHashMap as on a PersistentHashSet). No byte figure claimed - shell-axis term, nothing measured. Derivability proved by liveness-is-the-forward-edge-entry-and-there-is-no-second-record-of-it, which walks the reachable values and also pins the index value to exactly #{:sub->bs :b->subs}. Mutation-proven twice (exit 1, 13 and 79 named failures), both reverted byte-identically. Two bead corrections: architecture.md needed NO edit (it never names :live), and the stats :boundaries site lives in arm1/runtime.cljs not in the index ns. Gates on 10c073f5e8: test:cljs exit 0 (12472/62526), test:browser exit 0 (1040/6468); fast-PR spine exit 0 on 11800137e6.

title: hicasso: read_profile_app's local cell copy is no longer faithful — it still mints a watch keyword per cell
description:
FOUND during rf2-aqgr2 (the 415/499 B/read gap).

`implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/read_profile_app.cljs`
lines 361-414 carry a deliberate LOCAL COPY of the commit half
`arm1.runtime/make-subscribe` performs, and its docstring calls it a
"Faithful copy". It mints one watch key per cell:

    (def ^:private !local-watch-counter (volatile! 0))
    ... wk (keyword "rf-readprof" (str "w" (vswap! !local-watch-counter inc)))
    ... "watchKey" wk

rf2-aqgr2 removed exactly that mint from the runtime it copies
(`arm1/runtime.cljs`: one namespaced constant `cell-watch-key`, no
counter, no `watchKey` field), because the uniqueness it bought was
already structural — at most one cell per (frame, query), so no two cells
ever hold the same reaction. Measured saving on the per-read heap ladder:
-107 B/read (Reagent segment), -108 (UIx).

So the profiler now prices a cell shape the runtime no longer builds:
one Keyword, its name string and its fully-qualified string per cell, on
a per-read path, plus one extra field on the cell object. read_profile is
a CLOCK instrument (µs/read), not a heap one, so the drift shows up in
its phase-B stub deltas (C-FULL / C-NOWATCH / C-NOSUB / C-NOINDEX /
C-NOMAP) rather than in bytes — but the C-NOWATCH delta in particular is
now measuring "watch + disposal hook + a keyword mint" against a runtime
that mints nothing.

NOT fixed in rf2-aqgr2's PR deliberately: changing a timing instrument
moves its own published rows, and this worker had no mandate to re-take
them. The repair is small (a single `::rp-cell-watch` constant, keeping
its own namespace so it cannot collide with the runtime's watches on the
same cached reactions) but it should land with whoever re-runs the
profile and restates any row that moved.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #7431. read_profile_app's commit-local! now installs one ::rp-cell-watch constant, mirroring arm1/runtime.cljs's own cell-watch-key (rf2-aqgr2, f7fd0c6a52); the !local-watch-counter and the cell's watchKey field are gone.

NO PUBLISHED CLOCK ROW MOVES — checked, not assumed, and this corrects the bead's own diagnosis. The bead expected the C-NOWATCH delta to be 'measuring watch + disposal hook + a keyword mint'. It was not: wk was bound UNCONDITIONALLY, before the (when-not (identical? mode C-NOWATCH)) guard, so the mint was present in every mode and appeared on BOTH sides of all four published phase-B deltas in the-cold-read-mount-term.md §1 (c-local minus c-nosub / c-noindex / c-nomap / c-nowatch). It cancelled exactly. No row was re-taken and none is restated.

The one published figure that does involve c-local absolutely is the 'copy fidelity c-local/commit = 0.9718' cell, whose OTHER term was already re-based by rf2-aqgr2's merged runtime change independently of this work. Filed as rf2-gttif (P3, blocked on this bead), scope pinned to that single cell.

Gates: npm run test:browser exit 0 (1036 tests / 6445 assertions, 0 failures); sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 (PASS fast PR spine). No bench driver was run. Mutation-proved via the lane compile, which was itself proved able to fail (:undeclared-var at line 414) — and which exits 0 while doing so, corroborating rf2-2rtt6.73's fail-open finding from a second direction.

title: workers: backgrounded-spine completion notifications silently never fire — four stale-waiter incidents in one day
description:
PATTERN, now systemic (2026-08-02, four incidents): a worker backgrounds a long gate (fast-PR spine, typically) and ends its turn waiting on the completion notification. THE NOTIFICATION NEVER FIRES. The worker sits stale — sometimes through multiple idle ticks reporting 'standing by' — until the mayor notices the branch unmoved and sends a status check, which resumes it. Every resume has recovered cleanly because the work itself was committed; the only loss is hours of latency per incident.

INCIDENTS: burst-2rtt6-55 twice (once compounded by a wrapper-shadowed exit code), ime-o27h3 once, and the same shape underlies the walkopt/hosthatch 'placeholder expired' ticks. Distinct from the API-outage kills (those report failed status); this class reports nothing at all.

WHAT ALREADY MITIGATES IT: the standing brief line 'gates foreground only, to completion' — workers who foreground the spine never hit this. The incidents are workers who backgrounded it anyway, usually to keep working while it runs.

THE WORK, in preference order:
  1. Establish WHY the completion notification is lost for backgrounded shells on this box (harness-level: does the notification fire and get dropped, or never fire?). Evidence: the burst worker found one case where the notification DID fire but the exit code captured was the wrapper's — so there may be two defects wearing one symptom.
  2. If root cause is out of reach, harden the convention: briefs already say foreground-only; make the worker-side rule 'if you background a gate anyway, poll its log on a timer rather than waiting for a notification' — and put that in the dispatch template where the gates-foreground rule lives.
  3. Consider whether the mayor's status-check-on-unmoved-branch heuristic (which caught all four) should be a standing automation rather than judgement.

Cross-platform rule applies to any tooling. This is process/harness work — do not dispatch while it would displace implementation; it costs latency, not correctness.
notes:
MAYOR ASSESSMENT 2026-08-06: MITIGATED IN PRACTICE BY BRIEF TEXT, NOT BY A FIX — leaving open, recording the evidence.

THE BEAD'S PATTERN: a worker backgrounds a long gate, ends its turn waiting for a completion notification, and THE NOTIFICATION NEVER FIRES. Four incidents on 2026-08-02. Recovery was always clean because the work was committed; the cost was hours of latency each time.

WHAT CHANGED, AND IT IS WORDING RATHER THAN MACHINERY: every dispatch brief today has carried, verbatim, "GATES: foreground to completion; never end a turn waiting to be woken." Roughly thirty dispatches. NOT ONE WORKER STALLED ON A BACKGROUNDED GATE TODAY.

AND A REFINEMENT LEARNED TODAY, now also in the briefs: BACKGROUNDED IS NOT KILLED. A run that is DETACHED at the harness's 600s cap and then COMPLETES has a REAL exit code; only a run TERMINATED mid-flight has a meaningless one. The discriminator is the runner's own terminal marker, which the briefs already tell workers to read. Three workers today reported backgrounded-and-completed passes correctly, and two of them apologised for it unnecessarily - which is a wording cost, not a correctness one, and is why that refinement went into the briefs.

WHY I AM NOT CLOSING IT: the underlying notification behaviour is unchanged and untested. The mitigation lives entirely in brief text that a future mayor might not carry, and this bead is the only record of why that sentence is in there. Closing it would delete the reason.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: either the harness notification is shown to fire reliably, or the instruction moves somewhere durable - docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md - so it survives a mayor who has not read this bead. THE SECOND IS CHEAP AND IS PROBABLY THE RIGHT ANSWER; it is a template edit, not a fix.
close_reason:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN NOTE ABOVE, AND CLOSING (mayor, 2026-08-06).

I WROTE, an hour ago: "the mitigation lives entirely in brief text that a future mayor might not carry... WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the instruction moves somewhere durable - docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md - so it survives a mayor who has not read this bead."

THAT WAS WRONG, AND I DID NOT OPEN THE FILE BEFORE WRITING IT. The template ALREADY CARRIES IT, at dispatch-prompt-template.md, in the GATES section: "Foreground, to completion. A worker that backgrounds a long gate and ends [its turn] ... waiting to be woken." It is durable, it is not mine to remember, and it survives any mayor who reads the template - which the method's own loop requires.

THE TEMPLATE ALSO CARRIES A SECOND HAZARD I HAD NOT REGISTERED, immediately after: "Invoke a backgrounded gate by its ABSOLUTE path" - because the gate scripts derive paths and a backgrounded shell adopts whatever cwd it really has, not the one the command appeared to set. That is a distinct trap from this bead's and it is already documented.

SO THE BEAD IS DISCHARGED BY WORK THAT PREDATES IT BEING FILED. Evidence for closing:
  - The instruction is in the template, not only in a mayor's habit.
  - ZERO incidents today across roughly thirty dispatches, against four on 2026-08-02.
  - Today's refinement - BACKGROUNDED IS NOT KILLED; a run detached at the 600s cap that COMPLETES has a real exit code, and the discriminator is the runner's own terminal marker - is recorded in bd memories and reached three workers, all of whom reported backgrounded-and-completed passes correctly.

WHAT IS NOT FIXED, stated so nobody reads this close as more than it is: the underlying harness notification behaviour is unchanged and untested. If it recurs DESPITE the template instruction, that is a different bead about the harness, not this one about the practice.

title: Hicasso: count the fibers behind the memo wrapper's 2x instrument disagreement
description:
rf2-2rtt6.58 measured HD-026's memo wrapper at ~+100 B per boundary on the R=0
shell (p0_run.cjs --only ladder). The page-chrome row (rf2-2rtt6.52,
chrome_run.cjs) measured the SAME wrapper at +195/+220 B per boundary. Both
reproduce on their own instrument, so the ~2x disagreement is real and belongs to
the shapes rather than to a bad run.

LEADING EXPLANATION, PUBLISHED AS A HYPOTHESIS AND NOT AS A RESULT: React's
double buffering. The ladder MOUNTS AN ARM AND HOLDS IT with no writes, so only
the current tree exists and a memo wrapper costs one extra fiber. The page-chrome
instrument performs its four write ops BEFORE reading heap, and an updated
component retains an `alternate` fiber beside its current one — so a wrapper
position there can be holding two. Roughly 2x is what that predicts, and roughly
2x is what the two instruments differ by.

It was deliberately NOT claimed, because neither run counted fibers.

DO: count them. A heap snapshot on each instrument, classifying FiberNode objects
by tag (MemoComponent vs the boundary's own) and by whether an alternate is
present, would settle it outright. If confirmed, the general statement the
programme should carry is that a memo wrapper costs ONE fiber on a held tree and
TWO on a tree that has been updated — which is a per-shape rule, not a constant,
and it changes how any future Fiber cost is quoted.

WHY IT IS ONLY P3: the adjudication rf2-2rtt6.58 was filed for does not depend on
it. Both numbers are measured and both are published against the shape they were
taken on. This is about being able to state WHY, and about not quoting either
figure onto the other's shape by accident.

Evidence: docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md,
subsection "Why this instrument reads half of what the card-shaped one did".
close_reason: PR #7433. VERIFIED NEGATIVE — closed WITHOUT the fiber count, because the count is not needed. VERDICT: the PREDICTION (the published hypothesis) was wrong; both instruments are right. The double-buffering explanation rested on the page-chrome rig writing before it reads heap, and it does not: chrome_run.cjs:242-243 runs heapForArms to completion first, under the comment 'the heap half, first, on a quiet page', and the clock half's runOp calls do not begin until line 264; heapOnce (164-182) is resetRuntime -> baseline -> mountArm -> held, with nothing between the mount and the read. Byte-identical ordering at cb179b6b3c, the commit that published +195/+220, verified by git show. The ladder's own window (p0_run.cjs:588-593) is gc/pre-read/mountOne/gc/held-read. BOTH INSTRUMENTS MOUNT AND HOLD, so no alternate fiber exists on either, and the general rule this bead proposed — one fiber held, two updated — is NOT adopted: no measurement on this programme has read an updated tree's wrapper. Corrected in all three places it was published (the ladder subsection, the page-chrome page's 2026-08-02 correction block, HD-028 in decisions.md), struck through rather than deleted. Every measured figure stands; only the account of WHY was wrong. The ~2x itself remains open as rf2-2rtt6.79, which asks the fiber count on a different question: is the wrapper ONE fiber on both shapes, i.e. is the difference in what a fiber HOLDS rather than how many there are. No quiet box needed — snapshot classification is structural.

title: hicasso: HD-019 says flushSync is never the default, and the controlled converge makes it the default
description:
DECISIONS-RECORD AMENDMENT, raised by rf2-fki5d (PR #7371) and deliberately not
made by the worker.

HD-019 (docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md) rules that on the lean-React arm
`flushSync` is "the evidence-gated last resort, NEVER THE DEFAULT". The
controlled converge shipped by rf2-fki5d calls `flushSync` once per keystroke on
every controlled element — so it IS now the default there.

The evidence gate is met and is recorded: removing only the `flushSync` from
`front.controlled/converge!` reds 4 assertions, all caret readings at [5 5],
INCLUDING the ordinary accepted keystroke — without it the per-instance record is
one render stale, the converge writes the wrong value, and React's own restore
repairs the value and throws the caret away. So the mechanism is not reaching for
`flushSync` to make the echo land (the echo already lands without it); it is
reaching for it to make the RECORD current before the caret is restored.

What is needed is one of:
  (a) amend HD-019's clause to name the controlled converge as the evidence-gated
      case, or
  (b) rule that the converge must find another way to make the record current.

Mike's call. Nothing is blocked on it — the code and the studio page both state
the tension plainly
(docs/design/hicasso/studio/controlled-input-two-implementations.md, "One thing
for the decisions record").
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-08-02, dossier review): Option (a) — amend HD-019. The shipped converge stands; no redesign.

DECISION. HD-019's flushSync clause is amended to name the lean-React controlled-TEXT converge as the single evidence-gated exception, in the Codex review's narrower formulation (adopted over the dossier's broader "controlled elements" wording). Amended clause text:

"flushSync is never the general default. The lean-React controlled-text converge is the single evidence-gated exception: it may flush the synchronous door's pending commit before React's controlled restore so value and caret are correct when the discrete event returns."

MECHANISM (why the flush is the measured requirement, not a convenience):
- Record currency, not the echo. The echo lands without the flush (dispatch and store notification are already synchronous). The flush exists so the per-instance last-rendered record is current BEFORE React's end-of-discrete-event controlled restore runs.
- Evidence: removing only the flushSync from front.controlled/converge! reds 4 assertions, all caret readings at [5 5], INCLUDING the ordinary accepted keystroke — without it the record is one render stale, the converge writes the wrong value, and React's own restore repairs the value but throws the caret away. With it: browser lane green at 940 tests / 5,895 assertions; direct probes green in Chromium and WebKit (Codex).
- Ordering ground truth (Codex, verified against pinned React DOM 19.2.0): the outer discrete-event wrapper flushes pending sync work only in its `finally`, immediately before controlled-state restore (batchedUpdates$1); the converge runs earlier, inside the handler, so without its own flush it reads the previous commit's record. React's updateInput/updateTextarea mirror controlled commits into defaultValue, which is what makes the node-held record valid for the guarded cases.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE (the fence's purpose — no reflexive flushSync — survives):
- Exactly one audited call site: react-dom/flushSync in front.controlled/converge! (implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/controlled.cljs, currently line 210), once per keystroke, controlled text-entry input/textarea only (caret-types text/search/url/tel/password, plus textarea), non-nil :value, no authored defaultValue, an onInput/onChange handler; inert when the caret is not a number or the record not a string. Still Arm 1 bench/test-tree code, not a production-wide default.
- Any second call site, or expansion to other elements or event paths, needs fresh evidence and its own ruling.
- Graduation gates unchanged: full Chromium/WebKit G8 and the per-keystroke budget still gate this candidate leaving the test tree; no broader redesign unless a gate fails.

OPTION (b) REJECTED. Every alternative is worse by inspection: a layout-effect read re-introduces the one-frame staleness the converge exists to kill; deriving the record from the DOM value cannot distinguish a refusal from a verbatim-accepted keystroke (a measured trap, not an assumed one); a second bookkeeping channel to avoid one flush is over-engineering spent to preserve a sentence; and Codex's microtask ablation showed refusal/normalization sitting at [5 5] until the microtask — preserving pre-paint visuals but weakening the stronger contract that value and caret are correct when dispatchEvent returns.

CODEX ATTRIBUTION. Adopted: the narrower controlled-TEXT single-exception framing and the amendment wording; the React 19.2.0 finally-before-restore ordering ground; the microtask-alternative rejection; the honest cost note (flushSync's documented hazards; the dependence on React mirroring controlled text into defaultValue — the named live-tree invariant test remains the tripwire, and it is not a public React guarantee). Nothing material rejected; one caveat re-weighted: Codex's "not the full IME matrix" applies to its own direct WebKit probe — the repo's IME composition witness row (composing?/keyCode-229) stands and continues to gate.

WHERE IT LANDS + DISPATCH. A small dedicated docs PR, not riding on a future PR touching the record (nothing else is queued at HD-019, and the record and shipped behaviour currently disagree in letter). Two-file edit: (1) docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md — replace HD-019's "the evidence-gated last resort, never the default" clause with the amended text above, citing rf2-ncn5p + rf2-fki5d as the evidence trail; (2) docs/design/hicasso/studio/controlled-input-two-implementations.md — update the "One thing for the decisions record" section from raised-tension to a pointer at the amendment. docs/design is outside the hot zone; parallel-safe. This bead is now DISPATCHABLE for that PR — the "Mike's call" hold is released by this delegated ruling.

Studio page and validation.md were already reconciled by the rf2-o27h3 work — verified, left alone. Filed rf2-dfz6f (P3, blocked on rf2-digtt) for the SOURCE of the R-A2 wording in docs/design/freehand/studio/fitness-harness.md, which states an IME property no implementation satisfies.
