title: SSR: a coarse :redact / :omit hydrated row is also unaddressable and also persists
description:
Found while closing rf2-rjq9d (PR for the per-slot :key-projected arm).

rf2-rjq9d removed the row a per-slot :scope / :params declaration re-keys, because it hydrates as an ownerless, unaddressable, uncollectable duplicate. The COARSE :redact / :omit arms leave a row of the SAME class, and this PR deliberately did not touch them.

project-scoped-key replaces a coarse resource's scope and params with content-addressed {:rf/redacted <digest>} tokens, so the wire row installs under the DIGEST key-id. route-resource-plan and ensure-handler derive the ordinary scoped key and read (state/entry-path scoped-key) — the RAW key-id. So the coarse hydrated row is not addressed either, and, like the per-slot one, nothing collects it: inactive GC is timer-driven (gc-fired-handler fires against a handle armed by a commit fx) and hydration arms no timers. The new no-unaddressable-row-survives-hydration control in resources_ssr_projected_key_refetch_cljs_test PINS this: its exact expected key-id set names the two coarse rows under their PROJECTED key-ids beside three raw ones.

Why it was fenced out of rf2-rjq9d rather than folded in: the two arms are NOT the same hazard. The per-slot substitution is a CONSTANT sentinel, so it is many-to-one on precisely the slots that name a principal — two tenants collapse to one key, which is why no client may adopt by it and why removal was the only option. A coarse token is a content-addressed digest of the canonical value: one-to-one, and DERIVABLE in principle, since redact-value is a pure function of the live value the client already holds. So the coarse arm has a repair the per-slot arm does not.

Decide which contract the coarse arm should have, and make hydrate agree with it:
  (a) ADOPT — the client re-derives the digest from its live scope/params and reads the row under the projected key-id, turning the row into the cache hit it was presumably meant to be. Note this is a real behaviour change: these rows are metadata-only, so the win is the metadata, not data reuse.
  (b) DROP — treat it as rf2-rjq9d treats the per-slot row: withhold or drop, and let the client's one load stand.
Whichever is chosen, the acceptance criterion rf2-rjq9d was reopened for — no persistent unreachable duplicate — should hold for these rows too, and the end-to-end control should assert absence of the ROW rather than absence of its contents (the assertion shape that let rf2-rjq9d through).

Do not weaken key privacy: the raw scope/params must not ride, and the digest must stay one-way on the wire.
close_reason: Completed by merged PR #7391: coarse re-keyed rows are withheld server-side, dropped client-side, omitted from the refetch plan, and the host FNV arithmetic is aligned. Audit remainder rf2-hzcv8 owns the newly exposed off-box privacy/canonicalization defect without changing this locked scope.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7369 (2026-08-02) — the per-slot ghost removal is sound, but this owner’s coarse-token premise needs correction before choosing ADOPT.

PR #7369 deliberately exempts coarse `{:rf/redacted <digest>}` keys from `unaddressable-wire-key?`, and Spec 016 now calls that token “one-to-one and derivable in principle.” The current `redact-value` does not provide either property:

* Its CLJ branch hashes UTF-8 bytes with exact integer arithmetic; its CLJS branch hashes UTF-16 code units and multiplies 32-bit states with ordinary JS `*` rather than `Math.imul`. Even ASCII diverges: the landed CLJ `redact-value` maps `"tenant"` to `f93325e5`, while the CLJS branch’s source arithmetic maps the same `pr-str` bytes/text to `74e22aec`. Unicode has the additional UTF-8-vs-UTF-16 disagreement. A client therefore cannot re-derive the server token as option (a) assumes.
* FNV-1a-32 is a 32-bit non-cryptographic hash: it is necessarily many-to-one, reaches birthday collisions at roughly 2^16 distinct identities, and is brute-forceable for low-entropy tenant/account identifiers. The descriptions “one-to-one,” “never a collision,” “opaque,” and “one-way” are not true security properties of this token.

This does not undo #7369’s removal of constant-sentinel rows; it constrains rf2-4bjep’s coarse-row settlement. Acceptance should include a byte-identical CLJ/CLJS tokenizer fixture (ASCII, non-ASCII, surrogate pair), an explicit collision/privacy contract appropriate for identity-bearing scope/params, and no ADOPT path until the client can derive exactly the server’s token without making low-entropy identities enumerable. DROP remains available if durable metadata reuse is not worth a stronger token.

title: UNEXPLAINED: run 3's 34% bulk300 floor seam is beyond 38,000 null draws AND beyond every load-ladder rung
description:
LEFT UNEXPLAINED by rf2-cvvb7 (PR #7360), which refused to smooth it over. Filed so it is not quietly forgotten.

WHAT rf2-cvvb7 ESTABLISHED, and it is a strong negative result. A load ladder of 19 runs at a STATED number of competing busy cores (0/2/4/8/12/20 of 24) found the cross-segment floor seam DOES NOT RESPOND TO LOAD AT ALL: 4.3% at zero cores, 4.6% at twenty, while the ladder unquestionably moved the box (floor +80%). Not a threshold, not a gradient, not bimodal. It is also NOT segment-attributable — under an exact within-round relabelling null, no run reached p < 0.2 and every observed seam sat at or below the null's median (5.5%; q95 14.1%). The variation lives on the ROUND, not the segment. And the perturbation is MULTIPLICATIVE, so floor-normalisation cancels it exactly: ctl-2x/floor moved 6.5% across an 80% floor span and moved the WRONG WAY for additivity (corr +0.41), while the bar row moved with neither the floor (-0.10) nor the seam (-0.18).

SO THE ORIGINAL PREMISE IS REFUTED: the seam is not what a loaded box does to the three-segment design. Section 6's ground 3 is withdrawn as refuted; the bulk rows stay refused on the grounds that hold.

WHAT REMAINS UNEXPLAINED: run 3's bulk300 read 3.147 / 2.437 / 2.349 ms across the three segments — a 34% spread. That figure is BEYOND ALL 38,000 NULL DRAWS and BEYOND EVERY LADDER RUNG. Nothing in 19 controlled runs reproduced it. The worker had no mechanism for it and said so rather than inventing one.

WHY IT IS WORTH KEEPING OPEN: a bench lane that produced a value its own null model says is essentially impossible has either (a) a rare regime nobody has characterised, (b) a defect that fired once, or (c) a recording or attribution error in that run. All three matter. If it is (a), the band that rf2-cvvb7 introduced may not bound it. Note ALSO that the clock-audit page's 31.9% seam is a SINGLE-ROUND figure and therefore routine — the same worker saw 45% in one round of an IDLE run whose pooled seam was 3.8% — so the audit corroborates the observation but not the load attribution, and does not explain run 3 either.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: recover run 3's per-round vectors if they survive anywhere (the producing worktree may be gone; check transcripts before concluding they are lost — that is how rf2-b0tz5's observations were recovered). If the raw record is unrecoverable, say so and mark the figure as an unreproduced outlier rather than reconstructing it. DO NOT re-take the ensemble to chase it; the operator has deferred measurement and the band already bounds published rows honestly.

SEQUENCING: low priority. It is a loose end on an instrument question that is otherwise settled, and it must not displace rf2-yd52q (the bulk-broad re-take) or rf2-rguy1 (the external cross-check).
close_reason: CLOSED PER THE BEAD'S OWN INSTRUCTION — triage 2026-08-07. The bead itself says: 'if the raw record is unrecoverable, say so and mark it an unreproduced outlier ... DO NOT re-take the ensemble.' The raw record is unrecoverable, so the bead's own terminal branch is the disposition. Recorded here as the required saying-so: run 3's 34% bulk300 floor seam stands as an UNREPRODUCED OUTLIER, beyond 38,000 null draws and beyond every load-ladder rung, cause unestablished. Leaving it open invited exactly the ensemble re-take it forbids.

title: hicasso: a first registration inside the render->commit gap is pinned, not repaired
description:
FOUND while closing rf2-2rtt6.44's audit remainder (PR: worker/firstreg-2rtt6-44). Filed rather than left implied, and PINNED by an assertion rather than argued.

rf2-2rtt6.44 closed the MOUNTED case: a boundary that already holds a cell for a query registered for the first time now reaches the new computation and is notified by later writes, off registrar/add-registration-hook! funnelled into invalidate-cell!.

THE NEIGHBOURING CASE IS NOT CLOSED, and cannot be by the same route. A first registration landing in the RENDER->COMMIT GAP -- the body has returned nil, the registration lands, and only then does React run the effect that acquires the edge -- reaches NO CELL, because the boundary does not have one yet. first-registration! scans @!cells and finds nothing to invalidate. The epoch sum cannot report it either: a key with no cell contributes its frame's commit-basis, and a reg-sub moves neither term of it (that is exactly what generation_fence_coverage_cljs_test row 3 pins for a re-registration). So React's post-subscribe getSnapshot re-check reads the number the fiber captured at render, sees no tear, and schedules nothing.

MEASURED, and asserted as a deliberately-* row in arm1/first_registration_cljs_test:
  - the snapshot does not move across the commit;
  - the boundary is not notified (0);
  - BUT the cell the commit acquired holds the REAL handler (derefs 1, not nil).

So the cost is a DELAYED PAINT, not a retired computation: the boundary is correct from its next render onwards, and the next write to the frame notifies it. That asymmetry is why this is a P3 record and not a defect fix.

WHAT CLOSING IT WOULD COST, so the decision is costed rather than open:
  (a) the registry term in every key's contribution to getSnapshot -- the option rf2-2rtt6.44 costed and DECLINED (up to 15 whole-tree concurrent-render invalidations per HMR save, for zero correction in the mounted case). It WOULD correct this one, because here the extra render reads back through a cell that is alive and correct. That is a genuine argument the earlier costing did not have to answer, and it is the reason this bead exists.
  (b) recording what a read returned, so the commit can compare -- a fence Arm 1 exists to hold ("no commit-phase deref"; getSnapshot "holds no record of what any read returned").

Neither is obviously right, so this wants a ruling, not a worker.

REACHABILITY, honestly: needs a first-time reg-sub to land strictly inside one boundary's render->commit gap. That is a lazily-loaded module or a boot-order race, not steady state; and any subsequent write to the frame clears it.
close_reason:
Closed by PR #7411 (worker/rcgap-2rtt6-50).

RULED AS A FIX, NOT A RULING, AND THE BEAD'S OWN COSTING IS WHY. The bead
enumerated two closures and rejected both, then asked for a ruling. Option (b)
(recording what a read returned) is genuinely closed at Arm 1's fences and stays
closed. Option (a) was costed against the WRONG SHAPE, and that is the finding.

rf2-2rtt6.44 priced 'a registry term in every key's contribution to getSnapshot'.
But make-snapshot reads live in exactly ONE branch: a HELD key contributes its
cell's FROZEN stamp, and only a STAGED key reads commit-basis live. So a registry
term placed in commit-basis reaches precisely the keys inside a render->commit gap
and moves NO mounted boundary's snapshot. The 15-invalidations-per-HMR-save cost
does not materialise: an HMR save is a RE-registration, which reaches mounted
boundaries via invalidate-cell! with their cells still in !cells and their stamps
still frozen.

The proof is in the file already: the bill row
a-first-registration-of-an-id-no-cell-holds-disturbs-nothing asserts a mounted
boundary's snapshot does not move on an unrelated reg-sub, and it is UNCHANGED and
still green under the new term. That is the assertion that separates the option
taken from the option declined.

SHIPPED: commit-basis gains a third term, the arm's own :sub registration count,
bumped on the registration hook the arm already installs for first-registration!
(sub-registered!). Counted for first-time AND replacement, since both are the same
defect in the gap. observation/registry-epoch* stays ^:private; no substrate
namespace touched; no React hook (ledger still 2 at React's dispatcher); no
per-boundary object; subscribe still closes over the read set alone. Failure
direction is safe by construction — a monotone term added to a monotone sum can
only cause EXTRA renders, never a missed one. The :node-key axis stays open and
stays invalidate-cell!'s (the basis TIES across a same-id reincarnation).

PIN FLIPPED IN THE SAME COMMIT AS THE FIX (they are mutually invalidating):
  deliberately-a-first-registration-in-the-render-commit-gap-moves-no-snapshot
  -> a-first-registration-in-the-render-commit-gap-moves-the-snapshot
Two consequent renames: the-commit-basis-has-no-registry-epoch-axis ->
the-commit-basis-registry-axis-reaches-a-staged-key-and-not-a-held-one, and
closing-the-first-registration-cost-no-hook-and-nothing-in-the-snapshot ->
...-and-no-per-boundary-object (the snapshot arithmetic DID gain a term).

MUTATION-PROVED BOTH LANES by deleting the single term and reverting
byte-identically: test:cljs exit 1 with 3 assertions in exactly 2 named rows;
test:browser exit 1 with exactly ONE named row, actual (not (= ":arrived" "")) —
"" is (str nil), the delayed paint observed in real Chromium.

GATES (foreground, unpiped, worktree-local logs): test-fast-pr.sh exit 0;
test:browser exit 0 (1025/6337/0/0); test:cljs exit 0 (12424/62032/0/0).

NOT DONE, deliberately: docs/design/hicasso/hd-002-adjudication.md 6.1 is a dated
adjudication record already superseded by rf2-2rtt6.42/.44 without rewrite; left
alone rather than re-litigated.

title: build: a --config-merge focused compile poisons the shared node-test build cache
description:
SPLIT OUT of rf2-hofhx (its "SECOND, SMALLER FINDING"), left unfixed there
deliberately: the fix belongs in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, a hot-zone
file, and rf2-hofhx's PR touched only test-quiet test sources. Sequencing it
separately avoids a hot-zone conflict with the five clusters in flight.

SYMPTOM. A focused compile of the node-test build via

    shadow-cljs compile node-test --config-merge '{:ns-regexp "..."}'

shares the `node-test` build id with the full compile, so it leaves the build
cache in a mixed state. The NEXT full compile dies with

    aborted par-compile ... still waiting for ...

and no root error, which reads like a compiler bug rather than a stale cache.

CLASS. Identical to the rule the bench drivers already implement in
lane_cache.cjs: one build id driven with N different configs must clear the
cache between configs.

FIX, either of:
  - document it on the :node-test build in shadow-cljs.edn (cheapest), or
  - clear the cache automatically when a --config-merge is detected.

CONFIRMED still current while working rf2-hofhx (2026-08-01): the workaround
used there was simply never to run a focused compile on the shared build id,
and to select namespaces at RUNTIME instead (`node out/node-test.js
--test=<ns>`), which needs no recompile and cannot poison the cache. That
runtime-selector route is worth naming in whatever documentation lands.
notes:
AUDIT REOPEN — merged PR #7400 (2026-08-03).

CORRECTNESS. `scripts/compile-node-test.cjs` handles `result.status !== 0` by returning `result.status`. Node's spawn result uses `status: null` when a child is terminated by signal; the top-level `process.exit(main(...))` then treats that null as exit 0. A dynamic audit proof against the real exported `main` (with only its captured spawnSync result replaced by `{status:null, signal:'SIGTERM'}`) printed `did not complete (exit null)`, returned null, and the wrapper process exited 0. The output bundle is still removed, so today's `compile && node bundle` npm chains eventually red on the missing bundle, but the compile wrapper itself falsely reports success—precisely unsafe for the unchained compile caller this bead documents.

COMPLETENESS / IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY. No regression test references `compile-node-test.cjs`; the PR's green full compile exercises only the success path. Keep this bounded: map every signal/null-status termination to a nonzero wrapper exit, name `result.signal` in the diagnostic, and add a focused dynamic regression test that proves the real wrapper cannot exit 0 for that case (while retaining the stale-output deletion invariant). The browser drift-waiver half of #7400 is independently complete and remains owned by closed rf2-u0cy4.
close_reason: MAYOR RE-CLOSE 2026-08-03. This bead was closed when its PR merged, then REVERTED TO OPEN by a tracker-state rollback (the same class as rf2-rjqtj / rf2-51uz1 — five early closes reverted while every later one held). Re-verified before re-closing: PR #7400 is MERGED and 1 commit(s) naming this bead are on origin/main. No work is outstanding from the original scope; if an audit later reopens it for a NEW obligation, that reopen is legitimate and separate from this rollback.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
REPRODUCED 2026-08-01 WITHOUT any --config-merge, so the bead's premise is
incomplete: heavy box load alone is sufficient.

While measuring rf2-hofhx, a plain `npx shadow-cljs compile node-test` (no
--config-merge, no focused ns-regexp) run against a box deliberately
oversubscribed with 32 CPU burners + 6 I/O loops on 24 cores died with:

  aborted par-compile, [:shadow.build.classpath/resource
    "re_frame/ssr_keyword_head_contract_cljs_test.cljs"]
    still waiting for #{reagent.dom.server}
  {:aborted [...], :pending #{reagent.dom.server}}

An identical compile on the same tree minutes earlier, on a quiet box,
succeeded in 42s. So this is a par-compile thread-pool starvation under
load, not only a cache-config mismatch.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE ORIGINAL FRAMING. The failure is silent in the
worst way for an automated run: the script that invoked it continued (no
`&&`), the STALE `out/node-test.js` from the previous compile was still on
disk, and the suite then ran happily against the wrong bundle. A measurement
harness that does not check the compile's exit code will therefore report
numbers for code it did not build. Recovery was `rm -rf
.shadow-cljs/builds/node-test` followed by a compile on a quiet box.

Suggests the fix wants two parts: whatever cache handling the bead already
proposes, AND that callers treat a nonzero compile exit as fatal rather than
proceeding to run a stale artefact.

title: hicasso: establish the IME composition fence with a real CompositionEvent harness, on both input implementations
description:
STILL NOT ESTABLISHED, and now against TWO implementations rather than one.

Arm 2 owned a composition fence because it owned the writes. On React the row
`:ime-composition-commits-nothing` was probed with synthetic `Event`s named
`compositionstart`/`compositionend`; those do not exercise React's composition
path, and the field never converged after `compositionend` in that probe. It was
deliberately left unasserted, because a fence asserted without being
demonstrated is worse than no fence (rf2-n3dxw, rf2-m6if4).

WHAT CHANGED. There are two controlled-input implementations in play, not one
(rf2-heqwo), and they face composition differently:

- plain React: `SyntheticCompositionEvent` plumbing on a controlled element,
  with React's own `beforeinput`/composition fallback deciding whether a change
  event is produced at all.
- UIx's port of Reagent's workaround: owns the write itself and never consults
  composition state — `input-handle-change` fires on every change, and
  `input-node-set-value` will rewrite the field mid-composition if the model
  moved (`uix/compiler/input.cljs:81-88`, `:28-69`).

WHAT IS NEEDED: a harness that dispatches real `CompositionEvent`s (and the
`input` events a composing IME actually produces, with the right
`inputType`/`isComposing`), against BOTH implementations, before anything is
claimed. `document.execCommand`-style synthesis and `js/Event.` with a
composition name are both insufficient; Playwright's CDP `Input.imeSetComposition`
is the likeliest route on Chromium.

Until then the row stays unasserted in
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/controlled_restore_dom_cljs_test.cljs,
and validation.md no longer lists it as an asserted row of the controlled grid.
close_reason: Completed by merged PR #7386: the landed CDP-driven harness establishes the IME commit fence across Hicasso, plain React, and the UIx port; rf2-digtt already owns the measured mid-composition rewrite ruling.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7371 — this owner's composition matrix now has a third behavior to cover. The PR says the converge “touches composition” nowhere because it wraps only the change slot, but `install!` wraps `onInput`/`onChange` — precisely the input events a composing IME produces — and every invocation calls `flushSync` and then `setSelectionRange`, even when no value write is needed. That can collapse the active composition range or rewrite a refused/normalised intermediate value. Extend the real CompositionEvent/CDP harness to Hicasso Arm 1's new converge as well as plain React and UIx, and pin that it neither writes nor moves selection mid-composition. Exact existing owner updated; no duplicate.

title: hicasso: the DOM suites' residue gates cannot fail -- mount/release! resets the runtime before the assertion, and React-driven teardown is unwitnessed
description:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF LANDED CODE, origin/main @ 40e309600e (arm1 last touched by 7e40db6481).

`mount/release!` calls `rt/reset-runtime!` (arm1/mount.cljs:65-76), which drops every cell,
entry, edge and boundary (arm1/runtime.cljs:962-980) — BEFORE the assertion runs. So:

  - `the-screen-leaves-no-residue` (arm1/dogfood_dom_cljs_test.cljs:344-355), and
  - `the-fenced-boundary-leaves-no-residue` (arm1/generation_fence_dom_cljs_test.cljs:219-227)

both assert `{:cells 0 :cell-refs 0 :boundaries 0 :edges 0 :entries 0}` against a table the line
above just emptied. They cannot fail. A gate nobody has watched fire is not evidence.

The property IS genuinely witnessed at the node seam, through `commit-boundary!` with an `async`
macrotask horizon (arm1/runtime_cljs_test.cljs:462-499) — that pair is real and should be kept.
But that seam is NOT React. The stronger statement: NO SUITE WITNESSES THAT REACT'S OWN CLEANUP
RELEASES EVERYTHING. That is the path that runs in production, and it is the path a re-subscribe
cycle exercises on every read-set change (see rf2-2rtt6.47).

studio/arm1-lean-react-dogfood-judgement.md:176-180 states the opposite — "every DOM suite
asserts the same after its mount" — and needs correcting with whatever this bead lands.

FIX: assert the residue between the root unmount and `reset-runtime!` (either split `release!`
into `unmount!` + `reset!`, or take the reading inside `release!` before the reset and expose it),
and add the macrotask horizon so the cell/entry reapers have run. Then the DOM gate says what it
claims. Worth adding a deliberately-planted-fault check (as
`lane_release_dom_cljs_test.cljs` does for the lane's own residue gate) so the repaired gate is
shown to be able to answer false.
close_reason: Closed

title: Hicasso: reserve :ref's vector value-space now, refuse it loudly in v0, so the imperative escape can become data later
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained; do not rely on any untracked findings file).

This is a ONE-BRANCH design constraint, deliberately NOT a subsystem. It exists so
that Hicasso's best available lifecycle spelling stays reachable after v0 instead of
being designed out.

WHERE HICASSO STANDS TODAY. HD-003 (docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md:83-86) rules the
v0 answer for imperative mechanics as "component mechanics (composition, measurement,
focus, animation, SDK handles) may use ORDINARY REACT HOOKS at the honest escape
hatch", and HD-016 (decisions.md:337-339) makes :ref "legal on native tags and
defhost/[:>] crossings (CALLBACK REFS ONLY)". That is defensible: the corpus census
finds ONE :ref in 85 idiomatic files
(docs/design/freehand/studio/fitness-harness.md:336).

BUT IT IS THE ONE PLACE HICASSO IS PLANNED TO BE *LESS* DATA-ORIENTED THAN THE
SUBSTRATE IT REPLACES. Freehand's registered behaviors keep the USE SITE as data and
put the code in a registry — implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/behaviors.cljc:48,
"the use site is data all the way down and the implementation is registered code":

    [v/behavior {:use autosize :target :composer/body :config {:max-rows 8}}
     [:textarea.composer ...]]

with :config refusing a callback, a node, a ref or a host instance on both hosts
(docs/core/freehand/host/host-boundaries.md:211-213).

THE PROPOSAL (all of it). :ref accepts:
  - a function                       -> v0, the HD-003 escape hatch, unchanged
  - a vector [registered-id config]  -> RESERVED. v0 REFUSES IT LOUDLY with a
                                        diagnostic naming the reservation, rather than
                                        passing it to React as an opaque value.

That is the whole bead. One refusal branch and one error id. It costs nothing and it
keeps {:ref [::autosize {:max-rows 8}]} reachable without minting a second attribute
name later.

WHY THE LATER SPELLING IS MECHANICALLY SOUND — verified from react.dev
(react-dom/components/common, fetched 2026-07-31):
  - "React 19 added cleanup functions for ref callbacks."
  - "optional cleanup function: When the ref is detached, React will call the cleanup
     function."
  - on mount: "When the DOM node is added to the screen, React calls your ref callback
     with the DOM node as the argument."
  - on update: "React calls your ref callback whenever you pass a DIFFERENT ref
     callback."
  - Strict Mode: "React runs one extra development-only setup+cleanup cycle before the
     first real setup."

So a RUNTIME-minted ref callback is a complete attach/detach pair, with the node, in
the commit phase, and NO ref object or effect ever appears in user code. Three
obligations follow from those quotes and must be recorded when the later bead lands:
  1. the minted callback's identity must be STABLE PER SITE or React detaches and
     reattaches every render (this is Freehand's site-owned stable proxy —
     docs/core/freehand/authoring/events-and-handlers.md:404-414);
  2. connect/disconnect must be IDEMPOTENT because StrictMode adds a cycle;
  3. timing is commit-before-paint only, so Freehand's :passive (after paint) has NO
     ref-callback equivalent (behaviors.cljc:141 closes timings at #{:passive :layout}).

AND THE REAL GAP, STATED HONESTLY SO NOBODY REDISCOVERS IT: a ref callback fires on
ATTACH and DETACH, never on CONFIG CHANGE. Freehand's :update — "only when the
committed :config moves by rf=, receiving :prev-config alongside"
(host-boundaries.md:226) — has no equivalent without either changing the callback
identity (which detaches and reattaches the node owner: wrong for a Mapbox instance)
or spending an effect. The recommended later shape is attach/detach only, config

title: Reconcile validation.md's 'unstable map args thrash the index' shorthand
description:

The sentence (validation.md, 'The budgets' section, immediately after the budget table):

  Sub-key identity: (query-id, args) under value equality; unstable map args
  thrash the index -- documented, programmer-trusted.

'unstable' is ambiguous between reference-unstable and value-unstable. Under value equality only the latter churns: a freshly allocated but = -equal map is one cache key. The draft guide (02-views-and-reads.md) now states the correct reading and notes it is reporting a sibling page's wording it does not own; this bead removes that note's reason to exist.

Small, isolated, single-sentence edit to one normative file.

title: The reactive leg (headline 1) still has one witness: give reagent-ratom a second author
description:
RAISED BY rf2-2rtt6.17 (PR #7277), which was the audit's own item (d): 'consider whether the reactive leg deserves a second witness at all — one measurement is thin for the term the whole bar's like-for-like clause turns on.'

STATE AFTER rf2-2rtt6.17. Headline 1 — 'reading re-frame2 subscriptions rather than a bare cursor costs Reagent ~1.22x on mount and ~2.01x on a broad commit' — is now measured THREE TIMES rather than once:

  M1 mount reactive leg   1.218 [1.122-1.310] | 1.216 [1.185-1.241] | 1.213 [1.093-1.273]
  bulk broad reactive leg 2.008 [1.938-2.100] | 1.965 [1.875-2.000] | 2.073 [2.000-2.167]

publication run, plus two independent five-round re-runs at main 32cb224d6e. All disjoint from 1.0; the mount means sit inside 0.5% of each other.

WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT BUY. Three runs of ONE arm bound the instrument's run-to-run noise. They do NOT bound a systematic error in how :reagent-ratom is written — the same code produces the same bias every time. That is repetition, not replication.

THE GAP IS SPECIFIC. The converged witness set (rf2-a4x1o) IS a genuine second implementation of the DENOMINATOR: a different app namespace, a different schedule, and its reagent-subs/floor ranges overlap rf2-2rtt6.2's on all three shared rows. But it carries NO reagent-ratom ARM, so it corroborates the denominator and cannot touch the reactive leg at all. Every other P0 arm is likewise silent on it.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a reagent-ratom arm on the converged witness set (or any second author's page), measured beside its reagent-subs arm in the same run, so subs/ratom can be formed a second way. That is one arm on an existing instrument, not a new page.

The denominator page now states this limitation in its own 'What this settles, and what it does not' section rather than leaving it implicit, so nothing is currently overclaimed. This bead is the remedy, not a correction.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7310 — completeness / correctness / implementation quality.

The published M1/broad experiment is unusually well warranted: the ratom arm is opt-in, the measured rows share a segment and floor, starts are counterbalanced, per-round vectors and Student-t run intervals are durable, parity/read-back/control/order gates are fail-closed, the same-tree first-harness control is explicit, and the three authored patches landed exactly around unrelated chronological commits. The direction/magnitude distinction is also honest. Two implementation gaps remain under this exact owner.

The feature flag is global while arm presence is row-specific. With no `HICASSO_ONLY`, the driver intentionally selects all four rows; `HICASSO_RATOM=on` then reaches M2 and narrow. Those rows deliberately omit `:reagent-ratom` (`M2` ignores the flag and `bulk-arms` adds it only for `:broad`), but `row-record` still uses the global `ratom?` to divide by `[:reagent-subs :ratio :reagent-ratom]`, form `ratom-floor`, run the leg verdict, and label the row as carrying the arm. The natural flagged default therefore computes from a missing denominator (error or Infinity/NaN evidence) even though the driver says M2/narrow carry no ratom arm. Published runs avoided this only by always pairing `HICASSO_RATOM=on` with `HICASSO_ONLY=M1,broad`; neither CI nor the quality gates exercise the default flagged invocation.

The new replay test also asserts only `min(second-author rounds) > 1.24` while its diagnostic says 1.2500 exceeds first-author maxima 1.241 *and 1.273*. It does not exceed 1.273. The supported claim is that every second-author run mean exceeds every first-author mean; round ranges overlap, as the studio page correctly reports. The test message and threshold currently make a false round-level claim look pinned.

Bounded repair: decide leg presence from the actual row/slice (M1 or broad with a `:reagent-ratom` ratio), or reject flagged selections containing M2/narrow; add a cheap contract test for `HICASSO_RATOM=on` with the default rows and with M2/narrow-only, proving those rows emit no leg and no non-finite values. Rewrite the replay assertion to pin run-mean separation, or retract the round-level diagnostic. The published M1/broad measurements need not be re-run for either repair.

title: HD-008's batched narrow window prices its microtask asymmetry as 10x an unresolved quantity; batch the yield-cost control the same way
description:
P0 AUDIT FINDING (read-only cold read of the P0 baseline wave, 2026-07-31).

HD-008'S BATCHED NARROW WINDOW BOUNDS ITS OWN ASYMMETRY BY MULTIPLYING AN UNRESOLVED QUANTITY BY TEN, AND THE PAGE'S OWN NEW TECHNIQUE IS THE FIX.

docs/design/hicasso/studio/hd8-composed-donor-arm.md, Known limitations, after the rf2-9zysg batched re-take (PR #7270):

  "The batched window also contains TEN harness microtasks for every arm except the microtask-scheduled one, which contains none; each such turn measures 0.0 ms against this clock, so the asymmetry is TEN TIMES A QUANTITY BELOW THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN RESOLUTION."

Ten times an unresolved quantity is not unresolved -- which is the exact argument that justified batching the writes in the first place ("timing k operations as ONE window lifts the sample clear of the clamp, and it is NOT the same as summing k separately-clamped readings"). hd8-rows/yield-cost! reads p50 0.0, min 0.0, max 0.0 over n=10 against Chrome's 100 us clamp. That bounds ONE turn at < 100 us. It bounds TEN turns at < 1.0 ms, not at "below resolution".

WHY THAT BOUND IS NOT COMFORTABLE HERE. The batched narrow sample is 3.8-7.6 ms, so up to ~1.0 ms is up to ~26% of the window -- and it falls on EVERY ARM EXCEPT reagent-slim, which is the arm being read against the others on this very row:

  reagent-slim  4.222 - 5.944 x floor      (window contains ZERO harness microtasks)
  donor-r1      5.182 - 6.790 x floor      (ten)
  donor-r2      5.400 - 6.579 x floor      (ten)
  reagent       4.130 - 6.947 x floor      (ten)

An unpriced term that is present in three columns and absent from the fourth, bounded only at up to a quarter of the window, is the shape of thing that decides whether reagent-slim reads faster than the donor rungs. HD-008 is the donor gate, so that comparison is the point of the row.

THE REPAIR IS THE PAGE'S OWN BATCHING TECHNIQUE, applied to the control rather than only to the arms: price TEN yields inside ONE clock window (as yield-cost! already does for one), report the per-turn figure as sample/10, and either state the resulting number or subtract it. That turns "below resolution x 10" into a measurement. It is a small change to hd8_rows/yield-cost! and does not touch any arm's window, so no published row moves and no re-run of the arms is needed -- only the control is re-read.

SECOND-ORDER, worth stating in the same pass: the same reasoning applies wherever a sub-quantum per-item cost is asserted to be negligible across a batch. lane/verified-write!'s :gap-ms is priced per window; if a future arm batches k operations under one clock on the shared lane, the same multiplication appears there.

NOT A CLAIM THAT THE PUBLISHED NARROW ROWS ARE WRONG. The batch demonstrably did what it was for -- the floor moved from one-to-one-and-a-half quanta to nine-to-twelve, the per-write absolutes reproduce the unbatched run (reagent-slim 0.380-0.535 against 0.40-0.60 published), the guard did not refuse, the positive control passes HD-008's strict every-round-inside rule on all three runs, and 0 unverified of 780 on every arm. The defect is one sentence of arithmetic in the limitations section, and it is load-bearing because it is the only thing standing between the reader and a subtraction.

Files: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/hd8_rows.cljs (yield-cost!, window-of, arm-scheduler), docs/design/hicasso/studio/hd8-composed-donor-arm.md.

Related, no duplicate: rf2-pq7d8 (CLOSED) lifted the two-shape window into lane/verified-write!; rf2-9zysg (CLOSED) owns the batch itself. This is the control that was not batched with it.

Nothing here amends the bar, the budgets, the kill criteria, the red-zones or the clock.

title: lane/verified-write!: the fixed microtask yield is not neutral across scheduler families
description:
lane/verified-write! yields exactly one microtask between the write and the arm's force!, for every arm. Its docstring justifies the yield — "load-bearing for any arm whose notification is queued rather than synchronous", priced in situ as :gap-ms — and that justification is correct for the React-hook arms. It is NOT neutral.

rf2-z3vlz established that for a substrate whose OWN render scheduler is a microtask queue (reagent-slim: reagent2.impl.batching), the harness's yield hands the commit to React before the drain runs, and the arm reads N unverified of N while the DOM is in fact merely LATE. Stock Reagent is immune only because its queue is rAF-scheduled. So the one shared yield cannot serve both scheduler families, and the harness silently produces a precise wrong number for one of them — the sixteenth instrument fault on these surfaces, and the same shape as the fifteen before it.

Proposed (additive, no behaviour change for any existing arm): let an arm declare a :drain-with! slot. When present, verified-write! composes (drain-with! write!) with NO microtask gap and reports :gap-ms 0.0 with the window's meaning stated; when absent, today's path is byte-for-byte unchanged. The docstring should name the hazard by scheduler family rather than leaving it to be rediscovered.

NOT done under rf2-z3vlz on purpose: lane.cljs is a shared instrument with six live worker checkouts at the time of filing, and the arm that needs the slot (hd8_rows) is not on main, so the change would land unexercised and conflict-prone. Evidence and the exact composition are recorded in docs/design/hicasso/studio/slim-non-reactive-arm-diagnosis.md; the standalone rig that pins it is implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/z3vlz_*.
close_reason: PR #7280. The engineering was already done by 86188c93fa; this closed the two claims that said otherwise. hd8_rows/window-of's docstring and hd8-composed-donor-arm.md now describe the landed shape (an arm declares :scheduler; :microtask = write-then-drain, nothing between; anything else or absent = today's window unchanged), keeping the reason it was not made in the same pass. ALSO corrected the page's Known-limitations bullet, which forward-referenced this bead as where the two-shape asymmetry gets settled: it landed and did NOT settle it, it carried BOTH shapes into the lane. No re-engineering, prose only, NO NUMBER MOVED (no arm outside HD-008 declares :scheduler).

title: Consolidate the HD-008 donor arm onto lane.cljs's batched window and multi-probe read-back
description:
rf2-2rtt6.7's HD-008 instrument was written before rf2-2rtt6.2's shared lane landed on main. It now sits in the lane's directory and uses lane.cljs for mount/release/parity/across-rounds/slot-order/now-ms/summarise, but it still carries its own round driver, its own verified-write and its own positive control.

Two of the lane's mechanisms are genuinely better and should be adopted:

1. lane/mount-batch! - Chrome clamps performance.now() to 100us. The HD-008 write-narrow row reads p50s of ~0.4-1.2 ms, i.e. 4-12 quanta, and its published ranges are correspondingly wide (uix 4.500-8.000 x floor). Timing k operations as ONE window lifts the sample clear of the clamp. The mount rows (4-13 ms) are unaffected.

2. lane/verified-write! multi-probe read-back - HD-008 verifies ONE cell per write. The lane verifies a SEQ of probes including the far end of the grid, because a stale page can still carry one fresh cell from the previous write, so a single probe can pass a partial commit. HD-008's bulk row (:all) probes only cell 0.

Also adoptable: lane/ratio-between (HD-008 has its own head-to-head), lane/tally, lane/control-verdict, lane/guard! + lane's CLJS-side verdict (HD-008 adjudicates in the driver instead).

Neither gap invalidates the published HD-008 rows - the guard passed all twelve, the positive control passed in all three runs, and 156 of 936 writes were flagged unverified and SUPPRESSED rather than published. But the narrow-write ranges are wider than they need to be and the bulk read-back is thinner than the lane's.

title: SSR durable wire key ignores a :scope-rooted declaration (only the params component is registry-projected)
description:
Found while landing rf2-dl7bz (trace/tool key honours a :serialize owner's per-slot declarations).

WHAT DOES NOT HAPPEN. `classification/instance-declaration-paths` lowers a `:scope`-rooted declaration to the entry's ABSOLUTE `[:rf.runtime/resources :entries <key-id> :resource/key 0 …]` path — index 0 of the scoped key, the scope component — exactly as it lowers a `:params`-rooted one to index 2. The epoch/registry walk over the runtime-db therefore honours it.

But `ssr/project-entry` projects ONLY index 2:

    projected-key (if (= :serialize disposition)
                    (let [[scope rid params] projected-key]
                      [scope rid (classification/project-entry-params
                                   params key-id frame-id :rf.egress/ssr-hydration)])
                    projected-key)

There is no `project-entry-scope` counterpart, so on a `:serialize` owner declaring `{:sensitive [[:scope :tenant-id]]}` the resolved tenant id rides RAW in the SSR hydration wire key — while the same declaration redacts in the durable epoch export and (since rf2-dl7bz) in every trace / tool key.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN rf2-dl7bz. That bead's ruling is explicit: 'SSR untouched'. The trace/tool arm was fenced away from `ssr.cljc` deliberately, and widening the SSR projection is a separate change with its own byte-identity consequences for the hydration payload's key-id re-keying (`project-resources-runtime-db` re-keys wire entries on `state/key-id` of the PROJECTED key, so projecting the scope component changes the map key the client installs under).

SHAPE, if taken. The params counterpart is one call; the scope counterpart is the same call seeded at `[… :resource/key 0]` instead of `[… :resource/key 2]`, under the same `registry-classifies-under?` gate (so an undeclared scope rides verbatim and the CEDN-1 identity is preserved). Both would then agree with the trace/tool key, which rf2-dl7bz's `redact-key-declarations` already projects on both components.

PROOF STANDARD. A `:serialize` owner declaring `[[:scope :tenant-id]]` under a `[:rf.scope/session {:tenant-id …}]` scope: the SSR wire key's scope component must redact the declared slot, keep the tier keyword and any undeclared sibling, and the resource-id must survive. Two-sided control: an owner declaring nothing has its wire key ride BYTE-identical (`state/key-id` unchanged), and the client's `recompute-indexes` round-trip still lands.
notes:
CLOSED by PR #7255 (branch worker/wire-scope-5e2ye).

Q1 — THE RE-KEYING INTERACTION, established by probe before anything changed.
`state/key-id` is `identity/canonical-bytes` over the WHOLE
`[scope resource-id params]` vector, so the scope component IS inside the hashed
bytes and projecting index 0 DOES change the key-id. But that is the established
mechanism, not a hazard, and the probe showed it already firing on the params
side: `project-resources-runtime-db` re-keys each wire entry on
`(state/key-id (:resource/key wire-entry))` — the key-id of the PROJECTED key —
so the wire map key and the entry's own copy are one value by construction
(`project-entry` sets both from the same `projected-key`). The coarse
`:redact`/`:omit` digests have always re-keyed BOTH components that way; the
params arm has since rf2-d3pku1. Probe confirmed the raw key-id of a
params-declaring entry is ALREADY absent from the wire map today, and that the
scope component rode raw. `recompute-indexes` keys index members on the
`:entries` map keys it installed, so the client round-trip lands on the
projected identity. Nothing breaks. The honest consequence: a declared slot
makes the entry unaddressable by a client-re-derived key and it refetches — the
SAME designed consequence the coarse arm and the params arm already carry.
Closing the scope asymmetry extends an accepted cost by one index.

RESOLUTION — closed, not deferred. `project-entry-params` and the new
`project-entry-scope` are now two names for ONE parameterised body
(`project-entry-key-component`) differing in the index alone, so the two
components cannot drift into two rules again. Declaration gate and frame-scoping
kept on both arms.

BUILD POSTURE (the reason this half mattered more than rf2-dl7bz's): the SSR
hydration wire is NOT dev-only. It is the body behind
`:ssr/extend-runtime-db-projection`, called from
`payload-policy/project-runtime-db` on every SSR render, shipping to every
visitor of every page in a production bundle. No debug gate anywhere on the
path. rf2-dl7bz's trace/tool arm is dev-only by contrast. Stated explicitly in
the ns docstring and the suite docstring.

rf2-dl7bz RULING INTACT: `ssr/project-scoped-key`'s `:serialize` deferral
untouched; `project-scoped-key-still-defers-on-serialize` green (14 tests / 48
assertions, exit 0). Only its docstring changed.

TEST: new dual-target suite, 15 tests / 49 assertions, green in BOTH JVM
postures. Mutation-proved TWICE — (1) scope arm removed => 8 failures / 6 tests;
(2) declaration gate removed => initially PASSED, revealing the byte-identity
control was decorative. `=` cannot see a list<->vector collapse but
`canonical-bytes` can, so the undeclared owner's scope now carries
`:roles '(:admin :ops)`; with that, dropping the gate reds 4 assertions
(rf2-wgutc2). The no-over-redaction side is now load-bearing.

PROD-POSTURE MEASUREMENT (not asserted): `implementation/resources` has no
prod-gate lane and is not prod-posture-clean — 267 trace-emit assertions fail
under `-Dre-frame.debug=false` by design. Measured against origin/main
(ae1fb9b577) with this suite moved aside: baseline 757 tests / 6881 assertions /
267 failures; branch 772 / 6930 / 267 failures. +15 tests, +49 assertions,
+0 failures.

GATES: resources JVM dev 772/6983 exit 0; ssr JVM 592/2892 exit 0; epoch JVM
539/7131 exit 0; core egress-chokepoint source-scan 3/7 exit 0.

NOTE FOR THE MAYOR (not actioned, outside the fence): a `:serialize` entry whose
declared slot redacts is shipped with `:refetch-on-client? false` when fresh,
yet is unaddressable by a client-re-derived key. Pre-existing on the params arm
since rf2-d3pku1 and identical on both indices — not introduced here, and the
bead fenced the fix to the scope component. Worth its own bead if it matters.

title: bench: the allocation harness cannot certify an arm it has optimised to its own floor
description:
RAISED BY the rf2-2ix22 worker (PR #7253), which deliberately left it unfiled rather than expand its own scope, and flagged that it will bite the next worker on this surface.

THE PROBLEM. Every improvement on the ambient-reader / routed-hook surface now lands its arms AT the instrument's own floor, and the arm-order guard refuses a floor-level arm exactly as it refuses a contaminated one. So the better the optimisation, the less certifiable the result:

  rf2-2ix22's baseline run is guard-REPORTABLE at exit 0, so its 264.0 B/read BEFORE figure is fully certified.
  Both AFTER runs exit 2. The guard refuses H-ROUTED, H-SAMEH, H-SAMEFLAT, S0-SCOPE, S1-CURFRM and S2-TGTID -- every arm the two levers pushed to the floor.

THE SIGNATURE IS DIAGNOSTIC, and the worker named it: a per-WINDOW floor rather than a per-call cost, evidenced by an identical ~6.37x phase ratio across arms with nothing else in common. That is not the bimodality the phase factor exists to catch.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN #7253. The rf2-2ix22 ruling resolved this exact sequencing question against holding the production change: 'the production cleanup must NOT be made hostage to a benchmark enhancement' (Codex position, adopted). The worker honoured that -- changed no harness, did not hold the PR, and reported its after-figures as honest upper bounds with 0 UNVERIFIED of 1974 windows so nothing was DCE'd into looking cheap.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS. The floor-aware quote the ruling deferred. Same family as rf2-ktrvw (thunk-dominated arms read V8's escape analysis) and the resolved rf2-tmzie (a hardcoded 4000-window cap made a per-call cost indistinguishable from a per-window floor -- PR #7242 made the cap configurable, which is the precedent for how to approach this).

NOT A LICENCE TO REBUILD THE HARNESS. Fifteen instrument faults have been caught on these surfaces, each having produced a plausible precise wrong number first; a sixteenth instrument is the likeliest way to add one. The minimal honest change is what is wanted: let a run distinguish 'below the floor' from 'refused', and quote a floor-bounded arm as an upper bound rather than declining to quote it.

DO NOT loosen the guard's tolerance to make refusals go away -- four workers have hit refusals on this surface and every one repaired the arm, not the guard.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7292 (2026-07-30). The floor sweep is focused and the guard remains untouched, but `floor-verdict` is fail-open at its minimum legal boundary: it accepts `ratio >= span/2` with `span >= 4`, so at span 4 the threshold is exactly 2 and the known 2x closure-bimodality class it says must remain refused is classified `:floor`. Bounded live proof at landed 21d7b9ef4e1ba9df94e190422e160f6851370d70: temporarily add a self-test fixture `[{reps 1, p50 128}, {reps 2, p50 128}, {reps 4, p50 64}]` expecting `:per-call`; the :advanced ui-bench build succeeds, then the pre-measurement self-test prints `want per-call, got floor` and exits 1. Restore verified by identical normalized blob 014b9c649aeadc2625534b0ebfeeb98e6adde36e and a clean worker tree. Current origin/main still carries the inclusive comparison; no open PR or duplicate Bead owns this boundary. Make equality refuse (or otherwise separate the 2x class with a conservative margin/minimum span) and pin this exact minimum-span fixture; do not weaken order_guard or add another measurement framework.
close_reason: floor-verdict's collapse demand is now strict (> span/2, not >=) so the 2x closure-bimodality bound refuses at the minimum span 4, with the audit's exact minimum-span fixture pinned in floor-self-test; guard untouched. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7297

title: bench: thunk-dominated arms read V8's escape analysis, not their own allocation - read_attribution_cljs's N-CALLTHUNK / N-CWFRNOG refuse by PHASE
description:
FOUND by rf2-x0fe2 while building implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution_cljs.cljs. node 24.13.0 / V8 13.6.233.17-node.37, :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false, pointer compression OFF.

THE FAULT. An arm whose allocation is dominated by a THUNK CLOSURE handed to
another function reads V8's optimization tier as much as its own cost. Three
distinct manifestations, all reproduced:

 1. ELIDED ENTIRELY. call-thunk was (defn- call-thunk [thunk] (thunk)).
    Closure inlines a private one-liner, so the thunk never escaped, so escape
    analysis removed it and the arm read 16.0 B/call -- the instrument floor,
    i.e. nothing. Fixed by storing the thunk in a volatile so it escapes for
    real; the arm then reads a stable 64.0 B/read, one closure.

 2. A 2x STEP THAT WARM-UP DOES NOT TOUCH. N-CALLTHUNK and N-CWFRNOG are
    REFUSED by the arm-order guard on the PHASE factor in the FORWARD plan:
    settled 19,217 B/call, FIRST-THIRD windows up to 38,420 -- exactly 2x, i.e.
    two closures per inner iteration where one is expected. BIT-IDENTICAL
    across 6 warm windows, 12 warm windows and 8 rounds, so it is NOT a
    settling curve (contrast rf2-tb345). The predecessor factor passes; only
    position separates it. The REVERSED plan passes cleanly. The same
    ~19,300 B/call step appears as the HIGH end of N-CWFRBIND / N-CWFRGEN /
    N-CWFRRAW's ranges simultaneously.

 3. AN ASYMMETRY INSIDE A PAIRED CONTROL -- the dangerous one. The binding was
    isolated by a symmetric pair: two sibling fns differing in exactly one
    token, (binding [...] (thunk)) vs (thunk), each handed a fresh thunk. At
    n=300 both allocate their thunk (112.1 B/read each) and the difference is
    0.0, correct. At n=30 V8 elides the NO-BIND half's thunk (48.0) while the
    binding's try/finally blocks the same elision on the bind half (112.0), and
    the difference reads 64.0 B/read -- ONE WHOLE CLOSURE, reported as the
    binding. A paired control is only symmetric while both halves are compiled
    the same way, and that is not guaranteed by writing them the same way.

MITIGATIONS ALREADY IN THE HARNESS (PR for rf2-x0fe2):
  * the PRIMARY binding figure is N-BINDONLY, which contains NO thunk and so
    has nothing to elide (0.1 B/read at n=300, 0.5 at n=30, floor in both);
  * a BUDGET reconstruction, N-CWFRRAW - N-CALLTHUNK - N-GENREAD, which
    accounts for cwfr's whole 112.2 B/read with ~0 left for a binding;
  * an explicit SYMMETRY CHECK printed with the pair: the no-bind half's thunk
    must agree with N-CALLTHUNK or the pair is declared NOT QUOTABLE.

WHAT IS NOT DONE. The guard still refuses the FORWARD plan on N-CALLTHUNK and
N-CWFRNOG. That refusal is REAL and was left in place rather than tuned away --
no headline figure depends on either arm (N-CALLTHUNK is a control, N-CWFRNOG
is the arm the write-up explicitly says NOT to subtract with), and the reversed
plan is reportable. Open questions:
  * can a thunk arm be made tier-stable at all (a pre-allocated thunk hoisted
    out of the loop would remove the allocation the arm exists to price)?
  * does write_attribution.cljs have thunk-dominated arms with the same
    exposure? Its Q-SCHED / P-VALS / P-RKV arms pass closures to run!/reduce-kv.
  * the guard has no way to say 'this arm is refused, the rest of the run is
    fine'. Today one bad arm makes a whole run unquotable, which pushes toward
    deleting inconvenient arms. Worth a per-arm verdict.

DEPENDS ON NOTHING. Instrument hygiene, not a product defect.

title: bench: write-attribution's SMI control reads 2x its own prediction (16.11 B/slot, not 8)
description:
FOUND while diagnosing rf2-xu0ma, on node 24.13.0 / V8 13.6.233.17-node.37, pointer compression OFF, :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false.

write-attribution's SMI control is a .slice() of a PACKED SMI array. A tagged slot is 8 B with pointer compression OFF, so a D=100 copy is predicted at 32 (JSArray) + 16 (FixedArray header) + 800 = 848 B, and D=200 at 1648.

MEASURED (5 windows each, 0 unverified of 5):
  SMI D=100   1681.7 B/copy   predicted 848   +98.31%
  SMI D=200   3293.5 B/copy   predicted 1648  +99.85%

Almost exactly 2x, at both sizes, so the printed ';; SMI slope, SMALL pair (100->200) 16.1146 B/slot' is 2x the 8 B it is checked against.

WHAT IT IS NOT.
- NOT rf2-xu0ma's boxed HeapNumber. The SMI arms store an Smi, which does not box, and the 2x is unchanged after that fix landed (measured on both sides of it).
- NOT a window-size effect: the same figure comes back at reps=590 (~1 MB window) and reps=2193 (~3.6 MB).
- NOT a misread of the pointer-compression regime. The DBL pair beside it lands at +0.04% against 8.0000 B/double, and the SMI readout's own threshold is (< si 6.0), so 16.11 still answers OFF, which is correct for node.

WHY IT MATTERS, AND WHY IT IS P3. Nothing published rests on the SMI absolute: the pair exists to READ OFF the pointer-compression regime, and it gets that right. But it is the one control on this surface whose prediction is not met, and the whole discipline of the harness is predicted-vs-measured. Either the prediction is wrong (in which case the comment stating 8 B/slot should be corrected) or the arm is not measuring what it says.

FIRST THING TO CHECK: whether packed-smis' .push construction leaves the template with backing-store capacity beyond its length, and whether V8's .slice() fast path copies capacity rather than length for PACKED_SMI_ELEMENTS but not for PACKED_DOUBLE_ELEMENTS.

Raw: ai/findings/2026-07-28.xu0ma-probe-postfix.log (local-only), PROBE 2.
Reproduce: npx shadow-cljs release ui-bench --config-merge '{:main re-frame.bench.write-attribution/-diagnose :output-to "out/wa-diagnose.js"}' then node --expose-gc out/wa-diagnose.js

Fence: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/**.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7230 (2026-08-01) — REOPENED exact owner; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS: PR #7230 adds the right absolute SMI/DBL readout and current healthy runs exercise it, but adds no negative-path proof that a broken calibration makes the benchmark non-reportable. Every listed gate uses values inside the expected bands, so the newly introduced failure branch is never adjudicated.

CORRECTNESS: when the SMI/DBL ratio is outside both 0.95–1.05 and 0.45–0.55, the harness prints `*** NEITHER — the SMI arm is not measuring a tagged-slot copy ***`. That result does not feed any refusal state. The only assignment of process exit code 2 remains behind `guard/verdict`'s arm-order refusal. Thus the exact recurrence this bead exists to catch — a shared/changed call site making the SMI control invalid — can still end with exit 0 and an order `VERDICT: reportable`, despite the calibration explicitly saying the instrument is not measuring its stated control.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / BOUNDED REPAIR: retain the useful paired measurement and deliberate per-kind factory duplication. Compute one calibration-refusal boolean from the already printed SMI ratio/slope evidence, combine it with the existing order refusal for the final exit code/verdict, and add a small hermetic failure-path check with injected ratios. Do not turn the known large-object DBL deviation into a gate or build a broader benchmark framework; this owner only needs its own invalid-control state to fail closed.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7238 (2026-08-01) — UPDATED exact owner; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS: The new read_attribution_cljs.cljs copies this control protocol onto the CLJS read-path instrument, but adds no negative-path witness that an invalid small SMI calibration makes a run non-reportable. The 69 passing CI checks exercise only healthy recorded values.

CORRECTNESS: At the merged commit and current origin/main, the SMI/DBL ratio branch prints `*** NEITHER — the SMI arm is not measuring a tagged-slot copy ***` without contributing to refusal state. Only arm-order refusal or nonzero read-back verification sets process exitCode 2. Consequently this second harness can also exit 0 and print an arm-order `VERDICT: reportable` after its own calibration says it is not measuring the stated control. This is the same failure mode already owned here, not a new issue.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / BOUNDED REPAIR: Extend this owner fence to implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution_cljs.cljs. Derive a calibration-refusal boolean from the existing small SMI ratio/slope evidence, make it participate in final nonzero exit status, and add a hermetic invalid-ratio check. Preserve the deliberately separate SMI/DBL factories and do not gate the documented large-object DBL tail.
close_reason: PR #7433. VERDICT: the INSTRUMENT was wrong, not the prediction — already settled in 4231917178 (one arm-ctl body over both template kinds gave the harness a single polymorphic .slice() site; a PACKED_SMI receiver there loses the clone fast path and allocates its elements store twice, 16.11 vs a tagged slot's 8). What this PR closes is the audit reopening: the NEITHER branch printed and nothing consumed it, so a run could exit 0 under 'VERDICT: reportable' with its own control saying it was not measuring a tagged-slot copy. New re-frame.bench.calibration turns the ratios + slope into a boolean (ratio names a regime / sizes agree / slope within 25% of the width THE RATIOS selected — not one read off the slope, which cannot see a doubled slope at all). Both write_attribution and read_attribution_cljs now exit 2 on the OR of their refusals and run the calibration self-test before measuring. DBL LARGE pair's ~+9% deliberately not gated, with a fixture pinning that. calibration_cljs_test replays the injected ratios incl. the recorded 1681.7/848 and 16.1146 under npm run test:cljs. Mutation-proved: slope-tolerance 0.25 -> 2.0 gave exactly the 8 predicted failures in exactly the 2 predicted deftests out of 12,481 tests; reverted byte-identically.

title: ci: four freehand bench runners still inherit Playwright's 30s navigation default (rf2-taj9b waiver)
description:

FOUR sites could not be fixed in that PR: worker/bench-method-88pie held implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/** at the time (it had already rewritten b8_run.cjs), so the fence forbade editing them.

  implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/b8_run.cjs

Each is a page.goto with waitUntil load and NO timeout, so each takes Playwright default 30s.

title: bench: put the arm-order guard on the core allocation harnesses — write_attribution, read_attribution, B7
description:
FOUND by rf2-88pie (PR #7223). NOT DONE THERE because implementation/core/** was outside that worker's fence.

order_guard.cjs now guards b8_run.cjs and the B6 harness. The harness where the fault was actually FOUND is implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/write_attribution.cljs, and it is untouched.

Two things to carry over.

1. THE ROTATION TRAP. b8_run.cjs, b6-harness/round! and b6-rows/update-round! all selected the arm for slot j of round r as ARMS[(j + r) % n] and all three described that in published provenance as 'arm order rotating'. A cyclic rotation changes which arm goes FIRST and not which arm follows which: arm a sits at slot (a - r) mod n, so its predecessor is arm (a - 1) mod n in EVERY round. Check whether write_attribution / read_attribution / b7_run.cjs do the same.

2. THE GUARD. require('order_guard.cjs') - or its CLJS counterpart h/slot-order - stratify every arm's samples by immediate predecessor AND by position in the run, and refuse on either. Note the live finding: position is worth 27% (5.3x on a cold window) where the immediate predecessor is worth 0.0-0.3%, so a plain both-orders pass is not sufficient - it confounds the two.

Sequence AFTER PR #7223 merges (order_guard.cjs must be on main).

title: bench: widen B8's warm-up — one 4-write calibration window is not enough, the data says six
description:
FOUND by rf2-88pie (PR #7223).

order_guard.cjs's live sweep and B8's own first guarded run agree: a measurement site reads well above its settled value until it has run several windows.

  plain node, packed-SMI .slice() control, nothing else varying, sixteen consecutive windows:
    10.32 10.26 10.26 10.26 10.33 10.28 | 8.12 8.12 ... 8.12
  +27% for SIX windows, then a step to the 8.016 prediction. The very first window read 42.32 - 5.3x.

  b8_run.cjs, B8_ROUNDS=4 --kind narrow, real Chromium harness: the 'instrument' arm - the pseudo-arm whose entire purpose is to price the harness's own footprint as a CONSTANT - read 4,361 B/write in its first window and 440 in its last. 9.9x.

b8_run.cjs warms each (arm, D) with ONE four-write calibration window, which the calibration loop doubles as warm-up. That is not enough, and the arm-order guard's phase factor now refuses the run because of it (exit 2).

ACTIONABLE:
1. Warm each (arm, D) for >= 6 windows before the first measured one, or drop the first N measured windows per arm.
2. Raise the default ROUNDS so the guard's phase strata are not single samples - at ROUNDS=4 each stratum is n=1 and the guard has to adjudicate on a ratio rather than a range.
3. Re-run and confirm the guard passes.

Fence: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/**.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #7226 (2026-08-01): reopen exact owner. `reportWarmth` returns every site that hit `B8_WARMUP_MAX` while the guard still called its trajectory contaminated, and `report` persists that list as `summary.warmupUnsettled`; the process exit checks only `summary.orderRefusals` before printing `[b8] ok`. Make a non-empty warmupUnsettled a distinct refusal/nonzero exit (preserving raw output), and add a hermetic exit-path check proving an unsettled warm-up cannot be green. Keep the measured order refusal independent.

The process exit at :1036 still tests ONLY out.summary.orderRefusals.length. warmupUnsettled is never read on the exit path, so a run can print 'NOT SETTLED inside the ceiling' and still exit 0 whenever the measured-round guard is clean — exactly the audit's finding, unchanged.

title: verify-version-lockstep.sh: check_clein_main greps the whole file, not the :clein/build map
description:
Found while fixing rf2-2ii52 (PR #7217), same family as the defect that bead was reopened for; left alone there because it is outside the reopen's bounded repair.

`check_clein_main` in .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh asserts clein's required `:main` key with:

    grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*:main[[:space:]]' "${deps_file}"

That is a whole-file text grep. It does not read the `:aliases -> :clein/build` map it claims to be checking, so it is satisfied by a `:main` key sitting in ANY alias, or in any other map in the file, or (since only `;;` is not even stripped here) by a commented-out one on a line starting with `:main`. An artefact could therefore be reported buildable while `clojure -M:clein pom` still aborts on `(contains? % :main)` — the exact failure the check was added to prevent (machines-viz under rf2-4u3t1, mcp-base under rf2-2ii52).

It is also line-layout-bound in the same way the git-coordinate check was: `:main` has to start its own line. `{:lib day8/x :main foo.bar ...}` on one line passes nothing.

REPAIR (cheap, and the machinery is now right there): read `:aliases -> :clein/build -> :main` structurally through implementation/scripts/lib/edn.cjs, the same node authority local_root_coords() and git_coord_libs() already use in that file — test.yml runs this gate on a bare checkout with no JDK, so node is the available runtime. Add cases to the existing `--self-test` (PR #7217): :main present in :clein/build (CLEAN), :main present only in an unrelated alias (FLAGGED), :main on the same line as :lib (CLEAN), :main absent (FLAGGED).

Today's tree is GREEN either way — all five publishable tools genuinely carry :main in :clein/build — so this is prevention, not a live break.
close_reason: Closed

title: implementation/scripts/lib/edn.cjs: readSeq throws on a trailing #_ discard in a collection
description:
Found while fixing rf2-2ii52 (PR #7217).

`Reader.readSeq` in implementation/scripts/lib/edn.cjs cannot read a collection whose LAST element is a `#_` discard form. `readForm` consumes `#_` plus the discarded datum and then `continue`s to read the next form — which is the closing delimiter — so `readDatum` throws "unexpected '}'".

REPRO (exact, verified 2026-07-28 at main e0e2e076da):

    {:deps {org.clojure/clojure {:mvn/version "1.12.0"}
            #_day8/de-dupe #_{:git/url "https://example.invalid/x.git"}}}

  -> EdnReadError: unexpected '}'

Putting the discard anywhere but last reads fine, so the bug is specifically 'discard immediately before the closing delimiter'.

BLAST RADIUS. Every consumer of this reader fails CLOSED rather than passing vacuously, so this is a availability defect, not a correctness hole:
  - .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh — both assert_local_roots_inventoried and (as of PR #7217) check_no_git_coords_in_runtime_deps exit 2 with 'failed to read this deps.edn structurally'. A deps.edn that ends a map with a discarded coordinate makes the lockstep gate un-runnable.
  - implementation/scripts/lib/publishable-runtimes.cjs and the bundle-isolation gate consume the same reader.

A `#_`-commented-out last dependency is an entirely ordinary thing to write while debugging a dep, so this is reachable by normal editing.

FIX: in readSeq, after readForm() returns, re-check for the closing delimiter before treating the result as an item — or have readForm signal 'discard consumed, nothing produced' rather than recursing into the next datum. Pin it with a fixture in whatever suite covers edn.cjs.

NOT FIXED IN #7217 deliberately: the reader is a shared authority the bundle-isolation gate also consumes, it is outside that PR's fence, and the defect predates it.
close_reason: Closed

title: SSR: the boundary rejection now projects 400 under the gate — correct the stale listener comment and add the witness (follows rf2-mwv4e)
description:
SEQUENTIAL FOLLOW-UP to rf2-mwv4e (PR #7203). implementation/ssr/** was fenced (two live workers), so the worker verified by reading and reported rather than edited.

WHAT rf2-mwv4e CHANGED FOR SSR. A boundary rejection now fans an always-on STRUCTURAL-ONLY record `{:error :rf.error/schema-validation-failure :where :event :source :boundary :event-id :failing-id :schema-id :frame :recovery :time}`. Verified against HEAD by reading, NOT by running the SSR lane:
  - `error_listener.cljc` `error-emit-projection-listener` lifts EVERY non-`:error` slot generically onto `:tags`, so `:where :event` arrives where the projector looks.
  - `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` is NOT in `non-projection-eligible-errors` (verified at error_listener.cljc:137-144), so the record buffers for projection.
  - `error_projector.cljc` line ~222 gates the 400 arm on `(= :event (get-in trace-event [:tags :where]))` — which the record satisfies. So a boundary rejection on a server frame answers 400, closing the silent-200 hole that surfaced rf2-mwv4e.

DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from rf2-6jqa8, worth keeping straight: those three safe-redirect categories are NON-projection-eligible (a hostile probe must not conjure a 500). This one SHOULD project — a refused request payload is exactly a 400 (RFC 9110 s15.5.1).

(1) THE STALE COMMENT, and it is load-bearing prose rather than a nit — its own docstring calls itself 'the authoritative statement of which categories ride which bus'. `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_listener.cljc` ~334 currently reads: 'Two projection-eligible categories ride the dev bus ALONE and therefore elide under interop/debug-enabled? = false: :rf.error/no-such-route ... and :rf.error/schema-validation-failure (boundary validation is itself production-elided per Spec 010 SSProduction builds, so no production reject exists to project).' Both halves of that parenthesis were already wrong before rf2-mwv4e (the CHECK was never elided — only its emit; rf2-mnmzh and rf2-bx4bf corrected the same overclaim elsewhere), and the sentence is now wrong outright: the boundary arm rides BOTH buses. Move it into the 'the rest arrive on BOTH buses' paragraph beside `:rf.error/no-such-handler`.

(2) THE WITNESS, which does not exist in any lane. Under `-Dre-frame.debug=false`, a server frame dispatching an event whose handler references `:rf.schema/at-boundary` with a non-conforming payload must answer 400, with sibling-frame attribution intact. Model on `re-frame.ssr-safe-redirect-production-test` (posture-independent, in the ssr prod-gate lane by default). Assert: exactly one always-on record, status 400 on the wire, the record carries NOTHING from the rejected payload (use a sentinel), and a CONFORMING payload leaves the response untouched. Coordinate with rf2-dtpfv / rf2-lwtlk, which are live in this artefact.

(3) CHECK THE DEV/PROD SYMMETRY while you are here. rf2-6jqa8 uncovered a measured dev/prod wire asymmetry on its surface (dev stamped 500 via the trace-cb buffering path while production answered 200). Here BOTH buses now carry the rejection in dev, and `consume-pending-traces!` + last-write-wins should make the duplicate benign — but that is reasoned, not measured. Measure it: assert the dev arm answers 400 too, and that the duplicate buffering does not double-stamp.

TEST-ONLY / COMMENT-ONLY; no behaviour change is being requested in ssr src.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7234 (2026-08-01) — REOPENED exact residual owner; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS: the three corrected spec surfaces now agree with the runtime, but the same stale production-elision claim remains at the SSR listener registration site in `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc`. This is the direct mirror of the source-comment obligation this bead previously closed in `error_listener.cljc`.

CORRECTNESS: the surviving comment classifies `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` as a dev-bus-only category because “boundary validation is itself production-elided” and says there is “no production reject to project”. Both statements are false: the boundary check is ungated, its structural `:source :boundary` arm rides the always-on error bus, and the existing production witness proves it projects 400. The correct split is arm-level: ordinary dev validator failures remain trace-only, while an `:rf.schema/at-boundary` rejection rides both buses in dev and the always-on bus in production.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / BOUNDED REPAIR: update only the registration-site comment to match the already-correct `error_listener.cljc` authority and the three specs repaired here. The behavioral production witness already exists; do not add another test or new documentation machinery for a comment-only residual.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7235 (2026-08-01) — UPDATED the already-open exact residual owner; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS: the three edited citations are correct, but the same obsolete Spec 010 citation survives twice in `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_head_resolution_no_project_test.clj` (namespace posture explanation and the dev-control comment): it says boundary validation itself is production-elided and no production reject exists.

CORRECTNESS: the test's direct `trace/emit-error!` control is legitimately dev-only, so its assertions and posture guard remain sound. The reason is arm-level: that synthetic call exercises the dev diagnostic arm of `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` and carries no `:rf/boundary-rejected?` marker. The category as a whole is not dev-only; the real `:rf.schema/at-boundary` arm checks and reports on the always-on axis in production. The current prose teaches the exact inverse of the specs repaired by #7234/#7235.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / BOUNDED REPAIR: correct those two comments only, preserving the existing dev and always-on controls unchanged. State that the synthetic dev-bus arm elides while the marker-driven boundary arm does not. No new test or generalized citation checker is warranted.

Adjacent work landed alongside it (6c10135289 spec(011) 'the boundary rejection answers 400, not 200' under rf2-gdkyo, and b62ff21a17 docs(template) under rf2-hs3zv), so the 400-arm story is coherent across code, spec and template.
