title: ci: test-rigorous-local.sh no longer covers the seven Freehand bench DOM namespaces in a browser
description:
CONSEQUENCE of rf2-mf4uy (PR #7193), noted there because scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh is repo-root and was outside that PR's fence.

TESTING.md calls scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh the 'local mirror of the nightly sweep'. It runs test:browser, test:browser-schemas-boundary-prod and test:browser-prod-elision. It does NOT run bench:freehand-browser.

That was harmless while :browser-test also selected the seven re-frame.freehand.bench.*_dom_cljs_test namespaces. Since rf2-mf4uy it no longer does — those seven now run ONLY in :browser-test-freehand-bench, whose sole scheduled home is .github/workflows/freehand-bench.yml. So the local rigorous sweep has a hole the nightly CI sweep does not: 30 tests / 465 assertions of mounted Freehand evidence that a pre-release local run will not exercise.

THE DECISION, and it is a real one rather than an oversight to patch:

  (a) ADD 'npm run bench:freehand-browser' to test-rigorous-local.sh. Costs ~60s locally (measured: 16.5s compile + 31.8s run). Restores the mirror. But the script's inventory is pinned by implementation/scripts/_rigorous-local-inventory.test.cjs, so that pin moves in the same PR.

  (b) LEAVE IT and say so in TESTING.md. Defensible: the bench lane publishes EVIDENCE and asserts on provenance words, never on numbers; a developer workstation is not the pinned worker the records are comparable within; and freehand-bench.yml runs it nightly regardless.

Whichever way it goes, TESTING.md's 'local mirror of the nightly sweep' line should stop being ambiguous about it.

Surfaces: scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh, implementation/scripts/_rigorous-local-inventory.test.cjs, TESTING.md. Small either way.
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28, dossier review): Option (a) — add `npm run bench:freehand-browser` to scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh. The primary dossier analysis and the independent Codex review both chose (a); premises re-verified against the current checkout before ruling (the script's browser/bundle block omits the command; the inventory guard derives commands only from expensive-tests.yml; bench:freehand-browser exists in implementation/package.json). This bead now owns implementation: ONE small PR touching scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh + implementation/scripts/_rigorous-local-inventory.test.cjs + TESTING.md. Dispatchable.

IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL TO PRESERVE (dossier ai/decisions/rf2-rmtj0.rigorous-local-bench-lane.md is deleted; this note is the record):

1. ROLE FRAMING — the lane's local role is a mounted-correctness and harness-validity gate, NOT a source of comparable release benchmark numbers. The rigorous sweep consumes the command's test VERDICT and ignores its distributions. freehand-bench.yml (compiled-in revision, pinned hardware class, provenance checks, uploaded log) remains the SOLE authority for citable evidence. Do NOT auto-stamp a dirty local checkout with `git rev-parse HEAD` — that attributes modified source to bytes from the wrong revision. With no RF2_REVISION the build deliberately labels records unattributable, which is correct locally; an empty hardware-class define identifies the host as a developer workstation.

2. WHAT THE LANE ASSERTS (why omission was untenable) — B1 interpreted/compiled DOM equality at realistic and stress sizes plus a falsifiability control; B2 mounted cell-elision counts and DOM signatures; B4 exact event/write/recompute/render counts plus controlled-input value/caret/node identity under contention; B6 cross-substrate mounted parity, DOM read-back after updates, and synchronous commit; B10 predicted-vs-observed DOM mutations, zero unverified crossings, no dropped characters with correct caret/sibling settlement across its load ladder. These are deterministic browser facts even when collected inside a benchmark harness — per D021's own parity-vs-distribution split (semantic parity and no-dropped-input are hard correctness requirements; timing/byte distributions are evidence, not thresholds). Because the current files couple both classes in one build, omitting the build discards the hard checks along with the non-comparable local measurements.

3. COST — variable, not a frozen 60s: the scheduled run at the current revision measured 24.97s compile, roughly 110s end-to-end from npm command to test summary. Proportionate for an explicitly opt-in, release-sized sweep.

4. CENSUS CAUTION — the scheduled run reports 30 tests / 466 assertions (not 465 as earlier prose said). Do not pin prose (TESTING.md, script comments) to a fast-moving census; read the lane's own summary.

5. INVENTORY PIN (required, same PR) — implementation/scripts/_rigorous-local-inventory.test.cjs derives its command list ONLY from expensive-tests.yml's browser/bundle/Story job (missing-direction lockstep), so merely adding bench:freehand-browser to the script leaves its continued presence UNPROTECTED. It must be explicitly pinned in that test in the same PR. Place the command beside test:browser in the script's browser/bundle block.

6. TESTING.md WORDING — say the local script mirrors the expensive sweep PLUS examples compilation and the Freehand mounted-correctness lane. It must NOT claim to reproduce the scheduled workflow's evidence-publication semantics. Update the script comment to enumerate the scope likewise.

7. KNOWN RISK (accepted) — a contended workstation can red a harness CONTROL while product invariants are intact; that is triage cost, not a reason to drop mounted coverage. If it becomes recurrent, the follow-up is splitting stable mounted assertions into a small correctness build, leaving full timing workloads on the scheduled lane — a larger refactor, explicitly NOT in scope now.
close_reason:
Shipped as PR #7227 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7227), option (a) as ruled.

npm run bench:freehand-browser added to the browser/bundle block of scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh beside test:browser, per implementation detail 5. Ruling details honoured: role framing and the 'not evidence-publication' disclaimer are in both the script comment and TESTING.md (detail 1, 6); no revision auto-stamp added (detail 1); no census pinned in prose anywhere — the local run reported 465 assertions against the scheduled lane's 466, exactly the drift detail 4 warned about (detail 4); the inventory pin landed in the same PR (detail 5).

Inventory pin went beyond a bare array. The two ad-hoc required commands became DIRECT_PINS, a named map of command -> why the workflow parse cannot see it. Separately, the guard now runs the LOCAL SCRIPT's text through stripComments before parsing, as it already did for the workflow: its own header claimed comment prose could not satisfy the parse, and on the script side that was false. A pin a comment can satisfy is not a pin. Side effect: the script's prose mention of test:script-policy no longer counts as an invocation.

Mutation-proved both ways — deleting the command reds the guard (exit 1), demoting it to a comment also reds it (exit 1, and this one would have PASSED before the stripComments change), restore green (exit 0) with git diff --stat clean at 3 files.

Measured cost the sweep gains: 121s on a Windows workstation, cold (32.85s compile of 259 files + browser run), 30 tests / 465 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors. Neither the harness's pre-Chromium ownership refusal nor the navigation helper's explicit waitUntil/timeout fired.

Gate exits: inventory guard 0, test:script-policy 0, bench:freehand-browser 0, bash -n 0. shellcheck not installed on this workstation, deferred to CI.

Structural blind spot in the guard spun off to rf2-0l1nv (P4) — the lockstep parse can only ever see one job in one workflow. Twelve other implementation gates live outside that window; none judged a hole of the same kind, none proposed for the rigorous script.

title: ci: run-ui-g8.cjs inherits the same undocumented 30s page.goto ceiling rf2-dczpv just removed from the test runner
description:
SPOTTED while fixing rf2-dczpv (PR #7193), out of that bead's scope.

implementation/scripts/run-ui-g8.cjs:300 does a bare

    await page.goto(url);

with no options at all, so Playwright's DEFAULTS apply: waitUntil 'load' AND a 30s timeout. That is the same second, undocumented ceiling rf2-dczpv removed from run-browser-tests.cjs — a budget entirely separate from the gate's own TIMEOUT (which the very next line, page.waitForFunction(..., {timeout: TIMEOUT}), does pass explicitly, so the file already knows the pattern).

LOWER RISK THAN THE ORIGINAL, which is why it was not bundled: G-8 navigates to a small controlled-input FIXTURE page, not a 145-namespace test bundle, so 'load' fires quickly and the ceiling has not been observed firing. But the failure MODE is the identical one that made rf2-dczpv worth fixing: a 'page.goto: Timeout 30000ms exceeded' line in a CI log reads like the gate's own timeout, and the fix reached for would be a bigger TIMEOUT, which cannot touch it.

FIX, same shape as rf2-dczpv: pass an explicit timeout tied to the gate's own TIMEOUT, and prefer waitUntil 'commit' if the gate does not need subresources (it polls globalThis.__RF2_G8_RESULT__ afterwards, so it probably does not). Consider whether a named failure message is worth it here too.

ALSO WORTH A LOOK IN THE SAME PASS: implementation/scripts/check-story-static.cjs:231 already passes {waitUntil:'load', timeout:30000} EXPLICITLY — correct in that it is not inherited, but it is still a hard-coded 30s that no other lane's budget reaches. Decide whether that is deliberate.

Surface: implementation/scripts/**. Small.

title: Consolidate 73 ad-hoc IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT set/restore sites onto one shared fixture
description:
Carried over from rf2-76lhy step 2, which closed on PR #7190 having delivered step 1 (the capture-time profile). This half was never done and should not be lost with the parent.

73 test files set and restore the process-global IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT by hand, with no shared fixture. A test that throws between the set and the restore leaks the flag into every subsequent namespace in the bundle - a cross-namespace coupling that no assertion can catch and that only shows up as unexplained slowness or flakiness later in the run.

IMPORTANT CONTEXT, so this is not over-sold. rf2-76lhy originally advanced the leak as the explanation for a suspected 3-4x CI slowdown. The per-namespace profile shipped in PR #7190 dissolved that: 73% of the lane's wall clock is 7 benchmark namespaces, the three recorded CI stop points all sit at 92-97% of the lane, and the CI/local gap is a uniform ~1.7x. There is no longer evidence pointing at the leak.

So this is a HYGIENE bead, not a bug hunt. It retires a real hazard class on its own terms - one use-fixtures with the restore in a finally - and it is worth doing, but nothing is currently known to be broken by it. Size it accordingly and do not let it grow into an audit.

Fenced away from the PR #7190 runner work; this is implementation/**/test/** across many artefacts, so it wants its own dispatch.
notes:
INVESTIGATED, NOT DONE (PR #7193 worker, 2026-07-28). Recommendation: leave it, or do it per-artefact later. This is the honest 'not worth doing now'.

CENSUS IS BIGGER THAN THE BEAD SAYS: 78 files, 175 `set!` sites, across NINE trees — freehand 43, ui 15, adapters 7, ssr 6, tools/story 2, tools/machines-viz 2, machines 1, core 1, scripts 1. Not 73, and not one artefact.

THERE IS NO SMALL, OBVIOUSLY-CORRECT CONSOLIDATION TO ADOPT. The nearest existing shared fixture is `re-frame.ui.test/act-operation!`, which already does exactly the right thing (reads the prior value, sets true, restores the PRIOR value — not `false` — after React settles). But it lives in implementation/ui/SRC, a published and EXPERIMENTAL artefact surface. Adopting it from freehand / ssr / adapters / machines test trees would make those artefacts' tests depend on re-frame.ui. That is an architectural decision, not hygiene, and it is Mike's. The alternative — mint a new shared test-support surface every artefact may require — is also a decision, not a sweep.

WHAT DOES EXIST is per-artefact convergence: freehand already has mount_support.cljs and bench/b6_harness.cljs; ssr has SIX files carrying byte-identical `disable-act-env!`/`restore-act-env!` pairs. So the tractable shape is PER-ARTEFACT, ONE PR EACH — freehand first (43 of the 78 files, landing spot already present), then ssr (6 files, pure duplication), then ui.

WHY NOT NOW. (1) The motivation is gone: PR #7190's profile dissolved the 3-4x CI-slowdown hypothesis this was step 2 of, and PR #7193 confirmed it on a second box — the whole gap was seven benchmark namespaces (71% of the browser lane's wall clock), and the CI factor is a uniform ~1.7x. There is still no observed instance of the leak. (2) A 78-file mechanical edit across nine trees is a maximal merge-conflict change against every open PR touching a mounted test. (3) Every one of those trees was outside PR #7193's fence, so it could not have been done there in any case.

If someone does pick it up: rule FIRST on whether re-frame.ui.test's act door may be the repo-wide answer, because that ruling decides whether this is one shared fixture or nine private ones.
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28, dossier review):

DECISION — leave the sweep undone now; bead DEFERRED. No 78-file mechanical edit during the current mounted-test churn: the motivating CI-slowdown hypothesis was dissolved by measurement (seven benchmark namespaces + a uniform ~1.7x CI factor), and the sweep is a maximal merge-conflict change against every open mounted-test PR. Pick this up only when the high-conflict Freehand work settles AND either a real leak instance bites or an artefact's mounted tests are being reworked anyway — then land it artefact-sized, not repo-wide.

RECORD CORRECTION (from the Codex second opinion; commits verified in this checkout): "no observed instance" is true of the PERFORMANCE theory only. Flag leakage itself has occurred and been repaired — 43ce4cf9f6 and 1fff5b618b (shared-page act-discipline, ~361 warnings) and 0dd432b9ed (un-restored act boundary after a negative-control run, 755 warnings). The hazard class is real and observed; the slowdown attribution is what was disproved. P3 stands.

ARCHITECTURAL ANSWER (binding — do not re-litigate):
1. DONOR DEPENDENCY FORBIDDEN. No artefact's tests may require re-frame.ui (src or test): F6e deletes the artefact, and re-frame.ui.test/act-operation! is a private defn- coupled to donor internals in any case. Its invariant is the SHAPE to copy, never the namespace to require: capture the incoming flag value and restore the PRIOR value — not a blanket false — on every exit path (synchronous throw, Promise fulfilment, Promise rejection).
2. ONE repo-private implementation, NOT nine per-artefact copies. Home: the existing lightweight dependency-free shared surface implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_test_support.cljs (or a narrowly named sibling in the same core/test root). Verified: it is already required across an artefact boundary today (adapters/uix test) and sits on the consolidated Shadow classpath, so this mints no new architecture and survives F6e. Per-artefact is the DELIVERY boundary — artefact-sized PRs, freehand first (43 files, through its existing mount_support.cljs facade), ssr second (6 byte-identical disable/restore pairs) — not the implementation boundary. Nine permanent copies would reproduce at repo scale exactly the drift ssr's six copies already demonstrate.
3. Design floor for whoever lands it (from Codex, ratified): the helper takes the desired mode — both true (act-disciplined renders) and false (timing discriminators, hydration, deliberate un-acted negative controls) are legitimate, so no runner-wide constant. One save/restore engine with thin sync-wrapping and async-map fixture adapters (cljs.test forbids mixing the two fixture kinds; async tests need the map form) plus a Promise-aware operation bracket for callbacks that reject before done; overlapping async scopes rejected or serialized. Leave re-frame.ui.test self-contained until F6e and skip migrating ui test files the deletion gate removes.

Disposition: deferred (was open P3). Reopen against the conditions above.

title: Consolidate the Spec 015 URL-carrier scrub into core — two artefacts own one policy
description:
rf2-6jqa8 promoted SSR's safe-redirect rejections onto the always-on error axis, which required an EP-0015 fail-closed scrub on the caller-untrusted :location slot. The scrub policy already existed — re-frame.routing.egress/redact-url-carriers (rf2-ov56u applies it to the route-miss :url) — but implementation/ssr depends on core ALONE (Spec 006), so it could not be reached:

  - a production :require on routing would drag the whole route grammar onto the classpath of every SSR app that registers no routes;
  - a late-bind hook to routing's copy would FAIL OPEN in exactly the common case (a routing-free SSR host), and a fail-open scrub on a fail-closed egress boundary is the wrong failure mode by construction.

So implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/egress.cljc now carries a byte-for-byte sibling of routing's redact-url-carriers, deliberately spelled the same way (same fn names, same policy, same docstring shape) so this consolidation is a MOVE rather than a rewrite.

THE FIX: move redact-url-carriers / redact-url-tag into core, next to re-frame.privacy (which already owns redacted-sentinel and is the only thing either copy requires). Have re-frame.routing.egress and re-frame.ssr.egress delegate, or delete both and re-point the three call sites (routing/url_change route-miss-tags, routing's :rf.route/navigation-blocked :requested-url slot, ssr/response safe-redirect-tags).

NOTE the default slot differs between the two copies (:url in routing, :location in ssr) — the consolidated redact-url-tag should keep the two-arity shape and let each caller name its slot.

Low priority: the duplication is 45 lines of pure string surgery with no state, and both copies are covered by their own tests. It is a tidiness bead, not a correctness one.
close_reason: Closed

title: examples/core/login/model.cljs comments claim Credentials is enforced at 'the machine's :submit boundary' — it isn't
description:
FOUND BY rf2-bjkkd (PR #7185) while correcting the README's "rejected at the door" claim. The README is fixed; these are the source comments that taught it the same wrong thing, and they are the canonical login example's comments, so a reader copying the shape reads them.

THE FACT: Credentials never reaches the machine. AuthLoginEvent (model.cljs:136-146) is credential-free by construction — [:cat [:= :auth.login/flow] [:schema [:cat [:enum :submit :dismiss :success :failure] [:* :any]]] [:? :any]] — and the file says so itself at :121-127 ("Every sub-event here is credential-free ... the machine tracks the login lifecycle but never touches the password"). The only thing that checks a draft against Credentials is the private validate helper (:421-423, m/explain + me/humanize) called from :auth.login/submit-form (:539). That is a plain function call in a handler body: it runs in every build, and it is what actually rejects a too-short password.

SITES (all in examples/core/login/model.cljs):
  - :407-409 — "Its shape is Credentials (email regex, 8-char password) — the very schema the machine's :submit boundary will later hold it to." The machine's :submit boundary holds it to nothing; it never sees the draft.
  - :413-415 — "It checks the draft against the very same Credentials schema the machine's :submit boundary enforces, so the form and the machine agree on 'valid' down to the last character." Same error. The form is the only party that checks; there is nobody to agree with.
  - :121-122 — "The shape of every event vector dispatched at the :auth.login/flow machine. Get it wrong and the event is rejected at the boundary — the handler simply never runs." True in a dev build only (:where :event is validate-event!, inside the interop/debug-enabled? gate). Wants the same one-clause qualification the README now carries.
  - :516-521 — this block is CORRECT and is the model for the fix: "Handing a bad draft to the machine would only bounce off its :submit schema boundary — and since the view renders machine errors, that rejection would be *silent* ... So the form catches it first." Note it also says ":submit schema boundary", so it inherits the same imprecision even while reasoning correctly; the reasoning survives a rewording, the phrase does not.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the comments describe a two-layer defence (form checks, machine re-checks) that does not exist, and the layer they credit is the dev-only one. A reader who trusts the machine boundary and drops the form's validate call ships an endpoint with no credential check at all.

FENCE: examples/core/login/model.cljs comments only. THE CODE IS CORRECT — do not change behaviour, and do not add :rf.schema/at-boundary (PR #7185 explains why it is the wrong shape for an ingress that must answer with field errors). Comment-only diff; run the example gates.

CITE: rf2-bjkkd (the README fix), rf2-bkvu5 (the ruling), rf2-ueopx (the sweep).
close_reason: Closed

title: Publish the controls kit's composition reader, or the scalars a kit member needs
description:
GAP found building the FH-CTRL-019 typeahead witness (rf2-drpa3.182.8).

`re-frame.freehand.controls` publishes the composition DECISION — `key-intent`, a pure function of (key, composing?) — and its docstring explicitly invites reuse: 'a kit member with its own keyboard protocol answers the composition question through this function rather than re-deciding it'.

But the READER is private. `composing?` (controls.cljc) is a `defn-`, and it is the part that carries the real knowledge: the standard `isComposing` flag has to be asked of `nativeEvent` under React, and Chromium reports a composing Enter through `keyCode` 229 with `isComposing` FALSE. A kit member can therefore share the rule and cannot share the scalars.

CONSEQUENCE, observed: `re-frame.freehand.typeahead-witness` carries a four-line mirror of `composing?` (marked as such at the site). That is the exact duplication the kit's own design intends to prevent, and it is the duplication whose failure mode is silent — a member that mirrored only the standard flag is broken for every input method on Chromium and green on every keyboard its author owns. FH-CTRL-019's mounted tier presses the two signals separately for that reason.

OPTIONS (a ruling, not a foregone conclusion):
  a. publish `composing?` on `re-frame.freehand.controls` (a namespace-level public fn, not a door verb — no API-manifest verb lane);
  b. widen `key-intent` with an arity that takes the host EVENT rather than the two scalars, keeping the pure arity;
  c. rule that a kit member is expected to read its own scalars, and say so in the kit docstring so the next author does not treat the duplication as an accident.

Whatever is chosen, FH-CTRL-018's separate-signal press is the acceptance shape: an event carrying BOTH signals cannot fail for either one.
notes:
SHIPPED via PR #7201 (worker/composing-18216).

Published `re-frame.freehand.controls/composing?` as a documented public :advanced fn; `key-intent` unchanged as the pure (key, composing?) decision.

WEBKIT ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED in source, both browser suites (FH-CTRL-018/020) and the three conformance fixtures: the isComposing=false / keyCode=229 pairing was WebKit bug 165004, fixed April 2026 via bug 311717 (Safari branch backport) — not Chromium. 229 arm kept for deployed engines, documented as the UI Events legacy-algorithm compatibility signal rather than a Freehand policy value.

MIRRORS: exactly ONE existed — typeahead-witness/host-composing? — now deleted, call site reads c/composing?. Repo-wide 'keyCode 229' sweep found no others.

MANIFEST ROSTER: re-frame.freehand.controls IS on gen.clj's roster (unlike collection/splitter). Enrolled in api-manifest-metadata.edn (:advanced), regenerated api-manifest.edn (592->593), spec/API.md row, docs/api section, and FH-CTRL-017's exact :public-vars fixture (which went RED on the new var — that fixture is the 'exact ns-publics' check the ruling named). CLJS probe enumerates dynamically, no edit needed.

FOUR-CASE TEST added (raw flag / React nativeEvent / keyCode 229 alone / neither), each pressed alone.

GATES all 0: freehand JVM 1267 tests, test:freehand 1374 tests, test:browser 840 tests, plus all 6 manifest+projection checks.

title: The no-candidate handler fallback drops v/raw-fn and v/render-fn — the two roles that need no committed site
description:
Found while answering rf2-3slzz. LATENT and pre-existing — not reachable from any shipping declaration today, which is why it is P3 rather than a bug report.

WHAT. re-frame.freehand.react/handler-proxy's no-candidate fallback is:

    (if (some? cand)
      (events/site ...)
      (when (fn? raw) raw))

`raw` here is whatever the author wrote at a native `:on-*` position. For the two roster roles that need NO committed site — v/render-fn and v/raw-fn — events/site itself hands the carrier's function straight back (`(:f plan)`), records nothing on the candidate, and mints no proxy. They are deliberately outside the committed-proxy scheme: a render callback may run during an uncommitted foreign render, and a raw function's identity is the caller's to own.

So those two roles are exactly the ones that would be legal in a boundary with no cell — and they are the ones the fallback DROPS. A Callback deftype is deliberately not `fn?` in ClojureScript (carrier-called-directly! documents why at length), so `(when (fn? raw) raw)` answers nil for a (v/raw-fn f) or a (v/render-fn [...] ...) at a native `:on-*` with no candidate above it. The prop is never written. Nothing throws.

The same fallback is in re-frame.freehand.reactive/event-site (the compiled tier's lowering), spelled `(when (fn? value) value)` — identical shape, identical consequence.

WHY IT IS NOT REACHABLE TODAY. An `:on-*` key is an `:events` site to the compiled analyzer whatever value sits at it, so a compiled declaration carrying one never reaches `:view-cell :elided`; and the interpreted shell never elides. The only way to hit the fallback now is the documented "no boundary above this call" path (fr/element with a bare element), where dropping declarative intent is the documented behaviour — but dropping a v/raw-fn there is still wrong, because a v/raw-fn asks for nothing the fallback cannot give: it wants its own identity handed over unchanged, which is precisely what the no-candidate arm is for.

WHY IT MATTERS SOON. rf2-oxlpy (the {:reactive false} opt-out) makes shell-free boundaries reachable from ordinary interpreted declarations, and its brief already rules that these positions must classify with events/event-plan and let :render-fn / :raw-fn pass through. If that lands, this is fixed as a side effect and this bead closes as a duplicate. Filed separately so the latent defect is not lost if the flag is deferred, and so the fix has a home if someone reaches the fallback another way first.

FIX, if taken on its own: classify with events/event-plan in the no-candidate arm rather than testing `fn?`. nil -> nil (empty position). :render-fn / :raw-fn -> the carried function, unchanged, which is what the committed path answers for them too. :bare-fn -> the function (unchanged behaviour). Everything else -> nil, exactly as today, since those genuinely need a committed site the caller has no boundary to give.

EVIDENCE: ai/findings/2026-07-27.reactive-false-runtime-check-totality.md; implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/react.cljs:256-268 and :957-974; implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/reactive.cljc:99-105; implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/events.cljc `site` and `carrier-called-directly!`.

title: Browser lane treats a double-fired cljs.test done as diagnostic noise, not a failure
description:
Split out of rf2-0ke4x, which fixed five double-fired `done` calls in `controls_kit_dom_cljs_test.cljs`. The fix is verified, but the class of defect remains UNGUARDED: no gate fails on a double-fired `done`.

WHY NOTHING CATCHES IT. `cljs.test/run-block` wraps the async continuation in a `delay` and the second `done` takes the realized branch:

    (if (realized? d)
      (println "WARNING: Async test called done more than one time.")
      @d)

So a duplicate is a console `println`, never an assertion failure. `implementation/scripts/run-browser-tests.cjs` taps `page.on('console', ...)` and buffers every line, but by deliberate design (rf2-mwx08) 'Console output stays diagnostic-only; only `pageerror` is fatal'. The warning is therefore captured and then discarded unless RF2_VERBOSE_TESTS=1. rf2-0ke4x's six warnings rode green through PR #7162's merge and were found by a human reading the diff.

THE CHEAP FIX, and why it is not in rf2-0ke4x. The runner already has the exact hook: it collects `consoleLines` and separately treats `pageErrors` as fatal. Promoting the single literal 'Async test called done more than one time' to a fatal console pattern is roughly five lines next to the existing `pageErrors.length > 0` arm. It is general — it catches ANY suite in the mounted tier, not one file — which is why it is the right guard and a bespoke textual lint over the suite sources is not.

It was left out of rf2-0ke4x for two reasons. It is outside that bead's fence (`implementation/freehand/test/**`); and it changes the VERDICT semantics of the whole browser lane, so any other suite currently emitting the warning would go red on the same commit. That needs its own full-lane gate rather than riding a five-line deletion.

ACCEPTANCE. Promote the warning to a fatal console pattern in the browser runner; confirm the full browser lane is green on main with the promotion in place (i.e. no OTHER suite is currently double-firing); add a policy test alongside the existing `_impl-browser-runners-verdict-policy.test.cjs` family covering the new fatal pattern. A verified-clean lane plus the promotion means the next PR #7162-shaped regression reds instead of merging.

EVIDENCE THE LANE IS OTHERWISE CLEAN (rf2-0ke4x, browser run at 835 tests): before the fix, exactly 6 warnings, all attributable to `controls-kit-dom-cljs-test`; after the fix, 0. No other suite emitted one, so the promotion should not red anything today.
close_reason: PR #7400. The fatal-console promotion itself landed in PR #7343; this closes the hole auditing #7343 found. serve-and-run-browser-tests.cjs built its runner child env as '{ ...process.env, ...(cond ? {K: v} : {}) }', which only ever ADDS the key, so an ambient RF2_DUPLICATE_DONE_DRIFT_UNVERIFIABLE=1 rode through to the UNFLAGGED default test:browser lane and skipped the fail-closed duplicate-done matcher-drift verdict entirely. computeRunnerEnv (scripts/lib/browser-runner-drift-env.cjs) now pins both directions explicitly: the flag always forwards '1', its absence always DELETES the var. Extracted so the rule is unit-testable by CALLING it, not by asserting on source text (the same gap class a prior audit found in the matcher-drift check). Gates: sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 with the new _browser-runner-drift-env.test.cjs 6/6 in test:script-helpers; npm run test:browser exit 0, 1024 tests / 6335 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors on the UNFLAGGED default lane (the path that must CARRY the drift check).

It reads run-browser-tests.cjs and asserts that the runner still contains its own regex; if cljs.test changes the emitted warning, neither that file nor this test changes, so the gate remains green while FATAL_CONSOLE_RE stops matching. title: PR #7162 left five double-done calls in controls_kit_dom_cljs_test
description:
Found while flipping FH-CTRL-018 to :residue :none (rf2-n9rzw). Not a blocker for that flip — reported rather than fixed, because repairing it means touching a mounted suite and therefore owing a full browser gate, which would have widened a deliberately bounded PR.

WHAT HAPPENED. Before PR #7162, `implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/controls_kit_dom_cljs_test.cljs` ended each async row with:

    (teardown! container root)
    (done)

`teardown!` did not call `done`. #7162 (commit 78531340ca) replaced `teardown!` with the shared `finish!`, which DOES call `done` as its last form:

    (defn- finish! [container root done]
      (ms/destroy-root! container root)
      (ms/residue-clean! "FH-CTRL-018 — after teardown")
      (done))

The pre-existing trailing `(done)` was left in place at every site, so all five now double-fire:

    (finish! container root done)
    (done)

Sites: lines 296/297, 328/329, 363/364, 431/432, 528/529 (as of 8f6779be3e).

WHY THE BROWSER GATE STAYED GREEN, and why this is P3 rather than P1. cljs.test guards it — `run-block` wraps the continuation in a `delay` and the second call takes the realized branch:

    (if (realized? d)
      (println "WARNING: Async test called done more than one time.")
      @d)

So the second `done` is a no-op plus a console warning; async state is NOT corrupted and no test runs twice. That matches #7162's reported browser numbers (835 tests unchanged). The cost is five spurious warnings per browser run, plus five lines of dead code that contradict the file's own discipline — `mount-support`'s docstring warns specifically against double-firing `done`, and `run-async`/`each-mode` exist to make it impossible.

FIX. Delete the five trailing `(done)` forms. `finish!` owns the call; `fail-and-finish!` already does the same on the rejection path and has no duplicate.

GATE. Touching a mounted suite, so `npm run test:browser` with BROWSER_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS=600000, foreground. Expect the test count unchanged and the "called done more than one time" warnings gone from the log — the warning's disappearance IS the acceptance evidence, so capture the log before and after.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7164. Deleted the five trailing (done) calls; finish! keeps ownership, matching mount-support's run-async/each-mode. Browser lane: 6 double-done warnings before, 0 after; 835 tests / 5383 assertions unchanged, exit 0 both runs. freehand JVM exit 0 (1222 tests). Guard filed as rf2-u0cy4 (promote the warning to a fatal console pattern in the browser runner - outside this bead's fence).

title: trace: with-handler-scope allocates a HandlerScope + trigger-handler map on EVERY sub recompute in PRODUCTION (121 B/sub)
description:
FOUND by rf2-jr76s. Measured 120.8 B per subscription per write (node V8, :advanced, goog.DEBUG false, pointer compression OFF) — 4.3% of the pre-fix per-subscription slope and 12.8% of the post-fix one, i.e. it is now one of the larger remaining framework terms.

subs.memo/validate-and-trace brackets EVERY sub recompute in

  (trace/with-handler-scope (trace/handler-scope-from-meta :sub query-id sub-meta) ...)

and that bracket is NOT under interop/debug-enabled?. So a production :advanced bundle, in which the trace emit inside it costs literally 0.2 B because Closure DCEs the body AND the argument map (measured), still allocates a 5-field HandlerScope record, the trigger-handler map that handler-scope-from-meta builds, the inherit-scope cond-> result, and a dynamic-var binding push/pop — per subscription, per write.

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE DEV GATE, and why this is a bead rather than a patch: the scope is read by the ALWAYS-ON error path. validate-and-trace's catch branch routes :rf.error/sub-exception through error-emit/dispatch-on-error! and emit-error-both!, deliberately outside the debug gate, because Spec 011's SSR fail-closed posture depends on a sub that throws mid-render-to-string producing a 500 rather than a silent 200. Those paths resolve the failing handler's source-coord and trigger-handler from the in-scope HandlerScope. Gating the scope on debug-enabled? would therefore change PRODUCTION ERROR ATTRIBUTION — an error-contract surface, not a perf knob.

SHAPES WORTH CONSIDERING (none chosen):
  (a) Build the scope LAZILY — bind a thunk/holder and materialise the record only when an emit or an error actually needs it. Preserves the error path exactly; costs one closure instead of a record + map, or zero if the holder can be a hoisted constant per registration.
  (b) Hoist the per-registration part. handler-scope-from-meta's inputs for a given sub are (:sub, query-id, sub-meta) — all fixed at registration. Only :call-site / :dispatch-id inheritance is per-call. A scope cached on the registrar slot would make the per-recompute cost the inherit step alone.
  (c) Accept it and say so.

(b) looks the most promising and the least invasive, but it needs someone to check that nothing mutates a scope in place and that HMR/incarnation replacement invalidates the cached record — which is exactly the kind of thing rf2-vxgfnd.220 already had to reason about for sub-meta.

Evidence: ai/findings/2026-07-27.jr76s-narrow-write-attribution.md SS-1.
close_reason: PR #7158. Bead premise FALSIFIED then answered: the always-on SSR error path does NOT read the scope (implementation/ssr/src has zero handler-scope refs; error-emit resolves source-coord from the id-keyed source-coords registry, not the dynamic scope). But the scope still must not be dev-gated -- frame.cljc:2855's EP-0027 make-frame-in-handler guard tests scope PRESENCE, and frame.cljc:605 / router.cljc:2599 / freehand cell.cljc:1177 read :dispatch-id always-on. Shape (b) taken, matching the views.cljs:620 precedent: scope hoisted into the three memo wrappers' closures. Plus inherit-scope no longer assocs nil over nil (2 record copies per handler entry in production). Nothing dev-gated; scope still bound every recompute, every slot reads the same. Node V8 :advanced goog.DEBUG=false: coord-less slope 938.1/939.9 -> 815.9/818.3 (paired control predicted 120.0, measured 121.9, +1.6%); coord-carrying slope 1724.6/1567.5 -> 834.2/818.5 (predicted 744.1, measured 749.0 reversed, +0.7%).

title: frame: replace-app-db! costs 4,470 B with ZERO subscriptions — undecomposed constant that dominates a small app's write
description:
FOUND by rf2-jr76s while building the write-attribution ladder. Not a defect; an unexamined constant.

The ladder (node V8, :advanced, goog.DEBUG false, pointer compression OFF — absolutes are node's, shares transfer, Chrome's tagged slots are half as wide):

  MKDB       the application's own new-db value          921 B
  BAREATOM   + reset! on a watch-free plain atom         890 B
  SPINE0     + the substrate's replace-container!      1,004 B   (epoch open, reset, close, empty drain)
  RFWRITE-0  + frame/replace-app-db!, ZERO subs        4,470 B

So frame/replace-app-db! adds ~3,470 B over a bare substrate write, on a frame with no subscriptions at all: commit-frame-transition! -> commit-frame-record-transition! (read-container, the partition carry-forward, the next-fs map, the changed-set cond->, the two not= partition comparisons), bump-commit-epoch!, and the two partition PROJECTION derived values (:app-db and :runtime-db) recomputing and fanning out.

WHY IT IS WORTH A LOOK. It is a CONSTANT, so at 300 subscriptions it is 1.6% of the write and invisible — which is exactly why it has never been noticed. At 10 subscriptions, the shape a small app or a per-frame tool panel actually has, it is a THIRD of the write. And every frame in a multi-frame page pays it per write.

NOT DECOMPOSED. rf2-jr76s measured it as one number and went after the scaling term instead, which was the right call. This bead is the decomposition nobody has done: split RFWRITE-0 into commit bookkeeping vs the two projections vs bump-commit-epoch!, the same way the per-subscription slope was split.

DO NOT assume there is a win here — report the split first. Some of it is the two-partition contract doing exactly what Spec 002 SS-One physical container, two projection reactions requires, and that is not negotiable for bytes.

Harness: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/write_attribution.cljs already has the ladder and the RFWRITE-0 arm; this is adding rungs under it.

Evidence: ai/findings/2026-07-27.jr76s-narrow-write-attribution.md SS-1, SS-6.
notes: SUPERSEDED FIGURE (rf2-c0awb, PR #7230). This bead's close reason quotes 'C-FRAME registry lookup 0.0 B'. That arm was looking up :wa/frame, which build-rig! never registers, so it priced a registry MISS (frame/frame short-circuits on the registry get). With the arm pointed at a frame the rig actually built, the attribution reads C-FRAME 32.0 B / 1.3% of the delta, not 0.0 B / 0.0%. The other four components are unchanged. CAVEAT: that 32.0 is DISPUTED and must not be quoted — -diagnose PROBE 4 sweeps the same closure and reads a constant 32 B per WINDOW (i.e. ~0 B/call) where the plan reads 32 B/CALL at reps=4000. See rf2-tmzie.
close_reason: PR #7158. Decomposed. RFWRITE-0 4311.7 B minus SPINE0 1003.7 B = 3308.0 B to attribute (node V8, :advanced, goog.DEBUG=false): C-BUMP bump-commit-epoch! 881.1 B (26.6%), C-PARTS partition bookkeeping 705.8 B (21.3%), C-PROJ the two partition projections 670.3 B (20.3%), C-TAGPAIR two [::ok v] pairs 232.1 B (7.0%), C-FRAME registry lookup 0.0 B, residual 818.6 B (24.7%). ONE artefact found: bump-commit-epoch! spelled (fnil inc 0) INLINE, so every commit called fnil and allocated a fresh multi-arity variadic closure to express a constant -- paired control C-BUMP 881.1 vs C-BUMPH 136.0 = 745.0 B/write, 22.5% of the whole constant. Hoisted. Everything else is INTRINSIC: C-PARTS is the changed-partition set the change traces depend on, C-PROJ is Spec 002 SS-One physical container two projection reactions. Untouched. RFWRITE-0 [4223.5-4414.7] -> [3268.0-3532.6], disjoint.

title: bench: arm ORDER contaminates the next arm when the preceding arm allocates orders-of-magnitude-larger objects
description:
TENTH instrument fault class on the allocation-measurement surface. FOUND by rf2-jr76s.

The write-attribution harness carries two controls: .slice() of a packed DOUBLE array (predicted 8.000 B/element, since V8 never pointer-compresses a double) and .slice() of a packed SMI array (predicted 8.000 B/slot on an uncompressed build).

The SMI control read:

  FORWARD arm order   16.1052 B/slot   (2.01x its prediction)
  REVERSED arm order   8.0027 B/slot   (+0.03% of its prediction)
  plain node, outside the harness, same code   ~8.5 B/slot

The only difference is WHAT RAN IMMEDIATELY BEFORE. In forward order that is the DBL-10000 arm, which allocates an 87 KB object per call. In reversed order it is not. So a large-object arm reproducibly DOUBLES the reading of its immediate successor, and nothing in the method predicts it.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE HARNESS. Every allocation study in this repo (B7, B8, read_attribution, write_attribution) runs a plan of arms in one process, and several of them mix arms whose per-call allocation differs by three or four orders of magnitude. If proximity to a large-object arm can inflate a neighbour by 2x, then any single-order run can publish a wrong number for whichever arm happens to follow the biggest one — silently, with a tight range, looking green.

WHAT SAVED IT HERE was running the whole plan in BOTH orders (WA_ORDER=rev) and noticing the two controls disagreed with each other rather than with a prediction. Every other arm reproduced across the two orders to within 1%, so nothing quoted in rf2-jr76s is affected.

NOT DIAGNOSED: the V8 mechanism. Candidates worth eliminating are new-space page-tail filler left by the large arm, a semi-space growth heuristic firing between arms, and allocation-site pretenuring on the .slice() call. A gc() already brackets every sample, so it is not simply un-collected residue.

ACTIONABLE:
1. Treat BOTH-ORDERS as load-bearing method, not a nicety — a study that runs one order has not checked this.
2. Consider ordering plans so no arm follows one that allocates >100x its own per-call bytes, or interposing a settle arm.
3. Add this class to the running fault-class list the studio docs maintain.

Evidence: ai/findings/2026-07-27.jr76s-narrow-write-attribution.md SS-4.
close_reason:
Done in PR #7223 (worker/bench-method-88pie, 3 commits off origin/main).

THE HARNESS PROPERTY, and which of the three remedies was chosen: STRATIFY AND REFUSE, not randomise and not re-order. order_guard.cjs partitions every arm's samples by what ran IMMEDIATELY BEFORE it AND by WHERE IN THE RUN it was measured (first third vs last third), and applies the house rule - overlapping ranges are indistinguishable, so a stratification is a finding only when the ranges are disjoint AND the medians differ beyond a stated tolerance. One stratum on a factor is 'unchecked', and unchecked refuses as loudly as contaminated: a single-order result has not been checked and may not be quoted. Randomising was rejected because it spreads a contaminant across every arm instead of concentrating it in one; re-ordering by size was rejected because it needs each arm's per-call allocation before measuring it and produces no evidence that it worked.

IT CATCHES THE KNOWN 2x CASE, deterministically, by fixture replay: the recorded 16.1052 / 8.0027 pair is REFUSED at ratio 2.0125 on strata of ONE SAMPLE EACH (a guard insisting on ranges would have passed it). The same study's uncontaminated 2830.7 / 2842.8 slope passes. 7 of 7 self-test checks green; b8_run.cjs runs them before the browser starts, the way the key-renaming integrity probe does, and exits 2 on a refusal.

TWO FINDINGS THE BEAD DID NOT PREDICT.

1. THE MITIGATION EVERY B6/B8 ROW CLAIMED DOES NOT EXIST. b8_run.cjs, b6-harness/round! and b6-rows/update-round! all chose the arm for slot j of round r as ARMS[(j + r) % n] and published that as 'arm order rotating'. A cyclic rotation changes which arm goes FIRST, not which arm follows which: arm a sits at slot (a - r) mod n so its predecessor is arm (a - 1) mod n in EVERY round, and only the round seam differs - one sample in R. All three now rotate AND REFLECT on odd indices; the arithmetic is proven both ways in the self-test.

2. THE IMMEDIATE PREDECESSOR IS THE SMALLEST FACTOR, measured twice. Plain node 24.13.0 / V8 13.6, pointer compression OFF: the same packed-SMI .slice() control, nothing else varying, reads 10.32 10.26 10.26 10.26 10.33 10.28 then 8.12 for ever - +27% for six windows, then a step to its 8.016 prediction, and 42.32 on the very first window. Holding position fixed, the predecessor is worth 0.0-0.3% (8.1377 after an 87 KB-object arm, 8.1377 after a 3-element one). Window size, a knob unrelated to order, is worth 2.03x cold and +1.4% warm. B8's own first guarded run agrees: the 'instrument' pseudo-arm read 4,361 B/write first window and 440 last (9.9x), while the predecessor factor came out CLEAN on floor and freehand-interpreted with the ladder's 100 KB-per-write windows as their strata. So the contaminant is how long the process has been running, and BOTH a plan reversal and a change of window size move that - forward-versus-reversed confounds adjacency with position and cannot say which it caught.

This does not restate what happened inside rf2-jr76s's own harness, which is not reproduced here and lives outside the fence; its mechanism stays undiagnosed as the bead says.

Fault class added to docs/design/freehand/studio/freehand-vs-reagent-allocation.md section 5, with a provenance correction (its figures were taken under the rotation that was not a mitigation; no re-take is claimed).

Follow-ups: rf2-tb345 (widen B8's warm-up - one 4-write window is not enough), rf2-om73r (put the guard on implementation/core's write_attribution / read_attribution / B7, which were outside the fence).

Gates: bench:freehand-browser 30/465 exit 0; implementation/freehand JVM 1284/8803 exit 0; test:browser 841/5459 exit 0; order_guard --live exit 0. Raw: ai/findings/2026-07-28.88pie-b8-order-guard-raw.txt (local-only).

title: subs: subscribe's 1-arity builds its no-frame-context error payload on every call - 136 B/call on the happy path
description:
MEASURED (rf2-j8ls2, PR #7154, JVM, -Dre-frame.debug=false, n=300,
ThreadMXBean/getThreadAllocatedBytes, 9 rounds, controls +0.000%, arm
S1-CURFRM): 136.0 B/call, EXACTLY, in every round, and flat across
n = 30 / 300 / 3000.

WHAT IT IS. `subs/subscribe`'s 1-arity:

    (subscribe-in-frame (frame/require-current-frame!
                          :subscribe
                          {:where    're-frame.subs/subscribe
                           :event-id (first query-v)})
                        query-v)

The `extra` map is built on EVERY subscribe. `require-current-frame!`
reads it ONLY when `resolve-current-frame` returns nil -- the
`:rf.error/no-frame-context` path. On the happy path it is pure
garbage: ~96 B for the two-entry map plus ~40 B for `(first query-v)`,
which seqs the vector.

8% of `subscribe`'s post-fix per-call allocation (1612 - 1668 B).

SKETCHES, none of them free of friction -- pick on CLARITY, not bytes:

  (a) `require-current-frame!` accepts a THUNK for `extra`, called only
      on the error path. One more concept at every call site; the
      payload construction moves into a `(fn [] {...})`, which reads
      about as well.
  (b) the call site becomes
        (or (frame/resolve-current-frame)
            (frame/require-current-frame! :subscribe {...}))
      -- zero-allocation on the happy path, but it reads as a redundant
      double-resolve and invites someone to "simplify" it back.
  (c) leave it. 136 B, and the map is genuinely part of what makes the
      error message good.

`(first query-v)` -> `(nth query-v 0)` would save the 40 B on its own
but `first` is the idiomatic spelling and this project does not buy
performance with clarity. Mentioned for completeness, NOT recommended.

RECOMMEND: do not action until rf2-x0fe2 gives a CLJS figure. On the JVM
this is the smallest of the four terms; in CLJS its RELATIVE share rises
(the ~760 B binding term vanishes there), which may or may not change
the answer.

FENCE: implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc +
implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc.
INSTRUMENT: read_attribution.clj, RM_SUITE=subs, arm S1-CURFRM.
close_reason:
PR #7157. ARTEFACT, confirmed and removed by DEFERRING construction — the message is byte-identical.

Chose sketch (b), the reader-then-require spelling, over (a) the thunk: a thunk
would have added a concept at ~20 require-current-frame! call sites repo-wide (or
an ifn?/map type-dispatch) for a win at one, whereas (or (resolve-current-frame)
(require-current-frame! ...)) touches ONE call site and literally spells out the
relationship require-current-frame!'s own docstring already documents ('built on
this reader'). A comment names the site, says why, and says not to collapse it back.
Scoped to subscribe alone — subscribe-once / unsubscribe run once per slot and keep
the plain call.

ERROR UNCHANGED: same extra, same payload, same emit, same throw, same capture-site
ancestry. New .cljc test (subscribe_opts_arity_cljs_test, rides both lanes) pins all
four fields a caller on that path sees — :rf.error/id, :operation, :where, :event-id.
Existing coverage asserted the discriminator only.

MEASURED (JVM, -Dre-frame.debug=false, ThreadMXBean, n=300, 5 rounds = 3 forward +
2 rev, controls +0.000% in all 10): PAIRED CONTROL in read_attribution.clj —
S1-EAGER (retired) 72.0-136.0 vs S1-CURFRM (shipped) 32.0 FLAT in all ten
measurements. Saving 40.0-104.0 B/call.

THE BIMODALITY IS REAL AND EXPLAINED, not averaged away: S1-EAGER reads 136.0 in all
3 forward rounds and 72.0 in both reversed. 136 = 32 (JVM thread-bound
*current-frame* deref — Var.getThreadBinding allocates a MapEntry per read) + 40
((first query-v) seqing the vector) + 64 (the two-entry payload map). Reversed, the
64 B map is SCALAR-REPLACED by escape analysis when the arm runs earlier and
require-current-frame! inlines. The shipped arm is 32.0 flat because neither the map
nor (first query-v) is evaluated on the happy path.

The bead's 136 B figure was thus (var deref 32) + (payload 104), not (map 96) +
(first 40) as estimated. The 32 B floor does NOT exist in CLJS (no thread bindings),
so the SHARE this saves is larger there than on the JVM.

(first query-v) -> (nth query-v 0) NOT taken, as the bead recommended.

Gates: core JVM 2152/10616 green; npm run test:cljs 11799/58740 green.

title: bench: re-take B6's update row WITHOUT the microtask yield, gated on the non-vacuity check
description:
FOUND by rf2-huhno's re-take (PR #7152).

rf2-huhno asked whether the update row should be re-taken without timed-write!'s single microtask yield, on the reasoning that rf2-w2m25 / PR #7133 gives Freehand a synchronous commit so the yield is historical. b6-rows' own docstring carries the same suggestion.

THE RE-TAKE SAYS IT IS NOT A FREE TIGHTENING. Measured on main at 7c41225b4b, Freehand's broad-update window has RESTRUCTURED: the empty react-dom/flushSync that used to carry 3.0-3.5 ms now costs ~0.0, and the gap that used to be ~0.2 ms now carries 3.6-3.9 ms. Freehand's notification and React's render and commit run INSIDE that microtask.

So removing the yield does not remove the work. Either it moves into the flushSync (total unchanged, legs re-attributed again) or the notification has not yet fired when the empty flushSync runs, the commit lands after the measured window, and the DOM read-back fails — which is precisely the fault b6-rows records from the first attempt at this row (80 of 320 floor samples ended holding the old value).

WHAT IT NEEDS: a yield-free variant of timed-write! run against the flushSync non-vacuity check rf2-0fgth added, on all four arms, with the per-write DOM read-back as the gate. If every arm verifies, the row can be re-taken without the yield and every figure tightens by the microtask boundary. If Freehand fails verification, the yield stays and b6-rows' docstring should stop describing it as removable.

This is a change to the PUBLISHED WINDOW, not a re-measurement, which is why it is filed rather than folded into the re-take.
close_reason:
Done in PR #7223. ANSWER: THE YIELD STAYS.

b6_yield_app rides b6_prod_run.cjs's B6_INIT_FN seam so the driver, arms and fixture are the published ones. Chromium 147 headless via Playwright, :advanced, goog.DEBUG false. Six rounds of 3 warmup + 8 samples; THREE windows and five arms interleaved at the sample level (window rotating, arm order rotating and reflecting per rf2-88pie); every write read back out of the DOM inside its own window.

THE NON-VACUITY GATE, asked of every arm and every shape before any figure. Both Freehand arms FAIL the yield-free window. Across both rows 2,772 writes of 20,790 failed their read-back and EVERY ONE is a Freehand arm in the no-yield window: 66 of 66 per arm broad, 1,320 of 1,320 per arm narrow, and 0 in every other one of the fifteen (arm, window) cells. The write sits outside any flush, so rf2-w2m25 / #7133's closer never fires, the empty flushSync after it has nothing to commit, and the clock stops on the OLD value. It reads 0.7 ms against the published 3.5 - a 5x 'speed-up' that is the commit landing outside the window, exactly the fault b6-rows records from this row's first attempt.

BROAD, p50 ms/write, ranges across 6 rounds:
  floor                 yield 0.1 [0.1-0.2]  no-yield 0.1 [0.1-0.2]  in-flush 0.2 [0.1-0.2]
  freehand-interpreted  yield 3.5 [3.2-4.3]  no-yield 0.7 [0.6-0.8] INVALID  in-flush 3.5 [3.4-4.7]
  freehand-compiled     yield 3.1 [3.0-3.8]  no-yield 0.6 [0.6-0.8] INVALID  in-flush 3.2 [3.0-3.8]
  reagent               yield 0.4 [0.3-0.5]  no-yield 0.4 [0.3-0.5]  in-flush 0.3 [0.3-0.5]
  floor+spin (control)  yield 2.1 [2.1-2.1]  no-yield 2.1 [2.1-2.1]  in-flush 2.1 [2.0-2.1]

DID THE YIELD MATTER? No, and that is the second half of the answer. The ONE yield-free window that DOES verify on all four arms - flushSync(write) then the arm's drain - reads 3.5 [3.4-4.7] against the published 3.5 [3.2-4.3] on interpreted Freehand and 3.2 [3.0-3.8] against 3.1 [3.0-3.8] on compiled. OVERLAPPING RANGES on every arm, so indistinguishable. The legs say where it went: 0.6-0.8 write plus 2.5-3.2 gap becomes 3.4-4.7 write plus 0.0 gap. Same work, third re-attribution. rf2-huhno's hoped-for tightening does not exist, and #7133's extra commit pass is inside that window and not separable from it here.

THE NARROW ROW IS THE CAUTION. There the invalid no-yield window's range OVERLAPS the published one (7.5-9.9 against 8.9-11.5 per 20-write sample), so by this repo's own rule the clock would have called them indistinguishable and accepted a window in which 1,320 of 1,320 writes never reached the page. ONLY THE DOM READ-BACK CAUGHT IT.

POSITIVE CONTROL: :floor+spin, the floor arm with a 2.0 ms CPU spin around its own drain, predicted to read the floor's plus 2.0 ms PER WRITE OF THE SAMPLE. Broad predicted 2.1 / measured 2.1 (error 0.0) in two windows, -0.1 in the third; narrow predicted 41.7 / measured 41.1 (-1.4%). The per-write factor is not decoration - the first run predicted a flat +2.0 and read +39.1 on the narrow row, and the control caught the harness's own arithmetic.

b6-rows' docstring, its published :measurement-method string and b6_update_dom_cljs_test's namespace docstring have all STOPPED describing the yield as removable, which is what the bead asked for on this branch of the outcome. Recorded in docs/design/freehand/studio/bulk-rerender-where-the-time-goes.md section 7, where rf2-huhno left the question. The gate's own first-version bug is on the record there too: it ran its shapes back to back and read in-flush as failing while the measured in-flush window verified 660 of 660 writes; it now settles before each shape.

Gates: bench:freehand-browser 30/465 exit 0; implementation/freehand JVM 1284/8803 exit 0; test:browser 841/5459 exit 0. Raw: ai/findings/2026-07-28.vxfjt-yield-ablation-raw.txt (local-only).

title: bench: B6's mount arm binds no frame, so the published row measures a shape no application uses
description:
FOUND while settling rf2-prjh0 (PR #7146). Filed as a METHOD note, not a defect - no published figure is wrong.

rf2-prjh0 asked whether B6's Freehand mount arm overstates because it creates a frame per sample. It does not: a frameless v/mount runs no plan and creates no frame. But the measurement that settled it turned up the opposite, smaller point.

EVERY REAL APPLICATION BINDS A FRAME. B6's mount arm does not - it passes only a :disambiguator. So the published mount row measures a mount shape that ships nowhere, and it is the CHEAPEST such shape. Measured, paired within round, 6 rounds:
  W1 (1,203 el)  a shared pre-created frame costs x1.038 more than the published arm, higher in 6 of 6 rounds
  W2 (301 el)    x1.109, higher in 6 of 6

So interpreted W1 mount against Reagent is ~3.8% better in the table than an application would see, and W2 ~10.9%. Both are small against a ~2x gap and neither changes any conclusion - which is exactly why this is P3 and not a correction.

THE CHOICE, and it is a real one: either (a) move B6's Freehand mount arms to a shared pre-created :frame so the row prices the shape consumers ship, re-taking the whole row against a floor measured in the same run (the ratio is only meaningful that way), or (b) leave it and keep the note that now sits in freehand-vs-reagent.md §1. Option (a) makes Freehand look slightly worse and is probably the more honest row; option (b) costs nothing. Not worth a re-run on its own - fold it into the next occasion the mount row is re-taken for another reason.

The arms already exist and are shipped: b7_mount_frame.cljs carries fh-no-frame, fh-shared-frame and fh-frame-per-sample side by side, so whoever re-takes the row does not need to build anything.
close_reason:
Resolved as option (b) — keep the frameless arm, state the magnitude in the table rather than only in a linked report.

The mount row was re-taken on main at 7c41225b4b (fresh, as part of rf2-huhno's b6_prod_run): published arm 3.056 x floor [2.931-3.226], Reagent 1.588 [1.500-1.742] -> 1.92x Reagent. Applying PR #7146's measured x1.038 for the shared pre-created frame puts the shipped shape at ~2.00x Reagent.

Option (a) rejected: the correction is 3.8% on W1, smaller than the row's own round-to-round spread [2.931-3.226], and re-basing a release-gate row requires re-taking the floor in the same run. The conclusion is identical either way — interpreted mount is about twice Reagent — so the change buys a third digit and costs a gate re-base.

freehand-vs-reagent.md §1's note now carries both numbers and the rejection rationale, so the row is no longer quietly generous. PR #7152.

title: pair-mcp: invoke-and-guard drops ex-data — relay 1's half of the two-relay asymmetry
description:
Mirror image of rf2-6tzm5, found while fixing it.

pair-mcp has two consumer-facing error relays. rf2-6tzm5 fixed relay 2
(`tools/probe.cljs` `err->result`), which kept the ex-data and dropped
the ex-message; it now carries BOTH.

Relay 1 — `server.cljs` `invoke-and-guard` (~line 539) — still has the
opposite defect:

  (wire/result {:ok? false :reason :handler-threw :message (.-message err)} true)

It keeps the MESSAGE and drops `(ex-data err)` entirely. So a throw that
fires while a tool body BUILDS its request loses its `:rf.error/id` —
the machine discriminator a consumer's agent BRANCHES on — plus every
actionable slot the author put in ex-data (`:where`, `:recovery`, and
the per-site payload).

Live example: `tools/eval_form.cljs` `emit-name`'s
`:rf.error/pair-mcp-rt-let-binding-bad-shape` throw. Its message rides
(error_boundary_test pins the sentence + the trailing token, so the
token at least survives INSIDE the message string), but its ex-data
does not — an agent must regex the token out of prose instead of
reading a keyword slot.

Fix shape mirrors rf2-6tzm5's: merge ex-data alongside, letting the
explicit `:reason :handler-threw` and `:message` keys keep their
precedence over an ex-data map that happens to carry the same keys
(note the precedence is the OPPOSITE way round from relay 2, because
here the relay's own `:reason` is the envelope discriminator).

Not folded into rf2-6tzm5 because it is a distinct blast radius:
every relay-1 handler-threw envelope gains ex-data slots, and
`error_boundary_test`'s relay-1 rows plus any `:handler-threw`
conformance fixture want checking first. rf2-6tzm5 verified relay 2's
consumers; relay 1's are unmeasured.
close_reason: Closed

title: freehand-views browser sweep can now assert a reactively-driven repaint
description:
Follow-on to rf2-r83ni (record correction) and rf2-8cnxg / rf2-jt8vz (the fix).

The freehand-views deck's browser scenario in
tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs drives commits through
the mount verb (`Mount root`), which reads current values regardless of
the notification channel. It does that because, when it was written, a
Freehand ViewCell under the Reagent adapter never repainted — the
observation port held a watch on a Reaction that had captured no
sources — so a reactively-driven re-render was not assertable on any
host that also mounts Xray.

That constraint is gone. The port now activates the derived value via
`:adapter/activate-derived-value!`, so pressing `+` repaints
[[readout]] on this very deck. The mount-verb route is now a choice
rather than the only option, and the sweep could assert the stronger
fact directly: dispatch `+`, assert the readout's text advances
WITHOUT a remount.

Worth doing because it is the only browser-level proof that the
activation fix holds end to end in a real DOM — the substrate contract
tests cover the port, but not a Freehand cell repainting on a page that
is simultaneously hosting Xray's shell.

Scope: one added assertion in the existing
'freehand-views populated Views roster' scenario, or a small sibling
scenario. Prose in tools/xray/spec/017-Test-Coverage-Matrix.md already
says this is 'tracked separately' — this is that bead.
close_reason: PR #7136 — expectReactiveRepaint added to the freehand-views scenario: press + with the Xray shell mounted, assert the readout's text advances AND that it advanced on the SAME DOM node (a remount replaces it). Non-vacuity proven: neutering (interop/activate-derived-value! reaction) reds exactly this scenario ('expected text "1" but got "0"') with app-db shown at :count 1 in the trace; restored, green. tools/xray/spec/017-Test-Coverage-Matrix.md updated in the same PR (matrix row + the 'tracked separately' paragraph replaced by the fact).

title: Add the B6 witness twin pair to compiled_source_delta_jvm_test's twin-files table
description:

They are kept character-identical by hand, but they are NOT in the `twin-files` table in `implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/compiled_source_delta_jvm_test.clj`, which is what holds every other twin pair (tree_views/compiled_views, b1, b2, b4) down.

title: Rename the with-redefs 'production gate' suites — they cannot reach a load-time gate
notes:
Split out of rf2-f8x2i.

`re-frame.interop/debug-enabled?` is read ONCE, at namespace-load time. Every
suite in the repo that names itself a production-gate test reaches that gate
with `with-redefs` AFTER the framework has loaded, which cannot change anything
the gate decided at load. Those suites are testing a rebindable Var, not the

  implementation/core/test/re_frame/jvm_prod_gate_integration_test.clj
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/ep0008_producers_jvm_gate_test.clj
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/interop_debug_gate_test.clj

The name is the whole problem: rf2-9c2jf was a TOTAL dispatch failure under the
documented production gate that stayed green, and part of why it went unnoticed
is that the roster of "prod gate" suites looked full. A reviewer reading the
file list had no way to see that none of them ran under the gate.

  - Rename or re-docstring the suites whose names claim the production gate so
    they say what they actually pin (a `with-redefs` posture, which is a real

Mutation-proven (a probe file with no disclaimer reds the gate, naming it). title: CI: Maven Central 403s under concurrent-PR load break classpath resolution on the MCP conformance lanes
description:
OBSERVED TWICE on 2026-07-26/27 during a high-concurrency session (6-7 workers, 6+ open PRs), on two DIFFERENT artifacts:
  - org.jsoup:jsoup:jar:1.15.2 -> MCP conformance tools/story-mcp (PR #7117)
  - com.cognitect:transit-cljs:jar:0.8.280 -> MCP conformance wire-vocab (PR #7123), explicitly 'status code: 403, reason phrase: Forbidden' from https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/

SHAPE: 'Error building classpath. Failed to read artifact descriptor' / ArtifactDescriptorException / ArtifactTransportException. The classpath never builds, so the MCP server never starts, and the CLIENT-side symptom is 'FAIL: MCP error -32000: Connection closed' - which reads like a code fault and cost real diagnosis time twice.

Both cleared on a plain re-run, so it is transient, not a broken coordinate. 403 (not 404) points at rate-limiting/throttling of the runner rather than a missing artefact.

WHY IT MATTERS: it costs a re-run and a diagnosis every time, and the misleading downstream symptom invites a wrong conclusion - the first instinct is to suspect the diff. Under sustained parallel dispatch it will recur.

POSSIBLE REMEDIES, none investigated, deliberately not chosen here: cache the Maven/gitlibs dependency tree across jobs so the lanes stop re-resolving from central; use a mirror; or retry the classpath build specifically. DO NOT gold-plate - if dependency caching is already configured for other lanes and merely missing on these, that is the whole fix.

ACCEPTANCE: the MCP conformance lanes stop failing on artefact resolution under load, or - if that is not economically fixable - the failure names itself as an infrastructure fault rather than surfacing only as 'Connection closed'.

Filed by the mayor after diagnosing both instances; neither was a code defect.
notes:
Merged-PR audit of #7132: the pre-resolution wrapper retries every nonzero `clojure -P` exit and, after exhaustion, categorically annotates it as `INFRASTRUCTURE, not this diff`. That includes deterministic diff-owned failures such as a malformed deps file or nonexistent coordinate; the PR's own failure-path check used a bogus coordinate, demonstrating the misclassification. Keep the bounded resolution-only retry, but make the final annotation cause-neutral (or classify only known transient transport signatures) so CI does not tell programmers to rerun a real dependency defect.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7221 (2026-08-01): reopen exact owner. The classifier still makes the categorical claim this bead was reopened to remove. TRANSIENT_SIGNATURES includes broad ArtifactTransportException/MetadataTransportException plus every 403, UnknownHostException, connection-refused, and 5xx; those strings justify a retry, but do not prove ownership. A diff-added auth-protected repository, misspelled repository host, or intentionally unavailable endpoint can emit the same signatures. Hermetic reproduction with an exported clojure stub printing ArtifactTransportException: authentication failed for repository configured by this change plus status code: 403 produced three attempts and the final INFRASTRUCTURE, not this diff / not of any coordinate annotation. Keep the bounded retry for transport-looking failures, but make the exhausted verdict cause-neutral and quote the signature as evidence that a rerun may help, not as proof the diff is innocent. Add a hermetic classifier test for matched, unmatched, success, and changing-signature attempts; no retry framework or broad parser needed.
close_reason:
AUDIT REOPEN SCOPE FIXED in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7343.
Read the rest of this reason before treating the ORIGINAL acceptance as met —
part of it is not fixable from inside this repo, and that is a finding, not an
omission.

WHAT THIS PR FIXES (the #7221 audit's exact reopen scope). The exhausted
verdict no longer makes the categorical claim the audit demanded be removed.
It read `INFRASTRUCTURE, not this diff` / `not of any coordinate`. A transport
signature earns a retry; it does not establish ownership. The audit proved the
gap hermetically: a stub emitting `ArtifactTransportException: authentication
failed for repository configured by this change` plus `status code: 403`
matched, was retried three times, and was then told it was not its own fault —
of a failure the diff owned outright.

Narrowing TRANSIENT_SIGNATURES cannot fix that: the ambiguity is in the
strings themselves, not in the list's width — a diff-added auth-protected
repository, a misspelled repository host and a dead endpoint all emit them. So
the list is UNCHANGED and the bounded retry is KEPT; the verdict changed. It
still quotes the signature as evidence a re-run may help, and now says what
that signature does not establish, pointing the reader back at any repository
or coordinate the change touched.

HERMETIC CLASSIFIER TEST ADDED, as the audit asked, covering all four named
cases and two more: success on the first attempt; transient-then-success;
UNMATCHED (not retried, no cause claimed); MATCHED-and-exhausted
(cause-neutral verdict); the audit's own diff-owned auth 403; and a signature
that CHANGES between attempts, which must be re-classified per attempt rather
than latched from the first. It stubs `clojure` (scripted per-attempt output)
and `sleep` (so 45s of real backoff costs nothing) onto PATH and runs the REAL
script — no network, no JVM, no retry framework, no broad parser. Two of the
six FAIL against the pre-fix wording, so it is not vacuous. It lives in
test:script-policy because that CI job is Node-only (no Maven), which is also
why it stubs rather than resolving anything.

WHAT IS NOT FIXED, AND CANNOT BE FROM HERE. The 403 itself. It is Maven
Central throttling a shared CI egress IP under concurrent load. Dependency
caching was already ruled out as the missing piece and remains so: every MCP
conformance lane already restores ~/.m2 + ~/.gitlibs + ~/.deps.clj, and a
cache MISS (a deps.edn the PR touched, a cold key) is exactly when the lane
must go to Central, which is exactly when this fires. The remaining options
both cost real money or real repo weight and are maintainer decisions, not a
worker's:
  - a mirror/proxy (Artifactory, Nexus, or a GitHub Actions Maven proxy):
    removes the class outright, but needs a hosted service, credentials in CI,
    and an operational owner;
  - vendoring the dependency tree: removes the network entirely, at a large
    and ongoing repo cost.

Closing on the ACCEPTANCE's second limb, which is satisfied: the failure now
names itself at the resolution step rather than surfacing only as the
misleading downstream `FAIL: MCP error -32000: Connection closed`, and it no
longer tells a programmer to re-run a failure their own diff owns. If the
maintainer wants the mirror decision tracked, that is worth its own bead.

GATES: test:script-policy exit 0 (classifier 6 passed), bash -n exit 0,
node --check exit 0, test:cljs exit 0, test:browser exit 0.

title: an unregistered owner's NON-MAP-params scoped key still rides verbatim under an unnamed slot on a family trace row
description:
FOUND while closing rf2-wd9im's merged-PR audit #7013 (non-map canonical params). Filed rather than fixed because the remedy costs more than the leak, and that judgement is the mayor's — this may well be a correct-to-close.

THE RESIDUE. `re-frame.resources.trace-egress/scoped-key-shape?` now recognises a scoped key `[scope resource-id canonical-params]` on either of two proofs: a MAP at position 2, or the resource REGISTRY knowing position 1. A key with NEITHER — non-map canonical params AND an unregistered / cleared / hot-reloaded-away owner — is not recognised, so under an UNNAMED slot on a resource-family trace row (`:blocking`, `:identities`, `:optimistic-keys`, an embedded `:work/id`, …) it falls to the recursive walk and its scope + params ride verbatim. The fail-closed posture says an owner we cannot read is not provably safe, so in principle it should redact.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY FIXED. There is nothing left to read. `[:rf.scope/global :gone/thing ["x"]]` and `:owner [:app :l 1]` are the same shape to the projector once the map proof and the registry proof are both gone, so closing it means redacting EVERY structural 3-vector in the family — `:owner`, `:cause`, a three-id `:branch`. That is the over-redaction the shape-driven default was specifically designed to avoid (rf2-wd9im's own `:branch` control asserts it), and for the resource tools it is as much a defect as the leak.

WHERE IT IS ALREADY COVERED, which is most of the surface:
  - a NAMED slot (`:resource/key` / `:resource/keys` / `:matched` / …) projects BY POSITION, so an unregistered owner's key redacts there whatever its params shape;
  - inside an fx CARRIER, `named?` does the same job — position 1 of a `[:rf.work/resource …]` work-id and any `resource`-namespaced map key are family-planted by construction (this bead's sibling arm in the same PR restored that, and `fx-carrier-named-slot-fails-closed-for-an-unregistered-non-map-params-owner` pins it).

So the uncovered case is exactly: unnamed slot + family row + non-map params + unregistered owner. A live app hits it only when a resource is cleared or hot-reloaded between the row's emission and its egress projection.

OPTIONS IF IT IS TO BE CLOSED, none of them obviously worth it:
  (a) accept and document — the docstring already states the boundary explicitly;
  (b) have the emit sites TAG the slot (a `resource`-namespaced slot name, or wrap the key), which turns a shape question into a naming one and reintroduces the roster rot rf2-wd9im removed;
  (c) carry the family's own marker inside the key, which changes the canonical resource identity — far too big for this.

MY RECOMMENDATION: (a). Close as accepted boundary unless a real reproduction turns up.
close_reason:
CLOSED AS ACCEPTED BOUNDARY (mayor, per the finding worker's own recommendation on PR #7115).

THE CASE: a scoped key with NON-MAP params, naming an UNREGISTERED owner, under an UNNAMED slot on a family trace row. Both of the projector's proofs are gone at once — the map-at-position-2 shape proof and the resource-registry proof — so the key is structurally INDISTINGUISHABLE from ordinary app data such as [:app :l 1].

WHY THE REMEDY IS WORSE THAN THE DISEASE: closing it requires tokenizing any 3-vector that merely wears the scoped-key skeleton. That is precisely the 'tokenize a foreign payload wholesale' move rf2-1kiuj already examined and rejected, because it redacts a PLAIN owner's ordinary request map. The vector-of-vectors guard was also weighed and rejected on PR #7115: ':branch' is a vector of route ids on this very row, and the new control asserts a three-id :branch rides verbatim.

WHY CLOSING IS SAFE: an UNREGISTERED owner has no :sensitive?/:sensitive declaration to honour in the first place — there is no registration to read it from — so the redaction obligation that makes the other seven leaks real does not attach here. The boundary is documented in scoped-key-shape?'s own docstring, which outlives a bead.

POSTURE: pre-alpha masterpiece, but not gold-plating and not drowning in minutiae. An explicitly documented and reasoned boundary is engineering; contorting the projector to cover an unreachable case is not. Reopen if a real consumer hits it.

title: Donor row 284: relocate the scaffold-smoke lane out of implementation/ui, which is what re-blinds the row-409 gate
description:
Two findings converge here, both from workers that measured rather than reasoned.

FINDING 1 (rf2-nutll verification worker, 2026-07-26). Row 409 (examples/ui/minimal-counter) is MIGRATED and its disposition is correct — but its gate is now BLIND IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and the worker proved it rather than assuming:

  * Flipping the row back to `pending` does NOT yield rc=1, contrary to the predicted proof standard. `check_current` uses the loose DONOR_EVIDENCE_RE, which matches the bare substring `implementation/ui`, and README.md:89 still links `../../../implementation/ui/scaffold-smoke/test/scaffold_smoke_test.clj` — a TRUE path to the CI lane gating this scaffold.
