title: Read continuation reply of an INFINITE feed: a :data-rooted declaration does not match the merged-items vector (no index-free fork)
description:
Surfaced by rf2-ko5lm's widening and FILED not fixed per the dispatch rule.

WHAT LEAKS. rf2-ko5lm gave read continuations the mutation's declaration redaction: `trace_egress/redact-reply-declarations` applies `classification/redact-continuation-reply` over the read owner's spec, re-rooting a `:data`-rooted declaration onto the reply's `:value`. That reaches `re-frame.classification/redact-with-paths` -> `walk-with-paths`, whose `:decide` is an EXACT path membership test (`(contains? sensitive-set path)`), paths built by conj-ing map keys and vector indices.

For a SCALAR resource that is exactly right: `{:sensitive [[:data :email]]}` becomes `[:value :email]` and matches.

For an INFINITE FEED it does not match anything. `events/infinite-reply-value` delivers the MERGED / flattened item list as `:value` (rf2-c64uiz — both the fresh-skip cache hit and the async page-0 settle deliver that one shape), so the runtime path is `[:value <i> :email]` and the declaration is `[:value :email]`. No index-free fork, no match, and the declared field rides the fx carriers verbatim.

THE DURABLE SIDE DOES FORK, which is what makes this a disagreement rather than a uniform limitation. `classification/project-entry-data` says so explicitly: "INFINITE feeds ride for free: the lowered decl is `[… :data :token]`, the runtime `:data` is the page VECTOR, and `elide-wire-value`'s index-free fork (`fork-index-paths`) matches the index-free decl against the indexed runtime path `[… :data <page-idx> :token]` on EVERY page — no special per-page branch." So a feed's declared field redacts in the durable entry and rides raw in the continuation echo of it — the same two-carriers-one-rule shape rf2-ko5lm closed for scalars, still open for feeds.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD. The two walkers are different primitives. `redact-with-paths` is the path-substitution walker the carrier redactions use (mutation reply, execute event args, invalid-params error); `elide-wire-value` is the schema-first elision walker with the index-free fork. Making the carrier walker fork is a change to a CORE primitive with four callers, not a resources-family change, and it must not silently start matching indexed paths for the mutation reply / execute-args callers that never intended it. The alternative — route the reply's `:value` through `project-egress` instead — needs an absolute registry offset the reply does not have (it is a transient carrier value, not a runtime-db path), which is the whole reason rf2-ko5lm derived from the spec rather than reading the registry.

SCOPE NOTE. Only the `:data` axis is affected; `[:params …]` / `[:scope …]` declarations index a map and match fine. And a feed that declares its slot at the ITEM level today has no spelling that means "each item" — worth settling in the same ruling.

PROOF STANDARD: RED and GREEN with identical test and assertion counts differing only in failures, driving a real `[:rf.resource/ensure … :reply-to …]` against a registered infinite feed, plus the two-sided control (a feed declaring nothing rides byte-identical; an undeclared sibling field inside each item survives).
notes:
See rf2-dl7bz for the preserved in-flight state: a clustered worker holds uncommitted work for both beads in worktree C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/egress-keyfork (branch worker/egress-keyfork-dl7bz), zero commits, no remote, during the 2026-07-26 API 529 outage. That worktree must not be reaped by the hygiene loop; recovery is to resume the same agent, never to dispatch a second worker onto the branch.

FIXED — PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7099 (worker egress-keyfork, 2026-07-26).

SCOPING, which was the live question. The fork is OPT-IN and reaches exactly ONE
caller. `classification/redact-with-paths` gains a 4th argument; the 3-arity —
i.e. every pre-existing call site — delegates with `index-free? = false`, under
which the candidate declaration-coordinate set is the singleton `#{path}` and
matching is byte-for-byte the exact membership test the walker always applied.
`resources.classification/redact-continuation-reply` is the sole opt-in. The
mutation-reply and execute-args callers the bead warned about are NOT widened:
`project-execute-event-args` still calls the 3-arity, as do `redact-event-vec`,
`http.privacy-body/classify-decoded`, `machines.ssr/project-snapshot-data` and
`redact-by-classification`. `redact-continuation-reply` is shared by the mutation
reply and the read reply, and both get the fork deliberately — it is ONE
projection-relative declaration surface re-rooted onto ONE carrier shape, and
splitting them is what would let the two drift.

THE SPELLING QUESTION, settled rather than deferred. A feed needs no "each item"
wildcard: the index-free declaration already IS that spelling, because it is what
the DURABLE side has always meant by `[:data :email]` on a page vector
(`project-entry-data` -> `elide-wire-value` -> `fork-index-paths`). No vocabulary
was added; the carrier now honours the reading the durable side established.

GRAIN. Index fork ONLY — no `:map-of` key-skip fork. So the carrier walker stays
strictly MORE precise than the durable side's, and a positional index can never
float a declaration past a named slot.

PROOF. `epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj` §(rf2-zaopo), a real
`[:rf.resource/ensure … :reply-to …]` against a registered infinite feed
(`:declared/feed`, enveloped pages + `:page->items`), both continuation paths:
  RED   58 tests / 395 assertions / 19 failures / 0 errors
  GREEN 58 tests / 395 assertions /  0 failures / 0 errors
Identical test and assertion counts; failures the only difference.

TWO-SIDED CONTROL, both sides asserted:
  - `fx-carrier-keeps-an-undeclared-feeds-merged-items-byte-identical` — the SAME
    page through `:plain/feed`, which declares neither axis: every reply-carrier
    row's tags byte-identical raw vs projected, items readable field for field,
    no carrier row stamped `:sensitive?`. It PASSES ON RED AND ON GREEN (0
    failures in the RED run), which is what makes it a control rather than a
    second acceptance arm.
  - the undeclared sibling `:display-name` survives in EVERY item while `:email`
    redacts and `:large`-declared `:avatar` becomes the size marker.
  - `fx-carrier-index-free-fork-does-not-reach-an-undeclared-nested-slot` — an
    `:email` one NAMED slot deeper (`[:value 0 :meta :email]`) is a different
    position and rides verbatim.
  - `trusted-local-include-sensitive-keeps-raw-declared-feed-items` — the
    redaction is the off-box default, not a strip.

REGRESSION EVIDENCE for the un-widened callers (all foreground, EXIT=0):
  core       2126 tests / 10492 assertions / 0F 0E
  resources   734 tests /  6820 assertions / 0F 0E
  epoch       514 tests /  6859 assertions / 0F 0E
  http        493 tests /  3787 assertions / 0F 0E
  machines   1195 tests /  4164 assertions / 0F 0E
  test:cljs 11549 tests / 57808 assertions / 0F 0E

DOES NOT COVER rf2-rnsv2. That bead is the read-FAILURE continuation's `:error`
envelope. `carrier-decl-paths` re-roots `:data` -> `:value`, `:params` ->
`:params`, `:scope` -> `:scope` and nothing onto `:error`, so no declaration can
reach it and the index-free mode changes nothing there. Its ruling stands
untouched.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7107 (2026-07-26) — DEFAULT-MODE INVARIANT CORRECTED; CANDIDATE-CARDINALITY CLAIM STILL FALSE.

The new wording correctly says default mode carries `#{path}` while the concrete path remains a declaration prefix and `#{}` after pruning, so exact matching is preserved. But the preceding sentence still says the candidate set “stays bounded by the declaration cardinality.” In `:index-free?` mode, unchanged candidates ride an index while indexed interpretations are added, so one declaration can keep several of its prefixes alive at once. Against the merged private functions, declaration `#{[0 0 0]}` produced candidate counts `[1 2 3 4]` and final set `#{[] [0] [0 0] [0 0 0]}`: four candidates for one declaration. State the bound in terms of the finite declaration-prefix vocabulary (plus the retained root), not declaration count. No behavior defect was found; the projection gate remained green at 30 tests / 115 assertions and remote PR checks were 63 pass / 0 fail / 13 skipped.

title: Resource trace egress: a :serialize owner's projection-relative :params / :scope declaration is not honoured inside :resource/key
description:
SEVENTH-ish in the resource-egress leak family, surfaced by rf2-ko5lm's widening and FILED not fixed per the dispatch rule.

WHAT LEAKS. `re-frame.resources.ssr/project-scoped-key` projects a scoped key `[scope resource-id params]` by the COARSE `whole-entry-disposition` only. For a `:serialize` owner it returns the key VERBATIM. That is correct for the SSR durable path, which has a documented registry-driven counterpart (`classification/project-entry-params` walks the params component through `project-egress` seeded at the lowered registry offset, because it has the entry's `key-id` and the live frame). The docstring says so in as many words: "The trace / tool egress callers pass `:serialize` through verbatim (they rely on the coarse disposition + the digest below, not per-slot params)."

The TRACE / off-box egress callers have no such counterpart. So a resource declaring

  (rf/reg-resource :account/summary
    {:sensitive [[:params :account-id]] ...} ...)

with no coarse `:sensitive?` has its declared `:account-id` ride RAW inside `:resource/key` on every `:rf.resource/*` / `:rf.mutation/*` family row, inside every scoped-keys vector slot, inside every `[:rf.work/resource <key> <gen>]` work-id, and inside every fx carrier (`:rf.fx/args` / `:rf.event/fx`) the key reaches. Off-box, epoch, MCP.

THE SHAPE IS THE FAMILY'S USUAL ONE. rf2-ko5lm just closed the READ CONTINUATION REPLY's copy of those same params (`redact-reply-declarations` applies the owner declaration to the reply's `:params` slot). The key's copy sits one slot over on the same carrier and still rides. Two carriers of one value, one rule applied — the rf2-irwsq shape. `epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj` §(rf2-ko5lm) names this residue in prose and deliberately does NOT assert it, so no test has to change when this lands.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD, not part of rf2-ko5lm. The reply is ONE map on ONE pair of carriers and its fix is the mutation's own `redact-continuation-reply` reused. This is the scoped KEY, which is the family's universal carrier: the fix has to live in the shared `disposition+project-key` pipeline that SSR durable egress, the tooling algebra view, and the trace projector all reuse, so it changes three egress boundaries at once and has to be judged against `project-scoped-key`'s explicit deferral rather than around it.

THE HARD PART, which is why the deferral exists. A scoped key is a CEDN-1 byte-keyed identity (Spec 016 §Resource identity) and the cache-key-identity round-trip depends on it — `registry-classifies-under?` exists precisely so an unnecessary walk cannot collapse a list↔vector params kind (rf2-wgutc2). A per-slot substitution inside the params component changes the key's bytes, so any fix must decide what a tool's per-key JOIN means afterwards. Options, none free:
  - substitute in place and accept that a declared key no longer round-trips to its cache identity;
  - content-address the WHOLE params component when any `:params`-rooted declaration exists (the `:redact` shape, applied on a declaration rather than a coarse claim) — keeps distinctness and joins, loses the undeclared sibling params a tool can currently read;
  - leave the key and treat the declaration as data-axis-only, documenting that `[:params …]` declarations are an SSR-durable-only surface — which would need `reg-resource` to say so loudly rather than accept the path silently.

The second is probably right (it is the grain the coarse arm already uses and it preserves joins), but it is a RULING, not a mechanical fix.

PROOF STANDARD when it is taken: RED and GREEN with identical test and assertion counts differing only in failures, plus the two-sided control — a plain owner's key rides byte-identical and `:rf.scope/global` is untouched.
notes:
LANDED — PR #7254 (branch worker/slot-params-dl7bz), 2026-07-29.

RATIFIED SHAPE IMPLEMENTED AS RULED, and kept narrow. `ssr/project-scoped-key` is NOT widened: it still takes and ignores its spec argument and still rides a `:serialize` key verbatim, and `project-scoped-key-still-defers-on-serialize` is a standing test that reds if anyone moves the arm into the shared projection. `implementation/ssr/**` and `resources/ssr.cljc` are untouched by the diff. The per-slot arm is `trace_egress/redact-key-declarations`, beside `redact-reply-declarations`, built from the already-public `spec-declaration-marks`; `tooling/project-key-for-egress` opts into the same helper.

BOTH tooling.cljc DOCSTRINGS WERE STILL FALSE when checked, and are now true — one by implementation, one by CORRECTION. The EP-0015 section comment ('applies the resource's per-slot :params projection-relative declarations') is now true of the code. `project-key-for-egress`'s ':serialize projects per-slot :params-schema marks' could NOT be honoured as written — EP-0025 removed the schema route into durable classification — so that clause is corrected to name the projection-relative declaration, with the correction stated in the docstring itself.

A SECOND DEFECT SURFACED AND IS FIXED IN THE SAME PR. `row-owner-redacts?` borrowed `project-trace-scoped-key`'s `sensitive?` flag. Sound while that flag meant 'the owner makes a coarse claim'; UNSOUND the moment a `:serialize` key honours declarations, because a per-slot substitution makes the KEY redact (the row stamp must report it) while saying nothing about the free cursor or a reply's `:value` / `:params`. The epoch suite caught it: a declaration-only owner's whole reply body tokenized and its undeclared siblings vanished — the exact over-redaction rf2-ko5lm's grain argument forbids. The coarse arm is now extracted as `coarse-key-projection` and read directly. Regression-tested.

BUILD POSTURE: DEV-ONLY, stated plainly rather than implied always-on. Both callers sit behind `interop/debug-enabled?` (the epoch tool-pair's trace bus — `emit!` AND `emit-error!` are both gated) or bundle isolation (the tooling sibling). The always-on `:rf.observe/*` axis carries no resource scoped key.

MUTATION PROOF meets the bead's standard: src reverted to origin/main, test unchanged — 756 tests / 6930 assertions in BOTH runs, 14 failures vs 0. The `:341` failure prints the whole defect in one line (wire {:account-id :rf/redacted, :page 3} vs trace {:account-id "acct-SECRET-4417", :page 3}), and the tool-egress failures at :415/:418 are tooling.cljc's two claims red against their own prose. Every two-sided control passed in BOTH runs.

title: Decide whether the docs/core/freehand sample gate extends past its own tree
description:
RULING NEEDED, filed rather than taken - the rf2-kem4o worker was told to report a scope extension, not decide it.

WHAT LANDED (PR #7085, rf2-kem4o). The docs/core/freehand sample gate no longer accepts a roster owner that merely RESOLVES: samples_coverage_jvm_test.clj now reads each fixture namespace's source, pairs every top-level definition with the names it mentions, seeds the relation with the deftest forms, and requires each owner to land in the closure. Turning it on flagged 39 rows across six fixture namespaces, every one of which is now rendered or run. It also caught a live defect nobody had found: composition.md block 13 called `field` with :on-input where the declaration 22 lines above reads :on-change, so (conj on-change ::v/value) folded nil into a seq and a pasted example raised :rf.error/view-bad-event at render.

THE EXTENSION QUESTION. That roster covers docs/core/freehand/** and nothing else. Documented examples elsewhere - docs/api/**, docs/core/**, docs/story/**, migration/** - are covered by the call-position discipline in doc_api_check / doc_guide_check, which asks "does this name still exist as a public surface?" and never "does this example run?". Two of the five known instances of the defect class lived outside the freehand guide:

  - docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md's reg-error-projector example returned 2 of the 4 LOCKED public-error keys, so a reader who pasted it got their projector silently discarded (fixed in PR #6966); and
  - a reg-route example that throws at registry.cljc:455.

So the mechanism is proven and the scope is the open question: extend this roster to a second tree, or accept that outside docs/core/freehand an example is proof-read rather than executed. Extending is not free - the freehand roster works because a chapter fixture namespace exists per page and the samples are transcribed onto the real classpath. A second tree needs the same fixture spine before a roster row can point at anything.

NOT a request to build a second gate. That was already ruled out, and correctly: fixing this gate's holes is what made it BE the gate a parallel one would have had to become.

THE HONEST LIMIT, which any scoping decision must carry forward: this class of gate catches a fixture nobody exercises. It does NOT catch forms.md's instance, where a rendered example subscribes to the wrong thing. That is a correctness judgement about a running example and no mechanical gate finds it.
notes:
VERDICT (rf2-h5fkc): NO. The docs/core/freehand sample roster does not extend past its own tree. Evidence and cost below; recorded here and in the PR body.

THE COST OF EXTENDING, measured with the gate's own block splitter over tracked files:

                                 pages  blocks  hard-unexecutable
  docs/core/freehand (today)        21     137     28  (20%)   <- calibration: roster truth is 23 rows (17%)
  docs/api                          21      94     15  (16%)
  docs/core (minus freehand)        36     337     85  (25%)
  docs/story                        16      53     17  (32%)
  migration                          7     125     58  (46%)
  EXTENSION TOTAL                   80     609    175  (29%)

609 blocks is 4.4x the corpus the roster carries today, and each needs a row pinning a digest of its exact text. "hard-unexecutable" counts only the blocks that cannot be transcribed at all (a non-clojure fence, an elision marker, a bare `ns` form); on freehand that proxy reads 28 where the roster's own reason column says 23, so it OVER-reads by ~20% on a tree written to be fixture-able and UNDER-reads everywhere else, because it cannot see the `;; =>` illustrative fragment that has no surrounding code for a fixture to host. 175 is a floor, not an estimate.

FIXTURE SPINE. The roster works because a chapter fixture namespace exists per page group and the samples are transcribed onto the real classpath: 7 namespaces, 2,604 lines, for 137 blocks — 19 lines of fixture per block. At that ratio the ~434 executable blocks outside freehand need roughly 8,200 new lines across ~27 namespaces, on pages that were NOT written with a fixture beside them. The freehand corpus was.

THE DECISIVE NUMBER — YIELD. The bead names one known outsider: a `reg-route` example whose `:path` sits in the metadata map, so `registry.cljc` throws `:rf.error/route-bad-metadata` and the route never registers. A reader-based scan of every fenced clojure block in the repo finds EIGHTEEN instances of that defect (filed as rf2-txe8o with the full inventory). Exactly ONE of them lies inside the proposed extension scope (docs/core/how-to/keep-secrets-out-of-traces.md). The other seventeen are in spec/** (7, four of them in spec/012-Routing.md including the canonical :rf.route/not-found registration) and docs/EP/** (10) — trees nobody proposed rostering. So the extension buys 1/18 of the very defect class it is proposed to catch, for 609 rows and ~8,200 fixture lines.

THE SECOND COST, which the digest pin makes structural. Editing any fenced block in docs/core/freehand today reds this suite, because the row pins the block's exact text — every guide edit is a two-file change. Extending puts 80 more pages behind one roster def in one file: every doc edit anywhere becomes a two-file change, and they all serialise on the same file. That is a merge bottleneck across the whole documentation corpus, and this repo has spent beads removing exactly that shape.

ON THE OPT-IN MARKER, established rather than assumed. The bead's hypothesis — a marker on blocks that CLAIM to be runnable, not a sweep — is right OUTSIDE freehand and wrong INSIDE it, and the boundary is not a matter of taste:

  - Sweep-by-default is correct where a fixture spine exists and every block is a claim. It buys the three properties the gate's docstring names: adding a sample reds, editing a sample reds, deleting a fixture reds. Inside freehand all three hold and the 23 reason-rows (17%) are a tolerable tax.
  - Outside, most blocks are prose. A sweep needs >=175 rows whose only content is "this one does not run", which is the "excuse column" the gate's own `unexecutable-reasons` docstring says the closed set exists to prevent — and the closed set of seven reasons does not stretch to what those trees actually contain (docs/api alone is dominated by `;; =>` result illustrations and bare expression fragments). An opt-in marker removes the flake mode structurally instead of managing it: prose that never claimed to run cannot red the build.
  - The honest cost of opt-in: it gives up "adding a sample reds", which is one of the three properties. Outside freehand that property was never available anyway (there is no fixture for an unrostered block to point at), so nothing is lost that exists today.

So the two shapes are not competitors. They are correct in different regimes and the regime boundary is "does this tree have a fixture spine".

THE HONEST LIMIT, carried forward as the bead requires. No mechanical gate of this class catches forms.md's instance, where a RENDERED example subscribes to the wrong thing. The tightened rule proves a roster row's owner is a var some test exercises; an exercised fixture proves the spelling compiles and renders, never that the example teaches the right thing. That is a correctness judgement about a running example and it stays with human review, under either shape, in every tree.

FOLLOW-UP FILED: rf2-txe8o (the 18 reg-route instances, with the inventory and the spec/docs/EP disposition split). If a standing check for that class is ever wanted it belongs as a rule inside the EXISTING doc_api_check / doc_guide_check family, which already reads every doc tree and already asks call-position questions — not as a roster extension, and not as a second gate.
MAYOR ENDORSEMENT of a related judgement call (2026-07-26), recorded here because this bead owns the sample-gate reason set.

The PR #7096 worker added ONE member to the closed unexecutable-reasons set: :jvm-only-verb. Its justification, which I accept: the new v/check block needs a roster owner, but v/check is #?(:clj ...) and all seven fixture namespaces are cljs read with :features #{:cljs}, so NO fixture can reach it. Mislabelling it :prose-shape would have been exactly the excuse column the closed set exists to prevent.

I endorse it, on the ground that this is a STRUCTURAL unreachability, not an excuse: a cljs fixture cannot reach a JVM-only verb, and the set's stated rationale already covers the mirror case ('no JVM or node counterpart at all').

BUT NOTE THE STANDING TENSION, because the next such request should be harder to win: the closed set IS the mechanism that stops this gate degrading into an excuse column, and every added member widens the aperture. My earlier ruling on this bead declined to extend the gate PAST its own tree partly because seven reasons 'do not stretch to what those trees actually contain'. That reasoning cuts both ways — inside freehand a genuinely unreachable verb deserves an honest label, but each addition must name a structural impossibility, not an inconvenience. Additions should stay rare and each should be justified in the PR body.
close_reason:
MAYOR RULING: NO — the docs/core/freehand sample gate does NOT extend past its own tree. Closing on the analysis this bead itself produced.

THE ARITHMETIC SETTLES IT. Extending the gate would cost 609 fenced blocks across ~80 pages, and of the 18 known reg-route defects it would have caught exactly ONE. A gate that buys 1/18 at that price is not a gate, it is a tax.

THE WORKER'S OWN ANALYSIS REACHES THE SAME PLACE BY A BETTER ROUTE, and it is the reasoning worth keeping: outside freehand, most blocks are PROSE. A sweep would need >=175 rows whose only content is 'this one does not run' — which is precisely the 'excuse column' that the gate's own unexecutable-reasons docstring says the closed set of seven reasons exists to prevent. And that closed set does not stretch to what those trees actually contain: docs/api alone is dominated by ';; =>' result illustrations and bare expression fragments. So the extension does not merely cost a lot, it would corrupt the mechanism that makes the gate meaningful in the tree where it works.

THE REGIME BOUNDARY, which is the durable insight: the two shapes are not competitors. A roster gate is right where a tree HAS A FIXTURE SPINE; an opt-in marker is right where it does not. Outside freehand the 'adding a sample reds the build' property was never available anyway, because there is no fixture for an unrostered block to point at — so nothing that exists today is given up.

AND THE HONEST LIMIT, recorded so nobody re-derives it: no mechanical gate of this class catches forms.md's instance, where a RENDERED example subscribes to the wrong thing. A roster row proves its owner is a var some test exercises; an exercised fixture proves the spelling compiles and renders. Neither proves the example TEACHES the right thing. That is a correctness judgement about a running example and it stays with human review, in every tree, under either shape.

IF a standing check for the wrong-arity class is ever wanted, it belongs as a rule inside the EXISTING doc_api_check / doc_guide_check family — which already reads every doc tree and already asks call-position questions — not as a roster extension and not as a second gate. Follow-on rf2-txe8o closed; its wider class is rf2-rzuc7.

This applies the standing posture: pre-alpha, elegance and power, no gold-plating, and do not drown in minutiae.

title: Resource reads: projection-relative :sensitive has no read-continuation analogue — a read reply rides verbatim under {:sensitive [[path]]} without coarse :sensitive?

title: Interpreter headroom the lnecd bounded change did not capture: memo caches are persistent maps in atoms
description:
FOLLOW-UP from rf2-lnecd (PR #7032), which was capped at ONE bounded optimisation and took the one caller attribution named (memoising rules/caller-key-slot). This bead is the headroom that change deliberately did NOT capture, quantified in the report's 'Headroom the one change did NOT capture' section.

After the lnecd change, substrate is still 36.7% of the W1 interpreted mount in a production browser. Named remainders, from CDP caller attribution on the post-change profile:

1. THE MEMO CACHES THEMSELVES — 1.71%, the largest single remaining caller of cljs.core/array-index-of is re-frame.freehand.conversion/remembered. The caches are persistent Clojure maps held in atoms, so every HIT is a PersistentArrayMap linear scan plus a deref. A mutable js/Map on the CLJS side would remove most of it. NOTE: the cache lnecd added (rules/caller-key-slot-by-name) has the same shape and the same cost, so this applies to it too. The namespaces are .cljc and the JVM structural walk shares them, so a change here needs a reader-conditional or a shared abstraction — that is the actual work.

2. top-layer/present? via contains? — 0.42%, paid on every element.

3. react-style-name is STILL UNCACHED — it is the only one of conversion.cljc's four projections without a remembered cache, while the namespace's own §Remembered projections comment argues at length for the other three. lnecd memoised it speculatively FIRST, measured no effect (clojure.string/replace stayed at 5.89%), and REVERTED it, because self time had named the function but caller attribution named a different caller. Its real contribution is under 1%. Worth doing for consistency, not for speed.

Together these name 3-4 points of the remaining 36.7. The bulk is the walk itself — a props object per element, child classification, class composition, a persistent structure per node — and is not cacheable.

ESTIMATED CEILING: a determined campaign might take the interpreted arm from 2.75x the React floor to ~2.2-2.4x on the large-template witness. It would NOT close the gap to compiled (1.13x), because on that witness the remaining gap is substantially ViewCell elision rather than interpretation — see the W2 (3.35x, elidable) versus W2r (1.22x, not elidable) contrast in the report.

Method for anyone picking this up: the scaffolding is recoverable from git on branch worker/compiled-worth-it (deleted before the PR merged). Read the report's Method section first — wall clock on this box drifts 37% on an arm that cannot change, so everything must be normalised to an in-run no-substrate React floor.
notes:
QUALIFICATION from rf2-lnecd's elision ablation (PR #7112) — this bead's ESTIMATED CEILING paragraph cites the W2 (3.35x, elidable) versus W2r (1.22x, not elidable) contrast as showing 'the remaining gap is substantially ViewCell elision rather than interpretation'. Those two arms differed in three ways at once (300 vs 100 boundaries, a literal leaf vs one running (str (v/sub [:studio/tick])), and no floor arm on W2r), so the contrast was evidence CONSISTENT WITH elision, not a measurement of it.

The isolated ablation has now been run, on a base that INCLUDES this bead's own PR #7077. Same 300 boundaries both witnesses, same leaf, a floor arm each, and the compiled body object asserted identical? between the kept and elided arms:

  free-ik / free-ic  the ViewCell alone      1.712 [1.583-1.879] clock   6.256 retained heap
  free-i  / free-ik  interpretation alone    1.216 [1.092-1.425] clock   1.011 retained heap
  free-i  / free-ic  the two together        2.079 [1.896-2.419] clock   6.327 retained heap

The bead's directional conclusion SURVIVES and is now measured rather than inferred: elision is the dominant term, 73% of the log-effect on the clock and effectively 100% on retained heap, and interpreter tuning cannot reach it. What changes is the magnitude — the gap this bead was estimating against is 2.079x, not 3.35x, partly because the confounds are gone and partly because #7077 itself moved the interpreted arm.

TWO METHOD NOTES for anyone picking up the remaining headroom.

1. The ablation's WALL CLOCK shows a real 1.216 interpretation term (range excludes 1.0) that the RETAINED-HEAP instrument does not see at all (1.011). The likely explanation is that the interpreted walk's cost here is largely TRANSIENT garbage — which retention cannot see and which is exactly the class of cost this bead's remaining items (the walk itself: a props object per element, child classification, class composition, a persistent structure per node) would attack. That makes it a HYPOTHESIS about where the remaining headroom lives, untested, and the natural first question for any further work here.

2. DO NOT reuse the recovered scaffolding's --alloc mode. Its documented premise ('allocation is a counter, not an occupancy sample: a collection inside the window cannot make it smaller') is FALSE: V8's sampling heap profiler drops the samples of collected objects, so the same 80,000 objects report 4.77 MB when a global holds them and 0.00 MB when nothing does. Pointed at a mount/unmount loop it reports the residue of a discarded page. Any browser heap reading needs a positive control of known size, in situ, in the same window.

title: Grow the 009 ratchet by a Tags-column keys-set diff (NOT a trace-op arm) — ruled after rf2-wsopx
description:
MAYOR RULING: YES, and only the Tags arm (2026-07-26). The rf2-wsopx worker recommended this and asked rather than filing it, per its brief. I am adopting its reasoning as filed.

WHY THIS IS WORTH BUILDING AT ALL: the 009 ratchet pins the Channel column and the error/warning emit sites — not trace ops and NOT the Tags column. That blind spot is why spec/009 never received the EP-0037 planner rows: :rf.route/prefetched appeared ZERO times in the catalogue while shipping, and :rf.error/resource-route-plan Tags column omitted both :plan-cause and :contributor while its narrative still taught partial planning against the ratified atomicity rule. A gate whose coverage never reaches the column where drift accumulates will keep reporting green over it.

THE RULED SHAPE — Tags-column keys-set diff, and nothing else: Spec-Schemas.md ALREADY defines one *Tags schema per catalogue row, and both files are ALREADY parsed by existing gates. So the arm is a keys-set comparison between the schema and the row, which the worker describes as "a parser away". It would have caught the Tags omission directly.

WHY NOT THE TRACE-OP ARM, which is the tempting other half: there is no per-op schema roster to diff against, so the only available check is "is every emitted op documented somewhere in 2500 lines of prose?" — a scan with a bad false-positive rate. That is the expensive half for the weaker signal, and this repo has already learned that a census whose pattern cannot distinguish a correction from a defect will fight every fix. Declined.

CONSTRAINTS: extend the EXISTING gate, do not add a new script. No new vocabulary. If the keys-set diff turns out to need a second source of truth to be meaningful, STOP and report — a gate needing a hand-maintained roster is the drift generator this repo keeps removing (see the derived evidence-producer roster that ended its class after going stale twice by hand-copying).

NON-VACUITY IS MANDATORY: prove the arm reds against the PRE-rf2-wsopx catalogue state, where :plan-cause and :contributor were genuinely missing from the row. An arm that cannot red on the defect that motivated it has not been tested — and this repo has shipped exactly that mistake before, where an audit method could not have caught its own motivating instance.
notes:
BASELINE MATERIALLY IMPROVED BY rf2-dxuzp (2026-07-26) — read this before building the arm.

I ruled that this arm ships with the 23 currently-redding rows as a SHRINK-ONLY BASELINE. The dxuzp adjudication has since changed what that baseline consists of, in the arm favour:

Spec-Schemas carries a :tags schema ONLY FOR TRACE-EMITTING CATEGORIES. Thrown rows and always-on record rows therefore FALL OUT OF THE PAIRING BY CONSTRUCTION — they have no :tags map at all (error/thrown-ex-info builds a FLAT map, and spec/009 section The thrown-error shape already declares :recovery among four REQUIRED slots on it). So the arm never had to reason about them.

CONSEQUENCE: the shrink-only baseline is roughly 20 rows of HONEST DEBT rather than 130 of noise. The worker words. That makes the ledger small enough to be drained rather than tolerated, and it means a row entering the baseline is a real signal instead of a category error.

ALSO STILL TRUE AND STILL OWED — the arm has a known defect I recorded earlier: its pairing keys off the NAME HALF of the operation keyword, so :rf.http/stale-suppressed and :rf.route.nav-token/stale-suppressed collide and derive to the same schema name. Key the pairing off the WHOLE :operation. One line in the arm, not a corpus edit.
Audit of merged PR #7207: the PR explicitly confirms that the newly always-on `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` row is NOT protected by the Tags-column keys-set diff. The operation-derived name is `SchemaValidationFailureTags`, while Spec-Schemas publishes `SchemaValidationTags`, so invariant 6 never pairs or diffs them. The existing paired-count floor only catches loss of a previously counted pair; it cannot catch a row that was unpaired from the start. This is now a structural-only production egress record, making silent Tags drift material rather than theoretical.

Bounded acceptance: restore an explicit, stable pairing for this row—via a compatible canonical alias/mapping or a safe schema rename after checking consumers—without weakening the general operation-derived rule. Raise the exact paired-count floor in the same change, assert the live row is among the pairs, and mutation-prove that removing/adding a boundary-record key on either the catalogue or schema side reds the keys-set diff. Preserve the existing loss/rename floor tests and do not invent a second catalogue parser.
close_reason: PR #7385 merged: SchemaValidationFailureTags now pairs the live row, paired floor 94, with catalogue- and schema-side mutation proof.

title: RULING NEEDED: EP-0037's Tooling projection has no conformance row -- was the R2 plan-graph projection descoped or dropped?
description:
Found by EP-0037 review gate 2 (rf2-kqxe6.15, completeness). This is a RULING REQUEST, not an implementation bead. Per the gate brief: where a reviewer cannot tell whether something was descoped by decision or simply dropped, the ambiguity is itself the finding.

THE STRUCTURAL FACT. EP-0037 devotes a whole section (§Tooling and observability) to the plan projection -- nine bullets of what "Xray/trace projection shows" -- plus a staging clause:

  "This projection graduates with the planner. R0 exposes only the source, resolved target,
   cause, branch, and behavior-preserving leaf plan needed to prove the shared spine.
   R2 adds occurrence/dependency groups, contributor dedupe advisories, the grouped order,
   and the identity diff. R6 proves the integrated view."

But the EP's own §Conformance obligations rows 1-10 contain NO tooling/projection row. R6's per-row verdict table is therefore rows 1-10 and nothing else, so the R2 staging clause was never in an executable-proof matrix and nobody ever checked it. Compounding: rf2-kqxe6.6 is the only R2 bead in the epic and its title/description were overwritten by its audit follow-through (see the sibling bead filed by this gate), so the R2 tooling clause had no bead carrying it either.

WHAT ACTUALLY SHIPPED, checked against the tree. Mostly there:
  - source address and cause -- :rf.route/planned carries :cause; the source address is deliberately NOT carried, RULED on rf2-kqxe6.3 with rationale and both rejected alternatives recorded in spec/012 §Resolved target. CLEAN.
  - resolved target + parent-to-leaf branch -- :route-id, :branch, redacted :url, :param-keys/:query-keys. CLEAN.
  - blocking/readiness state -- :blocking (vec). CLEAN.
  - resource owners and activation/prefetch causes -- ensure :cause [:route-prefetch <id>]. CLEAN.
  - leave block / entry denial / planning failure -- :rf.route/navigation-blocked, :rf.route/entry-denied, :plan-error. CLEAN.
  - contributor dedupe advisories -- :redundant-children names ancestor + child + scoped-key. CLEAN (pinned by spec/conformance/fixtures/ep-0037-r2-identity-dedupe.edn).

NOT SHIPPED, and no ruling found:
  - "old/new kept/added/removed IDENTITIES" -- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc:1082-1092 projects :ensured / :kept / :removed as COUNTS; :identities is the whole next set. The diff IS derivable by diffing consecutive route-plan traces, and the fixtures pin the counts (ep-0037-r2-partial-activation.edn asserts :ensured 1 :kept 1 :removed 1) -- so this may well be the right shape. But the EP says identities.
  - "each route's contributed resource requirements" -- the contributor->requirement mapping is not projected; only :branch (route ids) plus :identities.
  - "local :after edges and plan order" -- plan order rides :identities order; :after edges are not projected at all.
  - "occurrence/dependency groups" (the R2 clause) -- not projected.

Also: tools/xray was touched exactly ONCE in the whole programme (5482fa18a3, R1, removing the retired on-match error display). tools/xray/spec/024-Resources-Panel.md:458 lists :rf.resource/route-plan as one lifecycle row with no tag detail, and there is no routing-plan panel.

WHY THIS IS PLAUSIBLY CORRECT AS SHIPPED, i.e. why I am asking rather than filing work. The same EP section fences hard: "No slice is permission to build a second Xray graph or a general-purpose public plan debugger", and the §Deliberate non-goals list rejects "a public general-purpose route-plan executor". The occurrence graph and identity collapse are explicitly called "internal planning mechanics" that do "not introduce a public graph API, a public graph value, or a new router abstraction" (EP:505-507). Under the pre-alpha posture -- trust the programmer, minimal ergonomic API, reject machinery for no consumer -- "ratified as a superset, shipped as the useful subset" is a defensible and probably correct outcome. Projecting :after edges and occurrence groups on every navigation trace, for no named consumer, is exactly the over-engineering triage rejects.

THE ASK, one of three:
  (A) RULE IT DESCOPED. Record that the shipped projection (counts + next identity set + redundant-child advisory) is the ratified subset, and that :after edges, occurrence/dependency groups, and per-contributor requirement mapping are deliberately not projected because the internal mechanics are not a public graph. Then this closes with the ruling as its artefact and a one-line erratum in the EP (see the errata bead filed by this gate).
  (B) RULE THE IDENTITY DIFF IN, only. The narrowest useful upgrade: carry :added / :removed as identity VECTORS beside the existing counts, so a reader of one trace can see WHICH identity moved without diffing two traces. One cond-> in route.cljc:1084, two fixture updates. Leave :after edges and occurrence groups out.
  (C) RULE THE WHOLE BULLET LIST IN. I do not recommend this -- it is the second-graph the EP forbids.

WHATEVER THE RULING: EP-0037's conformance matrix should not gain an eleventh row retroactively. If a future EP graduates a plan projection, that EP owns its own conformance row. Record the disposition here so gate 2's successor does not re-derive it.
notes:
OPERATOR-OWNED DECISION BEAD (Mike, 2026-07-26): one of six to be taken one at a time — rf2-ayq3v, rf2-9sluz, rf2-mhrwq, rf2-o0agl, rf2-4l67v, rf2-2ii52. Do NOT dispatch; do NOT re-surface as a ready-queue candidate.
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-27, dossier review): Option (B) — the identity diff is ruled IN, in the operationally-named form; every other unshipped item in EP-0037 §Tooling is DESCOPED by decision. Recorded from the dossier ai/decisions/rf2-9sluz.ep0037-tooling-projection.md (primary recommendation (B) + the appended Codex second opinion, which this ruling adopts in its corrected form; dossier deleted after recording per protocol — this note is the surviving artefact).

DECISION. The existing activation :rf.resource/route-plan trace row gains the exact identity partition beside the existing counts: :ensured-identities (requirements actually taking the ensure path), :kept-identities (requirements genuinely adopted without a fetch), :removed-identities (prior-plan identities absent from the next plan). Counts stay as the compact headline. :identities is corrected to carry the planner's grouped plan order (today it is (vec next-ids) from a SET — route.cljc:1060/:1110 — so the current vector does not in fact carry the order the EP names). Nothing else from the Tooling bullet list ships: no route-plan panel, no public plan value, no second graph, no new conformance row.

REASONING. (A) — descope everything — was defensible on the EP's own fences and pure no-gold-plating. But the descope pinches a real debugging workflow at exactly one spot: "which identity moved on this navigation?" today requires diffing two consecutive route-plan traces. Ruling it in costs ~one cond-> at the existing emit site, has an immediate consumer with zero new UI (Xray's Trace panel expands the raw trace event through the EDN inspector), and off-box safety already closes by shape, not tag-name roster (re-frame.resources.trace-egress/project-unknown-slot-value applies the owner's egress policy to scoped keys inside any collection — proven by existing epoch tests for the route-plan :blocking/:identities vectors). That is the "excellent tools" half of the posture: not machinery, legibility of the existing trace. (C) — the whole bullet list — is the second Xray graph the EP itself forbids; rejected by the bead author, the dossier, and this ruling. History note: this was compression, not silent dropping — commit 4bdeff9dac explicitly landed the "plan-diff trace" describing the counts as satisfying the EP's kept/added/removed-identity requirement; the gap is that identities were compressed into counts.

NAMING (load-bearing, from the Codex opinion, verified against the tree): since the retained-entry liveness repair (commit e95f46e6b6), a retained-but-unusable prior identity takes the ordinary ensure path (route.cljc:1044-1075) — so a vector named :added would disagree with the :ensured count. The operational names (:ensured-identities/:kept-identities/:removed-identities) tell the truth about what the runtime did.

DESCOPE ENUMERATION — each unshipped §Tooling item, with its deliberate disposition, so gate 2's successor never re-derives this:
1. Identity diff as identities — IN (this ruling). Ships per the brief on rf2-dlkou.
2. Per-contributor requirement mapping — DESCOPED, deliberate. Xray already derives the static route/resource graph from route registrations (declared requirements incl. local :after data); planning failures carry contributor/cycle evidence; the successful dedupe case carries :redundant-children (ancestor + child + scoped-key, pinned by ep-0037-r2-identity-dedupe.edn). Re-projecting the mapping on every navigation would duplicate those authorities for no named consumer.
3. Local :after edges and "plan order" as a projected structure — DESCOPED, deliberate. The edges are internal planning mechanics (EP:505-507; Spec 016) introducing no public graph API; plan ORDER rides the corrected :identities vector, which is all a trace reader needs.
4. Occurrence/dependency groups (the R2 staging clause's groups) — DESCOPED, deliberate. Explicitly internal; projecting them on every navigation trace is the second-graph the EP forbids, would enlarge a privacy-sensitive trace, and has no consumer.
5. Route-plan panel / general-purpose plan debugger / public plan value — DESCOPED, deliberate (the EP's own §Deliberate non-goals). A dedicated Xray plan view waits for a concrete workflow the raw trace + existing static route/resource graph cannot serve, under a future EP that owns its own conformance row.

BOUNDARY CONDITION (ruled): EP-0037's conformance matrix does NOT gain an eleventh row retroactively. Conformance for this correction is the enriched shape pinned in the existing R2 partial-activation fixture plus the shape-driven egress test. If a future EP graduates a plan projection, THAT EP owns its own conformance row.

IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF — carried in full on rf2-dlkou (filed by this ruling, discovered-from this bead). Summary: route.cljc trace/emit! at ~:1102-1112 — cond-> the three identity vectors beside the counts (:ensured-identities via (remove adopted? ordered), :kept-identities via (filter adopted? ordered), :removed-identities via (filterv (complement next-ids) prev-identities) for deterministic prior-plan order); emit :identities as (mapv :scoped-key ordered) instead of (vec next-ids) (verify ordered is post-dedupe); do NOT touch the return map's :identities set (commit-navigation consumes it). Fixtures: extend spec/conformance/fixtures/ep-0037-r2-partial-activation.edn (which today asserts :ensured 1 :kept 1 :removed 1) to pin the vectors + ordered :identities, and extend the shape-driven egress test (implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_resource_trace_test.clj). EP erratum: one line in docs/EP/EP-0037-route-planning-and-activation-ownership.md §Tooling staging clause recording this disposition — the gate-filed errata sibling bead named in the dossier does not exist in the tracker (open+closed searched 2026-07-27), so rf2-dlkou carries the erratum.

DISPOSITION: this bead CLOSES with the ruling as its artefact; the implementation splits to rf2-dlkou (ordinary dispatchable bead, NOT operator-owned — the decision hold applied to the ruling, which is now made).
close_reason: RULED (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-27): Option (B) — identity diff IN as the operationally-named partition (:ensured-identities/:kept-identities/:removed-identities beside counts, :identities corrected to plan order); all other §Tooling items DESCOPED by decision (full enumeration + boundary condition in notes). No eleventh conformance row. Implementation split to rf2-dlkou; this bead's artefact is the ruling.

title: day8/re-frame2 has no performance regression gate (every bench in the repo covers an UNPUBLISHED artefact)
notes:
MAYOR RULING: DEFER, on a MEASURED ground rather than a preference (2026-07-26). Do not dispatch.

THE REASON IS THE NOISE FLOOR, and it was measured today by the compiled-tier report (rf2-lnecd, docs/design/freehand/studio/compiled-tier-browser-worth-it.md): THE NO-SUBSTRATE FLOOR ARM DRIFTED 37% ACROSS ROUNDS — larger than most of the effects being measured — which is why every claim in that report is stated as a RATIO TO THE IN-RUN FLOOR rather than an absolute. On the same box, the same primitive measured 10.4ns and 21.7ns across two JVMs.

A REGRESSION GATE ON A SUBSTRATE WITH A 37% FLOOR DRIFT IS A FLAKE GENERATOR. It would red on noise, and this repo has a standing rule that A FAILING TEST ON A TOUCHED SURFACE IS NEVER A FLAKE — which is exactly the rule that makes a false red expensive to dismiss. We already have one such gate (rf2-yumaq: G-8 dying because its baseline was TOO FAST) and fixing it took a worker. Adding a second, broader one before the measurement is stable would manufacture that cost at scale.

A PREMISE CORRECTION THE BEAD INHERITS FROM ME: its notes classify the Freehand benches as covering an artefact that is "NOT published". Freehand is PRE-PUBLICATION and expected to ship — docs/release-process.md forecloses only day8/re-frame2-ui, and implementation/freehand/deps.edn:29 says staying out of the lockstep inventory "leaves the release train untouched until Freehand actually ships". I propagated that error into six briefs today. So the gap this bead describes is narrower than stated: the benches cover artefacts that are not published YET, not artefacts that never will be.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS DISPATCHABLE, in order: (1) a stable measurement method — the report shows allocation via getThreadAllocatedBytes gave min = p50 = max in nearly every arm, so an ALLOCATION gate is buildable where a wall-clock gate is not; (2) a named regression the gate would have caught, because a perf gate with no historical catch is an assertion that the future will resemble a past nobody measured; (3) the alpha tag, after which "published artefact" stops being a moving target.

NOT A REJECTION. The operator has ruled that performance matters — the compiler is KEPT for performance-critical applications not yet seen. A gate is the right long-term instrument; it is the wrong instrument today because it cannot yet distinguish signal from a 37% floor.

title: Retrospective facade-export classification sweep (re-frame.core, Story, Xray) for external-alpha prep
description:
The RETROSPECTIVE half of the facade-export classification audit has no bead. Surfaced 2026-07-25 while processing the rf2-fby7o api-freeze dossier; bd list across every status returned no owner for it.

## What it is

spec/Conventions.md:1198 defines the audit in two halves.

The FORWARD half is already running: every new facade export classifies and justifies itself at diff time (tier, owner, status, justification), which is why the Freehand rows in spec/api-manifest.edn all carry their four fields. That half needs nothing.

The RETROSPECTIVE half is unowned. Conventions calls it "the full retrospective sweep of every existing non-front-porch export - and the manifest table it produces" and says it "stays deferred to API-freeze / external-alpha prep".

## Scope

A repo-wide sweep of every non-front-porch export on re-frame.core, re-frame.story and day8.re-frame2-xray.core - the grandfathered exceptions Conventions explicitly records - deciding keep / rename / move / internal-public for each, and producing the manifest table.

NOT a Freehand audit. Freehand's 38 members are already classified at diff time; six are :facade? true (mount, unmount!, hydrate-root, ->react, active-connections, command-log) and every one is a CLJS-only verb re-exported from the namespace that owns it, which is exactly the deliberate single-import re-export the Conventions ruling sanctions.

## Deadline

Conventions sets it itself: before re-frame2's first meaningful external alpha/beta release - explicitly NOT "before v1". The reasoning is that the moment real users copy examples, a namespace move becomes a breaking change.

## Relationship to rf2-fby7o

DECOUPLED. rf2-fby7o's release condition names this audit as half of its api-freeze gate. Two independent analyses concluded that coupling is a drafting accident rather than intent: gating a Freehand guide on a re-frame.core sweep that Conventions itself schedules for external-alpha prep does not make the guide more correct. See rf2-fby7o notes (2026-07-25 dossier fold) for the full reasoning. Mike rules on whether the coupling is struck.

## Acceptance

1. Every non-front-porch export on re-frame.core, re-frame.story and day8.re-frame2-xray.core carries a keep / rename / move / internal-public disposition.
2. The manifest table Conventions describes exists.
3. Anything ruled rename or move is either executed or has a bead.
notes:
DEFERRED 2026-07-25 (mayor), with an explicit release condition so it stops being re-triaged every dispatch tick.

WHY NOT NOW: the bead's own charter defers it. spec/Conventions.md:1198 says the retrospective half 'stays deferred to API-freeze / external-alpha prep', and the FORWARD half is already running (every new facade export classifies itself at diff time, which is why the Freehand rows in spec/api-manifest.edn carry all four fields). So nothing is rotting while this waits.

THE DECISIVE REASON: it is a repo-wide sweep of every non-front-porch export on re-frame.core, re-frame.story and day8.re-frame2-xray.core, producing a manifest table. The alpha is gated on rf2-vxgfnd.99 (EPIC S7 — Helix-removal wave + alpha tag), which by its own title REMOVES a substrate and will move exactly the surface this sweep would classify. Running the sweep before S7 means classifying exports that S7 then deletes or renames, and redoing the table afterwards. Sequencing it after S7 costs nothing and saves the whole second pass.

RELEASE CONDITION — reopen when EITHER holds:
  1. rf2-vxgfnd.99 (S7 + alpha tag) closes, or
  2. Mike calls api-freeze / external-alpha prep explicitly.

Not a rejection: the work is real and Conventions mandates it. This is a sequencing decision only.

title: hic-056 — [DORMANT] The bounded Node/React SSR service
description:
# hic-056 — [DORMANT] The bounded Node/React SSR service

**Phase**: 5 tail · **Wave**: — (activates on a named caller; blocks nothing) · **Est.**: L · **Depends**: hic-046 + a named caller
**Surface**: SSR service package (new)

## Goal
Productize the proven Node spike into a bounded, fail-closed service — only when a real caller exists. The core per-surface hydration contract (hic-046) is already mandatory and does not wait for this.

## Deliverables (on activation)
Per-request frame/state isolation (immutable snapshots); allowlisted payload; one in-flight render per isolate until proven otherwise; timeout + hard termination; caller latency envelope pre-registered; hydration-byte tests against the client; JVM↔Node protocol kept separable (no "one complete string" baked into every layer, so a streaming caller later doesn't need a second semantics).

## Acceptance (on activation)
The five gates above witnessed; deployment documented; client v0 provably unaffected when the service is absent.

## Worker notes
Read synth-codex §7 SSR row; `codex/react-compatibility-notes.md` server section; the .88 close record via the governance beads. **Do not start without the named caller — record the caller in this file when known.**

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).

title: scripts/test-fast-pr.sh --help: backticks in the unquoted heredoc run as command substitution
description:
PRE-EXISTING on origin/main, found while working rf2-ketqy (PR #7642) and deliberately left alone as out of that bead's scope.

`scripts/test-fast-pr.sh --help` prints, before the usage text:

  scripts/test-fast-pr.sh: line 164: --plan: command not found

The usage block is a `cat <<EOF` heredoc with an UNQUOTED delimiter, so parameter AND command substitution both run inside it. The body carries markdown-style backticks around flag names, and the shell evaluates the backticked text as a command. The exit code is still 0 and the usage text still prints, so this is cosmetic noise rather than a broken flag — which is presumably why it has survived.

FIX, and keep it small: the heredoc genuinely wants $(basename "$0") expanded, so quoting the delimiter (<<'EOF') is the WRONG fix — it would stop that expanding too. Escape the backticks instead, or drop them for plain quotes.

Verified pre-existing rather than introduced: `git show origin/main:scripts/test-fast-pr.sh > /tmp/x.sh && sh /tmp/x.sh --help` reproduces it with no local changes in play.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7659. Backticks dropped (not delimiter quoted — line 168 needs $(basename "$0")), matching the block's bare-flag house style. --help/-h/--plan exit 0, unknown flag exits 2, 'gate root:' still first line. PR #7642's gate-reaper untouched.

title: Spec-Schemas: six *Tags schemas still declare :recovery, now that no 009 :tags cell rosters it
description:
FOUND by rf2-mb8yp (the corpus-wide :recovery strike). After that sweep NO catalogue row's sixth-column `:tags` cell lists `:recovery` — build-event strips the slot and hoists it to the envelope top level on every branch, so no consumer reads it there.

Six per-category schemas in spec/Spec-Schemas.md still DECLARE it as a map entry: MalformedSchemaTags, NoFrameContextTags, BadFrameProviderArgTags, EffectHandlerBadReturnTags, PrefetchBadAddressTags, NoAdapterSpecifiedTags.

This is currently HARMLESS and deliberately so: error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test's `envelope-only-tag-keys` (#{:recovery :category}) subtracts the slot from the SCHEMA side of the keys diff, whose docstring says 'a schema declaring them is not evidence of a row defect'. That exemption is why the strike could not red the tags-column arm, and why it is provably neutral there.

THE QUESTION, not an assertion of defect: with the cell side now uniform, the schema side is the last place `:recovery` appears as a `:tags` key. 009's own authoring rule (§'The `:tags` column is pinned, not documentary') says a schema declaring a key the category never actually carries is the defect and the fix belongs in Spec-Schemas. By that rule these six over-declare. Options: (a) leave it — the exemption documents the tolerance and costs nothing; (b) strike `:recovery` from the six schemas, after which the `:recovery` half of envelope-only-tag-keys is dead and could be narrowed to #{:category}.

NOT actioned under rf2-mb8yp: the ruling scoped that PR to the cells, the preamble clause and the gate, and explicitly barred surface-roster / authoring-map redefinition. Spec-Schemas.md is hot-zone; sequence it.
notes:
MAYOR RULING (2026-08-06): take option (b) — STRIKE :recovery from the six *Tags schemas, then narrow envelope-only-tag-keys from #{:recovery :category} to #{:category}. Strike FIRST, narrow SECOND, same PR: striking leaves the exemption dead-but-harmless, whereas narrowing before striking would red the gate.

THE ARTEFACT'S OWN RULE DECIDES THIS, not my preference. Spec 009 section 'The :tags column is pinned, not documentary' states that a schema declaring a key the category never actually carries IS the defect and the fix belongs in Spec-Schemas. The cell side is now uniform after rf2-mb8yp, so these six schemas are the last place :recovery appears as a :tags key. Option (a) would leave the artefact knowingly in breach of a rule it states about itself.

WHY THIS IS NOT GOLD-PLATING, since the bead is honest that the current state is harmless: the change is a NET DELETION that makes the gate STRICTLY STRONGER. The exemption exists to subtract :recovery from the schema side of the keys diff, and its own docstring says 'a schema declaring them is not evidence of a row defect' — that tolerance is precisely what makes the schema side unable to red. Removing the need for the tolerance removes a blind spot rather than adding machinery. Fewer lines, one less exemption, and a gate that can now see a class it could not.

SEQUENCED WITH rf2-j4bg3 in one worker and one PR: j4bg3 tightens NoFrameContextTags's :where slot, and NoFrameContextTags is one of the six. Splitting them puts two workers on spec/Spec-Schemas.md, which is hot-zone.

Reproduce this ruling and its reasoning in the merging PR body — a link into the tracker is not a durable record, and the git history is what a future reader will have.
close_reason: Implemented by merged PR #7603: all six dead :recovery declarations were removed and the conformance exemption narrowed to #{:category}, closing the schema-side blind spot.

title: check_ambient_durable_reads: four call spellings still one nesting level out of roster reach
description:
MEASURED while implementing the rf2-vcjpx roster widening (2026-08-06 13:16
AUSEST). NOT actioned there: rf2-vcjpx's ruling enumerated exactly which call
spellings to add and REJECTED free-form value matching, so extending the list
further is a second scope question, not a worker's call.

WHAT vcjpx FIXED. Seven entries, each anchored at value-form start, so these
now fire:

  :restored-at (.getItem js/localStorage "k")
  :restored-at (.getItem js/sessionStorage "k")
  :restored-at (.-href js/location)
  :restored-at (.-language js/navigator)
  :restored-at (js/matchMedia "(min-width: 40em)")
  :restored-at (some-> (.-localStorage js/globalThis) (.getItem "k"))
  :restored-at (some-> (.-sessionStorage js/globalThis) (.getItem "k"))

WHAT STILL MISSES (measured, each yields ZERO findings today):

  1. :restored-at (.query js/navigator.permissions opts)
     The Permissions API idiom. Also the reason the `navigator.` roster entry
     is the ONE host fact vcjpx did not make call-reachable: its bare spelling
     `navigator.language` fires, and `(.-language js/navigator)` attributes
     `js/navigator` rather than `navigator.`, so no call form reaches it.
  2. :restored-at (.getItem (.-localStorage js/globalThis) "k")
     The repo's storage idiom WITHOUT the `some->` head. vcjpx anchored from
     `(some->` because that is how cofx.cljc and todomvc/db.cljs spell it; the
     bare-nesting variant is one paren different.
  3. :restored-at (some-> js/localStorage (.getItem "k"))
     `some->` threading the global directly instead of `(.-localStorage
     js/globalThis)`.
  4. :restored-at (.-matches (js/matchMedia "(min-width: 40em)"))
     The media query actually READ — `(js/matchMedia …)` returns the list, and
     `.-matches` is the boolean anyone would store. One nesting level out.

NOT a miss, and deliberately: `(let [t js/localStorage] …)` is the documented
dataflow limit in the module docstring — the conformance replay fixtures are
the backstop there, not this gate.

THE SHAPE OF THE QUESTION. An enumerated roster costs one entry per nesting
level, and each of the four above is exactly one level off something the roster
already names. That is either (a) fine — the gate catches the spellings people
actually write and the residue is contrived; or (b) the same advertised-but-
hollow class vcjpx's own ruling cited (rr6do/bml5u), one layer up. Item 4 looks
most like a real authoring shape to me and item 1 second; items 2 and 3 are
near-duplicates of what now fires.

A THIRD OPTION worth ruling on rather than assuming away: rather than chasing
nesting levels one entry at a time, allow the ANCHORED entries to sit under one
level of wrapping — i.e. match a roster read at the head of the value form OR
as the sole argument of one enclosing call. That is narrower than the free-form
"ambient read anywhere in the value" vcjpx rejected (it cannot reach a threaded
value buried in a larger form) and would cover items 2 and 4 without new
entries. It would need its own false-positive measurement before anyone builds
it.

Gate is exit 0 on the tree either way — none of these idioms appears in any of
the 18 scanned files (verified 2026-08-06).
close_reason: RULED (a) — LEAVE THE ROSTER AS IT IS; rejected at triage under the pre-alpha no-gold-plating posture. The bead's own measurement settles it: NONE of the four residual spellings appears in any of the 18 scanned files (verified 2026-08-06), and the gate is exit 0 on the tree either way. The standing test for whether a guard is warranted is whether the failure is SILENT and HAS ALREADY HAPPENED. Here it has not happened even once, and the bead itself calls items 2 and 3 near-duplicates of what already fires. Chasing nesting levels one roster entry at a time is the minutiae this project rejects. The THIRD OPTION (let anchored entries sit under one level of wrapping) is the more elegant shape and is NOT rejected on its merits — it is rejected on cost: the bead states it needs its own false-positive measurement before anyone builds it, which is real work against zero current exposure. If a real authoring instance of item 4 or item 1 ever lands in the tree, that is a new bead with a live subject and the wrapping rule is the first thing to price. The advertised-but-hollow concern (rr6do/bml5u class) is acknowledged: the honest remedy there is to narrow what the checker CLAIMS, never to widen what it chases — if its own description overclaims, that is a one-line docs fix, not a roster expansion.

title: docs: report-errors-in-production still promises the frameless record a `:rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id` nothing sets
description:
RESIDUE from rf2-j4bg3 / rf2-f7j00, found by grepping the pattern rather than the file.

docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md, in the `:rf.error/no-frame-context` bullet of the error-catalogue list, reads: 'This record is itself frameless (`:frame nil`); in a *dev* build it also carries capture-site ancestry through the `:rf.trace/dispatch-id` / `:rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id` correlation keys'.

FALSE THE SAME WAY IT WAS IN spec/009, spec/Spec-Schemas, spec/002 (fixed by rf2-j4bg3) and docs/EP/EP-0002 (fixed by rf2-f7j00). `re-frame.frame/no-frame-context-payload` and `re-frame.frame/ambient-frame-refused-payload` each merge only `(when-let [did (some-> trace/*handler-scope* :dispatch-id)] {:rf.trace/dispatch-id did})`; `re-frame.trace/HandlerScope` is a five-slot record [trigger-handler call-site dispatch-id sensitive? no-emit?] with no parent slot; and spec/009 §Dispatch correlation scopes `:rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id` to `:rf.event/dispatched` only. The record carries the dispatch-id stamp; the parent link is WALKED from it through the correlation graph, never copied onto the payload.

FIX: drop `/ :rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id` from the sentence — the singular `:rf.trace/dispatch-id` correlation key. Everything else in the bullet (dev-minted, elided in production, the elision-list cross-ref) stands. Wording only, no payload key.

NOT DONE UNDER rf2-f7j00: that bead was fenced to docs/EP/**.

SWEEP EVIDENCE (2026-08-06, worktree at origin/main 7e7727b97f): `git grep -n -i 'parent.dispatch|capture-site ancestry'` over docs/ finds parent-dispatch-id in exactly five files. docs/EP/EP-0002 (fixed), this file (FALSE), and three that are CORRECT and must not be touched: docs/api/re-frame.core.md (the group-by-event projection record's `:parent-dispatch-id` slot), docs/core/observability.md x3 (the projection record + 'child run's opening :rf.event/dispatched carries :rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id' — the true, :rf.event/dispatched-scoped statement). No other EP carries the promise.
close_reason:
FIXED — PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7572 (branch worker/prodreport-e96mm, commit 2c84666ebf). Net line delta 0 (1 insertion / 1 deletion, one passage in docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md).

WAS (the :rf.error/no-frame-context bullet):
  "This record is itself frameless (:frame nil); in a *dev* build it also carries capture-site ancestry through the :rf.trace/dispatch-id / :rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id correlation keys, but those ids are dev-minted, so the production shipper this recipe wires receives the frameless record without ancestry (§5's elision list covers why)."

NOW:
  "This record is itself frameless (:frame nil); in a *dev* build it also carries the capture site's :rf.trace/dispatch-id — one correlation key, naming the run that captured the callback. There is no :rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id beside it: ancestry is never copied onto the record, it's WALKED from that id across the trace stream's :rf.event/dispatched events ([Observability](../observability.md#two-properties-that-shape-everything-downstream)). In production you get neither — the id is dev-minted, and the stream you'd walk it across is elided (§5's elision list covers why)."

Corrected in place rather than as a dated erratum: errata are the EP / design-record convention and this page carries none, so a how-to that is wrong simply becomes right.

RE-VERIFIED, not re-derived: re-frame.frame/no-frame-context-payload + ambient-frame-refused-payload each merge exactly {:rf.trace/dispatch-id did} off trace/*handler-scope*; re-frame.trace/HandlerScope is five slots with no parent; spec/009 §Dispatch correlation scopes the parent key to :rf.event/dispatched; re-frame.cascade-dispatch-id-test/parent-dispatch-id-only-on-event-dispatched asserts it. "Dev-minted" also checks out — re-frame.router mints the id under (when interop/debug-enabled? (next-dispatch-id)), so in a release build the key is simply absent.

WALKABILITY (the bead did not ask, the brief did): the walk IS genuinely available to a consumer in a DEV build — register-listener! :trace fans out corpus-wide ("receives *every* trace event"), so a consumer indexes the record's dispatch-id into the stream, finds that run's :rf.event/dispatched, and walks :rf.trace/parent-dispatch-id upward. re-frame.trace.tooling/trace-buffer offers the same lineage pre-grouped, but it is PER-FRAME and a frameless record does not name a frame, so the :trace listener is the path that actually works from this record. In production neither path exists: trace-buffer returns [] under goog.DEBUG=false and the record carries no id to index with. The new wording says exactly that and points at docs/core/observability.md rather than implying a workaround.

SWEEP: git grep -niE 'parent.dispatch|capture-site ancestry|correlation key' over docs/, widened with a grep for 'rf.trace/dispatch-id' outside docs/EP/. ONE false site — the one this bead named. No additional sites. The three CORRECT sibling hits are untouched and were each read first: docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1053 (group-by-event projection record slot), docs/core/observability.md:107 (the true :rf.event/dispatched-scoped statement), :140 and :674 (the same projection slot + the tree-walk framing).

GATES (worktree C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/prodreport-e96mm):
  python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py     -> exit 0
  python -m mkdocs build --strict       -> exit 0  (docs/core/** IS in mkdocs.yml, so this is the right gate here)

title: check_ambient_durable_reads does not reach a host read wrapped in a call
description:
FOUND while writing rf2-g1xpb fixtures (PR #7541). NOT actioned there: it is a SCOPE question about a required gate, not a self-test question, and widening a required invariant gate needs a ruling.

THE SHAPE. `_VIOLATION_RE` is `:KEY\s+(READ)` — the ambient read must sit IMMEDIATELY in the durable keys value position. So these FIRE:

    :restored-at js/localStorage
    :started-at  (.now js/Date)

and this does NOT (verified, zero findings):

    :restored-at (.getItem js/localStorage "session")

The gate already handles three call-wrapper spellings by enumerating them as their own roster entries — `(.now js/Date …)`, `(.getRandomValues js/crypto …)`, `(.matchMedia …)`. The host-fact entries `js/location`, `js/navigator`, `navigator.`, `js/localStorage`, `js/sessionStorage`, `js/matchMedia` have no such wrapper spelling, so they are reachable ONLY as bare symbol values.

WHY IT MAY NOT MATTER. A bare `js/localStorage` in a durable key value position is not how anyone reads localStorage; `(.getItem js/localStorage …)` is. If the call-wrapper shape is the realistic one, the six host-fact roster entries are close to unreachable in practice, and the gate is narrower than the roster advertises.

WHY IT MAY BE FINE AS IS. EP-0010 governs a DURABLE WRITE being non-deterministic; a durable field taking a host fact through a getter is the same defect, but widening the value-position match to "an ambient read anywhere inside the value form" risks false positives on a legitimately threaded value.

NO CHANGE MADE. rf2-g1xpb left the walk and the match alone deliberately (see also rf2-mjfj9 for the sibling scope ruling on the same checker). Both branches need Mike, not a worker.
close_reason: Widened in PR #7591. Seven enumerated _AMBIENT_READ_FORMS entries, each anchored at value-form start per the ruling: .getItem on localStorage + sessionStorage, .-prop on location + navigator, the callable (js/matchMedia ...), and the repo's own (some-> (.-localStorage js/globalThis) (.getItem ...)) idiom with its sessionStorage twin. Free-form value matching stayed rejected. Fixtures both directions: every_ambient_read_form.cljc 14 -> 21 findings with literal expectations, plus two new negatives (threaded :rf.cofx counterpart; ambient-ok escape over a getter read), both proved non-vacuous. Per-entry kill proof 7/7 red by name. FIVE of the six host-fact entries are now reachable in call position, not six: navigator. is the property-dot spelling whose bare form already fires, and no call wrapper in the ruling's miss list reaches it — that plus three sibling near-forms measured at the same time is filed as rf2-yt0pi rather than widened on a worker's say-so. Equivalence held: none of the seven idioms appears anywhere in the 18 scanned files, live arm 18 files / 0 findings / exit 0 before and after. rf2-g1xpb's literal expectations and rf2-mjfj9's pruned walk have zero diff hunks; both getRandomValues forms remain unexercisable.

title: perf: nine required checkers share the rglob+relative_to walk that cost the image-keys gate 37s

What it DOES share, along with eight others, is the file-walk shape:

  sorted(scan_root.rglob('*'))  +  path.relative_to(...) per file

That was ~0.5s of pure pathlib churn in the image-keys gate, and rglob enumerates implementation/node_modules (~50k paths in a checkout that has it -- which every worker worktree does) only to discard it one entry at a time. rf2-e1xx0 replaced it with an os.walk that PRUNES _EXCLUDE_DIR_NAMES in place plus prefix-string rel paths, proven to yield the same paths in the same order on a node_modules-populated checkout.

The nine sharing that shape:
  check_ambient_durable_reads.py       check_retired_composition_vocab.py
  check_failure_corpus_residue.py      check_retired_image_keys.py  (DONE)
  check_freehand_conformance_index.py  check_retired_spellings.py

If it is ever picked up, the non-negotiable is rf2-e1xx0's method: hold the finding SETS identical (real corpus, allowlist-bypassed corpus, and a per-token x per-context synthetic corpus), not merely both exit 0. A pre-filter that elides most of the regex battery is exactly the change that can silently narrow a gate.

DO NOT bundle these into one worker -- each checker needs its own equivalence proof, and a shared-mechanism refactor across nine guards is a much bigger change than nine small ones.
