I DESTROYED A LIVE WORKER WORKTREE (2026-07-19) — deterministic branch names collide with HISTORICAL merged PRs.

WHAT HAPPENED: my deferred-cleanup loop removes a worktree when `gh pr list --head worker/<name> --state all` reports MERGED. I derive branch names deterministically from the bead id, so I dispatched rf2-vxgfnd.195 onto `worker/shadow-host-gates-195` — the SAME name a previous session had used for the same bead, whose PR #6030 merged on 2026-07-16. The cleanup matched that historical PR, and removed the live worktree plus the branch (local AND origin) while the worker was mid-run. Work lost, worker orphaned.

WHY THE OBVIOUS GUARDS DID NOT CATCH IT: the worktree was clean (worker had not committed yet) so the dirty-check passed; the PR state was genuinely MERGED so the state-check passed; `--state all` is what made a long-closed PR visible. Every individual condition was satisfied. This is the SECOND time I have removed a running worker worktree (the first was k8l1m), and the deferred-cleanup pattern I adopted after that incident did not prevent this one, because it addressed timing rather than identity.

TWO FIXES, USE BOTH:
1. MAINTAIN AN EXPLICIT LIVE-WORKER SKIP LIST. I dispatch the workers, so I know their worktree names — skip every one still running, unconditionally, before any state check. This is the reliable guard; the PR-state heuristic is the unreliable one.
2. REQUIRE THE MERGED PR TO BE *THIS* WORKTREE WORK, not merely same-named: compare `git -C <worktree> rev-parse HEAD` against the PR `headRefOid` (`gh pr view <n> --json headRefOid`), or require `mergedAt` to be LATER than the worktree creation. A name match alone proves nothing — bead ids are stable across sessions, so a re-dispatch of any partially-delivered bead reproduces the collision exactly.

GENERAL LESSON: a deterministic naming scheme makes names non-unique ACROSS TIME. Any cleanup keyed on a name will eventually match a historical artefact. Key destructive operations on identity (a SHA, a creation time), never on a name.

ALSO NOTE: a bead can stay legitimately OPEN after a PR citing it merges — #6030 delivered part of rf2-vxgfnd.195 (the final_schedule probe harness) while its four synthetic arms remained. So "a merged PR names this bead" does NOT mean the bead is done, and must never be used to infer cleanup safety either.

I BRIEFED FROM A BEAD DESCRIPTION SIX TIMES IN ONE DAY, AND THE SIXTH SENT A WORKER TO REBUILD SOMETHING ALREADY MERGED (2026-08-06).

THE SIX: rf2-6ckzl (classifier arm had landed the day before in c1e833bb4c); rf2-6sg25 (alert already shipped, the note was a narrower cancelled-conclusion charge); rf2-2rtt6.120 (guide prose already corrected by #7523/#7543); rf2-2rtt6.115/.116 (both already RULED, with a seven-point implementation brief I never read); rf2-2rtt6.127 (the "rename" was a FILE rename that never landed, and the chapter never carried the claim at all); and rf2-2rtt6.125, whose newest note says verbatim "DELIVERED IN PART — PR #7524 … goals 1, 3, 4 and 5 landed".

I HAVE A MEMORY FOR THIS. It says brief from the newest note, not the title or description. I applied it correctly to some beads in the SAME dispatch pass and skipped it for others. So the failure is not ignorance of the rule — it is that reading a description FEELS like reading the bead, and the description is the one field that is written once at filing and essentially never rewritten.

WHY THE BOARD MAKES THIS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN CARELESS: a merged-PR audit reopens a bead by APPENDING a note and leaving title and description untouched. `bd show` prints DESCRIPTION FIRST and notes last, so THE OLDEST TEXT IS THE MOST PROMINENT. On a board where roughly one bead is reopened per merged PR, most reopened beads are therefore misdescribed by their own most-visible field. `bd ready` compounds it by showing only the TITLE, which is older still.

THE ONLY THING THAT HAS ACTUALLY WORKED, and it worked all six times: every brief carries "THE BEAD OUTRANKS THIS BRIEF — read it bottom-up, newest note first, description LAST. Tell me where I am wrong." Six workers refused six wrong premises. That sentence is a MECHANISM, not a courtesy, and must never be trimmed for brevity.

I FABRICATE BEAD IDS IN BRIEFS — FOUR-PLUS INSTANCES, AND A RECORDED NOTE HAS NOT STOPPED IT (2026-07-26). Mechanical fix below; stop relying on intent.

THE INSTANCES: rf2-t1nnf written into THREE audit briefs (real: rf2-ods8n); rf2-1i2fx (real: rf2-mom1g); rf2-zxa0j quoted in a status report for a bead I had just created and never captured the id of (real: rf2-8jbpe); and rf2-vqe8n briefed to a worker (real: rf2-yvy9x — it found the truth with bd search branch-error and told me). Every time the id LOOKED plausible, which is exactly why it survives review.

ROOT CAUSE: I compose a brief from context and reach for the id from recall, or I run bd create, do not capture the id it printed, and then refer to the bead later as though I know its id. bd create output ends with Priority/Status lines and I have repeatedly not scrolled to the id.

THE MECHANICAL FIX, which is the only thing that will work: never type a bead id into a brief, a report, or a bd command from recall. Resolve it in the SAME shell invocation that uses it — bd list --status=open --limit 0 | grep -iE <distinctive title words>, or bd search <token>. If a brief must name an id, paste it from a command run seconds earlier in that same turn. And after every bd create, immediately echo the created id (or grep it back by title) BEFORE referring to the bead again.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: a wrong id in a brief sends a worker to bd show on a nonexistent bead. Three audit workers hit that and had to be corrected mid-flight. Worse, a plausible-but-wrong id could resolve to a REAL DIFFERENT bead and silently redirect work — that has not happened yet and is the failure I am actually guarding against.

THIS IS THE SAME CLASS AS MY OTHER THIRTEEN WRONG MEASUREMENTS: reaching for a cheap proxy (recall) instead of the real lookup. The worker that caught this one also caught that my brief line numbers had drifted (mkdocs.yml 251/272, not 251/268) — same lesson, different field. Verify, do not transcribe.

THIS IS THE ELEVENTH MEASUREMENT ERROR OF MINE TODAY AND THE WORST-PROPAGATED — the others were single wrong numbers; this one was a wrong METHOD that I taught to workers as exemplary, and at least one earlier worker reported the coverage figure believing it discharged the obligation. THE PATTERN, AGAIN AND FOR THE ELEVENTH TIME: A CHEAP PROXY SUBSTITUTED FOR THE REAL MEASUREMENT. Before quoting a number as proof, ask WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE TRUE FOR IT TO BE MEASURING SOMETHING ELSE. I MISREAD "PARALLEL-SAFE" AS "SELF-CONTAINED" AND DISPATCHED A STRUCTURALLY BLOCKED BEAD (2026-07-26, rf2-3bjs8).

WHAT I DID: the bead title says "F6c/examples: migrate examples/ off re-frame.ui to Freehand names (parallel-safe)". I ran the pre-dispatch checks and they came back clean — 16 files under examples/ reference the donor namespace, and NO live worker had any examples/ file modified. I concluded it was dispatchable and fenced the worker to examples/.

WHY THAT WAS WRONG: "parallel-safe" means safe to run CONCURRENTLY with other work. It does NOT mean the fix is confined to that tree. The actual blockers live OUTSIDE examples/ — spec/conformance/freehand/donor-inventory.md, two implementation/ui test files, and .github/workflows/test.yml — every one of which my fence FORBADE. In the worker words: "an examples/-fenced worker CANNOT land this — that is structural, not a scheduling accident."

THE CHECK I WAS MISSING: my pre-dispatch discipline verifies (a) the premise still holds and (b) no live worker holds the surface. It does NOT ask (c) IS THE FIX CONFINED TO THE SURFACE I AM FENCING? For any bead whose title or notes mention a ledger, an inventory, a conformance roster, or a cross-artefact gate, the fix almost certainly reaches beyond the tree the bead is named after. Ask what gate OWNS the claim, and put that gate file in the fence — or do not dispatch.

THE DISPATCH WAS NOT WASTED, and this is the part worth keeping. Two earlier passes had REASONED that de-donoring examples/ would red gates outside the tree; this worker actually performed the migration, ran the gates, captured rc, reverted, and produced the measured list — three named failing gates with file and line, plus a rc=0 clean Freehand compile of the migrated scaffold proving the CODE half is ready. ALSO WORTH KEEPING — the sharpest thing in its report: of the 16 donor references, 4 are PROSE that truthfully describes the other 12 as donor-based. "Renaming the words while the clusters are still donor-based would make the docs lie." A grep count is not a work list; some matches are correct BECAUSE the code is not yet migrated.

I OVERRODE A RECORDED DEFERRAL WITHOUT ACKNOWLEDGING IT — SECOND TIME TODAY — AND THE WORK TURNED OUT JUSTIFIED FOR A REASON NEITHER I NOR THE DEFERRAL KNEW (2026-07-26).

rf2-jl7gz carried a note from the #7051 audit: "STAYS DEFERRED — measured zero corpus exposure". I dispatched it anyway, in a brief that never mentioned the deferral. The worker built it and FLAGGED the override rather than silently complying — same shape as rf2-n4by4 earlier the same day, where the bead said "ENFORCEMENT NEEDS A RULING, do not pick one silently" and my brief silently picked one. Two instances in one session of the same defect: I read beads for FACTS and miss their RECORDED DISPOSITIONS. A deferral, a reserved ruling and a held decision are all instructions addressed TO ME, and a brief that overrides one without saying so leaves the tracker unable to distinguish a considered reversal from an oversight.

BUT THE DISPATCH WAS RIGHT, AND THE REASON IS THE GENERALISABLE PART: THE DEFERRAL WAS MEASURED ON ONE DIRECTION OF A BIDIRECTIONAL GATE. "Zero corpus exposure" meant no FALSE GREEN was reachable today — no bad row passing. The worker found the same miscount was ALSO COSTING EVIDENCE: the `~#js [fx]` unquote island and the reader-conditional arm pairing were ALREADY DROPPING REAL EDGES, so the FALSE-RED direction was live and had never been measured. In its words, the miscount "was costing evidence as well as inventing it".

SO THE RULE: A DEFERRAL MEASURED ON ONE DIRECTION OF A TWO-DIRECTION CHECK IS NOT A DEFERRAL. Before honouring "zero exposure" on any gate that can be wrong in both directions — a census, a redaction, a refusal, a roster — ask which direction was measured. Under-matching and over-matching have different corpora and only one of them is usually counted.

THE OTHER THING WORTH KEEPING, because it is the cleanest instance yet of a probe that cannot discriminate: the bead own axis-2 case (`#_#?(:clj (def fx …))`) REDS UNDER THE OLD READER TOO, measured not assumed. Read short it does leave `(:clj (def fx …))` standing exactly as the bead describes — but `_DEFINER_RE` is anchored to a top-level form HEAD and the survivor head is `:clj`, not `def`, so no binding registers and the row reds either way. The wrapper the miscount leaves is INERT. A TAG target discriminates because there the survivor IS the form: `#_#js (def fx …)` leaves the `def` at top level to bind the fixture, giving a silent green. The worker kept the `#?` case but RELABELLED it as a regression guard on the anchoring rather than as evidence. That is the right disposal for a case that cannot fail for the reason it was written.

AND A SELF-CAUGHT REGRESSION WORTH THE SWEEP: `##NaN` is written straight into the adapter suites, and the first draft read the second `#` as a tag over `NaN`, turning `##Inf` into `##Inf 3`. Its own extent table caught it. When extending a reader rule, enumerate the OTHER `#`-prefixed forms — `#(`, `#{`, `#"`, `#=`, `#!`, `##`, and namespaced maps `#:ns{…}` — and say which need the rule and which do not.

I PRESCRIBED AN UNSOUND FIX AND A WORKER CAUGHT IT BY MEASURING (2026-08-01, rf2-8vvdo / PR #7336). Record the lesson, not the incident.

WHAT HAPPENED. A core test reddened under load because it asserted a PROCESS-WIDE weak-map count for strict equality; the diagnosing worker filed rf2-8vvdo proposing (<= (.size m) baseline) as a STRONGER replacement, and I briefed that fix as-is while telling the implementing worker 'the fix must be stronger, never weaker' and 'prove it still catches the original defect'.

THE IMPLEMENTING WORKER REFUSED IT AND WAS RIGHT. (<= (.size m) baseline) cures the false RED by buying a false GREEN under the same load: a SIBLING entry expunging in our entry's place satisfies it while OUR entry is still leaked. It did not argue this — it MEASURED it, with a probe of (and (<= (.size m) baseline) (.containsKey m our-key)) that PASSED, i.e. the proposed assertion held with the leaked entry still in the map, before the throwable was even released. That is precisely the fail-open class my own brief forbade.

THE CORRECT SHAPE, which the bead itself had offered as an alternative: assert THE ENTRY'S OWN ABSENCE, not a population count. (= (inc baseline) (.size m)) -> (= 1 (count our-keys)); (= baseline (.size m)) -> (not (.containsKey m our-key)). It also found the bead had diagnosed only ONE of the two assertions — the sibling assertion carried the identical defect and would have left the test load-sensitive.

THE GENERAL LESSON, which is mine: WHEN A BEAD PROPOSES A SPECIFIC FIX, THE BRIEF MUST TREAT IT AS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A SPECIFICATION. I passed a diagnosing worker's proposed patch through to an implementing worker with my authority attached, which converts a suggestion into an instruction and invites compliance over judgement. Correct form: state the DEFECT and the ACCEPTANCE CRITERION (here: 'the assertion must fail when this entry leaks, whatever else the process is doing'), cite the bead's proposal as one candidate, and say explicitly that a better shape is welcome and a refusal with evidence is a complete answer.

SECOND-ORDER POINT WORTH KEEPING: an assertion about a SHARED, PROCESS-WIDE quantity can almost never state a claim about ONE participant. Prefer identity over population whenever the property is about a specific object — count-based proxies fail open under concurrency in both directions.

I REPEATED THE gh --jq --arg BUG AFTER RECORDING IT (2026-07-26). gh accepts the jq PROGRAM as the argument to --jq, so writing "gh pr list --json ... --jq --arg B \"$b\" \x27<program>\x27" makes --arg the program and the real program a stray argument. The query returns EMPTY, not an error. I hit this once on a hygiene sweep where every PR read as pr=none, recorded it, and then wrote the identical construction again on the next hygiene sweep.

THE FIX: fetch once to a file with gh --json, then pipe/read that file with the jq BINARY, where --arg is valid: gh pr list --json number,state,headRefName > /tmp/prs.json, then jq -r --arg B "$b" \x27...\x27 /tmp/prs.json.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE TYPO: both times, the broken query fed a DESTRUCTIVE decision — branch deletion gated on "is this PR merged?". Both times the gate FAILED SAFE and refused, because an empty result does not match *MERGED. That is the only reason a broken query did not delete a live branch. Design destructive gates so the empty/unknown case refuses; do not rely on the query being right.

TWELFTH WRONG MEASUREMENT THIS SESSION, and the first outright repeat. The others were varied (loose greps matching comments, row-count as a proxy for content, diffing a worktree against moved main, reading a file before the pull landed, --is-ancestor after a rebase-merge). This one I had already written down. Recording a trap is not the same as building the habit that avoids it — for shell constructions specifically, the habit that works is: never put --arg on a gh command line.

identical? ON A KEYWORD LITERAL IS JVM-SOUND AND CLJS-UNSOUND — it silently makes a sentinel check unreachable on CLJS. Found by the rf2-6t6qk/rf2-uoy6m worker (#6452), 2026-07-19, while making the trace deferral seam cross-platform.

THE BUG: deferred-continue marked "baseline unread" with a ::unread KEYWORD and compared it with identical?. On the JVM keywords are interned so identical? works. ON CLJS KEYWORD LITERALS ARE NOT GUARANTEED REFERENCE-EQUAL, so the check never matched — every call fell through to level-testing the LIVE predicate instead. Consequence: a cascaded :rf.event/dispatched envelope whose target-live? was unbound post-drain read FALSE and THE EVENT WAS SILENTLY DROPPED. Not an exception — a dropped event.

THE META-LESSON, the important half: this was the CLJS-ONLY FACE of rf2-eaxnai REGRESSION 1. The JVM cure shipped in PR #6365 and looked complete; the CLJS half of the same defect survived undetected because no CLJS test exercised the path. A cross-host .cljc fix is NOT done when the JVM suite is green. It surfaced here only because making the seam cross-platform FORCED the CLJS gate to run it (4 cofx_cljs_test failures), and the worker instrumented the flush to diagnose rather than working around it. Fix was a dedicated OBJECT sentinel, not a keyword.

RULE: in .cljc, never use identical? against a keyword/string/number literal as a sentinel — use a dedicated object value. And when a .cljc correctness fix ships green on ONE host, ASK EXPLICITLY whether the other host exercises the same path; if no test does, that is a GAP, not a pass. Cross-ref rf2-eaxnai REGRESSION 1, PR #6365 (JVM-only cure), PR #6452 (cross-host fix).

ALSO FROM #6452 — JVM GATE TIMEOUTS ON THIS BOX ARE RESOURCE CONTENTION, NOT HANGS. Repeated 10-minute harness timeouts on implementation/core clojure -M:test were environmental: jstack showed the JVMs actively inside clojure.test with NO Java-level deadlock and no "waiting to lock". Cause: multiple agents running JVMs concurrently, AND each timed-out run ORPHANS a ~1.8 GB JVM that compounds contention. Worker guidance: if a JVM gate times out, jstack before concluding hang, kill YOUR OWN orphaned JVMs only, re-run. Mayor guidance: saturating 6 workers that each run a full JVM suite is a real resource ceiling on this machine — a timing-out gate is a signal to check concurrency, not to assume a stuck worker.

IN_PROGRESS IS A BLIND SPOT IN THE DISPATCH LOOP — audit it every few ticks, not just bd ready. On 2026-07-19 I found rf2-kxkag (P2) and rf2-lgeron (P3) sitting IN_PROGRESS with every stated blocker long since cleared: kxkag waited on rf2-74vlo (CLOSED), lgeron on rf2-sy7zr (CLOSED), rf2-vxgfnd.96.3 (CLOSED) and four surfaces that were all free. Both were fully dispatchable and INVISIBLE, because `bd ready` does not list in-progress beads and every saturation check I run reads from `bd ready`. They would have sat indefinitely.
SAME SHAPE AS the epic-child undercount (see backlog-counting-bd-list-status-open-excludes-epic): a whole CLASS invisible to the count in use. Different mechanism, identical consequence — I under-dispatched while believing the pool was drained.
THE CHECK: `bd list --status=in_progress --limit 0`, then for each, confirm a worker is ACTUALLY live. If none is, read the NOTES: it is either (a) a stale claim for shipped work -> close with evidence, (b) a PARTIAL delivery whose blockers may have cleared -> re-verify each blocker and DISPATCH, or (c) genuinely held on an operator ruling -> leave.

⚠️ AND THE TRAP THAT ALMOST BIT: my first instinct was to close all three as delivered, because their commits ARE in main. TWO CARRIED EXPLICIT "PARTIAL" MARKERS — one written by me: "PARTIAL in #6310 — DO NOT CLOSE ON THAT MERGE." A merged PR citing a bead does NOT mean the bead is done. Precedents this session: #6030 merged a FIFTH arm of rf2-vxgfnd.195 while all four DESCRIPTION arms remained; rf2-84173 shipped its second arm while AC1 and AC3-arm-1 stayed undelivered. CLOSING WOULD HAVE BURIED THE REMAINDER PERMANENTLY — a closed bead never resurfaces in any count.
RULE: before closing any bead on a merged PR, grep its NOTES for PARTIAL / remain / not delivered / arm N / AC-N. If the marker is there, the bead stays open and the remainder gets dispatched.

ENUMERATING THE BLOCKING STATUSES IS FAIL-OPEN. INVERT IT (2026-08-10).

FOUND BY THE rf2-vfsrd WORKER against the live CLI, not by reading docs. The merge criterion said "zero QUEUED and zero IN_PROGRESS". The GitHub CLI also returns REQUESTED, WAITING and PENDING. A check in any of those three is neither QUEUED nor IN_PROGRESS, so a blocklist of two names reads it as absent and the PR looks settled.

THE CORRECT FORM IS POSITIVE: every run at the CURRENT HEAD SHA must be COMPLETED. Then an unanticipated status blocks instead of vanishing - the same inversion the provenance-pins gate needed when its trailing-character blacklist accepted %3F, : and & (rf2-styo). Twice in one day, the same defect shape: enumerate what is bad and the unimagined case defaults to accepted.

MY OWN SWEEP SURVIVED ONLY BY ACCIDENT. I count total, ok, skip, canc, fail, q, inprog and I check that ok+skip == total. That sum catches a REQUESTED check, because it would be inside total and outside every named bucket. But the arithmetic was doing work I had not consciously assigned it. State the rule as: ok+skip must EQUAL total, and separately every run must be COMPLETED. Do not rely on q==0 and inprog==0 alone.

THE COMMAND MUST ALSO BE ABLE TO PERFORM ITS OWN JOIN, and the prescribed one could not. `gh run list`'s table has NO headSha column and `gh pr checks` has NO conclusion field, so the documented spelling could not key runs to the head SHA at all. The worker verified both against the live CLI and wrote an executable form: gh pr view --json headRefName,headRefOid, then gh pr checks --json name,state,bucket, then gh run list --branch <head> --commit <oid> --json status,headSha,name.

LESSON BEYOND THE CRITERION: a documented command is not a verified command. If a rule prescribes a check, run the check once and confirm the fields it names actually exist.

"IS THROWN?" IS NOT A WITNESS. A SABOTAGE PROVED IT GREEN (2026-08-10).

WHAT HAPPENED. The rf2-hic-011 worker built the I7 ambient-read legality matrix and ran the bead's own named sabotage: remove read-key!'s nil-frame guard. It expected the escaped-read rows to red. THE READS STILL THREW - from subscribe-once, with :rf.error/no-frame-context instead of :rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render. So a row written as (is (thrown? ...)) would have stayed GREEN under the exact perturbation the bead named as its acceptance sabotage.

THE POINT GENERALISES BEYOND THIS SUITE. A throw assertion proves that SOMETHING failed, not that the guard under test failed, and not that it failed for the reason claimed. Any second defence downstream keeps the test green while the mechanism it names is gone. In a layered runtime there is almost always a second defence.

WHAT TO DEMAND IN A BRIEF INSTEAD: assert the exact error identity - the id and the payload as an exact map - not merely that an exception occurred. That worker asserted :rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render, the emitting function, the phase and the query as one map, so a different throw from a different layer reds.

THE SAME REPORT CARRIED A SECOND INSTANCE OF THE FAMILY. Its P2 control caught a defect in its own suite: a timer row's follow-up body re-read a key the enclosing body had also read, so accumulation was swallowed by the row's own expected set. Only the perturbation exposed it. Three other workers tonight found defects in their own tests the same way - a StrictMode row that could not see additivity, a passive-effect race where four rows passed by luck, a coverage floor that survived deleting the sections it guarded.

SO THE RULE FOR EVERY WITNESS BEAD: perturb, confirm red, restore, confirm green - and when it does NOT red, that is the finding. Do not adjust the control until the witness is understood. Half of tonight's most valuable results came from a control refusing to red.

Junction detection via `cmd /c dir /AL <path>` DOES NOT WORK from the Bash tool on this Windows setup - it prints only the cmd banner and no listing, so every directory reports 'no junction'. A hygiene brief that keys 'rmdir the junction first' on that command silently degrades to 'treat everything as a real directory' (or, with a fail-closed rule, 'treat everything as a junction'). Working replacement: compare file identity with `fsutil file queryfileid` - a junction shares the target's id, a real directory has its own - validated against a deliberately-created control junction. Belt-and-braces: a NON-FOLLOWING `Directory.Delete(path, recursive:false)` before `git worktree remove` unlinks a junction and fails harmlessly on a populated real directory. Related: [[junction-safe-worktree-cleanup]].

Junction-rmdir trap (RECURRED 2x, 2026-06-10): a worktree's implementation/node_modules is often a JUNCTION to the mayor checkout's real node_modules (workers npm-install/junction it to run node gates). 'git worktree remove --force' on such a worktree DELETES THROUGH the junction into the mayor's REAL node_modules (emptying it to 0) UNLESS the junction link is removed FIRST. THE BREAKING BUG (hit twice): building the rmdir path via bash sed inside a nested powershell double-quoted string — e.g. cmd /c rmdir '$(echo $p|sed 's#/#\#g')' — the sed errors 'unterminated s command' (nested-quote mangling), rmdir gets a broken path + fails ('syntax of the command is incorrect'), the junction survives, and worktree-remove nukes the target. CORRECT junction removal (PowerShell-native, NO bash sed, NO backslash conversion): powershell -NoProfile -Command "$p='<FORWARD-slash path>'; $i=Get-Item $p -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if($i -and $i.LinkType){ [System.IO.Directory]::Delete($p,$false) }; Test-Path $p"  — [System.IO.Directory]::Delete(path,$false) removes the reparse point WITHOUT recursing into the target; forward-slashes work fine in .NET; VERIFY Test-Path returns False BEFORE git worktree remove. RECOVERY when nuked: npm ci --prefix <mayor>/implementation. Supersedes the prior trap note.

JVM alloc bench: escape analysis makes a retired arm bimodal by arm order. In read_attribution.clj (rf2-a8bw0, PR #7157) the eager-payload arm S1-EAGER read 136.0 B/call in every FORWARD round and 72.0 in every REVERSED round — a clean 64 B step, not noise. 64 B is the two-entry PersistentArrayMap; the JIT scalar-replaces it when the arm runs earlier in the plan and require-current-frame! inlines into it. So on the JVM an arm that ALLOCATES-THEN-DISCARDS can read its own cost or zero depending on position, while an arm that never evaluates the expression reads flat. Two consequences: (1) always run both arm orders and quote the RANGE for any arm whose object does not escape — a mean hides a JIT decision; (2) the SHIPPED (deferred) arm being flat across all rounds is the stronger evidence, because it has nothing for EA to remove. Separately: a thread-bound dynamic Var deref costs 32 B/read on the JVM (Var.getThreadBinding -> PersistentHashMap.entryAt allocates a MapEntry) — this is the floor under every *current-frame* read and it does NOT exist in CLJS.

JVM ALLOCATION PROFILES CAN MIS-RANK A CLJS TARGET, AND THIS PROJECT'S BROWSER SUBSTRATE IS A CLJS TARGET. Measuring `subscribe` on a cache hit (rf2-j8ls2), the LARGEST single term — ~760 B of ~1,800, 41% — was the JVM's dynamic `binding`. It DOES NOT EXIST IN CLOJURESCRIPT: CLJS `binding` expands through `with-redefs` to `let` + `set!` + `try`/`finally` restore (confirmed in cljs/core.cljc, clojurescript-1.12.145), allocating ZERO. Proof in the same run: the same fn with a nil target, binding nothing, measured 16-40 B against 752-808 B bound.
CONSEQUENCE: any bead RANKED off a JVM allocation profile may be ranked wrong for the browser. Three were, and needed re-ranking (rf2-x0fe2, P1). `ThreadMXBean/getThreadAllocatedBytes` is JVM-only and there is no equivalent CLJS instrument, so this is not a gap you can close by re-running.
WHAT SURVIVES: a RATIO between two arms that BOTH pay the JVM-only term (e.g. Freehand's port vs a Reagent view body, both bound) is much more robust than either absolute — removing the term moved that comparison only 97.4% -> 94.9%. WHAT DOES NOT: absolute B/call, and any ordering of terms.
RULE: state the runtime beside every allocation figure, and before ranking work off one, ask which terms are runtime-specific.

LARGE-BEAD WORKER PATIENCE: a big facade/refactor bead touching ~100 files (e.g. csbbwu, m90brg) legitimately runs 40+ min at '99 modified / 0 commits' — it commits ONCE at the very end after a long tail of call-site fixes + a heavy gate suite (test:cljs 8000+ tests, JVM core, bundle-isolation, adapter-smokes, mkdocs, manifest, skills-check, drift). Do NOT mistake 'no commits across several ticks' for a STALL on a large bead. Observed 2026-07-08: I prematurely TaskStop'd m90brg — the kill-reveal showed its last action was 'rerun core JVM tests to confirm this fixes all 3 errors' (actively debugging, not hung). DISTINGUISH stall-vs-working by the worker's LAST ACTION (a SendMessage status-ping, or the kill-reveal line), NOT by commit count. For a large-bead worker: send a status-ping first; only stop if it (a) confirms stuck, (b) doesn't respond across 2 pings, or (c) its last-action shows a tight retry loop on one gate (the mkdocs-stall pattern). WIP survives a stop (uncommitted files remain), so recovery = re-dispatch a finish-worker to the SAME worktree to continue from the WIP.

npm run lint:js LIVES IN A SEPARATE ROOT npm PROJECT, SO A WORKER WITH ONLY implementation/node_modules CANNOT RUN IT — AND THE FAILURE DOES NOT LOOK LIKE A LINT FAILURE (2026-08-06, rf2-t4j7c).

THE MECHANISM: lint:js belongs to the root package (re-frame2-lint), not to implementation/. A worker that runs `npm ci` inside implementation/ — which is the standard advice for a fresh worktree, because that is where the CLJS/node tiers need it — does NOT get eslint. Invoking the gate then fails with "eslint is not recognized", which reads as a broken environment rather than as a gate that never ran. The gate is SILENTLY UNRUNNABLE, and a worker can honestly report every other gate green while lint has never executed once.

THAT IS EXACTLY HOW PR #7609 REACHED CI RED. The worker ran test:script-helpers and node --check ×4 and reported them all 0; lint was the one gate it could not run and did not notice it could not run.

THE BRIEF LINE TO ADD FOR ANY JS-TOUCHING BEAD: run `npm ci` at the REPO ROOT as well as under implementation/, and report lint:jss own exit code. An "is not recognized" error from a gate is NOT an environment excuse — it is the gate telling you it did not run, which is the same class as the mkdocs soft-skip and the killed-wrapper exit 0.

AND A CORRECTION TO MY OWN BRIEF, in the repos favour: I told the worker the tree was at ONE live ESLint suppression with rf2-kvsm1 open to retire it. It is at ZERO — kvsm1 already retired the last directive, and eslint.config.mjs records it ("the suppression went with the code it guarded"). So a disable there would have been the ONLY one in the tree, not the second. My constraint was stale in the direction that made the wrong answer look cheaper.

THE FIX IT CHOSE, AND THE REASONING THAT MAKES IT MORE THAN A LINT SILENCER: the negative fixture requires the module and never calls it, which trips no-unused-vars. It dropped the BINDING (`require(./lane_cache.cjs);` with nothing bound) rather than suppressing. That is not quieter, it is STRONGER — a refactor that deletes the clear leaves one of two shapes, and they are not equally dangerous. If the binding SURVIVES, no-unused-vars reports the orphan and lint catches that driver a gate earlier. If the binding GOES TOO, nothing in the lint path can see anything wrong: the file parses, every name is used, and only the missing CALL separates it from a correct driver. THE SECOND VARIANT IS THE ONE NO OTHER GATE OWNS, so it is the one worth modelling. Proved rather than asserted: with a comment-only rider in the discovery directory, lint:js exits 0 while the gate exits 1 on the same file.

IT ALSO DECLINED AN IGNORES ENTRY on the configs own stated terms — that list is for trees that are GENERATED and can carry JS, "not when a file in it happens to have complained". These fixtures are hand-authored, and keeping them in the lint path is what stops them drifting into shapes no real driver could take.

LINTER DIAGNOSTIC CODES GET RENUMBERED — pin the fix against the runner version AND a newer one. On 2026-07-19 the rf2-lsp1i CI fix found shellcheck reports the same finding under two codes: 0.9.0 (what ubuntu-24.04 ships) emits SC2317 on the rm line; 0.10+ emits SC2329 on the function line. Disabling only SC2317 passes TODAY and goes red silently the moment the runner image updates; disabling only SC2329 leaves CI red now. The fix names BOTH, verified that 0.9.0 tolerates the unknown SC2329 silently. RULE: when suppressing a linter diagnostic, install the EXACT version CI runs (reproduce the failure byte-for-byte first) AND at least one newer version, then satisfy both. A suppression validated only against the current runner is a time bomb. DIAGNOSIS TECHNIQUE WORTH COPYING: the worker established the cause by BISECTION, not assertion — a minimal trap-cleanup script lints clean; truncating the real script at one line is clean and at another reproduces; deleting only the trailing `exit 0` makes the diagnostic vanish. That isolated the real trigger ("shellcheck models the EXIT trap as the fall-through ending, and every path here exits explicitly") rather than accepting the message at face value. SCOPE RULE: the disable was FUNCTION-scoped with a comment stating why the code is reachable — never file-level, never blanket. Removing the trap handler instead would have leaked three temp files per run.

MAYOR BRIEF ACCURACY — stop asserting file paths I have not verified. Three times in one session (2026-07-18) I named the wrong surface in a dispatch brief: rf2-s32bf (said core.cljc; real = implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/middleware.cljc), rf2-05kex (said examples/README.md + helix example; real = skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/views.md), rf2-wnhbm (said implementation/core/src/re_frame/conformance.cljc; real = implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/compiler/analyze.cljc). Each time the worker followed the BEAD over my brief and found the real file — the precedence held, so nothing was lost, but the wrong fence risks pointing a worker away from a live collision or into someone else's surface. CORRECTIVE: when my own grep has NOT positively confirmed the file, write the brief as 'LOCATE the surface: the bead names <symptom/error-id/PR#>; grep for it' rather than naming a path with false confidence. Naming an unverified path is worse than naming none — it anchors the worker and mis-draws the fence. Verified paths are still worth naming; unverified guesses are not. Always tell the worker the BEAD is authoritative over the brief.

MAYOR CI-merge gotcha: gh's statusCheckRollup includes STALE entries from superseded commits — when a worker force-pushes a fix, the prior commit's in-progress checks become conclusion=CANCELLED and its aggregates (e.g. 'Lint required','All required checks passed') linger as FAILURE in the rollup. A naive 'any conclusion!=SUCCESS' filter reads these as failures. For the merge decision use the DEDUPED latest-per-check view: 'gh pr checks <PR>' (pass/pending/fail/skipping per check). Merge only on 0 fail AND 0 pending there. Confirm ambiguity by checking a specific check has both a CANCELLED and a SUCCESS entry (latest wins).

MAYOR DASHBOARD: Mike does NOT want ai/dashboard.md maintained (told mayor 2026-06-20, overrides the mayor-method/bootstrap.md + CLAUDE.md 'keep dashboard up to date' instruction). Stop updating ai/dashboard.md. Surface operator-facing state in chat; keep decision gates in ai/decisions.md only. Do not spend tick cycles on the dashboard.

MAYOR dispatch anti-strand: do NOT tell workers to run 'scripts/test-fast-pr.sh' in a brief. On Windows it takes >10 min (slow shadow-cljs compile) and times out the worker's tool cap, so workers background it (or pipe through tail) and then STRAND with work uncommitted/unpushed — observed 4x this session (2dmtyl/.19/.21/.26). Instead brief: 'run ONLY your artefact's tests (clojure -M:test in the artefact dir) + npm run test:cljs in the FOREGROUND; do NOT run the full test-fast-pr.sh spine — CI runs it on Linux.' Those surface-specific gates finish fast + in-foreground. Recover a strand by SendMessage-resuming the agent: commit FIRST, then rebase/push/PR.

MAYOR DISPATCH DRIFT, caught 2026-07-24 on a reread of the method dispatch-prompt-template. Three things I had been omitting from briefs, in descending order of how much they matter.

1. ⚠️ THE WORKTREE BOUNDARY BLOCK MUST GO IN VERBATIM, AND THE GUARD SCRIPT IS NOT IT. I had been writing "run the worktree guard and report WORKTREE_ROOT" and stopping there. The method says plainly that a start-of-session guard CAN BE FOOLED: some edit-tool path resolution resolves a relative path against the SESSION ROOT rather than the git root, so a write lands in the mayor checkout even after the guard passed — the leak happens mid-session, in one tool call. The real backstop is two things I was not asking for:
   (a) re-verify the git root BEFORE EVERY EDIT — `git -C <worktree> rev-parse --show-toplevel` must print the worktree — and use ABSOLUTE paths under it for every write;
   (b) AFTER WRITING ANY NEW FILE, check BOTH TREES. A new GITIGNORED file leaking into the mayor checkout is INVISIBLE in the worker own git status, so it fails silently. This is the worst case and the one a guard cannot catch.
   On a leak the worker must STOP and report both paths — not repair, commit or push.

2. THE PR BODY NEEDS A SECTION HEADED EXACTLY `## Quality gates`. The verbatim heading is a CONTRACT for automated PR audits, not a style preference. List what ran with counts and exit codes; a skipped gate needs a one-line reason there, because a silent skip fails review. Some workers were doing this spontaneously; it should not depend on their initiative.

3. P1 IS ALWAYS SOLO — one bead, one PR — so it merges on its own green and is never blocked by a cluster-sibling. I bundled TWO P1s (rf2-berc2 + rf2-51d4q) into one dispatch because they were the same defect class in the same files. The surface reasoning was right and one agent SHOULD own that surface; the error was in the SHIPPING shape. The method already covers this case: a tightly-coupled surface is its own SERIAL LANE — one agent, but SEQUENCED PRs, later ones rebasing on the earlier merge. Corrected mid-flight by telling the worker to open a PR per bead.

THE GENERAL LESSON: I re-derived my brief boilerplate from memory each wave and it drifted from the written template. The template exists precisely because these are hard-won and non-obvious. Reread the SIBLING files on the cadence, not just the README — the boundary block and the shape-selection rules live in dispatch-prompt-template.md, which I had not opened this session while writing a dozen briefs.

MAYOR dispatch — grep for in-flight work FIRST (bitten 2x): before dispatching any bead/follow-up, run 'git ls-remote origin worker/*' AND 'gh pr list' and grep for a branch/PR already targeting that bead-id or its surface/error-id. A CONCURRENT monitor-loop session independently creates worker/* branches for the same beads I file — e.g. ahjbsi (my spec/009 route-keyword row) duplicated worker/qot6ii-009-row doing the identical row; both merged-collided, needed a cherry-pick rebase to drop the dup. Checking only MY running Task agents misses the other session. Grep remote branches + open PRs by surface before every dispatch.

MAYOR OPS: do NOT TaskStop a sole-owner background worker just because you haven't received a completion notification — no-notification != idle. During the EP-0002 greenup I killed ad423b1 mid-fix (it was actively reasoning + had an uncommitted correct adapter fix in the worktree); its killed-output showed it was completing the work. Recovery cost a re-brief. RULE: a worker with no completion notification is ACTIVE unless its worktree is idle >25min AND no push AND no new worktree writes. Wait for the completion notification; only TaskStop on the genuine >25min-idle hung signal.

Mayor drive-to-0 means the WHOLE open backlog, not just the active EP critical path. When the active wave is gated/in-flight, do NOT sit at 1-2 live reporting "quiescent" — pull P2/P3/P4 beads from `bd list --status open`, especially review/skills/docs/test/code-comments/final-review/conformance TAILS on ALREADY-MERGED EPs (EP-0008/0010/0011 etc.), which are dispatchable independent of the active wave. Cluster small same-surface ones (<=3/agent). "Quiescent" is only legitimate when EVERY open bead is gated on a specific in-flight PR/worker OR is a held Mike-decision/graduation. Mike flagged this 2026-06-12 ("does the loop make clear drive-to-0 means targeting P3/P4?") after I let ~40 backlog beads sit while gating on the active wave. The cron loop prompt was rewritten to force whole-backlog dispatch + raise the quiescent bar.

MAYOR OPS (observed 3x in one session 2026-06-10: d0631h, goum9x, adcmk8): background workers on INVESTIGATION-HEAVY review beads (best-practice-review / vestigial-review / test-isolation follow-ups) sometimes STALL — worktree goes clean tree + 0 commits + no PR + >30min idle + NO churning java/node test process. This is distinct from a slow-but-active worker (which has uncommitted edits OR a churning test process OR fresh worktree mtimes). DETECTION: check ALL of (git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD == 0) AND (git status --porcelain clean, excl node_modules/.cpcache/out) AND (no node/java proc >10 CPU) AND (newest non-cache source mtime >25-30min). If all hold → STALLED, reap is safe (nothing to lose). RECOVERY: reap worktree (junction-safe) + re-dispatch FRESH on a -v2 branch with a TIGHT brief: 'work efficiently, timebox, make the fix + COMMIT+PUSH promptly, cap test runs at timeout 300, if premise doesn't hold close no-op fast, do NOT over-investigate.' The tight re-dispatch SUCCEEDED for goum9x-v2 (efficient fix where v1 stalled 39min). Possibly an API-degradation window or analysis-paralysis on open-ended 'polish/audit' beads. Contrast: do NOT reap a worker with uncommitted edits (mid-fix) — that was the ad423b1 mistake.

Mayor loop 'no agents at zero' has three root causes, fixed 2026-06-09. (1) CI-drain gap: a PR going green is NOT a wake event, only worker-completions and the 15-min cron wake the mayor, so a draining green PR (and the gated next-wave it unblocks) sits until the next invocation. Fix: end-of-tick self-wakeup via ScheduleWakeup ~270s when workers<6 and a draining PR/gated next-wave exists. (2) Silent zombie workers: a hung worker emits no completion notification, so its idle worktree is counted as a live slot (1hncp2 sat idle 96min, 0 commits). Fix: STEP-1 liveness sweep each tick, worktree idle >25min with no PR = hung, salvage-or-reap + re-dispatch fresh. (3) Decision beads mis-dispatched as action work zombie the worker (1hncp2 was a Mike judgment-call, scroll durable-vs-transient). Fix: classify-before-dispatch, body says surface/judgment/confirm/choose-a-b = route to /ai/decisions + skip-list, never dispatch. Also: agent-* worktrees under .claude/worktrees are isolation:worktree leftovers that stay locked after their PRs merge (days-old cruft), not live workers.

MERGE-LOOP DRIFT, caught 2026-07-24 by finally reading .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md instead of re-deriving the loop from the cron prose. Three real drifts plus one stale line IN the skill.

1. ⚠️ I HAVE BEEN BLOCKING ON CI WITH BACKGROUND WATCHERS. The skill says explicitly: "NEVER block the session waiting on CI... Use a ONE-SHOT `gh pr checks <pr>` per open PR: merge the ones that are 0-fail/0-pending NOW; for any still-pending PR, LEAVE IT and re-check on the NEXT signal — the steady stream of worker-completions plus the cadence will catch it without a babysitting script."
   I armed `until [pending=0]; do sleep; done` background watchers roughly EIGHT times in one session. Each occupies a background slot and generates a notification, and none was necessary: worker completions and the 10-minute cadence re-invoke me constantly. STOP DOING THIS. One-shot check, merge what is ready, move on.

2. MERGEABLE=UNKNOWN IS GITHUB RECOMPUTE LAG, AND --admin MAY LEGITIMATELY BYPASS IT once CI is 0-fail/0-pending. I had been sleep-and-retry looping on that state (three attempts per PR at times). The skill names it as a sanctioned --admin case — distinct from the absolute ban on --admin past a FAILING TOUCHED-SURFACE gate, which stands.

3. THE MERGE CHECKLIST HAS A STEP I WAS SKIPPING: confirm "a `## Quality gates` section is present" in the PR body BEFORE merging, alongside CI-green, diff-matches-bead, and scope-did-not-sprawl. I required workers to WRITE that section but never verified it at merge time. Check it.

4. THE SKILL ITSELF IS STALE IN ONE PLACE: it ends the post-merge sequence with "then update ai/dashboard.md". Mike RETIRED the dashboard on 2026-06-20 and it must not be maintained. The rest of the skill is current and correct.

THE META-LESSON, now four rereads deep: the method says to codify loop bodies as commands so each is "one source of truth, rather than re-pasted prose", and .claude/commands/mayor-*.md exists precisely for that. I kept re-deriving each tick from the cron text and drifted from the written procedure in ways I could not see from inside. READ THE COMMAND FILE, not just the method README — the README carries philosophy, the command file carries the actual steps.

MAYOR MUST NOT CODE (the-mayor-method): the mayor does not edit files — not even one-line CI fixes or mechanical doc-flips. A failing PR check goes to a Shape-5 fix-worker on the EXISTING branch (run the actual failing gate, push to that branch). A graduation/status-sync/anchor-fix goes to a worker bead. Doing it inline feels fast but burns the mayor context window the method exists to protect. Mayor work = merge green PRs, dispatch to ceiling, surface hard calls, record rulings in beads, checkpoint bead state. Drift caught 2026-06-12 (Mike pointed at /docs/the-mayor-method after #4000/#4004 inline CI-fixes + EP-0015 inline graduation edits).

THE MAYOR MUST RE-READ A BEAD'S NEWEST NOTES AT DISPATCH TIME, not brief from an earlier reading of it. Three briefs in one session (2026-08-07/08) shipped stale or incomplete because I did not.

THE THREE, all caught by workers reading the bead:
- rf2-0fixc: I stated the witness suite had 37 top-level cases, derived from a cheap `grep -c "^test("`. It had 42. The worker established the real number itself, as briefed, so it cost nothing — but the figure was mine and it was wrong.
- rf2-2rtt6.138: I passed down "B <= 26 pessimistic" from another worker's report. The exact integer bound is 25 (300,000/(7*1,655) = 25.9). Arithmetic I repeated rather than checked.
- rf2-2rtt6.142: the bead carried an explicit PRIORITY NOTE — "sequence this AFTER rf2-2rtt6.139 and .140 are ruled on, or it will be re-done" — added after my earlier read. My brief did not mention it. The worker found it, proceeded anyway with a sound argument, and flagged it for adjudication rather than silently obeying or silently ignoring.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS ONE HABIT: reading a bead once, then briefing from that memory hours and several notes later. Beads accrete corrections BELOW the description, so the newest note is the most likely to change the work and the most likely to be missed.

THE METHOD ALREADY COVERS THE WORKER SIDE. dispatch-prompt-template.md makes "READ THE BEAD BOTTOM-UP; the bead governs over the brief" mandatory in the common preamble, precisely so a stale brief is caught on arrival. That safety net worked all three times. But it is a NET, not a floor — it should not be load-bearing this often, and each catch costs a worker context it should have spent on the work.

THE FIX, mayor-side: immediately before writing a dispatch, run `bd show <id>` and read its LAST note, even when you read the bead earlier the same session. Cheap. If the bead has a sequencing, priority or scope note, quote it into the brief verbatim rather than summarising — a paraphrase is what drops it.

MAYOR OPS: timeout-guard every test-heavy worker dispatch. A worker can ship a NON-TERMINATING fix (rf2-um6d9: a stranded flows fix had (recur (inc i)) lexically inside the inner loop [j ...], rebinding j not i → infinite oscillation) that makes the JVM/CLJS test suite never complete and silently burns the box (~9 cores, 5+ CPU-hours), masquerading as 'slow CI' for an entire session. DETECTION: a hung-but-IN_PROGRESS worker = check the worktree (uncommitted work + 0 commits + no PR across many ticks) AND per-process CPU: CPU-seconds >> wall-minutes (CPU-HOURS in wall-MINUTES, cores pegged) = runaway, not slow. RECOVERY: TaskStop the agent (kills its child JVM), verify children died (an orphaned node-test process may survive → Stop-Process it), then re-dispatch a FRESH worker that (a) distrusts the stranded fix, (b) hard-caps EVERY test run with 'timeout 180 clojure -M:test' / 'timeout 540 npm run test:cljs' so a runaway is caught in <3min not 5 CPU-hours, (c) is authorized to return a root-cause writeup instead of forcing a fix. Make timeout-guards STANDARD in test-heavy dispatch briefs.

MAYOR RULING — do NOT add the :class/:style refusal to the donor implementation/ui/ custom-element (2026-07-25). The rf2-oazgv worker asked whether parity there was wanted. No.

The donor is scheduled for deletion at the EP-0036 F6e gate (rf2-drpa3.57), and rf2-a32r7 already disarmed its publication so no consumer can ever depend on it. Adding a grammar refusal to code that is (a) unpublishable and (b) slated for removal is work whose entire value expires at deletion. The pre-alpha no-gold-plating posture rules it out, and the ruling that produced the refusal (rf2-5gliq's v1 roster) scopes to the FREEHAND surface by construction.

GENERALISE THIS: when a fix lands on Freehand and a worker asks whether the donor needs parity, the default answer is NO unless the donor behaviour is reachable by a consumer or by a gate that will outlive F6e. Ask which of those two applies before saying yes.

ALSO WORTH KEEPING from that slice — the SECOND-DOOR pattern, now seen twice on the same surface within hours. A declaration is read by more than one mechanism, and the mechanisms can disagree:
  * #6955: build/element-properties keyed its fallback on whether a prepare manifest EXISTS while the analyzer keyed its harvest on whether a compiler env is BOUND, so every shadow-cljs build baked the ATTRIBUTE lowering for a compiled view above its declaration — renderable, silent, wrong.
  * #6964: compiler/harvest.clj's valid-properties? would have seeded the exact classification the macro was about to reject, so a compiled view above the declaration would bake the property lowering.
The repair pattern that works in both cases is to put the shared fact in the ONE namespace both readers already require (here build.cljc's refused-property-names), so the doors cannot drift. When touching custom-element or property classification, ask 'what else reads this declaration?' before assuming one edit is sufficient.

MAYOR RULING — DO NOT BEAD THE UNMEASURED get-in REMAINDER (2026-07-25), endorsing a worker's recommendation against creating work.

After fixing rf2-sj5s7 (the measured 11%-of-allocation hot site), the worker surveyed and found ~32 literal-path get-in sites remaining across implementation/core/src — 15 of them in trace/**, which is fenced, dev-only and DCE'd under :advanced, so the least worth touching; the rest scattered across derivation/graph, substrate/adapter, router_transducer, conformance, classification, std_interceptors, observability, image_assembly, error_emit and derivation/egress.

IT RECOMMENDED I NOT FILE THAT AS A BEAD, and I agree. Its reasoning, which I am adopting verbatim as the rule: 'the audit named only MEASURED hot sites; sweeping the unmeasured remainder is the kind of unevidenced micro-optimisation this project rejects at triage.' A bead reading 'replace 32 get-in calls' would look like tidy progress and would be 32 opportunities to change behaviour for no measured gain — the 3-arity default alone has a branch where get-in and get-then-keyword differ if the stored value is false or nil.

THE STANDARD THIS SETS: a perf change needs a MEASUREMENT ON A HOT PATH, not a pattern match. rf2-sj5s7 qualified because a JFR profile put it at 2.784 GB of 24.63 GB sampled weight and frame.cljc's own docstring already prescribed the fix. Neither is true of the remainder. File a bead only if a profile puts a specific one of those sites on a hot path.

WORTH KEEPING from the same report — how to measure perf on THIS box: wall-clock micro-benchmarks swing up to 2x between JVMs under concurrent worker load (the same primitive measured 10.4 ns in one JVM and 21.7 ns in another), so ALLOCATION accounting via getThreadAllocatedBytes is the reliable metric, not timing. The method that produced a clean before/after: interleaved fresh JVMs (before, after, before, after…), warm-up then System/gc immediately before each timed window, three timed reps best-of, three JVM pairs, with the 'before' variant extracted from git rather than stashed. Its defensible headline was allocation — dispatch-sync over 200k events went 78,569 -> 61,193 bytes/event, −22.1%, where within-configuration spread was 0.35%/1.8% against a 28% gap. It explicitly refused to state the wall-clock improvement as a number, calling it a direction only, because n=3 on a loaded box is not a basis for a percentage. That refusal is the model.

ALSO: my stated test:cljs baseline was STALE (I said ~11423/57166; actual 11438/57234). It re-derived by reverting the three files IN THE SAME WORKTREE and re-running — same classpath, same machine, same node_modules — rather than trusting my number. Always re-derive a baseline in the worktree that will report it.

MY RULINGS AS MAYOR WERE LANDING ON BEADS ONLY, NOT IN PR BODIES. Caught 2026-07-24 on a full reread of the method bootstrap.

THE METHOD SAYS, and I had been half-following it: "Decisions go in BOTH the tracker AND the merging PR body — the PR body is the durable git-history record."

WHAT I CHECKED, rather than assuming: workers are mostly doing their half well. PR #6783 carries its D014 clause-8 divergence, #6770 carries the SSR :platforms behaviour change. But the rulings I make AS MAYOR — the projection-roster decision, the delete-vs-port recommendation, the sequencing calls — were going into bead notes and chat and nowhere else.

⚠️ WHY THIS MATTERS AND IS NOT BOOKKEEPING: the tracker is a separate database. A clean clone carries the GIT HISTORY, not the bead notes. Someone doing archaeology in six months on "why was this emitter deleted" or "why is the projection roster closed" will have `git log` and PR bodies. If the reasoning lives only in a bead, the answer is invisible exactly when it is most needed — and the next person re-litigates a decision that was already made carefully.

THE FIX, now standard: when I rule on a bead, the DISPATCHING BRIEF must require the worker to reproduce the ruling and its reasoning in the merging PR body. Not a link to the bead — the actual reasoning, because a link into a private tracker is not durable either. I have added that requirement to the two beads carrying live rulings.

RELATED GAP, same reread, smaller: the method dispatch discipline lists an explicit "do not merge PRs" instruction for workers, which I have not been including. No worker has merged anything, so it has cost nothing — but it is one line and the failure it prevents is severe.

STILL OUTSTANDING AFTER TWO REREADS: the repo has mayor-* skills (mayor-merge, mayor-dispatch, mayor-hygiene, mayor-cluster, mayor-posture) that codify these loop bodies, and the method says to use them as "one source of truth, rather than re-pasted prose". I keep re-deriving each tick from the cron text instead. That is exactly the duplication that produced the brief drift I found on the previous reread.

MAYOR SELF-AUDIT 2026-07-26 (mayor-method reread): I dispatched three workers and OMITTED THE PROJECT STANCE from all three preambles. dispatch-prompt-template.md Common preamble requires it in EVERY dispatch, and mayor-posture.md names "stance absent from preambles" as one of four drift signals to flag. Caught only by rereading the template, not by anything in the briefs themselves -- there is no gate on brief quality, which is why the reread cadence exists. WHY IT MATTERED RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC: all three beads offered a build-it-vs-declare-it fork (implement cross-generation teardown vs declare schema-4 reload-only; fix the commit boundary vs document an adapter restriction; migrate vs shim). The pre-alpha no-gold-plating stance is EXACTLY what decides those, so its absence left the highest-leverage instruction out of the highest-leverage sentence. Repaired by SendMessage addendum to each live worker; the tool response "Message queued for delivery" also confirmed all three alive. STANDING FIX: the stance is not decoration at the top of a brief -- when a bead has a smaller-answer-is-legitimate fork, state the stance AND apply it to that specific fork in one sentence, as the addendum did. A generic stance paragraph a worker skims is worth much less than "under this stance, the smaller honest answer wins HERE, and here is what would count as avoidance rather than restraint."

MEASURED 2026-07-26: gh pr merge --delete-branch IS A NO-OP ON THIS REPO AND SILENTLY ORPHANS THE REMOTE BRANCH. Every worker branch is checked out in a worktree, so the LOCAL delete fails ("cannot delete branch X used by worktree at ...") and gh ABORTS THE SEQUENCE BEFORE deleting the remote. Verified directly: after merging PRs 7091 and 7092 with --delete-branch, git ls-remote --heads origin still returned both refs. Result: 20 origin/worker/* branches accumulated this session. NOTE the check that does NOT work: git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> origin/main returns false for ALL of them because the repo rebase-merges, so the commits are rewritten -- that measurement says nothing about whether a branch merged. Use gh pr view state instead. THE FIX, which is what docs/the-mayor-method/README.md already prescribes: drop --delete-branch from the merge call entirely, then delete the remote branch separately AFTER verifying state==MERGED, and leave LOCAL branch + worktree cleanup to the hygiene loop, which already gates on worker liveness. Do not delete a remote branch whose worker is still live -- a live worker may push a follow-up commit or a second PR from the same branch, which happens routinely now that briefs tell workers to open a PR at the first commit. Keep --rebase, not the README generic --squash: this repo history is rebase-merged and preserves individual worker commits.

CLAUSE 4 OF THE MERGE CRITERION MUST BE QUERIED PER-BRANCH. A GLOBAL 'gh run list --limit N' TRUNCATES AND REPORTS 'NO LIVE RUNS' FOR A BRANCH THAT HAS FOUR (observed 2026-08-07, PR #7626).

WHAT HAPPENED: I evaluated 'are there queued/in-progress runs on this PR's branch' with a single 'gh run list --limit 40' grouped by headBranch. worker/shellbytes-2rtt6-82 did not appear, so I reported it had no live runs. Querying it directly — 'gh run list --branch worker/shellbytes-2rtt6-82' — showed FOUR runs queued on the PR's head sha (tests, portability, docs, lint). They fell outside the 40-item window because other branches' runs filled it.

WHY THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT AGAIN: clause 4 exists because statusCheckRollup can report pending==0 while runs are queued. I added a second source of truth and then read it through a truncating window, so the second source acquired the same failure mode as the first — it reported the absence of evidence as evidence of absence. Five variants of one bug in a single session: empty rollup passes '0 fail and 0 pending'; status==COMPLETED counts CANCELLED as passed; pending==0 while runs are queued; a rollup total that shrinks after a re-run still looks plausible; and now a truncated run list that omits a branch entirely.

THE RULE: for a MERGE DECISION, query the head branch DIRECTLY — 'gh run list --branch <headRefName> --limit 25' — and confirm no run is queued or in_progress, AND that the runs present are on the PR's current head sha (compare against 'gh pr view --json headRefOid'; stale-sha runs are not evidence about this head). Never use a global limited listing to decide a merge. A grouped overview is fine for a dashboard; it is not fine for a gate.

COROLLARY worth remembering: a rollup can show ONE check while four workflows sit queued on the same sha, because a queued run's checks are not yet attached to the commit. total==1 with 'no live runs' is therefore not 'this PR has one check' — it is 'look again, properly'.

MERGE-LOOP BUG (2026-07-18): my merge-loop's if-gate checks PRE-merge CI state but does NOT verify gh pr merge SUCCEEDED before running bd close + git branch -D + git push origin --delete. When a PR is 'not mergeable' (behind main / needs rebase), gh pr merge --admin FAILS but the loop still deleted the branch → PR AUTO-CLOSED + work stranded + bead wrongly closed (hit on zef0e #6214). Recovery: git branch <name> <tip-SHA from the 'Deleted branch (was SHA)' line>; git push origin <name>; gh pr reopen; bd update --status open. FIX: gate branch-delete on verifying gh pr view <pr> state==MERGED AFTER the merge call, never on the pre-merge check alone.

MERGE-LOOP CAVEAT (mayor, 2026-07-25): a merged PR does NOT necessarily close every bead named in its TITLE. Because briefs now tell workers to open the PR as soon as any commit exists (so work becomes visible and durable rather than waiting on a long local gate), a PR can be deliberately PARTIAL when the mayor sweeps it — title lists three beads, diff contains one file. Observed live: PR #6940 was titled for rf2-na9p0 + rf2-x4jda + rf2-rhg4q and contained ONLY spec/API.md; the two B5 beads were still uncommitted in the worker's tree at merge time. This is not a worker error and the early-PR instruction is still right — incremental delivery is fine and the merge was correct. The fix is on the MAYOR side: before closing beads after a merge, read the PR's actual FILE LIST (gh pr view <n> --json files) rather than trusting its title, close only the beads the diff really delivered, and tell the worker its branch is now partly merged so it rebases and opens a second PR for the remainder rather than assuming its work is lost.

MERGE LOOP — derive the bead from the BRANCH NAME, never from a guessed PR number. On 2026-07-19 I hardcoded a PR-number case statement (6373 -> rf2-2hkfy) by assuming PRs open in the order I dispatch. They do not: #6373 was worker/guide-register-bbdbs2 and rf2-2hkfy had not opened a PR at all. Merging would have closed the WRONG bead with a "shipped #6373" reason, corrupting state for two beads at once and being nearly invisible afterwards. FIX: read `gh pr list --state open --json number,headRefName` and map branch -> bead, since every worker branch is named worker/<desc>-<BEAD_ID>. The bead id is the branch suffix. Verify before every merge batch, not once per session — PRs open and close continuously while multiple workers run. GENERAL FORM: this is the same class as the stale ready-pool that made me dispatch a closed bead (rf2-lvrkp) — a cached mapping that was true when I built it and silently went stale. Any lookup table I construct from a moment in time needs re-derivation each tick, not reuse.

MERGE-LOOP HAZARD — I remove a worker worktree the instant its PR merges, but the WORKER MAY STILL BE RUNNING. On 2026-07-19 rf2-k8l1m reported: "The PR was merged by you, not me... The worktree and branch were cleaned up underneath me mid-command." It had finished writing and was only verifying CI, so nothing was lost — but a worker that is still editing, or about to amend and force-push, would lose work or fail confusingly. The window is real because workers commonly push, then poll CI, then write their final report; my loop sees pend=0/nf=0 and merges + removes during that poll. MITIGATIONS, in order of preference: (1) merge the PR but DEFER worktree/branch removal to the next tick — by then the worker has almost always reported; (2) if removing immediately, check the worktree is clean AND that no live agent is associated with it; (3) never remove a worktree whose branch has an OPEN PR (already the rule) or that holds gitignored-but-unique content (see retro-extended-context, 17KB invisible to git status). NOTE the merge itself was correct — CI was genuinely green; the defect is only in the eager cleanup. Also: my gh merges appear authored as mike-thompson-day8 because I use his gh auth, so a worker seeing "merged by Mike" may actually be seeing the mayor.

MERGE-LOOP JSONL CHECKOUT SILENTLY REVERTS WORKER BEAD CLOSES (observed 2026-07-25, re-confirmed). The mayor merge loop does 'git checkout HEAD -- .beads' before 'git pull --ff-only' (needed: an uncommitted issues.jsonl aborts the pull and silently freezes HEAD). But that checkout DISCARDS the bd auto-export of any close a worker performed since the last commit — and a later 'bd import' of the reverted file resurrects the bead as open/in_progress. Observed: rf2-kqxe6.17 and rf2-b617w both closed by their worker on PR #6895, both back to in_progress after the post-merge checkout; misdiagnosable as a reviewer reopen. MITIGATION: after every merge+pull, re-verify the merged PR's beads with 'bd show' and re-close any that reverted, citing the merge commit. Better: commit the .beads export BEFORE merging rather than checking it out — commit-before-pull, never checkout-before-pull, when a worker has just closed something. DISTINGUISH FROM A REAL REVIEWER REOPEN: a genuine reopen carries a MERGED-PR AUDIT / AUDIT-REOPEN note naming an unmet defect at a code site; a checkout-race revert has NO such note and the bead simply reads in_progress with its pre-close state.

MERGE-LOOP: NEVER "git checkout HEAD -- .beads" — IT HAS NOW DESTROYED NINE BEAD CLOSES (2026-07-25). The mayor merge routine says: after each merge, "git checkout HEAD -- .beads" then "git pull --ff-only". That checkout DISCARDS the bd auto-export of every close performed since the last commit, and bd tracked post-checkout/post-merge hooks then RE-IMPORT the stale file into the Dolt DB, so the close is undone in the database itself, not merely in the working file. CONFIRMED VICTIMS this session: rf2-a32r7 (three times), rf2-kqxe6.17, rf2-drpa3.178, rf2-8ewl1, rf2-zt65l, rf2-vxgfnd.99.4, rf2-qwsmv. Each showed ZERO AUDIT-REOPEN notes, which is the discriminator: a genuine reviewer reopen always carries a MERGED-PR AUDIT / AUDIT-REOPEN note naming an unmet defect at a code site. CORRECT MERGE SEQUENCE — export, commit, THEN pull; never checkout: (1) bd export --all -o .beads/issues.jsonl  (2) guard wc -l >= 2000  (3) git add + git commit  (4) git pull --ff-only (or rebase)  (5) merge the next PR. The reason the checkout was in the routine at all is that an UNCOMMITTED issues.jsonl aborts a pull — committing it first solves that without destroying anything. WHY THIS KEPT RECURRING: I fixed the CHECKPOINT flow early and left the MERGE flow alone, because the loop prompt literally instructs the checkout. Deviating from that literal instruction is correct — it demonstrably destroys tracker state — and the deviation must be applied in the merge path too, not only at checkpoint time. AFTER EVERY MERGE, re-verify the merged PR beads with bd show and re-close any that reverted, citing the merge commit.

MERGE-ORDER BEATS --admin ON THE BAKED LANE: when two PRs both rebuild docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js, a PUSH by one cannot invalidate the other — only a MERGE can. So the escape from the rebase-deadlock is to control MERGE ORDER (let A finish CI and merge, then merge B, which rebases once onto A), NOT to --admin past pending checks. I merged rf2-qg98y (#6302) past 4 pending checks on 2026-07-18 to break a 5-cycle deadlock; it worked and main stayed green, but sequencing would have achieved the same without the risk. Rule going forward: on the baked lane, hold every candidate, merge strictly one at a time on GENUINE green, and tell the next worker it is sole occupant so it rebases exactly once. Root fix is rf2-tzy13 (stop committing the bundle, build in CI).

MERGE-TIME RULE (post #6677 contamination): before merging ANY worker PR, eyeball its file list for .beads/ — a worker-worktree commit of .beads/issues.jsonl is a stale full-DB snapshot that time-travels the tracker (reopens closed beads, deletes new ones, replaces memories). Reject/strip it; never --theirs/--ours on .beads — resolve-then-regenerate. Standing until rf2-ia8o7's guards land.

A MERGED-PR AUDIT THAT REOPENS THE EXACT SOURCE OWNER APPENDS ITS FINDINGS AS A NOTE AND LEAVES THE TITLE AND DESCRIPTION INTACT. Never rewrite a bead's title/description into the follow-through defect. Evidence (rf2-twpp6, 2026-07-26): the EP-0037 R1 and R2 slice beads (rf2-kqxe6.5, rf2-kqxe6.6) each had title AND description destructively replaced by their own merged-PR audits (commits 1e2627315c and 7528f0b84b). 'bd search "EP-0037 R2"' then returned nothing, and review gate 2 could not check those two slices against the tree at all -- while rf2-kqxe6.3 (R0b) and rf2-kqxe6.7 (R3), which APPENDED, were checkable. The named casualty: the EP's R2 tooling clause ended up with no bead carrying it. Recovery is possible but expensive -- .beads/issues.jsonl is a full-database export, so the original text is readable with 'git show <sha>:.beads/issues.jsonl | jq "select(.id==\"<id>\")"' -- do not create the need for it. Related: 'bd update --notes' REPLACES; use --append-notes or 'bd note'.

MERGING ON GREEN CAN LAND A BRANCH STATE OLDER THAN ITS TIP (2026-07-25). Twice today a PR merged while its worker was still pushing, so the merge captured an EARLIER commit than the branch's tip: #6975 landed one commit short (the worker opened #6982 to carry the remainder), and #6973 landed the v/html code half while its worker was still writing the acceptance suites (which then landed as #6980).

MECHANISM: the merge sweep reads 'fail=0 pend=0' and merges. Between that read and the merge, a live worker can push. GitHub merges the ref as it stood, so the delta silently becomes a follow-up PR — or worse, is briefly absent from main while the bead reads closed.

NEITHER CASE LOST WORK, and the reason is worth keeping: both workers were pushing as they went and both noticed, so each opened a follow-up rather than assuming its work had landed. Push-as-you-go plus a worker that verifies its own merge is what made this benign.

WHAT IT IS NOT: a reason to stop merging on green. Waiting for workers to declare done would idle the pipeline, and a green partial genuinely is worth more than a perfect whole later — that policy is correct and stays.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD: (1) when merging a PR whose worker has NOT reported terminal, expect a follow-up PR and do not treat the bead as discharged on that merge alone — read the worker's eventual report; (2) tell workers in the brief that a merge may land a state older than their tip, so if their last push is not in the merge commit they should open a follow-up rather than assume it landed (both workers did this unprompted — make it explicit so it is not luck); (3) when a merged PR's beads stay open or in_progress, that is often this, not a partial delivery — ask before inferring.

RELATED, SAME ROOT: three times today I pruned a worktree from under a live worker because the merge sweep had 'PR merged' in hand while terminality lived in task notifications. The pattern across all four incidents is the same — the merge sweep is where mayor actions and live worker state collide, so every destructive or finalising step inside it needs a liveness signal read rather than inferred.

MERGING ON GREEN LANDED A STALE TIP AGAIN -- THIRD INSTANCE, AND I NOW HAVE A ONE-COMMAND MITIGATION (2026-07-26). PR #7091 merged at c67fe52a91 while the worker branch tip was aa824a27b5. Five of six commits rebase-landed; the sixth (the FH-CTRL-018 browser row) did not, leaving the slice INCOMPLETE ON MAIN while the PR read merged. Prior instances: #6975 landed one commit short, #6973 landed the v/html code half while its acceptance suites were still being written.

WHY IT KEEPS HAPPENING: the merge sweep reads fail=0 pend=0 and merges. Between that read and the merge call, a live worker can push. GitHub merges the ref as it stood. The policy of merging on green is CORRECT and stays -- waiting for workers to declare done would idle the pipeline, and a green partial is worth more than a perfect whole later.

THE MITIGATION, cheap enough that there is no excuse: before merging a PR whose worker has NOT sent a terminal report, compare the PR head against the remote branch tip --
  gh pr view <n> --json headRefOid   vs   git ls-remote --heads origin <branch>
If they differ, the PR object is stale: re-read it and merge the current head. This is the same identity-not-name discipline that governs worktree pruning -- read the tip, do not assume the PR object is current.

WHAT MADE ALL THREE BENIGN, and it is the thing to keep briefing: every worker was pushing as it went AND checked whether its own work was in the merge commit. Each opened a follow-up PR rather than assuming it had landed. So the brief line "a merge may land a state older than your tip; if your last push is not in the merge commit, open a follow-up rather than assume it landed" is doing real work -- keep it, and note that all three workers did it UNPROMPTED before it was in the brief.

MAYOR-SIDE COROLLARY: when a merged PR beads stay open or in_progress, suspect THIS before inferring a partial delivery or a worker error. And do not close a bead on a merge whose worker has not reported -- read the file list, not the title.

MOVING A TREE ASIDE WITHIN THE SEARCH SPACE DOES NOT REMOVE IT — a second probe-method defect, caught by the worker before its verdict was trusted (2026-07-26).

THIS IS THE SECOND PROBE DEFECT OF THE SAME FAMILY IN ONE DAY, and the first was mine: I told a worker to simulate a deletion by moving implementation/ui/ aside, and check_donor_inventory.py held rc=0 throughout because IT READS GIT, NOT THE FILESYSTEM — the 73 stale rows only appeared once the deletion was STAGED IN THE INDEX.

SO THE RULE HAS TWO HALVES, AND BOTH ARE ABOUT MATCHING THE PROBE TO THE SEARCH:
  1. MATCH THE MEDIUM. Filesystem gate -> move the files. Git-reading gate -> stage the deletion. Marker-discovering gate -> the marker must leave the search space.
  2. MOVE IT OUT, NOT SIDEWAYS. A destination inside the tree the gate scans is not a deletion. Park probes OUTSIDE the repo, or strip the discovery marker, and VERIFY THE GATE CAN NO LONGER SEE IT before trusting any verdict.
