THE THREE-POINT CONTROL'S REFUSAL IS A DENOMINATOR-CLASS FAULT, NOT A ROW-CLASS ONE — diagnosed 2026-08-07 from 42 refused runs across two ensembles (rf2-8a746).

TWO INDEPENDENTLY FATAL HALVES.
(1) THE PREDICTION IS WRONG. 2.0101x is the statistic's expectation only if T is AFFINE in the dirty set over [1,200]. On the published TaskDuration clock it is not: marginal cost is 12.6 us/cell over [1,100] and 6.8 over [100,200]. True centre is 1.55x, which sits 2.6% above the band's own rejection edge of 1.5076 — so half of every run's blocks fall out the bottom ON A PERFECTLY QUIET BOX.
(2) THE STATISTIC IS ILL-CONDITIONED. Differencing away the constant also throws away the PEDESTAL that made relative noise look small, leaving a denominator of 1.25 ms carrying 0.60 ms of dispersion — 2.09 sigma from zero. Even with the centre corrected only ~60% of blocks land in band, and a strict every-one-of-18 rule turns that into P(pass) ~ 1e-4.

THE DECISIVE CONTROL EXPERIMENT: ctl3Layout — the SAME statistic on LayoutDuration over the IDENTICAL blocks and samples — reads 1.9681 / 1.9801 with marginals affine to 5% and no sign-gate firing in 756 blocks. So the arithmetic, door, tare and aggregation are all sound; the PAGE is not affine on the counter the row is published on. The non-layout half carries it: 7.13 -> 1.83 us/cell, a 3.9x collapse.

WHY ctl-2x SURVIVES AND ctl3 DOES NOT — this is the transferable lesson: ctl-2x's denominator is a LEVEL (the floor's whole tared reading, ~4.5 ms) carrying the same ~0.4 ms of estimator error, so 9% relative against ctl3's 48%; and its centre sits 20% above the edge against ctl3's 4%. Distance-above-edge and per-block scatter, raised to the strict-rule exponent, reproduce every pass rate in the programme. A DIFFERENCE-OF-DIFFERENCES DENOMINATOR IS THE FAULT. The invariance argument ('an additive constant cancels in each difference') is true of the LEVEL and is not the problem; what destroys it is the error in each arm's ESTIMATE of that level, which is independent between arms and ADDS. Measured corr(T(1),T(100)) = 0.43, so differencing removes only 40% of the denominator's variance where the argument assumes nearly all.

THE DEGENERATES ARE THE SAME FAULT, NOT A SECOND ONE: den=+0.019 ms -> 86x, den=+0.026 ms -> 114x, and in 9 of the 10 worst blocks T(1) is elevated — it enters BOTH differences, so it drives the smaller one to zero first.

RE-SITING THE POINTS DOES NOT RESCUE IT. Re-adjudicating the same committed blocks at 100/200/300 (above the knee) gives 1.9975 / 2.0777 against a prediction of 2.0000 — the affine premise holds there — but den halves to 0.70 ms while its IQR does not, and in-band blocks FALL from 47% to 33%. Span the knee and the centre is wrong; avoid it and the denominator is gone.

THE ONLY CONSTRUCTION THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS has a denominator that is a LEVEL rather than a difference. That is a decision about what the lane measures and belongs to the operator.

THE HARNESS DOES NOT SIGNAL A CAPPED TOOL CALL — IT BACKGROUNDS IT, AND THE GATE KEEPS RUNNING (measured 2026-08-07 on rf2-ketqy, PR #7642). CORRECTED: an earlier version of this memory said the harness kills the parent and orphans the child. That model was wrong and the fix built on it would not have worked.

MEASURED, not inferred. Capped at 90s, a backgrounded 'sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh' kept running after the tool returned — its log grew 41822 to 49220 bytes and two more stages completed. TaskStop behaves identically: reports success, kills nothing, fires no trap. So there is no signal, and a signal handler alone can never see this case.

TWO FURTHER MEASUREMENTS THAT KILL THE OBVIOUS FIXES:
- 'kill the child PROCESS GROUP' would kill the CALLER. Every child shares the caller's PGID under Git Bash.
- bash DEFERS a trapped signal until the foreground child returns — measured at 22 seconds (SIGTERM at t+3s to a script running 'sleep 25'; handler ran at t+25s). So even when a signal IS delivered, a trap is late.
- 'taskkill /F /T' is silently mangled by Git Bash into 'taskkill F:/ ...'. Behind the customary '|| true' it is a NO-OP that looks like it worked. Needs MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 and MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'; Cygwin ignores both.

THE DAMAGE the orphan does: it keeps writing to the SAME log as the relaunch (two writers, NUL-riddled output), and its 'npm run test:cljs' unlinks out/node-test.js underneath the next run's per-namespace isolation sweep, which then reds with 'the bundle changed on disk during the sweep' and MODULE_NOT_FOUND. That red is the sweep working correctly and is indistinguishable from an isolation regression in the worker's own diff. The culprit java.exe is invisible to 'ps -ef' entirely.

THE SHIPPED REMEDY (PR #7642): a trap for the genuinely-signalled cases PLUS the same reap invoked at the START of the next run — the only moment it can act, because the path that actually bites delivers no signal. Not a lock: the second run never waits or refuses.

DISCRIMINATORS, unchanged and still the useful part: LAUNCH failure ('Command failed:') = spawn contention. 'changed on disk during the sweep' = a live orphan; kill it and re-run quiet. ASSERTION mismatch = real.

GATE LOGS MUST NOT GO TO /tmp UNDER MULTI-AGENT LOAD — /tmp is SHARED across concurrently running worker agents on this box, so one worker gate log silently OVERWRITES another. Found 2026-07-24 by the rf2-drpa3.112 SSR worker, which nearly shipped a false green.

THE MECHANISM: worker A runs "npm run test:browser > /tmp/gate-browser.log 2>&1". Worker B, running concurrently in a DIFFERENT worktree, writes the same path. A then reads a log that is really B run. In the observed case the log EXIT=0 and reported "0 failures" — every number looked right. The ONLY tell was the shadow-cljs banner naming the WRONG worktree (pilot-react-interop-46 instead of the reader own).

WHY THIS IS NASTY: it defeats the standard exit-code discipline. The capture-to-a-file-and-echo-the-exit-code rule was adopted precisely because piping into tail/grep discards the runner exit status. But if the FILE ITSELF belongs to another agent, the captured exit code is ALSO another agent — a correct technique reading the wrong evidence. Both the summary AND the exit code agree, and both are about someone else run.

THE FIX, now standard in every dispatch brief: write gate logs to the SESSION SCRATCHPAD or a worktree-local path, never a bare /tmp name. e.g.
  <gate> > "$WT/gate-<name>.log" 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?"; tail -30 "$WT/gate-<name>.log"
And VERIFY OWNERSHIP: the shadow-cljs "config:" banner line names the worktree whose build ran. Grep it and confirm it is YOURS before believing any number in that file. That is the cheap proof.

MAYOR NOTE: my own standing gate-discipline boilerplate said "> /tmp/gate.log". That instruction is now known-unsafe whenever more than one worker runs at a time, which is the normal case at saturation. Update the boilerplate; do not keep handing workers a colliding path.

GENERAL FORM: this joins the roster of ways green has meant nothing-was-measured here. The others are about a check that could not fail; this one is about a check that MEASURED SOMEBODY ELSE. When an assertion rests on an artefact OUTSIDE your process (a shared temp file, a shared port, a shared cache), ask WHO ELSE CAN WRITE IT before trusting what you read.

Topology / machines-viz VISUAL layout changes CANNOT be gated by CLJS unit tests alone. PR #3453 (post-ELK adaptive aspect + back-edge reroute) passed 454/454 machines-viz unit tests + xray-feature-gate 16/16 but regressed the rendered topology significantly (reverted in #3455). Root: :direction :auto default ran the new aspect-heuristic+transpose on ALL machines; unit tests assert projection data, not the rendered visual result. LESSON: any topology layout change must (a) default to known-good (opt-in for new layout behaviour, never :auto-default that re-lays-out every existing machine) AND (b) get visual verification before merge — regenerate the ai/topology/xray-pngs/ snapshots + eyeball, since the gates are blind to visual regressions.

THE TRACKER SILENTLY REVERTS CLOSURES TO OPEN, REPEATEDLY, AND ONLY A PER-TICK AUDIT CATCHES IT (observed twice on 2026-08-07: 2 beads, then 5).

WHAT HAPPENS. Beads closed with a verified reason read OPEN again a few ticks later, with no action of mine in between. First occurrence reverted rf2-2rtt6.56 and rf2-2rtt6.62. Second reverted rf2-kqac1, rf2-drpa3.182.12, rf2-2rtt6.103, rf2-ketqy and rf2-cvvb7 — every one of which had a PR I could verify MERGED at the moment of re-closing.

WHY VERIFYING AT CLOSE TIME IS NOT ENOUGH. I verified each of these CLOSED immediately after closing. They reverted anyway. So the audit has to run EVERY tick against the full list of everything closed this session, not just the recent ones — the second wave included beads closed many ticks earlier.

HOW TO AUDIT SO THE AUDIT ITSELF DOES NOT LIE: key on the STABLE BEAD ID, never an internal row UUID (a re-import regenerates UUIDs and a UUID-keyed diff reports phantom losses), and read the STATUS FIELD rather than grepping the whole record (the word 'open' appears inside titles). 'bd show <id> | head -1 | grep -oE CLOSED|OPEN|DEFERRED' is enough.

WHAT MAKES RE-CLOSING CHEAP: the close REASON is the durable artefact. If it names the PR number and the concrete evidence, re-closing is a thirty-second job of verifying 'gh pr view <n> --json state' still reads MERGED and pasting the reason back. If the original close said only 'done', a revert costs a full re-investigation. Write close reasons for the revert you have not had yet.

THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT CLASS THE PROJECT KEEPS FINDING IN ITS OWN INSTRUMENTS: a state that reports success while the underlying fact has moved. Treat the tracker as untrusted for closure state, exactly as you treat a statusCheckRollup.

TRUE-CONCLUSION-DEAD-REASONING — a documented defect class, seen twice on 2026-07-19 and subtler than plain drift.

DEFINITION: a document states a correct conclusion resting on an inference that has since been invalidated. Nothing looks wrong — the conclusion checks out — so a reviewer confirms the conclusion and moves on. But the NEXT reader follows the stated reason, finds it false, and "corrects" the conclusion in the wrong direction. The rot is in the justification, not the claim.

INSTANCE 1 (rf2-0qsp5, #6386): spec/005-StateMachines.md derived :rf.machine/join-dispatch target protection FROM its REJECT-tier membership. Worker verdict: "The conclusion is true; the inference is precisely what the split invalidated." Preserving the reasoning would have re-merged the two fx policies the next time anyone extended it.

INSTANCE 2 (rf2-vxgfnd.188, #6391, worse): the canonical W1 rule table declared SEVEN verbs unavailable — ui/adapter, local, effect, ui/event, ui/handler, ui/render-fn, ui/dispatch-fn. ALL SEVEN SHIP, exported from ui.cljc. MIG-16/17/18 "this gates" conclusions stayed TRUE, but the reason inverted: from "the verb has not shipped yet" to "the decision belongs to the human". Retiering alone would have let the next reader check whether S3 shipped, find it had, and UNGATE RULES THAT MUST STAY GATED. The worker rewrote the reasons and left the tiers.

HOW TO CATCH IT: when reconciling a document against code, verify the DERIVATION, not just the conclusion. Ask "if the stated reason were false, would the conclusion change?" If yes and the reason IS false, the conclusion is correct by luck and the next edit will break it.
HOW TO FIX IT: rewrite the reason, keep the conclusion. Do NOT retier/restate/delete the conclusion just because its stated basis collapsed.

RELATED, SAME FAMILY: a bead PREDICTION can be wrong too. rf2-vxgfnd.188 own preliminary map predicted six rule retirements; ALL SIX were refuted against shipped code (one, R-X7, had NO DETECTOR AT ALL and became a new rule; R-S3 was missing the cursor WRITE side). A worker trusting the bead analysis would have deleted six live rules. The bead is authoritative about WHAT TO DO, never about WHAT IS TRUE — always re-verify its factual claims against the code.

ALSO: my brief framed 36-vs-34 rules as "one book has two rules the other lacks". Wrong — the books cut the same work at different GRANULARITIES (one by construct area, one by detector), many-to-many both ways, so the deliverable was a crosswalk not a diff. When two artefacts disagree on a COUNT, check whether they share a unit before assuming they disagree on content.

TRUTHFUL-BUT-LATE vs FABRICATED — the discriminator for unfenced async writes. Established by the rf2-2amkm worker (#6410) when it RE-VERIFIED rather than inherited a judgement rf2-6pfpt (#6405) had left.

THE TEST: when a callback settles after its subject is gone, ask whether the value it writes is TRUE-BUT-STALE or FABRICATED-ABOUT-NOTHING.
  - TRUTHFUL-BUT-LATE: runner-events/run-step! emits an unfenced emit-trace! for an abandoned stepper session. The step REALLY RAN and REALLY produced that result; only the timing is wrong. #6410 checked every trace listener under tools/story/src and none consumes :rf.story.play/step. Verdict: LEAVE UNFENCED. Fencing it would mean inventing session identity for a public one-shot executor whose recorded verdict is already fenced caller-side.
  - FABRICATED: the a11y sites. (swap! run-state assoc frame-id :done) over a map the frame was dissoc-d from RESURRECTS the entry — measured 10/10 RED with 19 failures and ZERO ERRORS, so nothing throws. The phantom slot reads :done and the resurrected violations-by-frame entry beside it is exactly what browser/register-a11y-reader! serves to :rf.assert/a11y — A TORN-DOWN FRAME REPORTING A CLEAN VERDICT. Verdict: FENCE IT.
Same defect shape, opposite correct action. Do not blanket-fence every unfenced .then; ask what the write ASSERTS.

MECHANISM REFINEMENT worth copying: #6410 stamped the run token INTO the slot rather than beside it, so "existence and identity are one question with one answer, and every present and future clearing path revokes the claim with no side atom to keep in step". Strictly better than a parallel token map, which a new clearing path can silently fail to update.

⚠️ (inc nil) IS 1 ON CLJS. That is why this class never throws — it silently rebuilds state instead. Never test for it by expecting an exception; assert the slot is ABSENT and the status is the terminal value.

Naming a namespace re-frame.ssr.boundary and then exporting (def boundary ...) from the facade compiles to `re_frame.ssr.boundary = re_frame.ssr.boundary.boundary;` — THE ASSIGNMENT DESTROYS THE NAMESPACE OBJECT. (2) clojure.test HAS NO MAP FIXTURES — and the failure mode is a SILENT GREEN. A map is IFn, so `(use-fixtures :each {:before f :after g})` composes to a function that returns nil WITHOUT RUNNING THE TEST BODY. Output is "Ran 0 tests ... 0 failures", exit 0. The worker caught it ONLY because the suite count did not move off 456. RULE: use a plain fn fixture `(fn [t] (before) (t) (after))`. And this is the concrete reason every brief must demand a NON-ZERO, PLAUSIBLE test count rather than a green exit — "Ran 0 tests" is the single most common false green in this repo, and it has now appeared via (a) a bare `clojure -M:test -n <ns>` from implementation/, (b) a CLJS runner selecting no namespace after a rename, and (c) a map fixture swallowing the whole body.

DC-09 TWO-CLOCK ENVELOPE, MEASURED (rf2-drpa3.182.12, PR #7179, HeadlessChrome 147, dev build :optimizations :none goog.DEBUG true). Sustained semantic rate ~190/s at 0 dirty siblings, ~49/s at 200. 60 Hz crossing is comfortable to 50 siblings and breaks between 50 and 200; 120 Hz never clears p95 in a dev build; 240 Hz is unreachable because the BROWSER stops offering first, not because the framework refuses.

THREE STRUCTURAL FACTS worth reusing before re-measuring anything on this surface:
1. PEAK BACKLOG IS 1, at every offered rate and both sibling loads, with rf/dispatch (async). The setInterval callback IS the main thread, so overload manifests as OFFER LOSS at the host, never as a growing queue; latency stays bounded at one crossing and the settlement tail stayed <=5.4 ms even at 240 Hz requested against a 20 ms crossing. This is why no throttle/debounce/coalesce verb is warranted — the browser already back-pressures. CAVEAT: measured with a TIMER. Coalesced pointermove / pointerrawupdate bursts can deliver several events to one task and are the only shape that could exceed backlog 1; do not quote this for raw-pointer bursts without re-measuring.
2. THE EVENT HALF IS FLAT, THE COMMIT HALF SCALES. Splitting the window at the instant dispatch-sync returns: :event-ms (router, interceptors, reducer, app-db install, 300 subscription notifications) is 3-4 ms whether 1 or 201 cells moved; :commit-ms goes 0.4 -> 17.5 ms at ~0.085 ms per dirtied cell. An expensive crossing is expensive in React, not in re-frame — attribute before optimising.
3. WHERE YOU READ THE SUB COSTS MORE THAN HOW MUCH CHANGED. Reading a high-rate value in a view that ALSO builds a collection costs a CONSTANT 40-44 ms more than reading it one boundary down — independent of payload size (Vega 96 leaves 45.6->5.0 ms, Spread 900 leaves 63->18.8 ms) — while moving THREE FEWER DOM nodes. Same 'one leaf of app-db changed', 8-19x apart. Guidance: if a high-rate value must cross into app-db, read its subscription at the boundary that USES it.

EQUALITY IS FREE AND FREEHAND ALREADY ELIDES. Fresh-but-rf=-equal is indistinguishable from stable-reference (0.2-0.3 ms at 96 leaves, 0.4-0.6 at 900) and repaints nothing; a full structural walk of a 900-leaf map is under a millisecond. Behavior :update ran exactly 52 times for 52 changed crossings and ZERO times for stable or fresh-equal ones — elision is VALUE-based (rf=), not identity-based. Proved by counting, not by reading the runtime. No equality hook is warranted.

INSTRUMENT NOTES for the next perf bead in a browser:
* A COMPUTED-DURATION POSITIVE CONTROL DOUBLES AS A CONTENTION METER. A busy-wait of exactly 4.00 ms riding in every cell read p50 4.0 with overshoot never above 0.3 ms — which is what let the numbers be published without the usual 'other agents were running' caveat. On a loaded box it would have said so in every table simultaneously. Cheap, and it retires the standing wall-clock-is-unreliable worry per-run instead of per-repo.
* A COMPUTED-SIZE CONTROL CATCHES A KNOB THAT DOES NOT TURN. Predicted DOM mutation counts (host-only 1, fresh-equal 0, one-leaf k+1) matched measured at all 15 mode x rung combinations, and the driven arm independently reproduced exactly 201.0 per crossing. MutationObserver.takeRecords() answers SYNCHRONOUSLY, which is the only reason it can be read inside a flushSync-bracketed window.
* AN ARM WHOSE POINT IS THAT NOTHING CHANGES CANNOT BE VERIFIED BY NOTHING CHANGING. The fresh-equal arm is verified at the STORE (reference moved AND value equal), because an arm that silently did nothing would otherwise be the fastest arm in the table.
* ROTATING ARM ORDER FOUND A REAL FAULT: the first equality arm built its config from a FIXED generation, so a fresh-equal crossing following a one-leaf one was equal to nothing and failed its own read-back in 7 of every 10 samples. Build the comparison value from WHATEVER IS CURRENTLY IN THE STORE, and build it OUTSIDE the timed window.
* BOTH LADDER ORDERS: the only non-overlapping range tracked a monotonic round-1-to-4 warm-up present at EVERY rung in BOTH orders — drift, not order. Three warm-up samples per cell did not fully absorb first-round JIT.
* prov/result REFUSES a record with no revision, and the :browser-test lane has none. Do not route around it: catch the refusal and publish :d021 :not-release-evidence with the reason, so the same rows can run in the ordinary gate AND in the focused bench build with RF2_REVISION set.
* Chrome clamps performance.now() to 100 us. A sub-0.1 ms arm reads 0.0 and its honest report is 'under 0.1 ms', never 'free'.

STILL UNMEASURED: the PRODUCTION envelope (rf2-drpa3.182.15). Dev build means the Spec 009 seam, schema validation and trace emission are live on the measured path, so every cost is an upper bound. The b6-prod-app + b6_prod_run.cjs pattern is the one to copy; it needs a shadow-cljs.edn build target, which is hot zone.

TWO FREEHAND ADAPTER FACTS the rf2-vo8fb conformance found that reading could not (PR #6948, 2026-07-25):

1. A CLJS NAMESPACE AND A VAR CANNOT SHARE A JS PATH. The bead specified an internal ns 're-frame.freehand.adapter' alongside the published var 'v/adapter'. The compiler emits :ns-var-clash and ONE OF THE TWO SILENTLY READS nil — observed live: v/adapter installed fine while the test namespace's own reference read nil, so the fixture installed nothing and every assertion failed for the wrong reason. Homed at re-frame.freehand.substrate instead (the same split the donor arrived at). The ruled AUTHORING name is unaffected. Generalise: never name an internal namespace the same as a published var in its parent ns.

2. ADAPTER DISPOSAL MUST BE REFERENCE-RELEASE, NOT FRAME DESTROY, and the bug was CLASSPATH-DEPENDENT. Core's claim-installed-for-dispose! sets :disposing? and closes public delegation BEFORE calling the adapter's :dispose-adapter!, so every read-container inside that window raises :rf.error/adapter-disposed — and a frame's destroy recipe reads the runtime-db container. On a classpath WITHOUT the machines artefact that read IS the fallback path, so the defect was latent for some apps and fatal for others. Correct shape: drain-live-roots! releases claims + the frame REFERENCE + the ViewCells, while v/unmount! on a live adapter still destroys a root-owned frame; both share one tear-down-root! differing only in that function. The drain is the safety net for a FORGOTTEN root outliving the adapter, not a substitute for orderly teardown. Conformance carries two rows of different strength rather than one overclaiming row.

TWO GENERALISABLE FINDINGS FROM THE CI-COVERAGE WORK (2026-07-26, PR #7068).

1. WHEN AN INCLUSIVE PATH FILTER WOULD BE THE WHOLE REPOSITORY, DELETE THE FILTER — DO NOT EXTEND IT. rf2-kx06s asked to add two omitted files to a workflow push-path filter. The worker found the two-line fix "correct and incomplete": NEITHER checker in that job has a filterable read universe — one scans every spec/**/*.md, the other runs git ls-files over the WHOLE TREE. So any honest filter is the repository, and a filter that lists paths is a promise the job cannot keep. It deleted the push filter. The workflow OWN paragraph already said the job "belongs on an unfiltered job" while the trigger still carried one.

THE GENERAL RULE: before adding a path to a filter, ask WHAT THE JOB ACTUALLY READS. If the read universe is unbounded, the filter is not incomplete — it is WRONG IN KIND, and every future addition to it is a false sense of coverage. This is the same family as the roster-that-rots, one level up: a maintained LIST OF TRIGGERS rather than a maintained list of members.

2. A CROSS-TREE TEST-HELPER ALIAS MEANS AN EDGE THE BEAD WILL NOT NAME. (1) CDP `getHeapUsage` and `performance.memory` are TWO DOORS ONTO ONE V8 COUNTER — they agreed to the byte (3,868,954 both), which LOOKS like independent corroboration and is not. A heap SNAPSHOT is the genuinely independent third reading. (2) A 4.7 MB positive control built as `'x'.repeat(n)` read as SIX KILOBYTES on all three readers — V8 does not materialise it the way you expect, and it would have looked exactly like a broken instrument rather than a broken control.
