TWO MAYOR ERRORS THE rf2-n4by4 WORKER CAUGHT, BOTH ABOUT MY BRIEFS (2026-07-26).

ERROR 1 — I SILENTLY RESOLVED A RULING THE BEAD HAD EXPLICITLY RESERVED. rf2-n4by4 said in as many words: "ENFORCEMENT NEEDS A RULING — do not pick one silently", and listed (a) mark-and-refuse versus (b) leave it to the spec. My brief supplied (a) as though it were settled. The worker followed the brief and FLAGGED THE DIVERGENCE, noting that per my own standing instruction the bead is authoritative over the brief.

That is the sharpest form of a mistake I make often: I put "the bead is authoritative over this brief, and tell me if they disagree" into every dispatch, which is right — and then write briefs that quietly overwrite the bead. The instruction only works if I read the bead for RESERVED QUESTIONS before writing the brief, not just for facts. A bead that says "needs a ruling" is addressed TO ME, and the honest brief either states the ruling AS a ruling ("I am ruling (a), here is why") or asks the worker to return the options. Silently picking one means the tracker never records that a decision was made, and the next reader cannot tell a considered choice from an oversight.

THE RULING ITSELF STANDS, and the reason is worth keeping: the failure is SILENT — :className arriving as :class is a DIFFERENT React prop, so the component gets no class and nothing reports it. Guard warranted. And the cost turned out near zero: the author spelling rides in METADATA, refused at one seam, with =, hash and pr-str all ignoring it, so the legal element use pays nothing. But I could not have known the cost when I ruled, which is exactly why the ruling should have been visible.

ERROR 2 — MY COLLISION WARNING WAS A GREP, AND TWO OF FOUR HITS WERE FALSE POSITIVES. I warned that four test files contained both "spread" and "defhost" and might pin the accepting behaviour, so the flips had to ride in the same PR. NONE of the four pinned it. Two matched on "SPREADSHEET" and "SPREADJS". One already asserted the CORRECT behaviour (an earlier PR had landed that flip). The fourth was the digest gate, whose spread-forms row points at an element-level fixture.

So a plausible-sounding hazard cost the worker a verification pass it did not need. The mutually-invalidating-test rule is real and has reddened the trunk before — but a bare token grep is not evidence FOR it. Before warning about a witness collision, check whether the match is the CONSTRUCT or merely the SUBSTRING, and whether the assertion pins the old behaviour or the new. Sixteenth instance this session of the same underlying error: a cheap proxy standing in for the real question.

AND THE FINDING MY BRIEF SHOULD HAVE CARRIED, which the worker found instead: THE REFUSAL MUST RUN BEFORE THE EXACTNESS LAW. A spread canonicalises "class" into the keyword :class, so inexact-host-prop-names sees a CLEAN call — exactness would PASS and the corruption would be the answer. Ordering, not presence, is what makes that guard work. Generalise: when adding a check to a pipeline of checks, ask what the earlier checks NORMALISE, because a normaliser upstream can launder exactly the defect you are trying to catch.

TWO VACUOUS-PASS TRAPS WHEN MOVING TESTS UNDER A PRODUCTION GATE (rf2-d2841, PR #7142). Both make a suite report GREEN while proving nothing, and neither is visible in a passing run. (1) A NEGATIVE trace assertion — `empty?` / `not-any?` over a trace ring — passes automatically under `-Dre-frame.debug=false` because the ring is empty BY DESIGN. It must move INSIDE the dev-only guard with the positive assertions, not be left outside as 'posture-independent'. Same for any 'no :rf.error/... was emitted' read. (2) A namespace that is 100% dev instrumentation (trace-listener-*, trace-test, db-pending-trace-test, sub-dispose-trace-test) has NO semantic residue: guarding it wholesale and removing its exclusion-roster line makes the lane report green for a namespace that EXECUTED NOTHING. Those need a var-level tag (`-e :requires-debug`) so the runner skips them explicitly rather than running an empty shell. GENERAL RULE: when a gate's whole point is that instrumentation is absent, any assertion whose subject is that same absence is worthless in that posture — check what each assertion would do if its subject simply never existed.

A TWO-VALUED PROBE CONFLATES 'REJECTED' WITH 'CRASHED', SO TWO VALIDATORS THAT BOTH EXPLODE AGREE (rf2-dhl4d, 2026-08-03).

THE MECHANISM, and it is the best fail-open diagnosis this project has produced. A viz<->engine parity ratchet compared two validators by asking each "do you accept this definition?" — a BOOLEAN. On CLJS, engine-accepts? wrapped the call in (catch :default ... false). So when the engine raised a host ClassCastException on a non-Named key, the probe recorded FALSE — indistinguishable from a clean, documented rejection. The viz side crashed the same way. TWO VALIDATORS THAT BOTH EXPLODE AGREE, and the ratchet stayed green over a live crash in a security gate.

THE FIX IS THE SHAPE, NOT THE CASE: make the probe THREE-VALUED — :accept / :reject / :host-throw — plus a definition-validation-is-total assertion. Proof it now sees the divergence: (engine :reject, viz :host-throw).

GENERALISE IT. Any comparison harness that reduces its subjects to a boolean, or that catches broadly and maps the catch onto one of the two legitimate outcomes, is fail-open BY CONSTRUCTION — parity ratchets, differential tests, golden-file comparators, A/B benchmark agreement checks. Ask of every such harness: WHAT DOES IT RECORD WHEN THE SUBJECT CRASHES? If the answer is "the same thing as one of the normal outcomes", it cannot see the failure class it exists to catch.

ALSO FROM THE SAME BEAD, a distinct defect class worth naming separately: THE ERROR PATH ITSELF THREW. A (pr-str offending) in the diagnostic message reached an arbitrary object's toString, so a throwing-toString key DESTROYED THE FAILURE BEING DESCRIBED. A validator that rejects correctly but explodes while explaining why is still broken on hostile input. Exercise the diagnostic path with the same forged corpus as the validation path.

AND: the bead named ONE defect site; there were TWO (an inline copy elsewhere in the same file). A worker fixing only the cited line would have shipped a half-fix that passed its own new test. Grep for the PATTERN, not the line number.

MECHANICAL NOTE FOR WHOEVER WRITES THE NEXT MEMORY: do not pass prose containing backticks to bd through a shell double-quoted string — bash runs the backticked spans as command substitution and silently mangles the text. Write the body to a file and pass it with "$(cat file)", or avoid backticks entirely. I did exactly this while recording this memory, and a worker hit the same trap earlier the same day leaving a stray file in the mayor checkout.

UNBLOCKING A BEAD DOES NOT MEAN ITS PLAN IS STILL RIGHT — THE BLOCKER OFTEN CHANGED THE ANSWER (rf2-fwp31, 2026-08-03).

WHAT HAPPENED. rf2-fwp31 was to record the free :scope tag's off-box egress rule in spec/009. It was BLOCKED on rf2-hzcv8. When rf2-hzcv8 merged (PR #7419) I treated it as simply unblocked and dispatched the bead's plan. But rf2-hzcv8 IS THE THING THAT CHANGED THE RULE: it made ssr/redact-value pick its payload by classification, so the identity map now tokenizes to a CONTENT-FREE shape token, not the content-addressed digest the bead described. Only :omit keeps a digest.

So the bead's text — and my brief, which repeated it — asserted that distinct scopes keep distinct digests and PER-SCOPE JOINS SURVIVE OFF-BOX. That is FALSE on main, and the redactor's own docstring says so: 'Preserving JOINS is not a reason to emit one — that is the trade rf2-hzcv8 settles.' Writing it in would have made a NORMATIVE SPEC PAGE FALSE, which is worse than the gap it was fixing.

WHAT SAVED IT: the brief said 'VERIFY EACH CLAUSE AGAINST THE CODE, NOT THE BEAD — if they disagree, the CODE wins and you report the divergence.' The worker read trace_egress.cljc and ssr.cljc, found the 1-arity path, and recorded content-free instead. It also caught a second error neither the bead nor I named: the sentence said 'a RESOLVED concrete scope', missing the clear-scope warning row whose :scope is UNRESOLVED.

THE RULE: WHEN A BLOCKER CLEARS, RE-DERIVE THE BLOCKED BEAD'S ANSWER FROM THE POST-BLOCKER TREE. A bead blocked on a decision was, by construction, written BEFORE that decision. The likeliest thing the decision changed is the very thing the bead was waiting to record. Treat 'unblocked' as 'now re-plannable', never as 'now executable as written'.

COROLLARY FOR BRIEFS: never paraphrase a technical clause out of a bead into a brief as if it were established. Either quote it as the bead's CLAIM and require verification, or verify it yourself first. My paraphrase inherited the bead's staleness and amplified it, because a brief reads as the mayor's instruction rather than as a bead's assertion.

Untracking a gitignored-but-force-added path via 'git rm --cached' in a SEPARATE worker worktree then merging to main DELETES the files from the mayor checkout's disk on pull — because the resulting commit is a plain file-deletion, and 'git pull' removes working-tree copies of files a commit deletes (the --cached keep-on-disk only protected the worker's tree, which didn't have the files). Recovery: 'git show <pre-untrack-sha>:<path> > <path>' to restore each file as untracked local content (they're gitignored so git ignores them). Better approach next time: do the 'git rm --cached' + commit in the SAME checkout that holds the files (but the mayor hook forbids that), OR restore the files immediately after the untrack merge.

Before dispatching any bead >24h old, run: gh pr list --search '<bead-id>' AND/OR gh issue view <linked-gh-N>. Two dispatches in last hour (migration cluster + rf2-ihzz9) hit already-shipped work. The bootstrap.md 'Before dispatching' grep rule should explicitly include gh search not just codebase grep.

WHAT THE MERGED-PR AUDIT REOPENS, MEASURED — AND IT IS A DEFECT IN MY CLOSE REASONS, NOT IN THE AUDIT (2026-07-26).

THE MEASUREMENT. Of the open beads carrying audit-reopen language, the largest cluster by type is TEST / FIXTURE / GATE beads — 7 of 16, ahead of donor (4), spec-prose (3) and privacy (3). All 16 name an explicit residual.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, and it is clean. Gate beads I closed today WITH a mutation proof written into the close reason have stayed closed: rf2-4hc9p (3 mutation references), rf2-wns8d (8), rf2-xwa4n (3), rf2-kqxe6.25 (4). Gate beads that got REOPENED carry ZERO mutation references in their notes: rf2-wq17m (0), rf2-as6bg (0). Small n, but the mechanism is obvious once seen.

WHY IT HAPPENS. A gate bead asks "arm this check". The audit asks "does the check CATCH the thing". A close reason that says the job was added, the roster was widened, or the suite is green gives the audit NOTHING TO VERIFY AGAINST — so it reopens and writes the residual itself. A close reason carrying the planted defect, the gate reddening, the restore and the green gives it the verification already done, and it stays closed.

THE RULE: when closing a gate, fixture, census, lane or CI-arming bead, the close reason MUST carry the mutation proof — the specific defect planted, the observed red with counts, the restore, the green. "The job runs" is not "the job catches". If a worker did not supply one, that is a reason to ask for it BEFORE closing, not to close and let the audit find it.

CORROBORATING EVIDENCE FROM TODAY, all of it the same shape: rf2-wns8d proved a shipped deftest was a TAUTOLOGY by mutating the production wrapper and watching the deftest stay GREEN. rf2-4hc9p proved the pre-repair bijection gate was green on all seven planted defects and red on the one prose fixture — exactly inverted. The ci-arming worker found engine_grammar_parity_test.cljc armed on two lanes and matching NEITHER build ns-regexp, so it ran nowhere. In every case the arming was real and the catching was absent, which is precisely the distinction a close reason must record.

SECOND-ORDER POINT WORTH KEEPING: this means the audit reopen rate is partly MY OUTPUT, not just its diligence. Roughly one reopen per merged PR looked like an immovable property of running an audit; a meaningful share of it is gate beads closed on arming rather than on catching. That is fixable from my side.

WHEN A GUARD IS WARRANTED UNDER "TRUST THE PROGRAMMER" — the principle that reconciles three decisions I made today (2026-07-26).

The three look contradictory on their face:
  1. rf2-bk7z5 — CLOSED, refusing to validate :role against its documented closed set.
  2. rf2-8o66x — DEFERRED, refusing a performance regression gate.
  3. The empty-export finding — FILED, asking for a row floor in the pre-commit hook.

Two refusals and one request, all under the same posture. The distinguishing principle is not size, cost or priority. It is:

  A GUARD IS WARRANTED WHEN THE FAILURE IS SILENT AND HAS ALREADY HAPPENED. IT IS NOT WARRANTED WHEN THE PROGRAMMER CAN SEE THE FAILURE, OR WHEN THE FAILURE CANNOT OCCUR.

Applied:
  1. :role validation — the failure CANNOT OCCUR. Every producer is in-namespace; no caller can pass an invalid role. Enforcing it adds a failure mode, a message to maintain and a test to keep green, and catches nothing. That is a nag-diagnostic.
  2. The perf gate — the failure would be NOISE, not signal. The no-substrate floor drifted 37% across rounds, larger than most effects being measured, so the gate would red on nothing. And a false red is expensive here precisely because the standing rule is that a failing test on a touched surface is never a flake.
  3. The row floor — the failure IS SILENT AND HAS HAPPENED TWICE, six weeks apart, by the same mechanism. An empty tracker with a CLEAN git status is exactly what a programmer cannot see. That is not distrust; it is the only way the fact becomes visible at all.

SO "TRUST THE PROGRAMMER" IS NOT "ASSUME NOTHING GOES WRONG". It is: DO NOT GUARD AGAINST WHAT THE PROGRAMMER CAN ALREADY SEE. A loud crash needs no guard — it is already a signal. A wrong value that renders visibly needs no guard. What needs a guard is the state that looks correct: an empty file with a clean status, a gate green on a defect it was built to catch, a test armed on two lanes and selected by neither.

THE COROLLARY IS THE ONE I HAVE BEEN UNDER-USING: this principle is also a REJECTION criterion with teeth. Most proposed guards fail it, because most proposed failures are either impossible or loud. Ask which of the three cases a proposal is in before pricing it, and the answer usually decides the bead without further analysis.

AND IT EXPLAINS WHY THE ERGONOMICS CLAUSE IS A DETECTOR RATHER THAN A BRAKE: a bad diagnostic is the same defect class inverted. The failure IS visible, but it points somewhere useless — an author told to add a key the source already has, or handed a JSON encoding error naming a reified malli class. That is a signal that lies rather than a signal that is missing, and both are worth fixing where a merely-absent convenience is not.

WHERE A FINDING BELONGS WHEN ITS PREMISE IS AN OPEN RULING (2026-07-25, articulated by the R6 worker and worth adopting): a finding whose premise depends on how an OPEN P1 gets ruled belongs on the PR, NOT in the tracker, until that ruling lands.

Concrete case: R6's guide audit found seven canonical recipes omitting an explicit {:sensitive ...} map and recorded the roster on its PR rather than filing beads. rf2-kqxe6.20 then shipped option A — the framework retains its own carrier classification — and the finding DISSOLVED COMPLETELY: those seven recipes had been describing the correct spelling all along; the framework was what needed fixing. Had the roster been beaded, the tracker would now hold a bead instructing people to add boilerplate that spec/012 and the auth how-to explicitly FORBID.

So the test is not 'is this finding real?' but 'is this finding real under every live ruling?'. If the answer depends on a pending decision, park it on the PR where it dies quietly if the ruling moots it, instead of in the tracker where it becomes durable instruction. A dissolved finding is a GOOD outcome to be stated plainly, not salvaged — the R6 worker struck its own roster in the PR comment so nobody would act on it.

WIDE RENAME SWEEPS — check whether the rename silently DISABLES a gate rather than failing it. rf2-lgeron (#6356, 2026-07-18) found the landmine before sweeping 593 alias sites: doc_api_check.clj extracts references for the alias list ["rf" "story"], so renaming story -> rf.story in docs/story/api/** drops ~15 refs; the min-references floor is 20 against a live ~50, so the gate does NOT trip and the Story API page quietly loses reference checking. A green CI would have certified a switched-off check. RULE: before any mechanical rename, grep the GATES for the old token — a checker that counts or allow-lists the thing you are renaming must move in the same PR. Second trap from the same bead: routing/ as an alias is textually indistinguishable from the sanctioned :routing/* late-bind HOOK KEYS (:routing/extra-route-keys, :routing/on-frame-destroyed!), and the same holds for :epoch/* and :schemas/* — a blind sweep corrupts the DI seam grammar. Same family as rf2-bcjpq5 finding :routing/match-url also exists as a conformance CAPABILITY TAG. ALWAYS check for same-spelling distinct meanings before a bulk edit. Third: a sweep spanning surfaces held by live workers cannot be complete-in-one — report the site count and let the mayor sequence it.

WINDOWS EDIT HAZARD: 'sed -i' on a tracked file in this checkout silently rewrites CRLF->LF across the WHOLE file, producing a whole-file diff that buries the intended 3-line change (caught by the rf2-krdzy worker on #6293, 2026-07-18, on ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/guide/02-views.md; it spotted the churn via 'git diff --numstat', restored from git, and re-applied with the Edit tool). INSTRUCT WORKERS: use the Edit tool for tracked-file edits, never 'sed -i'; if a script edit is unavoidable, check 'git diff --numstat' immediately and expect only the intended line count. RELATED: 'git add' on the force-tracked synthesis tree (ai/findings/new-substrate-synthesis/) requires '-f' even for already-tracked files, because /ai/ is gitignored.

WINDOWS JUNCTION DETECTION - two wrong answers before the right one, both recorded here so neither gets retried. (1) `cmd /c dir /AL <path>` from the Bash tool prints only the cmd banner, no listing, so every directory reports 'not a junction'. (2) `fsutil file queryfileid` DOES NOT share the target's id - a control junction reported a DIFFERENT id from its target, so this test calls a real junction 'not a junction' too. THE WORKING DETECTOR, validated against a deliberately-created control junction: the `ReparsePoint` attribute plus `LinkType`/`Target` via PowerShell `Get-Item -Force`. Belt-and-braces that also validated: `[IO.Directory]::Delete(path, $false)` unlinks a junction leaving the target's contents intact, and refuses a populated real directory - safe to run before every `git worktree remove`. THIS IS NOT THEORETICAL: a worker worktree's implementation/node_modules was confirmed a live junction into the mayor's real node_modules, the exact configuration that destroyed it once already. ALWAYS validate a detector against a control junction you create yourself before trusting it. Supersedes [[junction-detection-via-cmd-c-dir-al-path]].

Windows unclean-shutdown can ZERO-FILL .git/config (12KB of \0), breaking ALL git ('fatal: bad config line 1'). Diagnose: od -c .git/config shows all \0; scan .git top-level for other all-null files (only config was hit). Recover: back up the corrupt file, reconstruct config from surviving data — remote URL from .git/FETCH_HEAD, committer identity from recent commit objects (read with config moved aside), core/* Windows defaults; restore beads.role via 'git config beads.role maintainer'. Verify with git fsck-lite (cat-file -e HEAD + HEAD^{tree}), ls-remote, and 'only tracked file modified is the expected one' (a zero-filled tracked file would show as modified). Happened 2026-07-08.

A DEFECT-WITNESS TEST AND ITS FIX ARE MUTUALLY INVALIDATING — merging both without flipping the witness REDS MAIN, in either order. Cost a P0 red-on-main on 2026-07-24.

THE MECHANISM: a validation pilot reproduces a known hazard and writes it down as a LIVE TEST asserting the CURRENT (broken) behaviour. A separate slice FIXES that hazard. Each PR is green against a main lacking the other. Merge both and the witness test fails, because the defect it documents no longer exists.

THE CONCRETE CASE: the dropdown pilot independently reproduced the ref-composition hazard and shipped `a-behavior-and-a-top-layer-state-on-one-element-lose-a-ref` — a test that PASSES ONLY WHILE THE BUG IS PRESENT. I merged the pilot, then merged the ref-composition fix, and main went red with 2 failures. Every other gate stayed green, so it read like a mystery regression in a slice that had been CLEAN as a PR.

⚠️ WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH A MEMORY IS THAT I HAD ALREADY IDENTIFIED THE PATTERN AND FAILED TO APPLY IT. Days earlier I wrote into a different brief: "both pilots assert the current REFUSAL in a test, so the blocked cell re-opens loudly. THOSE ASSERTIONS WILL START FAILING WHEN YOU SUCCEED — update them deliberately as part of this slice." I understood it for the compiled-browser refusal and did not carry it to the very next fix I merged. Recognising a hazard in one place does not transfer it to another unless it becomes a CHECK.

THE CHECK, now standing — BEFORE MERGING ANY FIX, ASK: does a merged test currently ASSERT THE DEFECT THIS FIXES? If yes, the flip belongs in the SAME PR as the fix, or main goes red the moment both are in.
  git grep -l "<hazard keyword>" implementation/**/test/
Pilot and validation suites are the usual home, because documenting current-state honestly is exactly what they are FOR.

THE REPAIR IS A FLIP, NOT A DELETE, and it has three parts:
  1. Assert the FIXED behaviour positively (both participants ran), never loosen to tolerate either outcome — that discards the only coverage of the combination.
  2. RENAME the test. A name asserting the opposite of its body is a trap for the next reader.
  3. Sweep for SIBLING witnesses in the same suite rather than discovering them one merge at a time.

⚠️ AND THE DIAGNOSTIC LESSON: the failure looked like a regression in the fix. The worker got it right by READING CI OWN LOG for the failing test NAME and MESSAGE — the name said "lose-a-ref" and the message said "one of the two refs was lost", which is the test DOCUMENTING a defect, not detecting one. A test name that describes a BUG rather than a PROPERTY is the tell. My own grep for the failure lines used a pattern chosen before I knew what the output looked like and returned only the namespace roster — capture the log to a file and read it.

GENERAL FORM: this WILL recur wherever validation pilots run alongside active development, which is the whole point of running them. It is a property of the arrangement, not a mistake by either author.

WORKER 'BACKGROUND-GATES-THEN-END-TURN' PATTERN: several workers (xray-tail, m90brg-finish, schemas-5a5qwp) did the full implementation + committed-or-staged it, then spawned their gate runs (npm run test:cljs, JVM suites) as BACKGROUND tasks and ENDED THEIR TURN saying 'I'll pick up when the background tests report' — leaving the work uncommitted/unpushed with the bead still IN_PROGRESS. The harness fires a completion notification but there's no PR. RECOGNITION: worker 'completed' but result says 'background test runs still executing / I'll wait for completion' + worktree shows modified>0, commits/pushed=0. RECOVERY (fast, no work lost): SendMessage-resume the SAME agent → tell it to run gates in the FOREGROUND (wait inline), commit, rebase, push, gh pr create, bd close. Its WIP survives. PREVENTION: put 'run gates in the FOREGROUND — do NOT background them or end your turn waiting on a background task' in dispatch briefs (already added to recent ones; the pattern still recurs, so keep the resume-recovery reflex). NOT a stall — the work is done, just the push step remains.

Worker brief gate-scope lesson (2026-06-09): do NOT require a worker to run the FULL gate matrix locally (all per-artefact clojure -M:test + npm test:cljs/test:browser + elision + mcp-conformance + xray-feature-gate). That makes a heavy-core bead run multi-hour (B6/rf2-vzld77 ran ~2h+, mostly serial gates + build-cache churn of thousands of files). Instead: have the worker run its SLICE gates (the artefacts it touched) + a quick smoke, then OPEN the PR and let the PR's CI run the full matrix. The mayor merges on green CI. Reserve full-local-suite only for the very few beads where CI can't cover it. Applies to future B7/B9 + any big core bead.

Worker briefs MUST forbid committing .beads/issues.jsonl (the mayor owns it; bd auto-stages it in the worker worktree but the worker should NOT git add/commit it). Root cause of PR #3494 stuck CONFLICTING/DIRTY: the worker committed a stale jsonl snapshot that collided with 21 commits of intervening bead changes, blocking CI entirely. Add 'do NOT git add/commit .beads/issues.jsonl' to every worker brief alongside the 'bd close cross-ref' line. Greenup fix: rebase, resolve jsonl by 'git checkout origin/main -- .beads/issues.jsonl', confirm the branch no longer touches it.

WORKER LIVENESS (Windows mayor loop): TaskList can return 'No tasks found' for background agents launched in a PRIOR turn even while they are actively running, AND their output-file mtime does NOT advance during a run (transcript flush is buffered). Both gave false 'dead' signals — a realm worker that TaskList showed as absent + mtime static for 9min actually completed a 624s run. NEVER infer a worker is dead from TaskList/mtime; NEVER recycle/--force-remove a worker's worktree on that basis (it clobbers live workers mid-edit). The ONLY reliable liveness signal is the completion/kill <task-notification>. To recycle, wait for that notification or confirm via a pushed branch with the expected commits.

Background workers and review agents MUST NOT create, claim, or close beads. Beads are mayor action only — filing them makes the mayor think they own the work. Worker outputs go in chat and ai/findings/ (local). Use background workers freely for parallel drafts/research; never bd create for that.

Worker node_modules junction destroyed the mayor's real node_modules AGAIN (2026-07-31, rf2-2rtt6.8 / PR #7311). A worker worktree with no node_modules cannot compile; the established repo convention (a live sibling worktree had exactly this) is a Windows junction: cmd /c mklink /J <wt>/implementation/node_modules <mayor>/implementation/node_modules. That works for the build, and then post-merge hygiene ran git worktree remove, which FOLLOWED the junction and emptied the mayor's REAL implementation/node_modules to 0 entries - breaking every local build in the repo. Repair is cheap and deterministic: cd <mayor>/implementation && npm ci (exit 0, restores the canary 101 entries; verify react + shadow-cljs are present). TWO fixes, both needed: (1) the WORKER should cmd /c rmdir the junction as its last act before reporting done, not leave it for hygiene; (2) HYGIENE must cmd /c rmdir <wt>/implementation/node_modules BEFORE git worktree remove, and re-check the mayor canary (~101) after each removal batch. This is the second recorded instance of the same class.

Worker path-leak mechanism (CONFIRMED 2026-07-17, rf2-r09qj + flagged by rf2-klyw5): a subagent that Reads MAYOR-checkout absolute paths during exploration can have its SUBSEQUENT Edit tool-calls carry that mayor path — so edits land in the mayor checkout, NOT the worktree. Invisible in the worker's OWN git status (the worktree looks clean); visible only from the mayor side. MITIGATION that works: the boundary-block's post-write BOTH-TREES check catches it — the worker self-recovers (git checkout-restore the mayor file, copy completed work into the worktree, verify mayor clean). HARDEN BRIEFS: instruct workers to Read AND Edit only worktree-absolute paths (never the mayor checkout, even for exploration reads), re-verify rev-parse per edit, and run the both-trees check after the first edit + any new file. Mayor-side detection: 'git status --short | grep -v .beads' in the mayor checkout should be empty; a stray modified file there = a live leak (capture the diff, don't blind-revert if the worker may be mid-recovery). This is a REAL Agent-subagent mechanism, distinct from the Workflow args-undefined misdiagnosis.

Worker PR-creation hang gotcha (2026-06-09): a worker (B6/vzld77) completed + committed + pushed its work, then hung ~1h LOOPING on 'gh pr create' with a heredoc body containing backticks/parens (bash kept mis-parsing). Mayor salvaged by opening the PR from the pushed branch. LESSON: in worker briefs, tell workers to create the PR with a SIMPLE body or '--body-file', avoid backticks/parens/heredocs in the inline body; and if a worker is committed+pushed but PR-less + idle, the mayor can open the PR for it (git -C <wt> push; gh pr create --head <branch>) rather than killing the work.

Worker recovery hazard (learned 2026-06-22, the #4910/#4913 xray-testbeds incident): (1) A worker coming to rest is NOT proof it finished. The xray-testbeds worker came to rest waiting on a gate it launched; the mayor misjudged it as done, committed its UNCOMMITTED partial work as a recovery PR (#4910) — but it had not yet written standard_epochs/core.cljs, so #4910 merged an incomplete state that crashed the two-frame surface on load and left a red gate on main. RULE: only recover/commit a worker's work after a genuine final report with a PR URL; an idle worktree mid-task is not a completion signal. (2) NEVER git worktree remove --force a worktree whose worker may still be live — it destroyed the live worker's workspace AND emptied the mayor implementation/node_modules via the node_modules junction cascade (the worker had to npm install to restore the mayor tree). RULE: only remove a worktree for a worker that has genuinely completed (final report received); the junction-rmdir-before-remove step does not protect against removing a still-active worktree.

"WORKTREE-LOCAL" IS ONLY HALF THE RULE FOR WORKER SCRATCH FILES — IT MUST ALSO BE GITIGNORED (2026-08-09).

THE SEQUENCE. Earlier in the day two concurrent workers overwrote each other's helper files and PR-body drafts in the SHARED scratchpad, and one nearly published another bead's PR body. The fix put into later briefs was "write every file you create inside your own worktree". Both workers complied exactly. Both worktrees then REFUSED to reap: REMOVE_REFUSED_DIRTY, each holding one untracked pr-body-<bead>.md that the disposability classifier will not accept as build output.

SO THE TWO HAZARDS TRADE OFF AND THE BRIEF MUST CLOSE BOTH. dispatch-prompt-template.md already says it: put EVERY gate artefact where git ignores it, and warns that one leftover is enough to make a tree unreapable (nine accumulated that way once). The ignored extensions are *.log, *.exit and *-exit.txt. A file named pr-body-something.md is worktree-local, safe from collision, and still blocks the reap.

THE COMPLETE INSTRUCTION FOR A DISPATCH BRIEF: write every file you create inside your own worktree AND give it an ignored name (*.log / *.exit), or delete it before you report done. Never a shared temp directory; never an unignored leftover.

RESOLVING IT WHEN IT HAPPENS IS CHEAP BUT MUST NOT BE BLIND. --dry-run prints each offending path tagged [KEEP] or [build output]; a PR-body draft whose content is already published on the merged PR is genuinely disposable, so --force is correct AFTER looking. Do not reach for --force-disposable (it refuses anything not recognised as build output) and never spray a blanket --force across a sweep list: when that guard was written, one worktree held four analysis files for an OPEN bead and three others carried uncommitted source and doc edits.

A WORKTREE YOU DID NOT EXPLICITLY DISPATCH MAY BE YOUR OWN WORKER SPAWNING A SECOND WORKTREE — not a concurrent session. Misdiagnosed 2026-07-24. I dispatched a 4-bead cluster to ONE worker; it did 3 beads in worktree A (PR one) then created worktree B for the 4th bead (PR two). My hygiene scan found worktree B, had no record of creating it, and I concluded a concurrent session was also dispatching workers. WRONG — it was my own worker branching per bead. THE COST: the false belief made me over-cautious about that surface being externally contested. THE DISCRIMINATOR before concluding concurrent-session: a branch named worker/<desc>-<beadid> whose bead you assigned to a live worker IS that worker, even as a second worktree. Check worker completion reports and open PRs first — a worker report names every worktree and PR it created. Track by BEAD ownership (who did I give this bead to), never by worktree count: one worker is NOT necessarily one worktree or one PR. The genuinely-separate process here (the pr-audit loop) FILES beads, it does not dispatch code-editing workers, so it never contests a code surface. No harm done — I correctly did not touch the worktree or re-dispatch the bead.

A WORKER STRANDS BY ENDING ITS TURN ON A BACKGROUNDED GATE, AND IT WILL DO IT REPEATEDLY UNLESS THE BRIEF SAYS HOW TO WAIT. Observed again 2026-08-08 on rf2-2rtt6.142, twice in a row after a resume.

THE SHAPE. A gate exceeds the tool's foreground time ceiling. The worker detaches it — correctly — and then ENDS ITS TURN "waiting" for a completion notification. Nothing is guaranteed to wake it. It reports "still progressing, continuing to wait", the turn ends, and the same thing happens on the next nudge. The work is usually fine; only the waiting is broken.

WHAT DOES NOT FIX IT: telling the worker again that gates must be foreground. It already believes that, which is exactly why it detached and then waited politely. The instruction it is missing is what to do INSTEAD of waiting.

WHAT FIXES IT — put this in every brief, not just the ones with long gates:
  "If a gate exceeds the tool's time ceiling, run it detached and BLOCK ON IT INSIDE THE SAME TURN by polling its exit file in a loop. Never end a turn with a gate outstanding."
and give the literal shape:
  for i in $(seq 1 240); do [ -f gate-<id>.exit ] && break; sleep 15; done; cat gate-<id>.exit

TWO RIDERS THAT MATTER AS MUCH AS THE LOOP:
- The detached invocation must use an ABSOLUTE path to the gate script. These scripts derive their repo root from BASH_SOURCE, and a relative invocation that gets detached adopts whatever cwd the shell really has — one did that inside ANOTHER live worker's checkout and produced a complete, internally consistent verdict about somebody else's diff. Check the run's "gate root:" first line names your own worktree.
- If the invocation writes no exit file at all, that is the real defect, not the waiting. Re-run as: sh <ABS>/scripts/test-fast-pr.sh > g.log 2>&1; echo "$?" > g.exit

MAYOR-SIDE RECOVERY, cheap and reliable: check the ground truth yourself rather than nudging twice. `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD` and a remote-vs-local sha comparison in the worktree tell you whether the work is durable; `ls *.log *.exit` plus the log's mtime tell you whether the gate is genuinely still running or dead. On this occasion the work was already committed AND pushed, so nothing was at risk — the only outstanding step was reading an exit code.

DO NOT MISREAD THE SPINE LOG WHILE CHECKING. test-fast-pr.sh prints lines like "ok  unexpected extra dependency -> FAILED" from a negative-test harness confirming its own mutations fail correctly. Those are PASSES. The verdict is the echoed exit code, never a line in the log.

WORKER TRAP — git mv then edit (2026-07-25, found by the misc-cluster-a worker on PR #6946): after 'git mv old.cljc new_cljs_test.cljc', a subsequent 'git add <path>' does NOT pick up content edits made after the mv. The worker's first pushed commit therefore carried the RENAMED file with the OLD ns name still inside it — a commit that would not compile. It was caught only by noticing a stray 'M' in git status, then fixed by rebuilding both commits from the base and force-pushing with --force-with-lease. This is the exact shape of the rf2-dn6v7 / rf2-lgozq lane-suffix work (rename file + edit ns in one change), so it will recur. Put in briefs for any rename-plus-edit bead: after a git mv, re-run 'git add' on the path AFTER the content edit, and verify with 'git diff --cached' that BOTH the rename and the content change are staged before committing; a rename-only commit of a .cljc test file is a non-compiling commit.

Worker worktrees have NO node_modules, so browser/shadow-cljs gates cannot run there by default. Do NOT junction into the mayor checkout's node_modules to fix it — that is the configuration that destroyed the mayor's real node_modules once and nearly again. THE SAFE ANSWER IS `npm ci` INSIDE THE WORKTREE (one worker did exactly this today, exit 0, no junction created, canary unmoved). Cost is a few minutes; the alternative is deferring every browser gate to CI. Put this in any brief whose gate menu includes `npm run test:browser`, a shadow-cljs build, or an adapter testbed spec.cjs — otherwise the worker hits 'shadow-cljs is not recognized', concludes the gate is unrunnable, and defers coverage that actually matters (the real-DOM gate catches repaint bugs test:cljs structurally cannot see). Related: [[windows-junction-detection-two-wrong-answers-before-the]].

Workers can get stuck in a monitor-wait loop on slow test suites (rul3ov burned ~770K tokens over 3 segments re-arming a Monitor for the full CLJS conformance run before committing). Recovery: SendMessage the agentId with a firm 'do NOT arm another Monitor — commit FIRST, push, gh pr create NOW; CI runs the full suite so CI is the gate, not your local terminal.' Over-cautious 'won't PR until local green' is the anti-pattern; the PR's CI is the real gate.

CONCURRENT WORKERS SHARE THE SESSION SCRATCHPAD AND OVERWRITE EACH OTHER'S FILES — including PR bodies (2026-08-09).

WHAT HAPPENED. Six workers ran in parallel on the hic-* Wave A set. The rf2-hic-004 worker reported that its verify.py and pr-body.md were BOTH overwritten mid-run by the rf2-hic-005 worker. Same filenames, same shared scratchpad directory. Its PR body survived only because gh had already read the file before the overwrite landed. A slower run would have published another bead's PR body under its own PR number.

WHY THE EXISTING RULE DID NOT COVER IT. The brief said 'use worktree-local log paths', and every worker complied FOR GATE LOGS — they all wrote gate-slugs.log inside their own worktree. The collision was in the HELPER FILES nobody thought to fence: scratch scripts, PR-body drafts, temp verification output. The known hazard was written narrowly as a gate-log hazard; it is really a shared-temp-directory hazard and applies to every file a worker writes outside its worktree.

THE FIX FOR FUTURE BRIEFS. Say: write EVERY file you create - gate logs, helper scripts, PR-body drafts, scratch output - inside your own worktree, never in a shared temp or scratchpad directory. If you must use a shared directory, prefix every filename with your bead id.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A WRONG GATE LOG. A clobbered gate log yields a plausible-but-wrong exit code, which the echo-the-exit-code rule catches. A clobbered PR body is published verbatim to GitHub under the wrong PR and nothing checks it.

THREE WORKERS IN ONE NIGHT STALLED WAITING FOR A "COMPLETION NOTIFICATION" THAT DOES NOT EXIST (2026-08-10).

WHAT THEY EACH DID. rf2-8a6s: "Still running. I'll stop here and resume when the watcher fires - no more polling." rf2-hic-009: "The spine is still running ... I have a waiter armed on its exit code and will report the moment it lands." rf2-hic-016: "The fast-PR spine is still running; I'll wait for its completion notification rather than end the turn" - and then the turn ended. All three had briefs that said, in terms, run gates in the foreground to completion and never background one.

THE BELIEF IS SPECIFIC AND WRONG, WHICH IS WHY THE EXISTING WORDING DOES NOT PREVENT IT. They do not think they are abandoning the task. They think a watcher/notification will wake them. Nothing does. A stopped subagent resumes ONLY when the mayor sends it a message, and the mayor only knows to because the completion report reads oddly. "Run gates in the foreground" does not contradict the belief - a worker can believe it ran the gate in the foreground AND that something will tell it the answer later.

THE WORDING THAT ADDRESSES THE BELIEF, not the behaviour: "There is no completion notification. No watcher wakes a stopped worker. If you end your turn waiting for a gate, the task stops until a human notices. Run the gate in the foreground, block on it, read its exit code yourself. A long foreground gate is fine; an unfinished turn is not."

THE REAL COST IS UNPUSHED WORK, AND IT VARIES. rf2-8a6s had committed AND pushed - fully durable, only the PR was missing. rf2-hic-009 had pushed and opened a PR - only the spine result and PR body were missing. rf2-hic-016 had THREE COMMITS AND HAD NOT PUSHED - one lost worktree from losing an entire three-engine browser suite. So the recovery order is: check `git log origin/main..HEAD` and `git ls-remote` FIRST, and if it is unpushed, make PUSH step 1 of the resume message before anything else.

RECOVERY IS CHEAP AND RELIABLE: SendMessage to the agent id resumes it from its transcript with full context. All three resumed and continued correctly. Do not re-dispatch a fresh worker - it would redo work that is already committed.

DETECTION: a completion report that says "still running", "I'll report when", "waiting for", or "watcher armed" is a stall, not a status. Treat it as a resume trigger immediately, and check push state before replying.

Workers strand because the long gate outlives their TURN budget, not because they disobeyed 'run foreground'. Three workers in one session (dispatch-sync, ci-test-lanes, tags-ratchet) ended their turn mid-gate with 'Waiting on the spine/watcher' — commits pushed, NO PR, nothing mergeable. A brief that says 'run test-fast-pr.sh foreground to completion, THEN open the PR' makes stranding likely on a loaded box, because the spine can exceed the budget. BETTER BRIEF ORDER: commit -> run only the FOCUSED, fast, arm-specific gates (plus any non-vacuity/mutation proof, which is cheap and is the evidence that actually matters) -> OPEN THE PR -> name the slow gates as 'deferred to CI' in the ## Quality gates section. CI runs the same surface and IS the merge gate; the local spine never was. Recovery is SendMessage-resume, which works and keeps the worker's context.

Workflow rule (Mike, 2026-06-10): beads marked in_progress are LOCKED - never update their title/description/notes/scope (a worker is executing against them). To add findings or scope to in-progress work, CREATE A FOLLOW-UP BEAD (dep on the in-progress one if sequenced). Check status with bd show before any bd update.

Worktree cleanup: a directory can be REUSED and re-pointed at a different branch mid-session, so a name-based safe-list goes stale while you are acting on it. Observed live: a hygiene agent was handed 'ci-test-lanes-cluster - safe to remove, PR #7116 merged', but between the list being written and the removal, a worker reused that same directory on a NEW branch (worker/xray-fuzzy-regression-pin) carrying an open PR #7119. Removing by name would have destroyed an in-flight PR worktree. Re-read `git worktree list --porcelain` IMMEDIATELY BEFORE each removal and re-verify the branch AND its PR state at that moment; never trust a safe-list compiled minutes earlier. Corollary: 'PR merged' is a fact about a BRANCH, not about a DIRECTORY. Related: [[rebase-merge-makes-a-worker-branch-look-unmerged]].

Worktree hygiene: `git status` ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH to decide whether a worktree holds work. The `/ai/` tree is GITIGNORED, so findings docs, gate logs, PR-body drafts and ad-hoc probes are INVISIBLE to git status — a worktree that looks pristine can hold real content. Sweep `ai/` (and any `.worker-logs/`, `.wt-logs/`) separately and READ any non-log file before discarding. Observed: three worktrees held hidden content (20 gate logs, a pr-body.md draft, an ad-hoc probe .clj) — all correctly judged residue, but only because they were looked at. Corollary for the other direction: a hygiene brief that says 'clean tree = safe to remove' is wrong on this repo.

WSL bash.exe DOUBLE-EXPANDS a -c command string. Found by rf2-sefx0 (#6357, 2026-07-18) with a decisive probe: bash -lc with FOO=hello then printf of the escaped dollar-FOO prints the literal dollar-FOO under Git Bash (single pass) but prints hello under WSL bash (an outer pass already substituted it). CONSEQUENCE: any -c string that READS BACK a variable the SAME string assigns is broken under WSL — the outer pass substitutes the not-yet-assigned name to empty. That is how a PATH= assignment referencing a FIXTURE_DIR assigned immediately to its left silently produced /bin:<real PATH>, so stub executables were never found and 15 of 15 cases failed before reaching the code under test. Pre-existing vars (PWD, PATH) survive both passes, which is why the bug looks selective. FIX SHAPE: build one env-prefixed command whose every dollar-NAME already exists in the parent environment; let the child script read the rest from its own environment rather than from the command string. DISPROVED on the way: the semicolon separator is fine, and double-quoting is fine — do not chase those. TESTING LESSON (the important half): a BEHAVIOURAL test for this cannot protect you, because Git Bash and the Ubuntu CI runner both expand ONCE — a reintroduced self-reference stays green on CI while breaking only for Windows contributors. sefx0 pinned the STRUCTURE instead (assert the command references only pre-existing variables) with a non-vacuity guard. Generalise: when a defect is invisible on the platform your CI runs, a structural pin beats a behavioural one.

A RULING DETAIL WAS EMPIRICALLY WRONG: notifications CAN arrive before dispatch returns on the stock-Reagent adapter (found 2026-08-07, rf2-ynved).

THE RULING SAID (item 8) that notifications never arrive before dispatch returns. FALSE on this adapter: :flush-render! is (fn [f] (f) (r/flush)), so dispatch-sync DRAINS THE QUEUE ITSELF. A test written to assert the ruling literally went red.

HOW IT WAS HANDLED, and this is the part to copy: the worker did not quietly conform the test to observed behaviour, and did not quietly conform the docs to the ruling. It reported the ruling was wrong, and changed the DOCS to say the re-feed rides a Reagent flush rather than an inline callback inside the app-db write — while telling the author to code as though it lands on the FOLLOWING commit. That last clause is the useful part: teach the WEAKER guarantee even when the stronger one currently holds, because the stronger one is an implementation detail of one adapter.

SECOND FINDING from the same run: a sibling unmount COMMIT re-runs a surviving tracker against an unchanged value, so the survivor takes one idempotent re-feed. The DOM-free counterpart drives the identical release with NO React commit and sees no duplicate. So it is a property of the commit cycle, not of the recipe — and the assertion was rewritten property-based with the reason recorded.

GENERAL RULE: when a test contradicts a recorded ruling, the ruling is a hypothesis like anything else. Report the contradiction, establish which is true FROM THE ADAPTER SOURCE, and fix whichever is actually wrong. Do not assume the ruling wins; do not assume the observation wins.

AFTER A CONTEXT CLEAR, PRIOR-SESSION AGENTS STAY ALIVE BUT GO INVISIBLE TO TaskList — AND I USED TaskList AS THE LIVENESS SOURCE (2026-08-10).

WHAT I DID WRONG. Recovering from a /clear, the handoff said the rf2-vsgq worker on worker/hmrbrowser-vsgq was "live and resumed". I called TaskList; it returned "No tasks found". I trusted the tool over the handoff, concluded the agent was dead, and dispatched a fresh fix-worker into that SAME worktree on that SAME branch. Two executors then ran on one branch — the exact thing "no concurrent workers same branch" forbids.

HOW IT SURFACED. Not from any check of mine. The original agent's own completion report flagged it: "A commit I did not author appeared on my branch at 15:50 — 13e9750dc9 ... it may be a second executor in this worktree." It was mine.

NO HARM, BUT ONLY BY LUCK. Both agents happened to fix different halves of the same red gate (one renamespaced the :dev-http build id, the other added the README build->port row), the commits did not conflict, and PR #7768 merged green. Nothing about that outcome was guaranteed.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS A TOOL BOUNDARY, NOT A JUDGEMENT CALL. TaskList reports the CURRENT session's task registry. A /clear starts a new registry. Agents spawned before the clear keep running and keep pushing commits, but they are absent from it. An empty TaskList after a clear therefore means "this session has spawned nothing yet", NEVER "no workers are running". It also returned empty immediately after I spawned six agents, so it is not a reliable liveness source in this harness at all.

WHAT TO USE INSTEAD, in order:
  1. The worktree list under the re-frame2-worktrees sibling — a live worker owns a worktree, and a finished one removes its own.
  2. Whether the branch's commit count has MOVED since the last tick. bootstrap.md already names this as the cheap reliable discriminator; a moved count says alive. A still count says nothing and never authorises a reap.
  3. Whether SendMessage finds a live task to deliver to.

A HANDOFF DOCUMENT OUTRANKS AN EMPTY TaskList. The handoff was written by the session that spawned those agents and it was right; the tool was answering a narrower question than the one I asked it.

AND THE SAFE MOVE WAS AVAILABLE AND CHEAP: SendMessage to resume the existing worker keeps its full context and cannot create a second executor. Never re-dispatch a fresh worker over one that may still be live — resume it.

title: ci: the classifier does not arm migration_hicasso_codemod from implementation/hicasso, so door-roster drift reds late
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-vi11 WORKER (PR #7762) and verified by the mayor in .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh. The classifier is off-limits to that worker (a CI cluster held it), so it reported rather than reached.

WHAT IS MISSING. PR #7762 adds a door pin: shared_rule_test.clj now reads the door's own codec.cljs and asserts the mirrored callback-contract roster equals it. That pin lives in the codemod's JVM lane. But the classifier arms migration_hicasso_codemod from implementation/freehand/* and NOT from implementation/hicasso/*. So a change to the door's roster in the hicasso package does not run the suite that pins it, and door drift reds late — on some unrelated PR that happens to arm the lane.

THE PATTERN ALREADY EXISTS IN THE FILE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS SMALL. The implementation/freehand/* arm carries a documented REVERSE EDGE (see the rf2-2rtt6.143 comment block around line 1088): the codemod's deps.edn puts the bench tree on its classpath so codemod and door share ONE slot rule per rf2-ani6y, and shared_rule_test.clj pins the two identical?. That comment states the design and even explains why the arm is deliberately COARSER than the edge - an arm naming the shared file alone would have to precede the general one and would shadow four outputs, silently narrowing Freehand's coverage. Over-classifying a seconds-long pure JVM suite is the cheaper error, and TESTING.md says to prefer it.

WHAT TO DO. Add migration_hicasso_codemod=true to the implementation/hicasso/* arm, on the same reasoning, and extend the comment there so the second reverse edge is documented like the first. Then the hicasso arm arms cljs_node_test, cljs_browser, the freeze gate and the codemod lane.

PROVE IT MATCHES. A rule that matches nothing looks like coverage. Show a diff touching only the door's codec.cljs arming migration_hicasso_codemod, and quote the output. VERIFY THE PROBE IS NOT VACUOUS: three workers tonight hit a first probe that proved nothing - one scratch repo had no origin/main so the classifier took its conservative fallback and the true was meaningless; another lost an uncommitted arm to a git reset and measured a rule that did not exist. Commit first, then probe against a real base.

Add the matching row to implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs. The first narrowing went stale unnoticed because no regression pinned it.

HOT ZONE: .github/scripts/ and .github/workflows/ are sequential, never parallel. Check no other worker holds them before dispatching.

GATES, each run ALONE with $? echoed to its own file, never a filter appended to a gate's command line: sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh in full, check_test_lane_bijection.py, check_jvm_lane_rosters.py, check_gate_scheduling.py, check_fast_pr_gap.py, and clojure -M:test from migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod. NOTE touching the classifier ARMS TIERS THAT WERE PREVIOUSLY SKIPPED, so any gate result taken before your classifier edit is stale, and a fresh worktree needs the implementation/node_modules junction for the CLJS tier.
notes: Merged-PR audit of #7762 independently reproduced this exact reverse-edge gap, so no duplicate was created. At landed commit 08cc1765, report-changed-surfaces.sh classifies implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs with migration_hicasso_codemod=false even though shared_rule_test.clj now reads that door file; the same probe for the codemod's report.clj correctly returns migration_hicasso_codemod=true. The codemod lane itself passed 28 tests / 300 assertions. This owner remains open for the classifier arm plus regression row.
close_reason: Merged-PR audit of #7767 found the implementation complete, correct, and proportionate. The Hicasso artefact-root arm adds migration_hicasso_codemod without dropping its existing outputs; the regression binds the arm to the exact codec.cljs path read by shared_rule_test.clj; a direct landed classifier probe returns all four intended outputs true; GitHub recorded 86 passing and 3 expected-skipped checks. No follow-up finding remains.

value: PR #7767 audited through independent completeness, correctness, and implementation-quality lenses. No new Bead and no duplicate owner: exact delivery owner rf2-erjv was closed as fully satisfied. The Hicasso arm widens scheduling additively, its non-vacuity row resolves the actual io/file target, a direct landed probe returned cljs_node_test=true, cljs_browser=true, migration_hicasso_codemod=true, and hicasso_controlled=true, and GitHub recorded 86 passing checks with 3 expected skips. Cursor persisted only after the review outcome.

title: hic: two I7 rows are owed to a browser suite — a read deferred into a React effect, and across a Suspense retry or Activity reveal
description:
RAISED BY THE rf2-hic-011 WORKER (PR #7763). Its I7 legality matrix is a Node-lane suite, so two rows of the matrix cannot be observed there. It named them rather than implying measurement, and recommended a follow-up in the same shape rf2-hic-015's report earned.

WHAT IS NOT WITNESSED:
  1. a read deferred into a React effect
  2. a read deferred across a Suspense retry or an Activity reveal

WHY: the hicasso package's lane is Node. No DOM, and react-dom/server never commits. Neither deferral can be driven there.

WHAT IS ALREADY BANKED, so this does not start from nothing. PR #7763 landed 14 rows: three legal shapes (nested helper two frames deep, both arms of a branch, a variable-length loop 2 to 4 to 1), seven refusals asserted as EXACT error maps, the commit-reconciliation clause, and the declared limit. Twelve of the fourteen were shown red under four reverted runtime perturbations. Model the two new rows on those.

THE LESSON THAT MUST CARRY OVER, and it is the reason this bead exists in this shape. That worker's P1 control removed read-key!'s nil-frame guard and the escaped reads STILL THREW - from subscribe-once, with a different error id. A row written as (is (thrown? ...)) would have stayed GREEN under the bead's own named sabotage. So assert the EXACT error identity as a map - id, emitting function, phase, query - never merely that an exception occurred. In a layered runtime there is almost always a second defence that keeps a throw assertion green.

TWO MORE BROWSER CAUTIONS, both measured tonight:
  - A value-level or text assertion cannot see these faults. React's end-of-event restore repairs value errors inside the same discrete event, and text assertions stayed green while a discarded hydration adoption went unnoticed. rf2-hic-016 established that the CARET is the only observable separating this runtime from plain React in a real browser.
  - Never let a CI step run a bare `npx playwright install`. It resolves a newer Playwright than the repo pins and prunes the pinned WebKit from the shared cache. The measured fix is `working-directory: implementation` after `npm ci`; `--no-install` blocks a registry fetch but NOT a cache hit.

DO NOT freeze the complaint prose. PR #7763 deliberately asserts collector/fail!'s shape as the pre-image of the hic-007 error shape, because rf2-hic-007 is still OPEN and that shape does not exist yet. Keep that property so hic-007 and rf2-hic-021 can re-route the text without reddening the suite.

SEQUENCING: rf2-ga8m owns the three-engine gate's CI scheduling and has merged; a browser lane exists at implementation/hicasso/testbed/ and browser witnesses at implementation/hicasso/test/.../roots_frames_*. Read both before choosing a home. Do not wire CI here unless TESTING.md says the new rows need their own lane.
close_reason: Merged-PR audit of #7769 found the browser witness complete, correct, and proportionate. It drives both React effect phases, a real Suspense abandonment/retry, and an Activity hidden/reveal; asserts exact refusal identity, acquisition census, liveness, and teardown; and carries non-vacuity controls that red under the named perturbations. The actual PR ran the browser, Node, and controlled-input lanes successfully. No follow-up finding remains.

value: PR #7769 audited through independent completeness, correctness, and implementation-quality lenses. No new Bead and no duplicate owner: exact delivery owner rf2-ouus was closed as fully satisfied. The one-file browser suite covers both requested I7 carrier families (layout/passive effects and Suspense retry) plus Activity reveal, proves the carriers ran, compares exact error identity rather than any throw, checks reader ownership and teardown, and preserves explicit remaining non-goals. GitHub recorded the browser, Node, controlled-input, lint, and invariant checks green. Cursor persisted only after the review outcome.

THE SESSION SCRATCHPAD IS SHARED ACROSS CONCURRENT AGENTS, AND PR-BODY DRAFTS GET SILENTLY OVERWRITTEN THERE (2026-08-10, twice in one hour).

WHAT HAPPENED. Two workers independently reported the same thing. The rf2-hic-093 worker found its `pr-body.md` overwritten shortly after it created PR #7771. The rf2-dmrm worker found its `pr-body.md` replaced by a DIFFERENT agent's PR body — text about rf2-x874/hic-013/hic-011 — shortly after it created PR #7772. Neither had its worktree touched; only the scratchpad file.

WHY MY BRIEFS DID NOT PREVENT IT. Every brief already said "put every gate artefact where git ignores it" and named worktree-local paths for LOGS AND EXIT FILES. It said nothing about the PR body, so workers reasonably wrote that to the session scratchpad, which is per-session and NOT per-agent. Concurrent agents in one session share it, and a fixed basename like `pr-body.md` collides by construction.

NO HARM EITHER TIME, AND THAT IS THE HAZARD. Both PRs were created BEFORE the overwrite, so both published bodies were correct and both workers verified them afterwards. Had the ordering been reversed — draft, get clobbered, then `gh pr create --body-file` — a worker would have published ANOTHER BEAD'S PR BODY onto its own PR, with plausible-looking content and no error anywhere. The handoff records a near-miss of exactly that shape already ("one nearly pushed foreign content").

THE FIX IN EVERY BRIEF, stated as its own line rather than folded into the logs rule:
  SCRATCH FILES GO IN YOUR WORKTREE, NOT THE SESSION SCRATCHPAD. Write the PR
  body to a gitignored path INSIDE your worktree, check `git status` before
  committing, and delete it before finishing.
Worktree-local is the right default for ALL agent scratch, not just gate logs, because a worktree is per-agent by construction while the scratchpad is not.

AND THE GENERAL RULE THIS INSTANCES: a shared mutable path with a fixed basename is a collision waiting for concurrency. The same class already bit gate logs (`/tmp/gate.log`, two workers, the loser read someone else's green). When a brief names a file a worker will write, ask whether two agents would name it the same thing.

PR #7770 audited through independent completeness, correctness, and implementation-quality lenses. No new Bead and no issue update/reopen: the docstring-only tail correctly explains why drain-checkpoint's returned zero is a healthy post-queue probe rather than a vacuity signal, and points to at-the-checkpoint's synchronous precondition as the real guard. The prose matches the landed promise-chain implementation and all 21 scheduled GitHub checks passed. Exact broader owner rf2-2l17 remains open because this PR deliberately carries only the tail that missed #7766. Cursor persisted only after the review outcome.

title: hic: three HMR matrix rows are owed to a browser suite — focused controlled input, child hook state in a host, active imperative host
description:
RAISED BY THE rf2-hic-015 WORKER (PR #7755). It could not file this itself: a worker branch must never carry .beads, so it stated the gap in the recorded contract and asked the mayor to file it.

WHAT IS NOT WITNESSED. Three rows of the HMR matrix have no measurement:
  1. focused controlled input across a save
  2. child hook state inside a host
  3. the active imperative host

WHY, AND IT IS A LANE LIMIT NOT AN OVERSIGHT. The hicasso package's test lane is Node. There is no DOM, no jsdom, and react-dom/server never commits. None of the three can be observed there. The worker did not fake them and did not imply measurement: the contract in invariants.md says plainly that these rows are owed to a browser suite.

WHAT IS ALREADY BANKED, so this bead does not start from nothing. The worker witnessed their SINGLE COMMON CAUSE exactly: the unconditional type re-mint. It proved that by memoising mint-view! per view-name, which reddened all three type witnesses while the sameness control stayed green. So the mechanism is measured; what is missing is the three surface behaviours under a real browser.

THE LANE THAT FITS ALREADY EXISTS. rf2-hic-016 built the three-engine Playwright suite (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) at implementation/hicasso/testbed/, and rf2-hic-012 landed browser witnesses at implementation/hicasso/test/.../roots_frames_*. value:
THE TWO gh COMMANDS IN THE MERGE CRITERION USE OPPOSITE CASE VOCABULARIES, AND A FILTER WRITTEN FOR ONE SILENTLY MISCLASSIFIES THE OTHER (2026-08-10).

  gh pr checks <pr> --json state    -> UPPERCASE:  SUCCESS, SKIPPED, IN_PROGRESS
  gh run list --commit <sha> --json status -> lowercase: completed, in_progress

CLAUSE 4 OF THE MERGE CRITERION USES THE SECOND ONE. I wrote its check as
`select(.status != "COMPLETED") | length` — copying the case from clause 2's vocabulary —
so it matched NOTHING and counted EVERY run as nonterminal. On PR #7774 it reported
"clause4 not-COMPLETED: 5" for a PR whose five runs were all `completed/success`.

THIS ONE FAILED CLOSED, WHICH IS WHY IT COST ONLY A MINUTE. An over-blocking clause 4
refuses a green PR; the method already names that failure ("a guard that blocks forever is
not safe, it is differently wrong") but it is far cheaper than the fail-open direction.
Had I written the inverse test — count runs EQUAL to "COMPLETED" and require the count to
match the total — the same typo would have passed a branch with live runs on it.

WHAT SAVED THE EARLIER MERGES. I printed the run list and read the statuses BY EYE for
every merge before this one, and lowercase `completed` reads correctly to a human. The
defect only bit when I switched from printing to counting. So: a filter you cannot eyeball
is exactly where a vocabulary mismatch hides.

THE FIX: compare case-insensitively — `select((.status|ascii_upcase) != "COMPLETED")` — or
print the values alongside the verdict so the two can never silently disagree. Prefer
printing: the criterion is read by a human every tick anyway.

THE GENERAL RULE, which this repo keeps rediscovering in its own instruments: when one
check joins two data sources, the join is where the vocabularies must be proved equal. Do
not assume a tool speaks one language because two of its subcommands describe the same
domain.

title: gate: check_provenance_pins fails OPEN on an unusable repository — a failed git diff reads as 'nothing changed', and a shallow clone reads as mass STRANDED
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-i19d WORKER (2026-08-10 16:17 AUSEST) while greening PR #7765. It
could not file this itself (a worker branch must never carry .beads). The mayor
verified both clauses in source before filing. This is the FIFTH fail-open in this
one checker; four were found and repaired on 2026-08-09 (per-block accompaniment
shielding a stranded sibling, _left_context reading across a table-row start,
trailing URL material, a case-sensitive .git rejection).

THE UNIFYING DEFECT: the gate does not fail toward refusal when the REPOSITORY
itself is unusable. It only reasons about the corpus. Both clauses below are the
same shape — an unanswerable question read as a clean answer.

--- CLAUSE 1: a failed `git diff` is read as "nothing changed" ---

scripts/check_provenance_pins.py, Git.changed_markdown, lines 681-692:

    base = self._run("merge-base", since, "HEAD")
    ref = base.stdout.strip() if base.returncode == 0 and base.stdout.strip() else since
    diff = self._run("diff", "--name-only", "--diff-filter=d", ref, "--", root)
    return {line.strip() for line in diff.stdout.splitlines() if ...}

Line 687's return code is NEVER checked. A failing `git diff` leaves stdout empty,
the set comes back empty, and the driver reads that as "no page under the root
changed" and exits 0 having verified NOTHING.

OBSERVED, NOT THEORISED. While the worker held the repository with a long
`git fetch --unshallow`, the spine's embedded `--changed-since origin/main` step
printed "no page under docs/design/hicasso changed since origin/main" and returned
0 — with 28 pages actually changed. A green badge over an unrun gate.

Line 686 carries a SECOND, softer instance of the same shape: when `merge-base`
fails it silently substitutes `since` as the comparison basis. That changes the
question being asked rather than refusing to answer it, and it does so with no
output. Decide whether that fallback should survive at all; if it does, it must
say so loudly.

--- CLAUSE 2: a SHALLOW clone silently poisons every verdict ---

`merge-base --is-ancestor` answers NO for every commit past a shallow boundary, so
on a shallow clone the gate reports mass false STRANDED. Measured by the worker on
this checkout before it repaired it: boundary bfb0dca1f0, 111 commits, and the full
corpus read 0 landed / 354 stranded / 360 findings. The true numbers on the deep
clone are 361 pins, 253 landed, 102 stranded, 5 unresolvable, 1 foreign, 7 findings.

That is worse than a crash. A worker trusting it would conclude a CORRECT fix had
failed, and might "repair" tokens that were never broken — the gate's own header
says it does not re-pin precisely because a human must decide each one.

The gate must DETECT shallowness and REFUSE, naming the remedy
(`git fetch --unshallow --no-tags origin main`; CI uses fetch-depth: 0). It must
not produce a verdict it cannot support.

--- FIX SHAPE (decide, do not assume) ---

Parse positively and fail closed, exactly as the four earlier repairs did. Check
every subprocess return code in this class and raise a REFUSAL distinct from a
findings-failure, so a broken repository can never be mistaken for a clean corpus.
Note the exit-code vocabulary already in the codebase: an arm-order guard elsewhere
exits 2 for a refusal precisely so it is not a plain non-zero failure. Follow that
if it fits.

--- PIN IT ---

scripts/check_provenance_pins.py's `--self-test` carries all four earlier fail-opens
and every case must stay green. ADD A CASE PER CLAUSE, and CONFIRM EACH REDS AGAINST
THE CURRENT IMPLEMENTATION BEFORE FIXING — that ordering is the proof. There are
already 19 self-test references in the file; follow the established shape rather
than inventing a harness.

--- FENCES ---

NEVER weaken the gate. NEVER add an ignore mechanism or allowlist. Do not change
any pin classification, and do not touch any corpus page — this bead is the checker
only.

--- ALSO WORTH KNOWING ---

The mayor checkout was shallow until 2026-08-10 ~16:10 AUSEST and is now full
(20,092 commits on origin/main, no .git/shallow marker). ANY LOCAL PROVENANCE-PIN
RESULT RECORDED IN THIS REPO BEFORE TODAY IS SUSPECT. CI was never affected; its
checkout uses fetch-depth: 0.

--- GATES ---

python scripts/check_provenance_pins.py --self-test --verbose; then
(git fetch --no-tags origin main; python scripts/check_provenance_pins.py
--changed-since origin/main --verbose); then sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh in full.
Run each ALONE and echo $? to its own file; never append a filter to a gate's
command line. Report the full-corpus finding count before and after with the set
difference in both directions on the same merge base; the corpus stands at 7
findings as of 2026-08-10 16:10 AUSEST on a deep clone.
