title: hic: a lowered callback silently writes a same-public-id SUCCESSOR frame whenever the frame-ops memo is cold
description:
FOUND BY MEASUREMENT, not inspection, by the rf2-hic-013 worker (PR #7749, 9 tests / 57 assertions green). It reported rather than fixed because impl/frames.cljs was fenced to a sibling worker. The witnesses that prove it are landing in that PR; this bead is the repair.

THE DEFECT. A lowered callback closes over the frame KEYWORD and resolves its bundle when it FIRES. So where a delayed callback lands depends on the frame-ops memo's warmth at that instant, not on the incarnation the callback was lowered under. After a same-public-id frame is torn down and a successor mounts:

  WARM memo  -> the write is refused. CORRECT BY ACCIDENT: it is the stale memo doing it, not any check.
  COLD memo  -> THE CALLBACK SILENTLY WRITES THE SUCCESSOR'S app-db. No error is emitted.

COLD IS THE ORDINARY CASE — a boundary that rendered but that nobody clicked before the teardown. So the common path is the broken one and the rare path only looks correct.

WHY "EXACT EVICTION ON DESTRUCTION" IS PROVABLY THE WRONG FIX. rf2-hic-013's own deliverable 3 names two candidate remedies: incarnation-keyed bundles, or exact eviction. Eviction was MEASURED and it makes things worse — it converts the single accidentally-correct branch (warm) into the broken one, making the silent successor-write UNIVERSAL. Do not implement it. Note also that forget-frame-ops!, the only eviction door that exists, has exactly ONE caller: reset-runtime!, a test fixture.

THE MEASURED FIX: pin the incarnation into the closure at mint time. The worker measured this repairing BOTH branches. It requires impl/frames.cljs.

WHY THE DOM CANNOT SEE IT, which is why this survived until now. The read path is address-directed and the write path is incarnation-pinned, so after a reincarnation the runtime READS the successor correctly while refusing to WRITE it — perfect markup above dead controls. And commit-basis ties (1 -> 1), so snapshot-of ties and React schedules no re-render; the repair arrives a macrotask later (snapshot 1 -> 2, one notification). A DOM assertion inside that window blames its own timing; after it, it reports green. Any fix must be witnessed at the same layer PR #7749 used, not through rendered output.

DO NOT WEAKEN THE WITNESSES. PR #7749 ships two shipped negative controls and six run controls (NC1 de-memoise frame-ops, NC2 incarnation-sensitive commit-basis, NC3 always-dispose, NC4 never-dispose, NC5 remove the macrotask deferral, NC6 apply the candidate remedy). NC6 in particular predicts exactly which branches a correct fix flips — treat a mismatch against NC6 as evidence your fix is wrong, not that the control is stale.

SECOND, SEPARATE ITEM RECORDED BY THE SAME WORKER, not part of this repair: React law 3 requires a render/commit tear to be "corrected before visible paint". The measured correction here is MACROTASK-DEFERRED, which carries no such ordering guarantee. That is a spec-conformance question about the correction path itself and wants its own ruling; do not silently resolve it inside this fix.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7749 (2026-08-10; completeness/correctness/implementation quality). Independent merged-tree rerun is green, but the witness proves this exact owner remains actionable: a cold or evicted predecessor-era lowered callback silently writes the successor, while a warm stale memo can refuse the live successor current route. The suite encodes the defect as a green test intentionally expected to fail when fixed, so remediation must replace or invert that test. Close only when retained callbacks always refuse, current callbacks route, memo and closure incarnation semantics are repaired together, and the defect test becomes a positive contract.
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-10, operator-overturnable): APPROVE Option A now — pin the frame incarnation into the lowered callback at mint time. Runtime-source edit AUTHORIZED, scoped to impl/frames.cljs PLUS the smallest corresponding change in impl/collector.cljs. Eviction-on-destruction stays REJECTED (measured worse: converts the accidentally-correct warm branch into the broken one, making the silent successor-write universal). Holding for more design rejected: P1 silent corruption in the kernel with Wave B building on top. WHY THE SCOPE ADDS collector.cljs (verified in source 2026-08-10, correcting the frames.cljs-only framing): the late-binding closure is minted in collector.cljs frame-dispatch — (fn dispatch-for-frame [event] (dispatch! frame-kw event)) memoised into frames/!frame-dispatch under the bare public keyword (collector.cljs ~501) — so frames.cljs alone cannot carry the fix. Fence the rest of the runtime. PR #7749 (witnesses) is MERGED 2026-08-09.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (preserves dossier + Codex analysis; dossier file deleted after this):
(1) MECHANISM — use core's existing capture-frame authority; do NOT invent a new incarnation fence and do NOT add a core late-bind hook. capture-frame called while a frame is LIVE pins that exact incarnation and, after supersession, recovers with :rf.error/frame-destroyed (recover-but-emit, never throw; core.cljc ~1266/1351). A capture made while the id is ABSENT is deliberately address-directed — so Hicasso must acquire the handle during render of the live frame, never at fire time.
(2) CONTRACT — a) at frame-dispatch lookup during render, resolve the currently live incarnation and obtain its rf/capture-frame bundle; b) memoise the ambient closure keyed by that incarnation/bundle identity; the closure calls the CAPTURED bundle's :dispatch-sync inside the existing with-commit window — it must never call dispatch! with the bare frame keyword and resolve again later; c) repeated renders within one incarnation return the identical closure with zero allocation on hit; when the same public id names a new incarnation, the lookup replaces the memo row and returns a fresh closure pinned to the successor; a retained predecessor closure keeps the predecessor bundle and is refused by core; d) treat !frame-ops and !frame-dispatch as ONE logical record — one per-id entry {incarnation, core bundle, batched dispatch closure} is the clearest shape; if two atoms remain, their hit/miss tests must be coupled by exact token/bundle identity so they can never describe different incarnations; e) correctness must NOT depend on a destruction hook — lazy incarnation-mismatch replacement of the one cached row; forget-frame-ops! remains reset/hygiene only (sole runtime caller is the whole-runtime reset, collector.cljs ~1828; other callers are test fixtures).
(3) BOTH HALVES TOGETHER — cold memo: retained predecessor callback silently writes the successor's app-db; warm memo: a freshly minted successor callback is refused by the stale bundle (perfect markup above dead controls). Cache warmth merely chooses between the two failures; safety of retained callbacks and liveness of successor callbacks are one repair, not two.
(4) WHY THE DOM CANNOT WITNESS IT — read path is address-directed (reads successor correctly) while the broken write path refuses; commit-basis ties so React schedules no re-render and the repair arrives one macrotask later, making DOM assertions blame their own timing. Witness at the instrumentation layer PR #7749 used, never through rendered output.
(5) PERF — preserve one shared handler identity per live frame incarnation; the extra live-token comparison lands on the once-per-body cache lookup, not on every event position or event. Run the existing boundary-shell/per-render benchmark; no material regression. Do NOT build a generalized callback-lifecycle subsystem for this bug.

FENCES: do NOT touch the macrotask deferral / read-repair timing — React law 3 "corrected before visible paint" is rf2-2l17's separate ruling; do not silently resolve or alter it inside this fix. Eviction must not be implemented. No public API additions. Runtime edits confined to impl/frames.cljs + impl/collector.cljs. Do not weaken PR #7749's witnesses or its negative controls NC1-NC6.

WITNESSES (the merged-PR audit note above requires the defect-recording green test be replaced/inverted into a positive contract): a) a callback minted under incarnation A refuses after A is destroyed in cold, warm, AND explicitly-reset cache postures; leaves B's app-db untouched; emits exactly one production-surviving :rf.error/frame-destroyed with correct frame and event identity; b) a callback freshly minted under B dispatches successfully in each posture — including the previously broken warm case — with no refusal; c) callback identity is stable across repeated renders of A, changes from A to B, and is stable across repeated renders of B; d) h/fn returning an intent, a plain intent vector, a key-map branch, and a handler minted inside a declared render callback all inherit the same pinned ambient dispatch (one table-driven test — the paths share the mechanism); e) reset still empties the memo inventory; focused Hicasso suite green; f) negative control: restore late keyword resolution and it must reproduce BOTH the cold predecessor-write and the warm successor-refusal (a test proving only stale-callback inertness is incomplete — an all-controls-dead cache would also pass it); g) NC6 rule: PR #7749's NC6 predicts exactly which branches a correct fix flips — treat any mismatch against NC6 as evidence the FIX is wrong, not that the control is stale.

FOLLOW-UP (separate bead, does not gate this repair): bounded seam audit of the two direct collector/dispatch! callers (h/boundary error reporting; the internal mount witness) and of ::h/navigate, which bypasses the ambient dispatcher and delegates an explicitly address-directed frame keyword to routing. Change those only if a retained-operation witness demonstrates the same revival.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7759 (2026-08-10 AUSEST; completeness/correctness/implementation quality). The functional repair is correct: one per-id row now couples the live incarnation token, captured core bundle, and closure over that bundle; same-incarnation hits retain identity, a successor lazily replaces the row, and retained predecessor callbacks are refused by core while fresh successor callbacks route. Independent merged-tree evidence is green: focused Hicasso 50 tests / 236 assertions; browser 1148 / 7100; controlled-input Chromium/Firefox/WebKit 55 checks each; freeze 7/7. The shipped negative control reconstructs both old failures.

KEEP THIS EXACT OWNER OPEN for the small but real completion sweep the PR missed. The normative ledger still says the defect is open and its test is failing-when-fixed (docs/design/hicasso/product/invariants.md:114) and repeats that late resolution is live at :122. Runtime/test documentation still describes two memo tables or the old live defect (collector.cljs:23, frozen-sources.edn:55, roots_frames_isolation_dom_cljs_test.cljs:14, hmr_registry_cljs_test.cljs:332). Also `git diff --check bb38d87..c996347` exits 2 for a new blank line at EOF in reincarnation_routing_cljs_test.cljs. Correct those claims/remove the blank EOF, then this technical owner can close; no duplicate Bead.

description:
# hic-013 — Kernel: same-public-id frame reincarnation + delayed callback routing

**Phase**: 1 · **Wave**: B · **Est.**: M · **Depends**: hic-010 (shares the collector/frame-routing file)

Move Hicasso from benchmark-tree prototype to an installable package a clean consumer can use, without changing semantics.

title: hic: retiring the arm1 rows left the public door's three macros unpinned — the authoring surface is now the least-checked thing in the package
description:
RAISED BY THE rf2-hic-001 WORKER (PR #7748, merged) as an explicit follow-up. It did not invent schema to avoid it, and it did not hide it — which is why the gap is precisely describable.

WHAT WAS LOST AND WHY. PR #7744 split impl/runtime.cljs into six modules. The freeze manifest's `:renames` is a ONE-TO-ONE table from bench namespace to package namespace and cannot express a 1-to-6 split, so four rows became inexpressible: arm1/boundary.cljs, arm1/mount.cljs, arm1/presence.cljs and arm1/lang.clj. They were retired per the manifest header's own third response ("retire the row rather than re-pin it"). Seven front/* rows remain, all whole-file, and the gate is green at 7 rows on main.

**RETIRING DROPS THE DONOR DIGEST TOO, not just the MOVED comparison.** #7744's worker had kept those rows precisely to preserve that half. Combined with the earlier retirement, NOTHING under the bench tree's arm1/ is pinned by anything now.

THE DISPROPORTIONATE LOSS IS arm1/lang.clj, AND IT IS THE PUBLIC AUTHORING SURFACE. That file defines the three macros the package's public door exposes. Only `defview` actually re-points to a new namespace; `hfn` and `defhost` still match their donor EXACTLY. But a row is judged whole — the alternative is a per-shape exemption, which is the one thing this gate must never grow — so all three went unpinned to retire one. The consequence: **the authoring surface is now the least-checked thing in the package.**

THIS IS RECORDED, NOT HIDDEN, which is what makes it actionable: case 8 of check_freeze.py's mutation self-test deliberately demonstrates the blind spot as GREEN rather than omitting it, and frozen-sources.edn's header states the cost. Read both before designing anything.

DO NOT: prune the rename table. 2 of the 5 now-retired entries (arm1.presence, arm1.lang) are still load-bearing for surviving front/* rows; pruning would red them. The worker checked this deliberately.
DO NOT: add a per-shape exemption mechanism to the freeze gate. That is the failure mode the whole-row judgement exists to prevent.

WHAT TO DECIDE (mayor/operator ruling, not worker work): how the three public macros regain coverage. Candidate shapes, none chosen:
  (a) a split-aware manifest field (many-to-one renames) — the worker deliberately did NOT add this, correctly, since schema is a design change;
  (b) re-pin the macro file alone under a narrower contract, accepting that `defview` needs a rename the current table cannot express;
  (c) cover the authoring surface by a different instrument entirely — the door has tests, and the freeze gate may simply be the wrong tool for a file whose namespace legitimately moved;
  (d) accept the gap and record it as permanent, on the ground that arm1/ is prototype provenance and the package is now the artefact.
RECOMMEND weighing (c) and (d) first. The freeze gate answers "is the package the prototype, moved". Once a module split makes that question unanswerable for a file, forcing the answer may be the wrong instinct — but the public door being the LEAST checked thing in the package is not an acceptable resting state either.
notes:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-10, operator-overturnable): Option (c) plus the (d) record, in the Codex-refined form — a SMALL public-door contract-witness addition to the existing package test lane. NOT byte-for-byte macro-expansion snapshots (incidental symbol/metadata/def-layout detail would make safe pre-alpha refactoring noisy for zero consumer confidence). Option (a) split-aware manifest schema REJECTED (turns a rigid extraction check into a transformation engine; every future refactor shape becomes a schema request). Option (b) narrow re-pin REJECTED (option (a) in miniature — defview needs a rename the one-to-one table cannot express). No freeze-schema extension, no new harness, no JVM lane.

REALITY CHECK (2026-08-10): freeze gate green at 7 rows, all front/*, all whole-file; nothing under arm1/ pinned; the blind spot is demonstrated rather than hidden — PR 7748 mutation-proof case 8 altered the hfn expansion and the gate exited 0. The dossier predates rf2-hic-012/013: the package lane NOW exercises h/defview (smoke + roots/reincarnation suites) AND h/defhost (roots_frames_isolation_dom_cljs_test.cljs:122 — defhost around a tiny React fn with {:ssr :render}, used as a hiccup head, real-DOM render). h/hfn is the one door macro with ZERO package-test usage.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (one worker, package tests only, the :node-test-hicasso lane):
(1) Witness A — the callback macro, current prototype spelling h/hfn (hicasso.cljc:90). Consumer-shaped: define one through the public door; assert it is an ordinary function, that invoking it returns the author value, and that impl.intent/callback? recognizes it (one own-property read); also assert a plain (fn ...) is NOT callback?, so the witness discriminates.
(2) Witness B — h/defhost. The isolation-test usage is incidental to a containment row and could refactor away silently; make the contract deliberate: assert the minted var is a host head (impl.codec/host-head?) and renders through ordinary Hicasso hiccup with one option forwarded ({:ssr :render} suffices, proving argument forwarding). Smallest diff wins: a tiny dedicated witness OR explicit assertions promoted onto the existing usage.
(3) The existing defview smoke is the third witness — unchanged.
(4) The (d) record: add ONE dated line to the frozen-sources.edn header — arm1/ provenance-pinning ended at the module split (PR 7744; retirement in PR 7748); the package is the artefact from that commit forward. The header already states the cost; this is a one-line disposition, not a rewrite.
(5) HARD FENCE: never prune the rename table — the arm1.presence and arm1.lang entries are load-bearing for surviving front/* reconstructions (front/presence.cljs, front/intent.cljs); pruning reds them.
(6) HARD FENCE: never add a per-shape exemption mechanism to the freeze gate. A row is judged whole; that rigidity is the value.
(7) MUTATION CHECK: each witness must be shown able to fail exactly once — temporary mutation applied, red observed, reverted, stated in the PR body — the same discipline as the PR 7748 mutation proof.
(8) NAMING: witnesses target the PROTOTYPE spellings that exist today (defview, hfn, defhost); the naming review recommends h/event for the callback form — the rename-sweep updates the witnesses mechanically when it lands; do not pre-empt it here.
(9) STOPPING RULE: if the fix starts requiring freeze-parser changes, expansion normalization, a new runner, or exhaustive macro edge-case tables — STOP. That is provenance litigation, not better SPA ergonomics.

UNBLOCKING: landing the two witnesses green (with the one-time mutation demonstration recorded) closes this bead and CLEARS the rf2-hic-001 blocker — no further freeze-gate work is owed for the authoring surface.

title: the-mayor-method: the merge criterion needs three more clauses, all earned after rf2-4j4hl landed
description:
FILED BY THE MAYOR 2026-08-07. PR #7641 (rf2-4j4hl) landed the first clause — 'Zero failures is not green; it is only the absence of bad news' — and it is on main. THREE MORE were learned the same day, AFTER that PR was written, each from a real near-miss or a real cost. The written rule is therefore one generation behind practice again.

CLAUSE 2 — CANCELLED IS NOT PASSED. Counting statusCheckRollup entries by 'status == COMPLETED' silently counts CANCELLED as green. I reported a PR as '85 of 86 concluded, one check from complete' when the truth was 79 passed, 6 CANCELLED, 1 pending — it needed six re-runs across four workflows, not one. Only conclusions in {SUCCESS, SKIPPED} count.

CLAUSE 3 — THE ROLLUP CAN READ pending==0 WHILE RUNS ARE QUEUED. A queued run's checks are not yet attached to the head commit, so the rollup does not know they are coming. PR #7630 reported ok=78 canc=0 fail=0 pend=0 total=78 — fully settled by every field it exposes — while 'gh run list --branch' showed two runs QUEUED. Merging there ships a PR two workflows short. So the branch must be queried directly, not just the rollup.

CLAUSE 4 — AND THAT BRANCH QUERY MUST BE KEYED TO THE CURRENT HEAD SHA, AND MUST NOT BE A TRUNCATED GLOBAL LISTING. Two failures here, in opposite directions. (a) I used a global 'gh run list --limit 40' grouped by branch; a branch with four queued runs did not appear because other branches filled the window, so the check reported 'no live runs' for a branch that had four. (b) Once fixed, I over-blocked: two PRs sat at 86/86 for three ticks because stale-sha runs from BEFORE a re-trigger commit were still queued. Stale-sha runs are not evidence about this head. A guard that blocks forever is not safe, it is differently wrong.

THE CRITERION, all four clauses, none sufficient alone:
  - total non-empty and in the band the repo actually produces (~86 here; verify with 'gh pr checks' on recent merged PRs rather than assuming)
  - every conclusion in {SUCCESS, SKIPPED} — CANCELLED is not passed
  - zero QUEUED or IN_PROGRESS entries in the rollup
  - AND 'gh run list --branch <headRefName> --limit 25' shows no queued/in_progress run WHOSE headSha MATCHES the PR's current headRefOid

ALSO WORTH A LINE, from the same day: 'Base branch was modified' usually means the PR BRANCH IS STALE, not that a race occurred — the remedy is 'gh pr update-branch', not retrying (I retried seven times). And a failed 'git fetch' makes every subsequent 'Already up to date' a lie; check the fetch's own exit, because the error and the false success print in the same output.

FENCE: docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md and .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md. Both must agree — a previous pass found THREE wording sites in mayor-merge.md, and fixing two of three left the file self-contradicting. Note .claude/commands/ is covered by NO gate (mkdocs builds only docs/; check_doc_slugs.py's roots are docs/spec/skills/migration/tools-spec), so hand-verify it.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7656 (merged 2026-08-07T01:50:24Z; landed f0c71ce43156f4b20e2e124edf0d7f89edd25dd0) — REOPENED this exact merge-criterion owner; no duplicate.

CORRECTNESS: clauses 3 and 4 reject only QUEUED and IN_PROGRESS, but the installed gh CLI's run-status vocabulary also includes REQUESTED, WAITING and PENDING. Those are likewise nonterminal current-head runs whose checks may not yet be attached to the rollup, so this enumeration retains the same fail-open class the PR is fixing. The simpler durable rule is: every workflow run for the current head SHA must have status COMPLETED; any other status blocks and is rechecked later.

COMPLETENESS / IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the prescribed one-shot command is `gh run list --branch <headRefName> --limit 25`, whose normal table does not provide the `headSha` field clause 4 requires comparing. Likewise `gh pr checks` exposes JSON fields `state` and `bucket`, not a `conclusion` field. Give the command file an executable, fail-closed spelling rather than leaving the crucial joins implicit: resolve `headRefName` and `headRefOid`; query `gh pr checks --json name,state,bucket`; query `gh run list --branch <head> --commit <oid> --limit 25 --json status,headSha`; require every check state in {SUCCESS, SKIPPED} and every exact-head run status COMPLETED. The live CLI confirms PR #7656 has 86 checks with states SUCCESS/SKIPPED, and the exact-head run query returns five runs all COMPLETED. Pin the parser/decision shape so a new nonterminal status cannot silently pass.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7759 (2026-08-10 AUSEST) — REOPENED exact merge-criterion owner after a concrete stale-base false-green.

Chronology: PR #7760 merged at 00:16:35Z and added required Hicasso browser plus three-engine controlled-input arms. PR #7759 merged later at 00:20:48Z, but its checked branch still had base 1b78f8f (before #7760). Consequently the Hicasso-touching PR's `cljs-browser` check was SKIPPED and the newly required `cljs-hicasso-controlled` check was absent from its rollup entirely. “All required checks passed” therefore described the old matrix, not the matrix already on main. The merged tree happens to be green — this audit independently ran browser 1148/7100 and controlled Chromium/Firefox/WebKit 55 each — but the merge guard did not know that.

The current mayor method explicitly says to merge the whole queue first during a moving-base burst, which is exactly the policy that exposed this gap. Extend the fail-closed criterion: a PR cannot rely on a check set computed before a newly merged workflow/classifier/required-job change that affects its surface. Prefer an enforceable current-base/merge-queue rule, or minimally update and recheck affected stale branches after matrix changes; do not infer coverage from an aggregate built against the superseded matrix.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7764 (merged 2026-08-10T04:38:30Z; landed 7f3f7479c1458190a270f0003e042c2c1a3aa6c5) — UPDATED this exact open merge-criterion owner; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS: the five-clause, fail-closed core now covers the original task plus the #7656 and #7759 audit findings. The overview was also touched, but its adjacent “Merge trap” still prescribes unconditional gh pr merge --squash --admin, while the new criterion says an empty/short/cancelled/live/stale-matrix result is never an admin bypass and the command/bootstrap text permits only a named structurally irrelevant pending check. Reconcile that overview with the actual policy, and make the pending-check exception explicit in the five-clause decision rule (or remove it); as written, clause 2 rejects every pending state while the next paragraph authorizes one.

CORRECTNESS: README.md and bootstrap.md now summarize post-pull verification as checking that HEAD “moved”. Movement is neither necessary nor sufficient: an already-current checkout legitimately does not move, and moving to the wrong commit does not prove synchronization. The command file and bootstrap’s later hard-won section state the correct invariant: git rev-parse HEAD must equal git rev-parse origin/main. Replace both summaries with that equality.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the command file now provides the executable CLI fields and fail-closed allowlists requested by the prior audit. Live validation on this PR found 89 nonempty checks, all SUCCESS/SKIPPED, and five exact-head workflow runs, all COMPLETED. check_doc_slugs.py and changed-surface provenance pins both passed; .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md was manually read end-to-end because no content gate covers it. Keep this owner open until the two cross-document contradictions above are removed and all three policy surfaces agree.

title: docs(agents): CLAUDE.md still prescribes 'gh pr merge --rebase --admin' and a bare 'git pull --ff-only' — the fourth policy surface rf2-vfsrd could not reach
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-vfsrd WORKER (PR #7775, merged as 877ddab91) and flagged rather than
reached: CLAUDE.md was outside its declared write surface, so it reported. Verified by the
mayor at 2026-08-10 ~17:30 AUSEST before filing.

PR #7775 reconciled three policy surfaces — docs/the-mayor-method/README.md,
docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md and .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md — so that all three
agree: the five-clause merge criterion admits NO exception, `--admin` bypasses no clause,
and the ONLY `--admin` the method sanctions is `MERGEABLE=UNKNOWN`, GitHub's own
merge-state recompute lag, which is not a check at all.

CLAUDE.md IS A FOURTH SURFACE AND IT STILL SAYS THE OPPOSITE.

  CLAUDE.md:91
  "Run `git pull --ff-only` as the very next step after
   `gh pr merge ... --rebase --admin --delete-branch`."

THIS IS WORSE THAN THE README PARAGRAPH #7775 JUST FIXED, for two reasons.

FIRST, CLAUDE.md IS LOADED INTO EVERY AGENT'S CONTEXT IN THIS REPO. It is not a page a
mayor consults; it is the standing instruction every worker and every mayor session reads
at startup. So it teaches `--admin` as the house merge command to everyone, silently, on
every dispatch.

SECOND, THE `--admin` IS INCIDENTAL TO THE RULE IT SITS IN. That bullet's actual subject
is "pull main immediately after every PR merge"; the merge command is quoted only to say
what "the very next step" comes after. An unconsidered example is exactly the kind of text
that hardens into policy because nobody reads it as a claim.

TWO DEFECTS IN THAT ONE LINE, not one:

  1. `--admin` must go. The merge command this repo actually uses is
     `gh pr merge --rebase --delete-branch`. Evidence: NINE PRs merged on 2026-08-10
     (#7769, #7770, #7768, #7765, #7771, #7772, #7774, #7773, #7775), every one with
     `--rebase --delete-branch`, every one reaching state=MERGED, and `--admin` used
     ZERO times.
  2. `git pull --ff-only` is written WITHOUT naming the remote and branch. All three
     surfaces #7775 touched say to write `git pull --ff-only origin main` and say why:
     the bare form both silently no-ops and outright refuses when the audit-hook push
     races it. CLAUDE.md's bare form is the one the method warns against.

WHILE YOU ARE THERE, CHECK — do not assume — whether the same bullet should also carry the
post-pull test. The method's invariant is `git rev-parse HEAD` must EQUAL
`git rev-parse origin/main`, not that HEAD "moved", and one mismatch is not yet evidence
because an asynchronous audit push can land between the two reads. CLAUDE.md's bullet
justifies the pull by "staleness leaves Mike with a wrong picture", which is a reason to
pull but states no verification at all. Decide whether adding the equality test here is
the right call or duplication of the method file, and say which you chose and why. Do NOT

title: hic: cell-readers promises a copy and can hand back a live alias — every reader-counting witness rests on it
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-vsgq WORKER while building the HMR browser suite. Its own control caught it: a "snapshot" baseline had silently become the POST-save reader list, so a correct runtime read exactly like a leak. It could not file this itself (a worker branch must never carry .beads) and it changed no runtime source.

THE DEFECT IS A FALSE GUARANTEE IN A DOCSTRING. implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/inventory.cljs, cell-readers (around line 87):

    (vec (.-readers c))

with the docstring "A witness reader, answered as a vector SO A CALLER CANNOT MUTATE THE LIVE LIST."

In ClojureScript `vec` on a JS array does not necessarily copy. It goes through PersistentVector.fromArray WITHOUT cloning, so for an array inside the tail threshold the returned vector ALIASES the underlying JS array. The collector `.push`es readers into that same array in place (three .push sites in collector.cljs). So a caller holding the "snapshot" watches it change underneath them.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY SHARP EDGE. The docstring states the opposite of the behaviour, and it names its own purpose: "it is what the reader-counting rows assert against". Every reader-count witness in this package is built on a guarantee the function does not provide. A test that captures a baseline, performs an action, and compares cannot see a leak - because the baseline mutated into the result. That is precisely how it presented: a CORRECT runtime looked like a leak, and by symmetry a leaking one could look correct.

FIX SHAPE (decide, do not assume): either make the copy real - `(into [] (array-seq ...))` or an explicit `.slice` before `vec` - or change the docstring to state that the result is a live view and must be copied by the caller. The first is almost certainly right, because the docstring names the witness use-case and witnesses need a stable baseline. Do NOT simply delete the sentence; that would leave every reader-counting row resting on an unstated assumption.

PIN IT. A test that captures cell-readers, triggers a registration that .pushes, and asserts the captured value is UNCHANGED. Confirm the test reds against the current implementation before you fix it - that ordering is the whole proof, and it is how this was found.

CHECK THE SIBLINGS in the same namespace while you are there: boundary-reads and any other accessor that hands out a collection derived from a live mutable structure. Report what you find rather than widening the fix without saying so.

GATES: the hicasso node suite and compile, the freeze gate, and sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh in full. Run each ALONE and echo $? to its own file; never append a filter to a gate's command line. NOTE the fast-PR spine now takes about 40 minutes, past the tool ceiling - run it detached and block on its exit file IN-TURN rather than ending the turn.

Completeness: package and retired bench donor both use the real copy, sibling accessors remain correctly scoped, and four focused rows cover remount, departure, arrival, plus live-list movement. Correctness: aclone severs the mutable JS-array alias before vec wraps it; independent focused compilation completed 183 files with zero warnings and the current suite passed 79 tests / 336 assertions with zero failures. Implementation quality: one explicit clone at the instrument boundary preserves the promised snapshot API without caller obligations or new machinery; full diff-check passed. A BASH HEREDOC ON THIS WINDOWS SETUP STRIPS BACKSLASHES, SO A REGEX INSIDE `python - <<'PY'` SILENTLY BECOMES A DIFFERENT REGEX AND RETURNS A FALSE ANSWER (2026-08-10).

REPORTED BY THE rf2-re0m WORKER after it nearly published a wrong number. It ran a
throwaway `python - <<'PY' ... PY` script to count Markdown links inside fenced regions.
The heredoc ate the backslashes in its patterns, so the pattern that should have matched
`](` matched nothing, and the script reported ZERO fenced links — on a tree that had seven.
It caught the discrepancy, re-ran everything from WRITTEN SCRIPT FILES, and got the true
counts.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE BACKSLASH BUG ALREADY ON RECORD. The known form is
`git worktree add` and `cmd /c mklink` losing path separators — those FAIL, loudly and
immediately, and you go fix the quoting. This form SUCCEEDS. Python compiles the mangled
pattern happily, the script exits 0, and you get a plausible number that is wrong in the
safe-looking direction: zero findings, nothing to do, ship it. A verification tool that
misreports is the same defect class as the bug it was written to catch.

THE RULE: never put a regex, or any backslash-bearing text, through a heredoc in the Bash
tool on this setup. Write the script to a file and run the file. If a throwaway script
reports a suspiciously clean result — zero findings where you expected some — re-run it from
a file BEFORE believing it.

AND THE GENERAL SHAPE, which is the reason to remember it: an ad-hoc verification script is
itself unverified. When its answer is the evidence for a claim, the script needs the same
red-first discipline as a test — prove it can report a non-zero count on known-bad input
before trusting its zero.

ANY BEAD THAT ADDS AN `:rf.error/*` ID IS A FORCED spec/009 TOUCH, SO IT IS NEVER HOT-ZONE-FREE (2026-08-10, found by the rf2-hic-007 worker).

WHAT HAPPENED. I dispatched rf2-hic-007 with the surface fenced to "the macro and error
files only" and treated it as parallel-safe against five other live workers. The worker
decided, correctly by my fence, to REPORT spec-drift rather than edit a hot-zone file — and
then the fast-PR spine failed it. `check_keyword_catalogue_drift` CHECK A reds on a new
`:rf.error/*` id unless spec/009-Instrumentation.md is edited IN THE SAME PR. It is an
explicit same-PR co-edit invariant, not a nightly reconciliation.

So the edit was mandatory, and the bead was hot-zone work that neither the bead nor my
brief had classified as such.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR DISPATCH, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT. spec/* is on the fixed hot-zone
list: sequential, never parallel. If two beads that each mint a diagnostic id run
concurrently, both are forced into spec/009 and they collide — and neither one's stated
surface says "spec/". The collision is invisible at dispatch time unless you ask the extra
question.

THE RULE: before dispatching, ask whether the bead can plausibly MINT A NEW DIAGNOSTIC ID.
If yes, treat it as touching spec/009 and sequence it against every other id-minting bead,
regardless of what its Surface line says. Beads that obviously qualify: a new refusal, a new
error shape, a complaint-catalogue entry, anything the guide teaches as "refuses with ...".
rf2-hic-021 (the complaint catalogue) is the clearest future instance — it mints ids by
definition.

AND THE GENERAL SHAPE: a bead's stated Surface line is what its AUTHOR expected to touch,
not what the gates will force. A repo-wide co-edit invariant can drag any bead into a hot
file. Where a gate enforces "change X and Y together", X's owners inherit Y's contention.

OPERATOR AUTHORISATION (2026-08-10 ~20:55 AUSEST, Mike, in session) — RUN THIS WHEN THE MACHINE IS QUIET.

Mike's words: "if you get to no dispatchable background agents, then the machine is quiet
and you can run measurement beads."

SO THE GATE IS NO LONGER 'ask the operator'. It is a measurable condition:
  when the dispatchable queue is exhausted and NO background worker is live,
  the machine is quiet and this measurement bead may be dispatched.

WHY THE CONDITION MATTERS, and it is the whole reason this bead was held all session: a
measurement window run against concurrent workers measures the CONTENTION, not the code.
Five or six shadow-cljs spines and a Chromium/Firefox/WebKit browser lane share this one
machine. Shape 6 says it in terms — "one run at a time, never concurrent" — and concurrency
is precisely the interference the window exists to exclude.

DISPATCH IT AS SHAPE 6, NOT SHAPE 1. The inversion is the whole shape:
  - THE CONTROLS ARBITRATE, NOT THE WORKER'S JUDGEMENT ABOUT THE BOX. A worker asked whether
    its machine was quiet enough will always find a reason it was. If a control fails, or the
    arm-order guard exits 2 (a refusal, deliberately not a plain failure), the run REFUSES and
    the worker reports the refusal without weighing it against how the box felt.
  - A REFUSAL IS A DELIVERABLE. Two of three window beads in one day came back as refusals and
    both were correct. If everything refuses, the window succeeded: you now know the rig cannot
    see what you hoped, which is what it was dispatched to find out. Say this in the brief or
    the worker reads its own refusal as failure and hunts for a way to turn it green.
  - NEVER 'fix' a refusal by loosening a gate. Widening a threshold to admit today's run
    retro-admits the failure the gate was built for.
  - DO NOT IMPROVE THE RIG MID-WINDOW. No new instrument, no extra rungs, no third estimator,
    however obvious. File the improvement and run it as its own window.
  - DO NOT RESTATE A PUBLISHED FIGURE ON THIN EVIDENCE. A worker holding four runs all reading
    below both published figures recorded them WITHOUT publishing. That was right.
  - VERIFY THE BOX WITH REAL COUNTERS. `Win32_Processor.LoadPercentage` read 93% while the true
    value was 11%. Use `Get-Counter '\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time'` and
    `'\System\Processor Queue Length'` — QUEUE LENGTH IS THE DECISIVE NUMBER, because it says
    whether anything is actually waiting for a core, which is the only thing the window cares
    about.
  - ONE RUN AT A TIME. Two runs the worker believes independent still are not.

AND THE MAYOR'S OWN PRECONDITION: verify quiet before dispatching, do not infer it. `git
worktree list` under the re-frame2-worktrees sibling must show no live worker, and the ready
queue must be exhausted of everything else. If a worker reports mid-window, do NOT dispatch
another — the window owns the machine until it finishes or refuses.

The two measurement beads are rf2-hic-006 (named reference profiles + pinned baselines) and
rf2-hic-029 (retaining-host callback identity: the experiment and the verdict). They are a

title: gate: check_doc_slugs cannot see an indented fence, so links inside admonition and list-item code samples validate as prose
description: FOUND BY THE rf2-re0m WORKER (PR #7780, merged as 97d6acecf) and PROPOSED rather than built, correctly — it judged that widening the fence matcher changes corpus-wide validation and deserves its own bead. Verified by the mayor in source before filing. THE BLIND SPOT. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py:159 _FENCE_RE = re.compile(r"^(```|~~~)") Anchored at column 0, with no indent tolerance. Used at line 493 to track whether the scanner is inside a fenced block. So a fence that is INDENTED — four spaces inside an admonition, two inside a list item — is never recognised as a fence at all, and the code inside it is scanned as ORDINARY PROSE. WHAT THAT COST, CONCRETELY. rf2-re0m: a bulk link pass rewrote six lines inside three Clojure examples, adding seven Markdown links that render literally and make copied code invalid. Worse, Markdown parsed the samples' own square brackets as link text, so the rewrite ATE OPENING BRACKETS — `(let [cell-props ...]` became `(let cell-props ...]`, and `[inbox-pane {}]]` lost its `[`. Three fences shipped unbalanced. check_doc_slugs.py passed the whole time, and it was right to by its own lights: every one of those seven links RESOLVED. The gate asks "does this link have a target", never "should this be a link at all", and it could not have asked the second question anyway because it did not know it was looking at code. THE FIX SHAPE (decide, do not assume). Teach the scanner about indented fences. Note that this is NOT simply relaxing the anchor to `^\s*`: - CommonMark allows a fence to be indented up to THREE spaces in ordinary context; - inside a list item or admonition the fence is indented by the container's content indent, which can be far more, and the closing fence must match the opening one's indentation; - a run of four or more spaces in ordinary context is an INDENTED CODE BLOCK, which is a different construct the scanner may also be mishandling — check. So the honest fix tracks container context, or is explicitly bounded and says what it does not cover. A regex that matches any leading whitespace will call a four-space-indented line a fence when it is something else. MEASURE BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THIS IS THE MAIN RISK. Widening the matcher means content previously scanned as prose becomes correctly skipped as code. That is the point — but it can also HIDE a real dangling link that the gate currently catches by accident. Report the full-corpus finding count before and after with the set difference in BOTH directions on the same merge base, and account for every link that stops being checked. A gate that gets quieter is not automatically a gate that got better. THE SECOND HALF, from the same worker's proposal: once fences are recognised, add the assertion that motivated this — a Markdown link (`](`) must not appear inside a fence under docs/design/hicasso/. That is the check that would have caught rf2-re0m at the gate instead of in a merged PR. Decide whether it belongs to this checker or beside it, and whether the scope is that one tree or the corpus. PIN IT. Add self-test cases for: a fence indented inside a list item; one inside an admonition; a fence at column 0 (must not regress); and an indented code block, which is not a fence. CONFIRM EACH REDS AGAINST THE CURRENT IMPLEMENTATION BEFORE FIXING — that ordering is the proof, and it is how rf2-re0m was found. This checker already carries self-tests; follow their shape rather than inventing a harness. FENCES. Do not weaken any existing check. Do not add an ignore mechanism. Do not touch the corpus — this bead is the checker only; the documents rf2-re0m repaired are already correct. ALSO NOTED BY THAT WORKER, PRE-EXISTING AND UNTOUCHED, worth a look while you are in here but NOT this bead's obligation: 50 explicit ids in glossary.md duplicate the generated slug of the heading they precede (`` above `### **portal**`). The anchors work; the checker's duplicate gate only covers HANDBOOK_COMPAT_ANCHORS, so it does not see them. Report whether that is harmless redundancy or a latent ambiguity; do not mass-edit it here. GATES: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py --self-test (or its equivalent — read the file), then the full-corpus run, then sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh. Run each ALONE and echo $? to its own file; never append a filter to a gate's command line.

title: gate: _inline_blocks bounds an inline code span at an indented ATX heading, but python-markdown requires column zero
description:
Found and DECLINED with reasons by the rf2-mmyc worker (PR #7795), which was fenced to five named fence shapes and correctly stopped at five. This is the sixth shape it found, and it is NOT a fence question at all — it reproduces with no fence present.

REPRODUCER

    Prose with `a code span
      ### not a heading to python-markdown
    [in](in-target.md)` closing here.

_LEAF_LINE_BLOCK_RE in scripts/check_doc_slugs.py bounds an inline block at an ATX heading indented three spaces or fewer, following CommonMark. python-markdown's HashHeaderProcessor requires COLUMN ZERO. So on an indented heading the two disagree: the gate sees two unpaired backtick runs, ends the inline block early, and extracts a link that the renderer renders as code. At column zero they agree and there is no disagreement.

DIRECTION: this is a FALSE POSITIVE, not a blind spot. The gate checks a link the renderer never resolves, so the failure mode is a spurious complaint rather than an unvalidated link. That is the safe direction, which is why it was right to leave it rather than widen rf2-mmyc's scope.

SURFACE: _inline_blocks in scripts/check_doc_slugs.py. Related to rf2-8wcbe, which owns that predicate.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING ANYWAY: check_doc_slugs.py runs in the fast-PR spine and in the docs tier, so a false positive here reds a PR for a document that renders correctly — and the fix is to match the renderer's column-zero rule, which is strictly simpler than the CommonMark rule currently encoded.

ACCEPTANCE: the predicate agrees with python-markdown on an indented ATX heading inside an inline code span; a renderer-derived case pins it in the self-test; the full corpus scan is byte-stable or its movement is enumerated.

DO NOT build a second Markdown parser. The established technique on this gate is to drive mkdocs.config.load_config('mkdocs.yml') into a real markdown.Markdown and compare against it — see PR #7795 for the working instrument, and note its --prove mode, which requires a planted known-bad page to move at least three items so a zero cannot be a false zero.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #7798, merged to main as 4d91e357c, alongside rf2-1cpt — one file, one technique: drive MkDocs' own configuration into a real markdown.Markdown and compare the gate against it. No Markdown parser was built. THE FIX: _LEAF_LINE_BLOCK_RE followed CommonMark's three-space allowance for ATX headings; python-markdown does not — HashHeaderProcessor.RE is anchored (?:^|\n)#{1,6} with no leading-space allowance, so an indented ### line is paragraph text. The ATX alternative is hoisted out of the shared prefix, while the thematic break, setext underline and table row correctly keep it, since HRProcessor.SEARCH_RE carries its own leading-space allowance. This also settles an inconsistency INSIDE the file: _HEADING_RE has always required column zero before minting a slug, so the indexer and the block-boundary predicate had disagreed about what a heading is. MY FRAMING ON THIS BEAD WAS TOO NARROW AND THE WORKER CORRECTED IT. I filed it as a false positive only. The same rule also costs the gate in the other direction: for a link whose text spans an indented heading line, the renderer emits the anchor because the three lines are one paragraph, while the gate split the unit and extracted nothing — so a REAL BROKEN LINK went unchecked. title: hic: testing-xray.md promises L2 renders a STORED/REGISTERED view body, but mint-view! retains nothing — decide retention or correct the documents
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-hic-020 WORKER (PR #7783, merged fd7b16fbc) while extracting the L0-L2
test kit. It measured the gap, shaped `ht/render`'s grammar so the fix is purely additive,
and did NOT reach for it — `implementation/hicasso/src/**` was outside its fence. Verified
by the mayor in `collector.cljs` before filing.

TWO NORMATIVE DOCUMENTS DESCRIBE A MECHANISM THAT DOES NOT EXIST.

  tools/xray/spec/testing-xray.md  — L2 invokes "the STORED view body"
  the same document, section 9    — "REGISTERED bodies"

Nothing stores one and nothing registers one. `collector/mint-view!` closes over `body-fn`
and keeps no reference to it; `boundary-head?` is a single property read, and the docstring
states the design in terms — "no registry, no map", the returned value is still the
function, and per the rf2-2rtt6.52 ruling no memo object escapes as the public
representation. The retention the test kit needs was never part of the shape.

THE OBSERVED CONSEQUENCE. `ht/render` can take a body fn, but handed a MINTED HEAD it must
refuse, because there is no way back to the body. The kit therefore refuses with
`:rf.error/hicasso-test-boundary-body-not-retained` and points at L3. Sabotage S3 measured
what happens if that refusal is removed: `Cannot read properties of null (reading
'useContext')` — a React internal error, from the runtime's own guts, with nothing naming
the real cause. That is the failure a consumer would meet.

THE FIX SHAPE, from the worker that measured it: ONE dev-only `unchecked-set` in
`collector/mint-view!`, attaching the body to the minted head under a dev-only property, so
L2 can recover it. `ht/render`'s grammar is already shaped so this lands purely additively —
no signature change, no new public API.

DECIDE, DO NOT ASSUME, and the decision is the substance of this bead:
  (a) retain the body dev-only and let L2 render a minted head; or
  (b) keep the runtime as it is and CORRECT BOTH DOCUMENTS to say L2 takes the body fn,
      not a minted head — the refusal then becomes the documented contract rather than a
      shortfall.
Either is defensible. (a) buys an ergonomic the kit's own users will expect; (b) keeps a
deliberately registry-free runtime registry-free, which is a stated design property and not
an oversight. What is NOT defensible is leaving two normative documents describing storage
and registration that no code performs.

FENCES.
- PRODUCTION ERASURE IS NON-NEGOTIABLE if you choose (a). The property must not survive an
  `:advanced` + `goog.DEBUG=false` build. rf2-hic-007 just landed a working pattern for
  exactly this — `error_source_coord_elision_prod_test.cljs` plus a sentinel namespace
  carrying no `deftest`, because `cljs.test` stamps `:file` into every report map and a test
  namespace names itself in the bundle before anything else does. Copy that shape; a
  sentinel that cannot fail is the fail-open class this repo hunts.
- Do NOT introduce a registry, a map, or any per-view retention beyond the single property.
  The rf2-2rtt6.52 ruling stands: no memo object escapes as the public representation.
- Do NOT weaken or delete the kit's refusal. If you choose (a), the refusal becomes
  unreachable for minted heads and its test should invert to prove the new path works —
  flip and rename it, never delete it, and never loosen it to accept both outcomes.
- `tools/xray/spec/*` must be updated in the SAME PR as any `tools/xray/` change.

SEQUENCING. `collector.cljs` is contended: rf2-hic-014 (Activity attach/detach), rf2-q9cf
(seam audit) and rf2-hic-023 (dev-only projection hooks) may each be in that file. Check
what is in flight before dispatching this, and sequence rather than parallelise.

GATES: the hicasso node suite, the test-kit DOM lane, the freeze gate, the production
elision lane, and sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh in full. Run each ALONE and echo $? to its own
file; never append a filter to a gate's command line. Note that a bead minting any new
`:rf.error/*` id is a FORCED spec/009-Instrumentation.md co-edit in the same PR — the
keyword-catalogue drift gate enforces it, and it has now caught two workers.

The bead offered two defensible shapes and asked the worker to decide. It no longer
decides: retain the body so L2 can render a minted head. Option (b) — correcting the two
documents so the refusal becomes the documented contract — is NOT taken.

WHAT THAT MEANS CONCRETELY. One dev-only `unchecked-set` in `collector/mint-view!`,
attaching the body to the minted head under a dev-only property, so `ht/render` can recover
it. The rf2-hic-020 worker already shaped `ht/render`'s grammar so this lands purely
additively — no signature change, no new public API.

THE FENCES ARE UNCHANGED AND STILL BIND:
  - PRODUCTION ERASURE IS NON-NEGOTIABLE. The property must not survive an `:advanced` +
    `goog.DEBUG=false` build. rf2-hic-007 landed a working pattern for exactly this
    (`error_source_coord_elision_prod_test.cljs`, plus a sentinel namespace carrying NO
    `deftest`, because `cljs.test` stamps `:file` into every report map and a test namespace
    would name itself in the bundle before anything else did). Copy that shape. Prove the
    sentinel can actually fail, then restore.
  - NO registry, NO map, NO per-view retention beyond the single property. The rf2-2rtt6.52
    ruling stands: no memo object escapes as the public representation.
  - Do NOT delete the kit's refusal. Under (a) it becomes unreachable for minted heads, so
    FLIP AND RENAME its test to prove the new path works. Never delete it, never loosen it
    to accept both outcomes.
  - `tools/xray/spec/*` updates in the SAME PR as any `tools/xray/` change.

SEQUENCING, and it is live: `collector.cljs` is contended. rf2-hic-014 owns the attach/
detach path in that same file right now. Your edit is in `mint-view!`, a different function,
so a clean rebase is the likely case — but rebase immediately before pushing and, on any

MY WORDING, in every dispatch brief for this whole session: 'Redirect to a worktree-local log and echo the runner's own exit code into its own file on the VERY NEXT COMMAND.'

title: docs-tooling: the in-fence assertion misses blockquoted fences, and 118 colliding fragment ids are an armed trap for HANDBOOK_COMPAT_ANCHORS
description: BOTH CLAUSES MEASURED AND EXCLUDED BY THE rf2-mmyc WORKER (PR #7785, merged 68a917359), which judged each too large a blast radius for a gate-correctness fix and documented them rather than half-doing them. That was the right call; this bead is where they land. --- CLAUSE 1: the new in-fence assertion has a blind spot in the tree it guards --- rf2-mmyc taught check_doc_slugs.py to see indented fences and added an assertion that a Markdown link must not appear inside a fence under docs/design/hicasso/. **Blockquoted fences are not covered.** `> ```clojure` is a real fence to python-markdown, and they exist in the guarded tree — verified by the mayor, `git grep '^ *> ```' -- 'docs/**' 'spec/**'` returns 12 matching lines, including docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-converged-witness-set.md and docs/design/hicasso/studio/rows-re-adjudicated-on-the-corrected-clock.md. The worker measured 28 content lines corpus-wide. WHY IT WAS EXCLUDED, and this is the number that matters: a prototype covering blockquoted fences flipped **138 lines back to prose and minted 36 rendered ids**. That is a corpus-wide validation change, not a fence fix — far too much to carry inside a bead about indentation. SO THE WORK IS: extend the fence model to blockquoted fences, and measure it the same way rf2-mmyc did — before/after counts in BOTH directions on the same merge base, with every link that stops being checked accounted for, and every rendered id gained or lost named. If the 138/36 figures reproduce, decide explicitly whether that is acceptable rather than absorbing it silently. A gate that gets quieter is not automatically a gate that got better. --- CLAUSE 2: 118 colliding fragment ids are a loaded trap, not harmless redundancy --- Across 15 pages, an explicit `` duplicates the generated slug of the heading it precedes. The concentrations: docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/glossary.md (the mayor counts 61 explicit anchors there), docs/routing/concepts.md (18), spec/015-Data-Classification.md (18), spec/012-Routing.md (10). WHY NOTHING HAS BROKEN, and why that is not reassuring. Duplicate ids are invalid HTML; browsers take the first. In the glossary pattern the explicit anchor comes FIRST and sits above its heading, so deep-links land correctly today — by luck of ordering, not by design. THE LIVE HAZARD: all 118 are traps for `HANDBOOK_COMPAT_ANCHORS`. Adding any one of them to that manifest reds the gate instantly with `DUPLICATE COMPAT ANCHOR`. Currently zero are in the manifest, so the mine is armed and untripped. Someone will eventually add one for a legitimate reason and meet a failure that looks like their own mistake. DECIDE, DO NOT MASS-EDIT. The options are not equal and the choice is the substance: (a) remove the redundant explicit anchors where the generated slug already serves — smallest corpus, but it silently changes which fragment a stale external link hits; (b) keep them and teach the duplicate gate to recognise the anchor-immediately-precedes- its-own-heading pattern as intentional, so the trap disarms without touching prose; (c) leave both and record the hazard where whoever edits HANDBOOK_COMPAT_ANCHORS will see it — the cheapest, and defensible if the pattern is deliberate house style. My inclination is (b) or (c); (a) touches the most files for the least benefit and can break inbound links. Say which you chose and why. --- FENCES --- Do NOT weaken any existing check, and do not add an ignore mechanism or allowlist. rf2-mmyc deliberately made the in-fence predicate `.md`/`#fragment` destinations rather than bare `](`, because `(fn [x](inc x))` is legal Clojure and the stance forbids nagging valid code — keep that. Corpus-wide scoping of the assertion is NOT available: 109 in-repo links live inside fences elsewhere, 88 of them in spec/Spec-Schemas.md as legitimate `;;` commentary, and the only way past that is an allowlist. --- GATES --- python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py --self-test, then the full-corpus run, then python scripts/check_readme_links.py (it imports the same extractor, so it moves with you), then sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh. Run each ALONE and echo $? to its own file; never append a filter to a gate's command line. Write every counting script to a FILE and run the file — a Bash heredoc on this machine strips backslashes, so a regex silently becomes a different regex while the script still exits 0 with a plausible answer. rf2-mmyc's worker gave each of its scripts a `--prove` mode that runs the same machinery over synthetic known-bad input and requires non-zero; that caught a real false zero. Copy that pattern rather than trusting a clean count.

# hic-020 — Extract `re-frame.hicasso.test`: the pure kit (L0–L2)

**Phase**: tooling lane (runs with Phase 1) · **Wave**: B · **Est.**: L · **Depends**: hic-001
**Surface**: `implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/` (exact path; new files); reads bench machinery, mutates nothing in it. The L3 mounted facade is **hic-027**.

## Goal
The unshipped superpower, shipped: extract the bench-private machinery (canonical-DOM compare, intent-script driver, witness helpers) into a supported, layered testing namespace. A named first move.

## Deliverables
- **L0 public contract**: the stated pattern + helpers for pure handler/subscription/state-transition tests (thin, but named and documented — a worker must know what L0 officially is).
- **L1 surface**: pure data/property helpers for codecs, intents, controlled/revision laws, and native-form macro-expansion assertions; the canonical-DOM comparator + intent-capture as public helpers.
- **L2 restricted semantic-tree harness**: invoke a registered hook-free body under a discardable read resolver; versioned semantic tree with `find`/`attrs`/`text`/`intents` helpers. Honest opacity: hosts, hooks, raw React, `n/$` results refuse with a pointer to L3; missing fixtures refuse. Audit the existing versioned structural-tree/Spec-011 assertion utilities first and reuse compatible data/helpers — no second schema without cause.
- Positive and sabotage controls for every tier delivered here.

## Acceptance
- The existing dogfood witnesses re-expressed on the public kit (proof of sufficiency); opacity refusals tested; no fake hooks runtime or shallow renderer anywhere.

## Worker notes
Read synth-codex §9; `codex/testing-xray.md`. The kit ships as its own reachable-when-used module — zero production reachability.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)

Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).

title: hic: h/defview's emitted body fn binds its own name, so a same-named helper recurses forever
description:
Found by the rf2-kjf5 worker (PR #7801) and NOT fixed there — it is a public-door macro bug and a naming decision, so it was correctly left alone.

THE DEFECT

h/defview names its emitted body fn `<sym>-body`. A NAMED fn binds its own name inside its body. So the spelling the kit itself teaches:

    (defn row-body [props] ...)
    (h/defview row [p] (row-body p))

expands to

    (fn row-body [p] (row-body p))

and recurses forever. The programmer's helper is shadowed by the macro's own emitted name.

EVIDENCE, both directions

- Confirmed by macroexpansion.
- Then MEASURED: rendering the suite's existing `greeting` head answers
  {:refused nil, :message "Maximum call stack size exceeded"}.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL NOW

It was unreachable while a minted head ALWAYS refused — the refusal fired before the body could run. PR #7801 (rf2-kjf5) made dev builds retain the body, which is what surfaced it. So this is not a regression introduced by that change; it is a latent defect that change exposed.

IT BITES IN PRODUCTION TOO. The worker states it bites under React exactly as it bites at L2. This is not a test-only artefact.

WHY P1

A programmer following the documented idiom gets infinite recursion with a stack-overflow message that names nothing useful. There is no diagnostic, no refusal id, and nothing points at the macro. That is the opposite of the ergonomics this project is built for.

SHAPE OF THE FIX — A NAMING DECISION, NOT ONLY A CODE ONE

The emitted fn does not need to carry a name a programmer can collide with. Options include gensymming it, or namespacing the emitted name so no ordinary helper can shadow-collide, or emitting an anonymous fn and carrying the display name by another route. Note that the emitted name currently feeds `displayName` and the performance entry id, so whatever is chosen must keep those readable — see the `displayName` stamp in mint-view! and re-frame.hicasso.impl.codec.

CURRENT STATE IN THE TREE

The rf2-kjf5 worker named its NEW fixture `farewell-text` rather than `farewell-body`, with a comment saying exactly why, and deliberately LEFT `greeting` carrying the defect so the reproducer stays in the tree. Do not "tidy" `greeting` away without replacing the reproducer.

ACCEPTANCE

- The documented `<name>-body` helper spelling works rather than recursing.
- A witness pins it, red-first, at L2 AND under React — the worker established it bites in both.
- displayName and the performance entry id remain readable; check the existing witnesses for those before changing the emitted name.
- If the answer is instead to forbid the spelling, it must REFUSE with a named diagnostic rather than overflowing the stack, and the guide must stop teaching it.

Surface: the h/defview macro expansion in implementation/hicasso/, plus whatever carries displayName/entry-id.
notes:
CLOSED VIA PR #7807, and the worker corrected a premise the bead carried: the emitted body fn's name does NOT feed displayName or the performance entry id. Both key on view-name, the '<ns>/<sym>' string the macro computes on its own line and passes to mint-view! as a value; nothing under implementation/hicasso reads a body fn's JS .name (grepped). So the constraint the bead flagged as the hard part cost nothing — which is what made the strongest option affordable.

THE ANSWER CHOSEN: the emitted fn is ANONYMOUS, (fn ~argv ~@body). Not a gensym and not a reserved prefix — those make the collision improbable, anonymity makes it UNREPRESENTABLE. A fn with no name has nothing to shadow with, so there is no reserved spelling to document and nothing a later edit can reintroduce by accident. It also needs no new :rf.error/* id, hence no spec/009 co-edit and no race with rf2-hic-021. Refusing the spelling was the alternative and was declined: the spelling is correct Clojure and the guide teaches helper extraction throughout.

RED-FIRST, both levels: two witnesses written before the macro changed, both RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded — one at L2, one through a real react-dom/server render of a boundary under mount/provider, so the collision is pinned under React too, not at L2 alone. Both controls stayed green either side, isolating the collision.

Also: the rf2-kjf5 reproducer (greeting in test_kit_cljs_test.cljs) is now RENDERED rather than merely declared, so it pins the fixed behaviour instead of sitting inert; and hmr_remount_cljs_test.cljs's namespace docstring, which documented the old expansion, was corrected. Declined to touch the freehand bench donor carrying the same expression — its frozen-sources row is retired and churning the measured tree to fix a package defect costs the one thing that tree provides.

Apply every hic-065 applied-default in one prompt sweep (land it before hic-060/068 start writing docs — that ordering is the merge-conflict mitigation for a repo-wide change). Operator overrides, when they arrive, re-run this protocol as a diff-sized second sweep. Renames are easy — the discipline is completeness.

## Deliverables

- Deprecation shims explicitly **not** added (pre-alpha, no back-compat).
- The naming ledger updated: every row status=done with the commit; the facade-freeze and Phase-3 freeze records updated to the final names.
- Full test suite green after the sweep (the witnesses are the proof the renames broke nothing).

## Acceptance
A grep for every retired name over `implementation/hicasso` + user-facing docs returns zero hits (greps recorded); suite green; ledger closed.

## Worker notes
Mechanical only — any rename that turns out to be *semantic* (behavior implicated) stops that row and files a bead instead of improvising. hic-060/061 build on this bead's output, so land it promptly after the ruling.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")

PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.

1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.

5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.

9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.

title: docs-tooling: _strip_fences' docstring claims the renderer agrees at '>' plus five spaces, and a prefix sweep suggests it does not
description:

A SWEEP'S GENERATOR DEFINES WHICH FAILURE DIRECTIONS IT CAN EVER FIND (2026-08-11, rf2-skpf worker, PR #7811).

THE CASE. PR #7803 swept 1,728 quoted-fence prefix triples against the real MkDocs renderer to characterise a docs-gate defect, and its numbers held up. But EVERY shape that generator emits has BALANCED backtick runs on lines 1 and 3. So the inline-masking defect could only ever manifest there as pairing that should not happen — a FALSE POSITIVE. The false-negative half needs an ODD backtick-run count either side of a boundary, a shape the fence-triple generator CANNOT EMIT BY CONSTRUCTION.

Result: in that domain the defect was 188/188 false positives and its expensive half was invisible. Not because 1,728 was too few — because the generator excluded the direction. Running 17,280 would have found nothing more.

THE LESSON, in the worker's words: 'a sweep generator defines its reachable failure directions, and the direction it excludes is invisible no matter how many shapes you run.' A sweep's SIZE is not its coverage; its GENERATOR is. So a big clean sweep is not evidence of absence outside the directions its generator can express — and the false-negative direction is usually the expensive one, because it is the one where a checker stays silent.

THE COUNTERMEASURE THAT WORKED: two probes over the same boundary, each mapping the disagreement onto the OPPOSITE error direction (a mask probe and a wrap probe over the same middle line), so neither direction can hide. When commissioning or reading a sweep, ask: what shapes can this generator NOT produce, and which error direction does that make unreachable? Put the answer in the report.

MAYOR APPLICATION: when a worker reports 'N shapes swept, zero disagreements', that is a claim about the generator, not about the surface. Ask for the generator's excluded shapes before treating it as clearance.

title: docs gate: lazy blockquote continuation can desynchronise inline-code masking
description:
Found by the merged-PR audit of PR #7803 (merged 2026-08-10T12:39:24Z as 062e87571352a153a869c79427313be5f937a61f).

THE MEASURED RESIDUAL. PR #7803 swept 1,728 quoted-fence prefix triples against the real MkDocs renderer. Its fence repair reduced disagreements from 235 to 123 with zero introduced, but the remaining 123 split into 72 cases where the renderer emits a link the gate never checks and 51 cases where the gate checks a link the renderer masks. In every residual case the renderer and _strip_fences agree that no fence exists; the disagreement is whether lazy blockquote continuation lets stray backtick runs pair into an inline code span. The surface is _inline_blocks / _mask_code_spans, not the quoted-fence scanner.

THE OWNER WAS NEVER DURABLE. PRs #7785, #7795 and #7803, plus rf2-1cpt/rf2-b2cr/rf2-feit ledger text, cite rf2-8wcbe as the owner. That ID exists neither in the pushed Dolt ledger nor in origin/main's issues.jsonl. A broad duplicate search found only rf2-b2cr, whose narrower indented-ATX mismatch shipped in PR #7798 and is correctly closed. This Bead is the missing owner; do not reopen rf2-b2cr or rf2-1cpt for it.

BOUND. #7803 reports every residual outside its declared depth-1 / in-quote-indent<=3 fence domain (48 nested-quote openers, 75 indented-code-block territory), with zero current-corpus movement. Do not expand the fence scanner or build a Markdown parser. First recover one renderer-derived false-negative witness and one agreeing control, with a --prove path that demonstrates the instrument can move. Establish whether the false-negative is reachable through supported documentation authoring. If it is, make the smallest parity correction in _inline_blocks/_mask_code_spans and pin both directions; if it is not, document that bound and correct the ghost-owner references without speculative implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A real-renderer witness proves or disproves a supported-surface false negative; any live mismatch receives a narrow _inline_blocks/_mask_code_spans fix plus regression/control coverage and corpus movement accounting. No fence-scanner widening and no general Markdown parser.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7809: stronger independent evidence and a new stale-reference surface. A real-MkDocs sweep of all 729 quote+0..8-space opener/body/closer triples, compared through the gate's actual _extract_links door, found 180 shapes where the renderer emits a link the gate never reports and zero in the other direction; every false negative has the opener past the allowance. It also landed rf2-8wcbe into scripts/check_doc_slugs.py's live docstring (and repeated it in PR/closure text) even though that ID does not exist. PR #7811 merged (fc4448d86). VERDICT: reachable, in the expensive direction, fixed — and the measurement produced a finding worth more than the fix.

TWO FALSE-NEGATIVE WITNESSES, both renderer-derived. (1) A bare '>' is a BLANK LINE inside the quote: BlockQuoteProcessor.clean maps a markers-only line to empty, so two backtick runs land in different paragraphs and neither opens a span — the gate joined across the break, paired them, and masked a real link out of existence. REACHABILITY MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED, and this is the right shape of argument: 569 bare-'>' lines in the corpus (house style), 0 currently adjacent to an odd backtick-run count. So the gate is ONE TYPO away from silently dropping a link in 569 places. Shape 2 occurs 0 times today and was fixed anyway — two lines, and it makes the code match its own documented rule.

In the fence-triple domain this defect produced ONLY false positives, 188 of 188; its false-negative half is unreachable from those triples AT ALL. Not for want of shapes — every triple #7803 generates has BALANCED backtick runs either side, so the defect can only manifest there as pairing that should not happen. The false-negative half needs an ODD run count across a boundary, which that generator cannot emit by construction. A purpose-built two-probe boundary rig (44 shapes, 18 -> 8) was required, each probe mapping the same disagreement onto the opposite error direction so neither could hide. Recorded in bd memory as sweep-generator-defines-reachable-failure-directions.

MOVEMENT, both directions: 0 links newly checked, 0 lost, but 117 files re-partition and 34,541 -> 34,985 inline units (270 replaced by 714) — the path is emphatically not dead. value:
A WITNESS DERIVED FROM THE FIX INHERITS THE FIX'S BLIND SPOTS — five instances in one session (2026-08-10/11, hicasso).

THE SHAPE: a test or table whose STATED SCOPE EXCEEDS THE CASES IT ACTUALLY DRIVES. Each was green, each was honest, each claimed more than it checked.

1. rf2-hic-020 — a runtime/kit parity table claiming both arms of the raw escape, driving only the VALID raw component.
2. rf2-hic-007 — a completeness test claiming all six constructor fields unforgeable, running only where declaring! had already supplied real values; outside every extent the guarantee did not hold.
3. rf2-hic-012 — a comment recording the EXPECTED result as though it were the measured one, contradicted by the very row it annotated.
4. rf2-hic-021 — a round-trip check whose both directions ranged over ids THAT EXIST, so thirteen taught refusals with no id at all satisfied it VACUOUSLY (fail-open).
5. rf2-hic-022 — a shadow-detection walker whose letfn arm reads [nm params] and collects params only when the second node is a VECTOR; in multi-arity letfn it is a LIST, so every arity is missed. PR body and README both claimed letfn was covered.

WHY IT RECURS, and it is not carelessness: the witness is written FROM the fix, so it drives the shapes the author had in mind while fixing. The shapes that break it are exactly the ones the author did not think of — the same set. Test-after-fix is structurally biased toward passing.

THE COUNTERMEASURE, now standing in briefs: DERIVE THE WITNESS FROM THE GRAMMAR OF THE THING, NOT FROM THE FIX. Enumerate the legal shapes of the construct (for letfn: single-arity vector, multi-arity lists, docstring/prepost variants) and drive each. Require the PR body to state which shapes of the grammar were driven AND which were not — the second list is the valuable one, and writing it is what surfaces the gap.

SISTER RULE: see sweep-generator-defines-reachable-failure-directions — a generator's excluded shapes make a whole error DIRECTION invisible. Same disease at a different scale: coverage is defined by what the instrument can express, not by how much of it you ran.

title: hic: realize-deep cannot see a deferral parked in a mutable reference — a real hole in I7's enforcement
description:
MEASURED BY THE rf2-hic-011 WORKER (PR #7763), row 11 of the I7 legality matrix. It is a real hole in enforcement, NOT a test artefact, and the worker measured it rather than disclaiming it.

THE HOLE. A read deferred into a mutable reference and forced inside another body is NOT refused. codec/realize-deep cannot see it: it walks the returned structure, and a deferral parked in an atom or volatile is not in that structure. realize-deep's own docstring already declares this a limit, which is why the worker treated it as a measured boundary of I7 rather than a bug in its own suite.

WHY IT IS FILED SEPARATELY. Closing it is a RUNTIME change, and rf2-hic-011 was fenced out of implementation/hicasso/src/ with an explicit STOP. Its PR changed no source.

ALREADY DONE FOR YOU: row 11 is written so that CLOSING the hole turns it RED. So the witness is in place before the fix, and a worker taking this bead has an oracle from the first minute. Read that row before designing anything.

WHAT TO DECIDE FIRST, because it may not be worth closing. realize-deep walks a returned value; seeing into arbitrary mutable references is a different and much larger capability.
