title: hic-012 — Kernel: multi-root + frame isolation + root-scoped hydration adoption
description:
# hic-012 — Kernel: multi-root + frame isolation + root-scoped hydration adoption

**Phase**: 1 · **Wave**: B · **Est.**: L · **Depends**: hic-001
**Surface**: `implementation/hicasso/test/.../roots_frames_*` (new); root-lifecycle/hydration files (distinct from the collector file — parallel with hic-010)

## Goal
Independent roots and frames cannot observe or corrupt one another; hydration adoption and mismatch attribution are root-scoped, never process-global.

## Deliverables
- Two live roots, two frames: dispatch, subscribe, unmount each independently; assert zero cross-frame reads or dispatches.
- Two *overlapping hydrating* roots with independent mismatch complaints and independent teardown.
- The shared hydration adoption window moved to root scope (or each remaining global justified in writing — feeding hic-017).
- Root-unmount failure containment: one root's teardown error cannot strand the other's state.

## Acceptance
- All witnesses green with residue-before-reset; sabotage: re-globalizing the adoption window must turn the overlapping-roots witness red.

## Worker notes
Read `codex/adversarial-risks.md` process-global + hydration-isolation rows; `codex/react-compatibility-notes.md` hydration section (identifierPrefix, per-root error callbacks).

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)

Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7800 (2026-08-10): correct implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/roots_frames_shared_frame_dom_cljs_test.cljs:240-243. The comment currently says arming the reaper unconditionally makes S2 red. PR #7800's measured M1 result and this bead's close reason both say that mutation stayed green because the callback rechecks reader count; removing only the callback guard also stayed green, and only removing both guards (M1-double-prime) produced the five S2 failures. Keep this a narrow evidence-comment correction; the four test rows and production behavior are sound.

MAYOR 2026-08-11 ~00:2x AUSEST — QUEUED FOR THE NEXT FREE SLOT (six workers live).
Legitimate audit reopen: there is a 'chore(beads): audit merged PR #7800' commit
and the note above is the hook's. Do NOT re-close.

THE CHARGE IS FOUR LINES, and it is worth noticing WHY it exists.

roots_frames_shared_frame_dom_cljs_test.cljs:240-243 comments that arming the
reaper unconditionally makes S2 red. That is the OPPOSITE of what the same PR
measured. The worker's own report was explicit and correct — M1 (release-cell!
arms unconditionally) stayed GREEN at 0 failures, M1' (reader check removed from
inside the reaper) also stayed GREEN, and only M1'' (both guards removed) produced

A later reader trusting that comment would believe a single-point mutation reds S2,

MY BRIEFS STATE THE IDEAL AND OMIT THE SANCTIONED FALLBACK, SO WORKERS IMPROVISE THE FORBIDDEN ONE (2026-08-11).

WHAT I HAVE BEEN WRITING, in every dispatch this session: 'run gates in the FOREGROUND to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail.' Full stop.

WHAT THE METHOD ACTUALLY SAYS (dispatch-prompt-template.md line 146-153): the same rule, PLUS a fallback I never pass on — 'If you background a gate anyway, POLL ITS LOG ON A TIMER; never end a turn waiting to be woken.'

WHY THE OMISSION BITES. The fast-PR spine outruns the harness's per-tool-call ceiling. A worker obeying my brief literally CANNOT finish it in one foreground call, so it is forced off-script with no sanctioned path — and every one of them improvises the same forbidden move: background it, end the turn, promise to report 'the moment it lands.' The template names that exact outcome ('standing by through idle tick after idle tick while its branch sits unmoved — four such incidents in a single day').

THREE MORE TONIGHT: prosetruth-hic012 twice (its own words: 'Started foreground, outran the tool ceiling, detached and blocked on') and catalogrows-vkle once. All three recovered intact the moment I sent a status request — which is also what the template says happens. The work was never at risk; the WALL CLOCK was, and so was my slot count, because a worker that has ended its turn looks alive by every measure I have.

THE CORRECTED BRIEF WORDING, use from now on:

  'Run gates in the FOREGROUND to completion — never piped through tail/head/grep. If a gate outruns the tool-call ceiling, DO NOT end your turn waiting to be woken: background it BY ABSOLUTE PATH, then poll its log and its .exit file in a bounded loop within the same turn until it exits, and read the exit code from the file. A turn that has ended has nothing left to wake it, and the completion notification does not always arrive.'

GENERAL LESSON, and it is the fourth boilerplate defect this session: A RULE THAT IS SOMETIMES UNSATISFIABLE NEEDS ITS ESCAPE HATCH STATED, or the worker invents one — and the invented one is the failure the rule existed to prevent. When I compress a method rule for a brief, the clause I am most likely to drop is the fallback, because it reads as secondary. It is not: it is the half that governs the hard case.

THE HARNESS HARD-KILLS A FOREGROUND COMMAND AT 10 MINUTES — so 'run the gate in the foreground to completion' is UNSATISFIABLE for the fast-PR spine (2026-08-11, measured by the catalogrows-vkle worker).

ITS WORDS: 'a foreground run is not achievable here — the harness hard-kills foreground commands at 10 minutes, and my first foreground attempt died exactly there (exit 143, mid-JVM tier).' Exit 143 is SIGTERM. I hit the same class myself at the mayor's own 2-minute tool ceiling when chaining bd export behind other measurements under six concurrent workers.

CONSEQUENCE FOR BRIEFS, and this supersedes the bare 'foreground only' line: the spine must be DETACHED to finish. That is not a violation and must not be briefed as one. What matters is not foreground-ness — it is (a) unpiped output, (b) the exit code captured on the SAME command line into a file, (c) the gate root line checked against the worker's own worktree, and (d) THE WORKER STAYING IN ITS TURN, polling the log and .exit file until it exits, rather than ending the turn to wait for a notification that may never arrive.

The catalogrows worker did exactly this and said so plainly: 'The run is detached only so it can finish; the output is unpiped and the exit code is captured the way you specified, and I am waiting on it rather than reporting around it.' That is the correct shape.

SEE ALSO brief-must-carry-the-poll-fallback-for-long-gates — same defect, this is the measured number behind it.

WHEN A GATE FAILED BECAUSE ITS PREDICATE WAS TOO NARROW, WIDENING THE PREDICATE REPEATS THE DEFECT (2026-08-11, rf2-hic-021 repair, PR #7813).

THE SETUP. The complaint-catalogue checker reads four file families. Its CI invocation sat inside a job gated on the changed-surface output cljs_node_test, which only implementation/hicasso/** sets true — so register-only, spec-only and guide-only edits all skipped the gate silently. The audit's bounded repair said: give it a CI path whose changed-surface inputs include every family it reads. My message to the worker repeated that framing.

THE WORKER DECLINED THE FRAMING, and it is right: "The defect being repaired IS an arm that failed to cover a checker's inputs, so A NEW ARM IS A FRESH CHANCE TO MAKE THE SAME MISTAKE and needs re-widening whenever the checker learns a new file." A widened predicate is correct exactly until the checker reads one more path — and nothing makes anyone revisit it then.

WHAT IT BUILT INSTEAD: an UNCONDITIONAL job — no needs:, no if: — listed in all-required-passed. That covers all four families and every future one BY CONSTRUCTION, with no predicate to keep in sync. It then drove all three previously-dead families red (R1, R3, R8 -> exits [1,1,1]), restored byte-identically, re-ran [0,0,0], AND drove the routing claim itself red by re-gating the job on cljs_node_test and watching the new scheduling test fail verbatim.

THE GENERAL RULE: a conditional that must be kept in sync with a growing input set is a standing liability, and the cheap fix (widen it) preserves the liability while looking like a repair. Prefer removing the condition when the job is cheap enough to always run. Ask "what makes someone update this predicate the next time the thing it guards changes?" — if the answer is "nothing", the predicate is the bug.

MAYOR NOTE: I passed the audit's remedy through verbatim. A worker that treated the bounded repair as a FLOOR rather than a CEILING produced a better answer. Brief the PROBLEM and the FENCE; do not hand over the audit's proposed mechanism as though it were settled.

SHELL NOTE TO SELF: this memory was first written with backticks around needs:/if: and bash ran them as command substitution. Use a quoted heredoc for any memory containing backticks.

title: hic: the test kit's refuse! carries the exact bypass just fixed in the package constructor
description:
Reported by the rf2-hic-007 worker, which correctly did not touch it: the file was fenced to the then-live rf2-hic-020 worker. That fence is now GONE — rf2-hic-020 closed and PR #7805 merged.

THE DEFECT. implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test.cljs:177, refuse! does (merge {..shape..} extra) — extra LAST. So a caller's payload can erase or replace :recovery, :where, and even :rf.error/id. This is the same expression, in the same direction, that rf2-hic-007 just removed from the package's own fail! (PR #7797, merge 4d86a0cff): there the fix was to merge extra UNDER the shape and to have the completeness check read the EMITTED MAP rather than the constructor's arguments.

WHY A P1 IN A TEST KIT. The kit is a shipped public surface — rf2-hic-020's whole deliverable was that the kit RAISES THE RUNTIME'S REFUSAL rather than paraphrasing it, and that parity is now asserted structurally by rows carrying :where. A constructor whose payload can overwrite :rf.error/id can make the kit report a different refusal than the one that occurred, which defeats the parity the kit exists to provide.

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX, and it is small: merge extra UNDER, and make whatever completeness check exists read the emitted map. Follow what landed in impl/error.cljc — read it first, and match it rather than inventing a second idiom.

WITNESS, and this is the part the last three beads on this surface all got wrong: drive the case where the guarantee is WEAKEST, not the case where it happens to hold. A test that calls refuse! with a well-formed extra proves nothing. Pass a payload that names :rf.error/id, :recovery and :where and assert the constructor's values win. Mutate the merge order and quote the red.

FENCE. Do not add a new refusal id, a new catalogue row, or reserved-key machinery — the rf2-hic-007 worker considered a reserved-key refusal for the package constructor and declined it, on the reasoning that policing package-internal authors is standing cost without a paying use case. That reasoning holds here. Merge order alone.

DECLINED, correctly and per the fence: no completeness guard added to the kit. The bead fenced to 'merge order alone', and there is no existing check to point at the emitted map.

title: docs gate: reference-style links are never validated — 10 live unchecked links in the corpus
description:
MEASURED by the rf2-skpf worker (PR #7811) while working the inline-masking residual. It corrected the stale comment that hid this and deliberately left the defect alone, because fixing it was outside its charge.

THE DEFECT. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py's _LINK_RE only matches inline links. Its comment claimed the corpus contains no reference-style links "per spot-check". It does. Ten links that the renderer emits from `[ref]: dest` definitions go completely unchecked:
  - 7 in tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md
  - 1 in tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md
  - 2 in tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md

THIS IS A LIVE FALSE NEGATIVE, which is the expensive direction for a link checker. Ten links could break today and the gate would stay green and silent. Compare rf2-b2cr, where the same class was found for indented heading lines: the renderer emitted the anchor while the gate had split the unit and checked nothing.

WHY THE COMMENT MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE CODE. "Per spot-check" is an unverified assertion wearing the clothes of a measurement, and it stood long enough to define the gate's scope. The worker replaced it with the actual count. Whoever takes this bead should keep that discipline: state the number you measured, not the impression you formed.

THE WORK. Extend link extraction to reference-style definitions and their uses, including collapsed (`[ref][]`) and shortcut (`[ref]`) forms, and resolve each to its definition before checking the target. Match the behaviour of the real MkDocs renderer — mkdocs.config.load_config('mkdocs.yml') into a real markdown.Markdown — rather than hand-deriving what you think it does; that is how #7803, #7809 and #7811 all established their claims, and it is why their numbers held up.

BOUNDS: no general Markdown parser, no fence-scanner widening. This is an extraction gap, not a parsing one.

WITNESS: red first. Point one of the ten at a target that does not exist and show the gate reporting it by file and line; then a control that stays green. Account for corpus movement in both directions — how many links the gate now checks that it did not, and whether any previously-checked link stopped being checked.

GATE NOTE: check_doc_slugs.py is SILENT ON SUCCESS, so exit 0 is not evidence it saw your file. Prove teeth by planting a bogus anchor, quoting the exit 1 that names file and line, then restoring byte-identically. The file also carries a --self-test suite (106+ cases, 10 added by #7811) — any change must keep it green and should add to it.

DEPENDS ON PR #7811 MERGING FIRST — it rewrites _inline_blocks and the surrounding masking, and this bead's surface sits in the same region.

PR #7816 merged (19c750f9b). THE WORKER CORRECTED THE BEAD'S OWN PREMISE, and the correction is instructive: the count is NINE, not ten. My ten was a MULTISET DIFF between renderer hrefs and extractor output, which answers a different question — a reference link whose destination is also written inline in the same file cancels out of that diff, and an unrelated miss lands in it. Counted at the source instead, by marking ReferenceInlineProcessor.makeTag across 719 files: 9 reference-emitted anchors from 7 definitions (6 in 003-Tool-Catalogue.md, 1 in DESIGN-RATIONALE.md, 2 in 002-Tool-Registry.md). MOVEMENT ACCOUNTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: 19,675 -> 19,682 checked links, +7 / -0. Zero removed is not free and the worker said so: definition lines are blanked before the inline scan, which is exactly the change that could quietly take a real link with it. Declared and deliberately NOT closed: a definition inside an indented container (needs container state, i.e. the parser the bead forbids), a use inside a raw HTML block, reference-style images, autolinks — all four measured, all zero in corpus. value:
I REAPED A WORKTREE MID-GATE, AND I HAD THE WORKER'S OWN WORDS SAYING IT WAS NOT DONE (2026-08-11, catalogrows-vkle / PR #7813).

WHAT HAPPENED. The worker sent two interim messages. The second said, verbatim: "Holding for the spine — not done yet, and I won't report a colour I don't have." Minutes later I merged #7813 and reaped its worktree in the same breath. Its spine was in the JVM tier. git worktree list stopped showing the tree, .git went, gate.log was deleted mid-write, and the run died. The worker found gate.exit = 1 afterwards and CORRECTLY REFUSED TO REPORT IT AS A FAILURE — that 1 was written by a script whose own checkout had been deleted underneath it. My cleanup manufactured a red.

WHY I DID IT, because the mechanism matters more than the apology: I batched the reap into the merge pass. The hygiene procedure forbids exactly this — "Never pair a merge with a reap in the same breath, and never put the reap in the merge loop." A merged PR is the moment a tree LOOKS finished, which is precisely why the pull is dangerous. I had also, without noticing, promoted "the agent sent me a message" to "the agent reported done". Those are not the same thing and the difference was written in the message I was reading.

SO THE REAP CONDITION IS NARROWER THAN I HAD IT: not "the agent has spoken", but "the agent has reported that it has FINISHED". An interim status, a progress note, a partial hand-off, a PR-opened announcement — none of these are completion. A BACKGROUND GATE STILL RUNNING IS THE WORKER STILL RUNNING, even though nothing in the branch, the tree or the PR shows it.

WHY IT LOOKED SAFE, and this is the trap for next time: every proxy agreed. PR merged, branch clean, commits pushed, no junction, worker had messaged recently. All six of the forbidden proxies pointed at "done" simultaneously. That is not evidence; that is what a disciplined worker mid-gate looks like BY DESIGN, since commit-and-push-as-you-go is what every brief demands.

WHAT SAVED IT: the work was committed and pushed incrementally, so only the RUN was lost, not the diff. And CI's 90/90 on the merged PR is strictly better evidence than a local spine anyway — which is worth remembering when tempted to wait on a local gate at all.

THE RULE I AM ADDING TO MY OWN LOOP: before any reap, re-read the LAST message from that agent and find the sentence where it says it is finished. If I cannot quote that sentence, the worktree does not get reaped. Cost of waiting: one stale directory.

title: docs(hicasso): the native-IME manual checklist claims app-db stays clean until commit, and the runtime says otherwise
description:
MEASURED by the rf2-hic-016 worker (PR #7815), which was fenced to the spec and testbed and correctly stopped rather than taking this.

THE FALSEHOOD. docs/design/hicasso/native-ime-manual-witness.md tells an operator that app-db stays clean until commit during a composition. It does not: `shadowed-props` calls the author's handler BEFORE it branches on `composing-input?`, so an ACCEPTING model takes every composing update and moves right through the exchange. Read the runtime before writing anything — the claim is about behaviour, so the source is the authority, not this bead and not the old checklist.

WHY P2. This is a checklist a human follows by hand during an operator session, and it tells them to expect something the runtime does not do. A tester who sees app-db change mid-composition will read a correct implementation as broken, or — worse — will "confirm" the checklist by not looking. It is the same species as rf2-hpoy: a document teaching something the code does not do.

THE WORK, per the worker's own hand-off:
  - Checks 3 and 6 must be NARROWED to what the runtime actually does. That behaviour is now measured in three engines by PR #7815 — read its spec sections rather than re-deriving them.
  - §4 and §5 should point at the new trace table and the armed bump/unmount buttons the testbed gained in #7815. Those exist because a real pointer-down closes the composition before a clicked action can land inside it, and because the store-on-screen readout is the only thing that separates "reached the store" from "the store took it".

SEQUENCING, and the worker checked this so you do not have to: this file is NOT in any other worker's diff. Only the hic-005 table in product/dispositions.md would need to wait on another owner — do not touch that table here.

FENCES: no runtime source edits. No spec/* (hot zone). Do not restate the three-engine coverage; cite #7815.

GATES: mkdocs build --strict does NOT cover docs/design/** (exclude_docs). scripts/check_doc_slugs.py DOES validate its links and anchors and IS SILENT ON SUCCESS — prove it saw your file by planting a bogus anchor, quoting the exit 1 naming file and line, then restoring byte-identically. Nothing validates tables; if you touch one, count columns by hand and say what you counted.

LONG GATES: the harness hard-kills a FOREGROUND command at 10 minutes (exit 143). If a gate outruns that, background it by ABSOLUTE path and poll its log and .exit file within the same turn — never end a turn waiting to be woken.
close_reason:
PR #7817 merged (399eb4ebe). CONFIRMED AT THE SOURCE and the old check could not have caught it: both change-slot wrappers call the author's handler UNCONDITIONALLY; composing-input? gates the CONVERGE, never the dispatch. So 'app-db clean until commit' was false as stated, and an operator following the checklist would have read a correct implementation as broken.

Checks 3 and 6 narrowed to what the runtime actually guarantees (the screen), with the trace row supplying the falsifier that was simply NOT ON THE PAGE before PR #7815 added it. Check 5 also touched — its 'nor written to the model' clause contradicted the corrected check 3 one screen above, which is the ordinary way a half-correction leaves a document arguing with itself.

Merge ordering was respected: #7815 landed first, so the instruments this checklist names exist on main before the checklist points at them.

title: docs(hicasso): does the witness matrix require a fallback the policy makes optional?
description:
Flagged, correctly, by the rf2-kckr worker (PR #7810), which declined to answer it because the bead did not name it and because it is a QUESTION rather than a defect.

THE SITE. docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md:25 — a table cell in the witness matrix reading "otherwise source refusal plus deterministic fallback and client activation".

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY THE SAME BUG. Five sites carrying "source-located refusal + deterministic fallback" as the DEFINITION of Client-only have now been corrected (PRs #7806 and #7810), because impl/codec.cljs makes bare :client-only the default and the fallback optional. This one is different in kind: it states what the WITNESS asserts, not what the policy requires. A witness that happens to exercise the fallback arm is entitled to say so.

SO THE QUESTION IS: should the matrix admit a bare-:client-only row — a surface that declares no fallback and renders nothing until adoption — as a case the witnesses cover? If yes, the cell is under-specified and wants a second row. If no, the cell is right and this bead closes as a verified no-op.

ANSWER IT BY READING THE WITNESSES, not the prose. Find what the matrix's rows actually drive, and say whether a bare-:client-only surface is among them. If it is not, that is the more interesting finding — the default configuration would be the one shape with no witness — and it becomes a test bead rather than a docs one.

BOUNDS: nothing validates tables under docs/design/**, so if you edit the table, count its columns by hand and say what you counted. Do not restate the policy definition; the five corrected sites are the authority and PR #7810's wording is what they say.

LOW PRIORITY DELIBERATELY. This is the tail of a claim already corrected everywhere it was load-bearing. If the answer turns out to be "the cell is fine", close it and say so — that is a good outcome, not a wasted bead.
close_reason: PR #7817 merged (399eb4ebe). NOT a no-op, and not a second row either — the worker answered the question by reading the witnesses rather than the prose, as asked. arm1/host_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs shows the bare arm HAS its own witnesses at every stage, including client-only-hydrates-with-nothing-there-and-mounts-after-adoption, deliberately paired with the fallback arm's twin. So the matrix was not missing a case. The actual defect was narrower: that cell was the ONLY Client-only row conjoining the fallback as REQUIRED ('plus ... and'), while its siblings already say 'if the caller supplies one' or 'refusal/fallback'. Fixed the cell AND the paragraph below the table that generalised the same conjunction to every row. title: hic — wire implementation/hicasso into the CI changed-surface classifier + schedule its freeze gate
description:
# Wire implementation/hicasso into the CI changed-surface classifier

**Found by**: rf2-hic-001, which created the artefact but is fenced out of `.github/`.
**Surface**: `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh`, `.github/workflows/test.yml`
(both HOT ZONE — sequence, do not parallel).

## The hole

TESTING.md §Changed-surface classifier states the rule directly:

> **Adding a new artefact directory needs two matching changes**: a classifier rule (which
> outputs the path lights) and a workflow gate whose `if:` reads them. Either side missing is
> a silent hole — code can land that mutates a surface no PR-time job watches.

`implementation/hicasso/*` is in neither. Observed rather than inferred: on the rf2-hic-001
branch `sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh --plan` reports `PLAN docs=false jvm=false node=true`, and
`node=true` only because that diff also touches `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`. A
hicasso-ONLY diff may light nothing at all.

## What to add

- A classifier case for `implementation/hicasso/*`. Today the artefact has no JVM suite (the
  runtime requires React, so every suite is CLJS), so the light that matters is
  `cljs_node_test`. Set only the outputs whose jobs the artefact's tests actually exercise —
  TESTING.md warns that coarse rules clutter the matrix with `skipping` entries.
- Whatever workflow `if:` reads it. The package's suites ride the always-on `:node-test`
  build (`re-frame.hicasso.smoke-cljs-test` matches its `cljs-test$` regexp) and the focused
  `:node-test-hicasso` build rf2-hic-001 added.
- Do NOT add `implementation/hicasso` to `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh`'s roster while
  the artefact has no JVM suite: `scripts/check_jvm_lane_rosters.py` fails both ways, so a
  roster entry without a required job is its own red.

## Also decide

`scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py` requires every `test:*` npm script to be reachable from a
workflow or carry a declared disposition. rf2-hic-001 deliberately added NO npm script — the
freeze gate is `python implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_freeze.py` and is currently run by
hand. Give it a scheduled home: either an npm `test:hicasso` wrapper reached from a workflow,
or a step in the fast-PR spine, or a declared disposition.

## Acceptance

- A hicasso-only diff lights the surfaces whose jobs actually cover it, demonstrated with
  `sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh --plan` on such a diff.
- `python scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py --verbose` and `python scripts/check_jvm_lane_rosters.py`
  stay green.
- `implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_freeze.py` runs somewhere on a schedule.

description:

THE CLAIM. docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/15-diagnostics.md:171 tells the reader that a plain `defn` used at the ROOT raises `:rf.error/hicasso-bad-head`. It does not: at the root, the root head IS the body function, so there is nothing in head position to refuse. `hicasso-bad-head` is a CHILD-POSITION rule.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN CLOSING AS MINUTIAE. This is the diagnostics chapter — the page a reader opens precisely when something has gone wrong and they are trying to match an error they are looking at against an explanation. Sending them to the wrong refusal for the wrong position is worse than silence, because it makes them doubt a correct reading of their own stack trace.

THE WORK: establish what actually happens for a plain `defn` at the root — read impl/codec.cljs and the complaint register (docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md, landed by PR #7808) rather than reasoning it out — and correct the chapter to name the real outcome. If the honest answer is that nothing refuses at the root, say that plainly; a documented absence is a true statement and this project prefers one to an invented refusal.

CHECK THE NEIGHBOURS while you are there: one wrong position rule usually means the section was written from the child case throughout. Say in the PR body which other examples you checked and found correct — the list of what you verified is worth as much as the fix.

FENCES: no runtime source edits, and do NOT mint a new refusal id to make the documentation true. spec/* is hot zone.

GATES: mkdocs build --strict does NOT cover docs/design/** (exclude_docs). scripts/check_doc_slugs.py DOES validate its links and anchors and IS SILENT ON SUCCESS — prove it saw your file by planting a bogus anchor, quoting the exit 1 naming file and line, then restoring byte-identically. The complaint-catalogue gate now runs unconditionally on every PR and reads the cited guide chapters, so a wrong id reference will be caught — read its rules before citing any id.

title: mayor-method: the gate snippet is one command line for a reason the template never states
description:
FOUND IN THE FIELD by the rf2-hic-092 worker, which hit it, noticed, and re-ran.

docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md line 173 gives the canonical gate invocation:

  sh <WORKTREE_ROOT>/scripts/test-fast-pr.sh > gate-fastpr.log 2>&1; echo "$?" > gate-fastpr.exit

That is CORRECT. The gap is that the surrounding prose (line 166) says only "redirect to a log file, echo the runner's own exit code explicitly" — it never says the two halves must share ONE command line, or why. So the single-line property is incidental to the example rather than stated as a rule, and any paraphrase loses it.

THE FAILURE. Each Bash tool call is a FRESH SHELL. Split across two calls, $? in the second reads whatever that new shell last did — typically the `cd` — not the gate. The worker's own words: "the brief's next-command pattern silently fails here; each Bash call is a fresh shell, so $? reads the cd, not the gate."

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE. It is SILENT and it yields a plausible ZERO. That is precisely the fail-open class the exit-code discipline exists to close — the rule written to stop a pipeline swallowing a red gets defeated a different way, because the mechanism was demonstrated but not explained. The bullet at line 164 already teaches the pipeline shape; this is its sibling and belongs beside it.

THE FIX IS ONE CLAUSE, and this bead is not licence to restructure the section: extend the line-166 sentence to say the redirect and the echo go on the SAME command line, in one shell, because a separate invocation starts a new shell whose $? is not the gate's. Keep the existing snippet as the example.

MY OWN BRIEFS CARRIED THE DEFECTIVE PARAPHRASE ("echo the exit code on the very next command") for a whole session before a worker caught it — recorded in bd memory under mayor-gate-exit-code-must-be-same-command-line. That is the evidence the prose, not the example, is what gets copied.

GATE: scripts/check_doc_slugs.py validates this tree's links and anchors and is SILENT ON SUCCESS — prove it saw the file by planting a bogus anchor, quoting the exit 1, then restoring. mkdocs build --strict does NOT cover docs/design/**, but docs/the-mayor-method/ IS on the site, so mkdocs --strict is the right gate here — check whether the tree is in mkdocs.yml's nav before relying on either.

PR #7818 reviewed: letfn repair is correct; reopened rf2-hic-022 because the claimed every-arity witness stays green when the first arity is skipped.

ENUMERATING GRAMMAR SHAPES IS NOT ENOUGH — EACH ROW MUST BE DISCRIMINATING (2026-08-11, AUDIT #7818 on rf2-hic-022).

THE REFINEMENT, and it is the eighth instance tonight of claim-exceeds-coverage — this time INSIDE a witness built to my own grammar-derived instruction, which is why it matters.

I briefed: derive the witness from the GRAMMAR of the construct, not from your fix. The worker did exactly that — eight legal letfn shapes, each committed as an independent negative row. It was still insufficient.

WHY: locals-bound-by unions all names for the whole letfn, and self-call-nodes suppresses the entire form as soon as ANY arity binds the view name. Every committed multi-arity row bound THE SAME view name in BOTH arities. So recognising only the LATER arity makes every row green, and the stated property — "every parameter of every arity" — is load-bearing nowhere.

THE AUDIT PROVED IT rather than asserting it: it changed fn-locals' multi-arity source from `forms` to `(rest forms)`, skipping the first arity, and the pinned live gate STILL EXITED 0. The existing mutation only removed ALL arities, so it could not catch the narrower regression.

THE RULE TO ADD TO BRIEFS, alongside grammar-derivation rather than replacing it:

  A ROW MUST BE ABLE TO FAIL FOR THE REASON IT NAMES. For every negative row, ask: what SINGLE NARROWING of the implementation would make this row pass while the property it tests is broken? If such a narrowing exists, the row is decorative.

  Practically: bind the target in the position HARDEST TO REACH, and have another position in the same form bind a DIFFERENT name, so the row can only pass if the arm truly reads that position. Then state in the PR body, per shape, WHICH NARROWING the row would catch. That list is the evidence the rows are load-bearing — and writing it is what exposes the decorative ones.

WHY THE GRAMMAR RULE ALONE FAILS: shape coverage answers "did I test this form?" It does not answer "can this test tell the difference?" A row can exercise a legal shape and still be satisfied by a wrong implementation, because the shape and the discriminator are different questions. Both are needed.

SISTER RULES: witness-derived-from-fix-inherits-its-blind-spots (the origin of the grammar instruction) and sweep-generator-defines-reachable-failure-directions (a generator's excluded shapes make an error DIRECTION unreachable). All three are the same disease at different scales — coverage is defined by what the instrument can DISTINGUISH, not by how much of it you ran.

MAYOR NOTE: the mutation self-test is the place this gets caught. A mutation that removes a capability WHOLESALE proves less than one that narrows it. Prefer narrowing mutations, and prefer several small ones to one large one.

title: the fast-PR spine cannot complete on the Windows host — bash spawn failure in test:script-policy
description:
INDEPENDENTLY REPORTED BY TWO WORKERS on different diffs and different worktrees, with matching diagnoses. That is what raises it above "flake".

THE SYMPTOM. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh clears its always-on repo-invariant steps (54 of them, 0 failures) and then dies inside `npm run test:script-policy` at implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs, with:
  Command failed: bash -lc ./.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh PATH

THE EVIDENCE IT IS A HOST SPAWN FAILURE AND NOT A TEST FAILURE, from both reports:
  - Run that suite ALONE on the same worktree and same diff: 322 passed, exit 0. Also 13/13 exit 0 on the other worker's tree.
  - The failing CASE DIFFERS BETWEEN RUNS (~477 vs ~1537 on one host; deploy-leaf "flows" then "routing" on the other). A deterministic assertion cannot do that.
  - One run printed the mechanism outright: dofork: child -1 ... exit code 0xC0000142, errno 11, then "fork: retry: Resource temporarily unavailable". Exit 127 is the bash -lc child never starting. 0xC0000142 is STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED.
  - Both failures happened while other agents were running concurrently; both hosts were under load.
  - It is unreachable from the diffs in question by construction — one was five markdown files and a comment, the other a script that classifies hard-coded path strings.

WHY P2, AND WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SYMPTOM. Every worker brief in this repo tells the worker to run the spine to completion and quote its exit code, and CLAUDE.md nominates it as the pre-checkin gate. If it cannot finish on this host under load, then either workers report a red they must argue away — costing a full re-run each time — or, far worse, someone learns to discount a real red because "the spine is flaky on Windows". A gate that cries wolf gets ignored, and that is how a genuine failure ships.

WHAT TO DO, in order:
  1. REPRODUCE UNDER LOAD, deliberately — run the spine with several concurrent node/JVM processes. If it does not reproduce, say so and stop; do not fix by inspection.
  2. Establish whether the fix belongs at the CALL (fewer concurrent bash -lc spawns from _changed-surfaces.test.cjs; batch the classifier invocations, or reuse one shell) or at the HARNESS (bounded concurrency, a retry on the specific spawn errno).
  3. A RETRY IS THE LAST RESORT, NOT THE FIRST. Retrying a spawn hides genuine classifier failures behind the same code path. If you retry, retry ONLY on the spawn signature (exit 127 with no output), never on a non-zero exit from the script itself, and say in the code why the two are distinguishable.

DO NOT weaken or skip the classifier assertions to make the symptom go away — that suite is what proves changed-surface routing is correct, and rf2-hic-021 has just shown what a mis-routed gate costs.

CROSS-PLATFORM: Mike is on Windows, maintainers are on Mac and Linux. Whatever lands must work on all three and must not make the POSIX path slower or more complex to serve the Windows one.
notes:
THIRD INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION, from the rf2-hic-023 worker (PR #7820), on a different diff and a different worktree again.

ITS OBSERVATION, and it is the strongest evidence yet because of the CONTROL it happened to run: the first spine run, on a box already loaded with the 13k-test node suite, produced 142 SPURIOUS changed-surfaces reds — every `bash -lc` classify call failing to spawn, AND EVEN A `git ls-files`. Meanwhile THE MAYOR CHECKOUT PASSED THE SAME HARNESS 322/322 CONCURRENTLY, a single classify call reproduced clean, and the quiet-box re-run was exit 0.

WHY THAT CONTROL MATTERS: it rules out the harness, the assertions and the repo state, and leaves process creation under load. And `git ls-files` failing alongside `bash -lc` widens the diagnosis — this is not specific to login shells; it is spawn exhaustion, and the login shell is merely the heaviest and most frequent caller.

Its diff touched no .cjs, no workflow and no .sh, so it cannot be causal.

RUNNING TALLY: three workers, three diffs, three worktrees — prosetruth-hic012, consumerapp-hic008, evidencev2-hic023 — plus the spawnfix worker's own measurements. The magnitude is quantified: 447 login shells per run at 713ms each on the base, 920s under load; 245 spawns and 83s on the fix branch for the same 324 assertions; `bash -lc` 713ms vs `bash <script> argv` 75ms.

NOTE FOR THE FIX WORKER (rf2-fal5, in flight): the crash signature has still not reproduced deliberately despite ~4,000 induced login-shell spawns. Reducing 447 spawns to 245 is a real and defensible improvement on its own merits, but IT IS NOT THE SAME CLAIM AS FIXING THE CRASH. Say which one the PR is claiming. If the honest position is "the mechanism is 11x smaller and the crash was never reproduced under controlled conditions", that is a good deliverable and should be written that way — it is exactly the claim-exceeds-coverage failure this repo has hit five times today, and a fix report is as exposed to it as a test is.
close_reason:
PR #7821 merged. CLOSING WITH THE VERDICT STATED PRECISELY, because the worker was scrupulous about what it did and did not establish and that distinction must survive in the record.

WHAT WAS ESTABLISHED: the cost, reproduced and quantified. 447 spawns over 235 distinct argument lists. Per invocation: bash -lc 713ms, bash -c 114ms, bash <script> <argv> 75ms — so ~319s of pure shell startup, with the login shell forking all of /etc/profile.d/ every time. Base: 478.3s quiet, 920.7 / 1003.9 / 1006.0s under load. Branch, same load: 245 spawns, 82.6s. AND THE SPINE COMPLETED UNDER THE LOAD ON WHICH IT PREVIOUSLY DIED — exit 0, PASS fast PR spine, gate root naming its own worktree.

WHAT WAS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND THE WORKER SAID SO IN THE PR BODY AND IN A CODE COMMENT: the crash did not reproduce. 18,289 deliberate bash -lc spawns, three concurrent copies of the suite on base code (the exact 'two agents running the spine' shape both original reports were under), a 150-path sweep instrumented to print status/signal/stderr on any child failing to start, and free RAM driven 14.3GB -> 4.1GB. No dofork / 0xC0000142 / Resource temporarily unavailable ever appeared.

Its own words: 'the causal step from 18x fewer, 9.5x cheaper spawns to the reported crash cannot recur is an inference, and I have said so plainly.' THAT IS THE RIGHT SHAPE OF CLAIM and it is why this closes rather than lingering: the fix stands on its measured merits — 18x fewer spawns, 9.5x faster, POSIX strictly faster too, nothing platform-gated — independent of whether it also removes the crash.

THE FIX IS AT THE CALL SITE, both halves: spawn the script as bash's argv (no login profile, and the hand-rolled shell quoting disappears because there is no shell to quote for), and memoize on the argument list (the classifier is pure over explicit paths). NO RETRY — the brief allowed one as a last resort and it was never reached; a retry would have hidden genuine classifier failures behind the same code path. Prior art cited: _playground-sci-inputs.test.cjs recorded the same lesson (56s -> 3s for 144 files).

TEETH PROVEN, not assumed: broke the implementation/core/*) arm's ui_gates=true and quoted four verbatim failures, restored byte-identically (git hash-object back to b9035b66..., clean status), 324 passed. Run in a THROWAWAY DETACHED WORKTREE so the in-flight spine was never disturbed, then removed via the script with all canaries identical.

ONE UNSOLICITED CORROBORATION worth keeping: mid-session an ordinary bash heredoc of the worker's own died with 'child_copy: cygheap read copy failed' / 'couldn't create signal pipe, Win32 error 5' — the same msys2 fork emulation giving way under the same load, on a command unrelated to this suite. That is consistent with process-creation exhaustion rather than anything specific to this test.

IF IT RECURS AFTER THIS, that is new evidence and warrants a fresh bead rather than reopening — the mechanism will have changed.

value:
I BROKE THE PIPELINE-EXIT-CODE RULE I BRIEF WORKERS ABOUT, IN MY OWN MERGE LOOP (2026-08-11).

WHAT I WROTE, trying to be defensive about the known post-merge pull abort:

  git pull --ff-only origin main 2>&1 | tail -1 || git pull --rebase origin main 2>&1 | tail -2

THE `||` NEVER FIRED. A pipeline's exit status is its LAST command's, and `tail` succeeds whatever it is fed. So the fallback was unreachable, and both merges left the checkout diverged (1/2 then 2/9) with the reassuring line "fatal: Not possible to fast-forward, aborting." printed and ignored. No damage — I noticed on the ref comparison and rebased cleanly — but the guard I wrote was decorative.

WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN JUST FIXING: this is the SAME defect class the method documents for gate runners, and I have put it in every worker brief tonight — "never pipe a gate through tail/head/grep, a pipeline's exit status is its last command's". I then wrote exactly that pattern into my own control flow, because I was thinking about the OUTPUT (I only wanted the last line) and not about the EXIT CODE. The trap is that piping for brevity and branching on success look independent and are not.

THE CORRECTED SHAPE, for any command I want to both trim and branch on:

  git pull --ff-only origin main > /tmp/pull.log 2>&1; rc=$?; tail -1 /tmp/pull.log
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || git pull --rebase origin main > /tmp/pull.log 2>&1

Redirect to a file, capture the code, THEN trim for display. Never let a display filter sit between a command and a branch that reads its result.

MAYOR-SPECIFIC: the post-merge pull now aborts routinely, because the audit hook pushes to main asynchronously and my own beads checkpoint commits locally. So the fallback is the COMMON path, not the exception — which makes an unreachable fallback exactly as bad as no fallback. Verify the outcome by comparing HEAD to origin/main rather than trusting either the printed line or a branch that may not have run.

title: Point impl/error.cljc + spec/009 at rf2-hic-021's builder-routing ruling
description:
rf2-hic-021 (PR #7808) made the ruling both files defer to: fail! keeps building its own complaint text and is NOT routed through re-frame.error's builder. ROUTING A FINDING TO A LIVE WORKER LEAVES NO DURABLE OWNER IF THAT WORKER DIES (2026-08-11, AUDIT #7825 on rf2-hic-021).

WHAT I DO, and it is efficient: when an audit or a worker surfaces a finding on a file another live worker already holds, I SendMessage it to that worker rather than filing a bead. It avoids a second worker contending for the same file, and it lands the fix inside an existing PR.

WHAT THE AUDIT CAUGHT: "#7825 identified this exact stale deferral but ROUTED IT ONLY TO A TRANSIENT WORKER, LEAVING NO DURABLE BEAD OWNER." Exactly right. A SendMessage lives in an agent's transcript. If that agent dies, times out, or simply declines the extra item, the finding evaporates — there is nothing in the tracker to re-surface it, and the merged-PR audit that found it has already run.

I had mentioned the routing in a CLOSE REASON on a different bead (rf2-ddqd). That is a record, but it is on the wrong object: nobody reads a closed bead's close reason looking for open work.

THE FIX, cheap and it does not give up the efficiency: WHEN ROUTING A FINDING TO A LIVE WORKER, ALSO PUT ONE NOTE ON THE OWNING BEAD saying what was routed, to which worker, and what happens if it does not land. Then the finding survives the worker either way. Keep routing — do not go back to filing a competing bead for a held file — but make the tracker carry the obligation.

THE AUDIT ALSO GAVE THE RIGHT RESOLUTION RULE, which I am adopting: "If the routed worker lands the correction first, VERIFY IT and close this owner; DO NOT CREATE ANOTHER ISSUE." So the sequence is: route, note on the owning bead, then on the worker's PR merging, verify the routed item actually landed and close. Verify — not assume — because a routed item is exactly the kind a worker may reasonably decline.

GENERAL SHAPE: this is the same class as everything else tonight. An obligation that exists only in a transient place is an obligation that can vanish silently. The tracker is the only durable place, which is why the method calls it the spine.

title: mayor-method: an interim message is not a completion report — the reap rule needs one clause
description:
EARNED IN THE FIELD TONIGHT, at the cost of a destroyed gate run. This is NOT a seventh proxy — the file rightly says do not add one — it is a sharpening of what the word "report" means in the rule that is already there.

WHAT THE FILE SAYS: "Reap a worktree only once its owning agent has delivered a completion report." Correct, and I followed it as I understood it.

WHAT I DID: the catalogrows-vkle worker sent two interim messages. The second said, verbatim, "Holding for the spine — not done yet, and I won't report a colour I don't have." Minutes later I merged its PR and reaped its worktree in the same breath. Its spine was in the JVM tier. git worktree list stopped showing the tree, .git went, gate.log was deleted mid-write. The worker afterwards found gate.exit = 1 and CORRECTLY REFUSED TO REPORT IT AS A FAILURE — that 1 was written by a script whose own checkout had been deleted underneath it. My cleanup manufactured a red.

THE GAP IN THE WORDING: I had promoted "the agent has spoken" to "the agent has reported done". Those are not the same thing, and the difference was written plainly in the message I was reading. An interim status, a progress note, a partial hand-off, a PR-opened announcement — none of these is a completion report. AND A BACKGROUND GATE STILL RUNNING IS THE WORKER STILL RUNNING, even though nothing in the branch, the tree or the PR shows it.

WHY IT LOOKED SAFE, which is the part worth writing down: every listed proxy agreed at once. PR merged, tree clean, commits pushed, no junction, agent had messaged minutes earlier. That is not evidence — it is what a DISCIPLINED worker mid-gate looks like BY DESIGN, since commit-and-push-as-you-go is what every brief demands. The better the worker, the more convincing the illusion.

THE SECOND MECHANISM, and the file already warns about it in the abstract: I had BATCHED THE REAP INTO THE MERGE PASS. The file says never pair a merge with a reap in the same breath. I did exactly that, because a merged PR is the moment a tree looks finished — which is precisely why that pull is dangerous.

PROPOSED WORDING, small and in the file's own voice: add to the existing bullet that the report must SAY THE WORK IS FINISHED, and that the operational test is "can I quote the sentence where this agent says it is done?" If the answer is no, the worktree stays. Cost of waiting: one stale directory. Also worth one clause: a gate the worker backgrounded is still that worker running, and the harness's ten-minute foreground ceiling (see dispatch-prompt-template.md) means long gates are ALWAYS backgrounded, so this is the common case rather than an edge case.

FENCES: do NOT restructure the reaping section or add a seventh proxy to the list. This is one clause on the existing rule plus, at most, one sentence of mechanism. docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md carries the full six-proxy history — if the same clarification belongs there, make the two agree rather than saying it twice differently.

GATE: mkdocs build --strict COVERS docs/the-mayor-method/ (verified: site/the-mayor-method/... exists while site/design does not). scripts/check_doc_slugs.py also validates it and IS SILENT ON SUCCESS — prove coverage with a planted bogus anchor and restore byte-identically.

title: hic: the complaint-catalogue self-test leads with a Python traceback instead of its own failure report
description:
Reported by the rf2-hic-021 worker (PR #7813), which surfaced it rather than actioning it — its fence said do not make the checker bigger, and it was right to hold.

THE WART. implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_complaint_catalogue.py opens --self-test with a bare `assert not check(...)`. So when a genuine breakage is present, the operator sees a raw Python traceback BEFORE the checker's own well-formed report (FAIL: ... R1 ...) ever prints. The useful message is there; it is just behind an AssertionError.

WHY IT IS WORTH ONE SMALL FIX RATHER THAN NOTHING. This is the first thing an operator hits when the gate genuinely fires, and this gate now runs UNCONDITIONALLY on every PR (PR #7813). A gate whose failure output leads with a traceback trains people to skim past it — and the whole reason rf2-hic-021 was reopened was a gate nobody could see working.

THE FIX IS SMALL AND MUST STAY SMALL: make the self-test report its own failure in the checker's existing voice rather than raising through a bare assert. Reuse the reporting the eight rules already have. Do NOT add a logging framework, a --verbose tier, a summary table, or error codes. Do NOT touch the eight rules or the register.

FENCE, inherited from rf2-hic-021 and still in force: preserve the small pure-Python checker and its current rules. This bead is about the SELF-TEST's failure presentation, nothing else.

WITNESS: run --self-test with a deliberate breakage present, and show the first line of output naming the rule rather than a traceback. Quote both the before and after output in the PR body — the before is what justifies the change.

GATES: npm run test:hicasso-invariants (renamed from test:hicasso-freeze by PR #7813 — use the current name), plus the checker's own --self-test. The unconditional CI job is `Hicasso complaint-catalogue contract (rf2-hic-021)`; it runs in about 16 seconds, so there is no reason not to see it green.

PR #7827 merged. The FAIL: ... R1 ... reporting is now a report(failures) that BOTH entry points red through, and --self-test's green precondition uses it instead of a bare assert.

WITNESS quoted both ways on the same breakage (one live row deleted, original recovered via git show HEAD:): BEFORE = 'AssertionError: the tree must be green before the reds are driven' behind a traceback; AFTER = 'FAIL: Hicasso complaint catalogue' then 'R1 :rf.error/hicasso-empty-vector is emitted by ... and has no live row in the register'. Both exit 1; register restored byte-identically.

THE DISTINCTION IT DREW UNPROMPTED, and it is the right one: the mask() and red() assertions DELIBERATELY STAY assertions. They fail only when someone edits the checker, where a traceback naming the line IS the useful output. Only the operator-facing path needed the checker's own voice.

A WORKER'S READING OF A FILE IT DID NOT EDIT IS A CLAIM, NOT A MEASUREMENT (2026-08-11).

WHAT HAPPENED. The rf2-6ync triage worker classified all 69 prototype suites — excellent work, independently reconciled by the merged-PR audit against the pre-port tree. In passing it also stated that two suites :require EACH OTHER and that both reach a bench SSR namespace with no package counterpart. I transcribed both into a note on rf2-6rw9 and made them THAT BEAD'S STATED CONTENT: "the package needs an SSR entry first."

BOTH WERE FALSE. The rf2-b6ja worker checked at the source: the two files name each other exactly once each, in docstring [[wiki-links]] (lines 31 and 57) — no code dependency — and neither reaches ssr.entry at all; they use React's own react-dom/server directly. So a bead I wrote described runtime work that does not need doing, and would have sent a worker to build an SSR entry for nothing.

THE DISTINCTION I MISSED: a worker's findings about the files IT EDITED are backed by the gates it ran. Its remarks about NEIGHBOURING files are ordinary reading — often right, sometimes not, and never gate-checked. I apply "verify the premise at the source" to code claims and to audit findings; I had not applied it to a worker's incidental observations, because they arrive inside a report whose main content IS verified.

THE RULE: when a worker's report supplies the CONTENT of a new bead — particularly a blocker, a dependency, or "X must happen first" — verify that specific claim before writing it down, or write it as REPORTED rather than as fact. One grep is usually enough; here `git grep ssr.entry` would have settled it in seconds.

AND WHEN IT TURNS OUT WRONG, correct the bead loudly rather than quietly amending: the wrong version may already have shaped a brief or another bead's framing. In this case it had also mis-assigned a third suite to the wrong bead.

SISTER RULE: the same shape as rows-must-be-discriminating and witness-derived-from-fix — the common thread is that CONFIDENCE TRAVELS FURTHER THAN EVIDENCE. A verified report lends its authority to the unverified sentences sitting next to it.

MY PR SWEEP COLLAPSES FAILURE AND CANCELLED INTO ONE LABEL, AND I NEARLY DISPATCHED A FIX-WORKER FOR NOTHING (2026-08-11).

THE INSTRUMENT BUG. My sweep's jq is:
  select(.state=="FAILURE" or .state=="CANCELLED") | "  FAIL "+.name
Grouping them is CORRECT for the merge decision — the criterion says CANCELLED is not passed, and both block. But printing both as "FAIL" is wrong for the DIAGNOSIS, and the two have opposite remedies:
  FAILURE  -> the gate ran and said no. Dispatch a fix-worker to the same branch that runs the ACTUAL failing gate.
  CANCELLED -> the gate did not run to a verdict, usually superseded by a newer run. Wait or re-run. THERE IS NOTHING TO FIX.

WHAT HAPPENED: PR #7831 showed "FAIL Beads PR boundary". I went looking for a real defect, checked the branch's three-dot diff (clean of .beads), read the checker script and the CI invocation (both correctly use merge-base, and the YAML even documents this exact hazard), and started toward a fix-worker. Then the run log said "still in progress" — and the check's real state was CANCELLED, with the `tests` run in progress at that head. Nothing was wrong. The earlier attempt had been superseded.

Cost: several minutes and nearly a wasted dispatch, on a PR whose only problem was that CI had not finished.

THE FIX, one word: print the state instead of a fixed label.
  select(.state=="FAILURE" or .state=="CANCELLED") | "  " + .state + " " + .name
Then a CANCELLED reads as CANCELLED and I wait, and a FAILURE reads as FAILURE and I dispatch.

THE GENERAL SHAPE, which is the same one this repo keeps finding in its own gates: A SUMMARY THAT MERGES TWO STATES WITH DIFFERENT REMEDIES IS A SUMMARY THAT WILL EVENTUALLY PRESCRIBE THE WRONG ONE. My instrument was built for the merge question, then reused for the diagnosis question, and it is only correct for the first. Exactly the fault I have been recording in workers' witnesses all session — a claim broader than what the instrument distinguishes.

TWO GATE FACTS THAT CORRECT MY OWN BRIEFS (2026-08-11, rf2-5i4e worker, PR #7833).

1. check_doc_slugs.py DOES NOT OPEN REPO-ROOT MARKDOWN — INCLUDING CLAUDE.md. Its own docstring (rf2-znup0) says repo-root markdown is out of scope and it "exits 0 on a broken link in any of them". The worker's words: "several briefs have nominated it for root-markdown edits and got a green that verified nothing." scripts/check_readme_links.py is the gate that owns repo-root files; it probed that one too (exit 1 on CLAUDE.md:128, restored, hash equal both sides).

WHY THIS IS THE NASTY SHAPE: check_doc_slugs.py is SILENT ON SUCCESS, so I already tell workers to prove coverage by planting a bogus anchor. But a plant in an OUT-OF-SCOPE file also produces silence — the proof technique and the failure mode look identical. Planting only proves coverage if you plant in a file the gate actually reads.

CORRECTED BRIEF WORDING: name the gate WITH ITS SCOPE. check_doc_slugs.py covers docs/** (including docs/design/** and docs/the-mayor-method/) and spec/**; check_readme_links.py covers repo-root markdown such as CLAUDE.md and README.md. If an edit spans both, nominate both and prove each in its own tree.

2. THE HARNESS'S REPORTED EXIT CODE IS THE LAST COMMAND'S, WHICH IS MY OWN ECHO. Live instance: `mkdocs` is not on PATH in this environment, the console script exits 127 with "command not found" — and the harness still reported the wrapper as exit 0, because the last command on the line was the `echo` writing the .exit file. (The spine's documented `python -m mkdocs` fallback, rf2-g7p7l, is what actually runs.)

So my snippet — `gate > gate.log 2>&1; echo "$?" > gate.exit` — is CORRECT, and it is correct precisely because it puts the real code in a FILE. But a worker who reads the HARNESS's reported exit instead of `cat gate.exit` sees the echo's zero. Same fail-open, one level up from the pipeline trap.

CORRECTED BRIEF WORDING, add one clause: "then READ THE .exit FILE and quote that number — not the exit code the harness reports for the command line, which is the echo's."

THE COMMON SHAPE, third instance tonight after my sweep conflating FAILURE with CANCELLED and my own piped `||` fallback: an instrument that is correct for the question it was built for, reused for a question it cannot answer. Name the scope, and read the artefact rather than the wrapper.

title: hic lint: the read rules carry the same shadowing blindness just fixed in direct-view-call
description:
REPRODUCED, NOT SPECULATED, by the rf2-hic-022 worker (PR #7804), which correctly left it alone as outside its charge.

THE DEFECT. With `sub` `:refer`red and then shadowed by a local binding, the `parked-read` rule still fires. That is the same class of false positive PR #7804 just removed from `direct-view-call`: the hook reasons about a symbol in head position without asking whether a binding in scope has taken that name.

WHY IT IS P4 AND NOT P1, and this distinction is the whole reason it is a separate bead. `direct-view-call` is ERROR level — it BLOCKS A BUILD, which is what reopened rf2-hic-022 in the first place. The read rules are WARNING level. A spurious warning is noise; a spurious error stops a programmer working. Do not let the shared mechanism tempt anyone into treating these as equally urgent.

THE FIX IS ALREADY WRITTEN, and reusing it is the point: PR #7804 added a shadow test to `check-direct-view-call!` covering the argument vector (destructuring included), the `let`-shaped family with `for`/`doseq` `:let` folded in and `:when`/`:while` excluded, `fn`/`fn*`/`hfn` params, `letfn` names, `catch` and `as->`. Read that implementation first and REUSE it rather than writing a second shadow walker — two walkers that disagree is worse than one that is blind.

TAKE THE SAME DESIGN RULING WITH IT: a binding silences the whole form it heads. That deliberately loses a real finding in the initialiser of a `let` that also binds the name. Silence is the only failure these hooks are permitted, and the README says so. Do NOT build whole-program analysis to recover that case — that is exactly the over-engineering this project rejects.

ALSO DO NOT USE `api/resolve`. PR #7804 established by probe that it returns nil for the cases that matter — the view's own name is not yet a var when the hook runs, and it never sees locals. Resolution cannot carry this.

WITNESS: red first, both directions, as #7804 did — a negative fixture proving the false positive is gone, and a mutation proving the rule still fires on genuine breakage. A rule verified only by "no findings on the corpus" is not verified.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7804 coordination note: do not reuse PR #7804's lexical-shadow helper unchanged. Its letfn arm recognizes single-arity params but misses every parameter of a multi-arity letfn, and direct-view-call consequently false-reds legal calls at ERROR (exact owner rf2-hic-022 reopened). When this P4 warning repair reuses the shared walker, sequence after or include that bounded arity fix so the read rules do not inherit it. Scope and priority remain unchanged.

title: hic-021 — The complaint catalogue: stable diagnostic ids as public contract
description:
# hic-021 — The complaint catalogue: stable diagnostic ids as public contract

**Phase**: tooling lane · **Wave**: B · **Est.**: M · **Depends**: hic-001 (hic-007 lands the shape; this catalogues it — coordinate, don't collide: this bead owns the catalogue doc + tests, not the error constructor)
**Surface**: `docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md` (new) + `implementation/hicasso/test/.../complaints_catalogue_*` (new)

## Goal
Every Hicasso refusal id catalogued, versioned, and tested as public API: id → meaning → payload shape → docs anchor → recovery ladder. The cheapest proven asset in the record (the predecessor shipped 83).

## Deliverables
- The catalogue: enumerate every `:rf.error/hicasso-*` id in the runtime with payload schema and recovery.
- A completeness test: every id raised anywhere in the suite appears in the catalogue (and vice versa — no dead entries).
- Stability rule recorded: ids never change meaning; retired ids are tombstoned.

## Acceptance
- Round-trip test green (raise-set == catalogue-set); each entry's recovery is actionable prose, not a restatement of the error.

## Worker notes
Read synth.md diagnostics paragraph; lessons-reframe-ui refusal-culture section (via its banner — evidence only). Lint (hic-022), the advisor (hic-037), and the MCP spike (hic-059) consume this.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).
notes:
From rf2-hic-001 (the extraction): scope boundary worth pinning before you start.

Your stated surface is docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md + this artefact's own round-trip tests. That is NOT the same catalogue as spec/009-Instrumentation.md, which is the repo-wide instrumentation catalogue that scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py defends. Moving the runtime from the bench test/ tree into implementation/hicasso/src/ brought all 40 :rf.error/hicasso-* ids inside that gate's scan for the first time, and it now reports every one as uncatalogued. rf2-cs0kd1 deleted the KNOWN_UNCATALOGUED construct from that gate, so there is no debt-ledger escape: the Spec 009 rows have to be written.

That work is filed separately as rf2-g85n and BLOCKS rf2-hic-001 from merging spine-green. Coordinate: the two catalogues should agree and yours can cite the Spec 009 rows, but neither substitutes for the other.

One id in the set is not hicasso-prefixed — :rf.error/no-frame-prop, emitted by impl/runtime.cljs. Whether it is a Hicasso id needing a rename or a core id with an existing home is an open question in rf2-g85n.
SCOPE ADDITION (2026-08-10, from the guide rewrite's Stage C): the catalogue must mint ids for 13 refusal families the end-state guide teaches by mechanism only — the defview direct-call refusal; the five n/$ refusal rows (props misclassification, hiccup child, intent-in-prop, :children, slot collision); three test-kit refusals (L2 opacity, missing fixture, assert-clean failure); the forms-module family; the contenteditable refusal; route-link :prefetch wrong-value; second-mount-same-node. Authoritative list after rf2-hic-092 merges: docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/REWRITE-NOTES.md section 'Stage C output' (catalogue gaps). Also note: :rf.error/hicasso-route-link-bad-on-click is attested and should be cited on guide ch07 when the catalogue lands.
MAYOR 2026-08-10 — THIRTEEN REFUSALS TO MINT ARE NOW WAITING FOR THIS BEAD, AND THE COMPLETENESS TEST AS SPECIFIED CANNOT SEE THEM.

SOURCE, now on main after rf2-hic-092 merged:
docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/REWRITE-NOTES.md
  section "### (b) The catalogue gaps (refusals taught by mechanism with no
  attested id)", 13 numbered entries beginning at line 126.
A shorter roll-up of the same set sits at line 50 under "## Missing error ids
(catalogue gaps — Stage C compiles; do NOT invent on pages)".

FOUND BY THE rf2-hic-093 WORKER while folding the minted-spellings register into
the naming ledger. It reported them as having no owner. THEY DO HAVE ONE — this
bead — and no duplicate should be filed. But the worker's instinct was half right,
and the half that is right is the point of this note.

WHY THIS BEAD'S COMPLETENESS TEST WOULD MISS THEM. The deliverable reads "enumerate
every :rf.error/hicasso-* id in the runtime" and "every id raised anywhere in the
suite appears in the catalogue (and vice versa — no dead entries)". Both directions
of that test range over ids THAT EXIST. These 13 are refusals the guide teaches BY
MECHANISM with no attested id at all — the guide describes what the runtime refuses
and how, without naming a diagnostic. A refusal with no id is raised by nothing and
appears in no catalogue, so it satisfies both directions of the completeness test
vacuously. That is the same fail-open shape this repo keeps finding in its own
instruments: the test verifies the absence of a mismatch rather than the presence of
coverage.

So the catalogue is not complete when the two enumerations agree. It is complete when
the two enumerations agree AND every refusal the guide teaches has an id. Treat the
Stage C list as a third input to the completeness test, not as background reading.

WHAT THE 13 COVER (from the line-50 roll-up; read section (b) for the full text):
the `defview` direct-call refusal; the `n/$` refusal family (props misclassification,
hiccup child, intent-in-prop, `:children`, slot collision); test-kit refusals
(opacity, missing fixture, assert-clean failure); forms-module rows; the
contenteditable refusal; the bare-intent veto at `route-link` `:on-click`; and
`:prefetch` wrong-value.

TWO CONSTRAINTS THAT COME WITH THE LIST.
1. "do NOT invent on pages" — the guide chapters deliberately did not mint these.
   Minting is this bead's job, in the catalogue, not a chapter edit.
2. Gap 12 records that THE RETIRED DECLINE ID MUST NOT BE REUSED. That is the same
   rule this bead already states as "retired ids are tombstoned", and it now has a
   concrete instance to honour.

ONE ID SITS IN TWO PILES. rf2-hic-093 landed naming-ledger row 30, which records
`:rf.error/hicasso-overlay-anchor-missing` as simultaneously a SPELLING question for
rf2-hic-065's naming packet and a CATALOGUE obligation here. Coordinate rather than
collide: the packet settles the spelling, this bead catalogues whatever it settles on.
Do not settle the spelling here.

THE EXISTING COORDINATION FENCE IS UNCHANGED: rf2-hic-007 lands the error SHAPE, this
bead catalogues it, and this bead owns the catalogue doc and tests rather than the
error constructor.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #7808 (merged 2026-08-10T13:31:50Z as 59bf33c0b) — REOPEN THIS EXACT OWNER; do not file a duplicate.

WHAT LANDED CLEANLY: the 59-live / 12-reserved / 1-pending / 0-retired register is coherent, the eight relational rules and red self-tests pass, every live id round-trips through an emitter and Spec 009, every cited anchor resolves, and the two Spec 009 clarifications are accurate. Independent audit runs passed the complaint self-test and live gate, the full npm freeze chain, keyword drift, doc slugs, and all 322 changed-surface tests. All three authored commits have exact landed patch identities.

COMPLETENESS / CORRECTNESS — THE NEW CONTRACT IS NOT SELF-PROTECTING IN CI. The checker reads four input families: implementation/hicasso source and test-kit code, docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md, spec/009-Instrumentation.md, and cited docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide chapters. Direct report-changed-surfaces probes on this merge set cljs_node_test=true only for implementation/hicasso/**. The register, Spec 009, and guide inputs each report cljs_node_test=false. In test.yml the only hosted invocation is inside the cljs job guarded by needs.detect_changed_surfaces.outputs.cljs_node_test == 'true'. Thus a register-only edit can drop or corrupt a live/reserved/tombstone row, a Spec-only edit can break R3/R4/R6, and a guide-only edit can break R8 while every PR check skips this gate. #7808 happened to touch the checker and package.json, masking the reverse-edge gap. The close reason's claim that chaining into test:hicasso-freeze created “NO scheduling hole” is disproved.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / BOUNDED REPAIR: preserve the small pure-Python checker and its current rules. Give it a cheap CI path whose changed-surface inputs include every file family it reads, or otherwise make those exact reverse edges executable and covered by the scheduling tests. Do not make a docs-only catalogue edit pay for the full CLJS/browser/HMR matrix merely to run a sub-second Python contract. Keep rf2-ibje scoped to the honest script rename; it is not an owner for this missing reachability.
MAYOR: the AUDIT #7808 finding is ACCEPTED and my close reason was WRONG. I wrote that chaining the checker into test:hicasso-freeze created 'NO scheduling hole'. The audit's direct report-changed-surfaces probes disprove it: only implementation/hicasso/** sets cljs_node_test=true, while the register, spec/009 and the cited guide chapters all report false, and the only hosted invocation is guarded on that flag. #7808 touching the checker and package.json is what masked it.

The lesson generalises past this bead, and it is the same shape the merge criterion keeps teaching: A GATE THAT RUNS ON THE PR THAT INTRODUCED IT PROVES ONLY THAT IT RUNS ON THAT PR. Its reverse edges — the file families it reads but does not live beside — are unproven until each one is driven on its own. The introducing PR is the single worst witness for reachability, because it necessarily touches the gate itself.

ROUTED, not separately dispatched: worker/catalogrows-vkle already holds .github/workflows/test.yml and implementation/package.json for rf2-ibje (the test:hicasso-freeze rename), and both are sequential-access. A second worker would need the same window and conflict. It has the audit's bounded repair — preserve the small pure-Python checker and its rules; give it a CI path whose changed-surface inputs include every family it reads, or make those reverse edges executable and covered by the scheduling tests — plus an instruction to DRIVE each of the three false edges (register-only, spec-only, guide-only) rather than assert them.

Note the interaction it must not miss: rf2-ibje asks it to prove the renamed gate still runs, and this finding says the gate does not run on three of the four families it guards. A rename that preserves an unreachable gate preserves nothing.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7825 (2026-08-10; completeness/correctness/implementation quality). REOPEN EXACT CATALOGUE OWNER.

WHAT IS SOUND: the three authored patches match their landed identities; error.cljc and Spec 009 now accurately cite rf2-hic-021's builder-routing ruling and distinguish required-key overwrite from ambient-key removal. The complaint-catalogue contract and doc-slug gates pass.

COMPLETENESS / DOC TRUTH: docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md still says the provenance of :source/:view when no origin names a view “is rf2-hic-007's to settle” and promises nothing. PR #7812 settled it: fail! removes both ambient keys from extra before merging, so they are absent outside a declaration/render extent and in production. #7825 identified this exact stale deferral but routed it only to a transient worker, leaving no durable Bead owner. Correct that one clause here (or point to the settled constructor rule) without restating the whole rationale or widening the catalogue. If the routed worker lands the correction first, verify it and close this owner; do not create another issue.
MAYOR: AUDIT #7825's critique of my routing is ACCEPTED, and its resolution rule is the one I am following.

THE FINDING (complaints.md:52's stale deferral to rf2-hic-007, a bead that landed and settled it) WAS routed mid-flight to worker/smallmisc-miw1, which holds that file — and that worker LANDED IT. Its report: 'Handed in mid-flight — done, not declined. complaints.md:52's deferral to rf2-hic-007 was stale and contradicted the paragraph above it. Confirmed at source (impl/error.cljc: ambient = [:source :view], fail! does (merge (apply dissoc extra ambient) ...)), replaced with one sentence citing Rulings this catalogue owns rather than restating it.' That is in PR #7827, currently one check from green.

SO PER THE AUDIT'S OWN INSTRUCTION — 'If the routed worker lands the correction first, verify it and close this owner; do not create another issue' — I will VERIFY the landed text on main once #7827 merges, then close this bead. No new issue filed.

THE CRITIQUE IS RIGHT ABOUT THE METHOD, not just this instance: a SendMessage lives in an agent's transcript, so if that agent dies, times out or declines the extra item, the finding evaporates with nothing in the tracker to re-surface it. I had recorded the routing in rf2-ddqd's CLOSE REASON, which is a record on the wrong object — nobody reads a closed bead looking for open work.

Corrected practice, recorded as bd memory routed-findings-need-a-note-on-the-owning-bead: keep routing to the worker that holds the file (it avoids two workers contending), but ALSO put one note on the OWNING bead naming what was routed, to whom, and what happens if it does not land. The efficiency is preserved and the tracker carries the obligation.

The exact routed correction landed, so this owner closes per its own note.
