title: hic: the bad-reads recovery keyword still tells the programmer to use a retired option
description:
Found by the rf2-0ckh worker (PR #7828) while renaming the kit's L2 entry, and correctly NOT taken — both sites are behind fences it was given.

THE RESIDUE. PR #7828 renamed the kit's L2 fixture key from `:reads` to `:subs` per naming-ledger row 23. Two artefacts still spell the retired option:
  - the recovery keyword `:add-the-query-to-reads`
  - the refusal id `:rf.error/hicasso-test-bad-reads`
Both are rowed verbatim in `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (hard fence for that worker), and `docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md:133` carries the row too.

THE TWO ARE NOT THE SAME QUESTION, and the distinction is the content of this bead:

  - THE RECOVERY KEYWORD GIVES WRONG ADVICE NOW. It tells a programmer to add the query to `:reads`, an option that no longer exists. That is a live defect: the refusal fires, the recovery instruction is unfollowable, and the reader has no way to know the word changed. Fix it.

  - THE ID SHOULD PROBABLY NOT MOVE. rf2-hic-021's law is that ids are a stable public contract; a spelling that is merely unfashionable is not grounds to break it, and renaming an id has a cost the recovery keyword does not — every consumer matching on it breaks. Weigh it, state the reasoning, and be willing to conclude the id STAYS while the recovery text changes. A documented "the id keeps a historical spelling, and here is why" is a good outcome.

The #7828 worker already updated the refusal MESSAGE text to say `:subs`, so the message and the recovery keyword currently disagree with each other — that inconsistency is the sharpest reason this cannot just be left.

HOT ZONE AND SEQUENCING: `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` is sequential-access. `complaints.md` was held by `worker/smallmisc-miw1` (PR #7827) — check it has merged before dispatching, and read what it landed, since it retired a reserved id in the same file.

GATE WITH TEETH: `implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_complaint_catalogue.py` runs unconditionally on every PR and reads BOTH the register and spec/009, so a half-done change reds. Run it and quote the exit code. Read its eight rules before editing either file — CHECK C in particular governs which ids may have a spec/009 row.

STANCE: no back-compat shim, no alias, no deprecation path. And do not widen this into a sweep of other recovery keywords unless you find they are wrong too — if you check them, say what you checked.
notes: CORRECTION: the follow-up bead is rf2-6640, not rf2-1t3f. I wrote the id into the close reason before filing the bead — the same slip I made earlier tonight and told myself to stop making. File first, then reference.
close_reason:
PR #7834 merged. THE WORKER REFUTED THREE OF MY PREMISES, and the refutation is the deliverable — my bead was written from the #7828 worker's report without verifying it, the second time tonight I did that.

1. THE TWO ARTEFACTS ARE ON DIFFERENT ROWS. :add-the-query-to-reads is the recovery for :rf.error/hicasso-test-missing-read-fixture (spec/009:2613). :rf.error/hicasso-test-bad-reads (line 2617) carries :pass-a-map-of-query-to-value — which names a SHAPE, not a key, and needs no change at all.
2. THE RECOVERY KEYWORD IS NOT WRONG YET. On main the option IS :reads (test.cljs:1179). PR #7828 CREATES the defect; changing the spec row now would make main wrong in the other direction.
3. NO MESSAGE/RECOVERY CONTRADICTION EXISTS ON MAIN. #7828's updated bad-reads message sits beside :pass-a-map-of-query-to-value — consistent.

THE ID STAYS, decided on merits rather than on the fence. Rule 1 does not fire: an id names the REFUSAL, not the option, and the refusal means what it always meant — only the option's spelling moved. Rule 2 prices the alternative: a tombstone kept forever, a new live row, a struck plus fresh spec/009 row, and a spelling every consumer re-learns, for one better word. A recovery keyword is read once by a human and branched on by nothing; an id is matched on by stored errors, monitor grouping and test assertions. The register already set this precedent with :rf.error/no-frame-prop.

THE KEYWORD FIX WAS CORRECTLY DECLINED. It has THREE sites — spec/009:2613, test_kit/.../test.cljs:1117 (PR #7828's), test/.../test_kit_cljs_test.cljs:558 (another worker's) — and the change is ATOMIC across them, because spec/009's recovery column states what the runtime raises and consumers may branch on it. NO GATE CATCHES A MISMATCH: check_complaint_catalogue.py tracks ids only, and the drift gate reconciles :rf.error/* ids. Taking the spec half alone would trade a stale-but-consistent word for silent untracked drift. The emit line is also a context line inside a #7828 hunk, so editing it guarantees a conflict.

WHAT IT SHIPPED INSTEAD: two rulings under 'Rulings this catalogue owns' — 'An id is frozen; the :recovery beside it is not' (settling the class, since the stability rule governed the id and said nothing about the rest of the row) and 'bad-reads keeps its spelling'. Both framed on naming-ledger row 23's recommendation ALREADY ON MAIN, so they are true today and after #7828 either way.

IT ENUMERATED ALL 56 hicasso recovery keywords and checked the ten naming a literal API spelling against implementation/hicasso/src — :callbacks, :ssr, :server, :timeout-ms, :prefetch, :on-mouse-enter, :event, :handler, :render all live. :add-the-query-to-reads is THE ONLY ONE pointing at a key being renamed. No sweep performed.

FOLLOW-UP: re-dispatch the keyword fix after #7828 merges, holding spec/009 + test_kit/** + test/** together — three lines plus wording in two Trigger cells and two register row descriptions. Filed as rf2-1t3f.

title: hic: the public door has no re-render, so a dev/after-load hook cannot be written on public namespaces only
description:
DESIGN FINDING from the rf2-hic-008 worker (PR #7814), reported rather than decided. Verify against the source first.

THE CLAIM. There is no re-render on the public door. The HMR testbed dev/after-load hook reaches into impl.mount/render! to do its job, and h/root! calls createRoot every time, so it is not the answer either. Consequence: a consumer writing an ordinary hot-reload hook ON PUBLIC NAMESPACES ONLY cannot. The consumer app that PR #7814 landed therefore deliberately carries no reload hook — that omission is evidence for this bead, not an oversight.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND CONVENIENCE. Hot reload is table stakes for a CLJS view library, and rf2-hic-008 own acceptance criterion is a consumer app on PUBLIC NAMESPACES ONLY. A public surface that cannot express the single most common dev-time affordance is an ergonomics hole in exactly the place this project cares about most: high productivity and low friction, for the programmer and the AI working with them.

THE QUESTION: what is the smallest public affordance that lets a consumer re-render a mounted root after a reload — and is it a new export, or does root! grow the ability to re-use an existing React root rather than calling createRoot each time? State the options and recommend; do not silently pick.

STANCE, and it cuts both ways here: no over-engineering — do NOT build an HMR framework, a reload registry, or a lifecycle-hook system. Trust the programmer: the goal is one obvious call they can put in their own dev/after-load. Equally, do not close this as minutiae — an affordance the library own testbed needs private access to achieve is a real gap in the public surface.

SEQUENCING: rf2-hic-027 is building the L3 mounted facade (mount!/render!/unmount!) in the test kit right now. Read that PR first — it may already have settled the shape of a re-render call, and the public door should not disagree with the kit about what re-rendering means. Related: the release! facade bead filed alongside this one.

FENCE: any new public export is classified and justified when it lands, per the standing facade-export rule.
close_reason:
PR #7830 merged. Claim verified at the source: the HMR testbed reached impl.mount/render!, and h/root! calls createRoot unconditionally — so a consumer could not write an ordinary dev/after-load hook on public namespaces only.

DECISION: EXPORT h/render!. The function already existed, already took the handle first, and already answered it — so the smallest public affordance was a promotion, not a new mechanism. It rejected the container->root REGISTRY (hidden page state, banned by the bead) and rejected REMOUNT (discards every node, subscription and scrap of state).

THE EVIDENCE CLOSED ITS OWN LOOP: the HMR testbed now calls h/render! and drops its impl.mount require, and the consumer app gained the three-line hook whose ABSENCE was this bead's evidence in the first place — PR #7814 had deliberately shipped it without one because it could not be written on public namespaces.

Gates re-run after rebasing onto merged PR #7822: browser lane 1179 tests / 7351 assertions including the merged mounted-kit suite against the non-detaching unmount!, and test:hicasso-hmr green across chromium, firefox and webkit with 36 real shadow reloads — the lane that would actually catch a broken reload path.

title: ci: check_gate_scheduling.py cannot see build:* scripts — decide whether that scope limit is intended
description:
MEASURED by the rf2-qy1j worker (PR #7823), reported rather than actioned because widening it has consequences it was fenced from deciding.

THE GAP. scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py's GATE_PREFIXES is ("test:", "bench:"), so a `build:` npm script can NEVER be flagged unscheduled. The checker's whole job is to catch a command that exists but nothing runs — and an entire naming family is invisible to it.

WHY IT IS DEFENSIBLE AS-IS, and this is the argument to weigh rather than dismiss: a GATE renders a verdict; a BUILD makes an artefact. Not every build wants scheduling, and forcing one to declare a disposition is paperwork if nothing depends on it.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS: PR #7823 added `build:hicasso-release` and scheduled it as a step of the existing cljs job. Its durable protection is that workflow step — NOT the checker, which cannot see it. If someone deletes that step, nothing complains. That is precisely the silent hole check_gate_scheduling.py exists to prevent, in the one family it does not scan.

WHAT WIDENING WOULD COST, measured by the worker: adding `build:` immediately flags `build:freehand-release`, `build:freehand-evidence-elision` and `build:freehand-matched` — all legitimate local-only aliases that would each need a written disposition. So the work is not one line; it is one line plus three honest dispositions.

THE DECISION TO MAKE: either widen GATE_PREFIXES and write those three dispositions, or leave the prefixes alone and record IN THE CHECKER why `build:` is out of scope, so the next reader does not mistake the omission for an oversight. Both are acceptable outcomes. What is not acceptable is leaving it undocumented — an unexplained scope limit reads as a bug to whoever finds it next.

If you widen it, take the rf2-hic-021 lesson: a scope predicate that must be kept in sync with a growing set is a standing liability. Ask what makes someone revisit GATE_PREFIXES the next time a new script family appears.

GATES: scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py itself (it self-tests), plus the fast-PR spine which runs it. Report the before and after counts — currently `44 gate commands, 38 scheduled, 6 declared (0 of them known holes with beads)`.

HOT ZONE: if the answer touches .github/workflows/*, sequence it — that file is sequential-access.
notes:
CORRECTION to the close reason above: one sentence lost a fragment to shell command substitution. It should read:

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: with the widening in, deleting PR #7823's step that runs "npm run build:hicasso-release" now REDS the checker. Before it, that deletion was silent.

That measurement is the whole justification for widening — it turns a gate whose only protection was an unguarded workflow step into one the checker can see.

(Mayor note: this is the second time tonight I have let backticks in bd content reach bash unquoted. Use a single-quoted heredoc for any bd text containing backticks; a double-quoted one does not protect them.)

SHELL HYGIENE FOR bd CONTENT — I have now broken this twice in one session (2026-08-11).

THE FAULT: passing bd text that contains BACKTICKS through a double-quoted string or an unquoted heredoc lets bash run the backticked span as command substitution. First instance: a bd remember whose backticked 'needs:'/'if:' ran as commands (bash printed 'needs:: command not found'). Second instance: a bd close whose backticked 'run: npm run build:hicasso-release' did the same, silently deleting that fragment from the close reason of rf2-rbdc.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN IT LOOKS: the bd command still SUCCEEDS. The text lands, minus whatever the shell ate, and the only signal is a stray 'command not found' line mixed into output I am often grepping. A close reason or a memory with a hole in it reads as complete.

THE RULE: for ANY bd text — remember, note, close --reason, create --description — write it to a file with a SINGLE-QUOTED heredoc and pass it with $(cat file):

  cat > /tmp/x.txt <<'XEOF'
  ...text, backticks and all, taken literally...
  XEOF
  bd close <id> --reason="$(cat /tmp/x.txt)"

The quoted delimiter is what matters — <<'XEOF' takes the body literally; <<XEOF does not. I already do this for long text; the lapses were both on text I judged 'short enough to inline'. Length is not the discriminator — CONTENT is. If it contains a backtick, a $, or a !, it goes in a quoted heredoc.

CHEAPER ALTERNATIVE when the text is genuinely one line: drop the backticks. They add nothing in a tracker field that renders as plain text.

MY MATRIX COLUMN IS A PROXY FOR CLAUSE 5, AND IT OVER-BLOCKS (2026-08-11, PR #7835).

WHAT I COMPUTE: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <latest .github/workflows commit> <pr base>` — "does this PR's base contain the newest workflow commit?" When it says NO I have been treating clause 5 as failed.

WHAT CLAUSE 5 ACTUALLY SAYS: when a merge CHANGES THE WORKFLOW MATRIX — a new required job, a changed classifier, a re-scoped path filter — the PRs behind it WHOSE SURFACE THAT CHANGE COVERS do not inherit its verdict. The trigger is a changed MATRIX, not a moved FILE.

THE CASE: #7835 showed matrix=NO because two workflow commits landed after its base — a comment reword in lint.yml (rf2-93u6) and the GATE_PREFIXES widening plus prose corrections (rf2-rbdc). NEITHER ADDS, REMOVES OR RE-SCOPES A JOB. I measured it instead of assuming: diffing the check-name sets between #7835 and the last PR that reached 91/91 showed exactly ONE difference — "All required checks passed", the AGGREGATOR, which attaches only once the jobs it waits on finish. The job set is otherwise identical, so the matrix is unchanged and clause 5 is satisfied.

THE 90-vs-91 BAND DIFFERENCE WAS ALSO THE AGGREGATOR, not a missing job. Reading a short total as "a job never ran" is the same over-blocking error one field over.

THE REFINEMENT: when matrix=NO, do not stop — DIFF THE CHECK-NAME SETS against a recently-merged PR. If they match (modulo the pending aggregator), the matrix did not change and the PR is not stale in the sense clause 5 means. If they differ, name the job that appeared or vanished and THEN require the update-branch.

WHY THIS MATTERS BOTH WAYS: the method already warns that this guard fails in both directions — keyed too loosely it lets a PR through against a superseded matrix; keyed too tightly it blocks forever on a base that is merely older. A guard that blocks forever is not safe, it is differently wrong. My proxy is the second failure, and update-branching on it costs a full CI cycle and can introduce a conflict for nothing.

SISTER LESSON: my-sweep-conflates-failure-and-cancelled. Same root — a cheap summary reused as if it were the criterion.

PR #7832 reviewed in merge chronology; reopened rf2-b6ja for the false seven-requirer count (fixtures is prose-only) and updated rf2-6rw9 with the same bounded correction; the three sequencing decisions otherwise hold.

A DOCSTRING [[WIKI-LINK]] READS EXACTLY LIKE A DEPENDENCY TO A GREP, AND NOTHING HERE DISTINGUISHES THEM (2026-08-11, three instances in one session).

INSTANCE 1: the rf2-6ync triage worker reported that two SSR suites ":require each other" and both reach ssr.entry. I transcribed it into rf2-6rw9 and made "give the package an SSR entry first" that bead's content. Both false — each named the other once in a docstring [[wiki-link]], and neither reached entry at all.

INSTANCE 2: the rf2-b6ja worker found and corrected exactly that, with evidence (lines 31 and 57).

INSTANCE 3, AND THE ONE WORTH REMEMBERING: the merged-PR audit of that same correction found it had made THE SAME MISTAKE IN ITS OWN PROSE — claiming ssr.entry has seven requirers including ssr/fixtures.cljs, whose two mentions are also docstring wiki-links. The audit's words: "the very false-dependency class this section corrects." Six semantic consumers, not seven.

WHY IT KEEPS HAPPENING: `git grep ssr.entry` returns requires, docstrings, comments and prose identically. The habit of "grep for the symbol" is right for finding candidates and wrong for counting dependents — and the wrongness is always in the direction of MORE COUPLED THAN REALITY, which makes work look harder than it is and can stall a bead for hours.

THE RULE: when counting or claiming a dependency, grep and then READ EACH HIT, or restrict the search to require/import forms. And when writing the count down, SAY WHICH QUESTION IT ANSWERS — "six semantic consumers, excluding strings and comments" — so the next reader knows whether docstrings were counted.

MAYOR-SPECIFIC: this is the concrete mechanism behind a-workers-reading-of-a-neighbouring-file-is-a-claim. The claim that keeps being wrong is nearly always a DEPENDENCY claim, and it is wrong because the tool everyone reaches for cannot tell prose from code.

CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY by the mayor before filing: there is no `tree` function defined in implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test.cljs. The only occurrences of the word are local bindings inside `(tree-seq map? :children tree)` expressions.

WHAT THE DOCS TEACH. docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/14-testing.md presents `ht/tree` as the L2 entry point — line 25's tier table ("the semantic harness — `ht/tree` under injected read fixtures"), line 140 ("`ht/tree` invokes a registered hook-free ..."), line 142 ("Four small helpers assert on the tree: `ht/find`, ...") and a worked example at line 152 binding `(ht/tree [views/todo-row {:id 7}] ...)`. glossary.md carries the same vocabulary.

TWO FAULTS, TANGLED, and they want separating before anything is written:
1. THE API NAME. Establish what the shipped kit actually exposes for this job and whether `tree` was renamed, never built, or is reached another way. The docs may be describing a design that changed under them — which is the ordinary case here — or they may be describing the RIGHT ergonomics against the WRONG spelling, in which case the kit is what should move.
2. THE 'REGISTERED' VOCABULARY. Both files still say 'registered hook-free', the loose wording rf2-0w0l corrected elsewhere. PR #7801 and PR #7812 landed the replacement vocabulary — match what they say rather than inventing a third phrasing.

WHY P2 AND NOT P3. A guide chapter that teaches a call a reader cannot make is worse than a stale sentence: the reader types it, it fails, and they conclude the kit is broken. 14-testing.md is the chapter that teaches the test kit, so it is exactly the page a new user reaches with an editor open.

DO NOT simply delete the examples. If the ergonomics the chapter teaches are good and only the spelling is wrong, say so and raise the kit-side change as its own bead rather than degrading the documentation to match a thinner API. That is a judgement call and I want it made deliberately.

FENCES: no runtime source edits from this bead — the test kit is a shipped surface and a rename there is its own change with its own witnesses. spec/* is hot-zone and out of scope.

GATES: mkdocs build --strict does NOT cover docs/design/** (exclude_docs). scripts/check_doc_slugs.py DOES validate link targets and heading anchors there, and IS SILENT ON SUCCESS — prove it saw your files by planting a bogus anchor, quoting the exit 1 naming file and line, then restoring byte-identically. Nothing validates tables; the tier table at line 25 is one, so count its columns by hand and say what you counted.

title: hic-023 — Versioned evidence projection + the four Xray views
description:
# hic-023 — Versioned evidence projection + the four Xray views

**Phase**: tooling lane · **Wave**: B · **Est.**: L · **Depends**: hic-001
**Surface**: `tools/xray/` (Hicasso producer + views) — **update `tools/xray/spec/*` in the same PR**; `implementation/hicasso/src/` only for the dev-only evidence projection hooks

## Goal
The glass, on the live tier: a versioned, adapter-neutral evidence projection from the Hicasso runtime, and the mounted / read / intent / explain-render views consuming it.

## Deliverables
- The projection: view, frame, source, current reads, known cause, attempt outcome, commit/unmount — projected from state the runtime already retains (no universal accumulator, no second history buffer); envelope carries schema, producer, scope, basis, completeness, loss.
- Honest loss states as first-class: `unknown` / `opaque` / `host-opaque` / `cap` / `uncorrelated` — never an authoritative empty.
- The four views in Xray: mounted boundaries; read attribution (sub → boundary); intent stream; explain-render (which reads changed → why this boundary ran).
- **The privacy projector as a witnessed contract**: query arguments and results pass the existing privacy projection; a witness proves a sensitive value cannot leave unredacted (seeded-value test); Xray and Pair consume the same projected schema byte-for-byte.
- Production: projection returns nil; no evidence/schema sentinels reachable (proof completed by hic-024).

## Acceptance
- Views answer their questions on the tiny consumer app; loss states visibly rendered; Xray/Pair consume one identical schema; `tools/xray/spec/*` updated.

## Worker notes
Read synth-codex §10; `codex/testing-xray.md` evidence contract. Timing proximity never fabricates causality — label uncorrelated links.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7789 (merged 2026-08-10T10:59:03Z as 07ecacf4f847b0dc002fd532ced0667147e7ad6e) — REOPEN THIS EXACT OWNER; NO DUPLICATE. COMPLETENESS: the versioned schema, four producer reads, four Xray views, consumer pin, spec, registration, and broad witnesses landed coherently. Actual Pair migration remains separately and exactly owned by open rf2-hic-076; do not duplicate it or call construction alone actual consumption. CORRECTNESS 1 — PRIVACY: projected-query protects the :reads/:edges query field, but entry-rows exports the raw read-key set as :boundary :key, edge-row exports it again under :readers, and explain-render carries it onward. hicasso-helpers then prints raw query vectors in boundary labels and derives DOM testids from them. A sensitive query argument therefore bypasses elide-wire-value, including after frame destruction; the seeded witness covers a secret RETURN VALUE only and its destroyed-frame row asserts only :reads :query. Preserve joinability without carrying raw application arguments, and add a sensitive-query negative control across mounted, attribution, and Why envelopes plus the rendered tree. CORRECTNESS 2 — FRAME ISOLATION: explain-render counts retained runs globally and indexes leads by sub-id alone. A run in frame B can make a frame-A row claim that its window was searched and can appear as an A candidate merely because both frames register the same sub id. Scope window state and candidate matching to the boundary frame, with a two-frame same-sub-id/asymmetric-window witness. The flat Intents roster also concatenates per-frame rings in frame-id order even though it promises dispatch order, and cross-frame bundles can represent fragments of one dispatch; either reconstruct the intended order/identity or state and render per-frame streams honestly. CORRECTNESS 3 — EMPTY SEMANTICS: the shared presence helper classifies every supported empty roster as :idle and renders Hicasso is running and nothing is mounted / clean bill of health. That is true only for the mounted census. Empty Intents is a capped retained window, not proof that nothing dispatched or mounted; empty attribution can coexist with mounted read-free boundaries. Make empties view-specific and keep their loss/remedy visible. ERGONOMICS: Why reports :latest-reads as sub ids only, so [:row 1] and [:row 2] collapse even though their projected query/frame rows are already available; either return the projected read identity or explicitly narrow the claim. IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the algebra and tests are otherwise cohesive and proportionate. Add only bounded witnesses for sensitive query arguments, two frames, per-view empties, and two query variants; no new store or framework is warranted. Full merged-range diff-check passed and all 89 PR checks were non-failing, demonstrating these are missing controls rather than known gate reds.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7792 LIFECYCLE SUPPLEMENT (merged 2026-08-10T10:59:35Z) — UPDATE THIS EXISTING OWNER; NO DUPLICATE. The real React witness establishes facts the #7789 Xray surface does not currently carry: Activity-hidden and unmounted collapse to the same live ownership census until a later 0-to-1 re-subscribe reveals retention retrospectively, while a Suspense-fallback-hidden subtree remains subscribed and therefore looks visible-connected in the tables while absent from the screen. The shipped four views contain no lifecycle view or state. Resolve the normative Xray distinguishes requirement honestly: either add a bounded, justified observable that can distinguish the live states, or render the host-owned distinction as host-opaque and amend the governing promise explicitly. Do not infer hidden-retained from an empty census, and do not label a Suspense-hidden connected row visible. This joins the already-open rf2-hic-023 audit repair; no new history store is presumed.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7802 (2026-08-10): two bounded residuals in the same evidence/Xray owner.

1. THE VERSIONED WIRE SHAPE CHANGED WITHOUT A VERSION BUMP. PR #7802 changes boundary-key elements from `[frame-id query]` to `[frame-id sub-id projected-query]`, intent rows from singular `:frame-id` to plural `:frames`, and `:latest-reads` from bare sub ids to `{:sub-id :query :frame-id}` maps; it also adds host fields. Yet the producer still stamps `:re-frame.hicasso.evidence/v1`, Xray still accepts that same literal, and Spec 027 still calls it v1. This directly defeats the consumer-owned pin whose docs say an evolved shape must mismatch rather than be mis-parsed as exact. Bump producer and consumer to v2 in lockstep (including fixtures/spec); pre-alpha needs no compatibility adapter, but the version must tell the truth.

2. XRAY STILL DROPS PART OF THE PROJECTED IDENTITY WHEN BUILDING ROW KEYS/TESTIDS. `boundary-slug` ignores frame-id, while `attribution-rows` slugs every edge by sub-id alone and the Reads renderer prints neither projected query nor frame. Distinct rows therefore share React keys/testids and can be visually indistinguishable. Direct JVM witness on merge 7c45f3ca9:
  boundary keys `[[:frame/a :row [:row 1]]]` and `[[:frame/b :row [:row 1]]]`
  -> slugs `["row-row-1" "row-row-1"]`;
  attribution rows for `[:row 1]` in frame A and `[:row 2]` in frame B
  -> slugs `["row" "row"]` despite distinct `:frame-id`/`:query`.
Preserve the full projected identity in React keys/testids and render enough of it (especially Reads, and the frame in Why) for a programmer to distinguish rows. Use only projected fields; no raw query data should return.

The producer's redaction, frame-scoped lead search, dispatch ordering/fragment merge, per-view empties, and host-opaque lifecycle wording otherwise review cleanly. Keep the repair within the existing schema/helpers/panel tests; no new store or framework.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7820 (merged 2026-08-10T16:27:25Z as dbbcf05584) — REOPEN THIS EXACT OWNER; no duplicate.

WHAT LANDED CLEANLY: producer, Xray consumer and Spec 027 now stamp v2 in lockstep; v1 and future stamps mismatch; no compatibility shim was added. Reads/Why render the projected query and frame, and the data plumbing uses projected fields only. Authored/landed patch ids match. Independent gates passed: tools/xray JVM 1287 tests / 6033 assertions, full implementation CLJS 13024 / 65811, doc slugs, and every edited spec table block has uniform columns.

CORRECTNESS — THE NEW “WHOLE PROJECTED IDENTITY” STRING IS NOT INJECTIVE. read-key-str concatenates each component's pr-str with `-`, then read-slug/boundary-slug pass that string through id-slug, which replaces every non-alphanumeric run with `-`. Namespace separators, hyphens, component boundaries and collection punctuation therefore collapse. Direct JVM reproduction against the landed helper:

  identities:      [:a/b :c :d]   [:a-b :c :d]   [:a :b/c :d]
  read-slugs:      a-b-c-d         a-b-c-d         a-b-c-d
  boundary-slugs:  a-b-c-d         a-b-c-d         a-b-c-d
  distinct counts: 1 and 1

All three are legal, distinct projected identities. The collision again gives distinct rows one React key and one DOM testid — exactly the residual this PR says it closes — and namespaced/hyphenated keyword ids are ordinary programmer inputs, not an adversarial edge.

COMPLETENESS / IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the new witnesses vary frame/query values that remain distinct after lossy slugification, so they prove those fields are present but not that the resulting key preserves identity. The green suites above confirm the collision is unwitnessed.

BOUNDED REPAIR: keep read-key-str as the single projected-identity door and keep raw queries out. Make the React key/testid encoding collision-resistant for the complete projected tuple (for example, a reversible escaped encoding or readable slug plus a stable full-identity suffix), then add the three-way namespace/hyphen/component-boundary control above for both read-slug and boundary-slug. Do not add an ordinal, store, compatibility layer or raw-data escape; rf2-hic-076 remains the separate Pair migration owner.
MAYOR — A CLAIM IN THIS BEAD'S DELIVERABLE IS FALSE, found by the rf2-hic-076 census (PR #7837). Recording it here rather than reopening: the bead's WORK is sound and merged; it is one sentence in the deliverable text that overstates.

THE CLAIM: "Xray and Pair consume the same projected schema byte-for-byte."

THE MEASUREMENT: Xray's Hicasso tab consumes :re-frame.hicasso.evidence/v2. PAIR CONSUMES :re-frame.freehand.evidence/v1. Pair was never moved off the donor at all — and its coupling is not even a require, so nothing in a classpath scan would have shown it.

A DEPENDENCY CAN BE A STRING, AND NO STATIC TOOL WILL EVER SEE IT (2026-08-11, rf2-hic-076 census, PR #7837).

THE CASE. The census had to classify every Xray, Story and Pair consumer of the donor surfaces. Pair has NO :require of any donor and NO deps.edn coordinate — a classpath scan finds it clean. It is not. view_tool.cljs:128 holds (def ^:private tier-ns "re-frame.freehand.tool"), and that STRING is interpolated into every nREPL form Pair emits. All five of Pair's view tools target the donor by wire protocol.

The worker's line is the one to remember: "A classpath scan finds Pair clean; it is not."

WHY THIS COMPLETES THE GREP LESSON. I already had a-docstring-wikilink-reads-as-a-dependency-to-a-grep: grep OVER-counts, because prose looks like code. This is the opposite failure, and it is worse: the dependency is REAL, LIVE and SHIPPED, and every static instrument — grep for :require, classpath scan, deps.edn audit, the bijection gate — reports nothing. Over-counting makes work look harder than it is; UNDER-counting makes a disposition look safe when it is not. This census exists to unblock rf2-hic-062, a bead about DELETING the donor tree. Acting on a classpath scan alone would have deleted a tree five shipped tools still call.

THE SAME WORKER MEASURED BOTH DIRECTIONS ON ONE SURFACE: 48 files matched a naive grep over tools/; 23 were load-bearing and 25 named a donor only in a comment, docstring or spec sentence — including a registry whose ten hits were all comments, four of them recording that it has NO donor dependency. And re-parsing ns forms by paren balancing with docstrings stripped caught TWO REQUIRES A LINE-ORIENTED REGEX MISSED. So the naive tool was wrong in both directions on the same files.

THE RULE: when a census or disposition asks "does anything still depend on X?", static analysis answers only "does anything NAME x in code". Also ask: is X reachable by a STRING — an nREPL form, a dynamic require, a keyword namespace, a URL, a build-id, a classpath entry assembled at runtime? Those are invisible by construction, and they are exactly the couplings a deletion breaks.

MAYOR APPLICATION: for any bead whose verb is RETIRE, DELETE, DISPOSITION or ARCHIVE, require the worker to state which dynamic-reference kinds it checked and how — not merely that the greps came back clean.

WHAT I HAD BEEN TEACHING: for every negative row, ask what single narrowing of the implementation would let it pass while the property is broken. If such a narrowing exists, the row is decorative. That is right, and it has caught real defects all session.

WHAT I PRAISED, AND WHY IT WAS ONLY HALF RIGHT: a worker wrote a cold-probe row, found its mutation red nothing, DELETED the row and recorded the finding in the namespace docstring. title: hic: decide the fate of the reserved residue-after-quiescence id — the facade reports rather than raises
description:

THE STATE. :rf.error/hicasso-test-residue-after-quiescence is RESERVED in docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md — reserved meaning it has no emitter and, per rf2-hic-021's CHECK C, must therefore have NO spec/009 row. THE ARGUMENT FOR RETIRING IT. The facade's assert-clean! REPORTS residue through cljs.test/do-report rather than throwing. That is the right shape: a residue finding is a TEST FAILURE, not a refusal of the instrument. A thrown refusal would make the tool that detects a leak indistinguishable from the tool breaking, and it would abort the test run at the first finding rather than reporting all of them. So the reserved id has no paying use case — which is exactly the standard this project applies to new machinery.

Reserved ids exist precisely to hold spellings. Retiring one is not free either.

Run it and quote the exit code. Its eight rules are the authority on what a reserved, live, pending-retirement or tombstoned row may look like — read them before writing the row.

MY FENCES ARE ENUMERATIONS, NOT RULES — AND A WORKER CROSSED ONE SILENTLY (2026-08-11).

WHAT MY BRIEFS SAY: "Your surface is X. You are fenced out of spec/*, .github/workflows/*, package.json, shadow-cljs.edn. Worker A holds Y, worker B holds Z." That is a NAMED SURFACE plus a LIST OF FORBIDDEN PATHS. A file that is in neither is UNDEFINED, and the worker has to guess.

WHAT HAPPENED: rf2-hic-030's worker was fenced to native.cljc|.cljs plus new test files, and out of the four hot-zone paths. It edited implementation/hicasso/resources/clj-kondo.exports/.../config.edn — neither named nor forbidden. I found it by reading its PR diff, not from a report.

I ALMOST GOT THIS WRONG IN THE EXPENSIVE DIRECTION. The directory belongs to another live worker (areduce-ka4d), so at a glance it read as a collision and I nearly told it to back the change out. Reading the actual FILE list showed no overlap — areduce holds hooks/*.clj, the README and the fixtures; config.edn is untouched by it. And the change was RIGHT: :lint-as clojure.core/defn because defcomponent is defn-shaped, with n/$ and n/props deliberately getting nothing so the grammar is not restated in a second place that can drift. Enforcing the fence mechanically would have destroyed a good decision.

THE TWO FAILURES THE ENUMERATION ALLOWS: a worker crosses silently into a contended file (a real collision nobody sees until the merge), or a worker DOESN'T make a correct small change because it was not obviously permitted.

THE FIX, one clause added to the fence paragraph in every brief:

  "Your surface is <X>. Anything outside it: if the change is trivially additive and the file is held by nobody, make it and SAY SO IN YOUR REPORT. If it is contended, hot-zone, or more than trivially additive, STOP and report instead."

That converts a list into a RULE, makes the crossing visible either way, and keeps the judgement with the worker — which is the stance. I already write the stop-and-report form for ANTICIPATED crossings (a new build id, an npm script, a new :rf.error/* id); this generalises it to the unanticipated ones, which are the only ones that surprise me.

MAYOR-SIDE COROLLARY: when a diff shows a file outside the brief's surface, READ THE FILE LIST OF EVERY OTHER LIVE WORKER BEFORE REACTING. Directory-level overlap is not collision. I check this now; I nearly did not.

title: mayor-method: the post-merge pull aborts for an undocumented cause and the documented remedy is inert
description:
THE POST-MERGE PULL NOW ABORTS FOR A CAUSE THE DOCS DO NOT NAME, AND THE DOCUMENTED REMEDY DOES NOTHING FOR IT. Hit three times in one session.

WHAT THE DOCS SAY. CLAUDE.md (two places) and the method treat a pull abort as caused by an UNCOMMITTED .beads/issues.jsonl — message "local changes would be overwritten" — with the fixed remedy: checkpoint, then `git checkout HEAD -- .beads`, then pull. bootstrap.md:211 mentions "Not possible to fast-forward" but only as one of three symptoms of a racing automated push, whose stated remedy is naming the remote and branch.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS NOW. `sh scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh` COMMITS. So by the time the pull runs, .beads is clean and there is nothing to clear — and the pull still aborts, with "fatal: Not possible to fast-forward, aborting.", because the local checkpoint COMMIT has diverged from origin's newer commits. The post-merge audit hook pushes to main asynchronously seconds after each merge, so origin gains commits while the mayor gains its own. Measured tonight: div=1/2, then div=2/9.

THE DOCUMENTED REMEDY IS INERT HERE. Clearing an uncommitted file that does not exist changes nothing, and naming the remote and branch does not fast-forward a divergent branch. The working remedy is:

  git pull --rebase origin main

then VERIFY THE OUTCOME rather than the message: no rebase in progress (.git/rebase-merge and .git/rebase-apply both absent), clean `git status`, HEAD == origin/main, and the tracker row count equal in the working file and at HEAD.

WHY THIS IS WORTH ONE PARAGRAPH RATHER THAN NOTHING: the loop hits this after nearly every merge now, so a mayor following the documented sequence will clear .beads for no reason, see the same abort, and have no next step. Worse, the two causes have DIFFERENT REMEDIES and one of them (the checkout) is dangerous in the wrong order — CLAUDE.md documents that clearing .beads after a bd close reverts the close.

THE FIX: distinguish the two aborts by their MESSAGE, which is unambiguous.
  - "local changes would be overwritten" -> uncommitted tracker state. Checkpoint, checkout, pull. (Unchanged.)
  - "Not possible to fast-forward" -> your own committed checkpoint has diverged from a racing push. `git pull --rebase origin main`, then verify the tree.

SURFACE: .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md is where the post-merge step lives; CLAUDE.md's two bullets name the cause. Make them agree rather than saying it twice differently. docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md:211 already has the symptom and may only need a pointer.

A RELATED TRAP TO MENTION IN THE SAME BREATH, because it defeats any fallback written carelessly: `git pull --ff-only ... | tail -1 || fallback` NEVER RUNS THE FALLBACK — a pipeline's exit status is its last command's. Redirect to a file, capture the code, then trim for display. I wrote exactly that bug into the merge loop tonight while briefing workers not to.

FENCE: this is a documentation fix, one paragraph plus a pointer. Do not add a script, a wrapper or a retry loop.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7833 (2026-08-11): the two-abort diagnosis and message-based branch are correct, but the fast-forward-divergence remedy omits the push required by its own outcome check. The authoritative block says `git pull --rebase origin main`, then requires `HEAD == origin/main`. A rebase preserves the local checkpoint commit by replaying it on top of origin, so before a push HEAD is necessarily ahead, not equal.

The repo captured the exact live counterexample on the first use immediately after this PR: main reflog records `084e142164 ... pull --rebase origin main (finish) ... onto 450dae1c` (#7833); 084e's sole parent is 450dae1c and its subject is `chore(beads): checkpoint`. `git rev-list --left-right --count 084e142164...450dae1c` is `1 0`. The rebase succeeded and preserved the checkpoint, yet the documented equality check was impossible. Repeating pull stays ahead; forcing equality would discard the checkpoint the drill exists to protect.

Keep the repair in the one authoritative surface: after a successful rebase, push the rebased checkpoint to origin (retry fetch/rebase/push if the asynchronous writer wins again), then verify the remote and local refs agree and the ledger row is present. Alternatively state the pre-push `ahead 1 / behind 0` condition, then push and verify equality. Do not add a wrapper or retry subsystem. The pointer surfaces need changes only if their short `then verify` wording becomes false.
MAYOR: AUDIT #7833 finding ACCEPTED. QUEUED — all six worker slots are full; the surface (.claude/commands/mayor-merge.md) is free and this goes out at the next opening.

THE FINDING, and it is exact: the two-abort diagnosis and the message-based branch are correct, but THE FAST-FORWARD-DIVERGENCE REMEDY OMITS THE PUSH REQUIRED BY ITS OWN OUTCOME CHECK. The block says `git pull --rebase origin main`, then requires HEAD == origin/main. But A REBASE PRESERVES THE LOCAL CHECKPOINT COMMIT BY REPLAYING IT ON TOP OF ORIGIN — so before a push, HEAD is NECESSARILY AHEAD BY ONE, never equal. The documented equality check is unsatisfiable at the point the drill asks for it.

THE COUNTEREXAMPLE IS MY OWN RUN, captured on the FIRST USE immediately after that PR merged. main's reflog records 084e142164 ... pull --rebase origin main (finish) ... onto 450dae1c (#7833). 084e's sole parent is 450dae1c and its subject is chore(beads): checkpoint. git rev-list --left-right --count 084e142164...450dae1c is "1 0". The rebase SUCCEEDED and preserved the checkpoint, and the documented check was still impossible. Repeating the pull stays ahead; forcing equality would DISCARD THE CHECKPOINT THE DRILL EXISTS TO PROTECT.

WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH RECORDING BEYOND THE FIX: my actual practice is already correct — checkpoint, pull/rebase, checkpoint, PUSH, then verify HEAD == origin/main, and it has been right through ten merges tonight. THE DOCUMENT DESCRIBES A SUBSET OF WHAT I DO, and the missing step is the one that makes its own verification possible. A drill that cannot be followed as written will be followed as remembered, which is exactly how it drifts.

AND IT IS THE THIRD TIME TONIGHT A CORRECTION REPRODUCED THE CLASS IT WAS CORRECTING: a PR proving a dependency false then miscounted requirers the same way; a lint repair whose new rows all passed while the rule it added was wrong; and now a pull-abort drill that omits the step its own check needs. Corrections are written under the belief that the fault has been understood, which is precisely when the next instance is least visible.

BOUNDED REPAIR, from the audit: keep it in the ONE AUTHORITATIVE SURFACE. After a successful rebase, push the rebased checkpoint to origin — retrying fetch/rebase/push if the asynchronous audit writer wins the race again — then verify the remote and local refs agree and the ledger row is present. Alternatively state the pre-push "ahead 1" as the EXPECTED state and move the equality check to after the push. Either is fine; say which and why.

DO NOT restructure the block, and do not add a script or wrapper — the surrounding text was deliberately kept to one inline block so a mayor mid-loop reads it without opening another file.
close_reason:
PR #7841 merged. AUDIT #7833's finding is closed: the drill's own outcome check is now reachable.

REPAIR (b) CHOSEN — state the pre-push 'ahead 1' as EXPECTED, then push, then verify — and the worker's reasoning for preferring it over (a) is about the mayor, not the mechanics: (b) subsumes (a) since the push is named either way, but it additionally names THE STATE A MAYOR ACTUALLY OBSERVES MID-DRILL. Its words: the failure mode is not 'forgot to push', it is a mayor seeing an unexplained inequality and reaching for reset --hard, DESTROYING THE CHECKPOINT THE DRILL EXISTS TO PROTECT. A step you are told to take without being told what you will see is a step people improvise around.

It verified the counterexample in the repo rather than trusting my brief: 084e142164 is chore(beads): checkpoint, sole parent 450dae1c (#7833's own commit), rev-list --left-right --count giving 1 0.

The push's rejection case (the audit-hook race) is ONE CLAUSE — fetch, rebase, push again — not a retry subsystem. The four outcome reads are unchanged; they now run AFTER the push, where they are answerable. One inline block, no restructure, no script. CLAUDE.md and bootstrap.md untouched, because their 'then verify' wording does not become false — CLAUDE.md's equality sentence resumes the ordinary --ff-only flow where no local commit exists.

IT PROVED A GATE'S BLIND SPOT RATHER THAN CLAIMING A GREEN: a bogus anchor planted in docs/index.md gave exit 1; the same planted in .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md gave EXIT 0 WITH ZERO OUTPUT. So neither check_doc_slugs.py nor mkdocs validates the file this PR changed — it read the sentence by hand and claimed nothing more.

It also hit the harness-vs-.exit-file trap itself and diagnosed it correctly as SELF-INFLICTED: its concurrent plant experiment had docs/index.md mid-plant when the spine's anchor step read it. Incidentally a live demonstration that the spine really runs that validator and really goes red on it.

title: ci: lint.yml's comment counts the self-test's mutations — delete the count rather than correcting it again

A WORKTREE PINS ITS BRANCH — SO A FIX-WORKER CANNOT CHECK OUT A BRANCH ANOTHER WORKTREE STILL HOLDS (2026-08-11).

WHAT I DID: dispatched a fix-worker with `git worktree add <new path> worker/native-hic030` to repair a red PR. That branch was still checked out in the original worker's worktree. GIT REFUSES TO CHECK OUT ONE BRANCH IN TWO WORKTREES, so my dispatch could not even complete its setup step.

AND I COULD NOT SIMPLY FREE IT. The original worktree held an UNCOMMITTED modification to spec/009 — the previous worker's local experiment, partially reverted despite its report claiming a verified clean revert. scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh REFUSED with REMOVE_REFUSED_KEEP, correctly: the file is not build output. And the method forbids building a commit from another worker's uncommitted work, because only its author knows whether it forms a coherent change.

THE CORRECT DISPATCH FOR A FIX-WORKER ON AN EXISTING BRANCH — use a detached checkout at the REMOTE head and push with an explicit refspec:

  git worktree add --detach <path> origin/worker/<branch>
  ...work, commit...
  git push origin HEAD:worker/<branch>

That updates the PR's branch without the branch ever being checked out, so it works whether or not the original worktree is still around. Verify afterwards that gh pr view's headRefOid equals the local rev-parse HEAD.

THE CHECK TO RUN BEFORE DISPATCHING TO AN EXISTING BRANCH: `git worktree list | grep <branch>`. If anything holds it, either reap that worktree first (only on a quotable completion report, and only if it is clean) or dispatch detached. Do not discover this in the worker's setup step.

THE SAME MECHANISM AS reap-before-merge-avoids-the-orphaned-branch: the worktree pins the branch, and nothing else does. There it cost an orphaned remote on every merge; here it cost a dispatch that could not start.

SECOND FINDING, WORTH ITS OWN LINE: the original worker reported "reverted both files with a verified git checkout -- (reverted-clean: True '')" and spec/009 WAS STILL MODIFIED. Its verification either ran before a later edit or checked the other file. So a worker's claim of a clean tree is not evidence of one — git status in the worktree is. Check it before reaping, which is exactly what the removal script's guard does and why the guard exists.

PR #7840 audited at merge 1767f46907b7178caf47a9fa325e6ebfa3e22234 (2026-08-10T20:17:53Z). The three driven transactional construction repairs and bookkeeping finalisation are sound; authored/landed blobs match and all 91 checks are non-failing. Reopened rf2-hic-027: PR #7840 reclosed the existing #7836 default-container success leak without fixing it, and its own test names but does not drive asynchronous hydration body refusals, which still report globally and degrade into a generic timeout instead of rejecting with the original runtime ex-info. rf2-cw7p is complete.

PR #7841 audited at merge ebbe4e4a96bdb0d43a6a07e0d0dc0c4e239fa054 (2026-08-10T20:24:10Z). Both bounded corrections are complete and accurate: the divergence drill now pushes the rebased checkpoint before equality verification and names the expected intermediate state; lint.yml now limits its ESLint claim to author-maintained JavaScript and names the tracked generated exception. Authored and landed blobs match, the two-commit diff check and six-job YAML parse pass, and all 91 checks are non-failing. No actionable finding; open rf2-fxpn already owns the separate stale counts in eslint.config.mjs.

A ONE-SYMBOL EXTENSION BEYOND A BEAD'S LETTER IS ACCEPTED WHEN IT IS THE SAME GRAMMAR, INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED, AND WITNESSED (2026-08-11, rf2-ka4d / PR #7843).

A worker fixing areduce in hic lint's direct-view-call roster also added amap, flagged it in the PR body, and invited a trim. Accepted. areduce and amap are the same grammar one argument apart - both bind an index symbol and an accumulator symbol, which is exactly the shape the roster mishandled - and the worker REPRODUCED the identical false ERROR with amap at the pin and landed a witness (self-call-in-amap) rather than reasoning by analogy.

THE GENERAL RULE: for a ROSTER or CLASS bug, class-completeness is the deliverable, not sprawl. Trimming a reproduced sibling to honour the letter of a bead written before anyone knew the sibling existed is scope discipline used against the point of the work - it knowingly ships a build-blocking false ERROR one line from the fix.

THE LINE THAT KEEPS THIS FROM BEING LICENCE - all three conditions, not one: SAME GRAMMAR (not merely related), INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED (a failing case of its own, not analogy), and WITNESSED (a test that goes red without the fix). A symbol that only felt related, or one added without its own failing case, gets trimmed.

AND THE WORKER'S CONDUCT IS THE PATTERN TO WANT: take it, flag it prominently, offer the trim. That gives the mayor a real decision instead of a silent widening or an unfixed sibling.

# hic-027 — The L3 mounted test facade

**Phase**: tooling lane · **Wave**: B · **Est.**: M · **Depends**: hic-020
**Surface**: the test-kit module, mounted-facade files only (L0–L2 files are hic-020's)

## Goal
The mounted half of the testing ladder, split from hic-020 so the pure kit and the mounted kit land in parallel PRs.

## Deliverables
- Isolated-frame `mount!`, `hydrate!`, `render!`, `dispatch-and-settle!`, `settle!`, `unmount!`, `assert-clean!` (residue vs pre-mount baseline before reset).
- Interop with Testing Library/user-event; no new selector language; no fake hooks runtime.
- Positive + sabotage controls for the facade itself.

## Acceptance

## Worker notes
Read spec §9; `codex/testing-xray.md` mounted-facade paragraph.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")

3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.

5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").

notes:

WHAT IS SOUND: frame isolation is structural; the public mounted APIs are compact; authored and landed patch identities match; the untouched browser suite independently passed 1177 tests / 7334 assertions.

CORRECTNESS/ERGONOMICS: a temporary browser witness mounted a valid registered Hicasso view whose body contains a plain function child head, a runtime :rf.error/hicasso-bad-head case. Its timeout branch only rejects; it does not unmount, remove the container, close the adoption window, decrement counters, remove the facade-frame entry, or destroy the frame. Since only assert-clean! records the verdict and releases private open/frame bookkeeping, these tests leave process-global facade state behind and prevent the unread-mount reset gate from reaching zero.

Capture and preserve the original runtime ex-info/id, prevent an uncaught browser pageerror, and restore the exact pre-call frame/container/census state on synchronous render failure or hydration timeout. MAYOR: AUDIT #7822 finding ACCEPTED. QUEUED, NOT DISPATCHED — it must sequence behind worker/kitname-0ckh (rf2-0ckh), which currently holds implementation/hicasso/test_kit/** to rename the L2 entry per naming-ledger row 23. The repair lives in test/mounted.cljs, the same tree. Dispatching now would collide.

WHY THE FINDING IS RIGHT AND WORTH THE FOLLOW-UP, in my reading:

The facade's OWN CLOSE RECORD claimed malformed form is surfaced by the runtime. The audit drove it: a valid registered view whose body contains a plain function CHILD head — a genuine :rf.error/hicasso-bad-head case — and hm/mount! RETURNED A HANDLE. React emitted an uncaught page error, and the call left one extra registered frame and one attached body container. So the programmer gets neither the structured error data nor a usable cleanup path, and the claim in the close record was broader than what the code does. That is the ninth instance this session of a claim exceeding what was driven, and this one was in a close reason I wrote.

Note the id is correct here and is NOT the rf2-z5ji case: hicasso-bad-head is a CHILD-POSITION rule, and this is a child head. rf2-z5ji corrected the guide for the ROOT position, where nothing refuses. The two are consistent.

SAME FAILURE CLASS BY INSPECTION, not driven: hydrate! allocates frame, container, handle and open/standing counters BEFORE settlement, and its timeout branch only rejects — it does not unmount, remove the container, close the adoption window, decrement counters, remove the facade-frame entry, or destroy the frame. A synchronous hydrate-root! failure has the same missing-rollback shape. AND THE FACADE'S OWN TESTS DO NOT EXERCISE ITS BOOKKEEPING: the two residue sabotage rows call hm/residue and manually repair their induced fault but never finalize with hm/assert-clean!. Only assert-clean! records the verdict and releases the private open/frame bookkeeping, so those rows leave process-global facade state behind and prevent the unread-mount reset gate from reaching zero. The tests for the cleanliness instrument are themselves unclean.

BOUNDED REPAIR (from the audit, and it is a fence): make mount/hydrate construction TRANSACTIONAL AT ONE SEAM. Preserve the original runtime ex-info and its id, prevent the uncaught browser pageerror, and restore the exact pre-call frame/container/census state on synchronous render failure or hydration timeout. MERGED-PR AUDIT #7836 — NORMAL SUCCESSFUL TEARDOWN STILL LEAVES THE FACADE'S OWN DOM CONTAINER BEHIND.

This belongs to the exact mounted-facade owner, not a new issue. Preserve a caller-supplied `:container` exactly where it is. Fold the same ownership rule into the already-recorded transactional failure rollback. Witness both arms by body-child identity/count; do not add a page-wide scrubber or generic resource tracker.

The namespace correction and async verdict threading in PR #7836 otherwise match the shipped facade. `hm/rerender!` remains a known deliberate naming divergence already owned by open naming-packet rf2-hic-065; do not duplicate or settle it here.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7840 (merged 2026-08-10T20:17:53Z as 1767f46907) — REOPEN THIS EXACT OWNER; no duplicate.

WHAT LANDED CLEANLY: the three driven channels are repaired at one small rollback seam. mount! now returns React render refusals to the caller, synchronous hydrate-root! failures reject, adoption timeouts reject after undoing root/container/frame state, and the two sabotage rows finally release their facade bookkeeping. RESIDUAL 1 — THE ALREADY-RECORDED #7836 SUCCESS-PATH LEAK WAS RECLOSED WITHOUT BEING FIXED. supplied? is used only by abandon!. A successful default mount still appends a fresh body div, handle-for records no ownership bit, unmount! deliberately leaves every container connected, and assert-clean! reports clean then finalises without detaching it. The canonical mount → unmount! → assert-clean! recipe therefore accumulates one empty facade-owned body node per test. BOUNDED REPAIR: carry one facade-container ownership bit through a successful handle and detach only that node after the cleanliness verdict. Add one hydration row using the existing bad-body witness and capture the root's onUncaughtError so hydrate! rolls back and promptly rejects with the original ex-info, while preserving the existing recoverable-error reporter.
