BUT IT IS BLOCKED TWICE, and the second blocker is this bead's real content:
  1. The two files :require EACH OTHER, so they port as a unit, not one at a time.
  2. Both reach re-frame.bench.hicasso.ssr.entry, WHICH HAS NO PACKAGE COUNTERPART. The package needs an SSR entry before either can move.

So the shape of this bead is: give implementation/hicasso an SSR entry, then port the pair (plus host_hatch) onto it. The entry is the deliverable that unblocks everything else; the port is the proof it works.

WHY THE COVERAGE MATTERS, restated from rf2-yvj9's finding: impl/codec.cljs makes bare :client-only the DEFAULT — it is what an author gets by writing nothing. So the package's most-reached SSR configuration currently has no package-level witness at all. And per rf2-6ync's triage, the arm1 suites carrying it are classified STAYS unless ported here, so nothing else will bring them across.

A MEASUREMENT FROM THAT TRIAGE THAT APPLIES DIRECTLY, and it should shape how you argue value: ALL 69 prototype suites already run on every PR (freehand/test is on :source-paths and :node-test's cljs-test$ matches them; :browser-test excludes only re-frame.freehand.bench.*, a different tree). So porting buys ZERO additional coverage of the prototype. It buys coverage of THE PACKAGE. That is the only justification a port needs, and it is a real one — but say it that way rather than implying the tests are currently unrun.

FENCES: do NOT edit the frozen bench tree — check_freeze.py must stay exit 0 with its manifest unchanged. If a port needs a new build id or npm script, STOP and report; those are sequential-access. spec/* is hot zone.

WITNESS DISCIPLINE: drive the case where the guarantee is WEAKEST — a Client-only surface that declares NO fallback, renders nothing where the host sits, and mounts correctly after client adoption. A witness that only ever supplies a fallback proves nothing about the default. Pair it with the fallback arm the way arm1 does, so the two are read together.
MAYOR CORRECTION — MY EARLIER NOTE ON THIS BEAD IS WRONG. Both blockers it recorded are FALSE, verified against origin/main by the rf2-b6ja worker (PR #7832). Read this note, not the one above it.

WHAT I WROTE, taken from the rf2-6ync triage worker's summary: that arm1/host_ssr_dom_cljs_test and arm1/fallback_contents_cljs_test :require EACH OTHER (so they move as a unit), and that BOTH reach re-frame.bench.hicasso.ssr.entry, which has no package counterpart — making "the package needs an SSR entry first" this bead's real content.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE:
  - THEY DO NOT :require EACH OTHER. Each names the other exactly once, in a docstring [[wiki-link]] — lines 31 and 57. There is no code dependency and no unit-move constraint.
  - NEITHER REACHES ssr.entry. That namespace's seven requirers are the five ssr/* STAYS suites plus the entry's own driver and corpus. These two use React's own react-dom/server DIRECTLY.

SO THE PAIR IS AN ORDINARY arm1/* PORT — classification PORT, not STAYS — AND NEEDS NO PACKAGE SSR ENTRY. This bead's content is therefore much smaller than I recorded: port the two suites onto the package. There is no runtime feature to build first.

AND host_hatch_dom_cljs_test IS NOT THEIR THIRD MEMBER. I put it here on the same bad summary. It is the only one of the three needing arm1.hook-probe — the blocker rf2-wjag already carries for hook_ledger and frame_prop. It belongs on that bead, not this one.

THE LESSON FOR ME, recorded as bd memory: I transcribed one worker's analysis OF FILES IT DID NOT EDIT into a bead note without verifying it. A worker's reading of a neighbouring file is a CLAIM, not a measurement, and deserves the same treatment I give code claims — especially when it becomes the stated content of another bead. The triage worker's classification work was excellent and independently reconciled; its incidental dependency claims were not, and I promoted them to fact.

WHEN DISPATCHING THIS: brief it as a two-suite port with no blocker, tell the worker to verify the requires itself before starting (that is how this correction was found), and fence it out of the frozen bench tree — check_freeze.py must stay exit 0 with its manifest unchanged. implementation/hicasso/test/** is held by worker/reauth-wjag; sequence behind it.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7832 FOLLOW-UP CORRECTION. The latest mayor correction above is right that this pair does not reach ssr.entry, but its supporting sentence repeats one small false dependency: ssr/fixtures.cljs only mentions [[ssr.entry/render]] and [[ssr.entry]] inside its namespace docstring; it does not require entry. The actual semantic consumers are six (the five named ssr/* suites plus ssr/node.cljs), not seven plus the corpus. This does not change this bead: port the same two suites with no SSR entry.
close_reason: Landed via PR #7842 (merged fdead7d060): host_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs (670 lines) gives the package its own Client-only SSR witness, so the default configuration is no longer covered only in the bench tree. NOTE the premise I transcribed onto this bead — that the two namespaces :require each other and reach ssr.entry — was FALSE; those were [[wiki-link]]s inside docstrings, which read as dependencies to a grep. The bead's actual finding (no package-local Client-only witness) held and is what was fixed.

value:
gh's TWO CHECK COMMANDS DISAGREE ON CASE, AND A CLAUSE-4 PROBE THAT IGNORES IT BLOCKS FOREVER (2026-08-11).

  gh pr checks --json state   -> UPPERCASE: SUCCESS, SKIPPED, FAILURE, CANCELLED, IN_PROGRESS
  gh run list  --json status  -> lowercase: completed, queued, in_progress

I wrote the merge criterion's clause 4 as `select(.status != "COMPLETED")` and it counted every FINISHED run as live. The tell was that the number was IDENTICAL (5) across three unrelated branches at three different head shas - it was not a live-run count at all, it was the total run count. PR #7842 sat at 91/91 with all five runs completed/success and my own guard reported it unmergeable.

WHY THIS IS WORTH REMEMBERING RATHER THAN JUST FIXING: it fails CLOSED, which feels safe and is not. mayor-merge.md already says a guard that blocks forever is not safe, it is differently wrong - and a case-mismatch is the quietest possible way to build one, because every field you print looks right and the comparison is what is broken.

THE DISCRIMINATOR THAT CAUGHT IT: an identical count across branches that share nothing. A real live-run count varies per branch. When a probe returns a suspiciously uniform number, print the RAW rows (`.[]|"\(.status) \(.conclusion) \(.headSha[0:8]) \(.name)"`) before believing it - the raw read settled this in one command.

WRITE THE COMPARISON CASE-INSENSITIVELY: `select((.status|ascii_downcase) != "completed")`. And keep requiring the TERMINAL state rather than enumerating the blocking ones - REQUESTED, WAITING and PENDING all exist and a criterion listing bad states fails open on the first one nobody wrote down.

title: hic-022 — First lint layer: bounded clj-kondo checks
description:
# hic-022 — First lint layer: bounded clj-kondo checks

**Phase**: tooling lane · **Wave**: B · **Est.**: M · **Depends**: hic-001
**Surface**: `implementation/hicasso/resources/clj-kondo.exports/` (new) + lint tests

## Goal
The honest static checks — syntactic facts only, no implied whole-program analysis — recovering part of the compile-time-shape-checking loss versus UIx.

## Deliverables
- Checks: direct `defview` invocation; `sub` in an obviously deferred position (fn literal inside a body); plain function in head position; `:&` carrying non-map; missing `:key` in mapped children (heuristic, warning-level); interactive element without accessible name (warning; full a11y in hic-043).
- Export packaging so a consumer's clj-kondo picks them up from the artefact.
- Each check tested against positive and negative fixtures.

## Acceptance
- Checks fire on fixtures and stay silent on the tiny consumer app; README documents each check's honest limits.

## Worker notes
Read `codex/ergonomics-api.md` (editor/diagnostic ergonomics); synth.md ergonomics paragraph. Do not attempt read-extent proof by lint — that is the runtime's law (hic-011).

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).
notes:
SCOPE NOTE (2026-08-10, from the rf2-djxr ruling): consider one syntactic warning — a reset!/vreset!/swap! whose argument is a delay or fn form that lexically contains h/sub. Warning level only. Skip it if the check cannot be honest syntactically. This is assistance, not enforcement (I7's ratified limit).
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7784 (merged 2026-08-10T09:45:06Z as 6120514a57ea6aae1524d49060e823615d3ade0c) — KEEP THIS EXACT OWNER OPEN; NO DUPLICATE.

COMPLETENESS: the export/package shape and six bounded checks are real, and the live committed witness passes, but the owner's direct-defview invocation, symbol/plain-function head, and broader deferred-fn deliverables were consciously omitted. Do not add whole-program machinery merely to tick those boxes; either obtain an explicit scope ruling or implement only an editor-reliable bounded slice. More immediately, `test:hicasso-lint` is registered as UNSCHEDULED: required `lint.yml` loads the hook against current repository code but does not run the positive fixtures, so a check can stop firing and CI remain green. Keep this owner open until the fixture witness runs in a lane with the Clojure CLI (a missing CLI currently SKIPs green), or an equivalent required witness exists.

CORRECTNESS / ERGONOMICS: an independent stdin probe against the shipped export found only the nested bad-head and a bare-anchor warning. It missed `(defview root [_] [(fn [] ...)])`, even though that returned root vector is itself the illegal Hiccup head; it also ignored literal `"button"` and qualified-keyword native heads. The runtime accepts strings and every keyword/symbol in `hiccup-tag?`, and `parse-tag` uses `name`, so the README/hook claim that `:app/button` is ordinary tagged data disagrees with shipped behavior. Conversely `[:a {}]` is not interactive without `href` or an interactive handler, yet the rule warns and calls it an unlabelled control. Preserve the conservative, trust-the-programmer posture: cover the decidable root/string/runtime-keyword cases and stop the definite bare-anchor false positive; do not broaden into guesses.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / EVIDENCE: packaging, resolution, props-map exclusion, exact-row fixtures, and the narrow rules are cohesive. `python implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_lint_export.py` passed with all six checks and a quiet negative/testbed corpus. The bounded repairs above belong here; no new framework or analyzer is warranted.
OPERATOR RULING (2026-08-10 20:36 AUSEST, Mike, in session) — OPTION 1: DISPATCH NOW WITH THE ROSTER CORRECTED.
ROSTER (supersedes the description's check list):
1. Direct defview invocation — ERROR (true invariant).
2. Plain function in head position — ERROR (true invariant).
3. sub inside a fn literal within a body (obviously deferred read) — WARNING.
4. Missing :key in mapped children — WARNING (heuristic; the runtime warning remains the authority).
5. Interactive element without an accessible name — WARNING (full a11y stays hic-043).
6. The rf2-djxr guardrail: reset!/vreset!/swap! whose argument is a delay or fn form lexically containing sub — WARNING; skip if not honestly checkable syntactically.
DROPPED: the ':& carrying non-map' check — the :& grammar key is retired from the end-state design (owned-wins merge recipe instead); do not police a ghost.
SEVERITY LAW: errors only for true invariants; warnings for heuristics; nothing blocks a build. Assistance, not enforcement.
NAMES: build against today's prototype spellings; the rf2-hic-066 rename sweep updates the configs mechanically (add the exports to the sweep's grep surface).
Everything else in the description stands (export packaging, positive+negative fixtures, honest-limits README, silent on the tiny consumer app). READY FOR MAYOR DISPATCH.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7791 (merged 2026-08-10T10:53:14Z as bde1cda6e9f4d5d3ba132b425cdd76de8c1c9a30) — RESOLVES THE BARE-ANCHOR FALSE POSITIVE RECORDED BY AUDIT #7784. The hook now follows both compiled substrates: a button always needs name evidence, while an anchor is judged only when literal props contain :href. Hrefless fragment/class anchors are pinned quiet; the existing href-positive fixture still fires. Diff-check and the live six-check export gate passed; all 89 PR checks were non-failing. No new audit finding. Keep this exact owner OPEN for its other recorded completeness/correctness obligations, especially required-lane fixture scheduling and the remaining root/head coverage; do not re-derive this fixed anchor item.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7794 (merged 2026-08-10T11:22:38Z as 33a4acacd513f6f45ca19cc73f0c3b5008ff34c4) — REOPEN THIS EXACT OWNER; NO DUPLICATE.

COMPLETENESS: the corrected six-rule roster, fixture scheduling, hard-fail tool discovery, and mutation witness landed, but the new ERROR-level direct-view-call rule has no negative fixture for ordinary lexical bindings that share the enclosing view name.

CORRECTNESS / ERGONOMICS: check-direct-view-call! compares token spelling only. Against the shipped export, both `(h/defview card [card] (card) [:div "ok"])` and `(h/defview via-let [_] (let [via-let (fn [] :ordinary)] (via-let)) [:div "ok"])` report re-frame.hicasso/direct-view-call at ERROR and clj-kondo exits 3, although each call resolves to a legal local binding rather than the view Var. Because the required lane runs with --fail-level error, this blocks correct programmer code.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / ACCEPTANCE: keep the bounded, editor-reliable self-call rule, but distinguish lexical bindings from the enclosing view identity (the hook already centralizes api/resolve). Add parameter/destructuring or let-shadow negative coverage while preserving the recursive self-call positive row. The shipped gate and its self-test otherwise pass; gate scheduling reports 37 scheduled and one known hole.

MAYOR 2026-08-10 ~22:10 AUSEST — QUEUED FOR THE NEXT FREE SLOT; NOT DISPATCHED YET
(six workers live). Recording the shape so the next pass does not re-derive it.

THIS IS A STANCE VIOLATION, NOT A NITPICK, WHICH IS WHY IT JUMPS THE P3s. The
project trusts the programmer and rejects nag-diagnostics. check-direct-view-call!
compares TOKEN SPELLING ONLY, it is ERROR level, and the required lane runs with
--fail-level error. So legal code is refused:

  (h/defview card [card] (card) [:div "ok"])
  (h/defview via-let [_] (let [via-let (fn [] :ordinary)] (via-let)) [:div "ok"])

Both report re-frame.hicasso/direct-view-call and exit 3, although each call
resolves to a legal LOCAL BINDING rather than the view Var. A gate that blocks
correct programmer code is worse than no gate.

THE REPAIR IS BOUNDED and the audit says how: keep the self-call rule (it is
editor-reliable, which is why it was chosen over whole-program resolution), but
distinguish a lexical binding from the enclosing view identity — the hook already
centralises api/resolve, so the mechanism is in hand. Add parameter/destructuring
and let-shadow NEGATIVE coverage while preserving the recursive self-call POSITIVE
row. Do not reach for whole-program analysis; that was already declined on this
bead for good reasons (cache-dependent ns-analysis fires in CI and stays silent in
an editor).

NOT A REGRESSION ON MAIN TODAY: main is green and no shipped code trips it. The
exposure is forward — any worker writing a hicasso view whose local binding shares
the view name will be blocked by a false ERROR and will reasonably assume its own
code is wrong.
CORRECTION to the close reason above: the two follow-ups are rf2-c6t6 (the same shadowing blindness in the read rules, P4 — WARNING level, not the build-blocking ERROR that reopened this bead) and rf2-zzdg (lint.yml's stale 'three ways' comment, P4, hot-zone). The ids rf2-yc4b and rf2-8sdq named in the close reason were written before the beads were filed and do not exist.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7804 (merged 2026-08-10T13:50:56Z as 5e33c4eb5) — REOPEN THIS EXACT OWNER AGAIN; no duplicate.

WHAT LANDED CLEANLY: the original false ERROR for a defview parameter, destructuring, ordinary let/for/fn/hfn, single-arity letfn, catch, and as-> is removed; the genuine recursive self-call remains red; the export README now matches the six configured checks. Independent audit runs passed the live lint gate and all four mutation self-tests, the tracked tree stayed clean, and authored/landed patch ids are exact.

COMPLETENESS / CORRECTNESS — MULTI-ARITY letfn PARAMETERS STILL FALSE-RED. locals-bound-by destructures each letfn form as [nm params] and collects params only when that second node is a vector. In a valid multi-arity letfn, the second node is the first arity list, so none of any arity's parameter vectors are recognized. Reproduced against this merge and the pinned :clj-kondo alias:

  (h/defview card [_]
    (letfn [(invoke
              ([card] (card))
              ([card x] (card x)))]
      [:div (invoke (fn [& _] :ok))]))

Both calls to the legal local parameter report re-frame.hicasso/direct-view-call at ERROR and clj-kondo exits 3; a genuine (genuine) self-call in the same probe still reports. This directly contradicts the PR/README claim that letfn parameters are covered and preserves the same build-blocking programmer-friction class #7804 meant to close.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / BOUNDED REPAIR: keep the small syntax-local walker and conservative whole-form silencing. Teach the letfn arm to collect the parameter vector of a single arity OR every parameter vector under its arity lists (the existing fn-locals shape is the nearby model), then add a multi-arity negative fixture and a red mutation witness. No api/resolve, whole-program scope engine, or custom-macro analysis is warranted.
MAYOR: AUDIT #7804 finding ACCEPTED, and this is the FIFTH instance tonight of one specific failure shape — a witness whose STATED SCOPE EXCEEDS THE CASES IT ACTUALLY DRIVES.

Here: locals-bound-by destructures each letfn form as [nm params] and collects params only when that second node is a VECTOR. In a valid MULTI-ARITY letfn the second node is the first arity LIST, so no arity's parameter vector is recognised and every use of a legal local parameter reports direct-view-call at ERROR — clj-kondo exits 3, the build stops. The PR body and the export README both claim letfn parameters are covered. They are covered for single-arity, which is the only shape the witness drove.

THE OTHER FOUR TONIGHT, same shape: rf2-hic-020's parity table covered only the valid raw component while claiming both arms; rf2-hic-007's completeness test claimed all six constructor fields unforgeable while running only where declaring! had already supplied real values; rf2-hic-012's comment recorded the expected result as though measured; rf2-hic-021's completeness check ranged over ids THAT EXIST, so thirteen refusals with no id satisfied it vacuously.

WHY IT KEEPS HAPPENING, and it is not carelessness: in each case the witness was written from the FIX, so it drives the shapes the author had in mind while fixing. The shapes that break it are precisely the ones the author did not think of — which is the same set. A test derived from the implementation inherits the implementation's blind spots.

THE COUNTERMEASURE I AM PUTTING IN BRIEFS: derive the witness from the GRAMMAR of the thing, not from the fix. For a letfn arm that means enumerating letfn's actual legal shapes (single-arity vector, multi-arity lists, with and without a docstring/prepost) and driving each, rather than testing the one the fix was written against. State in the PR body which shapes of the grammar you drove and which you did not.

BOUNDED REPAIR (from the audit, and it is a fence): keep the small syntax-local walker and the conservative whole-form silencing. Teach the letfn arm to collect the parameter vector of a single arity OR every parameter vector under its arity lists. Do not reach for resolution — #7804 established by probe that api/resolve returns nil for the cases that matter and never sees locals.

READY TO DISPATCH; held only because six workers are live. Surface is implementation/hicasso/resources/clj-kondo.exports/** plus scripts/check_lint_export.py, currently held by nobody.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7818 (merged 2026-08-10T16:16:28Z as 2e2471bc14) — REOPEN THIS EXACT OWNER; no duplicate.

CORRECTNESS: the repair is sound. A letfn fnspec is a fn tail, delegation to fn-locals removes the narrower duplicate parser, authored/landed patch ids match, and both the live export gate and all five mutation self-tests pass at the CI pin (clj-kondo 2026.04.15).

COMPLETENESS / IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the new fixtures do not make the stated “every parameter of every arity” property load-bearing. locals-bound-by unions all names for the whole letfn and self-call-nodes then suppresses that entire form as soon as ANY arity binds the view name. Every committed multi-arity negative row binds the same view name in both arities, so recognizing only the later arity is enough to make every row green.

PROOF: changed fn-locals' multi-arity source from `forms` to `(rest forms)`, deliberately skipping the first arity. The pinned live gate still exited 0: “OK: 6 checks fire on their fixtures, correct code is silent, and the artefact's own testbeds are quiet.” The source was restored exactly and the worktree verified clean. The current mutation only removes ALL arities, so it does not catch this narrower regression.

BOUNDED REPAIR: add one independent negative case in which the view name is bound only by the FIRST arity and later arities bind different names, plus a self-test mutation that skips the first arity (or an equivalent discriminating mutation). Keep the current small syntax-local walker and whole-form silencing; no resolution or scope engine. rf2-ka4d remains the separate exact owner for the six other binding-form omissions.
MAYOR: AUDIT #7818 finding ACCEPTED and ROUTED, not separately dispatched — worker/lintarms-ka4d already holds implementation/hicasso/resources/clj-kondo.exports/** and scripts/check_lint_export.py for rf2-ka4d, so a second worker would only conflict. It has the bounded repair (one negative case where the view name is bound ONLY by the first arity while later arities bind different names, plus a discriminating self-test mutation) and has been told to sequence this BEFORE rf2-ka4d, since this is a reopened P1 on code already on main.

I also passed on the generalisation, because it corrects an instruction I have been issuing all session: grammar-derivation is necessary and NOT sufficient. Enumerating legal shapes answers 'did I test this form?'; it does not answer 'can this row tell the difference?' The audit settled it by measurement — changing fn-locals' multi-arity source to (rest forms) left the pinned live gate at exit 0. Recorded as bd memory rows-must-be-discriminating-not-merely-shaped.

rf2-ka4d stays the separate exact owner for the six binding-form omissions; the worker is told to keep them in their own commit.

The PR correctly insists all evidence be measured at clj-kondo 2026.04.15 because the host native binary is 2025.10.23, but check_lint_export.py still searches clj-kondo before clojure and verifies no version. On the audit host the standard documented command selected C:\Users\miket\AppData\Roaming\npm\clj-kondo.cmd v2025.10.23 and exited 0 with the same reassuring OK line; the pinned :clj-kondo alias v2026.04.15 also passed. Thus a default green does not establish the pin the gate claims. BOUNDED REPAIR: accept a native binary only when its reported version matches the project pin (prefer deriving that pin from the artefact deps/established canonical source); otherwise fall back to the pinned alias, or fail hard if unavailable. No downloader, version manager, or new lane.

title: hic lint: six more binding forms are missing from direct-view-call's roster, each a build-blocking false ERROR
description:
MEASURED by the rf2-hic-022 worker (PR #7818) AFTER its own repair landed, each reproduced as a live false ERROR at the CI pin (2026.04.15). Fenced out of its bead, so filed here.

THE DEFECT CLASS. The export README says the check "refuses any call whose name has been rebound", but the roster of binding forms it actually reads is FINITE. Six binding forms are not in it, so a legal local bound by any of them is reported as a direct view call — at ERROR, which STOPS THE BUILD. This is the same build-blocking programmer-friction class that reopened rf2-hic-022 twice.

THE SIX, with the worker's probes:
  dotimes                 (dotimes [v 3] (v))
  this-as                 (this-as v (v))
  reify method param      (reify Object (toString [v] (str (v))))
  specify! method param   (specify! (js-obj) Object (toString [v] (str (v))))
  extend-type method param (extend-type T Object (toString [v] (str (v))))
  defmethod param         (defmethod mm :k [v] (v))

`dotimes` is literally one symbol short in the let-shaped set. The other five are one small arm each, of the same class as the existing `catch` and `as->` arms. Reuse `fn-locals` where the form is a fn tail — PR #7818 showed a fnspec IS a fn tail and deleted code by delegating to it rather than adding a branch.

FENCES, inherited and still binding: keep the SMALL syntax-local walker and the conservative whole-form silencing. NO whole-program analysis. **Do not use api/resolve** — PR #7804 established by probe that it returns nil for the cases that matter and never sees locals. A binding silences the whole form it heads; silence is the only failure these hooks are permitted, and the README says so.

WITNESS, DERIVED FROM THE GRAMMAR NOT FROM YOUR FIX — this is the instruction that finally worked on this surface. For each of the six, enumerate the form's legal shapes and drive each as an independent negative row, where the view's name is THE ONLY THING bound in that row so it cannot pass on a neighbour's coverage. Add at least one POSITIVE row per form too: a genuine self-call inside the same construct must still fire, which guards the over-silencing direction. State in the PR body which shapes you drove AND which you did not, with reasons — the second list is the valuable half.

MUTATION PROOF: revert each arm, quote the verbatim red, restore BYTE-IDENTICALLY and confirm green. Verify the mutation actually applied before believing any result — PR #7818 did this by sha256 before and after plus a token grep, because a worker on this exact surface had a heredoc silently mangle a mutation so that none applied while the suite reported green.

TREE-WIDE ACCOUNTING, to #7804's and #7818's standard: clj-kondo at the pin over lint.yml's exact path list, cold cache both sides; report errors and warnings before and after and diff the sorted finding sets. Both prior PRs held at errors 0 / warnings 4542 with an empty diff.

USE THE PINNED ALIAS: `clojure -M:clj-kondo` gives 2026.04.15; the npm binary on this host is 2025.10.23, and a pass from a mismatched version proves nothing either way.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7829 (2026-08-11) — REOPEN THIS EXACT ROSTER OWNER; no duplicate. WHAT HOLDS: all four authored/landed patch ids match; the first-arity witness is discriminating; the added binding-parameter rows and shared read-shadow repair pass the live export gate at the CI pin. GAP 1, FALSE ERROR: cljs.core/areduce is still absent. Its grammar is (areduce a idx ret init expr), and macroexpand binds idx plus ret in a loop. With ret initialized to (fn [x] x), a legal (ret idx) in expr is reported as re-frame.hicasso/direct-view-call at ERROR when ret shares the enclosing view name. The pinned stdin probe reproduced exit 3. Add the bounded core-form arm and a negative row whose ret is callable; no scope engine. GAP 2, FALSE SILENCE INTRODUCED HERE: fn-tail-locals feeds method lists to fn-locals, which adds the method HEAD as an optional named-fn self binding. A reify/extend method name is not lexical. The README now states the false rule that a method binds its own name. Pinned probe: (h/defview toString [_] ... (reify Object (toString [_] (toString nil)))) returns zero findings, although the correctly-arity view call is a real direct self-call. Separate letfn fnspec reading (include its local function name) from method reading (parameters of every arity only); add the same-name positive control while preserving all method-parameter negatives. Do not broaden beyond these grammar fixes.
MAYOR RULING — the amap extension is ACCEPTED, not trimmed.

The worker went one symbol beyond the audit's letter, flagged it prominently in the PR body so it could be trimmed, and asked. That is the right way to raise it, and the answer is keep it.

WHY. areduce and amap are the SAME GRAMMAR one argument apart — `(areduce a idx ret init expr)` and `(amap a idx ret expr)` both bind an index symbol and an accumulator symbol, which is precisely the shape direct-view-call's roster was mishandling. The worker did not reason by analogy and stop there: it REPRODUCED the identical false ERROR with amap at the pin, and landed a witness for it (`self-call-in-amap`). So this is not a second defect speculatively pre-empted, it is the same defect with the same cause, sitting one line away in the same roster.

Trimming it would mean knowingly shipping a build-blocking false ERROR that we have already reproduced, in order to honour the letter of a bead that was written before anyone knew the sibling existed. That is not scope discipline; it is scope discipline used against the point of the work. The bead's subject is "six more binding forms are missing from the roster" — a roster completeness bug — and a class-completeness fix is what a roster bug wants.

THE LINE, so this is not read as licence: the extension is accepted because it is the SAME GRAMMAR, INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED, and WITNESSED. A symbol that merely felt related, or one added without a failing case of its own, would have been trimmed.

value: PR #7839 audited at merge cf85bc9cd86a94a2f70e20bde7538272f237f2f3 (2026-08-10T20:49:47Z). The native grammar, macro/runtime slot parity, optional-module isolation and complaint promotion are sound; authored and landed commits are patch-identical, focused invariant/catalogue checks pass, and all required CI checks passed. Updated rf2-hic-046 because n/defcomponent records but does not enforce or validate the nominal Client-only/Render server policy; reopened rf2-hic-092 because three guide statements invert the deliberate clean-remount HMR contract.

HOW TO FIND AUDIT REOPENS ON BEADS YOU DID NOT CLOSE (2026-08-11).

The closure audit ("re-check everything closed this session") only covers ids I closed. The merged-PR audit hook also reopens beads I never touched, and those are invisible to it AND to a `bd list --status open` recount taken before the hook lands. rf2-hic-007 was reopened by MERGED-PR AUDIT #7842 and I found it only by accident - `bd close rf2-hic-024` refused with "blocked by open issues [rf2-hic-007]".

THE DELIBERATE SCAN, over the export:

  jq -r 'select(.status=="open") | select(((.notes//"")|tostring)|test("MERGED-PR AUDIT #(7839|7842|7843)")) | "\(.id) [P\(.priority)] \(.title[0:70])"' .beads/issues.jsonl

TWO GOTCHAS THAT MADE EARLIER ATTEMPTS SILENTLY RETURN NOTHING:
1. `.notes` is a STRING, not an array. `(.notes//[])|map(...)` throws "Cannot iterate over string" on every bead that has notes - i.e. exactly the ones you want.
2. A plain grep with `[^}]{0,4000}` between the id and the audit string CANNOT WORK: note bodies contain braces, so the character class stops early. It returned a clean empty for five PR numbers while hic-007 demonstrably carried the note.

ALWAYS RUN A POSITIVE CONTROL. Ask the scan a question you already know the answer to:

  jq -r 'select(.id=="rf2-hic-007") | ((.notes//"")|tostring|test("MERGED-PR AUDIT #7842"))' .beads/issues.jsonl   # must print true

An empty result from an unvalidated filter is indistinguishable from a broken filter, and this is the same fail-open class the merge criterion exists to close. The control is what turns "found nothing" into evidence.

ALSO: bd REFUSES to close a bead blocked by an open dependency. That guard is load-bearing - it caught this - but when the blocker was reopened for an UNRELATED later defect, the right move is `bd close --force` with a reason naming why the edge does not bear on this deliverable.

title: hic: release! is a test-fixture door on the public facade and tears down the whole page
description:
DESIGN FINDING from the rf2-hic-008 worker (PR #7814), reported rather than decided. Verify against the source before acting — this is a claim about behaviour.

THE CLAIM. h/release! sits on the PUBLIC facade but is unmount! plus collector/reset-runtime!. unmount! REMOVES THE CONTAINER FROM THE DOCUMENT, and reset-runtime! drops every cell, edge and frame bundle PAGE-WIDE. So a consumer with two roots who releases one has torn down the other runtime AND lost its mount point.

WHY THAT IS THE WRONG PUBLIC MEANING. It is exactly right for a TEST FIXTURE, where one app owns the page and teardown should be total. It is wrong for a public teardown door, where "release this root" should mean this root. A consumer cannot reasonably guess that releasing one of two roots destroys both, and nothing in the name says so.

  jq -r 'select((.status//"")=="open") | select(((.notes//"")|tostring)|test("MERGED-PR AUDIT")) | "\(.updated_at)  \(.id)  [P\(.priority)]  \(.title[0:56])"' .beads/issues.jsonl | sort -r | head -12

value:
"A SIGNAL THAT CANNOT CHANGE WHEN THE DEFECT APPEARS IS NOT A SIGNAL" (2026-08-11, rf2-qdqf / PR #7857).

I pushed hard for a particular fix to a fail-open gate: make it ANNOUNCE what it skipped, on the reasoning that converting an invisible hole into a visible one is the cheap half of the fix. I briefed it as the option I wanted argued seriously rather than dismissed. The worker argued it seriously and DEFEATED IT ON MEASUREMENT, and was right.

Two numbers killed it. First, 538 of 721 corpus files carry a fence, so the announcement fires on three quarters of the corpus - a permanent nag, and 88 of the noisiest lines would report an idiom already ruled good. Second and decisive: THE ANNOUNCEMENT'S TEXT IS IDENTICAL BEFORE AND AFTER A DOC LINK APPEARS INSIDE A FENCE. It says "I skipped N blocks" either way. So it cannot distinguish the healthy state from the defective one, which makes it not a warning but wallpaper.

THE GENERAL TEST, and it applies to any "surface the gap" proposal: ask what the output looks like WITH the defect present and WITHOUT it. If those two outputs are the same string, the signal carries no information no matter how visible it is. Visibility is not the property that matters - DISCRIMINATION is. This is the same rule the repo applies to test rows ("what single narrowing would let this row pass while the law is broken?"), turned on a diagnostic instead of a test.

ALSO WORTH KEEPING - the tuple I misread. FENCED_DOC_LINK_TREES is NOT a "validate links inside fences here" roster. It is a "a markdown doc link inside a fence is ITSELF A FINDING here" roster, because a fenced block is verbatim and a link inside one renders literally. So widening it does not mean "resolve links in a prompt full of placeholders" (my worry, which made me favour the announce option) - it means BAN them there, which is correct for a text fence whose idiom is already backticked bare paths. I had the semantics backwards, and that error is what made the wrong option look necessary.

METHOD NOTE: the worker established this from the block comment and from `git log -S` on the constant - ONE commit had ever touched it - rather than from the code's behaviour alone. Intent lives in history; when a constant looks arbitrary, read the commit that introduced it before proposing to widen it.

title: gate: check_doc_slugs skips fenced doc links outside one tree, so bootstrap.md's links are green-but-unchecked
description:
check_doc_slugs.py checks markdown doc links inside fenced blocks ONLY for trees listed in FENCED_DOC_LINK_TREES, which is `("docs/design/hicasso",)` — scripts/check_doc_slugs.py:1648. Everywhere else, a doc link inside a fence is skipped.

WHY THAT IS A FAIL-OPEN AND NOT MERELY A LIMITATION: docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md is ALMOST ENTIRELY ONE FENCED `text` BLOCK, because the file IS a pasteable prompt — the fence is the deliverable, not decoration. So the gate reports green on that file, the file is genuinely in the corpus, and its out-of-fence prose IS checked — and none of that says anything about the block that contains essentially the whole document. A future edit adding a doc link inside that block gets a green that verified nothing, and the green is more misleading than a skip would be, because the file is demonstrably covered.

THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE THE REPO HUNTS IN ITS OWN INSTRUMENTS: a gate that verifies the absence of bad news rather than the presence of good news. It is also the same shape as the two witnesses PR #7846 repaired — rows that ran in three engines and could not fail.

PROVENANCE, and it is a measurement rather than a reading: the rf2-fbi4 worker (PR #7849) planted TWO bogus anchors while proving gate coverage — one outside the fence, one inside it. The gate reported exactly the first, `BROKEN ANCHOR: docs\the-mayor-method\bootstrap.md:1 -> README.md#rf2-fbi4-bogus-anchor`, exit 1, and was silent on the second. Nothing was riding on it in that PR (the added text carries no markdown links), which is why it is filed rather than fixed in flight.

THE DECISION TO MAKE — this is deliberately not pre-judged, because the cheap answer may be the wrong one:
- Simply adding "docs/the-mayor-method" to the tuple would close this instance. But the tuple existing at all implies fenced links are skipped BY DESIGN somewhere, presumably because a fence can legitimately hold illustrative or non-resolving links (sample code, a template with placeholders). Establish what that design reason actually was before widening the list — the answer determines whether the right fix is a wider tuple, an inverted default, or a per-file opt-in.
- Consider whether the gate should SAY it skipped a block, rather than being silent. A gate that announces "this file has N fenced blocks I did not check" turns an invisible hole into a visible one, which is the cheaper half of the fix and may be the whole of it.

DO NOT invert the default across the whole corpus as a first move without checking what breaks — sample blocks under docs/core/ are digest-pinned, and a sweep that reds every illustrative link would be worse than the hole.

RELATED, from the same worker and NOT a defect: scripts/check_readme_links.py DOES cover .claude/commands/*.md path references via _check_command_file_refs, and the bare mayor-dispatch.md reference added in #7849 resolves against the tracked-basename set. That half is sound.
notes: MAYOR: PR #7857 open, and MY FRAMING IN THIS BEAD WAS WRONG in a way worth recording before it closes. I described FENCED_DOC_LINK_TREES as a roster of trees where fenced links get validated, and worried that widening it to a prompt full of placeholder paths might therefore be wrong — that worry is what made me push the announce-the-skip option. The worker established from the block comment at scripts/check_doc_slugs.py:1626-1648 and from 68a9173592, the only commit that has ever touched the constant, that it is the OPPOSITE: a roster of trees where a markdown doc link inside a fence IS ITSELF A FINDING, because a fenced block is verbatim and a link inside one renders literally. Widening therefore means BAN, not RESOLVE — which is exactly right for a text fence whose idiom is already backticked bare paths, and my objection evaporates. The announce option I argued for was then defeated on measurement rather than dismissed: 538 of 721 corpus files carry a fence, so it fires on three quarters of the corpus, and its text is IDENTICAL before and after a doc link appears inside a fence — a signal that cannot change when the defect appears is not a signal. The chosen fix widens the roster to docs/the-mayor-method, which measures 0 fenced doc links and lands green; docs/design/freehand/ stays out for want of an incident, which is the roster's own evidence-scoped discipline. bootstrap.md is 334 of 335 non-blank lines fenced (99.7%), and only two other corpus files exceed 80%, so the measured class is essentially this one file.
close_reason: Landed via PR #7857 (merged 892fa5c323, rebased onto main). Green on all five clauses at 91/91. MY FRAMING IN THIS BEAD WAS BACKWARDS, and the correction is the most useful thing in it. FENCED_DOC_LINK_TREES is NOT a roster of trees where fenced links get validated; it is a roster of trees where A MARKDOWN DOC LINK INSIDE A FENCE IS ITSELF A FINDING, because a fenced block is verbatim and a link inside one renders literally. Established from the block comment at scripts/check_doc_slugs.py:1626-1648 and from 68a9173592, the ONLY commit that has ever touched the constant — intent read out of history rather than inferred from behaviour. So widening means BAN, not RESOLVE, and my worry that a prompt full of placeholder paths would break under widening evaporates: banning links is exactly right for a text fence whose idiom is already backticked bare paths. That misreading is what made me push the wrong option. THE ROSTER IS EVIDENCE-SCOPED BY DESIGN: rf2-mmyc scoped it on a measurement (109 in-repo links live inside fences elsewhere, 88 of them legitimate ;; commentary in spec/Spec-Schemas.md samples) and deliberately left docs/design/freehand/ out because 'it had no incident, and widening a new gate past its evidence is how gates acquire a reputation for arbitrary friction'. This bead supplied the evidence for docs/the-mayor-method. THE OPTION I ARGUED FOR WAS DEFEATED ON MEASUREMENT, not dismissed — I had asked for it to be taken seriously and it was. Announce-the-skip fires on 538 of 721 corpus files, and decisively its text is IDENTICAL before and after a doc link appears inside a fence: a signal that cannot change when the defect appears is not a signal. Inverting with an opt-out needs the allowlist rf2-mmyc declined, whose first entry would be the file holding 81% of the corpus's fenced links. CHOSEN: widen to docs/the-mayor-method, which measures 0 fenced doc links and lands green; freehand still out for want of an incident. The cheap half of the announce option was taken as DOCUMENTATION — the module docstring now says the skip is silent and the roster evidence-scoped. PROVEN the way the defect was found: reproduced on unmodified main (outer link reported, inner silent), then after the change the inner-only plant reds with 'LINK INSIDE A FENCE: docs\the-mayor-method\bootstrap.md:6', exit 1, restored byte-identically. title: hic: the census calls registry.cljs's ten mentions all comments, but L273 is a runtime console.warn naming the donor
description:
The tool-consumer census (docs/design/hicasso/product/tool-consumer-census.md) files tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/registry.cljs under "Named, not consumed", describing it as "ten mentions, all comments". One of those ten is not a comment.

registry.cljs L273 is a runtime `js/console.warn` string that names both `re-frame.ui` and `re-frame.freehand.tool` to a developer at the point the warning fires. By the census's OWN definition of load-bearing, and by its own STILL-LIVE treatment of Pair's row P2 (which is load-bearing precisely because the donor name appears in MCP `:description` prose), that mention is load-bearing and the row's disposition is wrong.

WHY THIS IS THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION OF ERROR. This is the under-count trap, and under-counting is what makes a DELETION look safe. The mention is invisible to a require scan and to clj-kondo, so every static tool agrees the file is clean — and it survives any deletion of the rows above it, which is exactly when someone would be relying on the census to tell them what is left. A row that over-counts costs a wasted look; this one costs a developer-facing string that names a namespace nobody has shipped since.

PROVENANCE: found by the rf2-jkdy worker (PR #7845) while re-verifying the X1/X2/X4/X5 premises from source rather than from the census. It correctly did NOT apply the fix: registry.cljs is outside its cluster's fence, and the census document was held by another worker at the time.

REPAIR, bounded: re-classify the registry.cljs row against what L273 actually is, and say in the row why a console string counts. Do not re-derive the census, do not touch the other 26 rows, and do not delete anything on the strength of it.

SEQUENCING: the census document was being edited concurrently by the rf2-hic-076 repair (proof-paragraph arithmetic). Land that first, then this on top of it.
close_reason: Landed via PR #7852 (merged 6f34f70b36, rebased onto main). Green on all five clauses at 91/91, five runs completed/success, clean reap, canary held. VERIFIED AT SOURCE BEFORE EDITING: L273 is one line of a js/console.warn argument in warn-donor-ownership-resident! (L260), the .warn call spanning L268-277. The ten grep hits in registry.cljs split EIGHT TO TWO, not ten to zero — L165/166/183/184/239/245/356/357 are docstrings and ;; comments, but L270 AND L273 are inside that one runtime string. Load-bearing by the census's own definition and by row P2's precedent. The file left 'Named, not consumed' and became row X13, STILL-LIVE, with the row stating why a console string counts. A SHARPER FINDING THE BEAD DID NOT ANTICIPATE: one of the FOUR mentions the census cites as proof that Xray may not acquire a re-frame.ui dependency IS that warning string — the census was partly quoting a runtime string it had itself filed as a comment. Arithmetic followed through completely (23→24 load-bearing, 25→24 not-consumed, 27→28 rows, 18→19 STILL-LIVE, Xray 12→13), plus the X2-liveness note, the disposition prose and table, and both affected proof paragraphs; cross-checks reconcile three ways, X13 appended so no id shifts, and no other tracked document quotes the old counts.

title: hic-057 — Spike: schema-driven generative testing
description:

Timebox respected (≤2 h); verdict recorded with evidence; graduation (if any) filed as its own bead.

close_reason: Landed via PR #7853 (merged 0d6734cca8, rebased onto main). Green on all five clauses at 91/91. VERDICT: DO-NOT-GRADUATE — and the honest negative is the deliverable, exactly as this bead's pre-registered rule intends. Section 11's rule is CONJUNCTIVE (find a real defect or refusal gap AND shrink usefully). Shrinking was met decisively; the defect condition was not. THE TWO GENERATORS were both derived, not hand-written: state from mg/generator over the schema the app registered, read back with rfs/app-schema-at; intent sequences from each event's own registered :schema, read back with rf/handler-meta, then gen/vector over gen/one-of. THE MEASUREMENT TRICK WORTH KEEPING: a deliberately broken toggle as a p-sabotage property, so shrinking could be MEASURED without waiting on a real defect to appear. p-preserves-schema went red three times including once on its own previous fix, and the shrunk counterexample was one todo and one intent — 91 nodes visited, depth 13, 20ms, cause legible in the value. WHY IT IS STILL A NEGATIVE, stated without hedging: all three finds are in the pilot's OWN fixture app written minutes earlier, and two are artifacts of bounds the worker introduced to keep generation cheap. p-render — the property aimed at the substrate — never failed across 800 trials, and nothing in re-frame.hicasso, the L2 kit or any shipped surface was implicated. THREE FINDINGS THAT TRANSFER: (1) schema-derived states are far wider than app-reachable ones — 12 to 27 states per 100 carry duplicate todo ids, so closing that gap means a permanent schema-enrichment tax or abandoning the draw-states arm; (2) Spec 010's :cat spelling validates event vectors but GENERATES SEQS, a silent trap; (3) ht/intents reports authored, not materialized, intents. RECOMMENDATION ACCEPTED: do not commission the full study. If ever reopened, fund something narrower — drop the draw-valid-states arm, keep the intent-sequence arm with the app-db schema as a post-fold oracle only, and wait for Phase 2's vertical slice, which does not exist in-tree yet. title: core: the release bundle embeds the build machine's absolute filesystem path
description:
INCIDENTAL FINDING from the rf2-hic-024 erasure worker (PR #7838), reported rather than actioned because it is outside that bead and belongs to core.

THE OBSERVATION, measured while scanning the release bundle: out/hicasso-release/main.js carries THE ABSOLUTE FILESYSTEM PATH OF THE BUILD MACHINE, three times. It arrives via core's production registration coordinates — prod-coords-form keeps :file and :line and drops only :column — so every reg-sub and reg-event in a release build embeds its source path.

WHY IT MAY MATTER, stated without overclaiming: a release artefact that is not path-independent differs between build machines even when the inputs are identical. That defeats byte-comparable builds, leaks a developer's directory layout into shipped bytes, and makes any future "same inputs, same output" check impossible to satisfy. None of that is broken today — nothing depends on reproducibility yet — which is exactly why this is filed rather than fixed.

THE QUESTION TO ANSWER FIRST, before any change: is the absolute path DELIBERATE? The coordinate machinery is core's design and it drops :column on purpose, which suggests the retained fields were chosen rather than left over. Read core's prod-coords-form and whatever spec governs it. If the path is wanted — for stack-trace mapping, say — then the answer is to record why, not to strip it.

IF IT IS NOT WANTED: the smallest fix is a repo-relative path, which preserves whatever diagnostic value the coordinate has while removing the machine dependence. Do NOT strip the coordinate entirely without establishing that nothing reads it; hic-007's source-coordinate work is recent and deliberate, and its production-elision gates are the thing that would notice.

FENCE: this is a CORE surface, not hicasso. Do not touch implementation/hicasso/**. spec/* is hot zone. If the change reaches a shipped facade or a coordinate contract, STOP and report rather than taking it.

CONTEXT: found because the erasure worker needed to know whether a filename sentinel could be used to prove defview/defhost coordinates are elided. It cannot — consumer_app.cljs appears three times in a GREEN bundle from these very coordinates, so a filename sentinel there would be red on a correct build. That measurement is recorded in check_production_erasure.cjs's docstring.
close_reason: Landed via PR #7852 (merged 6f34f70b36) — but NOT as the fix this bead assumed, and that is the point of the close. THE BEHAVIOUR IS DELIBERATE AND ALREADY RULED. spec/Privacy.md's section 'What the production bundle itself discloses' names this exact disclosure, names rf2-wvsxg as the reason for it, says in terms that 'there is no knob ... the retention is the contract', and prescribes the remedy (build in a neutral working directory). So there was no defect to fix. SOURCE TRACED anyway, so the close rests on evidence rather than on the doc: absolutise-file (source_coords.cljc L621) resolves the compiler's classpath-relative :file at macro-expansion time, prod-coords-form (L736) calls it, and the rf2-3un2g gate DCEs the dev branch while keeping the prod one, so the absolutised literal survives :advanced with goog.DEBUG=false. WHY NO CODE CHANGE: relativising prod-coords-form would change a coordinate contract — compose-path joins :project-root for relative paths, which would regress production-mode inspection to the exact failure rf2-wvsxg fixed — and the ruling lives in hot-zone spec/. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG were two comments DENYING the contract: source_coords.cljc claimed 'production builds elide both the literal and the surrounding coord-form' (false, and the sentence that makes this look like a defect), and open_endpoint.cljs scoped the baked path to 'the dev bundle'. Both now state what production keeps and point at Privacy.md. Comment-only; no hot-zone file edited, so #7844's erasure-scan chaining in package.json is intact.

My jq scan reads .beads/issues.jsonl. That file is an EXPORT, refreshed only when a checkpoint runs - so it lags the Dolt database by however long since the last `sh scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh`. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LOOP: the CLOSURE AUDIT is the reliable detector, because it loops `bd show <id>` per id and reads the status FIELD from the database. The jq scan over the export is a convenience for spotting reopens on beads I never touched, and it is only as fresh as the last checkpoint. So: run the closure audit first and trust it; if the jq scan is used, CHECKPOINT IMMEDIATELY BEFORE IT so the export is current, and treat a disagreement between the two as the export being stale rather than the database being wrong.

THE GENERAL SHAPE, third time this session: an instrument that answers from a cached artefact rather than from the source will be confidently wrong exactly when the source has just changed - which is exactly when you are asking. The other two instances were `git branch -r` (a cache, not remote state) and `gh run list --json status` returning lowercase while `gh pr checks --json state` returns uppercase.

ON WINDOWS, `git diff` CANNOT VERIFY A BYTE-IDENTICAL RESTORE - VERIFY BY HASH (2026-08-11, found by the rf2-dly1 worker, PR #7859).

Every dispatch brief I write demands the same coverage drill for silent-on-success gates: plant a bogus anchor, quote the exit 1, RESTORE BYTE-IDENTICALLY, confirm green. A worker doing exactly that used `sed -i` to plant and restore, and `git diff` came back EMPTY while the sha256 DIFFERED. `sed -i` had rewritten the working copy CRLF -> LF. The content was identical; the bytes were not.

WHY git diff LIES HERE: with autocrlf normalisation, git compares the normalised form, so a pure line-ending change is invisible to `git diff` and to `git status`. Both report clean. The file on disk has changed for every tool that reads bytes rather than lines - and on this repo that includes the digest-pinned sample blocks under docs/core/, which hash exact block text.

THE FIX, two parts:
1. VERIFY BY HASH, not by `git diff`: record sha256 before planting and compare after restoring. The worker caught it precisely because it hashed.
2. RESTORE WITH `git checkout -- <path>`, which writes the exact checked-out bytes, rather than a second `sed -i` that re-applies the same normalisation.

PUT THIS IN THE DISPATCH BRIEF. I ask for this drill in nearly every dispatch, and until now the brief said "restore byte-identically" and let the worker choose how to check - which on Windows means most of them check with `git diff` and get a false pass. The claim "restored byte-identically, git status clean" is NOT evidence on this platform.

GENERAL SHAPE, and it is the same one that keeps recurring: an instrument answering from a NORMALISED view rather than the raw artefact is confidently wrong exactly about the difference you are checking for. Same family as `git branch -r` being a cache, `gh run list` returning lowercase status, and the beads export lagging the database.

description:

THE SHIPPED CONTRACT, from `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc` (~281-287 and ~452-455): minting a component is ALLOCATION, NEVER A LOOKUP BY NAME. description:
`:rf.error/hicasso-test-native-is-opaque` is still listed as RESERVED in docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md with the note "once the native tier lands". Every refusal carries the stable shape (id, source coordinate, view, frame where relevant, path/position, offending value, expected shape, recovery), and the defining macros capture file/line/column.

title: pair: the instructions tool is within tens of tokens of its 5000-token cap, and the next tool added will breach it
description:
`get-re-frame2-pair-instructions` is within a few tens of tokens of its 5000-token cap. The rf2-n3mb worker's first draft overflowed it at 5088 and reddened three tests before being trimmed.

CURRENT STATE, and why this is a warning rather than a bug: the prose that shipped in PR #7848 is SHORTER than what it replaced, so there is more headroom now than before. Nothing is broken. But the margin is small enough that the NEXT tool added to that list will hit the cap, and it will hit it as three red tests in someone else's PR, whose diff will have nothing to do with the cause.

WHAT TO DECIDE, not what to do — this is a design question and the answer is not obviously "raise the cap":
- Is a single instructions blob the right shape once the tool list keeps growing, or should it be paginated / split by surface?
- Should the cap be enforced at authoring time with a message that names the budget and the current usage, so the failure surfaces where the prose is written rather than in an unrelated PR's test run?
- Is 5000 tokens the right budget at all, given what a consuming agent actually needs on first contact?

DO NOT simply raise the constant to buy room. That converts a hard limit into a soft one and defers the same failure to a later, larger blob. Whatever is chosen should keep the failure loud and keep it close to the author.

PROVENANCE: flagged by the rf2-n3mb worker (PR #7848) as a possible follow-up after it hit the ceiling and backed off. It did not act on it, correctly — the cap is not that bead's surface.
close_reason:
Landed via PR #7863 (merged d2dc4ceb55, rebased onto main). Green on all five merge clauses at 91/91, five runs completed/success. Clean reap on the worker's report; canary held.

THE MEASUREMENT: 4888 tokens against a 5000 cap — 112 tokens of margin, about 226 characters, two or three catalogue lines. Taken through the PRODUCTION gate (cap/sum-payload-tokens over the real handler result), and independently reproduced by an emulation that predicted a planted overflow to the exact token.

THE NON-OBVIOUS FINDING, and it explains the earlier 5088 overflow: wire/ok-text writes the payload into BOTH :content[0].text (pr-str EDN, 9776 chars) AND :structuredContent (JSON, 9777 chars), and the cap counts both — correctly, since both ride the wire. THE PROSE IS MEASURED TWICE. One character of prose costs about 0.5 tokens, so the effective prose budget is roughly 2500 tokens, not 5000. Sizing a draft from the raw character count is wrong by a factor of two, which is exactly how the earlier draft landed at 5088.

AND THE REAL COST OF A BREACH IS WORSE THAN THREE RED TESTS: at egress the WHOLE payload is replaced by the overflow marker, so an agent's first-contact call returns no onboarding text at all — and the marker's hint, "re-call with narrower args", cannot help a tool that takes no args.

THE THREE QUESTIONS, answered: SHAPE — one blob, do not paginate or split, because splitting adds round-trips to first contact and does not stop the growth; the growth is one section (## Tool catalogue is 7188 of 9548 chars, 75.3%), every other section being a convention that is constant in the tool count. AUTHORING-TIME ENFORCEMENT — yes, landed. IS 5000 RIGHT — right for the wire and must not move, since it is mcp-base's cross-MCP constant shared with story-mcp and envelope/marker-text? uses it as the sub-cap test; but it is the wrong number to reason about here, because it buys ~2500 tokens of prose. The budget does not need to change; the content does.

LANDED: instructions_budget_test.cljs runs the production cap/apply-cap over the real result against cap/default-max-tokens — no duplicated arithmetic, no hard-coded 5000 — plus a (pos? tokens) self-check so it cannot go vacuously green. Proven to bite: ~300 chars of realistic catalogue prose planted, exit 1 with four failures at 5112 tokens, restored and verified by sha256. The failure message names the budget, the usage, the margin, the exchange rate, WHERE to shorten, and explicitly that raising default-max-tokens is NOT the fix.

ONE HONEST LIMITATION, itself evidence for the recommendation below: the authoring budget could not be set BELOW the cap with a reserve. At 97.8% consumed, any reserve is red on arrival, and trimming prose to make room is the deferral this bead forbids. The guard therefore sits AT the cap; a reserve becomes available once the structural question is settled.

THE STRUCTURAL RECOMMENDATION WAS NOT TAKEN, correctly — it is the operator's call and is filed as its own owner (see the follow-up bead). In short: retire the 33-line per-tool enumeration, which duplicates tools/list (already shipping 33 :description paragraphs totalling ~19,781 tokens before any tool is called), and replace it with half a dozen routing rules of the form "to read one sub, read-sub, not eval-cljs" — the one thing a descriptor structurally cannot say.

value:
`git worktree add` CAN BE KILLED BY THE HARNESS FOREGROUND TIMEOUT MID-CHECKOUT, LEAVING A STALE LOCK (2026-08-11; hit by two workers in one tick).

This repo's checkout is ~5308 files, and a fresh `git worktree add` can exceed the harness's 2-minute foreground limit. When it is killed partway (~25% in one observed case) it leaves BOTH a stale `.git/worktrees/<name>/index.lock` AND a `locked` marker reading `initializing`. The worktree exists, is registered, and is unusable; the guard script fails.

RECOVERY, in this order:
1. remove `.git/worktrees/<name>/index.lock`
2. `git reset --hard HEAD` from inside the worktree, BACKGROUNDED - it re-runs the full checkout and took ~9 minutes on this box
3. `git worktree unlock <path>`
Then the worker guard passes normally.

PUT THE MITIGATION IN THE DISPATCH BRIEF: every brief I write opens with `git worktree add`, so this is a first-command failure that costs a worker ten minutes before it has done anything. Tell workers to run the create BACKGROUNDED by absolute path and poll, exactly as they are already told to do for the 25-minute test spine - the same 10-minute ceiling applies to it and nobody expects it to.

Two workers hit this in a single tick (thirdsite-fbi4 and presence-5gka), so it is not rare. Both recovered without data loss, and both reported it rather than silently retrying - which is what made it diagnosable.

title: mayor-method: routing a finding to a live worker needs a note on the owning bead
description:
A PRACTICE THE METHOD DOES NOT DESCRIBE, developed under load tonight and then CORRECTED BY AN AUDIT — which is why it is worth writing down rather than leaving as folklore.

THE SITUATION IT ANSWERS. Running six concurrent workers, findings constantly land on files a live worker already holds — from a merged-PR audit, from another worker's report, or from the mayor's own reading. Filing a bead for such a finding creates a second worker contending for the same file; waiting until the holder finishes loses the context in which the finding was found.

WHAT I DO: route the finding to the worker that already holds the file, by message, so it lands inside the existing PR. It works — six routed findings landed tonight, none conflicted, and several were fixed within minutes of being found.

THE DEFECT THE AUDIT CAUGHT (AUDIT #7825 on rf2-hic-021): "identified this exact stale deferral but ROUTED IT ONLY TO A TRANSIENT WORKER, LEAVING NO DURABLE BEAD OWNER." A SendMessage lives in an agent's transcript. If that agent dies, times out, or reasonably declines the extra item, the finding evaporates — nothing in the tracker re-surfaces it, and the audit that found it has already run. I had recorded one routing in a CLOSE REASON on a different bead, which is a record on the wrong object: nobody reads a closed bead looking for open work.

THE CORRECTED PRACTICE, which is what belongs in the method:
  1. Route the finding to the worker holding the file. (Keeps the efficiency; avoids two workers contending.)
  2. ALSO put one note on the OWNING bead saying WHAT was routed, TO WHICH worker, and WHAT HAPPENS IF IT DOES NOT LAND. The tracker then carries the obligation either way.
  3. On that worker's PR merging, VERIFY the routed item actually landed — do not assume. A routed item is exactly the kind a worker may reasonably decline, and declining is often correct.
  4. Then close the owning bead. Do NOT file a duplicate; the audit's own instruction was "if the routed worker lands the correction first, verify it and close this owner; do not create another issue."

WHERE IT BELONGS: .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md is the natural home (it owns what happens when work is assigned), with at most a pointer from mayor-merge.md's verify-the-bead step. docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md's dispatch-discipline paragraph may want one clause.

WHAT NOT TO DO: do not turn this into a mechanism. There is no routing registry, no tracking field, no script. It is one message plus one note, and the note is the whole safeguard.

FENCE: this is a documentation addition of a few sentences. Do not restructure the dispatch loop, and do not add a seventh anything.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7849 — completeness/correctness/implementation quality: the route-and-verify rule, bounded-fence branch, three-surface placement, and focused documentation implementation are sound; landed-diff, doc-slug, command-link, MkDocs, and CI evidence are green. One material ownership gap remains. Both bootstrap.md and mayor-dispatch.md say “filing a bead puts a second worker on that file” and then prescribe a note on “the owning bead.” Filing and dispatch are separate acts, and a genuinely new routed finding may have no exact owner yet. In that case, putting a note on the holder’s unrelated active bead repeats the wrong-object failure this rule is meant to prevent. Bounded repair: state that routing begins by resolving an exact Bead owner—update/reopen an existing exact owner, otherwise file one—then route that owned item to the current holder only if its fence can absorb it; filing must not imply dispatching a second worker. If the fence cannot absorb it, leave the exact owner queued/sequenced and note the overlap. Preserve the one-message/one-note posture; no registry, field, script, or mechanism is needed.

A COVERAGE PLANT MUST NOT OVERLAP A GATE RUN (2026-08-11, rf2-eo9n / PR #7870).

Nearly every brief I write demands the same drill for silent-on-success gates: plant a bogus anchor, quote the exit 1, restore, confirm green. A worker's first fast-PR spine run went RED purely because the plant was still in the tree while the spine ran. Not a finding - the plant racing the gate.

WHY IT IS EASY TO HIT: the spine takes ~25 minutes and is therefore BACKGROUNDED (the harness kills a foreground command at 10). The plant-and-restore cycle takes seconds. So a worker naturally starts the long gate, then does the quick coverage proof while waiting - and the two overlap invisibly. The resulting red looks like a real failure in CI history.

THE RULE FOR BRIEFS: sequence them explicitly. Do the plant/restore drill FIRST, verify the restore by hash, and only THEN start the spine. Or wait for the spine's .exit file before planting. Never interleave.

AND IF IT HAPPENS: restore, hash-verify, RE-RUN, and say in the PR body that the first red was a plant race - otherwise a reviewer reading CI history is misled by a red that means nothing. The rf2-eo9n worker did exactly that, which is why it was diagnosable.

RELATED, same worker, worth keeping: plant with PYTHON rather than `sed -i`. On Windows sed -i rewrites CRLF->LF, so `git diff` and `git status` both read clean while the bytes differ - see crlf-defeats-byte-identical-restore. Restore with `git checkout --` and verify by sha256.

title: core: adapter use-frame memoises on the frame keyword, so a same-id reincarnation keeps serving the destroyed frame's bundle
description:
`re-frame.adapter.use-frame/use-frame` in CORE — used by the UIx adapter, which is first-class and actively supported — memoises its ops bundle on the resolved frame KEYWORD, compared by `=`.

THE DEFECT: a frame keyword is `=` across a same-id reincarnation. So after a frame is destroyed and recreated under the same id, that hook keeps handing out THE DESTROYED INCARNATION'S `capture-frame` bundle for the remainder of the mount. Nothing signals it; the keyword still compares equal, the memo still hits, and the consumer holds a bundle addressed to a frame that no longer exists.

THIS IS THE WARM HALF OF THE rf2-hic-013 FAILURE, IN CORE RATHER THAN IN HICASSO. The same class was already diagnosed and fixed on the Hicasso side; this is the same mistake living in the shared adapter surface, where it reaches every UIx consumer.

PROVENANCE: found by the rf2-hic-031 worker (PR #7855) while building `n/use-frame`. It did NOT touch it — outside its fence, and core's contract is core's to rule on. Correct conduct: it reported rather than followed.

WHY HICASSO'S OWN HOOK IS NOT AFFECTED, which is also the shape of the likely fix: `n/use-frame` keys on `impl.frames`' INCARNATION ROW rather than on the keyword, so a reincarnation is a different key and the memo correctly misses. A frame keyword is an ADDRESS, not an identity — the same distinction `native.cljc` draws about component names, and the same one that makes memoising on the keyword wrong here.

VERIFY BEFORE FIXING: read the current `use-frame` and confirm the memo key is still the keyword. Then establish whether any consumer DEPENDS on the bundle surviving a reincarnation before changing it — a memo that starts missing where it used to hit will re-run work, and that is a behaviour change for UIx consumers even though it is the correct one.

A WITNESS ALREADY EXISTS TO COPY THE SHAPE FROM: `native_hooks_dom_cljs_test`'s W6 (landing in PR #7855) drives exactly the destroy-and-recreate that would catch this. Any fix here needs a witness that reds without it — a same-id reincarnation, then a read through the hook, asserting it reaches the LIVE incarnation and not the dead one.

SURFACE: `implementation/core/**` (the adapter's use-frame) plus its witness. Not hot-zone, but core is a shared surface — check what else is in flight before dispatching.
close_reason:
Landed via PR #7868 (merged, rebased onto main). Green on all five merge clauses at 91/91, five runs completed/success, no workflow commits after its base. Clean reap on the worker's report; canary held at 103/2933/2.

THE PREMISE HELD, and the worker established it rather than accepting it — which mattered, because this bead came from ANOTHER worker's reading (rf2-hic-031's) and I had not independently confirmed it. The memo condition was `(if (and (some? prev) (= (aget prev 0) frame)) …)`, and `frame` comes from `frame/require-current-frame!`, whose own docstring says it returns "the frame stamp (id)" — a keyword. An ADDRESS compared by `=`.

THE OTHER HALF IS WHAT MAKES IT A BUG RATHER THAN A SMELL, and it is the part neither I nor the filing worker had: `make-capture-frame` PINS the incarnation live at capture (rf2-9pyles), and BOTH `capture-dispatch!` and `capture-subscribe!` REFUSE a superseded target (rf2-tdjv7p). Pinned bundle behind an address-keyed memo means that after a same-id reincarnation the hook served the DEAD incarnation's bundle for the rest of the mount, with EVERY OPERATION THROUGH IT SILENTLY RECOVERING.

THE FIX: key on the frame AND `frame/frame-incarnation-token` (the `:drain-lock` identity) by `identical?`. A `nil` token is a legitimate key rather than a special case — it pairs with the unpinned, address-directed capture `capture-frame` makes when the id is not live, and the frame appearing later moves it off `nil`.

BLAST RADIUS ESTABLISHED AND NOT MATERIAL, so no decision was needed: callers are the UIx re-export (every UIx consumer), four example sites, one template site, five freehand bench sites and the suite probe. Steady state costs one registry read per render — atom deref plus map lookup, no allocation — less than the `capture-frame` a miss performs, and negligible beside the neighbouring `use-subscribe`. THE DECISIVE ARGUMENT: the memo now misses only where it previously hit WRONGLY, and no consumer can depend on the bundle surviving a reincarnation BECAUSE CORE'S OWN FENCE ALREADY REFUSES EVERY OP ON IT — "surviving" means "silently dead".

THE WITNESS DISCRIMINATES, and avoided the trap I flagged in the brief: NOTHING ASSERTS EQUALITY, because the dead and live bundles compare `=` — that is the disguise. Three of four rows red with the fix broken, verbatim: `(not (identical? ops-1 ops-2))` → `(not (not true))`, and twice `(= 7 (:n (rf/app-db-value uf-frame)))` → `(not (= 7 100))` for the post- and pre-reincarnation bundles. THE STABILITY CONTROL PASSED under sabotage, which is the right result — the memo worked; only its key was an address.

FOLLOW-UP FILED, and it is the sharpest thing here: rf2-ow4e. `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` and `spec/API.md` say the bundle is "reference-stable across re-renders for the same resolved frame" — a sentence A KEYWORD-KEYED MEMO SATISFIES PERFECTLY. The spec described the buggy behaviour as the contract. Dispatched.

A frame keyword is an ADDRESS, not an IDENTITY — the third time this session that distinction has been a defect's root.

title: docs(hicasso): the testing chapter's hm/* door table omits advance-clock!, and the naming ledger has no row for it
description:
rf2-r7zq (PR #7861) landed advance-clock! on the L3 mounted facade, and two documents did not move with it — both fenced out of that dispatch and correctly reported rather than taken.

docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/14-testing.md carries an hm/* door table that enumerates the facade's doors and now OMITS advance-clock!. A table that lists doors and is missing one is worse than no table: a reader takes its absence as evidence the door does not exist, which is exactly the wrong conclusion for a facility that was added because a downstream bead could not proceed without it.

docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md is where a new door name earns a row. advance-clock! has none. The ledger is what the naming sitting reads, so a door absent from it is a door whose name has never been reviewed.

BOUNDED: add the door to the table with the same register as its siblings, and add its ledger row. Do NOT re-derive either document, and do not rename anything — the name is settled by the shipped code.

WORTH CARRYING INTO THE TABLE, because it is the part a reader most needs and cannot infer: advance-clock! moves setTimeout, setInterval AND Date.now in lockstep, and deliberately does NOT move requestAnimationFrame, microtasks/promises, performance.now, the Date constructor, or any setTimeout captured before the window opened. Read the docstring — it states each exclusion with its reason.

Both files are under docs/design/hicasso/**, which mkdocs excludes; check_doc_slugs.py is the gate, and nothing validates the tables, so count columns by hand.
close_reason: Landed via PR #7870 (merged, rebased onto main). Green on all five clauses at 91/91, clean reap, canary held. THE LEDGER ROW'S FINDING IS THAT THIS IS A CARRY-OVER, NOT A MINT: advance-clock! is already the repo's word for the operation in three places — re-frame.freehand.presence-runtime/advance-clock!, re-frame.ui.presence-runtime/advance-clock!, and a conformance fixture describing the harness step as :advance-clock — all three verified against source rather than recalled. So the verb has nothing for the naming sitting to weigh, and :clock is the row's only fresh spelling. The one adjacent candidate, re-frame.ui.test/flush-presence!, is named and rejected with its reason: it names one engine where this door names time itself. THE TABLE ROW went between hm/settle! and hm/unmount!, the order the facade's own docstring uses. THE EXCLUSION LIST would not fit a table cell and is the more useful half of the contract, so it went into a note — and it keeps the clause that matters most: requestAnimationFrame 'stays on the platform's schedule, WHERE IT STILL FIRES', which stops 'does not move' being read as 'is frozen'. That distinction is exactly where a downstream witness would otherwise pass for the wrong reason. The worker read mounted.cljs:781 in full and reports the docstring contradicted the brief nowhere; both additions came from the source rather than from my transcription. ONE OPERATIONAL FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE BEAD: its first spine run went red purely because a coverage plant was still in the tree — the plant racing the gate, not a finding. Recorded as a durable lesson, since nearly every brief demands that drill: do the plant/restore first, hash-verify, THEN start the spine, and if it does happen say so in the PR body or a reviewer reading CI history is misled by a red that means nothing.

title: hic: the census mis-files Story's runner_events as comment-only, but L1080 is a user-facing runtime string naming Freehand
description:
The tool-consumer census lists `tools/story/src/.../runner_events.cljc` under "Named, not consumed". That is a MIS-CLASSIFICATION of the same species rf2-kqls corrected for Xray and which was never applied to Story.

L1080 is a runtime `:message` string A USER READS on a `:cannot-run` refusal, and it contains "renders Freehand views". By the census's own definition of load-bearing — and by the precedent already set when registry.cljs's console.warn was reclassified as row X13 — that is a live donor mention, not a comment.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A TALLY QUIBBLE: the word is UNTESTED. L305 asserts only `#"install-presence-flush!|presence-host"`, so the "Freehand" in that user-facing message would go stale SILENTLY when Story's substrate moves. It is the under-count direction, and under-counting is what makes a deletion look safe: a reader disposing of Story's donor rows on the census's authority would leave a user-facing string naming a namespace nobody ships.

CONSEQUENCE: Story's row count should read 11, not 10.
