title: spec: 'reference-stable for the same resolved frame' describes the rf2-40kv defect as the contract — it is per-incarnation
description:
`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` (around lines 2620 and 2651) and `spec/API.md` (around line 579) all say the ops bundle is "reference-stable across re-renders for the same resolved frame".

THAT SENTENCE IS THE ONE THE DEFECT HID BEHIND, which is why it is worth correcting rather than leaving as a wording nit. rf2-40kv was exactly this: `use-frame` memoised on the resolved frame KEYWORD compared by `=`, and a keyword is `=` across a same-id reincarnation — so after a destroy-and-recreate the hook kept serving the DEAD incarnation's pinned bundle for the rest of the mount. A keyword-keyed memo SATISFIES the spec sentence perfectly. The spec described the buggy behaviour as the contract.

WHAT MAKES IT A BUG RATHER THAN A SMELL, and what the corrected sentence must convey: `make-capture-frame` PINS the incarnation live at capture (rf2-9pyles), and both `capture-dispatch!` and `capture-subscribe!` REFUSE a superseded target (rf2-tdjv7p). So the stale bundle is not merely old — every operation through it silently recovers. "Surviving a reincarnation" means "silently dead".

THE CORRECTION, in substance: reference stability holds for the same resolved frame INCARNATION, not merely the same frame id. The shipped fix keys on the frame plus `frame/frame-incarnation-token` (the `:drain-lock` identity) by `identical?`, with a `nil` token as a legitimate key pairing with the unpinned, address-directed capture. A frame keyword is an ADDRESS, not an IDENTITY — the same distinction `native.cljc` draws about component names, and the third time this session that distinction has been the root of a defect.

SCOPE: three sentences across two files. Do NOT re-derive either document, and do not change the API — the code is already correct as of PR #7868; this is the spec catching up to it.

HOT ZONE: `spec/*` is sequential-access. Dispatch only when no other worker holds it, and land it promptly rather than holding the file across a long gate run.

PROVENANCE: flagged by the rf2-40kv worker (PR #7868), which corrected the equivalent sentence in the UIx re-export's docstring but correctly did NOT touch the hot-zone spec files.
close_reason: Landed via PR #7873 (merged, rebased onto main). Green at 91/91, clean reap, canary held. All three sites corrected — spec/006 twice and spec/API.md once — with the line numbers verified by grep rather than trusted from my brief; all three were where the bead said. The landed wording is the one to propagate: reference stability holds for the same resolved frame INCARNATION, because a frame keyword is an ADDRESS, not an identity; capture-frame pins the exact incarnation live when it ran and every op on the bundle refuses a superseded target, so a bundle surviving a same-id reincarnation WOULD NOT BE MERELY STALE, IT WOULD BE SILENTLY INERT. A FOURTH CARRIER WAS FOUND AND REPORTED RATHER THAN TAKEN: implementation/adapters/uix/README.md:14 still carries the uncorrected sentence and was NOT in PR #7868's file list, so the code fix landed while the first thing a UIx consumer reads kept describing the defect as the contract. It also spotted a weaker variant at 10-native-tier.md:169 that drops the frame qualifier entirely. title: hic: a port is not reliably a move — six ports deleted their originals, the two :ssr ports left duplicates
description:
A PORT IS NOT RELIABLY A MOVE, and the triage tree is now inconsistent about it.

FOUND BY the rf2-b6ja worker (PR #7850) while recording the sequencing decisions; flagged in the document, deliberately NOT settled, because picking a convention is a ruling rather than a repair.

THE STATE: the six front/* ports DELETED their bench originals. The two :ssr ports DID NOT — so host_ssr_dom_cljs_test and fallback_contents_cljs_test now live in BOTH trees, the bench tree and implementation/hicasso/test/. That is precisely the "a second copy doubles the maintenance" case the triage document's own reasoning names as the thing to avoid.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: a duplicated suite drifts silently. The two copies compile in different lanes against different hosts, so a fix applied to one and not the other produces a green build with a stale witness still asserting the old behaviour — and the stale one keeps passing, which is the worst shape of test rot because nothing goes red to announce it.

THE RULING NEEDED — one of:
(a) A PORT IS A MOVE: the original is deleted as part of the port, always. Simple, and it matches what six of eight ports already did. The cost is that the bench tree loses coverage the moment a port lands, and if the port later proves inadequate there is nothing to fall back to.
(b) A PORT MAY LEAVE THE ORIGINAL, but only with a recorded reason on the row and a named condition for deleting it later. Honest about the cases where the donor suite is still earning its place (a different host, a lane the package cannot reach), at the cost of a standing obligation somebody must discharge.
My recommendation is (a) with (b) as a NAMED EXCEPTION requiring the reason in the row — the default should be the one that cannot rot, and the exception should have to justify itself in writing.

WHATEVER IS RULED, the two :ssr rows are then either deleted from the bench tree or given their recorded reason. Do not resolve this by deleting the bench copies before the ruling: rf2-b6ja established that implementation/hicasso/* does NOT arm implementation_jvm, so a bench original can be carrying a host the package copy does not have, and that is exactly the case (b) exists for.

CONTEXT: the census has also drifted — 63 of 69 files remain (25,268 lines). The document's header now says once that its counts are census-time values; renumbering it was deliberately fenced out of rf2-b6ja and is not part of this bead either.
notes:
MAYOR RULING: (a) with (b) as a NAMED EXCEPTION requiring its reason in writing.

THE DEFAULT IS (a) — A PORT IS A MOVE. The original is deleted as part of the port. Six of the eight ports already did this, so the default matches the practice rather than fighting it, and it is the option that CANNOT ROT: there is only ever one copy, so there is nothing to drift out of step.

THE EXCEPTION IS (b), AND IT MUST JUSTIFY ITSELF IN THE ROW. A port may leave the original standing ONLY with a recorded reason on the triage row and a NAMED CONDITION for deleting it later. "We might still want it" is not a reason. A reason is a capability the package copy does not have — and rf2-b6ja established that exactly such a case exists: implementation/hicasso/* does NOT arm implementation_jvm, so a bench original can be carrying a JVM host the package copy simply cannot reach. That is what (b) is for, and it is why (a) alone would be wrong.

WHY THE DEFAULT GOES THIS WAY RATHER THAN THE OTHER: a duplicated suite drifts SILENTLY. The two copies compile in different lanes against different hosts, so a fix applied to one and not the other leaves a green build with a stale witness still asserting the old behaviour — and the stale one keeps PASSING. Nothing goes red to announce it, which makes it the worst shape of test rot. An exception that has to be written down is cheap; a silent duplicate is not.

APPLIED TO THE TWO OPEN CASES: host_ssr_dom_cljs_test and fallback_contents_cljs_test currently live in both trees with no recorded reason. Under this ruling each is either deleted from the bench tree, or given a written reason plus its deletion condition. DO NOT DELETE THEM BLIND — first check whether either is carrying a host the package copy cannot reach (the implementation_jvm case above is the live precedent). If it is, that is case (b) and it gets the note; if it is not, it goes.

SCOPE NOTE: renumbering the drifted census (63 of 69 files remain, 25,268 lines) is NOT part of this. rf2-b6ja deliberately fenced it out and so does this bead; the document's header already says once that its counts are census-time values.
CORRECTION: the close reason names rf2-oc9j for the dangling codec.cljs citations; that id was written before the bead was filed and is wrong. The real id is the one created immediately after this close — see the bead titled 'hic: two codec.cljs prose citations name a bench suite the c78g port deleted'.

title: hic-081 — Spike: capability receipts
description:
# hic-081 — Spike: capability receipts

**Phase**: 5 · **Wave**: F · **Est.**: S (timeboxed ≤2 h) · **Depends**: hic-023
**Surface**: spike branch + report; nothing retained without graduation

## Goal
The §11 spike: mechanical attempt facts per boundary (self time, body runs, read calls, unique reads, cache hits, codec node counts) as a diagnostic receipt — attempts distinguished from commits, raw values omitted.

## Deliverables
- The receipt projection on the slice app, attached-only allocation proven, production erasure unchanged.
- The kill rule applied: stop if instrumentation changes hot-view rankings or requires production retention.

## Acceptance
- Timebox respected; ranking-perturbation check recorded; verdict + evidence recorded.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).
notes:
SPIKE VERDICT (rf2-hic-081, timebox respected — ~2 h, no overrun). Branch worker/receipts-hic081, three commits, pushed. NO PR: nothing here graduates as code, and the spike's own surface line says so.

VERDICT: SPLIT. The COUNTS receipt GRADUATES as a design; the SELF-TIME field is KILLED. The ranking-perturbation check is REFUSED on two named controls and the kill is carried by arithmetic and by the repo's own committed measurements instead.

=== 1. THE DESIGN FINDING, WHICH IS THE SPIKE'S REAL PRODUCT ===

Five of the six named fields need NO TAP ON ANY HOT LOOP. They are derivable post hoc, at the end of an attempt, from state the runtime already retains for its own reasons:

  - READ CALLS   = the length of the scratch array. `read-key!` already pushes every call, duplicates included.
  - UNIQUE READS = that array's distinct count.
  - CACHE HITS   = for each scratch key, whether `!cells` holds a cell with a live reaction — and THAT ANSWER IS STABLE ACROSS THE ATTEMPT, because `cold-read!` retains nothing and the generation fence guarantees a pass observes one commit. Recomputing at the end is the same answer each read got, not an approximation. This is the load-bearing step and it is what removes the per-read counter.
  - CODEC NODES  = a walk of the element the attempt returned, taken AFTER the element is in hand.
  - ATTEMPTS     = counted at the tap itself.

So the receipt costs ONE tap, in `run-once`, per ATTEMPT — the same cost class as the `bodyRuns` increment already sitting there, and three orders of magnitude below a per-read or per-node tap. Attempts are ~10^3 per interaction; codec nodes are ~10^5.

ATTEMPTS vs COMMITS is satisfied by keeping them on two seams rather than by a flag on one record: the receipt counts attempts (so a fence re-run is two and a `React.memo` bail-out is none); the existing evidence sink's `:commit` event already counts commits. No new commit tap.

=== 2. WHAT WAS MEASURED ===

(a) THE RECEIPT PROJECTS, on two boundaries with deliberately opposite mechanical profiles (implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/receipt_spike_cljs_test.cljs):

  {:view "spike/deep", :attempts 1, :read-calls 4, :unique-reads 3, :cache-hits 0, :codec-nodes 2}
  {:view "spike/wide", :attempts 2, :read-calls 2, :unique-reads 1, :cache-hits 0, :codec-nodes 22}

  read-calls 4 vs unique-reads 3 is a repeated read separating the two fields. codec-nodes 22 = 2 attempts x 11 nodes (ul + 5 li + 5 strings). The two rows are the diagnostic claim demonstrated: read-heavy/node-light told apart from node-heavy/read-light, with no clock involved.

  CACHE HITS ANSWER BOTH WAYS — a second row commits the read set first and reads 4 of 4 hits, so the field is not stuck at zero.

  GATE: `node scripts/compile-node-test.cjs node-test-hicasso` then the bundle — 530 tests / 2465 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors. 524 pre-existing tests unmoved by the tap.

(b) ATTACHED-ONLY ALLOCATION — PROVEN, negatively controlled. Detached, twenty renders attach nothing and leave no table (`(nil? (receipt/rows))`); after `detach!` a further render re-attaches nothing. The guard's deref is the outermost form at the tap, so nothing a receipt would be handed is built when nobody is receipting — the same discipline, and the same falsifiability argument, as `impl/evidence`'s sink.

(c) PRODUCTION ERASURE — MEASURED, AND IT FAILED FIRST. This is the finding worth keeping.

  The first cut put the versioned envelope in `impl/receipt`, which therefore required `re-frame.hicasso.evidence`. `npm run build:hicasso-release` FAILED:

      hicasso production erasure: FAIL
        DEV SURFACE LEAKED: evidence projection — the versioned envelope (rf2-hic-023)
          sentinel: "re-frame.hicasso.evidence"

  `re-frame.hicasso.evidence` is dev-only BY REACHABILITY — nothing under `src/` requires it. A collector tap is reachable from the public door by construction, so ANYTHING THE TAP'S NAMESPACE REQUIRES BECOMES REACHABLE TOO, and the schema pin landed in the `:advanced` bundle.

  THE RULE THIS ESTABLISHES, and it governs any future runtime-tapped evidence, not just this one: raw counters live where the tap is; the ENVELOPE lives in a dev-only consumer that is not reachable from the public door (`re-frame.hicasso.tool`). After that split the same gate reads:

      OK: no dev-only Hicasso surface in the :advanced / goog.DEBUG=false bundle
          (5 sentinels absent, 3 positive controls present).

  So "production erasure unchanged" is PROVEN, by an existing gate, with the receipt in the tree — and the route by which it would have broken is now on the record.

=== 3. THE KILL: SELF TIME ===

Self time is the ONE field that cannot be derived, because time is not retained, and it is therefore the only field that puts an instrument inside the body. It fails on the bead's own kill rule — "stop if instrumentation changes hot-view rankings" — on two independent grounds:

  (i) RESOLUTION. Chrome clamps `performance.now()` to 100 us; this repo states it in a dozen places and MEASURES it per run (`hd8_rows/clock-resolution!`, rf2-d2tzk, which exists precisely because the constant was being quoted rather than read). The quantity is single-digit microseconds: the frozen clock standard's own numbers are 6.8–12.6 us of marginal cost PER CELL, against a whole tared floor page of ~4.5 ms. A per-attempt interval of ~5 us on a 100 us grain reads 0 or 100 us — Bernoulli(p≈0.05) x 100 us. The mean survives; the variance does not. Relative standard error over n attempts is sqrt((1-p)/(n·p)) ≈ sqrt(19/n), so 10% needs ~1,900 attempts PER BOUNDARY. A diagnostic receipt read after a few interactions does not have that, and a ranking built on it is ordering noise.

  (ii) THE OBSERVER EFFECT SCALES WITH THE WRONG VARIABLE. Two clock reads per attempt add a fixed cost c to every attempt, so a boundary's inflation is n_i·c — proportional to ATTEMPT COUNT, not to true cost. Two boundaries close in true self time and different in attempt count invert. That is the ranking perturbation the kill rule names, by construction rather than by bad luck.

  A COROLLARY WORTH RECORDING SEPARATELY, because it kills the per-node tap the naive design would have used: `as-element` was costed in this repo at 8.9 ns/child (`walk_vs_reagent_app` candidate table, 1,908 children; 22.5 ns/child before rf2-2rtt6.63). An atom deref plus a nil test per node is a large fraction of 8.9 ns, and it lands PROPORTIONAL TO CHILD COUNT — the exact axis a hot-view ranking discriminates on. A tapped codec counter perturbs the ranking whether or not anyone times anything. The post-hoc element walk avoids this entirely and is why the design above takes it.

=== 4. THE RANKING-PERTURBATION CHECK: REFUSED, ON TWO NAMED CONTROLS ===

  (a) QUIET BOX. The frozen clock standard (`clock_check_standard.json`, id hicasso-clock/ctl-2x-level v4) carries quiet-box as a hard refusal and was calibrated on quiet-box ensembles. MEASURED at 2026-08-11 13:04:44 +10:00 with Get-Counter, 8 x 1 s samples, one measurement at a time:
        \Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time  — min 31.52, median 41.92, max 59.70
        \System\Processor Queue Length       — min 0, median 0, max 3
        24 logical cores.
      Queue length is 0 at the median, so cores were not generally starved; but it spikes to 3 and CPU sits at 42% median with five other workers live. That is not a quiet box, and the standard's own recalibrateOn list treats harness conditions as invalidating. Publishing a timing comparison taken here would retro-admit a run the standard refuses. REFUSED rather than widened.
      (Win32_Processor.LoadPercentage was not used: it is known on this machine to read 93% against a true 11%.)

  (b) NO CONTROL ARM EXISTS. Deeper than the noise, and it would refuse on a silent box too: the receipt's own clock would be THE ONLY per-boundary timing instrument in the tree. There is no independent per-view time source to rank against, so "does the instrument change the ranking?" has no comparator. The bench lane's TaskDuration clock is per-page, not per-boundary. You cannot A/B an instrument against itself; you can only bound its perturbation from its own resolution, which is what §3 does. Building a second per-boundary instrument mid-spike was refused — a rung added between runs makes the series two instruments, and it is its own bead if anyone wants it.

=== 5. WHAT WAS NOT CONCLUDED ===

  - NO BROWSER MEASUREMENT WAS TAKEN. Every number above is from the Node lane or from the existing release gate. The tap's cost has NOT been measured on a real Chromium render path; the argument that one per-attempt deref is below the noise is inherited from the `bodyRuns` docstring's own reasoning, not re-measured here.
  - THE 100 us CLAMP WAS NOT RE-MEASURED IN THIS RUN. It is cited from this repo's stated-and-instrumented constant (`clock-resolution!`) rather than freshly taken; no committed dataset in `bench/hicasso/data/` carries a `:clock-resolution` record, so the citation is to the instrument, not to a stored reading. If the self-time question is ever reopened, take that reading first.
  - THE SLICE APP USED WAS A TWO-BOUNDARY WITNESS, not `consumer-app` and not the testbed. The receipt was not driven through a real mount/commit/notify cycle in a browser, so the ATTEMPTS-vs-COMMITS distinction is demonstrated by construction (the tap sits in `run-once`) rather than witnessed against React re-running a fence.
  - CACHE-HIT STABILITY IS ARGUED FROM THE FENCE, NOT WITNESSED ADVERSARIALLY. The claim that `!cells` cannot move inside one attempt rests on invariant 5 and on `cold-read!` retaining nothing. A sabotage witness (mutate a cell mid-body, assert the derived hit count still equals the live one) was not written. If the counts receipt is graduated, that witness is the first thing it owes.
  - NO ALLOCATION LADDER WAS RUN. "Attached-only" is proven by the negative control and by the guard's structure, NOT by a heap measurement. The existing B7/B8 ladders were not used.

=== 6. WHERE THIS BELONGS IF GRADUATED ===

  The implementation-governing conclusions are (1) the derive-post-hoc rule that makes the receipt tap-free, (2) the runtime-tap reachability rule from §2(c), and (3) the self-time kill. Their owning tracked record is `docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md` §11 (the row currently reads "Capability receipts | Spike | Mechanical attempt facts only; stop if instrumentation changes rankings or exposes values") and `lanes/left-field-ideas.md` §Capability receipts.

  BOTH FILES ARE HELD BY WORKER doctruth-dsnq RIGHT NOW, so this spike did NOT edit them — a second worker on one file is how two workers silently revert each other. The mayor should route the §11 row change and the left-field protocol paragraph to that worker or sequence a follow-up bead behind it. Suggested §11 row: "Capability receipts | Adopt (counts only) | Attempt facts derived post hoc from retained state, no hot-loop tap; SELF TIME REFUSED — 100 us clock grain against microsecond bodies, and the per-attempt overhead scales with attempt count, not cost".

  §2(c)'s reachability rule is general and arguably belongs beside the erasure gate's own documentation rather than in §11.
close_reason:
SPIKE COMPLETE — VERDICT: SPLIT. The counts receipt graduates as a DESIGN; the self-time field is KILLED. No PR, correctly: this bead's own surface line says "nothing retained without graduation", and the spike graduated no code. Timebox respected. Worker reported FINISHED; worktree reaped on that report, junction removed first, mayor node_modules verified intact.

WHAT GRADUATES. Five of the six named fields need no tap on any hot loop — read calls, unique reads, cache hits, codec nodes and attempts are all derivable post hoc from state the runtime already retains. The load-bearing step is that the cache-hit answer is STABLE ACROSS AN ATTEMPT (cold-read! retains nothing; the generation fence guarantees a pass observes one commit), which is what deletes the per-read counter. THE RANKING-PERTURBATION CHECK REFUSED, on two named controls, and the refusal is a correct deliverable. Building a second one mid-spike was correctly refused as its own bead.

NOT CONCLUDED, recorded so nobody reads more into this than it says: no browser measurement at all — every number is Node-lane or the release gate; the tap's cost on a real Chromium render path is unmeasured. title: hic-088 — Requirements-mine consolidation
description:
# hic-088 — Requirements-mine consolidation

**Phase**: 4/6 · **Est.**: S · **Depends**: hic-004
**Surface**: `docs/design/hicasso/product/requirements-mine.md` (the one consolidation owner)

## Goal
The mine must be current when the audits read it. This bead owns the updates hic-004 only seeded.

## Deliverables
Two consolidation passes recorded in the file: one before the coverage checkpoint (every row's witness link resolves; "owed by" rows re-pointed to landed evidence or open corrections) and one before the final audit (same, plus final-name updates after the sweep).

## Acceptance
At each pass: zero stale witness links; zero rows owing to closed beads without landed evidence; pass dates recorded in the file.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).
notes:
MAYOR 2026-08-10 ~17:05 AUSEST — HELD, AND HERE IS THE MEASUREMENT SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES IT.

I evaluated this bead for dispatch three times today and held it each time. The first
two were on the reasoning that its two passes anchor to events that have not happened.
That is true but it is an assertion. This time I measured, and the measurement is the
better reason to wait.

WHAT THE FILE LOOKS LIKE NOW. docs/design/hicasso/product/requirements-mine.md is 95
lines and references 44 distinct rf2-hic-* beads. Of those 44, exactly FOUR are closed:
rf2-hic-005, rf2-hic-010, rf2-hic-039, rf2-hic-073. The other 40 are open.

WHY THAT MEANS WAIT. The acceptance has three clauses and two of them are already
satisfied or nearly so:
  - "every row's witness link resolves" — scripts/check_doc_slugs.py validates this
    tree's link targets and heading anchors and runs in the fast-PR spine, so a green
    main already means the links resolve. There is no backlog of broken links to clear.
  - "zero rows owing to closed beads without landed evidence" — this is the real work,
    and today it is FOUR ROWS out of 44.
  - "pass dates recorded in the file" — none are recorded, correct, since no pass has run.

So a pass run now would re-point 4 rows, about 9% of the eventual work, and the same
pass has to run again before the coverage checkpoint (rf2-hic-048) by which time most of
the other 40 will have closed. That is doing the job twice for a small fraction of the
value, which is the premature-consolidation shape the project stance rejects.

THE RE-TEST TRIGGER, so this surfaces on its own rather than on somebody's memory.
Dispatch when EITHER holds:
  (a) the closed fraction of the beads this file references passes roughly half — re-run
      the count below; or
  (b) rf2-hic-048 (CHECKPOINT 4, the coverage-matrix audit) becomes near-term, since the
      first pass is specified as "before the coverage checkpoint" and that is the reader
      it exists to serve.
The count, from the mayor checkout:
  for b in $(grep -oE "rf2-hic-[0-9]+" docs/design/hicasso/product/requirements-mine.md \
             | sort -u); do bd show $b | head -1; done

WHAT IS NOT THE REASON. This is not blocked, not gated on a decision, and not waiting on
capacity — a worker slot was free when I wrote this. It is simply not yet worth running.
If the operator wants it run early anyway, it is a small, isolated, low-risk dispatch:
one file, no live worker touches it, and the surface collides with nothing.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #7875 (merged 2026-08-11T03:20:09Z as 63644094fd23c0bd0c54203b1b7bdb094df65a56) — REOPEN THIS EXACT CONSOLIDATION OWNER; do not create a duplicate. Its Deliverables require two recorded passes. The landed file and close reason both say only pass 1 ran and pass 2 is not yet due, yet the Bead was closed. The new sentence “Two passes are owed by rf2-hic-088” therefore immediately points at a closed owner, and no open issue durably owns the final-audit/final-name pass. Keep this Bead open until pass 2 actually lands; being not-yet-due is an expected waiting state, not completion. Pass 1 itself is clean: all cited new evidence paths exist and every witness-cell “owed by” owner remains open.

EVIDENCE: PR #7875 is MERGED, on all five clauses at 91/91, and docs/design/hicasso/product/requirements-mine.md carries the consolidation on main.

PASS 1 DONE. The bead carried a mayor HOLD with a re-test trigger; the worker re-ran that trigger and found 16 of 44 referenced beads now closed, up from 4 the day before, so the trigger had moved sharply and the hold's own note sanctioned an early run. Five rows still owed to closed beads (nine beads, ten citations — rf2-hic-024 owed by two rows); all were re-pointed at landed artefacts. All nine pre-existing witness paths still resolve. ZERO rows owed to a bead that closed without landed evidence — reported as a measurement rather than an assertion, since that is the defect the acceptance criteria name. The row needing judgement was rf2-hic-021, whose deliverable is a CATALOGUE: a document is not an executable witness, and it has one in check_complaint_catalogue.py.

PASS 2 IS NOT DUE, and the file records its own trigger for it: rf2-hic-064 is open and the naming sweep has not run. The worker declined to manufacture a second pass, which would only re-point the same rows twice. That refusal is the correct outcome under the stance and is why this bead closes rather than staying open — a second pass belongs to whoever closes rf2-hic-064.

GATE COVERAGE, verified rather than assumed: mkdocs build --strict was NOT nominated, because mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs keeps design/hicasso/ out of the site and a gate run over an excluded path exits green having verified nothing. check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, and its NEGATIVE CONTROL exit 1 named requirements-mine.md:112 — proving the gate actually reaches the edited file. title: docs: two more carriers of the 'reference-stable for the same resolved frame' sentence the rf2-40kv defect hid behind
description:
TWO MORE CARRIERS of the sentence rf2-ow4e corrected, both verified on main after that bead's PR (#7873) was written.

SITE 1 — `implementation/adapters/uix/README.md:14`, the strong form, verbatim:
"The returned map is reference-stable across re-renders for the same resolved frame (safe in effect deps)."
This is the SAME sentence rf2-ow4e corrected in spec/006 and spec/API.md, and it was NOT in PR #7868's file list — so the code fix landed while this reader-facing document kept describing the defect as the contract.

SITE 2 — `docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/10-native-tier.md:169`, and it is WEAKER STILL:
"the map is reference-stable across re-renders. It is therefore safe to pull `:dispatch` off it and close over it in callbacks."
No frame qualifier at all. A reader takes "reference-stable across re-renders" unconditionally, which is broader than even the uncorrected spec sentence claimed.

THE CORRECTION, from rf2-ow4e's landed wording — do not invent a third phrasing: reference stability holds for the same resolved frame INCARNATION, because a frame keyword is an ADDRESS, not an identity. `capture-frame` pins the exact incarnation live when it ran and every op on the bundle refuses a superseded target, so a bundle surviving a same-id reincarnation would not be merely stale — IT WOULD BE SILENTLY INERT. Read PR #7873's diff and match it; the guide's register is lighter than the spec's, so compress rather than paste.

WHY THIS IS NOT A NIT: rf2-40kv was exactly this sentence made executable — `use-frame` memoised on the frame KEYWORD by `=`, and a keyword is `=` across a same-id reincarnation, so the hook served the dead incarnation's pinned bundle for the rest of the mount with every op silently recovering. THE SENTENCE IS WHERE THE DEFECT HID. Leaving two copies standing leaves two places for it to hide again, and the README is the first thing a UIx consumer reads.

SCOPE: two sentences, two files. Do not re-derive either document, do not touch `implementation/adapters/uix/**` beyond that one line, and do not change behaviour — the code is correct as of PR #7868 (merged).

PROVENANCE: the fourth copy was found and REPORTED rather than taken by the rf2-ow4e worker (PR #7873), correctly — `implementation/**` was outside its fence. The guide line was spotted in the same sweep and left because that tree was in flight.
close_reason:
Landed via PR #7877 (MERGED 2026-08-11; verified on main at 32df8bbaad). Green on all five clauses at 91/91.

Both surviving carriers of the sentence the rf2-40kv defect hid behind are corrected: implementation/adapters/uix/README.md:14 (the strong form, and the first thing a UIx consumer reads) and docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/10-native-tier.md:169 (the weaker form, which carried no frame qualifier at all and so claimed more than even the uncorrected spec did). The correction matches rf2-ow4e's landed wording from PR #7873 rather than inventing a third phrasing, compressed for the guide's lighter register as the bead directed.

The substance now stated in both places: reference stability holds for the same resolved frame INCARNATION, because a frame keyword is an ADDRESS, not an identity. capture-frame pins the exact incarnation live when it ran, and every op on the bundle refuses a superseded target — so a bundle surviving a same-id reincarnation would not merely be stale, it would be SILENTLY INERT. That is why this was never a nit: rf2-40kv was this sentence made executable, and leaving two copies standing left two places for the defect to hide again. No behaviour changed; the code has been correct since PR #7868.

title: hic: the census's X7 premise is an over-count by NAME COLLISION — index.html names the deck, not the donor
description:
The census's X7 row states its premise wrongly, and the failure mode is one the document has not seen before: an OVER-COUNT BY NAME COLLISION.

X7 names `index.html` as carrying a donor dependency. Its only two grep matches are the `<title>` string (L5) and a comment (L29), and BOTH name the deck's own namespace prefix `freehand-views` — not the donor `re-frame.freehand`. The file names NO donor namespace in any position. The census's own search pattern (`freehand|re[-_]frame[./]ui`) cannot distinguish "the donor" from "an artefact whose name happens to begin with the same word".

That is a THIRD species, distinct from the two already recorded: the docstring `[[wiki-link]]` over-count, and the runtime-string under-count (rows X13 and Story's runner_events). This one is neither — the text is real, load-bearing prose, and simply is not about the donor.

THE ROW'S STATED WIRING IS ALSO IN THE WRONG FILE: `freehand-views.core/run` is bound by `:init-fn` in `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` L2042, not in index.html.

SCOPE, and it is narrow: X7 REMAINS A GENUINE CLUSTER MEMBER — it carries the `#app` mount target and the `fh-mount`/`fh-unmount` ids — so THE 43/29 ARITHMETIC IS UNAFFECTED and no total moves. This is a premise correction on one row, not a reclassification.

WORTH ADDING WHILE THERE: the census's search command is recorded in the document precisely so the next reader can re-run it. A one-line caution that the pattern matches artefact names as well as donor namespaces would stop the next reader repeating this.

PROVENANCE: found by the rf2-u5b4 worker (PR #7869) while re-deriving X6-X8 from consumer code. It reported rather than applied, correctly — the census was held by another worker.

title: measurement: no committed dataset records a :clock-resolution, so the 100us clamp is an uncited constant
description:
A GAP IN THE MEASUREMENT RIG'S OWN PROVENANCE, found while rf2-hic-081 was killing the self-time receipt field.

That kill turns on ONE NUMBER: Chrome clamps performance.now() to 100 microseconds. The spike used it correctly and reached the right verdict — but it had to CITE the figure from this repo's instrument rather than take it, BECAUSE NO COMMITTED DATASET CARRIES A :clock-resolution RECORD.

WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. The clamp is the denominator of every timing decision this project makes: it is what says whether a quantity is measurable at all. A rig that measures durations but never records the resolution of the clock it measured them with cannot answer "was this measurable?" from its own data — the answer has to come from outside, from a number somebody remembers. The project spends its days hunting instruments that verify the ABSENCE of bad news rather than the PRESENCE of good news; an unrecorded resolution is the same shape, one level down.

SCOPE, AND KEEP IT SMALL: have the measurement lane record the observed clock resolution alongside the runs it takes, so future datasets carry their own denominator. This is a field on data the rig already produces, NOT a new instrument, NOT a new gate, and NOT a re-measurement of anything already published.

DO NOT let this grow. It does not want a checker, a threshold, or a refusal arm. If recording it turns out to need a rig change rather than a field, say so and stop — that is a different and larger bead.

Note the sequencing constraint that applies to all measurement work here: the operator authorises windows only on a QUIET MACHINE. This bead is a recording change, not a window, so it does not need one — but if it cannot be verified without taking a measurement, it inherits the quiet-machine hold and must say so rather than measuring on a busy box.
close_reason:
PREMISE PARTLY FALSE, RESIDUAL GAP FIXED AS A FIELD. PR #7879 (worker/clockres-dzus). Two of the bead's three claims do not survive contact with the tree; the third does, and was a two-line serialisation defect.

WHAT IS NOT TRUE.

(1) The 100us figure is NOT uncited. docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-candidates-clock.md S2.1 -- 'The resolution figures, verified rather than remembered' -- is a table quoting each figure with its primary source, checked 2026-08-01: Chrome for Developers 'Aligning timers with cross origin isolation restrictions' and MDN Performance.now S Security requirements, with the 5us cross-origin-isolated alternative beside it. the-clock-behind-the-published-rows.md S6 goes further and names the Chromium constant itself: time_clamper.h, kCoarseResolutionMicroseconds = 100 / kFineResolutionMicroseconds = 5, plus W3C High Resolution Time's coarsen-time algorithm. That is the strongest citation form this project asks for.

(2) A committed dataset DOES record a measured clock resolution. clock_run.cjs:1414/3008 serialises 'granularity' -- the sorted distinct non-zero per-sample deltas, whose minimum it prints as the row's grain -- and 16 of the 38 committed dataset files carry it (clock-0qj9w run1-2, clock-emvod run1-8, clock-w3yxd run1-6). Verified by reading the JSON: clock-emvod/run1 M1 min 0.107 ms, keystroke 0.152; clock-w3yxd/run1 bulk100 0.094; clock-0qj9w/run1 M1 0.085. the-candidates-clock.md's published range '0.092-0.153 ms over ~980 distinct values per row' recomputes from those files, which is exactly the property the bead says is missing.

(3) The in-page clock's grain is already measured in the run it governs, by name. hd8_rows/clock-resolution! + hd8_app.cljs:225 (record! :clock-resolution clock), built as rf2-d2tzk for this bead's own stated reason. rf2-hic-081 knew this -- its verdict text names the function.

WHY THE SPIKE STILL HAD TO CITE RATHER THAN TAKE, and why no field would have changed that: taking the number needs a browser run on a QUIET BOX, which the spike correctly refused (Processor Queue Length peaked at 3). A :clock-resolution field in a committed dataset would have left it citing somebody else's run on somebody else's box, one indirection further away. The denominator that governs a measurement has to be taken in the run it governs -- which is rf2-d2tzk's ruling, already implemented. This was a quiet-machine constraint, not a recording gap.

WHAT WAS TRUE, AND IS NOW FIXED. hd8_clock_run.cjs and shapes/census_clock_run.cjs both MEASURE the grain ('if (d.task > 0) granularity.add(d.task)', on the PUBLISHED raw TaskDuration) and both PRINT it, and neither KEPT it -- datasetFor dropped the set. Both took their contract from clock_run.cjs, which keeps it; this is the part they did not inherit. Same species as rf2-jo60g (blocksDecomp collected then dropped at write time), same remedy: ONE FIELD on data the run already produces. Nothing measured changes; nothing is backfilled; the grain travels with the next canonical run.

NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY -- and this is the rig-change line the bead asked me to draw. The IN-PAGE performance.now() grain is still in no committed dataset, because the lane that measures it (hd8_app.cljs, driven by hd8_run.cjs) WRITES NO DATASET FILE AT ALL -- its :clock-resolution goes to console EDN and window.HD8_RESULTS. Giving it one is a destination/publication/canonical discipline plus its coverage in clock_exit_path.test.cjs (~5,800 lines pinning exactly that for the lanes that do write). That is a rig change, not a field, and it is a different and larger bead. I did not start it. Filing it is not obviously worth it: no published figure depends on the in-page clock any more (the mount-gate amendment, rf2-2rtt6.1, demoted the in-page window to DIAGNOSTIC), and hd8_clock_app.cljs measures MOUNT ONLY precisely because rf2-d2tzk found the bulk floor sitting on the clamp.

GATES, run alone, exit captured on the same line: npm run test:script-helpers exit 0 (clock_exit_path.test.cjs: 375 passed) and npm run test:script-policy exit 0. That is the gate for this surface -- one step of test.yml:3000 and of scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:1355. check_fast_pr_gap.py --list: 96 required checks the spine does not decide, none reachable from a three-file .cjs diff. The three new tests are MUTATION-PROVEN: deleting the two serialised lines gives 3/375 failed naming exactly those three, exit 1; restored, exit 0. No measurement taken -- the tests drive datasetFor on a fixture row, so the busy box was never an obstacle.

INCIDENTAL FINDING FOR rf2-w8pz (do not action from here). That bead's mayor note asserts hd8_rows.cljs is 'in the frozen bench tree, kept verbatim by a hash manifest'. It is not. implementation/hicasso/frozen-sources.edn carries exactly ONE row -- front/slot.cljc -- after three recorded retirements. Its premise that an edit there 'moves a hash the freeze gate checks' is false, so the cannot-fix escape it offers is not available; the bead should be decided on its own merits (the wiki-link is prose, and closing it as not-worth-fixing still looks right).

value:
THE MAYOR MUST VERIFY A PREMISE AT SOURCE BEFORE FILING A BEAD, NOT ONLY BEFORE DISPATCHING ONE (2026-08-11).

WHAT HAPPENED. In one session I filed four beads from workers' incidental asides — findings reported out-of-fence, which is exactly the right thing for a worker to do. I wrote each finding into the bead description at filing time, as the routing rule demands. But I wrote them as FACTS, in the reporting worker's confident register, without opening the files. Two of the four premises were false, and both were caught only because the receiving worker checked:

1. rf2-w8pz. I asserted hd8_rows.cljs was "in the FROZEN BENCH TREE, kept verbatim by a hash manifest", and built the whole brief around the question "is this file editable at all", offering a recorded cannot-fix as the likely outcome. TWO separate workers independently read implementation/hicasso/frozen-sources.edn and found it pins exactly ONE file, front/slot.cljc, after three recorded retirements. The escape hatch I offered did not exist. The bead closed correctly anyway, but on an entirely different reason I had not supplied: git log -S proved denominator-resolution never existed as a binding at all.
2. rf2-dzus. I asserted "no committed dataset records a :clock-resolution, so the 100us clamp is an uncited constant". TWO-THIRDS FALSE. The figure is cited twice with primary sources in docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-candidates-clock.md and named as the Chromium constant kCoarseResolutionMicroseconds in the-clock-behind-the-published-rows.md; and 16 of 38 committed dataset files already serialise granularity. The one-third that held was a real two-line serialisation defect in two sibling runners.

WHY THE EXISTING RULE DID NOT CATCH IT. The method already says "grep for the alleged broken symbol before DISPATCHING" and "an audit finding is a CLAIM, not automatically work". Both are aimed at the dispatch decision. Neither fires at the FILING decision, and filing is where the claim becomes durable: a bead description outlives the worker, the chat and the mayor, and the next reader has no way to tell a verified premise from a relayed one. A false premise in a bead is worse than a false premise in a message, because it looks like a finding.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES THIS CHEAP TO FIX. Verifying costs one grep or one file read at filing time. Not verifying costs a worker's whole investigation — and it is a worker who is under a fence, on someone else's evidence, spending its context proving the mayor wrong before it can start.

THE PRACTICE:
- Before filing a bead from someone else's report, open the file at the named path and line. If the claim is about absence ("X does not exist", "nothing records Y"), run the search yourself — absence claims are the ones that fail, because the reporter searched for what they expected rather than what is there.
- If you cannot verify it in the moment, FILE IT AS A CLAIM IN THOSE WORDS: "reported by <worker>, NOT verified at source — verify before acting". That is honest and costs nothing.
- The two claim shapes that failed here are both worth naming in any brief you build on them: a FREEZE or manifest constraint (read the manifest; they shrink as things retire), and a NEVER-RECORDED / UNCITED claim (search the docs tree, not just the code).
- Tell the receiving worker explicitly that the bead text is yours and may be wrong. The line "my bead text is a claim, not a fact — verify every path, line number and structural claim before acting on it, and report anything that did not hold" turned both of these into corrections instead of wasted work.

THE SYSTEM WORKED, WHICH IS THE POINT. Both workers read the source, contradicted the bead, recorded the correction, and reached a better disposition than the one I framed. That is the bead-governs-over-brief rule running in the direction nobody designs for: protecting the worker from the mayor.

title: mayor-method: workers share ONE scratchpad directory, so a generic filename is silently overwritten by a peer
description:
FOUND IN THE FIELD, 2026-08-11, by the clockfix-4mvd worker while it was finishing rf2-4mvd/rf2-w2e6. It reported this out of its own lane, correctly, rather than just working around it.

WHAT HAPPENED. It drafted its PR body to the session scratchpad at the generic path `scratchpad/pr-body.md`. The doctruth-dsnq worker, running concurrently, wrote the same path. The first worker's file was GONE. It recovered only because it noticed and rewrote to `pr-body-clockfix-4mvd.md`, which then survived even the worktree wipe later that hour.

WHY THIS IS NOT A NUISANCE. It is the same defect class the method already records for gate logs — "concurrent workers share the machine's temp directory; two workers writing the same /tmp/gate.log overwrite each other, and the loser reads a green belonging to someone else's run". The recorded remedy is worktree-local log paths. But the SCRATCHPAD is a second shared surface with the same property and it is NOT covered by that rule: the harness hands every worker in a session the same scratchpad directory, and a worker following its brief exactly will still collide there.

THE FAILURE IS SILENT AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS. A worker that loses its draft may not notice — nothing errors, the write succeeds, the file simply holds someone else's content. Worse, the losing worker can READ the survivor and believe it is its own: a PR body describing another bead's work, with plausible structure and the wrong subject. That is exactly the shape of the gate-log case, where the loser reads a green with plausible numbers and the wrong code.

THE FIX IS ONE LINE IN THE BRIEF, and it should go in the canonical worker preamble in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, next to the existing shared-temp-directory rule rather than as a new section: EVERY scratch file a worker writes carries its worktree name — `pr-body-<worktree>.md`, not `pr-body.md`. And a worker must confirm a scratch file is its OWN before believing it, exactly as the gate-log rule already requires for logs.

DO NOT over-engineer this. No lock, no per-worker subdirectory scheme imposed by the mayor, no script. The naming convention plus the confirm-before-believing rule is the whole remedy, and it is the same remedy the sibling rule already uses.

SECOND, SMALLER FINDING FROM THE SAME REPORT, worth recording beside it because it strengthens an existing rule rather than adding one: the HARNESS reported that worker's revert-gate run as "completed (exit code 0)" while the gate's own captured status was 1. The method already says the exit code is the verdict and the summary is decoration, and already names the harness as one of the shapes that lies. This is a fresh, dated instance of exactly that, and it is why the one-line redirect-and-echo convention is not belt-and-braces but the only reliable verdict. If dispatch-prompt-template.md's wording on that point can be sharpened by citing this, do so; otherwise leave it alone — the rule is already there.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7880 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7880). One rule added to the paste-verbatim worktree-boundary block in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, beside the no-stash rule: every scratch file written outside the worktree carries that worktree's name (pr-body-<worktree>.md, never pr-body.md), and a worker confirms a scratch file is its own before believing it. Plus one entry in the Failure-modes index. No lock, no subdirectory scheme, no script. CORRECTION TO THE BEAD: it says to place this 'next to the existing shared-temp-directory rule' in dispatch-prompt-template.md, but that rule lives in bootstrap.md (lines 260-264), not in the template — the template has no shared-temp rule at all. Placed in the paste-verbatim boundary block instead, because the bead's own finding is that a worker following its brief exactly still collides, so the rule must reach the WORKER. Second item: the harness-vs-captured exit-code instance is ALREADY recorded in bootstrap.md (lines 231-241), so no new rule was added; the template's exit-code bullet was sharpened by one clause instead — the number you quote is the one you captured, never the harness's — since that bullet covered pipes and fresh shells but never named the harness.

A NEW :rf.error/* REFUSAL MUST TOUCH spec/009-Instrumentation.md, SO A BLANKET "NEVER TOUCH spec/**" FENCE IS WRONG (2026-08-11, rf2-hic-035 / PR #7876).

WHAT HAPPENED. I fence every dispatch with "HOT ZONE, sequential and never parallel: shadow-cljs.edn, deps.edn, spec/**, .github/workflows/** — STOP and report rather than editing." The rf2-hic-035 worker edited spec/009-Instrumentation.md anyway, flagged it in its PR body, and was RIGHT to. Its reason: check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py CHECK A REDS ANY PR THAT EMITS AN UNCATALOGUED :rf.error/*. So a diff adding a refusal cannot be green without its catalogue row. A blanket fence would forbid every new refusal in the repo.

THE DISTINCTION THE FENCE WAS MISSING. The hot-zone rule exists to stop two workers colliding on one file, and it is right about the files it names. But spec/009 has TWO kinds of edit and they carry completely different collision risk:
  - A CATALOGUE ROW appended for a refusal the same PR introduces. Mechanically forced by a gate, append-only, and unique to that refusal's id — two workers adding different refusals do not collide.
  - A NORMATIVE PROSE change to the instrumentation contract. That is genuine hot-zone work and stays sequential.
The same shape almost certainly applies to docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md, which carries the parallel row.

HOW TO FENCE IT INSTEAD. Say: "spec/009-Instrumentation.md — you MAY append the catalogue row your own new refusal requires, because check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py CHECK A reds a PR without it. You may NOT change its normative prose or any row you did not introduce; that is sequential hot-zone work — report it." Same for complaints.md.

TWO WIDER LESSONS, and the second matters more.

FIRST: a fence that forbids what a GATE REQUIRES is not a safe fence, it is an unsatisfiable one. The worker's options were to break the fence or ship a red PR. When a brief and a gate disagree, the brief is wrong — check what the gates demand of the surface before writing the fence.

SECOND, AND IT IS THE REAL FINDING: the bead's own WORKER PROTOCOL did not list spec/** at all; only my dispatch brief did. The worker noticed the discrepancy and told me. That is the bead-governs-over-brief rule working, and it points at a mayor habit worth breaking — pasting a STANDARD fence list into every brief without asking whether this particular bead's work can live inside it. A boilerplate fence reads as careful and is not; it is the same reflex as a boilerplate gate list, and it fails the same way.

title: hic test kit: a failed clocked mount leaves the global virtual clock installed
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7861 — correctness and transactional-completeness finding.

`hm/mount!` installs the page-wide virtual clock BEFORE `mint-frame!`, so `:initial-events` timers are correctly captured. But the only pre-handle release in the new code is the later render-refusal branch. If `rf/make-frame` throws while normalising or running `:initial-events` — core deliberately raises `:rf.error/initial-events-step-failed` on that path — control leaves from `mint-frame!` before a handle exists and before `release-clock!` runs.

The failed frame itself is rolled back by core, but `!clock` still owns one holder and global `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, both clearers, and `Date.now` remain replaced. There is no handle to pass to `unmount!` or `residue`, so the rest of the browser run inherits a frozen clock and can hang or false-green. This contradicts both `mount!`'s transactional promise (a throw leaves nothing behind) and the clock's mount-window promise.

BOUNDED REPAIR: keep clock installation before initial events, but make its hold transactional until `handle-for` succeeds. Every escaping pre-handle path must release exactly the hold this call acquired, without double-release on the existing render-refusal path and without restoring globals out from under an already-clocked peer mount. Preserve the original thrown refusal/ex-data; add no public API or new diagnostic.

PROVENANCE: PR #7861 merge c3b64aa4c02c75f15ecca6b424bf7e34437ff037, `implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test/mounted.cljs`.
acceptance_criteria: Add a real-browser witness that captures the five platform functions, makes a `{:clock true}` mount whose initial event deterministically fails, and proves: the original failure is returned; the provisional frame is absent; all five globals are identity-restored; and a subsequent real timer/plain mount settles. Add the holder-count control: with one clocked peer already live, a second clocked mount's initial-event failure releases only its own hold, leaves the shared clock installed for the peer, and the peer can still advance and cleanly restore it.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7883 — mount!'s clock hold is now transactional until handle-for, released once on every escaping pre-handle path. Witnessed by a-failed-clocked-mount-leaves-no-clock-installed (throw inside :initial-events; five platform functions read by identity; leaked-holder arm; real timer settles) and a-failed-clocked-mount-releases-only-its-own-hold (peer control). Confirm-by-revert: 6 + 2 reds without the fix.

title: EP-0038: Hicasso — the native view-layer programme
description:
The programme epic for EP-0038 (PR #7257). Hicasso = interpreted Hiccup on a UIx-class React FC host, optimised for re-frame2 (alias h; io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso).

AUTHORITY: docs/EP/EP-0038-the-hicasso-view-layer-programme.md + docs/design/hicasso/ (decisions.md HD-001..HD-021 is normative; then validation.md). Every brief filed under this epic carries the anti-regression fence + banned vocabulary (charter §Constraints) as normative.

WAVES: 0 = standard bead + four fresh like-for-like instruments + draft guide (parallel, off-clock; the old instrument beads rf2-mapni/m7xs7/ssn1o are CLOSED do-not-refile spec donors). 1 = donor-arm stop-gate (off-clock; ruling = delegated advisory vs the published P0 table), then shared front half, then the two tournament arms (six-week clock starts at the first Hicasso-arm commit that mounts the dogfood screen). 2 = P2 fork ruling (DECIDER: Mike; reviews advise) -> graduate one arm into implementation/hicasso/ and build v0, or stop with adapters-as-success (a SUCCESSFUL outcome).

TWO TOURNAMENT-LEVEL FINDINGS, both recorded because they bear on the comparison rather than on one arm:

OPERATOR RULING — HICASSO IS A REACT ADAPTER; ARM 2 (PATCH) IS DROPPED (Mike, 2026-07-31, verbatim: 'I want hicasso to be an adaptor for React that is optimised for re-frame2, user ergonomics and performance. I don't want ARM 2 (PATCH).'). Recorded by acting mayor.

THE TOURNAMENT IS OVER. It is decided by PRODUCT DIRECTION, not by measurement, and that distinction must be preserved in the record: Arm 2 did not lose on numbers and did not fail its gates — it MET its hard gate (controlled-restore on the 100-cell grid in real Chromium, 920 tests / 5,743 assertions / 0 failures, no act/flushSync/rAF). It is dropped because the operator does not want an own renderer, not because it could not build one.

WHAT HICASSO IS NOW: a React ADAPTER, optimised for three things in this order as stated — re-frame2 (it is built for this state layer, not a general-purpose view library), USER ERGONOMICS, and PERFORMANCE. rf2-2rtt6.9's lean-React arm is therefore no longer 'tournament arm 1' — it IS the product line. Its brief's competitive fences (own namespace, do not touch the rival, keep the comparison like-for-like) are DISCHARGED; the shared front half is no longer a neutral substrate to be preserved for fairness and may be evolved as the adapter needs, under normal review.

WHAT SURVIVES FROM ARM 2, and must not be thrown away with it:
  - THE LAZINESS FINDING, which is a SURFACE B property and applies to the adapter directly: a for's reads happen when the children are walked, NOT when the body returns, so a collector closed at body-return registers no edges for the rows. Arm 1 has been told to write a witness and report.
  - THE STRUCTURAL OBSERVATION that HD-002(a)'s ownership state machine is near-vacuous when the body runs inside the commit, and LIVE when React owns the render phase. Under this ruling React owns the render phase, so THE CANDIDATE-LEDGER TRIPWIRE IS FULLY IN FORCE for the adapter. That is now the single largest correctness risk in the programme.
  - The controlled-restore witness as EVIDENCE of what correct input behaviour looks like, whether or not the code that produced it is kept.

CONSEQUENT DISPOSITIONS (acting mayor, under the Hicasso authority delegated 2026-07-31): rf2-2rtt6.10 CLOSED as ruled-out; its three follow-ups rf2-2rtt6.26 (islands bridge), rf2-2rtt6.27 (witness rows) and rf2-2rtt6.28 (SSR/hydration) are Arm-2-specific and CLOSED as moot. A separate bead disposes of Arm 2's landed bench code once Arm 1 has mined what transfers.

UNCHANGED: the Surface B ergonomics ruling (only the ambient collector is acceptable; grouped use-subs is below the usability bar, so a collector failure means NULL, not a fallback); the tripwire that overrides the clock; K7, running from 2026-07-31.
OPERATOR DIRECTION — WHAT HICASSO IS, AND WHERE THE EFFORT GOES (Mike, 2026-07-31, two messages, recorded by acting mayor).

(1) VERBATIM: 'I want all the effort to be going into producing an excellent adapter which is a Hiccup interpreter that is highly efficient very data oriented including the mount and unmount capabilities supplied by Replicant and other very data oriented features And I want it to target React.'

(2) VERBATIM: 'I want the effort to go into adversarial design reviews and performance improvement.'

SO HICASSO IS: a HICCUP INTERPRETER, targeting React, highly efficient, VERY DATA-ORIENTED, optimised for re-frame2 + user ergonomics + performance. Not an own renderer (Arm 2 dropped), not a compiler (still a hard fence).

REPLICANT'S FEATURES, VERIFIED FROM PRIMARY SOURCE (replicant.fun, fetched 2026-07-31 — NOT recalled, per the standing rule about library claims):
  - ':replicant/mounting' and ':replicant/unmounting' — DECLARATIVE ATTRIBUTE OVERRIDES applied during mount and unmount. The site: 'you can specify overrides for any attributes during mounting and unmounting. This allows you to declaratively transition elements on mount and unmount, like fading in an element as it is mounted.' This is the capability Mike named. It replaces refs/callbacks/useEffect for enter-and-leave transitions with DATA IN THE HICCUP.
  - CUSTOM ELEMENT ALIASES — user-defined extensions that expand to arbitrary hiccup (their example: i18n without framework coupling).
  - DATA-DRIVEN EVENT HANDLERS — handlers declared as data passed to a global dispatcher, trivially testable.
  - Pure functions and data throughout; Replicant deliberately discourages stateful component abstractions.

WHAT RE-FRAME2 ALREADY HAS OF THAT: the data-driven event handler half is already the shape of Hicasso's intent lowering (event vectors as :on-click, the ::h/value placeholder, submit auto-prevent) and of re-frame's dispatch model generally. So the genuinely NEW capabilities to bring across are the MOUNT/UNMOUNT ATTRIBUTE OVERRIDES and ALIASES — and the harder question is what they mean when the target is React, whose own mount/unmount story is refs and effects. Making a declarative transition work through a React reconciler without leaking a ref or an effect into user code is a real design problem and should be treated as one.

WHERE THE EFFORT GOES, per (2): ADVERSARIAL DESIGN REVIEW and PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT — not feature sprawl, not further instrument bookkeeping. Design decisions on this adapter are to be attacked before they are built on, and the performance work is the point rather than a later phase. The mayor is to bias dispatch accordingly: reviewers whose job is to break a design, and workers whose job is to make it faster.

STILL BINDING: Surface B is the only acceptable read surface (grouped use-subs below the usability bar; a collector failure means NULL, not a fallback). The candidate-ledger tripwire is FULLY LIVE now that React owns the render phase. No compiler, no analyzer, no dual mode, no ViewCell-class object graph. K7 running from 2026-07-31.
OPERATOR CLARIFICATION (Mike, 2026-07-31, verbatim): 'replicant is just an example not an objective.'

CORRECTING THE PREVIOUS NOTE, which read too literally. Replicant is cited as an ILLUSTRATION OF THE SPIRIT — what 'very data-oriented' looks like when someone commits to it — NOT as a feature checklist to match, port, or be measured against. Do not make 'parity with Replicant' a goal, an acceptance criterion, or a comparison row. Its ':replicant/mounting' / ':replicant/unmounting' overrides and its aliases are worth understanding as EXAMPLES of expressing in data what other libraries express in callbacks, refs and effects; they are not a specification.

THE OBJECTIVE, stated without reference to any other library: an EXCELLENT ADAPTER — a hiccup interpreter targeting React, HIGHLY EFFICIENT and VERY DATA-ORIENTED, optimised for re-frame2, user ergonomics, and performance. Where a capability today is expressed as a callback, a ref, an effect or an imperative escape hatch, the data-oriented question to ask is whether it can be expressed as data in the hiccup instead — and whether doing so is genuinely better for the programmer, not merely more fashionable. Lifecycle/transition behaviour is one such area; it is an area to think about, not a deliverable copied from elsewhere.

AND THE EFFORT MODEL STANDS: adversarial design review and performance improvement. A data-oriented idea earns its place by surviving an attack on its design and by being fast — not by resembling another library.
OPERATOR STEER (Mike, 2026-07-31, verbatim): 'we've covered some of this ground already with freehand and reframe.UI.'

THIS IS THE CENTRAL DESIGN QUESTION NOW, and it must be answered BEFORE more adapter code is written. Hicasso is ruled to be a hiccup interpreter targeting React, highly efficient and very data-oriented. INTERPRETED FREEHAND IS ALREADY A HICCUP INTERPRETER IN THIS REPO, it ships, and it was measured to death by the withdrawn EP-0036 programme. re-frame.ui is the EXPERIMENTAL compiled-view substrate that sat beside it, and the whole donor-absorption ledger (just archived under rf2-lrtwj) exists because absorbing re-frame.ui was once the plan. So the honest question is not 'how do we build a hiccup interpreter' — it is:

  WHAT DOES HICASSO ADD OVER WHAT FREEHAND AND re-frame.ui ALREADY ESTABLISHED, AND WHICH OF THEIR MEASURED CONCLUSIONS DOES IT INHERIT RATHER THAN GET TO RE-LITIGATE?

Prior art that must be read before more is built (not summarised from memory — read):
  - implementation/freehand/ — the shipped interpreted substrate itself.
  - docs/design/freehand/** — the frozen design record of the withdrawn programme, including why the COMPILED tier was ruled out and the trap in removing it (elision dies with the compiled tier unless {:reactive false} lands first), where interpreted Freehand actually stands against Reagent, which row is NOT a valid target, and why the broad-update gap is architectural rather than fixable by effort.
  - implementation/ui/ — re-frame.ui, the experimental compiled-view substrate, and spec/004D / spec/Ownership.md for what it still owns.
  - docs/EP/EP-0036-*.md — the withdrawal record: what was killed (the programme, F0-F6, drive-to-zero) versus what explicitly survived (the implementation, CI lanes, shipped-behaviour specs).
  - spec/conformance/freehand/donor-inventory.md — now an archived snapshot; 229 tracked donor-tree files under 106 patterns and 30 external consumers, which is a map of how deeply re-frame.ui is still wired in.

THE RISK THIS STEER GUARDS AGAINST: spending the six-week K7 clock rediscovering, in a new namespace, conclusions that are already published with instrument evidence — or worse, building an interpreter that is measurably no better than the one already shipping, and finding that out at week five. Freehand's measured position against Reagent is the floor Hicasso has to clear to justify existing at all.

ACTION: an adversarial design review is dispatched with exactly this question as its brief, and adapter construction is held to what it has already landed until that review reports. This is the effort model Mike asked for — adversarial design review first, then performance work.
OPERATOR STEER, continued (Mike, 2026-07-31, verbatim, two messages): 'look at their ergonomics' and 'look at their data oriented structure Improve upon that.'

So the prior-art work is not merely defensive (what must Hicasso not repeat) — it is the SOURCE MATERIAL. The brief is: study what Freehand and re-frame.ui are actually like TO WRITE, study how DATA-ORIENTED their structures genuinely are, and IMPROVE UPON THAT. Not parity, not homage, not a survey — an improvement, argued and demonstrated in authoring examples.

Concretely, the questions to answer with evidence from the code rather than from memory:
  - What does a view look like in Freehand today, and in re-frame.ui? Write real examples of each, from their own docs and tests.
  - Where does each express something as a CALLBACK, a REF, an EFFECT, a MACRO, or an imperative escape hatch that could be DATA instead? Every such site is a candidate improvement.
  - Where is each ALREADY well data-oriented, so Hicasso inherits rather than reinvents? Freehand is a shipped hiccup interpreter; re-frame.ui is the compiled-view experiment. Both have been through real use and real measurement.
  - What is genuinely awkward about each — the thing an author works around, names badly, or has to remember? Those are the ergonomics defects worth fixing.
  - Then: what does Hicasso's authoring surface look like such that it is BETTER, under the operator's Surface B ruling (sub legal inside a when, a for, an inlined helper), targeting React, with no compiler?

Two reviews are dispatched: one constructive (study the two prior surfaces, propose the improvement, with before/after authoring examples), one adversarial (attack the proposition that Hicasso adds anything over what already ships, and name what it is on course to repeat). Neither writes production code; both produce findings and beads.
ADVERSARIAL DESIGN REVIEW OF EP-0038 AS RULED (2026-07-31, read-only pass).

BOTTOM LINE: continue, with three named changes -- not "continue as ruled", and not "reframe as Freehand improvements". The strongest single objection is arithmetic and it lands on the mount row: post-rf2-2rtt6.25 the ruled parent is at PARITY with Reagent on the 300-boundary mount witness (1.0243x [0.9937 - 1.0549], validation.md:268), so there is no headroom left for a codec, and reaching "mount <= 1.0x Reagent" would require a runtime hiccup interpreter to run for <= 0.98x the cost of UIx's compile-time $ -- interpretation free or negative. Two independent instruments in this repo price interpretation at 1.15-1.29x (donor-r2/uix 1.162-1.286 on mount-M, hd8-composed-donor-arm.md:231; free-i/free-ik 1.216 [1.092-1.425], compiled-tier-browser-worth-it.md:275), HD-008's own single-instrument donor-r2/reagent reads 1.353-1.460 and is still 1.13-1.22x after applying the full -16.2% post-.25 correction, and HD-004 has ruled the one accelerant class that could close it (template extraction with hole plans) into the arm that has now been dropped. Win condition (1) is internally inconsistent as a direct consequence: 1.0243 x 1.10 = 1.127, so "mount <= 1.0x Reagent" and "codec inside 1.10x direct UIx" cannot both be met -- rf2-2rtt6.30, operator's to amend.

WHAT SURVIVED, and it is substantial: the bulk-broad row is already won by the parent (UIx 0.6291x Reagent) where Freehand died at ~10x; the product shell and event-vector lowering are measured FREE (rung 2 indistinguishable from rung 1 on 6 of 8 rows) and no adapter has intent-as-data; the subscription->boundary index is a genuinely new mechanism aimed squarely at the parent's worst row (narrow, UIx 1.1754x Reagent); per-read retained heap is the one axis where one hook plus a shared index beats N uSES cells by design rather than by tuning, and it is the axis validation.md calls "the number a native layer actually has to beat"; and the governance survived its own test by scoring the donor gate FAILED in those words rather than softening it.

CONSTRUCTIVE DESIGN REVIEW REPORTED (worker, 2026-07-31): the prior-art ergonomics +
data-orientation study the operator's "look at their ergonomics / look at their data
oriented structure Improve upon that" steer asked for. Read Freehand's shipped source
and guide, re-frame.ui's compiler, both tournament arms, and the census; verified
React 19 ref semantics and Replicant's two mechanisms from primary sources today.

THE PROPOSAL. Freehand and re-frame.ui already solved most of what Hicasso needs, and
Arm 1 already solved the part I expected to design — Surface B with no candidate ledger,
because the read-set-keyed subscribe closure has React's OWN commit install the edges
(arm1/runtime.cljs "the only global mutation is the commit's"). I filed nothing against
it. What neither predecessor solved is CONCEPT COUNT, and K5 is a count: Freehand ships
8 public macros + ~20 public vars; re-frame.ui ships ~30 public names none of which are
callable, plus 99 distinct compile-refusal ids. So the improvement is mostly DELETION
WITH A DATA REPLACEMENT. Four items: (1) one callback form instead of Freehand's four,
because the POSITION already declares the contract and the census has 3 key-condition
handlers and 0 stopPropagation in 85 files; (2) one attribute-merge spelling — a
reserved :& key with HD-010(a)'s owned-literal law applied unconditionally — replacing
spread / spread-safe / plain-merge, whose wrong choice today SILENTLY forfeits the
controlled-input door; (3) presence phase as a PROP plus ::h/mounting / ::h/unmounting
attribute overrides as data, which deletes the trap Freehand's own guide records
(presence.md:62-66 — reading the phase inline gives you the PARENT'S phase) and lets a
fading toast be written inline with no child view; (4) reserve :ref's vector value-space
now and refuse it loudly in v0, so the imperative escape can become data later without a
second attribute name — this is the ONE place Hicasso is currently planned to be LESS
data-oriented than the substrate it replaces.

LIFECYCLE ANSWER. Transition overrides: YES, cleanly, no ref and no effect anywhere,
because the presence boundary owns the retained children and the merge is a
hiccup->hiccup transform before the codec. Imperative node ownership: YES without user-
code refs or effects, via React 19 ref callbacks with cleanup (verified on react.dev) —
but with a real gap stated plainly: a ref callback fires on attach and detach, NEVER on
config change, so Freehand's :update has no equivalent without an effect; v0 should ship
attach/detach only and route steady-state change through the command effect. Domain
lifecycle (fetch on mount / release on unmount): stays NO — causal owners are routes,
resources and machines. Also verified: Replicant's :replicant/on-mount is a CALLBACK,
so only its attribute-override half is worth taking, and Freehand's registered-behavior
use site is more data-oriented than Replicant's hooks.

ARM 1 — THE ADAPTER — HAS LANDED ITS CORE (PR #7321, recorded by acting mayor 2026-07-31). The ruled architecture is now demonstrated rather than proposed, and three of the programme's open correctness risks are closed by evidence.

THE <=2-HOOK SHELL IS HELD, AND MEASURED AT REACT'S DISPATCHER rather than declared: ['useContext' 'useSyncExternalStore'], exactly 2 at 1, 7 AND 20 reads, with no useRef/useState/useMemo/useCallback anywhere in the shell. The mechanism is the interesting part: React gives a function component no per-instance storage except a hook cell, so a shell wanting one has already spent a third hook. Arm 1 gives the shell NO per-instance render-phase state at all — 'subscribe' closes over the read SET and nothing else, so it is a pure function of a value: cached by that value, shared across boundaries, identity-stable exactly while the reads are unchanged, which is precisely React's own re-subscribe condition. getSnapshot returns a monotone epoch sum, so Object.is on one number is a correct change test with no memo. The raw-UIx comparator on the same probe and page RISES with read count. If React's internals slot moves, the witness records UNWITNESSED and FAILS — it cannot silently go green.

THE CANDIDATE-LEDGER TRIPWIRE DID NOT FIRE. Closest approach named honestly: the read-set entry cache is one line from the fence — keyed by read-set CONTENT, never by render or attempt, evicted by a macrotask reaper, and dropping an entry early costs one re-subscribe and no correctness.

THE LAZINESS DEFECT IS REFUTED FOR THIS ARCHITECTURE, STRUCTURALLY: the collector window closes around codec/as-element and the codec is eager everywhere (expand-seq, realize-children, clj->js). No doall, no widened window, no cost, hook budget untouched. Three witnesses, each asserting the SECOND half (a later write re-renders), because a broken implementation passes the first. Further, the four DEFERRED-read escapes (stored handler, invoked handler, delay, stashed lazy seq) now convert into a LOUD ERROR NAMING THE QUERY rather than a silent missing edge — which discharges the substance of rf2-2rtt6.32. One residual is named rather than hidden: a deferred read forced inside another boundary's render is attributed to that boundary.

SURFACE B IS PREFERRED ON EVIDENCE, AND NOT FOR BREVITY. Identical canonical DOM across collector / grouped / raw UIx with a can-answer-false control. The collector is the only surface where the read sits at the value's POINT OF USE, so 'what does this boundary depend on?' is answered by reading the body; grouped's declaration and body can DRIFT, and on the collector that drift is not expressible. Raw UIx loses decisively (no conditional read, no helper-donated read, seven hand-written handlers). Measured: the collector's conditional read holds FEWER edges than the declaration on the same page. This is direct evidence for the operator's Surface B ruling.

TWO FINDINGS OTHER WORK MUST NOT MISS:
1. HD-002's 'acquire without deref' IS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE against this substrate and FAILS SILENTLY. A derived value's unset baseline is never rf= a real value, and the render's own read went through subscribe-once (a different, disposed reaction) — so a freshly acquired reaction reports movement on the first later commit whatever it did: EVERY NEWLY MOUNTED BOUNDARY RE-RENDERS ONCE FOR NOTHING. One baseline deref per new unique key closes it. Caught by the narrow-write witness.
2. THE AMBIENT FRAME OUTRANKS REACT CONTEXT, INVISIBLY. The carried-invariant chain resolves the dynamic-var tier BEFORE context, so an ambient use-subscribe answers for the ambient frame while use-current-frame reports the provider's — and it presents as a RENDERING difference. ':ambient-frame nil' is now set in every DOM fixture here, with a probe asserting the two read forms agree.

DESIGN INPUT ON rf2-2rtt6.39 (delete the per-boundary frame hook by threading the frame as a codec prop): REJECTED FOR v0 ON CORRECTNESS, not cost. A frame-provider interleaved between two Hicasso boundaries is a React component the codec never sees, so a props-threaded frame SILENTLY KEEPS THE OUTER FRAME across it. Any measurement of .39 needs an interleaved-provider witness or it measures a design that is wrong in the one case providers exist for.

K7: Arm 1 also mounts the dogfood screen (arm1_dogfood_dom_cljs_test), so the clock is confirmed running from 2026-07-31 on both arms' evidence. rf2-2rtt6.9 stays IN_PROGRESS with rf2-2rtt6.41 filed for the remainder (100-cell controlled grid, StrictMode/HMR/h-boundary, H2, the allocation-slope half, candidate bar rows).
