THE RULING: Hicasso AUTHORS NO CODEC. It does not write a third runtime hiccup interpreter, and it does not adopt Freehand's. It CONSUMES reagent-slim's, which this measurement establishes as the cheapest interpreter in the tree.

WHY THIS IS CONSISTENT WITH THE OPERATOR'S DIRECTION, not a departure from it. Mike ruled Hicasso is 'a Hiccup interpreter that is highly efficient very data oriented... targeting React'. Consuming the cheapest proven codec IS being a highly efficient hiccup interpreter — it is the efficient answer. What is ruled out is AUTHORING a third one, which the adversarial review identified as the programme's single largest available waste (this repo already holds two: freehand/react.cljs ~1,203 lines with conversion.cljc ~906, and reagent-slim/template.cljs ~1,161). The three capabilities the review found genuinely new — the subscription-to-boundary index, intent-as-data lowering, one-hook-per-boundary — are all REACTIVITY mechanisms, and that is where the six weeks go.

CAVEAT CARRIED FROM THE MEASUREMENT, so nobody misreads it later: Freehand's walk asks per-element questions slim's does not (controlled-input door, caller split, top-layer, declared properties, id-conflict, class/style alias composition). That is a CAPABILITY difference, not merely implementation cost. If Hicasso later needs one of those capabilities, the cost of adding it to slim's codec must be measured rather than assumed — this ruling says slim's codec is cheapest AS MEASURED, not that Freehand's cost buys nothing.
THE P0 STAGED-READ TEAR IS FIXED (rf2-2rtt6.42, PR #7324; recorded by acting mayor). Worth recording HOW, because the shape of the fix is the finding.

THE DIAGNOSIS: the epoch-sum getSnapshot was driven by exactly one counter, and that counter sits downstream of a watch that only exists AFTER commit. For a key nothing holds yet there is no cell, hence no watch, hence no mark-dirty!, hence no bump — getSnapshot answered 0 before the commit and 0 after it, however far the value had moved. React's own post-subscribe re-check therefore had nothing to see.

THE BASELINE-DEREF REMEDY IS NOT A TEAR FIX, confirmed against the code rather than argued: it is ALREADY in acquire-cell! on main. It gives a fresh cell a correct baseline and NO COMPARISON, so it silently adopts the moved value as though it had always been that. It remains the right fix for the spurious first re-render (Arm 1's separate finding) and nothing more. The worker asserted this as a test row rather than a paragraph.

THE FIX — and this is the part to remember: a key with no cell contributes its frame's commit-basis = @!generation + re-frame.frame/frame-commit-epoch(frame); a cell records the basis it was CREATED at; flush! re-stamps rather than increments. frame-commit-epoch IS THE SUBSTRATE'S OWN observation-port evidence counter, and Spec 006 already uses it verbatim to detect 'the frame's durable state moved in the render->commit gap — without watching anything'. In the worker's words: THE ARM WAS MISSING THE ONE FIELD THE SUBSTRATE HAD ALREADY BUILT. Executable change: SIX LINES plus commit-basis and a snapshot-of accessor.

COST: hooks unchanged at 2; subscribe still closes over the read set and nothing else; zero allocation; ZERO in steady state (a mounted boundary holds a reference to every key it reads, so no staged term appears). Conservative only in the safe direction — a boundary mounting exactly as an unrelated write lands re-renders once.

THE TRIPWIRE DID NOT FIRE, and the reasoning is worth preserving: candidate (a), 'compare what the render read', was DELIBERATELY REJECTED because keeping what the render read requires a second render-populated buffer that the commit reconciles — which IS a ledger. Comparing BASES needs no record at all, because React already holds the per-boundary render-time value. That distinction is the difference between a legal fix and a design kill.

WITNESS: 6 rows in arm1/staged_read_tear_cljs_test.cljs against the arm's OWN runtime, plus Case 3 in the DOM test in real Chromium (the staged writer is a sibling boundary writing during the same render pass, so it needs no guess about passive-effect scheduling). Mutation with the fix reverted: test:cljs exit 1 (3 failures, all in the new ns), test:browser exit 1 — 'the real DOM painting stale forever'. After: both exit 0.

STILL OPEN, scoped out with reasons on rf2-2rtt6.44: the :registry-epoch and :node-key axes have no counterpart. Registry — a :sub re-registration is not a frame-state install, and observation/registry-epoch* is ^:private with no public reader, so the arm cannot read it without a substrate change; closing it for a retained key would mean re-rendering every boundary on every re-registration, which is a design decision rather than a defect fix. Node-key — frame/dissoc-frame! clears the commit-epoch entry, so a same-id reincarnation RESTARTS AT 0, making commit-basis monotone only within one incarnation, which is precisely why the observation port carries :node-key as a third field.

MERGE-ORDER NOTE for rf2-2rtt6.43: PR #7323 (already merged) carries generation_fence_coverage_cljs_test.cljs, which TRANSCRIBES the three functions #7324 changes — so its row 2 now asserts a defect the arm no longer has. It tests its own copy, so nothing reds, but .43 should RE-POINT it at the arm's runtime rather than repair the transcription.
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF THE LANDED ADAPTER (Arm 1), read-only, origin/main @ 40e309600e — arm1/ and
docs/design/hicasso/ are byte-identical to 6494d6e039; arm1's last commit is 7e40db6481.

BOTTOM LINE. The mechanism survives; the cost model does not, and one named correctness hole is
mischaracterised. I could not move the two-hook budget, could not find a candidate ledger, could
not construct a fourth blind spot in `commit-basis`, and could not make a read outside ANY render
go quiet. The strongest defect is the FIFTH ESCAPE, and the judgement already names it
(studio/arm1-lean-react-dogfood-judgement.md:237-241) while dismissing it as "not a missing edge
— the reader does re-render": that dismissal is wrong, because a LazySeq caches its realised
values, so the wrong reader re-renders ONCE, does not re-execute the read, drops the edge on the
next commit, and the value is then frozen for the life of the mount — the exact "correct on
screen, frozen thereafter, attributable to nothing" class the same page calls the worst failure
the ruled surface can have. The structural argument meant to make that class impossible ("a seq at
a prop position goes through `clj->js`") is FALSE at the boundary-prop position: `boundary-element`
(front/codec.cljs:341-349) hands the props map through raw, and `realize-children` flattens
exactly one level. Two further real findings: the read-set entry cache degrades to an O(N) scan
selected by read ORDER (an undocumented authoring detail, on the bulk K=100/300 rung), and
`record-reads`'s set difference — the operation HD-002(b) is discharged against — is never
exercised by the wired runtime, because every re-subscribe mints a fresh registration id and
therefore always diffs against the empty set, making a one-key change a full teardown+rebuild.

VERDICTS. (1) two hooks at 1/7/20 — SURVIVES, honestly measured at React's dispatcher with an
explicit UNWITNESSED failure path; the COST model sold with it does not. (2) no candidate ledger
— SURVIVES; entries are keyed purely by content, `refs` is a commit count, and the macrotask
reaper opens no disagreement window (walked three interleavings). (3) staged-read tear —
SURVIVES, and more strongly than claimed: the epoch sum is term-wise monotone so collision is
impossible, all three `replace-container!` sites bump, and there is no `reg-sub-raw`, so
rf2-2rtt6.44's two axes really are the two (corroboration + one refinement noted there).
(4) "Surface B is preferred, MEASURED" — PARTLY SUPPORTED: DOM parity and the collector<grouped
edge count are real, but the edge count is an efficiency reading against the arm the operator
removed, and nothing is measured against the surviving raw-UIx control; the preference itself is
an argued judgement, which the page is honest about. (5) the loud-error guard — BROKEN, see above.

WHAT SURVIVED: the two-hook budget; the tripwire; `commit-basis`'s completeness and the generation
fence including the mid-body staged move; the four witnessed escapes; the correct rejection of
"acquire without deref"; teardown symmetry (a stale cleanup cannot release a successor's cell);
and the parity plumbing probe that turned the ambient-frame bug into a finding.

BEADS FILED: rf2-2rtt6.45 (P1, the fifth escape, with a full reproduction and a recommended fix
that does NOT need per-boundary render identity), rf2-2rtt6.46 (P2, the O(N) entry-cache scan +
`:read-set-entry` misfiled as `:shared`, which will mis-price rf2-2rtt6.34's heap axis),
rf2-2rtt6.47 (P2, the dead edge diff and the re-subscribe cliff), rf2-2rtt6.48 (P3, the DOM
residue gates cannot fail — `mount/release!` resets the runtime before the assertion, and
React-driven teardown is unwitnessed anywhere).

WHAT WAS MEASURED. Arm 2's decisive controlled-input row was :unchanged-model-rejection — the user types a character the model refuses, NOTHING re-renders, and the field still converges back to the model with the caret at the position before the refused character. Arm 2 (the dropped own-renderer) DEMONSTRATED this in real Chromium. Ported to the shipped React adapter it DOES NOT HOLD: the model refuses and nothing re-renders (both correct), but THE REFUSED CHARACTER STAYS ON SCREEN. This finding sharpens what that trade actually costs: the own-renderer owned end-of-event convergence off React's discrete-event path and could therefore restore a refused character; the React adapter does not get that for free, and on this evidence does not get it at all without further work. ALSO WORTH KEEPING: the same port found that :same-turn-echo is NOT free on React either — re-frame.core/dispatch drains on a macrotask by design, so the queued door cannot echo inside the discrete event; the SYNCHRONOUS door buys it. THE CONTROLLED-INPUT DEFECT IS NOT A REACT DEFECT — IT IS CROSS-ADAPTER INTERFERENCE (rf2-n3dxw investigation, PR #7330; recorded by acting mayor 2026-08-01). This is the most consequential finding of the night and it reaches beyond Hicasso.

REACT DOES NOT LOSE THE REFUSED CHARACTER. Read out of react-dom 19.2.0 in this repo with line numbers: createAndAccumulateChangeEvent records the target; batchedUpdates$1's finally flushes sync work then calls restoreStateOfTarget, which hands the committed props to updateInput, which assigns element.value whenever it differs — ALL BEFORE dispatchEvent RETURNS, with ZERO boundary body runs. Measured: field '12', caret [2 2]. React's restore machinery works.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS: UIx PICKS ITS INPUT IMPLEMENTATION FROM THE CLASSPATH. uix.compiler.aot/create-uix-input branches on uix.compiler.input/should-use-reagent-input?, which asks 'is reagent.impl.util/*non-reactive* PRESENT and false?'. THE FIVE SOURCES AND WHAT EACH IS GOOD FOR:
  - FREEHAND (implementation/freehand/) — the shipped interpreted substrate this programme is measured against. Its codec question is already settled (Hicasso consumes reagent-slim's), but its DESIGN decisions — the controlled-input door, caller split, declared properties, the roster of callback contracts it needed and Hicasso collapsed — are the map of problems any interpreted view layer must answer. When Hicasso hits a design fork, check what Freehand did and WHY before choosing.
  - RE-FRAME.UI (implementation/ui/) — the EXPERIMENTAL compiled-view substrate. It is the other pole: what a compiler can do that an interpreter cannot (and rf2-2rtt6.41 already used its analyzer's :rf.ui.compile/sub-in-loop refusal as proof a compiler cannot deliver Surface B). Mine it for what compilation bought that the runtime should approximate cheaply, and for the analysis passes whose LESSONS transfer even where their mechanism cannot.
  - REPLICANT — from a DATA-ORIENTED point of view specifically (Mike ruled 2026-07-31 it is 'just an example, not an objective'). Its relevant ideas: pure-data hiccup all the way down, lifecycle as data (mount/unmount hooks in attributes — the ::h/mounting/::h/unmounting presence design is already in this family), event handlers as data. The in-band [::h/prevent ...] head ruling is exactly this school: behaviour carried IN the data where = can see it, not beside it where it cannot.
  - REAGENT — the incumbent. Its default shouldComponentUpdate (value-equality bail-out on props) is DIRECT prior art for the HD-006 memo ruling on rf2-2rtt6.52 — the cascade Hicasso just hit is precisely what Reagent's default stops. Also: ratom deref-capture (the 943 B/read floor nothing beats), cursor/track granularity, and its known losses (the charter's 'Known losses coming from Reagent' section).
  - UIX — the React parent. Its per-hook useSyncExternalStore pattern is what Hicasso's one-hook-plus-index beats on fan-out; its input wrapper (three hooks per input) is what the element-path converge beats; its classpath input-selection defect (rf2-heqwo) is the cautionary tale about implicit selection. Mine it for React-19 integration technique — it is the closest thing to a reference for driving React from CLJS without a legacy adapter.

HOW TO USE THIS IN BRIEFS: when a bead involves a design decision, name which of the five have faced the same decision and what each chose, BEFORE proposing. A choice that contradicts all five needs an argument; a choice one of them already made and regretted needs the regret cited.

CONSIDERED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FILED (2026-08-11): the theoretical clock-hold leak in hm/hydrate!. Recorded so a future auditor does not rediscover it, file it, and re-litigate a decision already taken.

THE OBSERVATION, from the rf2-4mvd / rf2-w2e6 worker (PR #7883), which reported it explicitly as "not a bead": hm/hydrate! installs the page-wide virtual clock (around mounted.cljs:798) immediately before handle-for, inside a setTimeout callback with nothing between them. IF handle-for ever threw there, the clock hold would leak — and because it sits in a timer callback, the throw would not reach the promise, so nothing would surface it.

THAT IS STRUCTURALLY THE SAME SHAPE AS rf2-4mvd, which was real and is now fixed: mount! installed the clock before mint-frame! and a throw escaped before any handle existed, leaving the page-wide clock installed for the rest of the run.

WHY IT IS STILL NOT WORK:
- Both beads scope their repair to mount! in terms. Widening a bounded repair on a hunch is the exact anti-pattern this project keeps paying for.
- handle-for is map-building. It does not realistically throw, whereas mint-frame!'s :initial-events path raises :rf.error/initial-events-step-failed BY DESIGN — a deliberate, reachable throw. That asymmetry is the whole difference between the two sites: one had a documented escape, this one has a hypothetical.
- The stance rejects speculative hardening. Filing it would be gold-plating, and the worker said so itself rather than quietly widening its diff, which was the right call twice over.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER — and this is the useful part of the record. File it if any of these becomes true:
- handle-for gains a genuine failure mode (validation, a lookup that can miss, anything that raises).
- Anything else is inserted between install-clock! and handle-for in that callback, widening the window.
- A hydrate! path is observed leaving a clock installed in practice. A reproduced symptom outranks this reasoning immediately; do not argue a live symptom away with this note.

DO NOT treat this entry as authority that the site is CORRECT. It is authority that the site was LOOKED AT, by someone who had just fixed the sibling defect, and judged not worth work under the current stance. Those are different claims, and the second is the only one anybody verified.

title: docs+hic: chapter 20 teaches a defhost :slots option that does not exist, and ch09/ch10 call an absent h/as-element
description:
TWO TAUGHT-BUT-ABSENT SURFACES, both found by the rf2-hic-032 worker (PR #7874) and both left alone because docs/** was outside its fence.

1. `defhost`'s `:slots` OPTION DOES NOT EXIST. `codec/host-options` is `#{:callbacks :ssr}` and an unknown key REFUSES AT MINT. So chapter 20's taught Suspense-host recipe — `(h/defhost suspense react/Suspense {:slots #{:fallback}})` — cannot be written today; a reader copying it gets a mint-time refusal. The rf2-hic-032 lazy DOM row hosts Suspense NATIVELY instead, which is the shape that works and is the obvious candidate for the corrected recipe.

2. `h/as-element` DOES NOT EXIST, while chapter 09 calls it and `h/as-component` "the two halves of one seam" and chapter 10 prescribes it as a recovery. `impl/intent`'s docstring already records that FOUR DESIGN DOCS copied the spelling before anyone checked it resolved (rf2-2rtt6.120). PR #7874 shipped `h/as-component` — the outward half — so the seam now has one real half and one imagined one.

WHY BOTH MATTER MORE THAN A WORDING NIT: each is a COPYABLE RECIPE that fails at the first attempt. That is the ergonomics half of the pre-alpha stance — a guide that teaches a verb the compiler refuses is worse than a guide that omits it, because the reader spends their first minutes debugging our documentation.

SCOPE: correct the two recipes to what the code actually supports. Do NOT add `:slots` or mint `h/as-element` to make the prose true — that is a design decision nobody has taken, and the inward bridge was deliberately NOT built (h/defhost and [:>] already hand a native component a raw JS props object; making a marked component a first-class hiccup head would put native-tier knowledge in the codec and break clause 6). If the seam genuinely needs an inward half, that is a separate ruling.

Chapter 10's troubleshooting and chapter 20's Suspense recipe are also the two places that promised `n/memo` and `n/lazy` before they existed; those two verbs landed in #7874, so re-read those sections as a whole rather than patching one line.

SUPERSEDED 2026-08-11 (rf2-j689 ruling) — REAP-FIRST IS NO LONGER A REASON FOR ANYTHING. THE ORPHANED BRANCH IS SOLVED AT THE SERVER, NOT BY ORDERING.

WHAT THIS MEMORY USED TO SAY, and it was measured, not guessed: `gh pr merge --rebase --delete-branch` lands the merge but cannot delete a branch that a worktree still holds, and gh abandons the REMOTE deletion along with the local one — so roughly twenty merges in one session each left an orphaned origin branch. Reaping the worktree first made the flag work completely, four for four (#7842, #7843, #7845, #7848), because the worktree pins the branch and nothing else does. The mechanism was real and the measurement stands.

WHY IT IS SUPERSEDED ANYWAY. The ordering only ever worked when the worker had already reported done — the three merges in that same session whose workers had NOT reported were correctly merged without a reap and orphaned their branches 3/3. So reap-first solved the orphan for the easy half of the cases and left the hard half untouched, while placing the reap immediately beside a merge: the exact structural condition of the catalogrows-vkle violation, where I reaped mid-gate holding the worker's own message saying it was not done. An efficiency that re-creates the shape of the worst mistake in the session is not a bargain.

THE FIX THAT REPLACED IT: `delete_branch_on_merge` is now ENABLED on day8/re-frame2, so GitHub deletes the head branch server-side the moment a merge lands, and the server does not care what a worktree is holding. Merge with `gh pr merge --rebase` — NO `--delete-branch`. Zero orphans by construction, for reported and unreported workers alike, with nothing to remember afterwards.

SO THE ORDERING IS MOOT, WHICH IS STRONGER THAN "DISCOURAGED". There is no orphan left to avoid, so reap-before-merge buys nothing and is not a reason to reap, to hurry, or to sequence anything. The never-pair rule in mayor-hygiene.md stands VERBATIM: never pair a merge with a reap, never put the reap in the merge loop. Reaping is a separate deliberate hygiene step.

THE AUTHORISATION IS UNCHANGED AND NON-NEGOTIABLE — only the agent's own report that it has FINISHED authorises a reap. Not merge state, not PR state, not elapsed time, not mtime, not cleanliness. The test is still: can I quote the sentence where this agent says it is done? See reap-requires-a-finished-report-not-just-a-message, which cost a destroyed gate run to learn.

THE ONE REMAINING MANUAL DELETE: `git push origin --delete <branch>` is now ONLY the post-MERGED fallback for a remote ref that survives the merge — head-ref branch protection, or a cross-repo PR whose head lives in a fork the server will not touch. Verify MERGED, delete that ref, and nothing else. A surviving remote ref is never grounds to reap a worktree early.

Landed by rf2-j689 in .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md, docs/the-mayor-method/README.md and CLAUDE.md. mayor-hygiene.md deliberately unchanged.

title: mayor-method: reap-before-merge fixes the orphaned-branch trap but contradicts the never-pair rule
description:
A TENSION BETWEEN A RULE AND A PRACTICE I ADOPTED TONIGHT. Flagging rather than resolving, because I am the one running against the written rule and the resolution is a judgement call.

THE RULE (.claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md, the paragraph after the reaping rule): "**Never pair a merge with a reap in the same breath, and never put the reap in the merge loop.** The merge loop is the natural home for cleanup, because a merged PR is the moment a tree *looks* finished; that pull is exactly the failure... Reaping is a separate, deliberate step, run from a list of names for which you can point at the completion notification you received."

THE PRACTICE I ADOPTED, four times tonight and recorded as bd memory reap-before-merge-avoids-the-orphaned-branch: reap the worktree FIRST, then merge. Measured benefit — `gh pr merge --rebase --delete-branch` then deletes BOTH the local and the remote branch, cleanly, 4 for 4. Before I noticed the ordering, roughly twenty merges each left an orphaned origin branch needing a manual `git push origin --delete`. The worktree is what pins the branch; nothing else does.

WHY THIS IS A GENUINE TENSION AND NOT A LOOPHOLE. My sequence preserves the AUTHORISATION unchanged — I reap because the agent reported it finished, and I check that I can quote the sentence. But the rule forbids the PAIRING ITSELF, not merely the inference, and it does so for a reason I proved correct tonight: putting the reap next to the merge is exactly how the authorisation got corrupted. I reaped catalogrows-vkle mid-gate during a merge pass, holding its message reading "Holding for the spine — not done yet". So my new practice is efficient AND it re-creates the structural condition of my worst mistake this session.

THE TWO HONEST OPTIONS:
  (a) KEEP reap-then-merge, and make the rule's exception explicit: the reap may precede the merge PROVIDED the quotable-completion test is applied first, in its own step, with the sentence actually quoted. The method's newly landed clause supplies that test, so the guard exists; the change is to permit the ordering rather than forbid the adjacency.
  (b) KEEP the rule as written, accept the manual `git push origin --delete` after every merge, and record WHY the cheaper ordering is refused — because proximity to a merge is what erodes the discipline, and one manual command per merge is a small price for that.

MY RECOMMENDATION IS (a), but weakly, and I would not act on it without Mike. The argument for (a) is that the orphaned-branch cleanup is not free either: it is a step I forgot or skipped on several merges tonight before the pattern became visible, and every orphan is a name that a later cleanup might match. The argument for (b) is stronger than it looks: the rule was written after six proxies each killed a live gate run, and I have just demonstrated that I am not immune.

WHAT IS NOT IN QUESTION: the reaping authorisation itself. Only the agent's own report that it has FINISHED authorises a reap, and the quotable-sentence test stays whichever option wins.

SURFACE: .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md, and docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md if the two need to agree. Whichever way it goes, the merge-trap paragraph in bootstrap.md and README.md currently prescribes the manual `git push origin --delete` as the remedy — under (a) that paragraph would need to say the ordering is the root-cause fix and the manual delete is the fallback.
notes:
SESSION EVIDENCE, 2026-08-11 — the contradiction this bead records now has a clean natural experiment behind it, seven merges, no ambiguity.

REAPED FIRST, then merged (a quotable completion report in hand each time): #7842 ports-a15c, #7843 areduce-ka4d, #7845 xrayviews-jkdy, #7848 pairwire-n3mb. FOUR OF FOUR: `gh pr merge --rebase --delete-branch` returned exit 0 and the remote branch was gone.

MERGED WITHOUT REAPING (no completion report yet, so the worktree correctly stayed): #7839 native-hic030, #7844 wirescan-hic024, #7846 ctrl-hic016. THREE OF THREE: exit 1 with "cannot delete branch ... used by worktree at ...", the merge itself succeeding and reading MERGED, and the REMOTE branch left behind — gh abandons the remote deletion along with the local one. Two were cleaned by hand afterwards; the third is still orphaned pending its worker's report.

SO THE MECHANISM IS NOT IN DOUBT: a worktree pins its branch, and a pinned branch defeats --delete-branch on both sides.

THE PRECISE SHAPE OF THE CONFLICT, because it is narrower than "the rule is wrong". mayor-hygiene.md forbids pairing a merge with a reap, and its stated reason is that a merged PR is the moment a tree LOOKS finished — the rule exists to stop the merge event from AUTHORISING the reap. Every reap above was authorised by the agent's own completion report and keyed on identity (worktree HEAD == PR head), never by the merge. What I am violating is the rule's mechanical clause (do not pair them) while fully honouring its protective clause (do not infer doneness from a merge).

EVIDENCE THAT THE PROTECTION HELD, not just an assertion: three times this session I DECLINED to reap for want of a report — ctrl-hic016, wirescan-hic024, and native-hic030 — and accepted the orphaned branch instead. The cost of the rule as written is a branch-cleanup chore; the cost of misreading it would be a destroyed gate run, which is what it is really guarding.

THE RULING NEEDED FROM MIKE — one of:
(a) Amend mayor-hygiene.md to permit reap-immediately-before-merge WHEN a quotable completion report exists, keeping the ban on merge-authorised reaps. My recommendation: this is what the evidence supports, and it makes the authorising signal explicit rather than relying on the two steps being separated in time.
(b) Keep the ban as written and accept branch cleanup as a separate hygiene pass — defensible, since the orphaned branch is cheap and the rule stays maximally simple.

Not urgent, and nothing is blocked on it. Recorded so the decision rests on measurements rather than on my preference.
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-11, operator-overturnable):

RULING: Neither (a) nor (b). Take the dossier's appended Codex route: DECOUPLE remote-branch deletion from reaping. Enable GitHub's server-side head-branch deletion; merge WITHOUT --delete-branch; the never-pair rule stands verbatim; reaping stays report-authorised in the hygiene pass.

WHY: It dominates both framed options. (a) still orphans every merge whose worker has not reported (the experiment's own 3/3 arm) and makes merge-adjacent reaping the sanctioned norm — the exact structural condition of the catalogrows-vkle violation, guarded only by caller discipline broken once this same session. (b) keeps a per-merge manual delete demonstrably skipped ~20 times, and its orphan queue feeds the 2026-07-19 name-collision hazard. Server-side deletion yields zero orphans by construction, needs no quoted-sentence ritual in the merge path, and moves no reap anywhere. Verified live: gh 2.89.0 mergeRun abandons the remote delete when the local delete fails (pinned branch); day8/re-frame2 has delete_branch_on_merge: false; no stacked PRs in the last 500 merged; bd memory reap-before-merge-avoids-the-orphaned-branch currently teaches reap-first while mayor-hygiene.md bans the pairing — a live contradiction this ruling resolves by making the ordering MOOT.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (one docs worker, ~30 min, not hot-zone, parallel-safe):
1. Enable the setting: gh api -X PATCH repos/day8/re-frame2 -f delete_branch_on_merge=true (verify with --jq .delete_branch_on_merge).
2. .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md L28: merge command becomes `gh pr merge --rebase` (drop --delete-branch). Replace the clause "--delete-branch does not survive a worker worktree ... git push origin --delete <branch> afterwards is on you (see the hygiene loop)" with: the server deletes the head branch on merge; `git push origin --delete <branch>` is ONLY the post-MERGED fallback when a remote ref survives (branch protection / cross-repo PR). Keep "NEVER git push origin --delete before the merge succeeds" and all five green-criterion clauses untouched.
3. docs/the-mayor-method/README.md L188-201 (merge-trap paragraph): root-cause fix is server-side deletion + merge without --delete-branch; manual remote delete demotes to the post-MERGED fallback; the "leave local cleanup until the worker has REPORTED done" sentences stay word-for-word.
4. CLAUDE.md L93 (pull-after-merge bullet): update the quoted command string to `gh pr merge --rebase`; the rule's content is unchanged.
5. .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md: NO CHANGE to the never-pair paragraph or the reap rule. Hygiene keeps owning: reap on quoted report, delete merged LOCAL branches, git remote prune origin.
6. bd memory reap-before-merge-avoids-the-orphaned-branch: rewrite to record supersession — the trap mechanism is eliminated at the server layer, so reap-first ordering is moot; never-pair stands; reap only on a quotable completion report.
7. Corrected surface (per dossier, verified by grep): the prescription lives in README.md + mayor-merge.md + CLAUDE.md:93, NOT bootstrap.md — bootstrap.md needs no reap-rule change; the six-proxies history stands.
8. Verify with one live same-repo merge: exit 0, PR reads MERGED, remote head ref absent, the worker's worktree and local branch still intact until its quoted report authorises the guarded reap.

FENCES: The authorisation clause is UNTOUCHABLE — only the agent's own completion report ("can I quote the sentence where this agent says it is done?") authorises a reap; PR/merge state never authorises anything about a worktree; no reap without a quotable report. The never-pair paragraph survives verbatim. For the rare surviving remote ref, verify MERGED and delete the remote ref only — never reap early to clean a branch. No wrapper scripts, no CI gate, no ledger.

DISPATCHABLE.

`.claude/commands/*.md` AND `CLAUDE.md` ARE GATED — BY check_readme_links.py, NOT by check_doc_slugs.py (2026-08-11, rf2-j689 / PR #7887).

I HAVE BRIEFED THIS WRONG. Twice in one day I told a worker that `.claude/commands/*.md` "may have no automated gate at all" and to verify by hand. That is false, and the worker on rf2-j689 established the real mapping at source:

- `scripts/check_readme_links.py` OWNS repo-root markdown — its docstring names `CLAUDE.md` — and, per rf2-1yy75, also resolves markdown path references inside `.claude/commands/*.md`.
- `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` EXPLICITLY DOES NOT COVER `CLAUDE.md`. Its own notes warn that briefs have nominated it and received a GREEN EXIT VERIFYING NOTHING — the precise fail-open defect this project spends its days hunting, arriving through the brief rather than through the code.
- `docs/the-mayor-method/` IS inside the mkdocs site build (proved by `python -m mkdocs build --strict` producing `site/the-mayor-method/`), and `check_doc_slugs.py` enrols that tree explicitly via FENCED_DOC_LINK_TREES.

THE COVERAGE IS REAL BUT NARROW, and the worker proved the boundary rather than assuming it. Its FIRST negative control was INVALID and it said so instead of burying it: a bogus `scripts/*.sh` path planted in `mayor-merge.md` was NOT flagged, exit 0, because the resolver matches `.md` references only. Re-run with a `.md` path, it failed correctly and named the file and line. So the gate catches broken MARKDOWN references in those files and nothing else — it will not notice a wrong command string, a broken shell path, or prose that contradicts itself.

WHAT TO PUT IN A BRIEF FROM NOW ON, for a diff touching CLAUDE.md or .claude/commands/**:
  Run `python scripts/check_readme_links.py` — it owns repo-root markdown and resolves `.md` references inside `.claude/commands/*.md`. Do NOT nominate `check_doc_slugs.py` for `CLAUDE.md`; it does not cover it and exits green having verified nothing. Prove the gate reaches your file with a negative control that breaks a MARKDOWN reference — a broken script path will not be caught, and a control that fails to fail proves nothing.

THE WIDER RULE THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF: never state a surface's gate coverage in a brief from memory. Establish it, or tell the worker to establish it and report. A brief that names the wrong gate is worse than one that names none, because the worker then trusts a green that means nothing — and the mayor reads that green as evidence.

title: freehand: the per-boundary constant is ~3 us — six React hooks, two of them layout effects
description:
Profiled on rf2-dq20a's follow-on (PR #7139).

An ablation held the DOM, the 300 reactive reads, the lowering and the emitter constant and varied ONLY how many boundaries the reads were spread across. 300 boundaries -> 1 boundary moved a broad write from [3.9-4.5] ms to [3.0-3.2] ms: about 0.9 ms, ~3 us a boundary, ~25% of the deficit. Disjoint ranges, canonical-DOM parity gated.

That 3 us is what a Freehand boundary costs before it does any work: a React component fiber, the shell, a ViewCell, and SIX hooks per render — useContext, useRef, useCallback, useSyncExternalStore, and TWO useLayoutEffects, one of which carries no deps array and therefore runs on every committed render.

Ranked LAST of the three levers and by far the least tractable, because every one of those hooks is named in the shell's stated contract (shell.cljs, spec/006 §The Freehand atomic shell): one useSyncExternalStore per view so N moving targets settle in one pass; the reconcile effect publishing each render's bundle; the lifecycle effect owning connect/disconnect.

Filed so the number is on record, NOT as a recommendation to act. Taking it would mean weakening a contract, and the honest reading is that 25% is not what closes a 10x gap.

## Context
cell.cljc / shell.cljs. cell.cljc is held by PR #7133 as of 2026-07-27.
acceptance_criteria: No code change expected. Closed by a recorded decision that the contract stands, or by a design that removes a hook without weakening it.
close_reason:
Recorded decision: THE CONTRACT STANDS, not actioned. This is the close the bead asked for (no code change expected).

All six hooks are named normatively in spec/006 §The Freehand atomic shell and in shell.cljs — one useSyncExternalStore per view so N moving targets settle in one pass, the reconcile effect publishing each render's bundle, the lifecycle effect owning connect/disconnect. Removing any one weakens a stated guarantee.

And the arithmetic got weaker, not stronger. rf2-huhno's re-take on main at 7c41225b4b puts the broad write at 4.8 ms [4.6-4.9] against Reagent's ~0.8, so the deficit is ~4.0 ms and the ablation's 0.9 ms per-boundary constant is ~22% of it rather than the 25% originally quoted — assuming the constant is unchanged, which has NOT been re-measured (the ablation arm was not re-run). 22% does not close a 10x gap, and this is the smallest of the three levers while being the only one that costs a contract.

Recorded in bulk-rerender-where-the-time-goes.md §5 item 3 as an explicit dated decision rather than a ranking. PR #7152.

title: ci: lint.yml's curl retry hardening covers the installer script but NOT the release-zip download that actually fails
description:
FOUND BY THE FIX-WORKER DISPATCHED TO PR #7881, which was red on the clj-kondo job. The job HAD NOT FAILED A LINT — it never ran clj-kondo at all.

THE EVIDENCE, quoted from the job log (gh run view 31456796279 --job 93672540971 --log). The entire content of the "Install clj-kondo" step was:

  Downloading https://github.com/clj-kondo/clj-kondo/releases/download/v2026.04.15/clj-kondo-2026.04.15-linux-static-amd64.zip to /tmp
  ##[error]Process completed with exit code 35.

Exit 35 is curl's SSL-connect error, thrown 0.24 seconds after the step started. There is NO lint output anywhere in the log — no file, no line, no finding.

THE REAL GAP, and it is a near-miss rather than an absence. lint.yml ALREADY carries `--retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 3` on that step's FIRST curl, added by rf2-cq0s2j after an identical class of red. Those flags cover fetching the `install-clj-kondo` SCRIPT from raw.githubusercontent.com. They do NOT reach the SECOND download — the release-zip fetch that the fetched script performs itself — which is exactly where this one died. So the hardening was correct in intent and one hop short in reach.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN RE-RUNNING. A transient install failure presents as a RED LINT GATE on somebody's PR. That is the worst possible disguise: the natural response is to hunt the diff for a lint error that does not exist, and this instance consumed a whole fix-worker doing exactly that before it read the log. It will recur, it will land on a PR whose author has no reason to suspect the installer, and the cost each time is one worker plus a mayor tick.

REMEDY OPTIONS, for the worker to choose and justify — do not implement all of them:
  - Pre-fetch the release zip with the same `--retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 3` flags before invoking the installer, so both hops are covered by one policy.
  - Or pin the binary through a cached action, removing the second download entirely.
The first is the smaller change and matches the precedent rf2-cq0s2j set. The second removes the class rather than the instance. Argue the choice.

HOT ZONE: .github/workflows/lint.yml is a hot-zone file — SEQUENTIAL, never parallel. Confirm no other in-flight PR touches .github/workflows/** before dispatching this, and remember that a merge changing the workflow matrix invalidates the check sets of PRs behind it.

VERIFY BEFORE EDITING: read the current lint.yml install step at source. The flags and their placement are quoted from a worker's report and were accurate against the tree it read; confirm which curl carries them now.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7888 (branch worker/kondoinstall-rkl9). Remedy: fetch the pinned clj-kondo release archive directly under --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 3, dropping the install-clj-kondo script hop entirely (two network hops become one, and the remaining one is retried). NOTE FOR THE RECORD: the bead's first remedy option as worded CANNOT work — script/install-clj-kondo does 'rm -rf $filename' immediately before its own un-retried 'curl -o $filename -sL', so a pre-fetched archive is discarded unread; any remedy keeping the installer keeps the bug. Cached-action option rejected: reverses a documented decision, adds a third-party action to a required gate, and does not remove the download on cold-tool-cache ephemeral runners. SECOND FILE REQUIRED: scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py reads the kondo pin off this exact step and knew only the 'install-clj-kondo --version <pin>' shape — dropping the installer broke that required gate (--check exited 1) and misreported the install step as an unrun gate; pin now anchored on the release URL. Check-NAME set verified UNCHANGED by parsing both sides (jobs, names, ifs, needs, triggers, path filters, step names all identical), so PRs behind it need no recompute.

value:
scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py READS THE clj-kondo VERSION PIN OFF lint.yml's INSTALL STEP BY ITS LITERAL COMMAND SHAPE (2026-08-11, rf2-rkl9 / PR #7888).

WHY THIS BIT. The rf2-rkl9 worker replaced lint.yml's two-hop clj-kondo install with a direct fetch of the pinned release archive. That is a one-file change by every obvious reading — and it broke a REQUIRED gate in a second file. check_fast_pr_gap.py knew only the `install-clj-kondo --version <pin>` shape, so with the installer gone `--check` exited 1 with "the clj-kondo version pin could not be read". Separately, the new lines stopped matching SETUP_PATTERNS, which misreported the installer as an unrun CI gate and moved the undecided-check count from 96 to 97.

BOTH FIXES WENT AT THE PARSER, not at the workflow: the pin now anchors on `clj-kondo/releases/download/v<pin>/`, which is a TIGHTER anchor than the old one, and the self-test fixture moved to match.

THE GENERAL RULE: a workflow edit can break a checker that parses that workflow, and nothing in the diff shows it. `.github/workflows/**` is already hot-zone for CONFLICT reasons; this is a second, independent reason to treat it carefully — the blast radius reaches scripts that read it. Before editing a workflow step, grep `scripts/` for the literal command strings in that step.

THE OTHER HALF OF THAT BEAD, worth keeping because it refutes a plausible remedy at source. The obvious fix was "pre-fetch the release zip with the same retry flags, then let the installer use it". IT CANNOT WORK. `script/install-clj-kondo` does `rm -rf "$filename"` immediately before its own `curl -o "$filename" -sL "$download_url"`, so a pre-fetched copy is deleted unread. Its curl carries no `-f` and no retry and is not configurable. **Any remedy that keeps that installer keeps the bug** — which is why the fix had to perform the download itself. I had written the pre-fetch option into the bead as the preferred, smaller remedy; only reading the installer showed it was unimplementable.

ADJACENT AND NOT A DEFECT, so nobody re-files it: test.yml's Babashka setup has the same two-hop shape, but wraps the WHOLE install in a 3-attempt outer loop, so its archive download is already covered.

title: hic-063 — [OPERATOR-ACTIVATED] Pilot applications
description:
# hic-063 — [OPERATOR-ACTIVATED] Pilot applications

**Phase**: 6 · **Wave**: — (activates when the operator nominates pilots; blocks nothing) · **Est.**: L · **Depends**: hic-060, hic-061
**Surface**: pilot support work as it arises

## Goal
Two real pilot applications each migrate/ship at least one substantial screen without framework-author intervention — the adoption proof §13 requires.

## Deliverables (on activation)
Onboarding both pilots on the released artefact + docs only; a friction log (every question they had to ask a human is a docs or API defect — file each as a bead); the §13 evidence: install, develop, test, diagnose, production-build, upgrade unaided.

## Acceptance (on activation)
Both pilots shipping; the friction log dispositioned; no critical public API change across one release candidate.

## Worker notes
This bead cannot be autonomous — it needs the operator's nominations. Everything else in the set proceeds without it; record nominations here when made.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).
notes:
DELEGATED DOSSIER REVIEW (operator-directed, 2026-08-11): NOMINATION PREPARED — AWAITING MIKE'S WORD (one line at the sitting suffices).

Nomination is Mike's alone (this bead: activates only when the operator nominates; cannot be autonomous). Nothing below is a nomination — it is the prepared slate so his ratification costs one line, e.g. "Ratified: pilots as prepared on hic-063."

== PREPARED NOMINATION ==
- Pilot 1 — RealWorld/Conduit (examples/real-apps/realworld_http/, ~5,200 lines, 13 namespaces, Reagent adapter): migrate the home feed + article editor screens to Hicasso.
- Pilot 2 — LinearLite (examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/, one namespace, resources pillar): migrate the board screen and grow it (card detail view) during the pilot — exercises develop, not just migrate.
- Both run fresh-agent, separate-workspace, released-artefact + published-docs ONLY (no framework checkout, no session context, no human coaching); friction log from the first command, every human question filed as a docs/API defect bead.
- Stretch third (non-blocking, never a gate): an external re-frame v1 app from Mike's orbit via migration/from-re-frame-v1/ + codemod — the only zero-manufacture independent candidate, but double-migration confounds the friction log; post-DoD third pilot, not one of the two.

== CANDIDATES CONSIDERED (all seven; analysis preserved from the deleted dossier ai/decisions/rf2-hic-063.pilot-nominations.md) ==
1. RealWorld/Conduit (realworld_http) — ACCEPT as Pilot 1. Widest app in orbit, cross-framework comparison standard; substantial screens by any reading; integration suite pins auth/feed/editor/comments/routing/SSR/pagination so the pilot compares behaviour, not rendered HTML. Against: in-repo (independence rests on the fresh-agent protocol); RealWorld-class flows overlap the hic-025 witness slice — overlap named here, not hidden.
2. LinearLite (capabilities/resources/linearlite) — ACCEPT as Pilot 2. Genuinely different product shape (tool-app board vs content CRUD) and different capability pillar (resources/optimistic mutations vs managed HTTP) — the substance behind "independent"; small enough to onboard fast. Against: thin (one file); "substantial" arguable until the pilot grows it; same in-repo caveat.
3. RealWorld resources variant (realworld_resources) — REJECT. Same product as #1, fails "two independent pilot applications" in spirit; its re-frame.ui screens face hic-062 retirement, contaminating the friction log with donor-exit work.
4. Xray panel (tools/xray/) — REJECT. Structurally disqualified: framework-adjacent (maintained by the programme, so "without framework-author intervention" cannot hold); dev-only, never production-built/shipped/upgraded per the §13 evidence list; Phase 6 schedules framework-side work in the same tree; pilots must USE Xray to diagnose — subject and instrument would conflate.
5. TodoMVC (examples/core/todomvc) — REJECT. hic-086 already builds a Todo-class witness in the engineering line; proves nothing the witness doesn't; not substantial.
6. External re-frame v1 app — DEFER to stretch third. Only real-and-independent candidate with zero manufacturing; but v1->v2 then Reagent->Hicasso double migration confounds the friction log, largest scope, and no candidate codebase is named anywhere in-repo — only Mike knows if one exists.
7. Greenfield app by fresh agent — REJECT for this pair. Cleanest independence, but Phase 6 says "recruit... and MIGRATE at least one substantial screen"; a greenfield app migrates nothing — satisfies §13 "ship" but strains the Phase-6 exit text under an adversarial hic-064 reading; "real application" weakest for an app invented for the pilot.

== INDEPENDENCE / FRESH-READER PROTOCOL (hic-069) ==
Pre-alpha, single-operator, no external users: "real" and "independent" must be manufactured, and hic-069's fresh-reader protocol is the programme's instrument — a fresh agent (no session context) follows the docs only, in a workspace provably containing only the released artefact + published docs + a frozen copy of the seed app. Independence is then auditable rather than asserted. Qualification to record at nomination time (hic-064 audits §13 verbatim and trusts artifacts over claims): these are CONTROLLED INTERNAL PILOTS, not external adoption — Mike should explicitly rule that two distinct applications migrated by two independent fresh-agent runs satisfy the pre-alpha meaning of "independent"; without that ruling they are rehearsals for a later external pilot. Second qualification: the codemod is NOT evidence for this pair — its report-only scan found zero sites across the 14 source files (it targets Reagent [:>] foreign crossings; neither app has one); these pilots test the documented reg-view->defview authoring migration.

== TIMING ==
Prepared path: one-line rider at the P2 fork sitting (recommended Thu 2026-08-27; K7 boundary 2026-09-11), conditional on a go/narrow-go ruling. Nominating early costs one recorded line and blocks nothing; it gives hic-064's red row a named target and lets the docs line (hic-060 cookbook, hic-068 troubleshooting) aim at the named pilots' actual shapes while being written. Waiting until hic-060/061/068/069 land wastes no words if the fork dies, but the docs are then written aiming at nobody and the release decision risks arriving with pilots unnamed — the unbounded wait this bead's design ("record nominations here when made") exists to prevent. (Codex second-review concurred on the pair and would nominate now rather than at the sitting — either moment works; the ratification line is the same.) ONBOARDING is separately gated regardless: tracker deps hic-060/061/068/069 (behind hic-066 -> hic-065 -> CP2/3/4) must deliver a released, renamed, documented artefact first; no implementation effort before that chain lands.

== VOID CONDITION ==
If the sitting rules adapters-as-success, the Phase-6 release line and this bead die with it — no nomination owed; a nomination already made cost one recorded sentence. Until pilots ship + friction log dispositioned + one RC without critical public API change, hic-064 keeps its product-definition-of-done verdict red ("red, pilots named and waiting" once ratified); the hic-085 sitting outcomes co-hold that verdict.

== ON RATIFICATION (mayor's checklist) ==
1. Record Mike's word here — that recording is the activation event. 2. File prep beads dispatchable once hic-060/061/068/069 land: per-pilot workspace scaffolding, pilot briefs (docs-only rule stated), friction-log format. 3. Proof stays outcome-based: preserve each app's behavioural tests, migrate the named screen, one post-migration feature change, hot reload, diagnose one induced failure via the supported Xray path, advanced build, upgrade across the RC. No prep scaffolding or comparison programme before the docs/release chain is ready.
OPERATOR RULING (Mike, in session, 2026-08-11) — PILOTS RATIFIED AS PREPARED. Pilot 1 = RealWorld/Conduit (examples/real-apps/realworld_http/, feed + article editor). Pilot 2 = LinearLite (examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/, board + grown card-detail). Independence protocol binds: fresh agent, separate workspace, released artefact + public docs only; the fresh-reader test (hic-069) audits it. External-v1 app remains the non-blocking stretch third. The nomination gate on this bead is SATISFIED — the sitting agenda item is removed. Onboarding remains gated on the docs chain (hic-060/061/068/069). rf2-hic-064's two-pilots requirement is now nominated; it goes green only when both pilots SHIP.

title: mayor-method: the posture loop carries only half the stance, so every brief it shapes loses the restraining clauses
description:
FOUND BY THE HOURLY METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-08-11. The mayor's own drift check found drift in the mayor's own command files. Both files below are TRACKED, so the mayor cannot fix them — the mayor-side commit guard refused the staged edit, correctly, which is how this became a bead.

## SITE 1 — .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md (the real defect, P2)

That file is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the stance the mayor injects VERBATIM into every dispatch preamble. It has not been touched in two months, and it currently states the stance as only:

  "primary lenses ELEGANCE + CLARITY + CORRECTNESS + GOOD PRACTICE; no back-compat shims; perf/completeness serve the lenses"

THE OPERATOR'S ACTUAL STANDING STANCE IS ROUGHLY TWICE THAT, and every clause missing from it is a clause that RESTRAINS a worker:
  - POWER is a fifth lens, absent entirely.
  - NOT over-engineering and NOT gold-plating.
  - TRUST THE PROGRAMMER — the goal is high productivity for them and the AI they use, via a library with excellent ergonomics, a minimal API, excellent tools and low friction.
  - We do not need to litigate every last fine detail or drown in minutiae: reject over-engineering and nag-diagnostics AT TRIAGE, and CLOSE minutiae rather than actioning it.
  - An audit finding is a CLAIM, not automatically work; the mayor may reject stale, moot or over-engineered remedies.
  - A source-located REFUSAL is an acceptable and possibly correct deliverable.

WHY THE ASYMMETRY MATTERS, and it is the point of this bead. The five lenses tell a worker what good looks like. The clauses after them tell it WHEN TO STOP. A file carrying only the first half does not read as incomplete — it reads as a stance that wants more of everything, which is precisely the failure mode ("preserve everything just in case", gold-plating, nag-diagnostics) the second half exists to prevent. So the omission is not neutral; it biases every brief the loop shapes.

EVIDENCE THAT THE MISSING HALF IS LOAD-BEARING: in one session, three of six dispatches came back as reasoned REFUSALS (rf2-jkdy, rf2-5gka, rf2-u5b4) and each was worth more than the work would have been — a migration performed on a false premise costs far more than a bead. A worker briefed only on the five lenses has no licence to return one.

ALSO MISSING: the operator's standing request for ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English in CHAT replies — short sentences, active voice, one idea per sentence, technical names (bead ids, paths, commands) kept exact. He has asked repeatedly and the drift returns within about ten turns, so it belongs in the recurring loop rather than in a session's memory. It applies to CHAT ONLY; bead text, PR bodies and documents keep their own register.

WHAT TO WRITE. Restructure the file so the stance is a single quoted block that can be pasted verbatim, followed by a short paragraph explaining which half restrains and why a paraphrase drops it; then the voice rule; then the existing one-line orchestration-not-implementation reassertion, unchanged. Widen the drift-detection list at the end, which currently names only mayor-coding, missing worktree-boundary block, absent stance and --admin misuse: add "stance PARAPHRASED rather than pasted", "minutiae actioned instead of closed", and "an audit finding dispatched without its premise checked at source". Keep the front-matter description line as it is.
DO NOT let this grow into a second copy of bootstrap.md. It is one command file; the method document remains authoritative for the reasoning.

## SITE 2 — .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md, clause 1 (trivial, P4-sized, do it while there)

Clause 1 gives the rollup band as "~86". Measured 2026-08-11, PRs #7874 and #7875 both carried 91 checks. Refresh the figure to ~91 with that date and those two PR numbers as the evidence, and ADD one sentence recording that the band MOVES as the workflow matrix grows — it read ~86 earlier in the same programme — because that is exactly why the clause already tells the reader to measure rather than trust the constant. Change nothing else in that file; the rest was updated three hours ago and is current.

## WHAT IS NOT DRIFTING, verified in the same pass — do not touch these
mayor-dispatch.md (updated 4h ago, carries the current routing rule and matches bootstrap.md), mayor-hygiene.md (updated 9h ago, carries the six reap-proxies, the husk modes and the SendMessage liveness signal), mayor-cluster.md (2 months old but still matches dispatch-prompt-template.md Shape 4 exactly). The three method documents under docs/the-mayor-method/ are themselves current; the drift is one-way, from method into these command files.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7880: mayor-posture.md now declares its quoted stance the single source to paste verbatim, but mayor-dispatch.md:21 still asks only for a paraphrased pre-alpha stance; dispatch-prompt-template.md:14 points to CLAUDE.md + TESTING.md even though neither carries the stance, and its preamble remains generic; bootstrap.md:90 still gives ~86 checks while mayor-merge.md correctly records ~91. title: hic: advance-clock!'s own docstring and throw message still say mount! only, after hydrate! was documented as an equal source
description:
REPORTED OUT OF FENCE by the rf2-3gej worker (PR #7877). It corrected the three exhaustive mounted-facade rosters and the guide/ledger wording to say that BOTH hm/mount! and hm/hydrate! can produce a {:clock true} handle — verified at mounted.cljs:700 and :734-738, where shipped hydrate! honours the option and returns a handle advance-clock! accepts.

TWO CARRIERS WERE LEFT BEHIND, and they are the most authoritative ones because they sit ON the function itself:
  - implementation/hicasso/test_kit/.../mounted.cljs:791 — advance-clock!'s own DOCSTRING still names mount! only.
  - the same file, around L849 — its THROW MESSAGE still names mount! only.

WHY THE WORKER DID NOT FIX THEM, and it was right: implementation/hicasso/test_kit/** was fenced to the concurrent clockfix worker (rf2-4mvd / rf2-w2e6, the virtual-clock repair). It reported rather than crossing. That fence has since cleared, so this is now ordinary work.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A SHRUG. A docstring is what an author reads at the call site, and a throw message is what they read when it goes wrong — so these two are the LAST carriers a reader consults and the ones most likely to be believed. Leaving them behind inverts the repair: every surrounding document now says mount! or hydrate!, while the function itself still says mount!, and a reader who trusts the code over the docs concludes hydrate! is unsupported. That is the same defect species rf2-dsnq closed — a confident sentence outliving the behaviour it described.

SCOPE, and keep it there: two strings in one file. Say mount! OR hydrate!, matching the wording PR #7877 landed in the guide and the naming ledger rather than inventing a third phrasing — read that diff first. Do not change behaviour. Do not re-derive the docstring. Do not touch the render!/rerender! naming divergence, which is rf2-hic-065's.

VERIFY BEFORE EDITING: the line numbers above come from a worker's report and were accurate against the tree as it then stood, but the clockfix repair (rf2-4mvd / rf2-w2e6) has since landed in this same file and will have moved them. Find the docstring and the throw by their text, not by line number. If a later commit already corrected them, close as verified-duplicate citing it.
notes:

  mounted.cljs:341-345 invokes the first handed-over interval callback BEFORE arming the real setInterval. If that callback throws, control never reaches the re-arm and the interval SILENTLY DIES. Handing it to you would turn a two-line correction into an unbounded repair mid-flight, which is the exact anti-pattern the method records. rf2-w2e6 already owns it, so the owner exists in the tracker and nothing evaporates; it is SEQUENCED behind your PR.

title: hic-085 — [DORMANT until 2026-08-27] Record the sitting's outcomes
description:
# hic-085 — [DORMANT until 2026-08-27] Record the sitting's outcomes

**Phase**: governance · **Wave**: — (activates after the sitting; blocks nothing) · **Est.**: S · **Depends**: hic-003, hic-070
**Surface**: the K1 amendment record + K3 disposition record (effective-revision fields) + consequence beads

## Goal
The sitting ratifies, amends, or rejects the drafted instruments. Someone must record the outcome — the drafts must not stay "effective revision: blank" forever.

## Deliverables
- The K1 price-acceptance record completed with the sitting's ruling and effective revision (ratified as drafted / amended / rejected — each with its consequence).
- The K3 disposition likewise.
- Consequence beads filed for any amendment (e.g., a changed ceiling re-pins hic-071's gates).

## Acceptance
- No governance record carries a blank effective-revision field after this bead closes; consequences traced to filed beads.

## Worker notes
Activates on the operator's sitting notes. Until then, dormant.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).
notes:
DELEGATED DOSSIER REVIEW (operator-directed, 2026-08-11): RECORDER BRIEF UPDATED — SITTING OUTPUTS + TEMPLATE + STALE-AGENDA STRIKES.

Source: ai/decisions/rf2-hic-085.sitting-outcomes-record.md (written 2026-08-11 13:21 AUSEST; deleted after this note — full substance recorded here). Companion: the p2-fork-sitting dossier (rf2-2rtt6) covers HOW to decide the fork; this covers WHAT gets written down. Verified this pass: rf2-diaud CLOSED (PR #7704 merged, canonical figures live), rf2-sza0w CLOSED (ruled 2026-08-10), rf2-hr9s CLOSED (PR #7737, section 9 back-fill landed — record current).

== FRAME ==
Sitting 2026-08-27 (Fri 08-28 fallback; 90 min; evidence packet freezes Tue 2026-08-25; not yet booked). The sitting produces MIKE'S NOTES; three recorders turn them into durable record and none moves without them: hic-003 (closed) holds k1-price-acceptance.md drafted/audited/current with effective revision blank; hic-070 (open) holds k3-disposition.md — NOT drafted yet, blocked on the unrun hic-006 quiet-machine lane; hic-085 (this bead) activates on the notes, fills both effective-revision fields, logs the section 9 amendment-ledger rows, files consequence beads. Clock: K7 expires 2026-09-11 ~21:00 AUSEST (pinned to dogfood-mount commit b27df87f42), explicit-extension-only; missing or refused rows count FOR the null. No sitting, no notes; no notes, no records; and at K7 the null wins by default without the dignity of a ruling.

== THE SEVEN REQUIRED OUTPUTS (agenda narrowed 2026-08-08 to: outcome-changing K3/K4/K6 interpretation or waiver, and the fork; "record the ruling, the price acceptance, and each explicit waiver before the room closes") ==
1. FORK VERDICT — GO / ADAPTERS-AS-SUCCESS / NARROW-GO (a narrow-go names a scope that removes a measured failure mechanism). Recorded verbatim on rf2-2rtt6.1, cross-referenced on the epic. Consumed by the mayor (dispatch consequences) + this bead (fixes which disposition both records take — coherence table below).
2. K1 PRICE-ACCEPTANCE SIGNATURE OR REJECTION — the held draft on rf2-2rtt6.1 (2026-08-08 07:48), whose hold condition is ALREADY RELEASED: rf2-diaud closed, PR #7704 merged, canonical figures exist — 1.1718x [1.1263-1.2190] emvod, 1.1976x [1.1504-1.2468] w3yxd, floor-normalised — K1 MISSED, DECISIVELY. Its three items: mount-premium waiver at those figures; bulk gap accepted as missing evidence with the 1.5x kill NOT waived; K3 disposed per item 4. Consumed by this bead (fills section 6 effective revision + section 9 ledger row). Ratification never recolours the miss — "no evidence row may cite this record to colour K1 green."
3. THE FIRED SECTION 7.1 RECONSIDERATION ANSWERED — rf2-sza0w ruled the two-iterations conjunct MET on 2026-08-10, so K1 is TRIPPED and the record's first reopen condition FIRED. Per rf2-hr9s's back-fill the record now states, in terms, that whether the accepted price stands or changes on reconsideration is an open operator question, pending. The K1 signature must say which — one clause is enough. Consumed by this bead (discharges the fired reopen).
4. K3 DISPOSITION — pick one, per the held draft: (i) the per-read trip (1,278 vs 947 B/read, 2026-08-04 anchor tree) WAIVED for the fork, named benefit as in the K1 item, structural win vs the UIx parent (2,115 vs 2,980, ~29% under) reported beside, v0 heap-hardening still executing the staged path on its own merits; or (ii) K3 stays a LIVE TRIP and the fork proceeds only bounded away from it. The staged path does not arithmetically reach 947 and the .72 shell saving cannot count toward it — no shorthand. Consumed by hic-070 (drafts with the ruling in hand) + this bead (effective revision).
5. K4 SCOPE SENTENCE — one sentence, only if outcome-changing: the kill table names Chromium AND WebKit while HD-019 records Chromium-only IME evidence; state as a known-evidence limitation rather than inventing a WebKit programme. Coupling: the bounded manual IME session (rf2-hic-016, its own gate dossier) runs on Playwright's Firefox and WebKit builds — done before 08-27 it turns this sentence from "limitation" into cited evidence. Consumed by this bead (files the validation.md consequence bead if the sentence amends a record).
6. K6 INTERPRETATION — "does the 1.10x-UIx line count as 'meeting K1-K3'?" — reserved to Mike, in the room only if outcome-changing; otherwise write "not reached." Same consumer as K4.
7. ANY OTHER EXPLICIT WAIVER — each named AS a waiver; standing rule from the governance findings: "a waiver must be recorded as a waiver, not described as the charter already being satisfied."

== COHERENCE items 1 and 2 (the notes must say this explicitly, not leave it implied) ==
GO -> K1 record RATIFIED (as drafted or amended); effective revision filled, waivers minuted.
NARROW-GO -> RATIFIED with the named scope recorded beside it.
ADAPTERS-AS-SUCCESS -> REJECTED — "rejection at the sitting has the same effect as a lapse from the outset": the registered 1.10x gate and its consequences resume, and a consequence bead re-records validation.md's K1 consequence as the stop arm taken (sza0w's narrow-and-price formalization rested on the selection of Hicasso).

== STRUCK FROM THE AGENDA (verified stale — spend no room time) ==
- Production server arm: ruled Arm B in chat, recorded and closed on rf2-2rtt6.88 (2026-08-08); implementation only on a GO with SSR in delivery scope, against that bead's five start gates.
- Dogfood verdict: recorded 2026-08-08 09:36 — a clear, scoped preference; the fork prior's first condition is met; the sitting turns entirely on whether Mike accepts the measured prices.
- Diaud hold on the K1 signature: RELEASED (rf2-diaud closed, PR #7704 merged). The epic's "sign once rf2-diaud lands" is now simply "sign"; nothing stops signing BEFORE the sitting — the held draft's variant B records the price-acceptance condition met and leaves the fork to the room, shrinking the sitting to items 1 and 4-6.
- Two-iterations question: ruled MET 2026-08-10 (rf2-sza0w) — left the agenda as a question, returned as an obligation (item 3 above).
- Record staleness sza0w flagged: REPAIRED — rf2-hr9s back-filled the ruling into the K1 record (section 9 row, 2026-08-10, PR #7737). The record Mike would ratify is current.
- Bulk-rule and K7-text cleanup: rf2-vh0e3/rf2-vp0j7 (PR #7706) and rf2-94eb7 (PR #7628) closed; the async pre-freeze items from the 08-07 prep notes are done.
- Naming: CANNOT fold in — the hic-065 packet is blocked on six open beads (hic-026/038/048/050/051/052) and cannot exist by 08-27; its design is defaults-apply-then-one-override-sitting, later and non-blocking. Nothing naming-shaped is owed at this sitting.
- Budgets (hic-006): an OPTION, not an obligation — spec section 6 wants Phase-0 ratification against named reference hardware and the prep lane has not run; fold the ratification in only if it lands before 08-27, otherwise it stays asynchronous. Can later reopen the K1 record only if the representative witness changes as a result (section 7.1's last condition).

== THE ONE REAL TENSION ==
The record file and spec section 6 say the instrument is inoperative until ratified ("PROPOSED. Not operative. ... Nothing on this page is in force until he ratifies it"; section 6 makes the sitting a Phase-0 exit condition), while the bead-level notes on 003/070 make it the operative default now — and sza0w's ruling already leans on that default to hold "narrow-and-price, not stop." hic-064 accepts either citation, verbatim: "K1/K3 — accept either rf2-hic-085 recorded or the operative-default notes on 003/070; blank effective revisions without that citation = non-release" — so nothing is broken today. But every week the sitting slips, more governance weight rests on the weaker device, and after K7 the citation would be defaults standing in for a fork the clock decided. The sitting collapses the daylight.

== SEQUENCING (K3 file) ==
This bead formally depends on hic-070; k3-disposition.md does NOT exist yet (the hic-006 -> hic-070 lane has not run). That delays only the RECORDING, never the ruling — the room rules K3 from the packet numbers regardless; the ruling then sits on hic-070 and the record drafts with its effective revision already known. Evidence labelling: 1,278/947 and 2,115/2,980 are named PROTOTYPE-ANCHOR evidence, not measurements of the live package (implementation/hicasso has intentionally diverged; its freeze manifest says the benchmark tree is a historical measured artefact and package changes are governed by contract tests, not donor identity). Prefer completing the package baseline + K3 draft before the packet freeze; failing that, Mike can still rule the three-scoreboard policy and accept the named anchor — but hic-085 is not complete until the K3 file exists and its effective revision honestly identifies the evidence it governs.

== THE TEMPLATE (fill in during or straight after the room; sufficient to activate everything; strike what does not apply) ==

P2 SITTING OUTCOMES — Mike Thompson, decider — <date> AUSEST
Packet: frozen 2026-08-25 at SHA <...>; rows frozen open: <none | list>

1. K-ROW ITEMS (only where outcome-changing)
   K3: [ (i) WAIVED for the fork — named benefit: point-of-use reads per my verdict;
         structural win vs parent reported beside; v0 heap-hardening still runs
       | (ii) LIVE TRIP — fork bounded away from it; bound: <...> ]
   K4: [ one sentence: <...> | not outcome-changing ]
   K6: [ not reached | interpretation: <...> ]
   Other waivers: [ none | <each named as a waiver> ]

2. K1 PRICE ACCEPTANCE (the held draft on rf2-2rtt6.1)

   | SIGNED, AMENDED: <what changed, e.g. ceiling X in place of 1.25x>
   | REJECTED — the registered 1.10x gate and consequences resume ]

   [ STANDS as reconsidered | CHANGES: <...> ]

3. THE FORK: [ GO | ADAPTERS-AS-SUCCESS | NARROW-GO, scope: <the named scope and
   the measured failure mechanism it removes> ]
   If GO: graduation-prep dispatch [ starts now | after the minute ]

4. CONSEQUENCES AUTHORIZED: <none beyond standard | e.g. re-pin hic-071 to the
   amended ceiling; explicit K7 extension to <date>>

(end template) Post it as a comment on rf2-2rtt6.1 (or paste it in chat — the mayor records it verbatim there and cross-references the epic). That posting is the whole gate; rf2-hic-085 activates on it. Codex refinement on venue: post the signed outcome on ACTIVE rf2-hic-085 and cross-reference the active epic — do not make the closed, superseded rf2-2rtt6.1 standard the sole home of new authority.

== AFTER THE SITTING (division of labour) ==
Mike: the notes above, nothing else — no record edits, no bead surgery. Mayor: records the ruling verbatim on rf2-2rtt6.1 and the epic, then dispatches this bead. The hic-085 worker: fills the K1 record's section 6 effective revision, logs the section 9 amendment-ledger row, records the answer to the fired section 7.1 reopen; does the same for the K3 record once hic-070 has drafted it (if 070 has not landed, the ruling sits on that bead and the record drafts with its effective revision already known); files consequence beads for every amendment (a changed ceiling re-pins hic-071's enforcement gates; an adapters-as-success verdict re-records validation.md's K1 consequence; K4/K6 sentences land where their records live). Acceptance: no governance record carries a blank effective-revision field, and every consequence traces to a filed bead. hic-064: its product-definition-of-done row flips from citing the operative defaults to citing hic-085 recorded — once the sitting has ruled, the default citation is stale and hic-085 is the honest route. On a GO: rf2-0puue's v0 heap-hardening trigger fires now; rf2-eoppe's fires when graduation executes; Arm-B server work starts only against its five start gates with SSR in delivery scope.

== CODEX RECOMMENDATION (recorded in full from the dossier; advisory — the ruling is Mike's) ==
Make ONE atomic product disposition: ratify the K1 instrument as drafted, state the 1.25x price STANDS after the fired reconsideration, accept K3's governed-row miss without calling it a pass, and confirm the already-selected Hicasso direction — do NOT ask a second, independent GO/NARROW-GO/ADAPTERS-AS-SUCCESS verdict. decision-brief.md owns both selected direction and sitting agenda and says the sitting is "recording and dispositioning," not go/no-go; specification.md starts from Hicasso as selected and makes the still-open act precise (the proposed K1 ceiling becomes operative only on ratification; rejection restores the registered gate and its consequences). Two separately worded decisions create an avoidable incoherent state (fork says GO while the price instrument says REJECTED, or vice versa); if Mike rejects K1 instead, that single rejection IS the reversal — record the null consequence and retire the selected direction. Substantively: K1 remains a decisive miss (both intervals wholly below the proposed inclusive 1.25x ceiling under the record's frozen comparison rule) — ratification accepts a bounded capability price and does not recolour the 1.10x result. K3: record all three scoreboards exactly once — Reagent viability row MISSED (1,278 vs 947 B/read on the named prototype anchor), UIx-parent architecture row WON (2,115 vs 2,980 B/read, ~29% lower), dogfood preference separate evidence; accept the miss for the selected product, retain the same-witness 10% regression rule, reopen/re-pin on the package baseline or substrate decision. Calling the UIx win a K3 pass, inventing a paper path to 947, or counting a shell saving against a per-read slope would all be denominator substitution. The sitting note can be much smaller than the template — it needs only: (1) decider, date, frozen packet commit; (2) "K1: RATIFIED AS DRAFTED" (or the exact amendment/rejection) + "The fired 7.1 reconsideration is discharged; the 1.25x price STANDS after K1 was ruled TRIPPED. K1 remains MISSED, DECISIVELY."; (3) "K3: ACCEPTED AS A RECORDED MISS" + the three separately labelled scoreboards + the package-baseline/substrate reopen; (4) any genuinely new amendment or waiver written explicitly, otherwise "none". Do not pad with settled facts: Arm B is already ruled; K4 has no outcome-changing ruling to take today (the maintained Hicasso testbed exercises the synthetic composition sequence in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, while product/dispositions.md correctly leaves native Firefox/WebKit IME to the bounded manual witness — evidence status, not a waiver); K6 is not "dissolved" or newly interpreted (the selected product does not require a compiler; the decision brief already bans compiler/dual-mode rescue); K2, the red read-free shell, ordinary correctness and application coverage keep their existing owners and gates — mention one only if its rule actually changes. EP-0038's older "open P2 fork" language should get a short consequence update pointing to the atomic ruling, not force the same direction to be decided twice. Recording mechanics for this bead's worker: change each in-tree status from proposed/default to RATIFIED or REJECTED; record the frozen effective commit and back-fill its hash per the existing resource-demand-criteria.md precedent, calling a back-fill a back-fill rather than an amendment; a pure provenance back-fill earns NO consequence bead — a real textual amendment or a rejection with implementation consequences does. End state: one durable product truth in the normative documents, no reliance on tracker-only operative defaults, and no extra layer of governance ceremony.
