title: hic-019 F1 — h/boundary reads four props off a free-form map and refuses nothing
description:
# `h/boundary` reads four props off a free-form map and refuses nothing

**Filed by rf2-hic-019 (CHECKPOINT 1), protocol §3 Quality / §1 Completeness. Severity: correctness.**

## What is wrong

`h/boundary` is the kernel's error boundary. It consumes exactly four keys out of the
props map an author writes, and there is no roster, no shape check and no refusal
anywhere on the surface. Every other declaration surface in the package refuses an
unknown key at the declaration — `mint-host!` does it explicitly
(`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:1643-1653`, whose own
message says *"Reading past an option it does not know is how a policy comes to be
set and never applied"*), and `h/reg-state` does it at
`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/state.cljc:275-284`. `h/boundary`
is the one surface with no such guard, and it is the surface whose silent failure is
worst: an error boundary that reports nothing.

Two distinct silent failures, both from legal-looking declarations:

1. **A misspelled key is simply dropped.** `props-of`
   (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:124-128`) hands
   the whole `rfProps` map through unfiltered. `:on-error` is consulted at `:143`,
   `:reset-key` at `:163` and `:186`, `:fallback` at `:194`/`:212`, `:children` at
   `:194`/`:213`. `{:on-errors …}`, `{:resetKey …}`, `{:reset_key …}` or
   `{:fall-back …}` mint, cross `rfProps` intact, and are consulted by nothing. The
   author believes they have error reporting; they have none, and nothing says so.

2. **An `:on-error` of the wrong SHAPE is silently ignored.** `report!` at
   `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:143-149` is
   `(cond (vector? on-error) … (fn? on-error) … :else nil)`. So
   `{:on-error :app/boundary-failed}` — a bare intent keyword, which is exactly what
   somebody writes who has not noticed intents are vectors here — swallows every
   caught error and returns nil. So does a string, a map, or a symbol. The `:else nil`
   arm is the whole defect: it is the *silent-declaration trap* the `:slots`
   reserved-name repair (commit `5e5c21f5fc`) exists to delete, one surface over.

This is the same class as `{:slots #{:constructor}}`: legal-looking declaration that
mints, reads back correct, and can never take effect.

## Where

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:124-128` — `props-of`, no filter
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:143-149` — `report!`'s `:else nil`
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:186` — `:reset-key` consult
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:194` — `:fallback`/`:children` consult
- Comparators that DO refuse: `impl/codec.cljs:1643-1653`, `impl/state.cljc:275-284`

## What should change (sketch)

Two guards, both cheap and both at the place the author's stack still points at the
declaration:

1. A roster — `#{:on-error :reset-key :fallback :children}` — checked once per
   render in the boundary's own `render`, refusing an unknown key with the recovery
   naming the four. Reuse `impl.error/fail!` and either the existing
   `:rf.error/hicasso-host-unknown-option` id or a boundary-specific sibling; the
   catalogue checker (`npm run test:hicasso-invariants`) governs which.
2. `report!`'s `:else` arm refuses instead of returning nil, naming the value it was
   given and the two shapes that work (an intent vector, or a 1-arg fn).

Do NOT add a third `:on-error` shape; the two that exist are right. Do NOT convert
this into a render-time nag that fires per commit — one refusal at the offending
declaration, in the `fail!` house style.

## Done when

- `{:on-errors …}` on an `h/boundary` raises at the declaration naming the key and the roster.
- `{:on-error :app/thing}` raises naming the value and the two legal shapes.
- The four legal keys are unaffected; the existing boundary rows stay green.
- The refusal ids appear in `docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md` and Spec 009
  if a new id is minted, and `npm run test:hicasso-invariants` passes (the catalogue
  checker enforces the pairing, and it counted 67 live rows at filing time).

## Tests / checks that matter

- New rows in `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/boundary_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs`
  (or a sibling): one per silent failure above, each asserting the REFUSAL, not the absence of a report.
- `npx shadow-cljs compile node-test-hicasso && node out/node-test-hicasso.js` — 553 tests / 2508 assertions green at filing time (`main`@`89029ac46d`).
- `npm run test:hicasso-invariants`.

## What NOT to touch

- `report!`'s vector and fn arms, and the "called from `componentDidCatch` and from
  nowhere else" property.
- The unconditional `intent/with-frame` binding in `render` (`:209`) and its `nil`-frame rationale.
- Anything under `impl/codec.cljs`'s host-declaration arms — `cbguard-hic035` is live
  on `implementation/hicasso/src` and `test` for the sibling `:callbacks` repair.
  Coordinate: this bead's surface is `impl/boundary.cljs` only.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7921 (commit 1f8d9361e2). h/boundary now refuses a prop outside the closed roster #{:on-error :reset-key :fallback :children} and an :on-error that is neither an intent vector nor a function, both in the class's own render. New ids :rf.error/hicasso-boundary-unknown-prop and :rf.error/hicasso-boundary-bad-on-error, rowed in Spec 009 and complaints.md. The shape check is in render rather than in report! as the bead sketched: report! runs from componentDidCatch, so a refusal there would replace the application's real error and escape upward, destroying the error path it protects. Witnesses: boundary_intent_dom_cljs_test rows 8-9, each with its near-miss control. Browser lane 1277/7883 green; sabotage removed = 7 failures naming both ids, sabotage widened (:children dropped, nil :on-error refused) = 36 failures + 5 errors across 14 deftests.

THIS CHECKOUT IS CRLF, SO A MULTI-LINE PATCH ANCHOR SILENTLY MATCHES NOTHING (2026-08-11, rf2-czlb / rf2-3f11).

WHAT HAPPENED. A worker planting a sabotage edit found its first multi-line patch attempt matched nothing and reported no error — the edit simply did not apply. Cause: the working tree carries CRLF line endings, so any anchor spanning a newline fails to match a pattern written with LF. It found it only because it verified the restore by SHA-256 rather than by reading `git diff`.

TWO PRACTICES THAT FOLLOW, both cheap:
  - USE SINGLE-LINE ANCHORS when patching by string match. A pattern that crosses a line boundary is a coin flip on this checkout.
  - VERIFY EVERY RESTORE BY HASHING THE BYTES, never by `git diff`. This is already the standing rule for sabotage restores, and here is the reason it exists: a CRLF-flipping rewrite reads CLEAN in `git diff` while having changed every line, and the inverse — an edit that never applied — also reads clean. `git diff` cannot distinguish "unchanged" from "not attempted".

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND SABOTAGE. The plant-and-restore discipline is how this project proves a guard is exact rather than merely present. If the plant silently does not apply, the sabotage run comes back GREEN and the worker concludes the guard fired when nothing was ever broken — a false proof of a real guard, which is worse than no proof at all. The same failure would make a "restored" tree quietly different from the committed one.

Brief it as: "verify the restore by hashing the bytes, not by reading `git diff` — this checkout is CRLF, and both a failed patch and a line-ending rewrite read clean there."

title: mayor-method: two brief rules the mayor hand-repeats every dispatch are missing from the template
description:
FOUND BY THE HOURLY METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-08-11. The method files themselves have not drifted; the gap is what they DO NOT contain. Both rules below were hand-written into roughly a dozen dispatch briefs across this session, which is the evidence that they belong in the template rather than in the mayor's head.

Verified absent: `grep -c` for each returns 0 in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md and bootstrap.md.

RULE 1 — VERIFY A SABOTAGE RESTORE BY HASHING THE BYTES, NEVER BY READING `git diff`.

The plant-and-restore discipline is how this project proves a guard is EXACT rather than merely PRESENT, and three separate workers today caught something with a WIDENED-guard control that a removed-guard control could not — one showed a near-miss stop minting, another produced 36 failures across four namespaces. So the discipline is load-bearing, and its verification step is currently unwritten.

TWO WAYS `git diff` LIES HERE, and the template must name both:
  (a) A CRLF-flipping rewrite reads CLEAN while having changed every line.
  (b) **A patch that never applied ALSO reads clean.** THIS CHECKOUT IS CRLF, and a worker today found its first multi-line patch anchor silently matched nothing — no error, no edit. It caught that only because it hashed the bytes.
`git diff` cannot distinguish "unchanged" from "not attempted". That second half is the dangerous one: a plant that silently fails to apply makes the sabotage run come back GREEN, and the worker concludes the guard fired when nothing was ever broken — A FALSE PROOF OF A REAL GUARD, which is worse than no proof.

Also worth one clause: use SINGLE-LINE anchors when patching by string match on this checkout, because any pattern crossing a newline is a coin flip.

RULE 2 — WHEN A BEAD CORRECTS A STALE FACTUAL CLAIM, SWEEP EVERY CARRIER IN THE SAME PASS.

rf2-2l17 corrected the claim "the repair arrives a macrotask later" FOUR times across THREE PRs. Every individual repair was bounded and correct. Each was found by the NEXT merged-PR audit rather than by the repair before it. That is three round-trips of mayor, worker and CI for what one `git grep` would have closed.

The wording that fixes it: "BOUNDED REPAIR" should bound the CHANGE, not the SEARCH. `git grep` the exact wording over TRACKED files, read every hit, dispose of each in one PR, and list in the PR body what was changed and what was left correct.

TWO CAUTIONS THE TEMPLATE MUST CARRY WITH IT, or the sweep does damage:
  - THE PHRASE IS OFTEN CORRECT ELSEWHERE. invariants.md's timer-callback row says "one macrotask later" and is RIGHT, because a timer callback IS a macrotask. The grep also hits core/substrate/spine.cljs, the react_shared_suite and two bench tests. Reading every hit is the work; the grep is only the index.
  - THE BRIEF MUST NAME THE DISCRIMINATOR, or the worker cannot separate stale hits from correct ones. There it was WHO SCHEDULES THE DEFERRAL — our own collector (repaired to a microtask) versus React or a timer (still a macrotask).

SCOPE: docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, in or beside the existing gate-discipline block. Keep both rules SHORT — a clause each plus the one-line reason. Do NOT add a script, a checklist or a wrapper; both are brief-writing rules, not mechanisms. Do NOT restate them in bootstrap.md as well — one source, and the template is where a dispatch is written.

VERIFY BEFORE WRITING: re-run the greps. If a later commit added either rule, close as verified-duplicate saying so.

Re-verified absent first, as the bead required: grep -c still returned 0 in BOTH the template and bootstrap.md for hash / single-line anchor / sha256 / Get-FileHash / every carrier / stale claim / git diff. (The lone 'bounded repair' hit at bootstrap.md:231 is a different rule -- a fence widened mid-flight by a second finding.) Rule 2 is a new sibling subsection '### Briefing a correction -- sweep every carrier' carrying both mandated cautions (the phrase is usually right somewhere; the brief must name the discriminator). title: hic-019 F5 — ::h/mounting outside a presence tray's direct child is a silent no-op and leaks to the DOM
description:
# `::h/mounting` written anywhere but a tray's direct child is a silent no-op — and leaks to the DOM

**Filed by rf2-hic-019 (CHECKPOINT 1), protocol §3 Quality. Severity: quality (see the note — the ruling this surface already carries argues for `correctness`).**

## What is wrong

`with-phase` (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:178-231`)
is applied to exactly one thing: the tray's own frozen entries.
`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:344-348` maps it over
`(:order state)` and nothing else. So the override keys are stripped and merged only on
a `motion/presence` tray's **direct** children.

Written anywhere else — on a grandchild, on a node inside a child view's body, on any
element in a body with no tray above it at all — `::h/mounting` / `::h/unmounting` are
seen by nothing in `impl/presence.cljs`. A repo-wide search confirms `override-keys`
(`presence.cljs:105`) has no reader outside that file.

The prop then falls through to the ordinary codec walk, which has no arm for it.
`convert-entry` at `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:783-788`
skips only `:key` and the revision key, then takes `(name k)` — which drops the
namespace and yields the emitted slot `"mounting"` / `"unmounting"`. That name is not
reserved, not an event position, not the class or ref slot, so the override MAP is
converted and written onto the props object handed to React. It reaches the DOM.

Two consequences from one legal-looking declaration:

1. The animation the author declared never happens, and nothing says so.
2. A stray `mounting` / `unmounting` attribute lands on the element.

## The sentence that outlived the behaviour

`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:184-185`:

> The two override keys are always removed, so an override never reaches the DOM as an attribute.

That is true of `with-phase`, and it is the sentence a reader relies on for the whole
feature. Outside a tray's direct children the second clause is false.

## The ruling this contradicts

Twelve lines below that sentence, at
`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:207-215`, an override
written on a **view head** raises `:rf.error/hicasso-presence-override-on-a-view`,
with the rationale:

> the boundary cannot see inside an opaque view, and **silently dropping the map is the class of failure this whole ruling exists to delete**.

The identical silent drop survives one level down on a native node, un-refused. The
ruling closed one door of two. This is the same shape as `{:slots #{:constructor}}`
(commit `5e5c21f5fc`): a legal-looking declaration, a walk that never reaches it,
nothing thrown.

## Where

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:105` — `override-keys`, the roster, read only in this file
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:172-176` — `override-for`, the only consult
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:184-185` — the universal-sounding sentence
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:207-215` — the view-head refusal, and the ruling
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:344-348` — `with-phase` applied to `(:order state)` only
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:783-788` — the walk that emits it to React

## What should change (sketch)

Refuse an override key at the codec's own prop walk, where every element passes.

The cost is affordable and should be stated rather than assumed: `PropSlot`
(`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:328`) is a cached
per-prop-name record already carrying `reserved?`, `event?`, `ref?`, `class?`. An
`override?` field computed once at mint makes the runtime check one boolean field read
per prop — the same cost class as the `reserved?` skip that already sits in that walk.
No new map lookup, no per-render allocation.

On a hit, `fail!` naming the element, the key, and the recovery: *an override belongs
on a `motion/presence` tray's direct child; a node deeper than that is not one the tray
can see.* Reuse `:rf.error/hicasso-presence-override-on-a-view` or mint a sibling — the
complaint catalogue checker (`npm run test:hicasso-invariants`) governs which, and it
counted 67 live rows at filing time.

Then correct the `:184-185` sentence to say what it means: *within a tray's direct
children the two keys are always removed; anywhere else they are refused.*

Do NOT make the codec presence-aware in any other way, and do NOT add a runtime
warning that fires per commit — one refusal at the offending element.

## Done when

- `[:div {::h/mounting {:class "in"}} …]` nested below a tray's direct child, or with no tray above it, raises naming the element and the recovery.
- A tray's direct children are unaffected: `motion_presence_dom_cljs_test.cljs` and `presence_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs` stay green.
- No `mounting` / `unmounting` attribute can reach the DOM by any route.
- The `presence.cljs:184-185` sentence states its scope.
- `npm run test:hicasso-invariants` passes.

## Tests / checks that matter

- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/motion_presence_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, `presence_cljs_test.cljs`, `presence_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs`
- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/codec_cljs_test.cljs` — the prop-walk home for the new refusal
- `npx shadow-cljs compile node-test-hicasso && node out/node-test-hicasso.js` (553 tests / 2508 assertions green on `main`@`89029ac46d`)
- If the `PropSlot` field is added, confirm the bench compile gate is unaffected — PR #7907 is open on that gate.

## Severity note for the mayor

Filed `quality` because the supported placement behaves correctly. The ruling at
`presence.cljs:207-215` — *"silently dropping the map is the class of failure this
whole ruling exists to delete"* — is an argument for `correctness`, and the ledger's
severity table would then make it blocking. The mayor decides which row it takes.

## What NOT to touch

- `with-phase`'s merge semantics, the `without-structural` filter and its `:key`/`:ref` rationale (`presence.cljs:187-198`) — correct and load-bearing.
- The view-head refusal and its message.
- `:rf/phase` as the boundary-child channel.
- `impl/codec.cljs`'s host-declaration arms — `cbguard-hic035` is live on
  `implementation/hicasso/src` and `test`; this bead's codec surface is the generic
  prop walk (`convert-entry` / `PropSlot`), not the `:callbacks` / `:slots` arms.
  Sequence behind that worker.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7923. Both halves refused: the DOM leak (an internal marker reaching the page) and the silent no-op. New id :rf.error/hicasso-presence-override-out-of-reach, raised at convert-entry AND host-entry — one refusal at two prop doors, check-ref!'s shape. Matched as the EXACT keyword rather than on the canonical slot (revision-key's doctrine exception): a name-derived PropSlot field, as the bead sketched, cannot tell ::h/mounting from a plain :mounting, and claiming the slot would confiscate an attribute the author is entitled to write. Both key defs moved to impl/codec.cljs beside revision-key; presence reads them from there. The 184-185 sentence now states its scope. Sabotage both ways: guard removed = 9 failures + 1 error on the node lane and 2 more in the browser lane (one of them the leak measured: [mounting] matched 1 painted node); guard widened to the slot = 5 failures + 2 errors, all in the too-eager control. Gates captured: node 561/2570 exit 0, browser 1278/7892 exit 0, hicasso-invariants exit 0, keyword-drift exit 0, hicasso-release exit 0, fast-PR spine exit 0.

title: hic-019 F2 — n/defcomponent's declaration map is recorded, never validated, never consulted
description:
# `n/defcomponent`'s declaration map is recorded, never validated, and never consulted

**Filed by rf2-hic-019 (CHECKPOINT 1), protocol §3 Quality. Severity: correctness (validation half) + coverage (witness half).**

Two faults on one surface, and the second is the reason the first survived.

## Fault 1 — the declaration map has no roster, and `:server`'s value is never checked

`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc:755-772` takes any map as the
declaration and reads exactly one key:

    server (get decl :server :client-only)

Nothing checks the map's key set and nothing checks the value's membership. So all of
these mint clean, with no refusal anywhere:

- `{:ssr :render}` — the `defhost` spelling, on the sibling door. Silently `:client-only`.
- `{:sever :render}` — a typo. Silently `:client-only`.
- `{:server :rendr}` — a typo in the value. Stamped as the string `"rendr"` at
  `native.cljc:333`, and read back by `n/marker` as `"rendr"`.
- `{:server :render :fallback [...]}` — the extra key vanishes.

`mint-host!` refuses exactly this on the neighbouring door
(`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:1643-1653`, roster at
`:1246`), and its message is the ruling: *"Reading past an option it does not know is
how a policy comes to be set and never applied."* `h/reg-state` refuses it too
(`impl/state.cljc:275-284`). `n/defcomponent` is the one declaration door in the
package with neither a key roster nor a value roster.

## Fault 2 — nothing on any runtime path reads the field, and the witness asserts the recording

`native.cljc:333` stamps `#js {:name … :server (name server)}` onto the tier sentinel.
The only other sites that touch that field in `implementation/hicasso/src/` are
`native.cljc:439` (`n/lazy` hard-codes `"client-only"`) and `carry!` at
`native.cljc:372-373`, which copies the marker object wholesale without reading it.
There is no server walk, no SSR branch and no gate that consults it. A verified grep
over `implementation/hicasso/src/` and `implementation/hicasso/test/` finds every
remaining reader inside test files.

And the witnesses assert precisely the recording:

- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_fence_cljs_test.cljs:192-195` —
  *"and an explicit `{:server :render}` is recorded. Narrowing caught: ignoring the
  declaration map entirely, which would pass the default row above"* →
  `(is (= "render" (.-server (n/marker server-rendered))))`
- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_abi_cljs_test.cljs:320` — the same shape.

That row was written against the right risk and lands one step short of it: a
declaration that is recorded and then consulted by nothing satisfies it perfectly.
It is the same instrument fault as asserting an fx is present in the registrar when
the fx is never reached.

Meanwhile the namespace's own headline example is `{:server :render}`
(`native.cljc:13`) and `n/lazy`'s docstring at `native.cljc:429-432` argues about
whether a component's declared policy may be overridden — prose that reads as though
the field decides something on the server. Today it decides nothing.

## Where

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc:755-772` — `defcomponent`, `(get decl :server :client-only)`, no roster
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc:333` — the only write
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc:372-373` — `carry!` copies, does not read
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc:13`, `:429-432` — the prose that implies an effect
- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_fence_cljs_test.cljs:192-195` — the recording assertion
- Comparators that refuse: `impl/codec.cljs:1246`, `:1643-1653`; `impl/state.cljc:275-284`

## What should change (sketch)

**Fault 1 is unambiguous and small.** Give `defcomponent` the same two rosters
`mint-host!` has: an option-key roster (`#{:server}` today) and a value roster
(`#{:client-only :render}` — whatever the settled set is), both refused at the
declaration where the author's stack still points at it, via `impl.error/fail!`.

**Fault 2 needs a ruling before code.** Either
(a) the native tier's `:server` policy IS wired to a server path, in which case the
witness must assert the EFFECT (bytes emitted / withheld) rather than the marker; or
(b) it is deferred to Phase 3 by design, in which case say so where the declaration
is written — `native.cljc:13`'s headline example and `:429-432`'s prose currently
imply a live policy — and the witness row's wording changes from "is recorded" to
"is recorded; the policy is not yet consulted (Phase 3)". Recording the declaration
is a legitimate thing to test; presenting it as coverage of the policy is not.

**Scope note the mayor should weigh**: `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/adversarial-risks.md:18`
defers native-surface risks to Phase 3 ("Native-surface risks enter only when Phase 3
introduces that optional surface"), so this does NOT block the Phase 1 kernel exit.
It is filed here because the code has shipped and the trap shape is the one this
checkpoint was told to hunt.

## Done when

- `{:server :render}` and an absent declaration map are unaffected.
- Either the `:server` field has a runtime consumer with a witness asserting its effect, or the deferral is stated in `native.cljc` and in the witness row's own wording.
- New refusal ids (if any) are rowed in `docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md` and Spec 009; `npm run test:hicasso-invariants` passes.

- `npx shadow-cljs compile node-test-hicasso && node out/node-test-hicasso.js` (553 tests / 2508 assertions green on `main`@`89029ac46d`).
- `npm run test:hicasso-invariants`.

## What NOT to touch

- `n/lazy`'s hard-coded `"client-only"` (`native.cljc:439`) and its rationale — that is correct and witnessed.
- The two-languages fence, `n/$`, the ABI helpers, or `carry!`'s wholesale marker copy.
- The `:name` back-fill window in `n/lazy`.
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/` — `cbguard-hic035` is live there.

title: hic: the reincarnation correction is macrotask-deferred, but React law 3 requires correction before visible paint
description:
RECORDED BY THE rf2-hic-013 WORKER (PR #7749) as a separate open item, deliberately not ruled inside its own bead and deliberately not folded into the successor-write repair.

THE QUESTION. Design law React 3 requires a render/commit tear to be 'corrected before visible paint'. The correction this runtime actually performs is MACROTASK-DEFERRED, which carries no such ordering guarantee. Measured shape: commit-basis ties at 1 -> 1 after a reincarnation, so snapshot-of ties and React schedules no re-render; the repair arrives a macrotask later as snapshot 1 -> 2, producing exactly one notification.

SO THE CORRECTION HAPPENS, BUT ITS TIMING IS UNGUARANTEED relative to paint. Whether that satisfies React 3 is a spec-conformance judgement, not an implementation detail: either the law means something stricter than the runtime provides, or the law's wording is looser than its name suggests and should say so.

WHY IT IS NOT PART OF THE SUCCESSOR-WRITE FIX. That repair pins the incarnation into the closure at mint time and changes WHERE a delayed callback writes. This item is about WHEN the correction becomes visible. A worker fixing the first could quietly change the second by altering the deferral, and that would be a spec decision taken by accident.

WHAT TO DECIDE: whether React law 3's 'before visible paint' is (a) a hard ordering requirement the runtime currently violates, (b) satisfied by a macrotask correction in practice, or (c) worded more strongly than intended and owed an amendment. Read the law and its owner before ruling; the page's own rule is that where a row and its cited owner disagree, the owner governs and the row is the defect.

EVIDENCE: PR #7749's negative control NC5 removes the macrotask deferral and reds 6 assertions, so the deferral is load-bearing for current behaviour rather than incidental.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7749 (2026-08-10; completeness/correctness). Independent rerun confirms only eventual macrotask repair: snapshot and notification stay tied at successor seating, then move later. The non-browser commit-seam harness cannot prove React law 3 before-visible-paint ordering. Keep this exact owner open for an owner ruling or a paint-order witness and runtime correction; do not infer conformance from the green 30 ms eventual-repair test.
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-10, operator-overturnable): OPTION (a). React law 3 stands as written — a hard pre-paint guarantee — and the runtime is repaired. Option (b) (satisfied-in-practice) rejected: it redefines 'before paint' as 'eventually'. Option (c) (amend the law) rejected: its premise is disproved, see below.

WHY (a). The case for (c) rested on 'painted values are already correct because reads are address-directed'. Verified false as a claim about the SCREEN: address-direction makes a FRESH body run correct (invariants.md L112), but the same paragraph records that no re-render is scheduled — commit-basis ties 1->1, snapshot ties, and per the useSyncExternalStore contract React re-renders only on subscription notification + changed snapshot. The committed fiber and DOM therefore retain PREDECESSOR-rendered values until the deferred mark-dirty! fires; collector.cljs's own comment concedes it ('a boundary that painted before the disposal painted the retired computation, and this is the commit that corrects it'). So this tear IS value-visible — exactly the class the strict clause exists for. Same-id reincarnation is a realistic SPA lifecycle (account/tenant switch, route/root recycling, HMR, test remounts); briefly presenting the predecessor's data is not cosmetic when it is another account's, and it self-heals before ordinary inspection — the worst diagnostic shape. A setTimeout(0) task has no ordering guarantee ahead of the browser's next rendering opportunity (HTML event loop: rendering may update between tasks), so the correction can miss a paint. (c) also under-priced the donor contract: Spec 006 invariant 5 (L1316) independently requires the host to correct BEFORE PAINT with reincarnation named (L1320-1321), so amending the design law would desynchronize it from the normative spec or force amending both. The value-visible vs write-routing vocabulary from the (c) draft survives as ANALYSIS vocabulary (x874's dead-controls tear is the write-routing side, with its own repair) — it just does not enter the law, because this window is value-visible. No real-browser paint witness exists yet, so the stale paint is an inference, not a measurement — but it is the conservative, technically direct inference, and W1 below turns it into a measurement.

THE REPAIR (proportionate; keep it this small):
1. In impl/collector.cljs invalidate-cell!, move ONLY the deferred phase from js/setTimeout 0 to a true microtask (js/queueMicrotask; Promise.resolve().then as fallback where needed). Preserve the two-phase split and the deferral itself: NC5 (PR #7749) made the rewire IMMEDIATE (setTimeout -> synchronous) and red 6 assertions, proving in-stack rewiring is unsafe — it says nothing against microtask deferral, and the docstring's own rationale (this callback runs inside the registrar's replacement/registration hooks and frame teardown, 'none of them is a place to subscribe') is fully satisfied once the stack unwinds at the microtask checkpoint. HTML event-loop pre-paint argument: the microtask checkpoint drains ALL microtasks — including ones queued while draining, hence also React's own microtask-scheduled sync-lane flush for the useSyncExternalStore notification — before the update-the-rendering step of the SAME task, so rebuild + mark-dirty! + React render/commit all complete before the next visible paint. setTimeout gets no equivalent promise.
2. Do NOT touch arm-cell-reaper!'s setTimeout: its one-macrotask grace for keyed unmount/remount reuse is a deliberate, separate contract.
3. Behavioural delta to watch, not fear: the rewire window narrows from one macrotask to the current microtask checkpoint. A successor seated in a LATER task now finds the cell disposed and recovers via cold-read!'s probe on the next render; section 3 of reincarnation_cells_cljs_test (branch chosen by frame LIVENESS at fire time) keeps its meaning — only the fire time moves earlier. The existing suite seats the successor synchronously, so it stays inside the window.
4. COLD/STAGED-PATH CHECK before calling the repair complete: a boundary rendered under incarnation A but committed after B seats may hold NO cell whose disposal can schedule any repair, while commit-basis is documented to tie across the transition (invariants.md L112: the frame term restarts and neither other term is a frame fact) — leaving A-rendered committed content above a B-baselined cell, corrected only when B's value happens to change. If the supported public lifecycle can produce that interleaving (destroy+recreate between render and commit; concurrent rendering/transitions are the suspects), repair it by making ONLY the existing cold snapshot branch incarnation-sensitive — a stable frame token or a monotone incarnation stamp in the basis — so the committing acquisition's incarnation mismatch forces the one corrective re-render. If the public lifecycle CANNOT produce it, prove that with the same mounted witness and add NO machinery. Fence either way: no universal hook, no per-boundary dependency ledger — design laws State 5 and State 6 (the two-hook shell is a ceiling) govern the remedy's shape.
5. WITNESSES — exactly three, no more:
   W1: a real React DOM case keeping a boundary MOUNTED across a synchronous A->B same-id reincarnation, proving the FIRST browser render opportunity observes B — and RESTORING THE setTimeout MUST MAKE IT FAIL (the sabotage control Evidence law 3 requires; the green 30ms eventual-repair test cannot witness paint order, per the merged-PR audit note above).
   W2: the same case forced through the staged render->commit gap, OR a proof that the public root lifecycle excludes that gap (this discharges item 4).
   W3: the existing no-successor cleanup case, proving the new scheduling still disposes exactly — zero cells, references, boundaries and edges.
6. Re-run the do-nothing/read-free boundary shell controls (Economics law 1 standing controls) to confirm no standing-cost regression; NO new performance programme.
7. When the repair lands, update invariants.md's 'Two open items' row: the second item (this question) becomes settled-by-ruling with W1 as its witness; the first item stays until rf2-x874's fix lands.

SEQUENCING vs rf2-x874 — conceptually and mechanically separate, keep them so: x874 changes WHERE retained callbacks write (incarnation pinned into the closure at mint time; impl/frames.cljs surface); this bead changes WHEN the correction becomes visible (impl/collector.cljs scheduling). Neither blocks the other; no dependency edge added; this decision did not wait on x874 because the collector's notification timing is orthogonal to callback write routing. BUT both repairs touch the reincarnation test namespaces, so per the parallel-dispatch rules sequence the PRs (second rebases over the first) rather than editing the same suite concurrently, and run the combined reincarnation suite after BOTH land (this preserves the original recommendation's re-measure intent — there is no wording left to finalize, so the re-measure becomes the combined-suite run). NC6's prediction discipline carries over: a mismatch against the existing witnesses is evidence about the fix, not staleness of the control.

Priority stays P2 (the window is short and self-healing; x874's durable silent successor-write outranks it at P1). This bead is the repair carrier — the merged-PR audit already holds it open for 'a paint-order witness and runtime correction', which is exactly what this ruling orders.
MAYOR 2026-08-10 ~17:15 AUSEST — ONE STALE SENTENCE THIS RULING SETTLED IS STILL WRITTEN AS OPEN, IN A PARAGRAPH NOBODY OWNS.

FOUND BY THE rf2-hicdocs-cluster WORKER (PR #7774, merged as ce1859e83) and deliberately
NOT fixed by it, correctly: no audit note names the paragraph, and it sits outside the
three beads that PR carried. It reported it rather than widening its own scope, which is
the right call and the reason it is recorded here instead of being lost.

THE SITE. docs/design/hicasso/product/invariants.md, the paragraph beginning
"**Two windows a rendered assertion cannot see, and this is where the narrowing bites.**"
It still ends:

  "... which carries that freeze's open question with it: a correction deferred to a
   macrotask has no ordering guarantee against paint, and [React 3] requires one.
   Not settled here either."

THAT QUESTION IS SETTLED, by this bead. The ruling on rf2-2l17 chose option (a) — React
law 3 stands as written as a hard pre-paint guarantee and the RUNTIME was repaired rather
than the law qualified. The repair landed: the deferred phase now runs at the MICROTASK
CHECKPOINT, which the event loop drains in full (including microtasks queued while
draining, so React's own sync-lane flush joins it) before the same task's rendering
update; and the re-stamp is floored at one above the stamp it replaces, because a same-id
reincarnation restarts the frame term and the basis alone could land on the number the
cell already carried — measured in Chromium at epoch 3 -> 3.

So the trailing clause contradicts a settled ruling that is stated FOUR PARAGRAPHS ABOVE
IT on the same page, where the "Two open items" passage now reads as settled-by-ruling
with its witness named. A reader arriving at the later paragraph is told the question is
open by the same document that already told them it is closed.

WHY IT SURVIVED. Two separate PRs edited within a few lines of it and neither owned it:
9cda6c7f (rf2-vsgq) rewrote the subsection two lines below while landing the HMR rows, and
PR #7774 corrected the "Two open items" passage above. Each stayed inside its own slot,
which is the discipline working — but it means the sentence needs an owner named
explicitly or it will keep being edited around.

THE FIX IS ONE SENTENCE. Replace the trailing clause so it points at the settlement rather
than restating the question: the macrotask deferral it describes was the pre-repair
behaviour, the correction now runs at the microtask checkpoint, and the ordering guarantee
React 3 requires is met. Do NOT delete the clause outright — the paragraph's subject is
what a rendered assertion CANNOT see, and the two-phase repair is a real instance of that;
only its "not settled" verdict is stale.

Whoever takes this should verify the wording against the settled passage above rather than
against this note, and should check whether the same "not settled" phrasing survives
anywhere else on the page.

CROSS-NOTE from rf2-hic-014 (delegated dossier review, 2026-08-11, operator-overturnable): the Activity concurrent-reveal question — same law, different mechanism — is ruled OPTION (b): the bounded, gated, at-most-one-frame stale window for concurrently scheduled reveals is ratified through the react-compatibility lane, with design law React 3 untouched. That ruling does NOT overturn this bead's (a): here the runtime owned the deferral (its own collector retired the cell and scheduled setTimeout 0 in code we own) and was repaired; at hic-014 React owns the deferral (passive-effect re-subscribe after a bailed-out reveal), no cell was retired, and this bead's microtask repair is unreachable there. ONE PRINCIPLE, SEEN TWICE: we never defer a correction we schedule past paint; where React owns the deferral, the contract states the measured, gated ceiling. Residual still owned HERE: invariants.md L126 still ends "Not settled here either" about the question its own page settles at L114 — the hic-014 contract sweep is explicitly fenced off that sentence, so its cleanup remains this bead's.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7899 — REOPEN. invariants.md now corrects the later unresolved-questions paragraph, but the same page's present-tense What is witnessed paragraph still says the reaction rebuilds a macrotask later. The cited cells witness and current collector implementation establish the microtask checkpoint. Replace only that stale timing phrase with at the microtask checkpoint; keep the separate React-controlled deferral under rf2-hic-014.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7910 — REOPEN. PR #7910 correctly repairs invariants.md:110, but the same present-tense mechanism remains stale in implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/reincarnation_seams_cljs_test.cljs:39-40: "the repair arrives a macrotask later." Current invalidate-cell! uses js/queueMicrotask and the dedicated witness asserts the microtask checkpoint. BOUNDED REPAIR: change only that carrier to "at the microtask checkpoint" (or equivalent). Preserve genuinely historical "was deferred" prose and the separate timer/Activity macrotask statements; no behavior or witness change.
MAYOR — HELD ON A SURFACE COLLISION, 2026-08-11. Not neglected; sequenced.

The fourth carrier is implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/reincarnation_seams_cljs_test.cljs:39-40, and implementation/hicasso/test/** is held right now by the worker repairing rf2-czlb and rf2-3f11 (two P1 kernel defects from the Checkpoint 1 review). Two workers in one tree merge-conflict, so this waits for that PR to merge. It waits on a worktree, not on a decision.

FOUR CARRIERS, THREE PRs, ONE SENTENCE — and that is the finding worth more than the fix. The claim "the repair arrives a macrotask later" has now been corrected four separate times:
  1. invariants.md L126's "Not settled here either" (first residual, landed).
  2. invariants.md L110's present-tense "What is witnessed" paragraph — plus a second stale sentence in the same paragraph that the worker judged inseparable (PR #7910).
  3. This one, in a test docstring.
Each repair was bounded and correct. Each was found by the NEXT merged-PR audit rather than by the repair before it.

THE LESSON, for whoever takes this: WHEN CORRECTING A STALE CLAIM, SWEEP THE WHOLE TREE FOR THE PHRASE IN THE SAME PASS. `git grep` over tracked files for the exact wording, read every hit, and dispose of each in one PR. A one-carrier repair guarantees the audit finds carrier N+1, and the cost is three round-trips of mayor, worker and CI for what one grep would have closed.

TWO CAUTIONS ON THAT SWEEP, both established here:
  - The phrase is CORRECT in several places. invariants.md L150's "| A timer callback | ✗ | Same, one macrotask later |" is right, because a timer callback IS a macrotask. So is the separate React-controlled deferral under rf2-hic-014, where React owns the scheduling and this bead's microtask repair is unreachable. `git grep "macrotask later"` returns hits in core/substrate/spine.cljs, the react_shared_suite, and two arm1 bench tests — READ each before touching any. This is the third failure species the census records: text that matches the search and is not about the subject.
  - The discriminator is WHO SCHEDULES THE DEFERRAL. Where the runtime schedules it in its own collector, the ruling repaired the scheduling and "microtask checkpoint" is correct. Where React or a timer owns it, "macrotask" stands.

VERIFY AT SOURCE: invalidate-cell! defers via js/queueMicrotask, and the dedicated witness deftest is named for the microtask checkpoint. Confirm both before editing, and change only the timing phrase — no behaviour change, no witness change, and preserve genuinely historical "was deferred" prose.

THE MICROTASK/MACROTASK DISCRIMINATOR IS `invalidate-cell!` SPECIFICALLY, NOT "THE COLLECTOR" — my brief's rule was too broad (2026-08-11, rf2-2l17).

WHAT I BRIEFED. Chasing the fourth carrier of "the repair arrives a macrotask later", I told the worker the discriminator was WHO SCHEDULES THE DEFERRAL: "where the runtime schedules it in its own collector, the ruling repaired the scheduling and microtask is correct; where React or a timer owns it, macrotask stands."

WHY THAT IS WRONG, established at source by that worker: the ruling moved `invalidate-cell!` ONLY. Other deferrals in the SAME FILE are still real macrotasks and their prose is correct:
  - `collector.cljs:332` and `:972` describe `flush!`'s render-phase deferral, and `flush!` STILL USES `js/setTimeout … 0` at `:1017`.
  - `arm-cell-reaper!` at `:623`/`:627` is a genuine `setTimeout 0` — "one macrotask of grace" for a keyed reorder.
  - `arm1/runtime.cljs` is a separate FROZEN DONOR COPY that still calls `js/setTimeout … 0` at `:807`, so its prose at `:798` and both `ratom_activation_cljs_test` rows are accurate for the code they describe.
  - `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1091` makes the core escrow reaper's macrotask class NORMATIVE — "It MUST be a macrotask" — which is what the `spine.cljs` and `react_shared_suite.cljs` hits are describing.

Had the worker applied my rule mechanically it would have "corrected" at least seven accurate statements and broken a normative spec line.

THE CORRECT DISCRIMINATOR: does the sentence describe `invalidate-cell!`'s deferred repair? Then microtask. Anything else — `flush!`, the cell reaper, the escrow reaper, a timer callback, React's own passive-effect scheduling, or the frozen arm1 donor — is still a macrotask and its prose is right.

THE GENERAL LESSON, and it is the same one three times over now: A DISCRIMINATOR STATED AT THE LEVEL OF A COMPONENT ("the collector") IS ALMOST ALWAYS TOO BROAD; STATE IT AT THE LEVEL OF THE FUNCTION THE RULING ACTUALLY TOUCHED. The worker's line is the one to keep: "source is the authority."

WORTH RECORDING TOO: the sweep was 362 hits across 123 files, every one read, and exactly ONE needed changing. That ratio is why "read every hit" is the work and the grep is only the index — and it is the evidence that the sweep-in-one-pass rule pays for itself. NO FIFTH CARRIER EXISTS; that hunt is closed.

description:
# Kernel risk rows 2 and 8 have no re-runnable sabotage control — the checkpoint cannot discharge its own §2

**Filed by rf2-hic-019 (CHECKPOINT 1), protocol §2 Correctness. Severity: coverage.**

## What is wrong

`docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/adversarial-risks.md:41` (Gate construction):

> Include a sabotage mutation that makes each correctness gate red.

and rf2-hic-019's own protocol §2 requires the checkpoint to *"independently re-run
**one sabotage control per risk family** (all eight)"*. For two of the eight kernel
rows there is nothing to re-run.

### Row 2 — Process-global ownership

Its three witnesses:

- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/roots_frames_isolation_dom_cljs_test.cljs`
  — **no sabotage in any form.** A case-insensitive search of the whole file for
  `sabotag|mutation|negative.control|redden` returns nothing.
- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/public_root_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs`
  — same: nothing.
- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/roots_frames_shared_frame_dom_cljs_test.cljs:240-252`
  and `:332-335` — two prose notes. The first is genuinely valuable reasoning (it

title: hic-026 — CHECKPOINT 2: slice review + the ordinary-facade freeze record
description:
# hic-026 — CHECKPOINT 2: slice review + the ordinary-facade freeze record

**Phase**: 2 exit · **Wave**: D · **Est.**: M · **Depends**: hic-025, hic-019, hic-021, hic-022, hic-023, hic-024
**Surface**: read-only review + `docs/design/hicasso/product/facade-freeze.md` (new) + corrective bead files; a follow-up rename bead if the freeze changes names

## Goal
Independent review of the slice against the Phase 2 exit, then the act the evidence exists for: freeze the ordinary authoring facade.

## Review protocol
1. **Completeness**: the flow covers routing, keyed list, edit, async mutation, controlled fields, errors, reset; testing facade L0–L3, evidence projection, four Xray views, complaint catalogue, lint, erasure proof all landed (hic-020…024).
2. **Correctness**: clean-checkout run of the slice suite; verify no artificial boundaries or internal imports by reading the app code; re-run one sabotage per testing tier.
3. **Quality**: the app reads like consumer code (would a re-frame2 user recognize it?); the authoring report's rough edges are dispositioned — each becomes a facade decision or a corrective bead, none silently dropped.

## Output
- `facade-freeze.md`: the frozen ordinary-surface **laws and semantics** — the reviewer reports the evidence; the freeze itself applies the **pre-resolved spec dispositions** (spec §4 + `codex/ergonomics-api.md`), so this is deterministic application, not reviewer governance. **Names are not frozen or changed here**: every naming finding is appended to the naming ledger for hic-065; prototype names remain in use everywhere.
- Checkpoint report + corrective findings filed as **real `bd` issues**, ids in the hic-073 correction ledger. The line continues regardless.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).
notes:
CLOSURE RULE (rf2-hic-073) — this paragraph is part of this checkpoint's protocol.

Every miss this protocol finds becomes a real bd issue — run `bd create`, one per miss, with the surface fence and acceptance in its description — and is appended as a row in docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md carrying its severity (correctness / coverage / quality), the protocol section that produced it, and its status. A row does NOT close when the corrective PR merges. It closes only when the protocol section that produced the finding is re-run against the landed fix and the result — date, section, commit, what was run, the outcome — is written into the row's Closure evidence cell. Trivial re-runs (re-read one fixture, re-run one sabotage control, re-count one roster) happen inside the corrective PR, which quotes the result. Non-trivial ones (clean-checkout suite, fresh reviewer, physical reference profile, a whole sabotage family) get a small closure bead depending on the corrective bead, named in the row. Rows are never deleted: a finding that proves mistaken closes as "withdrawn — <reason>", so the audit can see it was considered. rf2-hic-064 gates on this ledger — zero unresolved correctness or coverage rows, where unresolved means any status other than `closed`, or the audit returns a non-release verdict. A `resolved` row (fix merged, re-run outstanding) therefore fails the gate exactly as an `open` one does.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #7726 (protocol sync): PR #7726 supersedes any earlier sentence saying a trivial closure re-run happens inside the corrective PR. Corrective PRs never edit correction-ledger.md. After the fix is merged, the ledger keeper (the filing checkpoint while it runs, the mayor afterwards) verifies the remote merge, pulls main, independently re-runs a trivial producing section against the landed commit, and writes closed plus evidence in a ledger-only commit. Non-trivial re-runs retain an independent closure bead. All filing, severity, unresolved-row, withdrawal, and final-gate rules remain unchanged.
LEDGER MECHANICS: write naming findings to a per-checkpoint fragment file (product/naming-findings-cp2.md), not into naming-ledger.md; rf2-hic-065 consolidates fragments.
HEADLINE DATUM FOR THIS CHECKPOINT, from two independent ordinary applications built on the public API only (rf2-hic-025 the vertical slice, PR #7920; rf2-hic-086 the Todo class, PR #7926).

THE TODO CLASS REACHED A STRICT SUBSET OF THE SLICE'S NAMES. Between the two apps, NINE names carried everything, and NEITHER app reached: `hfn`, `hframe`, `portal`, `as-element`, `as-component`, `defhost`, or `motion/presence`.

That is the ordinary-facade freeze evidence this bead exists to weigh, and it arrived from two directions rather than one. The slice was chosen to be broad — two routes, a keyed list, a controlled editor, an async mutation the server refuses, an error region, a reset, runtime locale and theme. The Todo class is the canonical ordinary flow. Their union is nine names and three keywords.

READ BOTH AUTHORING REPORTS BEFORE RULING: docs/design/hicasso/product/authoring-report-slice.md and authoring-report-todo.md. They are tracked and indexed. The Todo report explicitly confirms slice findings 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 and 8 from a second angle, BOUNDS finding 5 (::h/revision is for a field that OUTLIVES its reset; Escape unmounts, so the Todo class needs no counter), and never met finding 4 or the boundary row.

ONE FINDING GOT WIDER, and it matters for the facade question: slice finding 6 said two clicks on one page settle differently and nothing says which. The Todo app shows this is NOT about async — an app with NO server, NO async mutation and NO reg-fx still needs the router drain, for a plain filter link. L3 has settle! and dispatch-and-settle! and nothing for "work is enqueued in the router; let it land."

THREE DOOR-LEVEL GAPS the reports name, all of the same species — the door does not document what the door accepts:
  - The KEY-MAP form (`:on-key-down {"Enter" [...] "Escape" [...]}`) is why the Todo views contain no callback at all, yet re-frame.hicasso's docstrings never mention that a map at an event position means anything. Only impl.intent states the four shapes — in the namespace the door tells authors not to open.
  - `reg-state` mints a sub AND an event under one keyword, so the concern belongs to neither the subs nor the events namespace, and nothing on the door says where it goes.
  - An event handler is on neither side of reg-state's pair: a commit handler reads `(get-in db [:ui ...])` by hand because the door exports no name for the `:ui` root, and clears via `:fx [[:dispatch [::h/clear ...]]]` because there is no db-level clear.

DO NOT treat this note as the ruling. It is the evidence, gathered before the checkpoint runs.

title: hicasso: six runtime error messages instruct the author to write `h/fn`, which is not a var
description:
Found by rf2-5l7l while sweeping the `h/fn` corpus. rf2-5l7l fixed the three
docstring CODE EXAMPLES; this is the same defect on a HIGHER-traffic surface,
left behind because both of its collateral files were fenced at the time.

There is no var `re-frame.hicasso/fn` — the macro is `hfn`, so the spelling
that compiles under the taught `[re-frame.hicasso :as h]` alias is `h/hfn`.
Six RUNTIME ERROR MESSAGES still instruct the author to write `h/fn`. These
fire at the exact moment the author needs to write one, so they are read more
often than any docstring:

  impl/intent.cljs:741   event-arg! — "Write an h/fn instead: the one form
                         receives every argument the invoker passed, in order."
  impl/intent.cljs:933   refuse-malformed-navigate! — the closed veto roster:
                         "nil, [::h/prevent [...]], h/fn, or a plain function"
  impl/intent.cljs:1162  refuse-dispatching-carrier! — "or write an h/fn that
                         does the <contract> work"
  impl/codec.cljs:2706   refuse-unclaimed-host-callback! — "was handed an
                         h/fn at <k>, which no CALLBACK contract claims"
  impl/codec.cljs:2712   same message, other branch — "An h/fn asks the
                         POSITION for a contract"
  impl/route_link.cljs:165  the same veto roster as intent.cljs:933

A CONSUMER FOLLOWING THE ADVICE gets rf2-5l7l's failure verbatim: "Use of
undeclared Var re-frame.hicasso/fn", plus one warning per argument naming
their OWN symbol; the build completes and the page throws at render.

WHY rf2-5l7l LEFT IT. Two collateral surfaces, both fenced to other work at
the time:

1. implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/intent_cljs_test.cljs:694
   asserts `(is (re-find #"h/fn" (ex-message e)) "and the spelling that
   works")`. The regex does NOT match "h/hfn", so changing the message reds
   this test — and the assertion's own rationale ("the spelling that works")
   is FALSE as it stands. The whole tree was fenced to a live worker.
2. spec/009-Instrumentation.md rows 2553 and 2554 repeat "write an `h/fn`"
   in the recovery column and carry the recovery ids
   `:write-an-h-fn-at-a-value-first-position` and
   `:declare-the-position-event-or-write-an-h-fn`. spec/** is hot zone and
   spec/009 was held by PR #7923.

SCOPE WHEN THIS RUNS. Message text + the test assertion + the spec/009 rows,
in one PR (they are one change; splitting them reds the spine). The RECOVERY
IDS are a separate question — they are hyphenated slugs rather than var
spellings, so leaving them is defensible; decide explicitly and say which.

NOT A RENAME. This changes no name. `h/fn` is naming-ledger row 1, reserved
to Mike's sitting and swept by rf2-hic-066; every PROSE mention of `h/fn`
(including the ledger, the design records and the docstrings that name the
naming gap outright) stays exactly as written. This only makes the
INSTRUCTIONS resolve under the name that exists today.
notes:
MAYOR — ROUTED, NOT DISPATCHED, 2026-08-11. Do not put a worker on this bead while rf2-5l7l is in flight.

This is the SAME DEFECT as rf2-5l7l — `h/fn` is not a var — in a different carrier class. rf2-5l7l covers the public door's docstrings (29 hits across five files in implementation/hicasso/src); this bead covers six RUNTIME ERROR MESSAGES. Its worker `hfn-5l7l` is live and was briefed to `git grep h/fn` over TRACKED files, read every hit, and dispose of all of them in ONE PR, on the standing rule that a bounded repair bounds the CHANGE, not the SEARCH.

Runtime error strings are tracked files, so these six should already be in that sweep. I have messaged the worker to confirm explicitly in its PR body, and to tell me if they are NOT in its hit list — because that would mean the grep missed a spelling and the sweep is incomplete in a way worth knowing.

WHY ROUTING RATHER THAN DISPATCHING. Two workers on one grep is how two diffs meet in one file and one silently reverts the other. It is also how a stale claim gets corrected four times across three PRs, which happened to rf2-2l17 today and cost three round-trips of mayor, worker and CI.

THIS HALF IS ARGUABLY THE SHARPER ONE, and whoever finishes it should treat it that way: a docstring is consulted optionally, but a REFUSAL MESSAGE IS READ BY SOMEONE WHO IS ALREADY STUCK. A wrong instruction there costs more than a wrong reference.

CAUTION THAT APPLIES EQUALLY HERE: read every hit before changing it. Some occurrences may be prose ABOUT a rejected name, a negative control, or the frozen arm1 donor copy. A worker today ran a 362-hit sweep, changed exactly ONE, and correctly left seven accurate statements alone including a normative spec line. Source is the authority.

AND THE SPELLING IS NOT SETTLED FROM HERE: a grep for a defmacro named `hfn`, `handler` or `event` in the public door returns nothing. rf2-hic-065's row-1 ruling settled the callback macro as `h/event` and rejected `h/handler`, but that ruling also says renames go through rf2-hic-066's single sweep — so correcting a MESSAGE to the ruled name is fine; renaming a var is not.

CLOSE THIS BEAD against rf2-5l7l's PR once the worker confirms the six are covered. If it reports they are NOT, this bead becomes a real dispatch and the sweep's completeness needs re-examining.

`re-frame.hicasso/as-element`'s docstring (implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc, the `:render-row` example) and `re-frame.hicasso.impl.intent`'s docstring (~line 630) both write the one callback form as:

    (h/fn [i] (h/as-element [:li.row …]))

`h/fn` is not a var. The macro is `hfn`, so the spelling that compiles under the taught alias is `h/hfn`. `h/defview`'s own docstring already acknowledges the gap ("The authoring surface those spellings were chosen FOR is `h/fn` and `h/frame`; closing that gap is a naming decision and belongs to the bead that owns naming") — so this bead is NOT about the naming decision. It is about the published examples being written in a spelling that does not exist yet.

WHAT A CONSUMER GETS. Copying it produces a WARNING, not an error:

    Use of undeclared Var re-frame.hicasso/fn
    Use of undeclared Var <your-ns>/e          (one per argument, pointing at the ARGUMENT)

The build completes, and the page throws at render. The second and third lines are the loud ones and they name the author's own argument symbol rather than the missing macro.

REMEDY (candidate, for whoever owns it): either rewrite the docstring examples to `h/hfn` today, or land the `h/fn` rename and leave them. Doing neither is the only wrong answer — the two docstrings are the most-copied statement of the one callback form.

Grep for the corpus: `git grep -n "(h/fn "` — prose mentions of `h/fn` are correct and should not be touched; only the CODE EXAMPLES are wrong.

I STATED A NAMING RECOMMENDATION AS A SETTLED RULING, TWICE IN ONE BRIEF, AND IT WOULD HAVE RE-COMMITTED THE DEFECT (2026-08-11, rf2-5l7l).

WHAT I WROTE. Briefing the `h/fn` sweep, I told the worker — twice — that "rf2-hic-065's row-1 ruling settled the callback macro as `h/event` and rejected `h/handler`", and instructed it to correct docstrings to the ruled name.

WHAT SOURCE SAYS. In naming-ledger.md row 1, `h/event` sits in the RECOMMENDATION column with STATUS = open, and the cell reads "Both candidates stand for the sitting (rf2-84w6)." rf2-hic-065's own note says "ALL NAMING ROWS RESERVED TO MIKE'S SITTING" and calls the appended recommendation "advisory, adopted nowhere as a naming ruling."

WHY IT MATTERED RATHER THAN BEING A PEDANTIC CORRECTION: `h/event` DOES NOT RESOLVE EITHER. Had the worker followed my brief, it would have replaced a name that does not exist with ANOTHER name that does not exist — re-committing the exact defect the bead was filed to remove, in the same files, under the authority of a ruling that was never made.

THE ACTUAL NAME IS `hfn`, so `h/hfn`. The worker established it three ways rather than assuming: the `(defmacro hfn ...)` and its self-refer in hicasso.cljc; `hfn`'s own docstring explaining WHY ("spelled `hfn` here because `h/fn` is qualified in the product and a bare `fn` would shadow cljs.core/fn on a :refer"); and a PASSING WITNESS in public_door_macros_cljs_test.cljs that writes `(h/hfn [e] ...)` under "Witness A — h/hfn, the one callback form".

THE RULE: A RECOMMENDATION IN A LEDGER IS NOT A RULING. Before citing one in a brief, read the STATUS column, not the recommendation text. In this repo a ruled row says so explicitly and names the operator and date; an advisory row says "open" and names the sitting it is reserved to. The two look alike in a summary and are opposite in force.

AND THE WIDER FORM, which I have now broken in three variants across one session: DO NOT ASSERT FROM MEMORY WHAT A RULING, A GATE OR A METHOD FILE CONTAINS. Grep it, read the status field, and quote it. The earlier variants were naming the wrong gate for a surface, and asserting the method already carried a discipline it had never contained. Same failure, three levels.

A "VERIFIED NOTHING-TO-DO" MUST BE VERIFIED BY MAKING THE EXISTING ASSERTION RED, NOT BY READING IT (2026-08-11, rf2-7b4m finding 2).

WHAT HAPPENED, and it is the best form of this outcome I have seen. A twice-relayed audit claim said an Xray hidden-retained / visible-connected / unmounted assertion was still missing. It was not: rf2-hic-023 had landed it in commit 7c45f3ca95 UNDER AN UNRELATED SUBJECT, which is exactly why the claim still read open — nobody had re-checked, and the commit's subject gave no hint.

THE WORKER DID NOT STOP AT READING IT. It inverted both assertions and confirmed each went red at a named line, and dropped the underlying fields (`:hidden-retained` from `host-projection`, then `visibility-note`) and confirmed three more panel reds. Only then did it report nothing-to-do. Its own phrase: "A verified nothing-to-do — but verified by making it red, not by reading it."

WHY THAT MATTERS. Reading an assertion tells you it EXISTS. Making it fail tells you it DECIDES something. This repo has found the difference three times in one day: a row asserting a label plus "nothing has happened yet" that a dead timer satisfied for weeks; a row asserting an fx was in the REGISTRAR, which a never-reached fx satisfies perfectly, with a real shipped bug underneath; and testbed rows that passed whether or not an intent ever arrived. An unverified "already covered" would have left any of those in place.

SO THE BRIEF SHOULD SAY: if you conclude the work is already done, PROVE THE EXISTING COVERAGE BITES before closing — invert it, watch it red, restore, verify the restore by hashing bytes. A close on a read is a close on an assertion nobody has ever seen fail.

TWO SUPPORTING NOTES FROM THE SAME RUN:
  - AN ARITHMETIC CONSTANT CAN BE LOAD-BEARING FOR A REASON THE ROW DOES NOT STATE. `(= 4 distinct-regs)` was not a count for its own sake: it proves `into #{}` counted four IDENTITIES, because a value-collapsing set would have answered 1. Changing 4 to 5 was the instrumentation control; neutralising the release call was the runtime control. Both were needed and they test different things.
  - AN AUDIT PHRASE CAN BE TRUE-SOUNDING AND ANSWERED. The audit said "no Xray lifecycle view/change landed". Today that reads as still-open if judged by "does Xray distinguish the three states?" — it does NOT, and correctly: the tables cannot, so the door states the distinction as `:host-opaque` and refuses to fabricate it. THAT REFUSAL IS THE LANDED ANSWER. When re-checking an audit item, ask whether a deliberate refusal already discharges it.

title: hicasso: no public or kit instrument answers 'how many boundary bodies ran'
description:
Found by rf2-hic-078 while measuring the per-keystroke budget from the two witness applications.

THE PROBLEM. Product specification §6 states a budget in bodies — *narrow-update body work scales with changed rows rather than all mounted rows* — and asks the four-field editor and the controlled grid to publish "state writes, subscription recomputations, boundary runs, write amplification, commit, and visible echo". There is no public or test-kit door that answers the boundary-run half.

WHAT EXISTS, AND WHY EACH IS NOT IT.

- `re-frame.hicasso.test.mounted/census` counts `:cells :cell-refs :boundaries :edges :entries` plus `:frames`. Those are RESIDUE — what is retained — not work done. A keystroke that ran a hundred bodies and a keystroke that ran one leave the same census.
- Spec 009's `rf:render:<view-name>` measures are the right shape, and are compiled out unless `re-frame.performance/enabled?`. No PR-lane build sets it (`node-test`, `browser-test` and the bench lane are all `:none`; the perf-on builds are nightly). So a PR gate cannot read them.
- `re-frame.hicasso.impl.collector/body-runs` is the instrument, it is always-on by an explicit ruling (rf2-2rtt6.84 (6)), and it is an INTERNAL.

CONSEQUENCE. `examples/editor/flow_dom_cljs_test` and `examples/grid/scaling_dom_cljs_test` both `:require` `impl.collector` to measure the budget of the applications they are witnesses for. The applications themselves name nothing but the public door and the fence in `examples/witness_surface_cljs_test` proves it — a test is allowed the reach an application is not — but an application cannot measure its own stated budget without one.

WHO ELSE NEEDS IT. rf2-hic-045 (publish the per-keystroke mechanics) and rf2-hic-071 (budget enforcement gates) are both downstream of rf2-hic-078 and both need this number.

CANDIDATE REMEDY, for whoever owns the kit surface: one door on `re-frame.hicasso.test.mounted` — `(hm/body-runs)` / `(hm/bodies-run handle f)` — delegating to `impl.collector/body-runs`. It is a test-kit surface, so it costs a production bundle nothing, and it puts the specification's own unit in the vocabulary of the facade that mounts the thing being measured. Whether the door should be per-boundary rather than page-wide is the real design question: page-wide is what the counter is, and per-boundary attribution today is done by arithmetic over an exact expected total.

NOT filed as a defect in the counter. `body-runs` is well-designed for what it is; the gap is that it has no public counterpart.
notes:
RESOLVED by PR #7931 (worker/bodycount-5mxe). Landed as a TEST-KIT door: hm/bodies-run on re-frame.hicasso.test.mounted, delegating to impl.collector. No public export, no hot-zone file, nothing new in a production build.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE — all three 'what exists and why each is not it' claims hold. census is residue (counted = [:cells :cell-refs :boundaries :edges :entries]). rf:render:* is emitted by hicasso (collector/mint-view! and mint-frame-prop-view! both wrap the component fn in performance/mark-and-measure :render) but compiled out: exactly two builds flip performance/enabled? — :node-test-perf-nightly (nightly, ns-regexp '-emit-nightly-test$', cannot select a -cljs-test$ suite) and :examples/counter-perf (bundle probe, runs no tests). body-runs is the instrument, always-on by rf2-2rtt6.84 (6), internal.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FRAMING.
(1) The reach-through was never a breach and is not two files. witness_surface_cljs_test states the ruling in terms — 'a test may reach past a door the application may not ... which is the whole reason the two are held to different rules' — and its fence is over APPLICATION namespaces only. 19 test files read the counter; 58 require impl.collector. The real cost was narrower: an application witness could not state its budget in the vocabulary of the facade that mounted it, and a CONSUMER's test would have to name an impl. namespace deps.edn calls 'not a consumer surface'.
(2) The Spec 009 path answers a DIFFERENT question, not merely an expensive one. The measure bracket deliberately spans the generation fence's whole retry loop ('the generation fence emits once'); body-runs bumps per body INVOCATION. On a fence re-run the two disagree by design, so the measure stream could not reproduce these numbers even with both goog-defines flipped.

PLACEMENT ARGUMENT. test.mounted already requires impl.collector (reset-runtime!), so no new dependency edge. test_kit/src is off the published :paths (deps.edn lists it only under :aliases/:test/:extra-paths) so build:hicasso-release cannot see it. Both consumers already require hm. Every one of the counter's 19 consumers is a test. Page-wide and handle-free beside census: a per-boundary form is UNAVAILABLE, not withheld — attribution needs a durable per-boundary id, which impl.collector states costs a third React hook and breaks the HD-020 budget hook_budget_cljs_test enforces.

The 17 runtime suites keep reading impl.collector directly, deliberately: runtime suites read the runtime's counter, application witnesses read the kit's door.

GATES (captured): build:hicasso-release 0 (erasure OK, door absent from the advanced bundle); test:browser 0 (1284 tests / 7971 assertions); test:browser SABOTAGE 1 with exactly 2 failures proving both rows execute through the door — actuals (not (= 3 2 2)) and (not (= 9 2)); test:cljs 0 (13329 / 67165); test:hicasso-invariants 0; clj-kondo pinned 0 errors 0 warnings. No measured number altered.

This is the same invisible class as the dangling bench-suite citation found earlier today — only a read finds it.

SWEEP RATHER THAN FIX FOUR.
