NOTE: the harness announced 'completed (exit code 0)' for run 1 against a captured 1.

value:
A FRESH WORKER WORKTREE HAS NO `implementation/node_modules`, AND THE SPINE FAILS ENVIRONMENTALLY THERE — the harness then misreports it (2026-08-11, rf2-gxry).

WHAT HAPPENED. A worker ran `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` in a newly-created worktree. It captured exit **1** on `CLJS node integration`, with `Cannot find module 'shadow-cljs/cli/runner.js'` — nothing compiled, because the worktree had no `node_modules`. **The harness announced "completed (exit code 0)" against that captured 1.** The worker junctioned `node_modules` at the mayor's real one, deleted the stale `.exit` and `.log`, re-ran the gate whole, and captured **0** with `[:node-test] Build completed. (2307 files, 2306 compiled, 0 warnings)`.

THE HAZARD IS NOT THE FAILURE, IT IS THE SHAPE OF IT. A missing-module error is not a test failure, but it PRESENTS as a red gate, and if a worker reads the harness's number instead of the captured one it presents as a GREEN gate over a build that never ran. Both readings are wrong in opposite directions, and the second is the dangerous one: a green that compiled nothing.

WHAT TO PUT IN A BRIEF for any worker that will run a compiling gate:
  - A fresh worktree has NO `implementation/node_modules`. If a gate needs one, create the junction to the mayor's real tree, and REMOVE THE LINK (never its target) as your last act — a later `git worktree remove` follows it and empties the shared tree. Canary the mayor's count before and after.
  - `Cannot find module` or `command not found` from a gate is ENVIRONMENTAL, not a verdict. Fix the environment and RE-RUN THE GATE WHOLE. Do not report the first number, and do not report it as a failure of the diff.
  - DELETE the stale `.exit` and `.log` before the re-run. A stale `.exit` survives the next run's `>` on its log, so the pair can disagree and the older verdict is the one you quote.

TWELFTH SIGHTING TODAY of the harness reporting a captured 1 as exit 0. The rule stands and is now in the method: THE NUMBER YOU QUOTE IS THE ONE YOU CAPTURED.

title: spec: the Spec 009 Hicasso row count is prose that must track a table, and it has gone stale three times in one day
description:
OBSERVED THREE TIMES ON 2026-08-11, by three different workers, each finding it independently while doing unrelated work.

THE DEFECT. spec/009-Instrumentation.md's Hicasso section states its row count in PROSE ("forty-six", "fifty-one", "fifty-two"), and that count must track the actual number of rows in the table below it. Nothing enforces the correspondence. Every PR that appends a catalogue row must also edit the prose, and the prose is nowhere near the row.

THE THREE SIGHTINGS, all on the same day:
  - PR #7905's worker found the prose saying "forty-six" twice while the table held 48 rows. It was exact at cf85bc9cd8; two rows had landed since without updating it.
  - PR #7912's worker corrected it again on the way past.
  - PR #7923's worker found it stale AGAIN — "forty-six" against 48 — and carried it to fifty-one.
Each repair was correct. Each was made by a worker who had come to do something else, and noticed.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A FOURTH MANUAL FIX. This is the "second thing to drift" pattern the project has already ruled on twice today in other places: a rollup-band constant was REMOVED from bootstrap.md rather than updated, on the reasoning that a second written number is a second thing to drift and mayor-merge.md already owned it; and a catalogue enumeration presented as exhaustive was called WRONG rather than merely incomplete. A prose count beside a table it must match is exactly that shape, and it is now the most reliably-stale statement in the repository.

THREE OPTIONS — argue one, do not implement all:
  (a) REMOVE the count. If nothing depends on it, the table is its own answer and the prose can say "the rows below" without a number. Cheapest, and consistent with the bootstrap.md precedent.
  (b) DERIVE it. If the count carries real information for a reader, generate the sentence from the table rather than writing it twice.
  (c) ENFORCE it. scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py or check_complaint_catalogue.py already read this file and already run on every PR that touches it. If either can assert prose-count == row-count in a few lines, the drift becomes impossible rather than merely discouraged.
My weak preference is (a) then (c): removing a fact nobody needs beats checking it. But establish first WHETHER ANYTHING READS THE COUNT — if a gate, a doc or a downstream check parses it, (a) is off the table and you should say so.

DO NOT widen this into a review of spec/009. The catalogue rows themselves are correct and heavily exercised; only the prose count drifts.

HOT ZONE: spec/009-Instrumentation.md is hot-zone — SEQUENTIAL, never parallel. Confirm no open PR touches spec/** before dispatching this. Note that PR #7923 is currently OPEN and adds three rows plus two count words to that exact file, so this bead waits for it to merge.

VERIFY AT SOURCE: read the current prose and count the current rows before acting. Three workers have corrected it today; it may be right at this instant and wrong again by the time you read it, which is itself the argument for the bead.
notes:
SHARPER AT SOURCE THAN THE BEAD SAYS, verified on main at 2026-08-11 after PR #7923 merged.

THE COUNT APPEARS TWICE IN ONE SENTENCE, NOT ONCE PER SENTENCE. spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2511 reads:

  "**Every one of the fifty-five is a thrown `ex-info`, never a trace event**, so all fifty-five are `diagnostic` by the §Channel rule."

So a single line carries the number TWO TIMES, and an editor who repairs the first occurrence and not the second leaves the file self-contradicting inside one sentence. That is a worse failure mode than the drift this bead was filed for, and it makes option (a) — REMOVE THE COUNT — stronger than my original weak preference suggested.

THE SENTENCE DOES NOT NEED THE NUMBER. Read it without: "Every one of these is a thrown `ex-info`, never a trace event, so all of them are `diagnostic` by the §Channel rule." The claim is universal quantification over the table; the cardinal adds nothing a reader can use and everything a maintainer must keep true. The table is its own answer.

FOURTH SIGHTING IN ONE DAY. The count was "forty-six" against 48 rows when PR #7905's worker found it; corrected again on #7912; found stale AGAIN by #7923's worker and carried to fifty-one; then the rebase of that same PR had to resolve a CONFLICT in exactly these two count words, because main and the branch had each independently repaired them. That last one is the tell: THE COUNT IS NOW GENERATING MERGE CONFLICTS, not merely going stale.

REVISED RECOMMENDATION: take option (a). Remove both occurrences and rewrite the sentence to quantify over the table rather than over a number. Only fall back to (c) — enforcement in check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py — if you establish that something actually READS the count. Verify that first; if a gate, a doc or a downstream check parses it, say so and (a) is off the table.

CURRENT STATE, so the next reader can tell drift from repair: main reads "fifty-five" twice on line 2511, and the table between `hicasso-empty-vector` and the `#### Adapter-internal` heading holds 55 body rows with 55 distinct ids. That was counted by the #7923 rebase worker, not inherited from either side of its conflict.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7933 (branch worker/rowcount-9oah). Option (a): the count is REMOVED. Established first that nothing reads it — git grep 'fifty-five' across the tracked tree returns only spec/009 lines 2511 and 2521 plus the bead's own JSONL; check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py and check_complaint_catalogue.py both read this file but parse row IDs only, with no number-word vocabulary; the two checkers that DO carry a number-word map (check_readme_inventories.py, check_skill_eval_docs.py) do not target spec/009; and the complaint register states no count. SHARPER THAN THE BEAD RECORDED: there were THREE occurrences across TWO lines, not two on one — line 2521's 'these fifty-five are the cases where repairing would mean overruling what the author wrote' had been missed by every prior sighting, including the sweep that concluded only 2511 carried a number. Both sentences make a universal claim over the table, so they now quantify over it ('Every row below is a thrown ex-info'; 'the rows below are the cases'). Row count at time of fix: 55 body rows, 55 distinct ids, lines 2527-2581. Options (b) derive and (c) enforce both rejected: (b) is machinery for a number no reader needs, and (c) was the fallback only if something read the count — with the number gone there is nothing left to check. Gates captured: check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py 0, npm run test:hicasso-invariants 0, python -m mkdocs build --strict 0, check_fast_pr_gap.py --list 0.

title: mayor-method: nothing tells the mayor to verify its OWN brief's factual claims, and three briefs were wrong today
description:
FOUND BY THE HOURLY METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-08-11 night. The method files have not drifted; this is again what they do not contain.

VERIFIED ABSENT. `grep -c` over docs/the-mayor-method/:
  - dispatch-prompt-template.md: 0 hits for premise-verification of any kind.
  - bootstrap.md: 1 hit, line 67, "Verified-redundant grep before dispatch" — which is about whether the WORK IS ALREADY DONE, not about whether the brief's own assertions are true.
  - "an audit finding is a CLAIM, not automatically work": 0 hits in BOTH files. It lives only in .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md, so a fresh mayor reading the method never meets it.

THE GAP. The method tells the mayor to check for redundancy. It never tells the mayor to check the FACTS IT WRITES INTO A BRIEF — that a named ruling exists, that a named gate covers the named surface, that a named symbol resolves.

THREE BRIEFS WERE WRONG TODAY, ALL THE SAME SHAPE, ALL CAUGHT BY THE WORKER RATHER THAN BY ME:
  1. NAMED THE WRONG GATE FOR A SURFACE. I told two workers `.claude/commands/*.md` "may have no automated gate at all". scripts/check_readme_links.py owns it. Worse, the plausible alternative is a trap: check_doc_slugs.py explicitly does NOT cover CLAUDE.md and its own notes record that briefs have nominated it and received A GREEN EXIT VERIFYING NOTHING.
  2. ASSERTED THE METHOD ALREADY CARRIED A DISCIPLINE IT HAD NEVER CONTAINED. I filed a bead saying the template "already demands plant-and-restore" and merely lacked the verification step. A grep for `sabotag|plant|negative control|restore` across the whole tree returned NOTHING.
  3. QUOTED AN ADVISORY LEDGER ROW AS A SETTLED RULING — twice in one brief. I said rf2-hic-065 row 1 "ruled" the callback macro as `h/event`. In naming-ledger.md that name is in the RECOMMENDATION column with STATUS = open, and rf2-hic-065's own note says all naming rows are reserved to the operator's sitting.

THE THIRD ONE SHOWS THE COST, and it is not pedantic: `h/event` DOES NOT RESOLVE EITHER. Had the worker obeyed, it would have replaced a non-existent name with another non-existent name — RE-COMMITTING THE EXACT DEFECT THE BEAD EXISTED TO REMOVE, in the same files, under an authority that was never granted.

TWO CLAUSES TO ADD, both short, both in dispatch-prompt-template.md beside the existing brief-writing rules:

RULE A — VERIFY EVERY FACTUAL ASSERTION BEFORE PUTTING IT IN A BRIEF. If the brief names a ruling, read its STATUS field and quote it — a recommendation is not a ruling, and in this repo the two look alike in a summary and are opposite in force. If it names a gate, confirm that gate covers that path — a gate run over an excluded path exits green having verified nothing. If it names a symbol, grep that it resolves. A brief that names the wrong gate is worse than one that names none, because the worker then trusts a green that means nothing.

RULE B — TELL THE WORKER THE BRIEF IS A CLAIM. Every brief should say, in terms, that the mayor's premises are claims to be checked at source and that a verified "already fixed" or "the premise does not hold" is a complete and good deliverable. This is the single highest-yield line in any brief here: workers caught mayor errors at source ELEVEN times today, and three of those prevented damage rather than merely correcting a word.

SCOPE: two clauses in dispatch-prompt-template.md. Do NOT add a checklist, a script or a verification step — these are things the mayor must do while writing, not machinery. Do NOT restate in bootstrap.md; one source, and the template is where a brief is written. Consider whether "an audit finding is a CLAIM" belongs in the method rather than only in mayor-posture.md, and say which you chose and why.

VERIFY BEFORE WRITING: re-run the greps. If a later commit added either rule, close as verified-duplicate saying so.
close_reason: Both clauses landed in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md via PR #7934. Greps re-run: bootstrap.md line 67 HOLDS; the CLAIM-sentence exact-phrase grep HOLDS. But 'dispatch-prompt-template.md: 0 hits for premise-verification of any kind' DOES NOT HOLD — the gate half of Rule A has been at line 151 since 81ce0ba455 (2026-07-31): 'Never nominate a gate that does not cover the surface being edited ... a gate run over an excluded path exits green having verified nothing ... Read the exclusion config before naming the gate.' The new section cross-references it rather than restating it. Added: a '## What the brief asserts' H2 (verify a ruling's STATUS field, grep that a symbol resolves; gates cross-referenced) plus one paragraph in the fenced common-preamble block making Rule B operative. DECISION on 'an audit finding is a CLAIM, not automatically work': NOT added to the method. Its substance is already there twice — Shape 3's 'not every finding is actioned' (line 304, missed by the bead's grep because the phrase wraps a line) and bootstrap.md:340 'a verified nothing-to-do is a good outcome; an assumed one is not' — and the sentence is a stance clause, which the template's own lines 17-27 reserve to the single file pasted verbatim into every preamble. Gates (captured): mkdocs --strict 0, check_doc_slugs 0, check_readme_links 0, check_fast_pr_gap --list 0 (97 required checks not decided locally). Negative control: planted a broken markdown anchor, check_doc_slugs exit 1 naming the right file:line, restored, sha256sum -c OK, re-run exit 0.

value:
A ZERO-HIT GREP IS NOT PROOF OF ABSENCE WHEN THE CORPUS WRAPS LINES — I filed a method-gap bead whose central claim was itself unverified (2026-08-11, rf2-owmq).

THE IRONY IS THE POINT. I filed rf2-owmq saying "nothing tells the mayor to verify its OWN brief's factual claims", and cited `grep -c` returning 0 on dispatch-prompt-template.md as the evidence. THE BEAD ITSELF CONTAINED AN UNVERIFIED CLAIM. Its worker found the gate half of the rule had been in that file since commit 81ce0ba455 (2026-07-31), at line 151: "Never nominate a gate that does not cover the surface being edited ... a gate run over an excluded path exits green having verified nothing ... Read the exclusion config before naming the gate." That is my proposed clause and its one-line reason, near-verbatim, already present.

TWO MORE OF MY GREPS WERE FALSE NEGATIVES IN THE SAME BEAD:
  - Shape 3 already ends "not every finding is actioned" — my grep missed it BECAUSE THE PHRASE WRAPS A LINE.
  - bootstrap.md:340 already carries "Read the current source at the named site before dispatching. A verified 'nothing to do' is a good outcome; an assumed one is not."

THE MECHANISM: these method files are hand-wrapped prose at ~78 columns. Any phrase longer than a few words has a NEWLINE SOMEWHERE INSIDE IT at an unpredictable point, so a multi-word `grep` pattern misses it. `grep -c "verify the premise"` returns 0 against a file that says exactly that, wrapped.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD when checking whether a prose corpus already says something:
  - Grep for SINGLE DISTINCTIVE WORDS, not phrases — `nominate`, `exclusion`, `premise`, `claim` — then read the hits.
  - Or use `grep -z` / `rg --multiline` so the pattern can cross a newline.
  - Or, best for a small corpus: READ THE SECTION. These files are a few hundred lines; a claim about what they do not contain is worth the read.
  - And state the method in the bead, so the worker can judge whether the search could have found the thing.

THE WIDER RULE, and this is the fourth variant of it today: DO NOT ASSERT FROM MEMORY OR FROM A WEAK SEARCH WHAT A DOCUMENT CONTAINS. The three earlier variants were naming the wrong gate for a surface, claiming the method carried a discipline it never had, and quoting an advisory ledger row as a settled ruling. This one is subtler because the evidence LOOKED mechanical — a grep with a number attached reads like proof, and a false negative reads exactly like a true one.

THE OUTCOME WAS STILL GOOD, because the worker was told the brief's premises are claims: it cross-referenced the existing line instead of restating it, preserving single-source. The honest residual gap was real and narrower than I filed — nothing told the mayor to check its own assertions, and that clause is what landed.

description:

re-frame.hicasso.revision-dom-cljs-test makes reincarnation_paint_dom_cljs_test's

  W1 sabotage control --  | DOM was "" | residue {:cells 0 ...}
followed by 'WARNING: Async test called done more than one time'. The failures are
reported against whichever test is CURRENT when they land, so they are attributed to
the innocent new suite, not to their owner.

EVIDENCE (all captured exit codes, local Windows, npm run test:browser):
  - witness present, release! teardown -> captured exit 1, W1+W2 red
  - witness moved aside (control)      -> captured exit 0, 'Ran 1284 tests containing

The third run rules out the teardown door as the cause: the collision does not depend
on whether the neighbour suite is torn down with release! or unmount!. It depends only
on a new suite existing at that position in the run order.

DIAGNOSIS. W1/W2 attach .catch AFTER the .then that calls done, and their trailing
cleanup (mount/unmount! -> inventory/quiesced! -> mount/release!) is allowed to outlive

container it reads has legitimately been emptied. 'DOM was ""' is that.

plus a verdict record, and this file belongs to rf2-hic-013's lane): chain the cleanup
BEFORE done rather than after it, so no promise outlives the test that armed it.

Fixed in PR #7937 (branch worker/donefix-d3tc), one file: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/reincarnation_paint_dom_cljs_test.cljs.

REPAIR. fail-and-finish! -> report-failure!: it reports and releases and does NOT finish the row. Both .catch handlers move UPSTREAM of the .then that calls done, so each of the three async rows now ends in exactly ONE done with nothing after it -- the shape checkpoint-support/at-the-checkpoint already uses. No assertion weakened, moved or deleted; no other suite touched.

PREMISE CORRECTION. The bead's diagnosis said the trailing cleanup 'is allowed to outlive their own done'. It is not: (.then (inventory/quiesced!) ...) is RETURNED into the chain, so the teardown is already awaited before done fires. What outlives the test is the .catch. cljs.test/run-block hands done a continuation that runs the whole remainder of the run synchronously, so a throw out there unwinds back into the callback that called done, and a catch placed after it claims the foreign failure. The second done then re-forces run-block's delay (a delay whose body threw is still unrealized), which is why the offending namespace runs twice. Same remedy, more accurate reason.

title: hic: route PATHS are process-global strings, so two apps in one node bundle collide silently
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-hic-025 WORKER (PR #7920) when the fast-PR spine went red — and the spine was THE ONLY GATE THAT COULD HAVE CAUGHT IT.

WHAT HAPPENED. The new vertical slice registered the routes `/` and `/article/:slug`. Twelve assertions in the RealWorld suite failed, naming the slice's routes. Cause: route IDS are namespaced keywords and therefore safe, but route PATHS are plain STRINGS in a PROCESS-GLOBAL registry — and the node test bundle loads a dozen applications into ONE process. So any two apps that both claim `/` collide, and the second registration wins for everybody.

NOTHING WARNED. `:rf.warning/route-shadowed-by-equal-score` requires EQUAL rank, and the log carried zero occurrences. So the collision is silent at registration, silent at dispatch, and surfaces only as another application's tests failing for reasons that name YOUR routes. The worker fixed its own case by namespacing every path under `/slice`, and `test:cljs` went from 12 failures to 0.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A CONVENTION NOTE. Every witness app this programme is about to add hits it. `rf2-hic-086` (Todo-class), `rf2-hic-078` (two public-package witness apps) and `rf2-hic-074` (pagination + runtime content) all live in the same bundle, and the natural path for a demo app is `/`. The next one to claim it breaks a suite it has never heard of, and the failure names the wrong file.

THE QUESTION TO ANSWER FIRST, and it is a design call, not a fix:
  (a) Is a process-global path registry correct, with the remedy being a CONVENTION — every in-bundle app namespaces its paths — plus something that ENFORCES it? A convention nobody can violate accidentally is worth more than one written down.
  (b) Or should the registry be frame-scoped or root-scoped, so two apps in one process cannot see each other's paths at all? That is the shape re-frame2 uses for nearly everything else, and a global registry is the exception rather than the rule here.
  (c) Or should registering a path that already exists REFUSE, rather than silently shadow? Note this is adjacent to the open ruling on rf2-04tx — whether the closed effect map should refuse an unknown key rather than ignoring it. Do not answer that one here, but read it: the argument shapes are the same, and so is the counter-argument about nag-diagnostics on a hot path.

ESTABLISH THE COST BEFORE RECOMMENDING. Read the registry, say what each option costs at registration and at dispatch, and whether a check can be dev-only and erased in production (the release build's erasure gate is the precedent). Then STATE THE CASE and stop — this is an operator call.

WHAT NOT TO DO: do not widen `:rf.warning/route-shadowed-by-equal-score` on a hunch; its equal-rank condition may be deliberate. Do not rename other apps' routes. Do not treat "namespace your paths" as landed just because the slice did it — that is one app obeying a rule nobody wrote.

VERIFY AT SOURCE: confirm the registry really is process-global and really is keyed by string path, and confirm the warning's equal-rank condition, before building any argument on this description. It is a worker's report, relayed by the mayor.
notes:
CORRECTION FROM THE REPORTING WORKER, and it removes an option a reader would otherwise reach for first.

"MAKE THE EXISTING WARNING LOUDER" IS NOT A FOURTH OPTION. `reg-route` does carry :rf.warning/route-shadowed-by-equal-score, and it NEVER FIRED — because the ranks DIFFERED. So the guard had nothing to say while the resolution was already wrong. It is asking a different question from the one that matters: it detects an ambiguous TIE, not a silent OVERWRITE across applications that share a process.

That distinction is the whole finding. A reader who sees a route-shadowing warning already exists will assume the mechanism is covered and the threshold merely needs lowering. It is not covered. Widening the equal-rank condition would fire on cases the warning was deliberately written to allow, and would still miss this one whenever the ranks differ — which is the common case, since two applications' paths rarely rank the same.

So the three options on this bead stand as the whole option set: convention plus enforcement, a scoped registry, or a refusal at registration. Do not add a fourth arm about tuning the existing warning, and if the ruling lands on convention-plus-enforcement, note that the enforcement CANNOT be that warning.

ONE DOCUMENTATION RESIDUAL, reported and deliberately not actioned: finding 8 of docs/design/hicasso/product/authoring-report-slice.md explains this collision and the /slice fix but CITES NO BEAD, because this bead's id did not exist when the report was written. Worth one line whenever that report is next touched. Not worth a dispatch of its own.
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-12, operator-overturnable):

RULING: Option (a). The route registry stays process-global. The in-bundle path-prefix convention gets written down once and enforced by one repo-side census gate with a one-entry allowlist. No registration refusal, no scoping. Dossier ai/decisions/rf2-wqnl.route-path-collision.md reviewed, every load-bearing claim re-verified at source (head 3ed7a442e6), file deleted per protocol; all analysis preserved below.

WHY (a):
1. The class bites exactly one composition - many apps loaded into one node test bundle - which exists only in this repo. A consumer's own registry holds only their routes (authoring-report finding 8, premise verified). Build the guard where the hazard lives.
2. The gate delivers the whole observable improvement refusal would give THIS repo - load-time failure naming both routes and both files, at the bundle boundary where the class bites - with zero framework surface, zero registration/dispatch cost, zero consumer-facing change.
3. Symmetric with the framework's own precedent: cross-source collision on a registration ID gets namespacing convention + a provenance-aware dev warning (:rf.warning/registration-collision, registrar.cljc:430-495), not refusal. Paths should not be held to a stricter standard than ids while rf2-04tx (refuse-vs-ignore, same argument shape) is still open; nothing here answers 04tx.
4. REJECTING (c) reg-route refusal: it refuses a LIVE legitimate usage - hicasso route_link_cljs_test.cljs:29 registers :conduit.profile/show at "/profile/:username", identical to RealWorld's :realworld.profile/show, emission-only (href synthesis by id, never URL ingress), coherent and harmless (verified). It forces the todomvc/RealWorld "/" pair to be resolved NOW with no allowlist possible, breaking a teaching example's URL fidelity (RealWorld routing.cljs follows the official contract "to the letter"; todomvc's / /active /completed are canonical TodoMVC, and guide code blocks are digest-pinned = multi-file change). Hot-reload id-rename (same path, new id, stale id seated) throws until cleared. And it would set the refuse posture by side effect while 04tx awaits ruling. Nag-diagnostics shape the posture rejects (u53yy.7).
5. REJECTING (b) frame/root-scoped table: scoped resolution ALREADY EXISTS opt-in - EP-0023 image-built frames resolve registrations generation-routed (registrar.cljc:861-870, verified: a generation-scoped query sees only the frame's own image's ids). Defaulting or duplicating that is new API surface or a fleet migration, taxing the single-app norm to fix a repo-internal testing artifact, and it mismodels the domain: the browser URL is one process resource with one owner. The bead's premise "frame-scoped is the shape re-frame2 uses for nearly everything else" is not accurate - the global static registrar is the rule for EVERY kind; per-frame is state plus opt-in image resolution.

VERIFIED MECHANISM (preserved from the dossier; re-checked at source 2026-08-12):
- One defonce registrar atom for all kinds (implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc:152-157). The path pattern is route metadata; match-url (implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:1226) takes ONLY a url - no frame, no app - and walks one rank-sorted table of ALL registered routes, short-circuiting on first match. One process = one shared match table.
- Ties go to the EARLIER registration: rank = structural 5-tuple + (- reg-index) (registry.cljc:499,506). Two identical patterns always tie structurally, so the earlier wins every URL forever and the later is unreachable for URL ingress. Namespace load order decides which app wins.
- IMPRECISION CORRECTION to this bead's earlier note: "the warning never fired because the ranks DIFFERED" is wrong for the observed pair. /article/:slug vs /article/:slug are IDENTICAL patterns - structural ranks EQUAL, and patterns-intersect? reports them co-matchable - so the scan's condition was satisfiable. The verified reasons nothing surfaced: (i) :rf.warning/route-shadowed-by-equal-score is delivered via trace/emit! into the instrumentation ring buffer and NOTHING in the node lane reads it - no console sink for trace warnings anywhere in core/src (grep-verified); (ii) prod builds erase the emit entirely (pinned by implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_trace_emit_elision_prod_test.cljs); (iii) the first registrant scans before the second exists, and test-support restore-registrar! reseats the registrar wholesale without re-running reg-route, so no scan runs on restore. For the GENERAL cross-app case (one app's literal under another's capture) ranks genuinely differ and the guard is structurally blind - that half of the note stands. NET, AND BINDING ON FUTURE WORK: no widening or tuning of this warning can be the enforcement arm, because even when it fires nobody in the failing lane can see it. Its tie-only condition is deliberate (rf2-6gzobp - warning on the tie alone floods every ordinary multi-page app). DO NOT BUILD ON THE PHANTOM WARNING.
- LIVE ARMED DUPLICATE today: examples/core/todomvc/events.cljs:28 registers :todo/all at "/"; examples/real-apps/realworld_http/routing.cljs:40-60 registers :realworld/home at "/". Both load into the node bundle. Asymptomatic only because todomvc suites never feed a URL in and RealWorld suites never ingress "/". The slice trap, armed.
- LIVE LEGITIMATE DUPLICATE: the route_link test above - emission-only registration is coherent; match-dead is harmless. Duplicate paths are not always a bug, which is a load-bearing reason refusal is wrong.
- The prefix convention has been independently invented 3x, written nowhere normative: /slice (rf2-hic-025, PR #7920), /hicasso-todo (rf2-hic-086), and the route-path per-substrate prefix helper in core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs. THE QUESTION. rf2-hic-025's bead named the surface implementation/hicasso/examples/slice/. Its worker found that path is on NO :source-paths entry, so a tree there is COMPILED BY NOTHING. Creating a fresh uncovered tree hours after closing that hole would be perverse. An artefact belongs where a gate already reaches it; a path is not worth a coverage gap.

The worker's own reasoning was sound and it asked rather than guessing, which is exactly right for a hot-zone file. Asking cost one round-trip; guessing would have cost a silent coverage hole.

BINDING ON THE SIBLINGS. rf2-hic-086 (Todo-class), rf2-hic-078 (two public-package witness apps) and rf2-hic-074 (pagination + runtime content) all name paths under implementation/hicasso/examples/. This bead carries an earlier note saying "namespace every route path UNTIL rf2-wqnl lands". That framing is now wrong in a way that matters: NAMESPACING IS THE PERMANENT, ENFORCED RULE, not a temporary workaround.

AND ONE THING THE SLICE PROVED THE HARD WAY: route PATHS are process-global strings, and the node bundle loads a dozen apps into one process. The slice claimed / and /article/:slug and broke twelve RealWorld assertions with nothing warning. NAMESPACE EVERY ROUTE PATH YOUR APP REGISTERS. MAYOR — RE-WORD THE ROUTE NOTE, DO NOT DROP IT (2026-08-12, from rf2-wqnl's worker, PR #7938).

THE ALLOWLIST IS NOT A PLACE TO ADD YOURSELF. title: hic: a testbed handler returned a v1-shaped top-level :dispatch-later, which the closed effect-map silently dropped
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-hic-016 PHASE-1 WORKER before it typed a single key, and it is the most valuable thing that dispatch produced. Repaired in PR #7896; this bead exists because the CLASS is wider than the two handlers it fixed, and because the gate that should have caught it was green throughout.

THE DEFECT. The testbed's `:tb/arm` handler returned a v1-shaped map with a TOP-LEVEL `:dispatch-later` sitting beside `:db`. re-frame2's effect map is CLOSED — `#{:db :rf.db/runtime :fx}` — so nothing carried the key and the timer was never scheduled. The armed edges NEVER FIRED. Measured: 15 seconds after the click the readout still read `armed`, while a plain `setTimeout(5000)` in the same page returned in 5006 ms.

WHY IT SURVIVED, AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. The gate `armed-edges-are-wired` was GREEN IN THREE ENGINES the whole time, because it asserts the LABEL and that NOTHING HAS HAPPENED YET — and a dead timer satisfies "nothing has happened yet" perfectly. That is the exact fail-open shape this project hunts everywhere else: a check that verifies the absence of bad news rather than the presence of good news. It passed because the feature was broken in the one way the assertion could not distinguish from working.

WORSE, THESE WERE THE OPERATOR INSTRUMENTS. They were added in PR #7815 and sharpened in #7846 SPECIFICALLY to reach a live IME composition. So the instrument built to answer the operator's question had been inert since it landed, and every green run said otherwise.

WHAT #7896 ALREADY DID, so this bead does not redo it: both handlers fixed; the gate section now WAITS FOR THE FIRE behind a `?arm-ms=300` override (under a second per engine, not the thirty seconds the #7815 audit refused); pins updated (section 5 to 9, sum 91 to 95, TESTING.md twice). Sabotage-proven: sabotaged `:tb/arm` exits 1 with "the armed bump never fired within 5000ms", restored exits 0.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWNS — the class, not the instance:
1. SWEEP for other v1-shaped top-level effect keys returned by handlers anywhere in the tree. `:dispatch-later` is one spelling; `:dispatch`, `:dispatch-n`, `:deregister-event-handler` and any other v1 top-level effect would be dropped the same silent way. Search handler return maps, not the effect registry.
2. DECIDE whether the closed effect map should REFUSE an unknown top-level key rather than ignoring it. This is the real question and it is an operator-facing call: a refusal turns a silent no-op into a source-located error at the point of the mistake, which is this project's whole posture on crossings — but it is also a behaviour change on a hot path, and the stance rejects nag-diagnostics. **Do not implement a refusal without a ruling.** Establish the cost, state the case both ways, and surface it.
3. AUDIT the sibling assertions in the same testbed gate for the same fail-open shape: any row that asserts a label plus "nothing has happened yet" cannot distinguish armed-and-working from armed-and-dead.

DO NOT re-fix the two handlers, do not re-run the IME rig, and do not widen into unrelated testbed work.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED — PR #7940 (branch worker/fxrule-04tx). Option C shipped as ruled: a foreign top-level effect key (case a) or a non-sequential :fx value (case b) in the FINAL effects map aborts the event in-band, uniformly in every build — no :db, no :rf.db/runtime, no classification install, no :fx. Case (c), a malformed entry inside a well-shaped :fx vector, keeps :logged-and-skipped per-entry recovery; its channel promoted with the rest of the category.

SHAPE. events/police-effect-map-shape! + fx-value-ok? + police-final-effects! replaced by the PURE first-defect-or-nil carrier events/effect-map-defect (the elision/classification-effect-defect pattern). commit-fx-effects no longer polices and is NOT a second abort site: it projects the handler return VERBATIM so a handler-returned key and an :after-inserted key reach the same single check. router/emit-effect-map-shape! reuses the exact in-band arm of emit-legacy-runtime-root! / emit-classification-effect-shape! (no throw). The envelope arm is ordered FIRST among the three effect rejections. Always-on record carries :offending-key only; :value and :reason stay dev-trace; :failing-id == :event-id so emit-error-both!'s lift never drags :reason on. emit-fx-error! gained a record-attrs arity so all three cases share ONE record shape.

SPEC (hot-zone, flagged in the PR body). 009 row -> Channel always-on, per-case recovery cells, ONE row kept, NO count added. Spec-Schemas §:rf/effect-map drops the 'legal siblings still apply' promise for a/b. Conventions §No silent swallow gains one instance row. Implementor-Checklist runtime-shape-policing row + two-planes paragraph flip. migration M-8 hazard INVERTED. Fixtures bad-top-level-key + bad-fx-value FLIP (no commit, :fix-effect, always-on record asserted); bad-fx-entry + surplus-entry-field STAY as the control; conformance README updated. The :tags cell is UNCHANGED so the three-arm co-edit invariant needed no schema/exercise edit. api-manifest untouched; no facade export.

GATES, CAPTURED. core JVM 2239/11669 exit 0; prod-gate lane (-Dre-frame.debug=false) 1982/8684 exit 0 with the new namespace IN the roster (the no-build-fork witness); all 19 implementation artefacts green; tools/xray JVM 1289/6051 exit 0; npm run test:cljs 13336/67196 exit 0; python -m mkdocs build --strict exit 0; check_doc_slugs exit 0; six static checkers exit 0; clj-kondo delta zero (all findings reproduce on origin/main). SABOTAGE BOTH WAYS: (A) shape-defect forced nil -> exit 1, 51 failures/4 errors, first red names effect_map_shape_record_cljs_test.cljc:125; (B) closed set narrowed to drop the four legal EP-0025 keys -> exit 1, 93 failures on the LEGAL path (sensitive-effect-records-path-and-redacts-at-egress etc). Restore verified by sha256sum -c, not git diff.

title: hic-006b — The package-resident heap instrument, and the re-pin it enables
description:
## Why

rf2-hic-006 (PR #7935) could NOT deliver its 'shell/per-read/teardown baselines re-measured on implementation/hicasso' item, and the reason is structural rather than incidental.

1. The pinned heap figures come from `p0_run.cjs --only ladder`, whose candidate arm is `re-frame.bench.hicasso.arm1.*` in the BENCH tree. That runtime's docstring: 'Residence: the bench/test tree, off every production source path (HD-017). Nothing under implementation/*/src requires this.' implementation/shadow-cljs.edn states the same separation from the other side and names hicasso/scripts/check_freeze.py as its enforcer. So implementation/hicasso/src is a deliberately frozen COPY and NO heap instrument points at the package.
2. Independently, the registered instrument has drifted from its own pin. The heap ladder identifies itself by CONTENT HASH, not commit SHA. At 0c0aa22898 not one of its eleven pinned blobs matches, and front/sub_index.cljs no longer exists. A reading taken today could not be compared with the pinned row: the delta would be un-attributable between instrument drift and the package move.

## What to build

A package-pointed heap build id (e.g. :hicasso-heap-bench) whose candidate arm requires re-frame.hicasso instead of re-frame.bench.hicasso.arm1, REUSING the existing p0_* driver and fixtures unchanged so the estimator does not move.

## How to run it

Its OWN measurement window, Shape 6, quiet machine, one run at a time. The package arm and BOTH donor arms must be taken IN THE SAME RUN: the two harnesses differ by a measured ~5% common-mode offset and no figure may be scaled from one onto the other.

## Notes

- HOT ZONE: needs a new build id in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn. Operator sequences it.
- Coordinate with rf2-hic-018, which already carries implementation/hicasso/test/.../substrate_* (new benches) on its surface line — this may fold into it rather than run separately.
- Until this lands, S1-S5 in docs/design/hicasso/product/budgets.md are BENCH-TREE figures, not package figures, and the page says so.
notes:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-12, operator-overturnable):

RULING — the three coupled choices:
(1) VEHICLE: Option 1 — a dedicated TWO-DISPATCH sequence ahead of rf2-hic-018. First an ordinary PR that makes the existing P0 heap instrument package-pointed; then ONE solo quiet-window Shape 6 run taking the package arm AND both donor arms in the same run, whose PR is the re-pin. Fold-into-hic-018 REJECTED; defer REJECTED (reasons in the WHY section).
(2) RIG RESIDENCE: ride the existing :hicasso-bench build id — ZERO hot-zone edits. The bead's proposed :hicasso-heap-bench id is DEFERRED to rf2-hic-071, reconsidered ONLY if this lane becomes a standing/recurring gate or a second independent workflow needs it (the stopping rule). Verified: hicasso/src is already on the top-level shadow :source-paths (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn ~L158, its comment naming :hicasso-bench), the driver documents the ride as the deliberate house shape ("No shadow-cljs.edn change, deliberately... One id serves N programs", lane cache cleared per build), and it stamps build + initFn into its output — provenance is complete without a named id, and instrument identity in this corpus is carried by content hash regardless.
(3) RIDER: the shell paper-fail line is FROZEN at the literal 1,024 B. Spell it "1,024 B" everywhere; the ambiguous "1 KB" spelling retires. Adjudication rule adopted with it: a confidence band that crosses 1,024 B is UNRESOLVED, not a pass, and no substrate is selected on a point-estimate difference inside that band. Basis: budgets.md section 5's standing recommendation; the row is red under either reading today (1,103 / 1,097 B) but the no-wrapper arm reads 994/992 B, so a remediation landing between 1,000 and 1,024 is a reachable coin-flip between readings. rf2-hic-018's shell disposition consumes this line; it is noted there before dispatch.

VERIFICATION (all re-checked live at HEAD 5f662c4ff2, not taken from the dossier):
- Instrument drift is real: p0_run.cjs live blob 30e16875... vs pin 4718aaea...; arm1/runtime.cljs live 202f7612... vs pin 69bfc6fc...; front/sub_index.cljs ABSENT. budgets.md section 6's pin table matches these live hashes exactly.
- No heap instrument points at the package: every candidate read goes through re-frame.bench.hicasso.arm1.runtime/sub (bench tree); check_freeze.py live output: "OK: 1 frozen row(s) match the bench tree... no package file imports it".
- CHECKPOINT 1 (rf2-hic-019) returned HELD 2026-08-11 17:28 AUSEST with rf2-hic-018 among the four open discharge deps; hic-018's own deps are all closed and it blocks hic-017 + hic-019.
- Driver overrides documented: P0_BUILD (default hicasso-bench, p0_run.cjs L119), P0_INIT_FN (default re-frame.bench.p0-app/-main, L122), one-line --config-merge of output-dir + :init-fn onto the existing :advanced :browser id.
- budgets.md section 4 carries S1-S5 flagged "not re-pinned on the package"; section 5 (~L258) carries the standing 1,024 B recommendation.

CODEX ADVISORY, adjudicated on the merits:
- ADOPTED — repoint-in-place, not sibling-arm-plus-entry. The dossier's "exactly two new files" sketch is mechanically INCOMPLETE, verified against the code: p0_heap.cljs (1,258 lines) hard-codes the prototype at exactly four candidate seams — mount door L154 (arm1.mount/root!), runtime reset L384 (arm1.runtime/reset-runtime!), live structural census L447 (arm1.runtime/residue), post-unmount residue L1244 (same) — and p0_hicasso.cljs's doors are arm1's (runtime/sub + lang/defview). The package equivalents exist 1:1, verified: re-frame.hicasso.impl.mount/root! (L145), impl.collector/reset-runtime! (L2015), impl.inventory/stats (L126) + residue (L162), facade re-frame.hicasso/defview (macro, hicasso.cljc L97) and /sub (alias of impl.collector/sub, L393). - This PR does NOT touch: budgets.md (its figures do not exist yet), implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, the freehand donor tree, frozen-sources.edn (the one frozen row is front/slot.cljc — untouched). Bench tree requiring re-frame.hicasso is the allowed direction (precedent: :hicasso-release's consumer app); the SEALED fence forbids only package -> re-frame.bench.*.
DISPATCH 2 — the window (only after dispatch 1 MERGES; at the operator-granted quiet):

- ONE invocation of p0_run.cjs --only ladder: package candidate + BOTH donor arms in the same run set (measured ~5% common-mode harness offset — Reagent +5.19%, UIx +5.17% — so no figure may be scaled across runs), the candidate measured in both segments as the arm already provides.
- The rig is frozen at dispatch-1 merge; any rig change invalidates and repeats the window. A refusal (guard exit 2, control not ok, unverified mounts) is a DELIVERABLE: record it on this bead, end the window, re-schedule. NEVER iterate the instrument to force a green. hic-018's heap half holds until an anchor exists.
- Deliverable = the re-pin PR: budgets.md section 4 S1-S5 become package figures with a fresh blob table; section 5 extends to the package readings and records the 1,024 B freeze as RULED (this note is the ruling); section 6's refusal section gets its closure note; the ladder page's provenance re-pins at the fresh blob hashes; publish raw round ranges, all quality verdicts, DOM/Q/structural read-backs, post-unmount residue, and the exact package commit + instrument blobs (the driver already stamps build + initFn).
SEQUENCING / DEPENDENCY DIRECTION: rf2-fe0l now BLOCKS rf2-hic-018 (edge added this session). This sequence feeds hic-018's acceptance: the same-instrument package baseline is taken BEFORE any collector-substrate mutation, which is what makes hic-018's before/after attributable; hic-018 then reuses THIS exact instrument, for viable substrate candidates only. rf2-hic-070 re-pins its K3 citations after hic-018, per its own text ("re-pins, never re-frames"). Context for both workers: the freeze manifest is down to 1 row, the package runtime is 18 owned impl modules (hic-009), and S1-S5 currently describe a diverging prototype — divergence is expected and permanent, which is why the re-pin cannot wait for a "stable" moment.

FENCES:
- NO hot-zone traffic in either dispatch (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/* untouched).
- NO new build id now; :hicasso-heap-bench reconsidered only from rf2-hic-071 under the stopping rule.
- NO instrument iteration to force a green — a window refusal ends the window and is reported.

WHY (options record, preserved from the dossier before its deletion):

title: hic: PR #7936's witness pairs a fn-form :each fixture with an async row, so cljs.test aborts its whole namespace
description:
THIS, NOT rf2-d3tc, IS WHAT ACTUALLY REDS PR #7936 (branch worker/cbident-hic029).

SITE. implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/retaining_host_callbacks_dom_cljs_test.cljs

    (use-fixtures :each
      (test-support/make-reset-runtime-fixture
        {:adapter uix-adapter/adapter :ambient-frame nil :init-fn ...}))

No ':async? true'. Without it make-reset-runtime-fixture returns the FN-FORM
fixture, and cljs.test/execution-strategy maps fn fixtures to :sync, which wraps
every test fn in disable-async. The file's row
'a-delayed-retained-callback-obeys-the-same-law' returns an (async done ...) object
in a browser, so disable-async throws ::async-disabled and test-var-block* rethrows
it as the bare String

    "Async tests require fixtures to be specified as maps.  Testing aborted."

That throw aborts the ENTIRE namespace -- every row in the file is lost -- and,
because it is thrown synchronously inside the preceding suite's 'done'
continuation, it also unwinds into whatever chain called that done.

WHY IT ONLY SHOWS IN THE BROWSER. In :node-test (mount/browser?) is false, so the
row returns the skip's (is true ...) rather than an async object, disable-async
never fires, and the node lane is green. Only npm run test:browser reaches it.

FIX. Add ':async? true' to that fixture's option map (the map-form variant --
see make-reset-runtime-fixture's docstring, 'Async map-form variant'). Every other
hicasso -dom-cljs-test suite with async rows already does this.

CAPTURED PROOF (branch worker/donefix-d3tc). A control namespace shaped exactly
like this witness -- fn-form fixture plus one browser-only async row, sorting

title: routing: realworld_http and realworld_resources register the same eleven route IDS from two files, so one silently replaces the other
description:
FLAGGED BUT DELIBERATELY NOT FILED by the rf2-wqnl worker (PR #7938), because it is a DIFFERENT HAZARD from the one that bead was ruled on. Filing it here so it is not lost.

WHAT IT SAW. implementation/.../examples/.../realworld_http and realworld_resources each register THE SAME ELEVEN ROUTE IDS, from two separate files. The registrar is id-keyed, so the second load silently REPLACES the first. Whichever file loads last wins, and nothing reports it.

WHY THIS IS NOT rf2-wqnl. That bead was about route PATHS colliding across applications in one node process — two distinct ids claiming one path string. This is the mirror image: ONE id claimed by two files. rf2-wqnl's census is explicitly built not to flag it, and its self-test pins that distinction as a deliberate rule: "one id from two files is an id replacement, not a path collision."

WHY IT MIGHT STILL BE FINE. Two ports of the same demo app may legitimately define the same route ids, and only one may ever load in a given bundle. VERIFY THAT BEFORE TREATING IT AS A DEFECT — read both files and establish whether they are ever loaded together. A verified "these are alternative ports, never co-resident" closes this bead and is a good outcome.

IF THEY ARE CO-RESIDENT, the question is what the registrar should do about a duplicate ID, and that is a design call rather than a repair — note the parallel with rf2-04tx's refuse-versus-ignore question and do not answer it unilaterally. STOP AND REPORT with the evidence.

DO NOT rename anyone's routes, and do not widen rf2-wqnl's census to cover ids — that census was ruled narrowly scoped on purpose, and its author drew the id/path line deliberately.
notes:
INVESTIGATED 2026-08-12 08:18 AUSEST. VERDICT: no defect. Read-only; no edit, no branch, no PR.

## The claim, checked at source, premise by premise

1. "the same eleven route ids" — HOLDS, exactly. Extracted and diffed both
   files' `reg-route` ids: 11 vs 11, identical sets, diff empty.
   :realworld/home, :realworld/home-tag, :realworld.auth/login,
   :realworld.auth/register, :realworld.user/settings, :realworld.editor/new,
   :realworld.editor/edit, :realworld.article/show, :realworld.profile/show,
   :realworld.profile/favorites, :rf.route/not-found.

2. "the second load silently REPLACES the first" — the replacement holds; the
   word "silently" does not. `registrar/register!` (core/src/re_frame/
   registrar.cljc:586) does `swap! reg assoc-in [kind id]`, so the resolver map
   is last-writer-wins. But line 598 also writes the EP-0023 provenance source
   store, where "cross-namespace duplicate (kind, id) registrations are BOTH
   retained". No provenance is lost.

3. "nothing reports it" — DOES NOT HOLD. Two surfaces fire on exactly this
   shape:
     - `:rf.registry/handler-replaced` (registrar.cljc:631) on every
       re-registration;
     - `:rf.warning/registration-collision` (registrar.cljc:485), whose
       `collision?` predicate keys on cross-source PROVENANCE — a different
       (ns, file, line) reassigning one id — which is precisely two files
       claiming one route id.
   `:route` is not incidental to that surface, it is the kind that shaped it.
   registrar.cljc:639-642 decouples the collision check from the
   handler-replaced dedup gate specifically because "a kind with no rotating
   :handler-fn — :route, :head — can be deduped-away by shape". And
   core/test/re_frame/registrar_warnings_test.clj carries an explicit
   rf2-3az1vn `:route` case (`collision-fires-for-no-handler-fn-kind-despite-
   shape-dedup`) pinning that the warning fires for routes and that the last
   registration wins. Both example files call the FACADE `rf/reg-route`, which
   is a coord-capturing macro (core.cljc:498 `rm/defreg-macro`; see also
   core.cljc:1636), so both sides carry the source-coords `collision?`
   requires. The warning fires.

## Are they ever co-resident? Two answers, and the split is the whole story

SHIPPED / BROWSER BUNDLES: NEVER. Three separate builds with three separate
output dirs — `:examples/realworld` (init-fn realworld-http.core/run),
`:examples/realworld-resources`, `:examples/realworld-resources-ui`
(implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:2199/2213/2230). Structural proof: ZERO
cross-references in either direction between the two source trees (grep both
ways, 0 hits each). Empirical proof: the built
`implementation/out/examples/realworld-resources/main.js` contains 11
occurrences of `realworld_resources.routing` and 0 of `realworld_http`.

CONSOLIDATED CLJS :node-test BUNDLE: YES. `:ns-regexp "cljs-test$"` matches
both `re-frame.realworld-cljs-test` and `re-frame.realworld-resources-cljs-
test`, both under the `adapters/reagent/test` source path. Empirical proof from
the built bootstrap `implementation/out/node-test.js`:
    3060: SHADOW_IMPORT("realworld_http.routing.js");
    3076: SHADOW_IMPORT("realworld_resources.routing.js");
http loads first, resources second, so at bundle load the registrar's 11 route
slots hold the RESOURCES table — exactly as the finding predicted.

## Why that co-residency is not this bead's defect

It is already known, already handled, and the handling names this exact pair.
rf2-h1vqa4 (+ rf2-22vzb) landed `sequester-app-namespaces!` /
`reinstate-app-namespaces!` in `core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc` for it.
The docstring at test_support.cljc:241 says it outright: "Two co-loaded example
apps that share id vocabulary (the RealWorld twins both register
:settings/load, ...)". And the registrar leg of both sequester helpers is
OWNERSHIP-GUARDED precisely for ids BOTH apps register (test_support.cljc:195,
:263) — "the registrar's single (kind, id) slot is the LAST writer's — for an id
BOTH apps register that may be a SIBLING's".

The wiring is live in the two suites:
  - realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs:146 sequesters the whole
    "realworld-http." tree at ns load, and :170 re-scrubs it per test;
  - realworld_cljs_test.cljs:158 reinstates "realworld-http." in its per-test
    :init-fn, so the http suite's route-dependent assertions (the auth-gate
    matrix at :870-980, the URL-shape cases at :842-865) run against the http
    route table, not the resources one.
No other co-loaded suite requires either `*.routing` ns, so nothing else is
exposed. (ssr_startup_recipe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:44-51 documents the same
bundle-co-load hazard class from the other side and avoids it by construction.)

## So there is no design call to make

The bead anticipated "what should the registrar do about a duplicate id" as an
open question paralleling rf2-04tx's refuse-vs-ignore. It is not open. Spec 001
§Re-registration of a different function already rules it: replace the slot,
retain both provenances, emit the collision warning. That ruling is
implemented, specced and tested, and the one bundle where these two files meet
already carries the hygiene that rf2-h1vqa4 built for it.

Closing as verified-no-defect. rf2-wqnl's census was NOT widened — its
id-vs-path line stands untouched. No route renamed. TESTING.md untouched.
close_reason: Verified no defect. The eleven-id overlap is real, but (a) the two apps are NEVER co-resident in any shipped bundle — three separate shadow builds, zero cross-references either way, 0 occurrences of realworld_http in the built realworld-resources main.js; (b) the ONE bundle where they do meet, the consolidated CLJS :node-test, is already handled by rf2-h1vqa4's sequester/reinstate hygiene, whose docstring names the RealWorld twins explicitly; and (c) the premise 'nothing reports it' does not hold at source — :rf.warning/registration-collision fires on cross-source provenance clash, with :route the very kind that motivated decoupling it from the shape-dedup gate (registrar.cljc:639-642, pinned by the rf2-3az1vn case in registrar_warnings_test.clj). The registrar's duplicate-id behaviour is Spec 001 ruled, so no design call is open. Full evidence in notes.

title: cljs.test: 21 remaining promise chains catch downstream of their own done
description:
Same defect rf2-d3tc fixed in reincarnation_paint_dom_cljs_test, in a second file, PROVEN BY CAPTURE rather than by resemblance.

SITE. implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/read_extent_dom_cljs_test.cljs:672-673

    (.then (fn [_] (done)))
    (.catch (fail-and-finish! done "activity-reveal witness" handle))

WHY IT IS A DEFECT. cljs.test/run-block hands 'done' a continuation that runs the
WHOLE REMAINDER of the run synchronously (this file's later rows, then every
namespace after it). Anything out there that throws unwinds back into the callback
that called 'done'. A .catch placed AFTER that callback claims the foreign failure
as its own: it prints this row's label against whichever test is current by then,
reads a DOM its own teardown already emptied, and calls 'done' a second time --
which does not merely warn, it re-forces run-block's delay, because a delay whose
body threw is still unrealized.

CAPTURED EVIDENCE (npm run test:browser, local Windows, branch worker/donefix-d3tc
with rf2-d3tc's fix applied and a throwing control namespace present):

    FAIL in (a-delayed-row-that-needs-async) (:)
    activity-reveal witness --  | ownership {:cells 0, :cell-refs 0, :boundaries 0, :edges 0}
    WARNING: Async test called done more than one time.

The blank message slot is the signature: what cljs.test throws there is a bare
String, which has no .message. The row is attributed to a foreign namespace's test.

FIX. The same positional repair rf2-d3tc took, and it is the shape
re-frame.hicasso.checkpoint-support/at-the-checkpoint already uses: split
fail-and-finish! into a report-only handler, put the .catch UPSTREAM of the .then
that calls done, and leave exactly ONE done at the tail of the chain with nothing
after it. Do not weaken the row's assertions.

NOT DONE IN rf2-d3tc because that bead's dispatch fenced the change to one file.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7937 (landed 727c185db792f9542a31b08c4a25b07313064b82) — broaden this exact owner beyond the one captured row. PR #7937 correctly repaired all three chains in reincarnation_paint_dom_cljs_test, but a landed-tree census finds 21 mechanically identical `.then (fn [_] (done))` then `.catch ... (done)` sites still present: 6 in Freehand (compiled_keyed_run:191, custom_element:302, mount_support:446/462, ownership_maps:541, pilot_react_interop:243); 10 in Hicasso (activity_suspense:408/582/720, kernel_commit_owns:323/401/460/566, read_extent:532/601/672); 4 in http_cljs_test:566/610/647/678; and 1 in Pair raw_state_test:367. Every one sits downstream of cljs.test/run-block's synchronous continuation and can claim a later row's throw, then call done twice. BOUNDED REPAIR: sweep these exact 21 sites, moving each rejection handler before one trailing done while preserving assertions and teardown; reuse each file's existing local helper shape and do not add a framework or broaden into unrelated async cleanup. Run the surface-appropriate browser/node lanes and retain a representative foreign-failure control long enough to prove attribution and no duplicate done, then remove it.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #7942 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7942). TRUE COUNT IS 22, NOT 21 — the bead's census missed implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/frame_ops_dom_cljs_test.cljs:93, which writes (.then (fn [] (done))) with a ZERO-ARITY fn and so slips a literal (fn [_] ...) scan. All 21 named sites were verified present at their named lines and repaired; frame_ops:93 makes 22. kernel_commit_owns:511 was repaired alongside them because that file's fail-and-finish! signature changed under it (safe: the trailing step now runs on both paths, so the duplicated (reset! !throw? false) is stated once).

WHY 21/22 IS THE RIGHT BOUND, MEASURED. A structural census of the landed tree finds 303 chains repo-wide (83 files) whose .catch sits downstream of a done-calling step. Of those, exactly 22 have a BARE (.then (fn [_] (done))) done-step — and that literal turns out to name precisely the chains where rf2-d3tc's swap is behaviour-preserving, because a .catch falling through to a bare done cannot re-run assertions or teardown. The other 281 bury done among assertions/teardown; behaviors_dom_cljs_test.cljs:179 is the counter-example, where a naive swap destroys the root TWICE on the failure path. Those need done split into its own trailing step first — a per-site judgement, not a positional edit. Filed as rf2-fyba with the full census and per-tree breakdown.

Testing aborted.', attributed to nobody, no misattribution, no duplicate done, ns announced once. Control then removed; restore verified by SHA-256, not git diff.

title: hic-028b — rename defhost's :ssr to :server + a sibling :fallback (the canonical two-policy spelling)
description:
# hic-028b — the `:ssr` -> `:server` + `:fallback` rename

Split out of rf2-hic-028 (portal helper + host server-policy witnesses),
whose PR landed the portal and the missing server-policy witness and
DELIBERATELY did not take this. Reasons, all verifiable at source:

## What the rename is

`defhost`'s declaration option is spelled `:ssr` today with THREE legal
values -- `:client-only`, `{:fallback <hiccup>}`, `:render`
(`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs`,
`declared-ssr` + `host-options` = `#{:callbacks :slots :ssr}`).

Every normative source spells it as TWO policies plus a sibling option:

- `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md`:11-14
  -- "one of two v0 policies: Render / Client-only", the fallback
  optional and belonging to Client-only.
- `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/ergonomics-api.md`:58 -- the
  `n/defcomponent` ABI, verbatim: `{:server :render}` / `{:server
  :client-only}`, omission means Client-only.
- `docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md` row 21 -- recommendation
  "keep `:server`", status `open`.
- The 22-chapter draft guide is uniform on it: ch09:58 says "The
  declaration takes four options: `:callbacks`, `:slots`, `:server`, and
  `:fallback`", and ch06/09/10/17/19 agree
  (`draft-guide/REWRITE-NOTES.md`:17-18 records the verification).

So: `:ssr` -> `:server` with values `#{:client-only :render}`, and
`:fallback` hoisted to a sibling declaration option legal only under
Client-only (Render + `:fallback` refuses -- the guide already teaches
that refusal, under the EXISTING id

4. **If B2:** close rf2-mo4o into rf2-hic-066 with a note carrying its file roster and acceptance so
   the sweep inherits them; optionally pre-rule row 21 without application.
5. Downstream unchanged either way: hic-048 and dormant hic-056 sit behind hic-046; the hic-060/068
   docs sit behind hic-066.

## Codex Recommendation

**Rule A1 + B1: presence takes Render, and `defhost` moves now to `:server` with a sibling
`:fallback`.** Treat the rename as pre-alpha convergence, not as a compatibility programme: add no
alias or deprecation path, and do not defer it to the later naming sweep.

The spelling divergence is already a programmer-facing defect. The host codec accepts
`#{:callbacks :slots :ssr}` and overloads `:ssr` with three value shapes, while the sibling native
declaration accepts only `:server` with `#{:client-only :render}`. The current guide corpus uses
`:server` throughout; its only `:ssr` occurrences explicitly identify the old three-shape form as
untaught. Thus the form a programmer copies from the guide succeeds for `n/defcomponent` and is
refused by `defhost`. The proposed shape fixes that at the declaration boundary: `:server` answers
which arm applies, while optional `:fallback` is the Client-only arm's payload. That is also easier
for tooling to display than an enum sometimes replaced by a nested map. Git history shows these
surfaces were introduced or rewritten on 10-11 August 2026, so preserving the split now would create
more migration work than changing it.

Presence is not Client-only in the implementation today: `react-dom/server` runs the tray and emits
its children. The mismatch is narrower. `presence-body` settles a new child only when
`roots/adopting-here?` is true; the sole product caller that provides that context is the client
hydration tree. A real server render therefore emits `:mounting`, while hydration's first client pass
emits `:present`. The executable seam test observes React's hydration complaint and replacement of
the stamped server node, while its tray-free control adopts cleanly; its hand-scoped control changes
the server phase to `:present`. Client-only would instead require a new refusal/gate/fallback path and
would remove every subtree wrapped by presence from server HTML--acceptable for a toast, but a bad SPA
default for routed-page transitions.

Use the smaller Render repair. The codec already has a stable, no-op `useSyncExternalStore` triple:
`codec/adopted?` is false during server rendering and hydration's first pass, and true on a fresh
client mount. Its inverse is exactly the fact presence needs to decide whether a newly encountered
child is born present. React documents that `getServerSnapshot` is used both while generating server
HTML and during hydration's initial client render
([`useSyncExternalStore`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useSyncExternalStore#adding-support-for-server-rendering)).
Reusing that internal seam replaces the current adoption-context hook rather than adding a hook,
needs no mutable request state, and works for direct React server APIs as well as any future Hicasso
server entry. Keep the root window for mismatch attribution; do not build a public server renderer or
request provider solely for presence.

Implementation proof should stay focused:

- For `defhost`, witness the final declaration matrix--default/explicit Client-only, Client-only with
  fallback, Render, and Render-plus-fallback refusal--while keeping existing complaint ids stable and
  making old `:ssr` fail loudly as an unknown option.
- For presence, drive real server bytes through `hydrateRoot`, require `:present` on both first
  renders, no React/framework mismatch, and retention of stamped server nodes; retain a fresh
  `createRoot` control that begins `:mounting`, plus the existing multi-root attribution and teardown
  witnesses.

==== END PRESERVED DOSSIER ====

"MAIN IS GREEN" IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT A BRANCH CAUSED A FAILURE — the failing job may be SURFACE-GATED AND SKIPPED ON MAIN (2026-08-12, PR #7945).

WHAT I DID. A node-test row reddened on a branch. I checked `gh run list --branch main` for the `tests` workflow, saw `success`, and concluded the branch caused it. I dispatched a fix-worker on that basis and told it so in the brief.

WHY IT WAS WRONG. `tests` reported success on main, but THE NODE-TEST JOB INSIDE IT WAS SKIPPED — surface-gated on paths the main commit did not touch. Run 31540419223 at the merge-base 5ac9d4aa17 never ran the job that was failing. A green workflow whose relevant JOB never executed is the same fail-open class this repo hunts everywhere else: it verifies the absence of bad news rather than the presence of good news.

THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT SETTLES THIS CLASS IN ONE STEP, from the worker:
  gh run list --workflow tests --limit 40 --json databaseId,headBranch,conclusion
then diff the FAIL line across branches. If an UNRELATED branch fails the identical assertion, the defect is pre-existing and no fix-worker should be pointed at the branch. Here a DOCS-ONLY branch (worker/cbident-hic029, two markdown files) had failed the same row four hours earlier with `actual: (not (= 4 1))`.

THREE MORE OF MY PREMISES FAILED IN THE SAME CALL, all from reading the rollup rather than the runs:
  - "Two CI failures" was ONE RUN, TWO ATTEMPTS. `gh pr checks` cannot show that; `gh run view` can.
  - "Identical numbers, so not a flake" holds PER RUNNER only. The same assertion gave 4→2 on one runner and 4→1 on another. FAILURE COUNTS WERE A STEP FUNCTION OF RUNNER SPEED, which is the signature of a wall-clock race, not of determinism.
  - So "deterministic numbers ⇒ not a flake" is a bad rule. The right question is whether the numbers are stable ACROSS RUNNERS.

THE ACTUAL MECHANISM, for the record: `arm-entry-reaper!` armed `setTimeout(…, 4)` at each entry's own minting inside `render-body`, while `lane/settle!` is `setTimeout(…, 0)` armed after ALL renders. Node drains one duration's timer list per pass, so the row turned on `settle-armed − first-mint < 3 ms` — and the harvest itself takes 1.2-2.0 ms. The test's own setup wall-clock was being charged against React's commit margin. Pre-existing on main; it only stops hitting other PRs once the fix merges.

THE RULE: before dispatching a fix-worker for a red on a branch, establish that the failing JOB actually RAN and PASSED somewhere the branch is not. A workflow-level "success" is not that. And sweep other branches for the same FAIL line first — it costs one command and it is the difference between fixing a defect and sending a worker to hunt one that is not there.

title: hic-089b — CI reachability for the budget-ledger gate (hot-zone workflow job)
description:
## Why

`rf2-hic-089` landed `implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_budget_ledger.py` and chained it into `npm run test:hicasso-invariants`. That chain's only hosted invocation is a step of test.yml's `cljs` job under `needs.detect_changed_surfaces.outputs.cljs_node_test == 'true'`.

The gate's inputs are docs/design/hicasso/product/budgets.md (the ledger), the same directory's substrate-decision.md (the disposition sections L3 resolves), and the witness files under implementation/hicasso/**. ONLY THE LAST ARMS THAT OUTPUT. Verified by direct classifier probe at the hic-089 branch head:

  $ bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh docs/design/hicasso/product/budgets.md
  cljs_node_test=false
  $ bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh docs/design/hicasso/product/budgets.md implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_budget_ledger.py implementation/package.json
  cljs_node_test=true

So a LEDGER-ONLY edit — exactly the edit this gate exists to police — skips every PR check. Same defect, same chain, same repair as test.yml's `hicasso-complaint-catalogue` job (its own comment records the identical hole at test.yml:875-905).

## What to add

An UNCONDITIONAL pure-Python job in .github/workflows/test.yml, a near-copy of `hicasso-complaint-catalogue`: checkout, setup-python 3.12, then `--self-test` and the live run. Unconditional rather than a new classifier output, for the reason that job's comment gives — a new arm is a fresh chance to make the same mistake and needs re-widening every time the checker learns to read another file. Sub-second static read; no node, no JVM.

It STAYS chained into test:hicasso-invariants: that chain is the local spine lane and the artefact's one-command run; the job is the CI reachability the chain cannot give it.

## Notes

HOT ZONE: .github/workflows/test.yml. Operator sequences it. The hic-089 worker stopped and reported rather than touching it.

The browser lane sits at 1293 tests / 8008 assertions; a moved count is evidence.

THE DEFECT (established rf2-d3tc, generalised rf2-qpns/#7942, re-proved under rf2-fyba).
cljs.test/run-block hands `done` a continuation that runs the WHOLE REMAINDER of the run
synchronously. A .catch downstream of a step that calls `done` claims whatever a later
namespace throws as this row's failure, prints it against this row's label, and calls
`done` a SECOND time — re-forcing run-block's unrealized delay, RE-RUNNING the offending
namespace, and stalling the lane with no summary line at all.

THE CURE. The rejection handler goes UPSTREAM of the .then that calls `done`: it reports
and returns nil but NEVER finishes. Exactly one `done` sits at the tail with nothing after
it. Worked example, and the reasoning, now live in the docstring of
`re-frame.test-support/poll-until` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc).

THIS IS NOT A MECHANICAL SWAP — that is the whole reason rf2-qpns did not do it.
Where the two arms do the SAME thing (an idempotent `restore`, a `destroy-frame!`, an
`unmount!`), hoist it into the single trailing step: written once, still run once per path.
Where they DIFFER, leave it. Two real examples from the repaired trees: a defensive
`(try (.unmount root) (catch ...))` that is failure-only because the success path already
unmounted upstream, and a `force-release!` that is failure-only because the success path
asserts the orderly `uninstall!` — hoisting either would have changed behaviour.

TWO SHAPES TO EXPECT (both hit in the repaired trees):
- THE .catch THAT IS THE ROW'S SUCCESS PATH — the row asserts the promise REJECTS, so
  `(is false "must reject")` sits in the .then and the real assertions in the .catch. Make
  the two handlers SIBLINGS of one TWO-ARG .then, then one trailing `done`. This is still
  an instance: the fulfilment arm calls `done` with the .catch downstream of it.
- HELPER-FORCED SHAPES — a local `(defn- unexpected! [done label e] ... (done))` takes
  `done` and calls it, so no caller can be repaired without it. Rename to `report-failure!`,
  drop the parameter, return nil (what #7942 did for the Hicasso `fail-and-finish!` helpers).

DO NOT adopt mount_support's `run-async` wholesale to avoid the work. Its handler reports
the generic "an async matrix cell rejected: ", which would REPLACE every row's own
diagnostic with one string. Measured under rf2-fyba: only 51 of freehand's 179 even
`:require` mount-support today. `run-async` stays right for NEW matrix cells.

DO NOT retune any suite to dodge the async window (the rf2-hic-029 refusal stands), do not
weaken assertions, and do not drop teardown to make a swap typecheck.

REBUILD THE SCANNER, do not trust line numbers (they drift). Signature: steps matching
^\s*\((\.then|\.catch|\.finally)\b, grouped into chains by equal indent with no intervening
lower-indent line; flag any chain where a step whose body contains (done) is followed by a
.catch step. Strip ;; comments first. The count is an UPPER BOUND — every chain needs
reading, and a source-located "left correct" is a fine disposition.

PROVE IT. A green aggregate is not proof — the runner echoes the console only on failure.
Use rf2-fyba's reproduction control: a throwaway ns whose name is a PREFIX EXTENSION of the
target ns (so nothing sorts between them), carrying a fn-form :each fixture plus an `async`
row — that selects cljs.test's :sync path, wraps the test in `disable-async`, and rethrows a
bare String synchronously inside whichever `done` continuation is running. Red before (the
target's own .catch message printed against the CONTROL's test name, control ns announced
TWICE, "WARNING: Async test called done more than one time", no summary), gone after (an
honest unhandled rejection naming the real cause, attributed to nobody). Delete the control;
verify every restore BY HASHING THE BYTES, not `git diff`.

Crossing the boundary in either direction without losing the contract: memo, lazy, and refs preserve the component marker and props ABI; a native parent renders a Hicasso view and a Hicasso view hosts a native component — one root, one frame, no ABI exposure.

This bead is the natural owner, which is why it is recorded here rather than filed separately.

Existing boundary-element/realize-children and the guide promise (:children props) as a realized ClojureScript vector. AUDIT #7874 REOPEN CLOSED by PR #7950 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7950).

REPAIR: h/as-component's outward-props copied React's props.children through unchanged. React's children slot is three shapes (absent / the child ITSELF at one / a JS array at several), so :children meant an element at one child and an array at two, against realize-children's realized-vector contract. A body that splices — (into [:ul] (:children props)) — THREW at one child. The prior PR's own test pinned the broken scalar.

New private outward-children normalises absent/single/multiple to the vector, members crossing by identity (no React.Children.toArray — it clones and re-keys), a nested array staying one member (React flattens at render; walking in would be the second level of conversion the bridge refuses), and an empty array answering nil so {items} over an empty list leaves :children absent — realize-children's own answer for (for [x []] ...).

WITNESS (falsifiable, not fail-open): the-children-a-body-reads-are-the-same-through-either-crossing — ONE view body rendered through BOTH crossings at 0/1/N/empty with the SAME child objects, asserting the props map AND the markup are equal on both sides.

NO new public export, NO new hook — I9 still two.
