title: cljs.test: 280 promise chains still catch downstream of their own done (the non-positional remainder of rf2-qpns)
description:
The remainder of rf2-qpns, measured rather than estimated. rf2-qpns fixed 22 chains
(PR: see that bead); this is the 280 it deliberately did not, and the reason they are a
DIFFERENT and larger job rather than more of the same.

THE DEFECT (unchanged, established by rf2-d3tc and re-proved under rf2-qpns).
`cljs.test/run-block` hands `done` a continuation that runs the WHOLE REMAINDER of the
run synchronously. A `.catch` placed downstream of the `.then` that calls `done` claims
whatever a later namespace throws, prints it against this row's label with a blank
message slot and a zeroed teardown census, and calls `done` a SECOND time — which
re-forces run-block's unrealized delay and RE-RUNS the offending namespace, then stalls
the lane. Captured on the browser lane under rf2-qpns with a throwing control:

  Testing re-frame.hicasso.read-extent-dom-cljs-test
  Testing re-frame.hicasso.read-extent-zz-control-dom-cljs-test
  FAIL in (a-delayed-row-that-needs-async) (:)
  activity-reveal witness --  | ownership {:cells 0, :cell-refs 0, :boundaries 0, :edges 0}
  Testing re-frame.hicasso.read-extent-zz-control-dom-cljs-test   <-- ns RE-RAN
  FAIL in (a-delayed-row-that-needs-async) (:)
  suspense-retry witness --  | ownership {:cells 0, :cell-refs 0, :boundaries 0, :edges 0}
  WARNING: Async test called done more than one time.

...followed by `Timed out after 360000ms waiting for cljs.test summary` — exit 1, no
summary line at all. The whole browser lane hangs.

WHY THESE 280 ARE NOT rf2-qpns's REPAIR. rf2-qpns took every chain whose done-calling
step is the BARE `(.then (fn [_] (done)))`. That literal is not cosmetic: when the
trailing step is nothing but `done`, moving the `.catch` above it is purely positional —
a `.catch` falling through to it cannot re-run assertions or re-tear-down. In these 280
the `done` is buried among assertions and teardown, so the same swap is NOT behaviour-
preserving. The counter-example, `behaviors_dom_cljs_test.cljs:179`:

  (.then  (fn [_] ... (ms/destroy-root! container root) (done)))
  (.catch (fn [e] (is false ...) (ms/destroy-root! container root) (done)))

A naive swap destroys the root TWICE on the failure path. Each of these needs `done`
split out into its own trailing step first, and whether the teardown belongs on both
paths is a judgement per site — sometimes it is idempotent (a `reset!`), sometimes it is
not (a root teardown, a released handle).

CENSUS (structural: a chain step containing `(done)` with a `.catch` step downstream of
it in the same `->` thread). 280 chains in 78 files. By tree:

  implementation/freehand        170
  tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp        39
  implementation/http             21
  implementation/hicasso          15
  tools/xray                      13

  implementation/adapters          8

  implementation/core              1   (a docstring example, not a live chain)

compiled_mount_dom 12, pilot_react_interop_dom 10, nrepl_test 9, native_abi_dom 9,
lane_window_dom 9, behavior_async_dom 7.

The scanner that produced this is ~60 lines of Python and is worth rebuilding rather
than trusting this list verbatim (line numbers drift). Signature: steps matching
`^\s*\((\.then|\.catch|\.finally)\b`, grouped into chains by equal indent with no
intervening lower-indent line; flag any chain where a step whose body contains `(done)`
is followed by a `.catch` step.

SIZING. This is not one bead. Suggest splitting by tree — freehand alone is 170 across
~45 files and would time out as a single dispatch. `implementation/freehand/test/
re_frame/freehand/mount_support.cljs`'s `each-mode` / `run-async` were already repaired
under rf2-qpns, which fixes the contract for every caller that routes through them, so
the freehand count may fall once someone checks how many of the 170 could simply ADOPT
those helpers instead of being repaired in place. That check is the right first move.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
rf2-53uz (pair-MCP, PR #7954) found the SCANNER SIGNATURE has a blind spot, so the census is a lower bound as well as an upper one — worth passing to the remaining sibling beads.

(1) NESTED STEPS SPLIT A CHAIN. Grouping strictly 'by equal indent' closes the outer chain the moment a deeper-indented .then appears inside a step body, so an outer .then->.catch pairing straddling a nested chain is lost. Keeping open chains on a STACK (pop only on a step or non-blank line at indent <= the chain's) recovers them. Effect measured on the shipped tree: implementation/freehand 179 -> 184, implementation/hicasso 16 -> 17; tools/xray 13, tools/machines-viz 1, tools/story 1 unchanged.

(2) (done) NEED NOT BE IN A STEP OF THE FLAGGED CHAIN. The stated signature looks for a STEP whose body contains (done). pair-MCP's dominant idiom put it in the -> HEAD EXPRESSION instead — inside the body-fn handed to a stub harness:

  (-> (with-canned-eval! canned
        (fn [] (-> (tool ...) (.then (fn [r] ... (done))))))   ; <- done in the HEAD
      (.catch (fn [e] (is false (str "rejected: " ...)) (done))))

The .catch is still downstream of a done and exhibits the full signature (foreign claim, double done, no summary) — the scanner simply cannot see it. 18 such chains in pair-MCP: handler_meta_test 14 (the ENTIRE file was invisible to the census) and tail_build_test 4. Fix: for each .catch step, test the region from the chain's head line (nearest preceding non-blank line at LOWER indent, scanning back past deeper ones) to that .catch for (done), rather than only the preceding steps' bodies.

I re-ran the extended scanner repo-wide: shape (2) occurs NOWHERE outside pair-MCP, so the sibling beads' FILE LISTS stand. Only their counts move, by (1).

Repo-wide remainder after PR #7954: 216 chains in 55 files.

Also note the half-repair trap this exposed: adding the trailing (.then (fn [_] (done))) WITHOUT removing the success arm's own (done) leaves the row calling done TWICE. Re-running the scanner after the edit catches it — a repaired chain must scan to zero, not merely gain a trailing step.

derivation and the count reconciliation.

`run-async` in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/mount_support.cljs, and their
docstrings now state the rule. Chains that already route through those helpers are fine.

rf2-fyba, its handler reports the generic "an async matrix cell rejected: ", so wholesale
adoption would replace every row's own diagnostic with one string, and only 51 of the 179
sit in files that even `:require` mount-support today.

`ms/destroy-root!` IS THE TEARDOWN TO WATCH. rf2-fyba's counter-example lives in this tree —
behaviors_dom_cljs_test.cljs:179 calls `(ms/destroy-root! container root)` on BOTH arms, so a
naive swap destroys the root twice. Hoist it into the single trailing step (written once, run
once per path); do not leave it on both sides of a swapped chain.

GATE: `npm run test:browser` from implementation/ — every one of these is a -dom-cljs-test
suite, so the browser lane is the one that decides. It sits at 1293 tests / 8008 assertions;
a moved count is evidence and must be explained. Run `npm run test:freehand` too (these files
are in the :node-test-freehand build). The bench/hicasso/* files are NOT in the browser-test
build (its ns-regexp excludes ^re-frame\.freehand\.bench\.) — check which lane covers each

cljs.test/run-block hands `done` a continuation that runs the WHOLE REMAINDER of the run
synchronously. A .catch downstream of a step that calls `done` claims whatever a later
namespace throws as this row's failure, prints it against this row's label, and calls
`done` a SECOND time — re-forcing run-block's unrealized delay, RE-RUNNING the offending
namespace, and stalling the lane with no summary line at all.

THE CURE. The rejection handler goes UPSTREAM of the .then that calls `done`: it reports
and returns nil but NEVER finishes. Exactly one `done` sits at the tail with nothing after
it. Worked example, and the reasoning, now live in the docstring of
`re-frame.test-support/poll-until` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc).

Where the two arms do the SAME thing (an idempotent `restore`, a `destroy-frame!`, an
`unmount!`), hoist it into the single trailing step: written once, still run once per path.
Where they DIFFER, leave it. Two real examples from the repaired trees: a defensive
`(try (.unmount root) (catch ...))` that is failure-only because the success path already
unmounted upstream, and a `force-release!` that is failure-only because the success path
asserts the orderly `uninstall!` — hoisting either would have changed behaviour.

  an instance: the fulfilment arm calls `done` with the .catch downstream of it.

DO NOT adopt mount_support's `run-async` wholesale to avoid the work. Its handler reports
the generic "an async matrix cell rejected: ", which would REPLACE every row's own
diagnostic with one string. Measured under rf2-fyba: only 51 of freehand's 179 even
`:require` mount-support today. `run-async` stays right for NEW matrix cells.

DO NOT retune any suite to dodge the async window (the rf2-hic-029 refusal stands), do not
weaken assertions, and do not drop teardown to make a swap typecheck.

^\s*\((\.then|\.catch|\.finally)\b, grouped into chains by equal indent with no intervening
lower-indent line; flag any chain where a step whose body contains (done) is followed by a
.catch step. Strip ;; comments first. The count is an UPPER BOUND — every chain needs
reading, and a source-located "left correct" is a fine disposition.

PROVE IT. A green aggregate is not proof — the runner echoes the console only on failure.
Use rf2-fyba's reproduction control: a throwaway ns whose name is a PREFIX EXTENSION of the
target ns (so nothing sorts between them), carrying a fn-form :each fixture plus an `async`
row — that selects cljs.test's :sync path, wraps the test in `disable-async`, and rethrows a
bare String synchronously inside whichever `done` continuation is running. Red before (the
target's own .catch message printed against the CONTROL's test name, control ns announced
TWICE, "WARNING: Async test called done more than one time", no summary), gone after (an
honest unhandled rejection naming the real cause, attributed to nobody). Delete the control;
verify every restore BY HASHING THE BYTES, not `git diff`.

title: hic-016 — Kernel: controlled input across Firefox and WebKit
description:
# hic-016 — Kernel: controlled input across Firefox and WebKit

**Phase**: 1 · **Wave**: B · **Est.**: L · **Depends**: hic-001
**Surface**: `implementation/hicasso/testbed/` (new spec.cjs) + `controlled.cljs` (distinct file — parallel with 010/012/015)

## Goal
The controlled-input law (same-turn echo, rejection/normalization, caret/selection, composition, revision reset) proven beyond Chromium: Firefox and WebKit via Playwright.

## Deliverables
- The existing Chromium witnesses extended to a three-browser matrix: echo, rejection, caret preservation, native IME composition + `beforeinput`, selection range/direction, revision reset, blur/unmount edges.
- Any browser-specific divergence either fixed in `controlled.cljs` or narrowed into an explicit per-control support/refusal policy (feeding the hic-005 table).
- Autofill and form-reset behavior recorded (full conformance matrix is hic-040 — do not duplicate).

## Acceptance
- Matrix green on all three engines in CI-runnable form; each refusal/narrowing documented with its browser and reason; sabotage: disabling the composition guard must turn the WebKit IME witness red.

## Worker notes
Read synth-codex §4.2; `codex/adversarial-risks.md` controlled-input row. Browser gates foreground, to completion.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7745 (2026-08-10; three lenses). CORRECTNESS: the full gate independently passed on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with 55 assertions per engine; all four recorded conducts were byte-identical, the six verdict teeth bit, lint and the scheduling checker were green, and no runtime defect was found. IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the claimed coverage floor is not fail-closed. MIN_CHECKS_PER_ENGINE=50 while selectionAcrossAnOutOfBandWrite and formResetAndFillProxy bank only 3 assertions each; deleting either whole section leaves 52 checks and belowFloor returns false. The recorded-row schema is also unpinned: all three engines returning {} gives divergenceReport zero problems, so every measured conduct can disappear together without reddening. Pin the required sections/record keys or otherwise make whole-section deletion fail before calling this witness durable. COMPLETENESS: rf2-ga8m already exactly owns the missing CI scheduling, so no duplicate was filed. The PR also explicitly uses synthetic composition events rather than a real Firefox/WebKit IME range; retain that honest limitation or explicitly amend/assign the native-IME acceptance before closing this owner.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7757 (2026-08-10 AUSEST) — the reopened fail-open findings are fixed; exact owner remains open for its original native-IME acceptance.

Correctness: the coverage verdict is now structural rather than a loose total. An independent direct drive confirms missing, under-counted, and extra sections each produce a problem; empty records produce four; missing-key and extra-record shapes each red; the valid shape is clean. The 13 mutation teeth bite. The merged three-engine gate passes Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit at 55 checks across the exact nine sections, with all four recorded rows byte-identical.

Implementation quality: only the testbed spec and its runner changed. The section roster stays declarative and ordered in the spec while the independent runner pins the exact name set/minima and exact record/key schema; whole-section deletion and unanimous empty recordings no longer disappear behind agreement. Full controlled gate, root ESLint, and git diff --check exit 0. No runtime semantics or composition claims were silently upgraded.

Completeness: do NOT close this owner yet. Its deliverable and acceptance still say native IME composition + beforeinput beyond Chromium and require disabling the composition guard to turn the WebKit IME witness red. The landed runner explicitly says real composition ranges and the abort signature remain Chromium-only; Firefox/WebKit dispatch a synthetic event sequence that cannot exercise the native range or an exchange killed without compositionend. PR #7757 deliberately retains that limitation but neither amends nor assigns the original acceptance, exactly the residual the #7745 audit said must be resolved before closure. Keep the work on this exact owner; no duplicate Bead. The separate missing CI schedule remains exactly owned by rf2-ga8m.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7760 (2026-08-10 AUSEST). The separate CI-scheduling residual is now complete and its exact owner rf2-ga8m is closed: GitHub actually ran the required Chromium/Firefox/WebKit job successfully. KEEP rf2-hic-016 OPEN for the native Firefox/WebKit IME acceptance already recorded by audits #7745/#7757. Also correct its exact documentation while doing that work: the new TESTING.md controlled-input row says “11 negative controls,” but the merged runner now contains and reports 13 mutation teeth after PR #7757. No duplicate Bead.
OPERATOR RULING (2026-08-10 19:47 AUSEST, Mike, in session) — OPTION 3: AMEND + ONE BOUNDED MANUAL WITNESS.
(1) AMENDED ACCEPTANCE: the synthetic composition sequence IS the recurring three-engine CI witness (ratified; the landed 55-check/13-teeth gate stands as-is). Real native-IME conduct on Firefox and WebKit is verified ONCE by a manual operator session, recorded, not automated, not recurring.
(2) THE MANUAL WITNESS: the operator types through a real Windows IME (e.g. Japanese Microsoft IME) in Playwright's Firefox and WebKit builds against a written checklist (~8 checks: draft text visible during composition; caret correct; app-db clean until commit; commit echo; Escape/abort mid-composition; compositionend ordering; revision reset during/after composition; blur mid-composition). Results are recorded in the hic-005 support table with date + engine builds. Anything strange becomes a bead.
(3) WORKER PREP (dispatchable now, one PR): amend this bead's acceptance text in the tracker-adjacent docs if restated anywhere; fix TESTING.md controlled-input row 11→13 negative controls; add the manual-witness checklist as a runnable session doc (page to open, the two launch commands with the PINNED Playwright CLI — never bare npx playwright install, per the rf2-ga8m note — and the checklist table with tick boxes); record in the hic-005 table that Chromium native IME is witness-verified, Firefox/WebKit native IME pending the manual session, synthetic gate green on all three.
(4) CLOSE RULE: this bead closes when the operator's session results are recorded. The prep PR does not close it.
FENCES: no changes to the landed gate's semantics; no automation attempts at real IME (ruled over-engineering).
NOTE (2026-08-10): the session-spawned prep worker was stopped before any edits (role correction: this session is a worker helping Mike, not the mayor). Ruling item (3) — the prep PR (TESTING.md 13-count fix; the manual-ime-session.md doc with pinned launch commands; the hic-005 support rows) — is READY FOR MAYOR DISPATCH as ordinary worker work. The full spec of the prep is in the ruling note above.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7787 (2026-08-10 AUSEST; completeness, correctness, implementation quality).

COMPLETENESS: the PR cleanly records the ruled two-tier acceptance, pinned launch path, pending Firefox/WebKit cells, and close rule; it correctly leaves this exact owner open. The bounded operator session is not yet sufficient to close it, however, because several advertised checks are not causally observable through the current screen-only surface.

CORRECTNESS: checks 3 and 6 overclaim what a controlled field can prove. During composition the DOM shows the IME draft, not a simultaneous independent view of app-db; `digits`/`empty` are reducer-refusing fields, so their final snap-back is unchanged even if composing inputs were dispatched, while `plain` consumes full values and makes progressive/duplicate writes visually idempotent. The screen therefore cannot establish “app-db clean until commit” or “arrives exactly once.” Checks 7 and 8 also provide only ordinary `on-click` bump/toggle buttons: manual activation can move focus and close/release the composition before the revision or unmount action, so it does not guarantee the claimed mid-exchange edge was exercised.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the session document is otherwise unusually runnable and disciplined; the Playwright 1.59.1 pin is present, the changed Markdown passes the slug gate and diff-check, and no automation is warranted. Before the session can close this owner, add the smallest screen-visible model/event trace needed for checks 3/6 and a focus-preserving way to trigger the mid-composition actions (or narrow those claims to what the UI truly observes). Also retain the PR's explicitly owed operator-source republication of the stale `adversarial-risks.md` acceptance. No duplicate Bead.
PR #7815 open. NOT CLOSED — per the operator's ruling this bead closes on the operator's SESSION RESULTS, not on a PR. Recording the measurement so the session has it.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND, and it is subtler than "some rows were Chromium-only". The job NAME was accurate: every section the spec contained really did run in all three engines, because the runner cannot run one in fewer. Four behaviours the bead names were simply NOT IN THE SPEC AT ALL:
  - a revision arriving MID-COMPOSITION — asserted only by front/revision_dom_cljs_test:512 on the :browser-test lane, which launches Chromium and only Chromium (scripts/run-browser-tests.cjs:31)
  - an ACCEPTING model taking every composing update — same file (:575), same one-engine lane

equal, heaviest first. The four are PARALLEL-SAFE with each other: disjoint file sets, all
under implementation/freehand/test/, no shared file. rf2-fyba's own comment carries the full
derivation and the count reconciliation.

MOUNT_SUPPORT IS ALREADY CORRECT — DO NOT RE-REPAIR IT. #7942 fixed `each-mode` and
`run-async` in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/mount_support.cljs, and their
docstrings now state the rule. Chains that already route through those helpers are fine.
Equally, DO NOT convert these chains TO `run-async` to avoid the work — measured under
rf2-fyba, its handler reports the generic "an async matrix cell rejected: ", so wholesale
adoption would replace every row's own diagnostic with one string, and only 51 of the 179
sit in files that even `:require` mount-support today.

`ms/destroy-root!` IS THE TEARDOWN TO WATCH. rf2-fyba's counter-example lives in this tree —
behaviors_dom_cljs_test.cljs:179 calls `(ms/destroy-root! container root)` on BOTH arms, so a
naive swap destroys the root twice. Hoist it into the single trailing step (written once, run
once per path); do not leave it on both sides of a swapped chain.

GATE: `npm run test:browser` from implementation/ — every one of these is a -dom-cljs-test
suite, so the browser lane is the one that decides. It sits at 1293 tests / 8008 assertions;
a moved count is evidence and must be explained. Run `npm run test:freehand` too (these files
are in the :node-test-freehand build). The bench/hicasso/* files are NOT in the browser-test
build (its ns-regexp excludes ^re-frame\.freehand\.bench\.) — check which lane covers each
before claiming it green.

THE DEFECT (established rf2-d3tc, generalised rf2-qpns/#7942, re-proved under rf2-fyba).
cljs.test/run-block hands `done` a continuation that runs the WHOLE REMAINDER of the run
synchronously. A .catch downstream of a step that calls `done` claims whatever a later
namespace throws as this row's failure, prints it against this row's label, and calls
`done` a SECOND time — re-forcing run-block's unrealized delay, RE-RUNNING the offending
namespace, and stalling the lane with no summary line at all.

THE CURE. The rejection handler goes UPSTREAM of the .then that calls `done`: it reports
and returns nil but NEVER finishes. Exactly one `done` sits at the tail with nothing after
it. Worked example, and the reasoning, now live in the docstring of
`re-frame.test-support/poll-until` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc).

THIS IS NOT A MECHANICAL SWAP — that is the whole reason rf2-qpns did not do it.
Where the two arms do the SAME thing (an idempotent `restore`, a `destroy-frame!`, an
`unmount!`), hoist it into the single trailing step: written once, still run once per path.
Where they DIFFER, leave it. Two real examples from the repaired trees: a defensive
`(try (.unmount root) (catch ...))` that is failure-only because the success path already
unmounted upstream, and a `force-release!` that is failure-only because the success path
asserts the orderly `uninstall!` — hoisting either would have changed behaviour.

TWO SHAPES TO EXPECT (both hit in the repaired trees):
- THE .catch THAT IS THE ROW'S SUCCESS PATH — the row asserts the promise REJECTS, so
  `(is false "must reject")` sits in the .then and the real assertions in the .catch. Make
  the two handlers SIBLINGS of one TWO-ARG .then, then one trailing `done`. This is still
  an instance: the fulfilment arm calls `done` with the .catch downstream of it.
- HELPER-FORCED SHAPES — a local `(defn- unexpected! [done label e] ... (done))` takes
  `done` and calls it, so no caller can be repaired without it. Rename to `report-failure!`,
  drop the parameter, return nil (what #7942 did for the Hicasso `fail-and-finish!` helpers).

DO NOT adopt mount_support's `run-async` wholesale to avoid the work. Its handler reports
the generic "an async matrix cell rejected: ", which would REPLACE every row's own
diagnostic with one string. Measured under rf2-fyba: only 51 of freehand's 179 even
`:require` mount-support today. `run-async` stays right for NEW matrix cells.

DO NOT retune any suite to dodge the async window (the rf2-hic-029 refusal stands), do not
weaken assertions, and do not drop teardown to make a swap typecheck.

REBUILD THE SCANNER, do not trust line numbers (they drift). Signature: steps matching
^\s*\((\.then|\.catch|\.finally)\b, grouped into chains by equal indent with no intervening
lower-indent line; flag any chain where a step whose body contains (done) is followed by a
.catch step. Strip ;; comments first. The count is an UPPER BOUND — every chain needs
reading, and a source-located "left correct" is a fine disposition.

PROVE IT. A green aggregate is not proof — the runner echoes the console only on failure.
Use rf2-fyba's reproduction control: a throwaway ns whose name is a PREFIX EXTENSION of the
target ns (so nothing sorts between them), carrying a fn-form :each fixture plus an `async`
row — that selects cljs.test's :sync path, wraps the test in `disable-async`, and rethrows a
bare String synchronously inside whichever `done` continuation is running. Red before (the
target's own .catch message printed against the CONTROL's test name, control ns announced
TWICE, "WARNING: Async test called done more than one time", no summary), gone after (an
honest unhandled rejection naming the real cause, attributed to nobody). Delete the control;

Batch 1's reproduction control captured behavior_matrix INHERITING the misattribution the moment behaviors_dom_cljs_test stopped claiming it: with a throwaway ns sorting immediately after behaviors-dom-cljs-test, the repaired tree printed 'the compiled behavior mount rejected: Async tests require fixtures to be specified as maps.' title: The spine's ambient use-subscribe cannot resolve a frame under react-dom/server
description:
Measured while writing rf2-hic-034's parity suite (PR #7962), reported rather than fixed.

re-frame.substrate.spine's ONE-ARGUMENT use-subscribe resolves the React-context tier through frame/require-current-frame!, which reaches the context by reading context._currentValue. That is a CLIENT-render fact: react-dom/server does not populate it, so the hook refuses with :rf.error/no-frame-context on the server.

Measured both ways, on the node lane, under React 19.2.0:
  - a UIx defui calling (uix-adapter/use-subscribe [::q]) inside a Hicasso tree under impl.mount/provider - REFUSED;
  - the same component wrapped in the adapter's OWN re-frame.adapter.uix/frame-provider, which SCOPES the frame the documented way - STILL REFUSED.

The two-argument explicit form (use-subscribe frame-kw query-v) works, and Spec 002's own error ladder names 'pass an explicit {:frame <id>}' as the third of three ways to establish a scope - so there IS a supported route and hic-034's UIx arm takes it, saying so where it bites.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE TEST. Every UIx-adapter use-subscribe witness in the repo is a *_dom_cljs_test - the browser lane - so the server behaviour of the ambient form has never been exercised. An application server-rendering a UIx tree hits this on its first page, and the diagnostic it gets names 'no established scope' when the author has established one.

THREE POSSIBLE DISPOSITIONS and this bead does not pick one:
  1. repair - resolve the context through React's own dispatcher (useContext) rather than by reading _currentValue, so the server renderer answers;
  2. document - state in re-frame.adapter.uix and in the SSR docs that the ambient form is client-only and the explicit form is the SSR route;
  3. refuse - decide the ambient form is a client affordance by design and make the refusal say so, naming the explicit form in its recovery.

The third is the cheapest and the current message already half-does it; the first is the one an author would expect.

Adjacent: rf2-hic-046 (per-surface SSR/hydration witnesses) is about to write SSR rows across surfaces and will meet this.

title: cljs.test: 40 HELPER-FORCED promise chains the rf2-fyba scanner signature cannot see (freehand 184 -> 224)
description:
FILES — 40 chains the rf2-fyba campaign's scanner signature CANNOT SEE, in four
implementation/freehand files named in NO bead:

  freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/typeahead_witness_dom_cljs_test.cljs   12
  freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/virtual_collection_dom_cljs_test.cljs  11
  freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/splitter_dom_cljs_test.cljs             9
  freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/controls_kit_dom_cljs_test.cljs         8

THE BLIND SPOT. rf2-fyba's stated signature flags "a step whose body contains
(done), followed by a .catch step". These four files route BOTH arms through
local helpers, so no chain step contains a literal (done) anywhere:

  (defn- finish! [container root done]
    (ms/destroy-root! container root)
    (ms/residue-clean! "FH-CTRL-018 — after teardown")
    (done))

  (defn- fail-and-finish! [container root done]
    (fn [e]
      (is false (str "the browser step rejected: " e))
      (ms/destroy-root! container root)
      (done)))

  (-> (render! root plain-field)
      (.then (fn [_] … (finish! container root done)))
      (.catch (fail-and-finish! container root done)))

The .catch IS downstream of a step that finishes, so the chain exhibits the full
signature — foreign claim, double done, namespace re-run. The scanner reports
these four files as ZERO.

THIS IS THE THIRD BLIND SPOT, and the first two are already recorded: rf2-53uz
found (1) nested steps splitting a chain under strict equal-indent grouping
(freehand 179 → 184) and (2) `(done)` living in the `->` head expression
(pair-MCP only). This is (3), and it is the largest: freehand 184 → **224**.

NOT SPECULATION — REPRODUCED IN THE BROWSER. Under rf2-d2xz's reproduction
control (a throwaway ns sorting as a prefix extension of the target, fn-form
:each fixture + async row, rethrowing a bare String inside the running `done`
continuation), with rf2-d2xz's five files REPAIRED, `npm run test:browser`
still printed:

  Testing re-frame.freehand.substrate-dom-cljs-test-zz-control-dom-cljs-test
  FAIL in (a-row-that-needs-async) (:)
  the browser step rejected: Async tests require fixtures to be specified as maps.
  WARNING: Async test called done more than one time.

`the browser step rejected: ` is `fail-and-finish!`'s own message — one of these
four files claiming a foreign namespace's throw as its own row's failure. With
the same five files REVERTED the same run printed THREE such claims and announced
the control namespace THREE times; repaired, it is down to this ONE, and this one
comes from here.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE CAMPAIGN. rf2-o0n1 (4 of 4) says "take every
implementation/freehand hit NOT claimed by parts 1-3" — but it derives that set
from the same signature, so a worker following it lands on 0 for these files and
the 40 are missed by the whole four-part split. `git grep` for the file names
across the tracker returns nothing: they are named in no bead at all.

THE CURE is the one the campaign has landed four times, plus the helper rename
#7942 used for the three Hicasso `fail-and-finish!` helpers and #7951 used for
`exact_render_capture`'s `unexpected!`: rename `fail-and-finish!` to
`report-failure!`, DROP the `done` parameter, return nil. `finish!` keeps `done`
and becomes the single trailing step. Per chain:

  (-> (render! root plain-field)
      (.then (fn [_] … ))
      (.catch (report-failure! ))
      (.then (fn [_] (finish! container root done))))

Note `finish!` already carries the shared teardown (`ms/destroy-root!`) that
`fail-and-finish!` duplicates — so hoisting is the natural shape here rather
than a judgement call. But `finish!` ALSO calls `ms/residue-clean!`, which
`fail-and-finish!` deliberately does NOT ("a second failure attributed to the
leak rule would bury the one that actually happened"). That asymmetry is
load-bearing and MUST survive: the trailing step cannot simply call `finish!`
on both paths without changing what a failing row reports. Read the two arms
before writing the trailing step.

GATE: `npm run test:browser` from `implementation/` — all four are
`-dom-cljs-test` suites. It sits at 1293 tests / 8010 assertions on main as of
2026-08-12 (NOT the 8008 several beads still quote — that figure is from #7951
and two assertions have landed since). No deftest is added or removed, so a
moved count is a mistake.

REBUILD THE SCANNER with all three corrections. Signature: steps matching
^\s*\((\.then|\.catch|\.finally)\b, chains kept on a STACK so a nested step does
not split its parent; a step counts as finishing if its body contains `(done)`
OR calls a local `defn`/`defn-` that takes a `done` parameter and calls it; and
check the `->` head expression too. Beware `\b` in the helper-name regex —
Clojure names end in `!`/`?`/`*`, which are non-word characters, so `\b` never
matches after them and the whole class silently reports zero. That is exactly
how these 40 went missing.

PROVE IT with rf2-fyba's reproduction control, both directions, and delete the
control verifying the restore BY HASHING THE BYTES.
close_reason: Repaired in PR #7964 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7964), branch worker/helper-29ua. All 40 helper-forced chains in the four files repaired: finish! -> teardown-clean! (drops done, success arm only), fail-and-finish! -> report-failure! (drops done, returns nil), one done at the tail. The ms/residue-clean! success-only asymmetry preserved in all four; teardown deliberately NOT hoisted. 16 nested catches absorbed by their parents. Census reproduced exactly at source (12/11/9/8) by an independent s-expression reader, calibrated against 184 blind / 224 helper-aware on the pre-repair tree. Post-repair the four scan to ZERO and freehand drops 140 -> 100. Control both directions: reverted = 3 foreign claims + control ns announced 3x + double-done, exit 1; repaired = 0 claims, announced once, throw escapes. Restore hash-verified. Browser gate 1293/8010 0F0E before and after, captured exit 0.

title: hic-044 — The typeahead resource-demand witness
description:
# hic-044 — The typeahead resource-demand witness

**Phase**: 4 · **Wave**: E · **Est.**: M · **Depends**: hic-025, hic-039 (the criteria are frozen before this bead starts — real pre-registration)
**Surface**: witness app + tests (new files only; no runtime changes — this bead *measures the need*, hic-050 decides)

## Goal
The deciding witness for the flagship: a real typeahead on today's honest answer (events + subs + settle-merge), instrumented so hic-050 can judge whether committed-read resource demand earns adoption.

## Deliverables
- The typeahead: debounce, stale-reply suppression, supersession, refresh-with-data, cancellation, abandoned-render behavior — built with current primitives, every awkward seam documented.
- Instrumentation: what ceremony exists, what defect classes threaten, what a committed-read demand would remove — recorded against the criteria hic-039 froze (cite its commit hash).

## Acceptance
Witness green incl. late-reply-cannot-clobber; the ceremony/defect report complete enough for a verdict without re-running.

## Worker notes
Read synth-codex §7 flagship paragraph + its three fences (reuse committed read membership; abandoned renders acquire nothing; no second ledger).

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).
close_reason: Witness landed in PR #7965 (branch worker/typeahead-hic044). A typeahead on today's public door — debounce, supersession, stale-reply suppression, refresh-with-data, cancellation, two async resources, hover prefetch — with no runtime change. Report: docs/design/hicasso/product/resource-demand-witness.md, written against the criteria frozen at afbb58febc. C1 census is READ OFF THE SOURCE by a .clj macro (typeahead/census.clj) and pinned by l0-cljs-test: 15 regions, 9 OWNERSHIP (6 release, 3 acquire), 5 POLICY, 1 DOMAIN. C2: three classes killed by construction with reachability mutations built from the app's own fns minus one thing; two of the six registered classes are UNREACHABLE on the status quo and are reported as not demonstrated rather than claimed; the late-reply class is reported NOT killed (policy stays explicit). Acceptance row a-late-reply-cannot-clobber-a-newer-term is green with its clobbering control. C3: abandonment population counted on the witness — 3 bodies plain vs 6 under StrictMode, 1 request either way. C5: retained structures measured at three moments (closed 5/5/2/5/2, open 8/8/3/8/3, closed again 8/5/2/5/3) — read-shaped structures return to baseline exactly, resource-shaped ones wait for the reaper. C6 flagged as UNMEASURED here (bytes cited from the landed pinned rows, not re-derived), and C3's on-the-witness scope flagged, so rf2-hic-050 can apply C7 rather than guess. Gates captured: fast-PR spine exit 0 (node step 13387 tests/67527 assertions, 0 failures); npm run test:browser exit 0 (1299 tests/8045 assertions, 0 failures); check_doc_slugs exit 0; check_provenance_pins --changed-since origin/main exit 0. Inversion proofs captured for both lanes with restoration verified by hash. NOT merged — the mayor merges.

title: cljs.test: a closure that closes over done finishes the row — 32 chains outside freehand
description:
THE THIRD CLASS, found by rf2-o0n1's reproduction control and closed inside implementation/freehand by PR for rf2-o0n1. This bead is the REMAINDER, outside freehand.

THE SIGNATURE GAP. rf2-fyba's scanner sees a literal (done) in a chain step. rf2-29ua's sees a helper that TAKES done as a parameter. NEITHER sees a let/letfn-bound closure that CLOSES OVER the row's done:

    (let [finish (fn [] (restore) (teardown! container root) (done))]
      (-> p (.then (fn [_] ... (finish)))
            (.catch (fn [e] (is false ...) (finish)))))

Same defect exactly: the .catch sits downstream of a step that FINISHED the row, so it claims whatever a later namespace throws, prints it against this row's label, and fires done a SECOND time — re-forcing run-block's unrealized delay and re-running the offending namespace. run-browser-tests.cjs promotes 'Async test called done more than one time' to a FATAL match (since #7190), so each of these can red the browser lane.

MEASURED, with a closure-aware s-expression reader (top-level defns taking done; letfn bindings; let-bound fns; plus cross-ns run-async/each-mode): 37 chains in 12 files repo-wide. 5 in 2 files were freehand's and are repaired under rf2-o0n1. THE REMAINING 32, in 10 files:

  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/form_3_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs            4  (done!)
  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/frame_provider_context_dom_cljs_test.cljs      4  (done! / finish / teardown-and-done!)
  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/views_synthetic_event_frame_dom_cljs_test.cljs 1  (finalize!)
  implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim_strict_mode_dom_cljs_test.cljs        1  (done!)
  implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim_synthetic_event_frame_dom_cljs_test.cljs 1  (finalize!)
  implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_abi_dom_cljs_test.cljs                   9  (fail-and-finish!)
  implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_hooks_dom_cljs_test.cljs                 8  (fail-and-finish!)
  implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_view_unmount_teardown_mounted_dom_cljs_test.cljs 2  (done!)
  tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/port_to_build_test.cljs                     1  (.finally after done)
  tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/a11y_stale_settlement_cljs_test.cljs                      1

NOTE the two hicasso native_* files are ALSO the only two the LITERAL signature still sees (17 chains) — they are the same rows counted twice, not 17 + 17. Repairing them once closes both censuses.

THE CURE, unchanged: the rejection handler goes UPSTREAM of the step that finishes. Rename the closure so its name stops promising to finish (teardown-clean! / release / report-failure!), drop the (done) from it, return nil, and put exactly one (done) at the tail with nothing after it. Do NOT hoist teardown mechanically — across six batches the split ran roughly half hoisted, half left in place, and the dominant reason to leave it is the failure arm doing LESS.

PROVE IT with the campaign's reproduction control: a throwaway ns sorting as a PREFIX EXTENSION of the target, carrying a fn-form :each fixture plus an async row, which makes cljs.test throw a bare String synchronously inside whichever done continuation is running. Reverted it reproduces the misattribution and the double-done; repaired, the throw escapes attributed to nobody. rf2-o0n1's PR carries a three-run gradient (2 claims -> 1 -> 0) as the worked example.

GATES: npm run test:browser decides the -dom-cljs-test files; tools/story and the MCP tool have their own lanes.

title: Prefetch: only the hover modality is measured in a real browser
description:
re-frame.routing.link/prefetch-intent-keys is the closed class [:on-mouse-enter :on-focus :on-touch-start], and Spec 012 sells all three as credible-intent triggers.

WHAT IS MEASURED TODAY:
- implementation/routing/test/re_frame/route_link_cljs_test.cljs :: prefetch-intent-dispatches-on-each-credible-intent-position covers all THREE, but by calling the handler off the attrs map directly (`fire-intent!` does `(h (mk-event {}))`). That proves the handler is installed under the key and dispatches the right payload to the right frame. It does not prove React attaches it to the real element under the real event name.
- implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/route_link_dom_cljs_test.cljs :: ui-route-link-prefetch-intent-warms-on-real-dom-intent drives a REAL DOM event - mouseover only. Focus and touchstart have no real-DOM arm on any surface.

WHY IT IS MORE THAN NOTHING: link.cljc's own docstring records that `re-frame.ui/route-link` still writes the three positions out LITERALLY rather than reading the class through the :routing/prefetch-intent-keys seam ("a position added here reaches rf/route-link and v/route-link and misses ui/route-link", rf2-drpa3.57). A literal copy is exactly the thing a real-DOM arm per position would catch.

WORK: add a :on-focus arm (a real .focus() on the anchor - the Tab-to-a-link gesture) and a :on-touch-start arm (a real touchstart) beside the existing hover deftest in implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/route_link_dom_cljs_test.cljs, reusing that file's `prefetch-log` helper. Keep the existing cold-link control on each gesture (a link that did not opt in warms nothing). Gate: npm run test:browser.

NOT rf2-hic-042's to land: Hicasso's h/route-link DECLINES :prefetch outright in v0 (:rf.error/hicasso-route-link-prefetch-declined), so the Hicasso surface has no prefetch to witness, and admitting the key is naming-ledger row 36, still open.

title: cljs.test: 54 promise chains in the freehand long tail catch downstream of their own done (4 of 4)
description:
FILES (4 of 4) — 54 chains across the 24 files carrying 3 or fewer. Rebuild the scanner
and take every implementation/freehand hit NOT claimed by parts 1-3. Includes
root_preflight_dom, presence_nil_key_dom, ownership_motion_dom, host_mounted_dom,
controlled_input_matrix_dom, buffered_controller_dom, bench/hicasso/ssr/spike (3 each);
root_teardown_dom, projection_roster_dom, presence_dom, presence_commit_ownership_dom,
ownership_radix_dom, ownership_maps_dom, compiled_keyed_run_dom, bench/hicasso/ssr/spike_dom,
bench/hicasso/ssr/instance_key_payload_dom (2 each); and 15 files at 1.
NOTE: compiled_keyed_run_dom and ownership_maps_dom were PARTIALLY repaired by #7942 (one
chain each) — the repaired chains are the model, the others are the work.

implementation/freehand carries 179 of rf2-fyba's 248 remaining chains across 46 files —
too many for one dispatch, which rf2-fyba says explicitly. Split into four by file, roughly
equal, heaviest first. The four are PARALLEL-SAFE with each other: disjoint file sets, all
under implementation/freehand/test/, no shared file. rf2-fyba's own comment carries the full
derivation and the count reconciliation.

MOUNT_SUPPORT IS ALREADY CORRECT — DO NOT RE-REPAIR IT. #7942 fixed `each-mode` and
`run-async` in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/mount_support.cljs, and their
docstrings now state the rule. Chains that already route through those helpers are fine.
Equally, DO NOT convert these chains TO `run-async` to avoid the work — measured under
rf2-fyba, its handler reports the generic "an async matrix cell rejected: ", so wholesale
adoption would replace every row's own diagnostic with one string, and only 51 of the 179
sit in files that even `:require` mount-support today.

`ms/destroy-root!` IS THE TEARDOWN TO WATCH. rf2-fyba's counter-example lives in this tree —
behaviors_dom_cljs_test.cljs:179 calls `(ms/destroy-root! container root)` on BOTH arms, so a
naive swap destroys the root twice. Hoist it into the single trailing step (written once, run
once per path); do not leave it on both sides of a swapped chain.

GATE: `npm run test:browser` from implementation/ — every one of these is a -dom-cljs-test
suite, so the browser lane is the one that decides. It sits at 1293 tests / 8008 assertions;
a moved count is evidence and must be explained. Run `npm run test:freehand` too (these files
are in the :node-test-freehand build). The bench/hicasso/* files are NOT in the browser-test
build (its ns-regexp excludes ^re-frame\.freehand\.bench\.) — check which lane covers each
before claiming it green.

THE DEFECT (established rf2-d3tc, generalised rf2-qpns/#7942, re-proved under rf2-fyba).
cljs.test/run-block hands `done` a continuation that runs the WHOLE REMAINDER of the run
synchronously. A .catch downstream of a step that calls `done` claims whatever a later
namespace throws as this row's failure, prints it against this row's label, and calls
`done` a SECOND time — re-forcing run-block's unrealized delay, RE-RUNNING the offending
namespace, and stalling the lane with no summary line at all.

THE CURE. The rejection handler goes UPSTREAM of the .then that calls `done`: it reports
and returns nil but NEVER finishes. Exactly one `done` sits at the tail with nothing after
it. Worked example, and the reasoning, now live in the docstring of
`re-frame.test-support/poll-until` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc).

THIS IS NOT A MECHANICAL SWAP — that is the whole reason rf2-qpns did not do it.
Where the two arms do the SAME thing (an idempotent `restore`, a `destroy-frame!`, an
`unmount!`), hoist it into the single trailing step: written once, still run once per path.
Where they DIFFER, leave it. Two real examples from the repaired trees: a defensive
`(try (.unmount root) (catch ...))` that is failure-only because the success path already
unmounted upstream, and a `force-release!` that is failure-only because the success path
asserts the orderly `uninstall!` — hoisting either would have changed behaviour.

TWO SHAPES TO EXPECT (both hit in the repaired trees):
- THE .catch THAT IS THE ROW'S SUCCESS PATH — the row asserts the promise REJECTS, so
  `(is false "must reject")` sits in the .then and the real assertions in the .catch. Make
  the two handlers SIBLINGS of one TWO-ARG .then, then one trailing `done`. This is still
  an instance: the fulfilment arm calls `done` with the .catch downstream of it.
- HELPER-FORCED SHAPES — a local `(defn- unexpected! [done label e] ... (done))` takes
  `done` and calls it, so no caller can be repaired without it. Rename to `report-failure!`,
  drop the parameter, return nil (what #7942 did for the Hicasso `fail-and-finish!` helpers).

DO NOT adopt mount_support's `run-async` wholesale to avoid the work. Its handler reports
the generic "an async matrix cell rejected: ", which would REPLACE every row's own
diagnostic with one string. Measured under rf2-fyba: only 51 of freehand's 179 even
`:require` mount-support today. `run-async` stays right for NEW matrix cells.

DO NOT retune any suite to dodge the async window (the rf2-hic-029 refusal stands), do not
weaken assertions, and do not drop teardown to make a swap typecheck.

REBUILD THE SCANNER, do not trust line numbers (they drift). Signature: steps matching
^\s*\((\.then|\.catch|\.finally)\b, grouped into chains by equal indent with no intervening
lower-indent line; flag any chain where a step whose body contains (done) is followed by a
.catch step. Strip ;; comments first. The count is an UPPER BOUND — every chain needs
reading, and a source-located "left correct" is a fine disposition.

PROVE IT. A green aggregate is not proof — the runner echoes the console only on failure.
Use rf2-fyba's reproduction control: a throwaway ns whose name is a PREFIX EXTENSION of the
target ns (so nothing sorts between them), carrying a fn-form :each fixture plus an `async`
row — that selects cljs.test's :sync path, wraps the test in `disable-async`, and rethrows a
bare String synchronously inside whichever `done` continuation is running. Red before (the
target's own .catch message printed against the CONTROL's test name, control ns announced
TWICE, "WARNING: Async test called done more than one time", no summary), gone after (an
honest unhandled rejection naming the real cause, attributed to nobody). Delete the control;
verify every restore BY HASHING THE BYTES, not `git diff`.
notes:
MAYOR — SCOPE RESTATED, 2026-08-12, from rf2-29ua's worker (PR #7964). READ THIS BEFORE STARTING.

THIS BEAD'S SCOPE WAS "every hit not claimed by parts 1-3", AND THAT PHRASE DERIVED FROM A SIGNATURE PROVEN BLIND THREE SEPARATE WAYS. It is now correct as written — but only once #7964 lands. RESTATE IT AS: "THE 100 REMAINING CHAINS THAT THE LITERAL-(done) SIGNATURE ALREADY SEES, IN 38 FILES." The helper-forced class is CLOSED by rf2-29ua and is disjoint from yours — the blind signature reads 0 in its four files both before and after.

THE COUNT, derived by an independent s-expression reader (not a line matcher) carrying all three corrections, calibrated against both campaign landmarks:
  literal (done), stack-correct : 184 pre-repair / 46 files -> 100 on main / 38 files
  + helper-aware                : 224 pre-repair / 50 files -> 140 -> 100 after #7964
184 and 224 reproduce rf2-fyba's and rf2-29ua's numbers by a DIFFERENT MECHANISM, and the per-file census matches exactly. RE-DERIVE ANYWAY — four workers have now produced four numbers and every reconciliation has been worth more than the repair.

CORRECTION TO CARRY: it is 100 remaining, in 38 files — not the 99 an earlier brief of mine stated.

A LEAD ALREADY WAITING FOR YOU. rf2-29ua's control found that once its four files stop claiming the foreign throw, the escaping throw is claimed one frame further down by implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/controlled_input_matrix_dom_cljs_test.cljs:685. THAT ROW HOLDS A LITERAL (done) WITH A .catch AFTER IT, SO IT IS ALREADY IN YOUR SCOPE. controlled-input-matrix sorts BEFORE controls-kit, so its callback sits deeper in the stack — the throw unwound past all four repaired files to the nearest still-defective handler. Expect the same inheritance as you repair: rf2-0r3j saw it at behavior_matrix:238, rf2-ua8r saw TWO rows claim it, and rf2-ua8r's escaped past freehand entirely into implementation/adapters/reagent.

ONE STALE DOCSTRING CLAIM, already dropped by #7964 but check for copies: the old finish! docstring said a duplicate done is "invisible to the browser gate". FALSE since rf2-u0cy4/#7190 — run-browser-tests.cjs promotes the duplicate-done literal to a FATAL match and drift-checks it against the installed cljs.test/run_block.

FIVE THINGS EARLIER BATCHES PAID FOR, all still binding:
  - A REPAIRED CHAIN MUST SCAN TO ZERO, not merely gain a trailing step. Two workers' first scripted passes left rows calling done twice; both were caught by re-scanning, not by the gate.
  - DO NOT HOIST TEARDOWN MECHANICALLY. Across five batches the split ran 24/8/25/0 left-in-place against far fewer hoisted, and the dominant reason is THE FAILURE ARM DOING LESS, NOT MORE. In three cases THE SUCCESS ARM'S TEARDOWN IS THE ACT UNDER TEST, with the next assertion reading a count as exactly zero.
  - BALANCE-CHECK YOUR PARENS WITH A READER. Three workers hit off-by-one tails; every one was caught by a checker rather than by a gate.
  - run-async ADOPTION IS NOT THE CHEAP WIN — its generic message would replace every row's own diagnostic.
  - THE BROWSER LANE BASELINE IS 1293 / 8010, measured independently by four workers. Do not trust 8008; MEASURE YOUR OWN BASE before editing.
close_reason: PR #7968. All 55 chains the literal-(done) signature saw on origin/main (NOT the 100 the note quoted — that number was four commits early; the derivation, calibrated against both campaign landmarks, is in the PR body). Plus 5 of a THIRD class the control found: a let-bound closure that CLOSES OVER done, invisible to both campaign signatures. implementation/freehand now reads ZERO under literal, helper-aware and closure-aware censuses. The 32 closure-forced chains outside freehand are rf2-e8kc.

title: hic — n/defcomponent's :server policy is validated but still consulted by nothing
description:
# The native tier's `:server` policy has a roster and still has no reader

Filed by the worker that closed **rf2-u9lk** (PR for rf2-34a7 + rf2-u9lk).
rf2-u9lk had two faults; this bead carries the half that was deliberately NOT
built.

## What rf2-u9lk fixed

Fault 1 — the missing rosters — is closed. `re-frame.hicasso.native/declared-server`
now refuses a declaration key outside `#{:server}` (`:rf.error/hicasso-native-unknown-option`)
and a value outside `#{:client-only :render}` (`:rf.error/hicasso-native-bad-server-policy`),
both at LOAD from inside the extent `declaring!` opened, so the refusal carries the
author's own file and line.

## What it did NOT fix, and why

Fault 2 — the field is consulted by no runtime path. `native.cljc` stamps it onto
the tier marker and nothing branches on it: there is no server walk in the tier and
no SSR arm. `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/adversarial-risks.md:18` defers

the machinery rather than validating the declaration.

reads: the namespace headline example (`{:server :render}  ; recorded; read in Phase 3`),
`defcomponent`'s docstring, and `declared-server`'s. The witness row at
`native_fence_cljs_test.cljs` says in its own wording that the policy is recorded
and not yet consulted, so it no longer presents itself as coverage of a live policy.

`native_abi_cljs_test.cljs`'s sibling assertion was deliberately left alone: there
the recording is the CONTROL for `n/lazy`'s hard-coded "client-only", a decision
that genuinely IS consulted, so asserting the recording is what makes the contrast
row mean something.

## Done when (Phase 3, not before)

- A server path in the native tier consults `:server`, or the field is removed.
- If consulted: the witness asserts the EFFECT — bytes emitted or withheld — rather
  than the marker, and the three deferral statements above come out.
- If removed: `component`'s third argument, the marker's `:server` slot, `n/lazy`'s
  hard-coded "client-only", `declared-server` and its two complaint ids all go with
  it, which is a bigger change than it looks and is why the deferral is the right
  answer today.

notes:

the establish-then-report step ended the work).

rf2-hic-046's chartered work, not this bead's; and the reader cannot be built here without either
inventing the second policy mechanism audit #7839 forbade or pre-empting hic-046's server door.
RECOMMENDATION: keep deferred; block this bead on rf2-hic-046 rather than dispatching it again.

1. THE CENSUS — `:server` HAS NO READER, AND NOR DOES THE MARKER THAT CARRIES IT.
   `git grep -n 'rf2:hicasso-native-tier'` over the whole tracked tree (minus `.beads`) returns

   not mention hicasso at all. This is the same census hic-046's 2026-08-11 note recorded for

   native component renders on the server, which is what the fence harness measures. So the entire
   content of the wiring is the `:client-only` arm, WHICH IS THE DEFAULT AND THEREFORE EVERY
   DECLARATION-LESS COMPONENT. Two shapes exist and both are owned elsewhere:

title: resources: :rf.mutation/execute is a SILENT no-op when the mutation id is not registered
description:
Measured while building rf2-hic-051's forms recipes.

## What happens

`[:rf.mutation/execute {:mutation :m/unregistered :params {...} :instance :i :reply-to [...]}]` mints NO instance, issues NO request, settles nothing, and reports nothing at all. The passive read `[:rf/mutation {:instance :i}]` answers the idle empty-state map afterwards -- byte-identical to what it answers before any write has ever run:

    {:settled? false :status :idle :result nil :optimistic? false
     :error nil :pending? false :error? false :affected-keys nil :success? false}

No console error, no thrown ex-info, no trace-visible warning.

## How it was found, and why the silence costs

In the `:browser-test` build a witness application's `reg-mutation`, performed at ns-load, was gone by the time a row ran (the reset fixture restores a registrar baseline and the resources artefact's own per-test reset clears the mutation kind). Every symptom pointed at the TRANSPORT: the form submitted, the gate passed, the handler ran, `:attempted?` was set -- and the `:rf.http/managed` recorder stayed empty. Four browser-lane runs were spent proving in turn that it was not the `:fx [[:dispatch ...]]` turn, not the mounted facade's frame, and not `with-new-frame`, before reading `rf/mutation-meta` showed `false`. Re-registering inside the row made the same execute work on the next line.

The same lane in `:node-test` was green throughout, which is what made it look like a build difference rather than a registration one.

## The ask

`:rf.mutation/execute` should FAIL LOUD on an unregistered mutation id -- the artefact's own `ex-info` with a canonical `:rf.error/id`, naming the mutation id, in the shape `reg-mutation`'s own fail-closed registration boundary already uses (`:rf.error/mutation-bad-spec`). A write the runtime cannot perform is not the same fact as a write nobody has asked for, and today the read cannot tell them apart.

Check the resource read path for the same hole before deciding the shape.

## Where it was met

implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/forms/events.cljs (register-save!) documents the workaround the witness uses.

title: hic — the error region is exported as h/boundary and documented as h/error-boundary
description:

document that names it calls it `h/error-boundary`. One of the two is wrong and

      boundary impl-boundary/boundary)

There is no `error-boundary` var anywhere under

`h/error-boundary` appears in:

- `docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/17-errors.md` (5 occurrences, including the

- `docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/21-code-splitting.md` (3)

title: Route-path census is blind to the app trees under implementation/ (two holes)
description:
rf2-wqnl's route-path census (implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_path_census_test.clj) has two blind spots, and TOGETHER they hide the exact application whose collision motivated it.

HOLE 1 - the tree roster. `app-roots` is ["examples" "testbeds"], repo-relative. The Hicasso witness applications live under implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/ (slice, todo, and now navigation, rf2-hic-042). They load into the SAME shared node bundle (`hicasso/test` is a :node-test source path), so their paths are just as process-global as an examples/ app's - and none of them is censused.

HOLE 2 - the column-1 filter. Those applications register through a `(register!)` FUNCTION called at column 1, because re-frame.test-support's reset fixture rolls back a registration made before the fixture snapshot. The `reg-route` forms therefore sit INDENTED inside a defn, and `top-level-reg-route` (#\"(?m)^\((?:[^...]+/)?reg-route\s\") cannot see them. So even adding implementation/hicasso/test to `app-roots` would census nothing.

EVIDENCE: rf2-hic-042 added implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/navigation/routes.cljs registering "/navigation" and "/navigation/article/:slug" at namespace load. `cd implementation/routing && clojure -M:test` ran 522 tests / 3086 assertions before AND after - an identical count, i.e. zero new claims seen. The prefix was verified BY HAND instead.

The slice's own routes.cljs docstring is the irony: it is the app that broke twelve RealWorld assertions, and the census cannot see it.

REMEDY (a suggestion, not a ruling): widen `app-roots` to include implementation/hicasso/test, and widen the claim scanner to see a reg-route indented inside a top-level defn that is CALLED at column 1. The second half is the harder one and may want a different instrument (e.g. reading the analyzer, as examples/require_graph.clj does) rather than a wider regex. Note the allowlist would then have to absorb nothing - slice, todo and navigation are all already prefixed.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7972 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7972). Both holes reproduced and measured: app-roots missed implementation/hicasso/test (0 hicasso claims), and widening app-roots ALONE moved files scanned 101 -> 231 with claims stuck at 39 -> 39. A THIRD hole not in the bead: even at column 1 the reader silently dropped any claim whose id was not a keyword literal, which is exactly how the three witness apps write theirs (a def'd symbol) - so the suggested regex widening alone would also have moved 39 -> 39. The column-1 regex + clojure.edn form-reader are replaced by clojure.tools.reader over the whole file at :features #{:cljs}: the walk never descends into a function body, follows a defn only when load-time code mentions its name (to a fixpoint), and resolves def'd-symbol ids and ::auto-resolved keywords against the file itself. A reached reg-route whose id or path is not a resolvable literal is REPORTED, never skipped. Claims 39 -> 45; routing lane 522/3086 -> 523/3105, exit 0. Planted collision between navigation and slice on /slice reds the lane naming BOTH claimants with file and line (exit 1); restore verified by sha256. No allowlist entry added or needed - slice, todo and navigation are all already prefixed. Subject unchanged: still a path gate, not an id gate. No hot-zone file, no deps.edn path.

## Deliverables

3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.

5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.

title: hicasso guide: 05-forms.md teaches a re-frame.hicasso.forms module that does not exist
description:

There is no such namespace. `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/` holds `evidence`, `motion`, `native`, `tool` and `impl/`, and nothing else. `naming-ledger.md` row 16 correctly records the module ns as *provisional / open*; the guide chapter does not.

rf2-hic-051 examined whether to build it and REFUSED, at source: the extraction gate is 'a second caller' (specification §7) and there is exactly one -- the Todo witness's edit-in-place row. The slice, which the bead names as a candidate, does not use the buffered protocol at all, and the vendor screen (rf2-hic-047) does not exist. `h/reg-state` is already the addressed-draft door.

## The ask

Rewrite the chapter onto the doors that exist -- `h/reg-state`, `::h/clear`, `::h/revision`, the `:on-key-down` key map, `reg-mutation` + `[:rf/mutation {:instance ...}]` -- or mark every `forms/` section explicitly as a proposal that has not shipped. The runnable recipes on the real doors landed with rf2-hic-051 at `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/forms/`, and `docs/design/hicasso/product/forms-recipes.md` states what each is written on -- both are usable as the source for the rewrite.
